issues.title: Support classifier models on custom providers (generic decisions-style classifier API)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
> [!note]
> this would mean making the llama.cpp carve out more general I think. Details were LLM generated at my direction.

## Context

pi supports classifier models (typed yes/no/choice/score questions with next-token probabilities) through two paths today:

1. **Built-in classifier providers** — `typesafe` (System One `/systemone`), `openrouter`, `cloudflare-workers-ai` (clef).
2. **llama.cpp providers** — implemented client-side: pi tokenizes label tokens ("Yes"/"No", letters) via `/tokenize` and reads next-token logprobs. This requires llama.cpp server endpoints (`/tokenize`, `/props`, `/completion`).

## Gap

OpenAI-compatible custom routers that expose their own decisions-style route cannot participate:

- `models.json` providers are chat-only — the `ProviderConfigSchema` has no `type` discriminant on model entries and no `classifiers` implementations map, so a classifier model cannot be declared statically. The documented workaround is `pi.registerProvider()` from an extension (custom-provider.md), which works but keeps the model out of the static catalog and requires every consumer to carry registration code.
- The llama-cpp path is unavailable to non-llama.cpp routers. Verified against a llama.cpp-router-style server exposing `POST /v1/decisions`: `/props` and `/tokenize` return 404, so `llama-cpp-classify` cannot reach a router that only offers OpenAI-compatible routes plus its decisions endpoint.

Concretely: a router exposing `POST {baseUrl}/decisions` with:

```json
{
  "model": "gemma4",
  "input": "…context text…",
  "questions": [
    { "id": "action", "type": "choice", "question": "…", "options": [{ "name": "approve" }, { "name": "ask" }, { "name": "deny" }] },
    { "id": "safe", "type": "yes_no", "question": "…" },
    { "id": "risk", "type": "score", "question": "…", "levels": ["none", "low", "high"] }
  ]
}
```

returning `{ "answers": { "<id>": { "type": "choice", "choice": "approve", "probabilities": { "A": 0.99, "B": 0.005, "C": 0.005 } }, … }, "usage": { "input_tokens": 368, "output_tokens": 20 } }` cannot be declared as a classifier model in static config.

## Proposal

Two parts, independently shippable:

1. **pi-ai: a generic `openai-decisions` classifier api** (name TBD — `decisions-v1` also works since the wire isn't OpenAI-standardized). Question mapping: `bool` → `yes_no` (criteria appended as "Yes means: …/No means: …"), `choice` → `options: [{name}]`, `score` → `levels`. Answer mapping: `yes_no.probabilities.yes` → bool probability; choice letters (`A`,`B`,`C`…) mapped back to criteria names in order. Follow the `typesafe-system-one` transport pattern (retry, timeout, usage passthrough — the routers report input/output tokens at no cost).

2. **Static classifier entries in `models.json`** — `type: "classifier"` model entries on a custom provider, same-model-id-across-operations-remains-distinct (registerProvider already guarantees this; replicate in the static path). Classifier models stay out of `/model`, reachable via `findOfType("classifier", provider, id)` and codemode `models.classify`.

With both, a router declares both bindings for the same weights:

```jsonc
"home": {
  "baseUrl": "http://grace:4000/v1",
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "models": [
    { "id": "gemma4", "name": "Gemma 4", "…" : "…" },
    { "type": "classifier", "id": "gemma4", "api": "openai-decisions" }
  ]
}
```

## Field notes from a real calibration effort

Built a tool-call safety gate (rm-guard) on these endpoints; findings relevant to the api design:

- **Answer keying differs by backend**: `/v1/decisions` keys choice probabilities by positional letters; System One echoes the criteria key names. The mapping must be per-api.
- **One question at a time**: adding a second question to the same call shifted yes/no calibration dramatically on gemma4 (identical input, p(yes) 0.99 → 0.03). Worth documenting: keep safety-critical questions isolated per call.
- **Phrasing sensitivity**: calibration flipped entirely on input-template wording; thresholds must be calibrated per model + template. ~100–250ms per call, logprob-based (`completion_tokens: 0`) — fine for inline tool-call gating.

## Offer

Happy to work on an implementation — the adapter for (1) exists as a working extension (`registerDecisionsProvider` in https://github.com/sdougbrown/pi-rm-guard, `src/decisions-provider.ts`) and can be ported into `packages/ai/src/api/` following the `typesafe-system-one` pattern, with schema changes for (2) in `model-config`. Point me at the preferred shape (api naming, error contract) and I'll send a PR.

issues.title: Compaction summaries ignore the transport setting (always WebSocket-first on openai-codex)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

The `transport` setting is not applied to compaction summary requests. With `"transport": "sse"`, ordinary openai-codex requests use SSE, but automatic and manual (`/compact`) summaries still go out over WebSocket.

In 1.1.0 (installed dist):

- `core/compaction/compaction.js` `createSummarizationOptions()` builds `{ maxTokens, signal, apiKey, headers, env, sessionId }` (plus reasoning). There is no `transport`.
- `core/agent-session.js` calls the default compactor with `this.agent.streamFunction` and passes no transport; `core/sdk.js` adds timeout/retry/header policy to the summary options but does not fill in the settings transport.
- `openai-codex-responses.js` then defaults the missing transport to `auto`, which is WebSocket-first. Because summaries use `cacheRetention: "none"`, there is no cache session id, so a summary also does not see the session's sticky SSE fallback after an earlier WebSocket failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"transport": "sse"` in settings and use an `openai-codex` model.
2. Lower `compaction.reserveTokens` so compaction triggers early, and run until an automatic compaction happens (or run `/compact`).
3. Observe the transport per request (for example with a custom `fetch` in the SDK): ordinary requests make one HTTP call; the summary request makes none, so it used WebSocket.

Observed in our test: `ordinary request: transport=sse, HTTP calls=1` / `summary request: transport=undefined, HTTP calls=0`. Passing `transport: "sse"` explicitly to the summary request made it use SSE and it succeeded.

### Expected behavior

Summary requests use the same transport as ordinary requests (or there is a documented setting for them). This matters when users switch to SSE to avoid WebSocket errors: we saw a Sol session near 255k tokens where auto-compaction failed with "Auto-compaction cancelled / This operation was aborted / WebSocket error", and switching the setting to SSE would not have changed the path that failed.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.1.0, Node 22, Linux.

(Drafted with an AI coding agent from a bounded test against the installed source, reviewed by me.)

issues.title: [Windows] Terminal left in mouse-tracking/focus/kitty-keyboard modes after abrupt exit -> escape-sequence flood in shell prompt

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

When pi 1.1.0 terminates without running its TUI teardown (crash, V8 OOM abort, native abort, hard kill — any path that bypasses `beforeTerminalStop()`), the terminal is left with **mouse tracking, focus reporting and the kitty keyboard protocol still enabled**. The shell prompt that follows (PowerShell in my case) is then flooded with raw escape sequences on every mouse move / key press, making it unusable — PSReadLine even crashes on the flood.

## Environment

- pi: **1.1.0** (updated from 1.0.4 via `pi update`)
- OS: Windows 10 20H2 (10.0.19042)
- Shell left dirty: Windows PowerShell 5.1 + PSReadLine 2.0.0 (plain conhost window)
- Observed on a long-running session; pi died abruptly mid-turn right after a `write` tool result (no error output, no Windows Error Reporting event — consistent with V8 OOM/native abort, which runs no JS hooks). The flood reproduces for **any** exit path that skips teardown, including killing pi from Task Manager.

## Observed behavior

After pi died, every mouse movement over the PowerShell prompt injected sequences like these as *input* (from PSReadLine's crash-report key dump):

```
ESC [ 35 ; 49 ; 14 M   ESC [ 35 ; 49 ; 15 M   ESC [ 35 ; 50 ; 16 M   ...
ESC [ I                (focus in)
ESC [ 1 : 3 ; 2 : 3 u  (kitty keyboard protocol key event)
```

- `ESC[<b;c;rM`-style motion reports → SGR mouse (`?1003` any-motion + `?1006`) left on
- `ESC[I` → focus reporting (`?1004`) left on
- `u`-terminated events → kitty keyboard protocol pushed (`ESC[>7u`), never popped

The prompt fills with literal garbage (`[I[35;49;14M[35;49;15M...`), and PSReadLine eventually dies:

```
System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: top (actual value was -48109).
   at System.Console.SetCursorPosition(Int32 left, Int32 top)
   at Microsoft.PowerShell.PSConsoleReadLine.ReallyRender(RenderData renderData, String defaultColor)
   at Microsoft.PowerShell.PSConsoleReadLine.ForceRender()
   ...
```

## Root cause (from `dist/bundle`, 1.1.0)

pi-tui's terminal lifecycle:

- `beforeTerminalStart()` writes `ESC[?1049h` (alt screen) + `ENABLE_BUTTON_MOTION_MOUSE` / `ENABLE_ALL_MOTION_MOUSE` = `ESC[?1000h ESC[?1002h ESC[?1004h ESC[?1006h` (+ `?1003h` outside tmux/screen) + kitty query/push `ESC[>7u ESC[?u`, and hides the cursor.
- Restore happens only in `beforeTerminalStop()` / `afterTerminalStop()`, guarded by the `altScreenActive` / `mouseEnabled` / `keyboardProtocolPushed` internal flags.

If the process dies without those running, the disable sequences are never written. Notes:

- The `uncaughtException` handler (`uncaughtCrash`) does attempt `ui.stop()` in a try/catch, which helps for that path — but there is no process-level last resort for paths where even that doesn't run (OOM/native abort aside, any future regression in the teardown chain leaves the terminal dirty again).
- On win32, console close (CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT) is not handled either: `signals=["SIGTERM"]; process.platform!=="win32"&&signals.push("SIGHUP")`.
- There is currently no opt-out: the TUI is instantiated without a `mouse` option, and pi-tui defaults it to `true`.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Process-level last-resort restore** — register `process.on("exit")` early and synchronously write the disable sequences via `fs.writeSync(1, ...)` if they were enabled (`?1006l ?1004l ?1003l ?1002l ?1000l`, kitty pop `ESC[<u`, `?1049l`, `ESC[?25h`). It costs nothing on clean exit (the normal teardown already restored, so the hook can no-op), and it covers every path where JS still runs (uncaughtException, unhandledRejection, any `process.exit`). Tracking "what is actually enabled" from observed stdout traffic rather than internal flags also makes it immune to flag desync.
2. **Handle SIGHUP / CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT on win32** — even a best-effort restore within the ~5 s grace beats nothing.
3. **Opt-out switch** — a setting/CLI flag to disable mouse tracking for users whose terminal or multiplexer misbehaves.

## Workaround shipped locally

I wrote a small extension that watches `process.stdout.write` for the enable/disable sequences (tracking the wire, not internal flags) and restores the modes from a `process.on("exit")` hook using `fs.writeSync`. Verified with a 20-assertion harness (enable/disable/push/pop/idempotency/passthrough) and a `pi -p` smoke test; it restores correctly after uncaughtException and `process.exit` paths. Happy to open a PR if you'd take one.

For reference, a sibling project hit the same class of bug on Windows: opencode#26198 ("Terminal flooded with raw mouse escape sequences (SGR) when running commands").

issues.title: Bun-installed pi + Node runtime: every extension fails with `Cannot find module 'jiti'`
issues.body:
_(AI-assisted report, drafted with an agent and reviewed by me. I confirmed with `pi -ne` that this is core, not an extension.)_

**What happened?**

pi installed with Bun (`bun install -g`), launched with Node (the `pi` bin is `#!/usr/bin/env node`). Every extension fails:

```
Failed to load extension: Cannot find module 'jiti'
Require stack:
- ~/.bun/install/cache/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0@@.../dist/bundle/chunks/jiti-static-loader-*.js
```

The same install loads extensions fine under Bun, and works when pi is installed with npm.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `bun install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`
2. Put any `.ts` extension in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (or pass `-e path`)
3. Run `pi` with Node: `Cannot find module 'jiti'`; the extension never executes

**Why (brief)**

The release bundle is built with `PI_BUNDLED_NODE=true` (`scripts/build-coding-agent-bundle.mjs`), so `isBundledNode` is true (`src/config.ts:29`) and the loader uses `jiti-static-loader` (`src/core/extensions/loader.ts:45,50`). For Node the bundle rewrites `jiti/static` into a lazy `require("jiti")`. That require resolves from the chunk's `import.meta.url`, which Node realpaths into `~/.bun/install/cache/...`; there is no `node_modules/jiti` anywhere up that tree because Bun hoists dependencies to `~/.bun/install/global/node_modules`. Resolution fails.

**Expected behavior**

Extensions load regardless of which package manager installed pi, as long as Node can read the files.

**Version**

pi 1.1.0 · node v26.3.1 · bun 1.4.2 · Termux/Android aarch64

Happy to test a patch against this install.

issues.title: codemode: Node --watch aborts sandbox execution
Editor: mouse-selected text is ignored by Backspace/Delete (deletes char-by-char)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

In the prompt editor (fullscreen TUI), after mouse-dragging to select several words and then pressing Backspace/Delete:

- the first delete removes a character at the mouse-click position (not the whole selection);
- subsequent deletes act on the internal cursor, which falls back to deleting one character at a time.

The selected text is never deleted as a unit. Reproduced with English/ASCII text too (not IME-related).

### Root cause

In `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`, `handleMouse()` only handles `click` events and explicitly leaves press/drag/release unhandled so the renderer's screen-level selection can run over the editor rows:

```ts
// Leave press/drag/release unhandled so the renderer's screen-level text
// selection can run over the editor rows (drag to select, release to copy).
```

So the visible "selection" belongs to the renderer (drag → release → copy), while the editor keeps no selection state (`state` is only `lines` / `cursorLine` / `cursorCol`). `handleBackspace()` / `handleForwardDelete()` therefore always delete one grapheme at the internal cursor, never the highlighted range.

### Related

PR #8678 ("feat(tui): edit selected prompt text") proposed exactly this fix — let the focused editor receive completed mouse selections so Backspace/Delete remove the selected text — but it was closed without merging (`merged_at: null`).

### Expected behavior

Mouse-dragged text should become the editor's internal selection; Backspace/Delete should delete the whole selection in one keypress.

### Environment / Version

- macOS, Apple Terminal.app (488)
- pi 1.1.0 (also reproduced on 0.87.1)
- tuiMode: fullscreen

issues.title: Apple Terminal: Enter inserts a newline instead of submitting (needs two Enters)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

In the prompt editor, pressing Enter does not send the message — it inserts a newline (equivalent to Ctrl+J). A second Enter is required to actually submit.

Reproduced with plain English/ASCII input, so it is not an IME issue.

### Root cause

In `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`, `handleInput()` checks the "new line" branch **before** the "submit" branch, and the new-line branch treats a bare `\n` as newline:

```ts
// New line (runs before Submit)
if (kb.matches(data, "tui.input.newLine") ||
    (data.charCodeAt(0) === 10 && data.length > 1) ||
    data === "\x1b\r" ||
    data === "\x1b[13;2~" ||
    (data.length > 1 && data.includes("\x1b") && data.includes("\r")) ||
    (data === "\n" && data.length === 1)) {   // bare LF treated as newline
    // ...
    this.addNewLine();
    return;
}
// Submit (Enter)
if (kb.matches(data, "tui.input.submit")) { /* ... this.submitValue(); */ }
```

At the same time, in `packages/tui/src/keys.ts`, `matchesKey(data, "enter")` returns true for `\n` when the Kitty keyboard protocol is inactive:

```ts
return (data === "\r" ||
        (!_kittyProtocolActive && data === "\n") ||   // LF == Enter on non-Kitty terminals
        // ...
       );
```

and `matchesKey(data, "ctrl+j")` also returns true for `\n` (raw control char). So a bare `\n` is ambiguous — it can mean Enter or Ctrl+J — and the editor currently always resolves it as a newline. Apple Terminal does not use the Kitty keyboard protocol, so an Enter arriving as LF triggers this path.

### Expected behavior

A single Enter should submit; a newline should only come from Shift+Enter / Ctrl+J.

### Related

- #5188 (shift+enter submits and does not create new line)
- #4922 (fix(tui): detect Apple Terminal Shift+Enter)
- #7126 (Rename session needs Enter pressed twice)

### Environment / Version

- macOS, Apple Terminal.app (488)
- pi 1.1.0 (also reproduced on 0.87.1)
- tuiMode: fullscreen

issues.title: Clarify Anthropic onPayload model-retargeting responsibility

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Document whether an `onPayload` hook that changes only `payload.model` must also repair every model-specific field. The [current callback contract](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c5f5b3282d5e4203c085e59837ba17aeaf2829b5/packages/ai/src/types.ts#L174-L178) permits inspecting/replacing a raw payload; it does not promise safe model switching. I am proposing clarification first, not assuming automatic rebuilding is already required.

### Why?

[`packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/c5f5b3282d5e4203c085e59837ba17aeaf2829b5/packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts#L639-L644) builds the request from the original model's compatibility flags, then runs `onPayload`. A model-only override from `claude-opus-5-5` to `claude-opus-4-6` retains the managed per-turn effort markers. Four live requests with pi-ai 1.1.0 at the native Anthropic endpoint isolated the result:

1. One user message (`Reply with exactly: ok`), `thinkingEnabled: true`, `effort: "low"`, `maxTokens: 128`, `cacheRetention: "none"`, original model Opus 5.5: **200**.
2. Same call, hook returns the original payload with only `model: "claude-opus-4-6"` changed: **400**, `output_config.effort requires a model that supports per-turn effort; this model does not`.
3. Same swap, removing only the generated `role: "system"` effort markers: **200**, response model Opus 4.6. `block_binding`, both betas and top-level effort `high` remain; this proves acceptance, not preservation of the requested `low` effort.
4. Same swap, removing only `block_binding` instead: **400**, same effort error.

This isolates the marker incompatibility for that request; it does not show that Opus 4.6 rejects binding controls. The one-user probe had no other system messages; deleting system messages is not a general workaround. No signed-thinking replay/drop semantics or proxy/OpenRouter route was tested. This was a direct pi-ai SDK probe with no extensions, not a `pi -ne` reproduction. Related: #4038 (raw hook ordering), #10759 (different trigger: explicit beta override).

### How? (optional)

Add a note to `packages/ai/README.md`'s “Debugging Provider Payloads” section: select the target model before serialization (pass its model object to the stream call); raw `onPayload` retargeting leaves derived fields and bookkeeping tied to the original model. No automatic rewriting is proposed.

I plan to contribute this focused documentation change. If model-only retargeting should instead be supported by core, please identify the desired contract before a separately designed correction. No fix is claimed here; requesting maintainer direction/approval.

issues.title: Bug Report: github-copilot provider fails on slow/flaky networks; no config to tune

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

The built-in `github-copilot` provider has no network resilience: hard-coded 5s timeout, zero retries, no progress during long waits, cancellation not immediate, and all knobs are hard-coded constants with no env var override. This makes login impossible on high-latency links (mobile, VPN, international) or any transient network hiccup.

Root causes in `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts`:
1. **5s hard-coded timeout** per request — catalog regularly takes 6s+
2. **No retry** on `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `ECONNRESET`, `EAI_AGAIN`, DNS failures, TLS hiccups
3. **No progress callbacks** during authorization polling (can run minutes silently)
4. **`AbortSignal` not respected in sleeps** — Esc during poll waits for current interval to finish
5. **`refreshModels` returns `[]` on error** — empties model picker instead of preserving previous list
6. **429 responses ignored** — no `Retry-After` handling for catalog/policy endpoints
7. **All parameters hard-coded** — no `PI_COPILOT_*` env vars to tune for corporate proxy, mobile, CI

Impact: users on unreliable networks cannot use Copilot; transient errors require manual `/login` retry; mid-session token refresh failure logs user out and clears model picker; cannot adapt without rebuilding Pi.


### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Add 6s latency (simulates typical /models response time)
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 6000ms

# 2. Login
/login github-copilot

# 3. Observe: "The operation was aborted due to timeout" on catalog fetch
#    (same failure occurs on device code, auth poll, or token exchange with any transient error)
```

### Expected behavior

Wrap all OAuth HTTP calls in a retry helper with configurable knobs (env with defaults):
- `PI_COPILOT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (20000)
- `PI_COPILOT_NET_RETRIES` (2), `PI_COPILOT_NET_RETRY_BUDGET_MS` (45000)
- `PI_COPILOT_NET_RETRY_BASE_MS` (500), `PI_COPILOT_NET_RETRY_MAX_MS` (4000)
- `PI_COPILOT_STAGE_RETRIES` (12), `PI_COPILOT_STAGE_BUDGET_MS` (240000)
- `PI_COPILOT_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` (8), `PI_COPILOT_RATE_LIMIT_BUDGET_MS` (180000)

Behavior:
- Exponential backoff + jitter on transient errors
- Per-stage attempt/time budgets (device code, auth poll, token, catalog)
- Progress callbacks on each attempt/retry/stage
- `AbortSignal`-aware sleeps; `CancelledError` never retried
- `refreshModels` returns `undefined` on error (preserves picker)
- Honor `Retry-After` on 429

### Version

1.0.4

The edit completed successfully, but its result contained a ~14.5 MB diff generated from HTML files with very long physical lines. The initial crash happened immediately after the edit. Resuming the same session caused the identical crash because Pi tried to render the saved edit result again. The failure occurs in `ToolExecutionComponent.render()`: ```ts lines.push(...contentLines); ``` A long line wraps into more display lines than V8 allows as function arguments to Array.push(), resulting in: ```text RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at ToolExecutionComponent.render (.../tool-execution.js:189:23) at Container.render (.../tui.js:61:38) at TuiMainScreen.render (.../tui.js:61:38) at TuiMainScreen.doRender (.../tui-main-screen.js:170:29) ``` I reproduced it with extensions disabled (pi -ne) and a synthetic session containing no project data. scene This occurred during a research workflow using marimo. I exported the notebooks as static HTML reports and was preparing the generated reports for commit to a Git repository. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create an HTML file containing one very long physical line: ```bash mkdir /tmp/pi-edit-repro cd /tmp/pi-edit-repro python3 -c 'open("large.html", "w").write("")' ``` 2. Start Pi with extensions disabled: ```bash pi -ne ``` 3. Ask Pi to use the built-in edit tool to replace before with after in large.html. ```bash use the built-in edit tool replace before with after in large.html. ``` 4. When Pi renders the edit diff, the TUI exits with: ```text RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at ToolExecutionComponent.render (.../tool-execution.js:189:23) ``` 5. If the edit result was saved before the crash, resume the session: ```bash pi -c -ne ``` 6. issues.title: github-copilot: on 401 or 403 before expires, refresh the session token once and retry

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**Package**: packages/ai, `auth/oauth/github-copilot` and `auth/resolve`
**Version seen**: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.99.1, @earendil-works/pi-ai 0.99.1

## What happens

Pi's `github-copilot` provider keeps the Copilot session token in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` as `access`, with `expires` set to the token's `expires_at` less five minutes. `resolveStoredOAuth` mints a new token from `refresh` only when `expires` is less than five minutes away. It never mints on an API refusal.

When GitHub revokes a session token before its `expires_at`, every model call answers:

```
github-copilot API error (403): 403 forbidden
```

The failure lasts until the stored `expires`, up to about 24 hours, or until someone edits `auth.json`. The stored `refresh` (the GitHub OAuth token) stays valid for the whole period.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-09-30)

- 30 Pi sessions ran on one GitHub Copilot Enterprise seat, each with its own `auth.json`.
- Between 10:45Z and 11:00Z GitHub revoked every session token minted before that time. 27 sessions held such a token. Each answered 403 `forbidden` on both `GET /models` and `POST /chat/completions` at `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`.
- A new mint from `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` with the same `refresh` answered 200, and that token answered 200 on both endpoints.
- The old and new tokens' claims differed only in `iat`, `exp`, `ip` and `sl` (`sl=0` on the revoked tokens, `sl=1` on the new ones). `sku` and the feature flags were the same.
- Workaround: set `github-copilot.expires` to 0 in `auth.json`. Pi read the file again and minted a new token at its next call, and every session worked.

## Request

When a request to the Copilot API answers 401 or 403 and the stored `expires` is still in the future:

1. Refresh the session token once from `refresh`, under the same credential-store lock `resolveStoredOAuth` uses, so that concurrent requests and processes mint once.
2. Retry the failed request once with the new token.
3. If the refresh fails, or the retry answers 401 or 403 again, report the error as now.

One refresh and one retry per request keep a real authorization failure (a removed seat, a policy block) visible and bounded.

## Impact

Every Pi session on a Copilot seat stops on each model call after a server-side revocation and cannot recover without a manual edit to `auth.json`. With the retry, the first failed call recovers the session.

issues.title: Extensions: keyed custom message drafts — keep one live copy of a recurring context block without tombstone + re-emit

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an optional `key` to `CustomMessageEntryDraft`. When a custom message draft is appended with a `key`, any earlier session entry carrying the same key is superseded in the same operation, leaving exactly one live copy of that block.

### Why?

Extensions that maintain a single recurring context block — a goal/todo recitation pinned near the tail, a status note, standing instructions — currently must emit the block twice per update:

1. a `context_edit` draft with `replacement: null` targeting the previous entry's id (tombstone), then
2. a fresh `custom_message` draft with the new content.

That is the only way to keep exactly one live copy of a block that also stays near the end of the transcript. The costs:

- The previous entry's id must be tracked across turns. A stale id (compaction removed the entry, or the block never existed yet) silently leaves two live copies or loses the block.
- Every update writes two entries, and session files accumulate a tombstone per update cycle.
- The two-draft window is observable: anything reading `getEntries()` between the two drafts sees zero or two copies instead of one.

A keyed draft collapses this to one atomic append: supersede-by-key when a prior copy exists, a plain append when it does not — which also survives compaction, branches, and forks without id bookkeeping.

`context_edit` with a `replacement` already covers in-place edits that keep their position; what is missing is the update-to-tail shape, which is the common case for live blocks the model should attend to most.

### How? (optional)

`CustomMessageEntryDraft.key?: string`. On append, the session manager first removes any existing entry with the same key, then appends the draft. No key set preserves today's behavior exactly.

issues.title: Extensions: settings write API and settings_changed event — extensions hand-roll read-modify-write of settings.json

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a write side to the settings surface exposed to extensions — `pi.updateSettings(patch)`, an atomic read-merge-write against the existing settings files — plus a `settings_changed` event so extensions observe settings mutations regardless of origin (another extension, `/settings`, `pi config`, manual file edit).

Today the extension API is read-only: `pi.getSettings()` is the only settings operation on `ExtensionAPI` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts`); no setter exists anywhere in the API.

### Why?

An extension that persists configuration has no sanctioned mechanism, so the only working pattern is a direct read-modify-write of the shared settings file: re-read `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (and `<cwd>/.pi/settings.json`), parse, mutate, re-serialize. Every extension reimplements it, and it has two structural problems:

1. **Lost updates.** Concurrent writes from two extensions — or an extension racing pi's own settings writers — silently last-write-win. I maintain several extensions that all hand-roll this, and one carries a comment that it must read-merge-write "so concurrent extension writes never clobber" each other: the workaround approximating the atomicity the harness could provide.
2. **No change notification.** Nothing tells an extension that a key changed, so extensions either re-read the file on every access or tell the user to restart pi / `/reload` for a write to take effect.

Pi already persists settings written by extension actions internally (e.g. theme persistence after `ctx.ui.setTheme(...)`), so the machinery for a sanctioned write exists — it is just not on the extension API.

Prior art and the delta:

- #4981 (completed) asked for typed extension-owned namespaces (`pi.settings.register` + CLI integration). The read side landed; the write side did not — the comments there record that extensions still re-read and deep-merge settings files by hand.
- #10375 asked for `pi.registerSetting()` with `/settings` UI integration and scope precedence, and was closed without action.

This proposal is deliberately smaller than both: no registration, no schemas, no UI integration, no new ownership model. It makes what extensions already do today safe and observable, rather than introducing a new subsystem.

### How? (optional)

- `pi.updateSettings(mutator: (current: Settings) => Partial<Settings> | void, scope?: "global" | "project"): void` — a serialized read-merge-write reusing the internal settings manager's existing writers, so `/settings` and any file watchers stay consistent.
- A `settings_changed` extension event carrying the changed keys, emitted after any settings mutation regardless of origin.

issues.title: Fullscreen: a focused overlay blocks transcript scrolling

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

In fullscreen mode (the default in 1.1.0), as soon as a focused overlay is open — anything from `ctx.ui.custom(..., { overlay: true })` — the transcript stops scrolling. Wheel, PageUp/PageDown, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+Up do nothing, even with the pointer over the transcript, well above the overlay. The events are not dropped either: the raw wheel sequence (`\x1b[<64;10;5M`) and `\x1b[5~` arrive in that overlay's `handleInput` as if they were keystrokes.

Why it matters to me: the questionnaire dialog I use to ask questions makes the conversation unreadable while it is open, so I cannot scroll back to the context the question is about.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne --tui-mode fullscreen -e ./repro-overlay-noext.ts` — a focused 12-row overlay that ignores the wheel (full file in my next comment)
2. send a prompt or two so the transcript is taller than the viewport
3. `/wheel-repro`, then wheel over the transcript above the overlay, or press PageUp → nothing moves
4. `Esc` → the same wheel / PageUp scroll immediately again

Same thing with a real dialog: wheel, PageUp and Ctrl+Home are dead until it is collapsed or hidden (`Ctrl+]` in the questionnaire extension I use; hiding it brings scrolling back instantly). `nonCapturing: true` also keeps scrolling alive, but then the overlay never takes focus and gets no keys, so it cannot be used for a dialog.

### Expected behavior

Wheel and page keys should still reach the transcript whenever the focused overlay does not consume them — at the very least when the pointer is outside the overlay's rect. A focused overlay should not be able to freeze the transcript just by ignoring the wheel, and mouse escape sequences should not be delivered to `handleInput` as keyboard input.

The guard that does this is `shouldDeferViewportInputToOverlay()` (`packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts:667`); code pointers and a core-only harness table are in my next comment. I can send a PR for the narrow version, but I do not know whether freezing the viewport under a focused overlay is intentional, so I would rather ask first.

### Version

pi 1.1.0, `--tui-mode fullscreen` (default since 1.0.0; 0.99.2's `--tui-mode` help still said `regular (default)`). Linux / WSL2, Windows Terminal.

issues.title: Make temporary sessions visible and allow saving them in place
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Two related improvements to interactive sessions started with `--no-session`:

1. Show a persistent, visible indication that session history is not being saved, for example “Temporary session · not saved” in the footer. `/session` already shows “File: In-memory”, but that requires explicitly checking.
2. Add an explicit action, such as `/save`, to keep the current session. It should automatically use Pi’s normal session directory and filename convention, preserve the existing session tree and current position, and enable autosaving for subsequent messages without choosing a path or restarting.Only show the session as saved after persistence succeeds. If saving fails, report the error and keep the in-memory conversation intact so the user can retry. Persistence should remain opt-in for `--no-session` sessions.

### Why?

I sometimes start a temporary conversation for a quick question, then realize it is worth keeping. I want to see clearly whether it will survive quitting and be able to keep it when I decide to.

JSONL export/import (#2274, #2356) provides a backup workflow, but does not offer this in-place transition with an automatically chosen session path.


### How? (optional)

Add a persistent temporary-session indicator to the TUI, based on whether the current session is being saved to disk.

Introduce a SessionManager operation, exposed through a command such as `/save`, to persist an in-memory session using the existing session directory and filename conventions. It should write the complete session tree, preserve the current position, and enable normal autosaving only after the initial save succeeds, without restarting the TUI.

If saving fails, keep the session in memory and allow retrying. Calling `/save` on an already-persistent session should not create a duplicate. Add tests for saving existing history, subsequent autosaving, and failure recovery.

I’d be happy to implement this feature and submit a PR if this direction makes sense. Feedback on the command name and where to show the temporary-session indicator would be welcome.

issues.title: Extensions: allow aborting an in-flight request and resuming the same run with an injected reminder

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`ctx.abort()` currently ends the run: the aborted partial stays in the transcript, queued follow-ups are stranded, and the only way to continue is a fresh user turn. I'd like `ctx.abort(continuation)` to optionally resume the same run instead: drop the aborted partial (`contextMode: "discard"`), inject a reminder as a user message, and keep draining follow-up queues within the same run. Additive `turn_start.continuation` marker; `maxAutoContinuations` setting (default 3, `0` disables) as a loop guard.

### Why?

Stream-rule guards (TTSR-style: watch output, abort on violation, remind, continue) can't do this today — they must wait for idle and re-prompt as a new turn, so the partial stays in context, once-only rule windows reset, and every correction costs a whole turn. Safety guards that need to rewind rather than append have the same gap. omp's native TTSR does abort → truncate → inject → continue within one run.

### How?

Store the continuation when `ctx.abort(continuation)` is called; at the aborted request's settle the run loop applies it (drop the partial via `context_edit` entries together with its tool results, prompt the reminder, clear the abort intent) instead of exiting. Dropping the partial and its tool results together avoids the orphaned-toolResults failure mode from #10263. Plain `ctx.abort()` is unchanged and doubles as user interrupt (drops the armed continuation). A failed continuation request settles like an error turn without auto-retrying.

I want to implement this myself — it's already done on my fork (`feat/extension-abort-continuation`, was draft PR #10766, auto-closed before I understood the contribution gate). `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass; the contract is covered by `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-session-abort-continuation.test.ts` (10 tests, one per contract row). Happy to re-raise the PR after approval and to adapt the shape (e.g. extending `steer()` semantics) — the contract is shape-independent.

issues.title: Extension API: acknowledge durable custom-message publication

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

In v0.84.1, `ExtensionAPI.sendMessage()` returns `void` and reports asynchronous failures only through extension error handling. Please add a public async custom-message publication API, for example:

```ts
publishMessage(message, options): Promise<{ entryId: string }>
```

It should:

- resolve with the custom-message entry ID only after a successful write through Pi's existing persistent session-file path;
- reject only if no persistent entry was created, including when persistence is disabled or the session is replaced before the write;
- remain resolved if a provider/model turn fails after persistence, and resolve without waiting for model-turn completion;
- preserve active `steer`, `followUp`, and `nextTurn` delivery plus idle `triggerTurn` behavior;
- define replacement semantics so persistence before replacement leaves the returned ID valid for the session that accepted it; and
- include public types, documentation, and tests.

Here, persistence means a successful write through Pi's existing session-file persistence path. In-memory state or queueing is insufficient; no new `fsync` or power-loss guarantee is requested. Keep `sendMessage()` unchanged for additive fire-and-forget compatibility.

### Why?

Extensions that retain retryable external work need a precise commit boundary before acknowledging or deleting that work.

The current internal `AgentSession.sendCustomMessage()` promise is not that boundary: active delivery can resolve after in-memory queueing, while idle `triggerTurn` waits for the model turn and conflates publication with provider success.

### How? (optional)

Implement this additively and test active and idle delivery, persistence-disabled sessions, replacement before and after persistence, and model failure after persistence.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Right-click paste does not work on Linux/WSL (WezTerm), while it works fine in Claude Code and
Codex in the same terminal. The right-click press IS received by pi (SGR mouse tracking is enabled
and `button === 2` is parsed correctly), but nothing is pasted.

## Cause

`handleRightClickPaste` in `packages/tui/.../tui-alt-screen.ts` returns early because of a hard
`win32` platform gate:

```ts
if (!this.onRightClickPaste ||
    process.platform !== "win32" ||          // ← this
    process.env.TERM_PROGRAM?.toLowerCase() === "vscode" ||
    event.release ||
    event.button !== 2) return false;
```

On Linux `process.platform === "linux"`, so paste is silently disabled. Right-click paste on
Linux/macOS depends on the terminal emulator, not the OS: WezTerm forwards the SGR mouse sequence
(the app sees `button === 2`) without pasting itself. The existing `vscode` carve-out already
delegates to the terminal correctly, so the platform gate is the wrong condition.

## Fix

Remove the `win32` check, keeping the `vscode` carve-out and the remaining conditions:

```ts
if (!this.onRightClickPaste ||
    process.env.TERM_PROGRAM?.toLowerCase() === "vscode" ||
    event.release ||
    event.button !== 2) return false;
```

## Note

Local workaround applied (runtime bundle `dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-2KTBZM5G.js`), but pi's managed
install self-updates and reverts it — needs the upstream fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi on WSL2 (Linux) in WezTerm.
2. Copy some text to the clipboard.
3. Right-click inside the pi TUI input area.

Result: nothing happens. No paste.

### Expected behavior

Right-click should paste the clipboard contents, as it does on Windows and as it does in other
coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) in the same terminal.

### Version

1.0.0

issues.title: skills array: ~ is silently not expanded in pattern entries — !~/path becomes a dead pattern with no warning

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
**Title:**

`skills` array: `~` is silently not expanded in pattern entries — `!~/path` becomes a dead pattern with no warning

---

**Body:**

## Summary

In the `skills` array of `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, plain path entries support `~` expansion, but pattern entries (`!pattern`, `+path`, `-path`, and wildcard entries) do not. A pattern containing `~` can never match anything, and pi produces no error or warning for it.

This is a silent footgun: the same `~` syntax works in one part of the array and is silently ignored in another.

## Environment

- pi 1.1.0, Linux

## Reproduction

`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "skills": [
    "~/.claude/skills",
    "!~/claude-backup/skills/pdf"
  ]
}
```

**Expected:** the `pdf` skill from `~/claude-backup/skills` is excluded (or at least a warning is emitted).

**Actual:** the exclusion has no effect — pi still loads that skill. No error, no diagnostic.

For comparison, all of these *do* work as exclusions:

```json
"!pdf"
"!skills/pdf"
"!/home/<user>/claude-backup/skills/pdf/SKILL.md"
```

So the only broken spelling is the one users are most likely to reach for first, given that `~` works right above it in the same array.

## Root cause

Plain entries and pattern entries go through two different pipelines:

- **Plain entries** → `resolvePathFromBase` → `resolvePath` → `normalizePath` (`utils/paths.js`), which performs tilde expansion (`expandTilde` defaults to true).
- **Pattern entries** → `splitPatterns` (`core/package-manager.js`) keeps the raw string; matching happens in `matchesAnyPattern` / `matchesAnyExactPattern`, which only normalize path separators (`toPosixPath`). Matching targets are fully-expanded real paths, so a pattern string containing a literal `~` never matches.

So `!~/x` is parsed as a valid exclusion pattern whose content is the literal string `~/x` — a pattern that is guaranteed to match nothing, silently.

## Suggestions

Any of these would resolve the confusion (in order of my preference):

1. **Expand `~` in patterns before matching** — run patterns through the same tilde expansion as plain entries. This makes `!~/x` do what users expect.
2. **Emit a warning** when a pattern contains `~` (dead-pattern detection), similar to the existing diagnostics for non-existent paths.
3. **Document the behavior** explicitly in the docs for the `skills` array.

I suspect the current behavior is an emergent property of the two pipelines rather than a deliberate decision, but if it's intentional (e.g. `~` is reserved for some pattern semantics), option 2 or 3 would still help a lot.

Happy to provide more details or test a fix if useful. Thanks for pi — it's a great tool.

issues.title: Headless pi -p hangs forever when OpenAI-compat provider silently drops in-flight connection (timeout not applied)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Headless `pi -p` processes hang **forever** (no error, no retry, 0 CPU) when an OpenAI-compatible provider silently drops an in-flight request connection. Today this happened in 3 separate waves within ~30 minutes during provider-side connection instability — every long-running headless request parked permanently; only external `SIGALRM` wrappers could reclaim them.

## Environment

- pi 1.1.0 (latest release), macOS (arm64)
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Zhipu bigmodel coding plan, custom `base_url`)
- Mode: headless one-shot `pi -p` (automation pipeline), also observed on long-running interactive/subagent requests during the same window

## What happens

1. A long model request is sent over an established connection.
2. The provider/network path silently discards the connection (no RST, no FIN, no error frame; keepalive bytes may still flow).
3. The pi process parks in the event loop awaiting the response promise — forever:
   - `sample` of a hung process: main thread in `AsyncFunctionAwaitResolveClosure` → `uv_cond_wait`; CPU flat at ~2s total after 6+ minutes elapsed.
   - No timeout fires, no retry is attempted (`retry.provider.maxRetries` defaults to `0`), no log line.
4. Fresh connections to the same endpoint work fine during the same window (a 10s curl probe returns in 150ms), so this is connection-lifetime-specific, not endpoint availability.

## Config already tried

- `httpIdleTimeoutMs` at default `300000` — did not trigger in the hung processes (suspect: byte-level idle vs event-level silence, see #8593).
- After the incidents we set `retry.provider.timeoutMs: 120000` + `retry.provider.maxRetries: 2`; not yet verified whether the timeout actually reaches requests on this provider class (#5294 mentions "for all providers that support it" — custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs may be outside that set).

## Request

1. Apply a hard request timeout / `AbortSignal` to **all** provider requests, including custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, with the failure surfaced as an error (so agent-level retry can take over).
2. Consider an SSE **event-level** idle timeout distinct from byte-level idle (a dropped stream with keepalive bytes flowing is invisible to the current check).
3. Reconsider the `retry.provider.maxRetries: 0` default for connection-dropped errors specifically.

## Workaround (for others hitting this)

Wrap headless invocations externally, e.g. `perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' pi -p "..."` — note `exec` preserves the pending alarm in the kernel.

Refs: #4707 (idle timeout config), #5294 (timeout respected for non-Codex providers), #8593 (event-level silence).

issues.title: 交互改进：回答运行中的附带问题后，保留并恢复尚未完成的原任务

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### 希望改变什么？

运行中插入一个附带问题时，希望 Pi 保留尚未完成的原任务：回答后继续执行，或者明确提示原任务已暂停，而不是无提示地结束。此报告是交互体验提案，不主张已确认底层程序 bug。

### 为什么？

实际会话：让 Pi 调研多个子代理插件并给出对比；工具调用之间插入“这个插件是官方插件吗？”；助手仅回答该问题，然后正常结束，直到再次要求“继续”才恢复调研。会话记录没有取消、报错或上下文丢失。

Enter 的 steering 行为符合文档，但“附带提问”并不等于撤销原任务。用户需要反复提醒继续，容易漏掉未完成的工作。此现象可能取决于模型；尚未验证在无扩展环境下是否复现。

环境：Pi 1.1.0；安装了 pi-subagents 0.77.0，但上述调研没有调用子代理。

### 如何实现？（可选）

可以先考虑待完成任务提示，或提供明确的“临时提问，回答后继续原任务”输入语义。暂不提交实现。

issues.title: Headless pi -p hangs forever when OpenAI-compat provider silently drops in-flight connection (timeout not applied)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

Headless `pi -p` processes hang **forever** (no error, no retry, 0 CPU) when an OpenAI-compatible provider silently drops an in-flight request connection. Today this happened in 3 separate waves within ~30 minutes during provider-side connection instability — every long-running headless request parked permanently; only external `SIGALRM` wrappers could reclaim them.

## Environment

- pi 1.1.0 (latest release), macOS (arm64)
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Zhipu bigmodel coding plan, custom `base_url`)
- Mode: headless one-shot `pi -p` (automation pipeline), also observed on long-running interactive/subagent requests during the same window

## What happens

1. A long model request is sent over an established connection.
2. The provider/network path silently discards the connection (no RST, no FIN, no error frame; keepalive bytes may still flow).
3. The pi process parks in the event loop awaiting the response promise — forever:
   - `sample` of a hung process: main thread in `AsyncFunctionAwaitResolveClosure` → `uv_cond_wait`; CPU flat at ~2s total after 6+ minutes elapsed.
   - No timeout fires, no retry is attempted (`retry.provider.maxRetries` defaults to `0`), no log line.
4. Fresh connections to the same endpoint work fine during the same window (a 10s curl probe returns in 150ms), so this is connection-lifetime-specific, not endpoint availability.

## Config already tried

- `httpIdleTimeoutMs` at default `300000` — did not trigger in the hung processes (suspect: byte-level idle vs event-level silence, see #8593).
- After the incidents we set `retry.provider.timeoutMs: 120000` + `retry.provider.maxRetries: 2`; not yet verified whether the timeout actually reaches requests on this provider class (#5294 mentions "for all providers that support it" — custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs may be outside that set).

## Request

1. Apply a hard request timeout / `AbortSignal` to **all** provider requests, including custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, with the failure surfaced as an error (so agent-level retry can take over).
2. Consider an SSE **event-level** idle timeout distinct from byte-level idle (a dropped stream with keepalive bytes flowing is invisible to the current check).
3. Reconsider the `retry.provider.maxRetries: 0` default for connection-dropped errors specifically.

## Workaround (for others hitting this)

Wrap headless invocations externally, e.g. `perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' pi -p "..."` — note `exec` preserves the pending alarm in the kernel.

Refs: #4707 (idle timeout config), #5294 (timeout respected for non-Codex providers), #8593 (event-level silence).

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

## What

Session-JSONL write-syscall coalescing (source-level slice, zero compiler events).

- **SessionManager**: initial file creation + rewrites carry every buffered entry in ONE write (was one write per entry). Appends stay synchronously durable (the session-manager suite pins same-tick reload visibility).
- **JsonlSessionStorage**: new `AppendBatcher` seam — write() coalescing with marker-ACK crash ordering (a caller's promise resolves only after the write() carrying its bytes reached the OS; SIGKILL never loses a committed mutation/turn), append-failure state convergence to the durable log, post-write fork staging.

## Before/after write-syscalls + bytes (real PTY runs, scripted 2-turn session, inotify write accounting)

| metric | BEFORE | AFTER | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| write() syscalls | 10 | **5** | **−50 %** |
| creation burst | 6 | **1** | −83 % |
| steady-state appends | 2 | 2 | 0 (sync-durability contract) |
| transcript bytes / entries | 2 775 / 10 | 2 774 / 10 | identical |

SIGKILL at idle after a committed turn: committed turn on disk (user+assistant present, file parses, reopen works). Clean exit appends 2 shutdown-bookkeeping lines a killed process never emits; committed content identical.

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): add deb and rpm package builds for Linux
prs.body:
Closes #10783.

## Summary

Add native Linux package builds (`.deb` and `.rpm`) to the release pipeline. Currently pi is installed via `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`, which uses npm outside the system package manager. On Debian/RHEL systems this means no `dpkg`/`rpm` tracking, no `apt`/`dnf` upgrade path, and no clean removal. Native packages solve all three.

This repackages the existing standalone Linux binaries (already built by `build-binaries.sh` using Bun compile) into `.deb` and `.rpm` packages. No changes to pi's runtime code.

## Files added

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `scripts/build-deb.sh` | Builds `.deb` via `dpkg-deb` from extracted binary dir |
| `scripts/test-deb.sh` | Validates metadata, contents, lintian, install/remove cycle |
| `.github/workflows/build-deb.yml` | Reusable workflow for amd64 + arm64 |
| `scripts/build-rpm.sh` | Builds `.rpm` via `rpmbuild` from extracted binary dir |
| `scripts/test-rpm.sh` | Validates metadata, contents, rpmlint, install/remove cycle |
| `.github/workflows/build-rpm.yml` | Reusable workflow for x86_64 + aarch64 |
| `.github/workflows/build-binaries.yml` | Modified: calls both workflows after `publish-github-release` |

## Package layout (same for deb and rpm)

```
/usr/lib/pi/pi                    standalone binary
/usr/lib/pi/photon_rs_bg.wasm     image processing
/usr/lib/pi/theme/*.json          UI themes
/usr/lib/pi/assets/*              interactive mode assets
/usr/lib/pi/export-html/          session export templates
/usr/lib/pi/docs/                 documentation
/usr/lib/pi/examples/             example extensions
/usr/lib/pi/native/               native TUI prebuilds
/usr/bin/pi -> /usr/lib/pi/pi     symlink
```

## Test coverage

Both test scripts validate:
1. Package metadata (name, version, architecture, license)
2. Package contents (binary, symlink, wasm, themes, assets, docs)
3. Symlink target correctness
4. Static analysis (lintian for deb, rpmlint for rpm)
5. Install/verify/remove cycle in Docker containers (debian:bookworm-slim, fedora:latest)

## Release flow

```
existing: build -> smoke-test -> stage -> npm -> announce -> publish-release
                                                                  |
                                                        +---------+---------+
                                                        |                   |
                                                  build-deb-packages  build-rpm-packages
                                                  (amd64 + arm64)     (x86_64 + aarch64)
                                                        |                   |
                                                  upload to release   upload to release
```

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): extension abort with same-run continuation
prs.body:
## Problem

An extension watching `message_update` can detect a rule violation mid-stream and call `ctx.abort()`, but the session then exits the run loop early, strands queued follow-ups, and settles. The only continuation hooks (`turn_end`/`agent_before_settle` returning `continue: true`) are skipped after an abort, and there is no way to trim the aborted partial. The best an extension can do today is wait for idle and re-prompt with the reminder as a fresh user turn — the aborted partial stays in context, once-only rule windows reset, and every correction costs a whole turn.

## Proposal

`ctx.abort(continuation)`: abort the in-flight request, optionally drop the aborted partial assistant message, append the reminder, and resume the same run.

- `continuation.reminder` (string or `AgentMessage`) is injected as a user message before the run resumes. `contextMode: "discard"` removes the trailing aborted assistant message together with its tool results (persisted as `context_edit` entries, so replays and compaction stay consistent — avoiding the orphaned-toolResults failure mode seen in #10263). `reason` identifies the requester.
- Additive `turn_start.continuation` marker (`{ reason, attempt, droppedPartial }`) lets handlers distinguish a resumed run from a fresh user turn.
- `maxAutoContinuations` setting (default 3, `0` disables) caps repeats as a loop guard; exhaustion behaves exactly like a plain abort plus a `continuation_budget_exhausted` notice.
- Plain `ctx.abort()` is unchanged and doubles as user interrupt: a plain abort during the window drops the armed continuation. Overlapping aborts coalesce (reminders merge, identical reminders inject once, `discard` wins over `keep`). A failed continuation request settles like an error turn without auto-retrying the continuation. `agent_settled` fires once, at true settle.

## Use case

Stream-rule engines (TTSR-style abort+remind guards) and safety guards that must rewind rather than append. Prior art: omp's native TTSR aborts, truncates, injects, and continues the same run.

## Testing

- New `test/agent-session-abort-continuation.test.ts` (10 tests) covers the contract: no-arg abort regression, keep-mode, discard-mode round-trip, follow-up queue drained in the same run, duplicate coalescing + reminder dedupe, budget exhaustion + notice, `maxAutoContinuations: 0`, user interrupt wins, failed continuation settles.
- Regression suites green (`agent-session-retry`, `compaction-extensions`, `extensions-runner`, settings, `agent-session-concurrent`); `npm run check` clean.

Happy to adapt the API shape (e.g. extending `steer()` semantics instead of an atomic `abort(continuation)`) — the contract table in the tests is shape-independent.

issues.body:
Follow-ups deferred from PR #13682 (`fix/hosted-approval-redelivery`, managed-agent session rename delivery) under that PR's recorded late-round rule — past roughly five review rounds only Criticals land in the PR, optional Suggestions are recorded here.

**Update 2026-10-11:** the original blocker recorded below — that `packages/sdk-java/**` "cannot be compiled or tested on the box that triaged them" — is no longer true. A Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1 + Maven 3.9.9 toolchain was installed on that box this round (deps warmed from the aliyun mirror, `~/.m2` ~212M), and `mvn test` now runs this module's surefire suite against in-memory H2. Item 2 was consequently landed in the PR rather than deferred; item 1 and item 3 remain deferred on **scope** grounds only, not toolchain grounds.

Recipe, since it unblocks every remaining `packages/sdk-java` follow-up: install JDK 21 + Maven, write a `~/.m2/settings.xml` mirroring `central` to `https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public`, then `mvn install -DskipTests` in `packages/sdk-java/runtime-broker` and `packages/sdk-java/qwencode` (the latter needs `-Dgpg.skip=true`) before `mvn test` in `managed-agent-server`. No Docker or MySQL is needed for the H2-backed `@SpringBootTest` classes.

Each item carries an apply-ready change below.

---

## 1. Title-blankness validation asymmetry between the create and rename routes

**Source thread:** R3-2 on PR #13682 — `ManagedAgentService.java:1321`, review comment id 4238791783
**Severity as filed:** Suggestion
**Introduced by:** PR #13682 itself (verified against `git diff origin/main...HEAD`)

`validRenameTitle` was widened to treat Unicode blanks (NBSP `U+00A0`, `U+FEFF`, `U+2007`, `U+202F`) as empty:

```java
// ManagedAgentService.java:1318-1324 at fbda4a2419
private static String validRenameTitle(String title) {
    if (title == null || title.length() > 256
            || title.codePoints().allMatch(character -> Character.isWhitespace(character)
                    || Character.isSpaceChar(character) || character == 0xfeff)) {
```

Its twin `validTitle` — reached from `metadataTitle` (`:1283-1308`) by both `createSession` and `createWorkspaceSession` — still decides blankness with `String.isBlank()`:

```java
// ManagedAgentService.java:1310-1316 at fbda4a2419
private static String validTitle(String title) {
    if (title != null && title.length() > 512) { ... }
    return title == null || title.isBlank() ? null : title;
}
```

`git diff origin/main...HEAD` confirms the asymmetry is introduced by this change — the removed line was `if (title == null || title.isBlank() || title.length() > 256)`, so before the diff both routes agreed on NBSP.

**Failure scenario.** `POST /v1/agents/sessions` with `title: "\u00a0"` is accepted (200) and persisted into `managed_agent_session`, because `String.isBlank()` is false for NBSP. A client that reads that title back and echoes it into `PATCH /v1/agents/sessions/{id}` is then refused `400 invalid_title` — the server rejects a value it stored itself. The stored title also renders as nothing while defeating `validTitle`'s null/"untitled" coercion.

**Apply-ready change** — share only the blankness predicate. Keep each validator's own length cap (512 create vs 256 rename) and its own failure mode: `validTitle` must keep **coercing to `null`** rather than throwing, or today's accepted `title: ""` and `" "` creates become 400s.

```java
private static boolean unicodeBlank(String title) {
    return title.codePoints().allMatch(character -> Character.isWhitespace(character)
            || Character.isSpaceChar(character) || character == 0xfeff);
}

private static String validTitle(String title) {
    if (title != null && title.length() > 512) {
        throw new ApiException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "invalid_title",
                "Title must not exceed 512 characters.");
    }
    return title == null || unicodeBlank(title) ? null : title;
}

private static String validRenameTitle(String title) {
    if (title == null || title.length() > 256 || unicodeBlank(title)) {
        throw new ApiException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "invalid_title",
                "Title must contain 1-256 characters.");
    }
    // control-character check and return unchanged
```

`unicodeBlank("")` returns `true` (`allMatch` on an empty stream), so the `""` → untitled coercion is preserved.

Add a create-route case asserting `POST /v1/agents/sessions` with `title: "\u00a0"` is coerced to null/untitled rather than persisted as NBSP, and confirm it goes red if `validTitle` reverts to `isBlank()`.

---

## 2. `cleanup` phase asserts nothing about the state the abandon-failure path leaves behind — **LANDED in #13682**

**Source thread:** R3-3 on PR #13682 — `ManagedSessionLifecycleTest.java:875`, review comment id 4238791788
**Severity as filed:** Suggestion

**Land this together with the R2-23 Critical on PR #13682** — both touch the same lines `873-881` of the same test method (`renameStoreFailuresPreserveTheOriginalErrorAndAllowRetry`), so they are one change, not two.

In that method the `cleanup` branch at `:873-875` runs `jdbc.update("UPDATE managed_session_rename_delivery SET lease_until = 0 ...")` with no return-value check and no following read, while the `else` branch at `:876-881` asserts `command_status == "FAILED"`. `cleanup` is now the only phase that actually reaches the abandon-failure path (armed rename failure → `RuntimeBrokerException` → catch → stubbed `abandonSessionRename` throws), yet it pins none of the observable state that path leaves behind: command still `PENDING`, delivery row still `RUNNING` under the dead inline owner with a live 60 s lease.

**Failure scenario.** A regression that makes the failed-cleanup path delete the delivery row, mark the command `FAILED`, or release the lease changes none of this test's assertions: the `UPDATE` silently affects 0 rows, `beginSessionRename` writes a fresh row, and the trailing `PATCH` still answers 200.

**Apply-ready change:** use the combined *park → assert → unpark* patch recorded in the R2-23 thread on PR #13682. Inside the parked window it asserts `delivery_state == 'RUNNING'` and `command_status == 'PENDING'` for the `cleanup` phase, and it checks that the unparking `jdbc.update` returns 1. The parking is required anyway to stop the 50 ms `SessionRenameCoordinator` tick from re-driving the row, so the two findings converge on the same edit.

---

## 3. The only lease-renewal test picks an interval below the clamp, so the clamp is unpinned

**Source thread:** R4-1 on PR #13682 — `ManagedActionsTest.java:876`, review comment id 4239687732
**Severity as filed:** Suggestion
**Introduced by:** PR #13682 itself — the clamp it added in response to R1-1

`approvalLeaseRenewsWhileDeliveryIsHeldPastItsInitialDeadline` sets `leaseDuration = 300ms` and `leaseRenewInterval = 50ms`, while production computes `Math.max(1, Math.min(dispatch.getLeaseRenewInterval().toMillis(), dispatch.getLeaseDuration().toMillis() / 3))` (`ActionResponseCoordinator.java:105-106`). `min(50, 100)` resolves to 50, so the clamp never binds. The shipped defaults sit exactly on the tie (`ManagedAgentProperties.java:504-505`: 60s lease / 20s renew = 60000/3), so no other test binds it either.

**Failure scenario.** The renewal period is what keeps a long delivery from losing its lease — the defect R1-1 was filed for. With the clamp unpinned, inverting or deleting it leaves the suite green, so the guard added in response to R1-1 is the one part of it that no test can catch regressing.

**Evidence as filed** (bot's mutation arms in a private out-of-tree copy; not re-run here): M1 inverts the clamp (`Math.min` -> `Math.max`, period becomes 100ms) and **survives** at `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0`. M2, the control with period = `leaseDuration*2` against a 300ms lease, fails with `Expecting an empty Optional but was containing value: OperationRecord[... leaseOwner=competing-replica, claimGeneration=2 ...]` — proving the test does detect renewal starvation and that the mutation site is the right one.

**Apply-ready change** — raise the interval above `leaseDuration / 3` so the clamp is what picks the period:

```java
properties.getDispatch().setLeaseRenewInterval(Duration.ofMillis(200));
```

With a 300ms lease the clamp then resolves to 100ms. **This is not a one-line change:** the latch and awaitility timings in the rest of the method were written against a 50ms period and will need to move with it. Acceptance: with the interval raised, the M1 inversion must turn this test red, and the M2 control must still fail.

<details>
<summary>中文说明（第 3 条）</summary>

唯一一个真正执行「按投递租约续期」的测试，选择的续期间隔低于 `leaseDuration / 3` 这个钳制值，因此钳制逻辑从未被执行 —— 把它反转或删掉，整个套件仍然是绿的。续期周期正是「让一次耗时较长的投递不失去租约」的机制，而那正是 R1-1 被提出的缺陷；所以钳制未被钉住意味着：为回应那条讨论串而新增的保护，恰恰是其中唯一没有任何测试能发现其回归的部分。改法是把间隔提到 `leaseDuration / 3` 之上（200ms），让钳制成为决定周期的那一方；但该方法其余部分的 latch 与 awaitility 时序是按 50ms 周期写的，需要一并调整，验收标准是 M1 反转必须让该测试变红、M2 对照组仍然失败。

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

从 PR #13682（`fix/hosted-approval-redelivery`，managed-agent 会话改名投递）按该 PR 记录的后期轮次约定延期的两条 Suggestion：超过约五轮之后 PR 内只落 Critical，可选 Suggestion 登记到这里。

两条都在 `packages/sdk-java/**`，分诊它们的机器无法编译或运行该模块（无 `mvn`、只有 JDK 1.8 而 CI 用 JDK 21、无 `~/.m2`），所以都没有推进 PR。每条都附了可直接套用的改法。

**1. 创建路由与改名路由的标题空白校验不对称（R3-2）。** `validRenameTitle` 已放宽到把 Unicode 空白（NBSP `U+00A0`、`U+FEFF`、`U+2007`、`U+202F`）视为空，但孪生的 `validTitle`（由 `metadataTitle` 供 `createSession` / `createWorkspaceSession` 调用）仍用 `String.isBlank()`。`git diff origin/main...HEAD` 可证这个不对称是本次改动引入的（被删的那行含 `title.isBlank()`），改动前两条路由对 NBSP 判定一致。故障场景：`POST /v1/agents/sessions` 传 `title: "\u00a0"` 会被接受并持久化，客户端读回再回传到 `PATCH` 却被拒 `400 invalid_title` —— 服务端拒绝了自己存下来的值。改法：把空白判定抽成 `unicodeBlank` 供两者共用，各自保留长度上限（创建 512 / 改名 256）与失败方式；`validTitle` 必须继续归一化为 `null` 而不是抛错，否则今天可接受的 `title: ""` 与 `" "` 创建会变成 400。

**2. `cleanup` 阶段对 abandon 失败后的状态不做任何断言（R3-3）。** `:873-875` 的 `jdbc.update` 既不检查返回值也没有后续读取，而另外两个阶段都断言了 `command_status == "FAILED"`；该阶段现在是唯一真正走到 abandon 失败路径的阶段。故障场景：若某次回归让失败的 cleanup 路径删除投递行、把 command 标记为 `FAILED` 或释放租约，本测试任何断言都不会变化。**应与 PR #13682 上 R2-23 那条 Critical 一起落地** —— 两者改的是同一测试方法（`renameStoreFailuresPreserveTheOriginalErrorAndAllowRetry`）的同一段 `:873-881`，是一个改动而不是两个：先停驻投递行、断言 `delivery_state == 'RUNNING'` 与 `command_status == 'PENDING'`、检查解除停驻的 `jdbc.update` 返回 1，再放行末尾的重试 `PATCH`。停驻本身也是阻止 50 ms 的 `SessionRenameCoordinator` tick 重新驱动该行所必需的。

**2026-10-11 更新：** 上面「本机无法编译或运行该模块」这个延期理由已不成立 —— 本轮在该机器上装好了 Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1 + Maven 3.9.9（依赖走 aliyun 镜像预热，`~/.m2` 约 212M），`mvn test` 现在能对该模块跑 surefire（H2 内存库，不需要 Docker/MySQL）。因此第 2 条已直接落进 PR #13682（head `7105fb1e4c`，20 次重复 0 红、整类 35/35、checkstyle 0），第 1 条与第 3 条继续延期，理由只剩**范围**（该 PR 已过其记录的「五轮之后只落 Critical」约定），不再是工具链。

**3. 唯一的租约续期测试选的间隔低于钳制值，导致钳制未被钉住（R4-1）。** 详见上方英文段与折叠说明。


</details>

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Overview

I would like to suggest several improvements to Qwen Code to make it a more complete, professional, and user-friendly coding environment, particularly for users developing websites and applications on mobile devices and desktop computers.

1. Universal File Upload System (+ Button)

Please add a dedicated + button that allows users to attach files directly to their coding sessions.

Expected functionality:

- Upload files through the device's file manager.
- Select images and photos from the gallery.
- Capture photos using the device camera, where supported.
- Upload multiple files simultaneously.
- Support common image, source code, text, document, and configuration file formats.
- Support drag-and-drop uploads on compatible devices and browsers.
- Display file names, file types, file sizes, and options to remove attachments.
- Provide clear upload progress, success, and error messages.

The experience should be optimized for Android and other supported platforms.

2. Download the Complete Project as a ZIP File

Please add a Download Project as ZIP button.

The Diff view is useful for reviewing modified files, but users also need an easy way to download the entire project.

Expected functionality:

- Export the complete project into a single ZIP archive.
- Preserve folders, file names, and directory structure.
- Include source code, relevant configuration files, dependencies manifests, and project assets.
- Offer separate options for downloading the complete project and exporting only changed files.
- Exclude secrets, credentials, API keys, and sensitive environment files by default.
- Provide clear feedback when the ZIP archive is being prepared or cannot be generated.

This would make it much easier to back up projects, transfer them between devices, and continue development elsewhere.

3. Improve Preview and Diff

Please retain the existing Preview and Diff features while improving their usability.

- Make switching between Preview and Diff straightforward.
- Ensure that Diff accurately represents project changes.
- Keep the preview synchronized with the latest successful build.
- Improve code readability and file navigation.
- Provide actionable error messages when builds or previews fail.

4. Professional UI/UX

Please consider improving the interface with a cleaner, more professional design.

- A consistent layout and visual hierarchy.
- Better organization of project files, uploads, code changes, and preview controls.
- Clear icons, labels, and action buttons.
- Improved spacing, typography, and navigation.
- Responsive layouts for mobile phones and desktop screens.
- An intuitive file explorer and project management experience.
- Accessible controls and clear loading, success, and error states.

The goal is a polished development environment without unnecessary visual clutter.

5. Reliable Database and External Integrations

Please improve the setup and management of external connectors and services, including:

- PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Supabase.
- Authentication providers.
- External APIs and cloud storage.
- Other supported databases, services, and development tools.

Useful capabilities would include:

- Clear, step-by-step connection setup.
- Secure credential and environment-variable management.
- Connection testing and troubleshooting.
- Useful diagnostics for failed connections.
- Documentation for required configuration and permissions.
- Secure handling of secrets so they are not exposed in client-side code or exported project archives.

Integrations should clearly explain any external setup or infrastructure requirements.

6. Mobile Compatibility and Reliability

Please test these workflows on supported mobile and desktop environments.

Particular attention should be given to Android users who need to upload files, select photos, review code changes, preview applications, export complete projects, and configure integrations from a phone.

All features should handle errors gracefully and provide helpful feedback.

Expected Benefits

These improvements would make Qwen Code more practical for end-to-end software development by combining file uploads, project export, code review, live previews, professional UI/UX, and reliable integrations.

Thank you to the Qwen Code team for developing this tool. I hope you will consider these suggestions for future releases.

### Why is this needed?

These features are important because they would make Qwen Code more practical, accessible, and efficient for real-world development. Easy file uploads, complete ZIP exports, a professional interface, and reliable database integrations would save time and simplify the workflow, especially for mobile users. These improvements would help users build, manage, test, and transfer complete projects more easily.

### Additional context

_No response_
