prs.title: fix(acp): preserve cancellation intent across session recovery
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Preserve explicit user cancellation across live and restored sessions while keeping infrastructure interruptions recoverable. A uniquely owned user cancellation cannot be continued. Timestamped cancellation of unknown intent requires confirmation of its current daemon identity, including ambiguous ownership of a user marker. Completed local commands retain that resolved identity; later model input, attempts or terminal outcomes supersede the unknown-intent boundary.

## Why it is needed

A cancelled tool turn can resemble a crash after restore. Older builds also stamped timestamps for deadline, connection-close and supersession aborts. Treating every timestamp as human intent suppresses valid recovery; silently resuming uncertain cancellation can repeat work the user stopped. The recovery flow preserves that uncertainty and asks before continuing.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Explicitly Cancel or Close active work, then restart and Continue. It should refuse without another model request, even with a confirmation identity.
- Interrupt through connection close, a deadline or runtime disposal. Recovery should remain available.
- Restore a timestamp-only cancellation or one with ambiguous ownership. Continue without an identity or with an outdated identity should start no model request; confirming the current identity should resume once.
- Use the public SDK in stream-json mode with the supplied confirmation identity. The emitted control frame should contain that identity; the existing no-option frame should remain unchanged.
- Complete a local command after a legacy cancelled turn and restore. The local command should stay out of model history while the original cancellation still requires its current identity.
- Remove pending work before dispatch, or after an interruption cancellation was already sent. The child should receive user intent; the next FIFO prompt should wait for outstanding cancellation acknowledgements.
- Exercise Bridge Retry after a turn error. Cancelled-turn attempt testing uses direct ACP Session retry; resubmission through the bridge after a cancelled completion is a new prompt.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The pinned `88ba18c5` source probes reproduced all four reported omissions. Consolidated review and a faithful dispatched source witness identified the additional removal upgrade gap. The current repair preserves user provenance through both dispatch windows and retains the later-terminal supersession control. [Current local report and retained actual tmux evidence](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13436#issuecomment-6081778123). Historical browser acceptance remains tied to its original commit and unchanged UI.

### Tested on

macOS, Node 22.22.0, candidate `22ab1b6039c8973d5ebc05194f6ae56333319ad4`. 244 focused tests passed, with fresh full build and affected Core/bridge/SDK typechecks. The final bridge-only repair was rebuilt and verified separately without repeating unaffected suites. Actual compiled daemon/ACP in tmux passed one cold legacy+/docs-fixture recovery profile: missing/stale identities sent no continuation request; the matching identity sent one and completed. Current runtime log excerpts are in the report; pane captures are empty because stdout was redirected. Earlier harness failures are retained; ambiguous-explicit ownership has focused-test evidence only. Current-head necessary CI is tracked separately.

## Risk & Scope

- Unknown or ambiguous ownership requires confirmation without certifying user intent. Invalid settlement payloads do not create provenance; a newer model input invalidates the previous recovery boundary.
- The change does not resolve unmarked cron/steering ownership or durable Close after an already idle interruption; those remain in #13502. It does not settle the entirety of #6710.
- Controlled local evidence does not establish real-model behavior, other platforms, a fresh browser run or release delivery. No whole-repository typecheck or full unit-suite pass is claimed.
- English and Chinese designs remain synchronized. No transcript migration or release is included.

## Linked Issues

Related to #6710; remaining policy decisions in #13502 and existing follow-ups in #13478.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): support copying selected reply content
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a mouse-selection menu to completed assistant replies with **Copy plain text** and **Copy Markdown** actions. Partial Markdown copies preserve the selected headings, emphasis, links, lists, code, tables, images, and math while excluding reply controls and unselected ancestor list markers. The menu uses normal-weight text and icons with the default foreground color.

Selections released outside the reply still open the menu. Clipboard failures keep the menu and restore the selection for a retry, including embedded Shadow DOM and host dialog focus traps. Whole-reply copying keeps using the original Markdown, advanced tables retain their own rectangle selection and TSV copying, and keyboard selections do not open this menu. Read-only HTML exports exclude the selection menu and Markdown converter.

Selected empty table cells retain their field positions, loose task lists retain checked/unchecked state on the task line, and ordered lists retain original item numbers across blank items. Markdown-only selections remain available with the empty plain-text action disabled. Diagram controls and loading/error labels are excluded; async reply resizing closes the menu, and disjoint multi-range selections retain native copying.

## Why it's needed

Long model replies often contain more information than a user wants to copy. The whole-reply button copies everything, while native partial copying does not offer an explicit choice between plain text and Markdown. This change lets users copy just the information they selected in the format they need.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Select part of a completed assistant reply with the mouse, including dragging out of the reply before releasing. Confirm that the two copy actions appear near the selection and copy only the selected content.
2. Select formatted content such as an emphasized phrase, numbered heading, nested list children, code, table cells, image, or formula. Confirm that plain text reads naturally and Markdown preserves selected formatting without adding unselected parent text or duplicate formulas.
3. Move the selection and confirm that the menu follows it. Scroll, resize, clear the selection, or click outside and confirm that it closes. Keyboard selection should not open the menu.
4. Drag across an advanced table. Confirm that its rectangle highlight, toolbar, and TSV copy shortcut remain available without opening the reply menu. Confirm that the whole-reply button still copies the original Markdown.
5. In an embedded Shadow DOM inside a host dialog, force the native clipboard API to reject. Confirm that the textarea fallback copies the selected value; if both clipboard paths fail, confirm that the selection and menu remain available for retry.

Validation passed after rebasing onto main: repository build, typecheck, bundle, 329 focused unit/build-artifact tests across eight files, two tracked Chromium E2E smoke tests, six compiled-standalone regression checks, and four reproduced review scenarios verified against the compiled bundle. The read-only transcript script is 1,322,066 characters against the unchanged 1,323,000 limit, and excludes the converter.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the whole-reply button copies the complete Markdown source; partial native selection has no explicit plain-text/Markdown menu. No before screenshot was captured.

After: the actual Web Shell UI shows both copy actions for a selected phrase. Browser checks copied `改进复制体验` as plain text and `**改进复制体验**` as Markdown.

![Selected reply copy menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/bba761b3f229680258dfee454cef6b97fc5425bf/web-shell-selection-copy/selected-copy-menu.png)

The advanced table retains its four-cell selection and TSV toolbar. The browser copied `选区复制\t已完成\n格式保留\t已验证` using the existing table shortcut.

![Advanced table keeps rectangle selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/bba761b3f229680258dfee454cef6b97fc5425bf/web-shell-selection-copy/advanced-table-selection.png)

Both screenshots were captured and visually inspected in Chromium against the actual UI with a **mock daemon**. Mouse selection and clipboard operations are real browser operations; these screenshots do not validate real Git backend behavior. Images are stored on an independent evidence branch, outside the implementation branch.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22+, Chromium, the Vite development UI, and the compiled standalone Web Shell; deterministic mock-daemon HTTP/SSE responses were used for browser checks. The embedded Shadow DOM clipboard fallback was also checked with the public library build inside a host dialog.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: selected Markdown is reconstructed from rendered semantic content, so whitespace and equivalent Markdown syntax may be normalized rather than matching the source byte for byte.
- Not validated / out of scope: full repository test suites, Windows/Linux, Firefox/Safari, HTML rich-text clipboard output, a keyboard or touch selection menu, sub-agent result panels, and workspace-agent run panels. Custom diagrams are limited to the rendered content available to the converter. Browser mock-daemon checks do not validate real Git backend operations.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; the feature is internal to the interactive reply UI and excluded from read-only exports.

The complete, synchronized design is available in [English](https://github.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/blob/310ddd9c5273e39905206b6d7f0ca8c268d704ae/docs/design/2026-10-10-web-shell-selection-copy.md) and [Chinese](https://github.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/blob/310ddd9c5273e39905206b6d7f0ca8c268d704ae/docs/design/2026-10-10-web-shell-selection-copy.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

None.

prs.title: fix(core): record one merged turn after MAX_TOKENS output recovery
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps the durable transcript aligned with in-memory history after MAX_TOKENS output recovery. The recovery flow now defers assistant records, coalesces successful continuations into the one surviving model turn, and writes exactly one record from that turn once recovery settles. Deferred records stay bound to the exact history object they belong to, so retries, abandonment, redaction, and concurrent history replacement cannot persist or remove the wrong turn.

The same recovery boundary now preserves text, thought-block boundaries and signatures, media/code parts, tool calls, usage, and per-attempt Goal billing. Send admission is reserved synchronously, canceled queued sends release their reservation without allowing later sends to overtake, and terminal handling uses a bounded drain whose first terminal result wins.

## Why it's needed

The transcript used by `--resume` and `--continue` was written once per successful stream attempt, while live history merged MAX_TOKENS continuations into one model turn. Resuming therefore rehydrated split, overlapping assistant turns that no longer matched the live session. Fixing the write side preserves the existing reconstruction contract and extends the record-vs-history invariant established for transport continuations in #8624 to output-token recovery.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/core`, run:

```
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts src/core/turn.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts
../../node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
```

Confirm that escalation and non-escalation recovery, tool-call skip paths, failed and abandoned continuations, history replacement, signed and unsigned thought boundaries, non-text output, missing or delayed usage, terminal races, queued-send cancellation, and per-attempt Goal billing each leave one durable assistant record matching the surviving history turn. The tests also round-trip the produced records through the production transcript preparation and history reconstruction path.

Exact rebased head: 636 tests passed; package typecheck, targeted ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check` passed. The required grogu+mario private review was rerun on the exact head after all correctness fixes; both reviewers found the core recovery mechanics sound, and every in-scope correctness finding was resolved with a regression test.

A fresh-workspace `npm run preflight` completed install, formatting, lint, build, and typecheck successfully. Its aggregate test phase exited non-zero with 26,281 CLI tests passing and 19 unrelated failures, plus 22,525 core tests passing and 108 unrelated failures. The failures were confined to sandboxed-home `EPERM`, watcher/file-descriptor `EMFILE`, and existing UI timing paths; the affected production areas are not changed here. The exact touched suites above remain fully green.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no UI layout changes. Under the old eager-recording behavior, the regression cases produce multiple assistant records for one live coalesced turn; with this change they produce exactly one record that reconstructs to the same ordered history content.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node 24.16.0 with the repository toolchain and mocked content generators. A global `qwen` executable was not installed, so the requested live-CLI baseline could not be run; Linux and Windows validation is left to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this is a non-refactor core correctness fix with 1,274 additions and 205 deletions of production code (5,981 additions and 784 deletions across the full six-file diff), so it exceeds the 1,000-line core advisory and needs maintainer awareness. The 13 commits are intentionally separated by invariant for commit-by-commit review. After the existing review rounds, subsequent changes were restricted to correctness findings.
- Deferral trades immediate persistence of a completed truncated attempt for one correct merged record. Cooperative cancellation flushes the surviving turn, but a hard process crash during the short recovery window can lose that partial turn.
- If a continuation emits visible, persistable output before a provider error, that output is now retained in the surviving turn and the stream receives a synthetic terminal event instead of losing content by propagating the provider error. Citation metadata remains ephemeral, as on ordinary turns, because resumable history stores model content parts rather than response metadata.
- Terminal draining is bounded to one second and requests cancellation when the bound wins; a non-cooperative provider is not guaranteed to terminate. Usage metadata arriving after that bound is intentionally not retained.
- Goal spend remains accumulated per model attempt even though the durable transcript contains one coalesced turn. The record keeps the final resume-usable usage boundary, or the latest usable boundary when the final response omits one; unknown fields remain absent rather than being coerced to zero.
- Recorded projection preserves text, signed and unsigned thought blocks, media/code parts, tool calls, and part metadata. Structured-output arguments remain redacted under the existing transcript privacy policy.
- Existing malformed transcripts are not rewritten. A pre-existing headless-subagent consumer also clears accumulated output on continuation retry; that file is unchanged here and should be handled separately rather than widening this already-large fix.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Closes #8979

Related invariant: #8624

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的作用

在 MAX_TOKENS 输出恢复后，使持久化 transcript 与内存 history 保持一致。恢复流程现在会延迟写入 assistant 记录，将成功的续写合并到最终保留的唯一 model 轮次中，并在恢复结束后只从该轮次写入一条记录。延迟记录会绑定到其所属的精确 history 对象，因此重试、中途放弃、脱敏或并发替换 history 都不会持久化或删除错误的轮次。

同一恢复边界现在会保留文本、思考块边界与签名、媒体/代码 part、工具调用、usage，以及按每次尝试累计的 Goal 计费。每次发送会同步预留队列位置；取消排队中的发送会释放其位置且不会让后续发送越过仍在运行的发送；终止处理采用有界排空，并以第一个终止结果为准。

## 为什么需要

`--resume` 和 `--continue` 使用的 transcript 原先会为每次成功的流尝试各写一条记录，而实时 history 会把 MAX_TOKENS 续写合并成一个 model 轮次。因此恢复会话时会重新水合出拆分且重叠的 assistant 轮次，与实时会话不一致。修复写入侧可以保留现有重建契约，并把 #8624 为传输中断续写建立的“记录与 history 一致”不变式扩展到输出 token 恢复。

## 审阅测试计划

### 验证方法

在 `packages/core` 运行：

```
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts src/core/turn.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts
../../node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
```

请确认升级与不升级恢复、工具调用跳过路径、失败和被放弃的续写、history 替换、带签名和不带签名的思考边界、非文本输出、缺失或延迟的 usage、终止竞态、排队发送取消，以及按尝试累计的 Goal 计费，都会留下与最终保留 history 轮次一致的一条持久化 assistant 记录。测试还会让生成的记录经过生产环境的 transcript 准备和 history 重建路径进行往返验证。

最终变基后的精确提交：636 个测试通过；包级 typecheck、目标 ESLint、Prettier 和 `git diff --check` 均通过。所有正确性修复完成后，又在精确提交上重新运行了必需的 grogu+mario 私有评审；两位评审都认为核心恢复机制可靠，所有范围内的正确性问题均已通过回归测试解决。

在全新 workspace 中运行的 `npm run preflight` 成功完成了安装、格式检查、lint、build 和 typecheck。其汇总测试阶段因环境问题以非零状态退出：CLI 有 26,281 个测试通过、19 个无关失败；core 有 22,525 个测试通过、108 个无关失败。失败仅涉及沙箱 home 目录的 `EPERM`、watcher/文件描述符 `EMFILE` 及既有 UI 时序路径，本 PR 未改动这些生产区域。上述精确受影响测试套件仍全部通过。

### 前后证据

N/A —— 没有 UI 布局改动。在旧的立即写入行为下，回归用例会为一个实时合并轮次生成多条 assistant 记录；修复后只生成一条记录，并可重建为相同的有序 history 内容。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境

Node 24.16.0、仓库自带工具链和 mocked content generator。系统未安装全局 `qwen` 可执行文件，因此无法运行要求的实时 CLI 基线；Linux 和 Windows 验证交由 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：这是 core 中的非重构正确性修复，生产代码新增 1,274 行、删除 205 行（完整六文件 diff 新增 5,981 行、删除 784 行），因此超过 1,000 行的 core 提示阈值，需要维护者知悉。13 个提交按不变式拆分，以便逐提交评审。现有多轮评审后，后续改动仅限正确性问题。
- 延迟写入以“不立即持久化已完成的截断尝试”换取一条正确的合并记录。协作式取消会写入最终保留轮次，但若进程在短暂恢复窗口内硬崩溃，该部分轮次可能丢失。
- 如果续写在 provider 报错前已经输出可见且可持久化的内容，该内容现在会保留在最终轮次中，流会收到合成的终止事件，而不会因传播 provider 错误而丢失内容。citation metadata 与普通轮次一样保持临时状态，因为可恢复 history 存储的是 model content part，而不是 response metadata。
- 终止排空最多等待一秒，并在达到边界时请求取消；不保证不配合的 provider 一定终止。超过该边界才到达的 usage metadata 会按设计不予保留。
- 虽然持久化 transcript 只保留一个合并轮次，Goal 花费仍按每次模型尝试累计。记录保留最终可用于恢复的 usage 边界；若最终响应缺少该边界，则使用最近一次可用边界。未知字段会保持缺失，而不会被强制填零。
- 记录投影会保留文本、带签名和不带签名的思考块、媒体/代码 part、工具调用和 part 元数据。structured-output 参数仍按既有 transcript 隐私策略脱敏。
- 已存在的异常 transcript 不会被重写。一个既有的 headless-subagent consumer 也会在续写重试时清除累计输出；本 PR 未改动该文件，应单独处理，而不是继续扩大这个已经较大的修复。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。

Closes #8979

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.title: Windows 10 1607: v0.10.1 fails to start — unresolved load-time import DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName (0xC0000139)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

After updating from v0.10.0 to v0.10.1 on a Windows 10 Pro 1607 (build 14393.447) machine, the app no longer starts. Before anything runs, Windows shows the loader dialog:

```text
无法定位程序输入点 DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName 于动态链接库 …
(EN: The procedure entry point DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName could not be located in the dynamic link library …)
```

and the process exits with 0xC0000139 (STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND) — no stdout, no logs. v0.10.0 (official asset, same machine) starts fine and prints `codewhale 0.10.0 (1be1a703b975)`.

Root cause: the v0.10.1 executable has exactly one load-time import this Windows build cannot resolve — `api-ms-win-security-base-l1-2-2.dll!DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName` (that API set forwards to KERNELBASE.dll; on this build, KERNELBASE/kernel32/userenv and the security API sets do not export the function). Because it is a static, non-delayed import, the loader fails before `main` — regardless of the fact that the only consumer (the extension-host LPAC sandbox, `crates/tui/src/extension_host/windows.rs`, the `registryRead` capability SID derivation from the 0.10.1 LPAC work `af5fa5c23` / `935c08662`) is experimental and off by default (`extension_host = false`).

Import-surface audit of the two official Windows binaries (every imported (dll, function) pair checked with GetProcAddress on this 1607 system):

- v0.10.0 — 411 imports / 29 DLLs — 0 unresolved
- v0.10.1 — 454 imports / 31 DLLs — 1 unresolved (the symbol above); nothing else is missing, and no OS-version gate or PE-header OS-version bump was introduced

The current `main` still contains the same call, so any 0.10.2-line build will fail the same way on this OS.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. On Windows 10, version 1607 (build 14393), take the official v0.10.1 asset `codewhale-windows-x64.exe` (sha256 `76a6156b…d22729`, matching the release's `codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt`).
2. Run `codewhale.exe --version` (or the `.bat` launcher).
3. The loader dialog appears and the process exits with `0xC0000139`; no output. For contrast, the v0.10.0 asset on the same machine prints `codewhale 0.10.0 (1be1a703b975)` and exits 0.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.0

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

GitHub Releases download

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

_No response_

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text

```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

## Proposed solution

Requirement-level scope (implementation follows the project's own conventions; no specific files or code are prescribed):

1. The `registryRead` capability SID does not have to come from that API — it is a stable, deterministic value that can be checked against the OS API on any Windows runner that has it. The sandbox can obtain it without a static import from a module that older Windows builds do not provide (runtime resolution, or obtaining the value another way — the project's call).
2. On builds without the capability API, refuse Native-host activation with a clear, feature-scoped error (consistent with the documented macOS/Linux "otherwise activation is refused" behavior) instead of failing the whole process at startup.
3. Keep LPAC behavior and the token checks unchanged on Windows versions that support them today.
4. Consider documenting the oldest supported Windows build and keeping release binaries within it, with a release-time check that every import resolves on that floor — this class of regression would then be caught before shipping.

>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Legacy launcher is still the production path: `pub struct LiveDaytonaLauncher` at crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs:1404, trait DaytonaLauncher at cloud_dispatch.rs:1213, impl at cloud_dispatch.rs:1528.
> - Still wired into every caller: crates/cli/src/dispatch.rs:9 and :114, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/dispatch.rs:8 and :105, crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/jobs.rs:107.
> - Credential slot not tombstoned: DAYTONA_TOKEN_SLOT = "daytona" at crates/secrets/src/lib.rs:48, with DAYTONA_API_KEY and CWC_DAYTONA_TOKEN env names at secrets/src/lib.rs:50-52.
> - docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md and computer/snapshots/cloud-agent/{Dockerfile,README.md} are still present in the v0.10.1 tree (git ls-tree); 65 'daytona' matches remain in cloud_dispatch.rs alone.
> - v0.10.0..v0.10.1 touched cloud_dispatch.rs only for cancel-race and audit fixes (af661abf6e, 430308f624), not for retirement; no commit in history references #5836.

---

## v0.10.0 planning update — 2026-09-19

This remains open. The Engine still wires `LiveDaytonaLauncher` into cloud dispatch; changing the product direction has not removed that runtime path. The provider-specific target in the original proposal below is historical, not a current implementation requirement.

Remaining acceptance is provider-neutral: one shared Engine/control-plane Computer contract; retirement of the legacy launcher and credential slot; fail-closed admission and metering; authenticated private access; cancellation and failure receipts; and a real end-to-end execution.

The reusable image requirements from #5837 are retained here: reproducible pinned Engine images, non-root execution, credentials supplied only through the approved post-create boundary, and real execution receipts. Closing that obsolete image proposal does not mark hosted Computers complete.

---

## Original report (retained for context)

Founder direction 2026-09-02 (TRUTH_LEDGER): Daytona is removed product-wide; AWS Lambda microVMs are the single managed Computer substrate. This issue covers the engine side. The apps-side flip (`MANAGED_SANDBOX_PROVIDER` pin + Daytona retirement) is tracked in the `Hmbown/codewhale-apps` repo.

## Daytona surface in the engine

- `crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs` — `LiveDaytonaLauncher::create_sandbox` (HTTP `POST {DAYTONA_API}/sandbox`), fail-closed proposal/confirm flow
- `crates/tui/src/dispatch_runner.rs`, `crates/cli/src/dispatch.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cloud/tests.rs`
- `crates/secrets/src/lib.rs` — `daytona` secret slot
- `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/utility/dispatch.rs`, `jobs.rs`, `config.rs`; `crates/tui/src/computer_meter*.rs` references
- `docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`, `computer/snapshots/cloud-agent/` (Daytona-shaped image — replacement tracked separately)
- `crates/tui/src/lib.rs`, `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` wiring

Note the snapshot README already records that the product dispatcher wiring for the Daytona snapshot is absent (no clone, env injection, or toolbox execution) — the engine dispatch path never reached product completeness.

## Deliver

- Extract an explicit Computer provider boundary in the engine (or ratify the alternative: engine consumes the apps control-plane provider contract over HTTP for cloud work — decide in this issue, document in `docs/`).
- Implement the Lambda microVM path under the same admission/meter rules the control plane enforces (`aws-lambda-microvm` adapter already exists in `codewhale-apps/services/control-plane/src/sandbox/`).
- Tombstone the `daytona` secret slot: readable/settleable, never usable for a new call.
- Move `docs/DAYTONA_CLOUD_DISPATCH.md` to a historical note; historic dispatch records remain readable and terminally settleable only.

## Acceptance

- No code path in the engine can create/resume a Daytona sandbox.
- `codewhale dispatch` (cloud-agent) acquires a Lambda microVM Computer end to end in a real run, with receipts.
- Clippy/fmt/tests green; docs tell one provider story.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add CLI installation and in-app OAuth sign-in
prs.body:
What and why

"PR #6805" (https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6805) introduced reviewed, host-managed OAuth AI providers. However, users still need a separate terminal command to sign in, and installing plugins from source lacks a simple CLI entry point.

This PR improves both workflows, taking inspiration from Pi's plugin installation experience while preserving Codewhale's existing security model.

1. Install plugins from the terminal

Add "codewhale install <source>" using the existing plugin installer.

Supported sources include:

codewhale install git:github.com/owner/repo
codewhale install git:github.com/owner/repo@v1.0.0
codewhale install npm:package@1.0.0
codewhale install npm:@scope/package@1.0.0
codewhale install ./local-plugin

- Reuse existing download, archive validation, and network approval checks.
- Keep installed plugins disabled and untrusted until explicitly reviewed and enabled.
- Require exact npm versions and native plugin manifests.
- Do not execute npm lifecycle scripts, install dependencies, or run Git hooks.
- Preserve existing "/plugin install" source formats.

This adopts Pi-style source syntax, not Pi's executable extension runtime.

2. Native OAuth login inside Codewhale

Integrate plugin authentication into the existing "/login" and "/provider" interfaces.

- "/login" opens the provider picker.
- "/login <provider-id>" starts browser-based OAuth authentication.
- "/provider" offers OAuth login instead of an API-key input for supported plugin providers.
- After successful authorization, refresh the provider's account-scoped model catalog and open the model picker.
- "/login status" continues to show Codewhale account status.
- "/logout <provider-id>" removes the named plugin's local credentials without signing out of the Codewhale account.

The existing "codewhale auth plugin-login --provider <id>" remains available for terminal use. Both entry points reuse the same host-owned OAuth implementation.

No separate token store or authentication implementation is introduced.

3. Improved first-use experience

The intended user flow becomes:

1. Install the plugin using "codewhale install".
2. Review, trust, and enable the plugin.
3. Start a new Codewhale session.
4. Enter "/login" and select the provider.
5. Complete authorization in the browser.
6. Choose a model and start using it.

Users no longer need to leave the TUI to run a separate plugin login command.

4. Security and compatibility

The changes preserve existing security boundaries:

- Installing a plugin never automatically trusts or enables it.
- OAuth credentials remain bound to the reviewed provider declaration.
- Provider authorization checks continue to apply to requests.
- Account-specific plugin model catalogs are not reused from disk cache.
- Login does not silently select a model or change billing groups.
- Provider logout removes local credentials only; it does not revoke remote authorization.
- A successful login grant remains stored if model catalog refresh subsequently fails.

Git shorthand supports GitHub repositories only. Npm sources require exact versions. Mutable Git tags are not integrity guarantees.

No device-code login or remote token revocation is added.

Documentation

Updated:

- "docs/PLUGINS.md"
- "docs/PLUGIN_PROVIDERS.md"
- "docs/features.toml"
- Localized OAuth login messages

Issue

No-Issue: Improve native plugin installation and OAuth usability following #6805.

How I tested it

Added regression tests covering:

- GitHub and npm installation source parsing
- Invalid source formats and version constraints
- Source parsing round trips
- "/login" provider picker dispatch
- "/login status" and invalid argument handling

Verification status: Upstream GitHub Actions currently report "action_required" for this fork PR, not passing CI results. The full upstream test suite and interactive browser OAuth flow have not been verified here.

Checklist

- [x] Reuse existing plugin installation and OAuth infrastructure
- [x] Preserve explicit plugin review and activation
- [x] Add focused regression tests
- [x] Update documentation and feature registry
- [ ] Verify upstream CI
- [ ] Complete interactive OAuth end-to-end testing

prs.title: fix(workflow): reject a gate that blocks its own role when the plan is admitted
prs.body:
## What and why

#6945: a gate with `role: "implement"` and `blocks_role: "implement"` holds back the role whose completion is the only thing that can pass it. The run fails when that phase is dispatched (`spawn rejected: workflow gate blocks role ...: waiting for required gate outcome`), after the earlier phases have already run.

`validate_runtime_gates` runs in `start_workflow` before anything is dispatched, and already rejects empty ids, empty roles and `role_start`. It now rejects this shape as well. The comparison happens after the existing trim and lowercase, so ` Implement ` against `implement` is caught too. The error for the plan in the issue:

```
Workflow gate `v1` has role and blocks_role both set to `implement`; a gate cannot block the role whose completion triggers it, so set blocks_role to a later role
```

Gates only exist on a compiled `WorkflowSpec`, so plan JSON and declarative JS/TS sources both go through this check.

`docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md` described this shape as a mid-run deadlock. It now says the plan is rejected up front, and keeps the dispatch-time message for the case that is still not caught (a `blocks_role` naming a role from an earlier phase).

Not in this change:
- The issue's third suggestion, flagging a `blocks_role` that names a role from an earlier phase. That needs the phase order, which `validate_runtime_gates` doesn't see.
- Two gates that block each other's roles (`x` blocks `y`, `y` blocks `x`) wait on each other the same way. I left that alone to keep this to what the issue asks for.

## Issue

Refs #6945

## How I tested it

- The new test, `native_gate_that_blocks_its_own_role_is_rejected_at_admission`, uses the gate from the issue as the failing case, checks that ` Implement ` is caught as well, and that pointing `blocks_role` at `verify` is still accepted. With the new check switched off it fails at the `expect_err`; with it, it passes.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags, and `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets`: clean. Clippy also on 1.99, plus `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 15249 passed, 44 failed. The same 44 fail on main (6084a025b) on my machine; most need an extension-host Node version I don't have.
- `check-dead-code-budget.py` and `check-blocking-calls-budget.py` pass.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, rebased on current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(artifacts): resolve a linked state root so a relocated Codewhale home keeps working
prs.body:
## Summary

On Windows, when the Codewhale state directory is reached through a junction —
the standard way to keep `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale` on another volume — every
session-artifact write fails with:

> Fleet artifact path must stay within the workspace

`/compact` fails outright, because it persists a pre-compaction checkpoint as
its first step (`compact_messages_safe` propagates that write's error with `?`).
Spillover saving, background-shell evidence, tool-media storage and the
workflow journal degrade on the same path, and the Runtime API cannot read an
artifact back.

## Cause

The strict opener in `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs` (Windows) walks every
component of the root path and refuses any reparse point — including the
components of the **state root itself**. `resolve_state_dir("sessions")`
returns `%USERPROFILE%\.codewhale\sessions` in the original spelling; when
`.codewhale` is a junction, `WindowsDirectory::open_inner` refuses that very
component and `invalid_path()` reports the Fleet-artifact message.

v0.10.0 resolved the root first (`workspace.canonicalize()`), and the Unix
opener still does; the v0.10.1 Windows rewrite dropped that resolution for
every caller. The state root is the application's own directory, not a
caller-supplied workspace: a user who relocates it behind a link is placing
their state, not widening a trust boundary.

## Changes

- **`WorkspaceFile::open_resolved_root`** (new): resolves the root once
  (`canonicalize`) and then runs the existing link-refusing walk. It exists for
  the application's own state directory, which the user may have relocated
  behind a link; a caller-supplied workspace root must keep using `open`. The
  doc comment says so on every platform. On Unix it forwards to `open`, whose
  confined opener already resolves the root — no second resolve and no new
  blocking-call site.
- **`crates/tui/src/artifacts.rs`**: `open_session_relative` opens through
  `open_resolved_root`.
- **`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/`**: `workspace.rs` gains
  `open_confined_file_resolved`, and the two session-artifact read routes
  (`resolve_session_artifact`, `image_evidence_summary`) move to it. Without
  this the writer succeeded and the reader still failed on a relocated root:
  the compact checkpoint was written and could not be read back through
  `GET /sessions/<id>/artifacts/<artifact_id>` or the turn-ref route that
  shares the same resolver. The two remaining `open_confined_file` callers
  keep the strict opener on purpose — their roots are
  `canonical_workspace(thread_workspace)` and the caller's workspace, neither
  of which is the application's state directory.
- **Nothing below the root is relaxed**: the walk still refuses any link inside
  the state directory, and `open` — used by Fleet workspaces, delivery files,
  the LSP root and the Runtime API workspace reads — is unchanged.
- **`session_artifact_absolute_path`** documents what it is: the recorded
  spelling for receipts and display, not a path to open, because it keeps the
  state root as spelled.
- **`scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.json`**: `crates/tui/src/fleet/files.rs`
  moves from one `path_canonicalize` site to two, with the reason below. The
  Unix variant adds no site.

## Evidence

Reproduced before the fix on 0.10.1 (Windows). A component-by-component probe
of both spellings shows the exact split:

```
[ok]      C:\Users\<user>
[REPARSE! C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale        <- refused here
[ok]      C:\Users\<user>\.codewhale\sessions
[ok]      D:\CodeWhaleData\sessions          <- same directory, no link on the chain
```

New Windows regression test
(`fleet::files::windows_root_link_tests::linked_state_root_resolves_once_and_keeps_the_inner_rule`)
creates a real junction and pins both directions: the strict opener must keep
refusing a linked root, `open_resolved_root` must write through to the real
target, and a link *below* the resolved root must still be refused.

Not run here: the repository's own gates. The change is Windows-only in
effect; the pushed branch is the design under review, and CI is the gate.

## Blocking-call budget

The file's recorded `path_canonicalize` budget is raised from one to two. This
is a synchronous, confined file-I/O layer whose callers already accept the
file's blocking work, and the new site sits beside the five `std_fs` sites the
budget already records. An adversarial review of the change independently
re-verified the count with the checker's own logic: base has one site, the new
method adds one, and the inline test module contributes none.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: observed in an operator session on 0.10.1 (Windows); the state
directory relocated behind a junction makes every session-artifact write fail.

prs.title: fix(tui): name the work that blocks a session switch
prs.body:
## Summary

A session-switch command refused because runtime work is active reported only
that it was refused:

> Cannot start a new session while runtime work is active. Wait for the current
> turn, maintenance, and background tasks to finish, or cancel that specific
> work. `/new --force` only discards draft or queued input.

In the session that prompted this, the real blocker was one background script
that had been spinning for five hours. The refusal never named it, so the first
question — *which work?* — had no answer in the UI, and `/new --force` read as
a way out it is not.

The gate itself is correct and unchanged: a session transition must not detach
a live runtime producer (`App::session_transition_blocked`, U02-10). What was
missing is the explanation.

## Changes

- **`App::session_transition_blockers() -> Vec<String>`** (new): the same
  predicates as `session_transition_blocked()`, rendered in operator terms. The
  boolean now derives from this list (`!blockers.is_empty()`), so the gate and
  its explanation cannot drift. Task rows carry the id, status,
  `agent_roster::format_duration` for the age, the command with the panel's
  `shell: ` prefix stripped, and the owning sub-agent when a child owns the
  shell. Rows are bounded by display width
  (`TRANSITION_BLOCKER_LINE_WIDTH`, 74 columns — the transcript Note body in an
  80-column terminal) and by count (five, then `…and N more`).
- **Facets**: `CommandSessionLifecycleContext` and `CommandSessionControlContext`
  gain `transition_blockers()`. The lifecycle adapter forwards to the App; no
  `App`/`SessionManager` type crosses the facet. The doc states it is a display
  projection, not a data source.
- **One shared renderer**: `transition_blocked_message(verb, blockers)` in
  `commands/groups/session/mod.rs`. `/new`, `/load`, `/fork` (both routes),
  `/branch` and `/resume` all use it. The tail names exits with their scope —
  Ctrl+C stops a running turn, `/jobs cancel-all` cancels running shell jobs —
  because that command only kills shell processes and answers "No running
  commands to cancel." for everything else.
- **`/clear`** consults the same gate, so it shows the same blocker list instead
  of its own content-free refusal.
- **`/new`** states the `--force` scope again, where the flag exists: the shared
  tail names the exits that clear a blocker, and `--force` is not one of them.
- **Not in this change**: the gate's decision logic, `--force` semantics, and
  background-task stall detection. `/home` and the restore-switch path in
  `tui/ui/apply.rs` keep their own wording; both have a much narrower error
  surface than the five lifecycle commands.

## Evidence

Existing test updates in the same slice: `branch` and `resume` compose the new
message; a real-`App` regression test asserts that a blocked `/new --force`
against a live turn names the turn instead of the old `--force` sentence.

New tests pin the two properties that would otherwise drift: every predicate
that closes the gate names itself when driven alone, and a row stays inside the
74-column body with a CJK summary (100 ideographs = 200 columns, so a
character-count budget cannot pass it).

Verified locally on the equivalent head (the same commits before this branch
was rebased onto current main):

```
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- transition_blockers lifecycle_portable_tests \
  session_lifecycle_regression resume_transition_blocking
test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. The remaining gates are the
repository's own CI.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

No-Issue: observed in an operator session on 0.10.1 (Windows); a stuck
background task held the session and the refusal did not name it.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish

issues.body:
## Summary

When using `google/gemini-2.5-pro` via the `google-generative-ai` API, three issues combine to cause rapid session context bloat, aborted runs, and silent Telegram delivery failures.

## Issue 1: textSignature Session Bloat (High Severity)

Gemini assistant responses include a `textSignature` field containing ~15KB of base64 data per response turn. OpenClaw stores these signatures verbatim in the session JSONL history. After 10+ turns, the accumulated signatures alone consume 150KB+, causing:

1. Context window bloat (observed: 416K tokens in one session)
2. Gemini API timeouts on re-submission of full context
3. Compaction failures (session too large to compact)
4. Silent message delivery failures (run aborts before reply is sent to Telegram)

**Expected:** `textSignature` should either not be stored in session history, be stored separately, or not be re-sent to the model on subsequent turns.

## Issue 2: Embedded `<think>` Tags in Text

Gemini 2.5 Pro embeds `<think>...</think>` tags directly in the `text` content field (not as separate `thinking` type blocks). If OpenClaw treats `<think>`-prefixed text as internal/thinking content, the reply is suppressed and never delivered to Telegram.

**Expected:** OpenClaw should either strip `<think>` tags from the delivered text, or not suppress messages that contain them.

## Issue 3: Mixed Text + ToolCall in Same Response

Gemini 2.5 Pro consistently emits text + toolCall in the same response turn. OpenClaw processes the toolCall, gets the result, then emits an empty `content: []` as the final stop. The original text from the first part of the response is never delivered to the user.

**Expected:** Text content from a mixed text+toolCall response should be delivered to the user, not silently dropped.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an agent with `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as primary model
2. Send 5-10 interactive messages via Telegram group topic
3. Check session JSONL — each assistant message contains `textSignature` (~15KB base64)
4. After ~10 exchanges, session reaches 150K+ tokens
5. Subsequent runs timeout or abort; replies never reach Telegram

## Workaround

Switched affected agent to Claude Sonnet 4.6, which does not exhibit these behaviors.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.3.13 (61d171a)
- macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (arm64)
- Gemini API key auth (google-generative-ai provider)
- Telegram channel with group topics

issues.body:
### Summary

On an otherwise idle Linux VPS, the OpenClaw 2026.9.9 Gateway shows brief CPU bursts at an approximately 60-second cadence. A five-minute, one-second process sample measured about 14% of one CPU core on average, with bursts reaching roughly 185–286% of one core. No model or agent run events occurred during the sample. The pattern persisted after an unrelated, custom Gateway watchdog cron was disabled.

This is a request to investigate the remaining idle maintenance cost and whether the merged reductions in #165922 and #167268 cover it. The observations below identify a strong timing match, **not a confirmed attribution of all CPU to placement reconciliation or SQLite**.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.9, Linux VPS
- Gateway RSS during sampling: approximately 2.3 GiB
- Multiple agents configured; no active model/agent runs in the five-minute sample
- No Gateway restart or configuration change made for this investigation

### Measurements

- One-second process samples over five minutes showed bursts at 12:22:17, 12:23:18, 12:24:19, 12:25:21, and 12:26:22 UTC (approximately 61 seconds apart).
- The installed Gateway bundle sets `WORKER_PLACEMENT_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS = 6e4` and schedules both `worker-placements:reconcile` and `worker-placements:disk-space` every 60 seconds. This is a cadence match, not proof that either job accounts for the full spike.
- A native 20-second `diagnostics.heapProfile` spanning a burst included samples attributed to `kysely-sync`, placement `reconcile` / `server-worker-placement-startup`, `gateway-scheduler` wake, placement-row codec, and SQLite worker-store paths. The profile was too coarse to assign a reliable CPU percentage or exact byte cost to each path. Main heap went from approximately 826 to 775 MiB; RSS from approximately 2336 to 2312 MiB across that window.
- Gateway worker-lifecycle counters read four times, five minutes apart, stayed at `sqlite-store.worker.js started=2 retired=0` and `openclaw-state-read.worker.js started=2 retired=0`. Thus this does **not** reproduce the SQLite/state-read worker churn reported in #159638.
- The installed 2026.9.9 bundle has the older placement reconcile path: it still wraps `sessionRetirement.reconcile()` with `publishPlacementChanges(...)`, and the `workers.placementEnvironmentOwner` read introduced by #165922 is absent. The idle-maintenance change in #167268 also appears absent from this installed bundle.

### Expected behavior

With no active runs or worker placements needing attention, periodic maintenance should do bounded, minimal work and allow the Gateway to settle close to idle between checks.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Are the merged changes in #165922 and #167268 expected to reduce this specific once-per-minute idle cost on the next release containing them?
2. Is there a supported diagnostic counter or trace that attributes each 60-second maintenance job's CPU time, SQL statements, and allocations without restarting the Gateway?
3. If the cadence remains after those changes, which additional idle reconciliation path would be useful to profile?

Related: #159638 has a similar cadence but a different observed worker lifecycle.

issues.body:
### Summary

With `workspaceAccess: "rw"`, the sandbox protects only the workspace skill roots as read-only, while the workspace bootstrap/instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `memory/`) stay writable. Please make the protected-path policy coherent and operator-configurable, keeping today's behavior as the default.

### Problem to solve

#85591 (for #17931) mounts `<workspace>/skills`, `<workspace>/.agents/skills` and the materialized `.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills` read-only (`protectedSkill`, `src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts`) with this rationale:

> Skills are instructions, they never themselves should need to be writable. It is impossible to enforce any runtime security if the very instruction sets agents are given can be modified by attacking code.

The same threat model applies at least as strongly to the bootstrap files, which are not protected:

- `AGENTS.md` (and `SOUL.md`/`TOOLS.md`/`USER.md`) is injected into **every** turn, whereas a skill is read only when triggered. A sandboxed process that can rewrite `AGENTS.md` controls all subsequent turns of that agent, including unsandboxed sessions sharing the workspace (e.g. `mode: "non-main"`).
- `MEMORY.md`/`memory/` are also loaded into context and persist instructions across sessions; they must stay writable for the agent, but that means the persistence risk the skill protection targets already exists there.
- The shipped template `docs/reference/templates/AGENTS.md` tells the agent: "Learned a lesson: update `AGENTS.md` or the relevant skill." In an `rw` sandbox the more powerful half (`AGENTS.md`) works and the less powerful half (the skill) is blocked.

So the current split gives a false sense of security for operators who want containment, and at the same time blocks operators who deliberately accept agent-maintained skills (there is no opt-out: user binds onto those paths are dropped with `skipping user bind … conflicts with a protected read-only skill mount`).

### Proposed solution

One operator-configurable protected-path policy for `rw` workspaces, defaulting to today's behavior, e.g.:

```json5
sandbox: {
  workspaceAccess: "rw",
  protectedPaths: {
    skills: true,          // default true (current behavior)
    bootstrapFiles: false, // opt-in: AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, USER.md, IDENTITY.md read-only
    extra: [],             // additional workspace-relative paths to mount read-only
  },
}
```

- Operators who want strong containment can protect the bootstrap files too (memory can stay writable, or be listed explicitly).
- Operators who accept agent-maintained workspace skills can set `skills: false` for **workspace** skill roots; the materialized copies of bundled/managed/plugin skills (provenance-bearing) can stay read-only regardless.
- File tools and the fs bridge follow the same policy, as they already do for `protectedSkill` mounts.
- Docs ("Workspace access") list exactly which paths are protected, and the AGENTS template wording follows the effective policy.

Names are illustrative; the point is a single coherent policy instead of a hard-coded skills-only rule.

### Alternatives considered

- Revert #85591 for `rw`: rejected; it removes protection instead of making it coherent.
- Status quo plus docs: at minimum, document that bootstrap and memory files remain writable in `rw`, so operators do not assume instruction integrity.
- Keep living rules outside skills (writable reference files read via a thin skill): works today, but reproduces the same unprotected-instruction situation by design.

### Impact

Affects every Docker sandbox with `workspaceAccess: "rw"`. Security-minded operators currently get partial instruction integrity without being told; operators who want agents to evolve their own procedures (e.g. sandboxed agents on CLI runtimes, which have no Workshop/learning path — see #91676, #163600) have no supported way to let them update workspace skills.

### Evidence/examples

- Observed on 2026.9.6 (Docker backend, `workspaceAccess: "rw"`): `docker inspect` shows the workspace bind `rw=true` with only `skills/` and `.openclaw/sandbox-skills/skills` overlaid `rw=false`; `AGENTS.md` and `MEMORY.md` are writable from inside the container.
- Same code on main (`src/agents/sandbox/workspace-mounts.ts`, `resolveReadOnlyWorkspaceSkillMounts`).
- Related: #17931, #85591, #112277 (writable materialized skills, kept read-only pending a decision), #94425, #91676.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

Default behavior would not change; this only adds explicit operator choices in both directions.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Regression (introduced by #128610)
**Beta release blocker:** No

## Summary

PR #128610 routes delivery-failure alerts to a fallback destination when the primary thread matches the announce route. For the PR's own target configuration (threaded primary announce + `delivery.failureDestination` set + no explicit `failureAlert.to`), the new condition flips `alternateRoute` to true and `maybeEmitDeliveryFailureAlert` fires on **every failed run** — there is no threshold, cooldown, or dedupe on this path. A broken topic + an every-minute job spams the fallback chat 1,440 alerts/day.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Job config: `every: 60_000`, primary delivery into thread 42 of a chat, `delivery.failureDestination` pointing at the same chat (top-level), no explicit `failureAlert.to`.
2. Delete topic 42 (or otherwise break primary delivery).
3. Let two consecutive runs finish with ok status + failed delivery.

## Expected behavior

Failure alerts should be policy-gated like every sibling path (threshold via `after`, cooldown via `lastFailureAlertAtMs`) so a permanently broken route produces bounded notifications.

## Actual behavior

Verified at pinned SHA:

- New condition `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts:170-176`: with failureDestination present + primary `threadId != null` + no `jobConfig.to`, `primaryRouteMatches` no longer suppresses the alternate-route flag (old code did).
- `maybeEmitDeliveryFailureAlert` (`failure-alerts.ts:313-326`) gates ONLY on `alertConfig.alternateRoute`; it never reads/writes `lastFailureAlertAtMs` and has no `after` check — contrast the sibling gated path at `:368-389`.
- Wiring fires on EVERY `status:"ok" && completionStatus:"failed"` outcome (`src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.ts:201-205`), and the gateway sender is unconditional (`src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:333-399`).

Unit repro: build that job, call the finalizer twice with ok/failed-delivery results spaced arbitrarily; assert `sendCronFailureAlert` called twice with nothing set in between. Contrast: two consecutive `status:"error"` runs inside `cooldownMs` emit once.

Related context: #128267 asks for conditioning/cooldown on the cron *announce* delivery path; this issue tracks the concrete unbounded-alert regression on the *failure-alert* path introduced by #128610.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: cron users relying on fallback failure alerts during outages (exactly when they fire).
- Severity: alert storms drown the very channel meant to surface failures; can trigger channel rate limits/costs.
- Frequency: one alert per failed run until fixed.

issues.body:
**Environment**
- Observed on OpenClaw 2026.6.10 (2026-07-31); the mechanism is unchanged in our reading of 2026.8.1-beta.3 but not re-tested there
- OL9 ARM64, rootful Podman Quadlets; Mattermost + Telegram channels

**Symptom**
When a pending exec is approved from outside the requesting thread (e.g. `/approve <id>` typed at DM top level), the async completion event can be delivered into a *different* session than the one that issued the command. Observed: a fresh, context-free session received "An async command the user already approved has completed… Exec finished (gateway id=…, session=…)" with **no command echo and no output**, and the agent (correctly) answered "I don't have context on what task we were working on… I'd rather not guess." Separately, some completions report "(no output recorded)" with exit 0 for commands that must produce output.

**Why it matters**
Multi-flow concurrency is the normal state for an always-on agent (tasks + inbound email at once). Approval ids are surface-agnostic, so users approve from wherever they are; completions that do not return to the requesting session with their payload strand the original task and waste a turn asking "what were we doing?".

**Proposed direction**
(a) Route async exec completion events to the **requesting session** regardless of where the approval was typed; (b) include the **original command line** (and the requesting session/task label) in the completion event; (c) investigate the "(no output recorded)" exit-0 capture gap for approved async execs.

**Workaround we're using locally**
A local session-forwarding patch for `approvals.exec`, plus user practice of approving in-thread.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow macOS Talk Mode overlay to use the configured assistant avatar instead of always rendering the default orb.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw already supports assistant identity in config, including `ui.assistant.avatar`, and users naturally expect that identity to carry through into voice interactions.

Today, when Talk Mode is opened in the macOS app, the overlay always renders the default animated orb in `TalkOverlayView.swift`. This breaks visual continuity between chat UI and voice UI. If a user has already configured a named assistant with a custom avatar, the Talk Mode overlay still looks generic instead of reflecting that assistant.

For character-driven assistants, personal companions, branded assistants, or multi-agent setups, this makes Talk Mode feel visually disconnected from the rest of the product.

### Proposed solution

In the macOS app, update `TalkOverlayView` / `TalkOrbView` so Talk Mode can render the configured assistant avatar when available.

Suggested behavior:

- If `ui.assistant.avatar` is configured and resolvable, show it as a circular cropped image in the Talk overlay.
- Preserve the existing voice-state visuals by keeping the animated rings / pulse / thinking arcs around or above the avatar.
- If no avatar is configured, fall back to the current orb behavior.
- Optionally make this toggleable later, but the fallback behavior already keeps this backward-compatible.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep the generic orb only
  - Simple, but loses assistant identity and visual continuity.

- Replace the orb entirely with a static avatar and remove all motion
  - Would preserve identity, but loses useful speaking/listening/thinking state cues.

- Support this only in web UI
  - Doesn't help the macOS Talk Mode overlay, which is where the visual mismatch is most obvious.

### Impact

**Affected users/systems/channels:** macOS app users who use Talk Mode, especially users with custom assistant personas, custom branding, or multiple agents.

**Severity:** Minor to moderate UX issue. It does not block use, but it makes Talk Mode feel generic and inconsistent with the configured assistant identity.

**Frequency:** Every time Talk Mode is opened on macOS.

**Consequence:** Users see a mismatch between the assistant they configured and the assistant shown in voice mode. This is especially noticeable for personal assistant setups and brand/character-driven agent experiences.

### Evidence/examples

Current implementation appears to always render the orb directly in `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/TalkOverlayView.swift`, via `TalkOrbView` using `Circle()`-based rendering.

That makes this feel like a good targeted enhancement with a clear fallback path.

### Additional information

Related issue:
- #22199 Per-agent UI identity overrides (name, emoji, avatar)

This request is narrower and specifically about carrying assistant avatar identity into the macOS Talk Mode overlay.

issues.body:
# Worker-placement cloud workspace recovery fails with `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` on high-latency storage

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.9.7 (c074824)
**Platform:** Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64, Linux 6.18.50+rpt-rpi-v8), node v24.21.0, storage = microSD
**Gateway:** local, `bind=loopback`, port 18789
**Severity:** Cloud-worker/remote-node sessions are unusable on this host; reproduces ~100%; survives gateway restart.

## Summary

Every remote/cloud-worker turn dies during **cloud workspace recovery**, before the worker executes anything, with:

```
[worker-placement] Cloud workspace recovery deferred: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=nested:<sessionKey> error="session writer claim changed before transcript persistence" errorName=SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError taskKind=turn
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:<sessionKey> error="session writer claim changed before transcript persistence" errorName=SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError taskKind=turn
[gateway] terminal session persistence failed session=<sessionKey> run=<runId> error=SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence
```

The originating `sessions.send` is *accepted* (returns `sentBeforeError: true`, a `runId`), then the run fails asynchronously ~23–30 s later. The placed worker slot is then held (available slots drop to 0) because the placement is stuck in the errored state.

## Reproduction

1. Pi gateway, one paired remote worker node (Debian VM, OpenClaw node host 2026.9.7, 1 slot). Exec policy on the node set to the permissive path (`security: full`, `ask: off`) — i.e. exec policy is not the cause.
2. Create a fresh session and dispatch it to the worker node:
   - session created cleanly, fresh remote workspace provisioned.
   - placement generation increments (e.g. 8, 9) each attempt.
3. Send any turn to the session (e.g. a trivial command).
4. Result: `sentBeforeError: true` on the send; ~23–30 s later the `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` above; slot held.

Reproduces on **fresh sessions, fresh placements, and fresh remote workspaces**, and **persists across a gateway restart**. It is not leftover per-session state.

Notably, the *earliest* attempt on this host (before the store had grown further) **did reach the worker and run a turn**; the failure appeared/worsened afterward. This points to a latency/data-growth-sensitive race rather than a hard misconfiguration.

## Code path

- Recovery driver: `dist/server-worker-placement-startup-*.mjs`
  - The `stagedResultOwners` publication block wraps `prepareAcceptedPublication(deps, turnClaim)`, `placements.acceptWorkspaceResult(turnClaim)`, `finalizeWorkspaceResultConflicts(...)`, and `settleStagedWorkspaceResult(...)`.
  - The outer catch logs `Cloud workspace recovery deferred: ${boundedWorkerError(error)}` and aborts recovery.
- Fence check: `dist/session-accessor.sqlite-scope-*.mjs` → `transcriptWriteScopeIsCurrent(entry, sessionId, scope)`:
  ```js
  entry.lifecycleRevision === scope.expectedLifecycleRevision
  && entry.activeWriterRunId === scope.expectedWriterRunId
  ```
- Refusal/throw: `dist/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-guard-*.mjs` → `resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal()` returns `{ code: "session-rebound" }` (or `session-entry-missing`) and `assertLockedTranscriptWriteAllowed()` throws `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`.

Interpretation: the placement holds its transcript-writer fence across the whole multi-second accept/publish sequence. If the session's `lifecycleRevision` (or `activeWriterRunId`) advances during that span — e.g. a competing placement/epoch mutation — the next transcript append fails the fence and the entire recovery is deferred, killing the run.

## Host characteristic that amplifies the race

On this Pi the agent DB **open** is extremely slow (doctor `[state/agent-db] slow OpenClaw agent database open`):

- `elapsedMs` 16,463–25,519, `admissionMode=sync`
- dominated by `validation`: `integrity_check` ~11–15 s (74 tables) + `quick_check` on `transcript_events` ~5–10.5 s
- the DB is 296 MB / 72,331 pages, `freelist_count = 0` (no reclaimable free space), WAL mode
- plus slow SQLite holds observed at 1–6 s (`execApprovals.commitAuthorizations`, `audit.writer.process`)

On fast local storage these operations are sub-millisecond/sub-second, the fence window is tiny, and the race would be rare-to-never. On microSD-backed storage every store operation costs seconds, so a competing revision bump lands inside the recovery window almost every time.

## Expectation

Cloud-worker recovery should be robust to slow storage, e.g.:

- keep the placement's transcript-writer fence revision-stable across the full recovery/accept/publish sequence, **or**
- retry/re-fence the transcript append after the publish rather than deferring and failing the whole recovery, **or**
- perform the lifecycle/epoch mutation *outside* the fenced publish span.

The current behaviour turns a transient fence mismatch into a terminal, slot-leaking failure of the whole worker turn.

## Impact

- Remote/cloud-worker sessions unusable on this gateway host.
- Failed placements hold worker slots, degrading node capacity until the placement is cleaned up.

## Attachments / further data available on request

- Full `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway` excerpts around each failure.
- `openclaw doctor` output showing `[state/agent-db]` validation timings.
- Table/page statistics of the agent DB (`transcript_events` 28,686 rows; 72,331 pages; freelist 0).
