issues.body:
## Feature type

Plugin SDK tool-policy contract

## Summary

Trusted tool-policy hooks can inspect host-derived requester identity and tool metadata, but they cannot inspect the host-issued capability scope that selected or configured the current invocation's tool surface.

This makes it impossible for a standalone policy plugin to distinguish two otherwise identical tool calls that were admitted under different host-owned capability bindings.

## Current-main evidence

Verified on `openclaw/openclaw` main at `bc4afcf0af27dada203428c7d6ff6e892a830bed` (2026-10-02).

- `PluginHookToolContext.requester` exposes host-derived channel, account, sender, owner, and provider-role facts.
- Merged PR #111190 intentionally owns that requester-origin contract.
- `OpenClawPluginToolContextBase.toolBindings` carries out-of-band host/plugin bindings to plugin-owned tool factories.
- `AgentRunMessageContext.messageActionTurnCapability` and other internal host capabilities remain runtime-owned.
- `runTrustedToolPolicies(...)` receives tool identity, params, requester context, and session-extension reads, but no per-invocation host capability summary.
- Plain JavaScript ingress strips forged host-owned tool bindings, so a policy plugin cannot safely reconstruct the missing facts from tool parameters.

## Reproduction at the contract level

1. Start two runs for the same agent, session, requester, and tool name.
2. Admit each run with a different host-owned capability binding or action set.
3. Register an installed trusted tool policy that must allow one scope and deny the other.
4. Observe that both evaluations receive the same relevant `PluginHookToolContext`; the per-invocation capability distinction is available to the tool factory but not the policy hook.

## Expected behavior

OpenClaw should choose and document one of these owner boundaries:

1. Expose an immutable, opaque-free, host-normalized capability summary to installed trusted tool policies for the exact invocation; or
2. Keep capability enforcement exclusively host/tool-factory-owned and document that policy hooks must not make decisions from host capability scope.

If a summary is exposed, it should:

- contain only a closed/versioned capability shape, never bearer tokens, private bindings, or transport identities;
- be derived by the host rather than accepted from tool params or caller hook context;
- be cloned/frozen per policy registration so one plugin cannot mutate another plugin's view;
- be absent when the host cannot prove the binding; and
- remain advisory unless the owning host rechecks the live capability at the final effect boundary.

## Actual behavior

Requester identity is available, and host-owned bindings are available to plugin tool factories, but a separate trusted policy plugin has no supported way to evaluate the invocation's capability scope.

## Relationship to existing work

- #111190 resolves requester origin and should remain the canonical identity contract.
- #97152 requested a much broader exclusive, capability-level external approval resolver across every harness. This issue is narrower: it asks where already-admitted per-invocation capability facts belong at the existing trusted policy boundary.
- #50291 tracks hook correlation/trace context, not authorization capability scope.

## Owner decisions requested

1. Should trusted policy hooks receive an opaque-free capability summary, or should this policy remain host/tool-factory-owned?
2. If exposed, should the summary be a generic Plugin SDK contract or a plugin-owned namespaced projection?
3. Which component owns final currentness revalidation before a side effect?

## Impact

Plugins can enforce requester-aware policy, but cannot safely express policy that depends on the host-issued capability scope of the exact invocation. Implementations either duplicate host logic, inspect forgeable parameters, or couple policy into the tool-owning plugin.

issues.body:
## Problem

Three Gateway e2e tests fail on pristine `main` (3f97b146a5a). Main CI doesn't notice because its `checks-node-changed` jobs don't run on main pushes; they only turn red on PRs that touch nearby paths (for example #168401).

| Test | Failure |
|---|---|
| `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts` > preserves model-input whitespace independently from canonical chat history | expected length 1, got 2 |
| `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-provider-review-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` > dispatches the exact acknowledged steer and preserves session and device authority | expected `{ status: 'error' }`, got `ok` |
| `test/gateway-completion-replay.e2e.test.ts` > does not repeat a real requester tool effect through fallback, settle wake, or restart | `childStarted` false |

## Cause

#163471 (cd9913f1b11) changed the runtime-context carrier from `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>` to "OpenClaw runtime context: … End OpenClaw runtime context." (`packages/agent-core/src/harness/messages.ts:199-225`). The three fixtures still exclude only the old envelope, so they treat the runtime carrier as a real user message:
- the whitespace test counts 2 user messages;
- the provider-review mock reads the carrier as the latest user text and skips its 403 branch;
- the replay requester never sees its START text.

`gateway-rpc-chat.e2e.test.ts:399-406`, `gateway-provider-review-product-proof.e2e.test.ts:61-77`, `gateway-completion-replay.e2e.test.ts:240-247`.

## Evidence

Reproduced in a clean main worktree with the same invocation (`OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`); identical failures on #168401's CI run 38101640658. The baseline also had two unrelated chat-timeout failures.

## Fix

Have the fixtures recognize the carrier through its owner (for example the `runtimeContextCarrier` marker or a shared helper next to `labelRuntimeContextContent`), not by matching envelope text, so future renames don't break them again. Keep all behavioral assertions.

issues.body:
## Summary

A repository-only session (`sessions.create` with `repository: {url, ref}`) placed on a paired device via `sessions.dispatch` executed its turn **on the Gateway host, in the agent's default workspace**, after the requested Codex model failed and the configured model fallback chain selected a model on the native OpenClaw runtime. The native-runtime turn ran `exec` locally and wrote files into `~/.openclaw/workspace/` (the agent workspace), not into the placed repository checkout.

The placement guard is inconsistent across fallback candidates: one fallback (anthropic/claude-fable-5-1) was correctly refused with `This repository session needs a cloud worker. Choose a cloud environment and retry.`, but the next fallback (google/gemini-3.5-flash) was admitted and ran locally.

Second, the trigger was a misclassification: an expired Codex node-execution approval (`Codex node execution approval expired before a decision`) was recorded as an **auth** failure with `status: 401`, which put the OpenAI subscription auth profile into cooldown and made the next fallback (openai/gpt-5.6-sol) fail with `Auth profile ... is temporarily unavailable`.

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (1391f7c), Gateway on Linux (Node 26.7.0). Paired device: macOS 26.6.2 node host, 2026.9.3, `nodeHost.workerRuns.enabled: true`, Codex plugin installed and enabled, `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["codex.exec-server.stdio.v1"]`.

## Reproduction

1. `openclaw gateway call sessions.create --params '{"key":"agent:main:repo-spike","repository":{"url":"https://github.com/<owner>/<private-repo>.git","ref":"main"}}'` with the agent's primary model on the Codex runtime (here `openai/gpt-6-astra`) and `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` containing a native-runtime model (here `google/gemini-3.5-flash`).
2. `openclaw gateway call sessions.dispatch --params '{"key":"agent:main:repo-spike","deviceId":"<paired-device-id>"}'` → placement `active`, `runner.kind: device`.
3. Send a turn that runs `hostname; pwd` and writes a file, via `sessions_send` from another session (or `chat.send`) **without** answering the "Run Codex on this node placement" approval within 120 s.

Observed (Gateway log, redacted):

```
[agent/embedded] codex app-server preparation timings ... stage=runtime-start outcome=error totalMs=121689
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: ... provider=openai reason=auth window=cooldown
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... error="Codex node execution approval expired before a decision. Retry the action and approve the new request."
model_fallback_decision candidate_failed requested=openai/gpt-6-astra candidate=openai/gpt-6-astra reason=auth status=401 errorPreview="Codex node execution approval expired before a ..."
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... error="This repository session needs a cloud worker. Choose a cloud environment and retry."   <- anthropic/claude-fable-5-1 correctly refused
[diagnostic] lane task error: ... error="Auth profile \"openai:<redacted>\" is temporarily unavailable for openai/gpt-5.6-sol."
model_fallback_decision candidate_succeeded candidate=google/gemini-3.5-flash candidateRouteOrigin=configured-fallback
```

The gemini turn's transcript shows `provider: google`, `exec` calls with output `hostname → <gateway host>`, `pwd → /home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace`, and a file created there. `sessions.describe` for the session still reported `placement.state: active` on the device throughout.

Retrying the same turn and resolving the approval promptly (`openclaw approvals resolve <id> allow-always`) ran correctly on the device (`hostname → <device>`, `pwd → .../node-host/.../workspaces/...`), and the result reconciled into `refs/openclaw/worker-results/...` on the Gateway.

## Expected

1. A session with an active device/cloud placement must never execute a turn on the Gateway host. If the placed runtime cannot run, the turn should fail with the placement guidance (as the anthropic candidate did), for **every** fallback candidate, or the fallback chain should be skipped for placed sessions.
2. An expired node-execution approval is a user-decision timeout, not an auth failure; it should not be classified as `auth`/401 and should not put the provider auth profile into cooldown.

## Impact

Silent execution of an untrusted-workspace turn on the Gateway host with the agent's local exec policy, while the UI/API report the session as placed on the device. Files were written outside the intended repository workspace.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Doctor marks already-canonical one-shot cron schedules as mutated, so a no-op normalization can enter the repair branch that creates a whole shared-state SQLite recovery copy.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

For an otherwise canonical job whose `schedule.at` already equals its normalized ISO value and has no legacy `atMs`, normalization should report no mutation. A no-op cron pass should not enter the pre-mutation backup/save branch. Real cron repairs should retain their existing backup and ownership checks.

This follows the current normalizer's mutation contract and the guarded field comparisons elsewhere in that function.

### Actual behavior

During an upgrade recovery on one Windows host, three Doctor passes created three automatic cron recovery copies of the shared state database. A read-only audit found all 178 authored automation definitions unchanged against the pre-activation state; 43 one-shot schedules already had canonical `schedule.at` strings.

No standalone backup command or job was launched. These copies were created by Doctor's cron repair path.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1-based local builds `225f13637745` and `e0e760586226`, based on `e178c39e9aae`; not unmodified official packages.

Local changes include #165420/#165982 backports, a Windows cron publication repair, SQLite diagnostics, and, in the later build, a caller-only plugin lease-window workaround. The three relevant files below are unchanged from the v2026.10.1 source. Current main `1d952d58b156` still has the unconditional timestamp mutation flag; it was inspected, not executed.

### Operating system

Native Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200, build 26200; Node v26.8.1.

### Install method

Locally built core deployed to an existing npm global installation. Doctor ran inside `update repair` during controlled maintenance.

### Model

Not applicable to this local cron normalization path.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

### Logs

Sanitized observation summary:

```text
Doctor passes with automatic cron recovery copies: 3
Recovery-copy sizes: 218701824, 159281152, 159285248 bytes
Total: 537268224 bytes

Authored automation definitions compared: 178
Definitions changed: 0
One-shot schedules already using canonical schedule.at: 43
```

The copies occurred across the first failed finalization and the two Doctor passes of a later repair. No additional Doctor invocation was performed to reproduce this report.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The source-level trigger is concrete:

- In [v2026.10.1 normalization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e178c39e9aae3fa440735217f9aef9574f286677/src/commands/doctor/cron/store-migration.ts#L454), any parseable `at` value causes `sched.at = normalizedAt` followed by unconditional `mutated = true`, including when the string is identical and no `atMs` exists.
- [Current main retains that behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/commands/doctor/cron/store-migration.ts#L395).
- [Doctor includes `normalized.mutated` in `storeChanged`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-repair.ts#L334), then [creates a backup before saving existing owned rows](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-repair.ts#L395).
- [The backup helper snapshots the shared state SQLite database](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/commands/doctor/cron/store-repair.ts#L197), not just the cron definitions.

The unconditional flag is sufficient to enter that branch for a canonical one-shot job. Other legitimate repair reasons have not been isolated for every observed pass, so this report does not attribute every byte copied exclusively to this condition.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one Windows installation with persisted one-shot automations.
- Severity: unnecessary repair work and recovery-copy storage.
- Frequency: three automatic copies observed across three Doctor passes.
- Consequence: 537,268,224 bytes of recovery copies, despite no change in the audited authored automation definitions. No data loss is claimed.

### Additional information

Minimal runtime reproduction and regression boundary: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No source edits, new tests, or further Doctor/backup invocations were made for this report.

Related but different: #19484 addressed backup churn in the retired JSON cron save path; #43855 concerned no-op `payload.kind` normalization. This report covers the current `schedule.at` normalization and SQLite Doctor repair path.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A completed `update repair` still reported that ACPX's data/settings upgrade was unfinished, although the canonical `migration_runs` completion receipt had already been written.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

[Repair's documented warning reconciliation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/update/repair-and-recovery) and #155389 suppress a matching warning after its migration owner records completion, while preserving genuinely pending or reintroduced obligations.

### Actual behavior

One observed `update repair --yes --json --timeout 2400` exited 0 with `status: "warning"`, but its final `postUpdate.doctor.warnings` retained this message:

```text
Plugin "acpx" data/settings upgrade is unfinished: The installed plugin has not confirmed that its saved data and settings are ready for this version. If Doctor cannot finish the upgrade, report this warning to the plugin maintainer. Your existing data and settings have been kept. Let the current update or repair finish. If this warning remains afterward, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to retry the upgrade.
```

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1-based local build `e0e760586226`, based on `e178c39e9aae`; not an unmodified official package. Retained local changes: #165420/#165982 backports, Windows cron publication repair, SQLite diagnostics, and a caller-only plugin lease-window workaround.

The warning timestamping/filtering blocks and fresh-Doctor warning forwarding are unchanged from the release source. The same relevant logic is present on current main `1d952d58b156`; current main was inspected, not executed.

### Operating system

Native Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200, build 26200; Node v26.8.1.

### Install method

Locally built core deployed to an existing npm global installation; repair run from PowerShell with the Gateway stopped for maintenance.

### Model

Not applicable to this local diagnostic defect.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

### Logs

Sanitized observations from the same repair:

```text
Canonical migration_runs metadata, read with SQLite mode=ro:
  id: deferred-plugin-migration:acpx
  status: completed
  finished_at: 1791685877430 (2026-10-11T02:31:17.430Z)

Later parent warning receipt for the exact retained wording above:
  step: warning:finalize:doctor:15
  endedAtMs: 1791686101466 (2026-10-11T02:35:01.466Z)

Final repair:
  exited 0 at 2026-10-11T02:37:46.398Z
  status: warning
  required Doctor lint: exit 0
  postUpdate.doctor.warnings: still includes the ACPX warning above
```

This is an owner-issued migration completion receipt, not a plugin cache/hydration marker. A separate Codex migration remained canonically pending; that warning is not claimed to be stale.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Relevant current-main source:

- [Fresh Doctor consumes its result after the child settles](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-doctor.ts#L410) and [forwards the result warnings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-fresh-doctor.ts#L446). stdout/stderr are replayed afterward; the structured warning callback is the relevant path.
- [The parent assigns `Date.now()` on first receipt of each complete warning string](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts#L324).
- [Reconciliation retains the warning when `completedAtMs < doctorWarningTimes.get(warning)`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-finalize.ts#L436).

The initial Doctor emitted a different ACPX warning about waiting for the parent's install records. That earlier message does not supply the first-receipt timestamp for the later, differently worded warning. The callback's exact timestamp was not instrumented; the warning receipt timestamp above is the recorded parent phase event.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: one Windows repair invocation.
- Severity: misleading completion diagnostics.
- Frequency: observed once on the retained upgrade state.
- Consequence: successful migration is still presented as unfinished, with instructions to rerun Doctor or contact the plugin maintainer. No data loss is claimed.

### Additional information

A minimal/current-main reproduction and regression boundary are not established. No extra Doctor invocation was run solely to reproduce this report.

Related: #166766 was closed after its supposed completion markers proved to be cache markers and the canonical migration remained pending. Here, the canonical ACPX migration receipt is completed. #155389 introduced the existing receipt-based suppression; this report concerns warning delivery later than that completion.

A focused acceptance case would cover a warning observed in a child before migration completion but delivered afterward: suppress that resolved warning while preserving a genuinely pending plugin and a genuinely newer obligation.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On one native Windows host, a 2026.10.1-based local build completed Doctor during `update repair`, then failed the plugin phase after 467.482 seconds with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST` for `core:plugin-lifecycle/global`.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The documented [update repair workflow](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/update/repair-and-recovery#update-repair) completes post-core Doctor and plugin convergence on the installed version. Genuine loss of ownership must still fence writes; this report does not request bypassing that protection.

### Actual behavior

Doctor completed. The subsequent `finalize:plugins` phase failed with the lease-loss error below, and the CLI exited with code 1. Update finalization remained incomplete.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.1-based local build `225f13637745`, based on the v2026.10.1 source at `e178c39e9aae`. This is **not an unmodified official package**.

Local changes comprise the upstream orphan OAuth scanner fix (#165420), Windows snapshot fix (#165982), a Windows cron publication repair, and bounded SQLite transaction/worker diagnostics. Neither `src/plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.ts` nor `src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts` was modified. A timing contribution from the local instrumentation has not been ruled out.

### Operating system

Native Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200, build 26200. The repair process used Node v26.8.1.

### Install method

Locally built core deployed to the existing npm global installation; repair launched from an independent PowerShell process.

### Model

Not applicable to this local lease error.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable to the observed failure.

### Logs

Reduced phase receipts from the same attempt:

```json
{"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"completed","endedAtMs":1791681522147}
{"step":"finalize:plugins","status":"in_progress","startedAtMs":1791681523303}
{"step":"finalize:plugins","status":"failed","detail":"plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost","failureFacts":[{"check":"plugins","code":"OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST","message":"plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost"}],"reason":"OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST","endedAtMs":1791681990785}
```

Final stdout, with exit code 1:

```json
{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost"}}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The observed sequence was: install the local 2026.10.1-based build during recovery from a failed upgrade; keep the managed Gateway stopped for controlled maintenance; run `openclaw update repair --yes --json`; observe Doctor complete and the plugin phase fail. The existing configured plugin/state set was retained. This is one observed attempt, not a clean-install or current-main reproduction.

The [v2026.10.1 plugin lifecycle helper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/src/plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.ts) supplies a five-minute renewable lease to `withOpenClawStateLease` without selecting worker heartbeat mode. The [state lease implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.1/src/state/openclaw-state-lease.ts) therefore uses the timer renewal path for this call. These are source facts, not proof of why this attempt lost ownership.

- Severity: blocks completion of the repair workflow.
- Frequency: one failure in one observed repair attempt on this build.
- Consequence: the core package was installed, but required post-core finalization did not complete. The Gateway was already stopped for maintenance.

### Additional information

Root cause and regression boundary: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No evidence yet establishes that the lease was stolen, expired, or lost because of a particular blocking operation.

Related reports were checked across open and closed issues/PRs:

- #164986 covers a post-Doctor plugin failure on macOS with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_STORAGE_FAILED` and an offline-maintenance verification error. This attempt instead reported `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`.
- #167406 includes the same global plugin lease-loss message during a Windows plugin install/startup investigation. This report records the separate offline `update repair` finalization path. A shared cause is not established.

issues.body:
### Problem

The `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold` setting is implemented as a **per-tool-type counter**, not a session-level global counter. This allows agents to evade the circuit breaker by switching tools, leading to unbounded loops.

### Real-world incident

- **Date**: 2026-05-08
- **Session**: feishu DM, model qwen/qwen3.5-plus
- **What happened**: Agent entered a loop calling `wecom_mcp` → blocked after 5 calls → switched to `exec` → blocked after 5 calls → switched to `memory_search` → blocked after 5 calls → switched again... repeated across 4+ tools.
- **Result**: ~60+ LLM calls, ~750k input tokens consumed, user had to manually `/stop`
- **Root cause**: `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold` resets its counter for each tool type, so switching tools resets the count

### Expected behavior

Per documentation: `globalCircuitBreakerThreshold` is described as "global no-progress breaker threshold". The word "global" implies it should count **across all tools** within a session, not per-tool-type.

### Actual behavior

Each tool type has its own independent counter. Switching tools resets the count:

| Tool | Calls before block | After block |
|------|-------------------|-------------|
| `wecom_mcp` | 5 | blocked → switch to `exec` |
| `exec` | 5 | blocked → switch to `memory_search` |
| `memory_search` | 5 | blocked → switch to `sessions_list` |
| ... | ... | continues indefinitely |

### Proposed fix

Track no-progress counts at the **session level**, not per-tool-type:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "loopDetection": {
      "globalCircuitBreakerThreshold": 5  // total across ALL tools in session
    }
  }
}
```

When the session-level counter reaches the threshold, block **all tool calls** (not just the current tool) and force the agent to produce a text response.

### Workaround

Lower the threshold to 2-3 to reduce the blast radius of each tool switch, but this does not solve the fundamental issue.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.6
- Ubuntu 24.04
- Model: qwen/qwen3.5-plus

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On a realtime voice call the agent's own audio leaks back through the line, and the local RMS speech gate treats that echo as caller speech — cancelling the agent's own turn (spurious barge-in) and producing `user` transcripts for words the caller never said.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a realtime call (Google live provider) where the agent speaks at length while the caller is silent.
2. Observe the call logs and the stored transcript.

### Expected behavior
Input energy that arrives while the agent's own audio is still draining is attributed to echo and does not count as caller speech.

### Actual behavior
Any input energy, including assistant echo, arms the barge-in gate and can be committed as a caller transcript. Leaked assistant audio also sets the "last local audio" timestamp, so the existing staleness guard can never suppress a phantom transcript while the agent is talking (the staleness half is always fresh); the observed guard suppressed zero transcripts across an inspected call.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 with plugin `@openclaw/voice-call`

### Operating system
Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0)

### Model
realtime provider: Google live (`gemini-live`)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> google realtime voice provider -> telephony carrier

### Logs
Guard instrumentation showed `maxRecentInputRms` and `maxEchoInputRms` both well above the gate threshold while the agent was speaking, with no caller audio present.

### Impact and severity
Affected: realtime voice calls in any deployment.
Severity: moderate (agent turns are cancelled mid-sentence; phantom caller lines pollute transcripts and can trigger downstream agent logic).
Frequency: intermittent, tied to line echo characteristics and agent talk length.
Consequence: lost agent output and wrong caller attribution in stored transcripts.

### Additional information
Fix submitted in a linked PR: input energy seen while the agent's paced audio is still draining (or within a short tail after the last outbound chunk) is recorded as echo and cannot arm a barge-in or become caller speech, and the final-transcript path only drops a transcript as phantom when no caller audio was seen for the guard window and the loudest recent input was weak.

issues.body:
## Problem

When a model fallback occurs mid-session (e.g., primary model rate-limits and the fallback chain fires), three user-facing gaps compound into a single failure mode: the session silently changes personality.

**Originally filed as part of #65824 (item 1) and #65812, audited against 2026.4.15. Re-audited against 2026.5.7 — all three gaps confirmed still present.**

## What 2026.5.7 gets right

The internal observability is significantly improved since our original filing:

- **Dedicated fallback module.** `model-fallback-DIXhOaxb.js` (was inline) now has structured fallback step fields, attempt tracking, and chain-position logging.
- **Verbose fallback notice.** `buildFallbackNotice()` emits `↪️ Model Fallback: <active>` as a lifecycle-stream event on transition.
- **Fallback lifecycle events.** `fallback_cleared` emitted on recovery — useful for debugging.

Credit where due: the fallback internals are now well-structured and debuggable. The gaps are in the user-facing layer.

## Remaining gaps

### Gap A: Non-verbose users see nothing

`agent-runner.runtime-DQsCsHUA.js:3929-3937` — `buildFallbackNotice()` is gated behind `if (verboseEnabled)`. On default settings, a mid-session switch from Opus to Gemini is invisible.

We understand the verbose gate is probably a deliberate UX choice to avoid noise. A lightweight opt-in — something like `agents.defaults.fallback.notify: true` or a one-line non-verbose notice — would bridge this for users who want awareness without full verbose output.

### Gap B: No workspace-context re-injection on fallback

`contextInjection: "continuation-skip"` (the recommended default for token efficiency) does not re-inject bootstrap context when the model changes mid-session. The skip logic at `selection-BeP8qtCb.js:4586-4587` checks `bootstrapMode` and `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` but not model-change state.

Result: the fallback model inherits conversation history but not SOUL.md / AGENTS.md / workspace persona. This is the root of the "session suddenly feels different" class of incident.

### Gap C: No event type for user hooks

`model_fallback_decision` at `model-fallback-DIXhOaxb.js:202` is a log event (subsystem logger), not a plugin hook event. There's no `model:fallback` or equivalent in the plugin hook system, so user plugins can't react to fallback transitions.

## Workaround

- **Gap B:** `contextInjection: "always"` re-injects on every turn, covering fallback turns — at a token cost. Our `canon-guardian` plugin (shared in #75750) selectively re-injects only on model switch, new session, and periodic safety net, covering the gap at ~2-4% of turns.
- **Gap A/C:** No automated workaround possible. Manual behavioral-drift monitoring.

## Proposed solution

1. **Opt-in fallback notification:** `agents.defaults.fallback.notify` config field. When enabled, inject a one-line system message on model switch (e.g., "⚠️ Session switched from claude-opus-4-7 to gemini-3.1-pro-preview due to timeout"). Not verbose-gated.
2. **Context re-injection on model change:** When `continuation-skip` is active and the model changes, treat the next turn as a bootstrap turn for context injection purposes. Check model-change state alongside `bootstrapMode` / `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn` in the skip logic.
3. **Plugin hook event:** Expose `model:fallback` (or equivalent) to the plugin hook system so user plugins can react to transitions.

## Impact

Highest. Every "my agent changed personalities" report we've seen traces back to the re-injection gap. Affects every user running a fallback chain with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.7 (eeef486) · macOS arm64
- 4-provider fallback chain (Anthropic → Google → OpenAI → xAI)
- Heavy use of workspace files for agent identity and operating rules

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Gateway `voice-call` commands run through the plugin's command service, which is bound to the runtime generation captured at registration time; if the live runtime slot is owned by a different generation (e.g. the plugin was re-registered by a config reload while a call is active), a command either throws a lifecycle error or retires/stops the runtime that is serving the live call.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start a realtime voice call so the runtime slot is `running` under generation A.
2. Cause the plugin to re-register (config reload) so the command service is bound to generation B.
3. Run a `voice-call` gateway command (e.g. status).

### Expected behavior
A read/control command operates on the live runtime and does not disturb an active call.

### Actual behavior
`ensureRuntime` resolves the slot for generation B while the slot is owned by generation A: if A is retired the runtime is stopped and rebuilt (dropping the live call), otherwise a `VoiceCallRuntimeLifecycleError` ("A previous voice call runtime generation is still active") is thrown.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 with plugin `@openclaw/voice-call`

### Operating system
Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0)

### Model
n/a (plugin lifecycle)

### Provider / routing chain
n/a

### Logs
Grounded in `extensions/voice-call/index.ts`: `createVoiceCallCommandService(ensureRuntime)` binds the registration generation, while `ensureRuntimeForGeneration` compares `slot.owner !== runtimeGeneration`.

### Impact and severity
Affected: deployments that reload configuration/plugins while a voice call is live.
Severity: moderate (a command can drop an active call).
Frequency: only when the registration generation differs from the live slot owner.
Consequence: an in-progress call is terminated or the command fails.

### Additional information
Fix submitted in a linked PR: the command service prefers the live runtime when the coordinator slot is `running`, and only falls back to `ensureRuntime()` otherwise.

issues.body:
## Summary
The ACP translator assumes Gateway assistant text only ever grows as an append-only prefix. When the model revises in-progress output so the new full text is not a prefix of what was already sent, the translator computes the outgoing delta by slicing the new full text at the byte length it has already emitted. For a divergent revision this emits a garbage tail, and for a shorter revision it emits nothing at all, so the ACP client (Zed, Codex ACP) renders corrupted or stale assistant text for the whole turn.

## Environment
- Commit: aad99747cd45b3845e027c2297b85835b0bef75f (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: ACP bridge (src/acp/translator.ts), every ACP front-end consuming Gateway chat events

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start an ACP session and prompt the agent so a prompt is pending.
2. Have the Gateway emit a chat delta whose full assistant text is "Hello world".
3. Have the Gateway emit a follow-up chat delta whose full assistant text is a non-append revision, for example "Goodbye world" (the Gateway marks this frame `replace: true` with `deltaText: "Goodbye world"`), then the terminal final frame with the same text.
4. Repeat with a shorter revision: full text "Hello world!" then revised to "Hi".
5. Observe what the ACP client receives as `agent_message_chunk` updates.

## Expected
The ACP client ends each turn rendering the Gateway authoritative final text ("Goodbye world" and "Hi"), matching what the Gateway actually produced.

## Actual
- Divergent revision "Hello world" -> "Goodbye world": the client renders "Hello worldld" (the stale prefix plus a nonsensical "ld" tail sliced out of "Goodbye world" at offset 11).
- Shorter revision "Hello world!" -> "Hi": the client stays stuck on the stale longer "Hello world!" and never sees "Hi".
- The terminal final frame carries the corrected full text but re-runs the identical slice, so it never repairs the client; the corruption survives the whole turn.

## Root cause
src/acp/translator.ts `handleDeltaEvent`, text path (the thinking path just above it has the identical defect):

```ts
const fullText = content
  ?.filter((block) => block?.type === "text")
  .map((block) => block.text ?? "")
  .join("\n")
  .trimEnd();
const sentSoFar = pending.sentTextLength ?? 0;
if (!fullText || fullText.length <= sentSoFar) {
  return;
}

const newText = fullText.slice(sentSoFar);
pending.sentTextLength = fullText.length;
pending.sentText = fullText;
```

The delta is `fullText.slice(pending.sentTextLength)`, which is only correct when each frame is a strict extension of the previous one. The Gateway does not guarantee that. src/gateway/server-chat.ts `resolveBroadcastDelta` explicitly detects non-append revisions and signals them:

```ts
if (!params.text.startsWith(previous)) {
  return { deltaText: params.text, replace: true };
}
```

The translator ignores both `replace` and `deltaText`. On a divergent revision `fullText.length` still exceeds `sentSoFar`, so it slices mid-string and emits a garbage tail. On a shorter revision `fullText.length <= sentSoFar`, so the early return drops the revision entirely and the client keeps the stale text.

Correct behavior: honor the Gateway `replace` marker (reset `sentTextLength`/`sentText` and emit the full revised text) and/or emit the provided `deltaText` instead of slicing by length.

## Sibling surfaces
- Thinking path in the same method (`fullThought.slice(sentThoughtSoFar)` with `pending.sentThoughtLength`) has the identical defect and corrupts `agent_thought_chunk` on any revised or Gateway-stripped thinking block.
- The merged fix that most recently touched this region, PR #44597 ("preserve final assistant message snapshot before end_turn"), only added final-frame processing; it kept the append-only slice and does not consider `replace`/`deltaText`, so this path is unaffected by it.

## Distinct from prior ACP reports
The earlier ACP text fixes (#17615, #24111, #24732, #44597) all address the append-only "final text dropped or truncated" family, and the closed symptom issue #20172 was resolved by those. None of them handle a non-append revision; the corruption here is a different mechanism (wrong delta arithmetic on a revised full text) and is live on current main.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: ACP translator emits corrupted or stale assistant text when Gateway assistant text is revised non-append.
Real environment tested: real AcpGatewayAgent driven through its public handleGatewayEvent chat path (handleChatEvent -> handleDeltaEvent -> AcpTranslatorSessionUpdates.emit -> connection.sessionUpdate), at commit aad99747cd45b3845e027c2297b85835b0bef75f.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: feed the real agent two chat "delta" frames plus a "final" frame for each case (divergent "Hello world" -> "Goodbye world"; shorter "Hello world!" -> "Hi") and concatenate the agent_message_chunk text the client receives.
Evidence after fix:
```
CASE divergent revision (Hello world -> Goodbye world)
  chunks emitted: ["Hello world","ld"]
  ACP client renders: "Hello worldld"
  gateway authoritative final text: "Goodbye world"

CASE shorter revision (Hello world! -> Hi)
  chunks emitted: ["Hello world!"]
  ACP client renders: "Hello world!"
  gateway authoritative final text: "Hi"
```
Observed result after fix: the client renders "Hello worldld" for the divergent revision and stays stuck on "Hello world!" for the shorter revision, instead of "Goodbye world" and "Hi"; the Gateway `replace`/`deltaText` revision markers are discarded and the final frame never repairs the client.
What was not tested: only the translator delta path was driven; I did not test against a live Zed or Codex ACP front-end, and I did not exercise the identical thinking-path defect end to end (established by reading, not by a driven run).

issues.body:
## Summary
Artifact-preserving config/metadata reads can pay for full shared-state SQLite snapshots. On a long-running installation the shared state is 169,709,568 bytes, of which 89,735,168 bytes are audit tables/indexes (99,337 events). This makes a small config/auth-status read depend on unrelated audit-ledger growth.

## Environment and evidence
- Installed OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Linux, Node runtime. Originally noticed on 2026.9.5.
- Current measurements taken 2026-09-26 PT using read-only SQLite queries and filesystem stat.
- 31,952 audit events older than 14 days at measurement time.
- Gateway cgroup memory.current observed at 12,673,167,360 bytes with 1,051 tasks. This includes reclaimable page cache and is NOT an attribution of all memory to SQLite or MCP.
- Multiple connected Control UI clients periodically query the service. An earlier operator diagnostic reported 82 RPCs from one connection in five minutes; that historical count has not been independently remeasured for this filing.

Installed source path inspected:
1. Config snapshot/read paths in `src/config/io` enter `withArtifactPreservingStateReads`.
2. `withFreshOpenClawStateDatabaseReadOnly` calls `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationSync` when artifact preservation is required and a suitable cached/scope-owned reader is absent.
3. `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationSync` starts the synchronous read-only worker; the readonly-location implementation copies the source SQLite database and relevant WAL prefix into private staging.
4. A live cached database or a shared synchronous snapshot scope can avoid repeat snapshots. Therefore this report does NOT claim that every read unconditionally copies the DB.

Local caveat: this installation has a local synchronous snapshot-reuse patch. No pristine-versus-patched timing comparison is claimed here; the underlying fresh-read copy path and current data-size measurements are the evidence. A syscall trace of one CLI config read completed but did not show copy_file_range/sendfile; the implementation uses descriptor reads/writes, so that trace is NOT a snapshot count.

## Reproduction / requested measurement
With a representative shared DB containing a large audit ledger, profile repeated ordinary config reads and Control UI auth/status polling. Count fresh snapshot-worker invocations, staged DB/WAL bytes, synchronous blocked time, and temporary-file lifetime. Compare with the same logical config and smaller audit ledger. Preserve credentials and actual ledger contents locally.

## Expected
Routine online config/auth reads should not repeatedly copy unrelated audit history, while retaining strict snapshot/ownership semantics for offline diagnostics and forensic reads.

## Suggested bounded investigation
Share a properly scoped snapshot or borrow the live owner where semantics permit; alternatively separate high-churn audit storage from configuration metadata. Do not weaken POSIX-lock safety, current-read admission, artifact-preservation contracts, or authorization freshness to avoid copies.

Related: #150138 addresses startup snapshot worker overhead; this report concerns steady-state reads and shared-state size scaling. #149984 also tracks startup snapshot waves.

## Local mitigation
Disable optional audit recording, preserve a verified backup, prune only events older than the authorized 14-day cutoff, then compact offline. Reduce unnecessary UI polling and scope per-agent MCP startup separately. These mitigate cost; they are not an upstream code fix.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Stored realtime voice-call transcripts lose the caller/bot ordering: every bot line is recorded first and the caller's side is appended at hang-up as a single glued blob, instead of interleaving `user`/`assistant` entries as a dialogue.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a realtime (Google live) inbound or outbound voice call through the voice-call plugin.
2. Have the agent and caller take more than one turn each.
3. Read the persisted transcript for that call from the voice-call store.

### Expected behavior
Transcript entries interleave the caller and the agent in dialogue order, one entry per turn, the way the pre-realtime (non-Google) transcript path stores them (`u b u b`).

### Actual behavior
The agent's entries land as they are spoken; the caller's side is flushed once, at connection close, and stored as one `user` entry whose text is every caller utterance glued together with no separators. Observed in 28 stored calls: e.g. call `9181a17b` = 21 assistant entries then a single user entry; `bd9c0eed` = 15 assistant entries then one user entry. No caller speech is persisted during the call.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 with plugin `@openclaw/voice-call` (also reproduced on 2026.9.4 / 2026.9.5)

### Operating system
Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0)

### Model
realtime provider: Google live (`gemini-live`); control model irrelevant

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> google realtime voice provider (websocket)

### Logs
Google realtime provider emits caller transcripts only as partials (`completeInput=false`) and sets `finished` nowhere, so the caller side is flushed as a single final in `flushPendingTranscripts()` at close. At the plugin layer, a `call.speech` partial persists nothing, so the caller never reaches the store until that final flush.

### Impact and severity
Affected: any deployment reading realtime call transcripts (search, summaries, post-call review).
Severity: moderate (transcripts are unusable as a conversation record).
Frequency: always with the Google realtime provider.
Consequence: caller and agent turns cannot be attributed or read in order.

### Additional information
Fix submitted in a linked PR: commit the pending caller partial as its own `call.speech` entry immediately before the first assistant entry of each turn, and dedupe the end-of-call provider flush against what was already committed.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On a realtime outbound voice call the opening greeting is generated once and queued as one large audio burst, and a barge-in that arrives while that burst is still queued clears the entire burst and cancels the greeting turn, so the callee hears only the first fraction of a second and then silence.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Place an outbound realtime call with an initial greeting (Google live provider).
2. Say "Hello" as soon as the greeting starts playing.

### Expected behavior
The opening greeting plays out in full; barge-in takes effect normally after it finishes.

### Actual behavior
The greeting audio is cleared a fraction of a second in and the greeting turn is cancelled. In one observed outbound call the greeting had queued a 53 760-byte (~6.7 s) burst; a provider barge-in cleared the whole burst 0.3 s after the callee said "Hello", and two local barge-in events (`queuedBytes=0`) had already cancelled the greeting turn during the ~9 s before the greeting audio was queued. On a later call the burst was preserved only until the first carrier mark was acknowledged with 34 240 bytes still queued, and the next barge-in then wiped the rest — cutting the opening mid-question.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 with plugin `@openclaw/voice-call`

### Operating system
Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0)

### Model
realtime provider: Google live (`gemini-live`)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> google realtime voice provider (websocket) -> telephony carrier

### Logs
```
[voice-call] realtime outbound audio cleared by provider barge-in callId=… queuedBytes=53760
```

### Impact and severity
Affected: any outbound/inbound realtime call with an initial greeting.
Severity: high (the caller hears a broken greeting, sometimes none at all).
Frequency: observed on 3 of 3 inspected outbound calls; the provider and the local gate both trigger it.
Consequence: the call opens with silence, and any consent or intro question in the greeting is never heard.

### Additional information
Fix submitted in a linked PR: a greeting-protection window armed when the provider becomes ready with an initial greeting that suppresses both barge-in paths until the greeting has genuinely played out, plus muting the caller's input to the provider for the duration so the barge-in is not taken as a user turn.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
When a realtime voice agent asks the caller a question and the caller does not answer, nothing in the bridge wakes the model, so the agent sits silently on an open line until the call is torn down by a duration/disconnect limit instead of closing politely.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run a realtime call (Google live provider) with instructions to ask the caller a consent/intro question.
2. Stay silent after the question.

### Expected behavior
The agent notices the silence and closes the call politely, e.g. one short apology, then hangs up.

### Actual behavior
The call holds the line. The realtime instructions ask the agent for a short window followed by an apology and hangup, but with no caller audio there is no transcript or speech event to prompt it, and no timer exists to do so — the call is only ended by an external limit.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.6 with plugin `@openclaw/voice-call`

### Operating system
Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0)

### Model
realtime provider: Google live (`gemini-live`)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> google realtime voice provider -> telephony carrier

### Logs
No caller transcript, speech, or turn event is emitted between the agent's question and the eventual teardown.

### Impact and severity
Affected: realtime calls where the caller is silent or does not answer the opening question.
Severity: moderate (unnecessary call time, carrier cost, and a bad caller experience).
Frequency: whenever the caller does not respond to a question.
Consequence: calls are held open instead of ending politely.

### Additional information
Fix submitted in a linked PR: a bounded watchdog arms when an assistant turn asks a question, cancels on any caller speech or transcript, and on expiry injects a user message telling the agent the window closed so it apologises and ends the call.

issues.body:
### Summary

On a small self-hosted gateway, ~650 MB of V8 heap stays resident in 11–12 long-lived worker isolates at steady state, and nothing short of a restart releases it. I'd like an opt-in way to let idle workers go (above all the prepared-model catalog worker, ~230 MB), or at least configurable pool sizes / heap limits / idle TTLs and a documented expected footprint.

This is **not** a leak report. The heap profile below shows no growth, and the catalog worker is flat. The catalog *growth* reports (#157842, #159514, #159596, #159662) are a different problem.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Docker image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest`, Node v24.19.0, linux/arm64
- Started as `node dist/index.js gateway --bind lan --port 18789 --allow-unconfigured`
- 3 agents; Telegram, WhatsApp and Signal channels enabled; cron jobs run several times an hour
- Container memory limit 2.5 GB on an 8 GB host shared with many other services
- Measured 2026-09-27 at ~23 h uptime

### Problem to solve

From `diagnostics.stability` and `diagnostic.memory.sample`:

| | |
|---|---|
| Process RSS | 1.35–1.45 GB, plus ~0.8 GB swapped out |
| `diagnostics.stability` | maxRss 1,578 MB, maxHeapUsed 794 MB |
| Memory pressure | `pressureCount` 12 in the last 1000 events; every one returned in the event window is `level: warning`, `reason: rss_threshold` (thresholdBytes 1280 MB) |
| Main isolate | heapTotal ~915 MB, heapUsed 690–780 MB, external ~104 MB, arrayBuffers ~12 MB |
| Worker isolates | 11–12 live, ~630–660 MB heapUsed / ~705 MB heapTotal in total |

Worker breakdown (`workerHeaps`):

| Script | Count | heapUsed (each) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` | 1 | 222–233 MB (heapTotal ~249 MB) |
| `session-accessor.sqlite-archive.worker.js` | 4 | 42–46 MB |
| `sqlite-store.worker.js` | 1 | 53–57 MB |
| `openclaw-state-read.worker.js` | 2 | 34–36 MB |
| `openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.worker.js` | 1 | ~23 MB |
| `other` | 3 | ~40 MB |
| `disk-budget.worker.js` (transient) | 0–1 | ~26 MB |

**Steady state, not growth:** a 30 s `diagnostics.heapProfile` (32 KB sampling) had main-isolate heapUsed go 726 → 700 MB, with only ~0.8 MB of retained new allocations (mostly `deserialize` under `decodeSqliteWorkerReplyValue`). The catalog worker stays well below its 512 MB limit, so the heap-flag override from #157575 / #157630 doesn't come into play here.

**Why it hurts on a small host:** each idle worker's baseline heap stays resident for the life of the process. The pressure events I can see are all warning level, so the critical-pressure path that retires idle workers (per `docs/gateway/diagnostics.md`) doesn't run; the kernel swaps the pages out instead.

**What I found in the 2026.9.6 source** (the same on `main` as far as I can tell):

- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.ts`: `GATEWAY_CATALOG_WORKERS = 1`, `CATALOG_WORKER_HEAP_LIMIT_MB = 512`, `idleTimeoutMs: 0`. I understand from the comment next to it (and from #154973) that this is deliberate: pool-level idle retirement would import a different source generation into an existing publication.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-canonical-worker-pool.ts`: `maxWorkers: 2` (`AGENT_DATABASE_PREFLIGHT_CONCURRENCY`), `idleTimeoutMs: 0`, `maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512`.
- `createSqliteTranscriptArchiveWorker` in `session-accessor.sqlite-archive.ts`: `maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512`.
- The database workers use the 30-minute idle window (`SQLITE_IDLE_HANDLE_TTL_MS`). With cron turns several times an hour, they probably never reach it.
- I couldn't find an env var or config key for any of these. `worker-idle-gc` runs a GC but doesn't terminate the worker.

### Proposed solution

In order of preference:

1. **Opt-in, owner-driven idle retirement for the catalog pool.** The docs say critical pressure already retires idle workers through their cleanup owners (#159596 shows the catalog worker going that way). Could the same owner tear down the pool and its publication after N idle minutes and rebuild on next use? On a small host I'd gladly trade a slower first catalog request after a quiet period for ~230 MB. Default off keeps today's behaviour.
2. **Configurable knobs** (env or config): the catalog worker heap limit, the canonical-validation `maxWorkers`, and the SQLite idle TTL. #159638 shows the opposite trade-off (too much worker churn), so a per-host setting seems better than changing the default.
3. **Documented footprint**: a rough per-worker baseline, and what scales with agents / channel accounts / databases, so operators can size a container limit without guessing.

### Questions

- What are the three `other` workers? My guess is the Telegram polling ingress workers. `telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.js` is missing from the 2026.9.6 name list in `src/infra/worker-cpu.ts`, `main` now adds it in `src/infra/worker-diagnostic-script.ts`, and this gateway polls three Telegram bot accounts. Is one ~40 MB isolate per polling account expected?
- Are the four `session-accessor.sqlite-archive.worker.js` isolates the per-database reclamation workers (30-minute TTL)? Or should the canonical-validation pool have closed together with its startup scope?

### Alternatives considered

- **Scheduled gateway restarts:** these reset the footprint, but they interrupt in-flight turns and discard the warm state the pools are there to keep.
- **A lower container limit:** this only moves the pressure into swap or the OOM killer.
- **`--max-old-space-size`:** this caps the main isolate, and per #157575 it can override the per-worker limits.

### Impact

- Affected: self-hosted gateways on small VPSes / SBCs (see also #156448, #157791)
- Severity: medium. Nothing breaks, but ~650 MB (~8 % of an 8 GB host) stays committed to mostly idle isolates, and the container runs close to its limit with swap in use.
- Frequency: always (steady state)

### Evidence/examples

Hourly RSS averages from host monitoring: ~0.5 GB on 2026-08-28, ~0.8–0.9 GB in early September, 1.1–1.5 GB since ~2026-09-20. That spans several upgrades, but configuration and workload also changed over the period, so it's context rather than a bisect.

Related: #156448 (empty-gateway footprint), #157791 (small arm64 host, high steady RSS), #154973 (why the catalog pool uses `idleTimeoutMs: 0`), #133278 (idle reclaim added for the embedding worker), #159638 (SQLite worker churn, the opposite trade-off), #157842 / #159514 / #159596 / #159662 (catalog worker growth, a different problem).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, but I'm happy to test a patch or a pre-release image.

### Additional information

Happy to run more diagnostics: a sanitized `openclaw gateway diagnostics export`, a heap snapshot of the catalog worker, a longer heap profile, or a before/after comparison on a 2026.9.7 or `main` build.

issues.body:
## Summary

Slash `/new` on a session placed on a device worker drops the session's worktree binding but retains active worker placement. The reset-triggering turn then fails with `dispatch requires a session-owned workspace` instead of replying.

Observed on main `4f227c5c76a64a45664701b4f75156207bccdbde` and as an unchanged control for #159506. The automatic daily/idle rollover repair deliberately does not change explicit resets.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated Gateway and the repository's paired-node worker wire fixture, with a local scripted model and a small synthetic Git repository:

1. Create `agent:qa:manual-new` through `sessions.create` with `worktree: true`, a synthetic repository cwd, and `worktreeBaseRef: "main"`.
2. Place it on the paired device through `sessions.dispatch`.
3. Send an ordinary message through `chat.send`; wait for the run through `agent.wait`. It completes successfully on the worker.
4. Send `/new Reply exactly: RESET-CONTROL` through `chat.send` to the same session key.
5. Read `agent.wait` and `sessions.describe`.

Observed result:

```text
ordinary worker turn: status=ok
/new turn: status=error
Session agent:qa:manual-new dispatch requires a session-owned workspace
sessions.describe: worktree absent; placement.state=active; placement.providerId=device
```

No live provider, personal Gateway, or production session was used. The fixture exercised real node RPC, workspace transfer and bundled worker execution; this is not a mocked placement-resolver assertion.

## Expected behavior and owner intent

Explicit reset should leave a coherent workspace/placement state so the next legitimate turn can execute. If it detaches the worktree, placement must reconcile that detachment rather than continuing to require the missing binding.

#100788 (`b4b1984fe7a9`) explicitly says a plain New Chat returns to the agent workspace instead of inheriting the predecessor's managed-worktree cwd. #121666 (`59d545d81f68`) fences same-key replacement sessions against worktree deletion by their predecessor. Those changes concern `sessions.create`/plain New Chat; they do not directly specify slash `/new` semantics. Please establish the intended slash-reset behavior at its owner before choosing whether to retain the binding or reconcile placement.

This is separate from #159452 and #159506, which cover implicit daily/idle rollover. No fix for this explicit-reset path is included there.

issues.body:
## Summary

`sessions.reclaim` reconciles file bytes from a cloud-worker Git workspace but does not adopt commits authored on the worker. The managed worktree stays on its dispatch base commit and committed files return as ordinary working-tree changes.

## Current behavior

Live isolated Gateway -> Crabbox AWS proof on current `main`:

1. Created a session-owned managed worktree at `00eb33fe8e6ebf278ad052f0cbbb257318d78323`.
2. Dispatched with `sessions.dispatch` to the configured AWS worker profile.
3. Ran a real `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` turn on the worker.
4. The worker created and executed a nonce-bearing Node artifact, then committed it as `d133369c71ad6e706041c1f3c6ef1710db052c3c`.
5. `sessions.reclaim` returned `ok: true` with placement `reclaimed`.
6. The Gateway-managed worktree still had HEAD `00eb33fe8e6ebf278ad052f0cbbb257318d78323`; the committed artifact was present but untracked.

The artifact bytes and SHA-256 matched, the source checkout stayed unchanged and clean, canonical `sessions tail` showed the complete remote lifecycle, and the worker lease was destroyed.

## Expected behavior

For Git workspaces, the Gateway should import the worker-authored commit objects, verify that worker HEAD descends from the recorded dispatch base, fast-forward the managed worktree to that head, and preserve any remaining tracked/untracked working-tree result. The worker remains credential-free; only the Gateway owns later push/PR actions.

This is the contract documented in `docs/gateway/cloud-workers.md` and `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md`.

## Root cause

The outbound sync creates a credential-free commit-capable clone, but inbound reconciliation transfers only the manifest-selected workspace files. `.git` is excluded, the manifest records only the original `baseCommit`, and the reconciliation test currently asserts that local HEAD remains unchanged after a worker commit.

## Proposed fix

- Authenticate worker HEAD in the immutable manifest.
- Export only worker commits/objects above the recorded base through a bounded pack.
- Import the pack on the Gateway, verify ancestry and the expected base, and adopt it with compare-and-swap semantics.
- Extend the durable reconciliation journal so crash recovery restores both file state and Git HEAD/index.
- Add focused commit, dirty-result, divergence, and recovery tests plus an end-to-end live proof.

## Cleanup

The proof left no AWS lease, session/worktree, proof branch/ref, tmux session, scratch state, or listening test port. The production Gateway was not restarted or modified.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug
**Beta release blocker:** No

### Summary

When `gateway.auth.mode = "password"` and a shared `gateway.auth.token` is also configured, the shipped macOS app's local (same-host) dashboard connection always authenticates with the shared token; the gateway rejects it with `password mismatch` and the app never presents (or retries with) the configured password, so the dashboard stays unavailable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a local gateway with `gateway.mode = "local"`, `gateway.auth.mode = "password"`, and **both** `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.auth.password` set in `openclaw.json`.
2. Start the gateway, then launch the shipped macOS app (unentitled build, default profile) on the same host.
3. The app targets the local gateway endpoint; the dashboard shows: `Dashboard unavailable — unauthorized: gateway password mismatch (provide gateway auth password). Open Connection or use Debug → Reset Remote Tunnel, then try again.`
4. The gateway log shows repeated ws auth attempts with `auth=token` rejected as `password_mismatch`, with backoff, and no password attempt ever appears.
5. Workaround (verified): remove the shared token — `openclaw config patch --stdin` with `{"gateway":{"auth":{"token":null}}}` — restart the gateway and relaunch the app; the app then presents the password and connects.

### Expected behavior

With `auth.mode=password` and a password configured, the app should authenticate the local connection with the configured password — either by preferring it when the gateway declares password auth, or by falling back to it after a token rejection. The password is already resolved client-side (see evidence below); it is simply never selected while a token exists.

### Actual behavior

The app always sends `auth: {token: ***}` for the local connection; the gateway (password mode) rejects every attempt with `unauthorized: gateway password mismatch (provide gateway auth password)`; no retry with the password occurs; the dashboard remains unavailable. The app's connection UI offers no local-gateway credential entry to work around this in-app (the guided flows that carry credentials are the direct/remote ones).

### Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.9.7 (npm global gateway + mac app 2026.9.7, both)
- **Operating system:** macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- **Install method:** npm global (gateway) + shipped mac app (client), same host
- **Model:** n/a — failure occurs in the ws auth handshake, before any model request
- **Provider / routing chain:** mac app → ws://127.0.0.1:18789 → local gateway (auth.mode=password)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Redacted auth shape in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
"gateway": {
  "mode": "local",
  "auth": { "mode": "password", "token": "***", "password": "***" }
}
```

No env overrides (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`/`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD`) were set for the app; the launchd snapshot's service-env contains no gateway token key either, so both credentials in play come from the shared config.

### Logs

```shell
# Repeated with backoff; every attempt presents the token; no password attempt observed
[ws] unauthorized conn=<uuid> peer=127.0.0.1:<port>->127.0.0.1:18789 client=<mac-app> ui v2026.9.7 \
    role=operator scopes=6 auth=token device=yes reason=password_mismatch \
    guidance=unauthorized: gateway password mismatch (provide gateway auth password)
[ws] closed before connect conn=<uuid> ... code=1008 \
    reason=unauthorized: gateway password mismatch (provide gateway auth password) \
    phase=auth_credentials_received cause=unauthorized

# After removing gateway.auth.token and relaunching: no further unauthorized events;
# dashboard queries (health / sessions.preview / usage.cost) succeed on the native connection.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source analysis at commit `32e30e59d9a` (main, synced with origin/main):

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/GatewayChannel.swift`, `selectConnectAuth` (~L669-676): `authToken = explicitToken ?? …` — the explicit/shared token takes precedence over the password; the password is only selected when no token is available at all.
- Same file, `applyConnectAuth` (~L612): when `authToken` is non-nil the connect params carry `auth: {token}`; there is no fallback to `auth: {password}` after a password-mode rejection.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/GatewayEndpointStore.swift`, `resolveGatewayCredential` (~L130-180): in local mode both `gateway.auth.token` and `gateway.auth.password` are resolved from the shared config, so the client holds both credentials and the token always wins.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager+Construction.swift` (~L93): the dashboard connection's `authTokenProvider` defaults to the token.
- Possibly related: #163433 "refactor(apps): retire pre-July Apple auth retries" removed earlier auth-retry machinery; observed behavior shows no credential retry on rejection.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** macOS app users whose gateway runs `auth.mode=password` while a shared token is also configured
- **Severity:** blocks the mac app dashboard entirely (gateway, CLI, and browser Control UI keep working)
- **Frequency:** always, in this configuration
- **Consequence:** app unusable until the config workaround (removing the shared token) is applied

### Additional information

Verified workaround: `openclaw config patch --stdin` with `{"gateway":{"auth":{"token":null}}}` (validated by `--dry-run` first), restart the gateway, relaunch the app.

Two suggestions for consideration: (a) let the client honor the gateway's declared auth mode when choosing between configured credentials, and/or (b) retry once with the password when a token is rejected with `password_mismatch`.
