issues.body:
## Summary

In an authenticated Control UI owner conversation on OpenClaw 2026.9.8, the parent can list/get existing automations with gateway-wide scope. After delegating implementation/review, yielding, and resuming on a native subagent-completion event, the **parent** still receives the child results and can continue local work, but its native automation tool falls back to caller scope. An existing cross-session automation becomes “not found.” A fresh explicit owner message in the same conversation restores access immediately, allowing the already-authorized update.

This report is about **management authority in the resumed parent**, not granting automation tools to children or recovering a missing child result. Please clarify whether this is intentional turn-scoped policy or a missing task-bound continuation handoff. Either way, the current behavior prevents completion of an explicitly authorized delegated automation-edit task without an extra owner message.

## Environment / important caveat

- OpenClaw CLI and serving Gateway: **2026.9.8**, build **fc23bc8**.
- Node **v24.19.0**; Linux **6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2**, user systemd service.
- Surface: authenticated owner in **Control UI webchat**, native hidden subagents, tool search / Code Mode.
- This is **not a pristine installation**. A locally reviewed three-module fix for a separate fresh-input/reconnect admission problem was installed October 8, plus a Playwright discarded-tab backport. On October 10, read-only verification still matched all three patched runtime modules and six preserved identities. Serving Gateway was active/reachable; current process started October 9, before the October 10 incident.
- No configuration, role, job ownership, permission changes or Gateway restart were used to restore access during this incident. The successful workaround was a fresh human message.
- Not yet reproduced on current main, on an unpatched clean install, or with #168068 installed. Please do not treat this as proof that #168068 regressed.

## Observed sequence (October 10, 2026; America/New_York, UTC−04)

1. The owner requested an audit, then explicitly authorized all proposed fixes and a job conversion at approximately **21:12**. In owner turns, native automation inventory was **scope=gateway, total=85**. Native get succeeded for the relevant existing jobs; their full definitions were saved.
2. The parent delegated code implementation and independent review to native subagents and yielded. Children returned their results successfully. The parent resumed from native completion/settle events and completed local deployment.
3. Around **21:28**, before attempting the remaining native message-only edits, the resumed parent called native get for one of those same job IDs. It failed. A subsequent native list returned **scope=caller, total=10**, excluding all jobs in this workflow. The tool remained discoverable in this incident. No update was attempted after the refusal.
4. The owner sent **“Finish activation” at 21:32** in the same conversation. Native get succeeded again. Both authorized message-only edits succeeded and were independently read back. Full before/after comparison showed only **payload.message, updatedAtMs, configRevision** changed; schedule, enabled state, next run, owner, tools and delivery were preserved.
5. A further read-only check later that evening again returned **gateway / 85**, and get of the same existing job succeeded.

The degradation was observed **between turns of one conversation**, not proven to occur within one uninterrupted model/tool run. Child delivery continued to work. We have not instrumented the precise original-source/grant lifetime transition for this occurrence, or established whether an intervening continuation invalidated a captured grant.

## Sanitized native evidence

Owner turn:


```text
automations({action:"list", includeDisabled:true, limit:200})
returned metadata: {"scope":"gateway","total":85,"hasMore":false}
```

Completion continuation:


```text
automations({action:"get", jobId:"<existing-job-id>"})
```

> cron job not found: <existing-job-id>. List automations and retry with a current job id. For cross-session management, use a fresh authenticated configured channel owner or Control UI administrator turn or the Automations page.

Independent inventory in that continuation:


```text
automations({action:"list", includeDisabled:true, limit:200})
returned metadata: {"scope":"caller","total":10}
```

Fresh owner turn: get/update/get succeeded for the same IDs. These were restricted-visibility “not found” responses, **not deleted jobs**. No CLI/store fallback, migration, recreation, grant injection or permission widening was attempted.

## Candidate reproduction (derived from the observed workflow)

This is a reproduction recipe for maintainers, not a claimed deterministic minimal reproducer:

1. Authenticate as a Control UI owner/admin. Have a non-critical existing automation that is visible through gateway-wide authority but not the narrow caller inventory.
2. In a fresh explicit human turn, call native list/get and retain returned scope. Ask the parent to make a specific permitted edit **after** a delegated review.
3. Spawn a native hidden child with an isolated context, wait using the supported yield/completion path, and let the parent resume automatically on completion. Do not replace that continuation with a new human message.
4. In the resumed parent, inspect tool availability, native list scope, and get of the same saved job ID before any edit.
5. If it downgrades, send a new explicit owner message in the same chat, then repeat read-only list/get. Compare the effective capability/source binding—not just session keys or owner labels.
6. Test variants with and without an intervening same-owner follow-up, because upstream authority lifetime work distinguishes them. Our report does not claim that distinction is already isolated.

Use a disposable fixture for mutation testing; list/get is enough to detect our observed loss.

## Expected behavior / policy question

For a still-valid original owner request authorizing this exact task, the resumed parent should either retain a narrowly task-bound management capability through the supported completion path, or clearly expose that management cannot continue and requires fresh human admission. It should not appear that the target disappeared.

**Not requesting** blanket admin on synthetic messages, indefinite session authority, borrowing a newer/stronger ambient caller, or bypassing revocation/replay guards. Reset/cancel/revoked-source/foreign-requester protections must remain intact.

## Previous troubleshooting context (separate mechanisms)

### October 4: confirmed fresh-message/reconnect admission defect

Instrumented normal-Send failure and success on the **same connection** showed:

- Failure: adminScope=true, controlUiAdmin=true, directExternal=true, mainTurn=true; reconnectResume=true → disallowed=true, admitted=false → missing entitlement → caller inventory 10.
- Comparator: reconnectResume=false → admitted=true and successful management binding.
- The UI applied `__controlUiReconnectResume:true` to fresh typed input, while backend admission treated reconnect resume as an exclusion. That explains the captured October 4 case; it does **not** prove tonight’s completion path shares the same cause.
- Temporary diagnostic instrumentation was removed. A local scoped fix distinguishing committed fresh-input custody from genuine replay was installed October 8; actual browser reconnect/first-send soak remains incompletely verified. Tonight’s patch-identity check shows it was not overwritten on disk.

### October 10, earlier: tool-catalog omission on another completion

Retained notes and bounded sanitized history review recorded a completion turn with a smaller tool catalog and no callable automations tool; a fresh owner turn restored native access. Tonight’s main incident differs: **automations existed but returned caller-scoped results**. We are reporting these as distinct symptoms, not claiming one proven cause. Full raw transcripts/configs are intentionally not attached.

## Related upstream work

- [#157404 — Owner turns after subagent work cannot edit automations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157404), merged September 24. Related workflow; its report says list/get worked and update failed. Our failure includes **list/get scope reduction**, so this may be another boundary.
- [#162761 — Same-owner followups revoke native subagent completion authority](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162761), closed by [#168068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168068).
- **#168068**, merged October 10 at **02:34:22 UTC**, commit **75510a24baad97e527a9ae14f5d9c721438b9f50**, repairs child-result delivery after a follow-up. Its description explicitly says valid completion delivery is preserved **without restoring old automation management**. Our results arrive; resumed-parent management is what is lost. Is this the intended remaining restriction, or should a task-bound management continuation exist separately?
- [#167047](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167047) is an earlier owner-only proposal for dropped results; not an installed fix here.

## Useful next diagnostic / regression target

Trace the parent’s actual originating human admission, yield/completion custody, current original-source validity, and native automation-management binding at: (a) authorized owner turn, (b) automatic resumed parent, (c) fresh owner workaround. Include the grant rejection reason and tool-policy derivation while excluding bearer tokens, credentials and user payloads.

A regression should reach the resumed parent’s **actual native list/get or disposable update/readback**, not only prove that the child result was delivered. Pair a valid-original-source case with revoked/reset/cancelled/foreign-source negatives. If the restriction is deliberate, a documented actionable “fresh human authority required” result would be clearer than job-not-found.

## Attachments / privacy

A small sanitized evidence JSON is included below. It omits job names/IDs, session IDs, phone numbers, channel recipients, prompts, config contents, tokens and private task data. Raw local snapshots are retained privately for a targeted follow-up, not suitable for wholesale public upload.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized evidence summary</summary>

```json
{
  "environment": {
    "version": "2026.9.8",
    "build": "fc23bc8",
    "node": "v24.19.0",
    "os": "Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2",
    "surface": "Control UI webchat",
    "localPatches": [
      "fresh-input/reconnect admission patch (3 runtime modules)",
      "Playwright discarded-tab backport"
    ],
    "patchVerification": "3 runtime modules and 6 preserved identities match on October10 follow-up"
  },
  "incident": {
    "ownerTurn": {
      "scope": "gateway",
      "total": 85
    },
    "completionContinuation": {
      "toolPresent": true,
      "scope": "caller",
      "total": 10,
      "targetJobVisible": false,
      "getError": "cron job not found: <existing-job-id>. List automations and retry with a current job id. For cross-session management, use a fresh authenticated configured channel owner or Control UI administrator turn or the Automations page.",
      "mutationAttempted": false
    },
    "freshOwnerTurn": {
      "message": "Finish activation",
      "getSucceeded": true,
      "updatesVerified": true,
      "changedFields": [
        "payload.message",
        "updatedAtMs",
        "configRevision"
      ]
    }
  },
  "currentReadOnlyCheck": {
    "scope": "gateway",
    "total": 85,
    "hasMore": false,
    "targetJobGetSucceeded": true
  },
  "limitations": [
    "No deterministic clean-install reproduction yet",
    "No claim of reproduction on current main or after #168068",
    "Continuation capability binding not instrumented",
    "Earlier catalog-omission symptom may have a different cause",
    "Historical session recall was bounded/truncated; retained native snapshots supplement it"
  ]
}
```

</details>

issues.body:
## Summary

Memory Wiki's compile rewrites every vault page whose managed blocks changed — Related-block refresh for regular pages, Generated-block refresh for index and dashboard pages — and `memory-wiki lint` rewrites the lint report the same way. Each rewrite reads the existing page with replacement-mode UTF-8 decoding and writes the whole file back, so a single undecodable byte in a page's human notes (a Latin-1 paste, a truncated export) is persisted as U+FFFD on every compile, and the compile reports success.

The rewrite sites (`refreshPageRelatedBlocks`, `writeManagedMarkdownFile`, `refreshDashboardPages` in `compile.ts`, plus `writeLintReport` in `lint.ts`) all decode existing pages through lossy UTF-8 reads, so the failure is reachable from every entry point that compiles or lints a vault.

## Reproduction

```text
$ printf -- '- a Latin-1 paste: caf\xe9\n' > <vault>/entities/router.md
$ openclaw wiki compile
  → reports the vault as compiled
  → entities/router.md now contains ef bf bd where the source had e9
$ openclaw wiki lint
  → rewrites the lint report the same way
```

Regression evidence from #168583: with the production files restored to the pre-fix revision and only the new tests kept, the added regressions fail — `compile` refuses to rewrite a page that is not valid UTF-8, `lint` refuses to rewrite a malformed lint report, and the CLI surfaces the refusal (5 failing tests across `compile.test.ts`, `lint.test.ts`, `cli-utf8.test.ts`). That is the defect being reported here: those refusals do not exist on `main`.

## Expected

The rewrite is refused before any write, names the affected page, states the recovery action (keep a byte-for-byte copy, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, retry), and leaves the page byte-for-byte unchanged. Read-only wiki surfaces (search, context digest, frontmatter discovery) keep their existing decode contract.

## Actual

Silent, permanent loss of the undecodable bytes in a page's human notes on every compile, reported as a successful compile.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (main)
- Linux, Node v24.18.0

issues.body:
### Summary
Under `tools.exec.mode = "auto"`, when the native exec **auto-reviewer returns a `deny` verdict, the command is sometimes executed anyway** (fail-open). Per docs (`docs/tools/exec.md`: "Auto-review approval is single-use … `deny` returns a reason to the agent, which must choose a materially safer alternative"), a denied command should not run.

### Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.9.6**
- Linux/WSL2, single-user local gateway; `tools.exec.host=gateway`, `tools.exec.mode=auto`, `strictInlineEval=true`
- Commands were issued as **nested shell calls inside the code-mode `exec` tool**

### Observed — denied but executed (2 runs)
1. **2026-10-04**: `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/feishu@2026.9.6 --force` → review recorded `status:"denied"` (risk high); the command **did execute** (spawned a real `npm install`).
2. **2026-10-05**: `gh issue comment <id> --repo openclaw/openclaw --body-file <path>` → tool result `status:"completed", exitCode:0`, plus `approvalReviews:[{status:"denied", riskLevel:"high"}] / approvalReviewOutcome:"denied"`; the comment was **actually published** (returned its URL).

### Counter-example — same mode, denied and correctly blocked
- **2026-10-05**: `grep -c apiKey ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` → `Exec denied by auto-review (risk=high)`, tool returned `code=null`, **not executed**.

### Why this looks like a bug
Identical `mode=auto` configuration yields **both** "deny blocks" and "deny still executes" → non-deterministic fail-open. Most likely a race/ordering issue: for **code-mode nested tool calls**, the review verdict appears to be attached **after** the nested command has already been dispatched, so `deny` is recorded but never enforced.

### Impact
Security-relevant. Anyone relying on the auto-reviewer's `deny` as a stop gets **false assurance** that a high-risk / external-publish command was blocked. For irreversible actions (public posts, publish, deletes) this defeats the guardrail.

### Expected
When the auto-reviewer returns `deny`, the command **must not execute** — return a blocked result with the reason (fail-closed). At minimum, the code-mode nested path should gate dispatch on `approvalReviewOutcome`.

### Suggested checks
- Does a nested tool call inside a code-mode `exec` respect the reviewer verdict **before** dispatch?
- End-to-end test: denied verdict ⇒ `exitCode != 0` and **no side effect**.
- If some path is intentionally post-hoc/advisory, rename the verdict (e.g. `flagged`) and surface "**flagged but executed**" explicitly, plus log a policy-bypass event.

_(No secrets, keys, or hostnames included.)_

## Summary

Short-term promotion ("dreaming") and `memory forget` rebuild the target file — `MEMORY.md`, or the `memory/*.md` file the candidate came from — from text decoded with replacement-mode UTF-8, then write the whole file back through the memory commit owner. One undecodable byte anywhere in the file (a Latin-1 note, a truncated paste) is persisted as U+FFFD over content the write never touched, and the promotion reports success.

The promotion/forget planning reads are lossy on purpose — they only feed ranking and LLM context. The corruption happens because the file owner that performs the rewrite never checks that the bytes on disk decode cleanly before replacing them. That owner is shared with the remote maintenance worker, so local promotion, explicit forget, and remote memory operations all reach the same defect.

## Reproduction

Isolated state, one seeded short-term recall for the workspace, and a `MEMORY.md` carrying a single undecodable byte in a note line the promotion never touches:

```text
$ printf '# Long-Term Memory\n\n- note: a\xffb\n' > <workspace>/MEMORY.md
$ openclaw memory promote --apply
  → reports the promotion as applied (exit 0)
  → MEMORY.md now contains ef bf bd where the source had ff
```

Captured on the pre-fix build while preparing #168574: exit `0`, file bytes `61 ff 62` → `61 ef bf bd 62`, sha256 `0cc22e72…` → `20aeff75…`. The same run against the fixed build exits `1` with the refusal message and leaves the sha256 unchanged.

## Expected

The rewrite is refused before any write, names the affected file, states the recovery action (keep a byte-for-byte copy, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, retry), leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged, and leaves the candidate unpromoted.

## Actual

Silent, permanent loss of bytes in note lines the rewrite never intended to touch, reported as a successful promotion.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (main)
- Linux, Node v24.18.0

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since #121103 (fixes #121046, released in 2026.9.x), every `memory/**/YYYY-MM-DD[-suffix].md` file gets the fixed 30-day recency decay. The decay multiplies the relevance score **before** the `minScore` cut (`query.minScore`, 0.35 in our config). A dated file older than about 45 days can then only come back if its raw relevance is near 1.0, so it doesn't just rank lower; it disappears from `memory_search` altogether, even when it is the only relevant document. The docs describe decay as a ranking signal ("Old notes gradually lose ranking weight so recent information surfaces first", `docs/concepts/memory-search.md`). What actually happens is that results are removed, and there is no opt-out: `hybrid.temporalDecay` is hardcoded (`enabled: true`, `halfLifeDays: 30`) in the memory-search config resolver, and `memory.search` user config only reaches `maxResults` and `minScore`.

This hits a common workspace layout hard. Durable records are named by date in subdirectories: verification reports, decision records, incident write-ups, e.g. `memory/hq/verification/2026-06-08-<slug>.md` or `memory/decisions/2026-05-02-<slug>.md`. Before 2026.9.x only root-level `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` decayed (`DATED_MEMORY_PATH_RE = /(?:^|\/)memory\/(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})\.md$/`), so those records stayed evergreen. After the update they aged out of search. The intent of #121046/#121103, decaying dreaming reports and session snapshots, is reasonable. The problem is the combination of (a) scope, where every dated file is treated as perishable, (b) decay applied before the eligibility threshold, and (c) no config escape hatch.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Default `memory.search` config (hybrid on, `query.minScore: 0.35`), OpenClaw 2026.9.5.
2. Put a durable record at a dated nested path whose date is more than about 60 days old, e.g. `memory/records/2026-06-08-db-failover-runbook.md`, with distinctive content, and let it index.
3. `openclaw memory search "<distinctive phrase from that file>" --json --agent main`.
4. Per the code path below, the file should be missing from the results. Renaming it to `memory/records/db-failover-runbook.md` (undated, so evergreen) and reindexing should bring it back.

The date comes from the **filename**, not the mtime, so a file created today with an old date in its name should reproduce this immediately. These steps follow from the code; what we observed live is the example under Actual behavior.

### Expected behavior

One of:

- Decay lowers an old dated file's rank relative to newer matches, as documented, but doesn't make a relevant file ineligible. Ideally `minScore` would be evaluated on the undecayed relevance and decay would only reorder.
- Or the scope and strength are configurable: honour `memory.search.query.hybrid.temporalDecay.{enabled,halfLifeDays}` from config, and ideally allow evergreen/decay path globs, e.g. `evergreenPaths: ["memory/hq/**", "memory/decisions/**"]`.

### Actual behavior

- **Multiplier at 30-day half-life:**
  - at 45 days: ×0.354; a result then needs raw ≥ 0.99 to clear 0.35;
  - at 108 days: ×0.0825, verified with the bundle's own `extractTimestamp`/`applyTemporalDecayToScore`.
- **Order of operations:** in `dist/extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js`, `applyTemporalDecayToHybridResults` / `mergeHybridResults` run first, then `.filter((entry) => entry.score >= minScore)` / `selectHybridSearchResults`.
  - The relaxed keyword pass only rescues entries with `vectorScore === 0`, so it rarely applies.
- **Live example:** a 108-day-old verification report that exactly matches the query scores 0.677 undecayed but 0.056 decayed. It is absent from the top 8. With the 2026.7.x regex restored, it is rank 1.
- **Golden-set eval on the same index:** 36 queries, about 25k chunks, stock 2026.9.5 vs 2026.9.5 with only the 7.x `DATED_MEMORY_PATH_RE` literal restored:
  - canonical recall@5: 0.257 → 0.714;
  - exact-term recall@5: 0.083 → 0.917;
  - entity: 0.33 → 0.83;
  - temporal: 0.40 → 0.80;
  - MRR: 0.164 → 0.530.
  - Recall dropped sharply when the fleet updated to 2026.9.x.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (behavior introduced by #121103; 2026.7.1-2 used the root-only regex)

### Operating system

macOS 26.5.1

### Install method

npm global (nvm, Node 26.4.0)

### Model

n/a (memory_search retrieval; embeddings: embeddinggemma via an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint)

### Provider / routing chain

memory-core builtin engine, hybrid (vector + FTS), local embedding endpoint

### Additional provider/model setup details

`memory.search`: `sources: ["memory"]`, `sessionMemory: false`; no `query.hybrid` overrides (the resolver ignores them).

### Logs

_No response_

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See the numbers above. We are running a local one-line patch that restores the 7.x literal in `dist/extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js`. It is re-applied after each update and fails closed if the bundle shape changes. We'd like to retire it.

### Impact and severity

High for agents whose durable knowledge is date-named. Retrieval of records older than about 6 weeks fails silently: no error, the search just returns nothing relevant, so agents answer from worse sources. It looks like a corpus or embedding problem, and took us about two weeks to trace to the runtime update.

### Additional information

Suggested fixes, least invasive first:

1. Evaluate `minScore` on undecayed relevance and use decay only for ordering, which matches the docs.
2. Honour `query.hybrid.temporalDecay.enabled` / `halfLifeDays` from `memory.search` config instead of hardcoding them in the resolver.
3. Add an evergreen/decay path-glob setting, or a frontmatter opt-out such as `evergreen: true`, so durable dated records can opt out while dreaming reports and session snapshots keep decaying as #121046 intended.

Related: #121046, #121103, #124869, #129884.

prs.title: refactor: migrate sidebar rendering to Solid 2
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Migrates the Control UI sidebar family from Lit to Solid 2 while preserving the shell's single live sidebar and its desktop/drawer placement.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Tags, routes, CSS classes, selectors, personal pins, navigation scopes, catalog sessions, attention surfaces, and keyboard controls remain stable. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical Solid bridge owns every ported tag and the corresponding Lit classes are deleted. Existing synchronous controllers retain session and navigation authority; Solid renders their publications. The port incorporates main's personal-navigation and compact-rail changes. Unported picker, avatar, tooltip, theme artwork, and plugin elements keep their existing owners.

The only coupled changes outside the sidebar family are concrete custom-element JSX types, type-only exports for those elements, and plugin fallback mounting/cleanup needed at the Solid boundary. No dependencies or session-library owners change.

Simplification removed duplicate theme artwork rendering, three single-consumer helper modules, and unused Lit approval/server-detail renderers. Affected production TypeScript is **18,054 lines before → 21,736 after (+3,682)**, counting added/deleted paths once and excluding tests/test helpers. Residual growth comes from explicit Solid bindings and controller lifecycle adaptation, plus Solid equivalents of stateless Lit helpers still used by unported callers. This does not meet the net-neutral target; it keeps one registered implementation per migrated tag.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar-update-card.test.tsx` | 20 passed, including retained action/details focus through progress updates |
| `exec-approval-card.test.ts` | 18 passed |
| `app-sidebar-nav-menus.test.tsx` | 3 passed; 64.05s wrapper / 12.04s Vitest |
| `app-sidebar-session-row-render.test.tsx` | 4 passed; stale pinned-avatar regression demonstrated fail-before/pass-after; 42.07s wrapper / 17.97s Vitest, regression 12ms |
| `sidebar-attention.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| Plugin fallback/cleanup | 15 passed; stale-cleanup regression demonstrated fail-before/pass-after |
| Avatar, badge, subtitle, marquee, attention derivation, contextual state | Focused checks passed during the port |
| Root sidebar local test | Worker exits before assertions on the ported head; the same file passes on merge base 53b8118 (1/1, 92.84s). Under investigation; no inherited-failure claim |
| Focused Solid lint | No errors; advisory warnings audited for reactive getter boundaries; pinned-avatar finding corrected |
| Ordinary type-aware lint wrapper | Prerequisite plugin-SDK declaration preparation timed out after 300 seconds; hosted proof pending |
| Testbox | One attempt exhausted the admission window in source-capsule preparation; no lease allocated |
| Types, build, UI unit/E2E | PR CI pending |
| Before/after visual evidence | Eight synthetic sidebar scenes × desktop/mobile × light/dark capture in progress; required before merge |
| Independent review | Full integrated review and correction reviews completed; final event/avatar delta clean at P0–P2 |

Remaining focused wall times were not retained during the initial port; CI seconds will be recorded with final evidence. No local whole suite, `tsgo`, Docker, or full E2E run.

prs.title: fix(state): bound startup deletion-journal reads below state-read pool admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #168585. The readiness phase of background agent-database preparation releases every deferred agent from the shared `activation.preparationReady` gate at the same moment. Each of them immediately runs its deletion-journal check through the shared state-read worker pool, so a large fleet (the reporter saw 773 configured agents) submits all of those reads at once. The pool admits at most `DEFAULT_WORKER_PENDING_TASKS` (128) pending tasks; the excess are rejected with `WorkerTaskError("worker task capacity reached", "overloaded")`, and the preparation catch treats that transient overload like a database failure: `failPendingAgentDatabase` records a permanent degraded refusal whose repair hint sends the operator to `doctor --fix` on a state Doctor had just certified. On the reporter's fleet, 645 of 773 agents came up degraded in the same millisecond, none recovered within 15 minutes, and a restart hit the same cap.

## The Fix

Bound the fan-out at its producer, inside the startup owner: `AgentDatabaseStartupAdmission` gains a `journalReads` permit pool (`AGENT_DATABASE_STARTUP_JOURNAL_CONCURRENCY = 8`, alongside the existing preflight/preparation concurrency constants) and `assertNotDeleted` admits its `readAgentDeletionJournalStatusInWorker` call through it. With at most 8 journal reads in flight, the pool's pending set stays far below its 128-task admission on any fleet size, the bounded reads drain in seconds, and capacity rejections from this path cannot happen. Open/migration/publication work was already serialized through the existing permit pools; the journal read was the one unbounded stage.

No global limits are raised, no deletion checks are skipped, and genuine deletion-journal hits still fail the agent with the same error as before. A capacity rejection originating elsewhere in the pool still surfaces through the existing catch unchanged.

## Evidence

Regression test (offline, no network, no workers): `src/state/agent-database-startup.journal-bound.test.ts` drives the real `AgentDatabaseStartupAdmission` through `defer()` with 64 deferred healthy agents (mocked journal read holding each read across a macrotask, mocked preparation/failure recording, real permit pools), activates them, and asserts:

- all 64 agents prepare exactly once, with both journal checks (2×64 calls), and none is failed as degraded;
- the observed maximum concurrent journal reads stays ≤ 8 (`EXPECTED_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOURNAL_READS`, mirroring `AGENT_DATABASE_STARTUP_JOURNAL_CONCURRENCY`).

Pre-fix red (fix reverted, tests only): `expected 64 to be less than or equal to 8` — all 64 deferred agents' journal reads were in flight simultaneously, the unbounded fan-out from the issue (64 here stands in for the reporter's 773; past 128 the real pool rejects and `failPendingAgentDatabase` fires, which the same test also pins via `admissionState.failed`). Post-fix: the bound holds and the test passes.

Neighbors unchanged on the same tree: `agent-database-admission.test.ts`, `agent-deletion-journal.startup.test.ts`, `openclaw-database-preflight.startup-prepared.test.ts`, `dreaming-startup-admission.test.ts`, `server-agent-database-startup.test.ts` all green.

### Fixture repairs from review (head b657dad8a71)

- The journal-reader mock now carries a `// mock-isolation:` declaration for the first-party mock export guard: it intentionally replaces the journal-read transport (instead of spreading it) so the fixture can observe admission concurrency without spawning real state-read workers.
- The manufactured overlap no longer uses real timers. Each admitted read awaits a deferred gate; the gate opens permanently the first time in-flight reads saturate the 8-read bound, so overlap is deterministic and the fixture pays no wall-clock scheduling delay. The overlap assertion was tightened accordingly: the observed maximum concurrent journal reads now equals 8 exactly (the bound is demonstrably reached, not merely not exceeded).
- The test-owned state directory is created through the shared `useAutoCleanupTempDirTracker`, so the journal-bound directory and SQLite placeholder are removed on both passing and failing runs.

Verified on the updated fixture: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/state/agent-database-startup.journal-bound.test.ts` — 1 passed; `oxlint` clean on the file. The real-Gateway recovery proof (a fleet above the 128-pending admission recovering without capacity refusals) remains the outstanding before-merge item and needs an isolated Gateway run with real state-read workers.

prs.title: refactor(infra): simplify database and worker coordination
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's infrastructure carries multiple generations of coordination for synthetic interleavings that ordinary deployments do not perform. This maintainer-requested simplification removes that machinery while retaining the actual storage, security, and shutdown owners.

## User Impact

Normal features, config, CLI and Gateway shapes, plugin SDK exports, stored schemas, snapshot bytes, and authorization remain unchanged. Rare internal reload/reentry/failure timing is deliberately best effort, as listed below. No new dependency or migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sharpened provenance audit re-evaluated all thirteen prior KEEP rows: twelve became partial/full removals; the caller-versus-recovery delivery ownership decision remains for ordinary retry durability. A PR's synthetic reproduction is not treated as a human incident.

The largest cuts are snapshot staging/cancellation custody, native worker shutdown/recovery graphs, SQLite writer registration and duplicate schema-scope bookkeeping, and outbound registry/preparation fencing. Existing owners now supply the straightforward path: one settled snapshot cleanup, one ordinary worker shutdown, committed cache revisions, one effect check, and idempotent row cleanup.

Real user reports remain protected: [#103910](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103910) describes a usage refresh stuck for roughly 22 hours, so exact-token cleanup after lost replies remains; [#159897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159897) describes a dead Windows update lease blocking upgrades for two days, so stale-owner repair and process-effect authority remain. Snapshot reclamation stays for bounded-resource and crash-cleanup reasons; #149978 is an instrumented pilot, not human-incident authority.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- **Nested cold admission graph and parent borrowers:** #167739 describes test-only nested brokers. Nested calls share the active outer turn; detached nested work or extra files can repeat first-admission work instead of expanding a dependency graph.
- **SQLite per-writer registration/ancestor census:** #167739/#167965 supply synthetic overlap scenarios, not human incidents. Caches use committed revisions without identifying every active writer. Reads during an unsettled sibling write may retain their last committed facts until publication; effect authorization remains independent.
- **Unused native ancestry bootstrap:** #167739's ancestry metadata only served the removed writer census. No value or raw environment-key reader remains, so its state, side-effect imports, file, and wrapper inventory entry are removed together.
- **Duplicate schema-scope registry/borrowers:** physical admission already owns the shared revision. The separate identity map/finalizer/counter is removed; unmanaged exotic aliases rely on the existing admission/native path.
- **Native reset error classification and nested-error stack:** #168029's synthetic callback cases do not require a second error provenance machine. A failed reset leaves the old cursor conservatively pending until reuse/close; original native errors and the delivery execution guard remain.
- **Schema first-step revalidation:** a sibling DDL placed exactly between snapshot preparation and its first native step is synthetic. Such an operation can use its earlier schema facts; ordinary snapshots/commit publication remain correct.
- **Input preparation generations:** the broker's closing state and joined preparations already own shutdown. Late internal reuse no longer carries a second epoch token.
- **Snapshot late-allocation and retryable cleanup custody:** forced supervisor loss or cancellation at each allocation boundary is synthetic. Accepted work settles through one cleanup owner; failed exceptional cleanup can remain for normal maintenance/manual recovery.
- **Snapshot cleanup tombstones/duplicate token registries:** allocator-generated directories are unique. Artificial directory recreation or repeated failed close does not get a separate recovery protocol; active-reader checks and normal cleanup remain.
- **Parent-token handoff around mkdir:** #155437 deliberately SIGSTOPs/SIGKILLs the mkdir/token gap and reports unknown production frequency. A kill in that gap can leave a tokenless child blocking automatic cleanup of its temporary parent tree until manual cleanup. This never removes canonical data.
- **Native per-owner shutdown graph and automatic broker retry history:** #160946/#162128 describe harness controls, not human incidents. One memoized shutdown joins accepted owners; an exceptional supervisor/resource failure is reported and may need restart rather than implicit rotation/retry.
- **Reentrant native terminal queue:** #165249 measured direct transport wins, which stay. A callback recursively servicing the same terminal notification no longer has an independent queue/pointer fence; ordinary message ordering stays direct.
- **Runtime closing/rebind fences:** normal update work already retains its source until settlement. Fire-and-forget registration after shutdown starts is best effort instead of growing another generation protocol.
- **Managed-update self-PID rechecks and synchronous receipt nonce:** a running process cannot acquire a new birth identity, and synchronous completion does not need millisecond equality. Cached self identity and a completed ledger step replace those checks; foreign process authority and final write identity remain.
- **Usage cache all-binding identity census and cleanup custody:** #152543's mid-report file replacement scenarios are synthetic. A changed cache file can fail or stale one report. One idempotent exact-token cleanup remains for the actual #103910 failure; failed cleanup is visible rather than automatically retried.
- **Retained rollback-reader revalidation:** external byte/header/journal replacement while an admitted reader stays open is not normal coordinated access. Validation occurs at initial open, not every observation; reopen/next run re-admits the file. Initial corrupt/WAL refusal, journal recovery and the final write identity check remain.
- **File-lock callback-disappearance retry:** #167051's exact callback-time sidecar race is synthetic. The canonical fs-safe acquisition retains its bounded wait and stale-owner handling; the rare disappearance can fail once.
- **State-owner one-second freshness fence:** #160139 measured the cache's syscall savings. The cache stays, but artificial file replacement during an owner lifetime no longer triggers continuous identity probing; real ownership/write boundaries remain.
- **First-start lock-parent recreation:** #110392's concurrent-creator test is synthetic; its linked human report #107227 concerns different legacy migration conflicts. Separate processes racing to create the first identity may receive a clear missing-lock-directory error instead of both succeeding. The canonical identity and ordinary exclusive-write/cryptographic checks remain intact; the next invocation reads the winner.
- **Dispatcher same-origin retirement fence:** each acquisition still has fresh DNS/policy in its key. Older keys can remain until ordinary TTL/LRU cleanup, but are not reused for different pins; active streams remain referenced.
- **Duplicate outbound bootstrap cache and registry rechecks:** #153105's loader matrix is synthetic. The plugin loader is the cache owner; reload during a preparation may fail or use its captured context, then recover on a fresh operation.
- **Binding-list and completed-read fences:** read-only enumeration may be a mixed view during plugin reload instead of being discarded. Actual binding changes and sends retain their effect checks.
- **Preparation renewal chains and clock-expiry timer:** a hook stalled beyond its five-minute claim can lose ownership at the next checkpoint. Active send renewal still exists; a real renewal error aborts rather than entering a transient retry protocol. #167467 was a frozen-clock CI overflow case.
- **Eager cancellation retirement/late cleanup handoff:** #138831's actual user issue concerned missing Telegram questions, not held-adapter cancellation. An uncooperative preparation keeps its unsent row until it settles; if its process restarts first, that row can recover once despite the earlier process-local cancellation. Abort is still checked before any send.
- **Identical nested proxy ownership/stale-handle probes:** #74905 added generic nested ownership beside the independent APNs fix. The real bootstrap stops before replacing its single proxy. Duplicate startup fails clearly; ordinary stop restores that handle's environment.

## Evidence

Current full diff: **2,210 net production lines removed** (+725/-2,935), excluding tests/support/generated declarations. All thirteen original KEEP rows were re-evaluated; twelve were narrowed or reversed after more than two hours of implementation.

The first native/schema run passed 101 cases across its project invocations and exposed four assertions of the removed in-flight visibility guarantee. Those now assert visibility after native settlement. The exact five affected native cases pass (308.03s wrapper, dominated by cold worker compilation; no new test timeout/skip/retry). Earlier snapshot proof passed 12 tests before the second staging rewrite and is not claimed as final staging proof.

Independent full-diff review completed in 12 passes. Three P1 claims were declined after combined-source verification: duplicate proxy owners are synchronously rejected, and the staging worker retains its native owner's launch-compatibility check. The complete dispositions are retained with the lane evidence; no accepted actionable findings remain.

Full Linux infra proof on pre-integration `18807df2eefaeb1350b012ca4fb5aeb15f8d9503`: **14,478 passed, 77 existing skips, 7 failed**, 2,877.69s. The failures exposed ordinary cancellation settlement (three), an original publication error displaced by cleanup failure (two), and two tests awaiting the deliberately removed early-retirement path. The first five tests remain unchanged; the outbound pair now proves adapter completion, queue settlement and lease-stop join. The minimal fixes are included. The suite's wrapper could not record its terminal receipt because the broker request timed out; counts come from the completed test output, not a successful wrapper claim.

The second conflict-driven integration retains main's admission snapshot performance cache and V2 binding API. **Focused proof: 67/67 tests across seven files** on `79d390c0c6e3b343b8c38f8e9307da0204c42f9d`, 645.21s wrapper wall time, including 332.57s cold worker preparation and a 237.15s native suite. It covers unchanged cancellation and destructive-transfer tests, integrated worker admission/V2 binding behavior, and sequential outbound settlement. Those runtime paths are unchanged by the final ancestry and mock cleanup. The integrated repair and final cleanup reviews are scoped-clean at P1.

The remote follow-up could not execute tests: a stalled large transfer was interrupted and replacement SSH/workspace verification timed out before command admission. The owned Hetzner lease was released and provider cleanup is complete. Final-head runtime and Madge checks both report zero cycles; SDK registration and lint suppressions (3/3) pass.

The branch-base SDK surface check sees stale budgets (3,656 public exports / 2,122 callable / 154 deprecated versus observed 3,672 / 2,133 / 158). Main already corrected these approved async migrations in `f9940dc8a794948cf24492fd881296b60296ff4a`, with provenance comments in `7562fd2b90129bef6674cc72247458da060c1d02`. An isolated uncommitted merge preview against `f28e5ba25b1ffc6e2980cbc65b5f714f4533718a` (tree `f3963611d798909254708dfe99a5288da94a80dd`) passes the unchanged current-main SDK gate and reports no unauthorized removals. P01 does not edit the checker or raise budgets, and was not rebased merely for green.

Caller integration on the loaded local host passed 81 Gateway cases but the Telegram dynamic-facade case timed out; the following delivery-preflight assertion also failed. Those test cases and their authorization handlers are unchanged, and their delivery/bootstrap mocks bypass p01's implementations. Source inspection identified a possible late continuation sharing one-shot mocks, but the exact interleaving was not observed. The requested sequential comparison passed **3/3 on clean main `54dd59bfb8c389521609ea1a9480777d0175d84b`** (476.40s wrapper) and **3/3 on candidate `c0f1e168371379230a4cc63bebf65fa6f8bc1fb7`** (156.68s wrapper), with their original timeouts/assertions. This is a non-reproduction, not a claimed fix or main-red proof. The earlier Linux integration run passed all 286 cases across nine files.

The changed-file check passed production core, all 28 selected test type graphs, formatting, ratchets, configuration docs, wrapper shadowing, and deprecation checks. Its production unused-export scan found the now-removed p01 ancestry exports and eight unrelated existing exports: `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2`, `SettingsSegmentedOption`, the three `PanelEmptyState` exports, and the three `PanelLoadingSkeleton` exports. prs.title: fix: recreate agent database after explicit close
prs.body:
Related: #129185
Related: #131331

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reopening an agent database after an explicit close could get an uninitialized replacement database when the original SQLite file had been deleted or recreated during the same process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Successful schema validation is now retained only while the pathname still identifies the same filesystem object. An unchanged database keeps the fast read-only reopen path, while a replaced or recreated file falls back to full owner/schema initialization. The identity check uses the repository's canonical filesystem identity helper plus birth time to distinguish rapid inode reuse. This does not change the database schema.

## User Impact

Agents can recover correctly when their database is explicitly closed and then replaced or recreated, without regressing prompt reopen behavior for an unchanged WAL database with another writer active.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that explicitly closes the database, removes the database/WAL/SHM files, reopens it, and verifies the complete canonical schema including `session_key_contract`.
- Focused test: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts` — 121 passed, 4 skipped.
- `scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/state/openclaw-agent-db.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts` passed, including formatting, lint, core/test typechecks, import-cycle checks, and database guards.
- Full `pnpm build` passed under Node 24.15.0.
- Exact-head CI passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and `check-sqlite-session-lifecycle`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Direct SQLite lifecycle reproduction is the relevant live proof; no UI or channel surface changes.

### Direct runtime proof

Executed against this PR's production database opener under Node 24.15.0 using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The script opened and explicitly closed an agent database, removed its database/WAL/SHM files, reopened it, and queried the resulting live SQLite schema. It then explicitly closed and reopened the unchanged file while an independent connection held a WAL `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer:

```json
{
  "explicitCloseSucceeded": true,
  "recreatedSchema": {
    "open": true,
    "userVersion": 19,
    "tableCount": 49,
    "sessionKeyContract": {
      "name": "session_key_contract"
    }
  },
  "unchangedWalResult": {
    "open": true,
    "elapsedUnderOneSecond": true,
    "elapsedMs": 13.8
  }
}
```

Production code grows to retain and compare a bounded filesystem identity. That state is required to distinguish replacement from an unchanged explicit reopen without forcing every reopen through the write-capable schema path.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenClaw-managed Codex was used for review and identified the unchanged-WAL reopen regression, which is covered on current `main`. The repository's standalone `autoreview` helper was unavailable because it uses separate CLI authentication; submission was explicitly authorized with that limitation.

prs.title: feat(install): add opt-in pinned Bun runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bun is opt-in for non-app installs, but the installer had no Bun path: users had to run `bun add -g --trust` with `OPENCLAW_PACKAGE_BUN_LAUNCHER` and pin services manually, while macOS Bun now refuses Apple's system SQLite (#168564).

## User Impact

Users can explicitly select `scripts/install.sh --runtime bun` for a verified, pinned Bun-only installation without Node. Node remains the default, and its installation behavior is unchanged. Merging updates the public installer through the existing website sync.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer owns runtime setup, package installation, and service pinning in one flow. `--runtime bun` (or `OPENCLAW_RUNTIME=bun`) resolves an exact npm version through npm dist-tags without Node, downloads that release tag's Bun pin, and verifies archive and executable SHA-256 hashes plus the revision before execution. It stages Bun atomically under `~/.openclaw/tools/bun-<tag>/bun`; `--bun-path` / `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` can select an existing matching executable.

On macOS it provisions and validates Homebrew SQLite. It performs a trusted Bun global install with the package launcher while Node is hidden during lifecycle execution, cross-checks the installed package pin when present, and uses the exact release-tag pin for historical packages without that metadata. `package.json` now ships `scripts/lib/openclaw-bun.json` so future packages carry their pin. Existing Gateway services are re-pinned to Bun; fresh onboarding receives `--daemon-runtime bun`. A dry run prints the runtime plan. These changes preserve state and configuration. The caller's original TMPDIR (including its unset state) is restored before onboarding or service installation, so disposable scratch is never saved in a service definition. Explicit package detection reuses the existing owner, including bare `.tgz` and `.tar.gz` names. Refused shell-profile writes remain nonfatal: the installer prints manual PATH commands and still re-pins an existing service, while unsafe external profiles remain untouched.

Release-note context: add an opt-in pinned Bun installer for macOS and glibc Linux, including verified runtime downloads, SQLite setup, Bun launcher installation, and Gateway runtime pinning. No changelog edits: this repository generates release notes at release time.

## Evidence

- Original reviewed head: `pnpm test test/scripts/install-bun.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 41/41 passed, 12.8 s wall time.
- Final head: `pnpm test test/scripts/install-bun.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 45/45 passed, 37.85 s wrapper wall time (31.37 s Vitest). Before the final one-line package-spec repair, the combined Bun and existing installer suite passed 229/229 in 152.37 s wrapper wall time (142.81 s Vitest); the final repair adds two bare-tarball cases. Unsafe-profile and service-TMPDIR cases both failed before their fixes and pass afterward, including service re-pinning, external-profile preservation, and caller TMPDIR/unset handling.
- `bash -n scripts/install.sh`, ShellCheck, docs check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex branch autoreview, full-candidate source review, and fresh review of the final staged repairs: all accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings resolved. Reviews caught unsafe-profile early exit, disposable TMPDIR leaking into service definitions, and bare-tarball classification; each was fixed with regression proof.
- Published `2026.10.1` no-Node smoke completed end to end: installer 17.79 s; `openclaw --version` and `openclaw status --json` ran through the Bun launcher. No service was installed.
- Scope: +409 net production LOC; 417 test lines added in `test/scripts/install-bun.test.ts`, plus documentation. Tests cover installer behavior and verification boundaries.
- Initial PR CI: `test/scripts/install-bun.test.ts` passed 41/41 in 1.477 s of test execution on Linux (run 38105900182, job 114371378884). Second-head CI: 42/42 passed in 1.713 s (run 38107561541, job 114376371733). Final-head CI: 45/45 passed in 2.490 s (run 38110638656, job 114385470802).

The local results above were completed on the reviewed branch before PR creation. Full-tree lint and unused-export checks previously reported failures in unchanged baseline files; PR CI results and any independently attributed inherited failures will be recorded here before landing.

### Existing-state and profile compatibility

No data model, config schema, session storage, or migration changes are introduced. The installer delegates service installation to the existing Gateway owner and does not run Doctor or rewrite stored data. The fixture replays two successive Bun pins against an installed service. The published-version live smoke proves the no-Node package path; it intentionally does not claim a live existing-service migration. The profile repair preserves the established behavior from #124779: skip unsafe targets, retain successful profile updates, and continue installation.

### PR CI

Initial CI run [38105900182](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38105900182) failed in eight test jobs. Second-head CI run [38107561541](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38107561541) failed in 16 test jobs: eight share a QA setup failure (Plugin inventory has retired); the others cover transcript cursor, Codex import/steering, Discord routing/bindings, Feishu routing, and Telegram history/model selection. prs.title: fix: continue memory recall after optional trigger lookup times out
prs.body:
Closes #142479

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking for remembered context could have model recall skipped when the optional trigger lookup reaches its deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional lookup and enclosing preflight timer each had a 1500 ms limit, but the enclosing timer started first and aborted the entire hook. Carry the authoritative remaining preflight allowance into optional lookup, suspending the enclosing watchdog only while that bounded lookup owns the deadline. Re-arm the watchdog with any remaining allowance afterward. Model recall retains its own full budget, and the existing total allowance is unchanged.

This revision follows the prior maintainer guidance in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/117534#issuecomment-5159725254 and removes the first revision's additional 1500 ms allowance.

## User Impact

A slow or unavailable optional trigger lookup can fall through to model recall, as an immediate lookup failure already does. Session-state stalls still stop preflight at its existing deadline.

## Evidence

- The added focused reproduction failed before the source change with undefined recalled context.
- 229 Active Memory hook and trigger tests pass, including lookup exhaustion after both immediate and near-limit preflight, stalled session state, and recall settlement. The timing regression verifies recall starts at the original 1500 ms deadline after 1490 ms of setup; it failed the initial revision, which started recall at 2990 ms.
- The same 229 tests pass after backporting only this repair to v2026.9.3.
- Extension production and test typechecks pass. Formatting, plugin boundary and contract checks pass.
- Independent autoreview through P2 inspected both the prior index and revised working tree. All five findings concerned the prior index and explicitly identified the working-tree revision as corrected; that exact reviewed revision is now committed. No unresolved findings remain in the submitted source.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain complete answers while previews are pending
prs.body:
Closes #139249

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex replies lose the end of their answer when a channel preview callback stalls. Even when Codex has supplied a complete final answer, terminal settlement could return only the earlier streamed prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep assistant-start, partial-reply, and reasoning presentation callbacks ordered in a projector-owned queue, independently of canonical native notifications. Finalization joins accepted presentation under the existing receipt-anchored settlement deadline and abort grace. Callback failures are isolated, and queued callbacks cannot start after cancellation or projection closure.

Media, transcript checkpoints, native plan persistence, and async-message delivery retain their existing awaited ownership. No new configuration, timeout, protocol, or storage changes.

## User Impact

Complete native answers remain available in the result and transcript projection even if presentation stalls. Settlement timeout and cancellation still release the run and retain their existing failure classification.

## Evidence

- Extended the existing stalled-presentation lifecycle reproduction on main `925fb0c3353ce98f1c8d6d1f2c27bbb8472af095`: before the fix, expected `Done. The complete answer survives pending presentation.` but received only `Done.`; the same regression passes with the repair.

- After rebasing onto main `efa4b5dfbb3`, 8/8 targeted regressions passed, including blocked-delivery timeout and user-stop cases; `git range-diff` confirmed the patch was unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report busctl-incompatible when busctl rejects --json
prs.body:
Fixes #142940 (minimum remediation path from the issue).

## What Problem This Solves

On hosts with systemd older than 240, busctl has no --json flag, so every manager inspection subprocess fails at argument parsing. Install conflated that tool-invocation failure with an uninspectable definition and refused with generic SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN, leaving systemd 239 users (RHEL 8 family, Alibaba Cloud Linux 8) with no actionable error.

## Change

- Adds throwIfBusctlJsonUnsupported guard plus BUSCTL_JSON_UNSUPPORTED marker (src/daemon/systemd-unavailable.ts). Native stderr never leaves the boundary; only the static classification maps to the reason.
- The manager query path throws the branded marker instead of generic unavailable when busctl rejects --json (src/daemon/systemd-service-files.ts).
- New busctl-incompatible service-definition reason with remediation: upgrade systemd to 240+, or manage the user unit with systemctl from the service account (src/daemon/service-types.ts).
- Definition-mutation capability maps the marker to the new reason (src/daemon/systemd-definition-mutation.ts).
- Initial install read preserves the allowlisted reason instead of the generic refusal, covering both ordinary install and --force before any write (src/cli/daemon-cli/install.ts).

No persisted data model changes: the marker and reason exist only in memory during inspection.

## Evidence

- src/daemon/systemd-definition-mutation.test.ts: busctl unrecognized-option stderr yields {kind unknown, reason busctl-incompatible}, redacts diagnostics, and stage() fails with SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN: [busctl-incompatible].
- src/daemon/systemd-unavailable.test.ts: guard-level cases (branded throw, unit-absence passthrough, non-exit passthrough).
- src/cli/daemon-cli/install.test.ts: initial readCommand rejection with the marker fails with SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN: [busctl-incompatible] before config reads or credential generation.
- src/daemon/systemd.test.ts (242 passed), systemd-definition-mutation (85 passed), install (42 passed) suites green locally.
- Real Linux Gateway install proof (ordinary install and --force on systemd 239 with redacted terminal output) is not available from this machine (macOS, no systemd) and is parked for a Linux host run.

## Scope note

This is the issue's sanctioned minimum: install still refuses on systemd < 240, but now with an actionable error instead of a generic one. A full legacy-output fallback (parsing pre-JSON busctl text) needs a systemd 239 fixture host and is left for a follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two New Session browser tests that still require automatic group-default revalidation after that behavior was intentionally removed in #168656.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Browser coverage continues to check updated folder/worktree defaults, renamed-group unavailability, disabled creation for an unavailable target, and draft preservation, using an explicit route refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introducing commit: 224c0bcd8991e31c1c8bc1123992739ff7b0d94b (#168656).

That PR explicitly accepts: “New Session groups: changing group configuration while a draft is open does not revalidate its loaded defaults; reload obtains new defaults.” It also states that a subsequent event or refresh corrects catalog display and retains authorization, account isolation and ordinary write settlement.

The tests now request route revalidation after updating or renaming the group, and check recovery after remote catalog invalidation settles rather than requiring the open route to fail closed during a background display refresh. Draft and final-state assertions remain.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

The original two failures are recorded on main in the A/B reproduction and hosted CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109867860.

Focused bundled browser proof passed all 11 tests in `session-management.group-defaults.e2e.test.ts` (42.77s). The remote case settles the authoritative `sessions.groups.defaults` response, explicitly refreshes the route, and verifies the new folder plus preserved draft. The local-write case verifies refreshed folder/worktree defaults and renamed-group unavailability. No retries, timeouts or skips were added.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores only the old test expectations. Blast radius is the New Session group-default browser suite, with no runtime or persisted-state changes.

prs.title: fix(update): complete the first upgrade from stable 2026.10.1
prs.body:
Related: #165233

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a failed CLI exit after an in-place update started by published stable 2026.10.1, even when the package replacement and Gateway restart succeeded.

## User Impact

Future packages let the existing 10.1 updater finish its first upgrade with its original pending cleanup queue intact. Older published updater cleanup and restart imports remain supported; no user action or config change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

10.1 loads its cleanup queue owner before updating but first imports a facade during final cleanup. The candidate ships a narrowly documented bridge through the original owner URL so Node reuses that loaded queue. Both paths remain in the postinstall output inventory; the comment specifies removal when upgrades from 10.1 are no longer supported.

Record only cleanup-scope imports that run in `finally`. Remove six unnecessary historical file requirements, the 139-line computed-asset syntax detector, and its lexical whitelist tests. Keep literal post-update imports and leave computed package assets with their installation owner. Regenerate the inventory from verified published packages, adding stable 10.1.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced premature shared-state shutdown before the shim; it now waits for the original queue, survives replacement, and preserves the update result.
- 133 compatibility/postbuild tests passed in 22.92s. The new regression took 42ms in that run; standalone `pnpm test test/scripts/update-compat-cleanup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 6.64s. Added CI work is one tooling test; measured body cost is 0.04s, with runner/transform overhead not yet measured in CI. No timers, subprocesses, or Gateway boots added to unit tests.
- Canonical regeneration and exact `--check` passed for all 12 SHA512-verified npm artifacts, preserving previous stable post-update contracts.
- Full `pnpm build`, package tarball integrity/import-graph checks, changed script/test typechecks, and focused lint passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- `check:changed` stopped on unused exports in unchanged session/Gateway/state/UI files; the script export scan passed and the remaining lint checks passed separately. No related source or Knip configuration changed.
- Full `update-first-hop-compat-docker.sh` source lane passed with the integrity-verified published stable 2026.10.1 package (Linux arm64, Node 24.21): first update exited 0, status `ok`, phase `finished`, exact selected build installed, service process replaced, and no transaction residue. The subsequent update also exited 0 and replaced the service process after 349 legacy compatibility files were removed from its target fixture. The final unsupported-admission target passed with the installed updater owning admission; supported admission remained candidate-owned.
- Fixture metadata alone was relabeled from this main checkout’s 2026.9.9 to 2026.10.2-first-hop.0/.1/.2 so the published driver exercised real upgrades. Compiled code was unchanged. Observed update times were 287s / 351s / 368s on local Docker. No source version or protocol bump is committed.
- The broader published-driver survivor harness stopped before updating on stale fixture setup (retired OAuth sidecar / `agents.list` rejected by 10.1). Session-survival coverage from that harness remains unproven; the first-hop harness creates valid config through the installed CLI.

prs.title: docs(macos-vm): use installer script so a fresh VM gets Node before OpenClaw
prs.body:
Closes #160256

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS VM guide's step 6 (`docs/install/macos-vm.md`) telling users to run `npm install -g openclaw@latest` inside a fresh macOS VM that has no Node.js or npm installed. A fresh Lume macOS VM (the guide's target scenario) has neither `node` nor `npm`, so the install step fails with `command not found`.

## User Impact

Anyone following the macOS VM guide on a new VM (the documented scenario) now gets a working install path. The installer script provisions Node 26 on macOS when missing, installs OpenClaw, and launches onboarding. The npm path is retained as a secondary option for VMs that already have Node 24.16+ or 26.1+. The `openclaw daemon install` step is added after the installer's onboard so the Gateway survives headless VM restarts (step 8).

## Why This Change Was Made

The guide's primary install command assumed npm was available. The installer script (`curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash`) is the recommended path in `docs/install/index.md` and handles Node provisioning. This aligns the VM guide with the general install documentation.

## Evidence

- **Before (this branch's parent):** Step 6 says "use the following command on npm 12 or npm 11.16+" followed by `npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw`. No prior step installs Node or npm.
- **After:** Step 6 uses the installer script as the primary path and moves the npm command to a secondary "if the VM already has Node" option.
- The installer script's macOS behavior is documented in `docs/install/index.md`: "installs Node if needed … Node 26 on macOS."
- No test files added or changed. No runtime, dependency, or schema changes. Documentation-only correction.
- `git diff --check` passes. Changed-page formatting and MDX structure verified.
