prs.title: fix(agents): persist visible child thinking state
prs.body:
Closes #137207

## What Problem This Solves

Visible native children selected the configured subagent model but bypassed the configured subagent-thinking resolver used by hidden native children. The child could therefore run with an unpersisted/default thinking selection, while session surfaces showed the selected model with an unrelated thinking level and runtime.

## Approach

The visible `sessions_spawn` path now resolves configured thinking through the existing `resolveSubagentThinkingOverride` owner and passes that level into `sessions.create` beside the already-resolved model. Both configured (saved subagent/agent default) and caller-inherited thinking are clamped through the selected child model/runtime policy before creation, so a saved level the child cannot honor is normalized instead of failing creation. Visible spawns reject per-call `thinking`, so no explicit request is ever downgraded. Auth-profile suffixes are stripped only for that policy lookup while the qualified model ref remains intact for Gateway creation. Gateway creation therefore persists one validated model/thinking pair before the first run, and existing session projection derives the matching model-scoped runtime.

That clamp is graded against the child's authoritative capabilities. `sessions.create` **rejects** an explicit `thinkingLevel` its prepared catalog does not support and clamps silently only when the field is absent (`projectSessionsPatchEntry`), so the clamp reads the same prepared catalog generation the Gateway validates against and, when that read fails, forwards no explicit level rather than an unauthorized one. An explicit `model` that is a configured alias is resolved through the same target-agent alias resolver the hidden subagent plan already uses, so policy grades the canonical child model instead of a bare alias under the default provider.

This remains deliberately narrower than #137170. It does not add a second effective-reasoning field, change transcript visibility, accept per-call thinking overrides with `visible=true`, or introduce a new wire contract. A saved thinking level the child cannot support is clamped to a supported level, so existing installations keep creating visible children as they did when the field was omitted.

## User Impact

A visible child configured as Luna + Codex + Max is created, executed, and displayed consistently as Luna + Codex + Max rather than showing the selected model with an unrelated `Off` state.

## Evidence

Exact head: `8a3772bab3c9b628c5dc5c27c94397377f6c4344` (signed, GitHub `verified=true reason=valid`; base `main`). Pushed fast-forward, non-force, from the reviewed head `b15ead458cfe560fd501cf5305a9b26079ac6201`. Sections below marked with an older head are kept as history.

### Round at `8a3772bab3c`: saved thinking is clamped, not forwarded

- **[P1] Preserve creation for existing unsupported thinking settings.** Saved subagent thinking now goes through the same prepared-catalog, runtime-row clamp as inherited thinking (`src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-visible-thinking.ts`). Regression in `server.sessions.agent-model-catalog.test.ts`: saved `agents.defaults.subagents.thinking: high` with an off-only child, driven through the real visible spawn into the real `sessions.create` handler. The child is created and persists `thinkingLevel: off`, and the same handler rejects the unclamped `high` with `INVALID_REQUEST`. With the production fix reverted, only that case fails, with the real Gateway error `thinkingLevel "high" is not supported for off-provider/off-only (use off|ultra)`.
- Low-value tests the review named are removed: the mock-manufactured rejection, the duplicate off-only replay, and the snapshot-shape runtime-row replays (real creation covers those).
- Branch-owned tests that recent `main` merges had broken are repaired: the gateway test's `vi.mock` now keeps the real `prepareModelChoice`; the harness-owned Ultra suggestion list is no longer pinned; `loadModelCatalog` is declared on `SessionsSpawnToolOptions`; the retired `agents.list` shape is gone; and a test `main` deleted in #165945, which a merge had brought back, is dropped. To satisfy the line-cap ratchet, the branch's tests now live in sibling files, and no over-cap test file grows.
- Gate on the committed tree `0adeeff517f`: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` all exit 0. Focused vitest: 79/79 plus 17/17. Full `pnpm check:changed`: exit 0.

### Real creation boundary for a catalog-defined off-only model

`server.sessions.agent-model-catalog.test.ts` drives the real `sessions.create` handler against a real on-disk session store with an injected prepared catalog:

- With `model: off-provider/off-only` (`reasoning: false`) and an explicit `thinkingLevel: high`, creation is **rejected**: `INVALID_REQUEST` / `thinkingLevel "high" is not supported for off-provider/off-only` (the suggested-level list now also carries the harness Ultra mode), and no session row is written.
- With the catalog-clamped `thinkingLevel: off`, creation succeeds and the row persists `thinkingLevel: off`.
- Two further cases drive the real `maybeSpawnVisibleSession` with its `callGateway` wired to that same real handler, one shared authoritative catalog feeding both the tool's clamp and the Gateway context. The off-only child persists `off`; a reasoning-capable child persists `high`.

### Discrimination (each fix proven load-bearing)

Ablations were run in a throwaway clone at the same head, with the new tests present and production reverted:

- Both fixes reverted: **3 failed / 141 passed** in `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` — all three new cases fail, no pre-existing case fails. Observed un-fixed values: the catalog loader is never called; `thinkingLevel: "high"` is forwarded where the fix omits it; and `model: "demo-fast@work"` + `thinkingLevel: "high"` where the fix sends `model: "demo/demo-max@work"` + `thinkingLevel: "max"`.
- Alias resolution reverted alone (catalog clamp kept): **1 failed / 143 passed** — only the alias case.
- Production reverted with the integrated cases present: the integrated off-only case fails with the **real** creation error `thinkingLevel "high" is not supported for off-provider/off-only (use off)`.
- Honest negative: the two boundary-characterization cases pass **37/37 with production fully reverted**. They pin why the fix is required; they do not discriminate it, and are not claimed as coverage of it.

### This round's gate at the published head

43 steps, one red. The committed tree `7588f7a176eea256bae82926f72dfa0697af03f9` was unchanged before and after every step and equals the pushed tree.

- All seven `tsgo` lanes green **cold** (`.artifacts/tsgo-cache` moved aside) and warm.
- `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `deadcode:exports`, `oxlint` (plain and the `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig` form), `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check` (worktree and `origin/main..HEAD`): pass.
- `deadcode:unused-files`: both Knip scans (production and full-tree) at **0 entries**.
- Six focused suites, each its own invocation, counts predicted then reconciled: 144/144, 39/39, 243/243, 112/112, 15/15, 135/135.
- All 18 `check:changed` lanes hidden by its first-failure bail were recovered with `--dry-run` and run individually: all pass.
- The one red is `check:changed`'s `plugin boundaries` lane, and it is **inherited, not ours**: a pristine `origin/main` worktree at `7e701b1208e` and this branch both exit 1 with byte-identical normalized 14-line captures, md5 `72b2184817e68494943215b5935f016c` (`eligibleForRemoval=1`, `plugin-sdk-media-understanding-public-demotion`). Nothing in this diff touches that surface.

### Prior round (head `1d80c0c4f3f369cea0a470e64eac3d1b403876d9`)

- Focused spawn, thinking-policy, and Gateway projection suites: **392/392 passed**.
- Profile-qualified regression: `openai/gpt-5.6-luna@openai:work` is canonicalized only for runtime-policy lookup, retains OpenClaw's `ultra` support, and crosses `sessions.create` with the qualified model ref unchanged.
- Unsupported configured-thinking regression: Gateway rejection is surfaced and `registerRun` is not called. (Superseded at `8a3772bab3c`: saved thinking is now clamped, so creation succeeds.)
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: pass, including production/test typecheck, lint, dead-export scans, import-cycle guard, and changed-file policy gates.
- `pnpm build && pnpm ui:build`: pass; production Control UI built from 3,227 modules.
- Isolated production proof: a real Gateway invoked `sessions_spawn` from a parent turn, created and completed a visible child through the real Codex app-server, and returned `PROOF137435`.
- Exact Gateway projection after completion: `modelProvider=openai`, `model=gpt-5.6-luna`, `thinkingLevel=max`, `agentRuntime.id=codex`, `status=done`.
- Exact Control UI state: model value `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, thinking value `max`; the selected model row rendered `GPT-5.6 Luna · 258.4k active · 1M max · Codex`.

### Round at `e0943adbb1e` — runtime-catalog clamp (answers ClawSweeper Revision 13)

The clamp now selects the **concrete runtime row** the way Gateway does, instead of grading against logical catalog entries. `loadVisibleChildThinkingCatalog` reads `loadGatewayModelCatalogSnapshot` and returns `{ entries, routeVariants }`; `selectVisibleChildThinkingCatalog` mirrors Gateway's `findModelCatalogEntry` → `selectModelCatalogRuntimeEntry` pair and grades against the selected row alone. The runtime id is resolved once through `resolveEffectiveAgentRuntime` and shared by row selection and level grading, so the two can no longer disagree about which harness owns the child's turn.

- **Negative control, written first.** Four new `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts` cases cross both catalog shapes (flat array, `entries`+`routeVariants`) with both mismatch directions. Production reverted to `edeef014260`: `EXIT 1`, **4 failed / 151 passed (155)** — the flat pair reproduces the finding's two mismatches exactly (`max` retained where `high` was required; `high` retained where `max` was available), the snapshot pair forwards no level at all. With the fix: `EXIT 0`, **155 passed**.
- **The two skipped creation-boundary cases are restored, and extended to four.** Root cause was the gateway harness's `MockModelRegistry` lacking `fork`, which killed the real prepared-catalog path with `templateModelRegistry.fork is not a function`; a test-only additive `fork` projection unblocks it. The block drives the real `sessions.create` handler and a real on-disk session store: **41 passed (41)**, `EXIT 0` (was 39 with 2 skipped). The clamped case also asserts that the unclamped level is genuinely refused (`thinkingLevel "max" is not supported for runtime-fixture/reasoner`), so the clamp is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. With production reverted, all four fail (`EXIT 1`).
- **Gates:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `config:schema:check`, `plugin-sdk:surface:check`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check` all `EXIT 0`; focused vitest across 7 files **891 passed**, `EXIT 0`. `oxlint` still emits the **pre-existing** `max-lines` *warning* on `sessions-spawn-visible.ts` (736 → 796 lines against a 700 limit); it exits 0 and is not claimed as fixed.
- **Whole gateway shard, both trees, sequentially, HEAD pinned and recorded at both ends.** Fixed `e0943adbb1e`: 293 failed / 25620 passed, `EXIT 1`. Pristine control `edeef01426`: 288 failed / 25653 passed, `EXIT 1`. **32 files fail on both** — inherited. Fixed-only is 6 files / 7 tests, and resolves to two proven artifacts: 5 tests are the `verifyBuiltGatewayHead` check `dist/build-info.json:commit === git HEAD` failing against a `dist` inherited from `edeef01426`, and 2 are `Test port block at 6056 is already claimed`. Re-running those six files after rebuilding `dist` at `HEAD` gives **6 files / 25 tests passed, `EXIT 0`**. Pristine-only is 1 test (`mention-inbox`, timed out at 143389 ms against a 120000 ms limit), so the residual noise is bidirectional. **No branch-owned regression.** The dominant inherited cluster is a host-toolchain limit, not a defect: ~121 shared failures are `git worktree list failed (exit code 129)` because this host runs `git 2.34.1`, where `worktree list --porcelain -z` exits 129 (`-z` arrived in git 2.36) while `--porcelain` alone exits 0.

### Remaining proof limits and open maintainer decisions

- **Upgrade compatibility.** Since `8a3772bab3c`, an existing saved subagent thinking setting that visible spawns used to ignore can no longer block child creation, because it is clamped to what the child supports. Whether visible spawns should persist configured/inherited thinking at all, rather than keep Gateway defaults, is still a maintainer decision. This PR implements the review's recommended option (inherit with capability clamping). Fresh-install and v2026.9.9 upgrade runs are not included here.
- `mergeable=true` / `mergeable_state=blocked`, polled twice at the published head. An earlier revision of this body reported `mergeable=false` / `mergeable_state=dirty`; that was true when written and is now stale — the merge commit `edeef01426` resolved it.
- The check rollup at this head contains **no build or test jobs**: `resolve`, `label`, `dispatch`, `PR context and evidence` succeeded, `label-issues`, `backfill-pr-labels` and `[code]smith` skipped, `review` and `auto-response` in progress. There is therefore no CI evidence for or against this head, and none is claimed here.
- The real-creation evidence above runs the real handler, validator and session store in one process. It is not a two-Gateway live transport trace.

prs.title: feat(backup): batch agent SQLite snapshot operations
prs.body:
Related: #163651

## What Problem This Solves

Operators moving several agents need to snapshot and restore their SQLite stores without starting OpenClaw separately for each store.

## User Impact

Operators can create snapshots, restore verified snapshots, or preflight several agent stores with `openclaw backup sqlite batch <request.json> --json`. Operations run in order, stop after the first failure, and report later operations as skipped. Completed operations remain completed; a batch is not an atomic transaction across stores.

Upstream maintainer acceptance of the new agent-only request/result contract remains outstanding. The requested decision is the bounded contract described here: explicit paths, ordered operations, partial completion, and stop-on-first-failure reporting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command validates the complete request before doing work and reuses the existing snapshot and preflight owners. Restore binds the requested agent identity before creating the target while retaining manifest, hash, integrity, schema, ownership, and fresh-target checks. Existing snapshot formats and the caller's isolated configuration remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Evidence applies to head `392d17495a90dc126c5f57d546503016136d2a21`. This adds a workflow; no claim is made that the previous single-operation command was defective. The retained tests exercise refusal cases as well as successful operations.


- Actual supported CLI proof on this head passed using two disposable agents: create and restore both completed, both preflights returned `exact`, and an owner-mismatch restore exited 1 while preserving the prior completed operation and skipping the later restore. Neither refused nor skipped target was created. Sanitized commands and output are below.
- Real SQLite/provider tests cover multiple agents, source-owner mismatch, restore-owner mismatch, corrupted snapshot bytes, existing targets and sidecars, preflight refusal, and complete request validation before writes. The retained provider/batch run passed 20/20, and a fresh unchanged-head Commander registration run passed 9/9. The final affected batch rerun passed 10/10 in 19.84 seconds with a warm compiled-worker cache (9.022 seconds in test bodies).
- Selected local gate checks all passed using composite evidence: source typecheck, all 27 downstream test typecheck groups, dead exports and repository guards; then corrected formatting/lint and the remaining eight checks. The final cleanup only added required braces and renamed a local schema constant. `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated Codex autoreview completed with no P0/P1 findings before that mechanical cleanup. A separate independent review covered the implementation and the final cleanup.
- Local runtime: Node 26.8.1, Vitest 5.0.1. Hosted runtime test duration is unavailable: the exact-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37042437063) was skipped while this PR was draft; skipped checks are not passing runtime evidence. The source-checkout CLI built and executed its real runtime; an installed release package and live migration latency benchmark were not tested. This proves the native batch contract, not a production downtime improvement. No external provider, operator Gateway, or customer data was used.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and measured times</summary>

Focused test commands (retained proof is reused; the registration run fills a missing timing receipt):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 9/9 passed on this head; wrapper wall time 4.88 s, Vitest 1.12 s.
```

| Changed test file | Passing cases | Reported case time | Invocation wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `backup-sqlite-batch.test.ts` | 10 | 9.022 s | 19.84 s, standalone final run |
| `backup-sqlite.test.ts` | 10 | 3.195 s | Shared 42.29 s run with batch tests |
| `register.backup.test.ts` | 9 | 0.067 s | 4.88 s, standalone run |

Case times are sums of the emitted per-case durations, not inferred CI timings. The batch suite uses real SQLite snapshot/restore workers to exercise the owner, integrity, and fresh-target boundaries. Hosted test seconds remain unavailable because the draft CI run skipped the test jobs.

Retained provider/batch commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# 20/20 passed after the snapshot identity regression fix, 42.29 seconds.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Final affected suite after strict fixture correction: 10/10, 19.84 seconds.
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --timed` passed source typecheck (10.51 seconds), all 27 core test graphs (175.84 seconds with incremental caches), dead-export scans (109.03 seconds), and the preceding selected guards. It stopped at style-only lint findings. After fixing those findings, the following remaining commands passed, plus a final formatting check, in 156.852 seconds total:

```sh
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- docs/cli/backup.md src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts src/cli/program/register.backup.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.ts src/snapshot/local-repository.ts src/snapshot/openclaw-snapshot-copy.ts src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.ts

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/cli/program/register.backup.test.ts src/cli/program/register.backup.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite-batch.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.test.ts src/commands/backup-sqlite.ts src/snapshot/local-repository.ts src/snapshot/openclaw-snapshot-copy.ts src/snapshot/snapshot-provider.ts

node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.mts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-media-download-helper-roundtrip.mts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-runtime-sidecar-loaders.mts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-webhook-auth-body-order.mts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-no-pairing-store-group-auth.mts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-pairing-account-scope.mts
```

The final formatting and lint checks took 0.343 and 22.432 seconds respectively. The seven TypeScript guard commands took 73.230, 0.482, 14.014, 15.822, 0.309, 15.313, and 14.850 seconds; the schema-version guard took 0.055 seconds. No full-gate success from one uninterrupted invocation is claimed.

</details>


<details>
<summary>Actual CLI proof: successful batches and refusal/skip output</summary>

Executed on the PR head with Node 26.8.1 and the repository-pinned pnpm 12.5.1. Two disposable agent databases (`alice`, `bob`) were initialized from the checked-in agent schema, including their distinct owner records. The config explicitly names those agents and disables plugins. `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` select only the disposable proof directory; `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=pr163684proof` isolates the daemon identity. The existing OS home is preserved for the wrapper's read-only service-path checks. No Gateway was started or stopped.

All path prefixes below are normalized to `$PROOF_DIR`. Each command used the supported source runner, with no command/provider mocks:

```sh
pnpm --silent openclaw backup sqlite batch "$PROOF_DIR/create.json" --json
# exit 0; wall 63.281 s (includes the first checkout build, whose own timer was 47.3 s)
pnpm --silent openclaw backup sqlite batch "$PROOF_DIR/restore.json" --json
# exit 0; wall 2.421 s
pnpm --silent openclaw backup sqlite batch "$PROOF_DIR/preflight.json" --json
# exit 0; wall 2.299 s
pnpm --silent openclaw backup sqlite batch "$PROOF_DIR/failure.json" --json
# exit 1 as expected; wall 2.238 s
```

Success output projection, preserving the emitted statuses:

```text
create:    ok=true  alice=create/completed  bob=create/completed
restore:   ok=true  alice=restore/completed bob=restore/completed
preflight: ok=true  alice=preflight/completed/exact bob=preflight/completed/exact
```

The mixed failure request first preflights the restored Alice store, then requests restoring Alice's snapshot with Bob as the expected owner, then attempts another Alice restore to a separate fresh path. Its actual output, with the detailed preflight object omitted:

```json
{
  "schema": "openclaw.sqlite-batch-result.v1",
  "ok": false,
  "outcomes": [
    {"id": "before", "operation": "preflight", "status": "completed"},
    {
      "id": "wrong-owner",
      "operation": "restore",
      "status": "failed",
      "error": {
        "code": "restore-failed",
        "message": "SQLite snapshot database identity does not match the requested restore owner."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "later",
      "operation": "restore",
      "status": "skipped",
      "error": {
        "code": "prior-operation-failed",
        "message": "Skipped after failed operation wrong-owner"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

A separate filesystem assertion confirmed both the wrong-owner target and the skipped later target were absent. The restored Alice and Bob databases remained available and passed exact schema preflight. These elapsed times describe this local smoke run, not a benchmark or claimed latency reduction.

Two initial harness attempts stopped before the batch command: the sandbox could not fetch pnpm signature metadata, and the sanitized environment initially omitted the OS home required by daemon-path inspection. Registry access and preserving the existing home corrected those setup issues without disabling verification or changing source. The successful run above is the resulting actual CLI evidence.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hosted CI qualification after marking ready</summary>

CI qualification: [checks-node-changed-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37047713229/job/110973708177) failed in the existing `backup create` product-path test, `src/cli/program/register.backup.product-path.test.ts:153`. The command exits 1 as expected for unreadable discovery state, but the test expects `Cannot read shared state for discovery`; default stderr now says `The CLI command failed.` and recommends `openclaw doctor`. The subsequent no-archive assertion is not reached in this failing case. The same job passes all 9 backup registration tests, including the new batch command.

This mismatch is inherited from native main. Commit [d0b48d63](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d0b48d63efb88ac4f9f5eb447a39ea95cb2b0542), already in this PR's parent, changed ordinary CLI failures to terse output unless debug details are requested. The fixture does not request debug output. GitHub's exact blob identities confirm the failing fixture, failure formatter, backup command, backup-create implementation, and discovery-state reader are identical between CI's main parent `cf43499dc96264542e69f726ede3bfee75221f2e` and tested merge `cf0aa26965705e3047c4ec7adcdc72b5de88827b`.

Local confirmation on unchanged PR head `392d17495a90dc126c5f57d546503016136d2a21`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/register.backup.product-path.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reproduces the same assertion failure (3 passed, 1 failed; Vitest 15.68s, native wrapper 38.82s including preparation). No unrelated source/test changes or broad CI reruns were made. This failed check remains unresolved before merge; the native test owner needs to align its diagnostic assertion with the explicit-debug/default-output contract, then rerun the affected gate.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ports the Agents settings pages from Lit to Solid 2 while the rest of the Control UI migrates on main.

## User Impact

The existing agent routes, custom-element tags, selectors, drafts, permissions, model choices, and file-preview behavior stay intact. Automatic roster reconciliation no longer changes browser history; only explicit agent-selection intent navigates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Agents and Memory element classes are replaced by one Solid implementation per tag through `defineSolidBridge`. Existing synchronous request/draft owners remain in TypeScript. Canonical Solid settings, icons, refresh status, and test-root ownership replace the draft adapters.

A small controller host preserves the existing Gateway, subscription, and avatar lifetimes. The remaining Lit content adapter owns only shared, still-unported template helpers. Diary controls and cards keep their DOM across owner notifications, and closed file previews retain their prepared snapshot until opened.

Agents production LOC: **7,255 → 7,795**. The remaining growth is explicit reactive bindings, retained-content components, and imports for the split Memory renderers. Memory rendering now uses modules below 700 lines and drops its grandfathered max-lines exception. The controller and retained-template adapters live in the existing subscription and Solid bridge owners; with sanitized Markdown rendering, they add 118 shared lines and have multiple consumers. The original route file retains only its stateless Lit template; no Lit page class or duplicate tag implementation remains.

## Evidence

| --- | --- |
| Latest Memory owner/bridge test | 18 passed; 1 existing Chromium-only skip; 18.16 s wall time after owner consolidation |
| Latest Memory view test | 19 passed after the renderer split; 60.63 s total wall time |

| Before/after screenshots | Initial baseline: all 52 shots passed. Refreshed main baseline and exact-head candidate captures are in progress (13 states × desktop/mobile × light/dark, plus focused mobile cron). |

Visual proof uses the explicitly permitted bounded local fallback after Testbox non-admission. The sole baseline build stopped on an isolated checkout dependency-link setup issue after 5 seconds; both captures use the same source-Vite mode. No local Docker, typecheck, or full E2E suite ran. prs.title: fix(cli): keep cached-only provider catalogs in isolated agent exec
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agent exec` runs its turn against a fresh temporary state directory unless
`--state-dir` is passed. Provider-owned generated model catalogs are stored in
the selected agent's per-agent SQLite cache (`agentDir/openclaw-agent.sqlite`,
scope `plugin-model-catalog-v1`), and that cache lives under the state root.

So the one-shot run prepared its model registry against an empty agent
directory: every generated catalog row the selected ambient agent had already
validated was missing, and a model that only that catalog advertises (absent
from the static plugin manifest) resolved as `Unknown model: <provider>/<id>`.

Root cause: state isolation repointed the only readable source of that metadata
without carrying the already-validated metadata with it.

Fix: the command captures the operator agent's retained catalogs before it
repoints `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, projects them onto inventory metadata only, and
hands them to the run through a request-owned `AsyncLocalStorage` scope (the
same shape as the existing run-pinned plugin install roots). The read-only
catalog reader appends handed-off rows **only for plugin ids the run's own
agent directory does not retain**, so:

- a fresh isolated run keeps session state isolated and still sees its
  provider's cached-only models;
- catalogs the run itself retains — including empty ones — stay authoritative,
  so the handoff can never shadow local state;
- the handoff carries **no credentials, request headers, request parameters,
  local-service environment, or source database**: the projection keeps only
  provider route (`api`, `baseUrl`, `compat`) plus model inventory fields. The
  generated-catalog consumer already treats those rows as inventory, never as
  request authority;

  carries nothing;
- ownership, suppression, and lifecycle checks are untouched: the rows enter
  through the existing read path and every downstream check still runs.

  request-owned handoff scope, and the retained-wins merge.

  handoff; the raw scope reader is exported for the capture path.
- `src/commands/agent-exec.ts`: capture before the state repoint (gated on the
  existing installed-plugin inheritance flag) and scope the run with it.
- `src/agents/plugin-model-catalog.handoff.test.ts` (new): projection,
  retained-wins, and cached-only model resolution.
- `src/commands/agent-exec.plugin-catalog.test.ts` (new): isolated `agent exec`
  keeps the metadata (and carries none for `--auth-env-only`).

prs.title: fix(agents): reduce message schema overhead for bound channels
prs.body:
Related: #14785

## What Problem This Solves

A conversation bound to one channel still receives `message` actions and parameters from unrelated configured channels. Channel-less sessions also receive whole action groups they cannot use, and the automation tool repeats lengthy documentation in every prompt.

## User Impact

The message schema now follows the current channel and the agent's route bindings. Multi-channel agents retain the union of declared actions and capabilities, including wildcard-account bindings. Unbound local sessions and scheduled runs retain configured-channel discovery. Delivery authorization is unchanged; there is no new setting or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core message discovery selects and sorts the channel set once per projection, then uses that selection for actions, capability-gated fields, and plugin schema fragments. Existing current-channel-only fragment visibility is preserved. The schema builder always filters core field groups by discovered actions. prs.title: perf(sqlite): keep transcript admission outside writer locks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A delayed host admission could leave transcript-index preflight holding an IMMEDIATE SQLite writer lock for seconds, blocking unrelated writers while almost no SQL ran. Existing event-loop warnings could not identify the synchronous callback responsible for the delay.

## User Impact

Long main-thread callbacks now produce bounded, always-on warnings naming their known scheduler, phase, timeline, or worker owner. Transcript-index preflight and sweep keep host-admission waits outside the writer lock. No configuration, schema, permission, retention, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary worker transactions obtain initial host admission before BEGIN and retain final commit validation. Bounded derived-index maintenance obtains both grants before a nonblocking BEGIN, rereads authoritative rows in the transaction, and returns pending work to the existing yielding drain on contention. Its final grant linearizes the maintenance effect; no grant crosses asynchronous work or a lock wait. Missing database facts remain conservatively unknown during transactions and refresh after release, closing a second, indirect host-wait path.

One Gateway-owned async-hook observer records the longest synchronous named segment in each callback without retaining async-ID histories or counting I/O waits as execution. It retains eight pending stalls and reports overflow. The extracted PR-wrapper inventory includes the new module.

Production grows because attribution is a new always-on contract: the observer itself is 118 lines, plus lifecycle, naming, and reporting integration. The admission module shrinks against its pre-change line-cap baseline after removal of a single-use wrapper. Net runtime production delta: **+189 lines**; the wrapper inventory adds one line. This growth is required by the new attribution contract; the implementation replaces the old in-lock admission path instead of retaining a second fast path.

## Evidence

Linux rig, Node 26.8.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.9.0, isolated synthetic state; no production Gateway was accessed.

| Same 20,000-session fixture, 2,200 ms injected host wait | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| IMMEDIATE writer-lock hold | 2,323.4 ms | 96.8 ms |
| End-to-end preflight | 2,370.9 ms | 2,300.9 ms |
| Competing writer admitted at both host waits | no | yes |
| Returned pending sessions | 128 | 128 |

The lock hold is about 24× shorter; the host delay still contributes to operation latency. A real scheduler/health-monitor probe emitted exactly one line naming `scheduler:maintenance:synthetic-json-reply` for a 1,259 ms synchronous callback. In an alternating CPU-only synthetic loop, median monitor cost was 36.982 → 46.570 ms per 10,000 events (+9.588 ms, about 0.96 μs/event, 26%). This is monitoring overhead, not an application throughput measurement.

- Initial Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4m6k6gjys14737hf66nbrk2`: both old-code preflight/sweep regressions failed because the competing writer could not acquire the lock; the initial attribution/sibling run passed 72 tests.
- The additional actual-worker negative control failed on unchanged base `73f2255d77f0` with one host lookup during the transaction, then passed with zero after restoration of the patch.
- Owner regressions: **104 passed across nine files**. Sibling writer suites: **208 passed across 15 files**. Source-closure checks: **20 passed** after repairing the inventory; matching CI planning checks: **123 passed**. The export-collision guard passed.
- Independent Codex reviews are clean through P2, including the main integration, wrapper inventory fix, and final simplification.
- The changed gate tested tree `9838cadf303c7b90f1db6e27e3551d4d7f8b3a3e`, the tree in reviewed head `1bac2c8ddb555a4f686d7845c915287c13a0a81f`. Formatting, all ratchets, core types, every core test-type graph, and the other selected checks passed. The only failed task was the dead-export scan, reproduced independently on untouched base `73f2255d77f0`: `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts: GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` and `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/skill-workshop-page.test-support.ts: reconnectGateway`. Neither file is changed here. No guard was skipped.
- CI on `1bac2c8ddb55` found two integration issues: an unbound `stop` method reference and a Bun-routed async-hooks test. Both are fixed in final head `536cf31101c7ebfd6a7df448cee528eed67535f9`. Targeted lint and 243 owner/runtime-routing tests pass. The pinned Bun 1.4.3 emits zero `async_hooks` before/after callbacks in the independent Promise/setImmediate probe; Node 26 emits 3/2. The native-hook contract now runs on Node without weakening its assertions. Bun retains explicit synchronous task scopes and unattributed delay warnings, as documented. Exact-head CI is pending.

Measured `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall costs, including runner/worker preparation: stall owner 2.86 s; event-loop health 38.31 s; transaction diagnostics 3.70 s; transcript-index status 36.48 s; worker admission 48.09 s. CI seconds will be recorded after the run.

The historical production callback responsible for the reported stall remains unidentified. Synthetic scheduling and admission experiments prove attribution and lock behavior, not historical causation. Native work outside named callbacks remains explicitly unattributed.

<details>
<summary>Remote execution and infrastructure gaps</summary>

The initial Testbox proof used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` after one frozen-lockfile install. Later Testbox sync attempts timed out before tests. The other queued Testbox (`tbx_01m4m6k4v9fwd8xamkhdw84myr`) ran no tests.

AWS fallback `cbx_26616232ffc1` and Hetzner `cbx_11fde6955756` did not complete workspace transfer before cleanup. The unused rebase lease `cbx_5d86199da72d` was stopped. Fresh-PR Hetzner `cbx_40d31edc9ba9` checked out source but lacked Node/pnpm, so no tests ran there. All leases were stopped.

The authorized Linux-rig fallback ran the same focused commands, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts`, the two source-closure files, and the matching `ci-node-test-plan` files. Measurements used the actual publication backend, native SQLite locks, and Gateway scheduler with synthetic data. Final `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` uses the recorded base and staged candidate tree. Local execution was limited to editing, Git, changed-file formatting, the permitted tiny overhead probe, and the remote review helper.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent config writes for provider typos in `models fallbacks add`, `models image-fallbacks add`, and `models aliases add`, while preserving plugin runtime compatibility aliases. Thanks @Sedrak-Hovhannisyan for the original fix; contributor commits remain in the branch and main was merged without rebasing.

## User Impact

With an available provider inventory, `ollmaa/qwen3:4b` now exits 1 without changing config bytes. Installed/configured providers and prepared runtime hook aliases remain valid. When the inventory is empty or a retained runtime generation has no providers, commands save with a warning because provider ownership cannot be verified. No config, dependency, schema, or migration change is required; existing invalid fallbacks can still be removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

All model mutations reuse the `models set` inspection owner. Inspection consumes the existing prepared registry's provider index, which already includes runtime hook aliases. It distinguishes an unavailable generation from a fresh exact lookup finding no owner. Warnings print after a successful save. The docs now limit missing-model catalog warnings to `set` and `set-image`, addressing the previous P1/P3 findings.

prs.title: refactor(cli): simplify update and service lifecycle bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CLI updates, Doctor, native service inspection and node workers accumulated repeated observations and ownership bookkeeping for synthetic interleavings, making their real lifecycle harder to follow.

## User Impact

Commands, flags, configuration and persisted formats stay intact. Updates retain initial validation, activation-time schema compatibility, rollback, live execution authority and ordinary shutdown settlement. Configuration changes during an update are best effort and may require another invocation. A busy plugin lifecycle request is surfaced directly instead of automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the root “Choose good compromises” doctrine: carry selected facts through a command, let native owners guard actual effects, and use straightforward singleflight/serialization for bookkeeping. This removes 1,026 net production lines across 59 files (tests, support, fixtures and declarations excluded). No SQLite schema, durability, retention or permission policy changes; no dependency, protocol or config-shape changes.

Re-evaluated all 11 original KEEP rows: eight were narrowed or flipped. The three unchanged rows protect shutdown settlement, pairing/approval security, and a measured real-host inspection failure. Human reports retained: [slow service inspection #168031](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168031) and [endpoint-protected plist #139813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/139813). Native account/process authority, rollback data, bounded resources and measured warm caches remain. The skill-bin cache keeps its existing 90-second security freshness bound.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Candidate config equality/re-admission and implicit-channel reselection: b36eb3e7b11 introduced synthetic mid-admission writes, not a human incident; the selected candidate remains authoritative and later edits may need another update/Doctor run.
- Repeated candidate rehearsal: the same commit injects edits at validation/stop/transfer checkpoints; validation runs once and incompatible later edits fail visibly instead of triggering more rehearsals.
- Repeated config/include capture comparisons: [#160443](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160443) forces edits while capturing; preimages/path proofs and conditional writer-owned rollback remain, but concurrent edits can require operator recovery.
- Run-object/executor-field identity checks: [#145335](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145335) tests internal object replacement; actual live requester/executor checks remain, and private run objects are not replaceable mid-call contracts.
- Per-phase/per-step worker handshakes and post-write rechecks: [#161385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161385)/[#161851](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161851) inject changes around bookkeeping; writes settle normally without extra custody, while external effects still require live authority.
- Signal-run inode/generation matching: [#161104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161104) forces state replacement during progress; one current executor/run check and native settlement remain, and external database replacement during a CLI is unsupported.
- Mid-signal schema-version mutation: [#155610](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155610) and [#162098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162098) force an external schema bump during an admitted invocation; this is distinct from the real migration report behind that work. Normal migrations and signal settlement remain, while that concurrent schema edit can now leave a visible pending-history warning for Doctor/repair.
- Executor re-entrant entry, repeated child-bind flag and terminal-only authority checks: synthetic internal-caller cases around #145335; native binding and joined children remain, with no supported concurrent re-entry.
- Whole-tree fingerprinting of a separate unchanged service installation: #145335 tests package mutation; recovery checks directory/version/launcher/Node/build/schema/service identity, while unrelated package-file edits during update are best effort. Actual package transaction integrity is unchanged.
- Repeated service/config/database context discovery around staging: b36eb3e7b11 and 16095df1d75 pin successive-read drift; activation still checks the actual target schema, and operator edits during one command may need a retry.
- Runtime-artifact old/new service/database/inode comparison: [#145664](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145664) injects changed observations; current consumer inspection, canonical output destinations and live effect authority remain.
- Shell-env plan convergence: [#93118](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93118) pins late policy edits; startup uses one plan and later edits apply on the next start.
- Plugin lifecycle UNAVAILABLE replay loop: [#158688](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158688) uses synthetic admission responses; one bounded RPC reports busy for an explicit retry, without changing consent or uncertain-effect handling.
- Sticky restart PID/boot-generation failure and migration-owner continuity: [#149760](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149760)/[#151387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151387) force owner replacement; current readiness and progress facts decide success under the same finite budgets.
- Local CLI ambient env/path/inode drift and duplicate rediscovery: [#163853](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163853) flips process.env while admission waits; the command pins its target and still checks owner/PID immediately at RPC dispatch.
- Doctor config/source equality and recovery-presence rechecks: [#151025](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151025)/[#159033](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159033)/[#166617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166617) inject edits between reads; the migration writer remains authoritative and concurrent edits may require rerunning Doctor.
- Repeated foreground lease polling and separate ownerless deadline: [#154200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154200) uses a harness owner-row swap; the physical lock and existing bounded wait decide admission, so replacement contention can consume that wait but cannot grant access.
- systemd Unit/bus-owner generations, Windows launcher/Task snapshots and launchd scan bracketing: [#140339](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140339), [#151608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151608), [#151674](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151674), [#97285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97285) force second-read changes; status may briefly mix concurrent-install observations and self-corrects on the next read. Native mutation authority remains.
- Systemd read-scope env fingerprint/closed-after-await checks: [#145597](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145597)/[#146090](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146090) test internal route mutation; production callers pin one manager, authenticated bindings and pending-read settlement remain.
- Node pause generation token: [#149517](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149517) injects pause/resume/pause outside the sequential caller; one paused state covers the real auto-update loop.
- Node update pre-download policy/mtime repeats and duplicate pause cleanup: [#151545](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151545) injects discovery/download policy edits; an unnecessary private download may occur, but final policy/mtime/cancellation checks still gate activation.
- Skill-cache waiter finalizer identity: [#156995](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156995) describes an old-waiter race; one producer now clears its singleflight promise, so no waiter can clear a newer fetch. The 90-second authorization freshness stays.
- Node idle-retention generation: [#161097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161097) injects a late idle acknowledgement; work finishing after disconnect may stay warm until the existing expiry/capacity eviction, with fresh per-turn security admission.
- Node journal post-settlement flag and repeated fixed request-shape checks: #149517 has no human late-scope incident; private callbacks do not retain the scope, while native uncertainty and transaction authority remain.
- Workspace retain-snapshot supersession: [#123889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/123889) adds an impossible same-namespace replacement; the existing namespace queue owns snapshot acceptance and all cleanup, with live deletion protection unchanged.
- Node terminal-recovery retry/sentinel loop: #149517 forces cancellation exactly at journal admission; the completed cleanup receives one terminal result, and a late cancellation need not rewrite that result. Native writes still settle before capacity release.
- Node promise/map identity finalizers and MCP replaced-entry guard: [#149517](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149517), [#160265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160265), [#125092](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/125092) have no replacing production setter while work is pending; the sole owner clears its slot directly.
- Prepared-workspace permit identity: [#143227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143227)/[#149519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149519) test an old permit after closure; serialized mutations use a Set, retaining durable interrupted-mutation recovery.
- Upload before/after stat identity: [#134200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134200) has no necessary metadata-change incident; actual copied length and SHA-256 remain authoritative, so equal bytes with changed metadata succeed.
- Bundle per-hash acknowledgement generations: [#124590](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/124590) forces install/retain overlap; an old retain list can evict a regenerable bundle, and the next turn reinstalls it. User workspaces and durable data are unaffected.
- Offline Doctor title generation/foreground guards: [#151211](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151211) injects foreground writes despite exclusive maintenance; initial manual/incognito checks and commit authority remain, while concurrent foreground title edits are unsupported.

## Evidence

- Fresh independent review covered the production cut and subsequent corrections; actionable findings resolved. Final P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Current candidate: `901f9cafb7a258e6ccc0468d7634dd264c5ee7b3`. Conflict-only integration retained main's nested/foreign-owner handling and p12's final dispatch authority check. The collected-unit test explicitly preserves post-stop requester revocation and no-publication coverage. Final one-file typed lint and whitespace checks passed.

The dead-export scan reported an untouched Gateway type; the earlier model-picker finding is fixed by included main commit `00e095399b203a2c71ef773fcf8ea1177bc2a5ef`.

prs.title: fix(agents): drop throttled exec update events
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: exec live output throttling capped detailed payloads, but throttled `tool_execution_update` events still emitted generic tool/item updates with no new user-visible payload.
- Solution: make throttled exec updates a true no-op until the next allowed live update or final result.
- What changed: `handleToolExecutionUpdate` now returns before emitting generic exec update traffic when the live exec update throttle suppresses the detailed output, with regression coverage for global agent events and `onAgentEvent` emissions.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): final exec result events, command completion items, non-exec tool updates, and the existing live exec output size cap are unchanged.

## Motivation

- #84850 captured a 60s gateway sample with average CPU at 83.66%, 42/60 samples at or above 100% CPU, and 0.00 kB/s average read I/O during an embedded exec tool run. Dropping redundant throttled update events reduces avoidable gateway projection/broadcast work in that hot path.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #84850
- Related #78645
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway CPU saturation from #84850 during embedded exec tool output. Throttled exec updates should not continue producing generic tool/item event traffic when they carry no new visible output.
- Real environment tested: Local Linux OpenClaw worktree on Node 24, using the repo Vitest wrapper plus the redacted pidstat/gateway log evidence from the affected run.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`, `git diff --check`, and `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Copied terminal capture from the patched worktree:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  76 passed (76)

$ git diff --check
(no output; exit 0)

$ codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted
No discrete correctness issues were found in the current local changes.
```

- Observed result after fix: The regression test proves the first exec live update still emits visible output, while the next update inside the throttle window emits no additional global agent events and no additional `onAgentEvent` traffic. Final result handling remains covered by the existing exec result tests.
- What was not tested: I did not rerun the private 60s live CPU-saturation gateway session because the original setup/session details are local and redacted; the fix was verified at the exec tool update seam that emits the redundant events.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Redacted source evidence from #84850:

```text
pidstat summary:
rows=60
avg_cpu=83.66
avg_usr=79.42
avg_sys=4.25
avg_rd=0.00
cpu_ge_100_count=42
max_cpu=190.0

redacted gateway correlation:
2026-05-21T05:07:47.187+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool start: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
2026-05-21T05:08:04.330+00:00 agent/embedded embedded run tool end: runId=[redacted run id] tool=exec toolCallId=REDACTED
```

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: the live exec throttle suppressed detailed output but still allowed generic exec update item/tool events to be emitted for every throttled update.
- Missing detection / guardrail: existing coverage checked output truncation/throttling but did not assert that suppressed updates stop all generic event emission.
- Contributing context (if known): #78645 bounded live exec output payloads, but redundant event emission could still keep gateway event projection hot during high-volume exec output.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a second exec update inside `LIVE_EXEC_UPDATE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` emits no global agent events and no `onAgentEvent` traffic.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the redundant CPU work starts at the embedded tool update handler before gateway websocket fanout sees the event.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing exec output throttling tests cover payload capping but not generic event suppression.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Exec tool output updates inside the live update throttle window are dropped completely instead of sending generic no-payload progress events. Start, allowed live update, and final result events are preserved.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [generic tool/item events] -> [gateway projection/broadcast work]

After:
[exec update inside throttle] -> [no emitted event] -> [next allowed update or final result closes state]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`): No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`): No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 24 local worktree
- Model/provider: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO for the original runtime sample; tests do not require provider credentials.
- Integration/channel (if any): Embedded exec tool event handling
- Relevant config (redacted): Original private session details were redacted.

### Steps

1. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`.
2. Run `git diff --check`.
3. Run `codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --sandbox danger-full-access review --uncommitted`.

### Expected

- First exec live update emits visible command output.
- A throttled follow-up exec update emits no generic event traffic.
- Final exec result behavior remains unchanged.

### Actual

- Targeted wrapper passed: 2 files, 76 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed with no output.
- Autoreview found no discrete correctness issues.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [x] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: allowed exec live update still emits output; throttled exec update emits no global or local agent event traffic; final exec output/result tests still pass.
- Edge cases checked: existing large-output truncation and final output redaction coverage still passes in the same target file.
- What you did **not** verify: private live CPU-saturation rerun from the original affected setup.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`): Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`): No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`): No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Suppressing throttled updates could hide command progress between allowed live updates.
  - Mitigation: the first allowed update and final command result remain emitted; only no-payload updates inside the existing throttle window are dropped.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep selected accounts when startup catalogs arrive late
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A delayed connection catalog snapshot can replace a user's newly selected account with the old account, both while the replacement catalog is pending and after it completes.

## User Impact

Chat keeps the current account and model selection when an older startup snapshot or transport reply arrives.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publication-receipt cleanup in `224c0bcd899` removed the guard that kept old connection snapshots from replacing newer catalog state. Keep read receipts until publication or transport settlement, retire matching connection snapshots on invalidation, and retire superseded replies when a catalog wins. Ordinary metadata invalidations still share their pending request; this does not restore the removed refresh queue or ordering counters.

This is a behavior-only fix. The follow-up Details selector repair already landed separately as `bc458a9d46e`.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Real-Gateway catalog ordering, unmodified main | Both pending and complete cases fail: Account A replaces Account B (Testbox `tbx_01m4mh3m3yr0w5mjgbwf4rttcf`, run 38109470092) |
| New owner regressions, unmodified main | Three assertions fail, including late transport overwrite |
| Same regressions on `224c0bcd899^` (`762930ce318`) | Four focused cases pass; 10.45 s command wall time |
| Catalog owner with fix | 17 pass; 20.26 s wall time |
| Catalog transport lifecycle | 9 pass; 11.66 s wall time |
| Application metadata integration | 12 pass; 20.21 s wall time |
| Focused type-aware lint, formatting, diff check | Pass |
| Independent review through P2 | Clean |
| Full catalog + metadata E2E and UI types with fix | Testbox stayed queued beyond the approximately 15-minute admission budget; PR CI supplies this proof |

Existing metadata E2E expectations were repaired by `39bb19aec7c`; all six variants passed on main before this patch. The new assertions cover snapshot retirement without weakening the browser assertions. No new timer, process, dependency, configuration, or public contract is added. Test time for the owner cases is milliseconds; the reported wall times include worker preparation on the shared Mac. CI seconds will be recorded from the exact PR head.

Canonical Gateway Home updates also preserve a pending prompt after a saved split collapses to one pane.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell consumes the existing Solid projections and ApplicationContext provider. One sidebar node moves between desktop and drawer. The outlet keeps loaded content while its loader is pending, preserves the 1,000 ms cold fallback, parks Chat with hidden/inert/aria-hidden and `presented=false`, retires connection-scoped content, and awaits MCP teardown before removing it.

Temporary root Lit ContextProvider, layout, and route-rendering adapters keep unported Lit callers working. They are removed at cutover when their last Lit consumers are ported. The shared bridge and layout owner are the versions landed by PRIM-A (#168576); there is one implementation per registered tag.

Preserves #168506's startup design: `window.openclawControlUi` is a getter whose first read imports readiness. There is no startup readiness observer. System busyness frame/loading/layout modules load only when opened. Automation polls the hook before one-shot reads, and the boot manifest was regenerated by its real owner on Testbox.

WebKit's previous 14 import failures came from Vite discovering `@solidjs/signals` mid-suite (`optimized dependencies changed. reloading`), losing suite context or registering tags twice. Pre-optimizing it fixes the harness. Built-app WebKit navigation was separately checked without module errors. The browser suite keeps the real runtime and assertions.

The E2E fixture cutover uses the DOM ApplicationContext instead of retired Lit host fields, including observers attached before connection. The sidebar fault fixture waits for the normal stale-import document reload before taking the mock Gateway offline; it still injects the failure and checks visible retry/reconnect behavior.

Release-note context: migrate the Control UI shell to Solid while preserving lazy startup, navigation, draft retention, and unported pages; fix Back after default-agent selection and Home prompt preservation.

prs.body:
## Summary
- gives Telegram prompt-context message-cache plugin-state rows a seven-day TTL
- normalizes existing no-expiry rows in a TTL-enabled namespace on the next write so upgraded `telegram.message-cache` rows can age out too
- preserves sibling namespace budgets and adds focused coverage for the Telegram message-cache persistent store options

Refs openclaw/openclaw#87332 and openclaw/openclaw#87357.

## Notes
Current `main` already contains the generic plugin-state cap fix from `e3395867507` (`fix(plugin-state): evict current namespace on plugin row cap`). This PR addresses the remaining `telegram.message-cache` permanence angle from #87332.

The follow-up commit also addresses the review concern about pre-existing `expires_at = NULL` rows. When a namespace writes with a TTL, plugin state now updates live rows in that same namespace that were previously immortal to expire at the same deadline as the write. That keeps the upgrade path bounded without touching sibling namespaces.

## Verification
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts -t 'plugin-state store|persistent'`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts -t 'default TTL|Telegram sibling|plugin row cap|plugin overflow'`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts`

Behavior addressed: Telegram message-cache plugin-state entries now get a TTL instead of being permanent live rows, and old no-expiry message-cache rows receive a bounded expiry after the namespace writes under the new TTL policy.
Real environment tested: local macOS source worktree at `upstream/main`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: focused Vitest and oxfmt commands above.
Evidence after fix: Telegram message-cache tests passed for persistent/default store coverage; plugin-state tests passed for TTL normalization, sibling namespace budget, and plugin cap behavior.
Observed result after fix: default Telegram message-cache plugin state opens with namespace `telegram.message-cache`, max entries `3000`, and a seven-day default TTL; existing no-expiry rows in that namespace are assigned the new expiry deadline on the next TTL write.
What was not tested: live Telegram traffic or a production SQLite file from a real user profile.
