prs.title: feat: use personal Tailscale identity in iOS chat and Dashboard
prs.body:
Related: #162164 (native identity umbrella), #136686 (cross-client personal sign-in). ## What Problem This Solves iOS users need native chat and the embedded Dashboard to use the same Gateway-verified personal identity instead of grouping all paired apps under shared credentials. ## User Impact Users can choose personal Tailscale sign-in when adding a secure Tailscale Serve Gateway, or change it through the visible control on an existing paired Gateway. Successful personal authentication is used for native chat and the existing embedded Dashboard/Profile; there is no second Profile screen. Leaving the choice off preserves token/QR access. Personal sign-in does not grant administrator permissions, and a failed personal connection never silently falls back to Shared owner. Device/node admission stays separate from human operator identity. Personal mode still excludes persistent offline chat/outbox and Watch command delivery; existing saved history is not migrated or deleted. The Gateway must serve the matching Control UI changes in this PR. Updating only the iOS app while retaining an older Dashboard parser is not sufficient. ## Why This Change Was Made The app reuses existing Tailscale admission, signed-device challenges, connection settings and the Gateway registry. Pairing admits the node before starting the personal operator connection; route changes retire obsolete attempts. Trust/retry intent belongs to the matching connection attempt, not a recreated screen. The Dashboard accepts credential-free Tailscale authorization only with a matching verified recovery scope. Its signing authority remains native and is retired on route changes. The authorization parser loads on demand so the fix does not add it to Control UI startup. Design help remains welcome: personal identity should follow the explicitly chosen and successfully verified authentication method. A Tailscale address alone is transport, not proof of a person. Broader Profile/account-linking UX, operator naming, local Mac Primary adoption and Cloudflare composition remain separate slices. ## Evidence Current candidate `830f5b8ae0b016c7ff4552705c2077eab26a0bd7` includes the normal integration of pinned main `8fc31c91811524b3bae3091a3861b5febd160151`, preserving upstream authorship and the existing Cloudflare ingress/admission owners. Personal auth is carried through the moved background-fleet owner and TLS trust/retry path. The integration also removes a duplicate connection-enable declaration and awaits the async test-isolation initializer. Negotiated personal Tailscale auth still has no shared/device credential fallback; node admission remains separate. The full 32-path integration received isolated Codex/Astra P2 review using exact public-source blobs. It found the duplicate Swift declaration; the correction received a scoped-clean follow-up review. `git diff --check` and the original staged-content hook pass. The six generated source-inventory additions were checked against their exact source literals and deterministic IDs. [CI 38110487032](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38110487032) identified a Swift initializer argument-order error in the controller. The correction places personal auth before ingress authorization, matching the existing declaration and fleet caller without changing argument values. Its isolated P2 review completed with no actionable finding; original hooks passed and the published head was verified. The same run failed two shared markdown-table focus tests. Its exact merge includes the upstream modal's microtask-based focus restoration, while those tests asserted focus synchronously. Three assertions now await the same expected buttons, including the reopened-dialog path previously blocked by the first failure. Production behavior, default timeouts, cancellation assertions and auth guards are unchanged. The separate test-only correction passed scoped P2 review, pinned formatting and original hooks. [Current CI 38111749029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38111749029) is running. Gateway smoke's update-finalize Doctor failure during plugin-inventory retirement remains unresolved. No current-head native build, test, visual or live-provider result is claimed. The following completed QA and CI belong to the previous candidate `706c6fccf7596f67f0504664bb3a74d7833dad65`, which integrated main `48c08e6ccba6b4cd12b2c7aafa75588abece6d18`. They remain historical evidence, not results for the new merge head. The historical worker-setup failure was reproduced in the old merge, then traced to repairs already merged upstream: [`7ecc80a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7ecc80a457366091dd61448bcc319cf1a82a5da9) (setup/runtime-preference handling) and [#165166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165166) (concurrent placement-read/publication preparation). This PR integrates those repairs rather than duplicating a Core fix. Against that pinned main, the PR has no Gateway/placement or worker-setup fixture delta. - [Exact-candidate isolated QA](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37266737400/job/111625056624): **102 tests passed** — owning placement/setup regressions (2 files / 27 tests), affected browser/native-authorization adapter tests (2 / 49), and the original 13-file real-Gateway E2E inventory (13 / 26). The previously failing worker-initial-setup case passed. Receipts verify product head, workflow `0721306776ae0691a0017645a30f4fef18702b7a`, frozen lockfile, Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.5.1, and clean product source before and after execution. [Receipt artifact](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37266737400/artifacts/11326064849). - [Historical canonical CI at `706c6fcc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37266735131) and [its CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37267879156) passed. That incremental run's iPhone/iPad screenshot jobs passed; full iOS build/release-E2E and macOS Swift jobs were skipped, not newly verified. - Independent Codex AutoReview of the full 32-file PR delta against pinned main completed **scoped-clean P2** before push. The separate fork-QA workflow also passed scoped P2 review. Review is static, not runtime or maintainer acceptance. **Proof boundary:** the new QA used standard Ubuntu (4 CPUs), not the original Blacksmith runner. It verifies the integrated upstream repairs with the strengthened current fixture, not a byte-identical replay of the historical fixture. Ordinary real-Gateway E2E uses synthetic loopback admission; browser adapter tests are not a live personal Tailscale session. New full native authentication-suite execution, live protected administrative effects, revocation, second-principal/provider ownership, and App Store migration are not claimed. Earlier native/Simulator receipts remain stamped to their actual revisions below. This green CI does not claim a full repository build/check/test run or remove those live-service gaps.
Historical candidate receipts and earlier verification limits These observations belong to the earlier candidates and their then-current CI. Their pending/failed checks are historical, not the current head's CI result. Published candidate: `caf0363c3b0`, integrated with pinned main `c81d86e82f6022b5bcacf2b7ebe5bd0e7f3fcf20`. This adds a test-only repair to `9a29286`; the preceding native/parser receipts are at `020970f` and earlier slices, not a claim that every subsequently advancing main commit is integrated. - Latest CI repair: the shared WebSocket fixture records the required connect role, but twelve existing expected frames omitted it. Expectations now explicitly assert `operator` for personal connections and `node` for legacy connections. The native `GatewayNativeTransportDeviceAuthTests` suite passed 7 tests (one with five parameterized controls) on the exact test patch; browser Gateway tests passed 45/45. Correct UI-chat test types, official focused Oxlint, formatting and two-file Codex AutoReview (scoped-clean P2) passed. Compiler warnings outside the changed assertions remain. No production authentication or role behavior changed. The unrelated Google Meet lint error from that CI run was not modified, and fresh hosted CI is not yet claimed green. - `test-audit` found that the existing personal-mode Watch denial test opened the shared journal before exercising rejection, unnecessarily invoking legacy storage preparation. The test-only follow-up removes that setup, retains the actual admission error check and checks for no delivery warning. Source parity, pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0 and independent scoped-clean P2 AutoReview passed. A fresh native rerun of this modified case is pending; no production auth, storage or Watch delivery behavior changed. - Pairing regression failed before the repair (operator attempted before node admission); the repaired native selection passed 97 tests. After pinned-main integration, 140 selected native tests and 257 Watch-owner tests passed with no failures or skips. - First-connection/settings verification passed 149 declared tests / 173 parameterized executions at the preceding integrated slice, including trust, retry, cancellation, target changes, saved-choice preservation and explicit off. - Isolated Simulator Dashboard/Profile reconnect and automatic relaunch passed. A private-candidate over-install also retained the paired route without new QR or trust approval. These are Simulator/private-candidate observations, not App Store migration or every personal Gateway's compatibility. - The final parser change passed 40 focused tests, UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting. Official same-input comparison: startup JavaScript 373,444 bytes against the pinned baseline's 373,454 bytes; no budget or deadline was weakened. - Independent Codex AutoReview completed scoped-clean at P1 for the integration repairs and the final three-file parser delta. Reviews did not execute tests or establish every live security boundary. - The complete changed-file wrapper is **not green**: the final UI run stops at inherited environment-count drift (475 observed / 476 expected), also reproduced without the UI source change. No unrelated budget or source fix is included. Vítor authorized publication using the completed QA and AutoReview, without additional visual proof on his personal installation. Existing sanitized recordings and the approved decision transcript are retained below as historical evidence, not final-head screenshots. Live second-principal/provider-ownership proof is not claimed. Simulator runs retain an unclassified responsiveness warning; the Watch suite retains audio-session main-thread warnings. Full repository build/check/test and new hosted CI are not claimed passed.
### Historical iPhone recordings **Embedded Dashboard — previously published recording, 5.2 seconds.** Settings loads and remains rendered. This is visible Dashboard behavior, not a trace of authenticated administrative side effects. **Authentication selector — same previously published recording, 3.3 seconds.** Shows full access followed by the long-press menu offering “Use Shared Owner.” The clip demonstrates availability; it does not show executing that choice. **Existing Profile — earlier recording, 4.3 seconds.** Shows Settings → the existing Profile and management permission. Historical evidence, not final-head Profile proof; personal details are redacted. **TLS trust/reconnect — earlier recording, 6.5 seconds.** Shows a trust prompt, reconnecting and Settings. Historical evidence; it does not establish a visible Trust-button click. Fingerprint and private details are redacted.
Agent transcript: Vítor's identity model, compatibility requirements, testing corrections and vanilla-first design decisions **Scope and provenance.** Selected dialogue from September 30–October 2, 2026, checked against the original session rollout rather than reconstructed from an agent summary. The quotation blocks are English translations of Vítor's original Portuguese dialogue, not verbatim English speech. Obvious transcription errors and product-name misspellings are normalized without changing the intended meaning; `[…]` marks omitted portions. The surrounding explanations are editorial summaries, not invented dialogue. This is a partial, task-scoped transcript, not a complete session export. The original helper reported `sourceTruncated: true`; this expanded selection was independently checked by streaming the original rollout. Raw logs, tool output, instructions, private endpoints, account identifiers and unrelated work are excluded. **Authorship.** Vítor supplied the product rationale, constraints, test observations and corrective decisions below. The assistant investigated and implemented the candidate, but does not claim authorship of those human decisions. Proposed directions are not presented as shipped behavior or maintainer acceptance. **The governing idea is not “remove Shared owner” and not “always use Shared owner.”** Preserve shared/token access where that is the chosen admission model; allow verified personal authentication to identify the person instead of collapsing every app into the shared principal. Keep identity separate from permissions and device pairing. Vítor further questioned the word “Shared” for a single-user harness and proposed addressing that naming separately. These distinctions, rather than GIF preparation, are why the contribution exists. ### 1. The problem is person attribution, not a new role system **Vítor — September 30:** > This is not about roles. I don't want to change those for now; I want us to resolve Shared owner in the apps right now. He distinguished the visible person identity from transport/client labels and permission policy. The immediate goal was to let native apps identify the person already authenticated, without redesigning roles or making every shared token claim to be a person. **Vítor — October 2, comparing simultaneous clients:** > All at the same time on my personal OpenClaw: three identities, one on Telegram, one in the app, and another in the browser's Control UI. This was an operator-reported cross-client attribution problem, not proof that all three connections had the same verified principal. The distinction mattered: a personal display name or avatar alone must not be treated as verified identity. ### 2. Separate the person from app/device admission to a Gateway **Vítor — September 30:** > In other words, who you are in relation to that Gateway is one thing. Who you actually are is another. Do you see what I mean? > At its core, the handshake between the app and the Gateway—or the apps and the Gateway, whatever the setup—is one thing. Your identity is another. > And I can choose not to link any account and use a vanilla Gateway with a token […] His conceptual model was a person who can interact through several apps or accounts, with Gateway admission remaining a separate concern. External-account linking must be optional; ordinary personal/local installations should remain usable through existing vanilla setup. This broader identity model motivates the umbrella; it is not a claim that this PR implements a portable global identity or changes Gateway trust policy. He also asked to investigate existing enterprise/current-main behavior and reuse it if applicable, rather than invent another auth system. No enterprise implementation or maintainer approval is inferred from that request. ### 3. Keep Shared owner for compatibility; add personal adoption incrementally **Vítor — September 30:** > For compatibility reasons too, I don't want to lose Shared owner. It needs to exist, for now. > I haven't configured that, versus I have configured authentication. So if I have authentication configured […] I should be able not to use Shared owner, do you see? > I'm using multiplayer and want everyone to use the apps, but everyone in the iOS or macOS app appears as Shared owner. That doesn't make sense. The retained requirement is compatibility with shared admission, alongside an explicit personal-authentication path for native human actions. The umbrella covers broader clients; this PR is the bounded iOS Tailscale implementation. Existing macOS personal sessions should be reused, not described as absent everywhere. **Vítor — September 30:** > But you need to look at this against current main, do you understand? Current-main inspection was required before deciding what was missing. This transcript records that instruction, not a claim that the candidate is integrated with every subsequent main revision. ### 4. Profile is where optional identities should eventually come together **Vítor — October 2:** > We need a way to link people's accounts […] I should be able to say, look, this is my account, and add it to Profile, do you see? > For anything that interacts directly with OpenClaw, such as channels, this matters, because otherwise the memory itself gets confused. He connected attribution to an agent harness's longer-term memory: treating one human as unrelated app/channel identities can fragment the user's experience and memory associations. He reported that concern while using a memory integration; this is product rationale, not a measured memory-corruption result. **Vítor — October 2:** > And Profile should be where you link or configure identities. > In more complex cases with multiple identities, such as channels plus authentication, they should all be able to belong to the same profile. Optional account linking and a unified Profile belong to the umbrella's follow-up work. They must not turn this first slice into automatic account merging, role changes, or inferred identity equivalence between Telegram and an auth provider. ### 5. Authentication should drive identity, without removing the Dashboard **Vítor — October 2:** > You're using Tailscale Serve, but you haven't chosen to use Tailscale authentication, for example. That's fine: you use Shared owner. If you decide to use Tailscale authentication, you use Tailscale and automatically stop using Shared owner, do you see? > In other words, I think this needs to be tied to authentication, do you understand? The distinction is intentional: using Tailscale Serve as transport is not the same as choosing and successfully verifying personal Tailscale authentication. The preferred UX should follow the validated authentication choice instead of adding an independent “who am I?” switch. This is the requested design direction; the candidate still has the temporary explicit selector. **Vítor — October 2, after reporting the missing native Dashboard:** > Not having the Dashboard is unacceptable. If we've fixed the Dashboard issue and then introduce a regression ourselves in another fix, that makes no sense. We need both. The requirement was **personal native attribution and a usable embedded Dashboard together**, with existing Gateway permissions respected. A chat-only fix that regressed Dashboard access was not acceptable. His report prompted the Dashboard correction; it was not an instruction to grant administrator permissions to every authenticated person. **Vítor — October 2:** > But logically, shouldn't it use whatever authentication the person has? Why complicate it? > At its core, authentication should determine which auth you use, and Shared owner or Owner should be for when you don't have that and only have a token. ### 6. Upgrade observations must retain differences between saved setups **Vítor — October 2, before replacement testing:** > Let's test whether it breaks existing setups. **Vítor — October 2, correcting an over-broad upgrade interpretation:** > No, that's not what happened. My personal Gateway's setup was preserved. The other one wasn't—the Hive one wasn't. […] But mine, the normal one, started directly. […] We're also comparing different experiences. The operator reported that one existing personal setup reopened directly while the other required QR pairing. His explanation of why the installations differed was tentative. The transcript must preserve the observed distinction, not convert it into “all saved routes upgraded without intervention” or a proven root cause. **Vítor — October 2:** > And we have video. We have the moment when I used the QR code; we have all of that. > I think it's working. It connected and authenticated directly with the QR code, opened Profile, and my profile appears here. **Vítor — later that day:** > Right, but now I've recorded video and everything. […] You've fixed it, the Dashboard appears now; the UX question is where we put shared versus non-shared. These are operator reports from physical testing. The attached GIFs show only their captioned portions; they do not independently establish complete cold-relaunch migration, forbidden final effects, or final-head coverage of every earlier observation. The remaining proof requests stay explicit rather than erasing the useful human observations. ### 7. Reuse the existing Profile; reject duplicated screens and shortcuts The assistant introduced a separate native Profile wrapper and entry points while trying to make the selector discoverable. Vítor rejected that direction. **Vítor — October 2:** > The problem is that a Profile screen already exists. Creating another one makes no sense. None at all. > And then you put shortcuts to that screen in several places. What sense does that make? It's vanilla first. The correction was to remove the duplicate UI layer and keep the existing embedded Profile, personal admission and Dashboard work. That rejected UI experiment is not part of the reviewed candidate. The temporary selector should not be disguised as the final discoverable UX. Vítor also explicitly requested the upstream `test-audit` workflow, not merely a generic principles review, and later checked that it had actually been used. The test cleanup removed redundant assertions without changing production behavior; its verification is reported separately in the PR evidence. ### 8. Small PRs, separate naming follow-up, and lead-designer integration **Vítor — October 2:** > Shared owner doesn't make sense unless it's a multiplayer harness. Otherwise, what does Shared mean? Shared with whom? […] I think we should keep it, but we need to think about this. > Yes, but Shared should only be for multiplayer. > We should split this into small PRs under the umbrella. One of them should cover those two options for Shared owner. Naming “Owner” versus “Shared owner” for single-user/multiplayer contexts is a proposed separate small contribution. It does not authorize silently renaming the current shared principal or removing its compatible behavior in this PR. **Vítor — October 2, authorizing this PR's temporary UX and design request:** > Make the PR like this and ask the lead designer to help us integrate it. But suggest synchronizing it with authentication: if it's Tailscale, activate it automatically, as I already told you. **Resulting contribution boundary:** ship no duplicate Profile, preserve existing shared admission, carry verified personal identity into iOS human operations and the embedded Dashboard, and ask the lead designer to integrate selection/recovery with the existing auth/Profile flow. Automatic identity adoption, account linking, naming, broader native-client adoption and maintainer acceptance remain separate proposals or gates. The transcript explains the human decisions behind the candidate; it is not a replacement for security or runtime qualification.

## What Problem This Solves

Placement dispatch and turn settlement duplicated mutation adapters, publication state, and reads already performed by the owning worker.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Placement admission, workspace recovery, and committed-result recovery retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route dispatch through the existing lifecycle worker and its receipt protocol, remove redundant exactly-once publication flags and an identity-only receipt wrapper, and reuse validated placement facts in workspace-result operations. Keep dispatch-specific receipt validation and all live authority checks.

Production LOC: **414 added / 573 deleted = −159**, measured from `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD` at the branch merge base, excluding tests and generated files. 20 changed files. The generated database inventory follows the relocated worker owners; there is no new main-thread database access or freshness probe.

The result operations avoid repeated placement reads; acceptance also reuses its already-validated pending claim. No wall-clock performance claim is made.

## Evidence

AWS Crabbox, isolated checkout pinned to the branch base:

- 211 focused tests across 12 files exercised dispatch, redispatch, activation, turn authority, claims, projection, staged results, move recovery, required placement scopes, and worker/CI registries. The initial run passed 210 and caught an internal `nowMs` field leaking into the dispatch reply. After correcting the identity projection, all five redispatch tests passed. Assertions were preserved.
- Initial focused command wall time: **286.14 s**. `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-store.redispatch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **33.14 s** after the correction.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed. Type-aware Oxlint on changed production TypeScript: passed, zero warnings/errors.

Knip reported only the unchanged `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` export in `server-instance-runtime.types.ts`; the same full export scan on the unmodified baseline produced byte-identical JSON. No changed-file export findings.

prs.title: fix(codex): run native account models on the first turn
prs.body:
Related: #156491
Depends on #156501

## What Problem This Solves

The native model picker can show a model before a fresh first turn can resolve it. A first-turn selection must match a current native provider/model/runtime catalog row, be ready for the selected auth profile, and remain current through the physical `turn/start` write.

## User Impact

Local regressions cover rejecting stale selections and changed account/profile bindings before the native turn write. Live proof for revoked or reassigned accounts remains outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker’s native catalog is not the executable model registry, and auth/profile state can change between discovery, prepared login, and inference. Resolving the exact selected row and binding it to the started client/account revision closes that gap without treating a host route or another profile’s readiness as native authority.

## Implementation

- Resolve first turns from the selected harness’s exact current catalog row and readiness. A successful exact targeted discovery can attest its selected row while the full inventory remains partial; failed, timed-out, incomplete, or non-ready selected-provider discovery cannot.
- Keep profile-scoped catalog results call-local so one profile’s ready row cannot warm or stand in for another. Forward explicit and automatically selected profile identity through the optional harness selection field; reject unsupported selected-profile transport instead of claiming readiness from a different profile.
- Preserve explicit auth order, profile pins, configured routes, and request overrides. Eligible automatic routes may defer model-only provider entries to Codex native auth. Identity-only ChatGPT credentials continue to deny inference under native deferral.
- Bind the selected native client and catalog revision after prepared login/account read. Immediately before physical `turn/start`, check that the client, revision, selected profile owner, and credential identity still match. Accept the expected prepared-login transition; reject a later account/config change before wire I/O.

## Integration

- Integration commit: `132364b957ddd416037184c7f14c7887b3714c5f`, merging official main `4a7d53616a5dbee3b0a8e2efc1b5ed7185325b13`; PR #156501 head `1773116cfe2f917680be1cfbb7fd14a865a2858b` remains an ancestor.
- Conflict resolution retains main’s provider-outcome and cancellation/retirement contracts alongside B’s exact native selection, account-read binding, selected-profile scoping, and final pre-write fence.
- SDK surface: 3,662 public, 2,128 callable, 158 deprecated exports.

## Evidence

- Six focused catalog/native test files passed 74/74 tests across four Vitest shards on this integration.
- The repository’s changed-path core test-type check passed all 27 selected graphs. Focused Oxfmt, Oxlint, SDK surface, and PR-diff checks passed.
- The full `check:changed` aggregate and full build were not run.
- In the last observed hosted run (38023535746), one compact test shard failed on a synthetic merge with prior main `2f92ecf`. The logged failure is consistent with an upstream test-fixture mismatch: commit `e048d9d` changed the status caller to read top-level `diagnostics`, while the test fixture still supplies only nested `manifestRegistry.diagnostics`; these status files are outside this PR. The mismatch is still present on current main. We did not independently reproduce the hosted failure, so its root cause remains unconfirmed. No rerun was requested.

## Remaining Review

There is no authenticated native-account canary or fresh-install/pre-existing model-only configuration exercise for this head. Maintainer review is still needed for automatic auth precedence, the additive optional harness contract, and the account/profile fence. The Sep 27 authenticated Sol canary on previous head `955431a` ([issue comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156491#issuecomment-5856964118)) demonstrates an allowed native turn only; it does not prove explicit-account isolation or rejection after revocation/reassignment. The historical host-auth E2E on `b8ca4512` does not exercise a native Codex account.

prs.title: feat: manage channel identity links in the existing Profile
prs.body:
Related: #162164 — this is the separate Profile-management slice for channel identity links.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

## Evidence

Current head `396297e94e34a0bedf461dbf09932613b8927e23` uses the supported Solid bridge, retaining its host tag, Settings controls, negotiated-admin checks and synchronous Gateway request retirement. Domain state remains in a plain TypeScript controller. The existing channel-link tests and geometry assertions remain intact. Pinned oxfmt 0.71.0 and original commit hooks pass. Isolated Codex/Astra P2 review found a scheduled-authority concern; the correction restores the synchronous subscription and its owned cleanup. The follow-up review completed with no actionable finding.

[CI 38109971803](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109971803) then identified a render-time signal write and two Solid/ARIA type errors. The current correction initializes the controller in the existing post-commit effect, preserves synchronous Gateway retirement, uses literal ARIA values and reads nullable links through the Solid accessor. Its exact-source isolated P2 review completed with no actionable finding. [Current CI 38111092386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38111092386) is running. Reviews did not execute project code; current tests and visual parity still require hosted verification.

The preceding main integration retains the intentionally consolidated Profile tests and moves the unique unsaved-name-draft regression into `profile-page.test.ts`. [CI 38107076864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38107076864) at `a230a565` rejected the new Lit production file and separately failed the cold New Session selected-person containment check. The Solid change addresses the demonstrated lint rejection. The containment failure's cause is not established; it is not claimed fixed or inherited. Canonical checks for the new source head are pending.

[Historical canonical CI 37258505016](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37258505016) passed at `f9081de0a2f5697e4967e049e57f4bf5779d6649`. The runtime and visual receipts below remain stamped to their actual earlier tested revisions, not the current merge head.

### Inspected pre-patch/after Profile comparison

prs.title: fix(mcp): release computer control with its admitted run
prs.body:
Closes #147420.

## Problem

MCP computer calls create a provider execution with no run cleanup owner. Rebuilding the tool catalog changes the execution ID; a later call or turn then fails with `COMPUTER_HOST_BUSY` until the node disconnects.

## Change

Use the admitted run's execution ID and release the computer through the existing run-closure hook. Catalog rebuilds retain the same identity, subordinate approval closure leaves it active, and cleanup runs outside the finished caller's authority.

This revision keeps the original contributor ancestry and narrows the repair to the existing run owner. MCP retains its current restricted action surface: recording, file-transfer, and trajectory actions still require a separate cleanup registrar. No timer, new lifecycle state, durable record, or public protocol field is added. A subsequent call can briefly observe busy while asynchronous cleanup finishes; node-disconnection recovery remains unchanged.

Production LOC: **+23 (+24/−1)** across three files, within the bug-fix exception. Five files change including one existing test suite and documentation.

## Proof

- The real MCP cache, resolver, computer tool, and provider ownership guard are exercised together. Only the external Gateway transport is adapted to the registered provider handlers.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **12/12 passed**, **59.71 s wall time**, including compiled-worker preparation. The same test with original production fails at the rebuilt catalog's screenshot with `COMPUTER_HOST_BUSY` (**1 failed / 11 passed**, 45.42 s).
- Adjacent computer-binding suite: **22/22 passed**, 38.59 s wall time. Updated Gateway test-type graph passed.
- Independent review: no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Production types and related agent/Gateway test-type graphs passed. The broad remaining test-type sweep was stopped in favor of the changed suite and required focused static checks; it is not claimed as a full pass.
- Formatting, type-aware lint, and export-name collisions passed. Knip reports the same pre-existing unused exports with the candidate and original production; no baseline was changed. Exact baseline qualification covers the approval-handler, GitHub-connections, and skill-workshop entries.

Thanks @ylcn91 for identifying the missing lifecycle and the original repair.

prs.title: refactor(automations): migrate periodic heartbeats and retire the executor
prs.body:
Related: #134994. Final sequential slice of #164265, following #166889 and #167113. Adopts the approved design from #135933 under Peter's October 3 decisions.

## Current integration status

Candidate `debdf5c798772385219100ba9fb6e9a7d318d2c9` is rebased on `1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6` and mergeable. Full exact-head CI: [38106569424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38106569424). No prior-head result is being treated as passing proof for this candidate.

Main's newer async account lookup, automatic config-repair topology, message-action preparation, session-event policy owner, and independent scheduler deadline are preserved. The periodic heartbeat executor, wake path, response tool and SDK aliases stay deleted.

The completed `02b567f7446` run had 207 successful checks, 44 skipped, one neutral and 29 failures (28 leaves and their aggregate), without cancellations. This candidate repairs owned stale imports, current browser controls, transcript-seeding and runtime-config fixtures, cursor race injection, timestamp-envelope parsing, and compaction-only fixture semantics. SDK budgets retain main's added APIs and subtract only the nine retired S3 exports/four callables; deprecated reply-runtime stays at 1. Main's separately fixed lint defects are incorporated. The early iPad checkout failure had no test proof and must complete on this head.

Main now owns accepted mutation dispatch: caller retirement after acceptance does not undo the committed operation. The updated scratch and portable-removal tests reject revoked authority after asynchronous preparation but before dispatch, retaining unchanged-data and no-publication assertions; durable definition, scratch, ref, install, lease and physical-source checks remain inside the worker. No private Cron nonce/commit handshake was restored.

Local proof includes core/owning types, runtime/Madge cycles 0/0, suppression and line-cap checks, two message-tool cases, 16 Doctor persistence cases, four routing cases, five scratch RPC cases, two portable cases, two cursor cases, two native session identity cases and the migrated-job UI case. The two E2E fixture fixes pass direct owner-function probes; their complete Gateway flows remain hosted-CI gates. Host compilation and native startup made some earlier local attempts incomplete; no timeout, retry, skip, suppression or budget increase was used to hide a failure.

The authenticated mutation proof uses real loopback WebSockets, signed device tokens and hello grants: operator.write leaves all job/scratch/provenance/install state unchanged; the identical operator.admin request performs the intended durable mutation. It passed in 24.722 seconds test time. The watchdog regression reproduces 4 failures/6 passes under a fresh-machine monotonic epoch and 10/10 after preserving native `hrtime`, without changing production deadlines.

No task lease remains active. No new remote lease was allocated in this continuation.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators manage scheduled monitoring through Automations while heartbeat still has separate scheduling, execution, delivery, and recovery machinery.

## User Impact

Existing monitors become ordinary editable Automations. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before startup after upgrading. The July-2026+ migration preserves job identity/history, scratch bytes and revisions, disabled state, schedule anchors, pending occurrences, quiet hours, model selection, target routing, and tool authority. It verifies durable conversion before retiring legacy inputs and retains ambiguous input with recovery guidance. Repeated Doctor runs preserve operator edits and deleted jobs.

Migrated jobs use **standard Automations delivery**, with no `delivery.duplicateWindowMs` or `delivery.skipIfNoRoute` options. Doctor emits this notice once when the cutover receipt completes:

> Migrated heartbeats now use standard Automations delivery. Heartbeat-specific duplicate suppression and no-route skipping were removed: repeated updates can be delivered, and a missing route no longer skips the run before execution. Delivery failures follow ordinary automation handling. Review the migrated jobs' delivery settings if you relied on either behavior.

This is a **breaking plugin-SDK change**: heartbeat execution and reply exports are removed outright, without deprecated aliases. Upgrade affected plugins using `docs/plugins/sdk-migration/removed-surfaces.md`. The deprecated `reply-runtime` export budget remains **1**. The existing nondeprecated prompt hook and protocol-v4 projections retain their documented contracts.

The approved shared-state schema fence advances **20→21** so older Gateways cannot ignore migrated job policies. No tables are added by this cutover. It preserves main’s separately landed agent schema **25**, without adding a per-agent schema migration. Keep the verified pre-update backup for rollback. Automatic updater admission normalizes supported July fields through the existing Doctor transforms; it preserves main's prior retirement of global `includeReasoning`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor conversion and periodic retirement land together because the old reconciler could otherwise recreate converted or deleted monitors. The ordinary scheduler owns periodic jobs, and the already-landed ordinary session event owner handles immediate follow-ups. The periodic runner, reconciler, dispatcher, response tool, SDK aliases, obsolete callers, and private status wrapper are deleted.

Immediate Slack interactions use ordinary occurrence receipts: failures are reported and settled. The old pre-adoption passive queue could retain a notice through a soft restart or later turn; there is no retained passive mirror or automatic failed-event replay in the new owner.

Durable migration receipts, portable Claw custody, and guarded scheduler admission account for the production growth. Idle deferral preserves unstarted slots and stream buffers; on-exit admission retains its exact receipt and command output while foreground work settles. Main's worker-backed deletion owner, terminal-write drainage, first-session identity, and memory-plugin lifecycle are preserved. Deferred notices stay with their selected scheduled occurrence and are accepted only when the complete batch fits the existing prompt limit.

## Evidence

The trusted-Git-environment finding is fixed in code using the existing `mergeProcessEnv` owner and exact named reads. The unchanged detector reports two findings before / zero after, with zero scanner errors. Existing environment/identity/node-host tests pass; independent P2 review is scoped-clean. No detector, allowlist, suppression, baseline or rule exception changed.

The original Mattermost dispatch failure did not reproduce across three main and three S3 full-file runs in the same environment (144 cases passed), and subsequently passed hosted CI. Its distinct expiry failure was repaired by main's fixture-generation change. The original failure is not claimed as a causal fix.

Provider fallback now reuses the persisted canonical user turn and applies retry context after harness selection. Its regression fails on the original producer and passes with identical serialized provider input and sender context; retained internal/decorated variants pass. Recording and live-authority guards are unchanged. Local full-Gateway attempts timed out before the target assertion, so they are not claimed as positive full-flow proof.

### Published v2026.9.9 updater and recovery proof

[The exact-155d AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_135e177e5bf7355440fb54ce06d71f76) passed the two existing official package cells with unchanged deadlines. Canonical build/pack passed in 425.961s, including tarball integrity, npm inventory and dist import-graph checks. The actual installed published baseline identifies commit `bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`; the candidate identifies `155d359fb027d2f05b964e72608ea5531bf421df`. Both report version 2026.9.9, so serving build ID, package identity and SHA-256 distinguish them. Candidate tarball: `7099381e622cb63a240253b413ee16d82d6086c90167b04ac78b564e7c9de8a0`.

- Published-driver update: **525.201s**, including the actual installed updater (401.574s), managed restart, readyz=200, exact serving identity, durable/incognito readback, repeat maintenance and service stop. Observed shared schema **19→21**, both agent stores **24→24**, with integrity and data checks preserved through update/stop/repeat.
- Package-publication recovery: **850.502s**. The actual published updater was interrupted after its publication-complete journal commit; public candidate repair, repeated repair and a distinct subsequent update all passed while preserving retained package/helper bytes and authored settings.

All 141 downloaded artifact hashes, the retained input tarball, final clean source and 103 selected source hashes were verified. Both cells left zero containers and volumes. The earlier attempt stopped before candidate execution because the proof-created tarball was unreadable to the container user; its failures remain recorded. The corrected attempt changed only that public task artifact to mode 0644 under its private 0700 parent and unchanged readonly bind mount. No product source, assertion, deadline, retry loop, suppression, baseline or budget changed.

These package cells cover disabled heartbeat configuration with real legacy session/storage data, plus genuine package activation/recovery. The prior natural flow below separately proves active heartbeat migration, scheduling and delivery. **Interrupted published-driver recovery with an active heartbeat job/history/scratch dataset remains untested.**

The build’s report-only UI check measured startup JavaScript about 0.4 KiB above its unchanged numeric ceiling. The prior hosted performance comparison also reported an overage and succeeded under the existing advisory policy. This is retained as a performance limitation, not mislabeled as a new failed hosted check or proven main-red finding.

### Real before/after migration proof

At published candidate `b5ed970d2c1d2fb2ee6f5fd884f008a53b103b22`, isolated AWS proof passed both builds, the canonical SDK API comparison (323.204s), all 16 selected Linux cases at their original limits, and the natural before/after migration flow (331.071s). Actual CLI, Doctor, Gateway, storage, scheduler, and delivery owners used synthetic loopback model/channel transports; no external-provider claim is made. Identity, schedule, routing, history, and scratch survived; the exact notice appeared once and zero times on rerun; identical updates delivered in natural slots **60,011ms apart**. Both Gateways shut down, and the lease was independently verified released. [Natural-flow run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7e3843b5e9fb0f6fed82f863010f9bd3).

The SDK comparison records nine approved export removals and four signature changes, documented in the migration guide. Earlier local startup/time-limit observations and the baseline SQLite-contention warning remain limitations; a passing replay does not establish a causal fix. Later corrections retain separate proof and require hosted CI on this exact head. The final rebase passed scripts types, both cycle checks (zero each), all four memory-host synchronization cases (184.53s), five SDK surface cases and all three suppression cases (61.06s together), docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check`. The SDK compiler case retains its existing local skip; no skip was added.

## Visual evidence

![Before: heartbeat monitor scratch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4722acc1-cd7c-4ed3-91a7-b398a623fbbd)

![After: ordinary automation scratch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2854bd77-4277-4186-8067-8725feb63b64)

![After: ordinary automation policies](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63059964-80e9-43de-ad7b-814c6c8e99ce)

![After: automation diagnostics](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5900049e-1051-4fc6-8265-9fbd2b41f3c3)


## Production size

Against base `1d952d58b156398fe62c34cbc918ce7bc1c604a6`: **+15,781/−14,344 = +1,437 production LOC**. S1 +724 and S2 +2,685 make the combined delta **+4,846**. Tests, test-support, docs, tooling and generated output are excluded. S3 tests/support together change by -9,227 lines.

Growth is durable Doctor conversion/recovery, portable Claw custody, ordinary scheduler policies, and typed UI/preparation boundaries. The retired runner, wake path, response tool, reconciler and SDK aliases remain deleted; no second execution path survives.

The final JSX-free renderer preserves inspected layout and content. The scratch image is byte-identical; the policies image differs only in button antialiasing. No real user data is included.

prs.title: improve(doctor): avoid loading channel runtimes for default capabilities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor spends seconds loading the full Telegram and WhatsApp runtimes merely to discover their default repair capabilities.

## User Impact

Doctor can inspect these channels without that startup cost. The unchanged sanitizer case dropped from 22.809s to 1.560s (93.2%) with identical warning assertions. No configuration, permission, dependency, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Declare the existing capability defaults in each plugin's package metadata so the existing catalog reader can answer without loading runtime code. Canonical catalog regeneration also includes Matrix's already-declared async authentication-presence metadata, correcting existing generated drift without changing Matrix source.

## Evidence

Both added regression cases failed before the fix on unexpected runtime-loader calls. All 15 capability cases passed in 2.57s wall; the two added cases took 11ms and 9ms. The unchanged real Doctor sanitizer case improved from 22.809s to 1.560s in test-body time; command wall time improved from 59.66s to 25.24s, including cold compilation.

Canonical catalog and bundled-channel metadata checks, unchanged WhatsApp npm-lock validation, targeted lint, formatting, and the owning Doctor test type graph (39.72s) passed. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. No channel network calls were needed or tested; this changes metadata discovery only. Hosted CI timing is pending.

The initial CI run failed Gateway smoke during update repair because Doctor's plugin inventory had already been disposed. The same failure was present on main (run 38109343421). Main repair [310bce6a751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/310bce6a751791a9f61ce7a3bfcb3fd79653642b) passed the exact Gateway smoke in 49.671 seconds. This branch now includes that fix; its capability metadata patch is unchanged. The failed run is retained as evidence, not represented as passing.

prs.title: feat(qa): compare recorded Decision answers offline
prs.body:
Related: #156341 (historical context; closed as not planned)

## What Problem This Solves

QA authors need to inspect how recorded Decision answers compare with explicit references without making another model call or dropping failed and unscored cases.

## User Impact

There is no change to normal agent behavior. The existing QA Lab confidence-report command gains an opt-in offline replay lane: JSON retains each identifiable case, its captured answer and provenance; Markdown summarizes agreement, disagreement, and unscored counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a standalone QA contribution, not a dependency of the withdrawn task-routing proposal. It changes no core routing, model selection, provider execution, SDK export, runtime configuration, or dependency. It remains useful for reviewing recorded JEV, local Decision-model, or other compatible typed results without adopting a new routing contract.

The replay compares Choice acceptable sets, explicit Boolean thresholds/operators, and inclusive Score intervals against scorer-only reviewed references. It preserves original probabilities and optional confidence. Missing, unreviewed, disputed, or unscorable references remain unscored; malformed and failed executions fail pipeline integrity separately from semantic disagreement. A valid replay can pass while answers disagree with references.

This does not run a live benchmark, certify model quality, measure calibration, enable consumers, or settle the closed RFC's broader evaluation roadmap. Repeat/group metadata is retained without treating repeats as independent samples. The existing report remains the only file-reading/output owner.

## Evidence

### October 10 maintenance rebase

Current head `ec7b620198aefa13063d23ce3f42d8b8824c47fe`, tested main `0aee279a71af78b8914dced0507ddb94c0d1f5b0`. Existing contribution behavior is preserved; no dependency, configuration or migration change is added by this refresh.

Focused Decision evaluator, confidence-report and Markdown suites: 88/88 passed; changed-source formatting/lint and whitespace checks passed. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent. The earlier actual offline CLI replay evidence is retained for unchanged contribution behavior; this is not a new CLI execution. QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains a maintainer decision.

Fresh independent Astra source/integration review found no actionable source defect. Current-head hosted CI and completed ClawSweeper review are pending after publication; older-head CI/review below are historical, not certification of this head. Main advanced to `dd036a4b1d855c366c7b3148a1814c83da765e50`; none of this PR’s changed paths intersects that base drift. Rollback is the prior head `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66`.

<details>
<summary>Retained pre-rebase evidence and review history (not current-head CI)</summary>


### October 8 rebase — current local evidence

Rebased onto main `05161b949bcded143f477df59834b831054f555e` at `d6d8e6a8871ab2f163459201b90ab5b41bb7af66` to incorporate upstream MCP advisory fix #166217. All three contribution commits are patch-equivalent and all six contribution files are byte-identical to the previous head; there is no new dependency or behavior change in this PR.

- Focused evaluator/report/Markdown suites: 88 tests passed across 3 files (Vitest 32.32s; wrapper 35.29s). Extension-test types, scoped typed lint, format/whitespace and line-cap/max-lines checks passed. Independent native Astra rebase/integration review passed with no actionable findings.
- Strict production audit returned no high-or-higher npm bulk advisories and exited 0; upstream repository advisories were not checked. This confirms the previously failing MCP advisory no longer applies to the inherited lockfile.
- Earlier actual CLI replay proof is retained for unchanged contribution behavior. No new local full-suite/build/CLI run is claimed.
- Exact-head hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37822096968) completed green: 127 contexts, zero failing or pending, including successful security-fast and effective CI/dependency/security gates. One cancelled evidence job was superseded by a successful same-head run.
- Completed exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/37823411855) reports no correctness or security findings and accepts the retained CLI proof. The completed review artifact names this head; the older public review comment is not current-head evidence. Human QA-owner sponsorship/adoption remains unresolved and is separate from technical readiness.

### October 6 rebase — retained prior-head evidence

Rebased onto main `cc7e664dfe34` at `c23fa8ec960573e8eb9e311283b41700b9469b0b`. The only conflict resolution preserves main's inferred report types. The evaluator, tests, private helper, fixture, and docs are byte-identical to the prior head; the report's emitted JavaScript is also unchanged. No scope or behavior expansion.

- Rebased focused evaluator/report/Markdown suites: 88 tests passed across 3 files. Extension-test types, scoped typed lint, format/whitespace and line-cap/max-lines checks passed. Fresh independent Astra rebase review found no actionable integration defect.
- Prior actual CLI replay proof is retained for the unchanged behavior; no fresh CLI/build or full-suite run is claimed for this rebase. New-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review must be reconciled after publication. Maintainer product acceptance remains a separate requirement.

### Retained pre-rebase evidence (`78870707014e`)

- `pnpm test:extension qa-lab`: exit 0; 332 executed test files passed, 3,877 tests passed and 3 intentionally skipped. The command also rebuilt the QA runtime. The runner discovered 347 files; its selected projects executed 332, so no claim is made that all discovered files ran.
- Focused timing at `78870707014e`: all 43 `decision-evaluation.test.ts` tests passed; `/usr/bin/time -p node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/decision-evaluation.test.ts` measured 2.82s wall time (wrapper 2.33s; Vitest 1.10s). Hosted changed-extension shard passed 322 tests across 10 files in 66.54s; its full job took 132 CI seconds, including setup. The hosted selector did not execute the focused file, so that file's CI seconds are unavailable; the shared-shard/job numbers are not attributed as its incremental CI cost. The focused file is covered by the successful local full-suite and timed focused runs.
- Scoped type-aware lint, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, formatting, whitespace, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, runtime import-cycle scan, and all-tree unused-export checks passed.
- Six targeted regression cases: five failed on the pre-repair implementation and the valid prototype-key control passed; all six passed after repair. Ambiguous duplicate outcomes are retained together without arbitrary scoring, duplicate cases remain unscored, nested nonfinite prototype-key values are rejected, and valid prototype-named data survives.
- Independent native Astra review accepted the repaired implementation with no remaining P0–P2 finding. The separate AutoReview CLI failed before producing a report; no coverage is claimed from it.
- Credential-free actual built CLI (`node openclaw.mjs qa confidence-report ...`) ran twice for each of captured replay, valid/malformed controls, and seven integrity variants. Reports matched apart from `generatedAt`; typed probabilities and absent confidence were retained. Captured replay: scheduled=3, scored=2, agreed=1, disagreed=1, unscored=1. Valid synthetic replay: scheduled=5, scored=3. Duplicate capture in either order: scheduled=5, scored=2 with both raws preserved. Duplicate cases: scheduled=6, scored=2. Nested overflow variants failed integrity; finite prototype-key data passed. Invalid manifests exited 1 as expected; captured valid replay exited 0.

The earlier isolated model-turn/Discord/telemetry capture used a synthetic Decision provider: it demonstrates capture plumbing, not real Decision-model inference quality. Refreshed-head proof exercises the real offline QA CLI; no live model or live Discord-quality claim is added.

The current-main integration preserves the newer report owner's classification/Markdown behavior. Its existing lane verdict/status/evaluation definitions move unchanged into a private QA sibling module so this PR does not grow the already over-cap report file. No safety coverage or lint threshold is removed.

Previous-head hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37145557773) passed, including the `openclaw/ci-gate` job and reconciled commit status. Dependency/security review passed. The [previous-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156484#issuecomment-5794588711) found no actionable code/security findings and accepted the real CLI evidence; maintainer acceptance of the new standalone QA capability remains required before merge. The previous September-head failures were in Telegram/Gateway tests, not QA replay; they are not claimed fixed or definitively runner-caused, and unrelated repairs are excluded from this PR.

AI-assisted: yes. Rollback is a revert of this QA-only change. Exact-head CI and technical review are complete; maintainer QA-owner acceptance remains required before merge.

</details>

prs.title: fix(node): recover worker capacity after host reboot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A node-host reboot could leave a native worker launch permanently running in its journal. Its dead process owner could no longer record descendant cleanup, so capacity stayed reserved, the session could not recover, and a subsequent Gateway restart could fail while stopping that environment.

## User Impact

After a reboot, a reconnected node releases the extinct native worker's slot, records the interrupted turn, and accepts the session's next turn. Existing same-boot cleanup checks remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the OS boot identity with each new launch and settle native launches whose recorded boot differs from the current boot. Reuse the existing platform reader and cache its result once per node process. Pending supervisor adoption transfers an existing boot record atomically. Pending and running container cleanup still verifies the original engine and container; a remote daemon can outlive the node host.

The optional first-use companion table needs no version bump, migration, or legacy backfill. Old rows and unavailable boot identities retain conservative recovery. macOS uses its stable boot-session UUID rather than wall-clock-sensitive boot time; Windows uses the existing bounded LastBootUpTime reader. Failure to read a boot identity remains an accepted recovery gap. Moving existing turn settlement into its shared worker module keeps the journal under its file-size limit.

Production TypeScript: **+130 / -79 = +51 lines**, within the explicitly authorized +60-line reboot-fix budget. Seventeen changed files. No public protocol/configuration change.

## Evidence

- Original pond failure: hard reboot stranded a native launch at 3/4 available slots; subsequent turn and Gateway restart failed.
- Restoring the old recovery implementation: all three reboot regressions failed, while three same/missing-identity controls passed.
- Fixed owner/sibling run: 135 tests passed across seven files (192.77 s wall).
- Final dedicated reboot tests: 9 passed (45.39 s wall); container tests: 15 passed (55.31 s); launch/turn stores: 48 passed (68.39 s combined).
- Two-host Linux pond: automatic hard-reboot reconnect restored 4/4 slots, the original session received its reboot interruption, and its next turn returned the exact expected reply. No pairing repair was needed.
- Independent review: accepted P1 container-cleanup finding fixed; final P0/P1 review clean.
- Gateway restart replay, final static gates, and published-driver update cell are still running; results will be recorded before landing.

prs.title: refactor(workers): simplify environment lifecycle bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Simplify worker-environment bookkeeping without removing worker features,
credential/approval checks, workspace durability, or ordinary shutdown settlement.
This is the p04 pragmatic-simplification lane, re-evaluated under the maintainer's
explicit best-effort policy for synthetic timing and mid-operation config changes.

The core change is ownership simplification: one check at an actual effect,
idempotent operations, and existing write settlement instead of repeated snapshot
comparisons, recovery loans, compensating cleanup chains, and reentrant guards.

## User Impact

Normal worker setup, inference, workspace recovery, credentials and shutdown stay
supported. Rare mid-operation config/reload or artificial interleaving cases may
now return an error or need a later request/restart instead of being coordinated
through additional state machines. The accepted cases are listed below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The removed machinery was justified by synthetic regressions rather than human
actual-use incidents. Retain the minimal effect and settlement boundaries instead
of paying their complexity cost on every normal operation.

## What changed

- Placement setup/recovery drops loan queues, permanent supersession history,
  self-validated receipts, and retry-until-stable reads. Per-session FIFO, final
  node/run/tool authorization and workspace-result ownership remain.
- Provider preparation takes one config/target snapshot. Mid-operation expiry,
  policy and cosmetic metadata changes no longer trigger extra cancellation and
  teardown. Paid allocation IDs, timeout settlement and normal expiry cleanup remain.
- Store projections drop reconciliation retry registries, revision tombstones,
  repeated read-time shape checks and reentrant cache fences. A failed readback
  closes the projection; a new store or Gateway restart reloads durable SQLite.
- Worker writes use the final live admission check without a redundant initial
  handshake. The narrow shared lease-owner adjustment preserves first-write
  preparation, live member/expiry checks, pre-commit authority and settlement.
- Synthetic-only tests are removed with their machinery. Ordinary expiry cases
  are moved unchanged to preserve the heartbeat PR's test inventory.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Plugin reload during enrollment may retire its old bootstrap archive; the next
  attempt uses the current producer. Borrower tracking in #133037 was separate
  from its synthetic source-build reproduction.
- Package/build metadata or umask changes during packaging are not polled a
  second time. Initial build validation and archive/path/digest checks remain
  (#133037; no human report for mid-build metadata mutation).
- Profile, provider target, catalog and expiry changes during preparation apply
  on the next request/pass. #143372/#143410 introduced synthetic late-change guards,
  not a human report requiring mid-request policy replacement.
- Trusted internal callers are assumed not to mutate prepared intent/request
  objects. Private repository and setup authority remain live at their effects
  (#143372/#157422; synthetic mutation/reentrancy cases).
- Presence changes do not carry version epochs across bookkeeping writes.
  Allocation still checks current human presence and source authorization (#160108).
- Recovery does not borrow another operation's admission queue. Results-only
  recovery can retry on a later pass while normal lifecycle operations retain FIFO
  (#160535).
- Stop/Move overlapping an existing setup waiter may let it return; the consuming
  turn still validates live placement (#145068).
- Destroy discovers durable owners once before taking its FIFO reservation,
  rather than maintaining phased discovery/reservation handoffs (#160299).
- An ordinary placement read racing a mutation may report authority changed rather
  than loop through settlement notifications (#165166).
- Same-process claim changes are published directly rather than wrapped and
  immediately revalidated against a freshly generated receipt UUID (#168094).
- Runtime refresh relies on the existing result-handoff writer and final effect
  checks rather than a second retained claim-authority loan (#159484).
- Serialized teardown uses its captured row rather than comparing every
  cosmetic state field after every await; exact epoch/lease/node checks remain
  at credential and destruction effects (#130733; no human same-lock replacement report).
- Selected prepared capacity is not reselected after every await; normal capacity,
  expiry and final node authorization remain (#143372).
- Shutdown diagnostics may describe a just-finished owner; durable shutdown
  retention and provider settlement are unchanged (#164252).
- A rare claim collision that disappears while inspected returns the existing busy
  error instead of transparently retrying (#123157).
- Disconnect after completed teardown may surface the existing disconnect error;
  the next operation sees completion (#112928).
- An uncertain receipt followed by a failed snapshot read requires a new store or
  restart. SQLite data is preserved and authority fails closed; the removed retry
  registry had synthetic provenance (#154804).
- Immutable projection/request fields are not repeatedly validated on every read
  or compared to captured copies. Initial decoding and real effect checks remain
  (#154804/#157422; internal mutation and reentrancy, not external-input validation).
- Companion-schema initialization remembers success after commit without a
  staged rollback latch. Nested initialization may repeat idempotent DDL within
  one transaction (#154804; no persisted schema change).
- Same-scope local-store reentrancy is not supported by a pending latch; callers
  already sequence operations under their lease (#165534).
- Cosmic-scale revision exhaustion is not guarded; normal finite lifetimes cannot
  approach JavaScript's safe-integer limit (#165534).
- Cosmetic status can lag one pass. After a profile is edited while a worker runs,
  that worker's summary can use the newer catalog's labels until it is replaced;
  execution placement and credential authority do not use those labels (#143864;
  synthetic reload/config-change coverage, not a human incident).
- Shared write admission accepts commit-first and does not police a synthetic
  two-stage message sequence; the final lease/member/expiry/authority check remains
  (#148859).

No PR or synthetic reproduction is being presented as evidence of a human incident.
Retained protections are justified by the explicit security, data-durability,
ordinary shutdown, public-contract, resource-bound, or measured-cache rules.
The warm placement read cache retains the measured 11.8 SQL-statement / 3.9 worker
request saving reported in #167194; its reentrant invalidation fence is removed.

<details>
<summary>Original KEEP ledger re-evaluation</summary>

Six of nine original KEEP rows are now partial removals; the previously deferred
profile-drift row is also implemented.

| Original row | Decision under the sharpened bar |
| --- | --- |
| Artifact shared producer | KEEP one shared builder and join it at shutdown before deleting files: ordinary write-capable shutdown settlement. Borrower retirement pins were already removed. |
| Artifact builder revalidation | PARTIAL REMOVE duplicate build/package/umask/source-byte rechecks; KEEP initial build/import/path/archive checks for public bootstrap and file/transfer integrity. |
| Provider owner lifecycle | PARTIAL REMOVE full-row comparison and repeated internal checks; KEEP exact credential/destroy effect checks and paid allocation settlement. |
| Runtime refresh | PARTIAL REMOVE duplicate guards and map-identity fences; KEEP user workspace handoff, worker stop, install and credential effect owners. |
| Node retention | PARTIAL REMOVE repeated transport/status fences; KEEP one destructive pruning guard, pending manifests and bounded requests for user-data durability. |
| Workspace operation queue | KEEP real per-workspace write ordering and join entered mutation before cancellation returns: data durability and write-capable settlement. |
| Worker session topology | KEEP live source turn, incarnation and authorized session tree at messaging/child effects: security boundary. |
| Prepared intent owner | PARTIAL REMOVE mutation snapshots and runtime metadata checks; KEEP only private-source authority association and setup admission at effect. |
| Machine metadata | PARTIAL REMOVE reload identity, stale completion and old-worker cosmetic comparison; KEEP the public machine-summary projection and normal refresh. |

No remaining row relies solely on a PR narrative, harness failure or synthetic
test as a claimed real incident. Additional store/cache, presence and coordinator
mechanisms are listed with their individual tradeoffs above.

</details>

## Scope and measurement

Aggregate production reduction: **818 lines** (+338 / -1156), including the first
p04 commit. Tests: **1699 lines removed net** (+522 / -2221), counted separately.
This uses the campaign's 500–999-line honest-pass exception; the whole-scope
KEEP re-evaluation above is the coverage log.
No schema, persisted data shape, config, dependency, or public Gateway
protocol change. No new lint suppressions, timeouts, retries or skips.

Heartbeat PR #167796's changed files are excluded. Three shared state-lease owner
files are a required caller cutover and are explicitly called out for p15–p17.

## Evidence

- Final independent review: scoped-clean through P2 after retaining one live
  enrollment-owner check and one combined forced-destroy reservation for durable,
  attached and in-flight owners. No multi-phase handoff restored.
- Testbox (Blacksmith) `tbx_01m4ksbxde2y7qmmjc3d72heyh`, workflow
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38085395330:
  earlier candidate tree `39c606689e2dfd558ebfc9df753fdf818e80b41f` verified before
  and after a frozen-lockfile install; 138 focused tests in five files passed,
  then all 11 lease-owner tests passed. The full scope run reached approximately
  3,000 passing cases but was cut off by the 60-minute Testbox workflow limit;
  this is partial proof, not a passing suite. Its eight observed failures led to
  removing stale cache/call-order expectations and retaining the small checks
  described below. The focused runtime-tested tree is
  `4b174954fcf63824a4290b1b49e643a2e2190e74`;
  the replacement lease timed out unallocated after 15 minutes and was stopped.
  Per the coordinator's capacity fallback, exact-head hosted CI is the remaining
  full Linux gate. Signed head:
  original head `2fc286fbe6cdd2a77ad4b545071f34e1249e0fe8` (the follow-up only removes an unused
  test import and renames a local variable; separately reviewed, linted and
  typechecked; final tree `3f98af3ff44ed7fcd3e8fe12185a89c358edfcef`).
- Both cycle checks passed: 0 runtime value cycles, 0 Madge cycles. Suppression
  suite: all 3 passed, with no baseline changes.
- Changed-file gate passed formatting, guard/ratchet, plugin boundary and wrapper
  checks, then stopped at the pre-existing UI graph budget (722 roots / limit 720).
  The UI graph and its budget are untouched. Upstream fixed this with a real graph
  split in `471035c7b7c8ea066ed302006ab3780994d27324`; no budget bypass or baseline
  weakening is part of this PR. Direct production, Gateway-test and state-test
  type graphs passed. All remaining targeted guards and lint passed. The script
  Knip scan also found the inherited `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs: default` export;
  upstream `ad598152583` models its real config consumer. Production/full-tree
  Knip scans each report zero unused exports. No affected file is named by either
  inherited failure.
- All 144 cases in the eight revised/affected suites passed sequentially on the
  signed candidate: placement claims, paired devices, recovery admission, human
  presence, node retention, allocation cleanup, pool lifecycle and pool expiry.
- Conflict-only rebase onto main preserves #168639's bounded local-turn cache
  and its measured 18-SQL/7-request saving. The single-read replacement follows
  the upstream extraction into `placement-read-authority.ts`; no cache was discarded. Rebased head
  `fe91d4453ff5257109a7b9e6ae3b854be6c98552` passed fresh P2 review, production
  and Gateway test types, all 73 cases in the four cache/authority suites,
  targeted lint, both zero-cycle checks, and all three suppression tests.
  Current heartbeat head `02b567f7446d48a928ab61a1f8ac746d3fa72637` has 1,468
  changed paths and zero overlap with this PR.
- The new forced-destroy regression failed against the intermediate over-simplified
  implementation and passed after the minimal fix. One-worker command:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-coordinator-destroy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:
  four tests pass, 30.09 seconds wrapper / 12.72 seconds suite / 0.77 seconds tests
  on the loaded shared Mac. It protects ordinary dispatch settlement before
  destructive teardown; no sleeps, retries or new timeouts.
- Kept one environment-ownership check at destructive node pruning. Restored
  persisted reserve expiry at the start of maintenance, without restoring the
  mid-operation retirement state machine. The held-presence regression failed
  before this fix and passed unchanged afterward (12.34 seconds test time on the
  loaded shared Mac; compiled-worker setup is additional).
- Initial exact-head CI (run 38100418923, head fe91d445) failed two shards:
  `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11-2` pinned permanent setup supersession
  from unimplemented/rejected fixture Stop/Move calls; `checks-node-changed-compact-large-2`
  pinned mid-flight config-disable rejection while Git credentials and live human
  presence remained valid. Four sibling shards were cancelled and are not counted
  as passing proof. No jobs were rerun.
- Test-only follow-up head `e666948a88acaed8ed6e90b5e332a9e0e26c8412` removes those
