prs.title: fix(agents): treat a Stop-hook bounce as a hard CLI stream segment boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #168676. When a Claude Code `Stop` hook rejects a reply with `{"decision":"block"}`, the model writes a corrected reply. If the model calls any tool before writing the correction, the CLI output parser delivered the rejected draft too — joined to the correction with a blank line, or delivered on its own when the correction is a silent token such as `NO_REPLY` — even though Claude Code's own `result.result` contains only the correction. The reporter measured 20 of 122 Stop-hook bounces over four weeks leaking the refused draft to the channel. Pre-tool narration joined onto the final answer has the same shape.

The draft survives because it lands in the parser's streamed-text candidate span: the message after a tool-only message is a tool-split boundary, so the span is never restarted past the rejected draft, and the terminal result prefers the preserved span whenever it differs from `result.result` while the last message equals it.

## The Fix

A Stop-hook bounce already has an explicit on-the-wire signature, and the parser was the one place not reading it: Claude Code replays the refusal as a top-level `user` record whose content is a text block ("Stop hook feedback: …") and/or a `system` notification whose key starts with `stop-hook`, always between the rejected message's `message_stop` and the rewrite's first delta.

`isClaudeStopHookFeedbackRecord` (in `cli-output-records.ts`, beside the other record predicates) classifies exactly those records: a `system`/`notification` keyed `stop-hook`, or a top-level `user` record with a text block and no `tool_result` block — real tool-result records never carry text alongside the result, and subagent echoes (`parent_tool_use_id` set) are excluded at the call site. `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` treats such a record as a hard segment boundary: it finishes the pending tagged-reasoning and commentary buffers, then restarts `segmentStart`/`currentMessageStart`/`preserveFrom` at the current offset and clears the pending-boundary flags, so the refused draft stops being a candidate to outrank the result envelope while the correction (which has not started yet) is never cut into.

The narration-then-answer case from the issue (effect 2) is intentionally left alone: changing the delivered text for turns without a bounce is a behavior change that needs its own decision, and this fix is complete for the reported P1.

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts`, replaying the issue's minimal stream shape through `parseCliOutput` (offline, no network, no workers):

- bounce → tool-only message → correction delivers only the correction (`"B"`, not `"A\n\nB"`);
- bounce → tool → `NO_REPLY` rewrite delivers only `"NO_REPLY"`, never the refused draft alone;
- two bounces in one turn, each rewrite routed through a tool, delivers only the final correction;
- unchanged, pinned both pre-existing: a bounce rewritten without a tool still delivers only the correction; a subagent text record and a non-`stop-hook` notification are not boundaries, so the existing pre-tool draft joining (`"Draft.\n\nTEST DONE"`) keeps passing.

Pre-fix red (parser fix reverted, tests only): exactly the three bounce-through-tool tests fail — `delivers only the rewrite...` expected `"B"` received `"A\n\nB"`, `bounced silent-token rewrite` expected `"NO_REPLY"` received `"A\n\nNO_REPLY"`, `each Stop-hook bounce...` expected `"C"` received `"A\n\nB\n\nC"` — while the four unchanged-behavior tests pass. Post-fix: all 27 tests in the file pass, plus the 38 tests in `cli-output-records.test.ts`; `oxlint` clean on all three touched files.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): avoid repeated missing avatar requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link repeatedly requests absent profile, agent, and workspace images; suppressing those requests must still preserve real profile photos in mentions and owner chips.

## User Impact

Profiles with advertised photos retain them. ID-only profile references show initials until the shared directory arrives, then display the versioned photo in the same space. Profiles without avatars produce no speculative avatar request. Hydrated agent identity owns image absence, and definite authenticated image misses can reuse a short private cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

One Gateway-scoped directory now supplies profile availability to mention chips, owners, and other typed-profile avatar consumers. It replaces the separate person-card and owner-menu directory reads, resolves canonical merged profiles, retires stale replies across connection changes, and retries failed or missing person-card lookups. Explicit presence/upload URLs remain authoritative over an older directory snapshot. The shared avatar renderer updates existing DOM without introducing layout wrappers.

The HTTP changes retain the existing authentication boundaries: definite user-image misses are cacheable for 60 seconds only when the requested revision matches the current profile. Unversioned/stale profile requests and transient errors remain uncached. Agent misses are private; workspace misses are cached only after resolving the workspace root. No configuration, protocol schema, or durable server shape changes.

Production LOC: **+394 / −195, net +199** using `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`. Growth is required to preserve photos for ID-only consumers through a shared, scoped, reactive directory. The former per-card/per-menu reads and speculative URL inference are removed.

## Evidence

Head: `7969c195a70b961f6b5415463e2e33ff0779487e`. Ready for review; not merged.

The campaign re-measurement observed approximately ten user-avatar 404s, one agent-avatar 404, and one workspace-icon 404 per signed-in dashboard reload. The synthetic Chromium cache benchmark produced **12 first-load / 12 reload network misses** with `no-store`, versus **12 first-load / 0 reload network misses** with the private 60-second cache. This is a cache measurement, not a claim about deployed end-to-end latency.

The restored mention browser proof measures **0 image requests while availability is unknown**, then **1 successful versioned request for the advertised photo and 0 for the profile without an avatar**. Both 1280px/light and 390px/dark, enlarged-text cases retain identical chip rectangles before and after the directory reply. Merged-profile references display the canonical photo while preserving the original mention label.

Synthetic before/after directory publication (same geometry):

![Before directory reply: initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b21375e5-750d-4abc-99a4-f25a535ce4bd)

![After directory reply: advertised photo, absent profile still initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79bcbc3b-a23f-48d3-b436-0e762eccef6b)

Validation so far:

- Testbox `tbx_01m4mf8j8y5fm7wfdd0xhjr84w`: initial restored mention E2E **9/9**, related avatar/owner E2Es **21/21**, owner-chip browser cases **117/117**. The subsequent two person-card recovery cases are included in final-head validation below.
- Focused directory, shared-avatar, owner-chip, and owner-assignment unit files passed individually. Final viewer file: **21/21** including live avatar updates over cached missing/older directory entries. `pnpm test ui/src/lib/profile-directory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **9.61 s wall time**, 2/2.
- Fresh detached review through P2: clean after fixing directory retry behavior and preserving newly advertised photos.
- Two later Testbox raw-sync attempts timed out. The host exceeded the permitted local-test load, so final validation uses AWS lease `cbx_258b8057d11b` with a clean checkout of this exact PR head.
- Final-head focused tests, full UI E2E, and exact-head CI are running. Their terminal results and any current-main failure comparisons will be recorded here before handoff.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI's tool results, attachment previews, and review panels still depended on Lit during the Solid 2 cutover.

## User Impact

No intentional visual or behavioral change. Tool details stay lazy, reused tool IDs retain independent tabs, full-output reads reject stale results, and HTML/SVG resources keep their owning lifetimes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace eight registered Lit elements and the tool-card rendering helpers with Solid. Existing Lit callers use the bridge; stateless PR/publication and composer attachment helpers remain with their unported callers. Domain state remains plain TypeScript. The shared dropdown adapter also preserves main’s connectivity-only focus behavior after integration.

Direct Solid mounting exposed initial loader effects running during a parent render and SVG observation starting before host attachment. The port separates those imperative effects, preserves source/connection fences, and proves direct mounting. Session-diff requests also retain their original dependency equality, so unrelated action callbacks do not refetch. Mixed Lit/Solid child content uses a stable Lit-owned container, preventing expansion from losing children captured before insertion while retaining collapsed laziness. Visual comparison caught the old Lit base’s implicit `display: contents`; the SVG and HTML hosts now preserve it through scoped CSS.

## Evidence

Independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings. Focused lint, formatting, i18n baseline verification, and whitespace checks passed.

| Focused proof | Result | Local wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool cards / purpose / sidebar / redaction | 71 passed | Individual wrappers: 4.49–17.16s |
| Message rendering / extracted attachment-source cases | 100 passed before the three-case extraction | 38.54s; final split verified in PR CI |
| Tool output, including direct Solid mounting | 26 passed | 42.13s |
| Session diff, stale results, collapsed refresh, callback equality | 17 passed | 6.81s |
| HTML transport / direct HTML and SVG consumers | 31 + 2 passed | 5.18s / 7.85s |
| Attachment cards / attachment lifetime suite | 2 retained functional cases + 26 lifetime cases | Final-head CI pending; unused callback-only case removed |

| CI repair regressions: activity headline / disclosure / MCP raw details | 22 + 27 + 1 passed | Vitest 31.41s for MCP; saturated-host wrapper 142.83s |
| Types, lint, ratchets, UI unit/browser/E2E and three retention suites | Passing on prior candidate except inherited metadata count cases; final cleanup head running | PR CI |
| Visual parity: five states × desktop/mobile | All 10 pairs exactly equal; 0 changed or raster-noise pixels | [Hosted capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38107440399) |

The isolated early tests used the exact shared primitive source while its PR was in flight; the primitive is now on the branch's main base. PR CI supplies final-head proof. Testbox stayed queued for 15 minutes without a runner and was stopped; no alternate provider or local E2E was used.

The temporary GitHub-hosted capture workflow has been removed after publishing its evidence. No Docker or E2E ran on the shared Mac.

### Screenshots

Inspected and verified original PNGs are embedded in the [desktop proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168739#issuecomment-6105177030) and [mobile proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168739#issuecomment-6105179160), and attached in the originating chat. prs.title: refactor(reply): simplify session coordination and bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Simplify reply/session coordination around its existing owners: remove synthetic-race snapshot protocols, redundant bookkeeping validation, and silent diagnostic fallback paths. Preserve session/queue features, live security checks, user-data durability, ordinary shutdown settlement, and measured caches.

The committed candidate removes 852 net production TypeScript lines (+488/-1340; tests, fixtures and generated files excluded). This uses the campaign's 500-999-line coverage exception after a scope-wide implementation and provenance recheck.

## User Impact

Reply, session, queue, export and cancellation features remain. Rare mid-call cache/config/registry changes use the best-effort behavior below rather than extra snapshot protocols. Security effect checks, transcript durability, FIFO ordering, ordinary shutdown settlement and measured caches remain. No config, schema, persisted-shape, retention, permission or dependency change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the requested p10 pragmatic-simplification lane. Each removed guard was checked against its introduction and actual callers; a maintainer/agent PR or forced race was not treated as a human incident. Nine of eleven prior KEEP decisions became partial/full removals. One owner performs the write; cache and bookkeeping callers retain the minimum effect check instead of parallel reconciliation protocols.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Mixed-version chunks in one process no longer backfill private registry state or compensate for pre-generation eviction callbacks (1bcc4c5e706/#103618, 4ff2cdd215c/#111699 and registry field-introduction PRs #121995/#138451/#141900/#125654/#129001/#156858). No human hot-load incident was established; current-version constructors initialize complete state, and an incompatible hot load now requires restart.
- A transient reply owner that enters and leaves during one admission read is not remembered by a registry-wide departure observer. Admission observes its captured predecessor and current owner. The removed protocol came from synthetic interleavings in #156858.
- Independent per-work finalization deadlines from 65aa7781714/#106792 are replaced by an active-work count and one longest active deadline. No human incident requires the per-task map; a completed long task may leave extra bounded grace while another task remains active. Ordinary delivery settlement is retained.
- Inbound debounce no longer uses key generations or a special synchronous reentry reservation (fd1ab08d352/#107422). No actual recursive-caller incident was established; ordinary FIFO and individual pending-input cancellation retain human Signal Stop behavior (#103309).
- An append during an asynchronous quiet-period check may share the earlier batch decision (db966d62ae0/#163863 was an induced-CPU Test Server harness, not a human incident). The maximum wait, FIFO and explicit flush contract remain; the batch can flush without a fresh quiet window.
- A delayed recovery closure may retire the current attempt of the same queue instead of refusing on a generation/source-set mismatch. One queue identity check and current active-input exclusion retain the recovery needed by human report #130810.
- Queue preparation and Stop no longer require pointer-identical config/run/lifecycle snapshots (9cbcd210805/#165370 and da27b336c0e/#154991 contain synthetic boundary proof, not a human pointer-replacement incident). Current target and authority checks still decide effects; harmless object replacement no longer invalidates work or prevents Stop.
- Repeatedly deferred overflow summaries use the ordinary cap/eviction policy instead of retaining another protected generation (1b8d8376744/#100123 provides a queue feature, not a deferred-generation incident). Continued input can evict an old deferred summary under the existing cap.
- A value-identical fallback reselected during recovery is not a distinct cache generation (ad1071bcd05/#108137 introduced synthetic cache-race cases). One persisted probe check protects explicit model/auth choices; the owner's persisted result replaces cache-only edits.
- Session initialization no longer reruns full preparation around binding touches and rollover waits (286ff4feba3/#154864, b28d51e01e7/#140417 describe synthetic transitions). One route-authority check and a lightweight identity check before cancellation remain. The bounded outer retry needed by human report #102400 remains; cache-only changes do not restart preparation.
- Skill cache preparation runs once and patches only owned fields (4e668c36a35/#146373 introduced generation reconciliation during an async-startup refactor). Cache-only changes can wait for the next turn; sandbox/exec and approval authority still revalidate at effects. The measured reusable-cache benefit from #167686 remains.
- Baseline capture drops repeated generation reads and capture-nonce settlement (91d3f533f17/#124796 uses forced delayed claims/replacements). Existing pending/result persistence and initial capture-before-tools retain restart durability; a synthetic overlapping claim no longer has a separate nonce settlement protocol.
- Lifecycle counts derive from the active set, without duplicate indexes or stale-generation filters (1bcc4c5e706/#103618, 9319ba0799c/#138071). Default admission validates once after earlier writes; explicit security validators remain (487ab99dc23/#104137). Mixed runtime generations are best effort, not a second scheduling authority.
- Upstream monitoring drops repeated provenance reads and transaction/commit idle handshakes (bb6874fddfa/#107009, ff51e006718/#162518, 313e200f0a7/#165796 use synthetic interleavings). One post-provider idle check, source CAS, event-before-marker durability and dedupe remain. An overlapping local turn can miss or receive one advisory notice; canonical upstream content is retained. The measured cache from #167549 remains.
- Native initialization no longer rechecks registry/function identity (f5f44faeca4/#134660 has no human hot-swap incident). The captured provider can finish; native-write policy and rollback capabilities remain checked.
- Participant settlement no longer resolves aliases for every pending record (1b66d30351d/#157268). A same-agent/key join in another custom store may also be awaited; writes are not redirected, and shutdown still joins them.
- Session-created notices no longer recheck config/store freshness (43ff5f17069/#164367). A mid-call config change may leave the notice in the originally selected Home store; normal routing and privacy checks remain.
- Diagnostic prompt building surfaces actual preparation failures instead of inventing empty tools/skills (49b5b862acf/#90431, 90104b0e5ea provide no human recovery incident). SQLite export drops the unused filesystem probe left by 5a292d07eb8/#167821; canonical transcript export and output-path security remain.
- Typing uses its existing bounded TTL when idle is never reported, instead of a second 10-second timer (79176cc4e50/684eaf289354 provides no human incident). prs.title: fix(minimax): match CN host on a dot boundary for region detection
prs.body:
## Summary

fix(minimax): bind CN region detection to the `minimaxi.com` host on a dot boundary, so look-alike hosts such as `notminimaxi.com` no longer route web search to the CN endpoint

## What Problem This Solves

The MiniMax web search provider infers the region (`cn` vs `global`) from `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or the configured provider base URL, and picks the search endpoint accordingly (`https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search` for CN, `https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` for global).

**代码证据**: in `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`, `isMiniMaxCnHost` used:

- `new URL(trimmed).hostname.endsWith("minimaxi.com")` — matches any host that merely *ends* with the string, e.g. `notminimaxi.com` or `evilnotminimaxi.com`.
- `trimmed.includes("minimaxi.com")` as the fallback for scheme-less values — a pure substring check that also matches look-alike hosts.

So a misspelled or maliciously crafted host like `MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com` was classified as CN, and search traffic (including the query and the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header) would be sent to the CN search endpoint derived from that wrong classification.

Trigger condition: any host value that ends with the literal string `minimaxi.com` without being `minimaxi.com` or a subdomain of it.

## Root Cause

- Violated invariant: region inference is a security-relevant routing decision (it selects which endpoint receives queries and credentials), but the host check was a suffix/substring match instead of a dot-boundary host match.
- `endsWith("minimaxi.com")` has no label boundary: `notminimaxi.com`.endsWith(`minimaxi.com`) is `true`. The scheme-less fallback `includes(...)` is weaker still.

## Why This Fix

- Option A: keep `endsWith` but prepend a dot (`endsWith(".minimaxi.com")`). Handles the URL-parseable path but leaves the scheme-less substring fallback untouched.
- Option B (chosen): extract a single `isCnHostname` predicate — `hostname === "minimaxi.com" || hostname.endsWith(".minimaxi.com")` — and use it for both paths; for scheme-less values, prepend `https://` so only the host is inspected (never the path or query), and return `false` if the value still cannot be parsed.
- Not chosen: a regex over the raw string — duplicates URL parsing logic and still mixes host and non-host content.

## User Impact

- Affected scenarios: users setting `MINIMAX_API_HOST` or a provider `baseUrl` to a host that shares the `minimaxi.com` suffix (typo'd or look-alike domains).
- Before: such hosts were classified as CN and search requests were routed to the CN endpoint.
- After: only `minimaxi.com` and its subdomains classify as CN; everything else falls back to global.
- Behavior change: legitimate CN endpoints (`https://api.minimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com`, `https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) are unaffected — still classified as CN.

## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** look-alike hosts sharing the `minimaxi.com` suffix were classified as CN, routing MiniMax web search to the wrong (CN) endpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `wt-minimax-cn-host-boundary` on latest `origin/main`, Node v24.19.0, importing the real `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` via tsx and calling the exported `testing.resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `testing.resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` set per case. No mocks of the functions under test.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  $ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs minimax-cn-host-boundary.proof.mjs
  $ npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (8/8 PASS):**
  ```bash
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://minimaxi.com -> region=cn
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://api.minimax.io -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=global
  PASS MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://example.com/redir?u=minimaxi.com -> region=global
  RESULT: ALL PASS
  ```

**Before (on main, same script, exit code 1):**

```bash
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global), endpoint=https://api.minimaxi.com/v1/coding_plan/search
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1 -> region=cn (expected global)
FAIL MINIMAX_API_HOST=notminimaxi.com -> region=cn (expected global)
RESULT: 3 case(s) show WRONG region/endpoint
```

- **What was not tested:** a live search request against the real MiniMax endpoints (requires valid credentials); the proof exercises the real region/endpoint resolution code paths end to end.

## Tests and Validation

- `npx vitest run extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts` — 23/23 passed, including new regression cases: apex CN domain still classifies as CN; `https://notminimaxi.com`, `https://evilnotminimaxi.com/v1`, scheme-less `notminimaxi.com`, `https://minimaxi.com.evil.com`, and a query-string-only mention all classify as global.
- `npx oxlint --deny=warn` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Before/after real-behavior proof logs are embedded above.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: unit tests on the real exported `resolveMiniMaxRegion` / `resolveMiniMaxEndpoint` (via the module's `testing` surface), with `MINIMAX_API_HOST` as the input vector.
- Target test file: `extensions/minimax/src/minimax-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: suffix-sharing look-alike hosts (`notminimaxi.com`, with scheme, with path, scheme-less) and non-host mentions (query string) never classify as CN, while the real CN hosts (`api.minimaxi.com`, apex `minimaxi.com`) still do.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it pins the exact predicate that makes the routing decision, using the exact inputs that previously misclassified.

prs.title: fix: stop worker provisioning effects after host authority closes
prs.body:
<!-- Keep Allow edits from maintainers enabled where safe under the fork Actions/secrets policy. -->
Related: #135838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could see worker provisioning continue after its host operation closed, leaving allocated resources without settled cleanup or rejecting valid enrollment from the same operation.

## User Impact

Worker provisioning stops admitting new effects after host shutdown or invocation closure, while cleanup keeps its independent authority. Expiring prepared workers retain successful or uncertain capture custody until independent teardown. A checkpoint returned after source closure is kept for cleanup, not made reusable; teardown cannot start a new project capture without live source authority.

Existing external providers keep the source-compatible default `WorkerProvider` type and optional provisioning arguments. `WorkerProvider<1>` opts into required invocation guards; bundled providers use that contract. **No legacy cutoff, removal date, configuration, protocol or database-schema change.** Legacy implementations that ignore the supplied callback remain a documented limitation. This is the provider slice, not completion of the entire linked workstream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing live owner assertion through provider preparation, allocation and effect boundaries rather than treating a physical cancellation signal as authority. Extend the existing cleanup catch across dispatched allocation, preserve settled cleanup receipts without a second stop, and keep same-operation enrollment valid. The same captured source assertion now gates final reusable-image publication. If publication is refused, only the surviving exact capture selector becomes cleanup debt; ambiguous persistence, admitted publication and successor selectors retain their existing recovery behavior. Independent teardown still collects cleanup debt, but does not recapture an expired project. No new state owner or schema is introduced.

Contributor credit: @sallyom and @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/70f8933b-db6b-4809-b9a8-941957263614)

prs.title: fix(gateway): reject non-profile session members
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session.members.add` accepts channel-scoped creation actors such as Slack channel IDs even though viewer authorization can only match durable profile identities. The write succeeds but produces an inert membership row.

Closes #133956

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter session-derived membership candidates to human actors created from a durable `profile` source. Existing authenticated profiles and stored profile records remain selectable. Previously persisted orphan rows are still projected by the list handler so owners can inspect and remove them without a migration.

## User Impact

Session owners can no longer select or add channel IDs that will never grant access. Existing invalid rows remain visible and removable.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway behavior

Verified on rebased head `0ef2aa48c0` using a built Gateway on loopback with an isolated temporary state directory. No mock Gateway or handler-direct call was used.

1. `session.members.listEvidence` omitted the channel-created actor `slack:channel:C012345`, retained the durable profile, and kept the historical orphan visible:

```json
{
  "members": [{ "identityId": "slack:channel:C099999", "addedBy": "historical-owner" }],
  "identities": [
    { "type": "human", "id": "12902ac7-a7f0-4b49-804d-2b9e94ad9054", "label": "Durable profile" },
    { "type": "human", "id": "slack:channel:C099999" }
  ]
}
```

2. A real WebSocket RPC add for the filtered channel actor failed as intended:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "unknown identity",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

CLI exit status: `1`.

3. A real `session.members.remove` removed the historical orphan, and the post-delete list contained only the durable profile:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:proof-target",
  "identityId": "slack:channel:C099999"
}
```

```json
{
  "members": [],
  "identities": [
    { "type": "human", "id": "12902ac7-a7f0-4b49-804d-2b9e94ad9054", "label": "Durable profile" }
  ]
}
```

Gateway verbose logs recorded successful `session.members.remove` and post-delete `session.members.listEvidence` responses. The Gateway-hosted Control UI also loaded the isolated `PR 134006 sharing proof` session.

### Automated verification

- Regression test failed on pre-fix code because `slack:channel:C012345` appeared in the identity picker.
- Rebased-head focused Gateway suite: 14/14 tests passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed on rebased head.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for both touched files.
- `oxlint` passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: +2/-1; test delta: +69/-0.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

AI-assisted with TRAE for issue triage, source/history inspection, implementation, test execution, and isolated Gateway verification. I reviewed the affected admission and authorization paths, verified the regression before the fix, and understand the final change.

prs.title: fix(node-host): Windows node commands with double-quoted arguments are split at the first space
prs.body:
Closes #158129

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Windows node host, any `system.run` command that contains double-quoted arguments is split at the first space, so the command that runs is not the command the operator approved. For example, delegating to Claude Code with `claude -p "Quel est le rôle du dossier checks ?" --permission-mode plan` hands `claude.exe` only `"Quel` as its prompt.

## User Impact

User impact: Windows node hosts now run quoted shell commands exactly as written and approved, so multi-word arguments (such as a Claude Code prompt) reach the program as one argument. Commands on other platforms, and any argv that is not the node shell envelope, are launched unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

On Windows, `system.run` wraps the command as `cmd.exe /d /s /c <command>`. The node launched that argv with Node's default argument quoting, which escapes inner quotes as `\"`. `cmd.exe` does not understand that escaping. At launch only, after every approval decision, the node now recognizes that exact envelope and passes `/d /s /c "<command>"` verbatim (`windowsVerbatimArguments`). With `/s`, `cmd.exe` strips the outer pair of quotes and runs the rest as written. Node uses the same form for its own `shell` option. Gateway-side command building, approval analysis, and `cmd.exe` path resolution are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **New focused tests** in `src/node-host/invoke.run-command.test.ts`:
  - the envelope from `buildNodeShellCommand(…, "win32")` is launched as `/d /s /c "<command>"` with `windowsVerbatimArguments: true`, including an absolute `CMD.EXE` path;
  - four or six elements, another program, a bare `cmd`, `/c` without `/s`, uppercase switches, and a non-Windows platform are all launched unchanged, without the option.
- **Real Windows spawn test** (runs only on `win32`): it goes through `runCommand` with `"node.exe" -e "…" "Quel est le rôle du dossier checks ?" --permission-mode plan`. The child receives `["Quel est le rôle du dossier checks ?", "--permission-mode", "plan"]`.
- **Regression proven:** with the source change reverted and the new tests kept, the two envelope tests and the real Windows spawn test fail (the spawn returns `success: false`).
- **Local run on Windows 11, Node 24.19.0, rebased on `main`:** `pnpm test src/node-host/invoke.run-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` gives 22 passed, 2 skipped (the existing POSIX-only tests). Wall time was 254 s on a cold vitest worker cache, 197 s of it preparing workers; the same file took 81 s warm before the rebase. The new unit tests take about 15 ms each and the real spawn test about 140 ms. CI seconds will be known once CI runs.
- **Checks on the touched files:** `oxfmt --check` clean, `oxlint --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` clean, `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. The test file was typechecked with a narrow config extending `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.shard.json`.
- **autoreview** (`--mode branch --base main --max-priority P1`, Claude engine because the local Codex CLI was not logged in): scoped-clean, no accepted findings.
- **Manual validation on a real Windows node:** a package built from this change was installed on a Windows 11 node paired with a Linux Gateway. `claude -p` with a quoted multi-word prompt then received the whole sentence as its prompt.

Not run:

- the full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` suite;
- the full `tsconfig.core.test.other.json` test typecheck shard (only the narrow config above);
- the spawn broker path on Windows: `src/process/spawn-broker/execa.test.ts` skips broker tests on `win32`. By reading the code, the broker forwards `windowsVerbatimArguments` (`SERIALIZABLE_OPTIONS` in `execa-client.ts`, spread into `execa` by the worker). The broker is also only started in the Gateway process, not in the node host.

prs.title: fix(ui): simplify chat controls and explain subagent waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat header spreads layout actions across several similar icon buttons, and a parent waiting on subagents is easy to mistake for a stopped conversation.

## User Impact

Chat keeps Share, Layout, and the session menu together. Layout includes the existing focus, split, swap, panel, and docking actions and their shortcuts. Empty conversations keep their width; a running subagent batch opens its panel once, respects dismissal during that batch, and leaves finished results visible. A muted composer line names the pending children and elapsed time; View opens and focuses Subagents. Actual work, model refresh, and the context gauge have explanatory text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production renderer for these surfaces is still Lit. The existing child-roster/status projection owns the count and yielded-parent facts, while the existing sidebar callbacks own layout changes. The pane gets no second Gateway subscription or new RPC. Narrow headers place the running count on its own row to preserve the three controls.

Running child rows reuse existing elapsed/tool activity and can show a current observer headline. The requested “earlier run interrupted by a Gateway restart; recovered” annotation is omitted: current client rows do not expose the predecessor interruption time and recovered-successor relationship. No server contract or configuration changes are included.

## Evidence

Details retains main's header placement, chat props, visibility, and open/close behavior; the count → Share → Layout → More cluster, pane presence, and waiting line remain intact. prs.title: fix(discord): batch queued messages by thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
When a user sends several Discord messages while an earlier turn is still running, the next follow-up turn should be able to see the whole compatible queued intent instead of only the last message. At the same time, Discord transport must keep every inbound event flowing into core admission so active-run steering and `/stop`-style control inputs are not delayed behind a local plugin queue.

Related: openclaw/openclaw#103287

## Summary
- remove the previous Discord-local same-session batch lane from `message-run-queue.ts`
- keep Discord inbound work event-keyed through the plugin queue so each message reaches core admission promptly
- carry Discord batch message IDs through typed preflight/finalized context fields when the dispatcher has an aggregate context
- add core follow-up queue support for aggregate `messageIds` on collected follow-up runs
- project collected queued message IDs into execution context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast` while keeping `MessageSid` as the current/latest message
- add a focused Discord dispatcher boundary proof that two debounced Discord source messages become one processed turn with both source IDs preserved

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

### Ephemeral Gateway + qa-channel proof on pushed head

Verdict: PASS on pushed PR head `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`.

This is the new qualifying proof path requested by ClawSweeper: it starts an ephemeral Gateway child, enables the real `qa-channel` plugin against the QA bus, uses the `mock-openai` provider, injects three inbound channel events, and verifies that the two queued channel messages become one executed provider turn.

Committed proof test:

- `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/qa-channel-queued-message-ids.e2e.test.ts`

Redacted runtime evidence from the test:

```json

  "transport": "qa-channel",
  "provider": "mock-openai",
  "gateway": "ephemeral-child",
  "receivedMessageIds": [
    "qa-msg-pr122238-active",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-first",
    "qa-msg-pr122238-queued-last"
  ],
  "collectedProviderRequestCount": 1,
  "queuedNeedlesPresent": [true, true],
  "sameSessionForAllIngressMessages": true,
  "executedTurnChannel": "qa-channel",
  "executedTurnChatId": "pr-122238-qa-channel",
  "secrets": "none"
}
```

What this proves at the boundary ClawSweeper asked for:

- `qa-channel` receives three real inbound channel messages via the QA bus, including explicit provider message IDs.
- All three inbound messages resolve to the same Gateway session.
- While the first turn is active, two later source messages are queued through core admission.
- The queued pair is collected into exactly one mock-provider request, and that executed request contains both queued source bodies.
- This path does not mock Discord preflight or processing; it exercises a complete mock-channel/mock-provider/ephemeral-Gateway run.

Current-main merge evidence:

- Pushed PR head: `6df1189d660a9320a83f04408154e1a502581ff6`
- Current `origin/main`: `39b39ca6eec684f0675cd93500646b578f6e7021`

- Merge status: conflict-free `ort` merge

Additional code cleanup in this proof update:

- Removed Discord preflight `batchMessageIdFirst` / `batchMessageIdLast` fields.
- The finalized context now derives `MessageSidFirst` and `MessageSidLast` from the aggregate `batchMessageIds` array, avoiding duplicate Discord-only preflight fields.

Commands run:


The after-fix boundary is owned by core follow-up collection rather than a Discord pre-admission lane:

- `message-handler.batch-ids.test.ts` proves the Discord debounce dispatcher emits one merged turn while preserving every source Discord message ID.
- `message-handler.context.test.ts` proves typed Discord batch fields project into finalized Discord context as `MessageSids`, `MessageSidFirst`, and `MessageSidLast`.

prs.title: feat: choose a profile name during Control UI setup
prs.body:
Part of #162164. Related to #164593, which separately changes how a configured shared operator name is displayed.

## What Problem This Solves

The existing setup flow does not offer a simple way to name an unnamed Gateway profile. Local or token-only users should be able to choose a profile name without connecting an external account or creating another identity screen.

## User Impact

During the existing Control UI onboarding route, a writable unnamed profile gets an optional “What should we call you?” prompt. “Maybe later” skips it for the current visit. A saved name remains editable through the existing Settings → Profile page.

An already named profile is left alone. Authentication, profile identifiers, permissions and Shared owner semantics are unchanged; entering a name is not personal sign-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt reuses `users.setDisplayName` and the existing profile storage owner. An optional `onlyIfUnset` parameter makes the condition atomic inside the existing write transaction: if another client establishes a name first, onboarding returns that profile without overwriting it or incrementing the profile version. Existing Profile edits remain unconditional.

The UI retires stale loads and save results when the Gateway connection or profile changes, and does not let an older save response replace a newer same-profile name observation. It uses the authoritative returned profile and offers visible retry after failure. It adds no Profile route, external account, role policy, name-to-person inference or persistent skip store.

## Evidence

Current head `7f1634c98923dbb576ae40cd104a126a2484adc2` merges pinned main `d5173ccc77b9ff5395cdbc38a8c37b45349d46e0`. Main independently repaired the wrong task-geometry DOM ancestry in [`bc458a9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bc458a9d46e); the conflict resolution adopts that canonical selector verbatim instead of retaining a duplicate variation. The Details button lives in the containing pane's header, outside the suggestions' gutter. All geometry assertions, fixtures, timeouts and three viewport cases remain intact. The preceding two-line correction passed pinned oxfmt 0.71.0 and isolated Codex/Astra P2 review. The current contributor delta passes `git diff --check`; hosted runtime verification remains pending.

[CI 38106716580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38106716580) at `512c9d67` failed three summary cases before reaching their geometry assertions because the old selector returned null. A separate late-catalog bootstrap test failed waiting for `fixture/current`; its cause remains unresolved and is not claimed fixed or inherited. Canonical checks for the new source head are pending. The preceding conflict resolution preserved main's session-error helpers and this PR's `UserProfile` import without changing production behavior.

The runtime and visual evidence below belongs to the stated earlier revisions. [Historical canonical CI 37264518694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37264518694) passed at `31c9aadb82cb4a0b99fbd49b12111eb204cf0a43`. That run is not a current-head CI result.

### Matched before/after: desktop and mobile

The pinned pre-change baseline `8db9539ee84a9c89f535c70fd39aa8fcaebc1bb9` and historical candidate `31c9aadb82cb4a0b99fbd49b12111eb204cf0a43` each passed one real-Gateway browser composition test using the same unnamed writable synthetic Profile and the canonical ordinary bundled E2E setup. Both captures wait for the same existing channel-onboarding card to load.

| Desktop baseline · 1280×800 | Desktop candidate · 1280×800 |
| --- | --- |
| ![Baseline without an optional name prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8753023-d175-476e-8d4e-ea452d44e655) | ![Candidate with an optional name prompt above the retained channel card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89570fdc-41f4-4314-a856-5a0d66caa512) |

| Mobile baseline · 390×844 | Mobile candidate · 390×844 |
| --- | --- |
| ![Mobile baseline without an optional name prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa33d90d-f905-49d2-8707-985993e71617) | ![Mobile candidate with the optional name prompt and retained channel card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a1bd112-f2a3-4db3-bfcf-439cd15d49aa) |

[Baseline run 37273872157](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37273872157) ([artifact11329104494](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37273872157/artifacts/11329104494)) and [candidate run 37273874940](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37273874940) ([artifact11329547257](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37273874940/artifacts/11329547257)) both report `test_exit=0`, unchanged tracked source/build/QA inputs and a pristine checkout after cleanup. Receipt durations are 114 and 107 seconds, respectively. Both used QA harness `7ccc29cf87a4fe4adadc5be3db1b98157b00e81a`, Node24.21.0/pnpm12.5.1 and secretless standard Ubuntu24.04.

All four actual images were inspected without DOM/CSS changes or cropping. The independent model greeting remains in flight in both captures; these prove the comparable onboarding layout, not model completion, native installation, live external authentication or an installed-version upgrade. They do not replay the save/skip/persistence sequence below.

### Actual onboarding save, skip and revisit

[Secretless standard-Ubuntu QA 37263226447](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37263226447) passed the existing production-browser/real-Gateway Profile composition E2E at `bccd53fc98f42ef0de495b3e01a8f1fe1a2cfc86`. It exercises the real Profile and Custodian routes through the existing Gateway storage/RPC owner, not mocked persistence.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Writable unnamed Profile | Existing onboarding shows the optional name prompt. |
| Maybe later | Prompt disappears for that visit; a fresh Profile route still has an empty saved name. |
| Save `Integration Test Person` | A fresh Profile route displays the saved name in both the hero and editor. |
| Return with that name already set | Successful `users.self` returns the saved name; after the Custodian has consumed it and rendered, no name prompt appears. Another fresh Profile route preserves the name. |

All six actual captures were inspected. Four decisive frames are embedded here; all six and the bounded receipt are in [artifact11325214624](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37263226447/artifacts/11325214624).

| Optional prompt | After Maybe later |

| ![Unnamed Profile onboarding prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5738c69-4545-446f-a880-4144a30a4a2f) | ![Onboarding after skipping the name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94d4051d-0b48-4853-985d-4a2d09c1876c) |

| Saved name in the existing Profile | Revisit without another name prompt |
| --- | --- |
| ![Saved name after a fresh Profile navigation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3803d4e6-d0a9-4615-8565-e9fa83d709af) | ![Named Profile onboarding revisit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f9ad860-2cfa-4513-bb5b-f3962b0f2a44) |

The rendered revisit image demonstrates prompt absence; the correlated RPC, loaded-page synchronization and subsequent Profile assertions establish that this is not an early screenshot taken before Profile loading. The existing name-projection test also retains its second-client rename/clear and unsaved-draft assertions.

Receipt: `test_exit=0`, 57 seconds; one file/one composition test, Vitest duration 53.71 seconds. Exact fork-only QA harness `09c1565ea555ebcc37cb1b38d04bf5d0110c0b2c`, Node24.21.0/pnpm12.5.1, standard Ubuntu24.04 without secrets. The UI identifiers are synthetic and the community invitation is absent.

This demonstrates real browser/Gateway name persistence and skip/revisit behavior with a task-only trusted-proxy identity. It is **not a pre-patch screenshot comparison, native-app installation, live Tailscale/Cloudflare authentication, another person's sign-in, or installed-old-version migration proof**. The competing-writer transaction and same-profile UI race are separately covered by the historical regression tests below, not claimed as reproduced by this single runtime sequence.

### Source and verification boundaries

Previously inspected main Custodian source at `bf0a6217a21161934fc0b7cc99bbf83a3115171f` (blob `04a18a13f5025e431fd6f7aa4682af93ea7d7c20`) still lacks this optional name prompt. The umbrella remains open; this does not close native identity work or implement macOS local Primary personal sign-in.

The previous runtime failure checked the sidebar's live presence label instead of the canonical saved Profile. The repaired test checks the actual `users.self` payload, waits for the existing Custodian profile state and Lit render, and retains the fresh Profile persistence assertions. No production test seam or arbitrary delay was added. Scoped P2 Codex AutoReview passed before the `bccd53fc` push. Canonical CI then caught a lexical `no-shadow` error in that test; the two-line identifier-only correction at `31c9aadb` also passed scoped P2 AutoReview. No assertion, timeout, scheduling or product behavior changed in that follow-up.

Earlier unsupported-matcher/readiness failures remain historical, not passing receipts. The successful run above supersedes those failures for the bounded onboarding runtime claim. The historical canonical CI passed; it remains separate from the revision-stamped runtime and visual evidence.

<details>
<summary>Earlier regression, type/lint and SQLite receipts</summary>

Verified against pinned main `8db9539`:

- Existing profile storage suite: 24/24. The competing-writer regression failed before the atomic guard and passes after it; an established name and profile version remain unchanged.
- Existing Gateway users handler suite: 53/53. Custodian page suite on PR head `e70fa765fd738e974aa2ebbb58e51f5e54330b78`: 29/29, including a mounted same-profile race regression. The regression fails on pre-fix `e27affa21efcf11642a5647bd3d3dc05e2cf582f` when a pending save response for “First name” settles after the same profile is observed as “Later name”; after the fix, the snapshot remains “Later name” and the stale response is not published.
- One selected rendered onboarding E2E passed; the unrelated locale case was filtered out. Inspected desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844 captures show the prompt and the full-height composer after “Maybe later,” without horizontal overflow. This uses synthetic browser fixtures, not a personal installation or persisted live-Gateway interaction.
- Production UI, UI-pages test and UI-E2E test TypeScript checks, targeted source-backed Oxlint, CSS Stylelint, formatting, localization verification and `git diff --check` passed.
- `test-audit` retained separate storage transaction, RPC, mounted UI and responsive-layout contracts. Scoped Codex AutoReview found a P1 empty grid-row regression; it was fixed, reproduced red/green with the eligibility cases and checked in the rendered E2E. The review is a completed findings report, not a clean verdict relabeled after repair.
- Scoped Codex AutoReview of the two-file patch later committed as `e70fa765fd738e974aa2ebbb58e51f5e54330b78` reported no findings. Its reviewer sandbox could not inspect surrounding checkout files, so this is diff-only review evidence; the mounted test and targeted type/lint checks provide independent context and behavior validation.

An earlier local changed-files wrapper reported SQLite T1 inventory growth (921 → 2054); the originating scan's exact inputs have not been established, so that result is neither reproduced nor classified as inherited. Historical canonical CI at `cc785cc7ae52ad3ccae60a9d754b70f119d38fdf` explicitly passes the SQLite worker ratchet against its immutable CI base `12785be2ff02a11e6587399ea3a0ac6ea2a4be36`: [run 37253040832, ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37253040832/job/111584655325). That supersedes the claim that SQLite is a confirmed current CI blocker, not the unexplained historical observation. Other CI and runtime QA results remain separate gates. Strict generated-catalog checking also reports the 10 new English keys; English verification passed, and generated translations are left to the repository's post-merge translation flow. These limitations are not waived by the narrower passing checks.

The feature is a separate optional onboarding slice; it does not close the native identity umbrella or implement macOS local Primary personal sign-in.

</details>

prs.title: feat(models): repeat provider auth setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adding a second model provider currently requires leaving the auth flow and repeating a broader onboarding/configuration journey. This makes multi-provider setups unnecessarily slow and makes manual model switching harder to discover.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `openclaw models auth login --repeat`. After each provider auth flow, OpenClaw asks whether another provider credential should be added. Subsequent iterations return to the provider picker, while existing credentials and the current default model are preserved.

Provider-scoped options (`--method` and `--profile-id`) are honored only for the first iteration and cleared before the next provider is selected, preventing invalid auth-method reuse or profile overwrites.

## User Impact

Advanced users can register several provider keys in one session and then use the existing `/model` picker to switch between the models exposed by those authenticated providers. Default-model changes remain opt-in through `--set-default`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` — 40/40 passing
- `git diff --check`
- Public CLI reference updated in `docs/cli/models.md`
- Rebased on `origin/main`

prs.title: fix: catalog list fails when Codex thread previews are huge
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the session catalog fails to parse Codex `thread/list` pages when stored previews are huge, then one bad host stalls `sessions.catalog.list`.

Fixes #156831

## User Impact

User impact: large Codex homes keep listing. A hung or unparseable host is fail-soft instead of blocking sibling hosts until the 60s deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog decoding drops the tail of a native `preview` string before JSON.parse, but only once the retained prefix already fixes the displayed text: the selector's 2,048-unit prefix, no terminal controls, and more than 500 units of collapsed, trimmed text. Each whitespace run is kept as one unit while reading, since the projection collapses runs anyway, so text after a long whitespace run survives. Controls before the first ANSI introducer (ESC, CSI, OSC) are deleted in place by the sanitizer, so each run of them is kept as one unit too. Only previews whose ANSI sequences leave the display undetermined are cut at 64 KiB. The displayed preview matches the existing projection and 8–24 MB pages still stay under the 8 MiB incomplete-frame recovery.

Each local catalog host gets one fail-soft deadline that covers page reads and adoption projection, on both the non-progressive path and progressive `finishLocalHost` / publication. It uses the existing 60s default request allowance (`CODEX_CATALOG_LOCAL_HOST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so slow large homes are not marked unavailable earlier than today; paired nodes stay at 8s.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest, all passing at f200f2f87f:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-preview-bound.test.ts` (19 tests): oversized preview parse, escaped quotes while skipping, skipped fragments vs the 1000-line recovery cap, and displayed-preview parity with the canonical selector for whitespace-heavy prefixes, escaped newlines, sparse words, terminal controls and a surrogate at the display boundary, text after whitespace, escaped newlines or removable controls beyond the 64 KiB fallback, removable controls between whitespace runs and before an ANSI sequence, and whitespace-only preview lines vs the recovery cap.
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-catalog-worker.test.ts` (25 tests): 9 MiB preview recovery, plus worker vs inline projection parity for a whitespace-heavy prefix, a control-laden preview, `" ".repeat(65_536) + "meaningful text"`, and `"\u0007".repeat(15_000) + "meaningful text"` (the last two fail before this change, pass after).
- `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-list-operation.test.ts` (16 tests): progressive and non-progressive host timeouts with sibling fail-soft, and a new case that holds the adoption read after paging completes (fails before this change, passes after).

`oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean.

Not yet attached: an after-fix `sessions.catalog.list` trace from a real large Codex home.

prs.title: fix(feishu): recover invalid tenant tokens
prs.body:
Closes #97287

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could stop receiving messages or streaming-card updates after Feishu revoked a cached tenant access token. OpenClaw kept reusing the rejected token until its normal expiry or a process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair lives at the two token owners:

- SDK-backed Feishu API calls now use an account-owned recoverable cache. An exact `99991663` response expires only the rejected tenant token, obtains a fresh token through the installed Lark SDK, and replays the original request once.
- Raw CardKit create, update, replace, note, and close calls share one client-scoped token state and the same exact-code, one-replay policy while retaining the existing SSRF-guarded transport.

Concurrent stale responses join one refresh, and a late stale response cannot invalidate a newer token. Explicit caller-supplied bearer credentials, other Feishu error codes, configuration, and persistence remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Feishu delivery and streaming cards recover automatically from server-revoked tenant tokens instead of remaining broken until restart. Persistent rejection still stops after one replay and surfaces the original Feishu failure.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `cdae502962330f12ddf58d58b23bb565a348bfca`
- Focused extension proof:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/dm-delivery-loopback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/drive-comments-loopback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.error-release.test.ts`
  - 5 files, 109 tests passed.
- The real installed Lark SDK loopback proves normal message delivery and Drive comment APIs converge through the repaired SDK request owner.
- Recovery tests cover fulfilled and thrown exact-code failures, explicit bearer isolation, one-replay bounds, concurrent stale responses, all five CardKit operations, and release-before-refresh ordering.
- Focused formatting and Oxlint passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview found no P0-P2 issues after the concurrency and response-release cases were tightened.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound/inbound conversation calls on Twilio without media streams did not play the initial greeting reliably, and the call dropped shortly after each reply when the caller stayed silent.

## User Impact

Callers hear the greeting and replies on the TwiML Say path, and the call stays connected while waiting for speech instead of hanging up after about five seconds of silence.

## Changes

1. For Twilio without media streams, `speakInitialMessage` now calls `speak(..., { listenAfterPlayback: true })` and skips the extra `startListening()` live TwiML update that was replacing the in-flight `<Say>`.
2. New `buildTwilioSpeechGatherVerbs()` adds `timeout="120"` and a post-`<Gather>` `<Redirect>` to the webhook. `playTts` only includes `<Gather>` when `listenAfterPlayback` is set.

Fixes #158262

## Evidence

Focused voice-call unit tests cover the three TwiML tails: the conversation gather plus redirect, the notify pause and hangup, and the direct-speech gather. After-fix proof on a real Twilio call still needs a human redacted trace (greeting, a silent pause, and the next reply, with numbers, keys, and endpoints removed). This pull request does not include a live call log.

prs.title: fix(update): prevent verification timeout after system clock changes
prs.body:
Related: #154693

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes package update verification timing out immediately after a system-clock jump forward, or outliving its configured budget after a jump backward.

## User Impact

Package update and rollback checks keep their bounded verification window when the system clock changes. There is no persistent-state or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The integrity reader already measures elapsed time with a monotonic clock, but enforced reads and cleanup against wall time. This uses one monotonic deadline for both, without changing the budget or filesystem checks.

## Evidence

- Two clock-jump regression cases fail against the previous reader and pass with this change.
- Earlier head evidence on Node 24.16 / Linux (WSL, ext4 temp): 107/107 related integrity and swap tests passed. This has not been replayed on the new head below.
- Changed-file formatting, lint, and diff checks pass; independent scoped review found no P0-P2 issue.
- Full core typecheck was not completed: the available borrowed dependency tree lacks unrelated workspace packages. CI remains the full-build check.

### Remaining proof and CI scope

The 107 passing tests are source-level integrity/swap regressions, not a published-driver-to-candidate installation or an installed-candidate update/recovery proof. The requested package-level proof remains open. The native Windows one-worker attempt below records cost and failures, and does not satisfy the full proof requirement.

The hosted run also reports failures in session-history budget ownership (SQLite worker exit) and Gateway incognito-lifetime assertions. Those are not the clock-jump regressions; their root causes have not been established. This PR does not claim a full-CI pass or a proven unrelated failure.


### Native Windows one-worker follow-up (2026-10-03)

Before resolving the new merge conflict, at head `43c21330832b507c7e2f59ac3119e4b1db83a6a7`, ran the repository wrapper with Node 24.16.0 and borrowed prepared Windows dependencies:

```text

Tests: 32 passed, 2 failed (34 total)
Vitest duration: 88.69 s (transform: 76.47 s)
Wrapper duration: 92.98 s
Measured process wall time: 93.940 s
Exit status: 1
```

Both failures were `returns after a stalled open/read without continuing the walk`: the live-to-backup package-directory rename returned `EPERM`, yielding `failed` instead of the expected `committed`. Their platform/fixture cause is unresolved; this is not a passing Windows result or a Linux CI cost estimate. An initial prerequisite attempt failed before tests while resolving QuickJS and is excluded from the timing above. The measured run includes shared-worker compilation/transformation; borrowed dependencies were not a new frozen-lockfile installation. No production code, assertion, timeout, retry policy, or CI guard was changed. No hosted CI run was started for this measurement (0 additional CI seconds).

Published-driver installation and installed-candidate clock-jump verification/recovery were not exercised. Completing that proof still requires a prepared isolated package environment; none was available for this follow-up, and the native Windows failures above need investigation.


### Conflict resolution and current-head limits (2026-10-03)

Rebased onto `fcdd8702174` to resolve the actual conflict in the bounds test, and published head `ff7df7d29411df161ce4f7bcc8e52fab7fbeb092`. Kept upstream's parallel-hash stall coverage and added `performance` to its existing fake timer set so advancing time also advances the monotonic deadline. Fresh static review found no actionable issue in the resolved diff; formatting, scoped oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. The production delta remains the monotonic-deadline fix.

The native one-worker full-file attempt passed 29 cases, including both clock-jump regressions, then the stalled-open case timed out at the unchanged 120,000 ms test limit. A diagnostic-only focused replay (5,000 ms test limit, original assertions intact) observed four admitted hashes after the 40 ms fake-clock advance, reached `beforeActivate`, and captured a real rename returning `EPERM`. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite runtime SDK requires writable native handles or host callbacks even when a plugin's runtime mutations belong in the database worker.

## User Impact

`openOpenClawAgentSqliteWorkerStoreV2` binds required live authority to a retained worker store and accepts serializable domain commands. Explicit `prepare()` admits or creates storage; `executeExisting` preserves absence. Bundled Memory origins, standing intents, and Forget now use this contract.

Released raw SQLite and callback signatures preserve completion and transaction ordering, with named replacements and shared warnings until the next Plugin SDK major. Read-only inspection, worker kernels, and offline Doctor maintenance remain explicit contracts. This changes no schema, stored bytes, retention, or update format.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement reuses agent execution admission and accepted-work settlement without handing a writable database to the host. Backends that initialize schema use separate binding and command admissions: a single-command admission cannot contain two independently committed transactions. Closing refuses new work and joins accepted operations; ordinary runtime mutations are not automatically retried after unknown outcomes. Host closures are neither serialized nor presented as worker transactions.

The wrapper guard admits only the 14 verified released-name warning adapters and fails on stale exceptions. The worker-call ratchet discounts only each exact compatibility forwarding expression; added or altered native calls remain charged. Both allowances end with removal of those adapters at the next Plugin SDK major.

## Evidence

Recorded pre-restack diff: production +529/−258 lines, tests +283/−61, and tooling +213/−16. The retired origin command and its worker references are removed together.

The recorded import/callgraph audit classifies all scoped imports and finds no ordinary bundled call to the retired raw agent callback/open helpers. Read-only external sources, offline maintenance, and deliberately labeled compatibility/QA fixtures are recorded separately.

Three review rounds resolved accepted findings; subsequent correction reviews passed at P0/P1. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): skip heartbeat turns for legacy docs-link boilerplate scratch
prs.body:
## What was wrong

Agents carrying the legacy monitor scratch template were running a heartbeat model turn on every interval, while sibling agents with comment-only scratch correctly skipped with `empty-heartbeat-file`.

The legacy template ends with a "Related" section whose only non-header line is a bare documentation link:

```markdown
## Related

- [Heartbeat config](/gateway/config-agents)
```

`isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` already strips headers, HTML comments, fence markers and empty list stubs, but a list item holding just a doc link fell through every branch and counted as real content. So the shipped boilerplate alone was enough to trigger heartbeat turns and token spend, exactly the thing the template tells users it prevents.

## The fix

One narrow addition to the emptiness check in `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.ts`: list items whose entire content is a single bare documentation link (a relative docs path or an anchor target, like the legacy Related link) are now treated as boilerplate.

Deliberately conservative:
- Links with surrounding prose, multiple links, or external URL targets still count as content.
- Fenced content with a real task still counts as content.
- Missing scratch still returns false so the monitor can run.

## Proof

- Reproduced on current main first: the exact scaffold from the issue returned `false` (not empty) before the fix.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.test.ts`: 39/39 pass, including 3 new regression cases (legacy scaffold, bare docs-link items, links that must still count as content). The related prompt tests were also exercised; an infra-level runner test errors on an unrelated missing `@openclaw/fs-safe/path` module in this environment, identically with and without the change.

Fixes #152916

prs.title: fix(agents): agent turns fail when workspace templates are unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On an install whose workspace templates are not present on disk, **every agent turn fails** — even when the agent's workspace is fully provisioned and the template is only wanted for a comparison:

```
Missing workspace template: SOUL.md (<root>/src/agents/templates/SOUL.md). Ensure workspace templates are packaged.
```

Observed live on a self-hosted gateway: a healthy install with a complete workspace (`SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, … all present and user-authored) could not run a single turn on **any** agent. `main` failed on `SOUL.md`, a second agent on `AGENTS.md`. The gateway was otherwise fine — nodes connected, CLI worked — so the assistant simply stopped answering with a packaging error that pointed nowhere useful.

The trigger is that templates serve two different jobs:

- **Provisioning** — creating a bootstrap file that does not exist yet. Genuinely impossible without the template; must fail loudly.
- **Comparison** — deciding whether an *existing* file is still pristine or has been edited by the user (`workspaceProfileLooksConfigured`, `workspaceRequiredBootstrapLooksCustomized`, `collectGeneratedBootstrapHashes`).

Both went through `loadTemplate()`, which throws. So a missing template turned a purely informational question into a fatal one on the hot path every turn takes.

Note the pre-existing asymmetry this fixes: `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` already tolerated a **missing workspace file** (returns `false` on `ENOENT`), but a **missing template** was fatal. Both are "cannot compare" — only one degraded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Comparison callers ask "is this still the pristine template?". When the template is unavailable the honest answer is *unknown*, and the safe interpretation is **user content**, because every caller uses the result to decide whether regenerating would destroy real work. Treating unknown as "customized / configured" preserves user files and keeps the turn alive.

Provisioning deliberately keeps the strict loader — writing a bootstrap file with no template is a real error and should still surface.

## User Impact

An install missing packaged templates degrades instead of hard-failing: agents keep answering, existing workspace files are never mistaken for regenerable boilerplate, and setup/provisioning still reports a clear error when it truly cannot proceed. No behavior change when templates are present.

## Evidence

- **Production trace (negative case):** the live outage above produced this exact error on two different agents against a fully provisioned workspace — that is the real-world reproduction of the failing path this patch removes.
- **Regression test:** `src/agents/workspace.missing-templates.test.ts` covers both packaged-install failure shapes — no template directory at all, and a directory that resolves but is empty — asserting the status call resolves and that existing user content is left untouched.
- **Test run:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace.missing-templates.test.ts` → **2 passed**.
- **Formatting:** `oxfmt` clean on both files.
- **Autoreview** (gpt-5.6-sol, high): clean — *"patch is correct (0.98)… comparison-only fallback conservatively treats content as customized when templates are unavailable, while provisioning continues to use the strict template loader."*

Scope is deliberately narrow: no change to template resolution, packaging, or the provisioning contract.

prs.title: refactor(ui): port board and system pages to Solid 2
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves the board, dashboards, plugin host and pages, portals, and systems rendering from Lit to Solid 2 while preserving existing tags, routes, classes, and plugin SDK contracts.

## User Impact

Existing UI behavior and appearance remain intact. Widget cells keep DOM insertion order independently of visual grid position, so reordering preserves the iframe and its state. Removed MCP widgets stay connected until teardown finishes. Plugin actions lose authority immediately when their view is removed or its registration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each ported tag now has one Solid implementation registered through `defineSolidBridge`; its Lit class is deleted. Remaining Lit callers use that bridge. Domain owners remain plain TypeScript and the pages consume existing projections. The plugin SDK is unchanged. Solid icons and existing settings helpers replace touched equivalents; unported custom elements remain interoperable.

The coupled bridge change provides the existing shell-layout owner to Solid views mounted by Lit. The coupled plugin-scope change accepts a live-view predicate so a detached view cannot retain action authority until deferred disposal. Both have boundary regressions. Dashboard pagination remains synchronous with the session-list owner's completion notification, preventing an append from being stranded by a deferred effect.

prs.title: fix(agents): worktree sessions write outside sandbox from prompt workspace path
prs.body:
Closes #129404

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running managed worktree sessions would get the shared agent workspace path and bootstrap files (`AGENTS.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, â€¦) in the system prompt while file tools were sandboxed to the session worktree. Agents then wrote to `.openclaw/workspace/...`, hit `Path escapes sandbox root`, tried to leave the worktree (including via `exec`), and could rewrite shared bootstrap so later agents inherited poisoned instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dashboard worktree sessions already remount managed `spawnedCwd` as `workspaceDir` at gateway/auto-reply ingress. `agentCommand` prepare only inherited `spawnedCwd` as `cwd` and left `workspaceDir` on the canonical agent home, so prompt/bootstrap and the file-tool root diverged. This change makes remount the shared owner for prepare (`resolvePreparedAgentCommandWorkspaceDir`) and uses `effectiveCwd` for the embedded prompt Working directory (same rule as CLI), so prompt path and bootstrap load from the worktree checkout.

Non-goal: changing `exec` host containment. That remains a separate policy surface.

## User Impact

Managed worktree sessions now see their own worktree as the workspace in the system prompt and load bootstrap from that checkout. Agents stop being steered toward the shared `.openclaw/workspace` for file tools, and a corrupted shared `AGENTS.md` no longer becomes the injected identity for every new worktree session that remounts correctly.

## Evidence

- Focused remount unit tests: `resolvePreparedAgentCommandWorkspaceDir` / `resolveIngressWorkspaceOverrideForSessionRun` (4 passed).
- Regression assertion in `attempt.cwd-split.test.ts`: when cwd and bootstrap workspace differ, embedded system prompt `workspaceDir` follows the file-tool cwd.
- Before: prompt showed `.../.openclaw/workspace/BOOTSTRAP.md` while sandbox root was `.../.openclaw/worktrees/<fp>/<name>`; writes failed with `Path escapes sandbox root`.
- After (intended): prepare remounts worktree as `workspaceDir`, so bootstrap resolution and prompt Working directory use the same checkout as file tools.
