prs.title: fix(whatsapp): bound deferred ingress handoffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- Keep the shared ingress watchdog bounded before and after explicit deferred handoff.
- Preserve the original claim-time deadline for every caller that does not configure a distinct deferred window.
- Let opted-in owners reset the watchdog at handoff so healthy scheduler waits receive their own bounded adoption window.
- Give WhatsApp a deliberately long seven-day operational bound instead of the generic five-minute bound.
- Fail closed with `handler-timeout` when a deferred scheduler never adopts or abandons, aborting late work and releasing the conversation lane.
- Close the shared state database before Windows test cleanup so SQLite-backed owner tests remove their temporary directories reliably.
- Keep core reply-queue lifecycle helpers out of the Plugin SDK test surface; exercise the WhatsApp owner proof through the supported `turnAdoptionLifecycle` contract.

Related to #120265 and #116547. This fixes the WhatsApp owner path without introducing an unbounded scheduler-owned deferral mode.

## What problem this solves

The generic ingress watchdog is appropriate while a claimed message is dispatching, but WhatsApp may legitimately defer adoption while its debounce and reply scheduler waits behind an active turn. Applying the same five-minute clock across both phases can dead-letter healthy queued work.

Clearing the watchdog after handoff is also unsafe: WhatsApp's scheduler has terminal callbacks but no independent liveness timeout, so a never-settling scheduler promise could refresh the durable claim and block the conversation lane forever.

This revision uses two bounded policies:

1. the generic watchdog starts at claim time and remains unchanged for callers that do not opt in;
2. an explicit `deferredAdoptionStallTimeoutMs` resets the watchdog only when deferral actually occurs;
3. WhatsApp opts into a seven-day operational safety bound for that second phase;
4. a missing terminal callback aborts and dead-letters the claim, rejects late adoption as guillotined, and lets the next same-lane message proceed.

The seven-day value is an operational recovery policy, not a scheduler-derived semantic maximum. A renewable scheduler heartbeat remains the stronger future refinement if arbitrarily long healthy waits must be supported.

## Safety and public contract

- No unbounded scheduler-owned deferral mode remains.
- Callers without an explicit post-handoff timeout keep the original claim-time deadline.
- The post-handoff clock resets only for an owner that explicitly configures it.
- Adoption and abandonment cancel the post-handoff watchdog.
- Timeout preserves claim-token fencing, abort, `handler-timeout`, and failed-tombstone behavior.
- Late adoption after timeout fails loudly instead of replaying work.
- The Plugin SDK channel documentation explains omission, explicit deferral reset, timeout behavior, the WhatsApp seven-day policy, and the renewable-lease alternative.
- Internal reply-queue admission helpers remain core-owned and are guarded by a negative SDK source-contract regression.
- Production configuration, services, queues, credentials, and WhatsApp traffic were not touched.

## Review verdict and scope

- Best-fix verdict: the distinct opt-in deferred watchdog is the narrowest compatible seam. A core-wide reset would change every channel, while clearing the watchdog would make lost scheduler ownership unbounded.
- Production TypeScript: **+38 / -11**.
- Tests: **+362 / -8**.
- Documentation: **+21 / -0**.
- Generated Plugin SDK contract: **+91 / -91**.

## Evidence

- Exact tested and reviewed head: `54b018b8ae641d29934291feb50c2cf948e3fa3d`.
- Latest frozen `main`: `5295f2578e1be11671987df79a2110f36e663daa`, normal-merged as `74b2cacc12c`; the sole genuine conflict was the generated Plugin SDK JSONL baseline, resolved by canonical regeneration. Earlier refreshes likewise preserved `main`'s generated-contract changes.
- Focused behavior proof: **61/61 tests passed** across four files and two Vitest shards covering WhatsApp durable receive, the mock-socket inbox owner path, the core deferred watchdog, and the core drain contract.
- SDK-boundary repair proof: the new negative source-contract regression failed before the fix with exactly the two leaked queue helpers, then passed after their removal; the complete affected WhatsApp file passed **17/17**, the complete SDK contract file passed **18/18**, and the focused core lifecycle-owner slice passed **3/3**.
- Windows cleanup regression: the first run's only failures were ten `EBUSY` removals of open SQLite temp files; the repository's test-only database closer was added before cleanup, after which all focused tests passed.
- Core production types passed: `pnpm tsgo:core`.
- Extension production types passed: `pnpm tsgo:extensions`.
- Core test-source types passed: `pnpm tsgo:core:test`.
- Extension test-source types passed: `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`.
- Plugin SDK API generation/check passed with the canonical JSONL contract.
- Plugin SDK surface check passed: 336 total entrypoints, 7,738 total exports, 151 public entrypoints, 4,847 public exports, and zero forbidden package subpaths.
- Exact changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Mandatory trusted exact-final-branch autoreview completed with **0 accepted/actionable findings** and **0.99 correctness confidence** (254,237-byte one-pass bundle).
- TruffleHog's exact committed branch scan passed clean against frozen `main`, including the review runner's independent 7.5-second scan.

## Owner-path proof available today

The current automated proof reaches the real OpenClaw ownership seams but uses an ephemeral durable queue and mock Baileys socket. It does not use credentials or send live traffic.

```json
{"scenario":"lost-scheduler-adoption","transport":"mock-baileys-socket","durableQueue":"ephemeral","timers":"real","configuredProductionBoundMs":604800000,"harnessBoundMs":50,"path":["messages.upsert","durable-delivery","whatsapp-debounce","turnAdoptionLifecycle.onDeferred","handler-timeout","same-lane-successor"],"sameLaneSuccessorDispatched":true,"lateAdoptionRejected":true,"credentials":false,"liveSend":false}
```

The sibling healthy-path regression uses the same owner path, keeps the second same-lane event pending, adopts through the supported `turnAdoptionLifecycle.onAdopted` contract, and then observes successor dispatch. Core-owner tests separately prove queue admission behavior, reset-at-handoff timing, timeout dead-lettering, late-adoption fencing, and adoption/abandonment timer cancellation.

## Outstanding acceptance — do not merge yet

1. Maintainers must explicitly accept the seven-day WhatsApp delivery-versus-recovery tradeoff. This PR documents the proposed operational policy but does not assume that product decision.
2. The mandatory real Baileys/WhatsApp lost-adoption trace is still missing. The mock-socket path above must not be represented as live external-account proof, and no synthetic external traffic should be created to satisfy it.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted investigation, implementation, tests, merge maintenance, and PR preparation. Review findings were independently reproduced by tracing the shared watchdog and the real WhatsApp debounce/reply ownership path before the bounded revision was implemented.

prs.title: fix(google): report embedding batch lifecycle statistics
prs.body:
Related: #120889

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an observability gap where operators running Gemini native embedding batches could not see the provider-reported request totals, success/failure/pending counts, lifecycle timestamps, elapsed time, or whether downloaded results fully reconciled with submitted requests.

The Gemini embedding API exposes `createTime`, `updateTime`, `endTime`, `batchStats`, state, and output metadata, but the adapter previously discarded those fields.

- https://ai.google.dev/api/embeddings#method:-models.asyncbatchembedcontent
- https://ai.google.dev/api/embeddings#embedcontentbatch

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google adapter now normalizes both current top-level Batch fields and the legacy Operation-metadata shape, with top-level terminal fields taking precedence over stale metadata. It emits structured subsystem events when a job is created, reaches a terminal state, and reconciles output.

Successful events report provider counts/timestamps plus separate provider and locally observed durations. Terminal failures report only structured provider codes. Output transport, HTTP, parse, record, missing-response, and unusable-metadata paths emit sanitized failure classes and reconciliation counts.

Durable events never include request text, provider error text, authentication, file URLs, response bodies, request IDs, or embedding vectors. Existing thrown error behavior and debug callbacks are unchanged.

This PR intentionally adds no configuration or quota claims. Public numeric batch knobs were deliberately retired upstream, and a real concurrency ceiling requires one shared admission semaphore across both file scheduling and group submission. That design remains separate follow-up work.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose Gemini batch progress and failures from durable, structured evidence without enabling payload-level debug logging or exposing user content. The counts distinguish returned embeddings, provider record errors, genuinely missing responses after clean EOF, and unreconciled responses after transport/parse failure.

## Evidence

- Exact refreshed head: `2f67cd46baaaf29072427f27c5588cabd481fd3d`.
- The branch was refreshed by a normal merge from validated upstream `main` at `e97c3450a2724a6189762fa0d6c76284b9b83071`; no rebase or force-push was used.
- 27/27 focused Gemini batch tests pass, including the disposable loopback HTTP lifecycle.
- Regression coverage includes current and legacy API shapes, canonical top-level output precedence over stale legacy aliases, fail-closed rejection when conflicting legacy output aliases lack a canonical field, provider statistics/timestamps, terminal failure/cancel/expire states, output HTTP/parse/record errors, full-stream reconciliation after a record error, missing output metadata, fallback and provider timing semantics, and log-content secrecy.
- All four TypeScript surfaces pass: core production, core tests, extensions production, and extensions tests.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, export synchronization, and public-surface checks pass; no SDK regeneration was required.
- Targeted formatting, direct type-aware extension lint on both changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The repository lint wrapper was attempted twice and timed out during broad plugin-boundary artifact preparation after 124 seconds and 304.1 seconds without a diagnostic. It is not counted as green; the underlying repository `oxlint` binary completed the equivalent type-aware two-file lint cleanly in 70.1 seconds.
- Mandatory isolated autoreview passed on the final branch against the frozen validated base: TruffleHog v3.95.9 reported the exact patch clean in 3.6 seconds, and Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` with high reasoning reviewed one complete 27,812-byte bundle and returned no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.98).
- Exact-head CI [run 31476497307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31476497307) is terminal with 29 successful and 15 skipped jobs; its only underlying failure is [`build-artifacts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31476497307/job/93731653297), followed by the aggregate gate. The Control UI build exceeded its startup-JS gzip ceiling by exactly two bytes (326,658 B versus 326,656 B). This PR changes only two Google embedding-batch files and no UI, build, dependency, or performance-budget path, so the failure is classified as an unrelated brittle size-budget result; no branch edit or blind rerun was made.
- The prior exact-head CI at `56270710c854831bd245d94d10c30ce93cecc5e5` attached after the PR was marked ready, but it was not green: [`check-test-types`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31384721572/job/93442832801) failed on Discord and Telegram test-harness types that this PR does not change.
- The same errors fail on the contemporaneous current-main commit `c3f4d5ee601ad6f3753daf72b0deac2ed171a286` in its own [`check-test-types`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31383550120/job/93442046283) job. A read-only merge-tree comparison confirms the PR merge result differs from that base only in the two Google batch files and leaves every reported failing path byte-identical to `main`. This is recorded as an unrelated upstream CI blocker; no branch code was changed and the known-bad lane was not blindly rerun.
- Production delta is +195/-15 (net +180); tests are +305/-4 (net +301). The production growth is confined to Google-provider lifecycle normalization and sanitized telemetry at the provider-owned boundary.
- No paid or authenticated live Gemini batch was created, and production was untouched. Deterministic fixtures and loopback HTTP do not substitute for the mandatory redacted real-provider created/terminal/reconciliation trace. This PR is therefore not claiming proof-complete or merge-ready status.

prs.title: fix(android): keep answered question cards in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users answering a question would keep seeing the completed card after newer messages, at the latest end of the chat. Continuing the conversation did not move the answered card back into history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep pending and submitting questions at the live edge, but place completed questions into the transcript by creation time. Insert them before transcript projection groups tool events, so an older tool row cannot drag a completed question out of order. Preserve completed cards when corresponding messages are not loaded.

This changes presentation only: no question-resolution, approval, persistence, or Gateway protocol changes.

## User Impact

Answered questions remain in their original conversational context instead of following the composer. Questions that still need an answer remain reachable and selectable.

## Evidence

<!-- puller-recovery-20260929:start -->
### Upstream integration — September 29

Merged upstream `c82063902aa1aee76da2ee1b965bab8643be4b20` into this branch; preserved question history and current upstream tool grouping. Published merge: `3cdd1d479510c5ec5cf61b30957da08d2013f7cc`.

- Third-party Android variant: **28 tests passed**, covering `ChatTimelineQuestionTest`, `ChatReaderScrollControllerTest`, and `ChatQuestionHistoryLayoutTest`.
- Normal pre-commit hooks passed in the secretless container.
- Astra/Medium autoreview: no P0/P1 findings in the selected code scope. Review noted limited surrounding context; this is not blanket whole-PR clearance. The three existing screenshot blobs are unchanged.
- No merge into upstream; remaining CI and maintainer review requirements still apply.
<!-- puller-recovery-20260929:end -->


- Original upstream code: both timeline chronology regressions and the real-screen answered-card assertion fail for the reported ordering defect; pending-question selection passes.
- An independent review caught ordering across completed-tool rows. A new regression reproduced the first candidate's failure, then passed after moving insertion before tool grouping.
- Current-main candidate: **66 tests pass**, covering chronology, real `ChatScreen` rendering/interaction, tool grouping, and completed-work summaries. Android app ktlint, other Android modules' lint, changed-file guards, native-state schema guard, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Inspected synthetic before/after Robolectric native-rendered captures show the completed card moving above the later user/assistant messages. The pending card remains selectable with Submit enabled. No personal device/data was used.

```bash
cd apps/android
OPENCLAW_CHAT_QUESTION_PROOF_DIR=/tmp/question-history-proof \
  ./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest \
  --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatTimeline*Test' \
  --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.ChatQuestionHistoryLayoutTest \
  :app:ktlintCheck
```

Capture reproduction writes `answered-history.png` and `pending-question.png` to the chosen directory. Before/after and pending-state captures are included in `.github/pr-proof/android-question-history/` because the attachment service returned inaccessible URLs.

Review/validation limits: the initial prescribed autoreview attempt lacked a standalone runtime; that runtime is now available, and the subsequent reader-fixture-only fix received a clean P0–P2 review with 53 focused tests and app lint passing; the earlier candidate received independent review; the current-main follow-up failed result-schema validation and is not claimed as a passing review. No physical-device installation or full cross-platform suite was run. This is an AI-assisted fix.

The current-main port also keys prepared-history caching on completed questions.

## Screenshots

Before:

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/fix/android-completed-question-history/.github/pr-proof/android-question-history/before.png)

After:

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/fix/android-completed-question-history/.github/pr-proof/android-question-history/after.png)


### Measured test cost and current CI

At head `a92e385a6f79857f0bd968526696796569865d04`, the [Android Play CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36288970265/job/108535459083) passed. Its [JUnit report artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36288970265/artifacts/10922095650) records:

- `ChatQuestionHistoryLayoutTest`: **1.116 s** for 2 passing tests (answered-card layout: 0.653 s; pending-card interaction: 0.456 s).
- `ChatTimelineQuestionTest`: **0.004 s**, 3 passing tests.
- `ChatReaderScrollControllerTest`: **0.055 s**, 23 passing tests.

These are JUnit class execution durations, not full build wall times. The complete Play CI Gradle invocation took **11m 32s**, including compilation and the wider test lane. prs.title: refactor(sessions): route transcript appends through the session actor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SessionManager repeatedly prepares writers and reloads transcript facts while appending messages and tool results. Cut these durable points over to the session actor without losing committed receipts, live authority, or accepted-write settlement.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible behavior change. The warmed append path removes **26 SQLite statements and one committed transaction with zero added requests**. No schema, durability, retention, or permission change; no operator action required. This lane does not by itself reach the campaign's under-500 warmed-turn aim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on `dbasync/actorb1`. The measured B1 base is `b11f7c318270752376f0129528c6a589b5bd6c51`; candidate is `0a5499ea1645ca4fb007ab304ccfe1fde7449351`. The parent subsequently integrated main; this lane keeps the proved pin instead of chasing that unrelated integration. Retarget as the parent lands.

Retain one exact physical/session actor for the attempt, including accepted descendants after a teardown timeout. Route SessionManager messages, metadata, tool-result persistence before acknowledgement, and bound transcript appends through `appendToolResult` / `appendTranscriptEvent`. Each durable append has one transaction. Capture the native receipt before fallible publication, preserve `SessionTranscriptMessageCommittedError`, and never repeat an unknown-outcome append.

B1 contract update 3 permits a synchronous replica snapshot and validates the optional expected preimage inside the command. The pre-append read is gone. Only a typed stale-version result, proving no mutation ran and carrying the current postimage, permits one retry; authority is checked again. The captured commit always wins over a contradictory reply. Session-scoped invalidation leaves unrelated sessions resident.

Preparation, anchors, watermarks, and context membership consume the actor's admitted metadata. Historical message payload hydration stays bounded; no full-history cache saving is claimed. Native-incognito uses B1's existing-owner adapter, not a replacement database. Its admission bridge borrows the enclosing native owner without self-queueing. Released unbound SDK/native calls and explicit compaction maintenance keep named compatibility adapters; actor-bound callers have no parallel old writer path. Writer-lease types move to a leaf owner, with existing exports retained.

### Deliberate compromises

The final audit against "Choose good compromises" retained the existing ownership contract rather than adding another coordination layer. This cutover removes the pre-append read and superseded actor-bound writer; it adds no fencing token, revocation generation, durable command ledger, caller-side reconciliation loop, or per-write cross-thread handshake. The existing writer-lease/navigation checks are preserved, not newly invented. The native-incognito queue bypass addresses an observed self-queue deadlock, and the drain callback releases the actor through the existing accepted-work lifecycle rather than introducing a second settlement mechanism.

Accepted edge case: a durable append can succeed while local view/receipt publication fails. The caller reports the existing committed-error contract and does not replay the append. An unknown result likewise stops this attempt. The current actor contract explicitly forbids command replay and does not make command IDs durable idempotency keys; message-level idempotency remains intact where supplied. General automatic retry is therefore not safe for every metadata/event append and is intentionally not built here. Only the typed stale-version outcome proves no mutation ran and allows the bounded retry above.

## Statement and request evidence

Four required alternating B1/C pairs ran on one Hetzner runner, followed by the required fifth pair because the initial first-turn median rose. All ten complete workloads passed. The tables below include **all five pairs**; medians are computed separately for each side. A warmed sample is its ten-turn sum divided by ten, then the five-sample median. All-thread counts include MAIN. MAIN requests identify the sender; MAIN statements identify the executing thread. Actor commands, logical requests, transfer frames, native calls/statements, and committed transactions are distinct counters.

| Initial four-pair medians | 1148 → 1314 | 675.6 → 643.9 | 15467.5 → 14929 | 2936.5 → 2945 |
| Required fifth pair alone | 1542 → 1168 | 677.3 → 654.1 | 15411 → 15010 | 2933 → 2935 |
| All-five medians | 1171 → 1187 | 675.9 → 648.1 | 15467 → 14975 | 2936 → 2935 |

The fifth pair alone is **+2 requests**, not a request saving. Under the campaign's median granularity, the whole-workload comparison after that confirmation is **−492 statements, −1 worker request, −2 DB requests**. The remaining first-turn +16 statements / +8 worker requests is redistribution, not reported as an improvement. Recorded stacks locate the shifted work in memory-index admission/indexing and memory-workspace locks, not the append path. The affected unchanged families have equal whole-workload medians:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory `schema.admit` | 1 / 130 | 1 / 130 |
| `cron.mutateJobs` | 2 / 24 | 2 / 24 |
| Memory lock `pluginState.compareDelete` | 34 / 153 | 34 / 153 |

| Memory lock `pluginState.observe` | 17 / 68 | 17 / 68 |

## What Problem This Solves

Adds explicit thinking-level control to visible `sessions_spawn` sessions while leaving omitted values under the Gateway's child-session default.

Fixes #134530

## Why This Change Was Made

Visible spawning now forwards only an explicitly supplied thinking value to `sessions.create`. The unused configured-default switch is removed, the docs distinguish visible and hidden defaults, and the shared thinking resolver remains the established contract for hidden subagent defaults.

## User Impact

Visible child sessions can set a supported thinking level; omitting it leaves the Gateway in control of the child-session default.

## Evidence

prs.title: refactor(ui): move meetings, memory import, profile, and debug to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves Meetings, Import Memory, Profile, and Debug onto Solid 2 while the remaining Control UI still uses Lit.

## User Impact

Keeps existing routes, host tags, CSS classes, selectors, and Gateway behavior. Settings switches and provider icons use the landed owned primitives where their consumers support Solid. No dependency or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each registered page or overlay now has one Solid implementation through `defineSolidBridge`; its Lit class is deleted. Existing synchronous domain owners and shared projections retain authority over reads, mutation targets, and disposal. Memory import/rollback confirmations retain their captured connection and agent; account wizard callbacks retain the step that rendered them.

The small shared fixes are explicit GitHub-context property typing, sparkline host typing, modal description typing, and materializing `SettingsRow.control` once. The latter prevents duplicate child mounts and duplicate Debug event-highlighter subscriptions. Stateless Lit frame/loading helpers remain for the still-Lit shell, and picker/wizard helpers remain for unported consumers.

Production TypeScript in the four page directories plus the two shared DOM/interop helpers grows from **6,291 to 7,149 lines**. Most growth is explicit JSX bindings, view prop types, and overlay request/disposal lifetimes formerly hidden by Lit controllers; temporary Lit/Solid frame helpers serve the two existing renderers. The final simplification removed about 200 production lines from the draft, including duplicated Profile view-state objects and forwarding wrappers. Tests/support change from 6,389 to 6,693 lines. No new store or dependency.

## Evidence

| `pnpm test ui/src/pages/debug/view.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 18 passed; 71.04s wall |

prs.title: fix(codex): render dynamic tool images in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tools can return image content successfully, but the durable transcript projection flattened those images to text. Control UI then hid or rolled up the surviving tool result, and chat-history budgeting replaced a typical screenshot-sized message with a message-too-large placeholder. The result was a successful computer screenshot that never rendered in chat.

## What Changed

- Preserve validated dynamic-tool image outputs as top-level transcript image blocks.
- Replace invalid inline image payloads with safe explanatory text.
- Keep image-bearing tool results outside completed-work and activity rollups.
- Render tool-result images even when tool details are collapsed or tool calls are hidden.
- Give image-bearing history messages a bounded 1 MiB per-message allowance while preserving the 128 KiB ordinary-message cap and existing total-history cap.

## Evidence

- Seven focused Codex projector, chat grouping/rendering, and history-budget suites: 387 tests passed.
- Changed-file Oxlint: passed.
- Changed-file Oxfmt check: passed.
- Full pnpm build, including Control UI compressed assets and performance checks: passed.
- Live pinned CUA Driver 0.19.0 gateway replay: the stored screenshot survives chat.history as toolResult + image with a 418,067-character data URL and no omitted-message placeholder.
- Live Control UI verification: the Linux XFCE screenshot visibly renders inline with the Computer screenshot tool result.

## Impact

Computer screenshots and other dynamic-tool images survive transcript persistence, history transport, grouping, and rendering, so they appear inline in Control UI chat without requiring users to expand tool details.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce turn completion database work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turn completion persisted related session bookkeeping through separate generic
patches: group intro, fallback notice, usage/context/billing, live-model cleanup,
activity, and final-delivery custody. Those independent prepare/commit cycles
repeated entry reads, side-table work, publication and transaction envelopes.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change: the session owner performs less
duplicated database work while preserving completion, accounting and delivery
custody. No operator migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on `dbasync/actorb1`. Route terminal work through its existing physical
session owner and `completeTurn`, without appending a second assistant message.
The shared pure bookkeeping reducers also serve the named native/SDK patch
adapter; the folded patch-fusion work suppresses unchanged entry/window/snapshot
writes and reuses authoritative postimages within the synchronous commit.

Restart delivery records `deliveryPending` before sending and `deliverySettled`
only after confirmed delivery or a proven no-send result. Pending-final settlement
retains exact intent/payload IDs, current harness authority, actual dispositions,
and recovery-wake decisions. Usage remains best-effort; live-model failure still
propagates. Captured model/auth fields prevent an older completion from clearing
a newer selection. Known commits survive fallible publication; unknown outcomes
follow B1's existing disclosure/reconciliation contract and are not replayed by B4.

The native-incognito adapter retains the already-open memory owner. Cancellation
rejects new actor admission/disclosure without revoking accepted phase work or
receipt installation. Maintenance consumes the same committed completion entry
and the existing reply-owner settlement; no new trigger or early intent clearing.

Deleted superseded internal `persistSessionUsageUpdate` and
`consolidateLiveModelSwitchAfterRun` writers. No schema, durability, retention,
permission, released SDK or foreign-commit freshness change is intended.

Queued/steering activity retains its own actor command because that branch has
no later durable point before returning. Ordinary terminal accounting is fused.

## Measurements

Four alternating B1,B4 pairs on one admitted, task-owned AWS Crabbox lease.
Each run completed 13 successful turns, a second session, control, cron,
compaction and shutdown. Warmed all-thread statements fell **681.95 → 615.35**
(−66.60, −9.77%); DB requests **168.5 → 163.9** and total worker requests
**169.9 → 165.2**. Explicit native commits fell **66.1 → 64.05**.
The overall actor target is not reached by this lane; only the verified saving
is claimed. No savings are attributed to moving work between threads.

The shared census harness is unchanged. Task-local analysis corrects a
source-map-sensitive CPU classifier: `recordProviderPrompt` has the same
zero-SQL CPU contract in source and bundled stacks. This removes 16 wrongly
classified candidate DB requests across each full run, without changing total
worker requests, statements, frames, or transactions. Native attribution groups
by thread, operation and normalized SQL, not source-map-dependent filenames.

pre-run entry's writer with the writer claimed by execution. The repair carries
the existing native settlement's exact writer through the execution result,
including zero-compaction turns, into ordinary and queued completion. It adds
no reads, requests or handshake. A real-finalizer regression failed with
`Terminal accounting session changed` before repair and passed afterward
(3.77 s test time; 47.83 s Vitest, 148.49 s wrapper including worker compilation).

native-incognito suite (6/6; 15.52 s Vitest / 51.50 s wrapper), and T1 no-growth

database, with no replacement worker owner or disk database. The broader
current-head owner selection then passed 80 tests across 13 files / five shards
(166.16 s wrapper) at `c7198b99c8f2e`. The preceding infra shard passed 124 tests
but found an obsolete two-command delivery assertion; the only intervening edit
updates that test to require one command and zero preparatory reads, preserving

227 real reply-runner cases and public non-main session creation durability
(448.26 s wrapper); 151 dispatch/settlement tests (142.20 s Vitest / 155.72 s
wrapper); and all 24 restart-recovery tests (133.75 s Vitest / 151.16 s wrapper).
The restart regression requires exactly one `deliveryPending` command and no
preparatory read. Later changes in that owner only add lint-required braces.

and clear mock calls in cleanup; all three corrected cases passed on Linux
(36.98 s Vitest / 38.67 s wrapper). No foreign-commit polling was restored.

schema-version/storage/media/sidecar guards, webhook ordering and pairing guards.

were repaired without widening budgets or suppressing diagnostics. Final B1
integration only changed pure-reader reuse, unused callback removal, fixture
types and the relocated assertion baseline; production types and touched lint
were rerun on the final head.

## Size and follow-ups

### Chosen compromises

No B4-specific fencing token, generation ledger, recovery journal, or settlement
handshake is added. Completion uses B1's existing actor contract and the existing
delivery intent/payload identity. A proven version refusal retries once from its
returned postimage without an extra preparatory read. An unknown
commit is not blindly retried because this actor contract does not promise
idempotent phase replay; B4 does not add a second reconciliation mechanism.

Usage-only persistence remains best effort with a diagnostic on a proven failure.
Group-intro and fallback-notice bookkeeping keeps arrival-order semantics: a
later terminal update can replace an intervening internal metadata choice. No
per-field versioning is added for that recoverable edge. Model/auth selection
retains its existing targeted guard because changing the selected credentials or
model can affect paid work. Session/intent/payload checks prevent a reset or
delivery retry from attributing data or sending a reply to the wrong operation.
Maintenance reuses the settled completion rather than adding a scheduler trigger.

Against pinned B1 `cc65e9aacc50b`: production/tooling +1,999/−1,054 (net +945);
tests/support +2,111/−1,005 (net +1,106). Guard baselines count as production/tooling.
Growth is the full terminal cutover, additive phase
contracts, receipt/authority handling, shared postimage reuse and regression
coverage; obsolete writers and duplicated old tests are removed.

Structural extractions keep the query cache, snapshot readers and queued activity
operation with narrow leaf owners. The native-runtime ownership check only retries
a publication that preceded its synchronous hook; it never retries an ownership
change made inside that hook. Otherwise suppressed no-op writes could let a second
hook invocation adopt changed authority. The existing five-field hook regression
protects that boundary.

Remote capacity: a prior Testbox waited 15 minutes without a runner and was
stopped; the authorized AWS fallback reused one task-owned lease and one remote
slot. The lease is now stopped; its campaign slot is released. Raw/duplicate
measurement downloads and automatic evidence archives were removed from active
proof storage; compact summaries and cited logs remain for the lander.
Other earlier capacity waits are recorded in the lane notes. No local
Docker was used. This is a READY stacked PR against `dbasync/actorb1`;
retarget as the parent lands. Do not merge this lane as part of publication.

Integration corrections: entry-only callers retain fallback/group bookkeeping
through the shared pure reducers (no second durable writer). Native-memory
acquisition permits canonical keys in an explicitly selected incognito store;
the exact path, original owner/incarnation, and canonical agent-key checks stay
in place. Durable integration assertions now consume the published postimage,
not a superseded object alias. The usage suite uses the existing broker-capable
test shard; its earlier hostless-thread failures were fixed, not suppressed.

The maintenance fixture repair does not restore foreign-commit polling. It keeps
the lifecycle and logical-source admission checks meaningful under SINGLE OWNER:
the changed lifecycle is published by the same native writer as production.
Regression owners: `agent-runner-result-accounting.persistence.test.ts` covers
the real finalizer and no-send completion, successor model/auth selection, and
committed failures; `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-writes.test.ts` covers no-op
entry/window/snapshot suppression; `model-setup.ownership.test.ts` preserves
authority when a native hook changes any of the five ownership fields;
`restart-recovery-receipt.test.ts` and `delivery-completion.test.ts` cover exact
custody, wrong-source/tool refusal, post-preparation revocation and confirmation.

prs.title: perf(sessions): batch input acceptance and run adoption
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat acceptance and run adoption repeatedly fetch the same session state and issue separate durable writes before acknowledging input or starting a run.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Accepted input remains durable before the started acknowledgement; retries adopt canonical input rather than append it twice. Restart recovery still verifies its source/run, and a handled hook cannot restart the model or broader tool surface. No schema, retention, permission, stored-byte, or operator migration change is intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the B2 cutover, stacked on `dbasync/actorb1` at `6e8a0034934cc2c914562f7bade42cf1d2c49a3e`. Gateway recorder acceptance uses `acceptInput`; run adoption and before/after-hook checkpoints use `adoptRun`. Input and lifecycle adoption share a transaction where no external effect separates them. MAIN reads the actor's published replica, while cold history, canonical retry bodies, Goals, and complex source predicates retain their bounded readers. A post-restart-abort readiness check retains its terminal reader because public actor disclosure is already revoked.

The existing admission owns actor retention and settlement. Native-incognito sessions use an adapter to their original memory owner, never a replacement file or durable database. Released native/SDK entry points remain named compatibility paths; actor-bound internal calls do not run the legacy writer as well. The superseded `restart-admission` operation is deleted. Exact committed receipts are captured before fallible publication, preserving committed-error custody and synchronous SDK completion semantics.

### Compromises and size

The implementation reuses the existing admission, writer, idempotency keys, and commit receipts. It does not add a retry journal, fencing token, nonce protocol, or a second settlement owner. Integration removed the adoption preflight/retry loop, the separate accepted-only replica reader, and the legacy outer FIFO reservation around actor staging (which reproduced a self-deadlock). Unknown worker outcomes retain the existing owner's contract; this cutover does not blindly replay them or create new reconciliation machinery. Optional cleanup warnings retain their existing best-effort behavior.

The remaining three actor reads per warmed turn are an explicit limit, not a hidden saving. Canonical retry payloads are read when needed rather than duplicating all transcript bodies in memory. Hook side-effect ambiguity across a process crash remains governed by the existing durable checkpoints; this PR does not promise exactly-once external hook execution.

Small additive contract changes carry an input-only transcript turn without a pending row, allow `adoptRun` to commit that turn with its lifecycle, and distinguish a lost response from a failed publication on an already-captured commit. These preserve existing recorder and SDK results; they are not new writers or retry protocols.

Diff against B1: production **+1,388 / −250**, tests/support **+1,406 / −173**, docs **+25 / −6**. Growth is principally the compatibility-preserving actor binding/commit bridge and regressions at native, recovery, and Gateway boundaries. No line-cap or lint suppression was loosened. Actor acquisition stays lazy, and its factory-owned recorder binding lives with the actor rather than making shared admission-receipt contracts depend on actor code. An unused actor accessor and its redundant test assertions were removed.

Remote evidence: the three alternating pairs ran in [the measurement run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a58e4ddd12da2e736cb060d066682fd4). Focused/static/SDK checks ran on AWS Crabbox lease `cbx_e814e91655e1` in [the final gates run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6423344f2dd33bdfd5109d5d9cf03659). The [27-graph typecheck](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c5cfaec9c915c1ac95eeef3bf88bdb81), [first targeted completion](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8212bfb122c32d2fe6a6eac31f6a38b4), [Gateway completion](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_935bdcfb794a13f15939b0c667abf820), and [final custody/type completion](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0a878d6fe7249a0e1e768c42bb37a3c7) used the same lease.

Targeted completions ran 278 s, 77 s, and 85 s, preserving passed graphs while fixing the remaining test-only optional calls and staged-snapshot discrimination. The final three graphs passed at `def5d6d30baf`; no production changes followed `09c3e2b0149f`. Follow-up runtime proof passed 27 recorder tests at `955ce1a44183` (18.68 s Vitest / 24.51 s wrapper), 38 Gateway pending-input tests at `7f87bdf310b4` (104.51 s / 107.67 s), and 16 native/custody tests at final `def5d6d30baf` (25.85 s wrapper). Final four-file formatting passed; lint reports only the already-disclosed Gateway test line cap, 1,038/1,000 lines, in 27 s. An earlier invocation's flag placement was rejected before any graph ran. These are pinned, composited results, not a claim of one full final-head CI run.

Full declaration inspection found actor completion keys/payload results, optional committed-receipt callbacks, internal reply/admission actor bindings, and removal of the superseded `restart-admission` variant. Existing two-argument transcript callbacks remain valid with the optional third argument. Actor-contract narrowing is against the unreleased B1 contract; the removed internal variant was introduced October 8, after published stable `2026.9.9` and beta `2026.10.1-beta.2`. No removed or narrowed released writable SDK input was identified; this is not a zero-diff claim.
- Published-driver × candidate update cell: **pending (lander)**, per lane proof split. No update success is claimed.

### Known inherited check failures and proof limits

The native changed-check plan was executed against B1 at `3f348fd8a8d2`: 33 commands, plus the separately disclosed line-growth advisory. Integration lint/test-type errors found there were fixed; final successor results are reported above rather than calling that old run green.

The remaining inherited diagnostics are pinned to the **stacked B1 base**, not mislabeled as current-main failures:

The parent-only unused `MockConfig` lint warning was fixed on main and is not claimed as a current-main failure. No main integration is needed merely to import these unrelated fixes; the chain's retarget/landing owner will pick them up.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse committed session projection facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session metadata and transcript publications discard independent Gateway row facts and repeat database reads; Memory also resolves the same queued session corpus twice.

This is Phase C `pcrows`, stacked on #168602 and targeting `dbasync/actorb1`.

## User Impact

Session lists and channel readers retain current Board, ACP, workspace, and summary freshness facts with fewer database round trips. Streaming presentation keeps its existing coalescing window. Memory indexing observes appends and forgetting tombstones committed while notifications are queued.

There is no schema, SDK, retention, configuration, update, Doctor, plugin-loading, or service-lifecycle change. Target selection, session-entry readers, and B2–B4 write commands are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway projection consumes canonical transcript receipts and keeps independent row facets across same-lifecycle metadata publications. A receipt installs its committed watermark before observers run; an unmatched notification or explicit invalidation follows the existing bounded read path. Shared facts stay reusable only while their bindings match. This uses the existing projection and writer receipt owners without another cache, generation protocol, or cross-thread handshake.

The actor hot snapshot does not contain Board presence, so this reuses the existing projection facets and transcript postimages without expanding the shared actor contract. Remaining initial/fallback row acquisition and activity-summary source reads stay visible in the measurements.

Memory queues session identities directly and resolves corpus membership and tombstones once in the indexing owner. The earlier notification-time resolution is removed. No SQLite-specific SQL is added.

The diff is +80 net production lines, +185 test/support lines, and +11 documentation lines. The extra production code connects existing receipt postimages to the existing row projection and preserves its invalidation/coalescing lifecycle.

## Evidence

Three alternating pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C) ran the shared harness on base `6e8a0034934c` and candidate `fa9baeee005e`. Each warmed observation is the mean of ten turns; values below are median [min–max] across the three observations. Every sample completed 13 successful turns, RPCs, cron, compaction and shutdown.

| Warmed metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All-thread SQL statements | 677 [659.1–677.2] | 663.4 [644.2–663.5] |
| MAIN SQL statements | 11.2 [8.6–11.2] | 11.2 [8.6–11.2] |
| All logical requests | 169.4 [165.1–169.5] | 163.5 [159.1–164] |
| DB requests | 146.2 [142.2–146.3] | 140.7 [136.5–141.2] |
| This lane: SQL / requests | 61.1 / 16.4 | 46.5 / 11.6 |

Logical requests include CPU and release operations, matching the census. DB requests exclude releases and the two source-identified CPU-only tasks; zero-SQL database commands still count. `session-entry` is excluded from this lane because pcentry owns it.

| Warmed operation | Base SQL / requests | Candidate SQL / requests | Delta SQL / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `session-row-facts` | 32 / 6.4 | 22 / 4.4 | -10 / -2 |
| `sessionRows.sharedFacts` | 4.3 / 6.4 | 2.4 / 4.4 | -1.9 / -2 |
| `session-corpus-inventory` | 2.6 / 0.8 | 1.6 / 0.4 | -1 / -0.4 |
| `session-tombstones` | 3.2 / 0.8 | 1.6 / 0.4 | -1.6 / -0.4 |
| `session-row-backfill` | 5 / 1 | 5 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| `session-activity-summary-source` | 14 / 1 | 14 / 1 | 0 / 0 |

First-turn SQL decreased 1727 [1701–1892] → 1693 [1505–1889]. Entire-workload SQL decreased 15544 [15533–15630] → 15383 [15322–15469], and logical requests decreased 2950 [2950–2969] → 2887 [2885–2903]. Warmed duration ratio was 1.014, with no phase-skew failure. The lane target remains an aim: the remaining row acquisition, preview backfill and summary-source reads are not eliminated by this change.

Phase attribution: boot+connect was +24 SQL (+0.76%); its increases are in unchanged delivery, cron scheduling, plugin-state, image and device owners, with zero lane work in that phase. Startup including the first turn decreased by 14 SQL. Cron performed three additional `session-row-backfill` requests (+15 SQL), and the same +3/+15 remains in the whole-workload backfill total. This is a known cost in the changed projection owner, not attributed to unrelated noise. Warmed backfill remains 1 request / 5 SQL. Receipt-triggered materialization can precede the normal transcript notification; further optional-preview coalescing is a follow-up, preserving immediate summary freshness. No new scheduling or invalidation protocol was added to hide this cost. Whole-workload statements and requests still decrease.

Remote focused proof on the candidate used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file | Passed | Command wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/gateway/session-row-projection.publication.test.ts` | 7 | 41.873 |

| `src/gateway/session-row-projection.backfill.test.ts` | 13 | 43.333 |
| `src/gateway/session-row-projection.transcript-regression.test.ts` | 1 | 43.484 |

These 97 tests cover projection publication, archived/current summary freshness, worker-read fallbacks, preview backfill, streaming coalescing, and queued Memory appends/tombstones. The new transcript regression warms the first append before measuring the real row-facts and shared-facts boundaries; it does not count a CPU-only worker wrapper as a SQL read. Focused command wall time totals 318.873 seconds; CI runtime itself has not been measured.

Madge passed (18.914s), T1 passed without growth, and the dialect ratchet passed without added SQLite-specific SQL. Two isolated Codex autoreview rounds were scoped-clean at P2. No SDK surface changed, and the published-driver × candidate update cell does not apply.

`check:changed --base 6e8a0034934c --head fa9baeee005e` completed remotely in 2094.031s. prs.title: refactor(ui): port identity components to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves identity rendering to Solid 2 while the Control UI continues to support Lit callers.

## User Impact

Avatars, person mentions, participant facepiles, and session ownership chips keep their existing tags, classes, accessibility labels, and navigation behavior. No settings or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each registered identity tag now has one Solid implementation through the shared bridge; its Lit class is deleted. The existing image cache, authenticated-route loader, presence projection, and hovercard controller still own resources and behavior. Lit callers retain the stateless artwork helpers during migration.

The image binding retains a replacement lease before releasing the previous lease, preserves loaded state on label updates, and drops stale completions. Promise-valued image resources stay opaque to Solid's async memo handling. Channel fallbacks use one stable child outlet so a Lit caller can update its range while the image is showing.

Small coupled changes let the existing avatar loaders accept Solid lifecycle callbacks, share card rendering with the sidebar, extract the presence-expiry lifecycle, and expose the existing i18n projection revision for labels derived by plain helpers.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused local lint | Passed |
| Local viewer-facepile | 19 passed; 20.31s wrapper wall |
| Local direct Solid identity cases | 6 passed; 14.08s wrapper wall |
| Local session-owner-chip | 5 passed; 12.62s wrapper wall |
| Local channel fallback | 1 passed; 11.68s wrapper wall |
| Local plugin session summary callers | 9 passed; 24.24s wrapper wall |
| Local sidebar people | 148 passed; 165.43s wrapper wall |
| Local authenticated routes | 13 passed; 52.59s wrapper wall |
| Local Lit ratchet | Passed against the merge base |
| Remote typecheck/build/E2E | Testbox source preparation exceeded the 15-minute admission window; no tests ran. PR CI is the heavy-check proof. |
| Autoreview | Scoped-clean P0–P2 on the cutover and follow-up type/plugin repairs |
| Avatar resource lifecycle | 20 passed; 78.22s wrapper wall (17.48s Vitest, 0.88s test bodies) |
| Plugin imperative avatar API | 2 passed; 72.54s wrapper wall (11.43s Vitest) |

### Size

Across changed production files, 3,536 → 3,984 lines (+448); tests and proof scripts excluded. This remains above the requested no-growth target. The retained growth has concrete causes: typed property/host contracts for six bridge tags; native JSX alongside stateless artwork still needed by unported Lit callers; a shared card render/clear entry point for the existing sidebar and Solid mentions; and callback lifecycle adapters for the existing resource owners. The full Lit classes and intermediate wrapper layers are removed, with no second registered implementation, new resource registry, or copied domain state.

### Screenshots

Inspected synthetic fixtures from the same browser: Lit at base `53b811864752`, Solid after the bridge cutover. The side-by-side frames use 1180px desktop and 390px mobile viewports and cover generated/emoji/image/system avatars, viewer sizes, pending/failed images, owner/participant/overflow stacks, facepiles, channel fallback/image, and mentions. Browser chrome was cropped before upload. The earlier mocked-Gateway person-reference/header run passed 13 tests on baseline `171df4e1c5a0`; current-head route E2E remains CI proof.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse actor replica for entry and target reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm chat turns repeatedly discover the same session store and reload the same session entry, despite the session actor already publishing committed facts. This is the Phase C entry/target reader lane, stacked on #168602.

## User Impact

Reduces database work during ordinary turns without changing session data, public APIs, configuration, or update behavior. Cold entries, historical session-ID lookups, and reads requiring missing membership/participant facts continue through the existing bounded worker read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Entry readers now share the actor's bounded MAIN replica instead of maintaining a second entry cache. Complete commit receipts refresh entry-only facts without certifying transcript/custody state; source-only metadata notices preserve those facts. Cache lifecycle resets clear residency and lazily restore the receipt subscription. Ordered cohorts keep their existing writer ordering and before/after consistency check. Native writes without a sealed postimage invalidate the projection and require one cold read before reuse.

Store selection reuses registry- and physical-identity-bound results. Fixed-store inventory also observes in-process writes; family/scoped inventories retain discovery because their sibling row dependencies are not exhaustively captured. Current-session transcript selection consumes the prepared entry; historical/keyless selection retains the persisted index. ACP metadata and subagent-run maintenance remain with their existing independent owners.

## Evidence

Pinned comparison: base `6e8a0034934c` vs candidate `15defc052238`; three alternating pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C) on the same AWS `c7a.8xlarge`, using the shared workload. Warmed values are each run’s mean of ten turns, summarized as median [min–max].

The extra warmed shift is +3 SQL/turn (+0.45%): corpus inventory contributes +3.3, unassigned/MAIN +1.1, tombstones +0.7, `session.entry.read` +0.5; inventory −1.3, runtime target −1.0, shared facts −0.3, exact entries −0.1, and ACP metadata −0.1 offset it. One queued `prewarm` request lacked an owner stack in the reducer: it remains counted in total requests and is labeled unclassified rather than guessed as database/CPU work. prs.title: fix(google): cap Gemini embedding request batches
prs.body:
Closes #134015

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gemini-backed memory indexing aborted when a token-bounded group contained more than 100 short chunks. The provider sent the full group to `batchEmbedContents`, exceeding Gemini's per-request limit instead of completing the sync.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gemini provider now owns its API-specific limit and sends document embeddings in sequential batches of at most 100 requests. It preserves input/output order and reuses the existing authentication, SSRF, abort, response-validation, and vector-sanitization path for every sub-batch. Generic memory batching and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

Memory sync and `openclaw memory index` can process large sets of short chunks with the default inline Gemini embedding path instead of failing at 101 requests. If a later sub-batch fails, the original provider error is still surfaced and no further batches are sent.

## Evidence

- TDD regression proof before the fix: the new 101-input test failed with `expected [101] to deeply equal [100, 1]` while the other 40 provider tests passed.
- Focused Google provider suite after the fix: **44/44 passed**.
- Boundary coverage verifies 100, 101, and 201 inputs split as `[100]`, `[100, 1]`, and `[100, 100, 1]`, with exact output ordering.
- Failure coverage verifies a rejected second sub-batch prevents a third request.
- Full `pnpm build`: passed on the rebased head.
- `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Review Follow-up

- The P3 finding is addressed on the current head by documenting that the 100-item value is the external Gemini `batchEmbedContents` API contract and linking the Google API documentation.
- The focused provider suite remained green after that documentation change: **44/44 passed**; `oxfmt --check` also passed.
- No simulated run is presented as real Gemini API evidence. A redacted post-fix run against Google's actual endpoint is still pending, so this PR intentionally remains in Draft.

## Risk

Low and provider-scoped. Calls with at most 100 inputs retain the existing single-request behavior. Larger calls become sequential requests, avoiding extra concurrency and preserving rate-limit and cancellation semantics.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

TRAE assisted with issue and source inspection, implementation planning, test drafting, the provider-scoped code change, and local verification. The contributor selected and approved the provider-boundary design, reviewed the resulting scope, and retains responsibility for the contribution. No credentials or private production data were provided to the assistant.

prs.title: refactor(ui): port the chat composer to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Port the Chat composer, its invocation menus, and model/effort/permission controls from Lit to Solid 2. Chat and New Session keep their existing host tags, classes, selectors, and callbacks while sharing one Solid renderer through small Lit adapters.

## User Impact

Users keep the existing composer behavior, including native typing, IME, undo, dictation, and menu focus, while the surface moves to Solid. There are no dependency upgrades, configuration migrations, or required user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing TypeScript controllers still own drafts, dictation, queue state, and capability decisions. Stable Solid boundaries retain the textarea, buttons, queue editors, and popup scroll containers. The existing composer controls `.ts` boundary owns Lit compatibility; new Solid renderers contain no Lit imports. Per-property adapter projections prevent unrelated changes from rewriting native input values. Native typing/IME keeps browser-owned input state; changing draft scope retires the old input and rejects its late events. Dictation completion retains the callback and draft scope that initiated Send.

This also ports the Add MCP Server dialog without changing its capability owner. Directly coupled files outside the composer prefixes only update renderer imports and dictation accessors. No dependencies, version pins, or changelog entries change.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(acp): keep long backend reviews running
prs.body:
Related: #156331

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the five-minute ingress startup watchdog can cancel an ACP backend review and replay its inbound message after the backend has already accepted the turn.

## User Impact

Adopted ACP reviews can continue beyond that startup watchdog. Explicit stop and the configured ACP execution deadline still apply. No operator configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry an optional, fallible adoption callback through the reply-dispatch hook and SDK adapter to the manager's prepared prompt-submission boundary. The host retires the callback with its dispatch; ACP acknowledges once across runtime retries and rechecks live input and run authority before and after adoption. Existing claiming-hook admission and binding-route checks remain in place.

Current upstream already removed acpx's full-turn hook deadline. This PR repairs ingress adoption; the manager retains execution deadline ownership. It addresses the ingress-replay portion of #156331, whose separate execution/progress watchdog request remains open.

The ADR and hook/setup documentation explain the boundary. No dependency, permission, queue schema, or retention change is introduced.

## Evidence

Tests use the real SQLite ingress drain and host reply-dispatch/SDK path with stubbed hook routing and backend execution. An adopted review survives past five minutes, tombstones the original event, suppresses redelivery, and delivers its result. A separate synthetic backend exercises the real manager and staged transcript input: retiring input custody during adoption prevents actual prompt effects. Regressions cover startup expiry, callback rejection, explicit stop, retry idempotency, and retained callbacks after dispatch completion/cancellation. The ingress test uses the existing forked SQLite-broker lane.

Earlier negative proof on base `8386945a08dfa2ae0fdd6e5c57b0875d42eaca62` restored only the upstream host hook and reproduced the active ingress claim after backend submission. Updated-base tests pass after the upstream test-helper rename. Final report-only source review of published head `2c9f635faabec1f8ebabdd1d3efd073105ca81c4` covers all 17 files and 14 aspects with no remaining actionable findings. No live Gateway deployment or Claude canary has been performed.

Single-file wall times measured before the helper rename with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: ingress 26.54s (includes worker preparation; cases about 1.7s), hook scope 9.69s, adoption 9.89s, owner 46.87s. The owner suite retains real custody, manager lifecycle, binding/question/reset settlement; a mock cannot prove custody retirement blocks backend effects. CI seconds are pending.

## Review feedback and remaining gates

At head `c328676`, the real-manager owner suite now verifies successful real SQLite ingress adoption, token reassignment preserving the successor claim while preventing backend prompt effects, and delegated-run revocation before or during acknowledgement. Authority closure is asserted outside caught execution; refusal cases require the intended error. All 18 owner tests pass (`pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 62.04s wall; Vitest 53.15s). Messaging test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, and fresh review of the test delta pass. Production code is unchanged from reviewed/built head `2c9f635...`; earlier whole-patch evidence stays pinned to that head.

The contributor/operator approved implementing the callback in the originating session. That does **not** establish OpenClaw maintainer acceptance: ADR-001 remains Proposed. Upstream public-contract acceptance and redacted shipped Gateway/channel evidence of one ten-minute Claude review plus a separate explicit-stop review remain outstanding. With operator approval, the compatible source-built 2026.9.8 backport has now been installed through the normal updater. The restarted Gateway reports the expected patched build ID; health RPC passes and readiness reports `ready=true` with no failing checks. Post-update status reports no unfinished plugin upgrades. This is deployment/health evidence only: the ten-minute Claude completion and separate explicit-stop channel canaries have not run. The local backport retains its release base and does not claim to be the upstream PR commit.

### Hosted CI follow-up

The [failed CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096634346) tested merge `6b4126ef1305aff0336fa29330c6fc2c2a94f502` against main `76a282c7a1c6ca958517ce15f13e17371c14be11`. Its three failing jobs were the SDK surface-report tests and lint stripes 2 and 4. The SDK checker, plugin-state observation cache, and SQLite comparison test are byte-identical to that base; this PR does not modify them. The next upstream commit, [f9940dc8a794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f9940dc8a794948cf24492fd881296b60296ff4a), repairs the exact SDK-budget, shadowing/type-conversion, and unbound-method failures.

Head `97ffab124d316290734c323154ba427b50ec67c0` rebases the same two patch commits onto that upstream repair. `git range-diff` reports both commits unchanged. Fresh local regression results: all 133 ACP/ingress tests pass, and five SDK surface tests pass; the compiler-lifetime test is Linux-only and is skipped on macOS. The registered `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, core production types, messaging test types, typed lint for the patch and upstream lint repairs, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. [Hosted CI run 38106646476](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38106646476) completed successfully at this exact head, including the SDK tooling shard, all five core lint stripes, production/test types, and the CI gate. Some unrelated/platform jobs are skipped by the selected plan; this is not a full release certification. Earlier full-build and whole-patch review evidence remains pinned to its original head.

## Test plan

### Pre-merge

- [x] On base `76352725380446589cb050ab252dddf8196a2c96`: full `pnpm build`, 4m 39.5s. Build emits a Control UI startup-size advisory (368.2 KiB gzip versus 366.1 KiB); no UI files change here.
- [x] 129 tests in eight files through the curated runner, including both corrected regression suites, real-manager custody, dispatcher, host callback scope, SDK forwarding, hook routing, and ingress watchdog; 1m 55.5s, no skips.
- [x] Core production types, the messaging test type graph, and typed lint/formatting for all 13 changed TypeScript/JavaScript files; `git diff --check`.
- [x] Earlier snapshot validation on base `8386945a08dfa2ae0fdd6e5c57b0875d42eaca62`: all 27 core-test type partitions, extension production/test types, SDK exports/surface, plugin boundary and staged contract guards. Documentation audit: 14,965 links, zero broken links. Callback source and docs are unchanged by the final test-import repair.
- [ ] Full repository static/test suites were not rerun after the final base refresh. Earlier `check:changed --staged` failed identically on unchanged base `8386945...`: 456 environment names versus budget 455, with identical name sets. The unused-export gate reproduced four identical baseline findings. Broad core lint reported seven unchanged files over their line caps; it was stopped after those failures, and remaining full core/extension/script lint was not completed. No budgets or suppressions were changed; focused lint passes.
- [x] Hosted CI and required CI gate pass at `97ffab124d316290734c323154ba427b50ec67c0`; see the linked run above for selected jobs and skips.
- [ ] Not run: live Claude/channel tests.

### Post-merge

- [ ] After deployment approval, install/build the merged revision through the normal OpenClaw update workflow and verify Gateway health.
- [ ] Run one Claude ACP channel review lasting at least ten minutes; record adoption/completion, verify no ingress handler-timeout or duplicate dispatch, and confirm one final reply.
- [ ] Verify explicit stop cancels a separate adopted review and genuine startup failure remains retryable.

Rollout: validate the approved deployment with that canary before relying on long reviews. Rollback: if accepted turns replay, lost adoption still submits, or stop fails, revert and rebuild/redeploy through the normal update workflow. Existing Gateway logs and runtime status provide evidence; no new flag or monitoring system is added.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep standalone headings with following content
prs.body:
Closes #149758

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heading-only memory chunks taking small search result windows away from useful content, especially with local embedding models.

## User Impact

Markdown headings stay with the following content chunk by default. Existing builtin indexes rebuild once on normal search or synchronization after upgrading; no new setting or manual reindex is needed. Memory source files and database schemas are unchanged. A trailing heading without following content stays searchable. Oversized headings already split by the chunker retain their fragments, and provider input limits still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index preparation now merges standalone ATX heading chunks before embeddings, preserving the following curated entry's annotation scope and source line references. It updates the chunk text, embedding input, and content hash together, including partial heading overlap. The existing chunking-version repair path handles version 5 → 6 and retains keyword access if rebuilding fails.

Production: +39/-12 lines (net +27). Tests: +74/-0. The old empty-chunk filter is folded into the preparation loop; making the change neutral would require unrelated deletion.

## Evidence

- Regression first failed on the original main source for both keyword-only and embedding publication: standalone headings remained in the stored index. Candidate: all 27 focused tests pass, including the oversized-heading continuation regression raised and resolved during independent review.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-chunk-writer.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 322.24 s wall including worker compilation on the shared host; test time 0.115 s, 25.489 s, and 114.034 s respectively. The existing upgrade suite exercises real SQLite publication, retirement, reopening, and failure recovery; those contracts need the manager/storage boundary. New assertions verify no second publication or embedding work after reopening.
- Live baseline: real offline `openclaw memory index` and `memory search 73190842 --max-results 3 --json`, Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic corpus with 16 heading/bullet sections and one numeric-ID document. Baseline returned the exact document plus two unrelated bare headings (`## People`, `## Miscellaneous`), with vector scores 0.485 and 0.480. This exercises real embedding transport, indexing, and search, not a chat-model answer.
- Candidate live upgrade: the first ordinary search rebuilt the existing version-5 index to version 6 (33 → 17 chunks; 16 → 0 heading-only chunks). All three results contain real content; the exact numeric-ID document remains first. A second ordinary index + search in new CLI processes left index metadata, revision, chunk IDs/text/timestamps, and schema identical. The upgrade warning appears only on the first search. Database schema SQL is unchanged across upgrade.
- `pnpm build` passes. Source/test ratchets, config docs baseline, plugin inventory, docs links, and core production/test typechecks pass. The first broad extension typecheck exposed a missing QA Lab workspace dependency in Gateway-only preparation; full worktree preparation and the affected checks are in progress. No source change for that setup gap.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 on `88ab5d0f7e674f2ff606ffb7ea52739044c793b0`; the one actionable finding from the first pass was fixed and regression-tested.
- Exact-head CI and ClawSweeper review are pending. The PR is not being merged by this lane.

## What Problem This Solves

Moves the lobster pet from Lit to Solid 2 while keeping the `openclaw-lobster-pet` host, CSS, selectors, and caller properties.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Solid bridge owns the registered tag. Its synchronous TypeScript controller owns animation decisions and timers, survives a same-host remount, and retires each view's listeners and timers. Solid observes committed scene snapshots. Geometry, interactions, and traffic have explicit lifetimes instead of Lit controllers. prs.title: fix(cli): invalidate Gateway-cached MCP runtimes on mcp reload
prs.body:
Closes #164642

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp reload` reported "Disposed cached MCP runtimes", but it only disposed CLI-local runtimes. The Gateway process owns its own cached session MCP runtimes, and the CLI command could not reach across the process boundary — so the Gateway's stdio MCP server kept serving the stale runtime and subsequent agent turns never saw the new MCP config.

## What Changed

- New gateway method `mcp.reloadRuntimes` (`mcp-app` family, `operator.write`): disposes the Gateway-side session MCP runtimes via the existing `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` owner.
- The CLI's `mcp reload` dispatches the method before the local dispose and degrades gracefully when no Gateway is reachable (the CLI-local dispose always runs; the log states which side was disposed).

## Evidence

- Handler regression (`mcp.reload-runtimes.test.ts`): the method disposes all session MCP runtimes and acknowledges `{ ok: true }`. Red on `origin/main` (no such method).
- Suites: recovery 222/222, `session-accessor.readonly` 26/26, `server-startup-post-attach` 115/115; `tsc` core clean in all touched files.
- The reporter's source inspection (CLI-local dispose only) matches the pre-fix behavior; the gateway-side dispose reuses the same owner the server-close path already calls.


## Update — 2026-10-04 (Rev 3 rework)

- **Lease-preserving reload**: the handler now runs the Gateway's own config-reload path (`reloadSessionMcpRuntimes`, the same one the hot-reload flow uses) instead of the shutdown-grade `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` — admitted calls keep their runtimes; only stale ones rebuild on the next turn. The manager's `reloadConfig` propagates per-runtime reload failures (no swallowed errors).
- **Authority revalidation**: the handler reads the request's mutation authority and asserts it current immediately before the reload — a caller revoked during the acquisition wait can no longer trigger it.
- **CLI output**: the failure branch now states which side was disposed and that the Gateway-side reload was **not confirmed** (no more misleading "active agents use new config" assurance when the reload did not run); the no-Gateway case is labeled explicitly. The import-boundary assertion follows.
- Handler tests: reload shape (`reloadPlugins: false`), authority revalidation observed, and the failure path responding with an error shape.

Still open: the authority-chain live evidence (allowed reload, read-only rejection, queued revocation preventing closure, discovery/active-call survival) and the command-scope framing — the reload semantics now match the Gateway's own hot-reload behavior rather than a Gateway-wide teardown.
