prs.title: feat: opt-in append-only runtime context for custom Chat Completions
prs.body:
Related: #158898

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Chat Completions models behind a prefix-caching proxy (for example GPT models on Amazon Bedrock served through LiteLLM) rewrite most of the prompt into the provider cache on every request in channel conversations, and rewrite a growing tail while runtime facts are active, because earlier requests are not exact prefixes of later ones.

## User Impact

User impact: operators of config-defined `openai-completions` providers can set `compat.appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` on a model so that each request is a pure append of the previous one and prefix caches hit again. Nothing changes for models that do not set the flag. Tradeoff when enabled: earlier runtime-context carriers and inbound channel metadata stay in context until compaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config-defined providers without a replay hook (LiteLLM, generic OpenAI-compatible gateways) resolve their transcript policy through the unowned transport fallback. On current `main` that policy breaks the prefix in two ways for upstreams whose automatic cache only matches a byte-identical earlier request:

- whenever the trailing runtime-context carrier is non-empty, it is removed from history on the next request and a new one is appended, so the previous request is no longer a prefix. In channel sessions the carrier carries the inbound conversation info (message id, sender) and is non-empty from the first request, so the upstream never gets a reusable cache point and the whole prompt is rewritten on every request;
- in CLI sessions the carrier is omitted while no runtime facts are active, so the cache survives until a fact appears (running exec, subagent, media task); from then on everything after the last carrier-free request is rewritten on every request, and the write grows with each turn.

#164804 enables append-only for Responses routes from existing capability flags and deliberately leaves `openai-completions` unchanged; tying retention to an existing transport flag also raised a semantics-expansion concern there. This PR uses a new, explicit per-model opt-in instead, honored only by that fallback on Chat Completions. Provider-owned replay policies stay authoritative. Only `appendOnlyRuntimeContext` changes; tool-id sanitizing, reasoning replay and turn validation are untouched, and the flag is part of the policy cache key.

The flag lives in `compat` but is an operator replay preference, not an endpoint capability, so catalog compat ownership does not apply to it: when a discovered or static catalog row matches the configured route, capability flags still come from the catalog and only this key is carried over from config, and `doctor` does not report it as a catalog override.

## Evidence

### Live, on a build of this branch

A self-hosted production gateway (1 vCPU / 3.7 GB, Linux arm64) runs this branch: the npm package was built from `779ba36f348` with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` on GitHub Actions (the host cannot run the full build), and reports `OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (779ba36)`. Upstream: LiteLLM 1.102.1 to Bedrock Converse (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`; automatic prompt caching only). All content below is synthetic. Each comparison runs on the same build and only flips the flag on the same model row (hot reload, no restart). Numbers are OpenClaw's per-request `cacheRead` / `cacheWrite` from `diagnostics.cacheTrace` and billed cost from the run metadata; "pure append" means `cacheRead` equals the previous request's full input.

Feishu direct-message session (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `/new`, then the same 8 messages including one exec tool call):

| | requests | cache hit from request 2 | pure append | cache writes | cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default (flag unset) | 10 | 33.2% | 0 / 9 | 117,686 | $0.301 |
| `appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` | 9 | 98.3% | 8 / 8 | 18,678 | $0.062 |

With the default policy the first seven requests read 0 cached tokens. Gateway-side byte comparison (below) shows why: every request drops the previous request's trailing carrier (444 characters, including the conversation info) and nothing before it changes; earlier user messages are identical across all requests.

CLI sessions through the gateway (no inbound metadata), excluding each session's first request:

| scenario | default | `appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| background exec running across 8 turns, `gpt-6.1-sol` | `cacheRead` stays flat; per-turn writes grow 97 → 426; pure append 3 / 11; writes 2,573 | ~132 per turn; 11 / 11; writes 1,327 |
| same, `gpt-6-luna` | 3 / 12; writes 2,551 | 11 / 11; writes 1,323 |
| spawn a subagent, then 3 turns after it completed, `gpt-6.1-sol` | flat `cacheRead` even after completion; writes 243 → 872 per turn; 4 / 10 | ~223 per turn; 9 / 11 |
| no runtime facts active | ~99%, pure append | ~99%, pure append |

So on current `main` the default policy is already fine for CLI turns without active runtime facts; the loss is in channel sessions and while facts are active, and there it grows with session length.

Other behavior checked on this build:

- Upgrade from 2026.9.6: `openclaw doctor --repair` migrated the agent database v23 → v24 and the state database 18 → 20; session, transcript and window rows were preserved (only new rows added). Two sessions created on 2026.9.6 resumed by `--session-id` with history intact, including carriers persisted earlier, and tool calls worked; the first request after the upgrade misses (new system prompt), then ~99%.
- LiteLLM model discovery refresh (`models list --refresh`) with the model also authored in config: the flag survives catalog merging.
- `openclaw sessions compact <key>`: one miss, then pure append again; runtime state answered correctly afterwards.
- Turning the flag off mid-session drops historical carriers from the request (about 160 tokens shorter); turning it back on restores the previous prefix byte for byte (`cacheRead` equal to the last request before the switch).
- Observation, append-only: one full miss at 00:00 UTC, where the system prompt suffix's Temporal Context changed and an earlier user message was reported as different.
- Observation, append-only: on the Feishu session the host's cache-break diagnostic reported "message N (user) differs", but the requests the gateway received were pure appends (below), so that diagnostic compares a different projection than the one that is sent.
- Remaining misses with the flag on, outside this PR: the once-per-day Temporal Context change above, and the separate model call that follows a background exec completion, which uses a different system prompt and first user message and therefore rewrites once (seen with and without the flag).

### Gateway-side verification

The LiteLLM operator compared the request logs of all windows above byte for byte, at the Chat Completions layer and after LiteLLM's Converse conversion (counts, lengths and positions only):

| window | flag | pure append (main session) | where the first difference is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Feishu | unset | 0 / 9 (plus one exec-completion call) | the previous request's trailing carrier, 444 characters, 9 / 10 requests; earlier messages unchanged |
| Feishu | `true` | 8 / 8 | none |
| CLI, background exec, `gpt-6.1-sol` / `gpt-6-luna` | unset | `cacheRead` pinned at the last carrier-free request | the trailing carrier, 203 / 205 characters, every break |
| CLI, background exec, `gpt-6.1-sol` / `gpt-6-luna` | `true` | 11 / 11 and 11 / 11 | none |
| CLI, subagent | unset / `true` | breaks at the 430-character carrier / pure append | as left |

Billing on the gateway matches OpenClaw's run metadata: Feishu $0.3450 with the flag unset (11 calls, including a $0.0443 exec-completion call) versus $0.0618 with it set.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.9.9)

Reproducible script on the same Linux host, in an isolated state directory (production untouched). The bundled `litellm` provider points at a local OpenAI-compatible mock that serves `/v1/models` (two models, one of them only known through discovery) and logs a content-free digest of every chat request (role, length, hash per message).

1. `npm i openclaw@2026.9.9` (`OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (bcfc888)`); configure `models.providers.litellm` with one authored model row; create two sessions (3 and 2 turns).
2. Install the package built from this head (`OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (747b906)`) and run `openclaw doctor --repair --non-interactive`: agent database v24 → v25 and state database 19 → 20 with pre-migration backups; session, window and transcript rows unchanged (2 / 2 / 23). Set `compat.appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` on the authored row; the other model settings are unchanged.
3. Start a temporary isolated Gateway and run `openclaw models list --provider litellm --refresh`: LiteLLM discovery calls the mock's `/v1/models` and lists both the authored and the discovered model; the authored row still carries the flag.
4. Resume both stable-release sessions by `--session-id`, then unset and set the flag again; run Doctor a second time.

What the upstream received (session A):

| step | request shape |
| --- | --- |
| 2026.9.9, turns 2–3 | the previous request's trailing carrier is dropped each time |
| first resumed request on this branch | system prompt and tools changed (new version): one full miss, as expected |
| flag set, 2 more turns | pure append; carriers retained 1 → 2 → 3 |
| flag unset | historical carriers dropped (15 → 14 messages, 0 carriers) |
| flag set again, 3 turns | the last request before unsetting (15 messages) is an exact prefix of the next one (20 messages), then pure append; carriers 4 → 5 → 6 |
| after the second Doctor | flag and model settings unchanged, history intact (46 transcript events), session resumes |

Session B shows the same pattern: one miss on the version change, then pure append with the flag.

prs.title: refactor(node-host): reuse manifest hash validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node-host Git materialization repeats commit-ID validation already owned by the workspace manifest receiver.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, protocol, configuration, or data change. Invalid manifest hashes still fail at the receiving boundary; Git still verifies that the supplied commit exists and matches the prepared objects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The only production caller of `initializeNodeWorkerGitWorkspace` obtains `baseCommit` from `decodeWorkspaceManifest`. Its canonical manifest parser already requires a lowercase 40- or 64-character hexadecimal commit ID. Remove the materializer's redundant length-only check and leave validation with that owner.

This is the final bounded cross-boundary pass after #168754. The worker, Gateway adapter, and process comparisons otherwise already use shared owners or retain distinct trust/lifecycle checks. It does not touch the active worker lane's supervisor/launch-descriptor files.

Production delta: **0 additions / 3 deletions, net −3 lines**, one file. No tests changed. No measured performance claim.

## Evidence

- AWS Linux, pinned source plus patch: `pnpm tsgo` passed (16.67 s).
- `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-workspace-git.test.ts src/node-host/node-worker-transfer-client.git.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9 passed, 1 platform skip, 30.90 s wall. Existing tests preserve Git object validation, prepared-project fallbacks, symlink handling, and platform configuration.
- Focused type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview at P0/P1: no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(release): record 2026.10.1 updater compatibility
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stable `2026.10.1` became npm `latest` at 2026-10-10T22:45Z. npm preflight runs `pnpm update:compat:check`, which requires the updater compatibility inventory to record every version selected by `latest` and `beta`. The inventory does not include `2026.10.1`, so preflight now fails for every release candidate, including `2026.10.5-beta.1` ([failed producer job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38095676471/job/114340992255)).

## Why This Change Was Made

Record `2026.10.1` with the existing generator: 56 emitted chunks. All eleven prior release records are byte-unchanged (diff is additions only). Package versions, the recorder, and runtime code are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on unchanged main: `pnpm update:compat:check` fails with `missing current npm release versions: 2026.10.1`.
- Downloaded every listed official npm tarball, verified each against its npm SHA-512 `dist.integrity`, unpacked to `.artifacts/update-compat/<version>/package`, and ran the exact `pnpm update:compat:gen` command the check prints.
- `pnpm update:compat:check` passes; `git diff --stat`: `scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json | 1589 +`, no deletions.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/update-compat-external-bindings.test.ts test/scripts/update-first-hop-package-fixtures.test.ts test/scripts/package-source-preflight.test.ts test/scripts/runtime-postbuild.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 177 passed, 60 s wall. No tests added or changed; CI test-cost delta is zero.
- `release/2026.10.5` carries the same inventory as main, so this commit applies cleanly as a backport.

prs.title: refactor(codex): simplify metadata and startup lifecycles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex carries multiple overlapping state machines for metadata changes and timing scenarios that do not warrant their ongoing complexity.

## User Impact

Normal features, security boundaries, persisted formats and public interfaces stay intact. Metadata and concurrent operator updates become explicitly best effort as detailed below; ordinary cancellation, shutdown, signed executable validation and current execution authority remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Simplify Codex metadata, desktop-artifact, startup and native-child lifecycles. Remove overlapping generation/fence state, whole-operation retries and regenerable-artifact compensation while retaining security checks at effects, durable receipts, FIFO and ordinary shutdown settlement.

The sharpened audit revisited all 13 original KEEP rows: 10 changed to full or partial removal. The three unchanged rows protect persisted catalog validation/shutdown, inference credential/prompt authority and persisted thread fingerprint upgrades. Retained pieces of the other rows protect account isolation, signed executable/path validation, current execution authority, measured caches, bounded resources and normal parallel-session ownership. No config, protocol, dependency, SQLite schema/durability/retention/permission or public SDK changes.

Production reduction: **1,583 net lines** (564 added, 2,147 removed), excluding tests, test support, fixtures, generated files, declarations and Markdown. Test deletion is not included in that count.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Plugin metadata finishing across invalidation/clear can repopulate an older snapshot; #108311 introduced the counters without a reported invalidation incident. The next refresh, TTL or restart repairs it.
- Coalesced plugin-metadata waiters share the original failure instead of recursively retrying; #108311 supplied no user requirement for waiter-owned replay. A later ordinary call retries.
- App-inventory success/error can publish across invalidation or a forced successor; #115866/#162032 give synthetic race/review evidence, not a human actual-use incident. TTL or the next refresh repairs metadata and diagnostics.
- Overlapping targeted inventory invalidations use one stale bit rather than scope subtraction; #115866 identifies the extra scopes as review hardening. Unrefreshed metadata can remain stale until its next refresh/TTL.
- Resident config replacement no longer waits on a per-home replacement protocol or rejects every old read by epoch; #151545 supplies feature/synthetic tests, not a human incident. Old views close and settle their writes; overlapping reads are best effort.
- Passive home discovery can finish using its starting config; #150004 supplied no human mid-discovery incident. Private binding and native execution still validate the source at their effect boundary.
- Catalog list/read/file projections can finish after rename/archive/status notifications; #150659's ordering evidence is synthetic. Native state is not changed; the next event or reconciliation repairs the display.
- A replacement becoming ready during failed hydration does not force an immediate generation-matched retry; #150659 supplied the harness case. Normal demand and existing bounded cooldown recover.
- Older remote node queries may replace newer cached pages; #153614 used fake-node ordering tests. Query-key compatibility remains and each caller receives its own response; later refresh repairs the cache.
- Old source-health completions may overwrite newer health observations; #150659 supplied no human incident. Bounded cooldown and terminal spawn-failure handling remain, the latter independently supported by the actual installed-Gateway report #154313.
- A watcher event during a rollout scan no longer recursively restarts or certifies the scan; #163706 measured cache performance but supplied no actual race incident. A dirty bit causes fresh stats on the next reconciliation.
- Desktop replacement during fingerprinting no longer forces repeated convergence or before/after stat certificates; #127778/#127024 supplied synthetic swap proof. Content hashes remain; the next notification/acquisition refreshes a transient fingerprint.
- Queued old watcher callbacks may trigger an extra refresh; #127778 supplied no human old-arm incident. Closed watchers and scheduler shutdown own normal cleanup.
- Watch registration failure gets one bounded rearm, not indefinite exponential retry state; no human incident required the latter. Service health reports persistent failure; another filesystem event or restart can recover.
- Desktop updates during artifact copies no longer force whole-operation retries or drain every old client; #127778's exact copy-window scenarios were synthetic. New acquisitions use the current fingerprint and existing leased work settles normally.
- Regenerable cache/marketplace publication no longer has multi-step rollback; #127778/#127024/#156556 did not report user-data loss requiring it. A failed publish may leave the derived artifact absent; the next acquisition rebuilds it.
- Concurrent different-source marketplace installs join one target publication rather than negotiate winners; #127778's scenario was synthetic. A later acquisition reconciles a different requested source.
- Signed-service installation no longer negotiates competing out-of-band installers or probes post-copy inode changes; #126080's competing-writer evidence was synthetic. Such an installer can be overwritten or cause a visible error; source/staged/installed signature checks and one normal rollback remain.
- Config changes racing thread start/resume/fork no longer use a private cross-request fence and delayed response/exit handoff; `96f0983a85b`/#102883 links onboarding/profile issues, not a config-write race incident. Wire authority and uncertainty classification remain; concurrent operator changes are best effort.
- Generic connection/startup failures are returned rather than replayed automatically; `33a26cd8079` credits a human contributor but links no report, `e5dc3f712e5` cites concurrent lanes, and #129505 supplies a maintainer onboarding reproduction rather than an independent human incident. A later run retries; one explicit settled-client replacement remains. #155612's forced OS/exit/stderr cases only pin the removed retry.
- Native history reads can finish across status notifications without revision certificates or reader accounting; #102060/#149864 and #93313 supplied synthetic/refactor evidence. Current owner/config/effect checks remain; the next notification/poll reconciles observations.
- Duplicate close events after completed cleanup no longer retain tombstones or reset a close state machine; #159325 supplied held-lock/synthetic transport tests. Current-target checks and shared in-flight settlement remain; failures are visible.

## Provenance ledger

All original KEEP rows were reconsidered; an agent/maintainer reproduction alone did not qualify as a real incident.

| Original mechanism | Decision and retained contract |
| --- | --- |
| App-inventory tokens and scoped invalidation (#115866/#162032) | Partial REMOVE: retain account partitions, TTL, ordinary multi-agent row merges and bounded coalescing; drop publication fences. |
| Resident catalog epochs/replacement waits (#151545) | Partial REMOVE: retain closed-state checks and ordinary write settlement; drop config-change admission protocols. |
| Home discovery generations (#150004) | Partial REMOVE: retain source validation at private binding/execution effects; drop passive discovery rechecks. |
| Field revisions/tombstones (#150659) | REMOVE: bounded last-completion-wins metadata; native operations remain authoritative. |
| Node publication generations (#153614) | Partial REMOVE: retain measured warm-page cache, query keys, disconnection eviction and bounded waits. |
| Catalog currency/backoff fences (#150659) | Partial REMOVE: retain coalescing and bounded failure cooldown; actual user spawn storm #154313 independently supports terminal-failure handling. |

On the follow-up head, the shared-client and request-authority suites passed **169/169** (373.50s Vitest, 77% transform); the no-admission settlement regression passed in 12ms. The mandatory lint-suppression suite passed **3/3** (68.04s Vitest). No test expectations, timeouts, skips, retries, or suppressions changed in this follow-up. The second CI run (`38106762435`, head `90975b240e4`) found a missed test caller: three `test/canonical-descendant.integration.test.ts` cases still used the removed `holdConfiguration` helper. These cases only created the retired native-config wait; they are deleted with that mechanism. The suite's prewrite policy, physical fork overload/revocation, rollback, retained-authority and transcript checks are unchanged. The test-only cutover passed independent review through P2. That run's 24 cancelled validation jobs are missing proof, not inherited failures.

Commit `c99770c81f2` completes that test cutover. The full remaining canonical-descendant integration suite passes **71/71** (1,030.85s Vitest on the loaded local host), and lint-suppression passes **3/3** (15.86s Vitest); combined wrapper wall time was 1,121.92s. The follow-up makes the predicate explicit and deletes that suppression. `check-test-types-core-1` completed all six typecheck groups successfully despite its cancelled job conclusion; other cancelled jobs remain missing coverage rather than passing or main-red.

Commit `a1f89cdb226` fixes both lint diagnostics. Independent review through P2 is clean. The no-admission regression failed before repair and passes with one completion check; duplicate wire admission is idempotent. Its existing boundary regression is retained unchanged and passed.

prs.title: refactor(scripts): simplify build snapshots and staging checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Build, source-transfer and catalog tooling carries extra state and repeated checks for source edits or competing writers during one operation.

## User Impact

No CLI, SDK, configuration or artifact-format change. Source edits during builds or capsule preparation are best effort: finish editing before running proof, or rerun from the intended candidate. Catalog publication continues to require one publisher, with old/new recovery artifacts retained after incomplete publication.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove transient compiler/build-input seals, their caller bookkeeping and mutation-only tests; keep content-based cache invalidation and measured warm reuse. Simplify capsule copying, locked staging bookkeeping and private catalog recovery cleanup without changing source privacy, effect-boundary checks, atomic publication, or ordinary process settlement.

Net production/tooling reduction: **575 lines** (127 added, 702 removed), excluding tests, fixtures, generated declarations and docs. This uses the campaign's 500–999-line fallback after the expanded scope audit; the coverage log below records retained mechanisms instead of inflating the patch with safety-critical removals.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Compiler source, configuration, toolchain or resolution namespace changes during one invocation no longer trigger a second snapshot seal. `09de7c9ef73` / #132532, `cc797c0491c` / #134528 and `c8eab360206` / #156829 pin synthetic interleavings; the actual between-run invalidation contracts remain. A concurrent edit can require another build.
- Edit/revert sequences and inode/ctime changes during build-input capture or asset preparation no longer produce a transient generation fence. #149866 explicitly used a temporary-Git reproduction; #165324 measured capture cost, not an actual-use mutation incident. Persisted producer content signatures and dirty-input facts still invalidate later runs.
- Sibling compiler outputs no longer require a producer-owned exception registry for the retired namespace seal. #156829 carried the speculative seal forward; normal output ownership, input containment and compiler failures remain.
- Source or symlink metadata changes while a capsule is copied, and HEAD/index/eligibility changes after capture, no longer cause a final full-source rescan. #158681 measured mirror reuse and injected mutation cases, not a human incident. Initial privacy selection, opened-descriptor containment, copy bounds, frozen bytes and receiver verification remain; rerun after source edits.
- Testbox HEAD or preparation-input changes after the command captures its fingerprint are best effort. The prior source-refresh repair's evidence was fixture-based; initial task/allocation/dependency admission and the final allocation-receipt check remain. The next invocation captures current inputs.
- Replacement of a held private mirror lock or mutation of locked staging metadata no longer gets redundant checks throughout one synchronous operation. #158681, #152006 and #166961 justify caching/recovery, not these forced interleavings. Payload, source, diagnostics and deletion-authority checks remain, with one current-receipt check at each receipt-write effect so writing cannot erase a newly recorded writer hold.
- A second writer replacing a lease claim exactly between its read and atomic rename is no longer detected by a second read. #164530 / #164499 used source inspection and synthetic proof, with live AWS reproduction pending. Exact lease/cwd selection and failed-restoration source retention remain; concurrent same-lease commands remain unsupported.
- Competing catalog publishers or replacement of randomized private recovery entries no longer gets an inode registry and repeated destination checks. `d36da73091c` / #160157 explicitly tested injected replacements; the documented contract requires one publisher. Ordinary preparation/write/rename failures retain both old/new recovery sets; concurrent publication may need manual reconciliation.
- Replacement of a cache lock/stamp during an exclusively locked transfer and byte-identical ctime changes are best effort. `8b2c9fbcc8b` / #153558 introduced these cache fences without a reported replacement incident. Cooperating writers still serialize; content/output hashes and exact inventories remain.

## Coverage log

Five prior KEEP decisions now have removals: build-input state, the shared compiler seal (including its SDK tooling caller), staging revalidation, claim restoration and Testbox preparation revalidation. The dist-artifact uncertainty latch was re-evaluated and retained for ordinary writer settlement, not on synthetic incident evidence.

Remaining KEEP mechanisms meet explicit rules: managed-child cleanup and fix44's nested-supervisor handoff implement ordinary SIGINT/shutdown settlement; run-vitest retains bounded resources/watchdogs and joined workers; check-changed distinguishes an executed failing check from unavailable remote execution; dist ownership retains real parallel-writer exclusion and uncertain-child holds. Measured caches, source privacy/containment, catalog validation and preservation before deletion remain. No PR description or failing test is claimed as a human production incident.

Successful compiler-membership validation remains one unconditional check at declaration publication, including when the build cache is disabled; only cache bookkeeping depends on cache state.

## Evidence

- Before further removals, sequential clean-main/head Testbox comparisons passed the exact cancellation file, strict teardown case, canonical SDK publication case and full Crabbox wrapper suite (280 passed, one existing platform skip on each). Main `aec6e7a56eb`, prior lane head `54b0c1150dc`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38077825843.
- Prior lane head real `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` SIGINT proof exited 130 with zero tagged survivors: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38080096489. Fix44 `7fd6d6738ce` remains intact.
- Focused owner proof: compiler-input snapshot/build-stamp 23 tests; capsule/Testbox freshness 50; catalog v1/v2 49; SDK baseline 26. All passed.
- Full local staging subsequently passed 72 cases and failed two: the preparation-callback case timed out at its unchanged 120-second limit, and the concurrent-recovery case received `Native claim inventory could not be verified.` instead of its expected lock reason. Sequential exact-filter clean-main/head comparison on the same Mac reproduced both identical failures (563.89 s main, 346.51 s head). No timeout, retry, assertion or source skip was changed; these failures are not claimed fixed.
- Final head `f56dc9ea0890c1e52c0a7708e6c7c46f6015fcb5`: real `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` SIGINT exited 130 with zero survivors among 41 observed PIDs; full declaration siblings and suppression suites passed 46 tests (four existing platform skips), 95.15 s; scripts and all root-test typechecks passed; runtime cycles 0 and Madge cycles 0. Hetzner run: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_94124c6692ddff8702550790263ba440. The real targeted changed gate stopped only at the identical untouched Gateway/UI dead-export findings described below.
- Earlier full-graph proof at `591befe77956bc44152816193afdada86fdc93f3`: wrapper/import closure 20 passed; effect/caller regression cases passed; production, core-test, extension and root-test typechecks passed. Later changes are limited to the receipt-boundary repair and its tests. Hetzner run: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f6ee167d27ce4bb6a007b4ee3e9d96de.
- Initial hosted CI `38103605876` caught one missed synthetic post-emit mutation case in `write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts`. This was a PR-caused failure. `54df97213dbf0694b0e4508335968decb80541a5` removes that case and its dead fixture branches with the retired seal; compiler-error and missing-receipt preservation cases remain equivalent. All 10 tests in the full file plus 3 lint-suppression tests passed locally (206.49 s wrapper), and fresh Codex P0-P2 review is scoped-clean. No retries, raised timeouts, or skips.
- Review caught cache-disabled publication skipping the receipt check. Its new regression failed before the repair; the check now runs independently of caching. Final focused regression and Codex P0-P2 review passed. One initial test assertion incorrectly expected a disabled cache directory to exist and was corrected to assert absence. The loaded-Mac full run hit two unchanged 120-second build-test deadlines; the unchanged tests passed on the clean Linux run above. Neither timeout was raised or suppressed.
- Hosted run `38105113343` on `54df97213dbf` had one originating failure: `checks-node-compact-small-9` / `publishes only verified source data: Venice unreachable`; `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected it. Clean current main `1d952d58b156` reproduced the identical empty `claude-cli` static-catalog validation error introduced by #168728, before any publication effect. Fixed directly on main in [04106e90e011](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/04106e90e0112d100e84552fc9dbb907f13880ff), preserving schema/manifest contracts. Its regression failed before the fix; all 59 catalog/suppression tests, touched typechecks/lints, cycles and Codex review passed. This repair is separate from the simplification diff.
- Codex P0–P2 review of the full simplification and the receipt/caller correction: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Subsequent conflict-free baseline integrations preserve every authored patch exactly.
- The first full AWS run passed all 1,875 PR-tooling tests (two existing platform skips), all changed-owner suites, closure/inventory checks, lint suppressions, both cycle checks, and the full SDK API comparison (no API changes). It caught a later receipt-mutation assertion on Linux and two missed test callers in typechecking; the follow-up preserves the receipt-write effect check and migrates those callers. The existing regression and caller tests pass; affected typechecks and a fresh Codex P0–P2 review pass.
- On the receipt-fixed candidate before patch-identical baseline integration, the full lifecycle/Crabbox/check-changed/run-vitest families passed 848 tests with five existing platform skips. The PR-tooling run's only failure was a missing `gh` prerequisite on the raw image; the exact case passed locally with `gh` installed. Full changed-owner suites also passed. Earlier full PR-tooling run: 1,875 passed with two existing platform skips.
- Final-head full Plugin SDK API comparison passed with no public API changes (digest `ff7b090f`): https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4a01f3a6f2a23a70bd03320cb86cc0c7. The preceding comparison exited with an unsettled native-compiler await; no code changed before this non-reproduction, and it is not claimed fixed. The dependency leaves pending RPC requests unresolved after an unexpected native child exit; the original exit's cause remains unknown.
- Three named inherited gates required baseline integration: UI graph budget, a channel-presence unused binding, and stale SDK surface budget. Their existing main fixes were incorporated without changing any budget or suppression in this PR. The final real changed gate passed all of those checks, then failed Knip on untouched Gateway/UI exports; scripts export scan passed with zero entries. A clean `66b120abd3a1` baseline replay reports exactly the same findings: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e9e0540192a7c70e99d7ae9c79a7b05c. Current main's `657715b3828` repairs the UI entries and explicitly records the remaining `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` finding from #168482. A second replay on `bb7c69ddd04b` could not start because the third dependency installation exhausted the lease's disk quota; no passing result is claimed for it.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep claimed hook replies in conversation history
prs.body:
Closes #149985

Related: #150011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a case where plugin replies claimed by `before_agent_reply` can be delivered without being recorded in session history. Media-only and captioned replies also lose attachment references when a text-only transcript receipt suppresses downstream mirroring.

## User Impact

Claimed replies remain available in conversation history and follow-up context without duplicate assistant entries. Media replies retain stable attachment filenames alongside captions. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why Change Was Made

Both CLI and embedded early-return paths persist through the existing transcript owners before returning ownership and idempotency metadata. Media history uses the existing outbound-media transcript-mirror projection; delivered payloads are unchanged. Session writer guards and detached/room-event no-persistence behavior are retained. Run-current assertions now also reach asynchronous transcript commit admission.

## Evidence

### Conflict repair and validation (`45014fa84c8cc44de442725c47f88137e11073cf`)

Merged upstream `main` at `8c9999b298c4a5db2d60b531efff7f8ec20acbeb`. Resolved conflicts in the CLI hook test, embedded run orchestrator, and reply normalization. Preserved upstream user-turn recording and exec-request context alongside claimed-reply history persistence. The claimed-history path now consumes upstream's canonical `stripMixedSilentReplyTokens` helper with `?? rawText` for its nullable unchanged-text result; the duplicate helper is removed.

- **304/304 tests passed across 9 files and 4 shards** (896.11 seconds wrapper wall time). This includes CLI/embedded cancellation during and after transcript preparation, claimed text/media delivery with SQLite/history readback and once-only assertions, token normalization, pending-final delivery, and database-worker routing.
- The previous head's BOOT compaction cleanup failure is covered by the passing `agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts`. Incorporated upstream fix `816dcc13e9ff0768c60f08bc6813e131c1c934ca` routes this suite through the host-owned database worker.
- Upstream removed `run.terminal-timeout-delivery.integration.test.ts` in `80239a7e6b2`. It was not restored or counted as passing; the current runtime-refresh integration suite passed.
- **Static validation:** production typecheck and all 28 core-test type graphs passed, along with formatting, ratchets, dependency/config/boundary checks, and the script unused-export scan. The repository-supported targeted type-aware lint passed for all 11 changed TypeScript files. Scripts lint and the remaining schema/storage/runtime/media/webhook/pairing guards passed. **Full core lint did not complete:** the repository's 900-second deadline terminated it with exit 124 and no lint diagnostics. The targeted lint result is separate evidence, not a passing full-core result.
- **The complete changed-file gate exited 1 at unused exports; it is not green.** [Exact-base main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38106494410/job/114373163685) reports the same eight production findings with the same Knip version/config: `captureSessionEntryMaintenanceAgeFact`, `SessionEntryMaintenanceAgeCapture`, `SqliteReclamationPreparedSource`, `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2`, `OpenClawAgentDatabaseWorkerCloseResult`, two `GitHubConnections` exports, and `GitHubConnectionsContent`. Their definitions and scanner/config inputs are unchanged from the pinned base. The local full-tree scan also reports `reconnectGateway` in unchanged UI test-support source; base CI stopped at the production scan, so no base full-tree execution result is claimed. No unrelated exports or scanner rules were changed.
- **Independent review:** the staged diff against the pinned main received a `scoped-clean` P0–P2 autoreview result, with no actionable findings. Two status-only chunks could not assess source; the source-diff chunk reviewed the repair. No source edits followed review.
- Environment: Node `24.21.0`, repository-pinned pnpm `12.9.0`, `@openclaw/fs-safe 0.26.0`. Tested and reviewed candidate tree: `56e4b74f1b37031cee7290f8b1fa950aff910faf`.

Functional validation:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/plugins/before-agent-reply.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-transcript.test.ts \

After its unused-export failure, the remaining commands from the same repository-generated plan were executed separately without skipping or weakening their guards. `git diff --cached --check` against that base passed.

This is local real-runner/SQLite evidence, not a new installed-plugin, live-channel, or live-model capture. Earlier installed-plugin evidence below remains labelled by its original head. Hosted CI must validate the new head; no all-green or merge-ready claim is made.


### Previous conflict resolution and validation (`cd4bfe4222412efde2fd1701f4bd77889cc68e28`; historical)

Merged upstream `main` at `43856f78ec629f0c72180359a0ce85f06759974f`. The only conflict was concurrent additions to `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`; the resolution keeps both the claimed-reply CLI test and upstream's cron-grant test exactly once. - **Static gates:** the complete changed-file gate against pinned upstream parent `214bb47b4ec0809e357d2e497e0bf8fd5d9f31eb` exited 0, including core production typecheck, all 27 core-test type graphs, three unused-export scans, formatting, type-aware lint, ratchets, and boundary/legacy-store/import-cycle guards. `git diff --check` also passed.

Both stop in shared harness warmup at `run.workspace-ownership.test-support.ts:68` with `real workspace consumer was exercised: expected 0 to be greater than 0`; all 16 tests are skipped. The assertion can mask an earlier warmup error, so the underlying cause remains unresolved. These test/harness files are unchanged from that upstream parent. No retries, weaker assertions, or unrelated source changes were used to obtain green results.

This is real-runner/SQLite regression evidence, not a new installed-plugin, external-channel, or live-model trace. The head-labelled installed-plugin/local-channel-adapter proof below is historical. Hosted CI on the updated head remains the merge gate.

### Earlier evidence (historical; see head labels)

- Before the media repair, all three CLI media cases failed SQLite history assertions; text-only passed.
- Registered plugin hooks exercise the real runner entrypoints and SQLite persistence for text-only, media-only, captioned, and multiple-attachment replies.
- CLI delivery exercises the `routeReply` durable outbound pipeline, asserting unchanged transport arguments and once-only assistant history after delivery.
- Dispatcher coverage verifies that transcript ownership disables downstream mirroring without dropping text/media payloads. Embedded coverage includes persistent turns, detached turns, room events, and replaced-writer rejection.
- Relevant functional suites: 323 passed (CLI 41, embedded shared integration 136, dispatcher 139, hook boundary 7). After final test-only type/lint cleanup, CLI 41/41 and embedded hook regressions 17/17 passed again.
- Independent review of the staged candidate found no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- Core and all core-test typecheck shards passed; targeted repository lint, formatting, line-count ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The changed-file gate's earlier test type errors were corrected, and the failed typecheck plus remaining lint step reran successfully; other completed guards were retained.

### Installed plugin -> claimed text/media -> delivery -> SQLite/history proof

Executed against exact PR head `f57cd074e95ba2e0bbedb527d5c41ecfb7948cec` with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.4.0, using isolated `HOME`, config, state, and session storage.

1. The production installer copied a local plugin package into `state/extensions/claimed-reply-proof` and enabled it. A fresh process reported plugin version `1.0.0`, `status: loaded`, and channel `claimed-proof`. The plugin declared `before_agent_reply`, and the isolated operator config explicitly granted `hooks.allowConversationAccess: true`.
2. A fresh `openclaw agent --local --deliver --reply-channel claimed-proof` process loaded that installed plugin. The hook claimed a captioned media reply before model execution. The configured model endpoint was the intentionally unreachable `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1`.
3. The command returned the claimed text/media and successful routed delivery:

```json
{
  "payloads": [
    {
      "text": "CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078",
      "mediaUrl": "https://example.invalid/CLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png",
      "mediaUrls": ["https://example.invalid/CLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png"]
    }
  ],
  "deliveryStatus": {
    "requested": true,
    "attempted": true,
    "status": "sent",
    "succeeded": true,
    "resultCount": 1

}
```

4. The installed channel adapter recorded exactly one outbound call, preserving both caption and media URL:

```json
{

  "kinds": ["media"],
  "texts": ["CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078"],
  "mediaUrls": ["https://example.invalid/CLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png"],
  "sequences": [1]
}
```

5. The production `loadTranscriptEvents` history accessor read exactly one assistant message from the same SQLite-backed session, with the media filename projected into transcript text:

```json
{
  "eventCount": 2,
  "assistantCount": 1,
  "assistantTexts": [["CLAIMED_TEXT_PR150078\nCLAIMED_MEDIA_PR150078.png"]],
  "idempotencyKeys": ["before-agent-reply:3d73e0fa-50d0-4b6b-8ad0-839f89d51be2"]
}
```

6. A direct SQLite count independently confirmed `assistant_count = 1` and `distinct_idempotency_keys = 1` for that session.

This is a real disk installation and real routed-delivery adapter execution with SQLite/history readback. The adapter is a local proof channel; this is not a live external-channel API or live-model test.


### Revalidated on PR head (2f60a04dc02c7c98cf6539027013e28df36b15bf)

### Silent-claim follow-up and exact-head proof (348ff0510adf6760dd093e6b52585e537cefcaa0)

ClawSweeper's Revision 10 found that a hook returning `{ handled: true }` without `reply` could persist the synthetic `NO_REPLY` token as an assistant message. Both CLI and embedded runners now return the existing silent payload without appending an assistant transcript event; they mark that payload transcript-owned so downstream delivery cannot mirror it into history.

- New CLI and embedded regressions use real session storage. Both failed before the fix because SQLite history contained a `NO_REPLY` assistant message, then passed after the fix with zero assistant messages for silent claims.
- The focused silent tests passed: 2 tests in 2 files, Vitest duration 27.85s and wrapper wall time 86.30s. The final silent plus text/media selection passed 18 tests in 2 files, Vitest duration 33.13s and wrapper wall time 50.22s.

- On this head, a fresh local CLI process loaded the installed proof plugin and returned `deliveryStatus.status = sent` with one payload result. ### Cancellation authority and exact-head proof (31a58fd33c10576b0d750e440838e4f5391e3439)

### Explicit silent-token claim regression (941a8a3bc30f1ad6b713697ec670b0c32d77f8a4)

## What Problem This Solves

About, Approvals, Labs, Lobsterdex, and Secrets still use Lit in the Control UI's incremental Solid 2 migration.

## User Impact

The five pages now render through Solid with their existing routes, host tags, CSS classes, and controls. No configuration or data migration is required.

Each page has one implementation, registered through the shared Solid bridge. Existing TypeScript owners retain Gateway requests, synchronous state transitions, configuration decisions, and secret mutation authority. View-owned mutable facts publish revision signals; source replacement and teardown retire the old subscriptions and requests.

The port uses the landed Solid icons and settings primitives. Two small shared adapters preserve the existing shell layout scope and reactive locale formatting. Stateless canonical lobster artwork remains in an isolated Lit island for its remaining callers; Secrets retains the existing dropdown and modal owners until their own migration. The only primitive interface addition is the modal's existing `description` property in its JSX declaration.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add inactive session actor and scoped receipts
prs.body:
Related: #168316 (stacked parent)

## What Problem This Solves

Chat turns repeatedly read and update the same session state through separate database requests.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible change: this PR supplies an inactive session actor for later input, transcript, and delivery cutovers, with no production caller switched. A supporting SQL-classification fix also avoids false invalidation in existing readers. Storage format, durability, retention, permissions, and released SDK contracts are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing writer owns each actor by captured physical database identity and session key. Phase commands reuse its synchronous transaction kernels and held preimages; cold commands hydrate inside that transaction. Retained handles cover accepted descendants until actual drain, while FIFO is held only for synchronous work. Durable and worker-backed incognito targets delegate to their current workers. **Contract update 2: native incognito: actor declines; existing owner until P12.** Acquisition returns `not-actor-owned` before constructing an actor. Accepted edge case: native incognito sessions get no actor savings until Phase E/P12 moves incognito onto the actor as its memory-only backend. Follow-on B3 #168539 and B4 #168592 must honor the decline.

Exact receipts capture complete postimages, adopted IDs/parents, custody, and reducer results before fallible publication. MAIN installs them before acknowledgement. Known commits stay known after publication failure; unknown outcomes fence and reconcile without replay. Live authority remains checked at effects. Session-scoped receipts preserve unrelated snapshots while related windows and aliases invalidate together; explicit broad events still fence all affected keys.

The persistence interface contains typed commands, explicit version/domain predicates, and complete postimages; native database handles and SQL dialect operations remain within the storage adapters. The actor's write path uses in-process receipt counters and bypasses the legacy TEMP generation read. This does not claim removal of legacy callers' reads before their cutovers.

Following “Choose good compromises,” the replica no longer clones and validates command IDs, phases, and before/after versions a second time, or repeats freshness checks around synchronous cloning. It trusts the existing command owner and keeps one freshness check before installation. This removes 33 production lines and 17 test lines. Accepted edge: the private replica does not independently reject a fabricated receipt after the owner has already validated it. Generic unknown-outcome replay remains disabled because additive usage reducers lack durable deduplication; no new retry ledger or recovery protocol is added.

Commands accept an optional expected version and return an authorized stale-version postimage on mismatch, so callers can retry once without a separate read request. Native admission callbacks cannot mutate the preimage. Shared SQL helpers preserve one mutation implementation, and the worker transport no longer imports host configuration capture. Inactive API roots remain explicitly audited until the cutovers make them reachable.

Final comparison base: `1d4f42e8f3852c8804da09edf2e81ed848762d78` on `dbasync/w11entrycache`. Five real conflicts required one parent integration, preserving its steer-only rewrites, empty-cleanup skip, expanded incognito facts, and admission lifetime fixes. Parent savings are not credited to this PR.

## Evidence

### Statement and request measurements

**Passed:** 14 complete alternating baseline/candidate pairs, stopped at the first duration-valid series. Warmed all-thread statements are **678.1 → 672.5**, DB requests **148.05 → 145.05**, and logical requests **171.25 → 168.10** per turn. The first-turn increase is **1.5 statements (+0.0713%)**, with fewer requests and attributed existing work. The additional whole-workload check is lower by **48 statements and 32.5 logical/DB requests**. The actor remains inactive; only the supporting SQL-classifier fix receives causal savings credit.

The first-turn increase is **+1.5 statements (+0.0713%)**, below the +0.5% noise floor; requests decrease by 2. Its complete contribution table is in `sql-attribution.md`. Positive native sites are existing admission/lease/maintenance work: `sqlite-schema-admission.ts` +6, `openclaw-agent-db-lease.ts` +5, `sqlite-busy-timeout.ts` +5, `sqlite-transaction.ts` +5, `sqlite-wal.ts` +4, `sqlite-staging-token.ts` +4, and `sqlite-pinned-read-snapshot.ts` +3. Those source files are byte-identical to baseline. Transcript identity/presence helpers contain the same statement forms previously in the store/header modules; moving those source locations is not new SQL. Participant projection changes only a type export. The per-site audit includes every positive site in `positive-owner-attribution.json`. These are contributions from the median-ranked runs, not independent causal saving estimates.

| Environment-name budget | 456 names versus 455 budget; suppression ratchet itself passes at 573 | Reproduces on `1d4` and exact main `8be3518e` with the unchanged native checker and an isolated index. |
| Test-graph boundary | UI-e2e has 722 roots versus advisory 720 limit | Reproduces on `1d4`; main `8be3518e` has identical root inventory, config, and checker. |
| Unused exports | Two session fixture stubs, `POST_ACTIVATION_INSPECTIONS_STEP`, and solid-lint default | Final candidate exactly matches four parent diagnostics. Diagnosed source/checker blobs match main `8be3518e`. |
| Full core lint | Unused `MockConfig` in untouched `agents-mutate.test.ts`; 16 untouched cap warnings are advisory | Reproduces on `1d4`. Current main uses the type and fixes this parent-only error. |

Main source parity for boundary/dead-export findings is not represented as a main scanner execution. Full core lint has a terminal failure log at `ebdb1bc`; the final changed files subsequently pass targeted lint. Its only error is the documented parent-only import. The native continuation passes scripts lint, schema/legacy-store guards, media and sidecar boundaries, import cycles, webhook and pairing-store guards, plus the earlier formatting, dependency, documentation, export-boundary and ratchet checks. All 35 selected commands are now accounted for by exact receipts and terminal logs, including the two final passing guards. Four inherited failure classes remain within this selection, plus standalone Knip; this is complete composed coverage, not a fully green `check:changed` invocation.

- Frozen dependency install passed in 15.922 s (pnpm 12.9). Static inventory is 2,435 → 2,436 total calls across 689 → 692 files; T1 is 707 → 707 calls across 247 → 249 files. Source callsites are not runtime statement savings.
- Full build passed in 631.039 s (native phases: 8m 55.3s). Untouched UI emitted nonfatal startup-JS budget output of 368.2 KiB versus 366.1 KiB, plus a startup-CSS warning with 491 bytes of hard-ceiling headroom. No UI source is changed.
- Worker transport imports stay independent of host configuration capture, preserving the 512 MiB worker heap cap. The final qaRuntime build passed; every completed SQL workload started successfully and completed all synthetic operations.
- Actor instrumentation calibration passed in 0.390 s: five commands/five settlements, including stale-version and duplicate-settlement suppression. Its owner source hash is unchanged. DB/CPU/resource requests remain separate from logical requests; actor requests recognize the domain-command envelope.
- Fourteen completed SQL pairs include 140 warmed turns per revision. Two incomplete attempts are recorded above; they are not complete-workload samples. Final measurement and SDK artifacts are pinned to `cc65e9a`, with final cleanup reuse explained below.
- SDK diff at `cc65e9a` passed against `1d4`: 148 reachable-only changes, all direct declarations identical, zero entrypoints added/removed; digest `38ea5a5ee9ff1385c6c5b38878609a9db0f23cc5e4a88dd47ef77f79d75a5ecb`. Matching declaration names across the 29 starred module pairs resolves moved aliases and unchanged helpers; this is not a zero-diff claim. New actor/receipt capabilities are additive. Two actual internal nuances are documented: the incognito facts constructor gains a required callback, and the internal pending-input snapshot narrows explicit-undefined assignment under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`. Their raw execution adapters are private-local-only in both revisions; neither is a released writable SDK input. No removed or narrowed released contract was identified by source/declaration inspection. This does not claim exhaustive downstream compiler compatibility.
- The dialect checker from #168382 at `b453af227b4ccf53475e8cba86c57733e06a14ad` ran read-only against `1d4`: all three construct groups are unchanged across 89 differing production files. No ratchet exception or baseline expansion is used.
- Published-driver × candidate update cell: attempted on final head `c098dab982890cccfd6b03d7aefb1bf7010f3ef4` on AWS after Testbox expiry. Candidate package build passed. The published `2026.10.1` driver stopped before candidate installation: the fixture uses legacy `agents.list`, while the driver requires keyed `agents.entries` (exit 78; `before-ready` failed). Update behavior remains unverified by this cell; this is a pre-candidate fixture failure. No schema migration is introduced.
- Three Codex P2 review rounds completed. Final backend review found no P0/P1; two P2 findings were not accepted with recorded rationale. Timestamp behavior follows canonical validated rebase; receipt observation intentionally captures commit evidence before fallible publication. These remain documented follow-ups, with no fourth review under convergence.

## Limits and follow-ups

Residency is bounded to 128 sessions with an 8 MiB soft budget. One oversized working set remains until another key displaces it, avoiding perpetual read-to-command epoch loss; large sessions can exceed that byte budget. Partial S1–S3 receipts invalidate the touched session’s full hot snapshot rather than claiming complete context/custody coverage; unrelated sessions remain resident.

Observed existing startup edge: read-only discovery can see a newly created database before another worker commits its first schema transaction, returning `UNAVAILABLE` from `sessions.create` before any session mutation. The five direct failure-path modules are byte-identical on the candidate, comparison parent, and inspected main `b7940621`; this is source parity, not a baseline replay of the race. The failed attempt and timing evidence are retained. A subsequent successful workload does not establish a fix. This lane leaves that visible, retryable startup condition to the admission owner instead of adding another handshake.

Regression coverage includes recovery terminal delivery, age maintenance, and the released SDK entry-patch path. It does not directly exercise every maintenance flavor, every SDK export, or the tombstone-successor clone entrypoint. Existing native mutation primitives remain shared. Subsequent caller-cutover PRs own production savings.

Diff at `6e8a0034934cc2c914562f7bade42cf1d2c49a3e` against `1d4f42e8f3852c8804da09edf2e81ed848762d78`: production/config +7,385 / −2,275 (net +5,110); tests/support +3,339 / −4; docs +87 / −0. Production includes audit-root configuration; tests/support includes the Vitest shard helper. Much of the textual churn scopes existing writers without changing their SQL. New code supplies the shared actor contract, transaction/hydration owner, retained host/replica, existing-owner adapters, and failure/authority regressions. Shared helpers preserve one mutation implementation.

Final proof reuse: `6e8a003` only removes duplicate validation in the inactive host/replica, updates the existing replica test and documents the interface. The full build/SDK proof and frozen SQL artifacts remain pinned to `cc65e9a`; final source types and focused behavior passed separately. No imports, dependencies, database statements or production callers change in that cleanup. Its internal `beginCommand` signature is absent from the SDK report; the public operation type receives only documentation. SQL traces record zero actor commands. This is explicit prior-artifact reuse, not a claim that the final source was rebuilt and remeasured.


### Native incognito ownership correction

Contract update 2: **native incognito: actor declines; existing owner until P12**. The inactive native adapter, registrations, exports, and adapter-only tests are removed. Acquisition returns `not-actor-owned` before constructing an actor or allocating a worker. Worker-backed incognito stays supported. Native incognito gets no actor savings until Phase E/P12; B3 #168539 and B4 #168592 must honor the decline.

The database-worker ratchet caught a real new main-thread transaction in the removed adapter. The transcript-state helper's broadened admission guard also obscured its migration-only scope; that original guard is restored. No ratchet baseline or limit was edited. Integration with current main passes the existing admission record to the scoped exchange and keeps descriptor record construction in the existing registry owner.

Adapter-removal candidate tree `52f360d30459afc84da503eea3a528b5e482e8d5` passed 62 focused actor/incognito/admission tests (six files; 65.83 seconds total wrapper time), type-aware oxlint, export-name collisions, production Knip, and core tsgo on AWS Crabbox run `run_2ff8b4c74d49802b3b1e7264e16db51b` (201.30 seconds command time). The local database-worker ratchet passed against main `756b2650a8544f5c0b852a00024e58e54c40eb46` with no baseline edit. The initial post-merge test/type failure was the receipt exchange callback signature and is fixed. Earlier measurement and validation entries above retain their original head scope. Scoped P0/P1 autoreview passed for the removal and final integration repair. Adapter-removal repair head: `8dc7b6750795aa6778d81040dd2abecdcff38ee5`. New-head CI remains required before landing; no static failure is waived.

Published-driver update proof remains incomplete: the 2026.10.1 driver rejected the fixture before candidate installation (`agents.list` moved to keyed `agents.entries`, requiring Doctor). Candidate packaging passed, but that failed before-ready cell is not update-success evidence. This correction removes the inactive native adapter and does not change the update path or schema.


### Final architecture guard repair

Head `17569dbde0719e4ef4bb12aef91b839f179411f6` removes the explicit Kysely helper result generic by using the existing insert/on-conflict builder for both paths. It still executes one statement and updates only `updated_at` on conflict. No ratchet baseline was edited. A conflict-only merge of main `83b5f5425eab6021ff03104c9de1b4826f0c3d97` preserves main's degraded-compaction persistence inside the actor-aware append path.

On candidate tree `caacb70b490fa7557919835743aa26f940917a53`, the complete local `pnpm check:architecture` (including both import-cycle checks and Kysely guardrails) and `pnpm check:database-worker-ratchet --base 83b5f5425eab6021ff03104c9de1b4826f0c3d97` passed. Scoped P0/P1 autoreview found no actionable findings. Earlier export-name collision and production Knip proof remains applicable to the adapter removal; this final repair adds no exports or dependencies. New-head static CI must pass before landing.

### Final worker-fixture repair and inherited CI qualification

The Kysely repair passed both `check-guards-architecture` and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` on `17569dbde0719e4ef4bb12aef91b839f179411f6`. No ratchet baseline was changed.

The remaining PR-caused worker-test failure was traced to the fixture's simulated macOS platform on a real Linux host. After the admission registry refactor, the retained registry and reloaded identity helper captured different birthtime policies. The fixture now loads the identity helper under the physical host platform before simulating library selection. Production identity/admission checks and all test assertions remain intact. The unchanged test failed twice before the repair and all 14 cases passed afterward on Linux; test-wrapper wall time was 52.57 seconds. Type-aware oxlint and formatting passed. Final head: `f0607fa83adf7a338032944be5ad94c91139495e`. In [CI run 38108783953](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38108783953), `check-guards-architecture`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, the repaired worker shard, production types, and all other static checks passed. prs.title: test(workers): reuse service readers and stabilize transcript fencing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker environment service tests repeatedly tear down and reload shared SQLite reader threads. The transcript-fence regression also waited for ledger reservation rather than the queued writer, making its result timing-dependent.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The same service, storage, recovery, and authority tests run with less fixture overhead and deterministic queued-write coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing path-scoped database close after each test, then close the reader pool after the suite. Each case still drains its accepted work, invalidates admission, closes native handles, and removes its own state directory. Only reader thread code survives between cases. Explicit full-close/reopen tests remain intact.

Remove the fixture switch and its redundant opt-ins. All 59 consumers were checked for additional database roots, module resets, and process-lifecycle expectations.

The transcript test now observes the real transcript worker store’s queued `run()` call before replacing its claim, and joins the pending commit during cleanup. Every existing assertion and the held writer remain intact.

Production LOC: **+0 / −0**. Seven test/support files, **+53 / −32**. No timeout, assertion, retry, or production seam changes.

## Evidence

On one Linux AWS Crabbox lease (`cbx_8d4dd0798673`, Node 24), after warming compiled declarations, the same command ran the same 102 assertions before and after:

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-provisioning.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/provider-reconciliation.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/service-lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=json
```

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Command wall time | 210.729 s | 142.960 s | −67.769 s (−32.16%) |
| Sum of file test time | 178.970 s | 110.805 s | −38.09% |
| Tests | 102 passed | 102 passed | unchanged |

[Remote comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_30e1fae3f54d084519d4a0c6483fcd8b). All **59 consumer files / 710 tests** pass. The transcript file passes before and after the ordering fix (44.620 s → 45.647 s; no speed claim for that fix); all 20 standalone runs and all three original four-file shard runs pass without retries. Standalone total: 916.598 s (45.558–46.220 s each); shard walls: 45.146 / 45.502 / 45.190 s.

Formatting, typechecks, lint and all changed guards pass except the dead-export scan. Running that exact scan on the original base independently reproduces the identical 29 findings (28 UI exports and `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2`). No baseline or guard was weakened. [Original-base qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6f1a2d4a978665b30af8acec1ebcbc7d).

The first [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38103285002) exposed the transcript fixture’s earlier gate; the repair above addresses that ordering. Both independent Codex P0/P1 reviews are scoped-clean. The [repair CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38108177388) passes, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: **440 s elapsed CI wall time**, with **1,270 summed job-seconds across seven Node test jobs**. prs.title: fix(models): allow API-key setup while the Gateway runs
prs.body:
Related: #168135, #168108, #168471

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes API-key setup from the CLI when a running Gateway owns local state.

## User Impact

Users can run `openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider <id>` without stopping the Gateway. The Gateway saves the key and refreshes its model catalog. Offline behavior is unchanged. An explicit, non-empty `--profile-id` still requires offline use.

## Why This Change Was Made

#168135 correctly stopped CLI processes from writing credentials around a live Gateway. It also kept CLI flows offline where the existing Gateway APIs could not preserve their behavior. Manual API-key setup already uses the same credential writer as `models.authSetApiKey`, so that subset can use the owner instead of refusing.

This change uses the canonical `local-state-owner.ts` route, as in #168108 and #168471. It binds the request to the discovered local owner and port, sends `expectedOwnerId`, requires `operator.admin`, rechecks ownership before dispatch, and never retries a possibly accepted write locally. API-key input is collected only after owner selection. The RPC checks the expected owner at credential and config writes; calls without that field retain their existing behavior. Owner-bound requests preserve the CLI's agent-selection rules.

Update behavior: an older Gateway that lacks `models-auth-set-api-key-owner-v1` is refused before the API-key request; update and restart it, or stop it and retry offline.

No request/response schema, new RPC method, config option, database schema, or paired-device fallback is added.

### Command-to-RPC mapping

| CLI command or option | Existing RPC | Result in this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `paste-api-key --provider <id> [--agent <id>]` | `models.authSetApiKey` | Delegate provider, key, and agent; print saved profile and any application warning. |
| `paste-api-key --profile-id <id>` | No profile-id field in `models.authSetApiKey` | Refuse this option with offline guidance. |
| `paste-token [--expires-in <duration>]` | No equivalent API-key write | Stay offline: token type and expiry must not become an API key. |
| `login`, including API-key plugin methods | `models.authLogin` and `wizard.*` | Stay offline: CLI method/profile/default/force semantics are not an exact manual-key mapping. |
| `login-github-copilot` | `models.authLogin` and `wizard.*` | Stay offline; device flow is outside this change. |
| `add` / `setup-token` | No exact generic mapping | Stay offline; these can run local provider CLI or import flows. |
| `list` | `models.authStatus` | Stay offline: the status projection lacks the CLI list's state-path, cooldown, disabled-state, and recovery fields. |
| `logout <profileId> [--yes]` | `models.authLogout` | Deferred; retain current offline behavior. |
| `order get` | `models.authStatus` | Deferred; retain the existing owner-aware read. |
| `order set <profileIds...>` | `models.authOrderSet` | Stay offline: the RPC requires the full profile order; the CLI allows partial lists. |
| `order clear` | `models.authOrderSet` | Deferred; retain offline reset behavior. |
| `activate <profileId>` | No exact test-and-activate mapping | Stay offline. |

## Evidence

- The new CLI regression fails with the original main-branch auth router: 12 existing refusal cases pass, and API-key delegation fails with `OWNER_UNAVAILABLE`.
- The initial candidate passed 153 targeted tests across CLI ownership, the real API-key writer, Gateway transport, and the real API-key RPC.
- Tests cover cancelled input, no local fallback, old-Gateway capability refusal before request dispatch, and rejected owner changes without credential/config writes.
- Existing unbound API-key RPC requests still pass the real credential-writer test.
- `pnpm build` passed.
- Isolated live profile: piped a real OpenAI key into `pnpm openclaw --profile <profile> models auth paste-api-key --provider openai`. The Gateway picker changed from zero available OpenAI models to one. A real `openclaw agent` turn returned `AUTH_OWNER_OK`, using the saved auth profile. The listener PID stayed the same; no restart was needed.
- The Gateway token was supplied only at runtime and was not in config. The same CLI path worked when it received that token. Without the token, it refused without a local write and named `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` / `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` as the next step.
- An earlier `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged` run passed the format, ownership, dependency, and other early guards, then stopped at main's UI-e2e test-root budget (722 versus 720). That result predates the empty-input regression below; no UI files are changed here.

### Review repair: authority at the final write

- The captured requester guard now reaches the auth store's existing SQLite worker admission, not only the updater callback. It also reaches config `beforeCommit` and the config writer's effect-time authority check.
- Credential observation: revoke after the real updater returns, before commit; the operation rejects, the original stored key remains, and config bytes do not change. The permitted control stores the replacement key.
- Config observation: revoke after the transform returns; the operation rejects and the source config remains byte-for-byte unchanged. The already saved, unchanged credential remains intact. The permitted control publishes the auth-profile config.
- The four allowed/revoked controls and 17 auth-store update tests pass. These tests use real credential/config persistence; only the revocation instant is controlled.
- Fixed the two `curly` lint errors in the CLI input adapter. Targeted production lint passes for the adapter, API-key writer, and auth-profile upsert owner.
- After merging main, the changed-file gate passed core typechecking and all 28 core test graphs. It stopped at unrelated unused exports in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/managed-binary.ts`, `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`, and `ui/src/test-helpers/solid-application-context.tsx`; those files are unchanged by this PR.

### Review repair: configured loopback auth-none

- Owner-bound shared-auth requests now enable the transport's existing bounded auth-none path. A Gateway explicitly configured with `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` uses the backend client identity without creating or reading device credentials. Remote targets and URL overrides retain the existing refusal rules.
- A registered `paste-api-key` regression invokes the real `resolveGatewayCallDeviceAuth` with the owner route's options. It failed before the fix with `GatewayLocalBackendSharedAuthUnavailableError` and passes after the fix. All 105 transport tests and 16 CLI ownership tests pass.
- The latest main was merged after these focused checks. Clean-main export-name collision checking passed at `76a282c7a1c6ca958517ce15f13e17371c14be11`; the channel collision was fixed upstream by `13296b17cd0`. The same clean main reproduced the three lint errors in the untouched plugin-state observation cache and SQLite comparison test. Remaining baseline runs were stopped at maintainer request while upstream CI repairs were being merged.

### Review repair: empty API-key input

- Empty or whitespace-only stdin now reports: `No API key was supplied. Rerun this command and paste a non-empty API key, or pipe one to stdin.`
- Two short tests read real streams and cover both inputs. Both failed with the old `Required` message and pass after this change.
- The changed-file gate passed formatting, core typechecking, and all six selected test graphs. It stopped at the unrelated `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` unused export in `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts`, which this repair does not modify.

### Existing CI failures checked on main

- On clean main `aec6e7a56eb03eaba1a648310876d2d6d4811745`, the UI cloud-startup toast-recovery case fails with the same `Control UI readiness hook is unavailable` error as this branch (two cases pass, one fails).
- The same clean main also reproduces the FIFO assertions missing `QUEUED_STEER_A` and `ORDINARY_MESSAGE_B`. Neither test nor its steer behavior is changed by this PR.
- The document-steer case also fails on clean main, but earlier: the initial turn does not reach the mock provider (zero requests). On this branch it reaches the later missing-document assertion. The baseline failure prevents an exact comparison of that later assertion; it is not claimed as an identical local reproduction.
- On the repaired head, [the Node shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082252267/job/114301617040) reports the same FIFO failures. A [separate cron shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082252267/job/114301616913) reports `hydrates runtime metadata for a reasoning-capable fallback candidate` (expected two calls, received four); its main-branch investigation is separate and no auth change is claimed to fix it.
- `src/cli/plugin-local-state-owner.test.ts` has the same result on this branch (`5033eb75ade`) and clean main (`9a165c492058ddf6fc3468cde27b201514c954f1`): 33 pass, one fails. The failed case is `routes memory search limits and JSON output through the discovered owner`; both report `The memory runtime does not support CLI search` inside `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. The fixture supplies a manager but not the `searchForCli` callback now required by the Memory Core handler. This is a main-branch fixture mismatch, not an auth routing regression; no test or routing behavior was changed to hide it.

No overlap with protected maintainer changes.

Two-way code change: a revert restores offline-only CLI setup. Keys saved through the Gateway remain saved. The affected paths are local CLI API-key setup and the existing Gateway API-key save handler.
