prs.title: refactor(channels): simplify speculative delivery and lifecycle guards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Maintainer-requested p13 simplification removes speculative delivery, cache and lifecycle coordination across the ten channel plugins.

Related: #156627

## User Impact

Normal delivery, public configuration/API shapes, authorization, platform rate limits, durable replay and ordinary shutdown remain. Rare overlapping lifecycle operations are deliberately best effort as detailed below. No schema, durability, retention, permission or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial pass retained too much code on the strength of synthetic tests and maintainer-authored PR descriptions. This pass re-evaluates all 28 original KEEP rows under the human-incident bar and flips 17 wholly or partly. It also fixes an actual producer mistake discovered during review: Discord routing preflight performed synchronous activity persistence even though message processing already owns the awaited worker-backed write.

Keep the existing owner, idempotency, one effect check, bounded resources and ordinary settlement. Remove generation histories, repeated admission checks and speculative cross-thread or retry protocols. The attempted voice prewarm simplification was reverted when it broke retained speech-transfer behavior; accepted speech and provider results are not disposable.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Discord thread-binding sync/worker overlap: #156627 introduced synthetic before/after-ack reconciliation. Deprecated synchronous SDK calls overlapping an async mutation can observe the prior row or be superseded. Normal ingress no longer makes that synchronous call; its existing async write owns activity.
- Discord manager replacement during queued mutation: the same migration's artificially paused manager-incarnation test is not a human incident. The queued operation uses the current available manager while ordinary account queues and shutdown settlement stay intact.
- Discord preview rotation during a held create/edit: #155641/#162174 have synthetic ownership evidence, not an actual-use report for this guard. The returned preview may remain attached to the previous slot until normal finalization/cleanup; final delivery and request authorization remain.
- Discord PCM input versus natural worker retirement: #154119 explicitly used synthetic callback/IPC barriers. One chunk may lose the narrow check-to-post race; the next chunk opens a fresh output. Atomic closed status, worker ordering, explicit cancellation and transcript/recording ownership remain.
- Discord repeated connect on the same private speaker object: #137433 supplies no human incident for a private generation. Production constructs/connects each speaker once; normal provider readiness and stop checks remain.
- Telegram transport-cache eviction during an active send: #101783 creates more than 64 synthetic account/config entries. Eviction closes immediately; an overlapping operation can return its existing transport error. The resource cap and all transport close paths remain.
- Telegram typing responses arriving out of failure order: the human report #138763 requires independent topic coalescing, not failure epochs. Any success clears the best-effort typing failure streak; bot-wide 429 waits and 401 suspension remain.
- Telegram overlapping authorization backoffs: #139292's extra retry queue/second sleep loop was synthetic. Each action waits once, then rechecks suspension/cooldown before sending.
- Telegram delayed preview result versus rotation/stop: `9dfa7dc87ad` identifies the exact case as a red-team finding. Returned previews are adopted without a generation ledger; normal pagination, single-use reply targets, finalization and authority remain.
- Slack cleanup overlapping a new turn: #155550 explicitly describes architecture/probes, not an actual-use Slack incident. Cleanup uses the current simple lifecycle rather than adapter generation snapshots.
- Slack human reply before the send acknowledgement: boundary tracking begins when Slack supplies the message identity; there is no pending-receipt custody registration.
- Slack human reply during final edit: an accepted final stays final instead of being changed back to progress and reposted. Ordinary thread boundaries and retention remain.
- Feishu media/independent stream overlap: #113152 provides authored/harness proof, not a human report for historical generation custody. One close promise/latest receipt replaces per-generation history. Normal serialized media, hooks and partial-result settlement remain.
- Feishu simultaneous terminal callbacks: one settlement flag replaces adopting/abandoning promise handshakes. The durable queue remains the replay owner and logical twin guards commit only after adoption.
- Feishu proxy resolution versus test reset: #86386's epoch only protects a test helper. Tests must settle their own pending proxy work before resetting; proxy routing and security are unchanged.
- Matrix hung startup/decryption/retirement: #129605/#134033 describe SDK/harness cases, not a human incident requiring multiple late-drain phases. One tracked shutdown retains crypto/write ownership, with a bounded caller wait. A genuinely stuck SDK needs restart rather than a second recovery state machine.
- Matrix same-state sync tick during encryption preparation: #163012's held-probe case is synthetic. A healthy repeated sync state no longer invalidates the probe; encryption, membership and current-owner checks remain at the effect.
- Mattermost reset during a thread-history fetch: human #93204 requests backfill after restart/session-clear, not this interleaving. The short fetch can populate its old window; the next turn observes the current identity. Sender authorization, bounded fetch and ordinary history merge stay intact.
- Teams append failure versus live-context replacement: no human report establishes the identity-matched cleanup guard. In the narrow overlap the optional live context can be absent; durable queue state and idempotency remain.
- Signal phone/UUID alias change across redelivery: #118970/#128093 use synthetic identities. The message may dispatch twice after such a change; canonical event IDs still dedupe and durable raw rows remain unchanged.
- Signal nested conflict retry: human #100944 requires eventual DM recovery. Recovery now stays with the existing durable queue and FIFO instead of a second 1/2/4-second inner retry owner.
- iMessage reaction before its approval send receipt binds: #112714 added a synthetic eager-reaction window. The normal lane rechecks the real binding, or the user retries/manual-approves. Sender, target and decision authorization remain.
- iMessage legacy sync hydration during async hydration: no human incident supports its late-read guard. The old sync API is best effort during overlap; ordinary async hydration, ordered persistence and outbound provenance remain.
- iMessage direct out-of-owner cursor write during a local update: #149605/#159998 use synthetic intervening writes. Supported writers serialize through a FIFO and perform one read/decision/awaited write. Checkpoints, failure-held watermarks, stored shapes and restart recovery remain.
- WhatsApp membership change during metadata lookup/hydration: #128283 uses held synthetic requests. The bounded cache converges on the next membership event or five-minute expiry; no per-group generation/retry loop. The artificial Date-maximum-year guard/test is removed too.
- WhatsApp failed temporary-directory cleanup: #109886's human report asks for live group discovery, not a background cleanup service. Keep exclusive credentials and await close/flush before release; a failed cleanup is retried on the next lookup or restart, without a recurring timer.

## Retained contracts and actual incidents

- Discord nonce idempotency, HTTP 429 handling, bounded queues/buffers and effect authorization stay. Its bounded reconnect allowance remains for human #56610 (54 disconnects over four days and missing notifications).
- Telegram's single-poller/restart protection remains for human #81507 (855+ duplicate-poller errors), and per-topic typing remains for #138763. Account-wide limits and authorization are independent security/platform requirements.
- Feishu logical content dedupe remains for human #46778 (real DMs with different message IDs). Slack message/app_mention twin dedupe is platform idempotency. Telegram batch rollback protects unadopted user data after partial commits.
- Mattermost server backfill remains for human #93204. iMessage age/recovery rules remain for human #89237's actual old-message replay. Signal's recovery remains for human #100944, with one durable retry owner.
- Matrix encrypted-room checks and coherent persisted crypto/sync snapshots remain under security/durability rules. WhatsApp credential exclusion, private atomic writes and flush-before-release remain under those same rules.
- Signal daemon exit joining, ordinary pending delivery/partial receipts, iMessage stable short IDs and approval provenance remain under shutdown, public-contract and authorization rules. The iMessage bridge invalidator is only one observed-failure cache deletion, not a speculative generation protocol.

## Evidence

- Net production LOC after the required conflict-only rebase and CI repair: **-1,116** (487 added / 1,603 removed), excluding tests/fixtures/test support/generated/declarations, measured with `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD`. Tests/support remain net **-2,508**. Assertion and max-lines baselines only shrink. No schema, retention, permission, dependency or public SDK shape changes.
- Production extension typecheck passes. Runtime value cycle check: 0; all-import Madge cycles: 0.
- Independent full-candidate review through P2 is clean after correcting Discord synchronous ingress persistence and Feishu fallback receipts. The Matrix failure-path drain preserves write settlement without duplicate normal-path draining. A separate review of the leftover test removal is clean.
- Focused Matrix shared-client proof: 20 tests, 17.54s Vitest / 26.87s command. Focused Discord preview REST proof: 18 tests, 423.91s Vitest / 452.30s command under host load above 130 (90% transforms). WhatsApp metadata/directory: 22 tests, 246.64s command. Earlier corrected Discord voice/routing/draft proof: 40 tests. Existing Feishu fallback recovery tests remain unchanged and pass (76 reply-dispatcher cases).
- Broad AWS proof visited all ten channels. Discord: 2,874 passed plus one obsolete queued-generation row, removed with the mechanism; its introducing PR #130392 explicitly disclaims that same-controller native-ingress route. Telegram: 2,006 passed plus three removed/adapted generation cases. Slack: 1,971 passed plus one removed delayed-receipt variant. iMessage: 880 passed; Mattermost: 550; WhatsApp: 1,203; Teams: 1,169; Feishu: 1,133. Matrix: 338 passed plus two adapted retirement expectations. Signal's original-error regression was fixed at the producer without weakening its restart assertion.
- Suppression check: 2 passed / 1 inherited baseline failure, 64.34s. The exact two extra SQLite test-support entries and the test are untouched from the merge-base; upstream commit `dab6a8de087` fixes the allowlist and is already on current main. No suppression added.
- Two initial Testbox requests never obtained a runner and were stopped. The subsequent AWS fallback lease is released with complete cleanup. Fresh Testbox proof passed the complete Signal scope: 575 tests, with three existing skipped cases (none added here). That Testbox was stopped after the source correction invalidated its reuse key. Only one remote lease is used at a time; no CI reruns or pushes for green.

Final follow-up: 201 focused cases pass across Signal partial/retry, Matrix SDK and Slack dispatch (106 database-worker cases + 95 Slack cases; 920.31s command on the loaded host). Telegram's corrected draft file passes all 37 retained cases. Both final production and test type graphs pass. The Signal restart test is unchanged and now preserves the original send error through the existing failure callback. Final follow-up review is clean through P2.

The coordinator approved the exact Signal SAFETY baseline shrink, 2 -> 1, including the heartbeat-owned baseline file. All local ratchets through plugin-boundary and package-patch checks now pass. A supplementary extension-only changed gate also passes both extension type graphs, coercion declarations and deprecated API usage; its remaining checks are in progress. GitHub reported CONFLICTING for the initial published head. prs.title: fix(active-memory): skip recall for inter-session deliveries
prs.body:
Fixes #143821

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users coordinating agents would pay for unnecessary Active Memory recall runs when a visible session received `sessions_send`, sub-agent settlement, or announcement deliveries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing typed input provenance through prompt-hook contexts in the embedded, CLI, Codex, and Copilot runtimes, including the shared harness projection. Active Memory excludes inter-session inputs at its existing eligibility boundary; the shared `user` trigger and normal human-message recall remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Agent handoffs and completion deliveries no longer start memory recall in the receiving conversation. Subsequent human messages in that same session still recall normally, including when no provenance metadata is supplied. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, three registered-plugin regressions returned recalled context for `sessions_send`, `subagent_settle`, and `subagent_announce`. CLI and embedded prompt-hook regressions also failed because provenance was absent.
- After the fix, 748 tests passed across Active Memory, embedded prompt provenance/tool policy, CLI preparation, Codex attempts, and Copilot attempts. Coverage includes real admitted-run/authorized-hook composition and the sequence of internal delivery followed by human input in the same visible session.
- Validation command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-provenance.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-tool-policy.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts extensions/copilot/src/attempt.test.ts`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`: all format, structural, core/plugin production and test typechecks, dead-export checks, and core lint passed. Plugin lint initially hit an ancestor-install isolation error in the nested worktree; after moving the worktree outside the parent checkout and running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the exact remaining plugin lint lane passed with declaration preparation enabled.
- Plugin contracts: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.contracts-plugin.config.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 1,117 tests in 47 files.
- Structured autoreview completed with no actionable findings at its default P0 threshold.
- Production delta: +10 lines to expose and forward existing origin metadata through all prompt producers and reject inter-session recall. No parallel dispatch path, configuration option, or database change.
- Codex contract inspected directly at `openai/codex@9e552e9d15ba52bed7077d5357f3e18e330f8f38`: [TurnStartParams and input conversion](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9e552e9d15ba52bed7077d5357f3e18e330f8f38/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs#L68) and [UserInput](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/9e552e9d15ba52bed7077d5357f3e18e330f8f38/codex-rs/protocol/src/user_input.rs#L15). This is host-side metadata propagation and does not change the Codex wire protocol.
- Proof boundary: runtime integration tests simulate the model/backend boundary. A full live Gateway/channel multi-agent round trip was not run; these results establish the producer-to-hook and recall eligibility boundaries, not live end-to-end delivery.

AI-assisted implementation and review.

prs.title: fix(openai): stop advertising retired Sora 2 video provider
prs.body:
Closes #158876

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `video_generate` keeps advertising and auto-selecting the bundled `openai` video provider as a working candidate (default `sora-2`, `configured: yes`) even though OpenAI shut down the Videos API and Sora 2/Sora 2 Pro on the public `api.openai.com` endpoint on 2026-09-24, so every request against it wastes an attempt and fails with an empty-body 404 before silently falling back to another provider.

## User Impact

User impact: installs with an OpenAI credential and no explicit `agents.defaults.mediaModels.video` no longer see `openai` listed as `configured: yes` or auto-selected as the first video candidate, so `video_generate` goes straight to a working provider instead of wasting a request on a route that no longer exists. Operators who point `models.providers.openai.baseUrl` at a custom endpoint (proxy/gateway) that still serves Sora are unaffected — that endpoint remains eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOpenAIVideoGenerationProvider`'s `isConfigured` only checked for an API key, so any OpenAI credential made the provider eligible for both `action=list` and automatic cross-provider fallback ordering (`resolveAutoCapabilityFallbackRefs` in `src/media-generation/runtime-shared.ts`), regardless of whether the endpoint still serves video. The fix adds a narrow endpoint check, reusing the existing `isOpenAIApiBaseUrl` classifier (already used elsewhere in the OpenAI extension to distinguish the official `api.openai.com` platform endpoint from custom/proxy endpoints): `isConfigured` now returns `false` when the resolved base URL is the retired public endpoint, while a custom `baseUrl` still passes through unaffected.

## Evidence

Ran the affected suite plus the two adjacent suites the issue's own review named as acceptance criteria, all against unmodified test infra:

```
$ pnpm vitest run extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.test.ts src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
...
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  105 passed (105)
```

Proved the new/changed assertion actually catches the regression: reverted the source fix only (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts`, keeping the updated test), reran the new test, confirmed it fails, then restored the fix:

```
 × ... does not advertise OpenAI video against the retired public Videos API endpoint
   → expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 25 skipped (26)
```

With the fix restored, the full file passes again (26/26), including a new case confirming a custom `baseUrl` still reports `configured: true`.

Also ran, clean:

```
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
$ pnpm lint:extensions
Found 1 warning and 0 errors.   # pre-existing max-lines warning in extensions/signal, unrelated to this change
$ oxfmt --check extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.ts extensions/openai/video-generation-provider.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ports the shared link reader, file preview, and image lightbox from Lit to Solid 2 while preserving the existing viewer experience.

## User Impact

Navigation, tab history, keyboard controls, file browsing, zoom, and read-only content keep their existing tags, classes, events, and selectors. Requests and object URLs remain scoped to their owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each registered viewer now has one Solid implementation through `defineSolidBridge`. The link reader retains plain TypeScript owners for tab/request state and hover/prefetch lifetimes. Its small Lit prefetch adapter and shared tab/resizer templates remain for the unported chat/panel callers. A synchronous bridge property-change hook preserves immediate preview invalidation on identity changes. The Solid Kbd property is normalized to `class` for the migrated file viewer.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 13 focused files, each `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` | 257 tests passed |
| Focused syntax/Solid lint and stylesheet lint | Passed |
| Lit migration ratchet against `09d58be4e650` | Passed |

| Types, UI build, UI unit and E2E shards | PR CI |

The initial failures exposed the intentional bridge mount/disconnect microtask boundary and Solid-owned state-write rules; the implementation and fixtures now honor those contracts. Native platform and release-only lanes are unrelated to this UI-only change.

Production LOC: **5184 → 5972**. Tests: **5696 → 5829**. Growth comes from explicit Solid view/lifetime bindings and typed props; the existing owners keep their contracts.

The first CI attempt found new assertions needing safety rationale and one CSS-only literal misidentified as user copy; fixed, with the now-unused assertion baseline entry removed. prs.title: refactor: prepare approval and placement state in workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approval requests such as `approval.get` can expire rows while reading them. Bundled in-process dispatch now selects the existing worker-capable approval path for the full method family. Explicit legacy approval callbacks retain their native transaction visibility. Session reset and deletion likewise await placement retirement through the existing worker, preserving current-authority checks before mutation.

## User Impact

Gateway startup now awaits stale local-turn cleanup in the placement worker while holding the state-directory lock, before admitting turns. A single `UPDATE … RETURNING` supplies the cleared records for publication. An uncertain result fails startup, and the next boot can safely repeat the idempotent cleanup. This bootstrap operation needs no live-turn batch staging or additional transaction/commit handshakes.

Released synchronous placement methods and opaque approval callbacks keep their signatures, return timing, and completion semantics. They are deprecated until removal in the next Plugin SDK major and use the shared warning helper. Custom Gateway contexts that implement only the released placement interface select its adapter explicitly; worker errors never switch to the native adapter. Schema, stored-data format, permissions, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The restart simplification removed **67 production lines and 60 test lines relative to the intermediate candidate**. Those are not reductions against main: the intermediate machinery never shipped. The final change uses the existing placement and approval owners.

## Evidence

<details>
<summary>Focused behavior and compatibility evidence</summary>

The recorded approval-routing regression passes both runtime and legacy entry points: an expired approval is persisted through the worker for a runtime request, while the explicit legacy callback keeps native transaction visibility. The initial fixture lacked the required request authority; after that fixture was repaired, both cases and the existing direct/tool commit-guard cases passed. Placement reset coverage passes with asynchronous retirement and with a custom context implementing only the released synchronous contract. The released Gateway placement type-compatibility fixture also passed.

The final restart implementation passed these focused commands on its reviewed source:

| Command | Result | Command wall time |
|---|---|---:|
| `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 14 passed; includes idempotent restart cleanup, preserved worker claims, and no host SQL during cleanup | 128.50 s |
| `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-claims.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 31 passed; existing live-turn settlement and authority contracts | 200.28 s |

These timings include runner setup. GitHub CI seconds are unavailable before publication. The restart-specific review found no P0/P1 issue. The focused results span recorded revisions; they are not one full-suite run on the extracted PR head.

<!-- FINAL_SLICE_VALIDATION -->
The exec-preparation extraction restores all 37 affected files byte-for-byte to the baseline. The remaining approval fixture and compatibility record name only the retained approval contract. Fresh static checks, changed/mock-dependent tests, and the published-driver update cell are in progress before merge; earlier combined-stack results are not claimed as final-head checks.
<!-- END_FINAL_SLICE_VALIDATION -->

</details>

<details>
<summary>Paired SQL measurements and attribution</summary>

The direct restart comparison used **ALL 7 → 6 statements and MAIN 7 → 0**. The new worker command accounts for one request and six worker statements. No latency improvement is claimed.

The following historical integration comparison contains six alternating pairs of `bc8f693d` and `14ee0251` on the same host. prs.title: fix(ui): keep Advanced settings visible on reconnect (#152874)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an already open Advanced settings form refreshed its schema after a Gateway reconnect, the form was replaced by **Loading schema…**. Returning to the form reset the reading position and closed the Setup disclosure. Keep the existing form mounted during that refresh and make its controls read-only until the schema returns.

## Root cause

`renderConfig` in `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` used `schemaLoading` to replace the entire form and Setup subtree, even when an existing schema was available. Lit removed and recreated their DOM, losing scroll position and disclosure state. The initial load still needs the spinner when there is no schema to render.

## Changes

- Show the spinner only when no schema has loaded yet; retain the existing form and Setup during later schema refreshes.
- Disable form and Setup edits while a refresh is pending, and mark the form region busy for assistive technology.
- Add a browser regression for the retained DOM, temporarily disabled controls, reopened editing, and initial-load spinner. Document the reconnect behavior in Settings.

## Evidence

On an isolated Gateway serving the rebuilt Control UI, Chromium exercised the real Advanced settings page before and after the change:

| Scenario | Current main before fix | This PR after fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop reconnect with form scrolled to `scrollTop=1800` | Spinner replaces the form; position resets to `0` | Same form remains mounted with 469 fields; position remains `1800` |
| Mobile reconnect with form scrolled to `scrollTop=1688` | Spinner replaces the form; position resets to `0` | Form and position remain at `1688` |
| Setup expanded while schema reloads | Disclosure disappears and reopens closed | Disclosure remains expanded; its controls are disabled during refresh and enabled afterward |

The served `/assets/index-*.js` hash changed after `pnpm ui:build`; the after-fix screenshots below show the retained desktop and mobile reading positions and open Setup section. The captures contain no real credentials or user data.

Before this change, on current main (the issue reporter's real-Gateway capture, with configuration text redacted): the form read at 1,800 px is replaced during the reload and returns to 0 px.

![Current main: Advanced settings returns to the top after a reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d23f1740-c873-40c1-be8f-8ea1559880f3)

After this change:

![Advanced settings keeps its desktop reading position after reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f71c3b38-17ba-444f-9c6c-a64c2b4df696)

![Advanced settings keeps its mobile reading position after reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dce75047-a220-44fd-aa4d-bcc605963e41)

![The Setup section remains expanded after reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/953c40c1-4ea5-41da-af21-a519decf4085)

## Validation and risk

- Focused config browser tests: 63 passed across the existing suite and new reconnect regression.
- New test file cost: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/config/view.reconnect.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reports 766 ms in Vitest (tests 3%), or 4.7 s wall including pnpm and Chromium startup. In this head's CI run, `checks-ui (3/3)` spent about 0.13 s on the file (103.5 ms collection, 8 ms test), within the 5 s per-file budget.
- Changed-file checks passed, including UI and core-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and line-cap ratchets. Documentation link check: 0 broken links.
- `pnpm ui:build` passed and the rebuilt bundle was exercised through the actual Gateway. The repository-wide `pnpm build` timed out in `write-cli-startup-metadata` on the unchanged base checkout, so it is not claimed as a passing check here.
- The initial schema load still shows its spinner; forms with a previously loaded schema are temporarily read-only during refresh. No configuration or schema contract changes.

Release-note context: fixes lost reading position and Setup expansion on Advanced settings reconnect. `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned.

Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski for the report. AI-assisted: yes.

Closes #152874

prs.title: fix(worktrees): repair missing partial-clone objects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Missing objects in a managed partial clone prevent live worktrees from being snapshotted or removed. Pack-index maintenance repairs lookup metadata but cannot restore the missing content.

## User Impact

`openclaw worktrees gc --retry-deferred` now fetches missing objects required by every Git-registered worktree index and current HEAD tree from the existing promisor remote. It preserves index bytes and working files. Ordinary maintenance remains network-free, and historical commits remain filtered. There are no schema or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance owner repairs pack lookup before enumerating live objects with native Git. Recovery fetches batches of 256, with a five-minute budget, bounded output, and a 4,096-object allowance per pass. Completed batches remain available after interruption; the next explicit retry starts with the remaining missing objects. Unavailable content produces a warning without reconstructing staged content from working files.

**The original historical blob-loss writer remains unidentified.** This is a recovery change, not a claim that the original incident is fully diagnosed. Current consolidation already copies all selected objects in separate promisor/ordinary batches, and native MIDX expiry is the only published-pack deletion path. Temporary cleanup targets aged `tmp_pack_*` files under a native file lease. The earlier automatic incremental-repack and per-removal pack-repair paths were removed by #167453 and #167695.

Production delta excluding tests/docs: **+139 lines** (144 added, 5 removed). Growth implements the requested bounded recovery contract; there was no previous recovery implementation to delete. No second pack writer, scheduler, cache, or compatibility path is added.

## Evidence

Isolated Ubuntu rig, Node 26.8.1 and Git 2.53.0; synthetic data only:

| Contract | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20 linked worktrees / 10,240 index references | 70 missing objects | 0 missing, repaired in 260 ms |
| Historical-only blob | Missing | Still missing |
| Inventory above the per-pass limit | 4,097 missing | 1 after the first pass; 0 after retry |
| Staged-only content with different working bytes | Snapshot blocked | Object restored; index and working bytes unchanged |

The subsequent ordinary maintenance pass took 76 ms. These are synthetic recovery timings, not deployed Gateway measurements. Clean-index and staged-index loss probes on Git 2.43.0, 2.53.0, and 2.55.0 preserved all 32 blobs across 20 linked worktrees; none reproduced the original loss.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.gc-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **15/15 passed**, 73.11 s wall / 69.73 s Vitest including worker preparation. The three recovery cases took 1.907 s, 0.534 s, and 1.412 s. Original-source controls fail for the intended missing-recovery behavior.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged`: all selected typechecks, including 28 core-test partitions, formatting and preceding guards passed. The sole failure was the pre-existing `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` dead export. The nine remaining lint/schema/database/media/import/auth checks were then run separately and passed. Proof is pinned to base `bbd2daf8b6def57eb0ac47c5e270c9b39cc168e6` and the exact three-file patch.
- All 60 worktree test files were exercised through explicit wrapper-selected targets: **618 passed / 35 skipped / 10 failed**. Nine failures are the independently reproduced branch-cache and signed-commit fixtures below. The tenth is `git.test.ts` assuming its temporary directory is outside a checkout, while the required rig TMPDIR is inside this worktree; unchanged main reproduces that same fixture mismatch. The ten failures remain explicit baseline gaps.
- Unchanged main `ddca97e26ac2d734869f4fe74d53fd3c99384152` reproduces the same dead export, all eight branch-cache assertions in `service-branches.test.ts`, and the signed-commit-age fixture's missing `host-marker` in `service.source-only-filters.test.ts`. Those failures are recorded, not counted as passing coverage. The same unchanged baseline also reproduces the checkout-discovery fixture mismatch caused by the required nested TMPDIR.
- Independent review through P2 is clean. The subsequent rebase preserves the patch and all three reviewed file blob IDs.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4m7ghbyc5v4hykby2mqa29t` ran the initial Git probes and original-source regression controls, then timed out during later source sync. AWS `cbx_2da5802573f9` and Hetzner `cbx_0a7dd709cf9f` were stopped after prolonged sync stalls and ran no validation commands. Final proof used the authorized rig fallback. All three leases are stopped; no production clone was changed.

prs.title: feat(telegram): support copy-text presentation buttons
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Add a portable typed `copy-text` presentation action. Telegram renders it as a
native Bot API `CopyTextButton`; channels without native support keep a readable,
safe manual-copy fallback.

This updates the existing contribution first explored in #36105. It does not
reintroduce the retired raw Telegram button input.

## Current maintenance head

- **Exact head:** `2d924e3da52c00b7ba343f5965275860dffb415e`
- **Frozen base:** `ef54f6720460ff4bc563e3222cbdf6eaf36e1d51`
- **Shape:** one signed semantic commit, 44 files, +2,392/-334.
- **Merge simulation:** clean against the frozen base; merged tree
  `8c9bf19e21d15d55311b498e73aae17a5318bf38`.

The frozen base has no equivalent portable `copy-text` presentation action or
Telegram `copy_text` encoder. Existing inline-code tap-to-copy behavior is a
separate rendering path and does not expose this capability to plugins.

## Behavior

- The message tool schema exposes a typed `copy-text` action with a required
  string value.
- The shared presentation adapter preserves the action only when a channel
  declares `copyTextButtons`; unsupported channels render readable manual-copy
  fallback while callback payload values remain private.
- Telegram emits `InlineKeyboardButton.copy_text` only for values satisfying
  the Bot API's 1–256-character contract. Values that cannot be encoded safely
  remain visible as escaped fallback instead of being silently rewritten.
- Native controls share Telegram's existing 100-action budget, including every
  option in a select that Telegram renders as an individual button. Provider-owned
  and usable legacy keyboards retain precedence; unusable legacy controls do not
  falsely displace a valid presentation keyboard.
- Presentation-only native controls use the standard message anchor without
  duplicating the copied value into the visible body.
- Drop-time copy identity keeps duplicate labels paired with the correct value
  when an action falls back after planning.
- Markup-only edits do not synthesize replacement body text. If a rejected,
  over-budget, or shadowed copy control needs readable fallback, the action
  returns a recoverable result requiring explicit content or caption.
- Copy targets are treated as data rather than rendered prose, preserving exact
  literal escape sequences and fenced/multiline bytes through fallback.
- Discord long-copy fallback uses a complete collision-safe fence in every
  independently rendered fragment. Mention suppression is derived from the exact
  rendered fallback text, including enabled and disabled labels. Focused route-seam
  tests cover component/outbound, webhook, interaction, direct-action, and
  fresh-final handoffs. The exact-head deterministic wrapper receipt is green at
  `proof/pre-pr-2d924e3da52c.json`.

## Evidence

Locally runnable focused evidence totals **253/253**:

- core payload, schema, visibility, and shared adapter: **100/100**
- Telegram native/fallback/action runtime: **60/60**
- Slack fallback: **27/27**
- Discord fallback, fencing, mention suppression, interaction, and webhook paths:
  **65/65**
- directly runnable Feishu fallback: **1/1**

The Discord **65/65** was rerun against the exact final tree after the

A retired worker inventory could make an otherwise completed Gateway shutdown fail. A reconciliation waiting on inventory readiness could also reject after shutdown had begun.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Reconciliation treats retirement as expected only after its existing stop flag is set. No lifecycle state, database schema, memory limit, or configuration is added. Thanks @Captain69G for the shutdown report.

Production LOC: **+26** across five files; eight changed files total. The bug-fix exception covers the typed error and the two narrow shutdown boundaries. The nearby tunnel status/live-owner code was simplified without changing behavior to retain the existing line cap.

prs.title: fix(config-cli): say the running gateway self-restarts, and name the deadline
prs.body:
## Summary

`config set` on a restart-required path always prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`, regardless of `gateway.reload.mode`. With live reload at its default that hint is wrong about **who** restarts, and silent about the fact that the restart has a **deadline**.

What actually happens when live reload is on:

1. The CLI writes the config file and prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`
2. The running Gateway's config watcher independently detects the change.
3. It classifies the path as restart-required and defers, waiting for active work to drain.
4. After `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` (5m) it **force-restarts anyway**, aborting whatever is still in flight.

So the operator is told to perform a restart that is not theirs to perform, and is not told that an automatic one is already scheduled with a hard cut-off. If the edit was made from inside a long-running agent turn, that turn is aborted by its own config write.

## Reproduction

On a running Gateway with default `gateway.reload` settings:

```console
$ openclaw config set plugins.load.paths '["/path/to/my-plugin"]' --strict-json
Updated plugins.load.paths. Restart the gateway to apply.
```

The operator does nothing, believing the change is inert until they act. Five minutes later, unprompted:

```
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (plugins.load.paths)
[reload] config change requires gateway restart (plugins.load.paths) — deferring until 1 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), 1 gateway request(s) complete
[reload] restart still deferred after 30330ms ...
[reload] restart timeout after 300053ms with 1 operation(s), ... still active; forcing restart
[gateway] forced restart requested; skipping active work drain
[shutdown] aborted 1 active run(s) during restart shutdown
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=<redacted> durationMs=1504983 error="agent run aborted for restart"
```

A ~25 minute agent run was aborted. Nothing in the CLI output suggested that was coming.

`plugins.load.paths` is not special here — it has no hot-reload rule, so it takes the default in `buildGatewayReloadPlan`:

```js
const kind = rule?.kind ?? "restart";
```

Any restart-required path reaches the same outcome.

## Fix

Split the hint by who owns the restart:

| `gateway.reload.mode` | hint |
| --- | --- |
| default / `hybrid` | `A running gateway restarts itself to apply this: it waits for active work to drain, then aborts in-flight runs after 5m. Restart manually if no gateway is running.` |
| `off` | `Restart the gateway to apply.` (unchanged) |

The deadline is read from `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` rather than hardcoded, so the message tracks the value the Gateway actually enforces.

Hot-appliable paths under `reload.mode: "off"` keep the manual hint — live reload is disabled, so the Gateway will not pick them up on its own.

## Tests

`src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 243 passed.

- Two new cases pin both branches: the self-restart wording including its deadline, and the unchanged manual wording under `reload.mode: "off"`.
- Five existing assertions updated; they asserted the manual hint for restart-required paths running with live reload on, which is the behaviour being corrected.
- `docs/cli/config.md` hint table updated.

## Scope

This changes the `config set` / `config patch` / `config unset` hint only. `plugins-cli.runtime.ts` and `plugins-uninstall-command.ts` print their own copies of the same string and have the same ambiguity — left for a follow-up to keep this diff reviewable.

This is a message-accuracy fix. It does not change restart behaviour: the 5m deferral is still hardcoded and its timeout intent is still `force: true`, so a restart-required config write can still abort an in-flight run. Making that window configurable (and non-forcing by default) is a separate discussion I'm happy to open if maintainers want it.

prs.title: fix(agents): tool-heavy turns stop after rejected tool calls
prs.body:
Related: #147040, #135111
Follow-up to #142176

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: terminal-confirmed Responses turns stop after a rejected tool call even though their earlier tool work has already finished.

## User Impact

For terminal-confirmed Responses rejections, the agent can continue from recorded results instead of abandoning completed work or replaying the original task. Refusals, cancellation, pending approvals, asynchronous work, and intentionally terminated turns stop this recovery. No configuration or migration is required. This avoids automatic replay of the original task; it does not make arbitrary tools idempotent or prevent the model from choosing an action again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Continue through the existing transcript owner only when the previous tool batch is proven settled, including recorded tool failures and prior visible progress. Recognize malformed-call rejections and structured `incomplete_tool_call` evidence from completed Responses output; keep output-limit and EOF recovery separate.

This refresh resolves conflicts with current main and uses the existing provider retry budget rather than adding a second counter or retry loop. Parsing remains strict, and rejected partial arguments never execute.

**Coverage is intentionally conservative:** this new post-effect continuation requires positive, coherent producer-recorded terminal facts before every malformed-code or legacy-text shortcut. Replay-safe attempts retain their existing retry policy, including when visible text makes that policy decline a retry. Early malformed item completions without terminal facts stop rather than guessing what an unread response would say. Providers/cadences without this terminal contract do not qualify. #149071 has now landed on main. This refresh preserves that canonical drain rather than copying or stacking its implementation: an early malformed item completion may recover only when the drain actually records coherent terminal facts. EOF or unsafe later facts still stop.

Both reported terminal-coherence gaps are repaired. The existing output tracker records bounded refusal, provider-error, and incomplete-detail facts before validation can throw, including refusal events observed while draining rejected output. Terminal status, canonical stop, and these facts take precedence over malformed-call codes and legacy rejection text. Failed, cancelled, refused, nonterminal, unknown, and contradictory terminal facts cannot authorize this continuation. No raw refusal or provider-error payload is copied into the new diagnostics. Omitted wire status remains compatible only through an explicit producer-recorded `absent` value; missing diagnostic metadata is not treated as that compatibility case.

Original implementation by @lraesly; the original contributor commit is preserved. Cleanup and additional regression coverage are co-authored with Dallin Romney.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/bc8ef321-823d-43cc-b6a5-1b4007712b09)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/34d86ce2-2c0a-4a5c-83cf-082c15f8faf0)

## Evidence

**September 29 conflict repair:** incorporated main after #149071 landed and this PR became conflicting. Current-head review is complete, but CI has two failed test groups under investigation. This is not RFR; no merge or auto-merge is requested.

- **Head/tree:** `07f3cfe72d05cf89a6e9fb38e79b554c97b3f980` / `4f5889456300c1ce501411910c7ceb501106ead4`, incorporating main `9b5b439dcb6e11b929c982d9b40e8ddcb4c9b2e5`. The signed merge preserves published `e980b8c1` and original contributor `b14f3008` ancestry. Both requested coauthors parse on this new commit; the separate historical trailer-metadata question is unchanged.
- **Conflict resolution:** retained both the bounded terminal-coherence tests and main's expanded rejection/ending fencing matrix. The canonical drain implementation is byte-identical to main. No new retry owner or relaxed safety condition was added.
- **Focused proof:** 113 transport tests and 218 recovery/controller tests passed locally. All 15 actual loopback cases passed in the configured clean Blacksmith environment; local loopback failures were traced to the host egress proxy, with no proxy or assertion changes.
- **Fresh Gateway composition proof:** one real Gateway/Responses HTTP/file-tool test passed all **11 scenarios**: two coherent positives continued with four requests; nine refusal/error/status/EOF negatives stopped after three. Every scenario preserved the single write and failed read without executing the rejected edit or repeating the write. Positives required exactly one `tool_call_rejection` retry and preserved the original prompt/results; negatives required none. The added actual HTTP EOF case supplies no terminal facts. Test body **22.079s**; build-backed E2E lane **512.49s**.
- **Source-bound execution:** [Blacksmith backing run 36514790813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36514790813), sealed carrier `655b77b90547c08f9a1fc759952b85882b9fb027`, exact tree above, input checks before/after, delegated command exit **0**, settled/stopped lease. The backing workflow can be cancelled by one-shot cleanup: this is a delegated-command receipt, not green workflow CI. Complete stdout, timing, manifest and lease receipts are retained in the implementation session. No live-provider inference is claimed.
- **Checks/review:** the supported staged, pinned-main changed-check plan reached clean final lint, including types and guards. Its quiet-success contract was inspected after the native process receipt expired; final lint was narrowly reconfirmed with exit 0, without repeating the full plan. Independent AutoReview returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head ClawSweeper R16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147611#issuecomment-5657488597) rates overall/patch platinum 4/6 and proof diamond 5/6, with no actionable or security findings. Sweeper did not execute the proof and could not independently inspect the backing receipt.

**Current CI failures:** [collector settlement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36516569050/job/109240425657) lacks the expected collector-completion record after terminal execution; [Gateway deletion lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36516569050/job/109240425514) has three SQLite pathname/active-owner errors. Both were observed on tested merge `a7b25b83719f` (base `59490dc752778` + this head). Cause and attribution remain unresolved: unchanged files do not establish a main-baseline failure or permit a waiver. #160838 is already present in that composition, so it is not treated as an absent fix. Exact-plan replay and owner analysis are in progress; no GitHub CI rerun or cancellation has been requested.

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier evidence and limits</summary>

September 25 head `e980b8c1` had green required CI/security gates and ClawSweeper platinum overall/patch with diamond proof. Those are prior-head results, not current-head admission. Earlier exact-merge and corrected-composition replays each passed 4,456 tests/327 files: [original merge replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36098563678), [corrected composition](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36099165775). The historical Discord third-preflight failure was not reproduced or conclusively attributed; #155965 independently corrected fixture ordering while preserving security assertions. No original GitHub CI cancellation/rerun or baseline waiver was used.

The earlier September 29 retry-policy composition on pinned main `da0b5812` supplied 331 existing passes at retained summary/tally granularity plus 31 corrected custom passes with direct command receipts. This refresh has separate fresh Gateway proof; older results are not relabeled as latest-main execution. prs.title: fix(discord): resolve digit-suffixed usernames
prs.body:
## Summary

- Treat a Discord username ending in digits as a username candidate instead of an all-numeric target.
- Add a regression assertion for `jane123` alongside the existing `jane` directory-resolution case.

## Issue

Closes #146441

## What Problem This Solves

Bare Discord usernames such as `jane123` currently match the trailing-digit alternative in `isLikelyUsername`. That skips the user directory lookup and returns a channel target, so a valid DM recipient can be sent down the channel-delivery path instead.

## Root cause

The numeric alternative in `isLikelyUsername` was anchored only at the end. Regex alternation precedence therefore made any input ending in digits look like a non-username. Anchoring the complete alternative set keeps explicit prefixes and all-numeric IDs out of username lookup while allowing mixed letter-and-digit usernames through it.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` (pass)
- Direct execution of the real `resolveDiscordTarget` module on Node v22.22.3 with temporary stubs at its dependency boundaries (pass after fix)
- Pure numeric sibling case: `123` remained a channel target with no additional directory lookup (pass)

The requested focused Vitest command could not load because this independently owned checkout has no installed repository dependencies:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/targets.test.ts -t "returns a resolved user for usernames"
Error: Repository dependencies are missing from the independently owned checkout's node_modules.
[test] FAILED (exit 1)
```

Remote Vitest proof was also unavailable. Blacksmith Testbox could not start because the `blacksmith` executable is absent, and the trusted direct AWS fallback could not obtain credentials because no EC2 IMDS role was available.

## Before/after

Before, direct execution of the real resolver returned a channel target without consulting the directory and failed the user-target assertion:

```json
{"input":"jane123","result":{"kind":"channel","id":"jane123","normalized":"channel:jane123"},"directoryCalls":0}
```

After, the same resolver path consulted the directory and returned the resolved user. The all-numeric sibling behavior remained unchanged:

```json
{"input":"jane123","result":{"kind":"user","id":"999","normalized":"user:999","display":"jane123"},"directoryCalls":1}

prs.title: fix(config): reject unconfigured secret providers during strict validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #147435.

When a configuration references a `SecretRef` targeting an unconfigured provider alias (for instance, `store:store:OPENAI_API_KEY` or an undeclared custom exec/file provider when `secrets.providers` is omitted or lacks that alias), `openclaw config validate` previously passed green. 

When the Gateway daemon subsequently started up, runtime resolution in `src/secrets/resolve.ts` threw `SECRET_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` during required secret activation. Under service supervisors (`launchd` / `systemd`), this triggered an unbounded crash loop (in the reported incident, 18 failed boots in ~6 minutes) with zero pre-restart warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two gaps in `src/config/validation.ts` allowed unconfigured secret providers to slip past validation:
1. **Empty-Providers Guard**: Line 740 guarded provider checks with `Object.keys(mutatedConfig.secrets?.providers ?? {}).length > 0`. If `secrets.providers` was absent or empty (the common case for operators using shorthand refs without having declared a provider map), validation skipped provider inspection entirely.
2. **Missing Existence Check**: `collectSecretRefProviderSourceIssues` previously only called `resolveSecretRefProviderSourceMismatch(config, ref)`. By design, `resolveSecretRefProviderSourceMismatch` returns `null` when `!configuredSource` (i.e. when the provider does not exist), checking only whether an *already declared* provider's source matches the reference source.

This change:
- **Existence Check in Strict Validation**: Checks `const providerConfig = params.config.secrets?.providers?.[ref.provider];` and `if (!providerConfig && !isBuiltInDefaultSecretProviderRef(params.config, ref))` emits:
  `Secret provider "${ref.provider}" is not configured.`
- **Removes Empty-Providers Guard**: Runs `collectSecretRefProviderIssues` whenever `opts.semanticValidation === "strict"`, ensuring empty or omitted `secrets.providers` maps are strictly checked.
- **Preserves Built-in Default Providers**: Respects `isBuiltInDefaultSecretProviderRef(params.config, ref)` so that built-in `env:default:*` and `store:default:*` references (as well as aliases configured via `secrets.defaults`) remain valid without requiring redundant provider definitions.
- **Preserves Non-Strict Runtime Validation**: Keeps `semanticValidation === "runtime"` lenient so that inactive plugin surfaces remain unblocked during non-strict passes.
- **Strict Credential Opacity**: Strictly avoids interpolating `ref.id` into the validation message, preserving the secret token sanitization invariant.
- **Clean Export Boundary**: Internal validation issue collector resides in `src/config/validation-issues.ts` without creating unused exports on the public `validation.ts` surface, satisfying Knip deadcode checks.

## User Impact & Compatibility Semantics

- **Early Rejection Before Boot Crash Loops**: Operators running `openclaw config validate` or saving configuration mutations via the CLI/API will immediately see a clear, actionable diagnostic (`Secret provider "store" is not configured.`) before service restart.
- **Whole-Config Persistence Contract on Inactive Surfaces**: Because `writeConfigFile` enforces `semanticValidation: "strict"` to protect the Gateway from boot failure, candidate configurations containing undeclared secret provider references across any section (including disabled channels) are caught prior to persistence. This guarantees that saving a configuration never leaves the Gateway in an unbootable crash-loop state.
- **Remediation & Recovery Paths**:
  - `openclaw doctor` does not synthesize missing external secret provider credentials or undeclared provider aliases automatically.
  - Instead, operators remediate undeclared provider references through normal configuration tools:
    1. Declare the provider in `secrets.providers` via `openclaw config set secrets.providers.<alias> '{"source":"<source>"}' --strict-json` (or editing `openclaw.json`).
    2. Switch the reference to a built-in default provider alias (`store:default:*` or `env:default:*`).
    3. Remove the stale/unused reference.

## Evidence

- **Unit Tests**: Added comprehensive test cases in `src/config/validation.policy.test.ts`:
  - Strictly rejects unconfigured secret providers when `secrets.providers` is omitted.
  - Strictly rejects unconfigured secret providers when other providers are declared.
  - Allows built-in default provider refs for `env` and `store` without explicit provider declarations.
  - Verifies that secret ref IDs are strictly redacted and never leaked in validation issues.
- **Integration Tests**: Added real CLI integration test in `src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts`:
  - `rejects unconfigured provider refs during real config validate` verifying real `openclaw config validate` exits with code 1, prints the diagnostic, and redacts the secret ID.
- **Architecture & Linter Hygiene**: `collectSecretRefProviderIssues` is placed in `src/config/validation-issues.ts` with path deduplication via `seenPaths`, preserving `src/config/validation.ts` line-count limits and passing oxlint and knip deadcode scans with 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- **Test Suite Results**:
  - `src/config/validation.policy.test.ts`: 22/22 passed.
  - `src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts`: 22/22 passed.
  - Knip production and full-tree unused-export scans passed with 0 entries.

<details>
<summary>Real-World Verification Proof Run (14 Scenarios)</summary>

```
=== Starting Real-World Proof for Issue #147435 ===

--- Scenario 1: Exact Incident Repro ---
  [PASS] Strictly rejected unconfigured store provider: Secret provider "store" is not configured.

prs.title: fix(secrets): mark audit header UNMEASURED when exec refs are skipped
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw secrets audit` without `--allow-exec` skips exec SecretRef resolvability checks but the human summary line is identical to a complete run (`unresolved=0`, exit 0). Only a trailing note distinguishes them. Operators read the first run as healthy: on 2026-08-26/27 this exact path kept a daily audit green for 19h with 22 unresolvable exec refs, surfacing only at restart as a crash-loop + 36min muted bots.

## Changes

Presentation-first per reviewer guidance (exit codes and JSON contract unchanged):

- `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:200-206`: when `report.resolution.skippedExecRefs > 0`, the audit header reads `Secrets audit: <status> (UNMEASURED — N exec resolvability check(s) skipped; re-run with --allow-exec for a complete audit)`. Complete runs render byte-identical to before. Trailing `Audit note:` at `:219-221` kept for compat.
- `docs/cli/secrets.md`: documents complete-audit gating (UNMEASURED = unmeasured, not healthy; re-run with `--allow-exec` before CI/restart gating).
- `src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts`: 2 new tests (UNMEASURED header with count + guidance; unchanged header when complete).

## Evidence

Real end-to-end run from this branch source (`bac648563f294b9d1ec281cc37bbfbfad62233a2`), isolated state (`OPENCLAW_HOME` temp dir, valid config with one exec SecretRef at `skills.entries.proof-skill.apiKey`):

Without `--allow-exec`:
```
Secrets audit: unresolved (UNMEASURED — 1 exec resolvability check(s) skipped; re-run with --allow-exec for a complete audit). plaintext=0, unresolved=1, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=0.
- [REF_UNRESOLVED] openclaw.json:skills.entries.proof-skill.apiKey Failed to resolve exec:default:proof/echo (...).
Audit note: skipped 1 exec SecretRef resolvability check(s). Re-run with --allow-exec to execute exec providers during audit.
```

With `--allow-exec` (complete run):
```
Secrets audit: unresolved. plaintext=0, unresolved=1, shadowed=0, storeResidue=0, legacy=0.
- [REF_UNRESOLVED] openclaw.json:skills.entries.proof-skill.apiKey Failed to resolve exec:default:proof/echo (...).
```

JSON contract (`--json`, no flag): `resolution: { refsChecked: 0, skippedExecRefs: 1, resolvabilityComplete: false }` — shape unchanged, only the header/Audit-note presentation differs. Complete runs render byte-identical to before.

Setup notes (reproducible): temp `OPENCLAW_HOME` with `openclaw.json` holding `{ source: "exec", provider: "default", id: "proof/echo" }` (canonical 3-key SecretRef; bare `{source,id}` without provider fails `config validate`, and an invalid config makes the audit skip everything and print a misleading `clean`). No real secrets involved — synthetic ref only.

Unit gates:
- `pnpm vitest run src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts`: 30/30 pass (28 existing + 2 new)
- `pnpm vitest run src/secrets/audit.test.ts`: 31/31 pass (unchanged)
- `git diff --check`: clean; unrelated `pnpm-lock.yaml` side-effect reverted
- Absent on main: `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts` on `main` has zero `UNMEASURED` hits; branch adds it at `:205-206`. Gap proof.

## Follow-ups (out of scope, noted for product decision)

- `audit --check` exit policy when `resolvabilityComplete: false` (currently exit 0 preserved)
- `doctor` surfacing the skipped-exec count (no resolvability block exists there today)

Refs #147341.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): keep committed writes succeeding when a post-commit observer fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users would see a failed write (and possible retry/duplicate side effects plus stale in-memory projections) when a post-commit observer threw, even though the SQLite COMMIT had already succeeded.

One throwing observer skipped all remaining observers and the error propagated as if the transaction itself had failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Isolates every post-commit `commit`/`publish` and every `rollback` in `src/infra/sqlite-post-commit.ts` with try/catch + `sqlite/post-commit` warn logging and continue. Success-path observer failures no longer fail the committed result; failure-path rollbacks log and preserve the original transaction error. This matches the existing cron `runPostPersistCronNotifications` contract and the file's own "non-throwing observers, never part of the durable transaction's result" rule. Adds `src/infra/sqlite-post-commit.test.ts` covering both cases plus rollback isolation.

## User Impact

Committed SQLite writes now report success even when one in-memory observer fails; all sibling observers still run, so caches/version captures stay aligned with durable rows. Observer failures remain visible as `sqlite/post-commit ... failed` warnings.

## Evidence

- New `src/infra/sqlite-post-commit.test.ts`: 3 passed (throwing publication runs siblings + returns commit; throwing staged commit runs remaining commits + publications; throwing rollback runs remaining rollbacks and preserves tx error).
- Existing suites: `src/infra/sqlite-transaction.test.ts` 26 passed; `src/cron/store.test.ts` 76 passed.
- Manual repro (`node --import tsx`, `:memory:` DB with two deferred publications, first throws): before → `ran: ["first"]`, threw `boom-first-publish` despite committed row; after → `ran: ["first","second"]`, no throw, warn logged.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json` OOM'd on this host (no type output); vitest transform + suites pass

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent stale snapshot flushes after invalidation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale chat history reappearing after cached snapshots are cleared during a gateway credential or profile switch.

## User Impact

Users with multiple tabs open who switch accounts or gateways will no longer see a cleared conversation snapshot come back on a subsequent read.

Per-session snapshot deletes are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A snapshot flush captures the store generation before its IndexedDB awaits. A cross-tab global invalidation can advance the generation while that flush is in flight, but the write path previously did not re-check it, allowing the stale transaction to commit.

The invalidation's own `deleteDatabase()` can then be blocked by the writer's open IndexedDB connection, leaving the stale snapshot available for a later read.

This change:

* re-checks the generation after the metadata read, aborting before any `put`;
* aborts an unsettled transaction when invalidation arrives during the commit tail;
* if the commit has already won, surgically removes only that flush's records inside a single readwrite transaction, matched by full write identity (`savedAt` + `sessionId` + snapshot content, so equal-timestamp replacements are distinguishable) instead of resetting the whole database;
* clears stale in-memory `savedAt` hints for suppressed flushes.

<details>
<summary>Race timeline</summary>

1. Tab B starts a snapshot flush under generation `G` and awaits IndexedDB.
2. Tab A publishes a global snapshot invalidation.
3. Tab B advances to generation `G + 1`.
4. The in-flight transaction commits the generation-`G` snapshot.
5. The invalidation's database deletion is blocked by Tab B's open connection.
6. A later read can resurrect the invalidated snapshot.

</details>

## Evidence

* `pnpm vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/session-snapshot-store.test.ts` — **26/26 passed**.
* New regression tests fail without the store fix and pass with it; the equal-timestamp same-key test specifically fails against the old `savedAt`-only comparison:
  * invalidation during `getAll()`;
  * invalidation after writes are queued but before commit settles (commit-won path forced, exercising the surgical-retraction fallback);
  * intervening same-key replacement committed before commit-tail cleanup;
  * equal-timestamp same-key replacement during commit-tail cleanup.
* Each regression test also verifies that unrelated pre-existing snapshots survive.
* `git diff --check` — passed.
* `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on both touched files — passed.

### Real-browser evidence (Chromium 152.0.7977.82, real IndexedDB)

Method: the production modules (`session-snapshot-store`, invalidation events, invalidation) bundled as-is and driven in two same-origin pages (shared IndexedDB + `storage` events, i.e. the real cross-tab channel). Interleavings forced via request-level hooks (`put` success → publish invalidation mid-flight; one run forces commit-won by making the live `abort()` throw). All data synthetic; peer-page reads used for final assertions.

```
[browserVersion] "152.0.7977.82"
[S1.flushResult] "flushed"
[S1.staleSuppressed] true
[S1.unrelatedSurvives] true
[S2.flushResult] "flushed"
[S2.replacementFlush] "replaced-flushed"
[S2.replacementSurvives] true
[S1c.flushResult] "flushed"
[S1c.replacementFlush] "replaced-flushed"
[S1c.replacementSurvives] true
[S3.flushResult] "flushed"
[S3.clearResult] "cleared"
[S3.afterClearSurvives] true
[S3.raceKeyAbsent] true
```

* **S1**: mid-flight invalidation → stale generation-G write never becomes visible; unrelated row survives (both read from the peer page).
* **S2**: commit-won + same-key replacement sharing the stale `savedAt` (`Date.now` pinned) → replacement survives; proves the retract compares full write identity inside one transaction.
* **S1c**: natural race + same-key replacement after publish → replacement survives.
* **S3**: concurrent `clearStoredChatSnapshots()` (publish + `deleteDatabase`) vs an in-flight flush → flush resolves cleanly, race key absent, post-clear writes/reads work (deletion completes via `versionchange` connection close; not permanently blocked).

Known boundary (not a defect in this change): a cross-tab `storage` event delivered only *after* the writer's commit has fully completed cannot be suppressed by any generation check — suppression requires the invalidation to be observed while the flush is in flight. Cross-tab delivery itself is covered by the existing `chat-flow.history-recovery` E2E (peer-page invalidation receipt).

## Verification Scope

Verification covers the focused snapshot-store test suite plus the real-browser probe above, rather than the full build/check/test lanes.

prs.title: fix: delivery queue update no longer resurrects terminalized rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a race where a delivery queue entry that was terminalized (dead-lettered or completed) concurrently could be silently resurrected back to `pending` by an update. The entry was read as pending, then a concurrent writer moved it to `failed`/`completed` between the read and the write, and the blind overwrite wrote the stale payload back over the terminal state. This re-enqueues already-settled deliveries for retry and can drop terminal outcomes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` (src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts) previously did a read-modify-write: it loaded the pending row, applied the transform, then issued a blind `upsert` with no `updatePendingOnly` guard. The `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` therefore rewrote every column unconditionally.

The fix marks the upsert `updatePendingOnly: true` and fails closed with the existing `ENOENT` contract when the row is no longer pending at write time, so the update only lands while the row is still `pending`. If a concurrent writer terminalized the row in between, the stale payload is never persisted. This matches the pattern already used by `reserveDeliveryQueueEntryAttemptInDatabase` and the platform-send transitions.

## Refresh against current main

Main moved delivery queue operations into a connection-bound kernel after this PR's original work; the fix was refreshed to apply at `updateDeliveryQueueEntryInDatabase` in `delivery-queue-sqlite.kernel.ts`, and the regression tests were refreshed to the kernel APIs. The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## User Impact

Operators no longer risk dead-lettered or acknowledged deliveries being revived as pending and retried after the terminal state was recorded. Delivery queue state transitions are atomic with respect to concurrent recovery and settlement.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts` covers:
  - `preserves an independently committed terminal outcome`: the row is dead-lettered in its own committed transaction before a stale update; the update throws `ENOENT`, the committed `failed` status survives, and pending reads return null.
  - `fails closed when a concurrent terminalize lands inside the update window`: the update callback dead-letters the row between the pending read and the write; the update throws `ENOENT` and never persists the stale payload.
  - `keeps a committed session delivery terminal across a real caller update`: enqueues a claimed session delivery, dead-letters it via the real settlement caller, then verifies the real recovery update caller throws `ENOENT` and the committed `failed` status survives.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite-atomicity.test.ts`: 3/3 pass.
- `delivery-queue-sqlite.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-sqlite-claim.test.ts` + `delivery-queue-terminal.test.ts`: 59/59 pass.
- `session-delivery-queue.storage.test.ts`: 12/12 pass.
- `delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` + `delivery-queue.producer-recovery.test.ts`: 48/48 pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on the changed files; `tsgo` reports no type errors for the changed files.

prs.title: fix(gateway): grant busy accounts reconnect grace on a validated typed disconnect
prs.body:
Fixes #146800

## What Problem This Solves

A health sample taken milliseconds after a typed Discord disconnect classified a busy account as `stuck` and restarted the whole provider, aborting the account's in-flight reply operations. The busy branch computed `busyAge` from the oldest active run's start age and returned `stuck` before the typed-disconnect branch could validate `lastDisconnect.at` and apply the 120-second reconnect grace, so a long-running but healthy run turned a transient socket blip into an immediate account-wide restart.

## User Impact

A busy channel sampled during a transient transport disconnect now rides out the transport's own reconnect window instead of being force-restarted: no aborted reply operations and no account-wide downtime for blips the client already schedules its own reconnect for. A disconnect that outlives the 120-second grace still reports `disconnected` and restarts. Stale run heartbeats still report `stuck`, and accounts without a validated disconnect keep the run-start-age proxy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run age is not a disconnect age. `activeRunStartedAt` measures how long a task has been running; only a validated `lastDisconnect.at` measures how long the transport has been down. While the run heartbeat stays fresh, the validated typed disconnect now owns the down clock: reconnect grace applies under `CHANNEL_RECONNECT_GRACE_MS` and `disconnected` is reported at the boundary. The lifecycle-validated disconnect extraction moved into a shared `resolveCurrentDisconnectAt` helper so the busy branch and the disconnect branch keep one owner for that invariant. Accounts without a validated disconnect are unchanged: run start age remains the only down-clock proxy there.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix policy red: with the issue's snapshot (busy, 4 active runs, run started 26 minutes ago, heartbeat 1 second old, `connected=false`, `lastDisconnect` 4ms old), `evaluateChannelHealth()` returned `stuck`; the new tests assert `reconnect-grace` (4ms) and `disconnected` (exactly 120s) and both failed before the fix, while the stale-heartbeat-stuck and patch-merged-disconnect guard tests passed throughout.
- Pre-fix monitor red (production change stashed): the new monitor test observed the monitor calling `stopChannel`/`startChannel` for the busy Discord account on a 4ms-old validated disconnect — the reported incident (`expected stopChannel not to be called, but called 1 times`); with the fix the monitor does not restart. The policy assertions ran through `evaluateChannelHealth()` and the monitor assertion through the real `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop.
- Real-transport proof inside the grace window (committed test `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts`, real clock, real TCP transport, no fake timers, no spy mocks on the monitor path): the production `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop drives a fixture manager whose transport is a real TCP socket to a loopback server. A 26-minute-old run keeps a fresh heartbeat while the real socket is destroyed mid-run; every monitor tick evaluates `reconnect-grace`, the transport really reconnects (`transport disconnected` → `transport connected` ~250ms later), and the run completes intact (`run 1 completed`). With the pre-fix policy checked out, the same harness fails: the monitor restarts the account, aborts the run, and the run never completes (`timed out waiting for run completion`).
- Real-transport proof of grace expiry (temporary harness, real clock, 124s run): after the real socket drop the loopback server stops accepting connections, so the fixture's real reconnect attempts fail with `ECONNREFUSED` 479 times across the window while the run heartbeat stays fresh. The monitor issues no restart until 120032ms after the disconnect, then stops the account (`monitor STOP (active run aborted)`), starts it again, and the account reconnects (`transport connected`) once the transport endpoint returns. A disconnect that outlives the 120s grace still restarts a busy account. Full transcript:
  ```
  [t=0ms] start (run 1)
  [t=16ms] transport connected
  [t=67ms] transport disconnected          <- real TCP drop; monitor evaluates reconnect-grace, no restart
  [t=321ms..119.8s] transport error (ECONNREFUSED) x479   <- fixture reconnect attempts fail; run heartbeat stays fresh
  [t=120133ms] monitor STOP (active run aborted)   <- 120s grace expired (first restart 120032ms after disconnect)
  [t=120133ms] start (run 2)
  [t=120335ms] transport connected         <- recovered after restart
  ```
- Post-fix: `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts` 58/58, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` 56/56, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts` 1/1, plus sibling consumers `src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts` 27/27, `src/infra/channels-status-issues.test.ts` 11/11, `src/plugin-sdk/status-helpers.test.ts` 25/25, `src/plugin-sdk/channel-lifecycle.queue.test.ts` 6/6 all green.
- `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` report only the pre-existing `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts(416)` TS2741 error on current `main` (unrelated to this change); the changed files introduce no new type errors. oxlint (type-aware, repo shard tsconfig) and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
