prs.title: fix: macOS native startup leaves interrupted identity import stuck
prs.body:
Related: #137085

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS native startup can stay stuck after an interrupted identity import when the canonical SQLite identity already exists.

## User Impact

Affected macOS upgrades can resume a fully verified interrupted native identity import, carry matching legacy device auth into the first native Gateway connect, and stop leaving a completed `.native-importing` claim behind.

Canonical startup remains available when legacy evidence is malformed, belongs to another device, conflicts across roots, changes during recovery, cannot be imported, or cannot be cleaned up. In those cases this PR leaves the remaining auth files and claims available for retry or Doctor.

This is intentionally narrow. It does not repair divergent multi-root identity/auth states; those need a separate preflight/operator recovery path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When SQLite already owns the canonical identity, native startup previously returned before inspecting legacy sources. That preserved ordinary downgrade-recreated `device.json` files, but it also skipped a pre-existing `device.json.native-importing` claim created by an earlier native import.

This change inspects only that pre-existing native claim in the canonical-SQLite path. A matching claim is eligible for recovery, but cleanup now has two read-only gates:

1. Before reconciliation, every cross-root auth source is bounded-read, parsed, normalized, matched to the canonical device ID, and checked for cross-root conflicts. The resulting path/bytes/file-snapshot set is retained as a receipt.
2. After the committed SQLite identity is re-read, the complete auth receipt is revalidated. Only an exact match may be imported; only a successful import may retire the claim.

If either gate fails, the verified auth cannot be imported, or claim cleanup fails, startup returns the existing canonical identity and preserves the remaining recovery artifacts. The fresh/noncanonical migration path keeps its prior strict failure-and-restore behavior.

Ordinary `device.json` files remain untouched for Doctor. The matching three-way state (`SQLite` + ordinary `device.json` + `.native-importing`) revalidates both identity files, preserves the ordinary source, and retires only the completed claim. If the source changes before cleanup, the claim is preserved.

Follow-up shape from the issue discussion:

- A separate "2+" PR should preflight native identity/auth consistency before opening the WebSocket so mismatched roots stop retrying as opaque handshake timeouts.
- The broader solution 3 should live with the existing operator recovery/state-machine work in #136149, because it needs an explicit product decision for choosing or repairing divergent identities.

## Retained-claim replay correction (current revision)

The Revision 6 P1 was reproduced before changing production code. After a verified cross-root import, an undeletable claim left its legacy auth available; each of the real role, gateway, and all-token clear APIs was followed by credential resurrection on subsequent identity loads. A real `URLSession` loopback connection also sent the retired token in its connect frame.

The correction records completion once per canonical `(device_id, profile)` in `device_auth_import_receipts`, in the same SQLite immediate transaction as the imported credentials. Empty verified snapshots are complete too. Clearing credentials does not delete completion; retrying claim cleanup therefore cannot replay the snapshot. Receipt failure rolls back token import. No cross-root auth means identity recovery does not consume or quarantine unrelated same-root auth.

This is a **proposed persistent-contract change awaiting explicit maintainer design acceptance**, not a claim of merge readiness. See the accompanying contributor comment for owner, alternatives, lifecycle, rollback, compatibility, and validation limits. The canonical SQL, Swift descriptor, generated Node types, lazy-additive contract and native-v0 bootstrap allowlist agree. Schema version remains 17 under the additive-table convention, but the schema itself changes.

Compatibility boundaries: old readers with the previous native-v0 table allowlist reject a database containing the new table. This does not reconstruct token clears that happened before any completion receipt existed, and does not claim to fix the separate same-root legacy-reader race. Do not delete receipts as a rollback while replayable legacy claims/auth remain.

Current-revision verification:

- Full `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --jobs 2`: exit 0; the main Swift Testing runner reported 1,736 tests in 135 suites.
- After formatting, focused identity, native transport, and native SQLite suites: 74 tests passed (53 identity, 7 native transport, 14 native SQLite).
- Node state database and schema-compatibility suites: 239 passed, 1 existing skip.
- SwiftFormat source scopes, SwiftLint all scopes, changed TypeScript formatting/lint, generated Kysely types, native v17 guard and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Independent final read-only review: no new actionable code blocker; the persistent-design acceptance and evidence boundaries remain open.
- Production dependency audit: 16 advisories, including 3 high, in the existing dependency tree; this revision does not change dependencies or the pre-existing local lockfile edits.

The new network proof uses production native connection code and a loopback fixture that captures outbound auth; it is not an installed-app upgrade run or a real Gateway credential-policy check. The installed-app proof below applies only to the older exact head. A current-head installed-upgrade/retirement run and maintainer storage-design acceptance remain explicit before-merge review items.

## Historical evidence (head `adf99e1`, before the replay correction)

- `swift test --filter DeviceIdentityStoreTests` passed after the final rebase: 49 tests. New coverage includes verified auth resume, wrong-device and malformed auth, conflicting auth across roots, auth mutation between preflight and cleanup, verified auth that cannot be imported, and repeated startup with an undeletable claim. Canonical-recovery failure cases verify identity availability plus preserved evidence; fresh migration remains strict.
- `swift test --filter GatewayNativeTransportDeviceAuthTests` passed: 6 tests, including a loopback `URLSessionWebSocketTask` proof that imported legacy auth is sent on the first native connect.
- Full `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit` passed before the final rebase: 1,745 tests across 137 suites, with 2 existing live-audio skips and no failures.
- `PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH" ./scripts/format-swift.sh all` passed: 0 files require formatting.
- `PATH="$PWD/.build/swift-tools:$PATH" ./scripts/lint-swift.sh all` passed after the final structural split: 0 SwiftLint violations across macOS, shared, iOS, watchOS, and extension sources.
- `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs` passed: native state schema version guard passed (v17).
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Two independent final read-only reviews reported no actionable findings.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>` was attempted on the earlier head. It passed the earlier gates and SwiftLint, then the broad macOS CI lane exited 143 in `test/scripts/mac-elevation-host.test.ts` while retaining a Vitest temporary resource claim. I do not see that failure touching the changed identity/auth files, so I kept the focused Swift evidence visible here instead of hiding the local gate gap.

### Historical installed macOS published-upgrade proof

Exact head `adf99e1ebc369d9b4831fb8e72c623c27955b0ff` was built as a real app and run in a disposable macOS 26.5.2 arm64 VM with the default profile, production root discovery, and no state/root overrides. This evidence has not been rerun for the receipt-adding revision; the schema-digest equality below is historical, not a claim about the current head.

- Official v2026.7.1 and v2026.8.2 apps generated the legacy and canonical state. A natural v2026.7.1 → v2026.8.2 upgrade produced one canonical identity, two auth rows, no claim, and SQLite integrity `ok`.
- From those unmodified published-generated identity/auth artifacts, the exact interruption boundary was deterministically reconstructed: canonical identity `1`, auth rows `0`, matching claim `1`, matching legacy auth `1`. This is disclosed as boundary reconstruction, not a randomly timed crash.
- Official v2026.9.4 launched from that snapshot but left it stuck at identity `1`, auth `0`, claim `1`, legacy auth `1`.
- The PR app launched from the same restorable snapshot and produced identity `1`, auth `2`, claim `0`, legacy auth `0`; the second launch retained the same result.
- Built-in status reported `local / connected` to a real v2026.7.1 Gateway, and Gateway logs recorded successful WebSocket RPCs.
- A fresh-state control created one canonical identity and one paired auth row, with no claims or legacy files, and connected successfully.
- `PRAGMA integrity_check` remained `ok`, and the SQLite schema digest was identical across the natural v2026.8.2 migration, reconstructed boundary, official v2026.9.4 control, and both PR launches. The source-level schema v17 guard also passed.

The proof build was debug/ad-hoc signed because no Developer ID identity was available; deep strict signature verification passed on the host and in the VM. The optional MLX TTS helper was omitted. No raw identities, credentials, tokens, keys, device IDs, IP addresses, endpoints, or databases are published. Full redacted methodology and result details are in the latest contributor comment.

No screenshots: this is a non-visual macOS identity/auth migration fix.

The native caller was overriding the existing 120-second wait default with a 45-second limit. This aligns that caller with the established web policy and classifies deadline errors separately from other failures without changing run ownership or delivery behavior.

- Confirmed on current `main` (`b778633e58f0`) that the iOS caller still passed 45 seconds and the target files had not changed since the issue review.

prs.title: fix(teams-meetings): accept newer Microsoft work meeting links
prs.body:
Closes #146824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes rejection of Microsoft's newer short work-meeting invitations by the Teams meetings plugin.

## User Impact

Users can supply the complete short work invitation to the existing native meeting workflow without recreating the meeting or converting it to a legacy link. Different opaque passcodes remain separate session identities.

**Actual meeting admission and live audio remain unverified.** Existing tenant, permission, ownership, and plugin-trust requirements still apply. Unrecognized browser launch routes deliberately fail closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Microsoft documents the newer work-link format in its [shorter meeting URL announcement (roadmap 381953)](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/publicsectorblog/march-2025---microsoft-365-us-public-sector-roadmap-newsletter/4394967).

This change adds the format to the existing parser and uses that same parser for browser identity checks. It preserves the opaque join query, compares meeting ID and passcode, and excludes unrelated tracking from identity. It does not reconstruct legacy links or interpret the token as the displayed meeting passcode.

Rejected URLs cannot fall back to an old meeting marker. Only the known same-origin application route remains eligible for existing owned-session retention. Legacy work and consumer formats remain covered. No trust/provenance bypass, new permissions, dependency changes, or configuration migration is included.

## Review Follow-up

The revision addresses the two actionable findings in [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146828#issuecomment-5651874677):

- Microsoft sign-in redirects retain `teams-login-required` guidance **after** the shared status guard denies ownership and cleans up the request-owned resources. Login pages do not gain join, microphone, camera, caption, audio, or leave authority. New tests cover short work, legacy work, and consumer invitations.
- The caption-rerender fixture now uses a consistent work origin and asserts that the caption observer is actually installed before detaching its control.

The revision also removes the added lint suppressions while preserving control-character rejection, and replaces potentially undefined split-array elements with definite strings in the negative URL fixtures. These address the two PR-caused CI failures in the suppression guard and test typing.

The earlier workflow-guard fixture error about missing `scripts/tsx.mjs` is not the failure reported by the revised CI run. The focused guard test passes on the local source base; neither that fixture nor CI configuration is changed in this PR. The remaining CI failures are classified below; this is not a claim that all CI is green.

## Evidence

- **245 Teams plugin tests passed across 17 files**, including the new login-diagnostic and denied-audio cases, existing parser/browser identity parity, session reuse/recovery, captions, and safe leave.
- **Two targeted tooling guard tests passed**: production suppression inventory and the previously failing workflow-routing guard. Other tooling tests were not selected for that focused run.
- Focused Teams test typing passed using the repository's inherited extension-test compiler settings and normal guarded compiler, with the include set limited to Teams tests plus the original declaration roots. **The broad all-extension local typecheck timed out and failed cleanup verification; it is not claimed as passing.** The retained ownership evidence was preserved and associated processes were verified stopped before recovery.
- Formatting passed. Guarded type-aware lint passed on the four revision files after correcting a test-only missing-braces style error.
- Repository autoreview of the substantive revision: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**. A subsequent change only added the required braces around an existing test assertion loop.
- Earlier SDK declaration generation, native runtime build, pack-only checks, and minified/packed parser assertions passed for the initial patch. **Those package-build results predate this revision and are not fresh package or live-deployment proof.**

**No live E2E or audio proof:** offline tests do not establish actual Teams redirects, admission, two-way speech, live captions, or completed departure. Full-repository and target-host installation qualification remain outstanding. Maintainer edits are enabled; no workflow files are changed.

## CI on the Revised Head

At **2026-09-13 09:10 UTC**, head `80fcf67331a709530490c06de5d69a308e2d018b` had **177 completed check runs: 129 successful, 44 skipped, 4 failed; none pending**. These counts include separate repository-automation runs on the same head, not 177 distinct tests.

- The original patch-caused failures are cleared: [test typing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939656) and [tooling guards](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939704) pass. [Production typing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939598) and [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939637) also pass.
- [The remaining test-shard failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103700939783) is `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.executable-invocation.test.ts:77`, **runs a verified plugin CLI script through its resolved interpreter**: `CLI produced no output for 1s and was terminated` (`cli_no_output_timeout`). Its shard reports 1 failed / 3,196 passed / 12 skipped tests. The failing fixture, its test helper, and the three CLI execution/error/timeout owners were verified byte-identical between this head and inspected upstream `0f23fae715b83f0ca9d7db09cef68f81d6ff1159`; none is changed by this seven-file Teams PR. This is an unrelated core CLI fixture timeout, not evidence of a Teams regression. The underlying runner timing cause was not reproduced or claimed fixed.
- [The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748563834/job/103701848409) is correctly red because the selected core-test shard failed; it is not an additional test defect.
- Earlier [auto-response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748503698/job/103700853196) and [label](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748503735/job/103700852905) jobs failed on GitHub API **HTTP 500** during repository automation, not contributor tests. A [later auto-response run on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34748768204) succeeded; the older failed runs remain in the observed check list.

**Overall CI remains red.** No unrelated code, test timeout, workflow, or suppression was changed to conceal these failures, and no workflow rerun was requested. Maintainer CI disposition and the trusted live-proof decision below remain outstanding.

## Release and Live-Proof Request

Please identify a supported way to obtain the requested real browser proof: an **official trusted preview artifact** containing this revision, or a **maintainer-run native Teams validation** with sanitized evidence. The locally packed archive cannot make privileged Gateway requests because it lacks trusted-official provenance. We will not weaken that check or tenant policies to manufacture live proof.

Please consider the qualified change for an official plugin release and identify its version and host/API compatibility requirements. A local development package is not an official release, and matching version numbers do not establish matching bytes or supported deployment.

prs.title: fix(secrets): secret inventory crashes on a prototype-named plugin provider id
prs.body:
Fixes: #147065

Fixes: `openclaw secrets audit`, `secrets apply`, and sandbox environment filtering crash when an installed plugin's manifest declares a prototype-named `setup.providers[].id`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin manifest declaring a provider id of `__proto__` or `constructor` made the next secret-env-var inventory throw `TypeError: object is not iterable` instead of completing, while the credentials that entry declared also stopped reaching the sandbox filter.

## User Impact

Declared provider credential names stay in the secret inventory, so sandbox environment filtering and `.env` auditing keep covering them, and the inventory no longer crashes on such a manifest. Ordinary manifests are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`setup.providers[].id` is plugin-controlled and is used as a key in two plain-object maps (`resolveManifestProviderAuthEnvVarCandidates` candidates and `resolveManifestRuntimeAuthFacts` evidence, plus the channel-env-vars candidates). On an ordinary object, `target["__proto__"] ??= []` resolves the inherited `Object.prototype` (truthy, so nothing is assigned) and `new Set(bucket)` then throws.

The maps are built locally and never escape, so they are now prototype-less. `__proto__` and `constructor` become ordinary own keys: no inherited member, no throw, and the declared names stay in the inventory. `prototype` was never an inherited member of an ordinary object, so its behavior is unchanged.

> An earlier revision of this PR rejected the id in `normalizeManifestSetupProviders` instead. That also discarded the entry's `envVars`/`authEvidence`, which removed the names from the inventory that sandbox filtering and `.env` auditing consume — a security regression ClawSweeper caught. This revision fixes the bucket rather than dropping the declaration. `isBlockedObjectKey` covers three keys, but only `__proto__` and `constructor` hit an inherited member, so rejecting the id would also have changed behavior for the working `prototype` id.

## Evidence

**Reproduction (pre-fix, Node 24.18 / SQLite 3.51.3, isolated remote checkout).** With an injected metadata snapshot declaring `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` providers:

```
Red  (unprotected buckets): 1 failed / 5 passed
  → expected [Function] to not throw an error but
    'TypeError: object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))' was thrown
Green (prototype-less buckets): 6 passed
```

The green assertions pin the security property the earlier revision broke: all three ids remain addressable and their declared names (`ACME_CREDENTIAL`, `CTOR_CREDENTIAL`, `PROTO_CREDENTIAL`) stay in `listKnownSecretEnvVarNames`.

**Suites.**

- `src/secrets` — 77 files, 849 passed.
- `src/agents/sandbox/sanitize-env-vars.test.ts` — 8 passed.
- `provider-env-vars.dynamic` + `channel-env-vars.dynamic` — 33 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on all four changed files.

**Installed-plugin CLI proof (2026-09-13, head ad7c011, Node 24.18).** Real `openclaw secrets audit` against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, with a plugin installed via `openclaw plugins install` whose manifest declares `setup.providers` ids `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` (env vars `ACME_PROTO_CREDENTIAL` / `ACME_CTOR_CREDENTIAL` / `ACME_PROTOTYPE_CREDENTIAL`) and a state `.env` holding `ACME_PROTO_CREDENTIAL`:

```
Red  (pre-fix, 3032d9b0e10): exit 2, audit aborts —
  {"ok": false, "error": {"type": "cli_error",
   "message": "object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))"}}
Green (this head): exit 0, audit completes —
  "status": "findings", plaintextCount=1,
  PLAINTEXT_FOUND  $env.ACME_PROTO_CREDENTIAL
  "Potential secret found in .env (ACME_PROTO_CREDENTIAL)."
```

The green run shows both required properties through the real CLI path: the audit no longer crashes on the installed plugin's prototype-named provider ids, and the `__proto__` provider's declared credential stays in the inventory that `.env` auditing (and sandbox filtering) consumes.

**Gap.** `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` cannot run in this environment (the checkout predates the `typescript-native` alias and the host has no registry access). The change only alters the constructor expression of three local `Record` bindings and adds comments, so no new type surface is introduced. CI covers the lane.

<details>
<summary>Call sites covered</summary>

All five `appendUniqueEnvVarCandidates` / `appendUniqueAuthEvidence` call sites write into exactly these three maps, and all three now have a null prototype. The two helpers are also documented to require a prototype-less `target`.
</details>

prs.title: fix(inworld): redact credentials reflected in TTS and voices error bodies
prs.body:
Fixes: #146804

Related: #141319 (earlier PR for the same fix, closed in queue management)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Inworld TTS and voices providers can echo a live Basic API credential into the thrown error message when a proxy or upstream reflects the request's `Authorization` header in its own error body.

## User Impact

User impact: credential material no longer appears in thrown Inworld TTS/voices errors, and therefore no longer reaches logs or transcripts. Status codes and surrounding diagnostic text are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readInworldErrorBodySnippet` already bounded the response read and truncated the diagnostic to 400 characters, but it returned the collapsed body verbatim, so any reflected credential survived into the thrown `Inworld TTS API error (...)` / voices message.

Inworld sends `Authorization: Basic <apiKey>`, and this is the same incomplete coverage the voice-call provider snippets had before they redacted. The change reuses the existing `redactSensitiveText` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime` with `{ mode: "tools" }` — the exact pattern `extensions/voice-call/src/providers/shared/response-body.ts` already uses — and applies it to the collapsed snippet before the length truncation. No new helper, no new plugin-SDK surface, and no behavior change beyond redaction.

Classification: behavior-completing (completes the redaction the shared provider error path already applies).

## Evidence

Before/after on the real extension test file (`extensions/inworld/tts.test.ts`), Node 24.18 with the repo's `run-vitest` wrapper:

- **Before (current main, `b667094a9ed...` tts.ts):** the new test fails at the expected assertion with the credential present in the message:
  ```
  AssertionError: expected 'Inworld TTS API error (502): proxy fa…' not to contain 'proof-prefix-inworld-loopback-secret-…'
  Received: "Inworld TTS API error (502): proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-prefix-inworld-loopback-secret-9876543210-proof-suffix; request rejected"
  ```
- **After:** `extensions/inworld/tts.test.ts` passes, 27/27. The sibling `edge: a small error body is preserved verbatim in the thrown message` case (401 `invalid api key`) stays green, confirming redaction does not clobber ordinary diagnostic text.
- **Extension suite:** `extensions/inworld/` passes 41/41 across all three test files.
- **Helper behavior confirmed directly:** `redactSensitiveText("proxy failure Authorization: Basic <secret>; request rejected", { mode: "tools" })` returns `proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-…ffix; request rejected` (`leaked: false`), so the fix targets the actual credential shape rather than relying on a generic pattern.
- **Boundaries/format:** `scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mts` reports no violations, and `oxfmt --check` is clean on both touched files.

Verification was run against a checkout whose `extensions/inworld/tts.ts` and `tts.test.ts` md5 match current `main` byte-for-byte. The `xai-oauth` timeout and `voice-call` compiled-subprocess build failure observed in the wider provider sweep are host-environment issues and are unrelated to this change.


### Real HTTP loopback proof (2026-09-13, head `8906063`)

ClawSweeper asked for proof through the real HTTP client rather than the mocked fetch guard. Harness: a local stub server plays a misbehaving proxy that reflects the request's `Authorization` header in its 502 body. The stub binds to a globally-routable address (`8.8.8.8/32`) temporarily assigned to `lo`, so the real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` policy evaluation (hostname allowlist derived from `baseUrl`) admits it and the request goes through the real undici HTTP client — no fetch mocking anywhere in the chain. Same red/green swap technique as #144172.

```
apiKey under test: proof-prefix-inworld-loopback-secret-9876543210-proof-suffix
```

**Before** (same checkout, `extensions/inworld/tts.ts` swapped to HEAD~1, i.e. current main):

```
TTS thrown error message:
  Inworld TTS API error (502): proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-prefix-inworld-loopback-secret-9876543210-proof-suffix; request rejected
TTS reflected credential in thrown error: LEAKED ❌
voices thrown error message:
  Inworld voices API error (502): proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-prefix-inworld-loopback-secret-9876543210-proof-suffix; request rejected
voices reflected credential in thrown error: LEAKED ❌
```

**After** (PR head `8906063`):

```
TTS thrown error message:
  Inworld TTS API error (502): proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-…ffix; request rejected
TTS reflected credential in thrown error: REDACTED ✅
voices thrown error message:
  Inworld voices API error (502): proxy failure Authorization: Basic proof-…ffix; request rejected
voices reflected credential in thrown error: REDACTED ✅
```

Both endpoints: live credential leaked on main, redacted at PR head, through the real guarded HTTP path.



### CI follow-up (2026-09-13, head `22cc319`)

The first revision's top-level `security-runtime` import pulled `src/logging/redact.js` into the cold capability-catalog descriptor import graph, tripping the import trap in `capability-catalog.contract.test.ts` (`checks-fast-contracts-plugins` shard). Fixed by lazy-loading the redactor inside `readInworldErrorBodySnippet`, matching the module's existing lazy imports of `ssrf-runtime`/`media-runtime`. Verified locally: `capability-catalog.contract.test.ts` 18/18, `extensions/inworld/` 41/41, and the real-HTTP loopback proof above re-run at the new head — both endpoints still REDACTED.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): report stuck-session force-clears as force-clears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` collapses two different recovery outcomes into one. A force-clear, which releases a lane without stopping any run, is reported with `status: "aborted"` and `action: "abort_embedded_run"`:

```ts
const action = aborted || forceCleared ? "abort_embedded_run" : "release_lane";
```

Issue #145152 documents the consequence: on the reported incident the recovery path fired about 67 times in a day and every one of those lines reported a success it had not achieved. An operator reading the diagnostics cannot tell a real reclaim from a no-op, which is what kept that incident invisible for over an hour.

ClawSweeper's review of that issue names this specific defect as source-proven and points at the evidence: an existing integration case expects `status=aborted` while `aborted` is `false`.

### Scope

This change fixes **one** of the five defects listed in #145152: the misreported outcome. The other four (queue accounting, ownership validation, the generation fence across awaited cleanup, and releasing the lane by session id) are deliberately left in the issue. It does not overlap with #145444, which addresses reply-owner recovery in `runs.ts`; the only file both touch is the shared integration test.

### Change

- `force_cleared` becomes a distinct outcome status next to `aborted`, so a release that stopped nothing no longer reads as a run that was aborted.
- The action follows the outcome: an abort reports `abort_embedded_run`, a force-clear reports its own action.
- A shared type guard covers the places that legitimately treat both reclaim outcomes alike, so existing accounting keeps working.

## Evidence

The existing integration case that pinned the wrong behaviour is updated rather than removed. It asserted `status=aborted` for a run that was not aborted; it now asserts the force-clear outcome. That is the correction of a pinned misreport, not a relaxed assertion, and the opposite direction is covered by a new case:

```
it("still reports an acknowledged abort as an abort")
```

so a genuine abort is still reported as an abort.

Measured on the branch head:

- `vitest run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-followup-recovery.integration.test.ts`: **2 files passed, 21 tests passed**
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: clean, exit 0


### Update after merging main (2026-10-03)

Main's #161759 added worker claim-recovery cases in `src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts` that also pinned the folded values (`status: "aborted"`, `action: "abort_embedded_run"`). Those cases keep the second turn blocked past the 15-second abort settle window, so `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` force-clears the lane (`forceCleared=true`). Their expectation now follows the split, like the integration case above. This is the same telemetry transition described under "Operator transition", not an additional behavior change.

Measured locally on `5971deb1308` (not a claim about the GitHub CI run):

- `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 file, 18 tests passed
- `pnpm deadcode:full` (knip): exit 0
- `oxlint --type-aware` on both files changed in that follow-up: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet`: OK

Refs #145152


## Runtime and telemetry proof (2026-09-14)

Plain Node/tsx before/after runs exercised the actual recovery owner, command
lanes, reply and embedded-run registries, recovery coordinator, diagnostic broker,
`diagnostics-otel` service and OTLP/protobuf exporter. The 15-second settlement
windows elapsed in wall-clock time. No Vitest, fake timers or mocked recovery,
registry, event or exporter functions were used.

Tested runtime: `3e06eab3abdd39c2c9f1ab1e51d8722b5e07e9f4`. Later commits merge main and adjust
operator documentation, type exports and test expectations; the outcome
classification block is unchanged. The before comparison uses the exact pre-PR recovery-owner
file from `ee6a7ef0cb5`, with remaining components held constant; it is not a boot
of the entire old release.

| Scenario | Actual flags: aborted / drained / forceCleared | Before status | After status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reply owner never acknowledges cancellation | false / false / true | aborted | force_cleared |
| Owner acknowledges cancellation and drains | true / true / false | aborted | aborted |
| Registered handle accepts abort but never ends within 15 seconds | true / false / true | aborted | force_cleared |

The actual coordinator emitted `session.recovery.completed` with matching
status/action and no stale-result flag in all six cases. Queued work drained and
all lane queues became empty. The timeout case uses a real registered run handle,
not a mocked `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` result.

Selected after-run terminal output (synthetic identities omitted):

```text
stuck recovery: reply owner settlement timed out ... settleMs=15000
stuck session recovery outcome: status=force_cleared action=force_clear_embedded_run ... aborted=false drained=false forceCleared=true released=1 queuedCount=1
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1 queuedCount=1
wait timeout: ... timeoutMs=15000
stuck session recovery outcome: status=force_cleared action=force_clear_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=false forceCleared=true released=1 queuedCount=1
PROOF_PASS before elapsedMs=30642
PROOF_PASS after elapsedMs=30713
```

### Actual event-to-exporter receipt

The task-owned loopback HTTP collector received `application/x-protobuf` from
the real plugin exporter. `protobufjs` decoded the received OTLP wire payload;
assertions checked the metric name, values and both label dimensions:

```text
metric: openclaw.session.recovery.completed
before: value=3 openclaw.status=aborted       openclaw.action=abort_embedded_run
after:  value=2 openclaw.status=force_cleared openclaw.action=force_clear_embedded_run
after:  value=1 openclaw.status=aborted       openclaw.action=abort_embedded_run
```

### Operator transition

`docs/logging.md` now documents the new event values and exported attributes.
Queries counting all run reclaims must include `force_cleared` alongside
`aborted`, or `force_clear_embedded_run` alongside `abort_embedded_run` for action
filters. Keep them separate when measuring acknowledged aborts. Queue accounting
is unchanged. The docs-only follow-up passed the repository formatter and
`git diff --check`.

### Exact limits

The backend work and loopback collector are synthetic. SDK specifiers resolve to
the real source facades. The eligibility request enters the actual coordinator
directly; this does not claim the full scheduled watchdog, an external provider,
or an installed Gateway run. No production Gateway/configuration/credentials or
channel was used. Force-clear proves release of recovery ownership, not that
remote work stopped. The standalone driver, raw logs, protobuf payloads and
decoded assertions are preserved together for reproduction.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): final replies disappear after unrelated reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp final replies can disappear when an unrelated configuration or plugin reload occurs during a turn because account settings copied into the turn configuration differ from the canonical Gateway configuration used by durable delivery.

## User Impact

Final replies continue to the selected WhatsApp account across unrelated reloads. Shared defaults and named-account response prefixes, chunking, streaming, and group settings remain effective.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor passes canonical Gateway configuration into the turn. WhatsApp's existing account owner resolves messaging settings through the optional `config.resolveMessagingConfig` adapter, and shared reply consumers use the complete selected settings. Filtered turn registries retain the admitting channel's configuration owner.

Shared group, chunk-mode, and outbound identity contracts use their type owners. Streaming directives call the core payload helper directly. This keeps the account-selected messaging path free of import cycles without changing its behavior.

Durable delivery still rejects relevant configuration changes, replaced channel registrations, and a closed Gateway. The shared single-account empty group-map contract remains intact.

## Evidence

Candidate head: `c4338573f45bf7156a4a9f7f6fbf1ea4a28e92d7`; base: `c6d71fae0ed1c0f7968c8d05c410345246af235b`; tracked source tree: `0665f7322f53b23689acf9c4335c916feaf9039b`.

Both commits have valid signatures. `git range-diff` reports both patches unchanged, and `git diff --check` passes. The rebase changes no authored behavior and requires no conflict resolution in the PR's changes.

Fresh validation could not start. The configured Crabbox `blacksmith-testbox` lease `tbx_01m4mgnms6jwdz9serhfsk7gax` remained queued for capacity and was cancelled. Native Testbox status confirms completion; its GitHub run association is unavailable. No passing result is claimed for this attempt. The planned checks were runtime and static import-cycle guards, the seven focused messaging/WhatsApp test files, core and extension types, and the Discord acknowledgement REST-client regression. No repository-wide build or deep test ran on the host.

The WhatsApp monitor regression exercises production admission, persistence, and durable final delivery with the external socket/session replaced. It covers default and named accounts across unrelated reloads and rejection after a relevant configuration change. prs.title: fix: activate context engines with distinct plugin and engine IDs
prs.body:
Related: #126972

## What Problem This Solves

Installing a context-engine plugin with a different plugin ID and engine ID can select the wrong identifier. The same ownership distinction must survive activation, update, Doctor and removal, including when plugin files are missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugins.slots.contextEngine` remains the **engine selector**. Optional manifest `contextEngineIds` resolves its eligible plugin owner before runtime imports. Existing install records retain `contextEngineIdsByPlugin` for lifecycle cleanup; no new dependency, table or sidecar store.

[Josh's September 16 contract acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146018#issuecomment-5705710381) covers the documented selector, manifest, persistence and recovery contract. This refresh implements its existing collision and explicit-selection guarantees; acceptance does not waive current-head CI/review or authorize merging.

October 7 refresh preserves the published contributor commits and merges current main `83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7`. Ownership integration is ported onto maintained loader/registrar owners; retired modules are not resurrected.

- Eligible declared and independently approved equal-ID legacy owners now cause an ambiguous selected engine to fail **before either runtime import**. Both discovery orders are covered.
- Actual install persistence uses the exact new candidate for kind/engine metadata and a complete manifest-owner snapshot from the post-migration install discovery for legacy migration. It cannot mistake another owner's explicit engine selection for the installed plugin's old equal-ID selection.
- Main's config-returning slot API and captured-generation/cache/custody behavior remain intact. Ownership discovery is install-time and uses existing keyed generation caches, not runtime polling. No dependency or assertion-ratchet bypass.

## User Impact

Distinct engine IDs work consistently through installation and lifecycle operations. An unset/default or old equal-ID selection can migrate to one declared engine; explicit custom selections and `none` remain unchanged. Multiple declared engines require an explicit choice.

Divergent owners still require independent trust and compliance with a nonempty allowlist. Global disablement, deny and explicit disablement win. Ineligible declarations cannot veto an approved legacy owner. Selecting `none` does not disable independently approved unrelated plugin capabilities.

Older hosts do not implement divergent-ID activation. Downgrade requires compatible config/install state and, when migrations prevent direct downgrade, a verified matching backup. Automatic failed-update rollback is not claimed.

## Evidence

### October 10 main refresh — current head

Current head: **34f893822c0e27d5dc64d7ed787ea2c58dae6cea**, rebased with merge history preserved onto main `06d231d65279a579b6cacbfb6a281e6fca1c5dbb`. The existing contributor commits and earlier integration resolutions remain intact; this is not a flattened linear history.

The refresh preserves the existing distinct-engine ownership contract, combines it with main's blocked-plugin Doctor diagnostics, and moves the prepared-owner adoption assertion into the maintained copied-view suite. Tests deliberately removed by main stay removed. No dependency, schema, public contract or unrelated production repair is added. Scope remains 81 files (+2,649/-146).

- Focused integration: **13 files / 171 tests passed**, four maintained Vitest shards, **33.91 s**. Includes Doctor, factory admission/fallback/logical-turn/selection/copied-view ownership, watchdog, consent, pre-import collisions, owner lifecycle, installer lifecycle/persistence and compensation. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <those focused files> --maxWorkers=2`.
- Changed-file formatting: **80 files passed**; `git diff --check` passed. Canonical config-documentation digest regenerated.
- Independent source/integration review accepted the resolved tree, including retained trust/allowlist policy, explicit selections, pre-import collision rejection and upstream owner APIs.
- Local verification reused existing package files without acquiring dependencies. Full typecheck is **not passing** with this older snapshot: it supplies Google SDK 2.24.0 versus main's 2.27.0 and lacks the pinned phone-package links. Full lint is **blocked before source analysis** by absent `eslint-plugin-solid`. These are local validation gaps, not a claimed passing or inherited-main gate.
- Full build and fresh built CLI/Gateway proof were **not repeated** for this rebase. October 7 runtime/build evidence below is historical. Fresh hosted CI and exact-head ClawSweeper review are **pending**; no new-head green or maintainer-ready claim. Human config-compatibility review remains required.

Before publication main advanced by eight paths; none intersect this PR's changed paths. The tested base above remains explicit. Rollback reference: previous published head `f45bd2a6ad6b7b7fc8eb2bf374ce95df2fe5529f`.


### October 7 validation — historical head

Candidate: **f45bd2a6ad6b7b7fc8eb2bf374ce95df2fe5529f**, base `83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7`.

Node 26.10.0, pnpm 12.5.1; base-frozen dependencies restored from cache with scripts disabled. No manifest/lock delta.

- Complete native changed-file check: PASS, including core types, all 27 selected test/caller graphs, type-aware lint/format, native guards/ratchets, generated docs, three dead-export scans and zero runtime cycles.
- All 32 changed Node tests, the three historical shutdown/chat-abort/Doctor regressions, and the other selected files from both freshly failing hosted leaves: **53 files / 1,302 tests**, 10 maintained shards in **517.76 s**, including E2E runtime preparation.
- Repaired fixtures alone: **5 watchdog + 9 install-compensation tests**, 24.14 s wrapper wall time. Vitest durations were 2.40 s / 5.62 s. CI originally spent 142.30 s / 142.82 s on their full hosted leaves, including the watchdog timeout; fixture assertions and timeout budgets are unchanged.
- Focused appearance/preferences real-Chromium E2E previously passed **8/8** using installed Chrome 154 and the supported browser executable override; mock Gateway. UI source is unchanged by this PR; this is the earlier local replay, not a fresh full UI validation.
- Exact committed full build: PASS in **194.6 s**, including UI and SDK/postbuild checks. Built `dist/index.js` SHA256: c9a65443c672008ff0c68db48f3a51220958c590472b252abafda28eb1100885.
- Build advisory retained: the non-fatal UI size report lists startup JS gzip 364.8 KiB against 364.7 KiB; builder exits 0. This is not claimed as a UI budget pass.
- Independent Astra source acceptance: PASS on the staged final merge; final committed behavior/publication acceptance: PASS for the exact committed source, checks, build/proof identities, evidence boundaries and scoped fast-forward publication.

Both owner bugs have specific red/green evidence: disabling only the pre-import admission guard makes both collision-order tests fail; the actual installer entry point changes `vendor-plugin` to `canonical-engine` before its repair, while sole-legacy and denied-owner counterfactuals pass. The repaired installer and retention suite pass 25/25 within the broader run. No assertions were removed to turn failures green.

Validation entrypoints:
```sh
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7 --staged --timed
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts
```
Exact selected regression files (changed tests, the three historical regressions and both failed hosted leaves):
```sh
python3 - <<'PY_TESTS'
import subprocess
base = "83a95401fb8a41278dba096add10406014aefee7"
paths = subprocess.check_output(["git", "diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD"]).decode().splitlines()
files = [path for path in paths if path.endswith(".test.ts")]
files += [
    "src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.shutdown.test.ts",
    "src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-errors.test.ts",
    "src/commands/doctor.runs-legacy-state-migrations-yes-mode-without.e2e.test.ts",
]
files += [
    "src/flows/bundled-health-checks.test.ts",
    "src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts",
    "src/tts/tts-streaming.resources.test.ts",
    "src/status/status-text.model.test.ts",
    "src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.test.ts",
    "src/tts/tts-request.preparation-resources.test.ts",
    "src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-frames.test.ts",
    "src/image-generation/runtime.resources.test.ts",
    "src/context-engine/runtime-settings.test.ts",
    "src/commands/doctor/shared/missing-configured-plugin-install.dependency-health.test.ts",
    "src/flows/search-setup.test.ts",
    "src/acp/control-plane/spawn.test.ts",
    "src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-publication.test.ts",
    "src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.reuse.integration.test.ts",
    "src/agents/tools/swarm-tools.integration.test.ts",
    "src/plugins/update.work-deadline.test.ts",
    "src/commands/doctor-memory-startup.test.ts",
    "test/openai-model-discovery-auth-order.test.ts"
]
files = list(dict.fromkeys(files))
subprocess.run(["node", "scripts/run-vitest.mjs", "run", "--maxWorkers=2", *files], check=True)
PY_TESTS
```

### October 7 built-Gateway ownership proof — historical

Passed **4/4** on clean `f45bd2a6ad6b7b7fc8eb2bf374ce95df2fe5529f`, using built `openclaw.mjs` Gateway processes and synthetic context-engine plugins:

- Declared owner `synthetic-distinct-owner` / engine `synthetic-engine`: real Gateway `agent` and `agent.wait` returned `PROOF_RESPONSE_declared-owner`. Import, registration, service, factory, `assemble` and `commitTurn` markers observed; the provider request contained the assembly marker. Legacy claimant did not import.
- Both independently approved declared/equal-ID owners: startup emitted `ambiguous approved owners: synthetic-distinct-owner, synthetic-engine`. **Neither module imported; zero provider requests.** HTTP readiness briefly preceded sidecar rejection, so readiness alone is not accepted as a successful startup.
- Denied equal-ID legacy claimant: declared owner still completed a real turn with its assembly marker; denied plugin did not import.
- Explicit `none`, noncolliding declared engine: both independently approved plugins imported and started their unrelated services; no agent turn was dispatched in this lane.

Reproduction inputs: fresh isolated state per lane, both fixture paths configured, explicit independent entries/allowlist for admitted owners, deny added only in the deny lane, and the selected engine or `none` as stated above. A local OpenAI Responses server returned deterministic text and recorded assembly markers in actual requests.

Earlier harness attempts at the first refreshed head were retained, not counted as passes. The initial fixture lacked the host's durable-turn contract and correctly degraded to legacy; the final stateless fixture uses current-turn fencing and an idempotent `commitTurn`. Collision failure also triggered the CLI's unrelated automatic-triage inference probe (`Reply with the single word OK. Do not use tools.`). **The final collision child alone used the existing `OPENCLAW_SHELL=exec` guard to suppress automatic failure triage**, keeping zero-model and zero-import assertions unchanged. It does not suppress plugin admission or change production source/config.

Post-run source and built hashes remained unchanged. All disposable states removed, owned Gateway processes gone, provider closed, and all proof ports independently bindable.

Boundary: exact built CLI/Gateway, fresh synthetic HOME/config/state, production loader and context-engine execution, real agent RPC against a loopback scripted OpenAI Responses provider. No production Gateway/config/state, external provider, plugin acquisition, or seeded install ledger. These lanes prove ownership/admission/assembly and unrelated services, not persistent-engine durability or a repeated updater/backup transaction.

### October 7 CI refresh and hosted reconciliation — historical

Current main includes direct upstream repairs for the three September30 failures: shutdown waits for actual model start (`22d7946296bf`), chat-abort holds marker publication rather than a child writer (`79f0e9bf1271`), and Doctor preloads compiled subprocesses outside its test deadline (`931c7b40b2e4`). The focused appearance/preferences real-Chromium suite passed 8/8 locally; the original provenance-poll timeout cause is **not established** by this replay.

The first October 7 refresh (`7e8ca294bc579ed4a5020a1e6f4b944c4ad0b34a`) ran fresh hosted CI on merge `c55ecc7d73c11d8776cb4c419f9707671abf9a45` into main `e73028f81cdadff4b7fe1cda28fce9eb4ab69adc`. Two candidate-owned fixture omissions failed: the watchdog's distinct engine owner lacked independent approval, so it exercised legacy fallback and blocked before advancing its fake clock; the installer-compensation mock lacked the required `plugins` metadata. Both reproduced locally before repair. The existing approval-config helper and complete typed metadata fixture repair them without weakening production policy, transaction assertions or timer limits.

Main moved afterward and conflicted only in generated config schema digests. The canonical generator resolves the combined schema, retaining both main's required worker policy and this PR's context-engine field. Contributor history is preserved by merge commits.

Final-head [CI run 37686021809](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37686021809) completed on merge `9a927e4a8a1ea88ea3ca7a376ce4e54e5ba05386` into main `c6698b1e9b2b4adc9e0c2b0ee10439fe9936b693`. All nine UI E2E shards and UI performance passed; no other leaf check failed. **Full hosted CI is not green:** [one Node leaf](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37686021809/job/113014607803) fails the inherited `subagent-control.test.ts` runtime-load late-registration case, and the aggregate gate fails consequently.

The unmodified exact CI base reproduces the identical helper-line186 assertion (start callback called once before the late descendant is held): **44 pass / 1 fail, 54.78 s**. The published head and exact CI merge each pass **45/45**, in 41.96 s / 43.35 s. Passing replays are not a fix. These comparisons use the full original-order suite, the same unchanged lockfile and existing local Node26 dependency snapshot; they are not fresh Linux installs. Reproduction command:
```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```
Independent source/history review verifies identical cancellation, registration, scheduler and admission owners across base/head/merge. The inherited helper activates a queued child before async registration without the production reservation hold; production reserves, holds, awaits registration, then activates. The helper's ungated runtime-load case remains after upstream switched to a static import. This establishes an inherited ordering-sensitive failure, not a contributor-only regression; the precise hosted interleaving and first-bad revision are not instrumented or claimed. No unrelated cancellation patch, weakened assertion, selective rerun or rerun-only commit was added. Upstream owner/maintainer disposition of this inherited red remains necessary.

Fresh hosted UI performance passed its differential limit: startup JS gzip 373314 B against 373454 B on Node24.19.0. This reconciles the hosted gate without relabeling the earlier non-fatal local absolute-budget advisory as a pass.

[ClawSweeper revision 18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146018#issuecomment-5646472200) reviewed exact final head `f45bd2a6ad6b7b7fc8eb2bf374ce95df2fe5529f`, reports no actionable contributor/security findings and sufficient runtime proof. **Human config-compatibility review remains required.** Local validation, hosted CI, durable review and maintainer acceptance are separate gates.

### Historical installed-package compatibility

[September16 published Lossless 1.0.0 compatibility proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146018#issuecomment-5705692110), tested head `17343ce69fbee21a081e183d6257ea16c6c1ba4b`, covers baseline conversation recall after package replacement/Doctor, metadata adoption, `none`, disablement, custom engine, deny, core-reserved collision, older-reader refusal and cold-backup recovery. It predates this refresh and is not exact-current-head proof. Its scripted-provider, Linux and recovery boundaries remain stated in that record.

<details>
<summary>Retained September14 updater, verified-backup recovery and earlier lifecycle evidence — historical, not current-head</summary>

### Published updater → candidate → verified-backup recovery

Passed September 14 in an offline disposable Linux/arm64 container. Published source `2026.9.3` (release commit `1391f7cd2d40ab5bbcf2f5f831d3a64f520e72d7`) invoked its real updater against packaged candidate `2db50b8f9db43b18b5776be232e1d5b48db413be`. This proof predates the evening main refresh. The original ownership patch is preserved; current-base build and regression validation are reported separately below. The full updater transaction was not rerun on the refreshed head. Candidate archive SHA256: `370ccb74df304c4a7651e55df570ab09330ad1b003bc5b4ba9e9f85b18030cda`.

The real npm-prefix source installation installed a synthetic equal-ID plugin through the CLI. A real Gateway agent turn invoked its `assemble()`. After a verified backup, the published CLI ran `openclaw update --yes --tag=<candidate.tgz> --json` successfully. The managed Gateway PID changed; RPC reported the exact candidate version/build; selector and plugin source hashes remained intact; another Gateway agent turn invoked the same engine. No update transaction residue remained.

Recovery stopped the Gateway, used `backup restore` on the verified pre-update archive, restored its assets to their original disposable paths, and reinstalled the matching old package offline. **The original SQLite owner record, selector, enabled entry and plugin source hashes matched exactly before Doctor or service repair. No plugin reinstall or seeded ledger masked restoration.** The restored Gateway reported the old release build and executed the engine again.

```text
publishedUpdaterExit: 0
backupVerified: true
restoreOwnerAndFilesExactBeforeRepair: true
pluginReinstalledAfterRestore: false
source 2026.9.3:   Gateway agent ok; engine assemble invoked; dependency graph verified
candidate 2026.9.4: Gateway agent ok; engine assemble invoked; dependency graph verified
restored 2026.9.3: Gateway agent ok; engine assemble invoked; dependency graph verified
```

Acquisition used 33 exact missing artifacts through Socket Firewall; all 356 frozen cache artifacts and their URL bindings were integrity-verified. The candidate's actual packaged npm graph was resolved offline and checked within that same acquisition set; source-checkout pnpm overrides were not falsely imposed on the published npm transaction. Direct bundled package manifests were separately matched to the verified archives.

Boundary: real Gateway processes managed by the canonical systemctl shim, with real Gateway agent requests to a local mock provider; no production service/state or networked provider. This proves **manual migration-safe verified-backup recovery**, not automatic failed-update rollback, native systemd behavior, divergent-ID support on the old host, or transcript persistence of a stateful engine. Earlier failed harness attempts were not counted as passes; the final complete rerun exited 0 with all assertions enabled.

### Full Doctor and real engine proof

Built head: `2db50b8f9db43b18b5776be232e1d5b48db413be`, version 2026.9.4. Full build passed September 14. The immediate subsequent head changed tests only; the evening head additionally incorporates upstream main. This is retained historical proof, not an exact-head Doctor transaction.

Fresh synthetic HOME/state/config; actual managed CLI installer; real SQLite. No seeded install ledger. Commands used the built checkout CLI:

```text
plugins install <synthetic-plugin> --force --accept-capabilities
# Add one stale plugin entry to disposable config.
doctor --fix --non-interactive
# Fresh production startup planner, loader, registry and engine assemble().

installExit: 0
doctorExit: 0
seededLedger: false
staleEntryRemaining: false
retainedSelector: synthetic-distinct-engine
ownerEnabled: true
retainedOwnership:
  synthetic-context-owner: [synthetic-distinct-engine]
importedDuringDoctor: false
importDuringPlanning: false
importedOnRuntime: true

```

This runs the **complete Doctor command**, not only its stale-config helper. Config was persisted/read back and retained ownership read from SQLite before the fresh runtime invocation. Doctor wrote its config backup.

Isolation boundary: network and writes outside task state denied; child executable allowlist limited to Node; external service-repair policy. Doctor could not enumerate launchd jobs (EPERM) and reported expected unconfigured-host diagnostics; this is not service-lifecycle, Gateway/provider-turn, or warning-free-host proof. No production state or runtime changed.

## Other retained evidence and limits

- At `a3d302e41be4fc5f04b82edf98c72d866edc56e7`, actual managed CLI install → cold planner/loader → real assemble → removal of original/installed plugin files → CLI uninstall passed. Uninstall removed selector and install record; disabled-entry tombstone remained. No ledger seeding. This older-head CLI proof is separate from the unit lifecycle fixture, which seeds a retained record before testing cleanup.
- At that same earlier head, the actual published 2026.8.2 image installed and ran an equal-ID engine. The candidate read its unchanged SQLite/config state and ran the engine, preserving a selected legacy owner outside an unrelated allowlist. This proves **installed-state compatibility only**, not an updater transaction.
- Missing linked-path uninstall is rejected by the existing CLI invalid-config guard; this PR does not bypass it.
- Original owner-trust and package-wide-uninstall findings were reproduced and repaired. Earlier hosted review of 2db50b8 confirmed the Doctor finding resolved and established no new blocking code defect; it required contract acceptance and upgrade/recovery proof; the latter is now supplied above.


</details>

## Reviewability and rollback

This remains one lifecycle ownership contract, not an unrelated installer feature stack. Review owner eligibility/pre-import admission first, then metadata/index/persistence adapters and retained-ownership cleanup. The October7 additions address the existing accepted behavior and current loader architecture; no public contract expansion.

81 changed paths, +2634/-157 against the pinned main. The retired CLI result wrapper/helper falls out of the delta; the maintained raw-config slot API is preserved. No changed package manifest/lock, unrelated feature/refactor, assertion suppression, or baseline ratchet change.

Independent source acceptance: PASS. Final independent Astra pre-publication acceptance: PASS for the exact committed source, checks, build/proof identities, evidence boundaries, cleanup and scoped fast-forward publication. Exact-head review is complete; the full hosted gate remains red solely from the reproduced inherited late-registration failure above. Maintainer config-compatibility review remains required.

Rollback: retain the previous source revision; installed-state downgrade uses a compatible host/config and verified matching backup as described above. Historical recovery does not establish automatic rollback.

AI-assisted: yes.

prs.title: fix(test): reject malformed PID receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The test helper accepted PID receipt text with a valid numeric prefix, such as `42stale` or `42\njunk`, because `parseInt` stopped at the first non-decimal character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete trimmed receipt as a positive safe decimal integer before returning it. Add regression coverage for trailing text, fractional, and hexadecimal inputs while preserving newline-terminated decimal receipts.

## User Impact

Test and CI cleanup helpers no longer treat truncated or contaminated PID receipts as real process identifiers.

## Evidence

- Current head: `54bc691dcb559cfdb020fd4992a87a9d0cef41ff`.
- Baseline source reproduction: current `main` at `a1ec6f7f4e1de7f2f27b52055096020f541b194f` still uses `Number.parseInt`, so a receipt such as `42stale` is accepted as PID 42.
- Claim-matched direct helper proof: a real temporary-file invocation of `waitForPidFile` accepted `4242` as PID 4242 and rejected `42stale` with `timeout waiting for pid (rejected)`.

  ```text
  {"validReceipt":"4242","acceptedPid":4242,"malformedReceipt":"42stale","malformedResult":"timeout waiting for pid (rejected)"}
  ```
- Regression coverage includes trailing text, newline-separated junk, fractional, and hexadecimal receipts while preserving newline-terminated decimal receipts. The newline case is stored as the escaped source literal `"42\njunk"`.
- Formatting: `oxfmt --check test/helpers/process-wait.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts` passed for both files in 953 ms.
- Current-head CI: run [36558054185](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36558054185) completed with all applicable checks passing, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. The successful `checks-node-changed` shard ran 2 tests in 97.61 seconds (4m18s job duration); its selected files did not include `test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts`, so this is not reported as the focused test result.
- Proof boundary: this proves complete PID receipt parsing in the shared test helper and the regression fixture only; it makes no production runtime or platform-specific claim.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #145309. Claude CLI transcripts could be looked up under the Gateway's configuration directory instead of the directory selected for the child process, breaking session continuity and imported history.

## User Impact

Custom Claude configuration directories retain native session continuity and imported history. Changing or unselecting the effective profile stops access to its old native transcripts while preserving canonical OpenClaw history. A profile change during response preparation now also prevents publication of a stale native-history result and asks the client to reload.

Existing bindings gain location metadata on subsequent turns. This PR adds no public configuration option or SQL schema migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final child environment and canonical cwd select the transcript root. Execution, settlement and recovery retain that location, and readers validate it against the currently effective root. Historical cwd locates an authorized transcript; current cwd determines authorization for relative or empty configuration roots. Paired-node bindings do not trigger Gateway-local native transcript discovery.

The latest correction retains the existing authorization check through the final response boundary for history, startup, retained-transcript and individual-message responses, plus embedded TUI and tool consumers. Canonical fallbacks remain independent of native authorization. Callbacks stay local and are not serialized into worker or response payloads.

## Evidence

Current head: `e24b56fe34f` (includes main `905a74d1bad`; a second merge picked up the regenerated workboard plugin manifest from #166786 that the bundled-asset CI check requires, with no conflicts). The first merge carries the branch over history page cursors, `sessionId`-scoped `chat.message.get`, the shared CLI binding clear helper and the embedded-gateway response owner that landed on main. Page and message readers keep main's shared scope helper and response preparation while still retaining the native-history authorization guard through publication; `chat.history` and `chat.message.get` pass the guard alongside the page cursor and requested session, and the embedded gateway checks it after `prepareChatHistoryResponsePage`. Missing-transcript preparation stays in the extracted `prepareCliSessionBinding`, while retry and failed-turn clearing use main's helper. The archive case main moved into the paging suite now passes the projects root it requires. To stay within the test line cap, the native-history authority cases moved unchanged to `chat-history-handler.cli-import.claude-config-dir.test.ts`, with shared fixtures in a `.test-support.ts` module. Production semantics are unchanged from the previously reviewed head.

Previous head: `ac69cbefb4d` (includes main `71b59f0b23df88e07b767b2e3d5cc298fb2af7d3`; the last commit is empty and only reruns hosted CI after a UI e2e shard timeout unrelated to these files). This merge carries the branch over the incognito session-history reader and the prepared message-get session read that landed on main: process-held and page readers accept both the incognito reader and the native-history authorization guard, native reads inside an incognito consume fall back to canonical history outside the consume when the profile changed, and `chat.message.get` checks the retained guard inside its prepared publication path. The doctor test case follows the process-environment contract main now uses. Production semantics are unchanged from the previously reviewed head; the earlier TUI note below is retained for history.

### Current worker and publication proof

Local Linux / Node 24.19.0 proof passed on `6d94a10bd6cd8b6944c14a898f5a97afbc910834`. The final follow-up only removes that duplicate test; production source is byte-identical. This is a direct **real `chat.history` handler → production session-transcript Worker → filesystem / SQLite** run with synthetic native JSONL and an isolated canonical database. No worker implementation or canonical-history result was mocked.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed profile | Real worker thread 5 imported the native message and retained canonical history; 13 host authorization requests, 1 native open and 1 native read. |
| Profile changed while waiting for the first worker→host authorization reply | Rejected before native I/O: 0 old-root probes, 0 opens, 0 reads. Canonical SQLite history returned successfully. |
| Profile unset at the same boundary | 0 old-root probes, 0 opens, 0 reads; canonical history returned successfully. |
| Profile revoked during asynchronous preparation after the native page was read | Final `chat.history` response rejected with retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; no native payload published. A subsequent canonical-history read succeeded. |

The observer delegates filesystem calls and records only the synthetic native root. A transparent Worker-constructor wrapper adds the observer to `execArgv` because the production lifecycle sanitizes its environment; the production entrypoint, messaging, authorization and I/O still execute. The queued cases hold the first actual host authorization roundtrip, then change/unset `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` before the host answers. The publication case holds `readChatStartupProjection` after the actual native read and revokes the profile before releasing that preparation.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized terminal output</summary>

```text
PROOF {"case":"allowed-real-worker-import","authorizations":13,"workerThreads":[5],"nativeIO":{"readdir":2,"access":2,"realpath":2,"stat":2,"open":1,"FileHandle.read":1},"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":true}
PROOF {"case":"changed-profile-before-worker-native-io","authorizations":1,"oldRootProbes":0,"oldRootOpens":0,"oldRootReads":0,"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":false}
PROOF {"case":"unset-profile-before-worker-native-io","authorizations":1,"oldRootProbes":0,"oldRootOpens":0,"oldRootReads":0,"canonicalVisible":true,"nativeVisible":false}
PROOF {"case":"profile-revoked-during-consumer-async-preparation","nativeIOBeforeRevocation":{"readdir":2,"access":2,"realpath":2,"stat":2,"open":1,"FileHandle.read":1},"responseAccepted":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"session changed while reading history; reload the conversation","details":{"method":"chat.history"},"retryable":true,"retryAfterMs":250},"canonicalSubsequentRead":true,"nativePublished":false}
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
Test execution: 11.111s; runner wall time: 44.60s; exit 0
```

The first instrumentation attempt correctly failed its positive I/O assertion because the observer did not reach the worker. After fixing observer propagation, the allowed case recorded actual opens/reads and all four scenarios passed. No product change was needed.

This establishes the current worker handshake, guarded reader and final handler publication boundary. It does not claim a new WebSocket, live-account, mid-chunk-revocation, incognito, native Windows/macOS, restart or updater run. The queued case is the pending authorization roundtrip, not a saturated worker backlog.
</details>

### Regression checks

- Current head (both merges), local Windows / Node 24.19.0, `--maxWorkers=1`: core and test type graphs, focused lint/format, max-lines, mock-export and conflict-marker checks passed. The two CLI-import files passed **22/22** (233.28s). The paging suite passed **3/3**. Across the other affected suites (embedded gateway stub, publication, Claude configuration history and snapshot, attempt execution, CLI runner, doctor, worker runtime and TUI), 9 cases failed on Windows only: eight worker-runtime selector cases expect POSIX `/tmp/...` paths, and the doctor "blocked workspace" case relies on `ENOTDIR`, which Windows reports as `ENOENT`. Both files' assertions and the doctor path classification match main; the worker-runtime case this PR adds passes. After the second merge, the bundled plugin asset check, type graphs and ratchets passed again and 7 overlapping and core files passed **161/161** (457.84s). Hosted Linux CI on this head is the authoritative run.
- Earlier head: the merged candidate passed **196 tests across five files** (CLI import, Claude configuration history, publication, embedded tool history and TUI), in 188.04s. After removing the duplicate TUI case, **all 127 TUI tests passed** again (40.08s including wrapper; 37.51s Vitest), leaving 195 distinct cases across those files. Both runs used `--maxWorkers=1`; hosted CI seconds are pending.
- Core types, the affected TUI test type graph, focused lint/format, line-cap, assertion-safety, mock-export and diff checks passed. Independent review found no actionable integration or proof findings.
- Previous head `7d9a1ff` has a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37187930902/job/111395019668). That result is historical; current-head upstream CI is pending.

Historical Gateway/official Claude Code allowed-root and changed/unset-root proof, plus accepted published-updater compatibility, remains available in [run 36616400271](https://github.com/Szqub/openclaw/actions/runs/36616400271), targeting `bd46b552`. The updater was not repeated: additive binding metadata is unchanged and revision 27 accepted the previous compatibility evidence.

## Maintainer decision still required

Please explicitly accept or narrow the current-root native-history access contract: changing/unselecting the effective Claude profile (or changing cwd for a relative root) makes retained native transcripts from the old root unavailable, while canonical OpenClaw history remains accessible. Passing tests do not constitute owner acceptance. This update requests review and the owner decision; it does not merge or bypass either gate.

Separate follow-ups include #155591 (native fork), relative auth-status probe cwd, manual-compaction cwd and moved-workspace discovery; they are not claimed fixed here.

prs.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): model discovery no longer hangs on repeated page tokens
prs.body:
No linked issue: found during a proactive source audit of provider discovery pagination.

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic Amazon Bedrock model discovery can loop indefinitely when `ListInferenceProfiles` returns a previously seen pagination token.

## Why This Change Was Made

The discovery owner tracks returned tokens and fails when one repeats, including multi-token cycles. The original nine-line production guard is preserved while resolving the current-main conflict. Tests cover strict failure, complete retry without a poisoned cache, and three advancing pages.

## User Impact

A cyclic response now reports a failed catalog refresh instead of hanging. Strict catalog acquisition remains all-or-nothing; successful pagination still collects every page. The public advisory failure behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Conflict repair based on main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `656559337ad7454e05a500206fe7ca783393f3fa`. Only two files changed: production +9 lines, tests +69 lines.
- Red-before on that main: both repeated-token and multi-token-cycle regressions fail; 33 other discovery tests, including the advancing-page control, pass.
- Green-after: `pnpm test:extension amazon-bedrock --maxWorkers=1` passed all 254 tests across 14 files in 44.9 seconds wall time (251 regular tests plus 3 temporary transport proofs). The added regression cases each took 3–4 ms. The temporary proof was removed after validation.
- Real AWS SDK transport proof used `BedrockClient` serialization, SigV4 signing, HTTP transport, and response deserialization against a controlled localhost peer. All requests carried AWS4 signatures with synthetic fixture credentials. No live AWS account or AWS endpoint was used. On current main, the repeated-token case made a third profile request and the three-token cycle made a fourth, reaching an HTTP-409 sentinel. The candidate stopped after two and three profile requests respectively with the expected pagination error.
- For both failing transport cases, the next call reacquired the complete foundation list and all three healthy profile pages; a subsequent successful call reused the cache. The independent advancing-page control also returned the complete four-model catalog on both revisions.
- Mutation control: deliberately retaining the rejected cache entry made both new recovery tests fail. The exact validated production source was restored afterward.
- Fresh isolated autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Formatting, conflict-marker checks, line-cap and max-lines ratchets, assertion-safety ratchet, timeout-race ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- On the exact candidate commit, `pnpm test extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 35/35 tests in 35.55 seconds wall time (32.73 seconds Vitest duration, dominated by transformation).
- Targeted type-aware lint passed: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` (3m32s including the first plugin-SDK declaration build).
- [Fresh-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37097599385) passed for `656559337ad7454e05a500206fe7ca783393f3fa`. The [Bedrock CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37097599385/job/111130806457) passed all 251 tests in 13 files: 33.96 seconds Vitest duration, 94 seconds job wall time. The new repeat, cycle, and advancing tests took 2 ms, 3 ms, and 2 ms respectively. Raw GitHub mergeability was clean after CI.
- Local validation was scoped as listed above; a separate full build, full-repository typecheck, and aggregate check were not run locally.

The earlier signed-transport proof on `c2f1c562000754490c9a22bd3017885aa92a1294` remains documented in the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145758#issuecomment-5644469536); the current-main proof above was rerun for this repair.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex was used for source review, implementation, and test authoring; all listed validation was run and inspected directly.
