prs.title: fix(buzz): replies from mid-thread messages preserve ancestry
prs.body:
Closes #145619

## What Problem This Solves

Buzz message-tool replies triggered by a mid-thread message can be rejected with `invalid: root tag does not match thread ancestry` when the tool call omits `threadId` and `replyTo`. The implicit reply names the triggering child, but the Buzz adapter does not supply the admitted thread root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Buzz now carries the admitted inbound root into the existing shared message-tool context and inherits it only when the outbound target resolves to the same canonical room UUID. The existing reply-transport hook remains the owner of implicit-root normalization. Explicit child replies and shared `topLevel`/null-thread opt-outs retain their behavior.

The October 3 refresh resolves the actual conflict against main `be8190f2f8c4f63eb2a3831a32dfd3e127573fe7`, preserving newer V2 Gateway and session-routing code. Main subsequently advanced without changing the Buzz channel or the relevant shared threading/dispatch modules. The patch remains two files: production +32, tests +70; no generic router, protocol encoder, or dependency changes.

## User Impact

Same-room message-tool sends from an existing Buzz thread retain valid ancestry and can be accepted by the relay. Sends to another room do not inherit the originating room's thread. Explicit nested replies remain nested, and callers can still send at the top level.

## Evidence

### Production dispatch and authenticated relay acceptance

[Reproducible proof and sanitized before/after wire traces](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/tree/034df5721f6e40f0591117feb3af1be5c944cb95/proof/pr145747) are pinned to candidate `9a0ccd6fb6025a9b8e3f0a1f554641889197e562` and the exact executed production-file SHA-256.

The proof exercises production `buildThreadingToolContext` → `runMessageAction` → Buzz outbound adapter → `sendBuzzTextOneShot` → NIP-42-authenticated, signed WebSocket publication. The dispatcher, adapter, tag builder, signer, and authentication path are not mocked. The isolated relay verifies signatures, authentication, membership, and stored-parent ancestry using the [real Buzz relay rule](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/8af2d91f37270365d5cd9170ac48349baa08475e/crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs#L922-L1007) and [NIP-10 marker semantics](https://github.com/block/buzz/blob/8af2d91f37270365d5cd9170ac48349baa08475e/crates/buzz-core/src/nip10.rs#L29-L81).

- Before: unmodified main emits the child-only reply tag; the relay returns `OK:false` with the exact reported ancestry rejection, which shared dispatch surfaces. Explicit child without a supplied thread fails for the same reason.
- After: all eight signed/authenticated sends receive `OK:true`. Controls cover implicit same-room inheritance, uppercase canonical room identity, different-room isolation, explicit child, explicit root, `topLevel`, null-thread opt-out, and a root-message trigger. The implicit scenario supplies neither `threadId` nor `replyTo`.
- Both variants used the same script, frozen dependencies, and Node 24.19.0/pnpm 12.5.1 environment. Only the production Buzz channel file changed. Wall time: baseline 22.14 s, candidate 22.59 s.

This is synthetic local relay transport proof with generated identities, not a hosted Buzz service or native-client recording. It closes the previously missing dispatch-to-accepted-publication boundary without transmitting real-account data.

### Regression and checks

- `pnpm test extensions/buzz/src/channel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: before-fix control fails the new regression (`expected Buzz threading adapter`, 1 failed/8 passed); candidate passes all 9. Candidate wall time 40.34 s, new regression 3 ms. Most wall time is existing compiled-worker/import preparation, not added test work.
- `pnpm test:extension buzz`: passes 34 files / 277 tests in 133.00 s, including authenticated socket and Gateway recovery tests.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The selected two-file diff was reviewed; integration confidence comes from the executed proof above.
- `git diff --check`: passes. `check:changed` passes formatting, dependency pins/patches, plugin boundaries, 6 doctor contract tests, and the initial repository guards. The whole-extension typecheck is terminated by the local environment with exit 137 after 115.35 s, so the aggregate is not reported as green.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/buzz/src/channel.test.ts extensions/buzz/src/channel.ts`: scoped type-aware lint passes (212.61 s, including SDK declaration preparation). `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/buzz/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: Buzz package-boundary production typecheck passes (2.06 s).
- [Exact-head normal CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37099518673), including production/test types, lint, extension package boundaries, dependency/security checks, and the selected Buzz suites. The [Buzz test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37099518673/job/111136322927) reports the new regression at 1 ms, its owner shard at 16.47 s, and the complete job at 127 s. The scoped CI plan skipped the full `build-artifacts` job; no local full-build or full-repository test pass is claimed.

prs.title: perf(state): share lease heartbeat workers during session creation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A burst of worktree-backed `sessions.create` requests starts a dedicated heartbeat worker for every lease, roughly doubling worker heap and delaying other sessions' writes.

## User Impact

Concurrent session creation uses substantially less memory and finishes faster, while unrelated session patches remain responsive. Lease expiry, live ownership checks, write settlement, and renewal during a blocked Gateway thread remain intact. No configuration, schema, storage, retention, permission, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one native heartbeat carrier and SQLite connection per physical state database and runtime source. Each lease retains its own port, expiry, current-owner checks, request completion, and cleanup. The final registration joins native worker exit; a failed native close retires the carrier. Shared occupancy prevents a slow sibling renewal from falsely timing out another lease.

Independent renewal is retained because #164521 fixed real lease loss during slow preparation and parent stalls. Production LOC grows by 293 (including the wrapper inventory entry) to separate per-lease custody from the shared native lifetime; this replaces per-lease Workers and native connections, rather than layering a second renewal path. Worktree loss fixtures now revoke and verify the exact lease instead of killing a worker that can serve siblings.

## Evidence

Same isolated Ubuntu rig (8 cores, Node 26.8.1), fresh synthetic state, three bursts of 20 worktree sessions, concurrent patches to an existing session. Baseline `09d58be4e65092a045a0228ad983513b9fc07d07` versus this change:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum workers | 37 | 16 |
| Maximum lease-heartbeat workers | 22 | 1 |
| Peak sampled worker heap | 1,561 MiB | 968 MiB |
| Worker heap growth during burst | +719 MiB | flat |
| Peak process RSS | 2,842 MiB | 1,970 MiB |
| Mean create latency | 18,978 ms | 4,043 ms |
| Three-burst elapsed time | 77.5 s | 18.4 s |
| Mean concurrent patch latency | 49.0 ms | 29.6 ms |
| Worst concurrent patch | 1,204 ms | 121 ms |

The peak-heap census attributes 712 MiB of the 719 MiB increase to extra heartbeat workers (~35.6 MiB each). History workers remain at five. Heartbeat retirement follows lease settlement, not an idle timer. Initial V8 committed heap varies between fresh processes; the after run begins at 981 MiB and stays flat through the burst. These are synthetic rig measurements; no production Gateway was touched. Patch sample counts differ because the after bursts finish sooner (1,111 before, 369 after).

Validation:

- Regression fails on the baseline: two simultaneous leases create two workers instead of one. Both close-order variants pass after the change, preserve the sibling lease, and join final native exit.
- Heartbeat startup, lifetime, diagnostics, real blocked-parent renewal, async lease, allocation, capacity, and acceleration checks passed, with the affected lease-loss recovery cases rerun after updating fixture settlement.
- Independent Codex reviews: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The conflict-resolution review is also clean; it preserves main’s removal of a redundant exit-event latch while retaining registration cleanup. Post-conflict lifecycle and real-heartbeat tests pass.
- `pnpm build` passed before and after. The same unrelated startup-JS size warning appears on both builds.
- New-module export guard: unchanged baseline collision `resolveChannelDmPolicy` in `src/channels/account-resolution.ts` and `src/channels/plugins/dm-access.ts`; reproduced on an unmodified baseline checkout. This diff adds no collision.
- Closure checks: 20 assertions passed. Focused final-head lint: zero warnings/errors. Final focused test rerun: 16 heartbeat and 6 diagnostics tests passed. `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times were 134.55 s and 87.91 s respectively on the shared rig, including worker compilation and test import; the existing heartbeat suite includes the >10 s blocked-parent contract. The new two-case sharing regression fails on baseline and passes on the change. Hosted CI exposed transport lint issues and a readonly transfer-list type mismatch; both are corrected. Final scoped core typechecking and lint pass without changing measured runtime behavior. The staged gate passed source, SQLite, formatting, docs, package boundaries, core types, all 27 test-type graphs, coercion, and deprecation checks. It stops on the unrelated `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` dead export in `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts`, reproduced on an unchanged `626eeac26d62c8ab45b09218b2216c27a9eea00d` checkout. Every remaining selected guard passed when run separately, including scripts lint, native schema, legacy-store, media, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing checks. Final scoped lint is clean.

Final publication: merged as `6125c6b44c23310ed8b2147fdf1fc9d927769995` after [CI run 38108861600](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38108861600) passed all 48 selected jobs on exact head `85a38d119e42019af15b4750d8cf7bafec9ece69`. Hosted typecheck jobs took 201–307 seconds; runtime regression proofs ran on the rig. Required CI and security gate was successful.

Remote routing: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4m11bxhdj7r70z6hg9xk503` had no runner after ~15 minutes; AWS `cbx_72837c1f8d08` provisioned but synchronization stalled before command execution; Hetzner allocation failed on IP capacity. Both allocated leases were stopped. Authorized rig fallback ran `pnpm build`, the synthetic Gateway burst, focused Vitest commands, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged`. All runtime state and artifacts were isolated to the task worktree.

prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). prs.body:
Closes #144812

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes widget cards moving away from their progress messages, or appearing twice, when a multi-step Control UI reply streams and finishes.

## User Impact

In ordinary Chat, `progress one → widget one → progress two → widget two` stays in that order through streaming, finalization, and history reload. No configuration or migration is required. This does not force every widget into its own bubble, and Dashboard's existing completed-work disclosure remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the outdated implementation with a rewrite against official main `6d3f75a1baa71ea5f51db7150ba1eb2d6f067be1`, following the current input-placement, run-boundary, coalescing, and grouping owners requested in the takeover review.

Widget projections inherit their tool's final placement bounds and predecessor. After coalescing, one display-turn-scoped pass reconciles tool-owned widgets with assistant display copies while preserving prose and richer preview metadata. Reused widget IDs in different runs remain distinct. Duplicate-text counts no longer mutate the input wrappers during regrouping.

Production changes stay in three Control UI projection files. Gateway payloads, plugins, approvals, widget HTML/CSS, canonical input order, hidden-row reply context, search behavior, and the global bubble-grouping policy are not replaced.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the pinned main using the real built Control UI and a deterministic mock Gateway: the second widget precedes its progress message during streaming, and finalization renders **four previews instead of two**. This fixture's ordinary history/reload stages already passed on main; they are compatibility coverage, not a claim that every reload is broken.
- The rewritten candidate passes **483 unit tests across 23 files** and **7 built-UI Chromium tests**. Coverage includes live → final → cold history → reload, forwarded/projected boundaries, reused IDs, hidden tools and reply attribution, accepted/pending inputs, retained streams, incremental caches, mixed shortcode/structured previews, MCP App rendering, and stable duplicate counts.
- An additional retained-live regression failed before run identity was included in the widget projection key; both tools-visible and tools-hidden cases now pass without changing input-placement policy.
- Independently inspected and manually replayed the built before/after pages, including final delivery and reload. These are synthetic transport/HTML fixtures, **not a live model or Gateway integration claim**.
- Independent canonical `autoreview` of the rewrite commit `5356490f791d47446a48aa8acfc4b43570255164` against the pinned main, with current owner source context, returned **scoped-clean at P0–P2**. The only follow-up in `90e9770bec4eeed1d39c670211c1006411affeb4` renames a shadowing callback parameter; that one-line diff was independently inspected. This is local review, not maintainer approval.
- The candidate also merges without conflicts with subsequently observed main `5861fe788ef5ed0acba609884d1dccfc7e0f31fd`; the changed projection files and principal placement/grouping owners are unchanged between these main snapshots.

### Before / after finalization

Fresh captures from the same deterministic conversation and built UI:

Before: widgets shift above their progress messages, and final display copies duplicate them.

![Before on current main: misplaced cards and four previews at finalization](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/738ea7fc-e962-4862-8918-970d08259b9e)

After: two widgets remain between their corresponding progress messages.

![After the current-main rewrite: two widgets remain interleaved with progress](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a9d4386-ba01-4393-898a-4d0c5c0eab29)

### Validation limits

The complete changed-file gate stops on a pre-existing stale entry in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt` for `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts`. Both files have identical blobs in the pinned main and the candidate. No unrelated baseline pruning is included.

The remaining checks were run separately: all nine selected core-test type graphs, UI typechecking, graph-boundary/i18n/coercion/dependency guards, formatting and changed-file stylelint passed. The dead-export scan reports `PUBLIC_SESSION_ENTRY_SCRIPT` and `isClaudeLikeLiveAgent` in two unchanged Gateway files; no Gateway exports or Knip configuration are changed by this PR. Those findings remain recorded, not suppressed. Full-monorepo runtime tests and live providers were not run; this is not an all-checks-green claim.

The first rewritten head's CI identified one `no-shadow` lint error in the new preview reconciliation helper. The follow-up renames only that callback parameter. The exact seven-file lint/format/style checks now pass, and the complete 483-unit / 7-browser selection was rerun successfully after the rename (9.80 s and 34.78 s wall time respectively). The earlier CI run remains failed; final-head CI is reported separately rather than inferred from it.

## User Impact

Agents can react to the current committed prompt, including queued and consumed steering inputs. Reactions remain agent-attributed and local to WebChat; existing external-channel reactions and send-only recovery tools retain their boundaries. No database schema or config migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presentation reuses the existing transcript and disclosure owners. Prompt reactions reuse the existing reaction store and events, with the authenticated prompt source kept separate from execution and dashboard-read authority. Retained tools revalidate the current run, source, session generation, and prompt binding at the write boundary.

prs.title: fix(auth): show the Claude CLI re-auth step when the login expires
prs.body:
Closes #135519

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Control UI users on a canonical `anthropic/*` model routed through `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` saw only a raw failure when the native Claude Code login had expired: `Error: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed`, with no re-authentication step. It appeared in the live chat bubble and again after reload, and retrying or starting a new session could not repair the login. Channel replies already answered the same failure with login recovery guidance (the `/login` hint and button, plus the re-auth command).

## Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle terminal event substituted recovery copy for the persisted run error only when the classified OAuth failure carried a `summary`. The claude-cli classifier returns a `provider` and `reason` but no `summary`, so the run error fell through to the raw provider string. That string is stored as the session row's `lastRunError` and written into the failed-run transcript marker, and the Control UI renders `lastRunError`. Channel replies were unaffected because they build their copy from the reply payload, not from `lastRunError`.

The fix falls through to the shared recovery text for any classified login expiry that has a `reason` (not only ones with a `summary`), and emits the structured `errorObservation` for it as well. The re-auth sentence is extracted into one helper (`buildOAuthRefreshFailureRecoveryText`); the channel reply's no-`/login` fallback and this path both use it, so the command text cannot drift. Provider-summary failures (e.g. OpenAI) keep their existing copy, and an expired CLI conversation session is still not treated as a login expiry.

## User Impact

When a `claude-cli` route's login expires, the Control UI now shows an actionable re-auth step instead of the raw provider error — `⚠️ Model login expired on the gateway for claude-cli. Re-auth with \`claude auth login && openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli\` in a terminal, then try again.` — in the live bubble, after reload, and in the transcript. The raw error stays in the Gateway logs.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI turn, before and after

Gateway built from this branch on Linux, a canonical `anthropic/claude-opus-5` model with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`, real Claude Code CLI `2.1.265` on `PATH`, and a subscription login whose OAuth token was expired (an isolated copy selected via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; no credential values involved). Turns sent from the Control UI chat.

The claude subprocess returns the reported failure (`is_error: true`, `result: "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed"`), and the Gateway records `cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli … reason=auth status=401`.

Persisted `lastRunError` (what the Control UI bubble renders) and the transcript marker, read back over `sessions.list` / `chat.history`:

Before (current `main`, `1a06c2f`):
```
lastRunError: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed
transcript:  This turn ended before a reply: Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed
```

After (this branch):
```
lastRunError: ⚠️ Model login expired on the gateway for claude-cli. Re-auth with `claude auth login && openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli` in a terminal, then try again.
transcript:  This turn ended before a reply: ⚠️ Model login expired on the gateway for claude-cli. Re-auth with `claude auth login && openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli` in a terminal, then try again.
```

**Before** (current `main`, `1a06c2f`) — the Control UI bubble shows the raw error:

![Control UI before: raw authentication error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ylcn91/openclaw/pr-135519-proof/135519-before.png)

**After** (this branch, fresh session on reload) — the bubble shows the actionable re-auth step, and the live error banner carries it with a **Details** expander:

![Control UI after: re-auth recovery text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ylcn91/openclaw/pr-135519-proof/135519-after.png)

One Control UI session showing both: the earlier turns (built from `main`) render the raw error; the turn on this branch renders the recovery text, and the live error bubble carries it with a **Details** expander (the structured `errorObservation`).

Note on the reported shape: on current `main` this classifies as `reason=auth status=410` in `2026.9.1-beta.1`, and as `reason=auth status=401` today; both shapes are covered.

### Regressions (red on `main`, green here)

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-lifecycle-terminal.test.ts`: a claude-cli `auth`/`401` and a `session_expired`/`410` login expiry publish the recovery text as `data.error` (the source of `lastRunError`) and set `errorObservation`. The existing OpenAI-summary and selected-profile cases are unchanged.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts`: the structured claude-cli `session_expired`/`410` shape classifies as a provider refresh failure, and an expired CLI conversation session stays out of the login recovery path.

### Checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` on the changed test files plus `agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`: all passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: lint (oxlint) clean, typecheck clean, and the changed-file test lanes pass locally; the draft PR also runs the full CI gate.



## Rebase onto main (`e8684576989`)

- Main removed `readStructuredClaudeCliAuthFailure` and moved the check into `classifyStructuredClaudeCliOAuthFailureReason` (expiry wording now checked in the same function). The PR's change is re-expressed there: the structured claude-cli shape is accepted as `auth`/`401` **or** `session_expired`/`410`; the expiry-wording requirement is unchanged, so an expired CLI conversation session still does not become a re-auth hint.
- `oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts` moved to `it.each` tables on main; the two PR cases are now rows in the existing `classifies $name` table.
- `agent-lifecycle-terminal.ts` keeps main's new `renderAgentHarnessPreflightUserMessage` precedence; the recovery fallback sits after it.
- Two commits squashed into one. The proof above was captured on the previous base; CI on this head is the gate for the re-run.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

- Real coexisting npm installations now have paired native proof at the unchanged PR head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. In [37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616), the candidate preserved an external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset. The single native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The parent baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9` failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected any other failure. Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations, verified against the same published SHA-512 integrity, on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup and preference/environment restoration completed, and both product checkouts remained pristine. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain the selection cells, installation identities, test logs, and strict verification summaries. This is real installed-CLI behavior proof, not a full signed-app update or permission-prompt test.
- The regression tests call the real CLIInstaller discovery, managed-inspection, update, and CommandResolver paths with temporary executable fixtures. They cover preserving an external selection through inspection, leaving an empty selection empty, selecting managed only after a verified update, and retaining the external selection when update verification fails. Fixtures are synthetic; they are not real-installation behavior proof.
- Exact-head [CI run 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816) passed at `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. The hosted `macos-swift (tests)` job compiled this test file and passed. Its main Swift test run reported 2,498 tests in 283 suites in 244.920 seconds; the full test job took 775 seconds including setup and build. CI did not report an isolated runtime for this file.

prs.title: fix(mac): preserve companion exec timeouts
prs.body:
Closes #139706

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running long commands through the macOS companion would hit an unexplained failure after about 20 seconds, even when the requested command timeout was much longer. The Gateway reported the companion as unavailable and could not return the command's real result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The companion request already carries the caller's command timeout, so the socket response deadline now follows it with a 5-second grace period. The transport also distinguishes pre-send unavailability, post-send response loss, and response timeout; submitted commands remain fail-closed and are never replayed locally. A zero command timeout disables the transport deadline as well.

## User Impact

Long-running macOS companion commands can now wait for their requested lifetime and return their actual result. A late response is reported as `TIMEOUT`, while a lost response is reported as an unknown outcome instead of being mislabeled as an unreachable companion. Safe fallback remains available only when the request was never submitted.

## Evidence

- Before fix, base `9e5bb4a3ecd`: the real UDS regression suite passed while its `timeout` case observed `null` after a signed request had started a child; the direct probe returned: `{"result":null}`
- After fix, commit `eb8b824922a`: the same 50 ms transport probe with a 30 s command timeout returned: `{"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"TIMEOUT","reason":"timeout","message":"TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown"}}}`
- Response-loss probe changed from `{"result":null}` before the fix to typed `UNKNOWN / response-lost` after the fix.
- Real UDS transport tests: **21 passed**, including child-started timeout, response-loss, malformed-response, zero-timeout, signing, and cancellation cases.
- Node-host system-run tests: **87 passed**; enforced response-loss path confirms `runCommand` was not called (no local replay).
- `pnpm test:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm check`: passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- Autoreview: `scoped-clean`, no accepted/actionable P0/P1 findings.
- No screenshot is applicable; this is a transport/runtime behavior change with no UI surface.

## Rebase onto `main` (`e8684576989`)

Main still uses a fixed 20 s socket deadline (`exec-host.ts`, `params.timeoutMs ?? 20_000`) and maps every transport failure to `COMPANION_APP_UNAVAILABLE`. Conflicts were re-expressed on main's current node-host code:

- `src/node-host/invoke.ts`: main removed `runViaMacAppExecHost` and moved the macOS app dispatch into `invoke-system-run.ts`. Main's version is kept; the response deadline is now derived inside `requestExecHostViaSocket` from `request.timeoutMs` (+5 s grace, `0` disables it), so no call-site timeout is needed. The previously exported `resolveExecHostResponseTimeoutMs` is inlined (it would otherwise be a test-only export); `exec-host.test.ts` covers the same three cases through the real call.
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts`: `sendSystemRunDenied` now takes `(opts, execution, message, reason)`; `timeout` → `TIMEOUT` and `response-lost` → `UNKNOWN` are mapped there.
- `invoke-system-run.test.ts` / `invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`: the two new cases are rewritten on main's `runMac` / `invokeResult` / `expectExecDeniedEvent` helpers; the socket test asserts the exact `UNKNOWN` result and the `response-lost` denial reason.
- `src/infra/exec-host.native.test-support.ts`: the macOS native transport proof expected `null` after a dropped response; it now expects the typed `UNKNOWN` / `response-lost` result.

The numbers above are from the previous base; CI on this head is the gate for the re-run. The native proof runs on macOS only.

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(codex): show unknown context usage instead of stale counts after native compaction
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #66263

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running native Codex sessions see misleading context usage after Codex app-server compaction. When the app-server completes compaction without reporting a reliable post-compaction token count, OpenClaw can fall back to stale transcript-derived usage and display the pre-compaction count as current context usage — making compaction look ineffective or reporting confusing context percentages in session status and /status output.

- **Related:** #66251 (parent tracker); cumulative projection tracked separately in #64669; #65503 (observed context inflation).

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the post-compaction usage boundary at the native compaction completion point (the shared manual/automatic compaction activity marker) using the existing normalized usage representation. If the app-server reports a count via `thread/tokenUsage/updated` during the compaction turn/item, the marker carries an `available` contextUsage snapshot that replaces the transcript-derived count. If no count is reported, the marker carries an explicit `unavailable` contextUsage so transcript fallback clears the stale pre-compaction total instead of presenting it as fresh.

Codex recomputes usage when the compaction item completes: the pinned app-server (0.153.4) zeroes the input/output split (`inputTokens: 0`, `outputTokens: 0`) and reports the estimated compacted context size in `totalTokens`. The boundary normalization therefore treats a zero prompt count as an artifact of that recompute and records the recomputed active-context total as the prompt side of the `available` boundary. Keeping zero verbatim would make transcript readers reject the boundary (they require a positive prompt count) and leave the stale pre-compaction total marked fresh after compaction.

- **Intended outcome:** after native compaction, Gateway session rows and transcript-derived usage either show the app-server's post-compaction count or an explicit unknown state — never the pre-compaction count.
- **Out of scope:** cumulative app-server token projection (#64669), UI layout, context-engine compaction paths.
- **Highest-risk area:** automatic compaction projection (event projector) must not attribute a pre-compaction token-usage event to the post-compaction boundary; the manual-compaction watcher must not keep parallel accounting state that can drift.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** only `thread/tokenUsage/updated` events observed while a contextCompaction item is active are treated as the post-compaction recompute; every compaction marker without such an event is written as explicit `unavailable`; the last reliable recompute snapshot wins and drives both the boundary and the outward `tokensAfter` result from one source of truth.

## User Impact

Session status and /status after native Codex compaction no longer show stale pre-compaction context usage as fresh: either the reported post-compaction count is shown, or usage is displayed as unknown until the next valid snapshot. Long-running Codex sessions give reliable signals about whether compaction succeeded and whether the session is safe to continue.

## Evidence

### Real native compaction proof (new in this revision)

A new committed, non-live native regression test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.native.test.ts`) boots the **real pinned @openai/codex 0.153.4 binary** with an isolated `CODEX_HOME` and a loopback model provider, then drives the **production manual-compaction path** (`maybeCompactCodexAppServerSession` in `compact.ts`) through a real `thread/compact/start`. The app-server performs a real native compaction; the changed watcher consumes the real notification stream and records the boundary.

Observed real run (terminal excerpt):

```text
app-server version: 0.153.4
notification item/started contextCompaction "01a07340-..."
compaction-window thread/tokenUsage/updated {"totalTokens":1010,"inputTokens":1000,...,"outputTokens":10,...}   # pre-compaction snapshot
compaction-window thread/tokenUsage/updated {"totalTokens":5049,"inputTokens":0,...,"outputTokens":0,...}       # codex recompute payload
notification item/completed contextCompaction "01a07340-..."
compact result ok/compacted/tokensAfter: {"ok":true,"compacted":true,"result":{...,"tokensAfter":5049,...}}
persistCodexContextCompactionActivity calls: [{"threadId":"01a07340-...","turnId":"01a07340-...","itemId":"01a07340-...","usageAfter":{"state":"available","promptTokens":5049,"totalTokens":5049}}]
zero-input recompute observed on real stream: {"totalTokens":5049,"inputTokens":0,"outputTokens":0}
expected boundary from real window: {"state":"available","promptTokens":5049,"totalTokens":5049}
```

Hard assertions in the test (all pass): the real stream contains codex's zero-input recompute payload (`inputTokens: 0`, `outputTokens: 0`, positive `totalTokens`); the recorded boundary is `available` with positive `promptTokens`/`totalTokens` (never a zero prompt count); the outward `tokensAfter` equals the persisted boundary total; and the recorded boundary equals `resolveCodexCompactionContextUsageAfter` over the last reliable compaction-window snapshot.

This is **real native execution with synthetic provider responses** (isolated homes + deterministic loopback provider), not an OAuth or external-model-service claim — the same standard as the repo's other non-live real-binary native tests (`thread-lifecycle.native.test.ts`, `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts`; see merged #139228).

- **Real environment tested:** real `codex app-server` 0.153.4 process (pinned `@openai/codex`), isolated `CODEX_HOME`, real thread with seeded context, real `thread/compact/start` native compaction, production watcher/persist code path; model responses served by a loopback provider (`requires_openai_auth=false`, no credentials used).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # New real-native regression proof (real app-server compaction, 1 test)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.native.test.ts
  # Existing deterministic behavior tests (aggregate boundary + marker + producers)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-compaction-activity.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.native.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.usage.test.ts
  # Type checks
  pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  compact.native.test.ts                1 passed (REAL app-server native compaction)
    - real zero-input recompute payload observed on the real notification stream
    - recorded boundary: available {promptTokens:5049, totalTokens:5049}; tokensAfter:5049
    - recorded boundary == resolve(last real window snapshot); never a zero prompt count
  session-transcript-derived-readers.test.ts  5 passed (compaction boundary x5)
  context-compaction-activity.test.ts         4 passed (usageAfter available/unavailable/omitted)
  compact.test.ts + event-projector.usage.test.ts  85 passed
    - 2 new cases: available/unavailable usage boundary after manual compaction
    - 2 new cases: available/unavailable usage boundary after automatic compaction
    - 2 NEW cases: zero-input recompute payload (inputTokens:0, outputTokens:0,
      totalTokens:>0) through BOTH producers records the recomputed context
      total as the boundary prompt side
  session-transcript-derived-readers.test.ts  1 NEW case: recompute boundary
    replaces the stale pre-compaction total instead of leaving it fresh
  validate.sh (changed files): oxfmt + oxlint + tests + tsgo:core 全部通过
  tsgo:core / tsgo:extensions:test: exit 0
  ```
  Key behavioral assertions covered:
  - `aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage compaction boundary > keeps a native compaction marker without a count from resurrecting pre-compaction usage` — marker with `contextUsage: {state:"unavailable"}` clears `totalTokens`/`totalTokensFresh` while billing (`inputTokens`/`outputTokens`) survives.
  - `... > records an available post-compaction count supplied by the app-server` — marker with an available snapshot sets `totalTokens`/fresh.
  - `... > replaces the pre-compaction total with the recomputed context total recorded at the compaction boundary` — an earlier 50,000-token count is replaced by the recomputed 1,000-token boundary, not left fresh.
  - `... > lets a genuinely later valid snapshot restore usage after an unavailable boundary`.
  - `compact.test.ts > records an available/unavailable usage boundary when the app-server reports [no] post-compaction count` — persisted activity marker receives `usageAfter` derived from the compaction-turn `thread/tokenUsage/updated` event or `{state:"unavailable"}` when absent.
  - `compact.test.ts > records the recomputed context total when the app-server reports a zero-input recompute` — the exact Codex recompute payload (`last: {inputTokens:0, outputTokens:0, totalTokens:1_000}`) is persisted as `{state:"available", promptTokens:1_000, totalTokens:1_000}`. Pre-fix this assertion fails (the marker carried `promptTokens:0`, which transcript readers reject, leaving the stale pre-compaction total fresh); post-fix it passes.
  - `event-projector.usage.test.ts > records the recomputed context total after automatic compaction reports a zero-input recompute` — same payload through the automatic-compaction projection path (RED pre-fix / GREEN post-fix).
  - `compact.native.test.ts` (real binary) — the same normalization is now asserted against the real app-server's own recompute payload.
- **Observed result after fix:** `validate.sh` on all changed files green (oxfmt + oxlint + tests + tsgo:core); `tsgo:extensions:test` exit 0; the real-native test passes against the pinned app-server binary; the two zero-input recompute producer tests were run RED against the pre-fix helper (observed `promptTokens: 0` in the persisted boundary) and pass GREEN after the fix.
- **Before evidence:** prior to this change the compaction activity marker carried no usage field, so `aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` retained the last pre-compaction assistant total through the marker and Gateway session rows presented it as fresh (`totalTokensFresh: true`) after compaction without a reported count. The first review revision additionally accepted Codex's recompute `promptTokens: 0` verbatim, so the boundary did not replace the stale total either. On a real app-server the recompute payload is exactly the zero-input shape this revision normalizes (observed in the native run above: `inputTokens:0, outputTokens:0, totalTokens:5049`).
- **What was not tested:** an external live model service / OAuth-backed Codex session (no credentials in this environment); the model provider is a loopback OpenAI-compatible stub. Gateway transcript-aggregation semantics over the recorded marker are deterministic and covered by the included derived-reader cases, which consume the exact marker shape the real run produces (`custom` `openclaw.context-compaction` message with `usage.contextUsage: {state:"available", promptTokens, totalTokens}`).
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real app-server binary + real native compaction + production producer code path; model responses synthetic via loopback provider, per repo native-test convention). Deterministic unit/integration coverage retained for aggregation semantics.
- **Proof limitations:** no live external-model session; the real native run proves producer-side behavior (recording the recomputed boundary) on the actual app-server, and the reader cases prove the aggregation consequence for that exact boundary.
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + review (this revision adds the real native compaction proof requested in the last ClawSweeper review cycle; live-session proof against an external model service is out of reach in this environment and is left to CI/maintainer review).

prs.title: fix(cli): reject non-decimal gateway suspend --wait strings
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

`openclaw gateway suspend --wait` used JavaScript `Number()` coercion, so radix-prefixed strings were silently interpreted as seconds: `0x10` as 16, `0b101` as 5, and `0o17` as 15. The CLI now uses the shared strict finite-number parser and rejects those strings before any Gateway request.

`--wait` bounds local polling while the Gateway is busy. It is not sent as `waitMs`, does not set the suspension lease duration, and does not change the `gateway.suspend.prepare` protocol; that request still carries only `requestId`.

## User impact

Decimal, fractional, and scientific-notation values retain their existing behavior. Scripts that intentionally supplied radix strings must use decimal replacements:

- `0x10` -> `16`
- `0b101` -> `5`
- `0o17` -> `15`

No config, environment, migration, Gateway protocol, or suspension-lease contract changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Reject radix-prefixed `gateway suspend --wait` values before RPC while preserving the normal decimal path.

Real environment tested:
Ubuntu WSL, Node 24, source checkout byte-matched to exact remote head `21f862176b5c7116391d7e903b8e04e355558d7d`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, no configured Gateway credentials. The registered production CLI command was invoked directly; no RPC mock was used.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

1. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway suspend --wait 0x10`
2. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway suspend --wait 0`

Evidence after fix:

```text
$ openclaw gateway suspend --wait 0x10
Gateway suspend failed: --wait must be a non-negative number of seconds
exit 1

$ openclaw gateway suspend --wait 0
gateway gateway.suspend.prepare requires credentials before opening a websocket
Fix: configure gateway.auth token/password, pair this device, or pass --token/--password.
exit 1
```

Observed result after fix:
The radix value failed at CLI validation. Decimal zero passed validation and reached the normal Gateway credential/RPC boundary, confirming that ordinary numeric input was not rejected. The exact local prepared tree and remote head tree were both `1b164d0b665728d82638a3c58059ab594e2cbddc`.

What was not tested:
A live Gateway was not suspended because this parsing fix must fail before connection and does not alter Gateway behavior. Required hosted checks for the refreshed head remain authoritative for the complete repository matrix.

## Supporting validation

- `src/cli/gateway-cli/suspend-cli.test.ts`: 24 tests passed.
- Added rows cover hexadecimal, binary, and octal rejection and assert `callGateway` is not invoked.
- Changed-file `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- Changed-file type-aware `oxlint`: 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Synthetic merge with current `origin/main`: clean; exclusive diff is 16 additions and 1 deletion across the parser and colocated test.
- Full `pnpm build`: passed during preparation.
- Local `pnpm check` could not complete in the maintainer wrapper's nested worktree because declaration resolution detected the parent checkout's `node_modules`; this is a checkout-layout failure, not a source failure. Hosted CI is pending on the exact refreshed head.

## Scope

This is a small CLI validation fix within the existing suspend/resume behavior. It does not add a hibernate API, change host/runtime ownership, or implement cold-replacement recovery.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): attribute rollover drain timeouts to the blocking session owner
prs.body:
Related: #167078

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a session rollover drain hits its pinned 15 s budget (`timed out draining work before reply session rollover`), the failure is unattributable — nothing says which admission still held the fence, so operators cannot tell which owner to repair.

## User Impact

User impact: every occurrence of the reported drain timeout now reports the redacted blocking owner (kind, phase, interrupt state, age) directly in the error, turning "mysterious session failed after 15s" into an attributable signal that identifies the repair target. No behavior, ordering, or cleanup semantics change in this revision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rev1 recommended retaining the intentional fence-until-durable-cleanup ordering and identifying the actual blocking owner **before** dispatching a bounded repair. This revision does exactly that first step and deliberately drops the earlier ordering change:

- Reverted (from the previous head): releasing the lifecycle fence ahead of the durable tail. The ordering is intentional (provenance `0a868179e4c7`, #96230, #159632) and Rev1 flagged the relaxed overlap as a merge risk; it is restored byte-for-byte.
- Kept: admissions carry a wall-clock start and a short owner label; the rollover drain timeout embeds a redacted blocking-owner summary instead of a bare fixed-timeout failure.

While re-validating we also found the earlier contended-cleanup test could not reproduce the reported chain at all — once the interrupted operation clears, the worker database-claim release settles on its own and the fence releases without the grace window. The mocked-stall fence tests were therefore removed rather than left asserting semantics the harness does not exercise; what remains guards the actual new boundary (redaction of the attribution summary).

## Evidence

### Live rollover drain repro (base vs head, real production path)

Source-level live run via the repo tsx toolchain (outside vitest) against two clean worktrees: base `297f0c57ec7` (upstream/main) and head `d5525d49c11`. The script drives the real production rollover path end to end: a sqlite-backed session store seeded stale at the daily reset boundary, a real visible `admitReplyTurn` admission held open (the in-flight owner, production stall shape from #167078), then a second ordinary turn calls the real `initSessionState`, which starts the real `rollover` lifecycle mutation, interrupts the held admission, and waits out the real pinned 15 s drain budget.

Base `297f0c57ec7` — bare fixed-timeout failure, no attribution:

```
[repro:base] turn A admitted and held (in-flight reply owner)
[repro:base] turn B starting initSessionState (stale session, rollover required)
[sessions/lifecycle] operation=mutation mutationKind=rollover ... elapsedMs=15009 phaseDurationsMs={"prepare":15008,...}
[repro:base] rollover failed after 22048ms (drain budget 15000ms)
[repro:base] ERROR: timed out draining work before reply session rollover: agent:main:telegram:topic:drain-proof
```

Head `d5525d49c11` — same scenario, error names the redacted blocking owner:

```
[repro:head] turn A admitted and held (in-flight reply owner)
[repro:head] competing-admission summary while held: 1 competing admission(s): reply-turn,phase=acquired,interrupted=false,ageMs=8755
[repro:head] turn B starting initSessionState (stale session, rollover required)
[sessions/lifecycle] operation=mutation mutationKind=rollover ... elapsedMs=15026 phaseDurationsMs={"prepare":15025,...}
[repro:head] rollover failed after 21944ms (drain budget 15000ms)
[repro:head] ERROR: timed out draining work before reply session rollover: agent:main:telegram:topic:drain-proof (1 competing admission(s): reply-turn,phase=acquired,interrupted=true,ageMs=30955)
```

The drain budget expiry is real (lifecycle diagnostic shows `prepare` phase consuming 15025 ms), the held owner is a real acquired reply-turn admission (age grows from admission), `interrupted=true` reflects the real interruption delivered to the stalled owner, and the attribution adds no identifiers beyond the session key the error already carried before this change. Identifiers shown are synthetic fixture values; no endpoints or credentials involved.

### Suite and static evidence

- Focused suites green on head `d5525d49c11`: `reply-turn-admission.test.ts`, `session-lifecycle-admission.test.ts`, `session-lifecycle-admission.pending.test.ts`, `dispatch-from-config.owner-settlement.test.ts`, `delivery.settle-reset.integration.test.ts` — 75/75.
- New test `keeps drain attribution redacted while a competing admission holds the fence`: with a real acquired reply admission holding the fence, the attribution summary carries `reply-turn` / `phase=acquired` and provably excludes the raw session key and session id; after release it reports `no competing admission held`.
- `oxlint` on touched files reports only the pre-existing `max-lines` finding already present on `upstream/main`; `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json` has no findings in touched files.
- Ordering parity: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` release ordering is back to the `upstream/main` shape (fence releases only after recovery-owner and database-claim releases settle).
- Revision note (head `09722d5c728`, Rev19 P3): the redaction test's post-release assertion now captures the admission release promise before owner completion and awaits it through the existing `withinTest` helper with a single summary assertion, replacing the `vi.waitFor` polling (root AGENTS.md prohibits polling in new tests, and a separate polling deadline could fail a slow-but-correct release); `reply-turn-admission.test.ts` green 22/22, `oxlint` clean on the file.

### CI failure attribution on head `09722d5c728` (run 38072468961, 2026-10-10)

Complete-log inspection plus base comparison for the failed jobs on the current head. Both root-cause failures are verified outside causes from the main side of the GitHub merge ref; neither is diff-caused, and both are already fixed on `upstream/main`.

**1. `check-lint` (job 114273147587) — outside cause, fixed on main after the run started.** Verbatim from the "Run changed lint" step:

```
scripts/lib/managed-cleanup-handoff.mts:224:9: error: Function 'release' expected no return value. (typescript(consistent-return))
```

Base comparison: `scripts/lib/managed-cleanup-handoff.mts` does not exist at this branch's head `09722d5c728` nor at the merge base `c718c709486` (`git cat-file -e` fails for both), so the PR diff cannot have introduced the finding — the file reaches the PR checkout only through the merge ref's main side. Main-side history: `7fd6d6738ce` / `a9d10dc7df4` build the cleanup-custody chain, and `493a499b86e` ("fix(tooling): return a promise from every cleanup release path", committed 2026-10-10T17:50:53Z — ten minutes after this CI run started at 17:40Z) changes exactly the flagged `release` paths (`return;` → `return Promise.resolve();`). The next merge-ref run includes the fix.

**2. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-8` (job 114272843574) — one failed shard, outside cause, fixed on main after the run started.** The only failed invocation is shard `agentic-control-plane-agent-chat-hosted-1` (204/205 tests passed):

```

AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
❯ src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts:2396:42
```

The `[shutdown] failed ... Agent database close failed` diagnostic lines elsewhere in the same job belong to shard `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-11`, which **passed** (`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 5 passed (5)`) — they are recovery-path teardown noise, not a failure. Base comparison: `server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts` is not in this PR's diff. Main-side fix `d1dc0c1c76d` ("test(gateway): wait for attachment dispatch before checking dedupe", committed 2026-10-10T17:58:56Z — after this CI run started) reworks exactly this test around the race between the chat.send acknowledgment and the detached skill-preparation/dispatch, including the `dispatchInboundMessageMock` expectations. The next merge-ref run includes the fix.

**3. `openclaw/ci-gate`** is the fail-fast aggregation of the two jobs above; it has no independent failure.

Branch-local evidence unchanged: narrow `oxlint` + `oxfmt` on the changed files pass at head `09722d5c728`, the changed suites are green (`reply-turn-admission.test.ts` 22/22), and `pr-fail-fast` passed on this run. No diff-caused failure to fix.

### Merge verification vs current main (`aa311a4b286`)

(GitHub's GraphQL mergeable was still recalculating as UNKNOWN at edit time; the local merge-tree result is the primary evidence this round, as in prior rounds where it matched GitHub's computation.)

## Risk and Compatibility

## LOC

## Not Tested
