prs.title: fix(macos): run bundle copy off the main thread during self-install
prs.body:
## Problem

When OpenClaw is launched under **App Translocation** (the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr is still present on `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`), `handleLaunch()` falls into the `.offerInstall` path and calls `install()` **synchronously on the main thread**.

`copyItem()` on a 2 GB+ bundle blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` for minutes:
- No menu bar icon appears, no window opens
- CPU sits at 200–286 % continuously
- The process **cannot be terminated with SIGTERM** because the main thread is stuck in a kernel `write()` syscall — only `kill -9` works
- macOS generates a diagnostic report showing ~2.1 GB written in 40 s

Root cause and stack trace are documented in #134736.

## Changes

1. **`install()` is now `async`** — `copyItem` runs in a `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated)` so the main thread can finish launching and present UI. `replaceItemAt` / `moveItem` stay on the main actor. Partial-copy and backup deletes are awaited off the main thread before exit.

2. **`.offerInstall` uses the existing activation-aware `confirmInstall`** (`AppActivation.shared.presentAlert`). When that alert is answered before `handleLaunch` returns, the result is `.installing`: MenuBar skips gateway/menu/onboarding/CLI startup from the transient bundle, a non-modal progress window shows “Copying to Applications…”, then the app relaunches from the installed location (or terminates if install / relaunch-spawn fails). A `--no-activate` confirmation is still deferred: `handleLaunch` returns `.continueLaunch`, launch continues, and a later approval copies in the background without terminating a session that already started.

3. **Relaunch** keeps the current activation-aware helper (`open` with `-g` / `--no-activate` when activation is disallowed).

## Testing

- Nesting-guard unit tests were removed with the unused staging containment surface (`isPath(_:nestedIn:)` / `UnsafeCopyDestinationError`); ClawSweeper withdrew that finding as unused surface when staging is under Applications.
- Manual macOS offer-install proof (fresh install, replacement, failure, relaunch) is **not** attached yet.

## Risk

- Normal activation no longer blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` on the multi-GB copy. The transient bundle does not start gateway, menu, or onboarding; the progress window stays up until relaunch or a failure alert.
- `FileManager.copyItem` work runs in a detached task with a task-local `FileManager()`; awaited cleanup avoids abandoning multi-GB staging/backup deletes on quit.
- A deferred `--no-activate` approval does not terminate an already-started session.

Fixes #134736

## What Problem This Solves

Moves the remaining MCP app, MCP server, and canvas widget components from Lit to Solid 2 while keeping their existing tags, classes, and user flows.

## User Impact

App frames retain their identity across ordinary updates, and app retirement remains awaited before a replacement appears. Server settings, app discovery, resource selection, and canvas behavior retain their current contracts. No dependencies or public configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each registered tag now has one Solid implementation, reached by existing Lit callers through the bridge. Discovery and frame protocol state remain with synchronous TypeScript owners. The MCP panel retains both the child root and its accepted launch while teardown runs; metadata updates remain live without relaunching or resetting app-reported height.

The small coupled bridge changes preserve public property setters and native `moveBefore` lifetimes. Shared wizard templates and confirmation templates remain with their unported Lit consumers; the new renderers reuse those decision owners.

## Evidence

| --- | --- |
| Focused MCP, canvas, bridge, and retirement tests | 135 passing across 13 single-file runs; details below |
| Synthetic component screenshots | Inspected before/after; baseline and candidate PNGs are byte-identical |

| Focused lint and whitespace | Passing |

The screenshots use synthetic configured servers, app discovery, a static canvas document, and a deliberately reconstructed/error app state. They were captured in an isolated single-file Chromium component test; no local application E2E, Docker, or OrbStack was run.

Changed UI production files: 4,288 → 5,123 lines (+835). Changed tests/helpers: 5,517 → 6,024 (+507). Growth is primarily explicit JSX/bridge property declarations and the retained shared wizard/form renderers; the seven registered Lit implementations are deleted.

A proposed live provider-context replacement protocol was declined: production `app-root.ts` publishes a new context only from `connectedCallback`, at a full application-tree epoch. prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve active chat input during announcements
prs.body:
Closes #165500

## What Problem This Solves

An announcement in a shared session can treat another active request's accepted user input as an orphan and include it in its own model context. This patch keeps that input available to its original request and excludes it from consecutive announcement prompts and context rebuilds.

## Implementation

Use the existing live custody registry before orphan reconciliation and filter keyed foreign-live messages at model-context conversion. Resolve database ownership asynchronously in the read worker, retain exact admission/cancellation/binding checks across that await, and publish aggregate ownership only after the writer commits. `promotedOwner` retains source-to-aggregate identity in host memory.

Foreign protection is released only for confirmed custody loss: the owner's lifetime recheck fails, or its authority denies the input with `SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError` (not the `SessionSharingProfileFactsChangedError` subclass). Worker failures and exhausted non-revoking profile refreshes are inconclusive. They fail discovery, so the announcement attempt stops before orphan repair instead of taking another request's input. The same rule applies during preparation, provider collection and per-owner collection, including after an earlier profile refresh.

Current PR head is one commit, `1a6d9a3a868e3dc50f0998548e4d42fa6c0a97c9`, on `main` `1f307d61d0f`. Worker-retained sharing authority is prepared off-thread; exact live owners are reselected across awaits, and cancellation, lifecycle and physical-database checks are retained.

```ts
  const observed = vi.spyOn(custody, "captureSessionPendingInputWorkerCustody").mockImplementation(() => {
    const value = capture();
    if (!value) return value;
    return { ...value, publish(receipt) {
      if (value.facts.sources?.length === 2) {
        workerPublications.push({ sourceCount: value.facts.sources.length, consumedCount: receipt.consumedInputIds.length,
          physicalLocator: value.facts.databasePath, serializesPromotedOwner: JSON.stringify(value.facts).includes("promotedOwner") });

  });
  let aggregate: ReturnType<typeof createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder> | undefined;
  try {
    const start = () => startGatewayWithClient({ cfg, configPath, token: "synthetic-proof-token", clientDisplayName: "pr163655-isolated-proof" });
    gateway = await start();
    const wait = async (runId: string) => {
      const result = await gateway!.client.request("agent.wait", { runId, timeoutMs: 45_000 }, { timeoutMs: 50_000 });
      expect(result).toMatchObject({ status: "ok" });
      return result;
    };
    const warmup = await gateway.client.request<any>("chat.send", { sessionKey, message: "PR163655_WARMUP", deliver: false, idempotencyKey: "proof-warmup" });
    await wait(warmup.runId);
    expect(requests).toHaveLength(1);
    scheduler.gate = async (actual, params) => {
      const body = JSON.stringify(params.ctx);
      if (!body.includes(SOURCE_A) && !body.includes(SOURCE_B)) return actual(params);
      const release = deferred<"original" | "cancel">();
      const index = held.length;
      held.push({ actual, params, release });
      entered[index].resolve();
      const mode = await release.promise;
      if (mode === "cancel") return { queuedFinal: false, counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 0 } };
      const ctx = { ...params.ctx };
      for (const key of ["Body", "BodyForAgent", "RawBody", "CommandBody", "BodyForCommands"]) if (key in ctx) ctx[key] = AGGREGATE;
      return aggregate!.withPendingInput!(() => actual({ ...params, ctx, replyOptions: { ...params.replyOptions, userTurnTranscriptRecorder: aggregate } }));
    };
    const accepted = [];
    for (const [index, message] of [SOURCE_A, SOURCE_B].entries()) {
      const ack = await gateway.client.request<any>("chat.send", { sessionKey, message, deliver: false, idempotencyKey: `proof-source-${index}` });
      expect(ack.status).toBe("started");
      accepted.push(ack);
      await entered[index].promise;
    }
    const entry = loadSessionEntry({ agentId: "main", sessionKey, storePath });
    expect(entry?.sessionId).toBeTruthy();
    const scope = { agentId: "main", sessionKey, sessionId: entry!.sessionId, storePath };
    const resolved = await prepareSqliteTranscriptReadScope(scope);
    const databasePath = resolved.path;
    expect(await fs.realpath(databasePath)).not.toContain("session-alias");
    const schema = () => {
      const db = new DatabaseSync(databasePath, { readOnly: true });
      try {
        const rows = db.prepare("SELECT type,name,sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE sql IS NOT NULL ORDER BY type,name").all();
        return { fingerprint: createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(rows)).digest("hex"), userVersion: db.prepare("PRAGMA user_version").get(), hasPromotedOwner: JSON.stringify(rows).includes("promotedOwner") };
      } finally { db.close(); }
    };
    const beforeSchema = schema();
    expect((await listSessionPendingInputs(scope)).total).toBe(2);
    aggregate = createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder({ message: { role: "user", content: AGGREGATE, timestamp: Date.now(), idempotencyKey: "proof-aggregate:user" },
      pendingInputSources: held.map(({ params }) => params.replyOptions.userTurnTranscriptRecorder), target: { ...scope, sessionEntry: entry, config: cfg }, updateMode: "none" });
    await aggregate.resolveMessage();
    const committed = await aggregate.withPendingInput!(() => aggregate!.persistApproved());
    expect(committed?.appended).toBe(true);
    expect((await listSessionPendingInputs(scope)).total).toBe(0);
    expect(workerPublications).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(workerPublications[0]).toMatchObject({ sourceCount: 2, consumedCount: 2, serializesPromotedOwner: false });
    const aliasEntries = await getForeignLiveSessionPendingInputEntries(scope);
    expect(aliasEntries.size).toBe(1);
    expect(await aggregate.withPendingInput!(() => getForeignLiveSessionPendingInputEntries(scope))).toHaveProperty("size", 0);
    const history = async () => gateway!.client.request<any>("chat.history", { sessionKey, limit: 100 });
    const durableCopies: number[] = [copies((await history()).messages, SOURCE_A)];
    for (const index of [1, 2]) {
      phase = `announcement-${index}`;
      const ack = await gateway.client.request<any>("agent", { agentId: "main", sessionKey, message: `PR163655_ANNOUNCEMENT_${index}`, deliver: false,
        inputProvenance: { kind: "inter_session", sourceSessionKey: "agent:main:subagent:proof-child", sourceTool: "subagent_announce" }, idempotencyKey: `proof-announcement-${index}` });
      await wait(ack.runId);
      const sent = requests.filter((request) => request.phase === phase);
      expect(sent).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(copies(sent[0].input, SOURCE_A)).toBe(0);
      expect(copies(sent[0].input, SOURCE_B)).toBe(0);
      durableCopies.push(copies((await history()).messages, SOURCE_A));
      expect((await getForeignLiveSessionPendingInputEntries(scope)).size).toBe(1);
    }
    phase = "original-continuation";
    held[0].release.resolve("original");
    await wait(accepted[0].runId);
    const originalRequests = requests.filter((request) => request.phase === phase);
    expect(originalRequests).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(copies(originalRequests[0].input, SOURCE_A)).toBe(1);
    expect(copies(originalRequests[0].input, SOURCE_B)).toBe(1);
    durableCopies.push(copies((await history()).messages, SOURCE_A));
    expect(durableCopies).toEqual([1, 1, 1, 1]);
    await gateway.client.request("chat.abort", { sessionKey, runId: accepted[1].runId });

    aggregate.finishPendingInput?.("interrupted");
    await aggregate.waitForPendingInputSettlement?.();
    await disconnectGatewayClient(gateway.client);
    await gateway.server.close({ reason: "isolated proof restart" });
    gateway = undefined;
    scheduler.gate = undefined;
    clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot(); clearConfigCache();
    gateway = await start();
    const restartedHistory = await history();
    expect(copies(restartedHistory.messages, SOURCE_A)).toBe(1);
    expect(copies(restartedHistory.messages, SOURCE_B)).toBe(1);
    expect((await listSessionPendingInputs(scope)).total).toBe(0);
    const afterSchema = schema();
    expect(afterSchema).toEqual(beforeSchema);
    const result = { head: "3461bd2c46b82ff5c467371ea4b069da5b1c50bb", transport: "real Gateway + SQLite workers + local deterministic OpenAI Responses HTTP; no external model",
      acceptedSourceRequests: 2, aliasResolvedToPhysicalDatabase: true, promotedWorkerSources: 2, consumedWorkerSources: 2,
      workerFactsContainPromotedOwner: false, requestEvidence: requests.map((request) => ({ phase: request.phase, httpStatus: request.status,
        alphaCopies: copies(request.input, SOURCE_A), betaCopies: copies(request.input, SOURCE_B) })),
      durableAlphaCopiesAcrossPromotionAndRuns: durableCopies, restart: { alphaCopies: 1, betaCopies: 1, pendingRows: 0 },
      schemaBefore: beforeSchema, schemaAfter: afterSchema,
      limitations: "Scheduling fixture binds two accepted source recorders through production collection API; no real child spawn or external provider inference." };
    await fs.writeFile(path.join(proofDir, "runtime-result.json"), `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\n`);
    console.log("PR163655_RUNTIME_RESULT", JSON.stringify(result));
  } finally {
    for (const item of held) item.release.resolve("cancel");
    aggregate?.finishPendingInput?.("interrupted");
    await aggregate?.waitForPendingInputSettlement?.().catch(() => undefined);
    scheduler.gate = undefined;
    observed.mockRestore();
    if (gateway) { await disconnectGatewayClient(gateway.client).catch(() => undefined); await gateway.server.close().catch(() => undefined); }
    await new Promise<void>((resolve) => endpoint.close(() => resolve()));
    // Keep isolated runtime state and proof files, as requested by the operator.
  }
});

```

</details>

## Preserved prior real-provider evidence

The [sanitized, previously accepted Gateway/SQLite/official DeepSeek Responses proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163655#issuecomment-5961406189) applies to **`6494b6a53871a9984e20dfa523949a9032615dd4` only**. Four forwarded requests returned HTTP 200 and `response.completed`; two consecutive announcements contained zero protected-input copies and the original continuation contained one. It did not exercise the revised worker preparation, aliased locator or multi-source aggregate composition. The current-head runtime proof above covers that composition without claiming the older DeepSeek trace was rerun.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve agent workspace instructions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserve the Codex-selected project instructions that established a thread, including effective native fallback names, root markers, and environment-owned sources, without substituting a new hierarchy on cold continuation.

## Why This Change Was Made

[The September 5 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/126986#issuecomment-5365198371) found that selected subpaths such as `.config/WORKFLOW.md` could be dropped and padded fallback names did not match native normalization. The prior head also had stale RPC fixtures, lint failures, and a missing authored Evidence heading.

## Repair

- Trim fallback names and discard blank entries as native Codex does.
- Capture from the preflight candidate set instead of classifying selected paths again by ancestry. Missing, changed, or unknown selected sources remain rejected.
- Separate the leading native global source from project sources without consuming the project budget. Preserve both lexical and canonical home paths and a later project occurrence of the same file.
- Refresh configuration-read and authority fixtures, remove unused imports, and preserve the current lifecycle owners through the upstream refactor. No tests were removed or disabled; no test-registration change is part of this PR.
- Integrate current main `d058e5d8c401fcaa7b327e1a4e176f90502855d3`, preserving its authored project-document byte budget, lifecycle owner split, and documentation split. Update docs and generated prompt snapshots to distinguish unavailable nonempty authority from portable frozen-empty authority.

AI-assisted implementation, testing, and review used Codex. No human maintainer approval is implied.

## User Impact and Maintainer Decisions

Configured nested/padded fallback files are retained for frozen replay. Nonempty project instructions owned by an unavailable execution environment still prevent physical cold resume/replacement. An empty selection remains frozen-empty and portable with native rediscovery disabled.

Two product/continuity decisions remain **pending maintainer acceptance**, separate from tests and ratings:

1. Require the original live thread or a new session when nonempty environment-owned instructions cannot be replayed by the Gateway; preserve the empty-selection exception.
2. Refuse reconfiguration of an explicitly attached legacy thread without stored authority, with native Codex or `/new` as recovery, instead of silently replacing the selected thread.

## Compatibility and Stored State

This follow-up's candidate sets and home-path handling are invocation-local, not persisted. Across the whole PR, the existing instruction-string field is retained and an optional unavailable-authority fact is paired with a marker and environment fingerprint. There is no SQLite DDL/schema-version migration. Legacy rows and the prior-reader empty-marker contract are covered by the binding suite. Readability by an old reader does **not** establish old-version enforcement of the new continuation cutoff or unrestricted rollback safety.

The native-process proof on production repair commit `2e5abd1db10` is historical. The prior sandbox/Gateway and restart trace below is also historical; neither is represented as a new integrated-head run.

## Evidence

### Current merge refresh — 2026-09-25

### Current head — 2026-09-25

- Head `5804a7675378f5422bd0bcbff6cab4b308ae3912` repairs the subscription recovery fixtures found in `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-20`: native-owned seeds now carry expected runtime ownership and frozen-empty instruction authority; the overflow fixture carries the same authority for both variants and waits for turn acceptance before notifying. The owning file passed **10/10** locally; format/diff checks passed. Exact-head CI is pending. The standalone extension-only `tsc` invocation cannot resolve repository plugin-SDK exports and is not claimed as a typecheck pass.
- Head `208a9f2fb380ed45e94a2806a65592091ff2ac5c` fixes the shared-client cleanup request-order fixture and gives the intentionally resumable bounded-continuity fixture explicit frozen-empty instruction authority. The entire cleanup owning file passed **17/17** locally; the resumed continuity case passed **1/1** in the focused two-file run. Formatting/diff checks passed. New exact-head CI is running.
- Head `0c739557a7d30daf9075cbad2fa1071a5a03fe75` updates five context-engine request-order fixtures for the now-authoritative project-doc preflight `config/read` and one resumed-binding fixture with explicit frozen-empty authority. The six exact failing CI cases passed locally **6/6**; formatting/diff checks passed. New exact-head CI is running.
- Head `afc5ca06d992c87223e78700cfde4e59cebe2a24` refreshes four native-run fixture files for the merged authority contract. The affected local batch passed 33/34 tests; the only local failure was an unchanged retry-model startup timeout (that same test passed in the preceding hosted shard). Formatting and diff checks passed. New exact-head CI is running; this is not a green claim.
- **Real native authority-chain proof on production-identical predecessor `96d7c60b643`:** a disposable test passed 1/1 through production `startOrResumeThread`, a real Codex 0.153.4 App Server, and a Docker-isolated real exec-server. Gateway and remote files shared one absolute `AGENTS.md` path but held different markers. The local native start froze the local marker; a remote replacement selected the nonempty remote source, started a new native thread, and persisted `CODEX_UNAVAILABLE_PROJECT_DOCS_AUTHORITY` without the forbidden Gateway marker. A later replacement targeting a missing remote environment failed before native start and preserved the binding. This proves the final binding/source effect, not a model turn or an unfixed-baseline comparison. The disposable test and container were removed. The fixture-only head above does not change this production path.
- **Cross-version rollback parser probe (2026-09-25):** In disposable checkouts, current main `847863aae3b` read a representative active binding carrying `projectInstructionsUnavailableToGateway: true` and the unavailable-authority marker, but its Zod schema stripped the unknown Boolean fact (1/1 probe passed). The PR head reader accepted the intact row and rejected the fact-stripped row (1/1 probe passed). Thus an older reader can erase the authority fact if it reserializes the binding; returning to this head then fails closed, but safe downgrade/continuation has **not** been demonstrated. These were parser probes, not a copied-database release preflight or model-turn proof. A maintainer-approved rollback contract is still required.
- **Storage design remains open:** authored `project_doc_max_bytes` can exceed the 1 MiB keyed-state value ceiling. A proposed bounded design is immutable UTF-8 chunks in a separate plugin-state namespace, followed by an atomic binding manifest with byte count, chunk count, and digest; reads fail closed on any missing/mismatched chunk, and cleanup follows a committed replace/clear. A maximum total size must be defined before native thread commitment. This changes durable representation/retention, so `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md` requires a linked accepted maintainer design before implementation. This is a proposal, not accepted or shipped behavior.
- Head `96d7c60b643` additionally marks the existing host-local replacement lifecycle fixture as authorized for native project-instruction capture. This fixes the only failure in `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-9`; the exact test passed locally (1 passed, 252 skipped), and new exact-head CI is running.
- Prior head `601a654b299eab751376f19c7cff7f8869787506` includes the remote-authority repair plus a typed request mock that clears the prior `check-test-types` tuple error. It also removes the sole unrelated onboarding-test delta from this PR; that changed-file shard had failed on an upstream owner-runtime assertion. New exact-head CI is running.
- Head `a51964eda5424a0f2c3cb039fc53b59179d54673` repairs the remote replacement authority boundary: a newly selected host-local environment may recapture native project instructions, while a remote selected environment never reads Gateway-local candidate paths. A remote fresh replacement drops the predecessor's frozen developer text, lets Codex select native docs, and persists the unavailable-authority marker with its environment identity when sources are nonempty.
- The focused lifecycle rotation suite passed **2/2** at this head. Its remote control uses a selected remote environment and a nonempty native `instructionSources` response; it checks the final binding marker, the absence of predecessor instructions in the new `thread/start`, and the absence of a Gateway capture preflight. This is a synthetic native-response test, not a current-head real-process proof.
- **Still open:** a valid authored project-doc budget can produce a frozen instruction string larger than keyed plugin state's 1 MiB value ceiling. This needs a separate durable storage contract; this commit does not claim to fix it. The prior integrated-head real-process/rollback proof remains historical. The latest ClawSweeper review remains below platinum; the real authority proof is now above, while storage design acceptance and the two maintainer continuity decisions remain open. New exact-head CI is running.

- Head: `b901aea31d4112fe3bf1e1660fa28c3da3d40646` (CI repair atop merge commit `9fb672657488c1caa6c41436a51111256f18ab85`); merged main `d058e5d8c401fcaa7b327e1a4e176f90502855d3` without rewriting prior PR commits. Resolved 31 conflicts across production, tests, docs, and generated prompt snapshots. GitHub reports **MERGEABLE**; exact-head CI is running/approval-gated, not claimed green.
- Preserved main's authored `project_doc_max_bytes` behavior. Fixed a merge-review finding: durable replacement threads now rediscover current Codex project docs and freeze their own selected sources, while cold resume replays the predecessor snapshot. Added real-`AGENTS.md` rotation coverage.
- A failed first read of an OpenClaw-carried workspace no longer freezes a false empty instruction set; a later successful read can establish authority. Updated four sandbox tests to the current per-attempt test-tool factory.
- Local verification: extension production and test typechecks passed; changed Codex files pass lint and formatting; all seven prompt snapshots are current. Focused initial suites passed 307 tests; an expanded pre-fix shard passed 257; the final targeted authority rerun passed 8/8. The expanded pre-fix run found five failures, which were corrected and rerun in the targeted set. These local results do not replace exact-head hosted CI or the historical native-process proof.
- CI repair on `b901aea31d4`: removed one unused lifecycle file and two unused exports identified by `check-dependencies`, and made the provider-runtime test mock partial to preserve upstream exports. Local `pnpm deadcode:full` and the affected auth suite (18/18) pass; replacement-head hosted CI is not yet claimed green.
- The two maintainer continuity decisions above remain pending.

## Separate Review Blockers

- Oversized frozen snapshot durability and exact-head real-process/rollback proof remain unresolved.
- Maintainer acceptance of the environment-owned cold cutoff and attached legacy-thread behavior remains separate from code/test results.
- Latest exact-head checks for `5804a7675378f5422bd0bcbff6cab4b308ae3912` are green (88 success, 47 skipped, 1 neutral, deduplicated by workflow/check name and latest start time). The older cancelled PR-context run is superseded by successful runs. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and remains gold, blocked on the bounded durable snapshot/rollback design and cold-continuation contract; no maintainer acceptance is recorded. GitHub currently reports a merge conflict. CI success does not resolve those separate review blockers.

### Conflict refresh — 2026-09-08

- Updated head: `8d5be50a25fe9c55fb5c97c96d95fdb34e20b83d`; tree: `05fcc466fd995d0153956c7fe34fc1f390c8cad7`.
- Integrated main `7069a4772ff40602566afc686a41530dc76c8d2d` without rewriting the existing PR history. Only three generated prompt snapshots required conflict resolution. Regeneration preserves this PR's project-instruction content and main's `sessions_history` descriptions; no production file required manual resolution.
- Scoped `check:changed` passed, including formatting, all seven prompt snapshots being current, repository guards, and script lint. The three focused test files passed **92/92 tests** (90 tooling/lifecycle tests and 2 OAuth regression tests).
- Independent read-only review found no issues in the resolved snapshots or the two automatically merged test files. Both SHA-bound prompt deltas also passed static reconstruction checks. The final committed tree matches the reviewed and tested candidate.
- Clean merge-tree check against subsequently advanced main `a9707e15bcdab23bfa472b53ae631910f7e1f42c`. GitHub reports mergeable after the push. **Hosted CI at publication time:** [new-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34265792688) is running; no new-head hosted pass is claimed.

Commands for this conflict refresh:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 7069a4772ff40602566afc686a41530dc76c8d2d -- \
  test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/discord-group-codex-message-tool.md.diff \
  test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-direct-codex-message-tool.md \
  test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-heartbeat-codex-tool.md.diff
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth.oauth-refresh-fail-closed.test.ts \
  test/canonical-descendant.integration.test.ts
```

The detailed native/Gateway/build and earlier CI evidence below remains tied to its recorded prior SHAs; this refresh is not a rerun of those historical proofs. The two maintainer decisions above remain unchanged.

### Previous verified revision

- Previous verified head: `3e52264032e005c8cb532d286fb64a3c90bdfe04`; tree: `4a3d7f1347d65740459231d13bb87408f64a571e`.
- Production repair/proof commit: `2e5abd1db10b502252c85f49864d343c9815f7e0`; tree: `0f5b3aaee47437ae41e35b494c544bcef883a4d3`. The two test-only follow-ups change four existing test files (+27/-1): settlement, turn watches, attachment continuity, and durable context. The Git diff was checked and production bytes are unchanged.
- Repair-commit parents: prior published head `d092f102025574625f4e65ae7f1afae7bce55ec2` and pinned main `a6bca1c6fd1b1469a17f517ae9f3e33ab517f1e9`.
- The complete PR delta includes the earlier feature, integration, coherent module moves, and expanded lifecycle coverage. The latest follow-up changes only the attachment-continuity and durable-context test fixtures; no production source is changed.

### Previous-revision verification

| Check | Result and scope |
|---|---|
| Focused lifecycle/integration run | **847 passed** across the canonical descendant integration and nine Codex suites. This run precedes the final home-spelling-only adjustment. |
| Final project-document suite | **25/25 passed** on the production repair source. |
| CI fixture follow-ups | **66/66 passed** across settlement/turn-watch tests and **14/14 passed** across attachment-continuity/durable-context tests. Resume fixtures now explicitly carry frozen-empty instruction authority instead of unintentionally representing cold legacy bindings. Original assertions and timeouts are unchanged. Both scoped autoreviews reported no P0–P2 findings; neither is represented as a new complete-PR approval. |
| Regression sensitivity | Initial nested/padded repair: 5 failed / 13 passed against the old owner. Global/project boundary: 5 failed / 19 passed before its fix, then 24 passed. Final lexical-home case: 1 failed / 24 passed before its fix, then 25 passed. |
| Formatting and guards | Changed-file formatting, conflict-marker/diff checks, max-lines ratchet, package/exports/import guards, plugin boundaries, and prompt snapshot checks passed; all seven generated prompt snapshots are current. |
| Required local checks | The repair-worktree required-check runner completed successfully, including core/extension production and test typechecks, root-test typechecking, dead-export scans, lint, import-cycle checks, and boundary guards. That long-running local invocation did not record a single immutable source SHA and is supplemental evidence, not an exact-head gate for `3e52264032e`. The latest two-file correction separately passed focused tests, formatting, lint, and scoped autoreview; [exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34190821064) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on `3e52264032e`. |
| Full build | On production repair commit `2e5abd1db10`, the resumed log reached all final build phases, including all 152 public SDK exports, UI budgets, build-info, and CLI startup metadata. The terminal exit was not captured across tool-session interruptions; a later cached retry also lost its completion record. No verified full-build exit-code pass is claimed. |
| Hosted CI | [49f10a0b CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34187521346) passed the earlier fixture repairs but found 11 failures in two resume-test files in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`. Those fixtures are now repaired, and both full affected files pass locally (14 tests). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34190821064) and `openclaw/ci-gate` **passed** on `3e52264032e`. At verification, all reported checks were completed: 145 successful, 46 intentionally skipped, 1 neutral, and no failures. GitHub reports clean/mergeable. The durable review names this exact head and rates it Diamond with Ready for maintainer look; documented owner decisions remain pending before merge. |
| Independent review | Two-pass P0–P2 autoreview found one home-spelling issue, now fixed and red/green tested. A bounded follow-up review of that exact change found no additional defect; it was not a second complete PR review. |

Commands used include `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the ten explicit affected suite paths; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/project-doc-thread-config.test.ts`; and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write`. The required-check runner uses pinned main as its base and explicit changed paths. No checks or budgets were weakened.

### Native contract and previous-revision proof scope

Personally inspected Codex source at `095ac4f131e759b204fa6368dc42d2feff6eb21a`: `core/src/agents_md.rs` discovery/source ordering, `core/src/config/mod.rs` fallback normalization, `codex-home/src/instructions/mod.rs` global precedence, and `utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs` lexical/default versus canonical/explicit home handling. Paths are under `codex-rs/`. The installed native binary reports **0.153.4**; it is not claimed to have been built from that inspected source commit.

The network-isolated, credential-free fixture uses real native `config/read`, `thread/start`, `thread/inject_items`, `thread/read`, and `thread/resume`, production lifecycle/canonical SQLite persistence, and a physically replaced native process. Four variants cover basename, nested fallback, padded basename, and padded nested plus blank entries. **All four variants passed on exact production repair commit `2e5abd1db10`.** The test-only follow-up has identical production code; this is not a claim that the fixture was rerun after that commit. An initial attempt reached the runner’s 120-second no-output watchdog before any case result. The retained retry passed without changing assertions, timeouts, isolation, or source; only its compilation cache was reused, with fresh synthetic homes and state.

Sanitized result for production repair commit `2e5abd1db10` (all four independent result files were inspected and matched its committed owner hash):

prs.title: fix(media): retry HTTP 429 rate-limit responses in core media fetch
prs.body:
## Summary

`fix(media): retry HTTP 429 rate-limit responses and honor Retry-After` — rebased onto current `main`.

Core remote-media downloads previously treated HTTP 429 as a permanent failure, while channel extensions (LINE, SMS, Telegram) already classify rate-limited media as transient. This PR adds 429 to the retryable status set in `shouldRetryMediaFetch` **and** honors the origin's `Retry-After` header before the generic backoff, per ClawSweeper's P2 finding.

The change is rebased on current `main`, which already carries abort-aware backoff (`sleepWithAbort`), so the PR now lands on top of that normalization rather than conflicting with it.

## What Problem This Solves

`shouldRetryMediaFetch` in `src/media/fetch.ts` (http_error branch) only matched `status === 408 || status >= 500`, omitting 429. A caller relying on the default retry policy (e.g. `MediaAttachmentCache` at `src/media-understanding/attachments.cache.ts`) silently failed on the first rate-limited media download instead of using its configured retry budget. 429 is also the one status where the server explicitly states how long to wait; ignoring `Retry-After` could re-request before the origin's requested delay.

**Code evidence**: the http_error branch of `shouldRetryMediaFetch` excluded 429, and the `MediaFetchError` discarded the `Retry-After` header entirely.

## Root Cause

- The media-fetch retry predicate was introduced without 429 in the retryable set and without threading the response's `Retry-After` into the retry scheduler.
- Violated invariant: 429 is a transient status — the server explicitly requests a retry — but the predicate treated it as permanent, and the scheduler never saw the origin's requested wait.
- Trigger: a rate-limited media download (HTTP 429 response) when `retry` is enabled (only `attachments.cache.ts` passes `retry` in production).

## Why This Fix

1. **Add `err.status === 429`** to the retryable status set in `shouldRetryMediaFetch`, matching LINE/SMS/Telegram extensions.
2. **Carry a bounded `Retry-After`** on `MediaFetchError` (`retryAfterMs`, parsed via `parseRetryAfterHeaderSeconds` and capped at 60s), populated in `assertMediaResponseOk`.
3. **Honor it in the retry scheduler** via `retryAfterMs` in `withMediaFetchRetry`, so a 429 is not re-requested before the origin's requested wait. The scheduler caps the honored delay at the caller's own `maxDelayMs` budget (e.g. the attachment cache's 3s), so a hostile header cannot stall a download.

This mirrors the established pattern in `src/infra/clawhub-retry.ts`, which parses `Retry-After` and wires it through `retryAfterMs`.

Alternatives considered:

- **Per-caller `shouldRetry` override** — rejected: inconsistent with the shared predicate's purpose; the channel extensions already proved 429 belongs in the shared set.
- **429 retry without `Retry-After`** — rejected: ClawSweeper's P2 finding (a rate-limited origin can be retried before its requested delay); honoring the header is the canonical fix and reuses the existing bounded parser.

## User Impact

- Before: a rate-limited attachment download (429) failed immediately — `MediaFetchError(http_error, 429)` — instead of using the configured 3-attempt retry budget, and any `Retry-After` was ignored.
- After: 429 responses are retried, matching LINE/SMS/Telegram extensions, and the origin's `Retry-After` is honored up to the caller's retry budget.

**Blast radius**: `shouldRetryMediaFetch` is only the default predicate. Of the production callers of `readRemoteMediaBuffer`, only `attachments.cache.ts` passes `retry`, with policy `attempts: 3, minDelayMs: 500, maxDelayMs: 3000, jitter: 0.2`. Its worst case is two extra requests inside roughly 3.5s, and the honored `Retry-After` is capped by that `maxDelayMs`.

## Evidence

- **Regression proof**: new tests "retries 429 rate-limit responses when retry is enabled" and "honors the Retry-After delay before retrying a 429 response" are **red on unpatched main** (429 → `MediaFetchError(http_error, 429)`, no retry) and green with the fix.
- **Focused suite**: full `src/media/fetch.test.ts` — **91 tests, all passed** (Node 26).
- **Lint/format**: `oxlint` on touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors; `oxfmt` — clean.
- **Guardrails**: `channel-import-guardrails.test.ts` — 164 tests passed (no `extensions/.../src/` literal in core).
- **Diff**: `src/media/fetch.ts` +34/-3, `src/media/fetch.test.ts` +50/-0 — 2 files, +81/-3, rebased on current `main`.

## Clamp long Retry-After values instead of discarding them (head `32b5f1577e0`)

ClawSweeper P2 (re-review): `parseRetryAfterMs` dropped any `Retry-After` over
the 60s media cap by returning `undefined`, so a valid `Retry-After: 61` fell
back to generic exponential backoff (500ms for the attachment cache) instead of
the caller's capped wait — re-requesting a rate-limited origin earlier than its
requested delay.

The hint is now **clamped** to the 60s cap instead of discarded. The retry
scheduler already caps the honored delay at the caller's own `maxDelayMs`
(`retryAfterMaxDelayMs` defaults to `maxDelayMs`), so a long or hostile header
cannot stall a download past the caller's budget, and the caller's capped wait
is used instead of generic backoff.

- **Regression**: `clamps an over-cap Retry-After instead of retrying on
  generic backoff` (`fetch.test.ts`) — **fails on the pre-fix discard** (429
  retried immediately on zero generic backoff) and passes here (retry waits the
  bounded 60s hint).
- **Real HTTP proof** (this head): a live `node:http` server returned `429` +
  `Retry-After: 61` on the first request, then `200`; production
  `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with `maxDelayMs: 3000` scheduled the retry at
  **3000ms** (the caller's capped wait) post-fix vs **500ms** generic backoff
  pre-fix, then returned `deadbeef`.
- Focused retry subset green (15/15) on this head.

## Maintainer decision: bounded early retry (intended)

The reviewer's "Decision needed" asks whether attachment downloads may retry
within their existing 3-second budget when a 429 origin requests a longer
Retry-After. The recommendation is **Accept bounded early retry** — and that is
the deliberate design of this patch: the clamp keeps a bounded hint so the
caller's own `maxDelayMs` budget (3s for the attachment cache) caps the honored
delay, rather than letting a hostile or overly long header stall a download or
silently dropping the hint. A 429 origin's requested wait is honored up to the
caller's budget; the alternative (waiting the full 61s) would defeat the
attachment cache's recovery budget.

## Diff stats

- `src/media/fetch.ts`: +34/-3 (429 in retryable set + bounded Retry-After on error + `retryAfterMs` wiring + parser import)
- `src/media/fetch.test.ts`: +50/-0 (429 retry test + Retry-After-honored test)
- Total: +81/-3, 2 files


## Real Behavior Proof (live HTTP 429 → Retry-After → recovery)

A real `node:http` server listened on `127.0.0.1` and returned `429 Too Many
Requests` with `Retry-After: 2` on the first request, then `200` with
`deadbeef0001` bytes on the second. The real production `readRemoteMediaBuffer`
was driven against it through the real SSRF guard
(`ssrfPolicy: { allowedHostnames: ["127.0.0.1"] }`) with retry policy
`{ attempts: 3, minDelayMs: 200, maxDelayMs: 30_000, jitter: 0 }`.

Actual output:

```
real server at http://127.0.0.1:39747/rate-limited.bin
  [server] request #1 received
  [server] request #2 received
RESULT: deadbeef0001 after 2 server hits in 2344ms
```

- Request #1 → `429` with `Retry-After: 2`; the client did **not** retry
  immediately.
- ~2.3s elapsed (the honored Retry-After delay plus backoff), then request #2.
- Request #2 → `200`; `readRemoteMediaBuffer` returned `deadbeef0001`.
- Total 2344ms ≈ the 2s Retry-After delay, proving the origin's pacing was
  honored, not replaced by an unconditional near-zero backoff.

**Test suite (regression, all green):** `src/media/fetch.test.ts` — 92/92
passed (Node 24.19), including `honors the Retry-After delay before retrying a
429 response` and `preserves a caller-provided retryAfterMs callback for
unheaded retries`. The timing test asserts the retry does **not** fire before
the delay elapses (4999ms), then fires on crossing the boundary.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): isolate progress posts and deliver finals separately
prs.body:
Related context: #109471
Related context: #114589
Builds on: #109555

## Current-head refresh — September 5, 2026

- Rebased feature head: [0270094e6c25](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0270094e6c250664df62ea88446d360ef3723d37), on upstream integration base [9dd869ec98eb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9dd869ec98ebd7ac08295f549856ab168d483261).
- Both review findings are repaired at their owner boundaries: default in-place source cleanup remains installed, and separate finals bypass progress-only receipt settlement so the durable sender still runs.
- Local verification on the current integration base: focused real-stream regression passed; boundary suites 123/123; Mattermost extension suite 892/892; canonical changed-file repository gate passed, including production/test/plugin type graphs, lint, formatting, generated contracts, import cycles, and policy guards.
- GitHub exact-head CI is fully green with zero failures and zero pending; GitHub reports the PR mergeable with a clean merge state.
- Prior canary package: [canary-mattermost-separate-progress-bd6d8288-r1](https://github.com/aolea/openclaw/releases/tag/canary-mattermost-separate-progress-bd6d8288-r1). Clean Node 22 Linux installation and runtime-entry smoke passed.
- Prior isolated single-agent canary: the package remained Ready with zero restarts; peer runtimes were left unchanged.
- Prior canary runtime identity: OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (bd6d828), bundled Mattermost 2026.9.1, and trusted official Codex harness. A no-delivery exact-model smoke completed in 7.1 seconds with provider openai, model gpt-6-astra, and payload ASTRA_CANARY_OK.
- [ClawSweeper reviewed the exact current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/120854#issuecomment-5229807960), accepted the live proof, confirmed both delivery findings repaired, and found no actionable correctness or security issue. The PR is ready for maintainer review; sponsorship of the opt-in configuration/API contract remains the product decision.

## Summary

This PR adds an opt-in Mattermost lifecycle that separates transient agent progress from authoritative final replies.

While an agent works, OpenClaw creates and edits one typed `custom_openclaw_progress` post. When the turn completes, OpenClaw sends the final answer as a fresh normal Mattermost post and deletes the progress post only after final delivery is confirmed.

Peers running this version discard typed/system posts before debounce admission, history construction, session handling, or model invocation. The visible progress label remains configurable and is only a human-facing cue; suppression does not depend on parsing message text.

Existing Mattermost behavior remains the default.

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost progress streaming currently asks one editable post to serve two different purposes:

1. transient operational feedback while the agent works;
2. the durable, authoritative answer after the turn completes.

That coupling is fragile and ambiguous in multi-agent channels. For humans, tool and progress output can look like a real reply. For other agents, an ordinary bot post does not provide a reliable machine-readable distinction between “work in progress” and “actionable final answer.”

The mutable-preview lifecycle has also produced adjacent message-delivery failures:

- #109471: a later tool warning deleted a successfully finalized answer;
- #114589: late verbose output overwrote a finalized answer.

Those specific bugs are already fixed on `main` by #109555. This PR does not replace that fix. Instead, it adds an explicit opt-in delivery contract that avoids making the progress artifact the durable final answer at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opt-in contract is intentionally explicit because delivery ordering and typed-post isolation are observable interoperability guarantees in multi-agent Mattermost channels. The implementation keeps the existing default, reuses the normal durable send path, and scopes the new behavior to Mattermost rather than changing shared draft-stream semantics.

## User Impact

Existing installations are unchanged unless `finalDelivery: "separate"` is enabled. Opted-in installations get one transient typed progress post, a fresh durable final post, cleanup only after final acceptance, preserved failure visibility, and suppression of typed progress before peer-agent dispatch.

## Design precedent

Discord already uses the safer ordering for progress delivery:

1. flush the working draft;
2. deliver the final through a fresh message;
3. delete the progress draft only after the final has landed.

This is necessary on Discord because a fresh `MESSAGE_CREATE` also advances unread state, whereas editing a preview only emits `MESSAGE_UPDATE`.

Mattermost now gains the same delivery invariant, with an additional Mattermost-specific requirement: typed progress isolation for multi-agent conversations.

Discord implementation references:

- [prepare fresh final and defer progress cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b91b1889c2353dd3108f311344ccdbd4dd72517/extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts#L392-L406)
- [delete progress only after accepted final delivery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5b91b1889c2353dd3108f311344ccdbd4dd72517/extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts#L550-L564)

## Mattermost lifecycle

With separate final delivery enabled:

1. OpenClaw creates one typed `custom_openclaw_progress` post.
2. Reasoning summaries and tool activity update that post in place.
3. Before final delivery, queued progress edits are quiesced.
4. The final answer is delivered through the normal durable Mattermost send path.
5. Progress is deleted only after provider-confirmed final visibility.
6. If final delivery fails, sanitized progress remains visible.
7. If cleanup fails after the final was accepted, OpenClaw preserves the final receipt and never sends a duplicate final.
8. Incoming typed/system posts are discarded before debounce admission, preventing transient progress from becoming another agent’s prompt.

Ordinary user messages beginning with the configured label remain actionable because suppression uses the Mattermost post type, not text matching.

## Configuration

```json5
channels: {
  mattermost: {
    streaming: {
      mode: "progress",
      progress: {
        label: "|",
        commandText: "status",
        finalDelivery: "separate",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

`finalDelivery: "in-place"` remains the default, preserving existing installations.

Mattermost preserves its existing account-level streaming replacement contract. `finalDelivery` resolves narrowly (account, then root, then `in-place`); a `finalDelivery`-only account override may use the root mode to activate separate delivery without recursively inheriting unrelated root preview or progress options.

## Latest lifecycle repair

ClawSweeper identified four successful-final boundary gaps across the separate-progress lifecycle, each repaired at its owning boundary.

1. Commit [`15e42366`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/15e4236667560cf08d71d582f4e18a87cf42560e) records provider-accepted source-routed/message-tool delivery before fallible progress cleanup, so a later terminal callback cannot recreate typed `Failed.` progress.
2. Commit [`4d825898`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4d825898bdaf940e70bafc17beadb1e53f772a2b) installs the observed-delivery callback whenever separate progress is active, independently of `toolProgress`, covering reasoning-owned progress with tools disabled.
3. Commit [`08c97b67`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/08c97b67edcef93cee1a9d472a81a5db5036d166) handles the direct final-delivery boundary: when `deliverPayload()` throws `ChannelPartialDeliveryError` after Mattermost has already accepted a visible final, the turn records successful final delivery before clearing progress and preserves the accepted final receipt if cleanup also fails.
4. Commit [`cc48c052`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cc48c052863a8f3345c14ab63b7116054ecb5d28) separates progress quiescing from the final-delivery catch. A provider-accepted progress post with an unreadable receipt can no longer be mistaken for the durable final before the final sender runs. The final remains safe to attempt because the progress stream has already stopped; only evidence from the actual final sender can latch final success, and an actual final-send failure settles as failure.

The fourth repair was developed red-to-green at both the delivery-helper and full-turn boundaries. Before the production change, the helper surfaced the progress receipt error instead of the final-send failure and the full turn recorded zero final sends. After the repair, the final sender runs exactly once, no successful-final latch is recorded for its failure, and terminal failure settlement is attempted.

Prior canary head [`3d1a6e419`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3d1a6e4197b2bcce4b90cd3fc5b6de8a5b1f24c0) rebases the feature onto upstream `main` at [`8160c6e90`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8160c6e90f39f5fb6f89a5dafcdbfb9695909c35). The integration preserves current sender-scoped Mattermost debounce keys and discards typed posts before debounce admission. Generated configuration metadata was regenerated canonically from the integrated tree.

## Evidence

### Human-authored lifecycle continuity (head bd6d8288837d)

A human-authored Mattermost turn exercised head `bd6d8288837d` in an isolated canary with separate final delivery enabled.

- Runtime route: provider `openai`, model `gpt-6-astra`.
- The turn emitted interim reasoning, executed one harmless shell tool successfully, and produced the exact expected final text.
- Runtime timing: session start `21:18:02.960Z`; tool call/result `21:18:08.340Z` / `21:18:08.353Z`; model completion `21:18:12.968Z`; session end `21:18:12.972Z`.
- Mattermost timing: the ordinary durable final was created at `21:18:13.117Z`; provider delivery was logged at `21:18:13.159Z`, 42 ms later.
- The settled thread contains exactly the human root and one ordinary durable final. No active progress, stale failure, or duplicate final remains.
- The private permalink and infrastructure identifiers are intentionally omitted. Deleted transient-post metadata is not retrievable through the canary bot after cleanup; typed-post continuity is therefore supported by the exact-head deterministic regressions and the earlier live evidence below.


### Prior live lifecycle deployment (head 3d1a6e419)

The prior canary head [`3d1a6e4197b2bcce4b90cd3fc5b6de8a5b1f24c0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3d1a6e4197b2bcce4b90cd3fc5b6de8a5b1f24c0) was packaged and deployed only to an isolated single-agent canary. The release tag resolves to that exact commit.

The first two canary attempts did not exercise this PR lifecycle: one used a config-origin plugin that could not register the reserved Codex harness, and the next used a locally packed managed plugin that remained untrusted at the keyed-store boundary. The deployed canary fixes those preconditions with the official npm plugin and a successful real harness turn. prs.title: fix(agents): validate MCP App resource blob encoding before rendering
prs.body:
## Summary

`fix(agents): validate MCP App resource blob as strict base64 and decode it as fatal UTF-8 so malformed payloads are rejected instead of silently rendered`

## What Problem This Solves

When an MCP tool result references a UI resource (`ui://...`), `fetchMcpAppView` reads the resource from the external MCP server and caches the HTML into the in-memory view store for rendering in the sandboxed iframe. For `blob` content (base64, per the MCP spec), the decode path uses Node's **lenient** base64 decoder and a **non-fatal** UTF-8 conversion: invalid base64 characters are silently dropped, and invalid UTF-8 sequences silently become `` replacement characters. The text path, the missing-content path, and both size caps all fail loudly; only the blob's actual encoding is never checked.

The directly reachable case on the real stdio transport: an MCP server returns `blob` that **is** valid base64 (so it passes the MCP SDK's own schema gate) but decodes to bytes that are not valid UTF-8 — a server-side encoding bug, a binary payload mislabeled as HTML, or truncation. Those bytes are converted with U+FFFD replacements and cached as a legitimate app view with **no error anywhere**; the user sees a garbled or blank app and there is nothing to act on. (On the stdio SDK transport, blobs that are not base64 at all are already rejected by the SDK schema — shown in the Evidence trace — so the strict-base64 half of this fix is defense in depth for that boundary; the fatal-UTF-8 half is the reachable repair.)

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts` (main, before this fix):

- `src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts:181` — `Buffer.from(content.blob, "base64")` — Node's decoder ignores invalid characters instead of rejecting them.
- `src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts:185` — `decoded.toString("utf8")` — non-fatal conversion turns invalid sequences into U+FFFD with no signal.
- Compare `packages/media-core/src/base64.ts` — `canonicalizeBase64` is the repo's shared validating canonicalizer (alphabet, padding, pad bits), already used for camera/media payloads.

Minimal reproduction: serve `blob: <base64 of 0xFF 0xFE 0xFD 0x80>` from a real stdio MCP server and run the real `fetchMcpAppView` over the real session MCP runtime — the view is accepted and the cached `html` is `""`. See the Evidence section below.

## Root Cause

- The lenient decode predates the current history root (the file arrives unchanged at the boundary).
- Violated invariant: untrusted external input entering the persistence/rendering pipeline must be validated for encoding validity, not just for size. `Buffer.from(x, "base64")` and `buf.toString("utf8")` are lossy, non-validating APIs — the two existing size caps bound *how much* data comes in but say nothing about *whether* it is what it claims to be.
- Trigger condition: any MCP server returning `mimeType: "text/html;profile=mcp-app"` with a `blob` whose decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8 (reachable today), or — on runtimes without the SDK schema gate — content that is not well-formed base64 at all.

## Why This Fix

- Option A (chosen): validate with the repo's shared `canonicalizeBase64` (whitespace-tolerant, accepts valid **unpadded** input, checks pad bits — no custom regex to drift) and decode with `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })`. On failure, throw inside `decodeResourceHtml`, which `fetchMcpAppView` already converts into a logged warning plus a rejected view (`undefined`) — the same failure mode as oversized/mistyped resources. Empty blobs (`blob: ""`) remain valid (zero bytes), exactly as on main and as in the adjacent empty-`text` path.
- Option B: keep the lenient decode but validate the result heuristically (e.g. "must contain `<`") — rejected: content sniffing is guesswork; the encoding itself is the contract and can be checked exactly.
- Option C: hand-rolled strict base64 regex (padded-only) — rejected during review: it rejects valid unpadded input that the shared canonicalizer accepts, and duplicates logic the repo already maintains in `media-core`.

## User Impact

- Affected scenario: MCP App servers that return malformed `blob` resource content (server bugs, mislabeled binary payloads, proxies, hand-rolled servers).
- Before: base64 of non-UTF-8 bytes is cached as U+FFFD-mangled HTML and rendered in the sandboxed iframe with zero diagnostics.
- After: view preparation fails with a clear logged warning (`MCP App resource blob is not valid base64` / `not valid UTF-8`) and no view is rendered.
- Behavior change: none for well-formed servers — padded, unpadded, and empty valid blobs behave exactly as before (all three covered by controls in tests and in the transport proof).

## Evidence

No mocked modules and no structural stand-ins: the proof spawns a **real raw-JSON-RPC stdio MCP server** process and connects through the repository's **real session MCP runtime** (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → stdio transport → `runtime.readResource`), then calls the real `fetchMcpAppView`. The server logs every inbound JSON-RPC message, producing the stdio resource-read trace shown inline. Scenarios: S1 raw-HTML `blob` (not base64 at all), S2 base64 of invalid-UTF-8 bytes (the reachable bug), S3 empty-`blob` control, S4 padded valid control, S5 unpadded valid control. `mcp-ui-resource.ts` is byte-identical between the main checkout used below and the current PR base.

### Before (on main)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-mcp-app-blob-transport.mjs   # main: lenient base64 + non-fatal utf8
S1 raw-HTML blob (malformed base64): view REJECTED -> OK      # rejected upstream by the MCP SDK schema gate
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app
S2 invalid-UTF-8 blob: view ACCEPTED html="" -> BAD   # passes the SDK gate, silently mangled by main's decoder
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
S3 empty blob control: view ACCEPTED html="" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
S4 padded valid control: view ACCEPTED html="<html>blob demo</html>" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
S5 unpadded valid control: view ACCEPTED html="<html>blob demo</html>" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
BEHAVIOR: FAIL - malformed MCP App blobs are accepted and/or valid blobs break
exit=1
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx proof-mcp-app-blob-transport.mjs   # HEAD: canonicalizeBase64 + fatal UTF-8 decode
S1 raw-HTML blob (malformed base64): view REJECTED -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app
[mcp-app] failed to prepare ui://proof/app from "proof": MCP App resource blob is not valid UTF-8
S2 invalid-UTF-8 blob: view REJECTED -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app
S3 empty blob control: view ACCEPTED html="" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
S4 padded valid control: view ACCEPTED html="<html>blob demo</html>" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
S5 unpadded valid control: view ACCEPTED html="<html>blob demo</html>" -> OK
   stdio trace: recv resources/read uri=ui://proof/app | recv resources/list
BEHAVIOR: PASS - malformed blobs rejected over real stdio MCP transport; empty/unpadded/padded valid blobs unchanged
exit=0
```

## Tests and Validation

- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts` -- 28/28 tests passed, including the regression tests `rejects blob content that is not valid base64` (raw HTML, `!!!!`, bad pad bits, `%4==1` length), `rejects blob content that is not valid UTF-8`, `preserves valid empty base64 blobs`, and `decodes valid base64 blob content, including unpadded input`, alongside the existing view-store suite.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.ts src/agents/mcp-ui-resource.test.ts` passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Manual verification (the proof above):
  1. On main, base64 of invalid-UTF-8 bytes passes the SDK schema gate and is silently cached as `` with no error -- FAIL.
  2. With the fix, the same payload is rejected with a logged warning, while empty, padded-valid, and unpadded-valid blobs are byte-identical to main -- PASS.

Note: proof and tests were run with Node 24.19.0; the stdio MCP server is a ~70-line raw JSON-RPC process written into a temp dir by the proof itself, and its trace log is printed inline above.

prs.title: fix(compaction): stop a large input reserve from inflating summary output cost
prs.body:
Fixes #119404

## What Problem This Solves

A raised compaction reserve can turn safeguard-mode staged summaries into disproportionately large model-output requests. The original generic agent-core cap was too broad: it changed budgets owned by callers outside safeguard mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained-summary policy belongs at the safeguard boundary. The safeguard caps only the reserve passed into its built-in `summarizeInStages()` path at 20,000 tokens; generic `generateSummary()` and split-turn `compact()` calculations continue to use the reserve supplied by their caller, subject only to the model output limit.

## User Impact

- Safeguard sessions with `reserveTokens=80,000` authorize a 16,000-token staged-summary request rather than allowing output to scale with the raised reserve.
- Generic agent-core callers retain caller-owned raised-reserve authorization: 64,000 for ordinary summaries and `[64,000, 40,000]` for split turns on the large-output test model.
- This intentionally changes persisted safeguard sessions above 20,000 only; it does not alter generic or split-turn caller budgets.

## Evidence

### Merge of current main (2026-10-11)

- Head `9ac491304b8` had become `CONFLICTING` again: #167916 replaced staged summaries with one bounded `summarizeCompactionHistory()` request and removed the old `summarizeInStages` dropped-history test next to the reserve rows.
- New head: `2ffdc3c48ed` (merge of `main` at `4e3707f634c`, then one comment-only commit). Only the test file conflicted. The removed test stays removed; the `cap-model-limit` and `cap-staged-limit` rows now assert through `mockSummarizeCompactionHistory`.
- Production change: unchanged. `resolveSummaryReserveTokens()` still caps the safeguard reserve at 20,000; its comment now says "summary requests" instead of "staged summaries".
- The accepted proof's arithmetic still holds on current `main`. The safeguard passes `resolveSummaryReserveTokens(preparation.settings.reserveTokens, model)` as `reserveTokens` to both `summarizeCompactionHistory()` calls; that reserve reaches agent-core `generateSummary()` through the sessions wrapper, which still authorizes `Math.floor((turn-prefix ? 0.5 : 0.8) * reserveTokens)` output tokens. #167916's input bound (`resolveSummaryInputChars()`) starts from the fixed `MAX_SUMMARY_INPUT_CHARS` and lowers it only when the model window cannot hold it next to the completion reservation, so the lower reserve never reduces summary input.
- Local validation on this head:

```text
# production file restored to current main, tests from this PR
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts
x summarizes with provider-prepared model settings: cap-staged-limit
AssertionError: expected 80000 to be 20000
Tests  1 failed | 66 passed (67)

# this PR
compaction-safeguard.test.ts: 67 passed
compaction-summary-output-budget.test.ts, compaction.test.ts, summarization-input-budget.test.ts: 73 passed

node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main
every lane passed (including typecheck core, typecheck core tests, line-cap and max-lines ratchets)
except the full-tree Knip dead-export scan, which reports existing src/agents/model-auth*.ts exports
outside this diff and nothing in the changed files
```

In `compaction-summary-output-budget.test.ts`, the real agent-core `generateSummary()` with a capturing stream turns a 20,000 reserve into a 16,000-token request and keeps generic callers at 64,000 for an 80,000 reserve. With the `cap-staged-limit` row, that is the accepted Anthropic chain (`reserve_in=80000 -> staged_reserve=20000 -> max_tokens=16000`) on this head. This is proof equivalence, not a new live provider run.

Earlier sections describe earlier heads and are kept for history.

### Rebase onto current main

- The previous head `87ba36cb11d4212a083849fd0a8ab9c91c487747` was `CONFLICTING` with current `main`, which rewrote the existing reserve test in `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` around its `configuredSession` and `createCompactionEvent` helpers.
- Rebased head: `244d12d98cb56e39b7a058a9bac272896d15fcf1`, parent `0c8e56cf9859f1be33edacf199f353d4db417b5b` (current `main`).
- Production change: the same 20,000-token ceiling on the reserve the safeguard passes to `summarizeInStages()`, now written inside the existing `requested` line of `resolveSummaryReserveTokens()`. `compaction-safeguard.ts` is already over its line cap on current `main` (1,283 counted lines, cap 700), and the line-cap ratchet rejects any growth, so the previous named constant and wrapped expression failed `check-changed` (1,283 -> 1,287). The expression is unchanged apart from the constant becoming `20_000`, so the reserve passed to `summarizeInStages()` is identical for every input.
- Tests: the existing model-limit test and the new ceiling case are now one `it.each` in `main`'s current helper style. Row 1 keeps the existing test name and still proves the model clamp (model limit 4,000 below the ceiling, reserve 8,000 -> 4,000). Row 2 proves the ceiling (reserve 80,000 with a 128,000 model limit -> 20,000). The generic caller-budget tests stay in `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-summary-output-budget.test.ts`.
- Not carried forward: the previous head's supplemental mocked end-to-end test (`runs raised-reserve safeguard compaction with capped output and recovery`). `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` is also over its line cap on current `main`, so that test would fail the same ratchet. Row 2 keeps the ceiling asserted at the safeguard boundary, and the recorded real Anthropic run below covers the end-to-end budget.

### Merge of current main (2026-10-04)

- Head `244d12d98cb` had become `CONFLICTING` again: `main` folded the reserve test into its table test `summarizes with provider-prepared model settings` in `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts`.
- New head: `028be472538` (merge of current `main`, then one test-only commit). The production change is unchanged.
- Tests: the two reserve cases are now rows `cap-model-limit` (model limit 4,000, reserve 8,000 -> 4,000) and `cap-staged-limit` (model limit 128,000, reserve 80,000 -> 20,000) of `main`'s table test. The file stays at 2,342 lines, the same as `main`, so the line-cap ratchet sees no growth.
- Local validation on this head:

```text

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts
x summarizes with provider-prepared model settings: cap-staged-limit
AssertionError: expected 80000 to be 20000
Tests  1 failed | 74 passed (75)   (45 s wall)

compaction-summary-output-budget.test.ts: 4 passed
```

The sections below describe the earlier rebased head and are kept for history; test names and counts there predate this merge.

### Local validation (rebased head)

- `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction-summary-output-budget.test.ts`: 16 s wall (Vitest 3.06 s, 4 tests).

### Staged-compaction performance (before/after)

Hermetic local benchmark, since no live provider run is available here. The real safeguard handler and the real `summarizeInStages()` compact a 24-message history of about 576,000 characters with `reserveTokens=80,000` on a 200,000-context, 128,000-output model. The provider is a local stream that writes up to its authorization (about 4 characters per authorized token), so the output size follows the budget the safeguard grants. Each side ran one warm-up and five measured compactions in a fresh Vitest process, and only `compaction-safeguard.ts` differed between the runs (current `main` vs this PR). The host load average was 22 to 32 during the runs.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): stalled media downloads block inbound messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp messages getting stuck when an attachment starts downloading but stops producing data.

## User Impact

After 30 seconds without another media chunk, the message continues with the existing attachment-unavailable fallback. Downloads that keep making progress are not subject to a total-duration deadline. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the timeout and teardown in the WhatsApp plugin. Baileys returns a decrypting stream piped from its HTTP response; releasing just that stream leaves the HTTP source open. The fix closes both sources on timeout or early media-store refusal, preserving current direct/quoted identity, normalization, byte limits and fallbacks.

This continues Pick-cat's original work in this PR. The separate retry-policy proposal in #117719 is not included.

## Evidence

- The real production inbound enrichment path, installed Baileys 7.0.0-rc14 download/decryption, media writer and encrypted loopback HTTP were exercised on Node 24.19.0 in an isolated AWS Crabbox.
- Current-main control remained pending after 31 seconds. The earlier helper timed out but left the real upstream HTTP source open.
- Fixed direct and quoted stalls returned their expected fallbacks after about 30 seconds, closed the sources and removed partial files. A subsequent healthy direct/quoted message recovered 65,536 exact plaintext bytes each.
- A progressing transfer completed after 32 seconds; byte-limit refusal cleaned its partial file. Zero unhandled rejections and zero live transport sockets remained before fixture teardown.
- The focused owner suite passed 18/18 with zero skips. After a test-only lint normalization, both touched cases passed again (the other 16 were intentionally unselected).
- Formatting, lint, both maintained extension type lanes and the complete selected guard plan passed. Independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- Qualified head: `ab8160fd6a3acafcfaa7a51d23d08cca2669fe10`; hosted exact-head CI and native landing are tracked on this PR.

[Real transport run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1476018ba25f) · [Before/negative controls](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5f804a624113)

The transport and Baileys implementation were real; the server, keys and messages were synthetic. No paired WhatsApp session or WhatsApp cloud service was used. AI-assisted integration and verification.

prs.title: fix(msteams): proactive sends fail after conversation migration
prs.body:
Closes #94939.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users could lose proactive Bot Framework sends after 6.x state migration when legacy conversation references were not visible under the canonical conversation IDs used by the runtime.

The affected source may already have been archived, including as a rotated `.migrated.N` snapshot. Without recovery, the bot cannot send proactively to those conversations until it receives a new message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams Doctor migration now verifies canonical plugin-state rows before archiving a non-empty active source. It stores references under the embedded canonical conversation ID, leaves an unsafe active source in place with an actionable warning, and recovers missing canonical rows from preserved `.migrated` and numeric `.migrated.N` archives.

Archive recovery is newest-first, accepts only references with the minimum proactive-send shape (Connector URL plus user and bot/agent identities), deduplicates aliases by canonical conversation ID before retention, never overwrites an already-present canonical row, and preserves every recovery archive. Unusable record-shaped entries therefore cannot consume retention capacity or displace valid references. Empty sources and successfully verified migrations keep the existing archive behavior.

## User Impact

Teams users and operators retain or recover conversation references needed for proactive sends after migration. The repair remains scoped to the Teams-owned Doctor migration and does not add a runtime compatibility fallback. Recovered references still pass through the existing proactive-send authority boundary; blocked Bot Framework service hosts are removed and rejected before SDK loading or Connector activity creation.

## Evidence

Exact head: `d24343e627ad2a3d30f2c3b5a87fa20e29f3cfc6`

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/send-context.test.ts`: 3 files / 45 tests passed.
- The migration regression alone passes 16/16, including canonical alias deduplication and recovery from a valid sibling archive when a newer archive contains `null`.
- The proactive authority regression proves a blocked stored service URL is removed and rejected before `loadMSTeamsSdkWithAuth` or Bot Framework `createActivity` is called.
- A cap-pressure regression proves a record with a Connector URL and user but no bot/agent identity cannot consume one of the 1,000 retained slots and evict the canonical valid reference.
- A redacted disposable-state proof on this exact head recovered the canonical SQLite row from `.migrated.2`, confirmed the legacy outer key was absent and the archive preserved, then completed one repository private-QA loopback Bot Framework Connector request with matching conversation/payload and returned message ID `qa-outbound-f4d5cd6f-c055-42e5-a812-e3fe482f4de1`. No external message or credential was used.
- Targeted oxfmt and oxlint: passed.
- Assertion-safety ratchet: passed after shrinking the stale Teams Doctor allowance from 7 to 6.
- `git diff --check`: passed; `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.
- Fresh structured autoreview of the integrated branch: clean, no actionable findings (0.98 confidence).
- Fresh structured autoreviews of all follow-up fixes: clean, no actionable findings (0.98-0.99 confidence).
- Local HEAD, fork ref, GraphQL `headRefOid`, and REST `.head.sha` all match the exact head above; the canonical worktree is clean and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. On final-head CI, Exact-head CI is running for the new validated head.

Earlier redacted Doctor recovery-to-proactive-send proof used disposable state and the repository's real Bot Framework HTTP client with its loopback Connector (no external message or credential). It proved canonical lookup, wrong-key absence, newest-archive precedence, archive preservation, a matching Connector round trip, and a returned message ID. The final head adds the requested archive-collision, malformed-data, authority-path, and current-main integration repairs on top of that behavior.

---

Migration note: This PR replaces #98862 with the same original published head, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #98862.
