prs.title: fix(security): prevent unsafe approval patterns from hanging command authorization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approval, cron, and plugin model argPattern values can use nested alternation or adjacent overlapping repeats such as a*a*...b or (a|b)*(b|c)*z. Those patterns hang the JavaScript regex engine (catastrophic backtracking) and can freeze command authorization. A zero-minimum separator (?, {0,n}, or *) can be omitted, so a*x?a* and a*x*a* are still adjacent on that path. The shared safe-regex compiler must reject those shapes, including complete branch unions, without banning required separators (a*xa*), disjoint optionals (a*x?b*), JWT-style {10,}.{10,} redact patterns, or safe Unicode class pairs used by group mentions.

Non-alternating grouped sequences such as (ab)*(cb)* must keep their complete languages. Reducing a group to its last token made (ab)* and (cb)* look like b vs b, so a safe pattern that should match abcb was rejected. Wrapping groups still flatten inner unions so ((a|b))*((b|c))* stays rejected.

Equal character-class twins such as corp-[A-Z]+[A-Z]+ are valid custom redaction patterns. Tightening adjacent-repeat checks on the shared compiler would drop those patterns from redactSensitiveText. Shared compileSafeRegex keeps those twins. Exec stays fail-closed so they cannot hang command authorization.

Braced Unicode \u{hex} is a code point only when flags include u or v. Without those flags, \u{2} is identity u plus {2}, so ^(\u{2}|u)+$ is overlapping (uu|u)+ and must be rejected.

Disjoint mixed alternatives of equal consumed length such as ab|[c]d must stay accepted. An unconditional mixed-structure fallback treated corp-(ab|[c]d)+ as overlapping even though both branches consume two characters and are disjoint. That dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^(ab|[c]d)+$. Shared analysis now compares equal-length atom sequences. Exec stays fail-closed on unsafe overlap such as (aa|a.)+ and (a+)+.

The mixed extractor must not treat every simple token as one consumed character. No-flag \141 is octal a and \x61 is hex a, so ^(\141\x61|aaaa)+$ is overlapping (aa|aaaa)+. Splitting \141 into \1, 4, 1 made 4 versus a look disjoint and let that ReDoS reach native matching. Decode complete escapes, or mark unknown-width atoms unproven, before positional disjointness.

Safe capturing wrappers such as ((ab)|(cd))+ must stay accepted. Both branches are fixed-width and disjoint. Treating group tokens as unknown overlap dropped corp-((ab)|(cd))+ from custom redaction and let Doctor delete ^((ab)|(cd))+$. Unwrap those groups. Conservative uncertainty is not grounds for deletion.

Decoded scalars must keep literal identity when overlap probing re-parses them as regex source. \x24 is `$`, not an end-anchor, so ^(\x24a|[$]a)+$ must reject. `\.` is a literal dot, not a wildcard, so corp-(\.a|[b]a)+ must stay accepted and still mask. Legacy octal first digit 4-7 consumes at most two digits, so \400 is \40 plus literal 0 and ^(\400| 0)+$ must reject.

Two-digit and three-digit numeric escapes are backreferences when that capture exists. The two-digit high-octal rule treated \40 as space even with 40 capturing groups, so ^ + 39 empty groups + (a)(\40b|abab)+$ compared space-plus-b with abab and accepted. Native JavaScript repeats overlapping ab|abab. Count captures before decoding decimal escapes, or keep potentially valid backreferences unproven. Same for three-digit \141 when capture 141 exists.

Escaped dollars in alternatives are literals. corp-(a\$|b[!])+ is a safe disjoint two-char pair. Stripping the final `$` from a\$ left a dangling escape, so atom extraction failed and the fallback rejected. Redaction then stopped masking corp-a$b!, and Doctor deleted the equivalent approval. Strip only actual anchor tokens.

Safe nested alternatives such as corp-((ab|cd)e|(fg|hi)j)+ have disjoint fixed-width languages (abe, cde, fgj, hij). Atom extraction used to return null at the inner `|` and the overlap fallback marked the outer `+` unsafe. Custom redaction then dropped the pattern, and Doctor deleted the equivalent anchored approval. Expand inner group alternatives into finite sequences so those languages stay accepted.

Unequal-length alternatives are not ReDoS by length alone. ^(a|[b]c)+$ safely matches abc because the first characters are disjoint, so repetition is unambiguous. An unconditional unequal-length return labeled that rule unsafe, so exec denied it and Doctor deleted it. Check prefix disjointness first. Prefix overlap such as (a|aa)+ still rejects.

Property escapes are flag-dependent. Without u or v, \p{L} is identity p plus {L}, so ^(\p{L}a|p\{L\}ap\{L\}a)+$ is overlapping (p{L}a|p{L}ap{L}a)+. Tokenizing \p{L} as one Unicode atom and probing it with u compared a versus { and accepted that hang. Decode property escapes with the actual flags before positional comparison.

Analysis budget exhaustion is not the same as an unsafe pattern. The 32-atom cap used to abort extraction for ^([a] + 32 b's | [c] + 32 d's)+$ even though the first characters are disjoint. Keep truncated prefixes so proven-disjoint languages stay accepted. Equal-length truncated prefixes that already overlap, such as 33 versus 66 copies of [a]a{32}, are proven overlap and must reject.

Decoded non-ASCII scalars must keep that identity in the selected probe mode. Flag selection removes u, so emitting \u{e9} made ^(\u00E9a|[é]a)+$ look disjoint. Emit \xNN or \uXXXX instead.

The 16-sequence expansion cap is unproven, not overlap. ^((a|b|c|d|e|f|g|h|i|j|k|l|m|n|o|p|q)x|zx)+$ is disjoint fixed-width. Returning unsafe at that cap dropped custom redaction and let Doctor delete the stored rule. Returning no-overlap at that cap is also wrong: ^((a|...|q)x|axax)+$ never compared ax with axax, so repeating ax plus a failing suffix reached native matching. Collapse single-atom unions so the 17-way |x versus zx rule stays accepted and the axax prefix language still rejects. Leftover overflow is not permission to execute.

Incomplete equal prefixes are not proven overlap. p=[a] plus 31 a's, then p+b versus p+c, is fixed-width disjoint. Both truncated to the same 32 atoms. Unconditional true deleted that stored rule and dropped custom redaction. Keep a stored continuation atom so b versus c stays disjoint, while 33 versus 66 overlapping [a]a{32} prefixes still reject.

Shared Unicode atoms must be compared as languages. A class containing U+0100 versus a U+0100 literal (each followed by ASCII a, then repeated) share that code point, but the finite probe set never visits it, so first positions looked disjoint and redaction compiled it. Probe characters named by each atom. Disjoint [猫]|[犬] stays accepted on the shared compiler. Exec's stricter unprobed fallback does not protect redaction.

Overlap probes must inherit the s flag. ^(.a|\na\na)+$ with s lets dot consume newline, so the branches overlap. Comparing them without s declared them disjoint.

Exec approvals keep a stricter unprobed-Unicode fail-closed helper that is not part of the public plugin SDK. Runtime still refuses those conservative patterns. Doctor --fix must not delete a stored manual rule that the shared compiler accepts. Only unsafe or invalid entries are removed. Detect must not create or migrate shared approval state.

The same persisted allowlist is also evaluated by the native macOS app. Node and JavaScriptCore share compileExecArgPattern.

Ref #90014

## Evidence


Latest head [`01fb611710d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01fb611710dc053b65805ba24663fea7d02a7036). Isolated worktree `/tmp/oc-82950`. Shared compiler keeps disjoint overflow `^((aa|bb|...|qq)|zz)+$` and mixed class `^([0\p{Script=Greek}]|[1])+$` with `u`. Exec still refuses those (Doctor-conservative). Overlapping `\p{L}` vs `[0\p{Script=Greek}]` still rejects. Native `ExecArgPatternSafetyJS.generated.swift` regenerated. `pnpm check:exec-arg-pattern:swift` exits 0.


Live production proof on isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR (not ~/.openclaw). Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, redactSensitiveText, collectRejectedExecArgPatterns, and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns.

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC HOME=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC node --import tsx /tmp/proof-82950-rev83.mjs
STATE_DIR /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
COMPILE
two-char-overflow shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition execArg=unsafe-nested-repetition
seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted execArg=accepted
greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
e-acute shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
nested-plus shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
ALLOWLIST two-char-overflow refused
ALLOWLIST seventeen matched
ALLOWLIST truncated-disjoint-32 matched
REDACT two-char-overflow id=corp-axaxax
REDACT seventeen id=corp-ax***
REDACT truncated-disjoint-32 id=corp-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabaaaaaa…aaac
REDACT greek-letter id=corp-αaαa
DOCTOR removed 2 /bin/unsafe,/bin/two-char-overflow
DOCTOR remaining /bin/seventeen-way /bin/truncated-disjoint /bin/truncated-disjoint-32 /bin/long-disjoint /bin/safe
```

Two-character expansion overflow stays refused and visible in redaction. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint suffixes still mask and stay stored. Letter versus Script=Greek under u stays refused. 17-way, truncated 31, long disjoint, and nested plus keep their prior outcomes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Shared compilation no longer treats incomplete equal prefixes as proven overlap, no longer treats expansion overflow as safe, and no longer declares unobserved Unicode property languages disjoint.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node v26.8.2, OpenClaw worktree on fix/exec-approval-redos-guard at b8d332b9bbe, isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-82950-state-iJFEBC (not ~/.openclaw).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Set OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR to a fresh temp directory. Called production compileSafeRegexDetailed, compileSafeRegexForExec, compileExecArgPattern, matchAllowlist, and redactSensitiveText on the three remaining cases plus the keep set (17-way, truncated 31, é, truncated 33 versus 66, s flag, nested plus). Seeded persisted exec approvals through production saveExecApprovals, then ran production collectRejectedExecArgPatterns and repairRejectedExecArgPatterns. Command: node --import tsx /tmp/proof-82950-rev83.mjs from the patched worktree.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the isolated production run:

  ```console
  STATE_DIR .../oc-82950-state-iJFEBC
  two-char-overflow shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  seventeen-way shared=accepted exec=accepted
  truncated-disjoint-32 shared=accepted exec=accepted
  greek-letter-u shared=unsafe-nested-repetition exec=unsafe-nested-repetition
  truncated-overlap shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  e-acute shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  nested-plus shared=unsafe-nested-repetition
  ALLOWLIST two-char-overflow refused
  ALLOWLIST seventeen matched
  ALLOWLIST truncated-disjoint-32 matched
  REDACT two-char-overflow id=corp-axaxax
  REDACT seventeen id=corp-ax***
  REDACT truncated-disjoint-32 id=corp-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaabaaaaaa…aaac
  REDACT greek-letter id=corp-αaαa
  DOCTOR removed 2 /bin/unsafe,/bin/two-char-overflow
  DOCTOR remaining /bin/seventeen-way /bin/truncated-disjoint /bin/truncated-disjoint-32 /bin/long-disjoint /bin/safe
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Two-character expansion overflow no longer authorizes `axax`. Incomplete 32-repeat prefixes with disjoint `b`/`c` suffixes stay stored and still mask. Unprobed Letter versus Script=Greek overlap no longer compiles as disjoint under `u`. Nested plus, é overlap, and truncated 33 versus 66 still refuse.
- **What was not tested:** Live click-through in the shipping menu-bar app against a private production allowlist. A published npm release upgrade on a user machine. Current native JavaScriptCore matching of this HEAD.

## Summary

Fixes remaining Revision 83 P1s: reject two-character expansion overflow ((ax|...|qx)|axax)+, keep truncated equal prefixes p+b versus p+c after 32 atoms, and fail closed when Unicode property languages are not both observed so Letter versus Script=Greek with u rejects without banning [猫]|[犬]. Prior 17-way accept, long disjoint accept, é overlap reject, truncated 33 versus 66 reject, s flag overlap reject, and (a+)+ reject still hold. Native matcher still shares compileExecArgPattern. Detect stays read-only. Repair stays on updateExecApprovalsSync.

prs.title: fix(pr): merged receipts stay unrecorded when auto-merge lands a pushed head
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native landing wrapper leaves a merged PR's retained outcome at `phase: intent` forever when GitHub auto-merge lands a head that was pushed after the auto request was armed.

GitHub's `--match-head-commit` precondition only applies at submission. A collaborator push after the accepted auto request keeps auto-merge enabled, and GitHub merges the pushed head. Afterwards `scripts/pr merge-run <PR>` (reconciliation), `merge-recover ... --cancel-auto`, and `merge-complete` all refuse: the retained intent head no longer equals the merged head, so the receipt can never be recorded and the operator has to clean the worktree and `pr-<PR>*` branches by hand. This happened on 2026-10-11 with #168651 (auto armed at `65f879f610cf`, maintainer pushed a merge-of-main head `fa4f746dacfd`, GitHub squash-merged it as `4754d394130a`).

## User Impact

User impact: maintainers can record the verified receipt for exactly this case with one explicit, investigated command and then finish `merge-complete`/cleanup natively:

```
scripts/pr merge-recover <PR> <OUTCOME_OID> --confirmed-operator-recovery --merged-head <SHA>
```

Reconciliation now also prints that exact command when it observes the drift. Every other drift keeps its refusal: identity, base, method, non-descendant or unselected heads, OPEN/CLOSED PRs, unaccepted intents, retired or uncertain-retirement requests, queue/immediate/admin routes, stale OIDs, and unreachable or mismatched landed commits. Outcome refs are never cleared; nothing is dispatched, cancelled, or re-armed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The route accepts only an accepted non-queue `auto` intent without a cancellation record, a MERGED PR with the retained identity and base, an explicitly selected merged head that equals GitHub's authoritative head and strictly descends from the retained head, a landed commit reachable from authoritative main, and a landed tree that reconstructs under the retained method. It writes one successor through the existing CAS ancestry: `phase: merged`, `landed`, and `headDrift { actor, outcome, mergedHead }`, retaining the merged head object as a parent. `head` stays the prepared intent head, so every existing invariant on it keeps holding; receipt comparisons use the merged head. The completion comment names both heads.

Shared change: the landed-receipt verification moved into one helper used by reconciliation and the new route, and squash receipts now require a single-parent landed commit. GitHub never squashes into a multi-parent commit, and this is what makes "retained method matches" checkable when the merge commit would otherwise reconstruct to the same tree.

## Evidence

New suite `test/scripts/pr-merge-head-drift.test.ts` drives the real Bash wrapper through the shared gh/git fixture harness: the incident end to end (drift refusal with the printed recovery command, refused cancel-auto and merge-complete, accepted receipt, stale-OID refusal, reconciliation, GC durability of the retained merged head, completion comment naming both heads) plus 13 refused variants (stale OID, same head, unselected head, identity, base, OPEN, non-descendant head, merge-commit shape under a squash intent, mismatched tree, landed commit not on main, confirmed cancellation, unaccepted intent, immediate route).

Local runs, one file at a time with `--maxWorkers=1` on a shared Mac at load ~16–20 (CI baselines for the sibling files are ~120–160 s):

| File | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-head-drift.test.ts` | 14 passed | 111.9 s |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-outcome.test.ts` | 54 passed | 508 s |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-receipt.test.ts` | 43 passed | 428 s |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-recovery.test.ts` | 43 passed | 513 s |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-completion.test.ts` | 16 passed | 184 s |
| `test/scripts/pr-merge-auto-recovery.test.ts` | 14 passed | 198 s |
| `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.source-owners.test.ts` | 32 passed | 51 s |
| `test/scripts/vitest-pr-exempt-retention.test.ts` | 3 passed | 19 s |

Also: `bash -n` on the three shell files including `/bin/bash` 3.2; shellcheck shows no new findings against the pre-change baseline; `oxfmt --check` and a targeted `tsgo` typecheck of the new test and harness pass; `git diff --check` clean. Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P2) returned scoped-clean.

Not done here: the live recovery of #168651's retained record. That ref lives on the operator machine that ran the landing; once this ships, `scripts/pr merge-run 168651` prints the exact `--merged-head fa4f746dacfd…` command for it.

prs.title: fix(config): report write-safety refusals during dry runs
prs.body:
Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.
- Conflict-resolved candidate: original seven-file shard, all 87 tests passed; the named test took 12.338 s. Config CLI and writer suites passed 202 tests (34 integration, 65 CLI, 103 writer), 67.86 s combined runner wall time; integration file 27.12 s Vitest wall time.

The original CI timeout remains unattributed. These passing replays are not presented as a timeout fix; no retry logic, longer deadlines, weakened assertions, or speculative production changes were added. The subsequent CI run [38082056748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082056748) passed all 86 jobs on `64e6949e85a3`; this is prior-head evidence.

Final local validation on `64e6949e85a3`: types, targeted lint, formatting, and all remaining selected guards pass. The aggregate check stops at 17 Knip findings; the same canonical scan on a separately installed, clean `0c94b6966078` worktree reproduces the identical set (15 authentication/runtime exports, one Solid lint export, one UI test-helper export). They are inherited rather than introduced by this PR.



### Review guidance and async conflict follow-up

Commit `3687439fae0` reuses `createConfigWriteSafetyRejectionError` for actionable recovery guidance in both JSON and text previews, retaining the size-drop reason. The existing registered-command case failed before the message repair and now verifies both output formats and unchanged config/files. No new test fixture or production abstraction was added.

Integrated main `c6d71fae0ed` to resolve the writer conflict from #168481: topology preparation is now asynchronous, so the preview and writer await it and the shared payload type consumes its resolved value.

Validation: 202 tests passed across config CLI integration (34), CLI (65), and writer (103); 101.20 s runner wall time. Integration-file Vitest wall time: 46.38 s. No hosted CI timing for this new head yet.

Final local checks: production types, all core-test type groups, scoped lint, formatting, and the selected ratchets passed. The aggregate changed check stops at four Knip unused exports outside the PR diff: `stripClaudeCliGeneratedUserPrefixes`, `createChannelApprovalHandlerAsync`, `GitHubConnectionsContent`, and `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files match the integrated base; no clean-base Knip replay was run for this head. These findings remain recorded, not suppressed.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: refactor(memory): move index publication writes into workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory index managers retain writable host handles, and shadow rebuild setup can create or mutate SQLite on the host despite worker-backed publication.

## User Impact

Published Memory index readers are physically read-only and retire with their agent owner. Index schema, vectors, metadata, embedding cache, shadow creation, and shadow WAL cleanup execute in the existing publication worker. Rebuild and recovery behavior, stored bytes, and update compatibility are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manager retains the same publication owner for a shadow database from creation through mutation and cleanup. Accepted writes keep their existing settlement and lost-reply handling. The backend preserves synchronous cleanup for borrowed connections and awaited teardown for connections it owns; changing that lifetime distinction would retire a borrowed worker prematurely. Native coordination locks and explicit offline repair retain their own contracts.

Successful vector setup is reused for subsequent writes with the same dimensions. The metadata already read at sync startup invalidates that fact when another manager publishes different dimensions or an empty rebuild. This avoids repeated worker setup without adding a query, shared registry, or cross-thread handshake. Scalar index commands now use the existing single-command publication route, and TEMP input tables are allocated only for staged row transfer. Ordinary borrowed bindings read only the two connection policies they use; full policy capture remains explicit. No-op vector commands return before extension setup. This removes unused work without adding a policy cache.

## Evidence

Recorded pre-restack diff: production +712/−494 lines and tests +475/−246.

The recorded import/callgraph audit traces published readers, shadow creation/WAL/cleanup, and index mutation commands to their physical owners. Three review rounds resolved accepted findings; subsequent correction reviews passed at P0/P1. Read-only/lifetime fixtures seed through explicit writers, drain before retirement, and inspect persisted data through scoped readers after manager closure.

The negative control with dimension caching but without metadata invalidation failed after a separate maintenance manager published an empty rebuild: the next write encountered a missing vector table. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 21 tests with invalidation in place (281.28 seconds command wall time, 11.63 seconds for the new case). The follow-up passed P0/P1 review with no findings.

<!-- FINAL_GATE_EVIDENCE -->
Validation spans recorded revisions, with source comparisons for reused results. These are historical results from before the stack was rebuilt on placement/approval; final assembled/merged-head checks are pending. The corrected scalar/borrowed-connection suite passed 41 tests across two files in 115.16 seconds at `eb8648bddde0d1d47db9588487f741faea605823`. Seven focused Memory files previously passed 98 tests in 191.238 seconds, with source comparisons supporting reuse for unaffected behavior. GitHub CI seconds are not recorded here; these durations are command wall time.

The previous stack's selected `check:changed` checks were covered by recorded runs and affected-delta reruns: core, extension, script, and root-test types; 27 core-test type shards; lint, formatting, docs, compatibility and architecture guards. Before the six-file Memory correction, the affected core-test graph passed in 1,667.81 seconds, core production types in 63.48 seconds, and Madge in 20.45 seconds with zero cycles. The missing-`rg` machine prerequisite was repaired before inventory and the worker-call ratchet passed. All four recorded source pins passed fresh source-mapped `qaRuntime` builds. Earlier Memory corrections passed inventory, worker ratchets and the six-file `check:changed` run in 966.34 seconds.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject blank channels capabilities selectors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw channels capabilities` silently treating an explicitly blank selector as omitted, which could widen an account/channel probe or skip a target permission audit.

## User Impact

Blank or whitespace-only `--channel`, `--agent`, `--account`, and `--target` values fail with a message naming the flag. Omitting a selector preserves the existing defaults and broader scope. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capabilities reuses the existing `parseChannelSelector` owner for `--channel`; the account option already uses `parseAccountSelector` before command startup. Only the agent/target guards remain local. Command validation stays after config validation and before capability secret resolution, plugin discovery, and account probes.

The selector matrix stays at the cheaper command boundary. The process suite keeps one capabilities smoke test for the distinct nonzero-exit and JSON-rendering contract.

Related: #133781, #136412.

## Evidence

- The blank and whitespace-only channel contract tests failed on the preceding PR head because capabilities returned a different error class from the shared selector owner; both pass with owner reuse.
- All 27 capabilities command tests passed, including selector rejection, omission controls, reporting, probes, and plugin installation.
- All 14 real-CLI process tests passed. The single capabilities smoke verifies exit code 1 and the exact `cli_error` JSON envelope.
- Formatting, targeted lint, core production types, all six selected core-test type graphs, the type-graph boundary, assertion safety, conflict-marker, line-cap, and whitespace checks passed.
- Canonical autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings in this three-file follow-up.

Measured single-worker cost, using the repository's supported direct Node equivalent of `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/channels/capabilities.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 58.29 s wall, including 39.66 s of compiled-worker preparation; test execution stayed below 5 s.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-backed-exit.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30.17 s wall with cached compiled workers. The retained capabilities smoke took 3.64 s and proves process exit/output rather than repeating selector policy.

Known verification limitation: `check:changed` stopped at the existing environment-variable budget mismatch (456 names versus a budget of 455). The same mismatch was reproduced against the unchanged index at the preceding PR head with `scripts/check-env-var-count.mts --staged`; this follow-up changes no environment-variable names or budget. Relevant checks were run separately. Hosted CI results and CI seconds for the follow-up head are separate from the local results above and are not yet available.

Historical original-bug proof was recorded at `19d8f01de3a0f3d1d1f57306dce151485defad29`: seven command regression cases failed on baseline `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`, then all 26 command tests passed with the fix. Subsequent upstream merges preserved the fix while reusing the now-shared account selector and removing redundant process coverage.

Agent runtime maintenance still requires updating repeated auth, execution, catalog, and message-processing paths that perform the same work.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Features, configuration, CLI flags, protocol and stored shapes, tool descriptions, prompts, and error text retain their existing behavior.

Share those operations within their existing owners, with explicit parameters for real differences. The main reductions cover identity/avatar read lifecycles, exec approval and denial results, shell scanning, model/auth projections, Code Mode dispatch, and message/tool transformations. Authority checks, lazy-loading boundaries, and cleanup ordering remain intact.
