prs.title: refactor(extensions): remove speculative runtime coordination
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces speculative runtime coordination in Browser, Memory Core, ACPX, QA Lab, Workboard, and Voice Call, as requested for the pragmatic-simplification campaign.

## User Impact

Normal features and public configuration/protocols stay available. Execution authorization, secrets, durable writes, Forget, ordinary shutdown settlement, and measured caches remain protected. Rare administrative reload races and in-flight read freshness become best effort as detailed below. No user database schema, retention, permission, or dependency changes; existing auxiliary lock files/rows are left untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous pass treated synthetic reproductions and maintainer PR narratives as production incidents. This pass re-evaluates all 44 KEEP rows against the stricter criterion: an actual human usage report or a specific security, durability, shutdown, resource-bound, or measured-performance contract. It removes or narrows 28 rows and retains 16 minimal owners under those exceptions.

The principal reductions are cross-process memory lock machinery, repeated reload/read fences, recursive Workboard inverse merging, browser lifecycle/config generations, voice provisional ownership protocols, and QA retry/rollback layers. Local FIFO ordering, current authority at external effects, bounded maps, persisted formats, and real failure recovery stay with their existing owners.

Production count including the follow-up repairs: **1,665 net lines removed** (767 added, 2,432 deleted), excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated outputs, and declarations.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

| Removed guard | Scenario, provenance, and behavior now |
| --- | --- |
| Browser profile generation/config-revision counters | #104601/#103784 includes a synthetic source/reproduction proposal, not an actual-use incident. Existing AbortSignals now cancel transitions; ordinary starts/actions remain concurrent and shutdown waits for their settlement. A config change during an already admitted operation can affect the next operation instead. |
| Browser repeated tail-stability admission | Repeatedly sampling a changing actor tail defended constructed overlap, not a human incident. Wait once on the current tail and use the captured cancellation signal at effects. |
| Browser cleanup retry/failed-handle custody | #137671 and related #137502 are synthetic reproduction/PR evidence. Close the captured handle once; an unusual failed cleanup is visible and can require an explicit retry/restart. Current-row and process identity still guard destructive closure. |
| Playwright/MCP retirement and attachment freshness layers | #149820 consolidates synthetic lifecycle cases. Keep shared connection ownership, cancellation and ordinary shutdown; remove extra stale-admission/retired-handle recovery. A stale handle may fail visibly instead of recursively recovering. |
| Browser role-reference invalidation generations | Synthetic replacement-wrapper/navigation cases do not establish a production incident for every generation layer. Preserve the ordinary ref cache and navigation ownership, accepting a stale wrapper/cache observation until the next snapshot. Selected-tab authorization remains unchanged. |
| Dashboard definition epochs | #156371's membership authorization remains at the effect; the definition-change epoch is separate speculative config freshness. Read/check the current definition through the existing owner without an additional epoch handshake. |
| Memory cross-process generation leases | #165568/#167926 provide synthetic coordination cases. Remove auxiliary SQLite admission/lock polling and dual release; keep local reader/writer FIFO. Foreign processes must obey the existing single-Gateway/exclusive-offline ownership contract. |
| Memory reindex SQLite lease | No actual-user incident requires a second cross-process lock owner. Reindex/reset use a local queue with the existing bounded busy timeout. Old auxiliary files are inert, not deleted. |
| Memory persisted workspace-lock custody | #152480 explicitly exercises injected reply loss and foreign writers. Remove PID/CAS acquisition, receipt retention and polling. Local nested-child ordering and settlement remain; old diagnostic rows and Doctor repair remain readable. |
| Memory reload/acquisition generations | #144252 is a feature foundation with constructed interleavings. Keep one entry check and normal close; overlapping reloads or a late acquisition can return an older manager and recover on a later request/restart. |
| Memory provider ownership maps | Separate pending/live/failed custody maps duplicated attempted-adapter tracking. One bounded attempted-adapter Set selects affected managers; actual active provider borrowers still settle before retirement. |
| Memory read fences and closed-manager retry | #162528/#125735 provide worker/extraction or injected-close tests, not human reports. Keep one open-handle admission check, vector validity and visibility. A stale/closed read fails once. An in-flight snapshot may outlive Forget, but tombstones/revisions still prevent late resurrection writes. |
| Memory post-embedding file reread | #144404 fixes reuse of paid work; its extra source-race cache-absence assertion was synthetic. Exact content/provider keys prevent wrong-content hits, so old-content vectors may remain unused until pruning while index publication still validates source. |
| ACPX snapshot/read/admission duplication | Human #106631 justifies poisoned-session reset isolation, which remains. It does not justify every speculative read fence. Keep actual generation/effect/write authority and physical identity, but let read-only results finish or fail without secondary custody. |
| ACPX probe-result/log generation checks | #150224/#154792 do not establish a stale-log incident. A health result may be logged after stop; it grants no authority. The reaper still validates live authority immediately before signals. |
| ACPX Pi prefix proofs and cached-path retry | #106941's larger same-inode rewrite is synthetic. Normal append scanning and measured catalog cache gains from #115259 remain. An in-place growing rewrite can leave metadata stale until refresh; a file replaced during a read gives one visible failure. Full-read identity and size validation stay. |
| ACPX catalog enabled-state rereads | #156278 addresses authentication classification, not disabling during one read. An admitted catalog read can complete after disabling; new execution/catalog requests still check current enablement. |
| Voice continuity counters and duplicate registries | #146546 is a feature/synthetic lifecycle PR. Keep the current bridge and AbortSignal at consult/delivery effects, but allow an already-running transcript write to complete across a provider reset. |
| Voice provisional constructor custody | #133018 describes a review-found synchronous-constructor scenario. Providers are expected to emit after connect; constructor errors and ordinary shutdown still clean up. Synthetic synchronous-close callbacks need not be reconciled by an adoption protocol. |
| Voice invocation transcript freezing | Human #145445 justifies distinct request identity, which remains. It does not require freezing an unfinished ASR buffer at every competing invocation. Later coalesced partial speech may be included before ASR finalization. |
| Voice cancellation race and rejected-call nonce | Use cooperative handler abort plus the current-bridge effect check, and a bounded rejected-call Set. An abort-ignoring handler can take its existing timeout; extreme eviction/reinsertion can allow another safe hangup attempt. No unrelated process or call is targeted. |
| Voice stale-index scan and injected malformed URL fallback | Supported writers maintain provider-ID indexes and construct stored callback URLs. Corrupting those internal invariants now fails visibly instead of scanning/catching around it. External input and signature validation remain. |
| QA generic startup/restart retries | #64562/#131643 describe validation or explicitly controlled fault injection, not human use. Prepare/launch once; retain only the explicit shipped migration-convergence restart and process/credential settlement. Bind/RPC failures are visible. |
| QA config CAS retry protocols | #108429/#67430/#107016 are suite-host/refactor scenarios. One suite writer makes one CAS request; concurrent edits or uncertain acknowledgments fail visibly rather than replaying a possibly committed write. Applied-revision/readiness waits remain. |
| QA FTS integrity retry classifier | a726bd73409 adds a synthetic settle-race loop. Surface the storage owner's integrity error immediately; do not reinterpret it as transient or sleep/retry. |
| QA receipt/Matrix interruption generations | #163046/#116071 are harness proof changes. A poll spanning reset can fail the scenario; final-message identity/content validation and explicit active-interruption handling remain. |
| QA failed-cleanup replay and post-action abort | #113874/#126407 use deterministic teardown/cancellation cases. Memoize the cleanup result, keep ordered shutdown, and check cancellation before actions/effects; do not rewrite an already completed result. |
| QA evidence-selection rollback copies | #147756 is an artifact feature, not a production incident requiring retry after invalid selection. Invalid selection aborts the invocation; independent publication validation still rejects the invalid partial state. Artifact shapes/history remain intact. |
| Workboard recursive inverse merging and CAS retry loops | #126161 demonstrates paused synthetic writers. Restore an unchanged owned card once; if another editor changed it, leave the whole edited record and partial failed work visible. Workspace/access restore together. Explicit revision conflicts still reject writes. |
| Workboard post-read receipt/replacement fences | Measured cache wins in #165058/#167965 remain. A read overlapping a mutation can return older facts; the next request's writer receipt invalidates them. No stale response is reinserted after ordinary owner invalidation. |
| Workboard catalog/load/live-refresh generations | #134943/#165058's extra interleaving fences are synthetic. Keep current promise/client checks and ordinary draft protection, but remove counters and queued-generation tokens. A reconnect can cause one extra harmless refresh. |
| Workboard per-entry nudge identity/log fences | Preserve current service authority before scheduling and bounded per-board cooldown. Remove object-identity bookkeeping and stale-log suppression; an unusual old completion can log after stop without authorizing a new effect. |

The retained real-report boundaries include ACP reset recovery ([#106631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106631)), browser warning-noise suppression ([#155193](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155193)), and voice request/interruption handling ([#112360](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112360), [#145445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/145445)). Other retained rows rest on the named security, durability, ordinary-shutdown or measured-performance exception, not synthetic provenance.

## Remaining KEEP decisions

All 44 old KEEP rows were reconsidered; 28 were removed or narrowed. These are the 16 rows retained without removing their central mechanism:

| Scope / retained row | Why it meets the sharpened bar |
| --- | --- |
| Browser durable cleanup claims | Current-row/process fingerprint checks authorize destructive tab closure; persisted intent survives ordinary restart. Security, durability, and persisted-shape rules. |
| Browser selected-tab access | Tab/document authority limits which actual user tab an extension may read or mutate. Security effect boundary. |
| Browser snapshot-delta cache | Bounded per-tab/options baseline implements the existing public delta contract, not speculative invalidation. |
| Memory provider borrowers | Actual parallel query/sync borrowers settle before their worker closes; nested sync writes remain covered. Ordinary shutdown settlement. |
| Memory publication tombstones/revisions | Prevent prepared writes from resurrecting forgotten user transcripts. Privacy and user-data durability. |
| ACPX empty-generation collection | #167308 measured three-hour runs: baseline 5,700 → 18,720 records and 5.2 → 17.2 MB; fixed 0 → 0 records and 1,632 → 1,632 bytes. Normal-use bounded-resource protection. |
| ACPX execution/disposal authority | Abort/live ownership before native execution and retirement; approvals and transcript admission. Security effect boundary. |
| ACPX process cleanup identity | Exact wrapper/Gateway/session ownership avoids killing unrelated processes; unsettled owned processes retain bounded recovery evidence. Security and shutdown settlement. |
| ACPX model reference fallback | Exact-ID-first, qualified and ambiguous references implement the existing public selection/dependency contract. No speculative retry/custody layer. |
| QA process boundary | Candidate processes can use real leased secrets; UID, trusted-root, process identity, termination and quarantine checks enforce isolation. Security effect boundary. |
| QA bus close checks | Settle waiter promises/timers and reject late long-poll allocation after close. Ordinary shutdown and bounded resources. |
| Voice response ownership | Human DonShelly's actual Twilio interruption report #112360; current-call/current-speech checks also guard external speech effects. |
| Voice pending operations/shutdown | Durable call/transcript writes settle before close; no new external effect after stop. Durability and ordinary shutdown. |
| Voice restore/provider state | Recover saved calls on ordinary restart, preserving them through unknown/network carrier results. Durability/public restart behavior. |
| Workboard operation drain | Accepted compound card writes finish before closing the SQLite worker. Ordinary write-capable shutdown settlement. |
| Workboard mutation authority | Gateway/session visibility and mutation permission checked at first accepted write; owned work may then settle. Security effect boundary. |

<details>
<summary>Coverage ledger: every original KEEP row (44)</summary>

NARROW counts toward the 28 flipped rows: it removes surrounding machinery while retaining a named minimum. PR narratives and synthetic reproductions are not treated as human incidents.

prs.title: fix(models): Anthropic pickers offer models the connected account cannot use
prs.body:
Closes #159267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Anthropic model pickers offer models the configured API key cannot use, and choosing one fails the turn with "model not found, HTTP 404".

## User Impact

User impact: a published Anthropic model that the connected account is not provisioned for (for example Claude Mythos 5 on a key without access) now shows greyed out with "Not available for the connected account" in the chat composer picker, Settings → Models, and Settings → Agents, and cannot be selected. Models that are unavailable because no working credential exists keep their existing behavior, including staying hidden from the global default pickers and routing to Model Setup. A second saved Anthropic account that does have access keeps the model selectable. The Gateway protocol gains one additive `unavailableReason` value, `not-provisioned`; the Android and Apple clients already fall back to a generic "Unavailable" label for unknown reasons and are unchanged here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Live discovery already asks Anthropic's `/v1/models` which models the credential can call, but the plugin then re-adds every manifest model the response omitted (from #113906, so shipped models Anthropic does not publish stay listed) without recording that they are not runnable. The Gateway's availability check only looks at credential acceptance, so those rows came out as `available: true`.

The plugin now reports the restored ids on its successful discovery outcome as `unlistedModelIds`, matching manifest rows by published identity so dated snapshots and aliases still count as listed. The catalog decision marks those rows `available: false` with reason `not-provisioned` for the credential that was tested, without overriding an existing auth failure or cooldown, and lets a profile's own successful read win over a provider-wide one. The pickers already grey out unavailable rows; the new reason keeps them from offering sign-in as the fix, and the Models defaults picker now lists such rows disabled instead of dropping them.

## Evidence

Before and after, captured on the mocked Control UI (`pnpm dev:ui:mock`) with a catalog row marked `not-provisioned`.

Chat composer picker, before:

![Chat picker before: Claude Mythos 5 is an ordinary selectable row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvaitKushe/openclaw/6f56a7ce7bbc5cab6a9ae3d9ab8611b82c832fd1/chat-picker-before.png)

Chat composer picker, after:

![Chat picker after: Claude Mythos 5 is greyed out and disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvaitKushe/openclaw/6f56a7ce7bbc5cab6a9ae3d9ab8611b82c832fd1/chat-picker-after.png)

Settings → Models default picker, before:

![Settings Models before: Claude Mythos 5 selectable with the Max 20x credential label](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvaitKushe/openclaw/6f56a7ce7bbc5cab6a9ae3d9ab8611b82c832fd1/settings-models-before.png)

Settings → Models default picker, after:

![Settings Models after: Claude Mythos 5 greyed with "Not available for the connected account."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdvaitKushe/openclaw/6f56a7ce7bbc5cab6a9ae3d9ab8611b82c832fd1/settings-models-after.png)

Checks run locally (Node 26):

- `pnpm test extensions/anthropic/live-discovery-auth.test.ts` (5 passed): restored rows are reported as unlisted; a dated snapshot counts as listing its dateless model.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.provider-outcomes.test.ts` (18 passed): unlisted ids project as `not-provisioned` for the tested profile and for a provider-wide read with no profile read; a different profile, or the selected profile's own listing, stays available; an auth rejection is not rewritten.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/provider-discovery.test.ts` (20 passed): the outcome copier keeps `unlistedModelIds` on `ready` outcomes and drops them elsewhere.
- UI: `ui/src/lib/chat/model-select-state.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-model-picker.test.ts` (a `not-provisioned` row is disabled and does not route to Model Setup), `ui/src/pages/model-providers/data.test.ts` (not-provisioned rows stay listed and disabled; missing-auth rows stay hidden), `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-model-setup.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, line-cap ratchet, `git diff --check`: clean.

Measured test cost (`--maxWorkers=1`): the Anthropic discovery file runs in about 4 s, the Gateway outcomes file in about 40 s (existing suite cost dominated by transform), the UI files in under 5 s combined.

Gaps: the live path was not exercised against a real Anthropic key from this branch; the mock fixture models the Gateway output. The Apple and Android clients show a generic "Unavailable" label for the new reason until they learn it.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): files and photos sent over Zalo reach the agent only as a link
prs.body:
Closes #159249

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: files, photos and videos that users send over Zalo personal account (`zalouser`) reach the agent only as a file name and a CDN link, so the agent cannot read them.

## User Impact

User impact: a PDF, photo or video sent over `zalouser` is saved to the media store and passed to the agent as inbound media, the same way as on Telegram and the Zalo Bot channel. If the download fails, the turn still runs and the agent is told the attachment is unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Normalization now reads the attachment the way zca-js delivers it: `share.file` → document (original file name from `title`), `chat.photo` → image, `chat.video.msg` → video. Only `https` URLs are used. Link previews and plain text are ignored.
- The monitor downloads with the existing runtime `saveRemoteMedia` helper (SSRF guard, `requireHttps`, the account `mediaMaxBytes`, header/idle/total timeouts, original file name), and passes the result to `buildContext` as `media`. The download runs only after access and mention gating, so dropped messages never fetch anything.
- A download can take up to two minutes, so access is re-checked after it finishes. A sender revoked in the meantime is still dropped.
- On failure it uses `formatInboundMediaUnavailableText`, matching `extensions/zalo`.
- No Zalo session cookies are sent: the Zalo CDN URLs download without them.

## Evidence

- `monitor.group-gating.test.ts`: 31/31 pass on this branch (rebased on `main`). Five new cases cover: download plus media facts, the failure notice, no download when mention gating drops the message, and a sender revoked during the download (with a not-revoked control). Fault injection: removing the post-download re-check turns the revoked case red while the control stays green; changing the notice text turns the failure case red.
- New normalization cases in `zalo-quote-metadata.test.ts` use real payload shapes (file, photo, video, link preview, plain text, `http`, invalid URL). On my Windows machine every test in that file fails in teardown with `EBUSY` (unlinking sqlite), including the untouched tests, so I also ran `extractZaloInboundAttachment` directly: 8/8 pass, and it goes red when the mapping is broken. CI on Linux should run the file normally.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: 0 errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `oxlint`: only the existing `max-lines` warning on `monitor.group-gating.test.ts`, which was already over the limit (1078 lines) before this change.
- Packaging check: `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack` of unmodified `v2026.9.5` is byte-identical to the published npm tarball. The patched pack differs only by this change.
- Live: on a production install (2026.9.5), PDFs and RAR files sent by users over Zalo were never saved. The same Zalo CDN URLs returned 206 for a ranged GET without cookies. Gap: I could not run the patched plugin live, because a locally built plugin does not get trusted plugin state (the credentials store), so it cannot log in. That is expected, and it is why this is proposed upstream.

Related: #84924 (photos only; closed for inactivity).

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve exact auth bindings in explicit fallback chains
prs.body:
Fixes #158600.

## Summary

Preserve an explicit `provider/model@profile` binding as part of model-candidate identity and carry it through the existing fallback engine into the embedded attempt as a hard user auth lock.

This applies to both:
- the explicitly requested primary candidate; and
- each explicit/configured fallback candidate.

Unbound `provider/model` candidates keep the existing auth-selection/rotation behavior.

## Problem

The model-ref parser already understands a trailing auth-profile suffix, but fallback candidate construction retained only provider + model and deduplicated on that pair. As a result:

- same-provider/same-model candidates that differed only by exact profile collapsed;
- the selected candidate's exact binding was not available to the attempt runner;
- normal provider auth selection could choose a different profile instead of the caller-selected binding.

That prevents an external planner from relying on a one-run ordered chain of exact qualified execution bindings.

## Implementation

This reuses existing owners rather than adding another router:

- `ModelCandidate` carries optional non-secret `authProfileId`;
- candidate dedupe includes the binding;
- explicit fallback refs retain their parsed profile suffix;
- an explicit primary `--model ...@profile` is retained as the requested candidate binding;
- fallback auth preflight scopes a bound candidate to that profile instead of the provider's normal ordered profile set;
- the existing fallback run options carry the candidate binding into execution;
- command execution gives candidate binding precedence over ambient/session auth and marks it as a `user` selection, reusing the existing embedded `lockedProfileId` semantics;
- binding-specific auth failure remains scoped by the existing profile-aware skip cache, while provider-wide failures retain existing behavior.

Compaction/plugin fallback consumers also forward the candidate binding rather than silently discarding it.

## Regression coverage added

- requested primary preserves exact binding;
- two same-provider/same-model fallbacks with different profiles remain distinct;
- a bound profile-A auth failure advances to bound profile-B;
- candidate binding overrides an explicit session profile and configured profile at the embedded attempt boundary.

## Validation

On the exact branch after merging current `upstream/main`:

- `oxfmt --check` on all 14 touched files: PASS
- `oxlint` on all 14 touched files: PASS, 0 warnings / 0 errors
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: PASS
- no-conflict-marker check: PASS

Local Vitest/type/max-lines-script execution is environment-blocked because this source checkout intentionally has no current `node_modules`. Reusing the installed 2026.9.5 runtime dependency tree is insufficient for current main (missing newer packages / TypeScript unstable APIs). I did not install or alter dependencies merely to obtain local test output. This PR was marked ready so upstream CI can provide the current dependency-set proof; ready-for-review status is not being treated as evidence that CI or human review has already passed.

prs.title: Skill Workshop: support purging rejected proposals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rejected Skill Workshop proposals currently cannot be permanently removed through a supported interface, leaving declined proposal records, event history, and retained artifacts in place. This change adds a narrowly scoped purge path.

## Summary

Add an explicit `purge` action for already-rejected Skill Workshop proposals, exposed through the agent tool and `openclaw skills workshop purge <proposal-id>`. The SQLite mutation runs in the current Workshop worker transaction and target lease. It removes the proposal, events, and rollback rows only after its retained artifact directory has been removed. Live skills are never targeted.

## Risk and invariants

High-risk: durable deletion, agent isolation, and concurrent proposal lifecycle.

1. Only a proposal owned by the selected agent and already in `rejected` status can be purged.
2. A stale reviewed revision cannot be purged through the agent action.
3. Pending and applied proposals, including an applied live skill, remain intact.
4. A failed artifact removal leaves the rejected database record visible and retryable; the database deletion is worker-transactional and target-lease guarded.

## Machine-Executable UAT

Starting data: disposable synthetic proposals in an isolated temporary OpenClaw state directory; no production/customer records.

1. Create pending, rejected, and applied proposals under one agent, plus a rejected proposal under another agent.
2. Attempt purge on pending and applied proposals; expect refusal and intact live skill content.
3. Attempt purge across agents and with a stale revision hash; expect refusal.
4. Purge the own rejected proposal with its current revision; expect no proposal row, event rows, or retained directory, while unrelated proposals and live skills remain.
5. Retry the supported CLI path after an interrupted artifact-first phase; the rejected record remains addressable until the worker transaction completes.

Forbidden outcomes: cross-agent deletion, deletion of an active skill, acceptance of stale revision, orphaned active proposal after a reported successful purge.

## Evidence

- The targeted Workshop service purge test and agent-tool stale-revision test passed locally; the same 53 tests and the formatter passed after the formatting-only repair at PR head `7df29c569`.
- The installed `openclaw skills workshop purge --help` now exposes the supported command.
- The explicitly declined proposal `engineering-acceptance-20260922-55e15ba311` is absent from Workshop inspection after purge; the live skill remains present.

## Deterministic checks and review boundary

- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts` — `purges only rejected proposals and their retained artifacts`: passed at exact candidate head.
- `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.lifecycle.test.ts` — `requires an exact revision to purge a rejected proposal`: passed at exact candidate head.
- `git diff --check` and changed-file `oxfmt --check`: passed.
- Full repository `tsc --noEmit` is not a passing gate in this checkout; its output includes errors in QA-lab, scripts, and UI files.

Review scope is this exact PR head, with one high-risk adversarial review and a bounded repair/targeted re-verification. The local owner is Skill Workshop; enforcement is the Workshop worker plus agent/CLI service. No harness repository is the owner of this OpenClaw product capability.

prs.title: fix(usage): Claude Code subscription usage missing for agents running on claude-cli
prs.body:
Related: #143419, #156296 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: agents that run through Claude Code (`claude-cli`) never show the subscription usage they actually consume. `usage.status` either has no Claude row or shows an error for a different Anthropic credential. ## User Impact Usage now follows the route an agent runs on. When agents run through Claude Code under the Gateway host's own login, `usage.status` reports a separate **Claude Code** row with that subscription's 5-hour and weekly windows and reset times. The row reaches the Control UI Usage page, chat `/status`, and Gateway clients. The **Anthropic** row is unchanged: an API key still shows spend and cost, a setup-token still shows its own result or error, and nothing is substituted between the two. The row appears after the first Claude Code turn following a Gateway start. It carries when it was reported (`observedAt`), shown as `as of 12m ago` in `/status` and `Observed 12m ago` on the Control UI usage cards, so a reader can tell when it may be out of date. ## Why This Change Was Made Anthropic has two billing surfaces, and OpenClaw can use both at once: - **Pay-per-use API** (API key): spend and cost, no subscription windows. - **Subscription through Claude Code** (`claude auth login`): the 5-hour and weekly windows. OpenClaw currently reports both as one "Claude" row and only asks the Anthropic credential for usage. For the Claude Code route that cannot work: - The usage request deliberately never uses Claude Code's login, because refreshing it would break Claude's own session (#129052). - A saved setup-token is refused with `scope requirement user:profile` (#143419). - An API key has no subscription windows at all. - Since `b9b2f455`, Claude Code runs never borrow a generic saved Anthropic credential. So whatever the Anthropic row reports can belong to a different account, or a different billing surface, than the one the agent is using. Claude Code already reports its own windows on every turn. Its stream-json output carries a `rate_limit_event` whose `rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows` has `five_hour` and `seven_day` utilization and reset times, and OpenClaw currently discards it. This change: - reads that record where the Claude stream is parsed; - keeps the latest windows in Gateway memory under a Claude Code identity; - reports them as their own **Claude Code** row whenever Claude usage is requested, beside the Anthropic row and never merged into it. **Recording is limited to the Gateway host's own Claude login.** It is skipped for: - paired-node turns; - turns under an OpenClaw auth profile (pinned, set on the agent's model, or picked automatically); - turns with a credential, auth endpoint, or provider switch in the child environment. Any `ANTHROPIC_*` variable counts except model selectors, OpenClaw's Admin API usage and API-key rotation keys, and Vertex project settings (inert without `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, which counts). Claude Code tokens and switches such as Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Mantle, or a gateway count too; names are matched case-insensitively; - turns with a `--settings` or `--managed-settings` backend argument; - turns with a different or skill-provided `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Each of those can be another account. A record that carries only some windows updates just those. The store clears with the model-auth status usage cache, which runs on any model-auth change. **Where the row shows.** - **`/status`** shows the Claude Code row only for a Claude Code session on the host login, and reads it from the in-memory store without a network request. Two checks must pass. First, the runner notes on every Claude Code turn whether the recording rule admitted it, using the turn's real environment, arguments, skills, and account; the session's latest turn must have been admitted. Second, the run's own account resolver (`resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId`) is asked with the session's pin, the agent's configured `@profile`, and the session's Claude Code binding, so a profile chosen since that turn also excludes it. Every other session keeps the usage line it had before, and the Claude Code row never stands in for its provider. - **The Models page** gives Claude Code its own usage-only card. Claude Code manages that login, so the card offers no credential actions: saving an API key there would have created a `claude-cli` profile that later Claude Code runs pick up. **Cache expiry.** A cached usage summary no longer serves a window after that window's reset time. The usage cache refreshes at the earliest reset in the summary instead of waiting for the 60 s TTL, and stale serves drop windows that have reset. A summary cached before Claude Code first reported its windows is also refreshed on the next read, so the row does not wait out the TTL after a Gateway start. This applies to every provider's windows, since a window past its reset is stale regardless of source. **Placement.** #129485 parsed the same record in core for turn-log diagnostics. It was closed because its target error was not an OpenClaw bug. This change uses the record for the documented usage surface. If maintainers prefer the Anthropic plugin to own the parser and row once #156296 moves Claude usage fetching there, both can move with it. **Known limits:** - The Claude Code row reflects the last recorded turn. Claude use outside this Gateway, or a `claude /login` switch, is picked up on the next turn or when model auth changes. The row's `observedAt` (the oldest time among its windows) makes that visible instead of presenting the windows as current. - The composer popover lists providers from auth profiles (`models.authStatus`). Matching a session to the Claude Code row there is a UI follow-up; this PR reports the row through `usage.status`. - A separate `openclaw status --usage` process does not see Gateway memory. - A user with a working Anthropic subscription OAuth login and Claude Code on the same account sees the same windows in both rows. Each row is still correct for its own route. No config, schema, or storage changes. One additive, optional field: `ProviderUsageSnapshot.observedAt` (epoch ms), set only on usage observed from runtime output rather than fetched. ## Evidence **Live proof** on a head-built dist and an isolated Gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and port isolated). Config: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, Claude Code 2.1.280 with its native subscription login, no Anthropic credential in OpenClaw. - **Before any turn:** `usage.status` returned `"providers": []`. - **One turn:** a single `openclaw agent` turn ran (`cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5 …`). - **After the usage cache refreshed,** `usage.status` returned: ```json { "provider": "claude-cli", "displayName": "Claude Code", "windows": [ { "label": "5h", "usedPercent": 56, "resetAt": 1790340000000 }, { "label": "Week", "usedPercent": 67, "resetAt": 1790784000000 } ] } ``` The trace showed `56.00000000000001` from `0.56 * 100`. The head rounds to two decimals, and a test covers it. **Control UI proof** (September 26). Same isolated setup for both: a fresh state directory, the Usage page opened first, one real `openclaw agent` turn through Claude Code, then the Usage page again. Headless Chromium 1187, dark theme, 1280×900 at 2×. Nothing private is shown; the session is the throwaway `ccusage-proof`. - **Before**, upstream base `516b1f8c4a6`, captured more than 60 s after the turn so the usage cache had expired: the page ends at Sessions. No provider section and no Claude Code row. - **After**, this head `127147da3e7`, captured on the first page load after the turn: the Claude Code card with its 5-hour and weekly windows, reset times, and `Observed just now`. The page had been opened before the turn, so this load also exercises the first-observation cache refresh below. | Before (base `516b1f8c4a6`) | After (head `127147da3e7`) | | --- | --- | | | | **Models page proof** (same isolated setup, one real Claude Code turn, Settings → Models). Before, the Anthropic card said "Not configured" yet showed Claude Code's windows as its own. After, Claude Code has its own usage-only card, and the Anthropic card reports its own (empty) usage with its usual actions. | Before: Anthropic card (`127147da3e7`) | After: Anthropic card (`fa180453a67`) | | --- | --- | | | | **Live `/status`** on the same Gateway and session after the turn (sent through `chat.send`): ``` Auth: native (claude-cli) Usage: 5h 92% left ⏱3h 19m · Week 83% left ⏱4d 4h · as of just now ``` **Wire shape** (Claude Code 2.1.280, identifiers removed), used as the parser fixture: `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"status":"allowed","resetsAt":1790305200,"rateLimitType":"five_hour","overageStatus":"rejected","overageDisabledReason":"out_of_credits","isUsingOverage":false,"unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.03,"resetsAt":1790305200},"seven_day":{"utilization":0.48,"resetsAt":1790784000}}}}` **Tests:** - **Record mapping:** fraction → percent (rounded), seconds → ms, reset times that overflow to `Infinity` or leave the Date range are dropped, malformed sibling windows, events without `unifiedWindows`. - **Stream parser:** emits the windows and still observes the session id; ignored outside the Claude dialect. - **Runner entry point** (`executePreparedCliRun` with a Claude stream on stdout): records under the host login, not under an OpenClaw-selected profile or a configured backend credential override. The recording rule also rejects other backends, paired nodes, account and endpoint variables (including lowercase spellings), settings arguments, and a different or skill-provided `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. It keeps recording for model selectors, OpenClaw's own Admin and key-rotation variables, and feature switches. - **`/status`** (`buildStatusText`): a host-login Claude Code session shows `Usage: 5h 80% left` from the store with no usage request; a session whose latest turn the runner kept off the host login (for example, a backend credential) does not show the row; a session whose run uses a stored Claude token profile shows the Anthropic row instead; a session whose agent model pins an API-key `@profile` does not show the Claude Code row. The runner test also checks the per-session verdict it notes. The selection helper passes the session pin, the configured `@profile`, and the Claude Code binding to the run's resolver. The `/status` tests fail without their fixes. - **Models page:** the Claude Code card is usage-only (no buttons, status badge, or credential line), and the Anthropic card keeps its own usage. The view test fails without the fix. - **Store:** expiry at reset, partial records keep the other windows and report the oldest `observedAt`, no recording of windows without a reset time or with one beyond the longest quota period (8 days), clear. - **Formatting:** `/status` summary and the usage report label observed rows `as of …`. - **Control UI usage card:** an observed row shows `Observed 12m ago` with the exact time on hover; a fetched row shows no age line. - **Loader:** - no Anthropic credential gives the Claude Code row; - the Anthropic row is kept unchanged beside the Claude Code row for a setup-token scope refusal, a timeout, an Admin API row, and fetched subscription windows; - no Claude Code row when Claude usage was not requested. - **Usage cache:** a cached window stops being served at its reset time and triggers a refresh before the TTL. A usage summary cached before the first Claude Code turn refreshes on the next read once that turn records windows. A newer reading of a window already shown waits for the normal TTL. The new test fails without the fix. - **Usage cache timing:** a window that resets while its refresh is still loading expires at its reset, and a timed-out refresh reports the timeout when every retained window has reset. Both fail without the fix. - **Observed store:** its window-set version changes only when a provider gains a window: the first observation, a new label, or the first window after a reset. **Test cost** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, vitest-reported, cold transform included): | File | Duration | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `provider-usage.observed.test.ts` | ≈0.3 s | | | `cli-runner/observed-usage.test.ts` | ≈9.6 s | 78% module transform of the runner harness; the three cases take ≈40 ms | | `cli-output-records.test.ts` | ≈0.8 s | | | `cli-output-stream.test.ts` | ≈0.5 s | | | `provider-usage.load.test.ts` | ≈24 s | 90% module transform; the new cases are ≈0.2 s together | | `usage.status-cache.test.ts` | three new cases | no timers | | `commands-status-claude-code-usage.test.ts` | ≈28 s | 74% module transform of `/status`; the four cases take ≈6 s. A new sibling file because `commands-status.test.ts` is at its line cap | | `status-usage-entry.test.ts` | ≈8.7 s | 73% module transform; the cases take <0.1 s | No sleeps or process boots. **Rebase (September 26):** rebased onto main `5be36d37cb7` as `53f2ce20d0b`. The only conflict was the upstream rewrite of the provider filter in `provider-usage.load.ts` (#158210); the Claude Code row block is unchanged and now precedes the new filter. `git range-diff` shows no other content change, so the proof above (captured on `127147da3e7`) applies to this head. The focused suites were re-run on the rebased head: 161 tests passed. **September 26, `2036029ad1d`:** rebased onto main `e518bd7310c` (263 commits, no conflicts; `git range-diff` shows the earlier commits unchanged). The last three commits address ClawSweeper Revisions 6 and 7 and two rounds of our own adversarial review (responses below). All 20 test files the PR touches, plus the session-override suites the refactor reaches, pass: 382 tests. `pnpm build` passed. The live proofs above were captured on `fa180453a67`; the only change since is the `/status` session check below, which a host-login turn satisfies. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed (format, lint, core and core-test typecheck, UI typecheck, boundaries, line-cap ratchet, dead-export scan). `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` reports no raw-copy drift. The Control UI usage and model-provider page suites pass (544 jsdom tests).
Review responses (ClawSweeper, September 25) - **[P1] Bind observed windows to the setup-token account.** Resolved by design. Claude Code's windows are no longer substituted into the Anthropic row under any condition. They are reported as the Claude Code row, which is the login that produced them. The Anthropic row, including a setup-token scope error, is left exactly as the Anthropic credential reports it. - **[P2] Expire cached observed windows at their reset time.** Fixed. The usage cache refreshes at the earliest window reset, and stale serves omit windows past their reset.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, second review) - **[P2] Validate `resetsAt` after the millisecond conversion.** Fixed. The parser keeps a reset time only when `resetsAt * 1000` is finite and within the Date range. The store also refuses a reset time more than 8 days after the observation (the longest subscription window is 7 days), so a finite but far-future value cannot pin a window either. Tests cover both. - **Login switch on the host.** The Claude Code row now carries `observedAt`, the time its windows were reported, and `/status` shows it as `as of …`. A `claude auth login` switch still shows the previous login's windows until Claude Code's next turn, but the row no longer presents them as current. Docs say so.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, third review) - **[P2] Show the observation age on the Control UI Usage card.** Fixed. The shared usage card renderer (`ui/src/components/provider-usage.ts`), used by the Usage page and both Models settings surfaces, now renders `Observed ` under the windows whenever a snapshot carries `observedAt`, with the exact timestamp as a tooltip. Fetched snapshots are unchanged. A new English string `usage.providerUsage.observed` goes through the standard locale workflow. Covered by a card test for both states.
Review responses (ClawSweeper, fourth review) - **[P2] Refresh cached usage when the first Claude Code windows arrive.** Fixed in `127147da3e7`. The observed store keeps a window-set version that changes only when a provider gains a window it did not have. Each cached usage summary records the version it was loaded against, read before the load starts, and a mismatch makes it stale. The next read refreshes as with an expired entry, and the Claude Code row appears as soon as that refresh finishes instead of after the 60 s TTL. Newer readings of windows already shown keep the normal cadence, so a busy agent does not re-query every usage provider after each turn. Covered by a `usage.status` cache test for the sequence "empty summary → first observation → row", which fails without the fix, and by a store test for when the version changes. - **Control UI before-and-after screenshots.** Added under Evidence: base versus head on the same isolated setup after a real Claude Code turn. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** These remain maintainer decisions. The row shows its observation age everywhere it is rendered, and the Docs describe the login-switch behavior.
Review responses (ClawSweeper Revision 6, plus our own review) - **[P2] Exclude configured Claude auth overrides before recording host usage.** Fixed in `3a469d30f3b`. Recording now fails closed: any `ANTHROPIC_*` variable in the child environment disables it except model selectors, OpenClaw's Admin API usage and API-key rotation keys, and Vertex project settings. Claude Code's own tokens, auth endpoints, and provider switches (checked against the Claude Code 2.1.280 binary) disable it too, matched case-insensitively. A runner-level test covers a configured backend `env` that re-adds `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`. - **Security: configured credential mislabeled as host usage.** Same fix. - **Our own review** found more, all fixed with tests that fail without the fix: - The Models page merged the Claude Code row into the Anthropic card, replacing Anthropic's own usage. It is now a separate usage-only card. - `/status` only loaded usage for OAuth/token auth labels, so a host-login session (`native (claude-cli)`) never showed the row. It judged the account by the session pin alone. It now uses the run's own resolver, including the agent's configured `@profile`. - A skill-set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` passed the config-directory comparison. Recording now fails closed on it. - The usage cache could re-query every provider on every read for a window reported past its reset, and a timed-out refresh could publish an empty entry. Both fixed: reset refresh uses the load start time, and the timeout is kept when nothing valid remains. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** Still maintainer decisions. The row shows its observation age everywhere it is rendered.
Review responses (ClawSweeper Revision 7) - **[P2] Check backend account overrides before showing host quota.** Fixed. `/status` cannot see a session's backend environment, settings arguments, config directory, or skill environment, so it no longer guesses. The runner already evaluates the recording rule on every Claude Code turn from the turn's real environment and arguments. It now also notes that verdict per session, and `/status` shows the host login's windows only when the session's latest Claude Code turn was admitted and the run's account resolver still selects no profile. A session with a backend credential override is therefore never shown the host's quota. The notes are process-local, bounded, and cleared with the observed windows. `/status`, helper, store, and runner tests cover it; the `/status` and helper tests fail without the fix. - **Security: quota attributed to the wrong Claude account.** Same fix. - **Before-and-after UI images.** They are hosted as commit-pinned `raw.githubusercontent.com` URLs on this fork's `pr-157753-proof` branch and return `200 image/png`; the review's media manifest could not fetch them. - **Login switch and security-sensitive approval.** Maintainer decisions, unchanged.

prs.title: feat(android): add Android Auto support with voice talk, navigation, media, and camera controls
prs.body:
## Summary
Adds native Android Auto support to the official OpenClaw Android companion app (`apps/android`).

### Key Features
- **CarAppService Integration**: Implemented `OpenClawCarAppService` and `OpenClawCarSession` using `androidx.car.app:app:1.7.0` (`IOT` category).
- **In-Car Screen (`OpenClawCarScreen`)**: Live gateway connection state and Push-to-Talk (PTT) action.
- **Audio Focus Management (`CarAudioController`)**: Uses `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_EXCLUSIVE` to pause car radio/music during voice interactions.
- **Vehicle Controls (`CarVehicleActionController` & `CarCommandHandler`)**:
  - `car.navigate`: GPS route dispatching via `google.navigation:q=` and `geo:` intents.
  - `car.media`: Media search and playback via `MediaStore.INTENT_ACTION_MEDIA_PLAY_FROM_SEARCH`.
  - `car.alert`: Priority in-car notifications via `CarNotificationHandler`.
- **Dashcam Integration (`CarCameraHandler`)**: Road snapshot (`roadSnap`) and short video clip capture via CameraX.
- **Tests**: Unit and Robolectric E2E test suite included.

prs.title: chore: remove CLAUDE.md symlinks in favor of AGENTS.md
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every scoped `AGENTS.md` in the repo carries a sibling `CLAUDE.md` symlink, plus a rule and three config entries that exist only to keep those symlinks intact. As of [Claude Code v2.1.277](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.277), Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` directly when a directory has no `CLAUDE.md`, so the symlinks no longer do anything.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Contributors adding a new scoped `AGENTS.md` no longer need to add a symlink beside it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removes all 24 `CLAUDE.md` symlinks and the maintenance around them:

- the "new ones need a sibling `CLAUDE.md` symlink" rule in the root `AGENTS.md`
- the two `-text` entries in `.gitattributes`
- the two ignore entries in `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`
- the "Sibling symlinks for scoped guides" block in `.semgrepignore`

Left alone on purpose: product code and docs that handle users' own `CLAUDE.md` files (`extensions/migrate-claude`, `extensions/anthropic`, `docs/install/migrating-claude.md`, and similar), the generic exclusion in `scripts/docs-list.js`, and the `docs/reference/templates` tree.

## Evidence

- `git ls-files -s | awk '$1=="120000"' | grep CLAUDE.md` returns nothing after the change.
- `git grep CLAUDE.md` shows only the product code and docs listed above.
- Docs and instruction-surface changes only, so no tests are affected.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support plugin-owned one-shot ACP runs
prs.body:
Related: #151901

## What Problem This Solves
Workflow plugins need to launch and manage their own one-shot ACP coding tasks through a supported host API. Today they otherwise need private host imports or user-session ownership that does not represent the plugin's work.

## Why This Change Was Made
Adds `api.runtime.acp` for availability, spawn, lookup/list, wait, observe and cancel, using the existing ACP admission/spawn, task registry and cancellation owners. Runs remain plugin-owned. Host-bound request authority expires with the callback; detached spawning requires an explicit trusted-plugin grant. Optional completion delivery uses the host-captured live requester route. Bounded process-local receipts deduplicate accepted and pending launches without evicting pending receipts.

This draft preserves the exact independently reviewed candidate, `0aaa1e3058dba74dd7199c68faff7a231331623c`, based on `3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107` (`release/2026.9.4`). It targets that branch **for scoped interface/design review only**, not a release backport request. Targeting current main directly would include unrelated release history. Integration into current main requires a separate port and fresh validation after maintainers agree on the contract and target.

## User Impact
Plugin authors gain a supported one-shot ACP workflow API with owner-scoped visibility and cancellation, normal admission limits, optional requester completion delivery, and structured errors. No deployment or live configuration change is part of this PR. Native plugins remain trusted same-process code; this is not a sandbox. Receipts and observers are process-local, not durable exactly-once delivery. Persistent/steer/resume/raw-manager APIs are out of scope.

## Evidence
Exact whole-card delta: 65 paths, 4,607 insertions, 74 deletions. Candidate tree: `d4f2b4011032f73b7f187c72eee29ea1f00e803e`.

### Fresh independent local review
- 867 scoped repository tests across 21 files passed (846 main scoped assertions plus 21 worker-packaging assertions).
- 19 independent probes passed: 15 authority/ownership/capacity/cancellation cases and 4 receipt/route cases.
- Historical pre-repair controls reproduced the repaired request-lease, exceptional-return, route-collision, and pending-receipt defects. These controls concern earlier unshipped revisions of this feature, not a claim of a released vulnerability.
- Included suites cover plugin ACP runtime, ordinary ACP spawn/control, registry persistence, loader/runtime binding, config, bootstrap/enrollment and standalone worker packaging.
- Candidate remained clean at the reviewed commit. Tests used isolated synthetic state and mocked provider seams; not OS-level isolation.

### Carried-forward producer evidence (not freshly rerun for publication)
- Full build and type/lint/dead-export/docs checks completed. After a host restart interrupted the aggregate checker, remaining stylesheet/import-cycle checks were completed separately; no uninterrupted aggregate exit is claimed.
- Source/emitted-runtime interoperability and relocated standalone worker startup passed.
- SDK comparison: no added/removed entrypoints, one added `PluginAcpRuntimeError` export, and 983 reachable type-graph changes. This is not a zero-API-change claim or SDK-owner acceptance.
- `git diff --check` passed again during publication preparation.

### Outstanding gates and explicit limits
- Repository `autoreview` helper was attempted during publication preparation. After resolving executable discovery, the reviewer engine exited 1 with `reviewer_unavailable` / `engine_failed`, no timeout and no report. This extra review is **not green**; it does not replace or invalidate the completed independent review above.
- SDK/security-owner acceptance of the public contract and authority/persistence boundary is requested before integration and downstream adapter implementation.
- No full application test inventory, live provider/Gateway run, Docker image build, cloud deployment, or current-main validation is claimed.
- Remote CI is not yet verified. Separate host restart/process-recovery errors are not fixed by this change.

Maintainer edits are enabled. Please keep this PR draft pending interface/target feedback and outstanding integration gates.

prs.title: feat(feishu): streaming.mode "progress" — coalesce work timeline into one live card
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a Feishu `streaming.mode: "progress"` that collapses an agent's entire work timeline — tool rows, commentary, narration, plan and reasoning — into **one live CardKit card** that updates in place, then **repaints that same card with the final answer** when the turn completes. No more one-message-per-tool / one-message-per-commentary flooding the chat, and no extra "final" card.

It reuses the shared OpenClaw progress-draft compositor (`createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`, also used by Slack/Discord/Mattermost/Teams) rather than a Feishu-specific pipeline. Feishu only owns transport: it renders the compositor's draft text into its existing streaming card and lets the final answer repaint it. Opt-in via `channels.feishu.streaming.mode = "progress"`; `"off"`/`"partial"` take none of the new branches and are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

With Feishu streaming today, every tool progress row and every 💬 commentary line is delivered as its own **standalone message**, and the final answer arrives as yet another message. A turn that calls a handful of tools produces a long vertical stack of transient messages that quickly buries the conversation — exactly the chat noise a card surface is supposed to avoid.

There was already a shared, cross-channel "progress draft" compositor in OpenClaw, but Feishu did not use it, and simply turning the mode on is not enough: in `progress` mode the shared compositor **defaults tool rows and commentary off** (a quiet default for channels that render rolling lines natively). Confirmed on a live tenant — with only `mode:"progress"` the card shows just "Working" while tool/commentary rows still leak out as standalone messages. This PR wires Feishu into that compositor and opts the rows/commentary in.

## How it works

`extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`
- Instantiates the shared progress-draft compositor in progress mode and renders its output through the existing Feishu streaming-card session.
- Forwards tool/item/commentary, narration, plan and reasoning callbacks to the compositor; `markFinalReplyStarted()` flips the single card from timeline to answer.
- Injects a normalized config entry that defaults `streaming.progress.toolProgress` and `.commentary` to `true`; any **explicit** user value still overrides them.
- `shouldStartNow` accepts both `tool` and `item` lines so the first tool starts the card immediately.
- Suppresses the now-duplicated standalone progress while the draft owns the lane:
  - `suppressToolProgressMessages` + `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages`
  - commentary ownership triple — `commentaryPayloadsEnabled: true`, `shouldDeliverCommentaryPayloads: () => false`, `progressPreambleEnabled: true` — so the core resolves `draftOwnsCommentaryProgress` and routes commentary into the draft via `onItemEvent` instead of sending 💬 standalone messages.
- Progress-mode answer text is not streamed as partial replies; compaction start/end and the empty assistant-start status line are suppressed so they don't blank/interleave with the live timeline.

`extensions/feishu/src/config-schema.ts`
- Adds `"progress"` to the `streaming.mode` enum and a strict `streaming.progress` block (`toolProgress`, `commentary`, `narration`, `commandText`, `label`, `maxLines`, `maxLineChars`) mirroring the shared channel progress config, so the opt-in defaults stay user-overridable and unknown keys are rejected.

During a multi-tool turn the single live card shows e.g.

```
Working

🔎 Web Search: for "上海天气"
• 正在查上海天气…
📖 Read: SOUL.md
• 读取 SOUL.md…
```

and that same card is repainted in place with the final answer.

## Evidence

- **Real-device (live Feishu tenant, both bot accounts):** ran a multi-tool turn (web search for weather + read a workspace file + summarize). Before the fix the card showed only "Working" and tool/commentary lines arrived as separate messages; after the fix, one card rolled through the tool rows and commentary with no standalone 💬/🔍 messages, and that same card was repainted in place to the final answer. This was reproduced across two gateway restarts; the final run is the passing one.
- **Root-cause proof against the real shipped compositor (not a mock):** fed real tool events and `kind:"preamble"` item events into `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`. With only `{streaming:{mode:"progress"}}` the snapshot `lines` is empty and the card text is just `"Working"`. With the injected `progress:{toolProgress:true,commentary:true}` entry the output is:
  ```
  Working

  🔎 Web Search: for "上海天气"
  • 正在查上海天气…
  • 读取 SOUL.md…
  ```
  This both reproduces the bug and verifies the fix at the compositor boundary.
- **Focused unit tests added** (`config-schema.test.ts`): `mode:"progress"` plus a full nested `progress` block parses at both root and account level, and the strict block rejects unknown keys. Existing `off`/`partial` cases are untouched. These are pure zod assertions and were additionally executed locally against the same zod version (all pass).
- **Type check:** `tsc --strict --noEmit` on the changed source files reports no new errors versus the pre-change baseline (the sparse-checkout environment has many pre-existing unrelated declaration errors; my two changed files are clean).
- **Backward compatibility:** every new branch is gated on `progressStreamingEnabled` (`previewStreamingEnabled && mode === "progress"`); `off`/`partial` paths are byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Not run locally (honest CI ask):** this is a sparse/shallow clone without a full monorepo install, so the extension's full `vitest` suite could not be executed here (no `pnpm`/`vitest` in the environment). Please run the `extensions/feishu` suite in CI.

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain final source replies for durable recovery
prs.body:
Related: #124279, #124310

**Not merge-ready:** the source-session lifecycle finding is confirmed below. No lifecycle repair or durability-owner acceptance is claimed. The earlier focused tests and scoped review did not cover this scenario.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost final replies when a terminal `message(action="send", final=true)` in message-tool-only source delivery encounters a retryable channel failure and the agent turn ends. Recovery also needs to wait out provider cooldowns without exhausting the retry budget when no provider request occurs.

## User Impact

The accepted original reply can survive a temporary channel failure and be delivered by native recovery without another model run. A queued result means retained custody, not delivery; the caller must not resend it. Progress, unrelated destinations, and provider-native actions keep their live-run restrictions. Unknown provider outcomes remain non-replayable without reconciliation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a canonical terminal send matching the admitted source channel, account, target, thread and receipt transfers to the existing durable owner. Current authority is checked after asynchronous preparation and immediately before custody admission and dispatch. Stable source-session/source-turn identity and the existing receipt prevent competing retries. The durable owner retains the original payload and transcript provenance, reauthorizes recovery, and remains the only retry owner.

The port preserves current main's composite authority and scheduled-write handling. Receipt/handoff preparation is a small Gateway sibling module; the existing oversized handler does not grow. No new queue, schema, configuration, or release/version changes. The September 18 follow-up adds one optional SDK recovery-capability marker, described below.

## Evidence

### Historical September 17 evidence

Ported onto actual main `efa5f7b90c5b1477d2fcd341a9a14377ce59f3c6`.

- The central checked-in regression fails against that exact main runtime because no queued result/custody is created, and passes with the fix.
- Real `message.action` → SQLite → native recovery tests cover retry after the live run expires, a second recovery, new tool-call IDs, ambiguous outcomes, cancellation, progress, and target/account/thread mismatch.
- New main-specific red/green proof covers authority revocation and abort while an asynchronous preparation checkpoint is pending; neither may admit replayable custody.
- 190 focused tests passed: 141 Gateway, 33 outbound, and 16 tool-result tests.
- Complete changed-surface check: all 31 steps passed, including production/core-test typing, formatting, module-size guards, lint, and storage-boundary checks.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of this exact current-main candidate: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/send.source-recovery.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/deliver-queue-admission.test.ts
```

Separate pre-port package acceptance on release 2026.9.4 used synthetic loopback endpoints and the actual packed channel plugin: original retained/recovered replies changed from 0/0 to 1/1, with no fallback reply or additional model request during recovery. Revoked current provider authority retained the intent but made zero mutations. That package evidence is not claimed as a build of this current-main PR head.

Validation boundary: no live provider mutation or complete Gateway-process crash/restart was exercised. Ambiguous untyped provider failures still require the plugin's existing typed non-dispatch/reconciliation contract. This change does not redesign failed-run diagnostics while durable delivery is pending. Exact-head GitHub CI is reported separately.


## Current-main cooldown follow-up — September 18, 2026

**Still not merge-ready.** This follow-up does not fix or waive the source-session lifecycle P1 or the maintainer durability/rollback decision recorded below.

Reconciled the existing fix with actual upstream main `4dc342303bcac0f50ed505c8ec8c6b445592fd42`. The `send.ts` conflict preserves main's scheduled generic-send queue restriction, downstream trusted context, extracted result helpers, and partial-delivery terminal receipt settlement.

### Bounded runtime fix

During a prolonged provider pause, repeatedly checking a retained reply must not consume its send-attempt budget. Supporting recovery now passes `supportsRecoveryDeferral: true` to the existing synchronous provider admission hook. A provider may return `{ status: "deferred", reason }` only with that advertised capability. Recovery leaves the existing row unchanged before persistent platform claims, attempt reservation, unknown-send reconciliation, or transport work. Its normal loop asks again; the provider owns and restores its cooldown deadline. Current authorization and unknown-send checks still run after the pause.

Live admission does not advertise deferral and must permit the original intent to reach its existing durable custody. A plugin on an older host must retain its previous admission behavior; older recovery interprets an unknown verdict as permanent rejection. This is an optional runtime SDK capability, not a persisted flag, schema change, new queue, host cooldown store, or second retry owner.

The repository's mandatory module-growth guard rejected seven extra lines in the oversized recovery orchestrator. Its existing retry-budget and permanent-error classifiers were moved unchanged into one small recovery-policy sibling. This keeps the orchestrator shrinking without altering those policies or weakening the guard.

### Current-source proof

- All three new cooldown regressions fail against the exact current-main recovery implementation and pass with the candidate.
- Startup recovery and recurring drains both preserve byte-equivalent queue rows and attempt counts through seven checks (more than the default five-attempt budget) and repeated database close/reopen, with zero send/reconciliation calls during the pause.
- After unpausing, queued replies deliver once; unknown-send custody reconciles first; a further drain produces no duplicate send.
- A newly permanent provider rejection after the pause prevents dispatch and retires the pending entry through the existing owner.
- Public SDK regression covers live admission, older-host capability absence, and advertised recovery deferral.
- Expanded focused suite: **269/269 passed** — 142 Gateway, 122 outbound, and 5 SDK tests. Current main's existing send, reconnect, producer-claim and retry-budget siblings are included.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the complete frozen candidate reported the already acknowledged source-session lifecycle P1 and no additional cooldown, extraction, or rebase defects. Its overall result remains incorrect because that P1 is unresolved; no whole-PR clean verdict is claimed.
- Full changed-surface check passed on the exact 16-file candidate, including production/core-test typing, module-growth guards, formatting, SDK and storage/import boundary checks. The first post-restart attempt stopped before source checks because pnpm was absent from PATH; the successful run used the existing pinned pnpm 12.4.0 without dependency changes.

Validation boundary: these are current-source tests with synthetic isolated SQLite state, not a package build, live provider mutation or complete Gateway-process crash/restart test. Earlier stable-package evidence remains distinct. The session deletion/replacement/reset authority concern and accepted downgrade contract still require the separate owner decision and correction below.

## Author follow-up — September 17, 2026

The [ClawSweeper P1 finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151035#issuecomment-5718999794) is accepted and reproduced on unchanged production head `462df411f1a92247c6b8267169af0f2fbde18cdc`.

### Current-head final-I/O reproduction (red, not a fix)

The diagnostic uses the real `sendHandlers["message.action"]` entry point, existing SQLite custody, `recoverPendingDeliveries` and `deliverOutboundPayloads`. Its synthetic channel adapter performs an actual HTTP POST to an isolated loopback receiver. No private state, credentials, live provider or extra model run is involved.

1. Admit an exact final source reply and force a typed proven-not-dispatched failure before HTTP I/O.
2. Verify one pending required-policy queue entry containing the original answer and no HTTP POST.
3. Retire live run authority and clear its session run markers. Separately keep the session, delete it through `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` with `deleteDeliveryArtifacts: true`, or replace it with a new session ID. Verify the deletion/replacement through the session owner.
4. Close and reopen the shared queue database; let native recovery retry after backoff.
5. In a fourth case, delete the session in the channel's asynchronous `beforeSendAttempt` checkpoint during recovery, before final transport I/O.
6. Count actual received HTTP requests and drain recovery a second time.

Observed sanitized output:

```text
source lifecycle       HTTP POSTs   first recovered   second recovered
normal completion          1              1                 0
deleted before recovery    1              1                 0
replaced before recovery   1              1                 0
deleted before final I/O   1              1                 0

Expected HTTP POSTs: normal completion=1; each revoked case=0.
Result: 1 passing control, 3 failing lifecycle assertions.
Each case began with one retained entry and ended with no pending entry.
```

This confirms externally effective sends after source revocation, not merely a late transcript-append failure. The fixture was diagnostic-only and is not committed as a knowingly failing regression. This is current-source loopback transport evidence, not a packed-provider test, full Gateway process-restart test, or upgrade/rollback acceptance. No corrected-head green result exists yet.

### Concrete repair proposal and decision requested

**Recommendation: accept a lifecycle-fenced handoff in the existing outbound queue, with the rollback constraint below, before implementing the persisted contract.**

- Capture an explicit internal source-reply lifecycle authority at the Gateway admission boundary: physical session-store locator, agent, canonical session key, expected session ID and a required nonempty lifecycle revision. Capture it from the session owner while the admitted live authority is still current; persist it with the original queue payload after the final synchronous admission check.
- Reuse `assertSessionWriterDeliveryAuthorized` for current session ID/revision checks, without `expectedWriterRunId`: normal run completion must not revoke the accepted reply. Session reset may preserve the session ID, so ID matching alone is insufficient. Missing lifecycle facts remain live-only; do not manufacture authority from transcript metadata.
- Reconstruct that guard at the existing direct-adapter and final platform-dispatch boundaries, rechecking after asynchronous preparation and immediately before transport I/O. Revocation is a permanent proven-not-dispatched rejection settled by the existing queue owner. Do not introduce another queue/retry owner or change unrelated provider authority, ambiguous-send reconciliation or retention.
- Old source-reply entries without an explicit fence must not acquire replay authority retrospectively. Existing non-source queue contracts stay unchanged. Do not fabricate a `pending-final` completion: that completion belongs to a different intent/settlement owner.

**Compatibility decision:** simply adding an optional authority field is not safe for binary-only rollback: older readers ignore it. A `preparedBatch.schemaVersion` change alone is not an enforced old-reader fence either. The proposed downgrade contract is: stop new admissions; on the fenced build settle or reconcile **all** unfinished source-reply custody, including unknown outcomes; stop the Gateway; and verify no affected unfinished entries remain before an older binary opens that state. If draining cannot finish, remain on the fenced build. Restoring a snapshot is not an automatic alternative: its consistency and any external effects since capture must first be reconciled to avoid duplicate sends. No automatic restoration or deletion is proposed here. If maintainers require unrestricted binary rollback against candidate-written state, an explicitly enforced reader/version boundary or a genuine migration onto an existing guarded final-delivery owner is required before this can ship.

The owning maintainer is asked to accept or amend this durable-lifetime contract and downgrade only after affected custody is settled under the [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/efa5f7b90c5b1477d2fcd341a9a14377ce59f3c6/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes). The bot's recommendation is not treated as owner acceptance. After acceptance: implement the narrow repair, convert the reproduction into regressions, demonstrate same-ID reset rejection and post-await revocation, and provide fresh-state, compatible-upgrade, agreed rollback and exact-head review evidence. Until then the P1 and owner-decision items remain open; this description update is not a request to waive them.

### CI failure attribution

The failing [core test-type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35259287051/job/105331358367) reports TS2741 at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.test.ts:626`: an `answerSegments` fixture omits required `finalMessageStart`.

This is upstream drift, not caused by this PR: GitHub test merge `04027af31553700b94cef4f7d6c67d42b1fcbee5` and its main parent `1a2cdc2c8400a0aaba7662f10a836887160c6cff` have byte-identical versions of both the failing test and its required type. The incomplete fixture was introduced by [9acc2f9ab83 / #151042](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9acc2f9ab83). This PR changes neither path. The unrelated fixture is left untouched per CONTRIBUTING; this explains the red CI but does not make CI green or resolve the lifecycle blocker.

prs.title: refactor: migrate Usage and Activity pages to Solid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves Usage and Activity onto the shared Solid 2 runtime while the remaining Control UI pages continue to use Lit.

## User Impact

Preserves the existing routes, host tags, classes, filters, charts, session details, media, Git cards, and Run Inspector. Gateway data and mutation authority remain in the existing synchronous TypeScript owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces the Lit element classes with four `defineSolidBridge` registrations and reactive JSX. Extracts the existing Gateway page binding so both renderers share its lifecycle, and uses the landed Solid icons and settings controls. A small isolated Lit outlet retains shared helpers whose owning surfaces have not migrated yet.

The port also preserves keyboard focus when changing date presets and keeps timeline drag handlers, keyed session rows, and media/Git state stable across updates. No dependencies or persistence formats change.

## Evidence
