prs.title: Consolidate Program Manager context and safety contracts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Program Manager had contract guidance, workspace instructions, runtime settings, and state validation spread across separate surfaces. That increased prompt/context cost and made it easier for the role to overclaim completion, loop on missing state, or cross its planning and handoff boundary.

## Summary

- Consolidates the Program Manager contract, compact bootstrap files, runtime limits, and state fixture rules into one fail-closed package.
- Keeps the checked-in state JSON as validation-only; live status must come from the current task packet, `get_goal`, and returned worker evidence.
- Enforces an exact read/planning/bounded-handoff tool policy with only `builder-agent` and `research-brief-agent` as delegation targets.
- Adds a no-packet terminal path, bounded low-verbosity output, explicit Qwen thinking-off parameters, and no-deliberation/no-policy-recap response rules.
- Adds reversible workspace install/rollback plus PM-only Director-config apply/rollback for both `agents.list` and `agents.entries`, preserving agent identity and unrelated config.
- Keeps bootstrap context compact by replacing generic TOOLS/HEARTBEAT prose with minimal role-specific files.

## Verification

- Source package check passed: 2,677 bootstrap bytes within the 10,000-byte budget.
- Canonical source runtime-config validation passed.
- Focused tests passed: 9/9.
- Workflow sanity passed previously; current hosted checks are running for the latest pushed head.
- `env OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=1 OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK_MODE=throttled pnpm check:changed` passed: typecheck, lint, import-cycle check (0 runtime value cycles), formatting, guards, and selected lanes.
- Governed workspace install/verify passed; the active Program Manager workspace now has compact TOOLS/HEARTBEAT files and unrelated workspace files were preserved.
- Active Director config synchronization is backed up and reversible. The governed managed runtime validated the active config successfully; only existing duplicate-plugin and readonly health-state warnings were reported.
- Managed Gateway loopback health returned HTTP 200 with `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`.
- Active Program Manager smoke completed through the managed local OMLX provider: bounded PLAN output, missing-packet truthfulness, one `get_goal` call only, no forbidden tool calls, stop finish reason, and no secret output.
- The OMLX payload contained `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` and `preserve_thinking=false`; the final response completed without hidden-reasoning budget exhaustion.
- Configuration and workspace backups remain available for rollback.

## Known Boundaries

- The active managed runtime is an older curator-managed release, so its governed launcher is authoritative for active-config validation; the source checkout's newer schema validator is not used against that older active config.
- Pre-existing duplicate-plugin warnings and state-database permission warnings were not changed because they are outside this PM package and could affect unrelated runtime state.
- Matthew must personally review and accept the final live behavior evidence before this role can be certified 100% complete.

## Scope and Safety

No merge, release, publication, spend, live-user-data mutation, or secret exposure. The latest verified commit is pushed to the existing branch; no SHA/promotion work was performed.

prs.title: docs: optional barycenters adapter under Documentation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first patch put an optional third-party adapter under `## Security`, which OpenClaw uses for first-party host-tool / pairing guidance (and points vulns at SECURITY.md). ClawSweeper correctly flagged that as an unverified security-control endorsement: `before_tool_call` is a plugin hook registered with `api.on(...)`, not a Gateway dispatcher config, and MCP is a side door — it does not wrap other tools.

This revision keeps `## Security` vendor-neutral (same text as main). Three honest lines now sit under `## Documentation`:

1. Optional third-party adapter — not first-party OpenClaw security guidance. Hook `before_tool_call` from an installed plugin via `api.on(...)` ([plugin hooks](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/hooks)); call npm [`barycenters`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/barycenters) (`bary.govern` / `admit`) in shadow.
2. MCP at `https://barycenters-admit.fly.dev/mcp/` is a side door (`admit`, `check_readiness`); it does not wrap other OpenClaw tools.
3. Spec: https://barycenters.ai/adapters

## Evidence

- Supported hook contract: https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/hooks (`before_tool_call` from a plugin via `api.on(...)`).
- Live MCP (Streamable HTTP): `https://barycenters-admit.fly.dev/mcp/` — GET 406 is protocol, not a down host. Tools: `admit`, `check_readiness`.
- Adapter spec: https://barycenters.ai/adapters
- npm `barycenters` 1.0.3: https://www.npmjs.com/package/barycenters
- ClawSweeper P1 (README.md:81-83): remove the unsupported global-admission recommendation from `## Security`. This patch does that.
- CI `check-docs` already passed on the prior head; this is docs-only wording + placement.

## Why

Operators who want an optional admission check need a pointer to the supported plugin seam and the live adapter. That pointer does not belong in first-party security guidance.

prs.title: fix(acp): run session/new prompts in the requested cwd
prs.body:
Closes #123557

AI-assisted contribution (Claude Code). I have read and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP clients that open a session with a specific working directory would have their agent run in the default workspace instead. An IDE extension, CLI wrapper, or automation script calls `session/new` with `cwd` set to a project directory, gets back a session whose `session.cwd` correctly reports that directory, and then every `prompt` on that session executes in `~/.openclaw/workspace`.

The confirming metadata is what makes this bite: the caller has positive evidence the session is scoped to their project, so files get read from and written to a directory the caller never intended.

The end-to-end capture below shows it precisely. On pre-fix code the model receives **two contradictory statements in the same turn**: the bridge's informational message prefix says `[Working directory: $ROOT/project]`, while the system prompt's own `## Workspace` section says `Working directory: $ROOT/workspace`. The agent is told one thing and executes against the other.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requested directory was recorded only in the ACP bridge's in-memory session record. Nothing carried it to the Gateway: the bridge never creates a Gateway session, `chat.send` has no `cwd` field, and the Gateway therefore created the session lazily on the first prompt with no directory to work from. The agent turn resolves its cwd from `requestedCwd ?? sessionEntry.spawnedCwd`, and `spawnedCwd` was never written.

The fix records the fact at the boundary that owns it. `sessions.create` already accepts an absolute `cwd` and persists it as `spawnedCwd`, so the bridge now creates the Gateway session at `session/new` and every later turn resolves it through the existing runtime path. Public `chat.send` is left alone — widening it with a competing per-request `cwd` would add a second source of truth for state the session entry already owns.

### Absence is decided by the Gateway, not the caller

Two earlier revisions of this PR got the ownership boundary wrong, and the fix for both is the same idea, so it is worth stating directly.

`sessions.create` applies `spawnedCwd` even when it *adopts* an existing row. So the bridge must not create over a session someone else owns — but it also cannot skip creation for explicitly routed keys, because `requireExisting` defaults to false and an explicit `_meta.sessionKey` / `--session` routes through **unresolved**, meaning the row may not exist at all. Deciding this from outside the Gateway is a check-then-create race: a row created between the bridge's probe and its write gets adopted, and the owner's directory is overwritten.

So the decision moved to where the answer is already known. `sessions.create` gains an opt-in **`cwdOnCreateOnly`**, applied inside the same mutation that already computes whether it created the row — right next to the existing rule that adoption must not stamp new-row facts (provenance, visibility, `projectId`). The bridge now calls create unconditionally with that flag:

- **new row** → the requested cwd is persisted.
- **existing row** → the owner's cwd is untouched, whenever it appeared.

This removes the ACP-side probe and its duplicate snapshot branch entirely; the bridge no longer reasons about session existence at all. Callers that omit the flag keep exactly the previous behavior.

### The bridge reports the directory the turn will actually use

Because an adopted row keeps its own directory, the bridge must not keep assuming its request won — the visible `[Working directory: …]` prefix and the provenance receipt are both built from ACP-side session state, so a mismatch there recreates the same false confirmation this PR removes. `session/new` now reads the authoritative value back out of the create response and records that.

That leaves one case where no honest directory exists to report: an adopted key whose row has **no** working directory at all. The turn will run in the agent workspace, so claiming the requested directory would be the original defect again. A create that passes a cwd always returns one for a new row, so a missing `spawnedCwd` identifies exactly that case, and `session/new` fails with what to do instead rather than reporting a directory the agent will not use.

**Path authorization is unchanged.** `sessions.create` already requires the cwd to be inside a configured agent workspace unless the caller holds `operator.admin`. The ACP bridge connects as a CLI-mode client, which gets `operator.admin` by default, so the reported flow works; narrower deployments keep the Gateway's existing containment rule.

`session/new` now also rejects a relative `cwd`, matching the sibling `session/resume` and the ACP contract (`NewSessionRequest.cwd`: *"The working directory for this session. Must be an absolute path."*, `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` `dist/schema/types.gen.d.ts:4649`). Previously a relative path was silently accepted and quietly ignored — the capture below shows pre-fix code happily creating a session for `relative/project`.

**Sibling surfaces:** `session/load` and `session/resume` are adoption paths, not creation paths — they attach to a Gateway session that already exists and owns its `spawnedCwd`, and `resumeSession` already requires that row via `getExistingSnapshot`. They are intentionally unchanged.

### Older Gateways never see the new field

`sessions.create` params are a closed schema, so unconditionally sending `cwdOnCreateOnly` would make `session/new` fail outright against a Gateway built before it — turning a bridge upgrade into a hard error. The field is therefore capability-gated using the mechanism this repo already has: the Gateway advertises `sessions.create.cwdOnCreateOnly` in `HelloOk.features.capabilities` (alongside entries like `chat-send-routing-contract`), the client retains the advertised set per connection, and the bridge sends the field only when it is offered. No `PROTOCOL_VERSION` change.

Against a Gateway that does not advertise it:

| Route | Behavior | Why |
|---|---|---|
| bridge-minted key | still provisioned, field omitted | a fresh id cannot collide with an existing row, so applying the cwd is harmless — the reported bug stays fixed |
| explicit `_meta.sessionKey` | not provisioned | that Gateway would apply the cwd to a row it merely adopts, so creating could overwrite an operator's directory |

The explicit-key route therefore keeps its pre-PR behavior against old Gateways — those callers keep the default-workspace bug until their Gateway updates — rather than risking someone else's state. Two consequences are deliberate and worth naming: the bridge reports the requested cwd on that degraded route even though the row may differ, and a reconnect onto a downgraded server uses the previous hello's capabilities until the new hello lands.

**Protocol follow-through:** the field is additive and optional, and the generated Swift bindings are regenerated in this PR (`Bool?` with a `cwdOnCreateOnly` coding key), so existing clients decode unchanged. Kotlin and `dist/protocol.schema.json` needed no changes. This does not reach model-visible prompt text — the agent-facing session tool schema is declared separately in `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-visible.ts`, and no protocol-only field (`emitCommandHooks`, `spawnDepth`, `catalogId`, `succeedsParent`) appears in the prompt snapshots.

**Production LOC:** +113 / −17 (tests +285/−14, generated Swift +5/−1), 15 files. That is well above the net-≤0 default for a bug fix and I am not going to present it as small. Roughly half is capability negotiation, which exists because shipping the field unconditionally breaks mixed-version pairings; the rest is the ownership boundary itself and the adoption-path repairs. Every increment traces to a review finding on this PR rather than scope I chose, and the one absorbing refactor available — moving absence into the Gateway mutation — was taken and removed the caller-side probe. Above the net-≤0 default, so naming it rather than burying it: the growth is a public protocol capability — opt-in create-if-absent semantics for a caller provisioning a key it may not own — plus the ACP contract assertion. Moving the decision into the Gateway is what let the ACP-side probe and duplicate snapshot branch be deleted rather than added to.

## User Impact

ACP callers that scope a session to a project directory now actually get their agent running there — whether they let the bridge mint a session key or name one themselves with `_meta.sessionKey` / `--session`. IDE extensions, CLI wrappers, and automation that pass `cwd` to `session/new` stop silently operating in `~/.openclaw/workspace`, which removes the risk of the agent creating or modifying files in the wrong directory while `session.cwd` reports the intended one. Sessions an operator already owns keep the directory they already had, with no window in which a concurrent creation could change it. `session/list` also reports the real directory for bridge-created sessions.

A relative `cwd` on `session/new` is now a clear error instead of being silently ignored.

## Evidence

### 1. Real-behavior proof — ACP stdio → isolated Gateway → agent turn

Harness, all real processes: the built `openclaw acp` stdio bridge → a real Gateway on its own port with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (never the operator's gateway) → the repo's own mock provider (`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`, wired through qa-lab `buildQaGatewayConfig` with `providerMode: "mock-openai"`). ACP JSON-RPC driven over real stdin/stdout. Re-run against the current `cwdOnCreateOnly` build.

**Both routing modes, one run**, each with its own directory and a real prompt turn:

| Route | Session key | Persisted `spawnedCwd` | System prompt `## Workspace` → `Working directory:` | Turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bridge-minted | `agent:qa:acp-bridge:e90914c3…` | `$ROOT/project-a` ✅ | `$ROOT/project-a` ✅ | `end_turn` |
| explicit `_meta.sessionKey` | `agent:qa:acp-explicit-proof` | `$ROOT/project-b` ✅ | `$ROOT/project-b` ✅ | `end_turn` |

The default workspace appears in **neither** model payload (0 occurrences). `session/new` with `cwd: "relative/project"` was rejected: `ACP session/new requires an absolute cwd.`

**Before/after on the same harness**, with only the ACP lifecycle reverted to pre-fix and the dist rebuilt:

| Observation | **Before** | **After** |
|---|---|---|
| Persisted `session_nodes.entry_json.spawnedCwd` | `None` | `$ROOT/project` |
| System prompt `Working directory:` | `$ROOT/workspace` ❌ **default** | `$ROOT/project` ✅ **requested** |
| Default-workspace occurrences in model payload | 8 | **0** |
| `session/new` with a relative cwd | **accepted**, session created | rejected |

What the model was actually told:

```
BEFORE:  ...verify memory snippets.\ ## Workspace\  || Working directory: $ROOT/workspace
         ...\"input_text\",\"text\":\"[Fri 2026-08-14 ...] [ || Working directory: $ROOT/project
                 ^ the bridge's message prefix claims /project while the agent runs in /workspace

AFTER:   ...verify memory snippets.\ ## Workspace\  || Working directory: $ROOT/project
```

Real ACP stdio transcript (abridged):

```
>> session/new {"cwd":"$ROOT/project-a","mcpServers":[]}
<< {"sessionId":"e90914c3-80b0-4a30-8a09-765f1cbd49e4",...}
>> session/prompt {"sessionId":"e90914c3-…","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"Which directory are you working in?"}]}
<< {"stopReason":"end_turn"}
>> session/new {"cwd":"$ROOT/project-b","mcpServers":[],"_meta":{"sessionKey":"agent:qa:acp-explicit-proof"}}
<< {"sessionId":"724124b2-47fa-4c54-bed7-1cb89470ecab",...}
>> session/prompt {"sessionId":"724124b2-…",...}
<< {"stopReason":"end_turn"}
>> session/new {"cwd":"relative/project","mcpServers":[]}
<< {"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"ACP session/new requires an absolute cwd."}}
```

Persisted rows, read out of the agent SQLite store after the run:

```
agent:qa:acp-bridge:e90914c3-80b0-4a30-8a09-765f1cbd49e4   spawnedCwd = $ROOT/project-a
agent:qa:acp-explicit-proof                                spawnedCwd = $ROOT/project-b
```

So the artifacts are not over-read: the Gateway's `[ws]` log records only failed or slow responses (`ok === false || durationMs >= DEFAULT_WS_SLOW_MS`, `src/gateway/ws-log.ts:395`, threshold 50 ms), so it is not a complete RPC census — the persisted rows and model payloads above are the authoritative signal. `$ROOT` is a temporary directory; paths are otherwise unedited, and no credentials appear (the Gateway ran unconfigured against a local mock provider).

### 2. Every directory-mismatch case is covered by a test that fails pre-fix

| Case | Behavior | Pre-fix failure |
|---|---|---|
| bridge-minted key | requested cwd persisted | `expected [ { method: 'sessions.list' } ] to deep equally contain { method: 'sessions.create' }` |
| explicit key, no row | requested cwd persisted | (same create assertion, explicit-key variant) |
| explicit key, row **with** cwd | bridge reports the owner's directory | `expected '/tmp/my-project' to be '/tmp/owner-project'` |
| explicit key, row **without** cwd | `session/new` refuses | `promise resolved instead of rejecting` |
| relative cwd | `session/new` refuses | `promise resolved instead of rejecting` |
| old Gateway, bridge-minted key | provisioned without the field | n/a — new degraded-path coverage |
| old Gateway, explicit key | not provisioned, `session/new` still succeeds | n/a — new degraded-path coverage |

The shared translator test helper now models the `sessions.create` response the bridge reads, instead of a bare `{ ok: true }`; partial mocks delegate to it. That stub had been hiding this path — six previously-passing tests only passed because they asserted against a Gateway shape that does not occur.

### 3. The ownership race, proven deterministically

`src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` creates a session with one directory, then issues a second `sessions.create` for the same key with a different cwd and `cwdOnCreateOnly: true` — modelling the interleaving where the row already exists by the time the create lands. Removing the guard makes it fail for exactly the right reason:

```
 × sessions.create cwdOnCreateOnly leaves an adopted session's directory to its owner
 AssertionError: expected '/tmp/acp-project' to be '/tmp/owner-project'
```

A companion test proves the flag still sets the directory on a genuinely new row.

### 4. Regression test fails before the fix, for the intended reason

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.session-setup.test.ts   # pre-fix
 × creates the Gateway session with the requested cwd for a bridge-minted session
 × rejects a relative cwd instead of silently running elsewhere

 AssertionError: expected [ { method: 'sessions.list', …(1) } ] to deep equally contain
                 { method: 'sessions.create', …(1) }
```

The ACP tests assert the exact wire shape for both routing modes, including the flag, and that a rejected relative cwd creates nothing. The mock gateway returns a realistic `sessions.list` payload rather than a bare `{ ok: true }`.

### 5. Owner-boundary and suite coverage

- Runtime consumption: `resolveSessionRuntimeCwd({ requestedCwd, sessionEntry })` returns `requestedCwd ?? sessionEntry.spawnedCwd` (`src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-reset.ts:269`), feeding the agent run's `cwd` at `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.ts:483`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` → **91 passed**.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp` → **182 files / 1451 tests passed**.

### 6. Gates

`autoreview --engine claude --mode uncommitted`: clean on every revision, *"no accepted/actionable findings"*, clean on the final revision, TruffleHog clean. `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` exit 0; `run-oxlint.mjs` exit 0; `oxfmt --check` clean; `git diff --check` clean. The full protocol gate was run locally — `check-protocol-registry`, `protocol-gen`, `protocol-gen-swift --check`, `protocol-gen-kotlin`, `check-protocol-since`, and the `git diff --exit-code` over all four generated paths — and passes; `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` is green on the current head.

**Known non-green check:** `check-lint` is **cancelled**, not failed — its `conclusion` is `cancelled` and its "Run check shard" step never completed. In the previous occurrence the log showed every lane reporting `finished` with zero violations before the runner received a shutdown signal (`[oxlint] FAILED (exit 143)` = SIGTERM) while in `oxlint:extensions`, a lane this PR does not touch; `main` was independently red at the same time. Every lint lane covering these files passes locally. I cannot re-run workflows from a fork; happy to push a no-op commit if a maintainer would rather re-fire it.

**Proof gap, stated plainly:** `pnpm check:changed` routes to Crabbox, which is unavailable from this machine (`selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks`), so per AGENTS.md the gates above were run locally instead of remotely. The end-to-end run uses the repo's mock provider rather than a live model; the observation it supports — which directory the agent is given — is independent of the provider. prs.title: feat(ui): add setting to opt out of right-click message actions
prs.body:
Related: #106765

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI chat thread binds a `contextmenu` handler that calls `preventDefault()` on every message bubble to show the message actions menu. There is no way to get the browser's native context menu back on a message, so users who rely on native Copy, Search or spell-check on chat text have no escape hatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit opt-out rather than changing the default: a **"Right-click message actions"** setting under Settings → Appearance → Chat, **enabled by default** so existing behaviour is unchanged. When it is turned off, `handleChatContextMenu()` returns before `preventDefault()` and the native menu opens normally.

The setting follows the existing `composerHoldToRecord` pattern — a browser-local preference persisted only when explicitly disabled. No gateway config schema change, and no change to the actions menu itself.

**Relationship to #106765 and #107137.** #106765 asks for native-menu access on *selected text* and lists three options; #107137 already implements option 2 (a Copy selection entry in the actions menu) and is further along. This PR is option 3 and is deliberately complementary, not a competing fix: it does not change selection behaviour at all, so it can land alongside #107137 or on its own. I am happy to close this if maintainers would rather keep the surface to one change.

Non-goals: no new menu entries, no change to selection handling, no change to link handling (which already falls through).

## User Impact

- Users who want the browser's native context menu on chat messages can turn off **Right-click message actions** in Settings → Appearance → Chat.
- Everyone else sees no change: the setting defaults to on and the actions menu behaves exactly as before.

## Evidence

Real-browser proof captured headless with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`.

### Screenshots

**1. Default — the actions menu opens on right-click**

![Actions menu opens on right-click by default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/04-actions-enabled-default.png)

**2. The new setting, Settings → Appearance → Chat (on by default)**

![The new Right-click message actions setting, enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/05-setting-on.png)

**3. Setting switched off**

![The setting switched off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/06-setting-off.png)

**4. After opting out — no custom menu, native menu restored**

![Right-click after opting out shows no custom menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tangotrick/openclaw/pr-proof-assets/07-actions-disabled-native-menu.png)

### Tests

New e2e case in `ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts` covering the whole chain in Chromium: the menu opens by default, the Settings toggle is clicked in the real UI and `aria-checked` flips to `false`, and the thread then leaves the event untouched. Suppression is read from `dispatchEvent()`'s return value, which is `false` only when a listener called `preventDefault()` — a browser-level fact rather than an assertion about internals.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  ui/src/e2e/chat-message-actions.e2e.test.ts -t "restores the native context menu"   → 1 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts                        → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts                    → passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts                           → 38 passed
oxfmt --check / oxlint / git diff --check                                              → clean
```

Two notes in the interest of full disclosure:

- The pre-existing case `offers Reply inline and mirrors every assistant action in the context menu` fails in my environment on a tooltip assertion. I verified it **fails identically on an unmodified `main` checkout**, so it is not caused by this change.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` exits non-zero, but it also does so on unmodified `main`, and none of the reported keys are the two added here.

I could not run a full-repo `tsc --noEmit` locally — it exhausts memory on my machine — so type checking on the changed surface is covered only by the test runs above and CI.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): detect pnpm CMD wrappers that launch .exe or .js directly
prs.body:
The resolveEntrypointFromCmdShim function only recognized npm CMD shims and direct-forwarder wrappers, but pnpm on Windows can generate CMD wrappers with a different format that was not being detected.

Extend the isPnpmCmdShim detection to handle:
- @SETLOCAL without explicit @ENDLOCAL (implicit on exit)
- @IF NOT DEFINED (not just @IF EXIST) for environment setup
- Direct .exe/.cmd/.bat/.js/.mjs/.cjs launches via %~dp0 paths
- @IF and %~dp0 appearing anywhere in the file, not on the same line

Add two new test cases for pnpm-style CMD wrapper detection.

<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query
-->

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on Windows with pnpm-installed CLIs (such as `opencode`) would see `LOCAL_READ_FAILED` errors in the OpenClaw Web UI session catalog, with the message "Local OpenCode sessions are unavailable."

The root cause was that pnpm generates CMD wrapper files with a different format than npm — using `@SETLOCAL` without `@ENDLOCAL`, `@IF NOT DEFINED` instead of `@IF EXIST`, and launching the target `.exe` directly rather than via `node`. The CMD shim resolution logic did not recognize this format, causing it to throw an `"unresolved-wrapper"` error instead of extracting the actual executable path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extended the `isPnpmCmdShim` detection in `resolveEntrypointFromCmdShim` to match the actual pnpm CMD wrapper format. The detection now checks for:
- `@SETLOCAL` presence (no longer requires `@ENDLOCAL`)
- Any `@IF` statement in the file (not just `@IF EXIST`)
- `%~dp0` appearing anywhere in the file (not only on the same line as `@IF`)
- Direct executable references via `%~dp0` paths matching `.exe`, `.cmd`, `.bat`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` (not only `node` invocations)

When a recognized pnpm wrapper is found, the resolution extracts the actual target executable path and launches it directly as an `exe-entrypoint` or `node-entrypoint`, bypassing the CMD shell entirely.

## User Impact

Users on Windows with pnpm-installed tools (such as `opencode`) will now see their local sessions correctly discovered in the OpenClaw session catalog, instead of the `LOCAL_READ_FAILED` error message. The session catalog auto-detection works without any manual configuration changes.

## Evidence

**Before:** `resolveWindowsSpawnProgram` returned `"unresolved-wrapper"` for pnpm CMD wrappers, throwing an error.

**After:** The same wrapper correctly resolves to `"exe-entrypoint"` with the actual executable path:

```
RESOLVED: {
  "command": "D:\\nodejs\\pnpm\\global\\5\\.pnpm\\opencode-ai@1.18.3\\...\\opencode.exe",
  "leadingArgv": [],
  "resolution": "exe-entrypoint",
  "windowsHide": true
}
```

**Tests:** 8/8 tests pass, including 2 new test cases covering:
- pnpm CMD wrapper that launches `.exe` directly without `@ENDLOCAL`
- pnpm CMD wrapper that launches a `.js` entrypoint via `@SETLOCAL` and `@IF`

All 6 existing tests continue to pass unchanged.

prs.title: perf(agents): preserve user envelopes across model requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes user-message envelope changes between the first model request and replay, and cache-drop reports that lose their explanation after a request without usage telemetry.

Related: #168392.

## User Impact

Persisted user timestamps, idempotency keys, and metadata are used on the first request as well as later requests. Prepared prompt content and attachment ownership stay intact. Cache-drop warnings distinguish tracked changes, changes in the final provider payload, unchanged-prefix loss of cache reuse, and unavailable evidence.

No configuration, database schema, or migration change. This does not claim that an unchanged provider payload guarantees a cache hit: provider eviction, expiration, and routing remain outside the client's evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persistence guard already correlates every runtime user with its committed row, including ordinary prompts, steering, follow-ups, and replay adoption. It now publishes that row's envelope before model transforms instead of leaving a freshly generated runtime envelope in history. Publication preserves prepared content, transient facts, and the existing image-to-attachment mapping. Late media remains a separate appended user turn; later media pruning keeps its existing owner.

The cache tracker now retains bounded change evidence until a request reports usage. The existing admitted-runner release gate additionally compares user-envelope digests before provider serialization, because providers omit many internal envelope fields from their wire payloads.

Production LOC: **+58 net lines**. The required bounded diagnostic attribution and one-time envelope publication add behavior that the old path did not provide; attachment ownership and already-frozen canonical inputs remain intact. No second projection cache, new configuration, or storage format is introduced. The existing timestamp fallback remains necessary for preflight/current prompts that have no persisted row.

## Evidence

The measured improvement is request-prefix identity, not a live cache-hit or billing claim:

- Four transformed-prompt envelope cases fail on the original code and pass with the fix. The full projection file passes **12/12**, covering steering, another turn, reopening, fallback, late media, and a preadmitted image.
- The admitted-runner release gate passes all **4 provider routes / 48 requests**, checking both serialized provider prefixes and retained user-envelope digests. System/runtime carrier rows retain their existing wire-prefix oracle.
- Cache attribution: original code fails **12 assertions**; fixed code passes **89/89** across the three diagnostic files, including omitted callbacks, missing usage, and explicitly unavailable cache telemetry.
- Image negative control: removing only preservation of the existing image-to-attachment mapping produces **2 images instead of 1**. Restoring it passes.

Heavy validation uses the authorized Linux rig fallback. Testbox `tbx_01m4m1007ys3937b520jpy2x91` had no runner after 17 minutes; AWS admission failed on regional vCPU quota; Hetzner `cbx_cb4e043e0846` was canceled after a stalled checkout sync and is confirmed deleted. No suites, builds, or typechecks ran on the saturated Mac.

Commands run on the rig use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <focused files> --maxWorkers=1` and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged`. The projection file's measured standalone run was **42.34 s Vitest / 100.34 s wall / 5,304,948 KiB peak RSS**, including a cold compiler generation. Cache diagnostic files together were **2.80 s Vitest / 5.70 s wall**. The slower integration file is necessary to cross the real persistence, prompt-building, provider, steering, and reopen boundaries; no new test file or per-test Gateway boot was added.

The rebased changed-file run passes production types, all **28 core test-type partitions**, formatting and the preceding structural guards. It stops only on the pre-existing unused `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` export in `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts`; the same dead-export scan fails on an unmodified checkout of base `6b13e9e4142d02427949b5ffbb10db574997686e`. No skip flag or unrelated fix was added. The remaining planner-selected lint, schema, database/media/sidecar, cycle and authorization checks all pass when run directly. The two closure suites pass **20/20** and docs inventory succeeds. Runtime proof totals **305 passing focused tests**, plus those 20 closure tests.

The optional export-name collision scan passes on that unmodified base. All heavy validation ran on the rig; no Team or live Gateway state was touched. CI passed on exact head `ffe4ac383afdf568d7d51c788f7ff347f2bfed36`: [run 38108141705](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38108141705), **514 seconds (8m34s)** elapsed. The required CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review statuses are green, with no pending or failed checks at merge preparation.

No live provider cache-hit measurement and no Team changes.

prs.title: fix: expose replayed chat.send errors to retrying clients
prs.body:
Closes #103703

Related: #98203
Supersedes: #98206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where backend clients retrying a failed `chat.send` with the same idempotency key could not tell that the Gateway had returned a stored result. A cached retryable error therefore looked fresh and could be resubmitted until the client's retry budget was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the broad metadata forwarding proposed in #98206 with a narrow negotiated contract:

- `response-replay` is an explicit client capability.
- The only wire metadata is the closed JSON shape `{ replayed: true }`.
- Core Gateway handlers use an internal responder with a dedicated wire-metadata argument.
- Plugin handlers retain the existing four-argument responder contract; the plugin adapter strips any attempted fifth argument.
- Clients without the capability receive the unchanged strict response envelope.
- The official TypeScript Gateway client advertises the capability and exposes `GatewayClientRequestError.replayed`, providing an in-tree consumer.

`runId`, diagnostic `error`/`channel` values, and plugin metadata are never copied into the response metadata object.

## User Impact

Retrying clients can stop resubmitting the same idempotency key after the Gateway returns a stored retryable error. Existing clients and native apps that do not advertise `response-replay` see no new response-frame fields.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `6f9a607b90393b14d769ec4696b99a6dc057498f`; current PR head is `4d4b07963d666bc2ac3ac5665b72998b3ab109da`.
- Exact-head loopback WebSocket proof passed through the current `message-handler.ts` and official `GatewayClient`:
  - legacy `caps: []` received the unchanged response with no `meta`;
  - the official client advertised `response-replay`, received only `meta: { replayed: true }`, and raised `GatewayClientRequestError` with `gatewayCode: "UNAVAILABLE"`, `retryable: true`, and `replayed: true`;
  - log-only sentinels were absent from both wire responses.
- Plugin ownership regression passed: a plugin's attempted fifth responder argument is removed before the core responder is called.
- Full plugin loader suite passed: 175/175.
- Focused protocol, client, Gateway handler, and cached-chat suites passed: 247/247 across 9 test files.
- Plugin SDK surface check passed with no forbidden package exports.
- Full TypeScript project graph passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json`.
- Protocol and Swift models remain aligned; `ResponseFrame.meta` is optional and legacy clients retain the strict old envelope.

The earlier live WebSocket capture in #98206 establishes the original dropped-metadata behavior. The current exact-head proof separately verifies the negotiated compatibility, core-only producer boundary, and official-client behavior introduced by this PR.

prs.title: feat(goal-driver): completion contracts, wait barriers, and an optional completion judge
prs.body:
# feat(goal-driver): completion contracts, wait barriers, and an optional completion judge

> **Stacked on #102261** (`feat/interactive-parity`) — only the last **3 commits** are new here
> (`82879720c8`, `21792a1a3f`, `67c5600a13`). Merge the parity PR first; this one then reduces to
> a small, purely-additive goal-driver series.

## What

Three opt-in upgrades to the experimental goal driver that make long goal runs **converge**
instead of firing continuations until the no-progress ceiling trips. 

### 1. Completion contracts (`82879720c8`)

`SessionGoal` gains an optional structured contract — `outcome / verification / constraints[] /
boundaries[] / stopWhen` — settable at goal-create time or later via the new **`set_goal_contract`**
tool. The driver folds the contract block into **every continuation prompt**, so each nudge restates
what "done" means and which constraints bound the work, instead of re-sending a bare objective.

- Absent or all-empty contracts are dropped on normalize → a free-form goal's prompt is
  **byte-for-byte unchanged**.
- Also fixes a pre-existing broken `completeQueuedChatTurn(2-arg)` call in
  `driver.integration-probe.test.ts` that left `tsgo:test` red on the base branch.

### 2. Wait barriers — gate g5 (`21792a1a3f`)

Goals can now **park** instead of burning continuation turns on async waits. `SessionGoal` gains an
optional barrier (`waitingUntil` epoch **or** `waitingOnSessionKey`), surfaced via the new
**`set_goal_wait`** tool (`seconds` backoff | `session_key` watch). New driver gate **g5**:

- While a barrier is set and unsatisfied → re-arm at the floor, do **not** fire, and do **not**
  consume a no-progress turn from the ceiling.
- A satisfied barrier (deadline passed / watched session's run ended) clears itself; the next wake
  resumes normal gating. Barriers auto-drop on any goal status change.

This is the "waiting on CI / waiting on a subagent" primitive: the goal stays alive without the
driver nudging a session that has nothing to do yet.

### 3. Optional LLM completion judge (`67c5600a13`)

Config-gated via **`tools.experimental.goalDriver.judge.enabled` (default: off)**. After a goal turn
completes and gates g1–g5 pass — and before a continuation fires — a bounded judge call classifies
the run: **`done`** → mark the goal complete (no continuation), **`wait`** → park behind the g5
barrier, **`continue`** → fire exactly as before.

- **No new provider plumbing.** The judge reuses the existing simple-completion utility-model seam
  (`prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` + `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel`) — the same
  seam `conversation-label-generator` uses. `judge.modelRef` overrides the model if desired.
- **Fail-open by construction.** Unavailable model, transport error, empty/unparseable output, or a
  thrown judge all resolve to a normal continuation — a broken judge can never wedge progress; the
  no-progress ceiling remains the backstop.
- **No async-gap races.** The judge await re-checks the pre-fire gates before firing
  (queue-nonempty → re-arm; goal deactivated mid-judge → safe no-op), so a user message landing
  during judge deliberation behaves exactly like the sync path.

## What Problem This Solves

Today the goal driver fires continuations blindly until the no-progress ceiling trips: a goal whose
work is actually finished keeps getting nudged, a goal waiting on CI or a subagent burns its
continuation budget on "still waiting" turns, and each nudge re-sends a bare objective with no
definition of done. With contracts + barriers + judge enabled, a goal run converges instead: every
continuation restates the verification surface (contract) → async waits park instead of spinning
(barrier) → the driver notices verifiable completion instead of nudging a finished session until the
ceiling trips (judge). Each piece is independently useful and independently off by default.

## Behavior when you change nothing

None. No contract → identical prompts. No barrier → g5 passes trivially. No judge config → the
driver fires continuations exactly as on main. All config additions are `.strict()` zod objects with
help + labels wired.

## Example

```jsonc
// openclaw.jsonc
{
  "tools": {
    "experimental": {
      "goalDriver": {
        "enabled": true,
        "judge": { "enabled": true } // optional; uses the agent's utility model
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```text
agent → set_goal_contract { outcome: "PR #42 merged", verification: "gh pr view 42 → MERGED",
                            stopWhen: "CI green and merged" }
agent → set_goal_wait     { seconds: 300 }        // parked: waiting on CI
driver: [g5] barrier unsatisfied → re-arm (no ceiling turn consumed)
driver: barrier cleared → gates pass → judge → { verdict: "done", reason: "PR is merged" }
driver: goal marked complete — no further continuations
```

## Evidence

- **40** passing in the focused goal-driver suite (`node scripts/test-projects.mjs
  src/agents/goal-driver/`) plus **27** in `src/config/sessions/goals.test.ts`, including new
  suites: contract prompt folding, g5 barrier gating (fire/park/clear/auto-drop), judge branching

prs.title: fix(cli): plugin commands hide their failure reason
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin CLI commands (for example `openclaw ltm`, `openclaw team-reports`, `openclaw workboard`, `openclaw onnx`) print only "[openclaw] The CLI command failed." when their action throws, hiding the actual reason (bad flag value, missing card, Gateway-side error).

## User Impact

User impact: a failing plugin command now prints its reason on stderr and exits 1, like core commands do. In `--json`/`machineOutput` mode the stdout failure envelope is unchanged. `--debug` still shows the reason and stack. This applies to every plugin registered through `api.registerCli`, including third-party plugins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root failure renderer intentionally keeps unclassified errors terse (#163381). Core commands opt out of that with `runCommandWithRuntime`, but plugins had no equivalent, and the only SDK path to it is the deprecated `plugin-sdk/cli-runtime` barrel. An inventory of the `registerCli` plugins found about 17 with actions whose errors escaped unreported.

Rather than add a wrapper to each plugin, or a new SDK subpath, the existing core binding that already wraps every plugin Commander action and hook (`bindPluginCliProgram`) now classifies escaping errors as `ExpectedCliError`. The root renderer and its terse policy for non-plugin errors are unchanged. The following pass through untouched: errors the root already classifies (Gateway transport guidance, credentials, state-owner errors), Commander's own exits, and `ExitError`. The same boundary also stops `run-main` from silently swallowing a `commander.*`-coded error thrown from a plugin action body. The classifier loads lazily at CLI registration, so the Gateway's plugin registry does not import CLI failure modules.

Two small plugin fixes ride along, because their messages are now visible. memory-wiki's `--backend`/`--corpus` parsers raise a Commander invalid-argument error so Commander names the option. team-reports reports "--period must be day, week, or month." instead of raw ZodError JSON. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/cli-and-discovery.md`.

Scope note: `openclaw qa` is registered by core (`register.subclis.ts`, private QA facade), not through `api.registerCli`, so it is unaffected here; qa-lab needs its own boundary.

## Evidence

Real CLI (`pnpm openclaw`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/config, dist built from this commit vs `origin/main` 5cdfc2f08e35):

| Command | stderr before | stderr after |
|---|---|---|
| `ltm list --limit abc` | `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint (reason only in stdout JSON) | `--limit must be a positive integer` (stdout JSON envelope identical) |
| `team-reports list --period yearly` | generic failure line + doctor hint | `--period must be day, week, or month.` |
| `team-reports show day 2026-01-01` against a real isolated Gateway | generic failure line + doctor hint | `Report not found; generate the requested UTC day first` (`--json` envelope identical) |
| `workboard show no-such-card` | generic failure line + doctor hint | `Card not found: no-such-card` |
| `onnx download bogus-model` | generic failure line + doctor hint | `Unknown ONNX model 'bogus-model'. Run openclaw onnx models.` |

All exit 1 before and after. Passthrough checks: `team-reports status` against an unreachable Gateway still prints "Couldn't connect to OpenClaw." plus the gateway status hint; `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` still prints Reason + Stack.

Tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Vitest duration):

- `src/entry.run-main.test.ts`: 12.7s, base 11.3s. Covers the full root path: a plugin command registered through the real instrumented API, exact stderr, exit 1, and the JSON envelope.
- `src/plugins/api-facades.cli.test.ts`: 7.9s, base 9.4s. Covers binding wiring for async and sync actions, hooks, prepared trees, Commander exits, commander-coded errors, and host-owned commands left unwrapped.
- `src/cli/failure-output.test.ts`: 9.9s. Covers the classification matrix and debug behavior.
- `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts`: 12.4s. Commander stderr for an invalid `--backend`.
- `extensions/team-reports/src/cli.test.ts`: 7.0s. Readable validation messages with no Gateway call.

Also passing: tsgo for core, extensions and the touched test projects; oxlint; oxfmt; `pnpm check:import-cycles`; `pnpm build` (including the CLI bootstrap import guard); `pnpm docs:check-links`; Codex autoreview (clean).

Known gap: no bundled `registerCli` plugin currently throws a commander-coded error from an action body, so that path is proven by the binding and root-path tests rather than a real command.

prs.title: feat(ui): add guarded Lit-to-Solid codemod
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Solid 2 migration needs a repeatable way to convert mechanical Lit bindings and identify the sites that still require ownership decisions.

## User Impact

No change to the shipped Control UI. Migration workers get a read-only codemod by default, optional TSX copies, and a lint error for unresolved conversion markers. This lane adds no dependencies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the native TypeScript parser for bindings and expressions, with a markup tokenizer checked against HTML parsing. Convert supported templates, properties, events, booleans, classes/styles, translations, conditionals, and lists; retain unsupported source with located `TODO(solid2)` comments. The regular boundary lint gate rejects those comments before a port can land.

Ordinary function children remain text; only known converted-JSX contracts opt in to execution. Controllers, lifecycle/cancellation, custom and async directives, and ambiguous rendering semantics remain manual. The converter does not synthesize reactive state or move ownership.

Release-note context: additive migration tooling, with no end-user behavior change. Built on the Solid toolchain foundation in #168305. The branch was rebased onto main before final CI; the PR contains only this lane's thirteen files.

## Evidence

- Final head: `b5be43b8be7280dc02f3b8ed227a3f077c9df72a`. [CI run 38101496892](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38101496892) passed the 264-test codemod file, production types, all selected test-type stripes, changed lint, core lint, source contracts, guards, ratchets, docs, and Node test shards. The codemod test file took 1.974 seconds in CI. Standalone `pnpm test test/scripts/lit-to-solid.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` was measured at 24.83 seconds on the shared Mac before the final deletion regression; that added regression also passed its focused replay.
- Overall CI remains red solely for `typescript(unbound-method)` at `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-operation.test.ts:51`, a file unchanged from the branch base. [Failed extension-lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38101496892/job/114358711752). This is outside P1-12's scope. Landing is explicitly authorized through the native inherited-failure route; no extra CI run was dispatched. A focused reproduction against a complete source archive of merge base `4754d394130ae9106c863e97c31392fba6bd614f` ran `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --type-aware --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-operation.test.ts` and exited 1 with the identical `typescript(unbound-method)` diagnostic at 51:19. The test, complete memory-core source tree, and lint/type configs are unchanged by this PR. CI actually tested merge `bf464214bb9dfb33cc41057c4dac4d29ad44bb6e`, with parents `6b13e9e4142d02427949b5ffbb10db574997686e` and the PR head; those same inputs are unchanged against its main parent too.
- Forty independently authored goldens come from eleven real UI files. Testbox lease `tbx_01m4kw7ks7b3qcktkxh69d1m03` / [run 38088606690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38088606690) passed native `tsgo` typechecking of all forty outputs plus three supplemental fixtures. All 43 generated files are byte-for-byte identical on the final head. Command: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/solid2-p1-12/corpus/tsconfig.json` after the fixture generator. Earlier Testbox lease `tbx_01m4ktds89zcn39k5j60xberjd` passed 262 tests in 3.74 seconds of command wall time.
- The suite exercises the CLI, marker lint gate, and generated TSX through the real Solid compiler/browser runtime, including lazy JSX rendering, DOM identity, and ordinary function text with zero callback execution. Codex review is clean for the full change and the subsequent validation fixes.
- About/Debug dry-run: fifteen production files, thirty-four converted templates, eighty-two manual diagnostics. Including tests: twenty-one files, thirty-nine templates, 122 diagnostics. Compared against the Debug hand port at `43baff259e650d61674d7df2049b8e712049341c`: form property/event mappings agree; reactive projections, polling/lifecycle, and keyed lane rendering remain deliberate manual work. About has no hand-port counterpart.
- Final-head remote capacity attempts hit a fifteen-minute Testbox queue timeout, AWS quota fallback to an undersized machine, and stalled Hetzner source sync. All three Testbox leases and both direct-provider leases were stopped/released; normal PR CI supplied final-head proof. UI E2E, UI performance, native-platform, and Docker lanes were not selected; no extra runs were dispatched.

## Size and landing

Thirteen lane files: 4,908 lines added and 2 removed (new codemod/parser: 3,404 lines; tests and fixtures: 1,407 lines). No shipped UI behavior change. Existing Codex autoreview is clean. Native `merge-run --auto-merge` refused before submission because the exact-head review retained the inherited failure. Landed through `scripts/pr merge-run --admin-evidence … --confirmed-operator-admin` as `f73493e43dfbf2bbc62a59fcf44135278783eff0`. The native receipt verified the attempted head. Its parent audit recorded intervening main movement (actual parent `4b5f6f99a563a2463cd9b0359129fa0290cc71c9`). Unselected platform and release lanes remain unrun.

prs.title: refactor(ui): render channels and automations with Solid 2
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ports Channels and Automations to Solid 2 while the Control UI continues to run alongside the remaining Lit pages.

## User Impact

Existing routes, host tags, CSS classes, selectors, channel setup, pairing decisions, Nostr editing, and automation workflows are preserved. Two small spacing changes are accepted: wizard notes no longer retain Lit template indentation, and settings sections no longer reserve an empty header. No dependencies, persistence, or Gateway contracts change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registered Lit page classes are deleted. Solid consumes the existing synchronous controllers and projections. Controller callbacks read plain owner state outside reactive tracking, while source rebinding remains reactive. Remaining shared Lit helpers render in a single owned leaf boundary. The bridge supplies the existing shell-layout owner to legacy-hosted Solid roots so page layout classes continue to apply and clear on teardown.

The simplification pass removed roughly 830 lines from the initial port, including duplicated shared controls and mirrored presentation snapshots. Page production LOC is **7,390 before / 7,864 after (+6.4%)**, excluding tests and shared interop. Remaining growth is explicit JSX/component props and owner setup/cleanup. The shared Lit leaf is 34 lines and serves multiple existing helpers; it retires with those callers.

## Evidence

All local test commands use `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, one file at a time. Times include the repository dispatcher on the loaded shared Mac.

prs.title: feat(system-agent): present generic QR setup steps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin setup flows sometimes need to present a short-lived QR code and wait for an external device without leaking the underlying credential URI into chat history or requiring each consumer to build its own Gateway and UI lifecycle.

This replaces #119341 because that branch predates current `main` and cannot be updated by the current maintainer token: GitHub requires the separate `workflow` OAuth scope when an existing ref is rebased across workflow history.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds one generic `WizardPrompter.qrCode` setup primitive.
- Reuses the existing bounded PNG data-URL contract.
- Keeps settlement, cancellation locking, capability gating, expiry, and scrubbing in the wizard/session owner.
- Preserves current-main setup safety behavior and Custodian session ownership.
- Keeps Control UI transport- and provider-agnostic.
- Avoids QR-specific Gateway polling or persistence layers.

This is part 1 of 2. The Signal consumer follows in #127226.

## User Impact

Plugins can present QR-driven setup through the hosted wizard with consistent rendering, cancellation, reconnect behavior, and credential cleanup. Unsupported clients receive a visible capability error rather than credential-bearing QR state.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `f636e328552524569a984ebbdf9b7d113806a57d`.
- Parent: refreshed current `main`, `b8d6e799a31d469f60277427472b87036b1f9be7`.
- Maintainer direction: adopt `WizardPrompter.qrCode` as the generic plugin setup contract; channel consumers stay plugin-owned and the host owns capability gating, bounded rendering, cancellation, expiry, and scrubbing.
- 375 changed-file tests passed across protocol, Gateway, system-agent, wizard, Control UI, and Signal boundaries; the final ownership split additionally passed 43 hosted-wizard tests and 35 combined hosted/Signal tests.
- Core, core-test, extension, extension-test, and root-test type lanes passed.
- Changed gates, targeted formatting/lint, protocol generation/Swift checks, diff checks, and autoreview passed.
- Real Chromium + mocked-Gateway QR presentation/completion/scrubbing proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127224#issuecomment-5394501002
- Follow-up owner repairs:
  - forward channel-setup cancellation to plugin adapters;
  - fence producer settlement during PNG rendering;
  - detach locked teardown from serialized chat disposal;
  - reject expired QR projection synchronously in generic poll and system-agent rejoin paths.
  - separate cancellable external-effect authority checks from persistent-effect cancellation locks.
  - bind Gateway wizard sessions to the canonical authenticated caller.
  - pump the terminal expiry error after rejoin projection retires an elapsed QR.
  - scrub the already-rendered Control UI QR at its advertised local deadline.
- No SQLite schema or config/default surface changes.
- Exact-head required CI is green.

Supersedes #119341 after replacement proof is complete.

prs.title: refactor(cron): remove receipt custody before worker cutover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron receipt custody serialized unrelated scheduler writes, approval operations, and agent removal around held launch handles. Gateway shutdown also had to drain that second ownership layer.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is PR **2a** of the [approved worker-owned cron design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/refactor/cron-worker-owned.md). The scheduling/launch step is split into 2a (remove custody and its consumers) and 2b (move timer, manual, and event scheduling to the worker together), with result/recovery consolidation afterward.

Remove the custody owner, attachments, publications, prepared-use handles, and dependent launch/read wrappers. Existing Gateway, run, tool, permission, approval-row, deletion, and transcript owners retain their checks. The host remains the sole scheduler for this PR.

The required importer proof also exposed a pre-existing real-Gateway UI fixture slowdown: its launcher rebuilt the dirty checkout on every start, restart, and auth bootstrap. The fixture now uses the already-prepared `openclaw.mjs` entrypoint, matching the sibling E2E fixture. Assertions and timeouts are unchanged. The proof also found a stale memory test observer: pruning moved to `execute`, but the test held the writer while waiting for `run`. It now observes `execute("cache.prune")`, retaining the real queue and all row assertions.

## User Impact

Scheduling, durable receipt accounting, and database format remain unchanged. A committed standing-grant consumption authorizes one start: revocation can race that already-checked launch, while subsequent consumption sees the revocation. Run liveness, host policy, expiry, and cancellation still gate initiation. The approval documentation now states that tradeoff.

No schema, dependency, config, or CLI changes. Updates and rollback need no data migration for this change.

Refs #168072.

## Evidence

Production: **+329 / −1,620 = −1,291 lines**. Tests/support: **+190 / −1,809 = −1,619 lines**. Retired tests described the removed custody contract; receipt recovery, local permission revocation, delivery, and lifecycle contracts retain executable coverage.

- Focused owner proof: 6 files, **101 tests passed**, with `--maxWorkers=1`; 289.29 s command wall time. Measured test time: standing grants 56.291 s, Gateway close 6.059 s, source replies 16.066 s, exec grants 15.584 s, receipt store 5.503 s, receipt currentness 5.818 s.
- Initial direct/one-barrel importers plus cron owner proof: 362 further files, **4,873 tests passed**, 36 Vitest shards, 2,178.96 s wall time. The additional shared-admission proof passed 196 files / 2,825 tests (one existing platform skip), the corrected UI file / 2 tests, and the remaining 55 files / 832 tests in 767.04 s. This covers **618 unique test files** overall; the four memory-helper importers also passed separately (61 tests).
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: **passed**, 1,091.63 s. This includes production/test types, full core lint, schema/worker/line-cap guards, docs, and runtime import cycles.
- The full dead-export scan was run separately. Its only remaining findings exactly reproduce on base `9cf7fc279c26cf3493b75e703aeadac6d0deb5ee`: the existing `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs` default export and 15 model-auth/prepared-runtime exports. The full-tree scan passes with zero findings. No ignore, suppression, dependency, or baseline files were changed.
- Scoped `check:changed` runs for the UI and memory fixture repairs also passed, including extension test types and lint.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: **0 cycles**. Removed-custody reference trace and `git diff --check`: clean.
- Isolated Codex autoreview was unavailable (HTTP 401); the lane's approved fallback applies and the lead reviews this PR head. A separate read-only diff audit found no remaining likely code defect; its documentation finding was fixed.

The test wrapper prepared the E2E runtime locally (about seven minutes per source generation, dominated by TypeScript bundling). Existing Doctor auth-consumer E2E cases took 47–67 s because they launch Doctor repeatedly to verify migration and idempotency with an older plugin fixture. No timeout or retry policy changed. One additional test preparation was interrupted when concurrent lint created its temporary config; the guard correctly refused it, and the final sequence runs serially. The UI fixture failed both cases at 180 s before the launcher repair, then passed in 30.696 s and 83.369 s (162.26 s file wall time, 241.23 s including preparation). The shared-admission canary reopen case took 37.457 s while exercising worker reopen and memory-pressure retirement. The memory pruning regression originally timed out at 240 s plus 180 s cleanup; after correcting the observer it passed in 1.647 s, and all four helper importers passed (61 tests). Hosted CI timing is pending the PR run.

Validation is for the authored head `1216af901792bb9337dfa010191a48201fca3890` on task base `9cf7fc279c26cf3493b75e703aeadac6d0deb5ee`. GitHub computed `mergeable: false` against the advanced main `bbd2daf8b6def57eb0ac47c5e270c9b39cc168e6`; integration is pending the lead’s landing workflow. No merge was attempted.

prs.body:
## Current candidate and proof status

Final exact-head CI [38108100245](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38108100245) is green, including the aggregate CI, security and dependency gates. The earlier source-contract, SDK, canonical fixture and lint failures do not recur. One duplicate PR-context workflow was cancelled when the PR body update superseded it; its replacement passed on the identical head. No CI reruns or green-only pushes were used.

Head after the second conflict-only rebase: `b09cf7ae6f38b16f418f6263fc11e827d879a9ec`, based on `cfcb7bda177`. Net production reduction is now **530 lines**; tests/support are **1,300 lines smaller**. The sole conflict was metadata refresh: main removed a duplicate facts capture for fleet performance; the simplified path already captures once per coalesced refresh, so it retains that improvement without restoring generations. Affected types, both cycle checks and suppression audit pass; fresh metadata proof passes **37/37** (549.50s local wrapper wall including the suppression shard; 368.99s metadata Vitest wall).

Publication settlement was repaired before landing. All 34 originally cancelled CI suites have terminal Testbox results (28 passes, 6 failures); the two lane-caused failures are repaired, and the remaining canonical-cache, SDK-budget and lint failures are attributed below. Those results belong to the original tested merge, not this rebased head. Earlier incomplete attempts below are historical records, superseded by this terminal accounting. The refreshed Gateway-methods type graph passes, runtime cycles are zero, and the suppression audit passes 3/3. The clean-main registered SDK surface command passes as well. Final exact-head hosted CI remains the landing gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Reduces the ongoing complexity of Gateway metadata, catalog listing, notifications, and setup by removing machinery that only guarded synthetic interleavings.

## User Impact

Features, Gateway payloads, configuration, persistence formats, credential checks, and sandbox policy stay intact. Rare changes during an in-flight read are best effort: callers can receive the prepared result or a retryable failure, and the next request refreshes it. Slow catalog scans keep their slot rather than yielding between pages; the existing response budget still returns cached or pending results.

No schema, durability, retention, permission, dependency, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provenance audit distinguishes human actual-use reports from agent/maintainer PR descriptions and synthetic race tests. Most of the removed mechanisms had only the latter evidence. The smaller owners retain ordinary shutdown settlement, current authorization at effects, bounded queues/caches, and the measured lazy-metadata and catalog-cache improvements.

Net production reduction: **530 lines** against the branch base, excluding tests and test support; tests/support are separately **1,300 lines smaller**. Test deletions remove only the corresponding synthetic paths; independent privacy, publication, failure, and shutdown coverage remains.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Catalog registry epoch/context replacement during a read no longer cancels it solely for freshness. #138674 addressed slow-host delivery, not a reported hot-reload incident; an in-flight read can finish with its original registry, with current visibility filtering retained.
- Epoch-only catalog reactivation no longer retires bounded cached pages. #159457 supplied slow-provider caching, not a human epoch incident; real config/registration changes still select a new owner on the next request.
- Displaced usage refreshes can update their detached entry objects. #131667 fixed real accounting behavior, but these writes cannot overwrite the map's replacement entry; the old map-identity checks were redundant.
- Metadata refreshes no longer carry epochs, per-attempt readiness promises, superseded-settlement fences, or retry-until-current loops. #139192 used a synthetic QA provider, not a production-prevalence report; a raced read can fail visibly or use its prepared snapshot.
- Metadata/history projections no longer guard eviction settlement or recheck optional history freshness after every await. #131613/#162920 supplied synthetic counterexamples; bounded caches rebuild on the next required read and personal-account authority stays enforced.
- Session changes no longer retain a tombstone lane and supplemental broad refresh for synthetic delete/recreate churn from #150270. Bounded leading/latest coalescing can omit intermediate notices; an old, formerly visible row may remain in a client until refresh. No new private data or authority is granted: durable state, effect-time privacy, and the payload-versus-current session-ID check remain authoritative.
- Catalog work no longer requeues every page or isolates one admission queue per provider. #149030/#155114/#155670 used synthetic saturated/held-provider fixtures; one global 16-active/32-waiter FIFO remains, and slow providers can delay peers.
- Catalog publication completion uses direct promise collection instead of a registration/custody wrapper; current plugin authority before effects and ordinary publication settlement remain. Late callback registration outside the provider contract is not separately supported.
- Progressive catalog delivery no longer loops through selection preparation for each queued frame. A concurrent projection update may make a frame fail until the next refresh; each delivery still checks the current caller and recomputes visibility.
- A never-settling catalog provider retains its bounded operation scope until settlement instead of a detachable cache-owner object. #163688's evidence was synthetic; it still holds an admission slot, so the global bound prevents unbounded active accumulation. Delivery expiration and callback detachment remain.
- Setup no longer checks for shutdown synchronously triggered from inside its constructor. #139783 forced this reentrancy; a pre-construction signal check, normal abort listener, and runner settlement remain.
- Setup auth retries no longer queue superseding replacements. #160574 used deterministic handler tests; one retry owns cancellation/cleanup and overlapping retries receive the existing busy response.
- Replacing fields on an internal request-options container no longer revokes its original authority. #150823/#166621 did not establish a human incident; captured transport facts and live security callbacks still govern every effect, with exact-object authority stored in a WeakMap.
- Forks no longer re-resolve upstream links, harness registries, or config targets after each await, or carry the nested source-transaction handshake from #155358/#165796's forced interleavings. #167504's forced link replacement/deletion test table is removed with that mechanism. The original upstream choice can finish; one source-incarnation check and current caller/creator/sandbox authorization remain.
- Message cuts no longer duplicate source-identity and placement checks before their effect-time checks. These duplicates originated in #110660's feature implementation, not an incident report. A rejected request can do read-only preparation first; the current source, caller, sandbox, placement and transcript guards still decide whether any effect is allowed.

## Evidence

Reviewed candidate: `b09cf7ae6f38b16f418f6263fc11e827d879a9ec`. Two conflict-only rebases preserve main's worker-prepared runtime ownership, formatted event errors, and single-capture metadata refresh. The conflict-resolved metadata owner is byte-identical to the independently reviewed pre-rebase candidate.

- Retained security effects: [final-effect authority proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168690#issuecomment-6103768761) exercises three real-writer/RPC cases and the actual native client/request adapter over loopback WebSocket: allowed caller sends one `thread/fork` frame; revocation during awaited preparation sends zero. This is synthetic protocol proof, not a live account or deployed Gateway claim. Those authority modules are unchanged by the repair/rebase.
- Publication correction: broad proof caught a real early-settlement regression if completion registration throws. The small helper now joins issued work and rethrows the registration error. Both full affected files passed **35/35** (1076.04s local wrapper wall); after the equivalent lint-safe extraction, both retained settlement cases and type-aware lint passed. No custody wrapper was restored.
- Focused coverage also includes 37/37 catalog/metadata cases after removing only obsolete scheduling expectations; 106 metadata/event cases before deleting the obsolete capture spy; the corrected event file then passed 13/13. The rewind/storage/upstream/incognito run retained 80 passing cases; its two synthetic mid-fork link-change cases were deleted with the removed guard.
- Bounded refresh regression: a 128-request burst produced 128 captures before coalescing and one after. The existing single-flight test passed; no timeout, skip, retry, suppression or baseline was widened.
- Fresh post-rebase Gateway-methods type graph passes; runtime cycles are **0**; suppression audit passes **3/3**. Final metadata/static-cycle results are recorded in the current status above.

[Original exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38095454560) tested merge `b429c1eff7ff658dacce8c6df860e8066f1b0ffb` (source `a873351c3417a36ad3ef1e4a48ab62feef894352`). `check-source-contracts` failed on duplicate `resolveChannelDmPolicy` exports in two unchanged channel files; the identical failure reproduced on clean main `97e81ce0d5d96449449b545b80fb0c989c591c78`. The aggregate gate failed downstream and 34 jobs were cancelled.

Every cancelled suite was subsequently executed on that immutable merge, using two sequential Testbox leases, now stopped: [38096290073](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096290073) and [38101073221](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38101073221). **28 passed; six retained failures** are individually attributed:

| Replacement job | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-2 | Obsolete source-link successor assertion removed; all security/source-incarnation/storage cases retained. |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-21 | Real publication-settlement regression repaired before landing, as above. |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-12 | Canonical fixture deletions omitted cache receipts. Main fixed this in `7cc1ca64798`; the two initiating cases pass on clean main `5ff4d101c72`. |
| checks-node-compact-small-1 | SDK export/deprecation budget drift. Both affected budget cases and the actual registered SDK surface command pass on clean main `5ff4d101c72`. The Linux-only test itself was not run on macOS. |
| check-lint-core-1 | Unchanged baseline lint debt. Twelve remaining max-lines findings reproduce on clean main across both core jobs; prior cache lint findings were fixed upstream. |
| check-lint-core-2 | Same baseline max-lines reproduction; prior unbound-method finding was fixed upstream. None of the named files or lint budgets was changed here. |

Passing replacement proof covers build, 85 Control UI tests, browser extension E2E, package boundaries, nine ratchets, production types, all selected core/root/extension/script test types and all other selected Node rows. Setup-only browser mode and missing-Bun failures were corrected without changing source or weakening guards; only unstarted groups were then run. Old-merge results are reused only for unchanged inputs, never described as final-head hosted CI. No CI rerun or green-only push was requested.

<details>
<summary>Coverage ledger: every original KEEP row re-evaluated</summary>

| Owner | Provenance and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Metadata superseded settlement/readiness | Remove synthetic epochs, per-generation promises and retry loops from #139192. |
| Metadata lazy preparation/cache bounds | Keep measured #149716 improvement (83.535s to 0.276s) and actual-use report https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149538; remove surrounding freshness fences. #148411 is itself a harness reproduction, not a human incident. |
| Optional history/model-list caches | Keep nonblocking exact-profile reads and #162326's measured CPU/allocation wins; remove #131613/#162920's post-await and eviction fences. |
| Personal-account authority | Keep live authority before credential-bearing requests; explicit security exception, not an incident claim. |
| Metadata shutdown | Keep ordinary active-work joins, including evicted preparation. |
| Session change ordering | Remove #150270 synthetic churn machinery; retain bounded coalescing and current identity/privacy at publication. |
| Catalog fairness/admission | Remove #149030/#155114/#155670 synthetic per-step/per-provider scheduling; retain global bounded FIFO and cancellation. |
| Catalog publication tail | Remove wrapper; retain plugin consumer settlement and authority before effects. |
| Catalog lifetime/operations | Remove repeated freshness/detachable cache-owner layers; retain 60s delivery expiration, callback detachment, 128-entry bounds, per-client isolation, per-host coalescing and ordinary shutdown. |
| Catalog planning cache | Keep #159900's measured 34.4% allocation and 22.2% instrumented-time improvement. |
| Catalog adoption/creator identity | Keep source-incarnation and provider-versus-local attribution/privacy boundary. |
| Setup admission | Remove #139783 constructor reentrancy guard; retain canonical write lock and ordinary runner/root settlement. |
| Setup retries | Remove #160574 supersession chain; preserve credential authority and one active replacement. |
| Config write CAS | Keep one effect-time check: documented public baseHash contract and ordinary concurrent editor writes. |
| Config auth response ordering | Keep security ordering and documented runtime-application contract; PR explanations alone are not treated as human incidents. |
