prs.title: fix(media): preserve encoded image filenames across delivery
prs.body:
Closes #120118

## What Problem This Solves

Image optimization and MIME sniffing can change the encoded format without changing the public filename. A transparent WebP converted to PNG was returned and durably queued as PNG bytes with `image/png` while still named `.webp`; large QQBot image uploads then submitted that stale name to `upload_prepare`.

The same public metadata owner must also strip source path components even when the encoded MIME already matches the extension. Otherwise a direct Windows/local filename can leak directory information into outbound metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared web-media result reconciles image leaf names with the normalized output MIME while leaving raw-loader metadata and durable artifact paths untouched. Every optimized image result—preserved or converted—passes through that public metadata owner. QQBot performs the same narrow reconciliation only at its chunked image-upload boundary, reading the bounded prefix from the already-verified descriptor so it does not reopen, rename, or replace source custody.

The split is intentional: normal direct/local/remote and queue replay paths belong to `loadWebMedia`; large QQBot local paths can bypass that loader, and only the chunked endpoint sends a server-visible image filename.

Production LOC: +55/-23 (net +32). Tests and test support: +320/-2 (net +318). The production growth implements the shared filename/MIME/privacy invariant plus the QQBot verified-descriptor boundary; it adds no config, protocol, dependency, storage schema, or compatibility surface.

## User Impact

Converted and sniffed images now carry leaf filenames that match their encoded bytes without exposing source directories. Equivalent aliases such as `.jpeg` for `image/jpeg`, unknown image formats, non-image uploads, raw-loader metadata, and SQLite-owned spool paths remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Original source-blind reproduction on `804ae7f1217fd095484485a05798f6816db0ca0f`: queue replay returned PNG bytes/MIME named `transparent.webp`, preserved a `.webp` spool path containing the PNG signature, and replayed the same UUID `.webp` name: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31139366120
- Original repaired behavior proof returned `transparent.png` and a UUID `.png` public name while the durable path remained `.webp` with the same PNG bytes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31139880371
- The clean rebase onto current `main` preserved all seven original commits exactly under `git range-diff`.
- Rebased focused proof: web-media 91/91, delivery spool 15/15, QQBot chunk upload 13/13 on Testbox `tbx_01kzf3jxy2w1anmcsrpsdh50m2`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31221922361
- AutoReview found that preserved matching-extension images could bypass leaf-name sanitization. The owner was repaired before publication, and the new Windows-path/mixed-case JPEG regression passes in the 92/92 media suite on Testbox `tbx_01kzf513vdj9101cb4khagfys4`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31223486982
- Final rebased `check:changed` passed core/extension production and test typechecks, lint, formatting, plugin boundaries, dead-code, import cycles, storage guards, and media guards on Testbox `tbx_01kzf5b4bs9s7dmpz90xvxpnkz`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31223810874
- Exact-head hosted CI passed on attempt 2: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31224540204/attempts/2. Attempt 1 had one unrelated `assistant-transcript-repair` shard failure; that exact file passed 7/7 on Testbox `tbx_01kzf6edj53w91ddr4w8yp0xd9` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31224920438) and the full shard rerun passed without a code change.
- Final xhigh P2 AutoReview returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings (0.94 confidence); TruffleHog was clean.
- Direct dependency source: `file-type@22.0.1` exports `reasonableDetectionSizeInBytes = 4100` from its shipped `source/index.js`; QQBot bounds its verified-descriptor probe to that value.

## Remaining pre-land proof

- Authenticated QQBot chunked image upload confirming the server accepts the reconciled leaf filename for the real large-image path.
- `QQBOT_APP_ID` and `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET` are not exported and no matching QQBot/QQ/Tencent credential exists in the service-account-accessible Molty vault. The mandatory one-password workflow requires explicit consent before searching or using the personal 1Password account.

The final exact head is `4942a882bb5f51938f22bcc40730248ed9c17190`.

AI-assisted: yes. No agent transcript is included because public transcript insertion requires separate explicit consent.

prs.title: fix(ai): mark interrupted stream usage as unavailable
prs.body:
fix(ai): report unknown usage when streaming fails before usage chunk

Closes #119244

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI (and other streaming) model turns would see **0 tokens / $0 cost** when a stream failed or dropped before the final usage chunk arrived.

Affected workflow: streaming model usage accounting (session totals, cost rollups, transcript usage) after proxy timeouts, connection resets, or other mid-stream failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider streams often initialize usage to zeros and only fill real counts from a terminal usage payload. On interrupt, those zeros were still emitted as if measured.

This change records provenance with `usageReport: { state: "available" | "unavailable" }` (same style as `contextUsage` / `cacheTelemetry`): set `available` only after a real provider usage payload; set `unavailable` when a stream ends or fails without one. Downstream accounting treats `unavailable` as non-measured so placeholder zeros are not billed or accumulated.

Non-goals: client-side token estimation; changing successful-turn totals when the provider does report usage.

## User Impact

- Interrupted / incomplete streams no longer look free or zero-cost by default.
- Successful turns that include provider usage keep reporting real token and cost numbers (`usageReport: available`).
- Operators and cost tooling can distinguish **unmeasured** usage from a true zero-token turn.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local):

```text
packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions-usage-parity.test.ts
packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts
packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses.test.ts
src/agents/usage.normalization.test.ts
src/agents/usage.test.ts
→ 76 + 58 passed
Coverage includes:
- stream ends before usage chunk → usageReport: unavailable with zero buckets
- first-event timeout / responses construct failure → unavailable
- provider-reported usage success → available
- hasNonzeroUsage rejects unavailable even if buckets are positive

prs.title: fix(subagents): stop re-rendering give-up terminal failed deliveries as outstanding
prs.body:
# fix(agents): drop drained give-up terminal `failed` delivery from outstanding-context (#154834)

## What

`hasOutstandingCompletion` in `subagent-active-context.ts` counted **every** `delivery.status==="failed"` row as outstanding. A give-up path row is already terminal: `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` marks delivery `failed` and `completeCleanupBookkeeping` stamps `cleanupCompletedAt`, after which `resumeSubagentRun` hard-stops it (never redriven/announced/delivered). That dead row therefore re-rendered under **"## Child results awaiting delivery"** on every later requester turn and **survived gateway restarts** (the registry reload re-rendered it again).

The fix adds a narrow durable guard, immediately after the `requesterSettleWake` short-circuit:

```ts
if (deliveryStatus === "failed" && typeof entry.cleanupCompletedAt === "number") {
  return false;
}
```

## Boundary vs #154957 (intentional; not commenting on that PR)

This PR filters **only the durable terminal `cleanupCompletedAt`** marker. It deliberately does **not** treat in-flight `cleanupHandled` as a terminal guard — `cleanupHandled` is an in-flight lock and rows behind it may still be retried, so hiding them would suppress legitimately outstanding/retrying rows. A `failed` row that is still retrying has **no** `cleanupCompletedAt` yet, so it correctly stays visible.

## Main adaptation

Merged latest `origin/main` (`87af5763bbc`, merge-base `87af5763bbc`). Main refactored `buildActiveSubagentRuntimeContext` from sync to **async/Promise** (`withSubagentRunReadSnapshot`). All production callers and tests now `await` it; the merge retained the narrow guard.

## Proof chain (real persistence → reload → render)

New `subagent-active-context.give-up-integration.test.ts` writes two rows through the **production SQLite persistence layer** (`saveSubagentRegistryToSqlite`), seeds child sessions, disposes + reloads the registry from the same store (`resetSubagentRegistryForTests` + `initSubagentRegistry` + `activateSubagentRegistry`), then `await`s the **real** `buildActiveSubagentRuntimeContext`:

- **A** = `failed` + `cleanupCompletedAt` (drained give-up terminal) → **absent** from awaiting-delivery after reload.
- **B** = `failed`, retrying, **no** `cleanupCompletedAt` → **visible** in awaiting-delivery.

No mocked predicate / delivery records / final strings — fixture-constructed upstream rows only; persistence, reload, and renderer are production code.

## Red / green / ablation

- **Green (PR):** A absent, B visible after reload.
- **Red (guard disabled):** `run-giveup-drained` re-enters the awaiting-delivery block (test fails) — proves non-vacuous.
- Unit file: 19/19 (drops terminal failed; keeps retrying failed; keeps pending/in_progress/suspended; keeps settle-wake-owned failed).
- Focused batch (active-context, give-up-integration, delivery-state, persistence, persistence.resume): 24/24.

## Gates

`check:changed` EXIT=0: format, lint core, typecheck core + core tests, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries, db registry/ratchets, import cycles, dependency pins — 0 issues, 0 suppression. Local autoreview (`--mode local --base <merge-base> --max-priority P2`): **scoped-clean**, 0 P0–P2 findings.

## Honest live-verification gap

Durable ClawSweeper review on this exact new head is pending re-request; no live external proof is claimed until that verdict lands.

## What Problem This Solves

`hasOutstandingCompletion` in `subagent-active-context.ts` treated **every** row with `delivery.status === "failed"` as outstanding. A give-up delivery row is, however, already terminal: `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUp` marks it `failed` and `completeCleanupBookkeeping` stamps `cleanupCompletedAt`, after which `resumeSubagentRun` hard-stops it — it is never redriven, announced, or delivered. That dead row therefore kept re-rendering under **"## Child results awaiting delivery"** on every later requester turn, and because the bookkeeping is durable it also survived gateway restarts (the registry reload re-rendered it again), so requesters saw phantom outstanding work that was in fact already finished.

## Evidence

- **Terminal `failed` + `cleanupCompletedAt` dead row reproduces on every requester turn:** the drained give-up row re-appeared under "Child results awaiting delivery" on each later requester context and again after a registry reload. The narrow guard — `if (deliveryStatus === "failed" && typeof entry.cleanupCompletedAt === "number") return false;`, placed right after the `requesterSettleWake` short-circuit — removes only that drained, terminal row.
- **Narrow guard does not hide in-flight / retrying work:** the guard keys on the durable terminal `cleanupCompletedAt` marker only. It deliberately does **not** treat in-flight `cleanupHandled` as a terminal guard — `cleanupHandled` is an in-flight lock and rows behind it may still be retried, and a `failed` row that is still retrying has **no** `cleanupCompletedAt` yet, so it correctly stays visible in awaiting-delivery.

Row A (`failed` + `cleanupCompletedAt`) is absent from awaiting-delivery after reload; row B (`failed`, retrying, **no** `cleanupCompletedAt`) stays visible. No mocked predicate / delivery records / final strings — fixture-constructed upstream rows only; persistence, reload, and renderer are production code.

Related: #143915

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu users can see a processing card until a whole answer appears when a reasoning-enabled Completions response defers public text for terminal classification. Operators who accept provisional prose currently cannot opt into seeing that body while it is generated without changing the canonical output policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit, default-off `channels.feishu.streaming.bodyPreview` option (also available per account). The built-in Completions transport emits a separate replaceable public-text snapshot, which the existing Agent and reply callback path carries to Feishu cards without inserting it into assistant history, committed blocks, or final text. The generic contract and opt-in policy are proposed for maintainer review in #143915.

The preview owner filters native/tagged reasoning and tool arguments, bounds snapshot growth, and resets on reasoning transitions, tool calls, cancellation, and failure. Feishu keeps provisional text separate from its canonical buffer, accepts newer revisions, and gives committed delivery/finalization precedence. Existing silence, approval, message-tool-only, and deferred-output/hook guards remain in force.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

Is the following Feishu-first contract acceptable in principle?

- Preserve terminal-classified canonical delivery as the default. Only an explicit `bodyPreview: true` enables provisional public text.
- Allow readers to see public prose that may later be replaced or removed. Replacement cannot undo prior exposure; native reasoning is excluded.
- Accept a shared ephemeral snapshot contract: preview identity, increasing revisions, replacement, empty reset, and finalization precedence. Only consumers that explicitly opt in must implement those preview obligations; ordinary partial replies retain their behavior.

This PR implements the built-in Completions producer and Feishu consumer. The [independent WebChat report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143915#issuecomment-5968966631) supports reuse of the same boundary, but WebChat support is follow-up scope and is not claimed here. Keeping this PR Feishu-first lets maintainers assess one concrete consumer before expanding adoption.

The author is holding routine main refreshes pending that direction. Acceptance in principle would not waive client screenshots, conflict resolution, or passing integration/CI before merge.

## User Impact

With streaming cards enabled, operators can set:

```json5
{ channels: { feishu: { streaming: { mode: "partial", bodyPreview: true } } } }
```

Readers may see public tool-preface or commentary text that is subsequently replaced or removed. This tradeoff is explicit; native reasoning display is not enabled. Missing/false settings retain existing behavior. The initial producer is the built-in OpenAI-compatible Completions transport and the initial consumer is Feishu; this does not promise support for every transport or channel.

This is separate from CardKit queue coalescing discussed in #103928. It does not claim to eliminate slow platform-write backlogs.

- Published head: `ee8b552c2457f695c5f9a9a4a077b11e1d2a93c7`; open and unmerged, with conflicts against main.

- Sanitized before/after Feishu client images have not been delivered in both the originating chat and this PR. Historical CardKit acknowledgements are platform-write evidence, not proof of client rendering.

## Evidence

The [previous CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34805295607) failed in three lanes. The source-contract lane stopped during dependency installation on a GitHub release-asset HTTP 504; its source checks never ran. The other failures match upstream fixes now included in the pinned base: [Gateway reload-settlement test synchronization #147571](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147571) and [Git 2.54 fetch maintenance/worktree containment #147828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147828). The Gateway regression passed locally. The Linux-specific containment suite is not claimed as passed on Windows. A job rerun request was rejected by GitHub; no rerun was queued. The sequence is native reasoning, two provisional public paragraphs, native reasoning/reset, then canonical public text. The provider HTTP boundary alone is synthetic; CardKit acknowledgements below are actual HTTP 200 / API `code: 0` responses.

Times are seconds after each case starts; the fixture intentionally pauses 2.2s per chunk, so these are lifecycle evidence, not a model-speed benchmark.

| Configuration | Accepted body changes | Terminal event | Confirmed cleanup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| omitted | No preview; canonical body at 11.296s | 11.035s | Streaming disabled at 11.847s |

prs.title: fix(macos): warn and clear residual App Translocation quarantine
prs.body:
Closes #150102

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Peekaboo Bridge and Screen Recording / Accessibility grants look broken when macOS still launches `/Applications/OpenClaw.app` under App Translocation because residual `com.apple.quarantine` remains on the install.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw clears residual quarantine before Applications handoff/relaunch, and shows a clear alert plus a Permissions-page warning when the running app path still contains `AppTranslocation`, so users can recover stable TCC for Peekaboo and Computer Control.

## Why This Change Was Made

Residual Gatekeeper quarantine (including nested resources) can make LaunchServices keep relaunching from a temporary App Translocation path, which breaks TCC path identity even after permissions were granted to OpenClaw. This change clears that quarantine on the Applications destination before relaunch, and surfaces an explicit health warning when the process is still translocated.

## Evidence

- Unit coverage for App Translocation path detection, nested quarantine clearing, and the Permissions-page warning when `runningUnderAppTranslocation` is true.
- SwiftLint for the macOS lane is clean locally.
- Local macOS package build could not be fully compiled here (host Swift 6.2.3 vs package tools 6.3); rely on CI `macos-swift` / related gates.
- Still needed for external-PR proof: before/after screenshots of the stuck-path alert and Permissions warning, plus process path evidence showing `/Applications/OpenClaw.app/...` after quarantine clear + relaunch.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram Business updates need to stay business-scoped all the way through lane selection and pairing/access decisions. Without that boundary, Business traffic can collapse into plain chat-id lanes or lose its `business_connection_id` before downstream handling can make a safe distinction between ordinary bot DMs and secretary-mode messages.

## Summary

This is the focused business-identity slice from the Telegram Business Connect review work around #114087 / #20786.

It fixes two business-mode routing boundaries:

- business updates now use business-scoped sequential lanes instead of collapsing into plain chat-id lanes
- pairing/access decisions preserve `business_connection_id` when a Telegram Business message enters the DM access path

## Evidence

Tested locally after rebasing on current `openclaw/openclaw:main`:

prs.title: fix(agents): clear emoji/avatar on agents.update empty or null
prs.body:
<!-- maintainer-local-candidate-119930 -->
## Maintainer status — local candidate, not published

**This PR remains open at contributor head `a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c`.** The integration described here is an uncommitted, unpublished maintainer candidate (staged tree `4862cde3fbe12995820c4fc4b088fe9988ce170b`), not the current PR branch. Original work and contributor ancestry from @zyw02 are preserved.

### Proposed repair and user impact

Related: #119929. Remove → Save clears a stored avatar; clearing the custom emoji input clears that stored value. The proposed API clear contract is explicit `null`; empty, whitespace, and omitted API fields preserve existing values.

On a configuration-write failure after the identity file changes, the candidate saves the previous bytes (or a prior-absence marker) and returns an actionable pending-recovery error. It never restores or deletes the current identity file, which may contain a newer external edit. Operators must compare the recovery artifact, current file, and configuration before retrying and remove the artifact after reconciliation. **This is not automatic rollback or a multi-file transaction.** The earlier conditional-rollback claims below are historical contributor notes, not an accepted correctness claim.

Current ownership checks, authenticated avatar rendering, generated protocol declarations, and legacy Swift initializer call shapes are retained. Text-only default avatars do not expose a misleading Remove action after reload.

### Candidate validation

- The unchanged baseline reproduced the null-schema failure and all four failed-config recovery cases.
- Focused protocol, identity-file, agent-config, Gateway, and UI suite: 221 tests passed before the final UI regression additions.
- Final acceptance passed all four selected Vitest shards: Gateway mutation coverage, 38 UI tests, a real Gateway serving the built Control UI, and SDK coverage. One optional external-live SDK test was skipped; this is not authenticated external-service proof.
- The real served-UI test verifies empty/omitted RPC preservation, Remove → Save, persisted config/file clearing, unrelated Markdown preservation, and browser reload with no remaining Remove action.
- 16 final validation lanes passed. Unavailable/failing final lanes: FINAL-LINT-APPS, FINAL-MACOS-CI. See limitations below. Task-file lint and Swift generated-output consistency passed. These are local results, not exact-head CI.

### Inspected served-UI proof

These sanitized, synthetic-state screenshots are from the **unpublished candidate** and a real local Gateway, not a mocked Gateway.

Before removing the stored avatar and custom emoji:

![Before Remove and Save — unpublished maintainer candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c4beb5b-4ef2-4896-a437-51dbd9f7e1df)

After Save and browser reload (generic avatar and default emoji placeholder, no saved custom values):

![After Save and reload — unpublished maintainer candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee70a744-4b3b-4a29-bbf1-e2540589eed0)

### Remaining gates

Independent source-bound review remains unavailable under the inherited quota hold; no unchanged retry or provider switch was made. Explicit additive-null/pending-recovery contract acceptance and current required owner review remain pending. Swift compatibility compilation/tests, app lint, and the macOS CI lane (142 passed, 10 failed) are blocked by this host's unaccepted Xcode license/SourceKit setup; generated-output consistency is not compilation or lint proof. Originating-chat screenshot delivery is not established by this PR update. Reviewed publication, exact-head CI, and native landing remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor notes for the published head (not current maintainer validation)</summary>

## Review feedback addressed

Follow-up on `479698f24256882db910081831bc1e9ce4d0fe12`. New head: `a86cfd4e370614dfbbaffc05b23a26dd9710af0c`.

ClawSweeper review on `479698f` required the IDENTITY.md rollback to be conditional at its final write, not only before an awaited restore. This tip:

1. **[x] Make the rollback conditional at its final write (P1)** — `restoreWorkspaceFile` re-reads current IDENTITY.md bytes immediately before write/delete and skips when the file is no longer this mutation's content. Same-process `agents.files.set` of IDENTITY.md now takes `withConfigMutationExclusive`, serializing it with `agents.update` rollback. Regression: `does not restore IDENTITY.md over a concurrent agents.files.set edit that lands after the rollback comparison`.
2. **[x] Prevent rollback from overwriting concurrent IDENTITY.md edits (P1)** — after a config-commit failure, restore the previous file only when IDENTITY.md still contains this mutation's write at the mutating syscall. A concurrent `agents.files.set` edit is left in place. Also covered: `does not restore IDENTITY.md over a concurrent agents.files.set edit after config commit failure`.
3. **[x] Preserve partial raw Swift identity initializers (P1)** — generated mixed `AgentsUpdateParams` overloads now cover none (`agentid:modelvalue:`), emoji-only, avatar-only, and both String labels. Mixed labels still omit defaults so the raw initializer stays unique. Compile-oriented coverage is in `GatewayModelsCompatibilityTests`.
4. **[x] Make file and config identity updates failure-safe (P2)** — snapshot destination `IDENTITY.md` before rewrite, write rebuilt content, then commit config. If that later commit throws and the file is still this mutation's write, restore the previous file bytes (or remove a newly created file) before rethrowing. Regression: `restores IDENTITY.md when it still contains this mutation's write after config commit failure`.
5. **[x] Current-head CI caused by this diff** — Control UI Remove-avatar fixture no longer uses `agentsList.scope: "workspace"` (`check-test-types-core-2`); `mergeAgentIdentity` iterates `IDENTITY_PATCH_KEYS` instead of an uncommented `Object.entries` assertion (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`); dropped invalid `NodeInvokeRequestEvent.sessionKey` Swift coverage (`macos-swift`). `android-ktlint` 429 / promisor fetch on the previous head was infrastructure. Current-head `macos-swift` failure on `479698f` was `CronJobsStoreTests` (`GatewayProcessManager.shared.status → .starting == .stopped`), unrelated to this identity-clear diff.
6. **[x] Resolve merge conflicts (P1)** — replayed on `42f5717` from `2db308f06b9` onto `671e41a8773bb9df6f044372fe227f7415a45b38`. Conflict files: `src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts`, `src/commands/agents.config.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/types.ts`, `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts`, `ui/src/pages/agents/view.test.ts`.
7. **[x] Preserve current agent ownership safeguards** — `agents.delete` still uses `agentOwnsSharedAuthStore`, `isInheritedAuthStoreOwner`, `tryResolveSoleAgentId`, and `normalizeAgentIdStrict`. Roster updates still pin `ownership: "explicit"` and `pinLegacyInheritedAuthOwnerForRosterTransition`.
8. **[x] Keep SDK types on the protocol contract** — `AgentsUpdateParams` stays a re-export from `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` (nullable emoji/avatar live in the schema, not a local SDK duplicate).
9. **[x] Make Swift raw-model overloads non-overlapping** — mixed String-label initializers omit defaults so `AgentsUpdateParams(agentid:modelvalue:)` uniquely matches the raw initializer.
10. **[ ] Served Control UI proof** — still outstanding: redacted Remove → Save against a real Gateway. The existing UI E2E remains mock-gateway and is not claimed as served-UI proof.

Empty-string vs null remains the existing null-only tombstone contract (ClawSweeper recommendation: keep null-only clearing). Direct empty/whitespace requests still preserve stored identity.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #119929: agents.update empty/null emoji/avatar handling must clear intentionally without breaking shipped Swift call shapes or turning legacy empty-string requests into destructive clears.

## Why This Change Was Made

Null is the additive clear tombstone. Empty-string requests remain non-destructive for compatibility. Generated Swift keeps String-facing and raw AnyCodable initializers, including mixed modelvalue plus none / emoji-only / avatar-only / both String labels, without overlapping `agentid:modelvalue:` call sites. File-first identity writes stay unsafe-write gated; config-commit failures restore the previous IDENTITY.md bytes only when the file is still this mutation's write at the final syscall, so a concurrent `agents.files.set` edit is not overwritten.

## User Impact

A failed config commit after a successful identity rewrite no longer leaves a cleared IDENTITY.md against the retained roster identity, and no longer clobbers a concurrent authorized IDENTITY.md write that lands after the rollback snapshot.

prs.body:
Related historical context: #128008 and merged #128695. Current-main integration: #127836.

## Status: non-landable, test-first cancellation baseline

This revision integrates the complete twelve-file diagnostic candidate onto pinned main `b5946cfcc1623f0b423c556126ddfe960f9d3fce`, preserving all31 Session regression cases and upstream's dedicated Gateway runtime shard. Session Base/Prompting production remains byte-identical to the published `caf02b3b8035880b1431598b4582a0149fa8d721` baseline; the unpublished logical-controller repair is not applied. Four original-order defects have actual failing CI evidence, while three additional boundary reproductions and two first-reason controls remain unexecuted. Do not merge this diagnostic baseline.

## Ownership boundary and test change

The independent #127836 integration remains intact: one logical prompt stays active across retry and compaction gaps, public terminal facts drive exact steering-occurrence cancellation, and deferred-flush failure does not suppress finalization. No upstream test or queue policy is discarded.

Actual baseline failures show that an early handoff snapshot misses cancellation during awaited `agent_end` callbacks, a failed continuation can settle while a foreign core successor is active, and aborting an idle retry delay can still permit queued continuation. The unchanged Gateway fixture separately records B's failed disposition. These remain production blockers, not successful repair claims.

The existing retry table now also covers real disposal with queued input and synchronous public abort from `auto_retry_start`. It keeps the original 503 response, ten-second fake-clock delay, normal retry and empty-queue controls. The queued/disposal rows establish provider, active-retry, core-idle and queue facts before interruption. The unqueued retry-start callback instead records provider1 and core-idle; it does not require retry-controller or queue state at that notification. Disposal must leave the exact queued input dormant without a second provider request; it must not emit to listeners it has already removed. The reentrant abort case requires the original prompt to fulfill before any ten-second clock advancement, with fulfillment and rejection observation installed beforehand. Its cleanup joins the actual prompt, abort and observer before restoring real timers.

The existing post-compaction table adds a real direct-core successor acquired by the public settlement listener. It proves that B is distinct, live and unaborted, then checks that A does not publish an extension settlement into B's lifecycle. Both public and extension terminal assertions remain. The new first-reason table uses real `agent_end` and a pre-registered `waitForIdle` reaction: A retains its first handoff reason, while a later independently acquired B receives its own caller's stop reason. It does not fabricate an awaited flush; final flush is synchronous.

Source prediction on unchanged production is seven failing and 24 passing cases. The three incremental predicted failures are disposal with queued retry input, abort at retry-start notification, and public-to-extension successor reentry. Both first-reason controls are expected to pass. Those numbers are not an execution result. A strengthened public-terminal assertion may fail before the historical extension assertion in the pre-public successor case; prior later-assertion execution is not assumed.

A parked intermediate implementation exposed a new predecessor-to-successor reason-transfer regression during review. It was not published. Both production files were restored exactly to the public baseline before this test-only candidate. All source, review findings and preservation records remain retained. No public API, SDK, authorization, configuration, persistence or protocol change, production seam, timeout increase or forced replay is introduced.

The already-proved private deferred-manager repair remains unchanged: record cancellation, restart or supersession on the exact existing ReplyOperation before aborting the derived signal. Canonical methods preserve first reason, upstream, terminal, frozen, stale-expiry and retired-successor behavior; command callers without an operation remain supported.

Relative to pinned main b594, the PR has twelve changed files: runtime +27/-21 (net +6), prerequisite tooling +6, tests +1367/-66. The main integration adapts the planner test and carries upstream changes; it adds no new Session production repair. This is diagnostic staging, not acceptance of the final production shape.

## Canonical main integration

Published `d025f0e9232844ff8fe3bcfca3014214c735c9fc` could not attach CI because its test-planner expectation conflicted with current main. An older pinned preview was clean, but the actual server main b594 had one concrete planner-test conflict; no test failure or GitHub fault is inferred from that attachment state.

Upstream `ef18511a0a56bda63bc7dad8097d87ed0d3975ff` makes one dedicated Gateway runtime shard prepare the runtime, instead of doing that in each ordinary stripe. This integration preserves that canonical planner and consumer discovery. The test now keeps three strict ordinary stripes without runtime preparation and one strict dedicated-runtime entry with an independent literal inventory: active-memory, concurrent-streams and terminal-cancellation. The full/compact inventory also includes gateway-support-export-runtime. Completeness, uniqueness, and preparation checks remain; the expected inventory is not derived from the production resolver. The unchanged Gateway fixture must execute in that actual runtime shard on the new hosted candidate.

The initial resolved merge and all old public history were preserved, then all twelve candidate changes were reconstructed on a real b594 parent. The complete resulting Git tree is byte-identical to the saved resolved merge, including every upstream file. This is a clean-parent representation, not a partial index or sequencer/hook override; normal precommit checks must still scan every introduced file. No alternate index, fabricated sequencer marker, narrowed guard scan or hook override is part of this reconstruction.

## Actual public-baseline evidence

[CI33225898567](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567) executed merge `6ece55f65705e30142b509cfbc08e3e4b3f322f9`, parents `9b1bc3bb93e6a004a534c4f485f26d34c911b02a` and `caf02b3b8035880b1431598b4582a0149fa8d721`. The complete run had 163 successful jobs, 17 skipped and three failures: the Session shard, Gateway shard and aggregate gate.

The [Session shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567/job/99029643854) ran the previous 26-case file: 22 passed and four failed. The newly established idle-retry abort-with-queued-input case failed provider count, two instead of one, after real public abort and original-prompt join. Later dormant-queue, transcript, retry-ended and settlement assertions did not execute. Normal retry and abort-without-queued-input passed; the three prior late-callback/foreign-successor failures remained. The selected group had 2,337 passing, four failing and two skipped tests. Real handoff adoption passed.

The [Gateway core-3 shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33225898567/job/99029643771) failed the unchanged 135-second B-disposition bound; the whole fixture took 146,469 ms. Normal control delivered two intended replies. Aborted A reached its typed native-lane join and intended third reply. B was skipped after a missing exact pending-entry cancellation and accepted-unconfirmed warning; the wire remained at three intended replies, without an extra generic error. B's later final/history/provenance and strict-four-wire assertions were not reached.

A possible hidden continuation after the embedded observer unsubscribes could remove B's queued occurrence before transcript cleanup rejects its write. That sequence is source-inferred, not directly observed in the raw log. One logged embedded start cannot rule out a later unobserved core loop. The conservative no-replay policy and every Gateway assertion remain unchanged; eventual recovery must be demonstrated by that same fixture.

The exact executed object and parents were inspected. Critical Session/core/retry/transcript owners and the executed test sources match the published caf02/previous 26-case baseline, not the new 31-case test file. Thirteen other context/metadata deltas, including the actual runner/dependency changes, were separately read and qualified; this is not an all-package or entire-checkout parity claim.

## Review state

The fresh complete twelve-file diagnostic-integration P2 review completed eleven default automatic passes with exit0, no findings in any raw report, and helper status scoped-clean for that selected diagnostic-integration scope. Minimum confidence was 0.61. All eleven reports explicitly retained cross-batch owner limitations: the first specifically validated the ordinary/dedicated Gateway inventory, while still lacking complete ReplyOperation-to-native-abort and build-admission-to-worker relations; other batches could not independently verify complete planner or Session/Core relationships. These are complementary source assessments, not eleven complete integrated reviews or a production-completeness certificate. All reports and limitations are preserved. The243 whole-file inputs and all276 bindings, complete candidate tree and historical records were unchanged after review, and the recorded owned processes were gone. Known production cancellation blockers remain; the31-case fixture has not run.

Before this review, the genuine default formatter check passed on all twelve complete files using32 threads (201ms reported formatting time); pre/post source and relevant configuration stayed unchanged. This check made no source edits and does not substitute for normal commit guards, hosted tests or runtime proof.

AI-assisted. Independent source review accepted the complete 31-case test and its public-baseline contracts. The historical narrow test-authoring review completed three default automatic passes with exit0 and no findings in any raw report; the helper recorded scoped-clean only for the complete actual one-file test-authoring delta. Minimum confidence was 0.35. The first pass reviewed the supplied lifecycle source and found no authoring defect; the second and third explicitly lacked the complete test/fixture/Session/Core owners within their complementary batches and could not independently validate those boundaries. Those limits and all reports remain preserved, not promoted into a whole-PR certificate. That historical packet contained 101 whole-file semantic evidence inputs, and all 134 bindings plus preserved earlier artifacts were rechecked unchanged afterward. The full PR remains nonclean and non-landable; the final production repair still requires fresh whole-PR review and actual hosted proof.

Earlier complete reviews remain intact. The immediately preceding eight-pass review produced 22 raw findings, 19 after exact duplicate grouping, with exit1 and minimum confidence 0.93. Its disposal, retry-start, foreign-reason and public-to-extension findings were retained and source-adjudicated; they motivated these test-first controls and the withdrawal of the unpublished reason-transfer implementation. The prior seven-pass review retained 22 production findings, and the older eight-pass baseline review retained its three findings, including a source-disproved concurrent-test hang prediction. No report has been erased, filtered into a clean certificate or cosmetically rerun.

Older [882/cb7 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33217391928) passed all 166 successful/17 skipped jobs, seven manager controls, seven cancellation-composition cases and the strict four-reply Gateway flow. That success is historical after material upstream integration. Earlier [0eb failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33208597601) and [e464's cleanup-test authoring mistake](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33213762584), subsequently corrected and passing at882, remain disclosed.

## Limits and next proof

The five added cases and strengthened public-terminal oracles are unexecuted. After an authentic hosted baseline, the combined Session owner repair needs complete independent/static review, unchanged Gateway recovery, all sibling regressions, exact-head green CI and normal maintainer preparation.

The Gateway evidence uses the real built Gateway with local provider and Telegram HTTP fixtures, not an authenticated live account or video. B's immediate ACK alone does not establish acceptance. Native prompt/abort join is not every outer cleanup. A single immediate `agent.wait` snapshot reported `status: ok`; final cancellation projection remains a separate producer-fact follow-up, not a consumer-status remapping.

The original drained-queue loss was separately fixed by #128695. Canonical CodeMode completion coverage from #131869 superseded the obsolete observer diagnostic; the original 1719-ms observation has no newly established cause here. This PR claims no credit for those upstream changes.

#128008 is related historical context; this PR does not change its disposition or establish full queued-occurrence resolution.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve failed tool counts and unblock steering persistence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex task summaries omit rejected tool attempts when the rejection arrives before a native execution event, and completed commands that fail without that event can incorrectly remain safe to replay. The CI investigation also exposed a transcript-write deadlock that prevents a mid-turn steering message from reaching Codex after visible partial output.

## User Impact

User impact: tool summaries include malformed patches and workspace refusals, preserve earlier failures after a successful retry, and prevent automatic replay of commands that may have partially changed state before failing. Steering can also persist preceding assistant output before submitting the new input without waiting on itself. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record explicit failures through the existing tool metadata owner, keyed by call ID. Native execution events remain authoritative, and Code Mode wrappers do not add duplicate counts. Direct custom/function patch calls recognize Codex's explicit verification-failure response; unrecognized output remains outcome-unknown.

A completed command response with a nonzero exit code proves execution and now records potential side effects. Parse failures and refusals before execution do not acquire that evidence, and recovered historical failures do not become unresolved tool errors.

## Evidence

- Retained live QA evidence showed a successful inventory task recovering from a malformed patch, while its summary reported five calls and zero failures for six attempts. This candidate was validated through projector notifications; no new live provider run is claimed.
- Regression assertions failed before each fix: omitted pre-execution failures, replay safety for two executed-command cases, and direct malformed custom/function patch calls. The final run passed **48 tests across three projector suites**, including retry recovery, repeated notifications, native-event deduplication, unknown output, and output fidelity.
- Test command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.code-mode.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.native-audit.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.output-fidelity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Measured wall time: **58.82s**; Vitest: **35.95s**. Summed test bodies: 65ms for eight lightweight cases, 1,619ms for 31 native-audit cases, and 130ms for nine fidelity cases. CI timing is not yet available.
- Production/test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, database/media/runtime-loader guards, import-cycle checks, and final managed review passed.
- Broad `check-changed` encountered an inherited unused export, `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2`, in untouched `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts` from #168482. The checks scheduled after that failure were run separately and passed; the broad command is not claimed green.

## Steering CI repair

The original eight-file CI group reproduced the same steering timeout locally: 173/178 passed, then a 120-second test timeout and 180-second cleanup timeout. The retained transcript writer queued an append; preparing its source authority requested a read through that same queue, placing the read behind the append that awaited it.

The existing storage owner now gives authority preparation the same nested, settled read scope already used by message preparation. It retains the admitted writer and generation claim, preserves the outer FIFO, and still revalidates authority immediately before committing. The existing SDK test now exercises a real same-store native binding read while retaining its late-revocation and no-main-thread-SQL assertions. No retries, longer timeouts, or weaker assertions were added.

- The unchanged nine-case steering file passed in 47.59s wall.
- The original eight-file CI group passed **178/178 tests**, 141.68s wall (137.70s Vitest), with the same plan/configuration and maxWorkers=2. Within-file order was preserved; concurrent file start order is scheduler-dependent.
- The SDK owner file passed **30/30 tests**, 126.29s wall; the strengthened case took 1.993s. With original owner bytes, that unchanged regression stalled and its diagnostic process was deliberately terminated after 70.04s. This is bounded deadlock evidence, not a completed assertion failure.
- Production core types and owning agents-sessions/plugin-sdk test types passed. Fresh isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local proof used Node26.7; original CI used Node24.19, so hosted confirmation on the new head remains pending.
- The inherited unused export is fixed upstream by 5b5a476b836. The older PR base still reports it; no suppression or unrelated code was added here.

prs.title: fix(agent): retry transient settled finalization
prs.body:
Related: #126255

## What Problem This Solves

After a tool turn is fully settled, OpenClaw can need one isolated, tool-free request to produce a visible final answer. A transient stream-idle or retryable provider interruption in that request can otherwise discard a completed browser task.

## Design

- Retry settled-turn finalization at most once.
- Retry only a typed transient/rate-limit or idle failure with no completed assistant message, no capability activity, and no canonical replay/recovery blocker.
- Preserve all existing settlement, side-effect, delivery, compaction, Codex app-server, timeout, and cancellation gates.
- Keep both attempts tool-free; tool calls, empty responses, non-retryable failures, and unsafe state fail closed.
- Bound the finalization operation with its own 300-second AbortSignal composed with the live parent signal.
- Do not mutate the model's `requestTimeoutMs`; explicit provider policy and the local-provider post-event idle exemption remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- 4 files, 286 insertions / 25 deletions against current upstream `main`.
- Current head: `9a3fffeab9008cc7a9b7c2a49f0e4dacba35aa37`, rebased onto `3ae680f7143336e6918f8819163a3cbf21882e92`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed after rebase.
- Focused finalizer/harness suites and both core typecheck lanes pass.
- Required branch autoreview found no finding and rated the patch correct at 0.97 confidence.

## Evaluation result

Combined with #126255 and #127796, [full run 32556602972](https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/32556602972) scored **86/106 (81.13%)**, above historical Laith OpenClaw at 82/106. prs.title: feat(goals): continue active session goals while idle
prs.body:
Related: #102260

This is the focused current-main replacement for the deterministic goal-driver slice discussed in #102261 and #103586. It deliberately does not carry forward their unrelated question, plan, judge, wait-barrier, UI, generated, or Hermes-labelled scope.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can persist, display, budget, pause, block, resume, and complete a session goal, but an active goal still stops whenever a turn ends. Operators must send another message to keep an otherwise idle goal moving.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a default-off, deterministic gateway driver that uses the existing session goal, active-run, queued-turn, system-event, heartbeat, context, UI, and `goal_changed` paths. It reserves each bounded continuation durably before enqueueing a wake, lets user work win races, and auto-pauses at the configured ceiling.

The driver is intentionally limited to agent-scoped session keys. Current-main system-event queues cannot safely distinguish the same bare `global` key in multiple agent stores, and expanding queue identity belongs in a separate change. The durable-owner repair in #104265 is also kept separate rather than duplicated here.

## User Impact

Operators who explicitly enable `tools.experimental.goalDriver.enabled` can let an active session goal continue after a fixed idle delay without sending a synthetic user message. Existing goal controls and status UI remain the source of truth. The feature remains inert by default.

## Evidence

- RED contract: fork CI at exact test-only SHA `b5c2f60d959a3714af01be27eddd00b46aa6e7e6` reported the expected missing driver, service, goal reservation/rollback, and gateway-wiring symbols: https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/actions/runs/29228761335
- Tests cover exact delay/no jitter, one timer per durable target, active/user/system queue precedence, persistence failure, race rollback, rejected enqueue, no self-rearm, dynamic disable, startup recovery, unsafe bare-key refusal, bounded concurrent reservations, resume reset, and terminal-persistence ordering.
- Structured pre-commit review of the tests-only contract completed with no actionable findings.
- GREEN exact-head CI and non-repository visual evidence will be added before this draft is marked ready.

prs.title: fix: start typing for queued followup turns and honor configured typingMode for Telegram room events
prs.body:
Fixes #92267

## Problem

`agents.defaults.typingMode: "instant"` is silently ineffective for message-tool delivery setups — the configuration the ambient-room-events docs recommend (`unmentionedInbound: "room_event"` + `visibleReplies: "message_tool"`). Two independent gaps:

**Gap 1 — queued/steered turns never start typing.** `createFollowupRunner` builds the typing signaler but never calls `signalRunStart()`; its only trigger is streamed renderable text, which `message_tool` turns never produce (their streamed final is the silent token). With `messages.queue.mode: "steer"` and long-running sessions, most real inbound messages take this path — observed in production as a full day of Telegram traffic with 42 `sendMessage` operations and **zero** `sendChatAction` calls, in DMs and groups alike. `runReplyAgent` already signals run start for fresh turns; the docs define `instant` as "start typing as soon as the model loop begins, even if the run later returns only the silent reply token", with no queued-turn exception.

**Gap 2 — Telegram hardcodes `suppressTyping` for room events.** `bot-message-dispatch.ts` sets `suppressTyping: isRoomEvent` unconditionally while simultaneously setting `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` — the exact mode `resolveTypingMode()` deliberately maps to `"instant"`. The suppression check runs first, so that mapping and any explicit operator-configured `typingMode` are unreachable for unmentioned group turns.

## Fix

- `followup-runner.ts`: call `typingSignals.signalRunStart()` at follow-up run start, mirroring `runReplyAgent`. The signaler gates on mode internally, so `message`/`thinking`/`never` semantics are unchanged; existing `markRunComplete`/`markDispatchIdle` teardown already handles cleanup (silent turns drop typing promptly).
- `bot-message-dispatch.ts`: suppress room-event typing only when the operator never configured a typing mode — `isRoomEvent && resolveConfiguredTypingMode(cfg) === undefined`. The new resolver (session override, then `agents.defaults`) mirrors how `get-reply` resolves the effective mode. Default installs keep today's quiet ambient-room behavior.
- `plugin-sdk/config-contracts.ts`: re-export `TypingMode` for the resolver's signature.

## Tests

- `followup-runner.test.ts`: queued turns start run-start typing under `instant`, and do not under `message` (regression for gap 1).
- `agent-config.test.ts` (new): resolver precedence (unset → undefined, defaults, session override) plus a guard on the existing reasoning-default fallback.

`vitest run` on both touched suites: 79 passed. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:extensions` clean; oxlint/oxfmt applied.

## Verification beyond tests

Both changes were first applied to a live 2026.6.5 deployment (as dist patches with identical semantics) and verified by the affected user: typing restored in DMs (gap 1 path) and in unmentioned group-topic messages (gap 2 path), with message-tool final delivery unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Telegram typing indicator (`sendChatAction: typing`) now appears during agent runs for both queued/steered turns and unmentioned group `room_event` turns with `typingMode: "instant"`, where previously neither path ever issued a `sendChatAction`; it still stops when the message-tool reply lands.

**Real environment tested:** Production OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a macOS gateway (LaunchAgent), Telegram channel polling, Codex app-server runtime, `agents.defaults.typingMode: "instant"`, `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`, `messages.groupChat: { unmentionedInbound: "room_event", visibleReplies: "message_tool" }`; both fixes applied to the live deployment with semantics identical to this PR and the gateway restarted.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** (1) restart gateway with both fixes applied; (2) send a DM to an agent whose session is mid-run (follow-up/steered path); (3) send an unmentioned message in an always-on group topic (room_event path); (4) observe the Telegram client and audit gateway logs for `sendChatAction`.

**Evidence after fix:** Telegram client visibly rendered the "typing…" indicator within ~1–2s of the inbound message on both the DM and the group-topic turn and held it through each run until the message-tool reply was delivered (operator-observed live); before the fix, a full day of runtime logs showed 42 `sendMessage` operations and 0 `sendChatAction` entries, and a direct Bot API `sendChatAction` returned `{"ok":true}` and rendered — isolating the gap to the run pipeline. Screen recording from the live deployment available on request.

**Observed result after fix:** Both previously-dead typing paths show live typing through the full run and stop on message-tool delivery; silent (`NO_REPLY`) turns tear typing down promptly; message-tool final delivery, mentioned-group, and fresh-DM behavior unchanged.

**What was not tested:** `typingMode: "thinking"` under this setup (needs streamed reasoning); heartbeat turns (excluded by design in the signaler); other channels sharing the room-event pattern (e.g. Discord's analogous flag, out of scope for this PR).

prs.body:
Related preservation material: [#115869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/115869). Local-model qualification remains separate from this supported-frontier stack.

## What Problem This Solves

Command completion could report terminal status while nested Code Mode work was still pending, and lifecycle blockers were mixed with request faults.

## Ownership Boundary

The command lifecycle owner reports quiescence only after nested work settles. Lifecycle blockers map to retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; actual request faults remain `INVALID_REQUEST`.

prs.title: fix(agents): detect reworded sessions_send floods via semantic loop-hash normalization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #119600.

The tool-loop detector hashes full `sessions_send` params, including the free-text body. A model that rewords every attempt therefore produces a new argument hash, preventing a repeat streak from forming even when it repeatedly targets the same peer session with stable outcomes. In the reported incident this allowed a semantic send flood to continue while the detector remained silent.

This is the send-side counterpart of #117637 (exec argument churn) and complements #89090, which stabilized send *outcome* hashes; this PR stabilizes the internal-session send *argument* hash.

## Change

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts`:

- Normalize free-text `message`/`text` fields for `sessions_send` before hashing.
- Preserve `sessionKey`, so different peer sessions remain distinct.
- Keep `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`, and `message` fully text-sensitive because they deliver directly to external conversations/channels where distinct text is legitimate.

## Tests

Regression coverage in `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts` verifies:

- reworded `sessions_send` bodies to one session hash identically;
- sends to different sessions stay distinct;
- 20 stable same-target outcomes cause the next reworded `sessions_send` admission to return critical `generic_repeat`;
- mixed-target fan-out remains allowed;
- `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`, and `message` remain text-sensitive.

## Evidence

### Exact-head runtime proof

A redacted runnable harness and its clean-worktree output are attached here:

- `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5231243497`
- reviewed head: `6e727cb08b0c4408f239607b935e49e40caa43ce`

The harness imports the reviewed head's source module and exercises `hashToolCall`, `recordToolCall`, `recordToolCallOutcome`, and `detectToolCallLoop`. It refuses to run unless tracked files are clean and `HEAD` matches the supplied SHA.

Observed boundary:

```text
{
  "reviewedHead": "6e727cb08b0c4408f239607b935e49e40caa43ce",
  "sourceModule": "src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts",
  "assertions": {
    "rewordedSessionsSendSameTargetHashesEqual": true,
    "rewordedSessionsSendTextAliasSameTargetHashesEqual": true,
    "sessionsSendDifferentTargetsRemainDistinct": true,
    "nextSessionsSendAfterTwentyStableOutcomes": {
      "stuck": true,
      "level": "critical",
      "detector": "generic_repeat",
      "count": 20
    },
    "rewordedConversationsSendRemainsTextSensitive": true,
    "rewordedConversationsTurnRemainsTextSensitive": true,
    "nextDistinctConversationSendAfterTwentyOutcomes": {
      "stuck": false
    },
    "rewordedMessageToolSendsRemainTextSensitive": true
  }
}
```

This demonstrates:

- same-target reworded `sessions_send`: critical `generic_repeat` after 20 stable outcomes;
- different internal targets: distinct hashes;
- distinct external conversation/channel text: remains allowed and text-sensitive.

### Integrated admission/outcome proof

A second redacted exact-head harness closes the production-lifecycle boundary identified by ClawSweeper:

- proof comment: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5233962446`
- selector-canonicalization follow-up proof (covers `prepareBeforeToolCallParams` selector resolution and the rotation block): `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119604#issuecomment-5381049977`
- reviewed head: `be424e866abae3a1eba1ab5de0cb87cd7ad84cc6`
- real `agent-core` tool-call loop and schema validation;
- actual `sessions_send.prepareArguments` alias canonicalization;
- real wrapped before-tool admission and outcome recording;
- actual `conversations_send` production execution with an injected contract-valid no-network gateway.

Observed integrated boundary:

```text
same-target sessions_send:
  model attempts: 21
  synthetic executor invocations: 20
  admission/history records: 21
  executed outcome records: 20
  prepared argument hash count: 1
  stable normalized result hash count with unique run IDs: 1
  prospective attempt 21: blocked (generic_repeat, count 20)

target-separated sessions_send:
  target-A synthetic executions: 20
  identical target-B call after target-A threshold: allowed
  next target-A call: blocked
  prepared argument hash count: 2

external conversations_send:
  model attempts: 21
  injected fake-gateway invocations: 21
  admission/history records: 21
  executed outcome records: 21
  prepared argument hash count: 21
  critical generic-repeat events: 0
  network delivery performed: false
```

The detector evaluates completed prior outcomes before execution; therefore the event reports `count: 20` while blocking the prospective 21st same-target attempt. The production `sessions_send` delivery body is replaced by a contract-shaped synthetic executor, and the external tool uses its production dependency-injection seam. No real inter-agent or external-channel messages are emitted by this proof.

### Local validation

```text
Focused Vitest: 178/178 passed across agents-core and agents-support
oxfmt (changed files): passed
type-aware oxlint (changed files): 0 warnings, 0 errors
tsgo:core: passed
tsgo:core:test: passed
```

The earlier full legacy `tsc --noEmit` command now exceeds even an 8 GB Node heap on the expanded repository; the maintained `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` project checks pass.

### Shipped beta.7 corroboration

A behaviorally equivalent normalization for the canonical runtime `message` shape was ported to the installed `2026.7.2-beta.7` loop-detector bundle and exercised through its shipped detector exports. It produced the same critical `generic_repeat` boundary for reworded same-session sends while 20 distinct-text external conversation deliveries remained allowed. The beta.7 port did not separately normalize the pre-canonicalization `text` alias, so it is corroborating operator evidence rather than a byte-for-byte copy of the PR helper. The exact-head harness above is the inspectable proof for both `message` and defensive `text` handling.

## Scope Note

Loop history is per run, so this closes the within-run evasion class. Cross-run loops driven by heartbeats, recall cycles, or separate autonomous runs additionally need session-level budgeting/policy containment and remain out of scope.

prs.title: fix(doctor): migrate hosted Ollama provider references
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Older Cloud-only Ollama setup stored `https://ollama.com` under `models.providers.ollama`. After the dedicated `ollama-cloud` provider was introduced, those configurations and their cron/session references still selected the local provider.

## User Impact

Doctor moves only the `ollama` entry whose URL origin is exactly `https://ollama.com`, including case, path, trailing-slash, and default-port variants. Localhost, LAN, custom endpoints, other provider keys, and local-daemon cloud models remain unchanged. An existing `ollama-cloud` provider keeps its authored settings and gains missing catalog entries.

Matching model references move with the provider. Their `@profile` suffix is removed rather than guessing which Cloud account to use; one Doctor note explains how to re-pin. This migration does not inspect or change saved credentials. Environment-backed URLs, API-key templates, and SecretRefs retain their authored references.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Ollama plugin declares the routing migration through its existing Doctor contract. The shared model-reference walker handles config and cron references; the existing session owner handles model/provider pairs and saved fallback/rollback routes. Preflight leaves the hosted entry intact. The config writer repairs persisted references first, then publishes config last. An interrupted run retains the hosted source entry as its retry signal; a completed migration never replays backups onto later local selections.

### Simplification

Removed saved-account discovery, per-agent/shared account selection, auth-profile remapping, the config walker’s per-agent split, agent-ID threading, per-reference session reporting, unused test API surface, and the separate lint-preview path. Consolidated duplicate auth/state fixtures into focused regressions.

Against merge base `e40606fdea96135758ec5bc0b1a355d08ead0c7e`, production is **+542/-78 lines** and tests/test support are **+714/-1 lines** (including two harness lines). The earlier candidate added about 830 production and 1,650 test lines. Documentation is +44/-1; the existing mock-export baseline shrinks by two entries.

The remaining non-core changes have specific owners:

- Config planning carries the matched declaration to the writer so state repair precedes config publication.
- Reference restoration applies the resolved routing decision to authored templates so renamed environment-backed URLs and credentials stay templates.
- Health runners retain readonly/legacy-handoff guards before state repair and publish config only after all state repairs succeed.
- Registry/module/SDK changes load and validate plugin-owned declarations. Compatibility execution stays in the existing compatibility module: adding declaration loading exceeds the registry’s 700-line limit without that split. Compatibility preflight itself does not perform the rename.
- Removed the speculative URL-userinfo/scheme restriction on plugin-authored rename declarations. Declarations still require valid provider IDs and a parseable URL; migration matching compares origins, which never include userinfo. The Ollama declaration and runtime matching are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused coverage passes **48 tests across five files**. Core and extension typechecks, affected test typecheck graphs (`plugins-platform`, `commands-doctor`), scoped core/extension lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. The migration runtime build at `391cefd415a2` passes; the later validator-only change was checked through focused declaration/registry tests and lint.

One bounded independent `gpt-6-astra` review of candidate `391cefd415a2` found no actionable P0/P1 correctness or data-loss defects. The subsequent validator-only simplification leaves the Ollama declaration and migration path unchanged; its focused declaration/registry proof was rerun.

| Case | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted vs local | Hosted URL variants; localhost, loopback, LAN, custom/spoofed origins, non-default port, HTTP, and unrelated provider remain unchanged |
| Config references | Default/per-agent refs, fallback arrays, model-map keys, utility/media slots, provider/model pairs, and role allow/deny policies |
| Existing Cloud provider | Canonical conflicts win; missing models/fields merge; rerun is idempotent |
| Account suffixes | Suffixes drop with one re-pin note; model date/quantization suffixes are preserved |
| Persisted state | Enabled/disabled cron jobs; raw/full/unscoped session pairs and fallback/rollback routes through the existing owners |
| Ordering/recovery | Readonly and legacy-handoff refusal preserve sessions; interruption after state repair finishes on rerun; later local selections stay local |
| Preflight/templates | Real Ollama contract preserves hosted entry and auth before publication; moved URL/key templates are restored without resolved-secret substitution |
| Declaration validity | Plugin ownership and config-repair declaration gating; valid provider IDs and parseable URL required |

The current-main negative control retains the legacy provider and references. No database schema or credential-store change is involved.

### Live proof on `391cefd415a2031624b11ebc53446f3707802929`

| Real entry point | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Doctor, literal hosted URL, twice | Six local-provider catalog entries became six Cloud entries; config, cron, and session refs migrated; second run left config byte-identical |
| Doctor, environment-backed hosted URL, twice | Same migration; URL/key templates and dotenv bytes unchanged; second run byte-identical |
| Doctor, local/mixed fixture, twice | All seven local-provider entries and local references stayed local; second run byte-identical |
| Fresh v2026.10.1 install → candidate update, no resume | Update result `ok`, ledger `succeeded`/`finished`, exact candidate HEAD/build, readyz HTTP 200; config plus API/stored cron/session references migrated |
| New local selection after completed migration | One local and six Cloud entries retained; new local default, cron, and session refs and prior Cloud refs unchanged |

The update’s Doctor step exited 0. The v2026.10.1 CLI later exited 1 solely on its known missing `runtime-cleanup` module, fixed on main by #165233; this is not a migration failure. The successful result, settled ledger, exact runtime identity, readyz response, and state assertions establish the update outcome. All fixtures retained their authored secret templates and byte-identical dotenv files.

Final head `fbd9a0bd83dc69e61f56dfcafc752d29432b3379` only removes the speculative declaration URL restriction and replaces its rejection fixture with an invalid-URL case. The Ollama declaration and migration behavior are unchanged, so the live evidence above is retained.

All nine isolated Ollama proof profiles were torn down; no matching state directory, LaunchAgent file, or loaded service remained. Evidence and reconciliation backups were retained.


### Limits and follow-ups

The existing mocked Doctor sandbox-warning E2E harness has a cold-setup timeout/missing `collectRelevantDoctorPluginIds` mock export on both the prior candidate and main; this is a separate harness issue, not used as proof of this migration. The previously attempted v2026.9.8 update is not claimed as successful; its workspace-symlink/runtime-retention problem is outside this repair. The required released-driver proof is v2026.10.1.

Reverting code does not automatically restore migrated config, cron, or session references. Existing Doctor config/state backups remain the recovery surface. Blast radius is legacy hosted Ollama routing; local Ollama, unrelated providers, credentials, and schemas are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(models): recover after catalog generation mismatch
prs.body:
Closes #126108

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a full model-catalog request failing on a stale configured worker generation instead of recovering in place.

## User Impact

The configured catalog recovery path can replace the stale owner while keeping unaffected owners available. Failed recovery remains demand-recoverable, and persistent generation mismatches cannot cause an unbounded retry or rebuild loop. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery owner captures the exact configured generation, coalesces concurrent mismatches, follows replacement gates before publishing, and preserves auth-publication ordering. Failed owner and adopted-auth transactions retain retry state. Persistent mismatch recovery is bounded and temporarily fenced so stale dispatch cannot remain published while the owner waits for demand recovery.

The recovery owner is loaded only after a generation mismatch. Ordinary Gateway catalog startup therefore does not load the exceptional recovery graph. Initialization is single-flight, rejected loads are evicted for retry, and shutdown completes normal cleanup before reporting a recovery-loader failure.

## Evidence

At commit `461d8eccfe4e1c8843ab61890a2984c94d7d813e`:

- The catalog recovery suite passed 17 tests, including failed rebuild, adopted-auth failure, stale-dispatch fencing, cooldown, demand recovery, and shutdown cases.
- Core type checking, focused formatting, changed-file linting, timeout-race ratchet, and conflict-marker validation passed.
- Independent correctness and security reviews found no actionable issue in the final lazy-load and teardown behavior.
- The signed remote commit matches the PR head, and GitHub reports the branch mergeable with current main.

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-recovery.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core

prs.title: Add Telegram per-group UI overrides
prs.body:
## Summary
- add Telegram per-group/topic overrides for UI streaming settings (`streaming.mode`, preview/progress toolProgress) and `ackReaction`
- resolve Telegram scoped overrides before account/channel defaults
- honor explicit `delivery.mode="none"` on main-session cron system events without waking the assistant

## Tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/group-config-helpers.test.ts src/agents/identity.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Telegram chats can carry per-group/topic overrides for `streaming.mode` and `ackReaction` that resolve ahead of account/channel defaults, so a chat configured with `streaming.mode="off"` and `ackReaction=null` no longer leaks intermediate tool-progress chrome (`Image:`, `Exec:`, progress markers) or applies acknowledgment reactions. Independently, main-session cron jobs configured with `delivery.mode="none"` no longer wake the operator's direct chat or generate visible system-event traffic.

Real environment tested: production OpenClaw gateway on a Hetzner-class VPS (Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, runtime `openclaw-gateway v2026.5.6` patched with the changes from this PR), with a real Telegram supergroup configured under the new per-group block. Vendista cron jobs (`vendista-events-poll` every 30 min, `vendista-terminals-health` every 6 h) reconfigured to `payload.kind: agentTurn`, `sessionTarget: isolated`, `delivery: { mode: "none" }`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: deployed the patched runtime; `openclaw-gateway.service` restarted at `2026-05-28T20:02:48 CEST` (verified via `systemctl --user status openclaw-gateway`, line `Active: active (running) since Thu 2026-05-28 20:02:48 CEST`). Applied per-group config to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` with the new schema fields (`streaming.mode`, `ackReaction`); runtime parsed the new fields after deploy, whereas the same JSON shape was rejected by the pre-patch runtime ten times in a row at `2026-05-28T11:20–11:21 CEST` with `invalid config: must NOT have additional properties`. Sent a test photo into the group from a real Telegram client at `2026-05-28T20:10 CEST`. Pulled `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway --since "yesterday"` (1802 lines) for the post-deploy window, grepped for the chat id (66 matches) and for chrome leak markers (zero matches). Live runtime config dumped via `jq '.channels.telegram.groups."<group-chat-id>"' ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.

Evidence after fix: the new fields `streaming` and `ackReaction` (introduced by this PR) are present and accepted by the patched runtime — `jq` output for the group block shows `"streaming": { "mode": "off" }` and `"ackReaction": null` alongside the preserved `requireMention: false`, `groupPolicy: "open"`, and `systemPrompt` (silent-observer policy, content redacted from this PR body). Pre-patch runtime rejected the identical config ten times (`May 28 11:20:36 GAS node[1378495]: channels.telegram.groups.<id>: invalid config: must NOT have additional properties` — and nine more sequential PID rejections through `11:21:09`); post-patch runtime accepted the same JSON with no rejection lines. The test photo turn entered the patched runtime as a fresh embedded run for the group: `May 28 20:10:09 [plugins] openclaw-mem0: registered (mode: open-source, user: openclaw-main, autoRecall: true, autoCapture: true, skills: true)` → `May 28 20:10:19 [agent/embedded] [trace:embedded-run] prep stages: runId=5e14b0bf-dfe7-4473-bc90-27485f002454 sessionId=c70bc90a-9b36-46da-aa2e-ff750f2a7b57 phase=stream-ready totalMs=9835` → `May 28 20:10:22 [diagnostic] liveness ... work=[active=agent:main:telegram:group:<group-chat-id>(processing/embedded_run,q=1,age=3s last=embedded_run:started)]` → `May 28 20:10:24 [plugins] openclaw-mem0: skills-mode recall (strategy=smart) injecting 1 memories (~95 tokens)`. PID `29275` is the patched gateway process (started `20:02:48 CEST`). Chrome leak check across the full post-deploy log window (~1h 30min of live operation): `awk '/2026-05-28T20:02:48/,EOF' tmp_log.txt | grep -cE "Nautiling|Image:|Exec:"` returned `0` — no streaming-progress chrome or tool-execution markers reached the log path between deploy and the latest entry. Focused unit suites (supplemental only): `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.test.ts`, `config-schema.test.ts`, `group-config-helpers.test.ts`, `src/agents/identity.test.ts` — 57/57 passed; `src/cron/service.runs-one-shot-main-job-disables-it.test.ts` — 13/13 passed.

Observed result after fix: in the live Telegram supergroup, the bot processed the test photo through an embedded run on the patched runtime (`runId=5e14b0bf-...`), recalled and stored memory entries through the `openclaw-mem0` plugin, and emitted no streaming-progress chrome strings into the gateway log path. The embedded run for the group completed without any subsequent `tool:image:started` or streaming-progress events in the same turn, consistent with the configured `streaming.mode="off"`. The previously failing schema-validation errors against the new per-group fields stopped after the patched runtime was deployed, demonstrating that the new fields are accepted at the config schema level and resolved at the per-group scope ahead of account/channel defaults.

What was not tested: cross-account interaction where multiple Telegram accounts override the same chat simultaneously — the current change resolves at the group/topic scope ahead of account-level defaults, but multi-account contention is out of scope for this patch. Specific delivery of Vendista cron isolated turns into a sink-only session was not separately captured in the post-deploy window pulled here; the cron portion is supported by the focused unit suite above.
