prs.title: feat(sessions): opt in to sessions_send thread targets
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR
Today `sessions_send` always refuses thread/topic sessions (Telegram forum topics, Slack/Discord threads). That is the right default, because it keeps inter-agent traffic out of human-facing threads (#52496). But an operator who runs one agent per forum topic has no way to let those sessions coordinate. This PR adds an opt-in `tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets` (default `false`) that lifts only that one check.

### Exact change
- `tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets?: boolean` in the zod schema, with help, label, docs and the generated baseline. It is tiered as advanced.
- `sessions_send` skips the thread-target rejection only when the flag is `true`. Every other gate still applies: visibility, agent-to-agent, sandbox, ownership, and existing-session checks.
- **No conflicting messages:**
  - With the flag on, the model-facing description drops "Thread chats rejected: target parent channel."
  - The rejection error now names the flag.
  - The conversations-tool guidance in `agent-tools.deferred-followup.ts` used to anchor on the removed sentence, which would have silently dropped it. It now anchors on either sentence. The default description bytes are unchanged.
- **Docs:** they state the real behavior. The target runs in that session (internal delivery). Anything it sends with the `message` tool lands in the thread.

### Scope boundary
Default behavior is identical. This adds no new delivery path, and replies are not auto-posted into the target thread.

## Verification
- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts src/agents/tool-description-presets.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 3 shards pass in 34 s. `sessions.test.ts` alone with `--maxWorkers=1` takes about 36 s, and the new test takes under 50 ms.
- New test: with the flag on, a Telegram topic target is accepted and an `agent` run is dispatched to that session key. Reverting the gate makes it fail.
- Guidance test now runs with the flag both off and on. Restoring the old literal anchor makes the "on" case fail.
- `pnpm config:schema:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm tsgo` are green, and `oxfmt` is clean on the changed files.
- `oxlint` reports `max-lines` on `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`. That error already exists on `main` (the file is over 700 lines before this change), and this PR adds 7 lines to it.

### What was not tested
I did not run a live Telegram topic-to-topic send for this exact head.

prs.title: fix: preserve replies while their agent finishes starting
prs.body:
Closes #157814.

## What Problem This Solves

New replies can fail with `prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published` when startup releases its grace period while the requested agent is still loading.

## User Impact

The reply waits for that agent to become ready. Other ready agents keep serving replies while the remaining fleet starts. Cancellation and actual preparation failures still take their existing paths; this does not change crash-replay or delivery durability.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared dispatch publication owner now wakes waiting readers whenever its publication changes. After startup's grace period, a missing runtime waits on that publication instead of being treated as permanently absent. The loop rechecks the current lifecycle and publication before granting access.

Production LOC is **+20** across two existing owners (+34/−14), within the bug-fix exception. Four files change; the existing startup test is extended and restart documentation explains the wait. No new timeout, lifecycle state, stored data, protocol field, or configuration is added.

## Evidence

- Trusted current-main baseline on AWS: both startup cases fail because admission rejects while the agent is still loading.
- Repaired startup suite: **10/10 passed**, including early auth refresh. It holds a later agent indefinitely while proving the earlier waiting agent can proceed. `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.batch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **34.19 s wall time**, 8.51 s Vitest duration.
- Same final tests with original production restored: **2 failed / 8 passed**, at the intended premature-settlement assertion; **33.71 s wall time**. Candidate source restored afterward.
- Targeted formatting and lint passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Core production types and all 28 covering test-type graphs passed. Adjacent auth/admission suites passed **38/38** (43.34 s wall time).
- `check:changed` passed its earlier gates but stopped on the unrelated pre-existing exported type `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` in `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts`. The same dead-export failure was reproduced with original production restored; no baseline was changed or suppressed. Required GitHub CI passed at this exact head.
- No real Windows service restart was exercised; the proof targets the platform-independent startup/publication boundary that emits the reported error.

prs.title: fix(announce): match Slack DM delivery receipts to source users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Slack completion delivered through the message tool to a verified DM conversation could still be reported as `visible_reply_missing` when the source target was recorded as the corresponding Slack user. It also preserves confirmed source progress delivery when final-recipient verification times out.

Fixes #144885

## Why This Change Was Made

Completion evidence resolves provider-native delivery identities before final verification starts, so a confirmed progress receipt is recorded independently of a later final lookup. Confirmed source receipts are evaluated before optional lookups, native lookups run concurrently, and the verifier keeps an independent finite deadline that aborts losing lookups after settlement. The direct-delivery owner is checked again after asynchronous receipt classification so a source session that loses ownership during Slack verification cannot settle the completion as delivered. The built-in Slack fetch removes the SDK's explicit empty body workaround, while a caller-supplied fetch receives its original request init unchanged.

## User Impact

Slack DM completions sent to the verified source user settle as delivered without weakening off-target or ambiguous-delivery checks. A stalled provider lookup cannot hold completion settlement beyond its verification budget, erase confirmed progress, or remain active after a successful match. A source completion whose owner changes during recipient verification is returned as an intentional non-delivery and does not trigger a fallback send. Custom Slack fetch implementations retain the request body supplied by the Web API SDK.

## Evidence

- Previous exact-head focused validation at `bfa46befb9647cd902df4230dd47f9d3adf71442` passed on Node v26.5.1 before the formatting and assertion-safety validation fixes in the current commit: five announcement/outbound test files passed (84 tests across three shards), and four Slack routing/Web API test files passed (25 tests).

```text
$ rtk node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-completion-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery-edge-cases.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-delivery.discord-thread.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-owner-continuation.test.ts src/infra/outbound/outbound-session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files 5 passed (3 Vitest shards)
Tests 84 passed
Duration 47.43s
$ rtk node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-slack.config.ts --reporter=verbose --maxWorkers=1 extensions/slack/src/client-options.test.ts extensions/slack/src/client.web-api.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-routing.test.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
Test Files 4 passed (4)
Tests 25 passed (25)
Duration 10.45s
```

- Exact-head production-boundary proof at `deff8c4d9e39bfca8f1cef92f107268b50d8e4d8` ran the three committed localhost drivers through the production announcement owner, Slack route resolver, plugin, and Web API client. A temporary Vitest wrapper installed test overrides at the Gateway dispatch and requester-session reader boundaries; production delivery, routing, Slack plugin, and Web API code ran unchanged against localhost. The drivers used no credentials or external Slack service, and sent no production messages.

- Real-path and negative-control results at this exact head: the matching receipt delivered directly; wrong-recipient and revoked-owner cases were rejected without fallback; stalled lookups closed after a match or cancellation. This is localhost-backed production-boundary evidence, not a live Gateway or external Slack delivery claim.

- The exact-head `pnpm check:changed --base 84b6b0858f387c5b3fbd3e4bc2bc72152b059692 --timed` run passed its ratchets, changed-file formatting, doctor contract tests, and all lanes before the core tsgo graph boundary. It exits there because the existing `ui-e2e` shard resolves 722 test roots against a 720-root budget; this PR changes no UI, UI-E2E, or test-tsconfig files. The review's requested live Gateway/Slack proof and maintainer decision on the optional public `AbortSignal` remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Temporary proof-tier harness</summary>

Save as `test/scripts/subagent-announce-proof-current.test.ts`, then run `rtk pnpm exec vitest run --project tooling test/scripts/subagent-announce-proof-current.test.ts`:


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes commands hanging after output during forced Node shutdown without retaining the blanket Maglev and concurrent-Sparkplug workaround.

## User Impact

CLI commands and the Gateway finish owned work and cleanup before exiting naturally, with Node's default compiler settings restored. Exit status, Unix signal termination, output, explicit compiler overrides, and system-CA trust are preserved.

The Gateway still joins native skills-watcher retirement. This can retain synchronous FSEvents shutdown latency on macOS; the separate upstream certificate-loader stall is not fixed. Native macOS/Windows qualification is not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing lifecycle owners retain admitted work, native workers, child transports, updater recovery, and watchdogs through actual completion. The boundary guard prevents new forced normal exits. Cleanup dependencies are retained before a command can replace its package, without eagerly importing them into CLI bootstrap. No new configuration, dependency, or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Earlier full pnpm build passed on composed tree faaafbe6b1f47e707f8392243898525990f3a452 (the terminal repair plus pinned CI base 97e81ce), including the canonical CLI-bootstrap import gate, in 4m35.7s. Broker regressions: 84 passed; real-process negative controls cover IPC disconnect and Unix signal propagation after output settlement.

The reconciliation case failed before removing an obsolete admission close. Scoped types, lint, and three-pass review are complete; this integration did not repeat the full application build.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Copilot models retaining the unknown-model 128K estimate after the selected account publishes a different context limit.

Related: #156635, #127239, #153864, #124911.

## User Impact

Execution uses accepted capacity for the selected route while preserving genuine model limits and explicit user caps. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mark unknown-model windows as estimates and carry that distinction through catalog publication and embedded execution. Accepted metadata replaces the superseded estimate; configured reasoning, input, parameters, and compatibility remain intact. The catalog publication extraction keeps the existing source-size contract satisfied.

The former aggregate is split into independently reviewable parts. This PR contains the core fix (34 files, +1113/-429). Contributor history is preserved.

- [Budgets and prewarming #138087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138087), based on this PR.
- [Run-result provenance #168730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168730), based on budgets.

- [Reporting #165991](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165991), based on accounting.
- [Selection #168809](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168809), based on reporting.

- [Cron accounting #168810](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168810), based on a prerequisite branch combining reporting and the mechanical extraction. Its diff excludes the executor move.

All these layers are published non-draft with auto-merge disabled. The independent [CI status selector repair #168804](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168804) targets main, rather than adding workflow code to this Copilot fix.

## Evidence

The estimate-versus-accepted execution regression fails before the fix. On current head `6e8d2927`, four affected owner suites pass 84 cases (71.77s), and the complete Copilot suite passes 48 cases (20.99s). Production types, affected test-type graphs, lint, line caps, and import-cycle checks pass. Fresh complete owner review has no actionable findings. The main integration preserves one catalog publication owner and its admission guards.

Earlier packaged head `e8b8d779` passes normal build and package validation, fresh Windows ARM64 installation, and authenticated Copilot inference. Its 18-model catalog reports eight distinct context windows (144,000–1,048,576); an installed-CLI turn returns `pong` with an actual 917,504-token execution budget and matching terminal/session metadata. Controlled installed-CLI turns prove estimate128K → accepted872K → explicit64K. These are prior-package results; final integrated-stack Windows, native-node interoperability, Telegram, and upgrade-continuity proof remain pending.

## Remaining Holds

Current-head CI fails in the unchanged catalog publisher after upstream #168728 emptied Claude CLI's static models. The publisher, test, schema, and manifest are identical to the actual tested main base `2e68184f`; this is an inherited production defect. Prior revision `ec784a58` has a passing [CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38098612181), which is not current-head CI. The independent CI status selector repair above addresses a separate status-publication issue.

The latest-stable upgrade proof is not complete. Published 2026.10.1 installs successfully, but standalone Doctor rejects an existing additive column in copied state. The final proof follows the installed updater first, then candidate Doctor. Earlier failed updater/helper cells remain failures and are not replaced by the passing inference results.

Current ClawSweeper has no code findings. Its prior review rates patch/proof platinum, while the overall gold rating retains the pending upgrade and integrated-stack proof. All layers are non-draft, with auto-merge disabled. **Do not merge: review readiness only.**

prs.title: fix(gateway): fence transport admission for a closing generation
prs.body:
Refs #127256 (partial fix: transport-admission slice; the canonical issue stays open for the worker pre-auth and operator-continuation gaps)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway that is directly closed (or is failing post-bind startup cleanup) keeps admitting new work into the generation it is already tearing down — it reports `draining` while it still serves new HTTP user requests, completes new WebSocket upgrades, and answers pre-auth connects.

Measured on a real public Gateway with `configReloader.stop()` gated, while `/readyz` already answered `gateway-draining` and `closePreludeStarted`/`connectionWork.isClosing` were both true:

| Real entry point | Before |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticated `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **HTTP 200 + a full chat completion** — new model work ran inside the retiring generation |
| Fresh WebSocket upgrade | **accepted**, socket then terminated; no 503 |
| Pre-auth `connect` on a socket upgraded before close | **no response, no close** (frame dropped) |
| New `status` RPC from a connected operator | **no response** until transport teardown |

Affected owners: direct/embedded Gateways (including the onboarding session Gateway) and managed post-bind startup-failure cleanup.

## User Impact

Starting a close now synchronously stops that Gateway generation from accepting new HTTP, upgrade, pre-auth connect, and worker connect work, using the contracts clients already understand: HTTP 503 `gateway_unavailable`, WebSocket upgrade 503 `websocket admission closed`, and retryable `UNAVAILABLE` for connect/RPC frames. Callers get a retry signal instead of an outcome-less wait or a socket that dies mid-request.

No user-visible change for managed stop/restart or suspension; already-admitted work still drains under the existing generation owners; readiness/startup probes stay reachable so operators can still observe `draining`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Process-global root work admission is the obvious fence, but closing it from a generic close would poison same-process successors and internal teardown — the issue calls this out. The generation already owns this exact decision: `GatewayConnectionWork.isClosing` is flipped synchronously by `markClosePreludeStarted()`, already terminates new sockets, and already routes close-time frames. This change makes that single generation-scoped fence authoritative at the remaining transport boundaries (HTTP stages/hooks/plugin routes, Gateway and Worker upgrades, desktop/node attach, pre-auth connect, worker connect, and new operator RPC frames) instead of adding a competing owner. Process-global admission is untouched.

`gateway-closing` is added to the protocol reason set with a detector and Control UI availability classification so the refusal is treated as transient rather than a hard error.

## Evidence

New regression test `src/gateway/server-close.transport-admission.test.ts` drives the real public server, gates `configReloader.stop()`, asserts each refusal contract while close waits, then releases the owner and joins the close.

- **Red on clean `main`:** fails at the first boundary — `expected 'upgraded' to deeply equal { status: 503, … }`; with that assertion temporarily removed, the next boundary fails — `expected 200 to be 503`.
- **Green with the change:** 1 passed, test wall **~14–33 s** (one real Gateway fixture; sibling `server.*` close/pre-auth cases cost 4–23 s each).
- `src/gateway/server-kernel.test.ts` 11/11 (direct + public close ordering), `server.request-lifetime.test.ts` 6/6, `server.preauth-hardening.test.ts` 10/10.
- `server-request-entry`, `server-methods.suspension-admission`, `message-handler.suspension-admission`, `plugins-http`, `server-http.probe`, `server-close`: passing.
- One expectation update in `src/gateway/server.node-shutdown.test.ts`: the direct-shutdown mode relied on the new connection being upgraded and then dying with 1006; it now asserts the same 503 upgrade rejection as restart drain (2/2 green).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/restart-unavailable.test.ts` 3/3; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, and oxfmt clean on changed files.

<details>
<summary>Pre-fix probe output (real server, close held on `configReloader.stop()`)</summary>

```json
{
  "closePreludeStarted": true,
  "connectionWorkClosing": true,
  "freshUpgradeHttp": "UPGRADED",
  "preauthConnectFrames": [],
  "preauthClosed": [],
  "existingRpcReply": null,
  "existingClosed": [],
  "httpChatAdmitted": "HTTP 200 {\"object\":\"chat.completion\",\"model\":\"openclaw\",…}",
  "httpHealthz": "HTTP 200 {\"ok\":true,\"status\":\"live\"}",
  "readyz": "HTTP 503 {\"ready\":false,\"failing\":[\"gateway-draining\"],…}"
}
```

</details>

Known gaps: operator continuation frames (`question.resolve`, `exec.approval.resolve`) are still not settled during close; worker frames on an already-connected worker keep the existing drain path; the post-bind startup-failure sibling shares the same `beginClosePrelude` fence but has no dedicated test yet.

prs.title: fix(gateway): node reconnects repeat the same withheld-command warning
prs.body:
Closes #168742

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway warn logs fill with the same `node command surface withheld` line every time a node reconnects with an unchanged withheld command set, so a new or changed withholding decision is buried among repeats.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see each node's withheld command set once at warn per Gateway run, and again whenever that set changes; identical repeats are still available at debug. Which commands are withheld is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warn line is useful the first time and whenever the decision changes, but nothing remembered what had already been logged. Node connect reconciliation now keeps a bounded record of the last withheld set logged per node (256 nodes, pruned with the existing `pruneMapToMaxSize`), tied to the existing `close-and-restart` global singleton lifecycle, and compares sets with the existing `sameNodeApprovalSurfaceSet`, so ordering and duplicates do not count as a change.

- First set for a node after Gateway start, or a different set: `warn` (unchanged message).
- Same set as last logged: `debug` (same message).
- A connect with nothing withheld clears the node's record, so renewed withholding warns again.
- The record is cleared on Gateway close and on in-process restart (unmanaged/container Gateways and `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` keep the process), so every Gateway start records each node's current outcome once at warn. Evicting a node from the bounded record only costs one extra warn on its next reconnect.

This follows the approach proposed in the issue and the ClawSweeper review on it.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway + signed node reconnects.** I used a throwaway harness modeled on `src/gateway/server.node-version-mismatch.test.ts` (not committed): it pairs a macOS node device, starts a real in-process Gateway with `startServer`, and reconnects the same signed node 3 times over WebSocket while it declares `ollama.chat` and `ollama.models` (not admitted by policy). Captured console output, device id redacted:

Before (current `main`), console level `info`:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

After, console level `info`:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

After, console level `debug` (repeats still visible):

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

**In-process Gateway restart** (follow-up to review): the same harness connects the node twice, closes the Gateway with `restartExpectedMs` (restart path), starts a new Gateway in the same process, and reconnects. Console level `debug`:

Previous PR head `8593b97` (module-level map survived the restart):

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
----- in-process Gateway restart -----
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

Current head:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
----- in-process Gateway restart -----
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

**Focused regression tests** in `src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.test.ts` cover repeated and reordered sets, a policy change (`gateway.nodes.commands.allow`) that changes the set, a cleared-then-returning set, separate nodes, and the first identical reconnect after `drainGlobalSingletonLifecycleState("close")` and `("restart")`. The repeat/policy/separate-node cases fail on `main`, the two lifecycle cases fail on the previous PR head, and all pass with this change (the cleared-then-returning case guards existing behavior).

**Local checks** (Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0):

- `pnpm test src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.test.ts`: 19 passed
- `pnpm test src/infra/device-pairing-node-desktop-migration.test.ts src/node-host/linux-node-plugin.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection`: passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` (first head); `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `core.test.gateway-root` shard after the follow-up: passed
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files: clean
- `pnpm check`: the line-cap, max-lines (env var budget), and assertion SAFETY ratchets fail on files this PR does not touch; the same failures reproduce on current `main`. All other checks pass.

Not covered: config hot reload of `gateway.nodes.commands` in a running Gateway (the unit test covers a changed set through config), and a restart through the CLI run loop or a process respawn (the harness covers the in-process `server.close` restart path).

## AI Disclosure

I used an AI coding agent (Cursor) to help find the issue, write the change and tests, and run the validation above. I reviewed the diff and the before/after output myself.

prs.title: fix(context): qualify saved capacity by runtime and account
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved context capacities surviving an account or model/runtime selection change, and missing capacities when a successful run omits context metadata.

## User Impact

Sessions retain capacity qualified to the successful account and current runtime. Changing the relevant selection clears stale facts; explicit limits retain precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduce the async budget operation alongside its first production accounting consumers, built on layer 2’s source-aware projection contract. Prefer recorded run metadata and call that operation only when metadata is absent. Carry the existing successful-auth fact through all accounting and invalidation writers; undefined remains unobserved and null remains observed without a profile. Depends on [run-result provenance PR #168730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168730), which includes layer 2.

## Evidence

Current head `2472befe` incorporates actual producer `d9c206ba`, with 34 own files (+3166/-286). All 33 prior accounting postimages are unchanged. The source-bearing projection export and its original five-row test table now travel with their first production callers, rather than appearing as an unused export in the budget layer.

The four complete provenance/accounting suites pass 106 cases (137.88 seconds wall time, including normal worker preparation). Production types, four complete consuming test-type graphs, staged guards, lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Fresh independent review raised one update-tracking concern. It is rejected: each invalidation predicate already sets `updated` before capacity deletion. The existing whole model-override suite confirms this, passing 17 cases (2.66 seconds wall / 1.77 seconds runner); no code or duplicate test was added. Earlier boundary proof covers 233 distinct capacity/accounting/writer cases. Accepted fixture findings were repaired, with both media-delivery sibling suites passing 22 cases and the two cron suites passing 33 cases. These results belong to their recorded earlier inputs; they are reused where source is unchanged.

## CI and Remaining Proof

Current-head UI shard 5/7 reports three failures and 134 passing cases. An unchanged geometry fixture queries the Details toggle inside the chat gutter; upstream #168494 moved it into the pane header. The fixture, harnesses, renderers, and CSS are identical across the actual tested producer base `d9c206ba` and this accounting head. This is an inherited fixture mismatch, not an accounting failure; no UI replay or green aggregate is claimed. Earlier `da4fcdfe` passed all seven UI shards, which remains prior-head evidence.

Earlier SDK and lint failures retain their source-qualified baseline attribution. No test expectation, scan guard, or budget was relaxed. Final integrated Windows/Copilot, native-node interoperability, Telegram, and upgrade-continuity proof remain pending.

**Do not merge: review readiness only.** Auto-merge remains disabled.

## What Problem This Solves

Memory flush and preflight compaction can use an estimated 128K budget or a capacity from the wrong account, runtime, or transport route.

## User Impact

Maintenance uses the current qualified budget, selected window, and authored limits. Revocation during budget preparation rejects the operation without recording a memory-flush failure or changing persisted flush state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a sibling of the selection fix, stacked on [reporting #165991](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165991). The existing follow-up adapter consumes the existing asynchronous accounting owner; it does not introduce discovery or authority ownership. Canonical catalog projection supplies the typed transport route, and existing currentness checks run immediately after awaited preparation.

## Evidence

The wrong-route control failed before repair, and the matching route remains a positive control. The ordinary operator-revocation regression failed on the original catch placement; after repair it rejects the exact revoked Error and leaves real persisted flush accounting unchanged. It lives in the existing accounting suite rather than increasing an oversized test file.

Prior reviewed-parent proof passes 64 cases across the maintenance owner, budget adapter, and accounting suites: adapter9 cases67.37s cold owner; maintenance51 plus accounting4 cases204.55s combined owner. Earlier moved-regression whole accounting suite RED3PASS/1FAIL54.07s, GREEN4PASS47.28s. Fresh full source review has no findings (.92). Production types and all28 native test-type graphs passed on that reviewed input. All six files pass type-aware lint and formatting;30 planned guards pass. The unused-export guard remains red on unchanged Gateway/UI files independently found without this memory change; the obsolete authored-budget bridge in the parent is removed by the separate cron cutover. No guard, budget, or expectation was relaxed. CI seconds will be available in the attached current-head run.

Published head `cf2c563300b` integrates the actual reporting parent without conflicts; all six owned files remain byte-identical. The 64-case behavioral proof is reused for unchanged source; it is not a current-head replay. New-head CI is pending.

Full-stack installed Windows/Copilot, Windows-node interoperability, and Telegram proof remain pending. No older package proof is claimed for this head. DO NOT MERGE: review readiness only.

prs.title: fix(agents): drain active runs before durable agent deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deleting an agent while one of its turns is running leaves it half deleted. On a dev Gateway (real OpenAI provider), `agents.delete` during a `sleep 30` shell turn:

- returned `ok` with `removed: 0`, while the turn kept executing for about 63 s and finished normally;
- left the deletion journal pending forever, surviving a Gateway restart (cron maintenance logged an error every minute; that part landed separately in #167907);
- blocked recreating an agent with the same name until someone deleted it again by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion retired the agent's stores while work could still enter or was still running. Nothing closed ingress, active runs weren't settled through the abort owner, and background memory work could still be catching up on sessions when its database workers were revoked. So the purge failed, the journal stayed pending, and the failure detail was reduced to a boolean.

Deletion is now a durable two-phase operation:

1. **Draining.** The journal records `phase = "draining"`. Admission owners refuse new work for the agent (chat send, session create, terminal open, cron, worker placement, plugin runtime agent calls, session maintenance). Active runs are aborted and settled through the existing abort owner, and Memory Core work is drained while storage is still open.
2. **Retiring.** The phase advances to `retiring`, stores are retired, files are trashed, and cleanup completes automatically. A restart in either phase resumes from the recorded phase.

Cleanup failures now keep the failing step, database path and underlying cause in the existing `failed[]` payload next to `purgeFailed`, so a stuck deletion says what failed.

## Persisted state (maintainer-approved)

Peter approved "Add durable draining phase" on 2026-10-09. That covers restart continuation and migration-safe handling of journals written by older builds. The only persisted addition is the nullable column `agent_deletion_journal.phase TEXT`. New deletions advance `draining` → `retiring`; old journals with a null or absent phase keep the previous retirement semantics. State schema stays v20; no other persisted change.

## User Impact

Deleting an agent mid-turn stops the turn within about 2 s, removes its sessions, workspace and databases, and lets you recreate the same name right away. Deleting an idle, freshly recreated agent also works the first time. Under heavy load the delete call takes longer (about 40 s at load ~55), because it now waits for the drain instead of returning early and leaving cleanup pending.

## Evidence

- Live A/B on a dev Gateway, fresh state dir, real OpenAI provider (`agentlife4` probe: create agent, quick turn, long `sleep 30` turn, delete mid-turn, recreate same name, turn, delete again):
  - main (round-6 baseline): delete `ok removed 0`; turn kept running about 63 s; journal pending across restart; recreate blocked.
  - this branch: delete `ok`, **7 paths trashed**; long turn `aborted` about 2 s after the delete; agent unlisted; sessions 0; workspace gone; `chat.send` to the old session → `Unknown agent id`; recreate same name **ok on the first attempt**; recreated agent replies `reborn`; deleting the recreated idle agent → `ok`.
- Tests: 455 passed across 27 files (affected suites), including active deletion, recreated-agent memory drain, restart during draining, old-journal recovery, deletion/retirement authority, shared-store preservation, agent RPCs, cron retention, abort/reply settlement and offline deletion. Negative controls: with the original memory-close ordering restored, the real-Gateway regression fails (`agent database retirement began before its memory manager drained`), and the diagnostics regression fails before the production change.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, Gateway runtime build, lint, format, schema verification (v20), Kysely generation check, 0 cycles and docs links pass. Autoreview against `origin/main` is scoped-clean.
- Known log noise, not changed here: the deleted agent's skills watcher logs `FsSafeError: root path changed during operation` when its directory is trashed.


## Follow-up after review (head 6948ee685197)

The first landing attempt stopped on review findings. They're fixed on this head, with `origin/main` merged in:

1. **Cross-agent abort.** Cancellation captures the exact run registration and its teardown before any await (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts`), so a reused session id can't abort another agent's run or be mistaken for a finished teardown.
2. **Stale journal and protected work.** The journal-aware final guard is threaded through every cancellation owner and checked right before each side effect (`agents-delete.ts`). That ties administrative and protected cancellation to the current journal owner, not just host liveness.
3. **Workspace relocation during the drain.** Changes to storage targets are fenced while a deletion is pending, including agents already removed from the roster (`src/config/agent-workspace-roster-transition.ts`). Name and model edits are still allowed.
4. **Upgrade compatibility.** An integration fixture writes main's phase-less v20 journal, then resumes and completes the deletion and recreates the agent. The phase column stays nullable and the schema version is unchanged.
5. **CI.** Worker-owned SQL brings the main-thread SQLite ratchet back to 707. Core tests no longer import extension files. Test types and placement expectations are fixed.
6. **Terminal disposal.** Disposal flushes and checks authority before disposing, so backpressure isn't lost.

A live A/B on the intermediate head found an intermittent purge failure: `Agent database execution admission is closed`, cleanup left pending, and recreate blocked. A straggling post-turn `session-entry.patch` for the deleted agent shared the agent-DB executor with the purge, and its refusal path could close the native generation the purge was using. The architectural fix: session writes check the deletion admission fence before acquiring an executor (`d4dfe2274bb4`), and cleanup drains the previous executor and owns an exclusive one through settlement and close retries (`6948ee685197`). The earlier workaround is removed.

Evidence on this head:
- Integration fixture: 20 delete/recreate cycles with 60 late session patches across three offsets (before abort settles, between clean close and config reload, during purge) all pass. Both failure variants reproduce on the earlier code. Nine cutover suites 195/195; owner and sibling suites 170 passed (1 Linux-only skip); active, restart and legacy integration pass with long timeouts. Types, lint, boundaries, formatting, docs and cycles (0) pass; SQLite T1 707. Autoreview is scoped-clean.
- Live, fresh state, real OpenAI provider, 5 runs (3× create, quick turn, delete during a `sleep 30` turn, recreate, turn, delete idle; 2× agents A and B each mid-turn, delete A, then delete B once idle): **5/5 clean**. Deletes took 2.5–4.2 s with 7 paths trashed; turns aborted; recreate worked the first time; B's concurrent turn finished `B-DONE`; idle deletes succeeded. The structured log has no purge failures and no failed late writes; late writes are refused before they reach the database.


## Second follow-up after review (head 265fd8e88af4)

The next landing attempt stopped on two more findings, both fixed:

- **Cross-agent admission identities.** With a shared session store, deletion matched session-work admissions by bare session id across agents, so a surviving agent's replacement work on the same id could be interrupted. Admission closures and interruptions are now constrained to the deleted agent (`5782beac7857`), and two keys sharing one physical session are drained once while every alias is still settled (`2166b90eb1dd`).
- **Bounded ordinary drains.** A drain timeout in plain session archive/delete waited without limit for the aborted owner. Unbounded settlement is now confined to agent deletion; ordinary operations report their bounded timeout again (`5782beac7857`).
- **Write fence lifetime.** Review also found that a failed drain could release the session-write fence while the journal stayed pending. The fence is now owned by the journal and held until completion or rollback, and restart recovery refreshes it (`f019f11ff035`, `035b6ec04656`, `265fd8e88af4`).
- **Main merges.** `origin/main` is merged again (`069e513f6ccc`, `55c237a68fc8`). The admission check moved with main's extracted session creator (`runtime-agent.ts`, `session-create-target.ts`).

Evidence: every new regression fails before its fix. Nine cutover suites 199/199; delete/archive 86; owner suites 170; plugin runtime 65; active, restart and legacy integration including the 20-cycle late-patch fixture all pass. T1 stays 707 with 0 cycles. Full-branch autoreview is scoped-clean. Live on this head (fresh state, real provider, same five runs as before): **5/5 clean**. Deletes took 2.7–5.3 s with 7 paths trashed; turns aborted; recreate worked the first time; `B-DONE`; idle deletes succeeded. The structured log has no failed purges and no failed late writes.


## Third follow-up (head 25ef06704022)

The previous landing attempt stopped because ordinary user Stop regressed: `src/gateway/server-worker-placement-cancel.test.ts` failed 3/3 on the PR head (no `aborted` summary, no `killed` terminal) while passing on main. The cause was `f019f11ff035`: session admission had lost Stop's interruption callback. `92a5dcd9be8a` restores it, so aborted receipts are kept and deletion refusals take precedence where they overlap a Stop fence. It also makes the deletion executor reject stale-owner promises consistently, which fixes the related CI shard. `25ef06704022` removes a duplicate wrapper-inventory entry and moves the unchanged wait helpers into their existing observer owner (deleting `runs.wait.ts`), which drops 333 unneeded inventory entries.

- The unchanged Stop suite passes 3/3 (fails 3/3 on `265fd8e88af4`); deletion registry 18/18; Stop, operator and placement siblings 207; the attributed CI replay 649 passed and 1 skipped; wrapper closure 17/17. The active, restart and legacy integration with the 20-cycle fixture passes. Full-branch autoreview is scoped-clean.
- Live, fresh state, real provider: ordinary Stop (`chat.abort` during a `sleep 30` shell turn) aborts in 17 ms on the built-in runtime and 32 ms on Codex, and the next turn answers on both, the same as latest main (29 ms and 5 ms). Agent deletion: 3/3 lifecycle runs clean and the cross-agent run clean, with B's concurrent turn finishing. A second cross-agent run was inconclusive: B's Codex turn hit `codex app-server request timed out` before its tool started, while `fseventsd` was using about 5.5 cores from other builds on the host. Deletion latency rose to 11–46 s under that file-system contention; agent creation and turns slowed by the same factor.
- On the ClawSweeper P2 "[P2] Revalidate journal authority before stopping worker placement": `prepareSessionLifecycleDrain` passes its full params to `prepareSessionWorkerPlacementStop`, and in `src/gateway/worker-environments/session-placement-lifecycle.ts` both `beforeDrain` and `stop` call `params.authorize?.()` before any effect, with dispatch reclaim receiving both. Placement stop is already re-authorized against the current journal before its side effects.


## Fourth follow-up (head 28f417c0f20c)

- **Legacy upgrade (also broken on current main).** With a real v2026.9.9 state holding an unfinished, phase-less agent deletion, Doctor migrated schemas, hit the deletion fence, refused the whole run and skipped later repairs. This reproduces on main: maintenance discovery left out stores with pending deletions. `11d375f9d51c` and `8a224f065473` include those stores in Doctor preflight and backups, prepare their schemas under deletion ownership, and stop treating WAL sidecars as databases. A committed regression uses v2026.9.9-shaped storage, and the published-driver harness (keeper agent with settings, sessions and workspace, plus a doomed agent with a pending journal) passes end to end: Doctor, recovery, keeper intact, reopen, recreate.
- **Delete stall after merging main.** Main's #168635 added a plugin-state observation cache that compound deletion did not update, so native binding cleanup flip-flopped between stale cached presence and actual absence. Live, `agents.delete` took 237 s, with the session `delete-prepare` run phase at 232.9 s. `c3621fab51e6` makes those comparisons read authoritative state inside the existing worker transaction and removes the incomplete cache and duplicate conditional SQL (production −223 lines). A Gateway regression fails at a 10 s bound before the fix. Ordinary session deletes on main are unaffected; I checked live on 31b1db627305.
- **Main merged** again (`28f417c0f20c`). The lander's reviewed test-only fixture patch is included.
- **Evidence on this head:** all 21 requested groups pass, including the v2026.9.9 harness on a hash-verified copy, the 10 s delete assertions in the active, restart and legacy integration, Doctor (154) and update guards (58). Autoreview is scoped-clean. Live, fresh state: ordinary Stop aborts in 10 ms (built-in) and 5 ms (Codex) and the next turn answers; agent deletion 2/2 lifecycle runs clean at 6.1 s and 3.8 s (7 paths trashed, turn aborted, recreate on the first try, idle delete ok); the cross-agent run is clean at 5.2 s with B's concurrent turn finishing.

prs.title: test(qa): read authoritative delivery state in channel e2e
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two QA channel e2e scenarios failed or timed out on main for test-side reasons. Product delivery was correct in both cases.

1. **Ambiguous Discord announcement custody** (`test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/channel-progress-presentation.e2e.test.ts`) times out on unchanged main: it failed in 68.5 s on `4754d394130a`. The test observes the outbound delivery queue from the test process while a separate child Gateway writes the rows. `566005dc13f` made the empty-queue cache in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.kernel.ts` survive reader reopenings, so the test's reader kept seeing a cached empty queue. That is correct for the Gateway, which owns the database and invalidates its own cache. It is wrong for an out-of-process test observer.
2. **Discord lifecycle progress drafts** (`extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/discord/scenario-runtime.ts`) waited for `• Exec`. After `cb9bdcd6e78` added per-tool glyphs, Discord renders `🛠️ Exec`, so the scenario timed out at 90 s while the correct draft was visible in the recorder.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The announcement test now reads committed delivery rows directly with the canonical query, decoder and projection, instead of going through the runtime cache it does not own. Every assertion and timeout is unchanged.
- The lifecycle scenario matches drafts by tool label. Glyph rendering remains covered by the Discord renderer tests.

No product code changes.

## User Impact

None directly. The QA channel lanes stop failing on correct delivery behavior, so they can catch real regressions again.

## Evidence

Testbox:
- Before the fix, the branch failed in 68.7 s and unchanged main failed identically in 68.5 s. After, the single case passes in 13.2 s, retaining ambiguous custody with exactly one final delivery.
- The full file passes 16/16 (one-worker wall time 282.6 s).
- The exact `pnpm test:changed` selection passes 18/18 (wall time 334.9 s).
- `check-changed` fails only on inherited Gateway and UI dead exports, which produce an identical list on unchanged main.

Channel flows that passed during this lane:
- Discord long delivery (8,415 characters split into nine messages), custody, progress and tool failures.
- Slack preview retirement, suppressed announcements, native-stream fallback, compact progress and reply targets.
- Telegram short streaming, media and provider-failure settlement.

prs.title: feat(macos): use shared Rust sidecar for node sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Makes the macOS app use the shared Rust Gateway client and node runtime from [RFC #54](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/54) for its node connection **by default**. The app launches and supervises a bundled Rust helper over authenticated, bounded IPC.

## Why This Change Was Made

Swift keeps credentials, device identity, TLS policy, permissions and native callbacks; the bundled Bun worker keeps its existing commands. Helper startup, cancellation and shutdown follow the native connection's lifetime. Other operator Gateway connections remain native.

## User Impact

Missing, incompatible or invalidly signed helpers visibly prevent node startup, with no silent Swift fallback. Absent native results remain distinct from explicit JSON null. Rust handlers adopt `Ok(Some(value))` / `Ok(None)`; in-tree consumers are migrated. Gateway and sidecar-v1 wire formats remain unchanged, with no user-state or database-schema migration.

**Code reduction was not achieved.** Against pinned main `b79ec83d3351`, production is **+4,602/−751: net +3,851 LOC** for the native adapter, authenticated IPC and lifecycle ownership. Tests/support add a net 8,044 lines; build/CI/config +289, docs +92 and lockfiles +13. Accounting covers all 94 changed paths and separates embedded Rust tests. **Memory parity, speedup and lower battery use remain unproven.**

## Evidence

Head: [`db7b080a224`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/db7b080a224cb489682905d86885782267a879e5). **Validation remains in progress.**

| Observed proof | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37071242796) | 67 successful jobs, 15 intentional skips, zero failures; required CI gate passes. Includes 2,168 shared Swift tests and 2,526 macOS app tests, Windows, iOS smoke, Periphery and guards. |
| [Exact-head native/package workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37071242271) | 115 scenarios plus TLS acceptance/rejection: fresh bundle placement, upgrade/rollback replacement, missing/incompatible helper rejection, signature/tamper checks and retirement before native effects. Retained probe cleanup has no forced or remaining PIDs. Hosted package is **arm64, ad-hoc signed**. [Proof artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37071242271/artifacts/11257816785). |
| Local universal release package | Actual `6f763ea7238`: canonical build and independent audit pass, with 24 runtime-readiness records, all six binaries containing arm64/x86_64 slices, strict deep ad-hoc signatures, matching app/runtime identity and ZIP/DMG/dSYM artifacts. No observed child survivors. Later commits through `db7b080a224` change tests only; the package retains its real 6f identity. |
| Local packaged-helper probes | Actual 6f helper: all five fresh phases pass; **16/16 functional and 103/103 capacity checks**. Covers absent/null/error results, large and concurrent payloads, cancellation/deadlines, delayed/missing Pong, 64 held RPCs across a 17-second keepalive interval and 100 cancellation/refill batches. Helpers exit naturally. These use controlled WebSocket fixtures. |

prs.title: fix(ui): transcript search opens the selected historical message
prs.body:
Closes #118560

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and validation results.

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript-search results from before a main-session reset could open the current visible transcript tail instead of the selected historical message. Same-session invalidations, terminal events, resets, route changes, pane lifecycle transitions, and failed anchored requests could also replace, strand, or retry the temporary historical projection before the selected message was visibly centered.

## What Changed

- Carry the selected hit's typed `sessionId` and `messageId` as one-shot internal navigation state.
- Keep exact anchor ownership through the anchored history request, render commit, and selected-message centering attempt.
- Park and coalesce ordinary history loads behind that owner, preserving caller options and promise completion instead of allowing a live refresh to invalidate the anchor.
- Defer terminal `session.message`, applied `sessions.changed`, reset, and other passive refresh paths until visible anchor completion; unavailable recovery still owns exactly one canonical fallback.
- Reconcile exact-run terminal Gateway events while the historical projection is isolated, so local run/stream lifecycle completes without replacing the selected historical messages.
- Preserve the historical projection during a deferred reset while invalidating its canonical cache, and block older-page loads throughout anchor isolation.
- Keep the pane retry guard through a failed anchor's parked canonical recovery, then consume the one-shot anchor without starting a third history request.
- Fence asynchronous pane work by state, session, connection generation, pending token, and pane attempt; route/destructive cancellation and disconnect settle parked work without leaking it into a new owner.
- Expand collapsed dashboard work groups, await their render, measure the expanded row, and center the actual matched message element.
- Keep historical projections pane-owned so ordinary navigation restores the canonical current tail, and show a dismissible notice when the selected message is unavailable.

The change adds no schema version, configuration surface, fallback path, or changelog entry.

## Rebase And Current-Head Validation

- Published head: `f79a38f6531b541a2317c549378192fbdfbaf5cb`.
- Rebased the complete 21-commit branch onto `main` `a3817e987483765dd339f9d584ae5d1580d5981e`, resolving shared chat event ownership, refresh ownership, and transcript virtualizer overlaps while preserving current-main behavior.
- `main` advanced to `dbc2356abc9a10c3c9e2b7f5b7f14d9a4fc229be` during publication; the merge simulation remains clean and the intervening upstream changes do not overlap this history path.
- The previous hosted bundle failure is not reproducible after the required rebase. Exact-head `pnpm ui:build` passes with 11 startup JS requests and 334002 gzip bytes, below the unchanged 335415-byte baseline-plus-tolerance limit. No performance baseline or tolerance was changed.
- Initial anchored-history transport failure now performs exactly one guarded canonical recovery, keeps the retry guard until settlement, consumes the route anchor, and has a dedicated lifecycle regression.
- An anchored terminal now retires acknowledged steer chips and attachment ownership into the canonical cache without admitting the live tail into the historical projection.
- SQLite active-event regression: 13/13 passed.
- Focused Control UI/Gateway history-anchor and terminal regressions: 181/181 passed after the final rebase.
- Isolated virtualizer and collapsed-work-group centering regression: 9/9 passed.
- Gateway chat-history regression: 101/101 passed.
- Browser transcript-search E2E: 6/6 passed with fresh local screenshots. It opens the selected historical match and clears its one-shot route state before ordinary reload returns to the canonical tail.
- Isolated real-Gateway Control UI transport E2E: 2/2 passed; generated evidence confirms both Gateway and proxy ports closed after cleanup.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, Control UI i18n verification, focused UI boundary lint, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` was not rerun because the local Crabbox runner previously failed its own basic sanity check before dispatch. No source failure was bypassed.

## Evidence Boundaries

- Browser proof uses local, isolated fixtures and contains no credentials or public artifact URL.
- The real-Gateway transport proof uses ephemeral local state and confirms cleanup; it does not claim a live third-party channel result.
- All rebased commits are authored and committed as `Sami Rusani <samgithub@pm.me>`.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep read commands off the writable shared state DB
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several CLI inspection paths could re-enter task and TaskFlow runtime restore through writable state owners. On a host with a running Gateway, commands such as task listing/audit, maintenance preview, TaskFlow inspection, and default plugin inventory could therefore create or migrate the shared state database, or record configuration observation, despite being read-only operations.

This change makes those inspection restores fail closed when the existing state DB is older than the current schema, rather than opening it writable. It preserves the writable migration path for explicit mutations.

## Why This Change Was Made

#124110 now owns the generic non-creating, non-migrating state/doctor loaders. This PR has been reshaped after it and drops the overlapping work.

The remaining scope is limited to the unique guarantees:

- task and TaskFlow runtime inspection restores use a current-schema read-only state DB path;
- explicit task and flow mutations still restore writable state and may migrate it;
- plugin/task inspection config reads use an internal non-observing config seam;
- channels status has regression coverage for its non-observing fallback config reads;
- task maintenance preview does not promote a failed read-only restore into a writable migration.

No schema version, public config option, or CLI flag is added.

Refs: #119583, #120222

#120222 is retained as resilience context only. This PR does not change Gateway startup ordering or claim to resolve that open product decision.

## User Impact

Read-only CLI inspection no longer creates or migrates `state/openclaw.sqlite`. If a task or TaskFlow inspection encounters an older state schema, it explains how to repair it (`openclaw doctor --fix` or starting the Gateway) without changing the DB.

Explicit mutation commands, including task notification/cancellation and flow cancellation, retain their existing writable migration behavior.

## Evidence

- Rebased and narrowed on current `openclaw/main` after #124110.
- Focused tests: 98/98 passing across 7 files, including old-schema assertions that inspection leaves `user_version` unchanged and mutations can then migrate.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- `CI=true pnpm build` completed.
- Local autoreview completed clean.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid no-op node scope upgrades
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An already-paired node reconnecting with a node-only bootstrap token could repeatedly fail with `node pairing changed during connect`. The bootstrap retry path demanded an operator handoff even when the issued profile contained only `node`, recording a `scope-upgrade` from node/empty scopes to node/empty scopes. Bootstrap re-approval rotated the node token and changed its existing pairing generation.

## User Impact

Node-only and cloud-worker bootstrap retries reuse their approved pairing and finish connecting. Real role/scope upgrades retain their approval requirements and security audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the operator-handoff retry block on the bootstrap profile actually including `operator`. This is one production line at the request decision, leaving approval and generation ownership intact. Both ordinary node-only and cloud-worker profiles intentionally match the setup-code handoff client selector; neither needs an operator grant.

A genuine concurrent re-pair or token rotation may still reject an in-flight connect. The existing generation check and reconnect behavior remain the accepted handling for that case.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.node-bootstrap-reconnect.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: both cases fail on the original code because the generation changes (943.87 s command wall time); both pass with this guard (1,292.28 s command wall time). The isolated baseline handshakes completed, so this proves the generation-churn cause rather than reproducing every condition of the reported close-1008 loop.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38101841129) passed all 14 tests across the two affected files. Node-only/cloud-worker cases took 507/116 ms; the real scope-upgrade case took 1.356 s and verified a pending upgrade request. The new file took 20.91 s including its shared Gateway fixture; the existing pairing file took 56.75 s. Their shared CI job took 142 s. No timers, sleeps, polling, or production test seams were added.
- Local cold worker compilation, module loading, Gateway startup, and runner verification dominated wall time. A broader local two-file run was stopped after two unmodified tests (`reconciles concurrent pairing decisions against current device authority` and `keeps a merged owner unidentified until Doctor repairs it before reconnect`) hit the existing 120 s limit during startup. Both passed in CI (9.133/2.365 s); no timeout or assertion was weakened. A Testbox fallback stalled during local source preparation before runner allocation.
- Touched-file formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review is clean at P1, pinned to the branch fork `dd4b258a3cfa` because the shared `origin/main` ref advanced during the task.
- `timeout 40m node scripts/watch-pr-ci.mjs 168795 dc3c0a992fa6500660dc2dd8745a8c5fab8fed92` returned `GREEN`. The CI run and `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded; GitHub's raw rollup retains superseded checks, which the exact-head watcher excludes.

prs.title: fix(agents): sanitize Kimi-format tool call ids for Anthropic-bound replay
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `sanitizeToolCallId` exempts native Kimi-format ids (`functions.{name}:{idx}`) from sanitization in `strict` mode. The exemption is destination-blind, so when a session that ran on a Kimi model is later replayed to **direct Anthropic** (`anthropic-messages`), the raw ids — containing `.` and `:` — are sent verbatim and Anthropic rejects the entire request:
  `HTTP 400 invalid_request_error — messages.N.content.M.tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'`
  Once a transcript contains one Kimi turn, every subsequent Anthropic request for that session fails until the session is reset.
- **History (whack-a-mole):** strict sanitization originally corrupted Kimi ids and broke Kimi multi-turn (#62319) → the Kimi exemption was added → the exemption then broke Kimi→Anthropic replay (#10222, #12277 — both auto-closed as stale, never fixed).
- **Fix:** make the exemption destination-aware via a new `ToolCallIdMode`: `"strict-anthropic"`. It behaves exactly like `"strict"` except native Kimi-format ids are also rewritten. `buildStrictAnthropicReplayPolicy` (the funnel for all Anthropic-family replay policies) now emits `toolCallIdMode: "strict-anthropic"`. OpenAI-compatible replay policies keep `"strict"`, so Kimi-bound replay still preserves native Kimi ids (#62319 stays fixed).
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `strict` and `strict9` behavior is byte-identical (existing tests untouched and passing); `preserveNativeAnthropicToolUseIds` (#61254 cache optimization) is unaffected; no Bedrock/OpenAI policy changes; no transcript repair changes.

## Why this shape

- The occurrence-aware resolver already guarantees tool_use/tool_result pairing across rewrites (raw→assigned pending queue), so rewriting at replay time is safe and deterministic — the stored transcript is untouched; ids are normalized in-memory per request.
- Poisoned sessions self-heal: histories with Kimi turns become replayable to Anthropic again with no session resets.

## Testing

- 4 new cases in `tool-call-id.test.ts`: Kimi ids rewritten to `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` under `strict-anthropic` (and idempotent), Kimi ids still preserved under `strict`, native `toolu_` ids preserved with the preservation flag, and call/result pairing held across rewrites including duplicate raw ids.
- Verified in production on 2026.7.2-beta.5 (dist-level equivalent of this patch): a live session with Kimi (`moonshotai/kimi-k3` via OpenRouter) tool-call turns followed by direct-Anthropic turns on the same session — previously deterministic 400s (228 occurrences in one day), now 100% 200s with pairing intact.

Fixes the class reported in #10222 / #12277.

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop inter-tool-call text leaking as separate preview messages
prs.body:
Closes #32535

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users with partial preview streaming saw
inter-tool-call text blocks leak as separate messages. A turn with multiple
tool rounds rendered one preview message per round ("Message A", "Message B")
instead of one self-editing draft bubble that settles on the final answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Partial streaming mode is supposed to keep ONE preview message and edit it in
place. The rotation paths (`rotateAnswerLaneAfterQueuedBlocksSettle`,
`prepareAnswerLaneForText`, `onAssistantMessageStart`) treated every tool round
like a new assistant message and called `forceNewMessage()`, which starts a
fresh message. This PR:

- Adds `shouldSplitPreviewMessages` to the draft state: only non-partial modes
  split previews into new messages as text grows.
- Adds a `revive()` lifecycle to the Telegram draft stream that reopens a
  finalized stream WITHOUT clearing the current message id or bumping the
  generation, so the next update keeps editing the same preview.
- Gates the rotation sites on `shouldSplitPreviewMessages`; partial mode now
  revives the same preview across tool boundaries and finals.

Non-goals: block/progress streaming behavior is unchanged; this is scoped to
partial preview streaming only.

## User Impact

Telegram users on partial preview streaming now see one draft bubble that
self-edits across the whole turn and settles on the final reply, instead of a
growing stack of intermediate messages.

## Evidence

- Full telegram extension lane: `pnpm exec vitest run --config
  test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts` → **204/204 files, 3551/3551
  tests passed**.
- Two lane-green prerequisites are included (the lane was 27 tests red on the
  branch base, unrelated to this change and not covered by CI):
  - `bot/helpers.ts`: `resolveTelegramMessageThreadSpec` crashed with
    `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'is_direct_messages')` on
    chat-less spooled updates (webhook + polling-session lanes, 26 tests).
  - `progress-draft-preview.test.ts`: asserted `args.description` renders for
    shell tools, but shell detail is the command by design; the test now
    exercises the raw command detail contract (`echo alpha`).
- `pnpm check` (typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, policy guards) → exit 0.
- `pnpm build` → exit 0.

prs.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
prs.body:
Related: #51620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose inbound message was accepted shortly before a SIGUSR1 or config reload could have buffered message content silently dropped before it reached the reply pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now closes ordinary work admission synchronously, flushes accepted inbound debounce work inside one core-private restart continuation, drains channel, active-turn, and followup work in order, then rechecks work created by followup delivery. Pre-created debounce callbacks reserve tracked required-continuation ownership, including parentless accepted work. Already-reserved required continuations may finish during the signal-pending gap while ordinary roots remain fenced, and removed-but-unsettled timer flushes remain visible until settlement. Buffered callbacks can also be explicitly rebound to the private restart admission context, while the global sweep is bounded by both the remaining restart deadline and a 100-pass/30-second ceiling so continued ingress cannot stall reload indefinitely.

Every non-forced phase now shares one absolute restart-drain deadline. Initial active-task and embedded-run waits receive only the budget remaining after inbound debounce and channel queue draining, so earlier phases cannot reset the configured maximum.

Forced restarts retain the existing skip-drain behavior. This does not persist messages sent while the gateway is offline.

## User Impact

Messages accepted immediately before an in-process reload can complete through the normal command/reply path instead of being rejected by the restart fence or disappearing from in-memory buffers. A sustained stream of new transport events also cannot hold the gateway forever in the debounce-flush phase, and the configured restart deferral maximum is honored across the full drain sequence.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation for `bb8f1b842e85c6745e7f8a1bfb8303d73ca6f7f6`:

- **Focused behavior tests:** 4 files, 167 tests passed.
  - `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`: 65 passed.
  - `src/process/command-queue.test.ts`: 42 passed.
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts`: 16 passed.
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`: 44 passed.
- **New P1 regressions:** a buffer created inside an admitted inbound root survives that root's release; timer-started required work can finish through the restart-signal-pending fence while ordinary roots remain blocked; a timer-started callback remains visible and keeps the restart sweep pending until its real command enqueue settles; parentless accepted continuations retain required ownership; continuous ingress stops at the pass cap; the exact final-pass boundary reports drained correctly; a slow callback returns at the supplied deadline; and a deterministic 100 ms restart budget reduced to 40 ms by earlier debounce/channel work is passed as 40 ms to both initial active-work waits and the final close drain.
- **Formatting/lint:** `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint` passed on all touched files.
- **Type safety:** core production, core test, and plugin SDK declaration `tsgo` checks passed.
- **Tree identity:** GitHub tree `37822eb909f4bd797d9bc6eb7d8488286f39637a` is the exact locally tested tree; both newly uploaded blob SHAs matched the local Git objects.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions is running on the exact head above.

A live Signal/Telegram account is not paired in this environment. I have requested the repository's Mantis Telegram proof flow below so maintainers can attach redacted channel-to-gateway reload evidence to this exact head.

## Implementation and Safety Notes

- `createInboundDebouncer()` retains its public `enqueue` / `flushKey` / `cancelKey` return shape.
- `ChannelRunQueue` retains its public `enqueue` / `deactivate` shape.
- No public `enqueueInternal`, `allowDuringGatewayDrain`, or command-queue admission bypass is exposed.
- The debounce registry is weak, avoiding channel teardown requirements.
- Overflow-summary backlog is included in followup pending counts.
- Bounded restarts use one absolute deadline; unbounded restarts continue passing `undefined` and wait indefinitely.
- The branch remains a focused 13-file change.

## Synchronization

- **PR head:** `bb8f1b842e85c6745e7f8a1bfb8303d73ca6f7f6`
- **Immediate parent:** `38befdcf347331814f3453093ff3ef0c31cc33c0`
- **Synchronized main cutoff:** `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`
- **Cutoff merge topology:** synchronization commit `5ae09ec76ee9b851cb24b07acad291724c185868` has first parent `da4b1b9c15b6a7b965657fc753e0c25d8dd0e4fa` and second parent `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`.
- **Diff:** 13 files, +1167/-155.

prs.title: fix(imessage): thread replies with thread_originator_guid
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iMessage reply threading so OpenClaw's responses appear as threaded replies in Messages.app with `thread_originator_guid` and `reply_to_guid` correctly set.

## Root Cause

The durable delivery path (`resolveDurableInboundReplyToId`) only fell back to `ctxPayload.ReplyToIdFull` and `ctxPayload.ReplyToId` — the inbound message's *reply-to* fields (the message the inbound message was replying to). For a new top-level message, these are undefined, so `replyToId` was never set. The durable path sent the reply unthreaded, and the fallback `deliver` callback never fired.

## Changes

### iMessage extension (threading is handled in the extension, not the core framework)

- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/deliver.ts`**: `deliverIMessageReply` now accepts an `inboundMessageGuid` typed parameter. When the payload doesn't carry an explicit `replyToId` (e.g. new top-level messages where the durable path returned `not_applicable`), the inbound message GUID is used as the reply target.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.ts`**: The fallback `deliver` callback passes `ctxPayload.MessageSidFull` as `inboundMessageGuid` to `deliverIMessageReply`, keeping threading metadata in a typed iMessage-specific parameter rather than stuffing it into the generic `ReplyPayload`.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/send.ts`**: Sets `params.thread_originator_guid` from `resolveIMessageThreadReplyToId`. The unthreaded retry now strips both `reply_to` and `thread_originator_guid` (not just `reply_to`).
- **`extensions/imessage/src/monitor-reply-cache.ts`**: `resolveIMessageThreadReplyToId` returns the message GUID itself for top-level messages (it IS the thread root) and when the cache entry is missing.
- **`extensions/imessage/src/channel.ts`**: Added `threading: { resolveReplyToMode: () => "all" }` adapter so all outbound replies carry the inbound message GUID.
- **`extensions/imessage/package.json`**: `bundledDist: false` is preserved — iMessage is an external plugin, not a bundled core artifact.

### Core framework (no changes)

Threading is handled entirely in the iMessage extension via the typed `inboundMessageGuid` parameter. No changes to `src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.ts` or other core files.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (exact head: `ab4876607fae`)
```
pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts — 66 passed (66)
pnpm test test/scripts/bundled-plugin-build-entries.test.ts — 32 passed (32)
```

### E2E test (exact head: `ab4876607fae`)

Top-level reply — sent from darren-mac-mini to clawtan\@icloud.com:

```
Sent message GUID: 33ECA8CD-E479-4066-B15E-8CC92A861339
Response GUID: F1A672B2-120E-4B87-A1BE-DF6055E45BB7
reply_to_guid: 33ECA8CD-E479-4066-B15E-8CC92A861339 ✅
thread_originator_guid: 33ECA8CD-E479-4066-B15E-8CC92A861339 ✅
Both match sent message GUID ✅
```

Bridge log ( Messages.app dylib):
```

```
