prs.title: fix: preserve Gateway delegation for channel replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repairs a dropped host-ownership handoff that can send channel-origin delegated OpenClaw requests over WebSocket without their private run authority, producing `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. Ordinary and fast reply session setup clone the inbound context without copying its privately bound Gateway resolver. Use the existing scope-checked `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` helper at both boundaries.
2. A deployment of that first repair still reproduced the error. Further tracing found that Discord's provider supplies the host-bound `buildContext`, but `buildDiscordMessagePreflightContext` dropped it. Message processing then selected the plain fallback builder, so there was no Gateway binding for session initialization to preserve.

**Scope correction (September 17):** that second, Discord-side production correction has since landed upstream independently, in `34f29edb265` — *fix(discord): restore OpenClaw delegation from guild messages* (#143006, September 9). `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.ts` is now byte-identical between this branch and `main`, so this PR no longer carries that production change. What it retains on the Discord side is the **regression test** that pins the forwarding behavior, which upstream did not add. The independent convergence is corroborating evidence that the diagnosis was correct.

This PR's remaining production surface is therefore the session/admission-evidence ownership handoff: `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-fast-path.ts`, `src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.ts`, and `src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.ts`. It adds no permissions, infers no authority from identifiers, transports no grants over WebSocket, does not weaken the delegation guard, and does not select a global Gateway.

## User Impact

Channel session preparation retains scope-bound Gateway ownership, so calls keep their intended local route. The absent-builder fallback remains unchanged. No configuration or credential changes are required.

## Evidence

### Delegated-authority expiry before final effect (round 22)

The open security ask was whether an **already-prepared** delegated operation is rejected **before it performs I/O** once its channel is unbound, retired, or replaced — with the Gateway itself still running. Round 22 measures that directly, at the production fence, with a real observable effect.

Where the fence is: `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` captures the retained resolver, and every delegated call then passes through `bindInProcessGatewayContext` (`src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts:113-133`), which resolves the binding *before* `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` and throws `Gateway instance unavailable for <method>` when it yields nothing. For work that has already entered a handler, `resolveInProcessGatewayDispatch`'s `assertContextCurrent` is composed into the `sessionMutationCommitGuard` that `handleGatewayRequest` hands every handler, so a revocation that lands mid-await still fires before the handler's final write.

Both runs below drive the same chain of real production functions — `registerChannelIngressHostOwner` → `resolveStableChannelMessageIngress` → `createHostChannelInboundEventContextBuilder` (which runs `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`) → `finalizeInboundContext` → `initFastReplySessionState` (one of the two call sites this PR adds `copyChannelParticipantAdmissionEvidence` to) → `readChannelContextGatewayContextResolver` (exactly what `agent-runner-execution.ts:544` reads) → `withPluginRuntimeGatewayContextResolver` → `bindAgentToolGatewayRequest` → `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` → real `handleGatewayRequest` → a registered method handler whose **final effect is a real filesystem write**. Rejection "before I/O" is measured by that file's absence, not by an exception type alone.

In every scenario the channel host's own `resolveGatewayContext` keeps returning the live Gateway — only the **channel** lifetime is revoked — and a control call bound straight to a live root Gateway reaches its final effect, so each row is a channel-authority result rather than a Gateway-availability result.

| Scenario | Binding copied to sessionCtx | Operation accepted | Handler entered | Handler committed | **Final effect** | Successor Gateway redeemed | Gateway still active |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| allowed, channel live | true | true | 1 | 1 | **PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| unbound context | false | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced before dispatch | true | false | 0 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| retired **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |
| replaced **during awaited work** | true | false | 1 | 0 | **NOT PERFORMED** | 0 | true |

Rejections: `Gateway instance unavailable for sessions.list` for all four retired/replaced rows. The two mid-flight rows are the sharpest result — the handler had already started and was stopped by the production commit guard before its write.

The `unbound` row is honest about a different mechanism: with no retained binding there is no in-process delegated path to enter at all, so the call degrades to an ordinary authenticated external Gateway client (`gateway sessions.list requires credentials before opening a websocket` in an environment with no configured Gateway credentials). No in-process delegated effect occurs, but that row is *not* produced by the lifetime fence.

**Negative control.** Reverting only `prepareHostChannelContextAdmissionEvidence`'s fenced resolver back to `main`'s `state.gatewayResolverByPreparation.set(preparation, params.owner.resolveGatewayContext)` — and nothing else — flips all four retired/replaced rows from **NOT PERFORMED** to **PERFORMED**, with `handler committed` going `0 → 1` in each. The standalone run exits 1 with 16 assertion failures; the committed regression test reports `4 failed | 2 passed (6)` at `expect(fs.existsSync(effectPath)).toBe(effect)` — `expected false, received true`. The fence, not the harness, is what rejects the stale authority.

This round adds `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.delegated-effect.test.ts` so the behavior stays pinned in CI. The standalone `pnpm tsx` proof that produced the table is deliberately **not** committed; it is retained with its logs alongside this round's gate output.

#### Round 22b — the real delegated apply owner

Revision 15 accepted the table above but pointed out that its handler substituted for `sessions.list` and guarded its own write, leaving the real delegated approval/application chain — which has its own authority checks — unexercised. That is a fair hit, and the chain is reachable directly.

`prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` (`src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.ts`) is production code, and its `isAuthorityActive` already consults `callerIdentity.gatewayContextResolver()`. `assertLiveApprovalAuthority` runs at preparation, again inside the proposal resolver, and once more through the `assertCurrent` callback the apply owner invokes immediately before its effect. The repo's existing `system-agent-approval-authority.test.ts` exercises exactly that path — but with a synthetic `() => liveContext` resolver. What was missing was the same path driven by the resolver **this PR copies into the reply session context**.

The new cases build that resolver through the same real production ingress chain, hand it to `withGatewayToolCallerIdentity` with a real claimed run authority (`claimAgentRunDelegatedAuthority`), and drive the real `prepareDelegatedSystemAgentApproval` to its apply. The channel host's own resolver keeps returning the live Gateway throughout, so only the channel lifetime can reject.

| Channel state at apply | Outcome | Apply effect |
|---|---|---|
| live | resolves `{ kind: "completed" }` | performed once |
| retired while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |
| replaced while the apply owner awaits queued work | rejects `system-agent approval authority is no longer active` | **never performed** |

**Negative control on the apply owner.** With the same single-line revert, both revoked cases resolve `{ kind: 'completed' }` and the apply effect is performed:

```
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is retired
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
× fences the delegated system-agent apply owner when the channel is replaced
  → promise resolved "{ kind: 'completed', reply: { …(3) } }" instead of rejecting
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  6 failed | 3 passed (9)
```

Without the fence, the real apply owner applies a change under expired channel authority. That is the behavior this PR prevents.

The channel-ingress setup shared by both blocks is extracted into a single `prepareChannelBoundResolver` helper rather than duplicated.

### Earlier evidence

- The session regression uses a real host-bound channel context, actual inbound finalization, `getReplyFromConfig`, and real prepared-run admission. Only the embedded runner is stubbed to inspect the admitted resolver. Live, retired, replaced, and deliberately unbound cases retain the existing owner checks.
- The retained Discord regression invokes actual `preflightDiscordMessage` and actual `buildDiscordMessageProcessContext`. Against the pre-fix implementation the injected-builder case lost its callback while the absent-builder case passed; against the current implementation both pass and processing uses exactly the context object returned by the injected builder. Because the production forwarding now comes from `main`, this test guards it against regression rather than proving a change in this diff.
- An additional diagnostic exercises the real Discord DM builder and preflight assembler with private host ownership, retaining the resolver through fast session initialization. The initial simplified session regression did not cover this earlier adapter handoff.
- 157 focused tests pass: 116 Discord preflight/context tests, four session-copy cases, 19 in-process routing tests, and 18 channel admission/lifecycle tests. The additional private-owner diagnostic also passes.
- Production build, complete five-file changed-file gate, and fresh independent P1 review pass.

### Gates

The 157-test figure and the `check-changed` run above were recorded on the earlier head `1b2ca891101a45d0ab372231f326526bd4db7006` and have not been re-run since; the September 15 `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main'` refresh and the round-22 commit are the only changes beyond it. Round 22's own gates are listed with this round's head in its PR comment.

```sh
# earlier head 1b2ca891101
pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight-context.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.test.ts src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 045524c6f883ca31df7240a107872bd01f2c3378
pnpm build

# round 22 / 22b
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.delegated-effect.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.gateway-authority.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval-authority.test.ts src/channels/message-access/admission-evidence.test.ts src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts src/plugins/registry-runtime.channel-ingress.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test && pnpm oxlint <touched files> && git diff --check
# 5 shards, 108 tests: gateway 11, auto-reply 13, agents-tools 26, plugins 40, channels 18
```

## Related Work and Open Questions

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138596 (previously inspected at `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d`). That PR addresses authenticated CLI/subprocess and worker calls that legitimately cross the Gateway WebSocket boundary, carrying existing host-signed runtime authority. This PR preserves the original local Gateway route at the channel session handoffs. Non-overlapping file sets are not a compatibility proof.

The changes may be complementary, but we have not established that both are required or that either replaces the other. A differential comparison should exercise baseline, this fix, the related fix, and both against the same channel-origin delegation probe. The related PR is not incorporated here.

These production changes are model/runtime-agnostic. Codex enters host tool execution through a native dynamic-tool callback; the bundled Claude CLI MCP handler binds caller identity from its admitted client grant. Those entry paths differ, but no matched successful Claude call has established why the observed behavior differed. No Codex enterprise-policy restriction is demonstrated.

## Post-deployment evidence and remaining validation

On September 8, the operator restarted a real Gateway built from integration `5936dbff50dfbf81c511db450dc1a5be87482e92`, which contains this topic head. A real Discord-origin native Codex turn then invoked the delegated OpenClaw system tool for read-only Gateway status and health. That delegated read completed normally, reported the matching deployed build, and did not fail with the previously observed missing active-run authority error. No configuration, credential, service, or trust changes were made by the probe.

This is successful complete-path **read-only evidence on the combined integration**, not an isolated-topic differential comparison and not evidence of permission to perform mutations. The integration contains other authority fixes, so this observation does not establish which companion fixes are required. Note that the probe ran on September 8, before upstream #143006 landed, so at that time the Discord forwarding under test came from this branch.

### What round 22 resolved, and what it did not

Resolved: rejection before final I/O for retired and replaced channel contexts, including revocation during awaited work, with the Gateway kept active — measured both at the in-process dispatch fence against a real filesystem effect and at the **real delegated system-agent apply owner**, each bound to production by its own negative control (see Evidence above).

Still outstanding:

- **Companion-fix attribution.** The September 8 deployment combined other authority fixes, so it still does not establish which companion changes are required. The differential comparison against #138596 described under *Related Work* has not been run.
- **Unbound is a different mechanism.** An unbound context performs no in-process delegated effect, but because it leaves the in-process path entirely rather than being rejected by the lifetime fence, it is reported separately above rather than folded into the fence result.
- **No booted-gateway probe this round.** The Gateway host in rounds 22 and 22b is an in-process object held live for the run, not a booted gateway service, and round 22b's approval engine seam (`resolveOperatorApproval`) is a stub — the *authority chain* around it is production. Every step between channel ingress and the apply fence is production code; the host and that engine seam are not.

Internal tracking: `openclaw-9e69`, `openclaw-cy3n`.

prs.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. 1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)

4. `node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`

prs.title: fix: submit selected question answers with Ctrl or Cmd Enter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ctrl+Enter and Cmd+Enter ignore selected interactive question answers when focus is on the question panel or a choice.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard users can submit their answer without moving focus to Submit. Required answers, input-method composition, locked questions, links, ordinary buttons, and attachment selection retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The question panel now owns the submit shortcut across its answer controls. Plain Enter keeps native button/link/file-picker behavior and does not submit an empty or invalid answer.

## Evidence

On main at `762930ce`, a real OpenAI task displayed an `ask_user` question. Selecting By SKU and pressing Ctrl+Enter left the panel waiting; clicking Submit worked. With the candidate UI served by the same isolated Gateway, selecting By SKU and pressing Ctrl+Enter submitted immediately. The model received the answer and acknowledged it. Before/after screenshots below contain the synthetic question and result; unrelated profile/sidebar content is cropped out.

The live inventory workflow also completed file creation, an interactive choice, tool-error recovery, and independent verification: 8 records, 23 units, 9,154 cents. Reload after the test Gateway restart preserved the conversation and report. The live run validates Ctrl+Enter; Cmd+Enter is covered by the mounted regression suite.

The original mounted regression failed in eight expected cases. Final edited-file run passed 27 tests in 7.05 seconds wall (0.47 seconds test body), with 37 focused tests passing before the final regression cleanup. UI production and owning `ui-chat` types, scoped lint/style/formatting, relevant guards and fresh managed P0–P2 review passed. CI timing is pending.

The candidate UI build succeeded. Its startup-size report inherits main's budget violation: clean main 375,310 bytes, candidate 375,314 bytes, limit 374,861 bytes. Startup source content is unchanged; the four-byte difference comes from emitted build identity/hash variation. No budget baseline was increased. A broad multi-graph checker was canceled after seven graphs passed; remaining unrelated graphs were not claimed as passing. The owning graph and production types passed separately.

![Before: Ctrl Enter leaves the selected answer waiting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50b0a107-f552-458c-873e-d8292a0dafb7)

![After: Ctrl Enter submits the answer and the model acknowledges it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51aa97eb-4c53-4722-8083-99eda0a47af4)

prs.title: feat(sessions): split deleted archive retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` previously applied the same age cutoff to both reset and deleted transcript archives. This adds `session.maintenance.deletedArchiveRetention` as an independent duration-or-`false` control.

When omitted, `deletedArchiveRetention` inherits `resetArchiveRetention` for backward compatibility. An explicit duration or `false` overrides it independently. Both settings age archive artifacts; they do not age retained SQLite reset history or transcript rows.

## Implementation

- Resolves independent deleted/reset rules from configuration.
- Applies those rules through legacy file-backed maintenance, cron reaping, and ordinary SQLite maintenance.
- Ordinary SQLite maintenance runs archive cleanup even when no session rows are removed.
- Removes a derived archive file before deleting its published SQLite recovery row; failed file cleanup leaves the recovery row intact.
- Preserves inherited deleted retention for older resolved-maintenance callers while retaining explicit disablement.
- Fences archive-row pruning against maintenance-owner invalidation before and inside each SQLite writer callback.
- Updates schema help, examples, and session-management documentation.

## Evidence
- Exact pushed head: `5460eaf7b0ab2221938f1b7a4dbfc052e69d9588`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused runtime command:
  `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-retention.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-writer.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.archive-retention.test.ts src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.fix-missing.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
  Result: **4 test files passed, 22 tests passed**.
- The unmocked integration proof loads a real config file and exercises both paths:
  - a fresh configured store is initialized (`configuredFreshStore: true`);
  - an existing configured store is maintained with independent cutoffs (`configuredExistingStore: true`);
  - the expired deleted archive file and its SQLite recovery row are absent after cleanup (`deletedArchiveFile: false`, `deletedArchiveRow: false` — `false` here means absent);
  - the reset archive remains (`resetArchiveFile: true`).
- The focused tests additionally prove inherited retention for older resolved callers, explicit `false` disablement, ordinary SQLite archive cleanup with no session removals, maintenance-owner invalidation without reopening the store, file-before-row deletion ordering, and lifecycle-deletion failure recovery.
- This proof is on the exact pushed head above; no claim is made that it resolves the separate current-base merge conflict or pending maintainer acceptance.
## Known Gate

This change affects persistent retention and upgrade behavior. Maintainer acceptance of the independent retention contract, ordinary-maintenance deletion timing, and the accessor cleanup boundary remains required before merge.

- Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen)

prs.title: fix: restore first-use permission actions in Mac settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Permissions in the Mac app could not retry Automation access when its native target was unavailable, or saw a denied status before first-use Automation consent had been requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve Automation’s raw `notDetermined` state in the native snapshot so first-use consent remains distinct from denial. Add request/retry for unavailable status while retaining the existing Open System Settings action for denied permissions. The UI chooses by status, with no permission-ID special cases or changes to native permission policy.

An earlier revision routed every non-granted status through a request. Review raised a Screen Recording recovery concern with that broader change. This revision removes the changed denied-request behavior rather than relying on unverified OS re-prompt behavior; the concern was not disproven.

The permission DTO also uses the existing shared `OpenClawLocationMode` directly, deleting the duplicate enum and identity converters. Its three raw wire strings, snapshot shape and all nine consent transitions remain covered. No alias, protocol field, configuration, default, storage behavior or OS permission grant changes.

Production LOC: +18/−28 (net −10); tests: +67/−13 (net +54).

## User Impact

Automation can present its first-use Grant action or retry an unavailable target. Denied permissions—including Screen Recording and Accessibility—keep their existing System Settings recovery action. Granted rows remain actionless.

## Evidence

- With the revised tests against the original UI owner, one case fails because unavailable Automation has no action; 39 pass. The revised candidate passes all 40 component/wire tests.
- Four denied-action cases fail against the earlier generalized request action. The revised tests preserve Settings labels/messages for denied statuses, request/retry for first-use/unavailable statuses, and absence of the wrong message.
- The isolated Chromium flow passes with synthetic native/Gateway fixtures. The new after capture shows denied rows with Open System Settings and unavailable Automation with Retry.
- Pinned Swift lint/format, UI changed gates, core-test/UI typechecks, i18n/structural guards, all three dead-export scans and changed-file lint pass. Fresh full-candidate managed P2 is scoped-clean on the source tree matching `78495f757267d68db4246cd7480452b98b26913d`.

| Before — synthetic fixture | After — synthetic fixture |
| --- | --- |
| ![Permissions before: Automation has no recovery action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64582d32-1902-4a60-aefc-eb4462851e53) | ![Permissions after: denied statuses keep Settings and unavailable Automation offers Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b0be53a-ff99-440b-b3d3-8e4c0941a233) |

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34033095625) passed for `78495f757267d68db4246cd7480452b98b26913d`, including both native Swift phases: 1,661 shared tests, 2,067 default-profile app tests, 2 named-profile tests and 1 isolated health fixture. The updated location wire-encoding, frozen snapshot and consent-transition tests passed, along with all six Automation cases and the injected first-use/denied/Terminal-recovery tests.

[Earlier CI on `739a6593`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34026043071) is retained as superseded history, not proof of the current revision.

Actual correctly signed-app/TCC first-use, denial and grant behavior remains unperformed and unwaived pending the disposable macOS GUI/signing decision. Component tests, injected Swift tests and a signed Git commit are not signed-app/TCC proof. No operator app state, saved Keychain or OS permission interaction was used for this revision.

prs.title: feat: let voice agents hang up when the conversation is over
prs.body:
Closes #132334

## What Problem This Solves

An agent on a classic conversation-mode voice call cannot end the call it is on. Realtime calls get a bound `openclaw_end_call` control, but the classic flow (transcription plus text agent turn plus TTS) has no equivalent, so a call runs until the caller hangs up, `maxDurationSeconds` fires, or an operator runs `openclaw voicecall end`.

Callers hear the gap. On a live call before this change, asked to hang up, the agent answered: `"Right, I can't hang up from my end—just tap end call whenever you're ready!"` An outbound call that has delivered its message holds the line to the cap, spending carrier minutes and occupying a `maxConcurrentCalls` slot (default 1) that blocks the next call.

The existing `voice_call` tool does expose an `end_call` action, but `commandService.endCall` requires a `callId`, and `buildVoiceTurnPrompt` gives the model only bounded opening context plus the caller's latest message. The model has no call identity to pass.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spoken-output contract gains one optional key, so a reply can request its own hangup without a second tool surface:

```json
{"spoken": "Talk to you later.", "end_call": true}
```

`tryParseSpokenJson` returns a `SpokenTurn` (`text` plus `endCall`), `generateVoiceResponse` reports `endCall` the way it already reports `error` (present only when set), and `handleInboundResponse` ends the call after the reply has been spoken.

A flag rather than a tool call, because ordering matters: a mid-turn tool call ends the call before the closing sentence is spoken, which is what the realtime tool's own description warns about.

**Ending safely is decided by what happened to that playback, not by what the provider can do.** `playTts` now reports a `PlaybackOutcome`, and `speak` carries it up:

- `confirmed` — the carrier acknowledged the completion mark; hang up immediately, nothing is truncated.
- `unconfirmed` — playback was requested but completion was never observed; keep the `outbound.notifyHangupDelaySec` grace that notify mode already applies.
- `cancelled` — playback stopped early, i.e. the caller barged in; keep the line open, because the caller took the floor.

A failed `speak` never schedules a hangup at all. `sendMarkAndWait` now returns whether the carrier actually echoed the mark, so a local timeout is reported as `unconfirmed` rather than passed off as confirmed playback. Notify-mode and agent hangups share one `scheduleHangupAfterPlayback` helper.

The early-delivery path is preserved: a hangup requested on an early flush is remembered and honored after the final payloads settle, and the outcome of whichever playback delivered the reply is the one the hangup uses.

Call control is never inferred from text that failed to parse: the malformed-reply fallback returns speech only.

Non-goals: no config key, no change to realtime call control, no change to the `voice_call` tool.

## User Impact

Voice agents can end a call when the conversation is finished. The closing words play first, then the line drops — no waiting out `maxDurationSeconds`, no carrier minutes burned on a finished call, and the concurrent-call slot frees immediately. Interrupting the agent's goodbye keeps the call alive, and a failed closing reply never drops the caller silently.

Backward compatible. Replies without `end_call` behave exactly as before, plain-text replies still route through the existing sanitizer, and a non-boolean `end_call` is ignored.

## Evidence

Live calls on Twilio media streams with Deepgram transcription and ElevenLabs telephony TTS, `responseModel: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.

**Normal goodbye — unconfirmed playback takes the grace, then hangs up:**

```
01:25:37 [voice-call] Transcript: nothing much i'm very sleepy so you know let's talk later
01:25:39 [voice-call] Early AI response: "Get some rest, Prince—talk later!"
01:25:43 [voice-call] Agent requested hangup for call 9d9b9955… (playback=unconfirmed)
01:25:43 [voice-call] Agent hangup: auto-hangup in 3s for call 9d9b9955…
```

**Barge-in over the closing reply — the call survives:**

```
01:27:04 [voice-call] Early AI response: "Bye bye!"
01:27:05 [voice-call] Agent requested hangup for call 7749d64c… (playback=cancelled)
01:27:05 [voice-call] Agent hangup: playback interrupted, keeping call 7749d64c… open
01:27:06 [voice-call] Transcript: wait wait wait are you here
01:27:07 [voice-call] Early AI response: "Yep, still here—what's up?"
```

The caller cut off the goodbye, the hangup was suppressed, and the conversation continued. Before this revision the same interruption ended the call.

Scope of the live runs: they exercise the `cancelled` and `unconfirmed` branches against a release build of the installed plugin, because the local install is 2026.7.1-2 while this branch targets main. That build sends the completion mark without awaiting the carrier echo, so it cannot produce `confirmed`; the immediate-hangup branch is covered by tests rather than by these traces. An earlier trace on the pre-review revision showed the agent ending a call after its closing words played.

**Tests** — `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 736 passed (64 files), 13 of them new.

- `response-generator.test.ts` — hangup request, absent and explicit-false replies, non-boolean ignored, fenced JSON, hangup with no closing words, contract reaches the prompt, and an `end_call` inside a reply that never parsed as JSON is ignored.
- `manager.agent-hangup.test.ts` — immediate hangup on `confirmed`, grace on `unconfirmed` (fake timers assert nothing fires early), no hangup on `cancelled` even after 60s, and a no-op for an already-ended call.
- `webhook.test.ts` — the observed outcome reaches the hangup, a failed final playback schedules nothing, and a barge-in is forwarded as `cancelled`.
- `media-stream.playback-marks.test.ts` — an echoed mark resolves `true`, an unechoed one resolves `false` after the timeout.

**Checks** — `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` both pass clean.

**Production LOC** — +265 / -78 across the branch including tests; the production delta stays small because the notify-mode consolidation and the removed capability offset the new outcome plumbing.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add graph-aware retention benchmark
prs.body:
Related: #137611

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw has no read-only way to compare the canonical session-retention order with relationship-aware alternatives on production-shaped SQLite metadata. This PR adds a measurement-only benchmark; it does not change production retention or cleanup policy.

The projection preserves `parent_session_key` and `spawned_by` independently when both are present and refer to different ownership groups. It uses the read-only database owner, loads no archive payload, and leaves the schema and store contents unchanged.

## Scope and limitations

- Reuses the canonical maintenance planner's eligibility and indivisible ownership groups.
- Projects bounded metadata from isolated disposable SQLite fixtures.
- Compares existing order, least-recently-active, size-first, graph-aware, and graph-aware-balanced policies.
- Makes no production cleanup-order, eligibility, archive-provenance, schema, or operator-state change.
- Synthetic scores are not empirical future-resumption outcomes, ground truth, a rollout recommendation, or evidence of FAGR equivalence.
- The benchmark result does not establish that the graph formula should ship. The spawn-tree workload where graph-aware loses is intentionally preserved.

Proposal #137611 is the separate governance path for deciding whether an outcome-validation experiment should be sponsored.

## Evidence

### Current candidate

Exact head: `e2ba29e29296b9f11020ff122b18d9f90ffc733d`

The late parser defect is fixed by using the shared strict SQLite benchmark parser. The old entrypoint accepted `--mode smoke --typo` and exited 0; the regression now requires an unknown-argument error and exit 2 before fixture construction or database work. Coverage includes defaults, smoke/default modes, invalid or missing values, duplicate and equivalent-duplicate mode syntax, unknown long options, positional arguments, and supported equals syntax.

The SQLite regression records both schema version and a logical store fingerprint before and after projection, while separately proving distinct historical parent and spawner relationships. Both remain unchanged after the read-only projection.

### Refreshed benchmark results

`pnpm sessions:retention:benchmark --mode smoke` — passed (exit 0).

`pnpm sessions:retention:benchmark --mode default` — passed (exit 0), 5 workloads × 5 policies. Synthetic evaluator values (`existing-order` → `graph-aware`):

- isolated stale bulk: `79.6896 → 80.2112`
- fork fan-out: `58.6894 → 60.5180`
- generation chain: `73.4577 → 74.6903`
- spawn tree: `67.3563 → 60.5568`
- mixed disk pressure: `35.5690 → 39.6483`

These are synthetic measurements, not observed recovery outcomes.

### Validation

The passing local results below were recorded before the final current-main merge. Current main changed stale durable-session maintenance from deletion to in-place archival; the final candidate updates benchmark deletion candidates to use the canonical disposable subagent key shape. Exact-head GitHub CI run `34420986603` validated that adaptation: 162 jobs passed and none failed.

- Focused session-retention tests: 3 files, 27 tests passed (exit 0).
- Smoke benchmark: passed (exit 0).
- Default benchmark: passed (exit 0).
- `pnpm docs:list`: passed (exit 0).
- Changed-path formatting gate: passed (exit 0).
- Fast analyzer on all changed TypeScript files: passed (exit 0).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed (exit 0) with `GOMEMLIMIT=3GiB`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed (exit 0).
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`: passed (exit 0).
- Independent repository guards: 19/20 passed. The remaining Plugin SDK boundary CI guard reports an existing time-expired exception (`sdk-untrusted-context-identifier-aliases`, expiry 2026-09-08); this PR changes no Plugin SDK boundary files.
- `git diff --check`: passed (exit 0).

Validation limitations are reported separately from code failures:

- `pnpm tsgo:test:root` exited 1 because this sparse checkout excludes tracked Android/live-updater modules and lacks an upstream QA fixture; no task-file diagnostic was emitted.
- The changed-file planner reached the package-lock guard, then refused the Windows Node 24 runtime because it has no colocated npm and would not use the mismatched system npm.
- Broad type-aware core/scripts lint exceeded the repository's 900-second/interactive resource window without a diagnostic. File-scoped analysis passed.
- Dead-code analysis could not load the full-tree resolver and its fallback exhausted host memory; it produced no task-code finding.
- Repository autoreview prepared and secret-scanned the complete `upstream/main...HEAD` candidate, but correctly refused to launch because it could not safely isolate the desktop's refreshed Codex credentials. That security control was not bypassed.

All benchmark fixtures use isolated temporary state. No providers, paid APIs, external services, operator state, or archive payloads are used.

prs.title: fix(irc): preserve message spacing and release displaced reconnect sockets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two IRC channel delivery defects:

1. Long outbound messages lose separator spaces at chunk boundaries. `sendPrivmsg` trimmed each chunk and then sliced the remainder by the trimmed length, so whitespace between chunks (indentation, code blocks, doubled spaces) was silently collapsed in the delivered message.
2. An overlapping reconnect can leave a displaced socket connected under the same nick, and a stale socket's later disconnect can tear down the healthy active connection: the `onDisconnect` handler unconditionally nulled `client` and scheduled a reconnect even when the closing socket was no longer the active one.

## User Impact

User impact: IRC recipients get readable, correctly spaced replies (multi-space runs and indentation preserved across 512-byte chunks), and flaky connections no longer risk a lingering duplicate connection under the bot's nick or a spurious reconnect that interrupts a healthy session.

## Why This Change Was Made

- In `sendPrivmsg`, slice the remainder by the trimmed chunk length so whitespace trimmed off a chunk tail stays in `remaining` as the next chunk's leading space, instead of being dropped by trimming both sides.
- In the monitor, `onDisconnect` now ignores a closing socket whose connection epoch no longer matches the active epoch, and `connect` closes a displaced socket it replaces (and retries when a freshly built connection drops before it activates) so no socket is orphaned and the active client is never nulled by a stale disconnect.
- Guarantee forward progress on whitespace-only chunks: `takeIrcPrivmsgChunk` no longer returns an empty prefix when a leading space is its preferred split point, and the send loop carries whitespace-only chunks forward as the leading space of the next non-empty chunk instead of sending an empty `PRIVMSG` and stalling forever.

## Evidence

- New regression test `terminates on whitespace-only chunks and preserves interior space runs`: with `messageChunkMaxChars: 1`, sending `"a  b"` completes, preserves both interior spaces byte-for-byte, and emits no empty `PRIVMSG` body (this hangs on the previous code by repeatedly sending an empty payload).
- New regression test `preserves interior runs of spaces when chunking long text`: `"aaaa bbbb  cccc dddd"` with a low char cap round-trips byte-for-byte through chunking (this fails on the previous code, which delivered `"aaaa bbbb cccc dddd"`).
- Updated `still prefers a nearby space when splitting long PRIVMSG text` to the corrected, space-preserving output `["alpha beta", " gamma"]`.
- Real-loopback monitor coverage (TCP, not mocks): `reconnects when an established IRC socket closes` drops an established socket, then destroys the replacement connection before it activates (`USER` never answered), and asserts the monitor retries and reaches a third ready connection with lifecycle `["ready", "recovering", "recovering", "ready"]` — exercising both the epoch-guarded stale disconnect and the drop-before-activation retry.
- `extensions/irc` suite: 178 passed / 3 skipped (the only failing file is `runtime-api.test.ts`, an environment subprocess-timeout unrelated to this change).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## Follow-up on re-review (Revision 7: relay-prefix budget + deterministic recovery test)

ClawSweeper's Revision-7 review confirmed no code findings on the previous head and raised two actionable items, both now fixed on `038c21cb685`:

- **Reserve the server relay prefix in the shared byte budget (P2 / merge-risk).** The whitespace-carry path could build a body that fit the client's own 512-byte line but exceeded the server's relayed-line limit once the `:nick!user@host ` prefix was prepended (e.g. 501 -> 520 bytes for `#general`), so a server could reject or truncate the newly combined chunk. The byte budget now reserves the worst-case relay prefix (`~` + USERLEN 10, HOSTLEN 63), coordinating with the same reservation in #159730. All chunking assertions now measure the **relayed** line (`RELAY_PREFIX + PRIVMSG #general :<body>\r\n`) rather than the outgoing line, which is direct recipient-side relay evidence: every chunking case, the 600-space run, and the mixed-whitespace case keep each relayed line at or under 512 bytes while preserving exact byte-for-byte content.
- **Await recovery after the replacement actually disconnects (P2).** The ready-then-drop monitor test previously resolved on the second `ready` patch, which fired before the fixture's timer destroyed the replacement, so the `connectionCount` assertion ran while the socket was still open. The fixture now drops the replacement through an explicit gate (`dropReadyReplacement()`), the test observes the socket close (`readyReplacementClosed`) and awaits the recovered (third `ready`) connection instead of the second-ready signal, then asserts `connectionCount >= 3` and a `ready -> ... -> ready` lifecycle with `recovering` in between.

Verified locally with node 24.16.0:
- `extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts`: 23/23 pass (all relayed-line assertions at or under 512).
- Full IRC suite: 143 passed / 3 skipped across 16/17 files; the only failure is the pre-existing `runtime-api.test.ts` subprocess timeout (environmental, unrelated).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: exit 0; oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- The `monitor.test.ts` database-workers shard cannot run green on this machine because a machine-wide Windows sqlite lock (`EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink ...openclaw.sqlite`) breaks cleanup for all monitor tests here, including unmodified ones; the new test's assertions pass before that cleanup error. This is the same environment limitation documented for the monitor evidence in prior rounds.

## Follow-up on re-review (Revision 8: recipient-side relay delivery + displaced-socket observations)

ClawSweeper's Revision-8 review (head `038c21cb685`) found no code findings and raised two evidence items, both now addressed on `905ca46c116`:

- **Recipient-side relay delivery (P1).** The prior relay evidence was a budget assertion over a locally constructed prefix; the fixture did not relay messages and had no receiving IRC client. The test now runs a real relay: the loopback server forwards every bot `PRIVMSG` to a separate receiving IRC client connection, prefixing each line with the sender's `nick!user@host` (worst-case USERLEN/HOSTLEN), and the test reads what that receiving client actually parsed. New `irc client PRIVMSG recipient-side relay` cases (`a` + 600 spaces + `b`, NBSP + 600 spaces, and 900 CJK code points) assert the receiving client reconstructs `bodies.join("") === text` byte-for-byte, that every received wire line is at or under 512 bytes, and that no lone surrogates are emitted.
- **Displaced-socket observations (P1).** The reconnect tests now assert socket-level facts: after a ready replacement is dropped and the monitor recovers, `openSocketCount() === 1` (the displaced sockets were closed; no lingering connection under the same nick) and the active socket `destroyed === false`. The multi-account test additionally observes the stopped account's socket `close` while the sibling account keeps the same live, non-destroyed socket (`betaSocket.destroyed === false`) — displacement closes the old connection without disrupting the active one.

Design note on activation-pending coverage: `ingress.pause()` resolves as soon as the pump returns from `drainOnce`, and the drain starts dispatches without awaiting them, so the `await ingressPause` activation window is effectively immediate on a healthy machine — a replacement always reaches the `ready` patch before any server-side drop can land. The displaced-close (`connect` closing `client !== nextClient`) and drop-before-activation retry branches are defensive against a race the single-flight reconnect timer plus the `onDisconnect` epoch guard already prevent; the reachable equivalents are covered by the socket observations above and the existing `ready -> recovering -> ... -> ready` lifecycle assertions.

Verified locally with node 24.16.0:
- `extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts`: 26/26 pass (23 existing + 3 recipient-side relay).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: exit 0; oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- `monitor.test.ts` database-workers shard: the ready-then-drop test passes with the new socket assertions (`openSocketCount() === 1`, active `destroyed === false`). The two DB-dependent reconnect tests intermittently time out on this machine under the known Windows sqlite `EBUSY` lock (machine-wide; also fails unmodified tests) and are unchanged in this revision.

prs.title: refactor(worker): reuse prepared launch and inference inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker launches revalidate an already-normalized plan, and inference paths make redundant copies or recompute constant credential spellings.

## User Impact

No intended behavior or protocol change. The child still validates the full launch descriptor, the RPC client still owns the immutable replay snapshot, and native output still checks the same raw and escaped credential bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the intermediate launch-completion wrapper and let the supervisor consume the plan it just validated. Keep the parser at the child/CLI boundary. Use the RPC client's synchronous snapshot instead of cloning context/options in the stream adapter; let native publish own the terminal clone. Prepare credential spellings once per native runtime and clear them at close.

Production delta: **+30 / -37 = -7 LOC** across five files. Direct tests were migrated to the retained parser; no assertions were weakened.

## Evidence

Exact head `7d3f58c4f4696dd54bd59d6b1fab81067bb24925` on one AWS Linux lease (Node 24): **211 tests passed** across 13 files, including nine actual child-process worker scenarios using a deterministic HTTP provider. The full core production typecheck and scoped production lint passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 issue.

The focused worker group (`native-runtime`, `native-inference-stream`, `inference-stream.runtime`, RPC clients, launch descriptor and native-worker integration) passed 109 tests in 90.34 s wall. The process proof covers local tools, durable transcript commit, cancellation, workspace/model rejection, and fencing. It is synthetic provider proof, not a paid live-model sample.

Changed caller file wall times (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`):

| File | Tests | Wall seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `worker-turn-execution.test.ts` | 36 | 249.09 |
| `worker-turn-launcher-claim-admission.test.ts` | 13 | 96.46 |

prs.title: fix(media): avoid false failures for queued generation results
prs.body:
Fixes #151964.

## What Problem This Solves

Generated media can be marked blocked after 120 seconds even when the durable session queue already owns its completion. In an isolated cron turn, retaining the requesting turn's wait can also retain the exact session lane needed by that completion: the image has finished, but the completion cannot run after the requester's model reply is released.

## User Impact

Confirmed queue admission now keeps the native operation running until real delivery settles and releases the cron completion wait. It does not report queued work as delivered. Genuine permanent failure, unconfirmed handoff deadlines and existing retention handling remain intact. The shared path covers image, music and video tasks, successful generation and provider-error completion.

**Known inherited limitation:** a delayed outgoing-media URL may return HTTP404 after exact cron alias cleanup. The final exact-head probe records this failure. This PR repairs queue custody, false failure and continuation waiting; it does not claim that retained media URL lifetime, real channel transport or the complete five-check image-download probe passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep durable admission and final settlement with their canonical owners. `wakeMediaGenerationTaskCompletion` distinguishes `session_queued` from an unconfirmed pending handoff. The existing native operation carries one internal `completionDelivery: "queued"` fact. Its retry loop applies the 120-second budget only before confirmed custody and continues observing the existing idempotent queue receipt afterward. Cron task waiting stops holding its lane only after this explicit fact; delivery or permanent failure still owns the operation's terminal outcome.

The repair replaces obsolete branch logic with current-main owners rather than recreating the old task APIs or adding a second queue. No new public task status, configuration, environment variable, protocol, SDK, database schema, lockfile or generated assets.

Owner map: native media tool → `media-generate-background-completion.ts` → existing durable announce/session queue → Gateway continuation runner → committed transcript. Cron admission/wait lives in `attempt-async-tasks.ts`; stream preparation and settlement share that wait. Existing scheduler scope, admission fences, abort/deadline rules, queue idempotency, requester identity and cleanup owners remain intact.

Existing-solutions preflight: another image/provider plugin cannot change OpenClaw's native operation and requesting-lane ownership. The maintainer's real Gateway observation in [the September 25 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154064#issuecomment-5833541464) identifies the unresolved continuation path; the actual compiled Gateway path below exercises that path without replacing its delivery adapter.

Seven-file diff against canonical main `278d66f2459a088cd6c770a92fe30a2fa48cc226`: four production files **+32/-11, net +21**; three existing tests **+85/-2, net +83**. The small production increase carries explicit custody across the existing operation and cron owners, avoiding false terminal outcomes and a circular wait. The seventh file updates the Gateway sibling expectation after successful queue custody; its actual SQLite, requester binding and lifecycle-fence assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

### Current exact-head acceptance and limits

Current contributor head is `0e00ee3d838952d0e20bd165a0fd29b9d40003f3`, tree `7a5fad5bcb88675f47fcf2e7b3e54408543ef63f`, parent `6b88940dfd53dec5f0e8505da673292334e77088`. Both author and committer use Leon's company identity. All four production files are byte-identical to that parent; the only follow-up change is the existing Gateway test's `pending`→`queued` expectation.

The actual current commit was rebuilt with the same canonical private QA runtime command, exit0, **166.44 seconds wall**. CLI/version, build-info and native stamps identify the current head with clean inputs. The unchanged harness below was then executed against this actual built head, **172.74 seconds wall**:

```sh
MEDIA_PROOF_CHECKOUT=./154064-custody-fix node --import ./validation-main/scripts/tsx.mjs 154064-gateway-spike.mts --held
```

It held the original model requester **125,341ms**. At120seconds the native operation remained running with queued custody. On release, the real completion model request started **2,656ms** later; exactly one image provider call, one assistant attachment and one completed SQLite queue row/retry0 were observed. Native operation succeeded and original cron completed ok. Committed false failure messages, blocked operations, duplicate image calls, duplicate attachments and failed queue rows were all0. This is acceptance-green for the stated custody/continuation/false-failure repair, paired with the identical frozen-main RED below.

The independent download control still returned **HTTP404/9bytes**, matching frozen main. Current full probe is **4/5, PARTIAL**, not all-five PASS. The unchanged all-five assertion fails; no image-download, permanent-URL, external-channel or restart claim is made. The successful harness exit is separate from this known failing control.

Current raw receipt SHA-256: `43542fc2b9f01727fd3045c77a6ed302da59f3aa10298f17d72dd3af69d52d86`; sanitized summary: `9128b424109dcf3efed18a56e3a01dd301acc956d4e288d2ce311f4bbe1f899d`; evidence manifest digest: `40cafad6e898f5f5494736ec06c45b2b651a075c2d9501b4d976dd6b3ac1f01a`. Source/build head, source tree and tracked cleanliness match before and after the real scenario. The current summary below provides the public readback; the complete unchanged harness and prior paired evidence remain further below.

- Candidate head: `6b88940dfd53dec5f0e8505da673292334e77088`; reviewed tree `766116f1e658af9de090e4b186d0cc306810675f`. Normal merge parents are canonical main `278d66f2459a088cd6c770a92fe30a2fa48cc226` and the previous contributor head `2d1ec3dd57dbea1f7f928d1bae44df217672b40a`.

prs.title: fix(agents): retire warm CLI sessions before manual compaction
prs.body:
## What problem does this solve?

Manual native CLI compaction starts a one-shot process without attaching the existing warm process to that run. Cleanup at the end therefore cannot retire the warm process, which can keep using stale conversation state after persisted history changes.

Fixes #157483.

## User impact

The next turn after manual compaction starts from the compacted history instead of reusing the previous warm process. Ordinary turns and other session owners keep their processes.

## Why this approach?

Retire the exact owner's warm session inside the existing serialized CLI queue, before the one-shot compactor starts. The existing restart helper waits for cleanup and rechecks current authority. End-of-turn cleanup stays bound to the process created by that turn, preserving successor ownership.

## Evidence

Passed in [isolated validation](https://github.com/deepujain/openclaw/actions/runs/36077242249) at `052cc590865fbeaca9c44abee84a1435936aa6ea`:

- Baseline: the new compact case fails on unchanged production code because the warm process was not closed; ordinary and revoked controls pass.
- Fixed: 106 tests pass across the CLI spawn, live-session registry and native compaction suites.
- Core types, agent test types, changed-file lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The tested tree `a4bbe62ff91bb0de6f52a34d2c515a090d5b4458` exactly matches the signed branch.

Independent source review and scoped P0-P2 autoreview found no actionable findings. The regression exercises the production execution queue and live-session registry with a mocked process handle, including compact, ordinary and revoked callers and an unrelated owner. It does not run a real Claude CLI or prove persisted transcript behavior with a live model.

This remains an unmerged draft; the required third integration, reduced-head push, remaining validation, and landing were not completed.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible change. Features, authorization, lifecycle ordering, persisted state, and public contracts are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared private helpers replace repeated approval operations, worker-environment transport/validation/provisioning operations, and UI connection/resource bookkeeping. Pure rendering stays with its owning UI surface. This combines three previously below-threshold branches into one change.

## Evidence

Stopped: the owned runtime campaign was cancelled after the size threshold was crossed. Hosted CI and full runtime qualification are incomplete; this draft is not ready to merge.

Candidate: `d88473051bf96192241d9a3dc960c797c5631a65`; base: `a825abb1fae404fd186ab65cb427019f0f9b4d9c`. The final follow-up changes only the recovery test fixture; UI, SDK, and production inputs are identical to the previously reviewed `c47c34ab7f51aed1b9b37025e32aaf4cc1782ef6` tree.

- Full-diff independent review through P2 and the separate recovery-fixture review are clean. The candidate commit has a verified Peter Steinberger signature.
- All 21 retained visual states are pixel-identical between this base and candidate. Every capture is repeat-identical and has no page errors. Meeting Capture and Session Storage use the shared helper's explicit same-target centering; natural smooth-scroll timing is not claimed identical. Captures contain synthetic fixtures only.
- Focused final UI proof covers 232 unique cases across 12 files. The corrected Custodian renderer passes all 29 cases; the other 11 files passed 203 cases. UI types pass. Earlier changed-file proof covered all 124 unique cases, including explicitly enabled Chromium memory coverage; that is prior-head evidence.
- Final-base/final-candidate qualification exercised all nine historical UI gap files six times in A-B-B-A-A-B order: 109 distinct cases, 654 executions, equal pass counts, and every command exited zero. Composer recovery retains the same eight ResizeObserver browser errors in every run. Timing qualification is mixed and remains explicitly pending; a passing replay is not called a fix.
- The current Lit migration ratchet passes without changing its baseline. The original attachment-button consolidation is dropped to preserve baseline template identity without another directive import.
- The refreshed selected changed-check plan completed: 44 of 48 commands passed. The four nonzero steps are independently reproduced on clean base: environment-name budget (456 against 455), UI E2E shard-root budget (722 against 720), direct sequential Knip, and whole-core lint's unchanged 900-second deadline. Knip names four exports in three untouched files (`update-command-post-activation-inspections.ts`, `sessions-channel-fixture.test-support.ts`, and `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`). Neither budget nor those files are changed by this bundle. Whole-core lint did not complete on either revision and is not claimed green; direct lint of all 49 changed core files passes. Core/core-test/UI types, runtime cycles (zero), Madge cycles (zero), UI lint/styles, storage guards, the macOS contract lane, and final lint-suppression tests pass.
- Both refreshed plugin SDK renders passed. The comparison has zero direct signature changes, no added/removed entrypoints, and 148 reachable-only changes from three unique declarations: an optional workspace-ID callback parameter and two internal helpers. Candidate rendering used `d0070dc83def36fd1a700e19fa67cd3c13c70aca`; its SDK/core/package/config/tooling inputs are unchanged in the UI-only follow-up to the final candidate. No method/property variance drift remains.
- The isolated AWS comparison used independent base/head Git checkouts, Node 26.5.0, one recorded warmup and seven measured runs per side. Completed metrics, retention, undo/redo, preview, and pane-identity groups have equal passing counts and closely matched timings. The campaign was stopped after detecting the below-threshold main-wins resolution; remaining full-directory coverage and hosted CI attribution are incomplete. Raw logs were streamed with hashes before lease shutdown.

### Recovery fixture repair

The broad Gateway sweep exposed a real fixture-lifetime race. Recovery acknowledges a started continuation before dispatch and independent dashboard-title work have settled. The test registered global singleton drain after its harness; reverse `afterEach` order therefore closed shared database owners before the harness joined accepted work. A stage trace reproduced post-dispatch finalization overlapping global drain, an unreleased `chat-send:background` root, title settlement crossing into the next case, then database-identity and closed-admission failures.

The repair registers global drain before harness setup, so settlement runs first, and replaces only incidental label-model generation with a deterministic fixture. Dispatch, title scheduling/persistence, root ownership, identity, authorization, and recovery assertions remain real. A reorder-only trial passed four of six identity cases but exposed unrelated real title-generation latency in two; the combined fixture repair passed all six with zero roots before global drain. Temporary diagnostics were then removed. The normal full recovery file and dedicated title-preparation tests passed all 27 cases (814.83 seconds native; 838.57 seconds wrapper). Independent P0–P2 review of the fixture repair is clean. The incremental changed-check continuation completed 27 commands: 24 passed, with the same baseline environment budget, UI E2E root budget, and Knip findings noted above. No assertion, timeout, retry, skip, or budget was altered.

## Coverage log — 500–999-line exception

The published candidate removes **515 net production lines** across 101 production files (+1431/-1946) against its recorded base. The main-wins resolution against `83b5f5425eab6021ff03104c9de1b4826f0c3d97` leaves **477** across 100 production files (+1401/-1878), so it is below the campaign threshold. This resolution was measured in a private merge-preview tree (`9a3bb98c4cf87ffbc6491e2fd49d0ad34525e7b1`), not pushed. Ten test/support files change by +134/-75 (net +59), excluded from that count. No changelog, dependency, protocol, schema, timeout, retry, skip, baseline, budget, or suppression changes are included.

Applied in order:

| Input | Scope | Original reduction | Retained reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| d30-p2 at 3e90b8c1c2b | Gateway top-level approvals, nodes, accounts, sessions, delivery | 154 | 141 |
| d40 at b1aec6e82a2 | Worker-environment transports, validation, provisioning, mutations | 106 | 95 |
| d34 at ba65f1fedb9 | UI pages a–l, resources, connection/recovery, rendering | 278 | 274 |
| Post-rebase Lit-owner consolidation | Fewer rendering modules and direct framework dependencies | — | 5 |
| **Total** | | **538** | **515** |

Dropped changes:

- d40's complete `src/gateway/worker-environments/store.ts` change (2 net lines): main replaced publication with authoritative receipt installation.
- d40's `placement-turn-claims-store.ts` extraction (9 net lines): converting methods to function-valued properties changes TypeScript parameter variance; a compiler counterexample proved the difference.
- d30's complete `server-node-events.ts` change (13 net lines): main replaced that module's source/authority ownership and extracted its helpers.
- d34's `chat-message-attachment-status.ts` button consolidation (4 net lines): preserve the original distinct templates rather than add a Lit directive under the current migration ratchet.

Two conflict-only integrations preserved main's behavior. The latest conflict keeps main's reasoning cleanup inside the consolidated local-run cleanup block. Clean automatic merges retain main's session authorization, model policy, chat gateway and page-state changes. No superseded main behavior was restored.

### Retention timeout qualification

The final isolated comparison passed all 11 activity-file tests in every measured run (seven clean-main and seven candidate runs), with no errors or remaining owned children. Native whole-file medians were 4.63 seconds on main and 4.62 seconds on the candidate (-0.2%); outer command medians were 6.593/6.544 seconds (-0.7%). Both warmups also passed. All 16 original logs have been recovered locally and their streamed hashes verified. This satisfies the requested equal-count/~5% file-median parity rule; it is not a claim that a passing replay repaired a product defect.

The earlier shared-host comparison is retained separately: six runs passed all 11 tests, but its individual answer-candidate case varied by +17.5% under concurrent host load. Those per-case timings are not relabeled as isolated parity.

The current base/candidate comparison finds all 58 behavior/test closure files and all 104 resolver/tooling/config/package inputs byte-identical, with no bundle overlap. The original d34 base/head likewise has all 58 behavior files and 76 resolver inputs identical; no original d34 retention-path hunk exists to drop. The actual test and spawned subprocess root are included. The historical failure was the child's 20-second wall-clock `spawnSync` deadline before retention assertions, not a failed retained-heap or preview assertion. This establishes the boundary and source independence, not the exact historical scheduler cause. No timeout or assertion was weakened.

No landing attempted. The draft is conflicting and below the size threshold after the required main-wins resolution. Full runtime and hosted CI gates remain incomplete; no cancelled job or partial run is claimed as passing proof.

prs.title: fix(channels): dispatch replies in ACP-bound conversations
prs.body:
Related: #146365

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text follow-ups in Discord and Matrix conversations bound to a spawned ACP session can fail with `prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published` when the harness is not a configured Gateway agent.

## User Impact

Text follow-ups retain the configured channel agent for reply-runtime admission while ACP execution, session storage, and transcript identity keep the bound harness target. No configuration or stored-data migration is introduced.

Native Discord slash commands remain outside this change, so this PR does not close the broader issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Conversation bindings rewrite the routed agent and session to the ACP target. The optional reply-dispatch owner preserves the configured source agent across the Discord and Matrix inbound-context builders. The refreshed implementation retains current main's route-observation symbols, asynchronous binding activity checks, and revoked-binding revalidation. Callers that omit the field retain the previous source-session fallback.

AI-assisted: yes. The refreshed code and sanitized local evidence were independently reviewed.

## Evidence

- Refreshed onto main `fd2fa6b904a2069bf9c2c150302475dffdc51e29` to incorporate upstream fixes for both prior CI roots: restored script lint directives (`392166d0`) and the prepared-catalog import-cycle repair (`80bfd0f5`).
- ACP production behavior is unchanged from the reviewed repair (+20/-3 lines). The refresh preserves upstream runtime-lease propagation and disposal; the relocated two-case regression now retains the upstream `onRuntimeLease` assertion. Optional-owner fallback, binding observations/revalidation, and harness-scoped execution/storage remain covered.
- On the refreshed tree `0159e2b0ee280f9f1102e4eb4c1be2f80e986767`, 188 tests in ten files passed in 202.278 seconds total command wall, including cold worker preparation. These cover dispatch ownership/lifecycle, binding activity and revocation, shared context/routing, Discord preflight/context/binding, and Matrix routing/binding observation.
- Native runtime-import and Madge checks passed with zero cycles (25.609s and 25.537s). The canonical full scripts lint owner passed (47.243s), directly exercising the scope that failed in CI. An initial single-file lint probe reported the restored directives unused; that narrower Program is not the CI scope, and its result is retained in the diagnostics.
- Canonical messaging and plugin-SDK test type graphs passed (144.523s combined). Conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety and formatting checks passed; changed-core type-aware lint passed.
- Independent native review and fresh canonical AutoReview were scoped-clean at P0–P2. The earlier red control (removing only the owner override) remains historical evidence of the same owner-selection defect; it was not rerun on this refreshed base.
- The complete native changed aggregate and a new extension-wide type/lint sweep were not rerun for this refresh. Earlier local scoped extension checks belong to the prior tested base. The completed hosted CI below is separate evidence and does not relabel the unrun local aggregate.
- Source composition with subsequently observed main `447144510b899463ee89774b62d015631d3bd891` is clean and preserves the exact main-relative ACP patch. Local runtime/type results belong to pinned `fd2fa6b9`, not that later composition.

Live proof remains outstanding: the dispatch regression mocks runtime publication, ACP execution and delivery; it does not establish real runtime-lease acquisition or configured-owner admission followed by real harness execution and receipt in Discord or Matrix. Before merge, provide current-candidate after-fix channel/harness evidence plus unauthorized-sender and removed/reassigned-binding rejection before ACP I/O. Existing local negative controls do not establish the full cross-owner channel path.

### Publication and prior CI/review

- Current published head: `a9c6c0551fcc68851d3bbf795af3aedb792b8c2a`, one commit on tested `fd2fa6b9`, exact tree `0159e2b0ee280f9f1102e4eb4c1be2f80e986767`. [Exact-head CI 37886818337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37886818337) completed successfully: 55 successful jobs, 25 skipped, no failures. The required `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and applicable security-review statuses are success. Hosted architecture and full lint both passed, clearing the two previous CI roots.
- [Prior-head CI 37877414792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877414792) on `eaabfe1` finished with 52 successful and 25 skipped jobs, two root failures and the failed aggregate. Madge matched a [failing main control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37868734021/job/113621794431); the [script lint failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877414792/job/113649619465) was attributed by source comparison to newer-main removal of the directives, without a matching failed-main runtime claim. The refreshed executed checks above now pass both failing scopes.
- The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149801#issuecomment-5693135353) at `a9c6c055` found no concrete introduced bypass or actionable code defect, and removed the compatibility risk label. It lists two remaining checklist items: real channel/harness behavior proof and a medium security concern that cross-owner unauthorized-sender or removed/reassigned-binding denial lacks final-effect evidence before real ACP I/O. Both remain open; green CI does not satisfy this proof requirement.

prs.title: refactor(ai): type the streamed tool-call argument buffer once
prs.body:
Related: #168614

## What Problem This Solves

Streaming tool-call producers attach an in-flight argument buffer (`partialJson`) to tool-call blocks, but the field was never part of any type. Every producer re-declared it through casts such as `delete (block as { partialJson?: string }).partialJson` or `ToolCall & { partialJson: string }`, so the contract lived in 20+ scattered assertions instead of one place.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers get one documented owner for the streaming buffer, and the type checker now verifies every producer's set/append/delete instead of trusting casts.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ToolCall` in `packages/llm-core` (re-exported by `@openclaw/ai` and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/llm`) gains an optional, documented `partialJson?: string`. It is the block type the partial `AssistantMessage` in stream events already carries, so producers and the consumers that read the live buffer now share one declaration. Every producer cast and local re-declaration is removed: in packages/ai providers and transports, the Bedrock, Radius and OpenCode plugins, and the worker/proxy stream reconstruction.

Behavior stays identical. The buffer is set, appended, parsed and deleted at the same points, and it is never left on final messages or transcripts:

- Cleanup loops over mixed content now delete the field only from tool-call blocks, the only blocks that carry it.
- Bedrock and Anthropic error cleanup no longer delete it, because those loops run right after `output.content` is filtered to drop tool calls (the delete was dead).
- Worker, proxy and Radius appends use `(block.partialJson ?? "") + delta` instead of `+=` through a required-field cast. Start always initializes `""`, so every reachable path behaves the same.

I chose the optional field on the existing type over a new exported `StreamingToolCall` alias. The alias would add plugin-SDK surface and still need casts wherever code iterates `output.content`. The tradeoff is that the type also allows the field on finished messages; the doc comment states the lifecycle, and transcript repair and display sanitizing already strip it as a backstop. Two local narrowings that encode an "initialized buffer" invariant for `+=` stay (`ToolCallBlock` in the completions stream, `StreamingToolCallBlock` in the Responses stream), because converting them would add code.

Production code is net negative (about -15 lines), and the assertion-safety baseline shrinks by 13 assertions across 9 files.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/ai/src/transports packages/ai/src/provider-transport-parity.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers extensions/amazon-bedrock extensions/radius extensions/opencode packages/tool-call-repair src/worker/inference-stream.runtime.test.ts src/worker/native-inference-stream.test.ts src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts`: 145 files, 2,390 tests passed (835s wall locally).
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: passed, output identical to baseline (368 entrypoints, 7,013 exports, no surface change).
- `pnpm tsgo` / `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: only `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts` TS6133, which is pre-existing on main and not touched here.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0-P2): scoped-clean, "patch is correct".
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (local, rebased on 0fc11d74d3e): conflict markers, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety (pruned, shrink-only), SQLite, typecheck, coercion, and deprecated-API checks all pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts` and `ui/src/components/settings-controls.ts`, both untouched here and both reproduced on clean `origin/main` at the same base.
- `pnpm test:changed`: 939 files and 8,627 tests passed. 3 files fail, all untouched here and all reproduced on clean `origin/main`: the `doctor-session-canonical-keys.scale` timeout, two `codex-model-runtime-choice` assertions, and an `outbound-custody` setup timeout.
- No tests added: the change is type-only and lifecycle-preserving, and the existing transport/parity suites already assert that final blocks carry no `partialJson`.
