prs.title: perf(control-ui): restore dashboard name links before hello
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link with a display-name-only reference waits for Gateway hello before resolving the session, even when the browser already has its scoped roster and transcript. The measured campaign reload showed the header and right panel appearing at about 2.5 s, and the board document starting at 3.29 s.

## User Impact

A unique cached dashboard name now paints its title, saved split layout, cached right-panel transcript, and one board skeleton before hello. Full-ID links retain their existing warm-load behavior. Missing or ambiguous names still use authoritative resolution.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both route namespaces now use the existing cached session-reference lookup and foreground transcript scheduling. No new cache or server state is introduced. Production delta: **+5 lines** (16 added, 11 removed); the added contract is safe, scoped resolution of cached display-name references, while the chat-only scheduling distinction is removed.

Board documents still require `board.get` to issue a fresh ticket after live authority checks. The HTTP route requires that ticket and checks authority again at consumption. Starting board bytes before hello would require a separate authenticated issuance transport; this change does not persist tickets or grants.

## Evidence

- Old-code negative control: the display-name route stays on the page-wide skeleton with hello held. The same scenario passes after the fix; the first recorded content frame has its title, main-panel board skeleton and cached side-panel transcript. Full-ID and name-only dashboard cases both pass.
- Mock board document request starts about **133 ms after hello release**, with config refresh held independently. No board request is made before fresh ticket issuance.
- Injected-latency rig before → after: one document in both; hello **3649 → 3603 ms**; board request **3914 → 3865 ms** (**265 → 262 ms after hello**); widget paint **7389 → 6432 ms**; visual transitions **6 → 7**; layout jumps **3 → 2**. One sample each, with intervening main changes: this is not an isolated widget-speed claim. The rig uses a literal-key route; the name-only regression is covered by the delayed-hello browser test. Both captures lack the visible task-progress card; the after capture also lacks the target online roster, so these are not full Team-equivalent captures.
- Local focused proof after Testbox fallback: warm-route tests **14 passed** (3.01 s command / 1.18 s Vitest); route-resolution tests **30 passed**; bootstrap tests **24 passed** (10.99 s command / 9.24 s Vitest); bootstrap-location tests **13 passed**; dashboard browser cases **2 passed** (19.46 s command including bundle / 5.17 s test body). Commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`, with the UI E2E config for browser cases.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4ks1e5jhw5q96nr37v7erb4` reproduced the failing name-only case. Subsequent workspace sync failed twice at its 2-minute limit; the lease is stopped. Per campaign fallback, GitHub CI supplies changed-file checks.
- Full UI E2E on `4af452f34a09`: **731 files passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped; 3357 tests passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped** (5647.94 s). The failures were Workboard drag visibility, Workboard native-bundle card retention, QA host-command copy, roster request rate, and terminal screenshot geometry. The drag and host-copy assertions have since been repaired on main (`fab68f488caf`, `6c0df3c1d4c3`) and are included by rebase. Native Workboard retention and the roster-rate assertion reproduce on current main (`acf2ede76d21`); terminal font proof passed in isolation and its earlier screenshot timing failure remains recorded, not claimed fixed.
- The required full UI run is now in progress on **`b8018f9e1fc7`**, using two local workers under the campaign's remote-sync fallback. Its final pass/fail list will replace this pending status. Detached independent autoreview completed with no P0–P2 findings.
- Earlier CI blockers were an instrumentation lint error (fixed) and an inherited mock-export assertion (identical on main). prs.title: fix(gateway): prepare agent sessions from worker reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents API requests read SQLite synchronously on the Gateway main thread, which blocks every other client while the reads run. With concurrent turns, remote instrumentation of the Gateway main isolate traced two paths:
- `agent → prepareAgentRequestRouting → respondUnavailableAgentSessionForKey → loadGatewaySessionEntry → row/participant SQL`, at `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-handler-helpers.ts:104`;
- `prepareAgentSession → loadGatewaySessionEntry → SQL`, at `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts:65,84`.

Root `AGENTS.md` says database access runs in worker threads and never on the Gateway main thread, and that legacy main-thread access is migrated when touched. These reads go back to `6df0fb818d6`. `b8b094b57a1` kept the initial read and added a post-await read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Routing and preparation now use the existing worker reader, `loadGatewaySessionEntryReadOnlyInWorker`. Preparation also needs whether the transcript physically exists and the mutation timestamp. Those facts come from one new bounded metadata selection on the existing transcript read worker. This avoids the transcript statistics reader, whose size-dependent scans `945370229d5` deliberately removed.

The prepared row and facts are carried forward instead of re-read. The mutation owner's current-row/authority check stays at the effect boundary as the single live check. There is no schema or persistence change, no new worker owner, and no extra handshake. At the final reuse decision, the rare failed-session and terminal-main paths always read fresh transcript metadata through the worker, because transcript events change independently of the session entry. Production −22 net across both commits.

## User Impact

Agents API turns no longer block the Gateway main thread on session reads, so other clients stay responsive under concurrent turns. Behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Remote main-isolate instrumentation: synchronous SQLite statements on these paths dropped from 49 to 0.
- Behavior was unchanged for concurrent turns, same-session concurrency, duplicate idempotency, archived-session rejection, and crash/restart.
- Both new regressions fail on main and pass with the change. Two more regressions append to the transcript after preparation and verify that the final reuse decision sees it. All 35 focused tests pass.
- `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times:

  | File | Wall time |
  | --- | ---: |
  | `agent-session-preparation.worker.test.ts` | 40.4 s |
  | `agent-session-reuse.test.ts` | 40.1 s |
  | `agent-session-patch.test.ts` | 49.4 s |
  | `session-accessor.sqlite-metadata-read.test.ts` | 34.1 s |

  About 21 s of each is compiled-worker preparation; the test bodies run in under 5 s.
- A remote `check-changed` run on the pre-rebase branch, which was 91 commits stale, reported line-cap growth only in files this PR does not touch, where main had grown. The changed-lane suite was not completed before the lease timeout, so required CI on this head is the remaining gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a selected agent avatar being silently discarded when you edit the name or emoji, choose an image, and click Save before image processing finishes.

prs.title: fix(exec): avoid truncated verdicts from reasoning reviewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Exec approval reviews can exhaust a reasoning model's 1,024-token completion limit before it emits the JSON verdict, forcing human approval even for an authorized local calculation.

## User Impact

Reasoning reviewers receive an automatic, bounded thinking allowance in addition to the verdict budget. Non-reasoning reviewers keep their existing budget, and requests remain clamped to the model's advertised output cap. This replaces the proposed `reviewer.maxTokens` option; no new configuration or migration is required.

The existing timeout and human-approval fallback remain unchanged. The allowance does not guarantee a verdict from every model or input, and provider-specific thinking-budget handling still applies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec reviewer now reuses the shared completion thinking-budget calculation, using the configured thinking level or a bounded medium allowance when omitted. Budget selection stays with the reviewer; schemas, labels, help text, and generated config docs retain their main-branch behavior.

Thanks @leapdragon for identifying the failure and the original fix. The contributor commit is preserved, with main merged into the branch rather than rebased. Relative to merged main: production **+16/-6** (net +10), tests **+119/-0**, docs **+2/-0**. The production growth implements automatic sizing and cap normalization without another policy table or configuration surface.

## Evidence

Live requests used native Ollama `/api/chat`, observed through a transparent loopback capture proxy. A real `pnpm openclaw ... agent` turn invoked `exec`; the reviewer then decided whether an authorized synthetic AWK calculation could run. The failing Qwen3 4B case was exercised through both the embedded CLI and a real isolated Gateway. The before/after Gateway runs kept the same configuration and prompt.

| Reviewer | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen3:4b`, thinking on | Limit 1,024; generated 1,024; `done_reason=length`; thinking only, no verdict; headless exec denied after human fallback | Limit 3,072; generated 2,239; valid low-risk `allow`; command ran and printed the expected sorted values, sum, and median |
| `qwen3:8b`, thinking on | Tested input already succeeded: limit 1,024, 265 generated tokens | Limit 3,072, 265 generated tokens; valid `allow`, command ran |
| `llama3.2:latest` | Limit 1,024; 29-token valid verdict | Same limit and identical 29-token verdict; command ran |

The reported exhaustion reproduced with **Qwen3 4B**; Qwen3 8B did not exhaust its budget on the tested inputs. Both versions used the existing `reviewer.timeoutMs: 180000` setting to isolate token truncation from latency on the shared local-model host; the default timeout remains 30 seconds.

Reproduction flow: isolated state/config and workspace, Gateway on port 19436, `pnpm openclaw --profile reviewer-budget gateway run --port 19436`, then `pnpm openclaw --profile reviewer-budget agent --agent main --session-id <unique-id> --message-file <synthetic-prompt> --thinking off --timeout 240 --json`. The main agent used `qwen2.5:7b`; only the approval reviewer used the models above. No operator state was used.

- Regression on main: **9 expected failures, 4 passes**, 64.43s wall time; reasoning returned `ask` instead of a valid verdict. Reviewer/transport source is identical between reproduction main `ea4693e04a70f5a9048a6cd4ac23f97581bf62a9` and merged main `f0a64d10805d2e7e21b4fa45235d8074a95e033d`.
- Candidate reviewer suites: **38 tests passed**, 71.44s wall time (including cold compiler preparation).
- `pnpm build`: passed, 6m33s. Scoped lint and the agents-root test typecheck passed. Prompt bytes are unchanged: token delta **0**.
- Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, database-worker, database-dialect, test-timeout, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks passed.
- Updated-head validation after merging main: core typechecking, scoped lint on every originally failing file, export-name collision guard, all required ratchets, and the registered SDK surface check passed. Reviewer suites plus SDK surface tests: **43 passed, 1 Linux-only skipped**, **55.66s** wall time.
- Codex autoreview of head `0a315cc6f847e2f9230372831c34263726a24e2d`: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. The reviewer source, test, docs, shared budget helper, and native Ollama transport are unchanged by this main merge; the live proof above remains applicable.

### CI failure classification and refresh

[Previous run 38093916507](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38093916507) tested head `80ae610482edeb7f54227dc6cf3608126ed3fc5c` merged with main `09d58be4e65092a045a0228ad983513b9fc07d07` (CI merge `343cd42e97bf4e75d64280334dbe078d8c014382`). Every failed job was inspected from its retained log. All failures reproduced independently on that exact main parent; none was caused by the reviewer-budget diff.

| Failed jobs | Inherited cause and independent baseline proof | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-test-types-core-2`, `-3`, `-4`, `-5` | Unused `env` at `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts:519`; all eight failing compiler configurations reproduced the same TS6133 on the CI main parent | Main fix `243b6dbf63d2`, merged here |
| `check-lint-core-2` | Observation-cache name shadowing and unnecessary conversion; same oxlint errors on the CI main parent | Main fix `f9940dc8a794`, merged here |
| `check-lint-core-3` | Same unused `env`; oxlint reproduces on the CI main parent | Main fix `243b6dbf63d2`, merged here |
| `check-lint-core-4` | Unbound Worker method in `sqlite-worker-plugin-comparison.test.ts`; oxlint reproduces on the CI main parent | Main fix `f9940dc8a794`, merged here |
| `check-source-contracts` | Duplicate `resolveChannelDmPolicy` export; the exact export-name guard fails on the CI main parent | Main fix `13296b17cd0f`, merged here |
| `checks-node-compact-small-5` | SDK surface accounting: baseline suite **2 failed / 3 passed / 1 Linux-only skipped**, 7.32s; the skipped test's underlying `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` independently reproduces all five budget violations in 4.96s | Main fix `f9940dc8a794`, merged here; candidate suite and registered command pass |
| `checks-node-changed-3` | `bash-tools.process.e2e.test.ts`: the same **five failures / six passes** on the CI main parent, 54.86s Vitest / 472.74s including cold E2E preparation | Still inherited: fixtures expect passive system events for nonexistent session destinations after completion delivery moved to admitted session events |
| `openclaw/ci-gate` | Aggregate of the failed job groups above | Updated-head CI now fails only for the inherited process shard |

The five remaining inherited process cases cover explicit stop/finalizer failure, post-exit finalizer failure, timeout after clean exit, quiet nonzero completion wake, and notification acknowledgement. The PR does not change those tests or their notification owners. Linux process-lifetime behavior was not exercised on macOS; its registered SDK command failure was independently reproduced instead.

Main `fab68f488caf061cf0d72e3413ee33888a54ef24` was merged normally into the contributor branch, preserving ancestry and credit; no rebase, force push, suppression, or test weakening was used. `ci:no-fail-fast` was added before this single refresh push. [Updated-head CI run 38102698936](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38102698936) completed with **41 successful jobs, 28 skipped, and only the inherited process shard plus aggregate gate failing**. Every earlier type, lint, source-contract, and SDK surface job is now successful. No PR-caused failure remains.

The remaining shard was also reproduced on this new run's exact main parent `bb7c69ddd04b01330e60489d1057d6e1e3319ad2` (CI merge `eb70dc12c40779c02ef4f5aef16b748713053c00`): **the same five assertions fail, six pass**, 42.73s Vitest / 447.94s including required E2E build preparation. The CI classification is **READY-WITH-INHERITED**; this is retained failure evidence, not a green rerun or a claim that those fixtures were repaired.

[ClawSweeper's exact-head re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150200#issuecomment-5702028724) reports no findings, no Before merge items, complete fix scope, and sufficient live proof. The separate [security-sensitive review gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38103215021) still requires a maintainer to approve the current revision. This PR has not been merged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discard waited for an outstanding write, then replaced the entire draft without checking whether the user had edited it again. The existing draft coordinator now identifies newer editing intent so an outdated discard cannot clear pending patch recovery or replace that draft. The same check protects the subsequent reload response. Existing offline, conflict, and reconnect handling remains with its current owners.

The new regression was then moved unchanged to the existing draft-revision test owner to stay within the coordinator file’s line limit; that final owner suite passed 11 tests.

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes context-capacity provenance being lost between embedded run preparation and terminal results.

## User Impact

Run results distinguish a synthetic estimate from an uncapped, model-owned capacity. Authored limits and selected context windows remain removable policy rather than trusted saved capacity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify capacity at the existing run-result producer and forward its recorded facts through terminal metadata. Depends on [budget/projection PR #138087](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138087); the Copilot synthetic marker comes from #156636.

## Evidence

Current head `d9c206ba` incorporates actual budget parent `c3d80d52`. Ten producer postimages are unchanged; the setup conflict retains all four cap/budget cases and removes only the classification assertion retired to the run-result producer. The complete setup and real-entry provenance suites pass 40 cases (345.77 seconds including normal cold E2E preparation). Production types and both complete consuming graphs pass, as do staged guards, lint, formatting, and fresh P0–P3 review. Current-head hosted CI is pending.

On original parent `84b88588`, the actual seven-case run regression fails only the synthetic-estimate case; the other six controls pass (317.41 seconds wall time). These timings include normal compiled-subprocess prerequisites. Prior-head production type checking retained only the independently reproduced main failure in `channel-presence-policy.ts:519` (unused `env`). prs.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention
prs.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  26 passed (26)
      Tests  313 passed (313)
```

New tests cover:

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.

Additional local validation:

- `npx tsc -p extensions/line/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean, exit 0
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/line` — 0 warnings/errors

- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check` / `markdownlint-cli2` / `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` — all clean on `docs/channels/line.md`
- `codex` CLI was not available in this environment, so `codex review --base origin/main` could not be run locally; noting this per CONTRIBUTING.md instead of skipping silently.

prs.title: fix(memory): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting MEMORY.md
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #168821

Short-term promotion ("dreaming") and `memory forget` rebuild `MEMORY.md` (or a `memory/*.md` file) from text decoded with replacement-mode UTF-8, then write the whole file back. One undecodable byte anywhere in the file — a Latin-1 note, a truncated paste — is persisted as U+FFFD over content the write never touched, and the promotion reports success.

The promotion/forget planning reads are lossy on purpose (they only feed ranking and LLM context). The corruption happens because the *file owner* that performs the rewrite never checks whether the bytes on disk decode cleanly before replacing them.

Precedent: issue #114895 established this rule for the `edit`/`apply_patch` tools — "they should reject the operation before writing and leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged" — enforced through `src/agents/utf8-file.ts`. The same rule was adopted for `oc-path` file edits (#168491) and `config` writes (#167118). This PR moves the same admission into the single owner every memory rewrite funnels through.

## User Impact

`openclaw memory promote --apply`, the automatic dreaming sweep, and `memory forget` now refuse to rewrite a malformed memory file instead of silently corrupting it. The refusal names the file, states it was left unchanged, and says how to recover:

```
Memory file is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: <path>. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
```

The dreaming sweep catches the refusal per workspace (`dreaming promotion failed for workspace …`), logs it, and continues with the remaining workspaces. Valid Unicode — Chinese, emoji, and an intentional U+FFFD — is unaffected, and a missing `MEMORY.md` is still created on first promotion.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commitMemoryContent` (`extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-memory-write.ts`) is the single file owner for every memory rewrite: promotion append and consolidation, `memory forget`, in-process and through the maintenance worker (`remote/memory-files-worker.ts` routes `commitContent` back into the same function). The admission lives at that choke point, before any write attempt, with a recheck in the atomic `beforeRename` hook (the window between admission and rename) and in the in-place fallback used when directory ACLs block replacement.

Read-only consumers (`readMemoryContent` callers that feed recall ranking and LLM context) keep their existing decode contract; only the mutation path is strict.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — the shipped CLI, not the file owner

Both runs use the same harness: seed one recall through the production `recordShortTermRecalls` writer, then drive the packaged command `node dist/index.js memory promote --apply` against a fully isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` whose workspace holds a `MEMORY.md` containing one undecodable `0xff` byte in an untouched note line. The two runs differ only in the build: the PR's parent commit versus this PR.

**Before — parent commit build (`memory promote --apply` reports success and corrupts the file):**

```
-- shipped command: openclaw memory promote --apply
exit code: 0
Processed 1 candidate(s) for ~/.../workspace/MEMORY.md.
appended=1 reconciledExisting=0
-- MEMORY.md sha256 BEFORE: 0cc22e725e2a48dd1eb32386a61080d1d613f86ecb4d3ac7c213105030a48a71
-- MEMORY.md bytes  BEFORE: ... 6e 6f 74 65 3a 20 61 ff 62 0a
-- MEMORY.md sha256 AFTER:  20aeff750a13c5ac44e2e13acae3d00da2502bf9c63158c13c3b39e65f17e616
-- MEMORY.md bytes  AFTER:  ... 6e 6f 74 65 3a 20 61 ef bf bd 62 0a ...
-- verdict: ORIGINAL BYTES MODIFIED (silent corruption)
```

The unrelated `61 ff 62` became `61 ef bf bd 62` (U+FFFD) and the command exited `0`.

**After — this PR:**

```
-- shipped command: openclaw memory promote --apply
exit code: 1
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Memory promote apply failed: Memory file is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: /tmp/.../workspace/MEMORY.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
[openclaw]     at async Module.runMemoryPromote (file:///ws/dist/cli.runtime-*.mjs:1066:2)
[openclaw]     at async OpenClawCommand.<anonymous> (file:///ws/dist/extensions/memory-core/cli.js:29:3)
-- MEMORY.md sha256 BEFORE: 0cc22e725e2a48dd1eb32386a61080d1d613f86ecb4d3ac7c213105030a48a71
-- MEMORY.md bytes  BEFORE: ... 6e 6f 74 65 3a 20 61 ff 62 0a
-- MEMORY.md sha256 AFTER:  0cc22e725e2a48dd1eb32386a61080d1d613f86ecb4d3ac7c213105030a48a71
-- MEMORY.md bytes  AFTER:  ... 6e 6f 74 65 3a 20 61 ff 62 0a
-- verdict: MEMORY.md byte-for-byte UNCHANGED
-- post-refusal dry run (candidate must remain unpromoted):
Store health: 1 entries · 0 promoted · 1 concept-tagged · 0 spaced · scripts=1 latin
```

Identical sha256 on both sides, the `ff` byte preserved, and the candidate is still unpromoted after the refusal.

**Valid-Unicode control (same harness, PR build, `MEMORY.md` holding a deliberate `ef bf bd` U+FFFD):**

```
exit code: 0
Processed 1 candidate(s) for ~/.../workspace/MEMORY.md.
appended=1 reconciledExisting=0
-- MEMORY.md sha256 BEFORE: d05b2093549fb187d42fbbf4b521fb0dfad1cac04b082de9936710da0f9145bd
-- MEMORY.md sha256 AFTER:  97e9ba55ab54a4e08b64ed50860bc51df8309506ccc90caa96ab944e0469de5c
-- verdict: original 44 bytes preserved, promotion appended:
```

```
## Promoted From Short-Term Memory (2026-10-10)

<!-- openclaw-memory-promotion:memory:memory/2026-10-10.md:1:1 -->
- vlan runbook verified on the lab switch [score=0.592 signals=1 recalls=1 avg=0.910 source=memory/2026-10-10.md:1-1] <!-- trigger: vlan, runbook, verified --> <!-- importance: 6 -->
```

The real U+FFFD in the original content survives byte-for-byte; only the promotion block is appended.

### Regression tests

`extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-memory-write.test.ts` gains four cases: malformed file refused with bytes preserved (atomic path), refusal before any write attempt when the parent directory is read-only, valid non-ASCII content including a literal U+FFFD merging byte-cleanly, and a missing `MEMORY.md` still being created. The valid-Unicode case is a real guard: its fixture bytes contain `ef bf bd`, so a validator that rejected every decoded U+FFFD — rather than the undecodable input — fails it.

```
$ vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-memory-write.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-store.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  107 passed | 1 skipped (108)
```

### Lint / types / ratchets

```

    extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion-memory-write.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ tsgo -p <scoped memory-core tsconfig>
✓ exit 0

prs.title: fix: Control UI Web Push notifications stay silent on macOS
prs.body:
Closes #163544

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI Web Push notifications arrive silently on macOS even when the user enabled notification sounds for the site.

## User Impact

User impact: macOS users with notification sound enabled now get an audible alert for Control UI Web Push attention notifications (approvals, agent questions, agent completion), so they are no longer missed while working in another window. Notifications that replace an existing same-tag notification stay quiet, and the operating system's notification settings remain authoritative.

## Why This Change Was Made

macOS defaults Web Push notification sound to off; the platform only plays sound when the notification options explicitly request it. The Control UI service worker built its notification options without a `silent` value, so macOS kept its silent default. Setting `silent: false` on the shared options requests audible delivery at the single notification-presentation boundary.

Keeping the same shared options preserves the existing quiet-replacement behavior through `renotify: false`, so approval terminal replacements still do not re-alert. `silent: false` is the standard Notifications API field and matches the platform default on other operating systems, so no non-macOS behavior changes.

Platform reference: Apple WWDC23 "What's new in web apps" — sound is on by default on iOS/iPadOS and off by default on macOS, and an audible notification must specify the value explicitly.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof through the Control UI notification entry point, before and after this change. Both runs execute the shipped `ui/public/sw.js` push handler in a service-worker context (the same load technique the repository's `ui/src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts` uses) and print the exact options object handed to `ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification`.

**After fix — the worker requests audible delivery:**

```

    node logs/real_behavior/issue-163544-sw-options-capture.mjs /workspace/repo/ui/public/sw.js

  "badge": "./favicon-32.png",

  "renotify": false,
  "silent": false,
  "data": {
    "url": "https://control.example/openclaw/",
    "explicitUrl": false
  }
}
audible delivery requested (options.silent === false): true
quiet replacement preserved (options.renotify === false): true
```

**Before fix — the same entry point produced a notification with no audible request:**

```
$ docker exec -u 1001:1001 -w /workspace/bot openclaw-repro \
    node logs/real_behavior/issue-163544-sw-options-capture.mjs /workspace/repo/ui/public/sw.js

sw.js: /workspace/repo/ui/public/sw.js
push payload: {"title":"OpenClaw","body":"Send test notification","tag":"openclaw-notification","renotify":false}
showNotification options: {
  "body": "Send test notification",
  "icon": "./apple-touch-icon.png",
  "badge": "./favicon-32.png",
  "tag": "openclaw-notification",
  "renotify": false,
  "data": {
    "url": "https://control.example/openclaw/",
    "explicitUrl": false

quiet replacement preserved (options.renotify === false): true
```

**Focused regression test (run in the reproduction container):**

```
$ docker exec -u 1001:1001 -e HOME=/tmp/openclaw-repro-home -w /workspace/repo openclaw-repro \
    pnpm --dir ui test src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 ✓ src/app/service-worker-lifecycle.test.ts > Control UI service worker notification scope > requests audible delivery on macOS without making replacements alert
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

The new test asserts `silent: false` for both an initial notification and a same-tag replacement, and the existing quiet-replacement test continues to pass.

**What was not tested:** Actual audible playback on macOS Safari. The reproduction container is Linux, so it cannot play a macOS notification sound. The audible-delivery mechanism is taken from Apple's documented platform contract (sound off by default on macOS; explicit `silent` value required to override) plus the captured options object above proof that the worker now sends the request. System and browser notification settings remain authoritative, so audible playback also depends on the user's macOS settings for the site.

prs.title: fix: clear stale automation topics when delivery destinations change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: editing an automation's delivery destination in the Control UI can keep the previous destination's topic ID after saving.

## User Impact

User impact: changing an automation's agent, delivery mode, channel, account, or recipient clears its previous topic; unchanged destinations, including whitespace-only edits, keep their topic. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already cleared its hidden topic when routing changed, but the save request omitted that field. Gateway patch merging interprets omission as preservation. The save path now uses the existing explicit-null contract to clear a previously stored topic. Route comparisons use the same trimmed values as saving, so harmless whitespace does not discard the topic.

## Evidence

Regression proof exercises the editor route-change owner, save controller, JSON serialization, actual Gateway patch normalization and merge, and reopening the saved job. Before the fix, all five route-change cases retained the old topic; the whitespace regression separately reproduced three unwanted clears. prs.title: fix(llama-cpp): model discovery fails when llama-server host resolves to a link-local address
prs.body:
Closes #160389

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: llama.cpp model discovery fails with "Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address" when the configured llama-server host resolves to a link-local address (for example `host.containers.internal` -> `169.254.1.2` under rootless Podman), while inference to the same endpoint works.

## User Impact

User impact: with `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` set on the llama-cpp provider, `openclaw models list` and the llama-server setup flow can discover models from a llama-server on a link-local host gateway, matching what inference already allows. Unset or `false` keeps today's strict discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inference transport honors `request.allowPrivateNetwork`, but discovery only trusted the exact origin, which still rejects link-local answers. Discovery now accepts the flag, and only an explicit `true` counts (absent or `false` changes nothing, even though inference defaults to true for llama-server). It always tries the existing exact-origin policy first. Only when that attempt is rejected by the SSRF guard and the flag is `true`, it retries once with `allowPrivateNetwork: true` and `maxRedirects: 0`, so the flag cannot carry to a redirect target. The catalog, dynamic-model, interactive-setup and non-interactive-validation callers all forward the saved value.

## Evidence

- New tests fail before the change and pass after: shared discovery (no retry when the flag is absent or `false`, no retry for non-SSRF errors, exact-origin policy kept when the first attempt succeeds, one retry with the flag and `maxRedirects: 0`), llama-server flag forwarding, setup forwarding of saved `false`, `true` and unset in both setup paths, and guard-level tests.
- Guard-level tests: a link-local answer is blocked without the flag and allowed with it, a redirect to `169.254.169.254` is refused when redirects are disabled, and a real HTTP check (two local servers) shows the redirect target receives zero requests.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/llama-cpp/src/external-server src/plugins/provider-self-hosted-discovery.test.ts src/infra/net/fetch-guard.allowed-origin-private.test.ts`: 9 files, 104 tests pass.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on all touched files.
- Security note: a bare `allowPrivateNetwork: true` policy follows redirects to private and metadata addresses (confirmed with the guard), which is why the retry disables redirects. Whether llama-server discovery should honor the flag at all is a maintainer decision.
- Not run: full typecheck, and a live link-local reproduction (no link-local interface or Podman host here); the link-local DNS answers in the guard tests are injected.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject malformed UTF-8 before rewriting vault pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #168822

Memory Wiki's compile rewrites every vault page whose managed blocks changed — Related-block refresh for regular pages, Generated-block refresh for index and dashboard pages — and `memory-wiki lint` rewrites the lint report the same way. Each rewrite reads the existing page with replacement-mode UTF-8 decoding and writes the whole file back, so a single undecodable byte in a page's human notes (a Latin-1 paste, a truncated export) is persisted as U+FFFD on every compile, and the compile reports success.

Precedent: issue #114895 established this rule for the `edit`/`apply_patch` tools — "they should reject the operation before writing and leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged" — and it now also covers `oc-path` file edits (#168491), `config` writes (#167118), and Doctor's root-memory merge (#168490). This PR applies the same admission to the vault-page rewrite surface and makes the refusal visible through the shipped CLI.

## User Impact

`memory-wiki compile` (including the automatic compile after every ingest) and `memory-wiki lint` now refuse to rewrite a malformed page instead of corrupting it, and the running command reports why:

```
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/router.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
```

The refusal names the page (or report) and states it was left unchanged, so a user can find the file and recover its encoding. The shared JSON envelope and nonzero exit code are unchanged for machine callers. Missing pages still fall back to their rendered defaults, and valid Unicode — Chinese, emoji, an intentional U+FFFD — compiles exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rewrite sites (`refreshPageRelatedBlocks`, `writeManagedMarkdownFile`, `refreshDashboardPages` in `compile.ts`, plus `writeLintReport` in `lint.ts`) all decode existing pages through lossy UTF-8 reads. They now share one strict decoder in the markdown module (`decodeWikiPageUtf8`) that admits the raw bytes with `node:buffer` `isUtf8` before decoding. Pure readers (search, context digest, frontmatter discovery) keep their existing decode contract; only the rewrite paths are strict.

The CLI boundary renders the refusal because the root failure renderer intentionally suppresses unclassified error messages in human output (`formatCliFailureLines`). `runWikiRewriteAction` prints the refusal for human `wiki compile` / `wiki lint` and keeps the generic `--json` machine envelope with a nonzero exit.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof — isolated vault, real files, local head `e78e9795043`

Environment: `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pointed at an isolated directory with `memory-wiki` enabled and an isolated vault; commands run through `pnpm openclaw`.

Malformed entity page (`entities/router.md` with one `0xff` byte in human notes):

```console
$ openclaw wiki compile
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/router.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

`sha256` before and after are identical (`72379ebf9aa287587b3694de32e58730b3748bafa75da143b6a4d4a93797feff`) and the `0xff` byte is still present.

Malformed lint report (`reports/lint.md`) in a second isolated vault:

```console
$ openclaw wiki lint
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: /<vault>/reports/lint.md. The file was left unchanged. ...
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

`sha256` before and after are identical (`d2006ab0c4f32e82cfc0ce2beae106a4d8a918e0717d97f345ca9dbf73530978`).

Valid-Unicode control (Chinese + emoji + a literal U+FFFD):

```console
$ openclaw wiki compile
Compiled wiki vault at /<vault> (10 pages, 0 indexes updated).   # exit 0
```

The human-notes line is preserved verbatim and the `openclaw:wiki:related` managed block is added.

JSON mode still returns the shared machine envelope with a nonzero exit:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/router.md. The file was left unchanged. ..."
  }
}
```

### Regression tests

`cli-utf8.test.ts` covers the human compile and lint refusal output plus the JSON rethrow. `compile.test.ts` covers malformed entity refusal with bytes preserved and valid non-ASCII compilation; `lint.test.ts` covers the malformed report.

```
$ pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
```

### Lint / types

```
$ oxlint extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

Typechecking the extension against the root source paths reports no errors in `extensions/memory-wiki/**`; the only scoped failures are two pre-existing `TS7016` errors for missing `qrcode` types in `src/media/qr-runtime.ts`, an environment devDependency gap unrelated to this change.


### Base-failing regression run (pre-fix)

The added regressions fail against the pre-fix production code, so they detect the defect instead of restating the implementation. In the same worktree, the four production files were restored to this PR's base revision (`36c194736bb`) while the new tests stayed at the head:

```console
$ git checkout 36c194736bb -- extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts
$ pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
FAIL extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts > compileMemoryWikiVault > refuses to rewrite a page that is not valid UTF-8 and leaves it unchanged
FAIL extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.test.ts > lintMemoryWikiVault > refuses to rewrite a lint report that is not valid UTF-8
FAIL extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts > memory-wiki cli UTF-8 refusals > prints the compile refusal and leaves the malformed page unchanged
FAIL extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts > memory-wiki cli UTF-8 refusals > prints the lint refusal and leaves the malformed report unchanged
FAIL extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts > memory-wiki cli UTF-8 refusals > rethrows the refusal in JSON mode for the shared machine envelope
 Test Files  3 failed (3)
      Tests  5 failed | 37 passed (42)
```

### Current CI state

The only failing gate on this head is `check-additional-boundaries`, and it fails on a file outside this PR's diff: the merge ref was built while `main` carried a duplicated mock-Gateway import in `ui/src/e2e/mobile-sidebar-session-menu.e2e.test.ts` (introduced by `5816754cafb`). `main` has since fixed that file in `48588a65222 fix(ci): drop the duplicate mock Gateway import in the mobile sidebar e2e`, so a fresh CI run on the current merge ref is green; until it re-fires, this failure is inherited-only. The other results on `e78e9795` are 35 pass, 56 skipping.


### Every wiki action shows the refusal (head `51e3d613546`)

The refusal boundary previously wrapped only `compile` and `lint`. Every wiki action now registers behind one boundary, so actions that reach the same decoder through ingest, OKF import, source synchronization, mutations, or search show the refusal as well; `--json` keeps the `cli_error` envelope and non-refusal errors are unchanged. This head re-runs CI on a merge ref that already contains main's `48588a65222`, so the earlier inherited `check-additional-boundaries` failure no longer applies to it.

Shipped-CLI evidence for the reported ingest path (isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, vault with a `0xff` byte in `entities/router.md`):

Before this commit the human output hid the affected file and the recovery steps:

```console
$ openclaw wiki ingest ./notes/alpha.md
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
# exit 1
```

After this commit the same command names the file and the recovery step, with the page's bytes preserved:

```console
$ openclaw wiki ingest ./notes/alpha.md
Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/router.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry.
# exit 1, sha256 of entities/router.md unchanged (72379ebf9aa287587b3694de32e58730b3748bafa75da143b6a4d4a93797feff)
```

JSON mode keeps the shared machine envelope:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Wiki page is not valid UTF-8 and cannot be rewritten safely: entities/router.md. The file was left unchanged. Keep a byte-for-byte backup, convert a copy to UTF-8 with its original encoding, then retry."
  }
}
```

`cli-utf8.test.ts` now also drives `ingest` through the registered CLI and asserts the refusal on stderr, the preserved bytes, and the JSON rethrow.

```
$ pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.agent-scope.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  5 passed (5)
     Tests  84 passed (84)
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions   # clean
$ oxlint extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli-utf8.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

prs.title: fix: keep runtime envelopes out of repaired sub-agent titles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: running Doctor fills unnamed native sub-agent titles with internal task-envelope text such as `[Subagent Context]` or `<<<BEGIN_OPENCLAW_INTERNAL_CONTEXT>>>`.

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor preserves native sub-agent labels instead of replacing missing names with runtime instructions. Visible dashboard child sessions still receive ordinary title repair, and explicit names and session activity remain unchanged.

This prevents new title pollution during repair; it does not clear titles already stored by earlier Doctor runs. Existing names remain protected from automatic replacement. There is no schema, transcript, or updater-driver change: candidate Doctor applies the same exclusion to existing operator state when it runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A native child's first user-role message is a generated task envelope, not a human naming request. Title repair previously treated it as an ordinary session request. Doctor now uses the existing native sub-agent key predicate to leave those labels with spawning and explicit renames, including thread-bound children. This avoids teaching Doctor a second envelope parser or filtering legitimate human text that happens to begin with the same words.

## Evidence

- Before the production fix, the new regression failed on all four combinations of run/session children and historical/current task envelopes. Each failure showed Doctor adding an internal-wrapper title. After the fix, all 9 tests in `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-title-repair.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed: 89.067 seconds measured wall time, 83.27 seconds reported by the test wrapper. The single added scan took 5.632 seconds and also checks explicit child labels, visible dashboard children, ordinary human lookalike text, and unchanged session metadata.
- Production core type checking passed in 94.91 seconds. The owning test graph, `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-commands-doctor"]'`, passed in 47.0 seconds (51.407 seconds measured wall time).
- Scoped oxlint on both changed TypeScript files passed in 38.744 seconds. Changed-file formatting, `git diff --check`, Doctor deprecation registry, core graph boundary, config-doc baseline, and the completed changed-file ratchet/dependency/boundary guards passed.
- Fresh managed Codex review of the final three-file diff returned no actionable P0–P2 findings.

The regression uses one real isolated SQLite state and one Doctor scan because the contract includes repair eligibility and persistence through the registered maintenance boundary. It adds no timers, polling, or per-case process boots. Local timings include shared-host load and worker compilation; CI timing is pending.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and recovered setup failures</summary>

The broad changed-file checker selected all 28 core test graphs and was intentionally canceled after the production checks passed. Its exit 130 is a cancellation, not a complete passing gate; validation continued with the owning Doctor graph and scoped lint. Unrelated remaining checks and a published-updater-driver × candidate run were not executed. Proof used isolated Doctor state; no existing live state was modified.

An initial test launch ran zero tests because concurrent installs shared hardlinked dependency files, changing a worker-integrity timestamp. Reinstalling each checkout with `--package-import-method=clone-or-copy` after all owners joined gave independent files and restored valid execution. An early regression fixture also used an epoch-aged child that automatic maintenance legitimately reclaimed; current timestamps and pre-scan existence assertions corrected the fixture before the clean negative baseline. Neither issue was hidden by retrying the same failing setup.

</details>

prs.title: fix(memory): keep relevant dated notes eligible before recency decay
prs.body:
Fixes #157392

## What Problem This Solves

Relevant dated memory notes can disappear once recency decay pushes their score below `minScore`, even with spare result slots and a complete embedding index.

## User Impact

Old notes remain eligible based on their pre-decay relevance. Recent notes still rank ahead, and final returned scores can be below `minScore`. The fixed 30-day half-life, result limits, exact-path priority, keyword fallback, and MMR remain in place. No configuration change or reindex is needed.

This resolves the eligibility cutoff. It does not promise that every eligible note fits a small result window; the larger-corpus ranking losses reported in the issue, including the October 7 Ollama measurements at `minScore=0`, remain a separate tradeoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory retrieval owner now separates eligibility from ranking. Hybrid merge carries an internal pre-decay score through recency/MMR and removes it at selection; keyword-only and vector-only retrieval filter before decay and truncate afterward. Importance and project weighting continue to affect eligibility. The bounded keyword relevance fix (#167004) and AND/OR fallback (#161165) remain intact.

- Standalone single-worker cost: hybrid **59.38 s** on the final fixture (29 tests, including cold worker preparation; the earlier run took 44.12 s); manager temporal ranking **38.62 s**, with **9 tests** and about **23 s** of test execution. The manager cases exercise real indexing, provider-mode routing, SQLite retrieval, and final selection; the hybrid algorithm cases are millisecond tests. The project-ranking expectation adds no new test execution. Doctor contract checks: **6/6**, **10.75 s** wall time.
- Real local-model proof: isolated synthetic four-note corpus, real Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, supported `pnpm openclaw --profile recency-eligibility memory index/search` entry points. No running Gateway, chat generation, or mocked embeddings. Same corpus and index before/after; the old note is 60 days old at `memory/records/2026-08-11-quartz.md`.

| Search at `minScore=0.35`, `maxResults=10` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recent dated copy | Rank 1, 0.714717 | Rank 1, 0.714240 |
| Evergreen copy | Rank 2, 0.712868 | Rank 2, 0.712868 |
| Old nested dated copy | Missing | Rank 3, 0.178560 |
| Unrelated note | Excluded | Excluded |

The baseline `--min-score 0` control returns the old note at 0.178677, proving it was indexed. Candidate exact-path lookup ranks it first at 1.0, and `--max-results 1` still chooses the recent note. Small score differences between runs are wall-clock decay. The final-head search replay takes **8.13 s**; status confirms Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, four indexed files/chunks, and a clean index.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): hand completed source replies to queued successors
prs.body:
Fixes #126813

**Human-led, AI-assisted:** I led and actively contributed throughout this work, including problem selection, architecture, implementation, code-level decisions and review, test design, edge-case analysis, and final validation. Codex assisted with portions of code drafting and editing, test execution, and adversarial review. I reviewed and approved every material code, design, test, and evidence change.

## What Problem This Solves

A message-tool-only turn can finish a visible source reply while peer or user messages are already queued. The queued successor still receives the normal answer-expected delivery hint, but the queue clear/drain boundary currently loses the causal fact that the immediately preceding owner already completed its reply. In multi-agent rooms, the successor can therefore replay the preceding answer before handling its own queued request.

The missing owner is the ephemeral boundary from the canonical `ReplyOperation` through the concrete queue/drain owner into successor admission. Transcript text and historical session outcomes cannot safely reconstruct this fact because they do not prove current-source delivery or exact predecessor order.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed, immutable, process-local completion handoff from the canonical `ReplyOperation` to the exact next eligible queued successor. The ordinary message-tool-only guidance remains intact; admission adds narrowly scoped runtime context that the preceding reply is complete and that the current queued request must still be answered normally.

The implementation enforces these invariants:

1. **Confirmed delivery only.** A fact is minted only after a settled, successful, non-aborted run has canonical completed current-source delivery evidence. Failed, aborted, partial/progress, foreign-source, and unrelated tool sends cannot mint it.
2. **Producer-before-clear ownership.** The fact is stored against the canonical operation before execution returns. A tagged one-shot take makes duplicate after-clear callbacks no-ops while allowing a canonical no-delivery completion to replace an older predecessor.
3. **Exact queue successor.** The concrete queue owner holds one ephemeral predecessor claim. Each actual predecessor replaces it; aborted entries are skipped, admission deferral preserves it, and successful admission consumes it once. This covers A→B→C as well as B-completes-without-delivery clearing A's fact.
4. **Fail-closed fencing without request loss.** Session key/id, lifecycle generation, and one canonical reply-delivery target must match. That target includes channel/to/account/chat/thread plus the normalized reply anchor, reply-to policy, and chat type; queue identity, owner abort/reset, session rotation, and room-event class are also fenced. A mismatch drops only the fact; it never suppresses, drops, or reclassifies the queued request.
5. **Current requests remain answerable.** The runtime-only directive prevents accidental replay merely to finish the preceding turn while explicitly requiring normal handling of the current request, including an intentional request to repeat or discuss the prior answer. It is not written to the transcript.
6. **Intentionally non-durable.** WeakMap ownership keeps the causal handoff process-local. There are no session-state, queue-codec, transcript, or message-tool outcome schema changes.

This is the canonical minimum fix because it records the delivery fact at its authoritative producer and transfers it only across the owner boundary that currently drops it. Inferring from prompts or persisting the fact would broaden trust and restart semantics unnecessarily.

Compatibility was checked against active neighboring work. #119736 is complementary durable restart evidence; this handoff is immediate and process-local. Draft #113554 can broaden the canonical explicit-route predicate without changing the fencing here. The current exact-head rebase composes the narrow hook with upstream's extracted message-tool outcome module and drain-owner generation fence without widening persistence or restart semantics. #82572 persists queue state, while this claim is deliberately excluded from persistence and must not be persisted without a new trust design.

## User Impact

Queued multi-agent turns no longer need to guess whether the preceding message-tool-only owner already answered. The next eligible successor receives exact causal context, avoids an accidental duplicate, and still answers its own request normally.

Ordinary queue ordering, overflow/drop policy, automatic delivery, user-request classification, and restart behavior are unchanged. Legitimate follow-ups—including “repeat the prior answer”—remain answerable and are covered end to end.

## Evidence

### Current exact-head rebase update

Current exact head `4d3b1169f3f15fd65c6827bd362c9f357a66c080` rebases the reviewed nine-commit series once onto `main` snapshot `cddf5165ee8f153c3e4fefb6181ed0928da141e6`, which includes the repository-owned Telegram userbot harness from #131715. Range-diff maps all nine commits one-to-one. The only semantic conflict adaptation moves the same completion evidence into upstream's extracted message-tool outcome module and composes the handoff with the new drain-owner generation fence. The final surface remains 18 files, `+1540/-52`.

Exact-head hosted CI is green: [run 33261641621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33261641621) completed 258 check contexts with zero pending and zero failures, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Local validation on the rebased head passed 218 related tests, the exact queue/owner-clear/collect-admission handoff E2E, `tsgo:core`, the messaging test type graph, changed-file type-aware Oxlint, formatting, runtime and Madge cycle checks, conflict-marker, max-lines, assertion-safety, and `git diff --check` guards. The only local failure is the previously documented unrelated Windows SQLite cleanup `EBUSY`, which also reproduces when its overflow-session test runs alone.

#131715 retired the old Telegram Desktop/Mantis workflows after the earlier recording. The remaining exact-head real-behavior proof must therefore use `.agents/skills/telegram-e2e-userbot`: hold A's provider response, enqueue fresh B and C requests, confirm two pending followups before drain, release the drain, and record for 90 seconds. The pass contract is exactly one visible A reply, one fresh B answer, one fresh C answer, no replay, and exactly three provider requests where B and C each contain the completed-predecessor directive once. The earlier native Mantis artifacts remain useful historical behavior evidence, but they are not claimed as proof of this exact head.
Prior reviewed integration head `138b970da9b33d1400016c4a54fd1d0477ba9bf8` combined behavior head `bb47f213255e5c7f934b20511654230a1f6a66ee` with upstream snapshot `3b0cad5d7087e08a5288f4f3d513a06571be4f9e`. Its review and hosted CI remain historical evidence; the current rebase update above supersedes that commit topology while preserving the reviewed nine-commit patch mapping and centralized reply-delivery target identity.

Validation used bundled Node v24.19.0:

- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-message-tools.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.handoff.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/queue.drain-restart.test.ts` — 95/95 passed.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/queue.collect.test.ts -t "hands one completed predecessor to the admitted collect aggregate"` — 1/1 passed.
- `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts -t "hands a confirmed source reply through owner clear and collect admission without suppressing the new answer"` — 1/1 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- The messaging test type graph, runtime import-cycle check, and Madge source graph — passed with zero cycles. The completion core imports the queue leaf contract, while the delivery/agent adapter is a one-way producer module.
- Changed-file type-aware Oxlint (including max-lines), formatting, conflict-marker, assertion-safety, `check:changed --dry-run`, and `git diff --check` guards — passed.
- Pre-rebase hosted CI — `check-dependencies`, `check-test-types-core-4`, `check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture`, every remaining shard, and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed on patch-equivalent head `c3fb29731b586996ed905a244bed42a856adb3ac`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32584209718
- Prior exact-head hosted CI — 207 passed and 41 skipped check contexts, with zero pending and zero failures on `138b970da9b33d1400016c4a54fd1d0477ba9bf8`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32797492241

The real E2E spans confirmed current-source tool delivery → actual `ReplyOperation` completion with duplicate clear callbacks → actual collect/drain → successor admission. Its successor is message-tool-only, sees both `MESSAGE_TOOL_ONLY_DELIVERY_HINT` and the new handoff directive, answers an explicit repeat request through a new current-source final message-tool send, and emits no automatic duplicate.

A maintainer-owned native Telegram Desktop Mantis run supplied channel-visible proof on behavior head `44d8d8277f31af9d968e175420f7528dc95df905`: baseline and candidate both visibly delivered the first answer and the fresh queued successor answer; baseline provider facts lacked the completion handoff, while candidate provider facts contained it and the second Telegram answer addressed the queued request without replaying the first. Both lanes passed, with screenshots, GIFs, MP4s, and raw QA facts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/32583508198. The current exact head preserves that matching-target behavior but additionally fences reply anchor, reply-to policy, and chat type in response to the P1 review. Because that predicate changed after the recording, the old run remains historical evidence. A fresh exact-head run through the repository-owned Telegram userbot harness described above is now the authoritative real-behavior proof step; contributor-side CI cannot substitute for that credentialed lane.

The principal regression fails when only the producer hook is removed: admitted context retains the ordinary message-tool-only hints but lacks the completion directive at `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts:1664`. Restoring the hook makes the same E2E pass. Exact base does not contain the new primitive, so removing the producer is the conservative intended-cause counterfactual while keeping the integrated test harness buildable.

The suites also cover foreign/partial/progress/failed/aborted producer negatives; one-shot and deferred admission; lifecycle, route, reply-anchor, reply-policy, chat-type, room-event, owner-abort, and session-rotation rejection; duplicate clears; A→B→C replacement; a no-delivery predecessor clearing stale evidence; aborted first entries; and exactly one directive over a real B+C collect aggregate without losing either current request.

A full local `queue.collect.test.ts` run additionally passed all new handoff coverage but reproduced one pre-existing Windows-only SQLite `.shm` cleanup `EBUSY` in the unrelated overflow-session test. Exact-head hosted Linux CI ran the complete checkout and passed that suite and the aggregate gate.

ClawSweeper's earlier review rated the native Telegram behavior proof highly, while the latest review found one P1: the handoff route omitted reply anchor, reply-to policy, and chat type. Prior reviewed head `138b970da9b33d1400016c4a54fd1d0477ba9bf8` resolved that finding with one canonical delivery-target key and focused mismatch coverage. Current exact head `4d3b1169f3f15fd65c6827bd362c9f357a66c080` preserves that repair on the new upstream architecture and has fully green hosted CI. A repository-owned Telegram userbot recording is now requested; ClawSweeper re-review will follow once its exact-head artifacts are attached. No remaining contributor-side code finding is known. The repository reporter has also been invited to provide an optional production-room diagnostic with a 90-second negative observation window, outbound counts, current-request preservation, explicit-repeat handling, and strict redaction requirements: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127967#issuecomment-5381411670.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): newly-paired senders receive no approval confirmation
prs.body:
Closes #56619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users pairing a WhatsApp sender would never receive an approval confirmation message. The shared pairing-approval path is documented and works for Slack, Feishu, and Synology Chat, but WhatsApp's channel adapter ships no `notifyApproval` callback, so the shared notifier (`src/channels/plugins/pairing.ts`) returns early and the approval is a silent no-op. The Control UI also hides the "notify on approval" option for WhatsApp, because `notifySupported` is derived from `Boolean(adapter.notifyApproval)`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the missing `notifyApproval` callback to `whatsappPlugin.pairing`, modeled on the existing Slack implementation. When an approval fires, WhatsApp resolves the account, normalizes the sender JID, and sends `PAIRING_APPROVED_MESSAGE` (the shared confirmation string) via `sendMessageWhatsApp`. The change is purely additive — the shared notifier and the `notifySupported` UI surface already handle the optional callback, so no shared, gateway, or protocol code is touched. WhatsApp's send path is simpler than Slack's (no write token or team-scoped target formatting), so the callback stays minimal.

This is a small, scoped gap-filler that brings WhatsApp to parity with the three sibling channels that already ship this callback. The broader operator-approvals refactor (`docs/refactor/operator-approvals.md`, #103505) is a future reshape of the approval lifecycle; this PR does not introduce a new approval abstraction — it wires the existing per-channel notify seam that the shared notifier already calls, so it composes with rather than preempts that later work.

## User Impact

WhatsApp senders who complete pairing approval now receive a confirmation message, matching the behavior of Slack, Feishu, and Synology Chat. Operators also see the "notify on approval" option enabled for WhatsApp in the Control UI.

## Evidence

- New test `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel.test.ts` asserts `whatsappPlugin.pairing.notifyApproval` is defined and sends `PAIRING_APPROVED_MESSAGE` to the paired sender. Red on `main` (callback is `undefined`); green on this branch.
- `pnpm test:extension whatsapp` — the two new tests pass (included in the 1341 passing). The 7 failures in `session.test.ts` are pre-existing on `main` (verified: same 7 fail on an unmodified `main` checkout — they require WhatsApp credential/auth state unavailable in the test environment and are unrelated to this change).
- Prior art: Slack (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`), Synology Chat, and Feishu all implement the same `notifyApproval` callback.

prs.title: fix(codex): use monotonic clock for migration marketplace discovery deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During `openclaw migrate codex`, the plugin marketplace discovery polling loop can hang far longer than the configured 30s timeout (or timeout prematurely) if the system clock adjusts via NTP correction or sleep/resume. The fix switches the discovery deadline from `Date.now()` (wall clock) to `performance.now()` (monotonic) so the budget stays bounded across clock domains.

- **Problem:** `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` in `extensions/codex/src/migration/apply.ts` seeds its deadline and computes remaining budget with `Date.now()` (wall clock), but both downstream consumers — `requestCodexAppServerJson({timeoutMs})` → `withTimeout` → `setTimeout`, and `sleep(waitMs)` → `setTimeout` — measure elapsed time with the monotonic clock. A wall-clock rewind inflates `remainingMs`/`waitMs` beyond the configured budget; a forward jump shrinks them, prematurely tripping the deadline.
- **Solution:** Replace all 6 `Date.now()` calls in the polling loop with `performance.now()`, aligning the deadline with the monotonic clock used by the downstream timers.
- **What changed:** `extensions/codex/src/migration/apply.ts` — 6 `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` in `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` + 2-line comment. New regression test `apply-deadline-real-transport.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change:** No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface. The discovery logic, poll interval, and timeout constants are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same cross-clock-domain bug pattern fixed in the sibling function `buildCodexPluginThreadConfigWithinDeadline` by #155863 (BUG-088). That PR switched `plugin-thread-config-deadline.ts` from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`. This PR applies the identical fix to the other deadline in the same module — `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` in `migration/apply.ts` — which was identified during the same anchor sweep but is an independent function in a different file.

- **Best fix:** Direct `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` replacement at the canonical owner (the polling loop itself). No wrapper or helper needed — the function is the sole owner of this deadline.
- **Alternative:** None considered. This is a mechanical clock-domain fix matching the merged precedent #155863.
- **Risk:** `performance.now()` returns sub-millisecond floats, but both consumers (`requestCodexAppServerJson` → `withTimeout` → `scheduleTimeout` → `setTimeout`, and `sleep` → `resolveTimerTimeoutMs` → `setTimeout`) internally floor or clamp the value, so no `Math.floor` is needed. Node 16+ provides global `performance`.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw migrate codex` will no longer experience marketplace discovery polling that exceeds the configured timeout budget when the system clock adjusts (NTP correction, sleep/resume). The migration's plugin discovery phase will respect the 30s default timeout regardless of wall-clock fluctuations.

## Evidence

**Real-transport regression (production request owner + in-memory CodexAppServerClient):**

The `apply-deadline-real-transport.test.ts` test retains the real request owner (`requestCodexAppServerJson` → `withCodexAppServerJsonClient` → `client.request`) and replaces only the transport boundary (`shared-client.js` acquisition) with an in-memory `CodexAppServerClient` via `fromTransportForTests`. It exercises the full `applyCodexMigrationPlan` → `ensureCodexPluginActivation` → `requestTargetCodexAppServerJson` → `requestCodexAppServerJson` → `withCodexAppServerJsonClient` → `client.request` chain. Fake timers control `setTimeout` and `performance.now`; only `Date.now()` is skewed −120s after the first armed timer.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/migration/apply-deadline-real-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

PROOF_TRACE [{"requestIndex":1,"armedTimeoutMs":30000,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":2,"armedTimeoutMs":30000,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":3,"armedTimeoutMs":29750,"bounded":true},
 {"requestIndex":4,"armedTimeoutMs":29750,"bounded":true}]
Tests  1 passed
```

**Pre-fix RED (source reverted to Date.now, same real-transport test):**

```console
FAIL  expected 150000 to be less than or equal to 60000
```

The second request allowance inflates to **150000ms** on a 120s wall-clock rewind; post-fix it stays at **29750ms** (within the 30s discovery budget).

**What was not tested:** A real OS clock shift was not induced; the skew is injected by stepping `Date.now()` between the deadline seed and the remaining-budget read. The in-memory transport replaces only the shared-client acquisition boundary; the real `CodexAppServerClient` JSON-RPC framing, `withCodexAppServerJsonClient` timeout/guard logic, and `withTimeout`/`scheduleTimeout`/`setTimeout` timer arming all run in production code.

**Open PR collision check:** Searched open PRs touching `extensions/codex/src/migration/apply.ts` — no open PR touches this file. Sibling PR #155863 only touched `plugin-thread-config-deadline.ts` (different file, different function). No duplicate.
