## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where updating from 2026.9.2 could leave the Gateway unusable after rollback: target Doctor migrated persistent state, package rollback restored the old binary, and that binary failed with `no such column: workspace_dir`. It also fixes no-op updates stopping healthy Gateways, completed legacy captures blocking later updates, and repair capture overhead growing with every inventory entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the [accepted lossless-capture contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140339#issuecomment-5614409997) and [transaction-scoped lifecycle decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/140339#issuecomment-5614508856). Peter's explicit 2026-09-10 approval: “update should always work. It's best effort. If there are minor hiccups we add that in the warning log. We should backup things before, and rollback restores the backup.”

### Capture, restore and retirement

Before protected mutation, existing backup machinery captures config/include files, shared and per-agent SQLite, Skill Workshop and inventoried plugin resources. SQLite uses online backup; recovery captures remain unsanitized, without delivery-row or TTL pruning. One immutable manifest binds numbered resources by size and SHA-256; the terminal outcome is separately write-once.

Sets live at `<stateDir>.update-captures/<captureId>/` with private ancestors and owner-only permissions. The shared privacy marker excludes them from ordinary backup/support exports, including explicit containing/nested selections. User archives retain their existing behavior. Capacity admission covers capture, package/recovery staging, growth and reserve; insufficient space preserves live data and earlier sets.

Generic JSON/plan adapters and custom bundled migration owners enumerate inputs through existing collectors. The optional read-only `requireLocalResources` collector argument rejects remote resources when complete local capture is required; it is not configuration. Missing declarations refuse protection.

Rollback restores package files and captured state, then verifies the previous managed Gateway. State-only finalization restores its capture without inventing a package transaction. Database-directory restore removes migration-created files only within the declared boundary; reopened LanceDB verifies captured schema, rows and version. The shared copy helper clears restored `state_leases` and `agent_database_leases`: process leases cannot survive copying. Captures remain lossless.

Both finalizer Doctor phases share one verified capture and config-write receipts. Mutating children settle before restoration. Manual recovery retains protection through subsequent Doctor/bootstrap writes, restores again if continuation fails, and closes reopened stores. Standalone repair never starts the Gateway. Data failures are hard errors; reporting failures after verified recovery are advisory.

There is no count, age or capacity-pressure pruning. Existing terminal owners retire captures only after durable, identity-bound success and settled recovery dependencies. Admission reconciles completed prior transactions through Doctor's resolution owner, requiring confirmed matching runtime/version/build and successful Doctor/Gateway verification. Explicit false readiness fails; missing newer fields remain compatible with 9.2. Nonterminal, restored, failed-restoration and unverified sets are not automatically adopted.

### No-op and tagged-upgrade contracts

Convergence requests protection only for actual plugin/config mutation, using facts already available inside its existing lease. Unchanged baseline publication and repeated failure of an already-disabled plugin preserve their no-change result. Real enablement, alias and slot changes remain mutations. Exact target identity is always validated; an already-current core uses its installed schema/runtime metadata. Lease ordering, publication fencing and `--no-restart` semantics are unchanged.

Admission checks capacity and independent writers before shutdown. A late pre-mutation refusal restores the original service, including with `--no-restart`. Native parent/launcher identity and Gateway-lock checks distinguish a supervised Gateway child from unrelated writers. Capture callbacks now check live executor/maintenance fences; full recovery admission runs before and after capture, avoiding repeated SQLite snapshots per resource.

The named **tagged 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 rehearsal contract** accepts their disposable copies only with the existing update-in-progress marker, exact private environment/config/data layout, observed live parent chain and matching copied-ledger identity. It verifies local resources, OAuth paths, SQLite companions, ownership and links under existing maintenance authority. Identity-bearing driver/capture calls remain strict. Admission emits a typed `legacy-driver-rehearsal` fact and warning. Remove this compatibility path when those tags cease being supported upgrade sources.

Inline Git RPC remains explicitly unprotected, recorded in its parent run and reflected in result/status: “This Gateway-initiated update is not protected by a recovery capture. Run `openclaw update` from a terminal for a protected update.” The external drain/stop/capture continuation is [#144422](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144422).

This builds on @fuller-stack-dev's #143693, #143799 and #143899, and reuses @vincentkoc's cleanup fencing (#143791) and terminal settlement (#143921). Package activation stays with #143750/#143752. Please keep maintainer edits enabled.

### Data-model compatibility

No SQLite schema/column, protocol, configuration option or dependency change. One recovery-set kind and existing run metadata hold config receipts, restoration facts and unprotected RPC identity. No ratchet increased; the upstream environment-variable budget passes at **492/492**.

### Owner flow map

Pre-fix references are pinned to `298493fa54b8d2f9091e504c178f850591a1757c`:

Published 9.3's previously healthy rollback preserved schema compatibility; it did not restore SQLite.

## User Impact

Protected failures recover state before restarting the previous Gateway. True no-ops keep healthy Gateways serving. Retained sets appear in `update status --json` with `npx openclaw@latest doctor --fix` guidance. With 9.2, a failing target Doctor restores state before package rollback; because that updater may leave the Gateway stopped, output also names `openclaw gateway start`.

prs.title: fix(macos): localize gateway setup alerts
prs.body:
Related: #125967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users running OpenClaw in a non-English locale would still see English-only Gateway setup, primary-Gateway confirmation, error, and alert button copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway alerts used raw Swift strings, so the native localization extractor could inventory some copy without the runtime actually resolving translations. This changes the owning macOS alert paths to `String(localized:)`, uses a `%@` template with `String(format:)` for dynamic endpoint and transport text, and adds targeted extraction contracts plus exact English-formatting tests.

Only the canonical native source baseline is regenerated here. Locale catalogs remain owned by the Native App Locale Refresh workflow; #125967 should update after this source PR lands.

## User Impact

Gateway setup and primary-Gateway alerts can now render their titles, explanatory text, errors, and buttons using the active macOS locale while preserving the existing English wording and interpolation.

## Evidence

- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` -> 4,261 entries, no drift after rebase
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` -> 1,286 macOS source keys
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts` -> 16 passed
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter DashboardGateway` -> 33 passed across 6 suites
- scoped SwiftLint -> 0 violations
- scoped Oxfmt check and `git diff --check` -> passed
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --dry-run -- <six reviewed files>` -> macOS CI lane identified; heavy `test:macos:ci` fan-out intentionally deferred to the shared QA FIFO
- local ClawSweeper reviewed `c2b61a40..74219a2b`; it reported one low-severity adjacent raw-title path in `DashboardManager.swift`, outside this independently reviewed six-file fence and not introduced by this change

prs.title: perf(nodes): reuse live placement facts through worker turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Paired-node OpenClaw turns repeatedly read the same placement and claim from SQLite while checking execution authority. A six-turn diagnostic cohort observed 6,708 placement-table reads on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

Worker turns reuse the placement owner’s live published facts. A fresh-session five-warm-turn comparison on the same two-member Linux pond measured median TTFT of 2,172 → 1,782 ms for loopback and 1,971 → 1,780 ms for the remote node. The local control measured 1,561 → 1,897 ms. Provider latency varies; these are observed live medians, not a fixed latency guarantee. Final response delivery still follows workspace reconciliation, and tail latency did not improve.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the existing publication-owned placement reader once per admitted attempt, reuse its current facts with the same placement/claim predicates, and release it on every exit. Existing committed postimages update the reader; pending publication, replacement, revocation and release still fence it. This adds no cache, lifecycle state, schema, protocol, or configuration.

Production LOC: **+5** (8 added, 3 removed; one production file). This uses the campaign exception for a measured win above 100 ms. Test LOC: +15. Two changed files.

## Evidence

- Real `sessions.create` → `sessions.dispatch` → `chat.send` → `agent.wait`, OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`, OpenClaw harness, empty managed workspaces, six sequential turns per fresh session (one warmup + five measured). The Gateway/loopback and remote node used two Hetzner ccx33 members after AWS quota rejection; remote traffic used a direct member-to-member SSH tunnel.
- Tail medians: loopback 399 → 443 ms; remote 503 → 501 ms; local 130 → 132 ms. Reconciliation ordering and required-reply completion are unchanged.
- In a separate five-warm diagnostic cohort, median whole-turn Gateway SQLite execution calls fell **2,103 → 1,384** (−34%); main-thread placement `get()` calls fell **1,102 → 340** (−69%). Worker-task counts stayed similar, as this removes repeated synchronous reads rather than changing transport. Background work within the window remains included.
- The extended owning-boundary regression failed before the fix on observed main-thread SQLite `get()` calls; after the fix repeated execution checks execute zero main-thread SQL and a retained check rejects after release.
- 28 focused tests passed across `worker-turn-launcher.lazy.test.ts`, `placement-session-read.test.ts`, and `worker-turn-launcher-reconciliation-authority.test.ts`. Command with `--maxWorkers=1`: 132.33 s wall time. The baseline single-file regression command took 89.78 s and failed for the intended SQL-read assertion. No new test cases or process boots were added.
- Required CI gate workflow completed successfully in 44 s ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38102066062)); per-file hosted duration was not exposed. Candidate build passed. Changed-file gates passed except the baseline unused `env` error in `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts:519`, already fixed on main by `243b6dbf63d2`. Baseline and candidate builds also report the same unrelated Control UI startup gzip advisory.
- Deslop and independent Codex review completed with no accepted P0/P1 findings.

Post-merge-tree static verification against main `bb7c69ddd04b01330e60489d1057d6e1e3319ad2`: targeted type-aware Oxlint and export-name collision checks pass. Knip reports identical inherited unused exports on the candidate and exact main source: `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` in `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts` and `reconnectGateway` in `ui/src/pages/skill-workshop/skill-workshop-page.test-support.ts`. No ratchet was changed. Required GitHub CI is green. Native worktree allocation was blocked beyond the campaign timeout; landing uses the authorized exact-head squash fallback.

prs.title: test(memory): assert the CLI search runtime without an unbound method reference
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`main` currently fails the `memory-core` extension lint stripe. `extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-operation.test.ts:51` takes a capability method as a value (`assert(runtime?.searchForCli)`), which the repository's type-aware `typescript/unbound-method` rule rejects:

```
[oxlint:extensions:11] extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-operation.test.ts:51:19: error: Avoid referencing unbound methods which may cause unintentional scoping of `this`. (typescript(unbound-method))
```

That stripe lints the whole extension package rather than the diff, so every PR whose change classification routes `memory-core` into these shards now goes red for a file it does not touch. Observed on #168574, a two-file memory-core change whose own files lint clean on the same run (`oxfmt --check` → `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`; changed-path oxlint → `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`).

Fixes #168808.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrow the optional runtime first, then assert the hook with the `assert(typeof x === "function")` shape already used elsewhere in the tree (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts:142`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.native.test.ts:259`).

`searchForCli` is optional on the capability runtime (`src/plugins/registry-contribution-types.ts:273`), so the guard keeps its purpose for the call on line 72. The only semantic difference from the removed line is that the guard now requires the hook to be a function rather than merely truthy; the hook is invoked on the very next lines, so any other value already failed there. No production code is touched.

## Evidence

### Lint — the gate this PR repairs

Local, with the same rule and tool versions CI installs (oxlint 1.85.0 + oxlint-tsgolint 7.0.2003), `oxlint --type-aware extensions/memory-core/src/memory-search-operation.test.ts`:

- **Before** (`main` at `bb7c69ddd04`): `51:19: error typescript(unbound-method)` — same file, line and column as the CI annotation.
- **After**: exits 0 with no diagnostics; `oxfmt --check` passes.

On this head, CI ran the real gates on `c8c19081463`: `check-lint` ([job 114363876677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38103305951/job/114363876677)) completed `success` including the memory-core stripe that previously failed, and `check-test-types` passed. The modified test itself ran in the shipped `extension-database-workers` configuration ([job 114363687060](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38103305951/job/114363687060)): `✓ makes routed CLI recalls available to dreaming in the requested agent workspace`, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 1 passed (1)`.

### Shipped behaviour — real captured terminal output (not the mocked fixture)

The guard belongs to the shipped CLI search path, so below is that path run end to end from the **packaged binary** with the real search manager, in fully isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` state. Paths are the proof harness working directory; there are no credentials, host addresses, or external endpoints in the run.

```

qa workspace     : /tmp/proof168814.XXXXXX/qa-workspace     (memory/2026-10-11.md: "- NEBULA-73 belongs in durable memory.")
other workspace  : /tmp/proof168814.XXXXXX/other-workspace  (memory/2026-10-11.md: "- ORBIT-11 belongs in the other agent workspace.")
state dir        : /tmp/proof168814.XXXXXX/state

== 1) shipped CLI search, agent qa, three distinct matching queries ==
-- $ openclaw memory search "nebula" --agent qa --json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "memory/2026-10-11.md",
      "startLine": 1,
      "endLine": 2,
      "score": 0.397950269027249,
      "textScore": 9.99999000001e-7,
      "snippet": "- NEBULA-73 belongs in durable memory.\n",
      "source": "memory",
      "provenance": { "originClass": "agent", "sessionKind": "unknown", "observedAt": 1791684745859 }
    }
  ]
```

prs.title: feat: let the agent request compaction itself (session_compact tool)
prs.body:
Closes #138083

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running assistant sessions that switch between unrelated topics carry the
finished topic's history until token pressure finally triggers compaction. The
model has no way to say "this discussion is done, archive it now," so context
budget is wasted and the eventual pressure-driven summary mixes unrelated
topics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a `session_compact` built-in tool that lets the model request compaction
of the current session, following the established `sessions_yield` pattern:
the tool records the request, the runtime owns execution.

Key design decisions:

- The tool is only offered when the runtime provides a compaction request
  receiver, so unsupported contexts never see a dead tool. Heartbeat turns do
  not install the receiver at all (they never execute agent compaction).
- Execution runs after the reply's delivery settlement — strictly later than
  the turn's deferred lifecycle completion, which releases the embedded
  active-run handle first (the manual pipeline rejects requests with
  `active_run` while the handle is still registered). Scheduling the work
  behind delivery keeps a non-streamed final reply from waiting on the whole
  summarization request. The run itself goes through the existing manual
  compaction pipeline (`trigger: "manual"`, `force`, focus passed as
  `customInstructions`), reusing lane queueing, checkpoints, hooks, quality
  guards, and provider/model overrides unchanged.
- A committed compaction is recorded through the same accounting owner as
  `/compact` (`incrementCompactionCount` with the committed successor entry as
  the writer fence), so finalization never persists the pre-summarization
  usage as the current context.
- The tool is registered in `CORE_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` under the `sessions`
  section with `coding`/`messaging` profiles and the OpenClaw group, so
  profile allowlists, `group:sessions`, and `group:openclaw` agree with
  runtime eligibility.
- No new config options, no SQLite schema changes, no new file storage: the
  summary lives in the session transcript as today, and full history stays on
  disk.

## User Impact

The agent can now proactively compact on topic shifts instead of only
reacting to context pressure. Behavior is the same contract as `/compact`:
recent turns are preserved, the summary is stored in the session transcript,
and the operator can always inspect the full on-disk history.

## Evidence

- New focused tests (`pnpm test` scope):
  - `src/agents/tools/session-compact-tool.test.ts` (4 tests): error paths
    without session context or runtime receiver, scheduling with and without
    focus, callback payload.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.agent-compaction.test.ts`
    (7 tests): manual-pipeline invocation with focus/force, committed-entry
    writer fence plus `incrementCompactionCount` accounting on success,
    accounting failure logged without throwing, no-op without a request,
    heartbeat skip, skip outcome and failure both non-fatal.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-agent-compaction.test.ts`
    (2 tests): drives a full `executeAgentTurn` with the real
    deferred-lifecycle manager and asserts the turn surfaces the recorded
    request on the settled outcome without running compaction in-turn (the
    finalize side owns execution, after delivery settlement).
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-maintenance.agent-compaction.test.ts`
    (3 tests): the scheduled compaction runs only after `ownerSettlement`
    resolves, is skipped without a recorded request, and is skipped when the
    reply operation aborted before settlement.
- Regression: `agent-runner-execution-command-events.test.ts` (4 tests),
  `agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts` (24 tests),
  `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens.test.ts` (7 tests) all pass.
- `tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.core.json` clean on this branch (core and core
  test graphs).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on all touched files; docs updated in
  `docs/concepts/compaction.md` (Agent-initiated compaction section).

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` pass locally on this branch (check includes the
  tool-display and assertion-safety ratchets that this change updates).
- Live verification: not feasible in the author's environment — the execution
  path is the embedded auto-reply owner, which needs a full channel + provider
  setup (none available locally; the CLI-direct runtime intentionally does not
  expose the tool). The ordering and accounting guarantees are instead proven
  against the real deferred-lifecycle manager and the real settlement gate in
  the regression tests above; CI owns the full-suite run. The change touches no
  bundled plugin artifacts.

## Follow-up noted during this work

- `src/system-agent/chat-turn-router.ts` (untouched by this PR) has a
  pre-existing type error: `resolveOperatorApprovalDecision` infers `T` from
  both `apply` and `denied`, and the narrow literal returned by `denied`
  conflicts with the wide `SystemAgentChatReply` returned by `apply`. It does
  not affect the `pnpm check` lane (no full-project tsc there) and is unrelated
  to this feature; flagged here as a named follow-up for the owner of that
  surface.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): long replies never play and the caller hears silence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long reply is synthesized as one request. `playTtsViaStream` hands the complete reply to `synthesizeForTelephony(text)` and races it against `synthesisTimeoutMs`, a fixed value (default 8000ms) that does not scale with text length. Playback is all-or-nothing: not one speech frame is sent until the whole buffer exists. So when a long reply loses that race, the turn fails **before a single speech frame is sent** and the caller hears nothing at all. The longer and more useful the answer, the more reliably it is lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Splitting belongs inside the existing serialized Twilio playback owner, not beside it. Speech directives are resolved once, up front, over the complete reply; the resolved spoken text is then split into bounded segments and played back-to-back through the same queue slot, so ordered playback, barge-in and a single final mark per turn all still hold. Resolving before splitting means a split can never divide an inline directive block, and one resolved override set applies to every segment.

Segment length is capped by `MAX_TELEPHONY_TTS_SYNTH_CHARS = 320`, chosen so each synthesis request stays far inside the timeout that the whole-reply path was losing. It is a bounded internal of the stream synthesis path, not a new configuration surface: the limit exists to keep one request inside the provider synthesis timeout, which is not a property an operator is positioned to tune per call.

The playback body moves out of `providers/twilio.ts` into `providers/twilio/stream-tts-playback.ts`, which leaves the capped file **smaller** than before (831 to 742 lines).

### This revision was re-expressed against current main, not rebased

The previous head was based roughly 25,800 commits behind main and conflicted. Upstream had restructured `providers/twilio.ts` across ten commits — four "deslop" passes plus `refactor: simplify runtime adapters and remove obsolete code` — so this revision is **not** a replay of the old diff. It is the same intent re-applied to upstream's current shape, and re-scoped against what upstream now ships:

- **Dropped as already dead upstream.** The old head reintroduced a `chunkDelivered !== chunkAttempts` / `"incomplete audio delivery"` guard. Upstream deleted that in `398a85faeb6` because it was provably unreachable — the counter was incremented unconditionally right after the send-success check. It is not reintroduced here, and no test referenced it.
- **Dropped as out of scope.** The old head also added `webhook/auto-response-speech.ts` carrying duplicate-suppression for the auto-response turn. That is a separate defect on a different path, the module does not exist upstream, and it collides with #136847 which also creates it. This PR is now the playback fix only; the duplicate-suppression change belongs in its own PR.
- **Checked and deliberately not duplicated.** Upstream's newer adjacent machinery does not cover this symptom. `webhook/realtime-audio-pacer.ts` has exactly one non-test importer, `webhook/realtime-handler.ts` — the Realtime transport, a different path — and it paces frames it is handed rather than bounding a synthesis request. `MAX_PENDING_TTS_OPERATIONS_PER_STREAM` bounds how many playbacks a stream may queue, which is orthogonal, since this fix uses one queue slot per turn. Core `src/tts/tts-telephony.ts` passes `text` straight through with no length bound. `providers/twilio.ts` on current main still calls `ttsProvider.synthesizeForTelephony(text)` with the complete reply.

## User Impact

Long replies play. Previously the most substantial answers were exactly the ones that silently failed, and the caller heard nothing at all for that turn.

Short replies are unchanged. Text at or under the cap is returned as a single segment, so it remains one synthesis request ending in one completion mark.

## Evidence

### Baseline: the defect, captured

Neutralising only the new bound — `MAX_TELEPHONY_TTS_SYNTH_CHARS = 320` to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which reproduces the whole-reply path exactly — fails six of the new tests:

```
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > synthesizes every segment in order and sends one completion mark
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > clears buffered audio when a later segment fails to synthesize
  -> expected 'resolved' to be 'rejected'
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > never interleaves keep-alive silence with a segment's speech frames
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× twilio.tts-segments.test.ts > cancels every remaining segment when a barge-in aborts playback
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× telephony-tts-segments.test.ts > resolves inline TTS directives once for the whole reply, not per segment
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
× telephony-tts-segments.test.ts > splits the resolved spoken text, so a directive block is never divided
  -> expected 1 to be greater than 1
```

Read honestly: four of those six are the structural precondition `expect(chunkTelephonyReply(text, CAP).length).toBeGreaterThan(1)`, i.e. an 813-character reply collapsing to **one** synthesis request. That is the defect stated directly, but it is a structural observation rather than a timing one. The substantive failure is `expected 'resolved' to be 'rejected'`: without the bound, a synthesis timeout part-way through a reply resolves as though playback had succeeded.

The guard was restored from a backup taken before editing, and `grep` afterwards confirms no neutralisation survives in any changed file.

### Shipped upstream coverage is preserved, not replaced

Every case in `providers/twilio.media-stream.test.ts` drives a short text — `"Timeout me"`, `"Dropped audio"`, `"Empty audio"`, `"hello"`, `"first"`/`"second"`, `"cancel me"`/`"play next"` — each of which is a single segment under the cap. So `expect(f.synthesize).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` and `.toEqual(["first", "second"])` still hold unchanged. No shipped assertion was deleted or weakened; the only edits to that file are two additive `prepareSpeech` stubs on existing fakes.

### Gates, on this exact head

| Gate | Result |
| ---- | ------ |
| `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/voice-call/src` | `All matched files use the correct format.` |
| `oxlint extensions/voice-call/src` | `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.` |
| `check:max-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` | `max-lines ratchet OK: 702 grandfathered suppressions.` |
| `check:assertion-safety --base upstream/main` | `assertion SAFETY ratchet OK: 3206 files, 8257 grandfathered assertions.` |
| `vitest run` on the 8 affected files | `Test Files 8 passed (8)` / `Tests 62 passed (62)` |

The line-cap ratchet's bundled env-var budget step reported `OPENCLAW_* count 476/476` here, so it was not the binding check.

The one new type assertion in the diff (`mediaStreamHandler as never` on a test fake) carries a `// SAFETY:` comment, which is why the assertion ratchet stays at its baseline.

### Pre-existing failures, separated

Running the wider `extensions/voice-call` sweep surfaces two failures in files this PR does not touch. Both reproduce identically on clean `upstream/main`:

```
× index.test.ts > voice-call plugin > registers Twilio configs with SecretRef auth tokens
× index.lifecycle.test.ts > rejects retained concrete and cold-registry A tools once B activates
  -> expected '""' to contain 'superseded'
```

### What is NOT covered by real-behaviour evidence

Stated plainly rather than papered over:

- **There is no telephony capture at this head.** The previous revision of this body carried a real Twilio trace, but it was produced by a build of the pre-port code. Presenting it as proof of this revision would be false provenance, so it has been removed rather than reused. Nothing in this revision has run against a live call.
- **The timing premise is not measured here.** That a long reply actually exceeds a given provider's synthesis timeout depends on that provider. What this PR demonstrates is the structural property that makes it fatal when it happens: one unbounded request per reply, a fixed timeout, and no audio emitted until that request completes.
- **The whole-directory suite was not run to completion locally.** The run was cut by a local time budget. The eight affected files are green, and the two pre-existing failures above were isolated individually against clean main.

I can add diagnostics behind a temporary tag, capture a redacted exact-head trace, and strip them before merge if that would settle it.

prs.title: fix(google): stop advertising unsupported Gemini filters
prs.body:
Closes #118894.

## What Problem This Solves

Gemini Web Search exposed `country` and `language` in its model-facing schema even though its runtime rejects both arguments. The schema also crosses lazy plugin loading, agent normalization/hook wrappers, metadata-free credential auto-detection, and automatic provider fallback, so removing two fields only at one call site is not sufficient.

## What This Changes

- Gemini's provider-owned schema omits unsupported `country` and `language`; crafted, stale, or legacy calls are still rejected before provider fetch.
- Core resolves the selected provider schema through the execution-compatible scoped provider loader and preserves the late-bound accessor through normalization, metadata, `before_tool_call`, and tool-definition wrappers.
- Schema publication constructs only the selected provider definition. Fallback runtimes stay lazy until the selected provider actually fails.
- Automatic fallback validates supplied arguments against each candidate's published schema. It immutably drops only undefined CLI options and the unsupported CLI-only `limit` alias; defined canonical arguments remain, and genuine provider-specific arguments are still rejected instead of being forwarded incorrectly.
- Metadata-free credential discovery remains runtime-lazy. A new optional `webSearchProviderMetadata` manifest family lets a web-search provider declare cheap `configSignals`, parallel to the existing image/video/music capability metadata, without provider-specific core code.
- Manifest credential signals now pass through the existing control-plane plugin-availability policy before they can enable schema resolution or security-audit exposure.
- Explicit provider selection keeps its provider's complete schema and continues to disable fallback. Unknown/unresolved selection retains the existing generic schema.

No web-search feature or supported provider argument is disabled.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

This PR proposes adopting `webSearchProviderMetadata` as a documented optional plugin-manifest contract for static web-search credential/config signals. The field is normalized, preserved in registry records, documented beside the parallel capability metadata families, and covered by compatibility tests.

Recommended decision: adopt the generic manifest field. It keeps external providers provider-neutral and runtime-lazy. If maintainers do not want this public contract, the alternative is to reject the field and request a narrower supported seam; this PR does not claim contributor-side approval on the maintainers' behalf.

## Regression Evidence

Focused regressions cover:

- Gemini's generated schema omits `country` and `language`, while crafted unsupported calls still fail before fetch;
- selected schema resolution uses the execution-compatible scoped loader and does not eagerly construct fallback tools;
- provider schema access remains late-bound through agent normalization and hook wrappers;
- query-only fallback succeeds for the CLI-shaped `{ query, count: undefined, limit: undefined }` input and executes with `{ query }`;
- defined canonical `count` is preserved, while actual provider-specific arguments cannot cross into an incompatible fallback;
- model-provider credential fallback is discovered from static manifest metadata without importing provider runtime;
- explicitly disabled, denylisted, and restrictive-allowlist-excluded plugins cannot enable manifest credential discovery;
- manifest normalization and registry persistence retain the new optional metadata family.

Official exact-head Actions run [30943248594](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30943248594) is the verification authority. Exact-head documentation/formatting, lint, production types, test types, prompt snapshots, plugin contracts, security, static analysis, and the other completed Node shards passed. Three nondeterministic lanes need a maintainer rerun: a Doctor test timed out at 120 seconds, the `agents-core` Vitest process was terminated after 300 seconds without output, and an unrelated TUI/PTTY shared Gateway fixture closed with WebSocket 1006 before eight dependent tests. The exact job evidence and passing counts are recorded in [this CI triage comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/118896#issuecomment-5183816840). GitHub rejected the contributor-side native failed-job rerun with `Must have admin rights to Repository`; no permissions were bypassed and no replacement workflow was created.

The repository's pinned `oxfmt@0.60.0` output for the two previously listed files was obtained in a temporary read-only fork workflow and applied exactly: [formatter run 30943092912](https://github.com/ZYV5ge/openclaw/actions/runs/30943092912). The temporary branch and workflow were deleted after the patch was retrieved.

`git diff --check` and plugin-manifest JSON parsing pass. No local dependency installation, test, or build was performed. A live credentialed Gemini provider call remains honestly unclaimed.

## Scope and Safety

- Exact head: `5b87cceb6972b815830506e163d6d8b77830326c`
- Frozen upstream base: `832459d2ae76a08f17dfdb95dad78a5db4599762`
- Surface: 23 files, +1073/-51

The change is limited to Gemini's existing provider schema, internal web-search schema/candidate handling, manifest-owned static credential metadata, preservation of a dynamic parameter accessor through existing agent-tool wrappers, documentation, prompt snapshots, and focused tests. It does not change credentials, models, Gateway configuration, workflows, dependencies, versions, or user data.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to trace the schema lifecycle, prepare tests and implementation, inspect exact-head review findings, and draft this description. All behavior and evidence claims are limited to the exact diff and linked official Actions.

prs.title: fix(sessions): degrade duplicate keyed-user dedup when the transcript index is transiently dirty
prs.body:
# PR #154904: fix(sessions) — degrade duplicate keyed-user dedup when the transcript index is transiently dirty

Repair for #152511. After the agent replies into a captured conversation turn, reply-capture writes audit artifacts with `appendMode: "side"`, which transiently marks the transcript projection index as needing reconcile. While dirty, `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchor` returns undefined. A duplicate keyed-user delivery in that window previously hit the in-memory dedup branch and hard-threw "Session transcript anchor was not returned".

The fix keeps a three-state decision:
- **(A) projection index transiently dirty** (`needs_rebuild=1`) — a benign ~0.5–10s window after a concurrent side append: degrade to an idempotent no-op (return the cached entry, no anchor) without throwing.
- **(B) index clean and the cached turn IS active** — return its canonical anchor.
- **(C) index clean but the cached turn has no active row** — another manager removed/rewrote it (stale cache): REJECT, never silently false-acknowledge a non-existent turn.

Implemented by `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchorStatus()` (single opened handle; reconcile state read before the active-join; fail-closed: only an explicitly dirty index degrades).
The canonical-adoption strong anchor constraint in `session-manager-persistence.ts`
(`result.messageId !== entry.id`) is untouched; the async user wrapper shares this decision.

## What Problem This Solves

Duplicate keyed-user message delivery after a transiently dirty transcript projection hard-throws instead of degrading idempotently. This PR bounds that into a three-state decision (benign dirty window degrades; clean-active returns anchor; clean-stale rejects), reusing the production current-turn owner so a completed/displaced/runtime-context turn is never false-acked.

## Evidence

ClawSweeper Rev4 P2 findings fixed in 251ffb39945: (1) a dirty index alone no longer degrades -- the cached turn is revalidated against the authoritative `transcript_event_identities` log in the same snapshot, so a suffix-removed cached turn still throws; (2) the reconcile probe and anchor join now run inside one read transaction instead of separate autocommits (TOCTOU closed). New regression test F covers dirty-index + deleted-identity-row -> throw.

All evidence below is from a local isolated detached worktree, Node 24, authoritative runner `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <files>` (real SQLite, not mocked persistence/transport).

- New `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` (registered in
  `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`): 8/8 passing.
  - A transient dirty (`needs_rebuild=1`) duplicate -> no throw, `appended:false`, same id, anchor undefined.
  - B clean index duplicate -> returns the existing canonical anchor.
  - C two managers: m1 writes keyed K, m2 `removeTrailingEntries` removes K, m1 re-delivers K -> throws.
  - D fresh append -> `appended:true` + anchor.
  - E async user wrapper shares the dirty degrade.
  - F dirty index but cached turn deleted from the durable log -> throws.
  - G dirty index but cached turn displaced off the canonical active path by a real branch switch -> throws.
  - H duplicate delivery inside an enclosing write transaction reaches the savepoint replay.

## Rev9 P2 resolved (head b774fd18c9f)

- Nested-safe snapshot uses runSqliteDeferredTransactionSync (savepoint-aware); test H opens the outer transaction on the SAME fixture db via {agentId, path}.

## Rev10 P2 resolved (head 395efe0e2ca)

- Dropped the handwritten max-seq recursive CTE. On a dirty projection the cached turn is now revalidated through the SAME canonical visible-path owner the projection rebuild / parent-fork / tail resolver use: `isTranscriptEntryOnActivePathInTransaction(database, sessionId, entryId)` (scans the durable event tree, selects the leaf's visible branch). No SQL or algorithm is copied; imported from the sibling internal module, not the public barrel. The clean path delegates to `readActiveTranscriptEntryAnchorInTransaction`, removing the duplicated identities⨝active⨝rewrite join and keeping the main-thread SQLite T1 callsite count at the base ratchet (database-worker ratchet OK).
- All dirty probe / current-turn / anchor reads run inside the single `runSqliteDeferredTransactionSync` nested-safe (savepoint-aware) snapshot.
- Test G now drives a REAL production branch switch: m2 appends an assistant turn after K, then `appendLeafControl({ targetId: existing-assistant, appendParentId: existing-assistant })` moves the canonical leaf back off K's branch. K's identity history is retained (not deleted). Non-vacuity: the old raw max-seq chain walk is replayed in-test and asserts `hit === 1` (would have false-acked / stays red), while the new owner rejects (throws). No `DELETE identity` / direct `leaf_event_id` edit.
- Test F deletes the durable `transcript_events` row (FK cascades identities) so K truly leaves the tree; the off-path owner rejects.
- Test H opens the SAME fixture db in an outer `runOpenClawAgentWriteTransaction` and asserts `db.isTransaction === true` and that a raw `db.exec("BEGIN")` throws `/cannot start a transaction within a transaction/` -- proving the nested tx is real and the old unconditional-BEGIN read would have failed -- while the savepoint-safe replay passes with `replay.appended === false`.

Gates on head 395efe0e2ca (Node 24, real SQLite runner):
- `session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` 8/8.
- `tsgo:core` exit 0; `db:kysely:check` 5/5; `check:database-worker-ratchet` OK (no T1 growth vs base 259033fe97); `deadcode:exports` 0 entries; oxfmt --check and oxlint (boundary guards) 0/0 on both changed files.

Inherited failures reproduced identically on the previous head b774fd18c9f (not introduced by this PR, zero suppression): `check:env-var-count` 477>476 (also on main; this PR adds 0 new OPENCLAW_* names); one gateway test-file tsgo error (`worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts` `appendMessage` on a Promise<SessionManager>); `settled-turn-finalization.provider-error.test.ts` 3 failed (provider error-string text).

## Rev11–13 correctness follow-ups (final head 4246b643e61)

ClawSweeper Rev10->Rev11->Rev12 surfaced three bounded correctness P2s, all fixed; Rev14 verdict on 4246b643e61 reports **Findings: None**, patch quality platinum hermit.

- **Rev11 (5682aec80e8) — visible-path membership was too weak.** A cached user turn K whose turn another manager completes with a *same-branch* assistant reply remains an ancestor on the visible path, so the Rev10 active-path check would have wrongly degraded it (false-ack). Added `resolveTranscriptCanonicalCurrentTurnEntryIdInTransaction`, a durable mirror of the manager's in-memory `resolveCurrentTurnEntryId`: it drives the shared `walkSessionCurrentTurn` generator up from the append cursor, applies the same traversability rules (thinking/model/custom/label/session_info/compaction + runtime-context custom_message), and returns the first non-traversable entry id (the durable canonical current turn). The dirty anchor path now degrades iff the cached entry id **equals** that resolved current turn (exact equality, not ancestor membership). New regression **G2**: same-branch assistant completes K -> reject (the old active-path check stays red, the new exact match rejects).
- **Rev12 (53ba4c3f326) — customType was stripped.** The resolver consumed `readTranscriptNavigationEvents`, whose shared `TRANSCRIPT_NAVIGATION_KEYS` projection omits `customType`, so the runtime-context discriminator was always undefined and every `custom_message` row looked like a turn boundary. Added a resolver-specific reader that projects the same navigation keys **plus `customType`** (json_set), leaving the shared projection and its other cursor consumers untouched. New regression **G3**: runtime-context metadata above a cached keyed user, dirty projection -> replay degrades (walk skips the metadata row, resolves back to K) instead of throwing.
- **Rev13 (4246b643e61) — test-only type fix.** CI's test-types stripe typechecks the test files; G/G2 manager-side assistant replies now use a complete `AssistantMessage` (`createZeroUsageFixture()`). No production change.

Gates on final head 4246b643e61 (Node 24, real SQLite runner): `session-manager.anchor-dedup-3state.test.ts` **10/10** (A–H + G2 + G3); agents-sessions test tsgo stripe clean; `tsgo:core` 0; `check:database-worker-ratchet` OK; `deadcode:exports` 0; oxfmt/oxlint 0 on changed files.

**CI honesty:** the remaining red shards are pre-existing on base/main and not in this PR's diff — `doctor-state-integrity.test.ts`, `settled-turn-finalization.provider-error.test.ts` (3), `check:env-var-count` 477>476, and the `worker-turn-launcher.claim-recovery.test.ts` gateway tsgo error. The prior anchor-dedup test-types stripe failure introduced in Rev11 was fixed in Rev13. No session/anchor/db-regression failure is attributed to this PR.

**Outstanding (per ClawSweeper, not a code finding):** after-fix production trace exercising synchronous cached replay after a real side append, subsequent assistant persistence, and stale-turn rejection (`live_verification=absent`). Supplied evidence is real-SQLite regression tests + static checks.

prs.title: fix(agents): reload durable OpenAI auth for Codex runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An embedded Codex run could reuse a stale in-memory auth-profile snapshot after Gaia's durable OpenAI OAuth profile changed. OpenAI/Codex runs now read the durable profile for each auth plan while preserving the current provider auth-pin behavior. Non-OpenAI routes retain the existing snapshot-based loader behavior.

This PR does not change model routing, the Codex transport-override compatibility check, Slack recovery, runtime configuration, or live deployment behavior.

## Evidence

- The regression creates an empty runtime snapshot plus a durable OpenAI OAuth profile and verifies the OpenAI path reloads the durable profile.
- The regression calls the production auth-store decision helper with `usesOpenAIAuthRouting: false` against an empty runtime snapshot plus a durable Anthropic profile; it verifies non-OpenAI behavior remains snapshot-based and would fail if durable reload became broad again.
- The existing OpenAI API-key provider-pin test remains green.

## Testing

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-store.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-pin.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-plan.auth-store.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`

No live runtime, install, restart, activation, or Slack request was performed.
## ClawSweeper after-fix proof

- Existing stale-snapshot regression: 3 test files passed, 6 tests passed.
- Real OpenClaw local-agent CLI proof used a fresh temporary HOME, CODEX_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, config, workspace, and agent directory.
- Provider/Codex token variables were unset; external CLI and keychain overlays were disabled; no API key was configured.
- Before starting the model process, the effective auth store contained exactly one synthetic OpenAI OAuth profile and zero ambient profile IDs. Any other profile would have aborted before a request.
- Loopback-only endpoint: 1 model request, model `proof-model`, Authorization header present, 0 embedding requests, 1 transport probe, deterministic `PROOF_OK` reply, and no startup error.
- Direct Codex contract check: the sibling auth manager caches its snapshot and exposes an explicit reload that rereads storage (read-only source check at `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs`).
- This proof used synthetic OAuth data only; no real credential, token, transcript, or live Gaia runtime was used or included.

prs.title: feat(watch): add direct Gateway conversations
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142916

Stack base: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142957

**Draft, not merge-ready.** Current signed head: `64df8e2f3db1940e230d618c2d834bcc42b91d74`, based on refreshed HTTPS parent `f5f5c1fe4185d687ffbb7d2966b443d7cd96117c` and audited main `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b`. The new main conflict is resolved and the targeted TLS production module compiles. Current-head native test, HTTPS/voice, and screenshot qualification is not complete. [Qualification run 37029162622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37029162622) remains prior-head evidence: 148 shared and 71 Watch tests passed, but simulator readiness and cleanup failed. Auto-merge remains off.

## What Problem This Solves

Apple Watch lacks on-Watch Gateway setup, direct conversations, and session-scoped approvals independent of the iPhone relay. Its existing node and voice connection do not provide operator chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add Watch-owned setup and foreground conversations on the parent's paired operator HTTPS transport. One controller owns setup, credential handoff, and node/voice/operator lifecycle coordination.

Reuse existing Watch Keychain configuration, preferences, device identity, and Gateway-scoped credentials. No configuration option, schema/protocol version, or independent-app metadata is added. The companion delivery journal stays separate.

## User Impact

- Enter an existing voice-node setup code using native Watch text input; choose an agent and conversation, read bounded history, and explicitly request chat and approval scopes.
- Send messages, stop replies, and resolve session-scoped approvals using only offered decisions after the scope upgrade is approved. Direct sends never silently fall back to **Chat via iPhone** or replay after an uncertain connection failure.
- A canonical timeout ACK selects `This run ended or was cancelled. Check history before sending again.` without changing run IDs, history, wait handling, ownership checks, or resend behavior.
- Static labels perform localized lookup; agent and conversation names remain verbatim. Approval details use constant localized format keys with unchanged authoritative scope values.
- Replacement operator grants retire active Watch voice before credential replacement. Backgrounding retires direct chat; returning reloads canonical history and subscriptions.

Initial setup retains `operator.read` and `operator.talk`. Chat adds `operator.write` and `operator.approvals`, never administrator or pairing scope.

## Evidence

### Main Refresh at fecba819

- Replayed the stack onto audited main. Main's shared TLS evaluator and this branch's request-owned HTTP failures now compose through an explicit failure-recorder callback. WebSocket acceptance retains its existing caller-owned clearing behavior. The complete resulting tree differs from the precomputed full-stack merge only in `GatewayTLSPinning.swift`; the generated native inventory was resolved from that clean merge's exact blob, without hand-editing entries.
- `git diff --check`, Swift frontend parsing of the TLS owner and test file, and commit-signature verification passed. No test assertion, timeout, permission, configuration option, or dependency pin changed.
- Targeted production compilation passed: `swift build --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --target OpenClawKit --jobs 4` completed in 26.37 seconds. The ordinary macOS execution checkout remained at `4f69548a62fbc48beb3fd15298ba1ec53a8b7d35`, with the exact resolved TLS owner and unchanged TLS test file temporarily mirrored. Their SHA-256 values were `20b515c41c4538eae85b6fc99430387170add402fc551bc7f598a45db810b80d` and `cd74a453dbaca1dd1b9d38ac70521b49c5fbcc31aaede89824b26c13900708ba`. Those mirrors were restored after execution. This is source-bound module compilation, not an exact whole-candidate build.
- The focused `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --jobs 4 --no-parallel --filter GatewayTLSPinningTests` could not execute: this host's Command Line Tools lack the `Testing` module. Its initial missing Mermaid resource was generated with the existing owner script before the module limitation was observed. No fresh native test pass is claimed.
- Autoreview returned one P1 allegation that Foundation routes HTTP trust failures past the task delegate. This was rejected for this delta after inspecting the SDK task-delegate contract and the retained [native run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37029162622) at `8b7a56096b6a4a76c1eb74b4f17a47005eb8ebcb`, Xcode 27.0/27A266a. The unchanged tests actually passed HTTP rejection attribution, both overlap orders preserving a pending WebSocket failure, and cancellation after another request rejects. The HTTP delegate and those tests are unchanged by this resolution. The review result is retained as a finding with this evidence-based disposition, not relabeled as a clean reviewer verdict.
- Required current-head checks, native HTTPS/voice completion, and fresh screenshots remain open. The separate stopped admission experiment remains stopped.

### Previous Integration Checkpoint

- At restack checkpoint `58748e8497da4f2bb757ff8337f91f35c2c7b58c`, replayed all 29 child commits from the published `6229999db3c52ff1f1c2bcbf9f600bd5dcfb9c59` onto the current published HTTPS parent `b50449929ea3f04c4de3e23be7ecf99e6440afbb`, then added two scoped repairs. All 31 resulting commits have verified signatures. Publication used an exact old-head lease. The separately signed tooling repair below is a normal fast-forward update.
- Source baseline is frozen at main `7a62f6ec184f2e2c9dbb7ddd6cc1a848e359531b`. A complete Git comparison against subsequently observed main `0272aba9cee72fce7456834887519fd9d5e703a5` found 47 additional commits and 966 changed files. The only path overlap with this 57-file parent/child stack is the generated native string inventory; its two changed Apple playback source-site entries are untouched by this stack. That is drift evidence, not a substitute for integration CI. No additional rebase was performed.
- Preserved main's consolidated Watch control surface, canonical node connection shutdown, async setup handoff, current request APIs, generated protocol package, voice-close contract, and expanded iPhone CI selection. The extracted normal Watch test lane again prepares its paired companion before booting the Watch.
- Confirmed default read-only failure: the canonical session-subscription validator rejects `includeApprovals:false`. The Watch producer now omits the opt-in without approval access and emits `true` with access. Both repaired wire shapes pass the real schema validator. The two-case native controller regression passed in the exact-head hosted run below.
- The paired-companion fixture failed in both paired and unpaired cases before restoring the owner script. All 51 focused Watch workflow cases passed after repair. The composed workflow fixture now propagates child-shell failure instead of accidentally masking it.
- Three changed Node tooling suites reported **270 passed / 1 failed**. The sole failure was a stale numeric-timeout call to main's AbortSignal-based process helper. After adapting that caller, its exact regression passed (**1 passed / 208 skipped**). The other 270 tests were not rerun without a relevant change.
- The changed-file gate passed its first 21 steps, including protocol event coverage, conflict markers, ratchets, dependency guards, formatting, scripts and all four root-test typecheck shards, coercion checks, all three dead-export scans, and script lint. The new temp-directory report is warning-only; this fixture owns and joins the deliberately held child pipes before cleanup.
- The gate stopped at native Swift lint. Pinned SwiftLint 0.65.1 was installed, but SourceKit cannot load in this host's Command Line Tools-only environment. This is **not** a full `check:changed` pass. SwiftFormat 0.63.0 separately passed all 21 changed Swift files; the v20 native-state schema guard, targeted type-aware test lint, and whitespace checks also passed.
- Broader macOS tooling: group 1 passed 123 tests; group 2 passed 542 and failed four marker-mode assertions. All four reproduce unchanged on frozen main `7a62f6ec184f2e2c9dbb7ddd6cc1a848e359531b` with the same `0600` actual versus `0644` expected result under host umask `077`. The production writer and test are unchanged by this stack. The remaining group was interrupted after repeated checkout-fixture timeouts: its isolated environment omits HOME, which the local low-data Git wrapper requires. The task-owned supervisor joined and exited 130; retained diagnostic fixtures were preserved. No full macOS tooling pass is claimed, and neither environment constraints nor assertions were weakened.
- One bounded P0 autoreview of the final committed child diff completed in two chunks with **zero actionable findings**. It excluded the stopped parent experiment and did not certify native proof.
- No new schema, schema version, protocol version, configuration option, dependency override, or compatibility fallback was added during this integration repair.

### Latest Completed Hosted Qualification

The prior `1f14ba2c` structural check was superseded when observed main `32e30e59d9a7fd1f5b3a9e9659427d45145779dd` introduced the native-i18n v3 inventory. The HTTPS parent merged that main without conflicts. This child then merged the refreshed parent, resolving its sole generated-inventory conflict with the canonical v3 serializer: 93 child sites added, 17 removed, 5,704 resulting sites and 4,488 entries. Independent read-only audit verified exact parent-plus-child semantics, all 341 Watch sites, main's two realtime-audio site relocations, stable IDs, and iOS/macOS catalog equivalence. Signature and whitespace checks passed. The combined merge-tree against that exact main now resolves to this candidate's tree `fe164e2abc3cb53ab7fbfb7b95f6fad94aaa489c`. The PR still targets its HTTPS parent. Full source re-extraction, dependency-backed tests and runtime qualification were not rerun on this refreshed head.

[Run 37029162622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37029162622) was dispatched once for exact head `8b7a56096b6a4a76c1eb74b4f17a47005eb8ebcb`, with `watch_qualification=true`. Its [qualification artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37029162622/artifacts/11238271345) has a matching `source-head.txt`.

- Shared Swift: **148 tests in 7 suites passed**, 59.922 seconds; native Watch: **71 tests in 5 suites passed**, 25.474 seconds. The separate live speech XCTest remained skipped, not passed.
- Live proof: `watchSDK=27.0`, `failureStage=watch-ready`, `errorCode=ETIMEDOUT`, 122,956 ms including termination/join, 2,611 captured output bytes, `unjoined=false`. Neither native HTTPS nor voice execution was qualified.
- The new diagnostic returned `simulatorAfterFailure={"unavailable":true}`. It does not establish the owned simulator's actual state or a pairing/runtime root cause. Shutdown also failed; `cleanupFailures=["watch-shutdown"]`, `privateStateRetained=true`. Joined command children do not prove successful simulator cleanup. No new screenshots were produced and no unchanged live-proof redispatch was made.

The following older run belongs to head `f5c5e8dc638`.

[Run 37020910671](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37020910671) is the one dispatched run for exact head `f5c5e8dc638e922ca5e6401ee5e29adb3699cf3d`: `workflow_dispatch`, `.github/workflows/ios-periphery.yml`, `watch_qualification=true`, attempt 1. The [uploaded artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37020910671/artifacts/11234527837) has a matching `source-head.txt` and retains the native xcresult, test logs, and failure receipt.

- Shared Swift: **148 tests in 7 suites passed**, 61.948 seconds of test execution.
- Native Watch: **71 tests in 5 suites passed**, 27.448 seconds of test execution; `TEST EXECUTE SUCCEEDED`. The two-case conversation subscription test passed with and without approval access. The separate XCTest `testLiveReplacementAndStopRetainCurrentPlaybackState` was **skipped** because native speech/audio qualification was not enabled; it is not voice proof. The previous universal-binary verification blocker is cleared for this run.
- HTTPS/voice: runtime selection now found the active Watch SDK **27.0**. After creating and booting its separate owned simulator, `simctl bootstatus <owned-id> -b` timed out: `failureStage=watch-ready`, `errorCode=ETIMEDOUT`, 129,808 ms including termination/join, zero captured output, `unjoined=false`. It failed before native phase build/launch and Gateway startup. Both proof verdicts remain false; this is not an observed HTTPS or voice product failure.
- Cleanup: the owned `watch-shutdown` child also ended by `SIGTERM`, with zero output. The receipt has `cleanupFailures=["watch-shutdown"]`, `privateStateRetained=true`, and no simulator-deletion attestation. Joined child processes do not prove successful simulator cleanup or runner teardown.
- Capture was skipped by the existing success gate: **no fresh screenshots**. Do not relabel the historical gallery as current-head proof. Next qualification work is to diagnose owned simulator boot/cleanup, including the paired-companion lifecycle; this receipt does not establish a root cause. No timeout increase, global simulator reset, or unchanged redispatch was performed.

The retained log and xcresult identify the passing destination as Apple Watch Series 12 (46mm), arm64, watchOS 27.0 (24R362), on Xcode 27.0 (27A266a). Its paired iPhone 18 Pro Max finished booting in 92 seconds; the subsequent Watch readiness check reported an already-booted device. This does not establish readiness of the separately created Watch. The failure receipt lacks that new device's actual state/model/pairing observation, so neither pairing nor SDK incompatibility is established as the cause.

[Diagnostic commit 8b7a56096b6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8b7a56096b6a4a76c1eb74b4f17a47005eb8ebcb) records bounded owned-device state, public Apple runtime/type identifiers, companion state, and booted-device counts after a joined boot/readiness failure. It preserves the first failure, cancellation, timeout and cleanup rules. Six observation tests plus 40 existing command-diagnostic tests passed in 9.38 seconds; the complete changed-file gate passed against `f5c5e8dc638` plus this candidate, including script/test typechecks, formatting, lint and export scans. Independent P2 review completed after restoring the review helper's runtime. Its sole finding suggested dropping observation errors from the cleanup error list; direct source inspection rejected that change because the list fences unjoined children, while `failedChild` is write-once and `failureStage` retains the original failure. A two-line invariant comment was the only subsequent edit; whitespace checks pass. Product runtime delta is zero; proof tooling adds 76 lines and tests add 80, covering the missing diagnostic observation and its privacy/ambiguity contract. This is not a boot repair or completed hosted proof.

The normal draft PR workflow skipped its native build/test work and `openclaw/ci-gate`; a successful draft scope check is not full-CI proof. The dedicated run above supplies the bounded native result, not complete qualification. The separately held backend admission experiment remains stopped and is not covered by this run.

### Observed Native Tooling Blockers and Repair

[Run 37017682342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37017682342) completed with failure on checkpoint `58748e8497da4f2bb757ff8337f91f35c2c7b58c`, using Xcode 27.0 (27A266a). Its [evidence artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37017682342/artifacts/11232808519) was downloaded and its `source-head.txt` verified against that exact SHA.

- Shared Swift: **148 tests in 7 suites passed**. The Watch app/test build reported `TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED`, but native test execution never started: the host-verification helper passed a universal Mach-O executable to `segedit`, which accepts only thin input. This is not a native Watch test pass or a demonstrated app runtime failure.
- The subsequent HTTPS/voice coordinator stopped at `watch-runtimes`, before simulator creation or Gateway startup. Its stale watchOS 26.5 pin did not match the current Xcode qualification environment. The receipt reports `unjoined:false`, `cleanupFailures:[]`, and no successful HTTPS or voice qualification. No new screenshots were captured.
- [Repair f5c5e8dc638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5c5e8dc638e922ca5e6401ee5e29adb3699cf3d) enumerates executable slices with Apple's `lipo`, extracts universal slices into private temporary files, and validates each slice's existing simulated identity before installation. It never changes the signed product or skips signing/identity checks. The coordinator now requires the available runtime matching the active Watch SDK and records that SDK in its evidence; hosted-only execution and all existing cleanup gates remain intact. [Apple's lipo implementation](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/cctools/blob/main/misc/lipo.c) owns the slice-extraction contract.
- Regression proof: the new universal-product and mismatched-second-slice cases both failed before the fix; afterward **53 focused workflow tests passed / 158 skipped**. A separate installed-Apple-tools probe reproduced fat-input rejection and successfully extracted sections from both `x86_64` and `arm64e` slices without modifying the source binary; its disposable slices were removed. This tool probe is not Watch runtime proof.
- The changed-gate plan passed its initial 15 checks, then caught a TypeScript possibly-undefined array element. After a type-safe calculation repair, script typechecking and all four root-test typecheck shards passed; the remaining coercion guard, three export scans, script lint, targeted test lint, formatting, and Bash syntax checks passed. This composite tooling validation does not replace the earlier unresolved native SwiftLint limitation. One bounded P0 review of the three-file repair found no actionable findings; the subsequent type-only calculation correction was typechecked without another review loop.
- Incremental scope: **production app/Gateway LOC unchanged; tooling +19 net; tests +18 net**. No backend admission experiment, schema, protocol, configuration, dependency, or native product behavior was changed.

### Historical Native Qualification (622)

One normal fast-forward push to this PR branch and one dispatch are verified. Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34824933376 is bound to full head `6229999db3c52ff1f1c2bcbf9f600bd5dcfb9c59`, `workflow_dispatch`, `.github/workflows/ios-periphery.yml`, `watch_qualification=true`, attempt 1. GitHub verifies the commit signature and tree. It ended in failure on September 14, 2026 at 09:22:57 UTC.

- **Shared/Watch tests:** 140 tests in six shared suites and 69 tests in five Watch suites passed, including the four-case timeout-ACK matrix and late-readback control. The separate live speech XCTest remained skipped.
- **Container repair:** build and all four phase children exited 0. Identity, negative, positive, and voice results passed the current-container run/phase/nonce, owner acknowledgement, and input-consumption gates. The final voice bridge still shows `sameCanonicalHome:false` and an unavailable original path, while the resolved current path supplied the admitted result. No old-path fallback or diagnostic-only acknowledgement was used.
- **Negative trust:** the default native `GatewayOperatorHTTPSession` rejected the untrusted certificate before owned-simulator CA installation. The stored grant stayed unchanged; no operator HTTP responses were observed.
- **Positive HTTPS:** after owned-simulator CA installation, the real Gateway and Watch-generated identity/persisted grant completed a tokenless hello without rewriting the grant. `agents.list` and `sessions.list` passed. All recorded operator responses used TLS 1.3: begin 201, frames 202, poll 200, and the same connection's completed DELETE 204. `https.ok:true` is separate from the failing voice verdict.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add paired operator HTTPS connections
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142916

Stack base: `main`, integrated through `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b`. The shared connection foundation landed via https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145950; the original https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142931 was closed without merging.

**Current qualification: draft, not merge-ready.** Signed candidate `f5f5c1fe4185d687ffbb7d2966b443d7cd96117c` refreshes the HTTPS layer onto audited main `fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b` so its Watch child can resolve the new shared TLS conflict. This parent needed no manual resolution; its complete tree equals the predicted clean merge tree `e17870062aebcf0727e8ab92b9570941d637f9b6`. Earlier runtime validation remains bound to its recorded heads, not this refresh. Required exact-head checks, security-owner disposition, and the held admission qualification remain outstanding. No admission experiment was retried.

## What Problem This Solves

Already-paired watch clients need direct conversation and approval access over HTTPS without duplicating Gateway authentication or requiring an ordinary WebSocket connection.

This is the Gateway transport layer of the phone-optional watch program. The native Watch conversation client remains separate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142967.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add bounded, in-memory operator connections at `<basePath>/api/operator/connections`. Begin returns a challenge; later HTTP requests carry ordinary Gateway frames, ordered submission sequences, and cumulative output acknowledgments through the shared connection and RPC owners.

Admission requires a signed, already-paired device and explicit device-token authentication. The scope ceiling is read, write, approvals, and Talk. Shared secrets, bootstrap credentials, ambient proxy authentication, administrative scopes, and pairing scopes do not replace that contract. Existing method authorization, device invalidation, profile binding, and request lifetime owners remain in the canonical path.

Each request retains its prepared ingress through awaited work. Retired authenticated output is discarded. Poll cancellation does not cancel accepted RPCs; an uncertain submission is retryable only within the same logical connection. Rejected connections retain their per-IP capacity charge until final removal. Expiry, termination, and failed delivery settle outstanding callbacks.

## User Impact

Already-paired clients can carry conversation and approval requests over HTTPS. HTTPS is required except on direct loopback. An IP or forwarding-policy change requires reconnecting; seamless network handoff is not claimed.

This does not provision watch credentials, redeem setup codes, add configuration options, change persistence or protocol versions, or enable independent-app metadata. Connection keys, queues, and sequence state are ephemeral. Native UI, physical-watch, and background qualification remain separate.

## Main Integration

- Current refresh: [f5f5c1fe418](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5f5c1fe4185d687ffbb7d2966b443d7cd96117c) integrates [fecba819ef2e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/fecba819ef2e67952e52896501278dc9bee72d4b). Complete-tree equality and `git diff --check` passed. The parent and child were published together with exact-head leases; auto-merge remains off. No fresh parent runtime test pass is claimed.
- Previous refresh: [38c10d27592](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/38c10d27592d43b3f33a3f78a0289ecb0e3c3640) merges observed main [32e30e59d9a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/32e30e59d9a7fd1f5b3a9e9659427d45145779dd). Its tree `cb18bbb3d5c4c0bb12a06b1c59ef85cc886cf880` exactly matches the conflict-free merge-tree prediction; signature and whitespace checks passed. This parent refresh is required for the downstream Watch child's real native-i18n v3 conflict, not cosmetic drift. No new transport behavior, security verdict, admission experiment, or current-head runtime pass is claimed. Subsequent bullets describe earlier integration history.
- October 2 drift check: main was audited through `0272aba9cee72fce7456834887519fd9d5e703a5`, 47 commits and 966 changed files after the frozen base. The combined 57-file HTTPS/Direct Watch stack overlaps only the generated native string inventory, with no overlap between changed entry IDs. `git merge-tree --write-tree` for this HTTPS head and that exact main SHA completed without conflicts, producing tree `a8f517381c8461cb266836acdecd0b20c1fd582d`. No branch rebase or merge was performed. This is source/mergeability evidence, not behavior, CI, or held-qualification proof; the outstanding boundaries remain unchanged.
- Replayed only the HTTPS layer onto the audited main revision. Kept the current client registry, preauth queue, request-context, profile/policy, worker-setup, and request-lifetime APIs.
- Preserved main's byte-backed JSON text delivery. Both string and Buffer frames use the same HTTP delivery/ACK path; the WebSocket adapter retains `binary: false` for Buffer-backed text.
- Grouped shared transport startup in `server-startup-connections.ts`. Both handlers attach before listening, and heavy transport imports remain lazy. The retired `server-ws-runtime.ts` adapter is not restored.
- Fixed a reproduced shutdown stall: an unpolled startup rejection retained a tracked delivery callback, while HTTP cleanup was registered after the connection drain. The connection-dependent sidecar now retires HTTP delivery before that drain. No timeout increase or polling workaround was added.

Production: +1,228/-191 (net +1,037); tests: +1,255/-0; docs: +128/-1. Production growth supplies the new bounded HTTP transport and its integration with existing owners. No policy baseline or exemption was weakened.

## Evidence

The focused tests, build and static checks below predate the current main refresh. They are retained as source-bound historical evidence; fresh exact-head qualification remains required.

- Before the shutdown fix, the real-server regression failed because `server.close()` did not settle until fixture cleanup forcibly terminated the pending transport. After the owner-ordering repair it passed.
- At `fa7aaad7fd116e68a993f0aafa1da653a4a0b739`, six focused files passed 46 tests with one host-network skip (`127.0.0.2` is not bindable). Coverage includes real HTTP requests, sequential scope upgrades and chat/approval effects, established-connection revocation, cancellation, replay, Buffer delivery, startup, and shutdown. Reply generation is stubbed; approval fixtures do not execute commands or deliver externally.
- Final `b50449929ea3f04c4de3e23be7ecf99e6440afbb` changes only the regression spy's argument lookup from that run. The exact-head shutdown regression passed again (14.15 seconds including its wrapper), and the Gateway-server test type graph passed. The assertions and production tree are unchanged.
- The selected static checks passed across the initial run and scoped retries: core types, all 27 test-type graphs, graph boundaries, formatting, ratchets, dependency/plugin guards, dead-export scans, changed-file lint, native schema guard, runtime import cycles, sidecar/media guards, and webhook/pairing guards. The initial run stopped at spy-style lint failures; those were repaired, and all nine remaining plan steps passed. The complete pipeline was not restarted from the beginning.
- `pnpm build` passed on exact head `b50449929ea3f04c4de3e23be7ecf99e6440afbb` in 8m 47.2s, including runtime bundles, native protocol generation, declarations, built-module load checks, SDK exports, and the Control UI build.
- One scoped autoreview at `6f80d5712e5543925e62d7aed4e0f49e33f7d491` returned no P0 findings. Only test-observation lint cleanup followed; production is byte-identical. This review does not qualify the held admission experiment or clear the security-owner request.
- The eight local integration commits have valid signatures. Added source was checked for private path and endpoint literals; public evidence excludes local paths and credentials.

The current focused runs do not explain the historical `sessions.create`/`sessions.delete` fixture timeouts recorded on `79ac553afc522863f453308687bfbb446f188c2a`. No assertion of flakiness or retrospective root-cause repair is made.

### Remaining Qualification

- The previously held verification-to-registration admission qualification remains unexecuted. Established-connection revocation and shutdown tests do not prove it. No reproduced defect or passing result is claimed for that gap.
- The latest ClawSweeper review requests security-operations owner disposition of the bounded transport contract and missing admission proof. No completed owner acceptance or waiver is recorded.
- Required hosted `openclaw/ci-gate` must pass on the published head. Local checks are not a substitute.
- Native Watch onboarding, direct conversation, delayed-hello, physical-device, and background proof belong to the downstream client work.

Rank-up disposition: the requested admission evidence and security-owner acceptance remain open, not silently skipped. This body refresh records only the completed main-integration and lifecycle proof. The PR stays draft.
