prs.title: fix(compaction): stop a failed summary audit from leaving a session permanently uncompactable
prs.body:
Related: #120162
Related: #138416

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long sessions becoming permanently uncompactable when a small model repeatedly fails the safeguard summary audit or required facts cannot fit the summary budget.

## User Impact

OpenClaw commits the best available bounded summary and continues the session. It marks the compaction record as degraded, keeps a degradation warning in `/status` for that history, and always displays a notice—even with `notifyUser: false`—that older details, exact identifiers, or pending requests may be missing. The notice suggests resending important context, `/new`, or a larger model.

**Maintainer decision (Peter Steinberger, 2026-10-10): accept marked lossy fallback for exhausted quality audits and infeasible retention, including manual compaction.** Preservation is best-effort on this path. Complete messages remain in the stored transcript, but facts omitted from active context are not automatically recovered by later summaries. This introduces no configuration switch or database schema migration. Existing installations use the same behavior after updating; older versions ignore the additive quality metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancelling a failed audit leaves the context at the same size, so every later compaction can fail again. The safeguard now keeps the generated candidate with the fewest audit failures, reuses it if a corrective generation fails, and preserves as much request, identifier, and split-turn context as the existing budget permits. An incomplete structured summary is normalized without discarding its generated facts. Caller cancellation remains terminal; missing models, credentials, and an initial generation failure keep their existing error paths.

The transcript writer projects only committed degraded boundaries into session metadata, so stale bookkeeping cannot erase the warning. A fresh session lifecycle clears it. Completion events and recovery receipts carry the same committed details through manual commands, automatic compaction, and notifications. Imported histories conservatively retain the warning if they contain a degraded boundary.

This preserves @amittell's original contribution and commits, merges current main instead of rebasing, and reconciles the merged CJK fitting fix. The two documentation findings are resolved: request retention is best-effort under constrained budgets, and caller abort signals are distinguished from provider-local timeouts.

## Evidence

Native Ollama `llama3.2:latest`, an 8,192-token context, 48-token model output cap, two quality attempts, and isolated synthetic history through the public `sessions compact` CLI and Gateway:

- Main `5c7004136d9c`: both attempts returned `ok: false`, `compacted: false`, and `Compaction safeguard finalized summary failed quality checks.` The log reports missing sections/identifiers; after repeating the command the original ten messages remain with zero compaction records. CLI wall time: 9.14 s, then 5.01 s.
- Main regression: the candidate's summary-budget test fails both lossy-recovery cases with `{ cancel: true }`; the affordable CJK case passes. Cold wrapper wall time: 74.55 s.

Candidate `6def8754a71a` merges main `76a282c7a1c6` to include the upstream typecheck and mock-isolation repairs. The compaction owner is unchanged by that second merge.

- **Exact candidate `6def8754a71ae44bd09f2982661573b62e1f6ab1`**: the same failed audit commits a degraded boundary, reduces active history from 296 to 250 estimated tokens / ten to five messages, prints the warning with `notifyUser: false`, and shows `Compactions: 1 · degraded history` through real `/status`. The same native Ollama session then answers “A ripe banana is typically yellow.” Both durable markers remain after continuation. Compaction: 8.40 s CLI / 2.857 s runtime; correct continuation: 5.24 s CLI / 1.386 s runtime. Its first continuation completed but produced tool-shaped text; one explicit no-tools follow-up answered correctly without changing model or configuration. This is a response-quality limitation, not an audit-cancellation loop.
- 305 tests passed across 14 focused files (323.38 s total wrapper wall time, individual commands below); all 17 persistence/direct-notice/CJK cases were rechecked on the final merged head (85.35 s). The three CJK/budget cases pass on the candidate; main failed the two recovery cases. This includes SQLite reopen, warmed metadata reads, stale bookkeeping, same-ID/new-lifecycle reset, caller abort, provider-local timeout, direct callers without dispatchers, and command/event notices.
- Full `pnpm build` passed on the exact final head (4m 59.8s). It emits the same non-gating UI startup-size warning seen in the main control build; this PR changes no UI bundle source.
- Core typecheck and the agents-other, agents-sessions, messaging, commands, and other test graphs passed. Targeted type-aware lint passed. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc, and plugin-inventory guards passed.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P2 on `6def8754a71a`. The first review caught an obsolete fallback fixture; it now asserts retained generated facts instead of discarded template text.
- Prompt snapshots regenerated with no diff: static prompt token delta **0**. Docs listing, MDX/format checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

Production **+477/-219 (net +258)**; tests/support **+1060/-473 (net +587)**; docs +40/-19. Production growth is needed for committed degradation/status state and complete mandatory-notice delivery across manual, automatic, preflight, and direct-return paths. Existing presentation owners are reused; discarded fallback scaffolding and duplicated exact-artifact fixtures were removed. The stored flag is additive session metadata in the existing SQLite owner; no schema/version/configuration change.

<details>
<summary>Focused test cost</summary>

Commands: `TMPDIR=<isolated-temp> node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`.

| File | Passed | Wall time |
|---|---:|---:|

| `compaction-safeguard.degraded-fallback.test.ts` | 5 | 39.89 s |
| `compaction-safeguard.summary-budget.test.ts` | 3 | 10.62 s |
| `compaction-safeguard.test.ts` | 62 | 21.62 s |
| `compaction-safeguard-quality.test.ts` | 4 | 2.98 s |
| `compaction-safeguard-tool-failures.test.ts` | 3 | 2.26 s |
| `compact.hooks.test.ts` | 82 | 50.36 s |
| `agent-session-compaction.degraded-reload.test.ts` | 2 | 15.71 s |
| `agent-session-compaction.provider-boundary.test.ts` | 5 | 13.00 s |
| `agent-session-compaction.test.ts` | 17 | 17.78 s |
| `agent-runner-execution-compaction.test.ts` | 9 | 33.04 s |
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 66 | 67.01 s |
| `agent-runner.direct-replies.test.ts` | 12 | 26.02 s |
| `sessions-compact.test.ts` | 9 | 3.66 s |
| `status-message.test.ts` | 26 | 19.43 s |

Wall time includes cold compilation/imports. The persisted-reload cases exercise the actual SQLite writer and reopen path; most pure safeguard test bodies take milliseconds. Existing hook and reply suites retain their established coverage and setup. Exact-head CI completed with 62 successful jobs; the three failing jobs took 148 s, 352 s, and 503 s. They fail inherited native-binding tests, as detailed below; these are whole-job wall times, not incremental test cost.
</details>

### Review and inherited CI

Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P2 on this exact head. [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130393#issuecomment-5431244544) has **Findings: None** and acknowledges the approved product decision and both documentation fixes.

Maintainer-approved proof limitation: additional Telegram Test Server, latest-stable upgrade, and data-compatibility runs are deferred; exact-head native Ollama/Gateway behavior and real SQLite reopen/stale-write/reset coverage are supplied above.

[Exact-head CI run 38098684939](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38098684939) finished **failure**, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Build, production/test types, lint, and baseline-ratchet jobs passed. Each failed test family was then reproduced without this PR's changes in a clean detached main checkout at `76a282c7a1c6ca958517ce15f13e17371c14be11`:

- `test/canonical-descendant.integration.test.ts`: the full file in original order fails the same 70 initialization/rollback binding cases; 4 pass. Main control wall time 107.53 s. prs.title: feat(huggingface): support device-code login and token refresh
prs.body:
Related: #163235

## What Problem This Solves

Hugging Face inference users with a public OAuth app cannot sign in through OpenClaw or refresh the resulting credentials automatically.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw models auth login --provider huggingface --method oauth`, enter your public client ID, and authorize the displayed code from any browser. Only `inference-api` is requested. Existing API-key setup remains available.

An operator-owned public OAuth app without a client secret is required. Access-only grants expire and require re-login; refreshable grants use the existing auth-profile lifecycle. No client registration, hosted metadata, configuration schema, or new dependency is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Device authorization works on remote hosts without an inbound callback. The provider owns the protocol and uses existing auth profiles for expiry, client identity, and refresh-token rotation. Catalog discovery uses the existing OAuth-aware resolver so an OAuth-only account can discover models.

This is the usable base of a two-part stack. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163244 exposes the same method in onboarding and should land second.

## Evidence

- Focused plugin tests: 20 passed (`pnpm test extensions/huggingface/oauth.test.ts extensions/huggingface/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), 72.13 seconds wall including cold compiler preparation; new device/lifecycle cases use fake timers. CI timing is not yet available.
- Final provider suite: `pnpm test:extension huggingface --maxWorkers=1` passed all 30 tests in four files, 62.03 seconds wall, including existing discovery/proxy behavior.
- Covered public-client request scope, pending/slow-down/transient polling, both HF verification hosts, cancellation, caller revocation, device/token expiry, access-only storage, refresh-token preservation/rotation, redacted errors, and OAuth catalog credentials.
- Provider documentation passed the scoped MDX check. Independent review findings were addressed with regression coverage.
- Scoped type-aware lint, provider package-boundary typecheck, provider test-fixture typecheck, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Validation ran in an isolated checkout with independently owned frozen dependencies. Broad repository gates were not run.
- Live proof gap: no operator-owned public OAuth client ID or authenticated grant was available. No real login, refresh, or inference request was performed; mock boundary proof is not production-readiness proof.

Contract references: [HF public-client/device OAuth](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/oauth), [HF device/refresh implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/blob/main/src/huggingface_hub/utils/_oauth_device.py).

prs.title: feat(agents): add warn-only usage budgets
prs.body:
## Current-head repair status

Current source head `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a` addresses both actionable P2 review findings:

- Budget warnings now use the canonical successful terminal source-delivery contract. A completed, non-aborted terminal block stream can be followed by one standalone warning; reasoning-only, commentary-only, status/progress-only, message-tool-only progress, and aborted streams do not claim or emit one.
- The documented per-agent override now uses canonical keyed `agents.entries` with an explicit default agent.

An independent static review found no remaining issue in these two repairs. The contributor head was not executed locally because it is untrusted; exact-head secretless GitHub CI is required. The existing runtime proof below is from an earlier head and must not be treated as proof of this repair.

The maintainer product decision on accepting the public `usageBudget` config/default surface remains open. This source-only head also still conflicts with current `main` in generated config baseline count/hash files; those generated files were deliberately not guessed or hand-edited.

Related to #42475.
Closes #113481.

AI-assisted: this change was implemented with Codex assistance. I reviewed the code and understand the implementation. No agent transcript is included.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw exposes estimated session cost, but an unattended agent cannot proactively tell its owner when known daily spend crosses a meaningful amount. The broader #42475 design covers enforcement before provider dispatch; this PR implements only its informational `warn` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the standalone `modelSpend` implementation with a smaller consumer of existing usage infrastructure:

- `agents.defaults.usageBudget` and per-agent `usageBudget` accept a daily USD interval with `action: "warn"`.
- Per-agent `{ usageBudget: { enabled: false } }` disables an inherited default.
- Existing per-session cost rollups provide the estimated spend total; this PR adds no spend ledger or SQLite table.
- Only the warning watermark is stored in the existing per-agent `cache_entries` table.
- The current session rollup refreshes after primary and queued follow-up runs. A one-time background warm includes the agent's other sessions.

Warnings repeat at each crossed multiple, reset at 00:00 UTC, and are appended only to direct replies for an owner-authorized sender. Delivery and accounting are best-effort. Unpriced calls are excluded from the known total and called out in the warning.

This mode never blocks a model call, pauses an agent, switches models, rotates credentials, or changes retry/fallback behavior. Pre-dispatch reservations and enforcement remain in #42475 / #104060.

## User Impact

Operators can opt an agent into daily spend warnings without changing model execution:

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      usageBudget: {
        daily: { usd: 10 },
        action: "warn",
      },
    },
    entries: {
      local: { default: true, usageBudget: { enabled: false } },
    },
  },
}
```

At known UTC-day spend of $23.50 with a $10 interval, the next eligible owner DM receives the $20 threshold warning. Repeated replies do not duplicate that threshold; later spend can trigger $30.

## Evidence

Current exact head: `2283dc79eebccced7ccdb06c4a0a2c5a6b96924a`.

### Prior-head runtime proof

This proof predates the current head and does not cover the streamed-warning repair below. An ignored proof runner started an isolated real Gateway child and the real `qa-channel` inbound dispatch/reply pipeline at the exact head above. Only the model provider was deterministic (`mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna`). The Gateway used this effective policy:

```text
agents.defaults.usageBudget.daily.usd=10
agents.defaults.usageBudget.action=warn
commands.ownerAllowFrom=["qa-channel:qa-owner"]
channels.qa-channel.allowFrom=["qa-owner"]
```

The isolated `qa` agent was seeded with one current-UTC-day assistant usage entry costing `$12.34`. The first owner turn warmed the real SQLite cost rollup. The proof then sent a non-owner direct turn followed by an owner direct turn. Redacted QA bus evidence:

```text
exact head: 2fa01bd6688b44d6fa4720e1f9dabefa27016d77
runtime: isolated real Gateway child + qa-channel inbound dispatch + mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_WARMUP_OK"
cursor=2 kind=outbound-message text="OWNER_WARMUP_OK"

inbound  sender=qa-guest chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: NON_OWNER_OK"
PASS     no outbound reply and no usage warning

inbound  sender=qa-owner chatType=direct text="Reply exactly: OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=5 kind=outbound-message messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="OWNER_ALERT_OK"
cursor=6 kind=message-edited  messageId=04616fda... replyToId=c314b44c... text="Usage budget warning: Known spend is at least $12.34 UTC today, crossing $10.00. Warn-only mode; model calls continue. 1 unpriced model call is not included."

PASS model reply completed before warning delivery
PASS warning remained scoped to the authorized owner direct route
PASS warn-only mode did not prevent the model call or reply
```

`qa-channel` maps a second final payload onto an edit of its existing preview, so the event timeline is the durable evidence: the model reply and warning have the same message ID and `replyToId`, and the reply event precedes the warning edit. The redacted local artifacts are under `.artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-113548-usage-budget-proof-2fa01bd/`.

The prior Feishu capture targeted the superseded standalone accounting design and is intentionally not claimed as proof for this head.

### Automated proof

- Exact-head CI run [30631148220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30631148220) completed with 71 jobs and no failures.
- Structured Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings and 0.88 correctness confidence.
- Focused Vitest proof passed 119 tests across five focused files:
  - `src/agents/usage-budget-warning.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/config/zod-schema.usage-budget.test.ts`: 3/3
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: 59/59
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts`: 5/5
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts`: 47/47
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` emitted successful format, config metadata, API baseline, boundary, dead-code, typecheck, lint, database-first, import-cycle, and guard stages. Blacksmith CLI was unavailable, so this used the repository's trusted-source local fallback; GitHub CI remains the exact-head broad gate.
- Config baseline generation/check passed with the intentional core schema count update.

### Scope reduction

| Version | Files | Additions | Deletions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous standalone implementation | 37 | 1544 | 93 |
| Current warn-only slice | 20 | 615 | 22 |

Removed scope includes provider allowlists, provider-call instrumentation, custom spend tables, timezone configuration, compaction accounting callbacks, cross-channel delivery plumbing, and the standalone nano-USD ledger/tests.

## Relationship to #42475

This is the non-enforcing warning action from #42475, using the same `usageBudget` configuration namespace and UTC daily window direction as draft #104060. It intentionally leaves hard limits, reservations, concurrency control, monthly budgets, provider admission, and status/doctor surfaces to the broader enforcement work.

prs.title: fix: configured model fallbacks are skipped when the primary model times out
prs.body:
Related: #141838, #103697
Consolidates #165844. Thanks @von8794 and @alkor2000; both contributor histories are preserved through normal merges, with explicit coauthor credit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a slow primary model exhausts its timeout and the configured fallback never answers. A separate diagnostic-watchdog path could expire the parent reply before the model attempt's recovery policy ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Peter's October 10, 2026 maintainer decision is **per-attempt budgets**: each configured fallback receives its own `timeoutSeconds`. Replay-safe prompt timeouts advance to fallback, the Gateway renews its reply deadline, and the CLI waits for the Gateway's final outcome instead of applying another whole-run timeout.

The diagnostic watchdog interrupts an eligible active model request before expiring its parent reply. Phase, committed-outcome, replay-safety, settlement, and user-cancellation checks remain authoritative. A producer that ignores interruption cannot retain queue capacity indefinitely: the existing lane owner reclaims it after 30 seconds, and repeated recovery no longer shields an aborted parent. Queue release does not falsely certify physical producer settlement.

No new configuration, schema, dependency, or protocol changes. Documentation now explains per-attempt timeout semantics and independent outer deadlines such as cron.

## User Impact

Configured fallbacks can recover from eligible primary timeouts. Total elapsed time can exceed one timeout budget. User Stop cancels the entire chain; unsafe replay and non-prompt phase timeouts remain terminal.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway, native Ollama, `qwen3:4b` primary behind a 45-second delay proxy, `llama3.2:latest` fallback, 20-second attempt budget. Main `5c7004136d9c` stops with `agent_run_terminal_timeout` and sends no fallback request. Candidate returns `LOCAL_TIMEOUT_PROOF` from Llama; the fallback's recorded model duration is 4.169 seconds. CLI wall time is 31.70 seconds including startup.
- Full-budget live proof through the same native-Ollama Gateway path: 180s per attempt, primary held for 210s, fallback held for 165s. The primary request is cancelled after 179.290s, the fallback completes after 165.003s, and the CLI receives `recovered` (352.66s total wall time). The reply survives beyond the former parent deadline plus grace and maintenance interval. Tool Search and Code Mode are disabled for this plain-text probe.
- Real `chat.send` watchdog proof using local Ollama through `/v1/chat/completions`: a proxy forwards the first genuine SSE event, then holds model data for 480s while sending comment keepalives. The standard loopback hostname `localhost.` selects the self-hosted 300s idle/600s progress policy; the attempt budget is 900s with no provider override. Main aborts the parent after 395s and starts the primary again, without fallback. Candidate retains the original run through watchdog interruptions and the existing same-model retry window, then selects Llama and publishes its final reply after about 783s. Llama interpreted the uppercase proof token as a tool name before answering; this proves recovery and delivery, not exact-token instruction compliance. The plain native-Ollama proof above delivered its exact token.
- Live user cancellation: SIGINT after observing the actual primary HTTP request closes that request after 82ms and records `caller_signal_aborted`; no fallback request follows.
- Seven composed regression cases: the two eligible timeout cases fail on main because fallback is never attempted; five phase/cancellation/replay safety cases pass. Candidate's complete embedded fallback file passes all 32 cases (76.07s Vitest, 90.49s wrapper; no per-test Gateway boots).
- Gateway deadline/lifecycle, CLI cancellation, watchdog stream custody, phase, model-call lifecycle/events, lane-control, and diagnostic-recovery focused suites pass. Reclamation negative control fails exactly when the parent-abort guard is removed. The focused deadline/CLI/reclamation rerun passes in 56.47s wall; additional five-file owner/sibling selection passes in 71.36s wall. Cold combined setup took 1115.60s, including the first complete compiled-runtime build; that initial selection exposed the contributor deadline fixture's now-fixed auth-store isolation requirement.
- `pnpm build` passes (363.38s). Scoped type-aware lint and four affected test type graphs pass. Docs MDX/format checks and `git diff --check` pass. Max-lines, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race, config-docs, and plugin-inventory checks pass.
- Core typecheck fails on unchanged `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts:519` (`env` unused); the same command reproduces it on pinned main. `check:changed` reaches the mock-export ratchet and fails on unchanged `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection-placement.test.ts:56`; the same ratchet fails on pinned main. These are inherited failures, not passing gates. Upstream main has since fixed them in `243b6dbf63d2` and `00e095399b20`; hosted CI must still pass for this PR head.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the committed branch is **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**. ClawSweeper on the prior head reported no findings or Before merge items; the Stop-owner failure is now repaired by the main integration below.

Production: **+344/-144 (net +200)**. Tests/support: **+986/-240**. Docs: **+31/-26**; exact mock baseline shrinks by one. A neutral production diff was not reached: active-call identity, phase-safe interruption, and the Gateway/attempt deadline handoff require explicit lifecycle state. The consolidation removes redundant deadline APIs/comments and keeps one existing reclamation timer rather than adding a competing timeout owner.


### Stop-owner repair integration

prs.title: improve: keep latest commentary visible in progress draft headers
prs.body:
Related: #132781

## What Problem This Solves

When newer work lines evict model commentary from a bounded progress draft, the latest model-authored status disappears with them. This PR keeps the latest completed preamble available as a headline independently of the rolling history.

## User Impact

Progress drafts retain the current model-authored status above the work history. Where `streaming.progress.commentary` is supported and enabled, a completed preamble is both a headline candidate and a bounded history entry. Compact previews can display both; Slack Block Kit cards keep their existing deduplication of matching narration/history text. No configuration keys or channel narrators are added. Matrix and Mattermost retain their existing configuration surface and do not expose the optional commentary setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared compositor stages headline and commentary changes together before publishing, including keyed retractions. Incomplete preambles do not replace the last completed text. Current-main startup, final-delivery, quiet-mode, and Telegram ownership rules remain intact. Telegram dispatch and adopted action-edit snapshots both retain authored history when the existing commentary option is enabled.

### Narration interaction

- A fresh completed preamble has headline priority for 20 seconds; narration received during that window is retained.
- At expiry, retained narration takes over, otherwise a retained plan explanation can take over. Without either fallback, the preamble remains visible.
- A distinct new preamble can regain priority. Existing identity/deduplication rules remain unchanged.
- Headline selection neither reorders commentary history nor exempts it from `maxLines`.

## Evidence

Current head: [cdfa980c158](https://github.com/MertBasar0/openclaw/commit/cdfa980c158f4eae91454d00f890851b80b29244), incorporating main `553c6bde778c0c55b7418a5908d5fdeef735cf82`. All six local merge conflicts were resolved. The following evidence supersedes the previous-head validation summary.

- The final focused repository-wrapper run passed all four shards with `--maxWorkers=1` in **168.18 seconds**: Telegram dispatch HTTP **29/29** (89.54 s), Telegram action-edit HTTP **9/9** (36.76 s), shared compositor suites **63/63** (4.23 s), and the complete Slack preview-fallback suite. Other affected boundary runs passed: Discord process draft progress **18/18**, Discord REST draft preview **11/11**, Telegram progress lifecycle **14/14**, Matrix visibility **2/2**, and streaming/progress helpers **37/37**. Hosted CI time for this head is not yet measured.
- The two commentary-enabled Telegram action-edit variants failed before forwarding the existing account commentary setting, then passed after the fix. A dispatch negative control also failed the four enabled-commentary reasoning variants when forwarding was omitted. The correct source was restored before final proof.
- All six freshness-order/commentary combinations passed. The independent review's suggested startup/expiry P2 was rejected after inspecting the unchanged startup owner, which already schedules expiry. No speculative scheduling change was introduced. A fresh independent diff review of the final behavioral patch completed `scoped-clean` with no P0–P2 findings; this is not independently executed runtime or live-channel proof.
- Core production, all 27 core-test type graphs, extension production/test types, both full lint lanes, formatting, and the other 35 planned diagnostics passed. **The aggregate changed check remains failed:** the environment-variable budget is 476 while pinned main and this candidate both contain the same 477 names, with no additions or removals. No budget, ignore, suppression, or dependency override was added. The diagnostic continuation is not presented as a green aggregate gate. A full global test run and build were not rerun.
- The previous-head CI task-progress failure belonged to the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime subsequently removed by [#159179](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159179). Its retired test was not restored or described as passing. The gateway teardown race was addressed upstream by [#153302](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153302); the unchanged current-main reset suite passed **20/20** after integration. Obsolete Telegram test copies were removed only after preserving their six reasoning/preamble variants and two atomic-publication cases in the canonical HTTP suite.

## Open Review Work

- Maintainer agreement is still needed on independent headline/history presentation, as noted in the [earlier review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137696#issuecomment-5533988664). Atomic publication and narration/plan handoff are covered locally.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof and inspected before/after screenshots in both chat and this PR remain outstanding. The QA broker/login and required QA credentials were unavailable. Local HTTP mock-transport tests are boundary evidence, not live evidence or a substitute for the screenshot completion/landing gate. Team QA access or validation by an authorized team member is needed.

Related to #103697. Thanks to @mushuiyu886 for reporting the lost phase-safe recovery behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

This PR addresses phase-safe retry/fallback within #103697. It does not complete the separate bounded-settlement requirement, so it does not request automatic closure of that issue. Accepting retained physical custody remains a maintainer decision.

The diagnostic watchdog cancels a stalled model's parent reply and lane before configured recovery or fallback can finish. Eligible model recovery keeps its existing reply, lane and physical stream/write custody; explicit user cancellation, committed outcomes and current-run authority keep their existing protections.

## Current Maintenance Evidence

Head: `38e8deb827757bb45d88757b586b1d450863017b`. A normal merge preserves incoming `7236677` and pinned official main `6fd3171`. prs.title: fix: failed turns lose their "ended before a reply" notice when another session is mid-turn
prs.body:
Related: #150372

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose turn fails before any reply would see the turn
marked failed but get no explanation in the conversation, when the failure is
handled while another session's agent turn is still running.

The affected surface is durable conversation history: the "This turn ended
before a reply: ..." notice that normally explains a failed turn. On an affected
run the session status still becomes `failed`, but the transcript has no notice,
so the conversation simply stops with no visible reason. The Gateway logs
`terminal session persistence failed ... SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`.

Observed on 2026.9.4 on a subagent session whose run failed after provider
context-overflow recovery was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway's definitive lifecycle write now runs detached from any inherited
owned-transcript write context, which is what every comparable detached Gateway
and registry path already does (`update-run-notice.runtime.ts`,
`session-event-wake.ts`, `subagent-registry-run-wait.ts`,
`sessions-send-tool.ts`, and the explicit `else` branch in
`session-prompt-state.ts`).

Cause: agent events dispatch synchronously through `notifyListeners`, so the
Gateway handler executes in the emitter's async context and inherits that
attempt's writer context. Inside `withCurrentTranscript`,
`withOwnedSessionTranscriptWriterFence` spreads the inherited fence last, so it
replaces the `sessionId` and `expectedLifecycleRevision` that
`persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` had just read from its committed status
write, and adds an `expectedWriterRunId` the Gateway never supplied. That last
part is what makes the failure loud: without a writer id a fence mismatch
returns `err(refusal)`, but with one `withCurrentTranscript` throws. The status
write is awaited first and had already committed, which is why the session shows
`failed` with no notice.

Non-goal: this does not change the ownership guard itself. It changes only which
context the Gateway's own write is validated against. `chat-send-dispatch-errors.ts`
still calls `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` directly, outside this owner
seam; that path is guarded by `if (!hasActiveRun)` and is left alone here.

## User Impact

A failed turn keeps its durable explanation even when the failure is processed
while another session's turn is running. Operators reading a session after the
fact see why it stopped instead of a silent gap, and the spurious
`SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` no longer appears for writes whose
owner never actually changed.

## Validation

`src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts` (new, 9 tests),
verified against `main` at `cea9c9cb7695e8817ca72d7fcc2884d031e5ff30`.

With the source change reverted, the 6 inheritance tests fail with the exact
production error, `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer
claim changed before transcript persistence`; the 3 ownership-protection tests
pass both before and after, so they are not vacuous.

Coverage: ordinary failed run; same-session compaction followed by failure under
an unchanged owner; duplicate suppression when the run already has a durable
assistant error; repeated terminal events; a delayed retained callback that
reinstalls a settled context; the non-definitive `persist()` fallback; and three
cases that must stay rejected (cross-session report, replaced session, expired
run authority).

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-terminal-write-detach.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-lifecycle-persistence-owner.test.ts
  -> 43 passed  (6 fail without the source change)

pnpm tsgo:core                      -> exit 0
oxlint --type-aware (changed files) -> exit 0
oxfmt --check       (changed files) -> exit 0
```

The 21 pre-existing tests in `session-lifecycle-run-failure.test.ts` are

prs.title: fix(trajectory): session.ended timestamp matches model.completed before cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #102014

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trajectory exports showed `session.ended` with the same timestamp as `model.completed`, so cleanup duration looked like zero even when teardown took real wall-clock time.

## Why This Change Was Made

`session.ended` was recorded at finalize time, right after model completion, so its timestamp preceded session teardown. This PR captures the terminal payload at finalize and records `session.ended` only after attempt cleanup completes, on both the embedded runner and the Codex app-server. No new event types or exporter knobs; payload fields are unchanged, only emit timing moves from finalize into post-cleanup.

Rebased note (2026-08-26): the original branch predated the embedded-attempt lifecycle rewrite, so this was re-implemented onto current `main` (`attempt-finalize.ts` / `attempt-session-settle.ts` / `attempt-settle.ts` on the embedded side, `run-attempt-finalize.ts` / `run-attempt-cleanup.ts` / `run-attempt-turn-start.ts` for Codex). Review findings from the previous round are addressed:

- P1 "Guarantee terminal recording when Codex cleanup throws": `cleanupCodexAttempt` now records `session.ended` (captured payload, or the derived fallback) inside its `finally` block as the `codex-trajectory-terminal` step, followed by a terminal flush, so a teardown failure can no longer skip terminal recording.
- P2 "Finish startup-failure teardown before ending the session": the Codex turn-start failure path now captures the payload and records it only after binding clear, thread unsubscribe, route release, sandbox release, and shared-client lease release all finish.

## User Impact

Operators reading trajectory traces can measure real session end time versus model compute time, including cleanup latency.

## Evidence

Verified at head `0d46a743604` (current `origin/main` `636e21b1985` plus these two commits), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0.

Embedded runner tests:

```
npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-cleanup.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-settle.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-execution-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-finalize.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-result.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.media.test.ts

Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  141 passed (141)
```

Codex app-server tests (new ordering coverage: `session.ended` recorded after `thread/unsubscribe` and after the one-shot client `closeAndWait`, on both the success path and the startup-failure path):

```
npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts -t "session.ended"

Tests  2 passed | 146 skipped (148)
```

Full `run-attempt.test.ts` A/B on this machine: 13 failures are `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink *.sqlite` temp-dir cleanup flakes that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (13 failed / 133 passed baseline vs 13 failed / 172 passed with this PR's files in the same run); the failure set is identical test-for-test, so they are pre-existing Windows-only flakes, not regressions.

Revert-red check: with only the production hunks stashed, the new Codex ordering tests fail (2 failed) and the new/updated embedded cleanup tests fail (12 failed); all pass with the hunks restored.

Repo checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` all clean. `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files. `pnpm check` guards pass, including the assertion SAFETY comment ratchet (the one new field uses a typed spread instead of an `as` assertion).

### Live embedded trajectory artifact (2026-08-26, this head)

Ran on this PR head (`0d46a743604`), Windows 11, Node v24.15.0, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, embedded `openclaw agent --local --json`, model `mistral/mistral-small-latest` (no Telegram / Vertex / gateway secrets).

Runtime event order from `trajectory_runtime_events`:

```
seq=0 session.started      2026-08-26T10:52:02.672Z
seq=1 trace.metadata       2026-08-26T10:52:02.680Z
seq=2 context.compiled     2026-08-26T10:52:02.741Z
seq=3 prompt.submitted     2026-08-26T10:52:02.746Z
seq=4 model.completed      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=5 trace.artifacts      2026-08-26T10:52:05.364Z
seq=6 session.ended        2026-08-26T10:52:05.371Z
```

`session.ended` is recorded after `model.completed` and after `trace.artifacts` (7ms delta on this short no-tool turn), matching the fixed ordering: the terminal event now carries the post-cleanup wall-clock time instead of sharing the `model.completed` timestamp.

### What was not tested

- `pnpm test` full suite and `pnpm build` artifacts beyond the local build used for the live run above (targeted suites only, per above).
- Codex app-server live run (its ordering is covered by the new harness tests instead).

## AI-assisted

Yes. Authored with Cursor/Grok assistance. Human: Stan Shih (stantheman0128). Rebase onto current main, review-finding follow-up, and live proof also Cursor.

prs.title: fix(mcp): accept projected names in tool filters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp probe` prints provider-safe tool names such as `docs__read-page`, but per-server `toolFilter` rules previously matched only raw MCP names. Copying an exact name from probe could therefore hide the intended tool, especially when sanitization, App-only tools, utility tools, or reserved names introduced collision suffixes.

## Summary

- accept exact model-facing names printed by `openclaw mcp probe` in per-server include and exclude filters
- keep simple `*` globs scoped to raw MCP names
- keep model-visible raw exact names ahead of projected aliases; App-only raw names do not shadow model-visible aliases
- allocate the complete projected namespace before filtering, including resource and prompt utility tools
- preserve the planned model-facing IDs after filtered or session-denied tools disappear
- keep external/native reserved names safe without reusing a filtered tool's planned alias
- implement matching in the canonical `mcp-tool-filter.ts` owner and name allocation in `agent-bundle-mcp-names.ts`
- document the raw/projected matching contract

Fixes #98193.

## Evidence

The regressions cover:

- exact projected include and exclude matching
- raw-only wildcard behavior
- listed-tool sanitization collisions
- hidden App-only raw-name collisions
- resource/prompt utility aliases
- listed/utility duplicate raw names
- collision suffixes retained after filtering
- session-denied inventory
- external reserved names skipping every pre-filter planned alias
- a real stdio MCP runtime catalog and materialization path

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-tool-filter.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-names.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` (48 passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` (94 passed)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all changed TypeScript files (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `oxfmt --check` on all changed files
- `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>`; all completed gates passed through core typecheck, and its final core-test lane was rerun separately after the combined 600-second orchestration window ended
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (PASS)
- independent fail-closed review of projected-name, utility, session-denied, and external-reserved collision matrices

## Duplicate Check

Checked current `origin/main`, issue #98193, this PR, and open PR search for MCP probe/projected-name filter fixes. Current main centralizes raw matching in `mcp-tool-filter.ts` but does not implement the projected-name contract added here.

## Browser / Playwright

Not applicable. This changes MCP runtime filtering, materialization, CLI/config documentation, and TypeScript tests; it does not change browser or Control UI behavior.

prs.title: refactor(state): remove speculative runtime bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

State storage carries duplicate lifetime owners and defensive protocols for unsupported concurrent file/configuration changes and internal re-entry.

## User Impact

Normal storage, permissions, crash recovery, and public configuration remain unchanged. Warm executors no longer drain just because configuration changes; existing work keeps its selected physical store and idle resources expire normally. No schema, persisted data format, retention policy, or permission change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This maintainer-requested pragmatic simplification removes speculative protocols while preserving the checks at actual security, destructive-write, integrity, and concurrent-session boundaries. Committed readers use the existing reader lifecycle; avatar publication uses the native committed receipt rather than a separate settlement reader.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Config-triggered executor retirement (`1240759624a`, #165993): the reported problem was repeated opens during normal agent switching, not config changes during work. Existing executors now expire through normal LRU/TTL/shutdown; caller-owned routing selects new requests.
- Separate committed-reader lifetime (`140ae96507a`, #148868): the duplicate timer/cache and one-shot nested-reader fallback were performance scaffolding, not a reported nested-read failure. The normal read scope owns cleanup and snapshots; nontransactional nested callbacks may share it.
- Per-feature schema presence/completion WeakSets (`5f0aa4f7c56`, #133457): these duplicated the current schema-admission owner. Existing shared facts/ensurer now own installation and rollback; accepted-input durability and same-version migration stay unchanged.
- Deep private inspection-response schema (`0f748036332`, #143802): the same-build child already owns SQLite validation and emits typed results. Its response now uses one shared producer-checked type; request matching, process failure, cancellation, actual integrity checks and error serialization remain.
- Nested cold-schema read (`2fe7995d5c6`, #166183; later #167965): this repeated the same admitted-fact lookup without a new snapshot. Owner-published schema revisions still apply; external concurrent DDL remains unsupported.
- Second synchronous TTS publication lookup (`7517981b5e6`, #168002): no asynchronous work can publish between the first lookup and synchronous SELECT. Normal writer invalidation remains.
- Registration compensation (`82bff47f981`, #167687): private Set/Map insertion invokes no callbacks. Allocation failure is not a recoverable registration protocol; real maintenance registration retains its cleanup catch.
- Post-synchronous-read lifetime/schema checks (`bb7d32e55d4`, #167739; `9324ed61ca5`, #167115): these only catch an internal read callback closing or changing its own reader. Entry admission remains; such a callback may return the value it already read.
- Per-write internal DDL surveillance (`000af986dc9`, #140339): fixed repository row-write callbacks do not run arbitrary DDL. Schema changes belong to their migration owner/review, not a listener and catalog comparison around every row transaction.
- Repository column-presence WeakSet (`140d9e705ea`, #138900): shared admitted schema facts replace this competing cache; existing rollback and first-use installation remain.
- Lease-source object/function/environment surveillance (`cd2330cd69d`, #156110): internal contexts are immutable by contract; captured live authority callbacks remain. Mutating the context object mid-call is unsupported.
- Duplicate lease grant phase tracking (`cd2330cd69d`, #156110; `65bc5f6ed94`, #148859): trusted native transactions own stage order. Every effect still checks current authority; duplicate internal delivery no longer gets a separate host FSM.
- Duplicate profile grant phase tracking (`c69b8b986867`, #153508): the native transaction already owns stage order; live role, identity, and publication checks remain.
- Duplicate preference grant phase tracking (`1b66d30351da`, #157268): internal transaction/commit sequencing no longer has another host counter; coauthor/publication validation remains.
- Duplicate background grant phase tracking (`afafe747c340`, #168301): the native transaction owns sequencing; current caller authority and cancellation remain at every grant.
- Duplicate workspace grant phase tracking (`124ddc0a49fe`, #161124): removed only the host stage counter; current session, receipt, and cleanup authority remain.
- Idle operation generation (`19c6ef8d9e0`, #158848): timer identity, active operation count and owner membership already reject obsolete inspections.
- Second heartbeat-worker exit wait (`8b16e5328ec`, #157413): Node's terminate promise already joins the exit event; existing startup/renewal joins remain.
- Repeated synchronous maintenance-schema check (`f31d9d8fa92`, #121069): the same connection was checked immediately above without an await or DDL.
- Error retagging for module reload (`3ec01cec1b8`, #146741): the guarantee was tested with resetModules, not a reported deployment failure. Initial typed decoding, shared/cyclic causes, redaction and independent raw cached errors remain; decoded errors keep their original constructors across manual reload.
- Cleanup-time read readmission (`9c93bc347ce`, #160946; synthetic cleanup-abort test `e0d80000067`, #154069): the result already passed its post-query authority check. A scope changing during cleanup no longer discards that accepted value; cleanup still joins all resources. Actual startup cancellation and deletion authority remain checked at publication.
- Avatar settlement fallback reader (`7b741f627c8`, #152670; #165914): known commits now publish their native receipt even if ordinary reply delivery fails. Unknown writes are not replayed; no-overwrite SQL and current database admission remain.
- Publication-only catalog borrower leases (#166283): active prepared readers retain their real leases; late-publication witnesses and authorization revisions remain. Publication no longer keeps an otherwise unused catalog alive solely for bookkeeping.
- Fact-installation reentrancy guards (`73039895153`, #168094; #168025): current internal installers/subscribers do not issue writes. Commit receipts and all-facts-before-observers ordering remain; unsupported recursive writes are not given a separate protocol.
- Startup filesystem fingerprints (`8a3d30de7d5`, #151805): large-fleet startup was the reported issue, not out-of-band WAL/file mutation between passes. Bootstrap can reuse compatibility metadata; explicit readiness/Doctor and native write admission still validate their own contracts.
- Whole-journal fingerprint (`8a5b4af6607`, #111678; #160382): unrelated completed rows no longer abort a deletion claim. Every current pending row, operation ID, path fence, lease and destructive effect remains checked.
- Duplicate deletion predicate (`24d599636ab`, #167547): the immediately following canonical predicate checks the same agent/operation/completion fields; missing rows still explicitly refuse.
- Idle-only schema-owner recheck (`215f1c6e2a6`, #152341): idle resource inspection need not re-certify the admitted schema. Operation entry keeps its retained-cache lookup, including schema and terminal-failure admission; invalid stores still refuse writes.

Kept deliberately: real #162750 contention recovery, native/WAL shutdown joins, pending-registration concurrency (#166860), physical identity and corruption/receipt handling (#166867, #168361), credential/authorization checks, and ordinary concurrent profile preparation retries.

## Evidence

The candidate removes 814 net production source lines (plus one obsolete wrapper-inventory entry); tests are counted separately. No new lint suppressions, retries, skips, timeout increases, schema versions or dependencies.

The replacement head `eb5d1a9215f5ccc8260f7be74503ada3042e5671` completed hosted run `38100826020`. All selected jobs passed except `checks-node-changed-compact-small-10` (`114356461669`) and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` (`114358633506`); no product job was cancelled. The test job reports three 120-second timeouts in the unchanged `session-native-binding.reclamation.test.ts`, followed by an 8 GB worker heap exhaustion. All three exact timeout cases also reproduce on independently installed clean main `626eeac26d62c8ab45b09218b2216c27a9eea00d`: typed reset without/with a successor and native-veto artifact reclamation. The candidate's focused two-case probe also reproduces both timeouts (627.39s Vitest / 660.21s wrapper). Temporary instrumentation, removed afterward, confirmed native module loading and codec preparation complete before the stall; no causal regression from the committed-reader cutover was found. The underlying settlement timeout and exact cause of CI's eventual heap exhaustion remain unresolved. This is inherited-failure evidence, not a claim that the failing run is green.

- Production TypeScript and the state/infra test type graphs pass. Type-aware lint passes. Runtime import cycles: 0; Madge cycles: 0. `git diff --check` passes.
- The full unit-state run completed with 1,184 passed, 8 failed and 4 skipped across 143 files (1,407.66s Vitest; 1,599.51s wrapper). The full native-state run completed with 1,365 passed, 8 failed and 3 skipped across 88 files (6,228.90s Vitest). These are original-candidate results, not claimed clean runs.
- Investigating those failures restored the real retained-cache schema-admission guard. Tests requiring completed startup inspection now explicitly use the existing nondeferred mode. The resident no-SQL fixture stops unrelated WAL maintenance before observing the read. The physical-identity fixture applies its selected synthetic timestamps to both pathname and descriptor stats. Ordinary cancellation/deletion/security tests remain; only the synthetic cleanup-after-accepted-read abort case was removed with its guard.
- Corrected unit proof: 43 passed, 1 failed across five files (300.64s Vitest; 484.11s wrapper). The exact remaining snapshot-close marker deadline reproduced on clean current main `f3af0db8fcee85e181c86876f24740f9ec928fae`, independent installation and identical test bytes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.lifecycle.test.ts -t 'joins all snapshot children and closes their readers before close-failure settlement'` failed at line 218 with `close-0=false` (16.023s test, 241.23s wrapper). This qualifies only that exact inherited failure. The two other lifecycle deadlines and concurrent-WAL case passed the corrected probe, which does not establish their prior cause.
- Corrected native proof: 107 passed, 1 failed across six files (725.40s Vitest). All five modified native files pass, including schema refusal, typed worker errors, completed startup inspection and physical-identity checks. The unchanged Doctor ownership test reaches its 120-second timeout. The exact case also reproduced on clean main `f3af0db8fcee85e181c86876f24740f9ec928fae` using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/state/openclaw-state-ownership.test.ts -t 'refuses unauthorized Doctor admission before staging a public snapshot'` (297.83s Vitest, including cleanup). No timeout or retry change was made; the underlying timeout cause remains unknown.
- Gateway shared/personal publication boundaries: 13 passed across two files (404.02s Vitest). TTS preferences: 3 passed (63.23s Vitest). Session pending-input operations: 12 passed (222.06s Vitest). All three boundary shards pass, 28 tests total (847.78s wrapper).
- The required suppression test completed (2 passed, 1 failed; 51.62s wrapper) with only the coordinator-owned #168002 allowlist mismatch. No suppression was added by this PR.
- Isolated P2 review found and resolved the avatar receipt-stage mismatch and realistic concurrent profile-preparation retry removal. The retained-worker schema-admission regression was also restored. Rejected findings and their source evidence cover duplicate deletion predicates, unsupported external startup file changes, impossible private registration failures, internal callback DDL policing, and a second TTS lookup inside synchronous host code. The actual late-worker TTS installation continues to prefer the current host publication. Review emitted a finding; this is a resolved review, not a claim of a clean automated verdict.
- First hosted CI run `38091697654` passed 85 jobs and exposed a missed direct-caller fixture cutover in `src/config/io.health-state.test.ts`: two artificial module reloads poisoned later error-class assertions after the intentionally removed reload re-tagging. The same whole-file failure reproduced locally (7 passed, 2 failed); removing only those reloads while preserving broker reuse, live retirement, and maintenance/audit assertions passes all 9 (529.05s Vitest / 576.82s wrapper). Focused config types, lint, and a fresh P2 review pass. The required pre-push suppression check again reports only the coordinator-owned #168002 mismatch.
- The follow-up required one conflict-only rebase: main had added an exact error-identity assertion in that same test. The resolution retains the assertion. On the rebased tree all 9 health tests pass (533.72s Vitest / 591.49s wrapper), production/config types and focused lint pass, runtime and Madge cycles remain zero, and the suppression guard passes all 3 cases. prs.title: fix(telegram): cap rich message media at 20
prs.body:
Closes #129004

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram rich sends can silently lose the media and trailing content after the twentieth attachment. The shared splitter previously allowed 50, and direct edits bypassed the splitter.

## User Impact

Exactly 20 media stay in one rich message; 21 are delivered in ordered pages of 20 and 1. An edit replaces one message, so over-limit rich edits use one complete plain projection when it fits 4096 Unicode characters. Larger replacements fail explicitly before the plain edit request, preserving the existing message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing rich-block planner owns the 20-media budget and keeps galleries, nested lists, and trailing text intact. The direct edit owner checks the same budget for both Markdown and supplied native blocks. Its plain fallback counts Unicode code points: emoji must not consume two characters merely because JavaScript uses UTF-16 strings.

This update integrates main `364f1ddf3b6646a016c06fd29ddce3186a39892f`, uses its maintained block measurement and HTTP transport fixtures, and removes the retired mock test files. No new SDK surface or configuration is added.

## Evidence

Candidate: `c7d640a93d1ff80cc7274a8f0eb901e49a38ab64`.

- 168 unique focused HTTP/planner cases covered. The initial run passed 167 and exposed one overly strict test assertion for an optional receipt; after correcting that assertion, both 20/21-media cases passed (63.15 seconds). No production change followed the initial run.
- Syntax/boundary lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, and whitespace checks passed. Full build and repository-wide typechecks were not run locally; hosted CI passed on this commit.
- Independent autoreview identified the Unicode length issue; a direct check against the configured server bot accepted 4096 emoji and rejected 4097 with `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`. The guard was corrected and the existing HTTP boundary regression now includes both cases.
- Exact-head live verification through the configured server bot: **7/7 passed** in 25.29 seconds. Twenty media used one rich send; 21 used two sends preserving all 21. Complete 4001/4096-character edits succeeded, including emoji; 4097-character ASCII and emoji replacements were rejected locally with zero API calls.
- Exact-head [hosted CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36124480972) passed. Previous-head checks are historical evidence only.

The owner selected the Telegram bot and Bot API already configured in the server's OpenClaw as the live test environment. The checks above use the candidate source sender, isolated state, and the owner's private chat. The working Gateway was not restarted. Packaged Gateway startup and the Convex-leased environment were not exercised; screenshots were explicitly waived. Acceptance of the recorded evidence remains a maintainer decision.

Historical proof retains its original identity: `6caa2b268277e205fd069b5da890492ae5fb1730` had real Telegram/recipient readback for 20-media, 21-media, and full edit fallback; `21332384fb81adc6e366ff6159ce214b5505f9df` had 378 focused tests and a full Linux build. These are not claims about the new commit.

prs.title: fix(feishu): preserve self mentions in agent-facing group messages
prs.body:
Fixes #72504.

The Feishu inbound parser previously removed the receiving bot's own mention from the agent-facing body. In multi-bot groups, that could leave each bot without its own addressing context even when event metadata had already activated it.

This preserves all normalized `<at>` markup for the agent and keeps group command handling separate: `CommandBody` uses the command-only normalized probe, so `@Bot /model` continues to dispatch as `/model`.

Credit: this repair carries forward analysis from @AxelHu in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72532 and @Bojun-Vvibe in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72661. Their closed PRs are not reopened.

Release-note context: fixes Feishu multi-bot group messages where a receiving bot could lose its own mention context and incorrectly return no reply.

prs.title: fix(ui): show the pending cron action instead of a generic saving label
prs.body:
Closes #147801

## What Problem This Solves

En la página de Automations, pulsar **Run now** o **Remove** y dejar la operación en vuelo hace que el botón de guardar pase a decir **"Saving…"**, aunque no se esté guardando nada. El usuario no puede distinguir "guardando" de "ejecutando" o "borrando".

El defecto es más amplio que el reportado: también ocurre con Pause/Resume pendiente.

## Root cause

`ui/src/pages/cron/view.ts:1096` hace:

```ts
props.busy ? t("cron.form.saving") : t("cron.form.saveChanges")
```

pero `props.busy` es `state.cronBusy`, un **cerrojo de mutación**, no un anuncio de guardado. `withCronBusy` envuelve **cuatro** operaciones distintas —

| call site | operación |
|---|---|
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:744` | `addCronJob` (guardar) |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:929` | `toggleCronJob` |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:953` | `runCronJob` |
| `ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts:972` | `removeCronJob` |

— y solo **una de cuatro** anuncia un guardado. La identidad de la acción se pierde en `index.ts:440`, que solo pone `cronBusy = true` sin registrar quién lo tomó. `CronState` (`ui/src/lib/cron/types.ts:146`) no tenía ningún campo para ella.

## The fix

`CronState` gana `cronPendingAction: "save" | "run" | "toggle" | "remove" | null`, que se publica al entrar en `withCronBusy` y se anula en su **mismo** `finally`, junto a `cronBusy = false`. Los cuatro call sites pasan su identidad.

Las **etiquetas** dejan de leer el cerrojo:

- submit → `pendingAction === "save"` → "Saving…"
- Run now → `pendingAction === "run"` → "Starting…"

Los doce `?disabled` y `aria-busy` **siguen** usando `busy`: el cerrojo no se toca, y un Run now en vuelo deja el guardado igual de deshabilitado que antes. Una clave i18n nueva.

## Evidence

**Antes del fix** — con las siete fuentes de producción revertidas a `main` y los tests finales en su sitio, los cuatro escenarios de página fallan con el texto exacto del issue:

```
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected '\n                  Saving...\n      …' to contain 'Save changes'
×  → expected undefined to be 'save' // Object.is equality
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  4 failed (4)
```

Esos 14 tests discriminan en total: 4 de página, 1 en `view.editor.test.ts` y 9 en `action-feedback.test.ts` (que afirman la identidad y su anulación en `run`/`toggle`/`remove`).

**Después del fix:** `4/4`, y las suites del área en `29/29`, `15/15`, `203/203` sin regresión.

Lo que fija el comportamiento: con `cron.run` en vuelo el submit dice **"Save changes"** y Run now dice **"Starting…"**, ambos siguen deshabilitados; al resolver *y* al rechazar ambos vuelven a idle y `cronPendingAction` queda `null`; con `cron.remove` pendiente el submit tampoco dice "Saving…"; y con `cron.update` pendiente el submit **sí** sigue diciendo "Saving…" — ese último caso es el que ancla el fix, porque es el único correcto que ya pasaba.

## Two decisions worth a look

1. **Los tests de página van en un fichero nuevo** (`cron-page.pending-action.test.ts`) porque `cron-page.test.ts` ya está en el tope de la regla `max-lines` del repo (1000, `.oxlintrc.json:390`) y añadir el bloque lo subía a 1113. `cron-page.test.ts` queda idéntico a `main`.
2. **"Starting…"** usa `…` (U+2026) mientras su vecina `cron.form.saving` usa `"..."` ASCII. Es deliberado — convención de la app para "arrancando" — pero un revisor puede pedir simetría local.

`toggle` y `remove` pendientes no anuncian nada: el editor y Run now quedan en etiqueta idle, solo deshabilitados. Es lo que pedía el encargo (una clave i18n, no cuatro) y el andamiaje ya está para añadir "Pausing…"/"Removing…" si se quiere.

## Checks not run

`pnpm tsgo:ui` no es ejecutable en un worktree con `node_modules` compartido: el guard hermético de `scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts:131` lo aborta, y al esquivarlo el compilador nativo agota el techo obligatorio de 6 GB incluso con el `include` reducido. Como sustituto se ejecutó **el mismo binario** con un `tsconfig` restringido a los ficheros tocados: el conjunto de errores es **byte-idéntico antes y después** (`diff` de ambos logs vacío), 7 errores preexistentes todos en `src/**` sobre `WriteTextAtomicOptions`, **cero** en los ficheros tocados, también sobre el shard de tests. **El typecheck oficial queda pendiente de CI.**

Nota: `ui/src/lib/cron` tiene 5 fallos **preexistentes** en `main` (falta `quickjs-wasi` en el store compartido, y contaminación de locale entre ficheros del mismo worker). Verificados idénticos antes y después; no los introduce este cambio.

## Process note

Este issue lleva una nota de mantenedor de *"work already in progress"* aunque no hay PR en el timeline. Abro igualmente por si el trabajo en curso no llegó a abrir rama; si hay alguien ya encima, con este diff le sirve de base o lo cierro sin problema.

prs.title: fix(auth): treat an empty legacy auth profile set as no provider scope
prs.body:
Closes #141791

## What Problem This Solves

Un `auth-profiles.json` **retirado y vacío** bloquea todas las peticiones de todos los proveedores con `AUTH_PROFILE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`, aunque el fichero no contenga ninguna credencial. Bajar el fichero vacío no lo arregla: basta con que exista, y el store canónico vacío tampoco ayuda.

## Root cause

`src/agents/auth-profiles/legacy-source-diagnostic.ts:58` mezcla dos cosas que significan lo contrario:

```ts
if (!isRecord(profiles) || Object.keys(profiles).length === 0) {
  return null;
}
```

- `!isRecord(profiles)` → el fichero es ilegible o tiene una forma desconocida. **No sabemos** qué proveedores tiene.
- `Object.keys(profiles).length === 0` → el fichero es un conjunto vacío. **Sabemos** que no posee las credenciales de nadie.

Las dos devuelven `null`, y `blocksProvider` hace:

```ts
if (!provider || !this.affectedProviders) return true;
```

o sea, `null` se amplifica a **refusal agent-wide**. Un JSON vacío es dato positivo y se trata como desconocido.

## The fix

Separar los dos casos y distinguir `null` (alcance ilegible) de `[]` (no nombra a nadie):

- `!isRecord(profiles)` → `return null` (se mantiene el refusal agent-wide)
- **envoltorio reconocido** (`profiles` presente) con conjunto vacío → `continue`: esa fuente no aporta scope
- objeto pelado `{}` (sin clave `profiles`) → `return null`: no dice si pretendía ser envoltorio o set plano, así que sigue fallando cerrado
- el `return` final pasa a `providers.size > 0 ? [...providers].toSorted() : []`

Se añade `formatAffectedProviderScope` para que el mensaje de error y la nota de `doctor` no impriman `affected providers: ` vacío.

El límite entre "conjunto vacío" y "desconocido" es la clave `profiles`, no el tamaño. Un fichero con `{"version":1,"profiles":{}}` sí es un envoltorio reconocido y vacío: dato positivo. Un `{}` a pelo no declara qué forma pretendía, y se sigue rechazando — que es justo lo que fija `model-auth.profiles.test.ts`.

**Lo que deliberadamente no se hace:** no se crea `AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError` para ficheros vacíos. Duplicaría el parseo y rompería el contrato de *"recorded refusals remain until the lifecycle explicitly clears them"*.

## Evidence

**Antes del fix** — el test nuevo falla con el error literal del issue:

```
× empty legacy auth profile set does not block known providers
  → expected [Function] to not throw an error but
    'AuthProfileMigrationRequiredError: Auth profile store …/openclaw-agent.sqlite
     requires legacy credential migration; affected providers: all
     (legacy provider scope unavailable); run openclaw doctor --fix.' was thrown
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 12 passed (13)
```

**Después del fix** — `13/13`, y los 12 preexistentes que exigen refusal agent-wide para JSON malformado y formas desconocidas siguen verdes.

El caso de tres_controls que sostiene el veredicto:

- **A** (estado del issue): JSON vacío + store canónico vacío → los cuatro proveedores lanzan `all (legacy provider scope unavailable)`.
- **B** (control): sin el JSON, con la tabla vacía presente → **no lanza** en ninguno. Demuestra que sí existe un estado válido y que la tabla no es el disparador.
- **C** (parcial): JSON que nombra solo `anthropic` → `["anthropic"]`; `deepseek` y `openrouter` no lanzan, `anthropic` sí.

**Regresión en verde:** `src/agents/auth-profiles` completo y `model-auth.profiles` — **822 tests** (677 + 99 + 46) en tres shards, cero fallos. Más las suites dependientes `sdk.auth-migration` (19), `inference-route-runtime` (26) y `doctor-auth-flat-profiles` (81).

> Esta suite de 822 la fija la CI, no el entorno local: `pnpm tsgo:core` no es ejecutable aquí, y la primera versión de este fix pasó los tests que el subagente eligió pero rompía `model-auth.profiles.test.ts`, que fallaba en CI con *"promise resolved instead of rejecting"*. Ese fallo destapó la confusión entre `{}` y `{"version":1,"profiles":{}}`, y el segundo commit la corrige.

## What this proves, and what it does not

El test escribe el `auth-profiles.json` real junto a un store canónico real y prueba sobre disco que `anthropic`/`openai`/`litellm`/`deepseek` no lanzan, que la llamada **sin** `provider` sigue lanzando (el fail-closed se preserva) y que los bytes del JSON no se tocan. Es 100 % observable en Linux, sin credenciales ni red.

## Risks

1. **Semántica:** un JSON vacío pasa de "desconocido" a "no posee credenciales de nadie". El refusal sin ámbito y la valla `hasUnresolvedProviderAuthEndpoint` quedan intactos, y el fichero vacío no concede ninguna credencial: la base canónica sigue siendo la única fuente.
2. **Texto de error:** el caso vacío ahora dice `none (retired files declare no credentials)`. `sdk.auth-migration` e `inference-route-runtime` assertan `code`, no el mensaje, y ambos pasan; el único consumidor del texto nuevo es el test.
3. `src/commands/doctor-auth-flat-profiles.ts` (~2238 líneas) es el fichero con más superficie de conflicto de los tres, aunque el cambio son 8 líneas.

## Checks not run

`pnpm tsgo:core` no es ejecutable en un worktree con `node_modules` compartido: el guard hermético de `scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts:131` lo aborta (`Declaration input escapes checkout…`) y, saltándoselo, el compilador nativo agota el techo obligatorio de 6 GB incluso con un `tsconfig` de un solo fichero. **El typecheck queda pendiente de CI.** Sustitutos ejecutados: `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errores) y `oxfmt --check` limpios en los tres ficheros.

prs.title: fix(openai): enable prompt cache keys for Azure
prs.body:
## Summary
- centralize Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt-cache-key detection in the shared completions compat defaults
- apply that default in the legacy provider builder, boundary-aware OpenAI transport, and embedded-agent extra-params retention eligibility path
- include traditional Azure hosts, Azure AI Foundry project hosts, and regional `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` Foundry hosts
- preserve Azure long prompt-cache retention (`prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`) when callers request `cacheRetention: "long"`, and preserve explicit `cacheRetention: "none"`
- add regression coverage for Azure prompt-cache key emission, long/disabled retention, extra-params propagation, and both request paths

## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw already gates OpenAI-compatible prompt cache keys behind `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`, but Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints were not auto-detected. Azure users therefore needed explicit per-model compat config before stable session prompt-cache keys were forwarded, which can silently reduce prompt-cache hit opportunities for long stable prefixes.

The change treats Azure OpenAI chat-completions endpoints (`azure-openai`, `.openai.azure.com`, `.cognitiveservices.azure.com`, `.services.ai.azure.com`, and `.api.cognitive.microsoft.com`) as prompt-cache-key capable by default. The default now lives in the shared completions compat path used by both request builders and by embedded-agent extra-param cache-retention eligibility; explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey` / `compat.supportsLongCacheRetention` overrides continue to win.

## Evidence
- Searched existing issues/PRs before filing. Found related prompt-cache work (#78747, #82939, #94518, #83709, #69272, #67427), but no open PR specifically enabling Azure OpenAI chat-completions prompt cache keys by default.
- Verified upstream `main` only enabled chat-completions `prompt_cache_key` for `api.openai.com` or explicit `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`; Azure endpoint detection was absent in both relevant request paths and extra-params retention eligibility.
- Added regression tests that confirm Azure OpenAI chat completions forward `prompt_cache_key`, preserve `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"` for long retention, preserve `cacheRetention: "none"`, cover the regional Azure Foundry host, and propagate embedded-agent `cacheRetention` for detected Azure models.
- Live Azure proof, redacted terminal output from `thomais2026v2-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/chat/completions` using `gpt-5.5`, `prompt_cache_key`, and `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`:

```json
{"label":"warmup","status":200,"ok":true,"model":"gpt-5.5-2026-04-24","elapsedMs":1328,"promptTokens":4090,"completionTokens":8,"cachedTokens":0,"hasPromptCacheKey":true,"requestedRetention":"24h","errorCode":null,"errorMessage":null}
{"label":"repeat-prefix","status":200,"ok":true,"model":"gpt-5.5-2026-04-24","elapsedMs":1204,"promptTokens":4090,"completionTokens":5,"cachedTokens":3840,"hasPromptCacheKey":true,"requestedRetention":"24h","errorCode":null,"errorMessage":null}
```

## Test plan
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts`
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/openai-completions-compat.test.ts`
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner-extraparams.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extra-params.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner-extraparams.test.ts src/agents/openai-completions-compat.ts src/agents/openai-completions-compat.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/openai-completions.ts src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`
