prs.title: perf(boards): refresh cached Actions reads in background
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub Actions dashboard widgets wait for GitHub again whenever their polling interval exceeds the 30-second result cache. A typical once-per-minute board read therefore pays the network round trip even while the Gateway is idle.

## User Impact

After the first successful read, an expired result returns with `stale: true` while one background request refreshes it. Widget authors should display a refreshing indicator for this flag. Cold reads and changed credential/filter scopes still await GitHub; current widget grants and credentials are checked before every delivery. Failed refreshes log sanitized guidance and retire the old result, allowing the next read to retry normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Actions cache and singleflight owner for refreshes, retain each transport through the Gateway execution owner, and bound outstanding transports separately from current callers. Keep the current credential-scoped keys, response validation, redirect refusal, timeout, and live delivery checks. Remove the eager expiry eviction and duplicate cached-response clone.

Production code grows by 21 lines. The added code implements the explicit stale-result contract, Gateway-owned refresh lifetime, transport bound, and failure eviction; it does not add a second cache or a new configuration option. There are no schema, persistent-state, permission, or update migrations.

## Evidence

An isolated real WebSocket Gateway uses 120 synthetic worktree-backed sessions, 40 local Git worktrees, and a 20-run Actions response of 8.7 KB. Ordinary `sessions.list` through a widget is already under 20 ms p95. The repeated slow path is the Actions binding, not the Workboard Sessions-board projection.

The real WebSocket rig used Node 26.8.1 and a controlled 1,200 ms Actions response. Each case has 11 measured polls after its first read; both revisions made 12 upstream Actions requests per case. The cache clock advances between polls only after the preceding result is published.

| Poll condition | Before p50 / p95 | After p50 / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity verification cached | 1,235 / 1,245 ms | 29 / 119 ms |
| Identity verification expired, controlled 150 ms verification | 1,385 / 1,395 ms | 181 / 189 ms |

The first uncached request remained about 1.9 seconds. The expired-identity case misses the 150 ms p50 target because it retains current identity verification; it still improves 7.7×. The change intentionally returns the previous successful snapshot while refreshing, potentially one widget polling interval behind.

The regression fails on the old source while the next upstream response is held. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- Hetzner Crabbox `cbx_565ada3c3d21`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/board*.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 104 tests across 9 sibling files passed.
- Same lease: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/board.github-actions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 29 passed; 38.608 seconds wall time, with 199 ms combined for the two added cases. Existing fixture/compilation work dominates this file; no per-case Gateway boot, sleep, or timer was added.
- The first changed-file gate encountered an unrelated unused binding in `channel-presence-policy.ts`. The branch was rebased onto main's existing fix; the patch is identical by `git range-diff`.
- Staged rig gate on baseline `9cd6be8c39e7`: production types and all 28 core test type projects passed. The sole failure was the existing unused export `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` in untouched `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts`; the same full dead-export scan reproduced it on the clean baseline. The remaining planned lint, schema, legacy-store, media, sidecar, cycle, webhook and pairing guards passed separately; import cycles: 0. No check was disabled.
- Corrected source/test lint: 0 warnings and 0 errors. The final complete candidate has a clean independent P0–P2 review.
- Exact-head [CI run 38102859446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38102859446) passed for `a0589c65d12a34f8e886994dc3db28f0326e00b7` in 451 seconds overall. Hosted security and workflow checks passed. The first CI run found a shadowed test callback parameter; that one-line naming correction is included.

The rig controls upstream latency and advances only the Actions cache clock. It does not contact GitHub or a production Gateway. Live network variability and deployment timing remain unmeasured. The existing 60-second GitHub identity verification cache is preserved, so a poll that must verify identity can still pay that separate network round trip.

prs.title: fix(ui): bridge tool stream state to composer run status indicator
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the agent is actively running tools, the Activity panel correctly shows "Activity: N tools Exec" with a spinner, but the composer area displays no "In progress" indicator and no Stop button — appearing completely idle. Users cannot tell whether the agent is working or has stalled.

Root cause: the composer's in-progress state is driven exclusively by `chatRunId` and `sessionsResult[].hasActiveRun`, while the Activity panel uses an independent agent event stream (`activityEntries[]`). There is no bridge between these two data paths. When `chatRunId` is cleared by a racing `sessions.changed` event (via `reconcileChatRunFromSessionRow()`) while tools are still streaming, the composer goes idle while Activity correctly shows running tools.

Fixes #98540

## Changes

- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.ts`** — Add `hasActiveToolExecution()` and `resolveActiveToolRunId()` helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`** — Re-export the new helpers
- **`ui/src/ui/app-chat.ts`** — `hasAbortableSessionRun()` checks activity entries as third signal; `handleAbortChat()` falls back to tool stream runId
- **`ui/src/ui/activity-model.test.ts`** — 9 unit tests for new helpers

## Evidence

**Test results (9 new + 26 existing pass without regression):**

✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is undefined ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when activityEntries is empty ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are done ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns true when at least one entry is running ✓ hasActiveToolExecution > returns false when all entries are error ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when activityEntries is undefined ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns null when no running entries ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the runId of the running entry ✓ resolveActiveToolRunId > returns the most recently updated running entry's runId


Existing `app-tool-stream.node.test.ts` (26 tests) pass without regression.

**Screenshot showing the bug:** See #98540 for screenshot evidence.

prs.title: fix(msteams): reset isolated DM context after app removal
prs.body:
Related: #99054. Follows the closed Teams lifecycle proposals #100371 and #104690.

This is the smaller, account-aware follow-up to those attempts. It uses the existing session lifecycle API and replaces the previous proposal for a new public reset capability. The prior PRs remain available for their discussions and historical proof; their published branches are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained pre-removal context when a Microsoft Teams bot/app is uninstalled from an isolated personal chat and later reinstalled.

## User Impact

The removed installation’s isolated DM starts a fresh session after reinstall. Historical transcript content is archived through the existing owner. Shared main/per-peer sessions, sessions shared by bot accounts, and model-locked sessions remain intact and are logged. Retiring an entry also clears its session preferences. Ordinary upgrades, install-add events, other members leaving, and Teams local **Remove chat history** keep their existing behavior. There is no new configuration or public SDK API.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removal events enter Teams durable ingress. Cleanup routes the stored DM owner with the bot’s account, then uses the existing session lifecycle API to archive and delete the active entry. Failure retains the conversation reference for retry; failed durable admission rejects the webhook request. The implementation stays within the Teams plugin.

## Evidence

- Historical live Teams signal evidence: [uninstall/reinstall and local clear-history capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100371#issuecomment-4887052082). This exercises the earlier implementation, not this head's archival/deletion path.
- Historical canonical-owner and authority tests: [exact-head redacted packet at fc3e2b425251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104690#issuecomment-5398588721). The earlier reset contract differs from this head's deletion contract, so its authority proof is historical only.
- Three new routing/admission regression cases fail against pinned unpatched upstream `76a282c7a1c6ca958517ce15f13e17371c14be11`.
- 71 focused tests passed, covering real SQLite session/conversation storage, account and agent isolation, transcript archival, retry failure, restart/redelivery, webhook lifecycle, and adaptive-card behavior (31.54 seconds locally).
- After extracting transport coverage and correcting its replay context fixture, all 28 cases in the affected test files passed with one worker in 46.78 seconds: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/msteams-ingress.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.removal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- The full packaged build passed, including external plugins and SDK declarations/exports. Production and test type checks passed.
- Whole-tree checks remain red on unchanged upstream unused exports and an unchanged Crabbox file exceeding its line limit. All candidate unused-export findings reproduce in the exact upstream snapshot; reported source files match upstream byte for byte.
- Authored Teams lint, script lint, formatting, storage/media/loader guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent Codex review returned one P2 concern about completion of removal ingress. It was ruled out: the existing ingress monitor automatically adopts successful non-deferred returns. The strengthened real-queue restart/redelivery regression passed without an explicit adoption callback (1 test; 9.29-second shard). No accepted/actionable findings remain. The canonical ingress owner completes successful non-deferred returns; no explicit reply-lane adoption is required.
- Live Teams validation has not been repeated for this implementation. Historical live results belong to the earlier published version; hosted CI duration is unmeasured. The serial boundary tests use real session/queue storage because routing, archival, rollback, and durable replay are the contracts under test.
- Proof was collected on pinned upstream `76a282c7a1c6ca958517ce15f13e17371c14be11`. Upstream advanced afterward without changing any authored path; the published patch tree matches the reviewed and tested candidate exactly. Full monorepo `pnpm check`/`pnpm test` and fresh live Teams proof were not run. Broad plugin lint and the changed-file gate were run and retain the inherited failures described above.


Current review gaps at `5ebed9858af6203c31400509362fce56524fabcb`: fresh authenticated Teams uninstall/reinstall and readable archived-history proof; delayed retired/reassigned-account rejection; the unrelated unbound-sibling routing finding; and latest-stable upgrade/preferences proof. The prior [maintainer preference-preservation direction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104690#pullrequestreview-4678944814) still needs resolution because this implementation deletes the active entry and its preferences. Historical proof does not clear these current-head blockers.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves
A Slack agent serving several private customer channels needs to recall sibling threads without opening every conversation belonging to the agent.

## User Impact
Operators can opt into `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` to allow verified same-agent, same-channel session access while excluding other channels. Defaults and existing visibility modes are unchanged; thread sessions stay separate and recall is on demand, not automatic prompt injection.

This is **not a complete multi-tenant sandbox**: shared memory files, filesystem access, message-plugin history tools, external integrations and already-mixed transcripts need their own boundaries. Missing route facts deny cross-session access. Archived memory transcript hits are conservatively excluded. No production deployment or live Slack test was performed.

## Why This Change Was Made
The existing visibility decision owner already serves history, list, search, send and status. This extends that owner rather than introducing a second memory system or provider-specific policy in core.

- Compare trusted stored provider, explicit account, opaque destination, chat kind and workspace/space. Thread IDs are not part of the channel comparison; arbitrary peer IDs are not split to infer authority.
- Require the same agent; main aliases, spawned ownership, A2A permission and scoped grants cannot widen the new boundary. DM/main callers remain self-only.
- Prepare requester metadata once for list/search and filter candidates before returning metadata or reading snippets. Direct access uses exact owner-qualified descriptions and propagates the described session incarnation into the existing lifecycle fence.
- Apply the same policy to memory transcript hits, reject conflicting transcript aliases, and keep the default sandbox spawned clamp from widening `channel` to `tree`.
- No new storage, migrations, background jobs or model calls. Channel-only overhead is one requester metadata read for inventory/search, or two exact metadata reads for a direct cross-session access; unchanged modes do not incur these reads.

## Evidence
- Focused shared-policy, history, list, search, access and memory suites: **233 tests passed** (initial 6-file run, 4 shards, 46.09 seconds wall with `--maxWorkers=1`). The list regression was subsequently moved into its own small file to satisfy the repository line-cap guard.
- Final targeted recheck: **58 tests passed** across the policy suite and the extracted list regression (16.23 seconds wall). `pnpm check:changed` passed, including core/extension/test typechecks, SDK exports/surface/boundary checks, changed-file lint, config docs, dead exports and import cycles. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent native Codex review: no actionable P1/P2 findings. The repository `autoreview` helper was also invoked, but its separate CLI account could not access its configured review models; it did not produce a review, so the independent native review was used instead.
- Mock-Gateway tests exercise actual session tool entry points; they verify that another channel's history is never read and its metadata/snippets are not returned. SDK cases cover account/workspace/provider/agent mismatches, main/DM, malformed or missing facts, opaque peer IDs, incognito, scoped grants and sandbox clamps. Memory proof includes conflicting aliases and archived-hit denial.
- No live customer or Slack traffic, production config change, broad benchmark, or production deployment. CI timing is not available at submission; no workflow dispatch or rerun requested.


## 2026-10-10 refresh and after-fix proof

- Refreshed with current `main` by a normal merge at exact head `9b99db182f547aba65f3edfef8e9fd2d376ae932`; no force push. The search path now re-authorizes each channel-scoped candidate immediately before `sessions.search` and uses the exact session incarnation fence when available.
- Focused session visibility/search/history/memory suites: **141 tests passed**. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed all changed-file typechecks, SDK/boundary/config checks, lint, dead-code and cycle checks. Full `pnpm build` passed; its advisory Control UI startup gzip budget message was unchanged outside this backend patch.
- Isolated after-fix behavior proof used the built package at this exact head, an actual child Gateway process, canonical SQLite session storage, the model-facing `sessions_search` tool, and synthetic Slack-shaped routes/transcripts. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used.
- Result: the requester and a same-agent/same-provider/same-account/same-channel/same-workspace sibling were searched and returned. Other-channel, other-account, and other-workspace markers were excluded, and no `sessions.search` call was issued for those targets.
- Fresh-authority result: after inventory, the sibling route projected by the host was changed while preserving its session ID; the new pre-I/O authorization rejected it, no sibling `sessions.search` call was issued, and only the requester result returned. This reassignment step was a controlled host-projection injection around the real Gateway call; the surrounding inventory, persistence, tool execution, and transcript search were real isolated runtime paths.

The remaining question is the maintainer-owned product/SDK contract: retrieval-only versus also permitting sibling send/status through the shared visibility owner.




<!-- shannon-followup-2026-10-11 -->
## 2026-10-11 exact-head security follow-up

- Integrated current main with a normal merge and published exact head ba0fe780e129dc2a4b3bf4ccc09f07f1a0b37306; no force push.
- Restored memory privacy ordering so archived-session inventory completes before the channel visibility catalog is read. The existing direct-to-group reset-recall regression now passes again.
- Channel-scoped search, history, send, status, and patch effects now re-read requester/target route facts and re-authorize at the final writer-ordered admission boundary. A preserved session ID no longer preserves stale channel authority after route reassignment.
- Added two explicit regressions: same-ID target reassignment after description is denied before transcript I/O, and a route change between initial and final scoped admission is denied before the effect callback.
- Focused result: 60 existing/new search, history, memory, and visibility tests passed; the final scoped-admission suite then passed 2/2 after its added regression.
- Changed-file checks passed conflict, line/max-line, SQLite, format, config/docs, SDK/boundary, core/extension/test typechecks, deprecation, and import guards. The only check:changed failure was the full-tree dead-export scan for GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2 and reconnectGateway, both in files untouched by this PR.
- Proof boundary: these are isolated exact-head source/SQLite/tool tests. No production Gateway/config, customer data, live Slack, or model call was used in this follow-up. The prior isolated Gateway proof remains scoped to its recorded old head and is not relabeled as current-head runtime proof.

The product/SDK choice remains maintainer-owned: retrieval-only, or permitting sibling send/status through this shared visibility owner.

prs.title: fix(qa-lab): show the real error when qa commands fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw qa ...` commands fail with only `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` and a doctor hint (or with no output at all) when the command rejects its input or its run fails, so the operator never sees the actual reason.

## User Impact

User impact: every `qa` subcommand (run, suite, mantis, the live transport lanes such as telegram/discord/matrix/slack/whatsapp, plugin-provided runners such as msteams/buzz, credentials, docker, ui, reports) now prints its real failure message to stderr and still exits 1. For example, an absolute `--output-dir` now says `--output-dir must be a relative path inside the repo root.` instead of the generic line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root CLI failure renderer intentionally hides the message of any error it does not classify as expected (terse default output; `--debug` shows the reason). Core commands classify their own failures, but the qa commands just threw, so their messages were dropped. Validation errors built with the Commander invalid-argument helper inside an action were worse: the root parse handler treats Commander-coded errors as already printed, so they exited 1 silently.

The fix stays with the owners of the `qa` command actions instead of changing the root policy. qa-lab wraps every qa, mantis, and inactive-runner action in one boundary that writes the formatted message to stderr and sets `process.exitCode = 1` (not `process.exit`, so CLI exit finalization still runs). The SDK-built QA runner command registration gets the same handling, which covers qa-lab's live lanes and external runner plugins. Action-time validators now throw plain errors; the Commander-coded helper is kept for argument parsers, which Commander reports itself.

Accepted tradeoffs, limited to `qa` commands: caught failures print the message (including causes, redacted) but no longer show the root `--debug` stack trace, and a failing `qa coverage --json` prints the message to stderr instead of the root JSON failure envelope (`qa credentials --json` already emits its own JSON errors; no scripts consume the coverage failure envelope).

Release note: QA CLI commands now report their failure reason instead of the generic "The CLI command failed." message.

## Evidence

Real command, private-QA build (`OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1`), isolated `--profile qaerr`:

Before (origin/main 5d1f1a91dcc9):

```text
$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa run --repo-root . --qa-profile smoke-ci --output-dir /abs/qa-out --scenario memory-dreaming-sweep
QA run profile: smoke-ci; categories: 9; scenarios: 1
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw --profile qaerr doctor`.
exit=1

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa run --repo-root . --qa-profile smoke-ci --scenario ''
exit=1            (no output at all)

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa suite --repo-root . --output-dir /abs/qa-out --scenario memory-dreaming-sweep
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw --profile qaerr doctor`.
exit=1
```

After (this branch):

```text
$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa run --repo-root . --qa-profile smoke-ci --output-dir /abs/qa-out --scenario memory-dreaming-sweep
QA run profile: smoke-ci; categories: 9; scenarios: 1
--output-dir must be a relative path inside the repo root.
exit=1

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa run --repo-root . --qa-profile smoke-ci --scenario ''
--scenario must name at least one non-empty scenario id.
exit=1

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa suite --repo-root . --output-dir /abs/qa-out --scenario memory-dreaming-sweep
--output-dir must be a relative path inside the repo root.
exit=1

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa telegram --repo-root . --scenario ''
--scenario must name at least one non-empty scenario id.
exit=1

$ openclaw --profile qaerr qa telegram --repo-root . --output-dir /abs/qa-out
--output-dir must be a relative path inside the repo root.
exit=1
```

Focused tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, local wall time including Vitest startup; all fast unit tests, no timers or process boots):

| File | Result | Wall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.test.ts` (new regressions: reported `--output-dir` failure, empty Telegram `--scenario`, SDK runner failure) | 47 passed | 35.9s |
| `src/plugin-sdk/qa-runtime.test.ts` (SDK runner blank `--scenario` now reported, not dispatched) | 12 passed | 27.4s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli-scenario-selection.test.ts` | 14 passed | 12.8s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` | 79 passed | 54.4s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/cli.test.ts` | 14 passed | 36.5s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/matrix/cli.test.ts` | 6 passed | 11.5s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/shared/live-transport-suite.runtime.test.ts` | 28 passed | 31.0s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/slack-desktop-smoke.runtime.test.ts` | 15 passed | 30.3s |

The new regression cases failed before the production change; `cli-scenario-selection.test.ts` covers the blank-scenario run/suite paths. Existing tests that asserted rejected actions now assert the stderr message and exit code, which is the user-visible contract. Added test cost is a few milliseconds of in-process Commander parsing; no new CI seconds of note.

The dashboard's existing failure-output owner now uses `formatCliJsonFailure`, the same formatter used by the onboarding follow-up in #168488. All four failure entrances share this owner; no second formatter or new policy is introduced. The command documentation and existing failure assertions are updated, with one regression for JSON-mode loopback ownership refusal.

## Evidence

Proof source identities: baseline `3666e847aac206c4f1a8805d97de96861c9c56ca`; candidate `3ed4cce149e2718ccab2339f4a3ee38f853e6d60`. [Successful secretless fork Actions proof](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38102846605) and its [downloadable artifact](https://github.com/ly85206559/openclaw/actions/runs/38102846605/artifacts/11688596601) retain the frozen test, hashes, raw test logs, CLI stdout/stderr, exit codes, and timings. Node v26.8.2 / pinned pnpm 12.9.0. The proof-only workflow is not part of this PR.

- **Regression:** the identical candidate test file, placed on unchanged baseline production code, produces **5 assertion failures / 4 passing success controls**. The candidate passes all 9 cases. Across the dashboard command, dashboard link, and shared CLI failure-output suites, **36 tests pass**; focused formatting, lint, and whitespace checks also pass. Frozen regression SHA-256: `bc778301138c92b72f14d26493d3b29e3ad233f328d1432a41b0b54f2f0e7de6`.

Failure controls still prohibit browser-token issuance for preparing assets, certificate mismatch, and unverified loopback ownership; the latter also prohibits document probing, clipboard writes, and browser launch. - **Review:** complete 3-file, 2-commit branch diff reviewed at the exact candidate SHA against its true `main` merge-base. P0–P3 findings are empty, with no priority-filtered findings; confidence 0.97. Production change is one import and replacement of the existing failure-output expression.

## What Problem This Solves

Moves Connection, Device, Permissions, and Devices rendering onto Solid 2 as part of the Control UI migration.

## User Impact

Preserves the existing page tags, routes, CSS classes, connection/session drafts, device controls, pairing actions, and approval editing. Gateway and native capability owners retain authority over requests and writes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registered page tags now share one Solid implementation through `defineSolidBridge`; their Lit classes are removed. The pages consume the shared Solid icons/settings primitives and canonical test mounting helpers. The shared page lifecycle and visible polling helpers each serve multiple pages. Stateless Lit pairing, vitals, and capacity helpers remain only where unported callers still need them.

The simplification pass removed the extra mount helper, the single-caller pending-edit module, redundant capability synchronization, the Devices view wrapper, and copied route data. Remaining production growth comes from explicit reactive JSX and temporary stateless renderer coexistence; final counts and visual comparison will be recorded below before merge.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Connection view | 27 passed |
| Connection page lifecycle/credentials/session | 25 passed |
| Native device/permission pages | 26 passed |
| Devices page lifecycle/authority | 37 passed |

The Testbox attempt stalled in source preparation before VM admission; heavy checks use PR CI under the migration work-order fallback. No local Docker, UI build, typecheck, or E2E suite was run. prs.title: fix(nodes): preserve workspace retention across scheduler ticks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes periodic node workspace and worker-bundle retention failing with `This operation was aborted` after a scheduler callback finishes.

## User Impact

Paired nodes can complete their scheduled retention and bundle-status publication instead of repeatedly abandoning maintenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The coordinator already owns cancellation and joins its pending operations at shutdown. Start those operations outside the caller's short-lived async-work scope, preserving the existing node and placement authority checks.

Production LOC: **+1 net** (2 added, 1 removed); 2 changed files. No configuration, protocol, schema, or retention-policy change.

## Evidence

- Reproduced recurring failures on an isolated Linux Gateway with three paired node processes, including a loopback node. The scheduler/real-placement-store regression failed with the same abort before the fix.
- Fixed regression and sibling file: `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-read-projection.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **16 passed**, **56.51 s wall time** on Hetzner; new regression body **0.904 s**. Cold compiled-worker preparation was 22.7 s.
- Independent correctness/security review: no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Required GitHub CI gate: passed on `143778ff247d0838dd62c1d4790151e27cc522b1`. Current-main core and test typechecks passed. The full-tree dead-export check reports the existing `GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` export in untouched Gateway code; the same finding was reproduced on the unmodified baseline.
- Candidate build passed. Live candidate: a fresh hosted tool turn passed; no periodic AbortError over four minutes of maintenance observation, and all three node identities report installed worker bundles.
- Baseline 30-minute soak: 60/60 exact replies, with RSS and descriptor samples. Workspace binary/text/symlink/deletion transfer, six concurrent sessions, node-process restart, and a 156-second turn also passed.

The original AWS pond request encountered vCPU and memory limits; live proof uses two Hetzner machines with three isolated node identities. Separate hard-reboot recovery failure is recorded for a follow-up and is not changed here.

prs.title: fix(release): separate publication inventory from upgrade admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release inventory incorrectly treated every recorded publication as a supported first-hop upgrade. A newly published higher-schema package could break release preparation or lead the candidate to promise unsupported upgrade bridges. Tracking: [#168257 — publication inventory and first-hop admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168257).

## Why This Change Was Made

Inventory v2 records the exact source package schema versions. One dependency-free contract admits only publications whose state/agent schemas are supported by the candidate manifest. Inventory generation, bridge/output generation, first-hop lanes, frozen-target planning and package fixtures consume this canonical admission decision. Unsupported publications remain accounted for with an explicit reason; missing facts fail closed. Blanket publication admission and the duplicated local record guard are removed.

Frozen v1 artifacts retain the named admitted-list contract shipped in stable `v2026.9.9`; new generation requires v2 facts. Runtime schema refusal is unchanged. No schema guessing or new compatibility fallback.

## User Impact

Maintainers can account for a newer-schema publication without claiming downgrade support. Supported uncovered publications still fail with an actionable verified-package refresh command. No operator options, SQLite schema/store semantics, production publication or live Gateway changes.

## Evidence

### Accepted ClawSweeper findings

Latest durable [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168280#issuecomment-6094673630) is bound to prior head `37877`, reviewed `2026-10-11T01:13:33.936Z`. Its two before-merge items are resolved on `3f477`: exact fallback-only hydration assertion with unchanged `off`/`medium` proof, and conflict integration preserving canonical #168618 refresh behavior. Both repairs have local owner proof and passing final-head CI below. This dispositions that review; it does not claim a new ClawSweeper verdict on `3f477`. No unaddressed Rank-up moves were present.

- **Early tooling integrity:** the frozen tooling owner verifies `scripts/lib/update-compat-contract.mjs` before importing/executing its planner closure; the redundant late consumer check is removed. Existing dirty/missing-helper sentinel regressions fail before this repair and pass after it.
- **Copied harness closures:** package acceptance, preflight, no-push, publication/inventory producer, package-source and Docker harnesses carry the dependency they actually execute.
- **Manifest overwrite:** launcher/scaffold callers prepare schema-bearing source after their caller manifest metadata, before capturing the fixture's committed identity.
- **Dirty source after build:** the shared fixture separates source preparation from dist generation. Live-updater and UI-prebuilt fixtures commit the prepared manifest first; building outputs never rewrites source. Existing dirty-checkout failures were captured before repair. No assertion, timeout, or validation was weakened.

### Current candidate and hosted CI

Published head: `3f477f87d3398466d38535d6abbed91be909ae74`, on pinned main `bbd2daf8b6def57eb0ac47c5e270c9b39cc168e6`. Nine commits. The four inventory patches and the prior test-lint/cron patches remain byte-identical through conflict integration. No merge.

Previous-head `37877c4f5131cfda7f40d0888dfa037a0289d57e` [CI run 38099612940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38099612940) completed with **66 successful, 3 failed and 22 skipped jobs (91 settled)**. Two underlying failures, now repaired at their fixture owners; aggregate also failed:

- **Cron catalog reuse:** the old three-scoped-read assertion fails locally with exactly one read. Canonical main `dd4b258a3cfa6fdef41535e5518fe260f5665a9c` deliberately reuses matching admitted host rows. The fixture now proves one admitted-owner/global-catalog load, exactly the missing fallback's scoped hydration, and unchanged emitted `off` → `medium` levels. No redundant production reads restored.
- **Menu hover readiness:** a real Chromium held-opening probe fails both original RGB assertions: opening scale 0.9 → 1 moves Photo upward about 12 px, leaving File under the stationary pointer. Both inspected screenshots show File highlighted, Photo transparent. The existing `openMenu` helper installs `wa-after-show` before the actual trigger click and joins completed opening before settled-hover/focus assertions. Attachment, library, browser-card and disabled/danger cases share this path; every color assertion and intentional during-animation test remains. The same held-opening condition passes both themes after the join. Installed Web Awesome's popup/next-frame/animation completion contract was directly inspected; no dependency patch, retry, timeout increase or production CSS change.
- **Required conflict integration:** canonical [#168618 — refreshed models in local turns](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168618), commit `76a1a8043866891d4bdeca57599ea68bc0e7f845`, adds a real offline-refresh caller. Its force/deadline contract and owner checks remain intact; the internal publication helper stays private with fixed standalone provenance. The worker timeout import follows its new canonical module. Main already localizes `SettingsSegmentedOption`, so the redundant branch change drops out.

Final local proof on this candidate:

Final mechanically typed fixture: **20/20**, **6.93s**, owning UI-components type graph **exit 0**. Before-fix shard pass alone was not treated as a fix; the held-opening red/green diagnosis establishes the cause.
- Fresh convergence and two-fixture P0–P2 AutoReviews: **scoped-clean**. Static-review scope limits remain; the lead directly checked unchanged owners/dependency contracts and executable proof. A final explicit DOM-query typing correction is separately typechecked.
- Affected changed gate: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base bbd2daf8b6def57eb0ac47c5e270c9b39cc168e6 -- src/cron/isolated-agent/run.runtime-thinking.test.ts ui/src/components/menu-surface.browser.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.types.ts src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native.integration.test.ts` — **exit 0**, production types, all **28/28** core-test graphs, all three dead-export scans **zero findings**, changed lint, storage/loader/pairing guards and **zero** runtime cycles. All failed leaves came from unchanged main-owned files:

- Plugin-state cache shadow/redundant TTL conversion and intentionally receiver-restored Worker extraction: canonical repair `f9940dc8a794948cf24492fd881296b60296ff4a` is integrated. Local duplicate repairs were dropped.
- Internal async DM resolver colliding with the public SDK config resolver: canonical `13296b17cd0f30a1242f36378d8a61448b6fbd55` uses `resolvePluginDmPolicy`; public `resolveChannelDmPolicy` stays unchanged. The local duplicate repair was dropped.

Fresh proof:

- Dead-export repair: all three Knip passes **zero findings**, focused UI **29/29**, browser **8/8** across Lit/Solid, light/dark, desktop/mobile; final P0–P2 AutoReview **scoped-clean**. These browser/scanner receipts precede the byte-identical rebase.

SDK/runtime/plugin/declaration/UI build phases completed. An initial build failed on missing installed Workboard Solid dependencies already declared by its manifest; `pnpm install` exited 0 without tracked changes, then the complete retry passed. The earlier gate was intentionally stopped before dependency reconciliation; its exit 143 is not a product verdict.

Earlier `37877` dead-export correction delta: production **net -153**; tests **net +13**; proof fixture **net +12**; Knip tooling **net +8**. ### CI root causes and canonical repairs

- The old inventory head reproduced all five native lifecycle failures. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): reject unknown login actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The WhatsApp login tool is reachable through a Gateway tool-invocation seam that does not validate plugin-specific nested arguments. Before this fix, an explicit malformed `action` could be treated as a login start; `null` specifically was converted to `"start"` by the fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The execution owner now validates the raw action before applying the intentional omitted-action fallback. Only `start` and `wait` continue; explicit `null`, numbers, and unknown strings fail before either QR login or wait polling is called. An omitted action remains compatible with the existing `start` default.

## User Impact

Malformed direct tool calls return `Unknown WhatsApp login action: <value>` and cannot begin QR login. Valid owner `start` and `wait` calls are unchanged. The plugin-compatible `ToolInputError` maps to HTTP 400 through the real Gateway instead of a generic 500.

## Evidence

- Exact product head: `21940a82b1fc9eb50bfe03a52a2731d518d00811`. The branch integrates pinned main `aceda1bdd357f7dc67b123720c45d2169f54258f` without force-push. The original guard is unchanged; main's `readNonBlankString`, `textResult`, sender-owner restriction and invocation-lifetime checks are retained. The main-relative diff remains only the login tool and its regression test.
- Acceptance-red regression: with the pre-fix fallback and no guard, the registered-tool test for `{ action: null }` resolved through the mocked `startWebLoginWithQr` path instead of rejecting. This is the test-level red observation; I have not claimed a pre-fix live Gateway run.
- Fresh integrated-head regression and controls: `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/agent-tools-login.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **12 tests / 1 file**. The repository wrapper reported **8.62 s elapsed**; Vitest reported **5.63 s**. It covers malformed `bogus`/`null`/`42`, valid `start`, valid `wait`, and invocation-lifetime authority. Omitted action is preserved by the explicit undefined-to-start fallback; no dedicated omitted-action test is claimed. The native staged-content guard and main-relative `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head CI/file-only CI seconds remain pending rather than borrowed from an older head.
- Fresh runtime build: `pnpm exec node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` passed in **2m 2.2s** at the integrated head, including CLI-bootstrap import and runtime-postbuild checks. Dependencies use this checkout's frozen lockfile and pinned **pnpm 12.5.1**. The mirror returned 404 for a locked package; installation from the official npm registry passed without changing the lockfile or registry configuration.
- Real production proof on October 8, 2026, freshly repeated at the integrated head: Node **24.16.0**, then the actual `pnpm openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback` CLI. prs.title: feat: add session stream mode command
prs.body:
Implements the session-scoped streaming control discussed in #74077 (closed automatically for inactivity).

Related: #80989

> AI-assisted with OpenAI Codex; the resulting code and tests were reviewed and validated locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Preview streaming is configured globally per channel, so users cannot switch one active chat between off, partial, block, and progress behavior without editing config. This adds a session-scoped control that preserves channel configuration as the fallback.

## User-Facing Behavior

Authorized Telegram, Discord, and Slack users can run:

```text
/stream status
/stream off
/stream partial
/stream block
/stream progress
/stream default
```

`/streaming` is an alias. Text commands also accept `final` as a compatibility alias for canonical `off`.

The selected mode is persisted only for the current session. `/stream default` removes the override and reports the inherited channel mode. `off` disables previews without suppressing normal final delivery or an inherited block-delivery fallback.

## Implementation

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.streamingMode` state and preserves it across the same lifecycle boundaries as adjacent session preferences.
- Lets supporting channel plugins declare their inherited streaming mode and resolve account config without core assuming a plugin-specific config shape.
- Applies the session override before Telegram, Discord, and Slack account configuration in both preview selection and block arbitration.
- Capability-gates native command registration. ClickClack and other non-participating plugins do not advertise `/stream`; unsupported text invocation returns a clear response and does not persist state.
- Uses conflict-aware session persistence with `touchedFields: ["streamingMode"]` so a concurrent lifecycle change returns the standard retry response instead of acknowledging a lost write.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

This PR intentionally introduces one optional public channel-plugin contract: `plugin.streaming.sessionModeDefault` plus `resolveSessionMode({ account, sessionMode })`.

The contract keeps defaults and account-shape knowledge inside each channel plugin and makes native registration capability-aware. Please confirm whether this is the preferred long-term opt-in boundary for session-scoped streaming controls. The feature should not merge without that API sponsorship.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `7b98d15970f59dd3441bf4de782f67880f9c38da`  
Feature base: `d09401295626bebd53aa84492b91e7909e22487f`

- Production-focused matrix on the immediately preceding, production-identical head `9f8a86c87baf7a1528a85f6ac2638e0ec2b5c4d2`: 16 files / 699 assertions passed, covering command selection/persistence, lifecycle carry-forward, capability gating, stream/block resolution, and Telegram/Discord/Slack preview plus final-delivery behavior. A diff-caused duplicate Slack stream-mode mock was reproduced at 205/207 and repaired to 207/207.
- Exact-head boundary repair: the prior hosted `check-additional-boundaries` correctly found that a new standalone Gateway test root raised `gateway-root` from 720 to 721. That regression assertion now lives in the existing `sessions.recover` production-path test; the standalone root is removed. The exact-head recovery file passes 29/29, the repository boundary guard passes at the 720-root cap, and formatting/type-aware Oxlint/`git diff --check` pass.
- Clean merge simulation against live `openclaw/main` `89a1abd12ff92d78e0a5d2cf22641968dce828ea`: passed (tree `23fbae78977fb69774005b763f246b9b21dcdbdb`), with no paths changed on both sides since the feature base.
- Current repair gates: lower-level exact build, 49-file current-format check, direct type-aware Oxlint, `git diff --check`, and docs format/MDX/internal-link/config-example/glossary checks pass. Full wrapper `check:changed` remains delegated to hosted clean-install CI because local shared dependencies were intentionally not reconciled.
- Conflict-marker, coercion/deprecation, boundary, dead-export, dependency-pin, Plugin SDK export-sync, surface-budget, subpath-export, and wildcard-re-export guards pass.
- Fresh independent `gpt-5.6-sol` Max review found no actionable P0-P2 issue.
- A prior clean-install hosted core type shard passes after the test fixture was typed from the public resolver contract; no production behavior changed. A prior compact declaration-tooling failure also passed on rerun and was not diff-caused.
- Hosted exact-head run `34457781315` is terminal with **171 successes, 39 skips, and five failures** including the derivative `openclaw/ci-gate`. The four primary failures are outside this PR's changed paths: the current-main UI max-lines violation, runner-native tsgo `ETXTBSY`, a database-preflight artifact timeout, and a real-heartbeat cron timeout.

prs.title: fix(media-understanding): forward allowlisted ElevenLabs transcription options from providerOptions
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #168580

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ElevenLabs batch speech-to-text silently ignores transcription options
configured through `providerOptions.elevenlabs`, so settings such as `no_verbatim` and
`tag_audio_events` cannot be applied. Users configuring these options (e.g. Scribe v2 filler-word
removal or audio-event tagging) would get the API defaults instead, keeping filler words and
audio-event annotations in transcripts such as the user-visible `echoTranscript`.

- **Related:** None (no linked PR or maintainer comment; fix-shape-clear / source-repro labels).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `tools.media.audio` / `tools.media.models[]` `providerOptions.elevenlabs`
  are forwarded to the ElevenLabs `/v1/speech-to-text` multipart body, so configured
  transcription options are applied. Only an allowlist of synchronous options that preserve the
  `payload.text` response contract is forwarded (`no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, `diarize`);
  options that change the response (e.g. `webhook`, `use_multi_channel`) are intentionally
  excluded. The allowlist keys never collide with the dedicated `model_id` / `language_code` /
  `prompt` fields, so no precedence ambiguity is introduced.
- **Out of scope:** No change to the runner query-resolution precedence (audio defaults vs model
  entry already resolved upstream), no streaming/realtime path, no new models.
- **Highest-risk area:** Forwarding a field whose boolean `false` could previously not be
  represented — mitigated because the shared multipart builder stringifies `false` to the
  non-empty string `"false"` and appends it correctly.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Regression tests assert both `true` and `false` forwarding, and
  that non-allowlisted keys are dropped.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** With `providerOptions: { elevenlabs: { no_verbatim: true,
  tag_audio_events: false } }`, the multipart request to ElevenLabs contains
  `no_verbatim=true` and `tag_audio_events=false`; non-allowlisted options are not sent.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`
  (allowlist merge) and its regression tests in
  `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Executed base-failing regression against the pre-fix provider
  (RED) and the patched provider (GREEN); a shipped OpenClaw CLI runtime run
  (`openclaw infer audio transcribe`) exercising the real media-understanding runner, the
  registered ElevenLabs provider, the shared multipart transport, and a real HTTP socket —
  the request body was captured by a local endpoint standing in for ElevenLabs because no live
  ElevenLabs account or Telegram Test Server credentials were available. Docs config-example and
  link audits against the OpenClaw docs pipeline.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Base-failing regression: pre-fix provider from origin/main, then patched provider
  git checkout origin/main -- extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.test.ts   # RED
  git checkout HEAD -- extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.test.ts   # GREEN

  # Shipped CLI runtime flow (qaRuntime dist build of this branch)
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated> ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=<local-key> \
    node openclaw.mjs infer audio transcribe --file sample-440hz.wav \
      --model elevenlabs/scribe_v2 --json

  pnpm exec node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.test.ts
  skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.test.ts docs/providers/elevenlabs.md
  pnpm docs:check-config-examples
  pnpm docs:check-links
  ```
- **Evidence before fix (executed RED on origin/main provider):**
  ```text
  FAIL |extension-media| ... > does not forward non-allowlisted query options
  AssertionError: expected null to be 'true'
  - Expected: "true"
  + Received: null
       80|     expect(form.get("no_verbatim")).toBe("true");
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
       Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  ✓ |extension-media| ... > posts multipart audio to ElevenLabs speech-to-text
  ✓ |extension-media| ... > forwards allowlisted providerOptions into the multipart form
  ✓ |extension-media| ... > does not forward non-allowlisted query options
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  [validate] 全部通过 ✅   (oxfmt + oxlint + extension-media shard + tsgo:core)
  docs_config_fences_validated=1318
  checked_internal_links=14968  broken_links=0
  ```
- **Runtime evidence after fix (shipped CLI, real HTTP request captured):**
  ```text
  $ node openclaw.mjs infer audio transcribe --file sample-440hz.wav --model elevenlabs/scribe_v2 --json
  { "ok": true, "capability": "audio.transcribe", "provider": "elevenlabs", "model": "scribe_v2",
    "outputs": [{ "text": "<transcript returned through the runner>", "kind": "audio.transcription" }] }

  captured multipart POST /v1/speech-to-text (32517 bytes):
    model_id         = "scribe_v2"
    no_verbatim      = "true"
    tag_audio_events = "false"          # boolean false stringified by the shared transport
    file             = sample-440hz.wav (32044 bytes)

  negative run (providerOptions also set webhook=..., use_multi_channel=true):
    captured body still only contains model_id / no_verbatim / tag_audio_events / file
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** `no_verbatim=true` and `tag_audio_events=false` appear in the
  multipart `FormData` in both the unit-test boundary and the shipped CLI runtime flow;
  `webhook` (non-allowlisted) is not sent.
- **What was not tested:** Live end-to-end transcription against the real ElevenLabs API and the
  Telegram Test Server echo path (no ElevenLabs credentials and no Telegram Test Server
  credentials were available in this environment); streaming/realtime STT path is unaffected and
  untested here.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** The runtime HTTP capture uses a local endpoint in place of
  `api.elevenlabs.io`; everything else in the flow (config parsing, runner precedence, registered
  provider, multipart serialization, real socket POST, response handling) is the shipped code path.
- **Review state:** CI green on head `f223905`; addressed the ClawSweeper "base-failing
  regression not shown" note with executed RED/GREEN logs above.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep local mutations with the Gateway state owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale plugin metadata when a separate local CLI process changes installed plugins while the Gateway owns their database.

## User Impact

Local plugin install, hook fallback, uninstall, enable/disable, registry repair, and package update now use the existing state-owner boundary. Online lifecycle commands retain their Gateway RPC route. Registry repair and the interactive plugin/hook updater require exclusive offline ownership and explain that the Gateway must be stopped. An interrupted offline update also restores accepted package/index changes before releasing ownership.

No schema, stored-format, durability, retention, or permission contract changes. Core `openclaw update` retains its existing updater owner; this applies to `openclaw plugins update`. Hosted marketplace catalog snapshot writes are a separate follow-up outside this installed-index scope.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under the single-owner database contract, a second process cannot write safely while the serving Gateway relies on in-process write receipts. This change reuses `runWithLocalStateOwner`: offline custody surrounds the existing plugin lifecycle lease, package/config CAS, and accepted compensation settlement. A queued registry refresh reads configuration after acquiring its plugin lease, so it sees a preceding command's policy publication.

Request cancellation must stop forward mutations without revoking custody needed for accepted rollback. The shared lifecycle helper keeps queued admission cancellable, then retains physical ownership through compensation; forward writes still check request authority. The update pipeline uses a separate synchronous forward guard so cancellation cannot poison the sticky transaction-ownership hook. Existing config-publication acceptance semantics remain unchanged.

This PR stacks on the roster/config and shared state-owner foundation at `74f5fe25a6b3` (`dbasync/ow2`). It contains 740 changed production lines (+425/-315, net +110), tests/support +175/-140 (net +35), docs +9/-3, and one exact obsolete mock-baseline deletion. Growth covers the reused owner scope, extracted registry command, and cancellation/custody split shared with Claw composition. The superseded registry runtime export and obsolete mocks are removed.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(codex): keep app-server process inspection deadline monotonic across clock skew
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Codex app-server tears down an orphaned transport (e.g. `codex` exits while a child app-server process is still registered), the containment sweep inspects the process tree under a 2s deadline. That deadline was seeded and consumed on the wall clock (`Date.now()`), but its remaining budget is handed to monotonic timers (`setTimeout` / `AbortSignal.timeout`). An NTP step between seeding and reading inflates the 2s budget by the rewind amount, so the sweep can hang far past its deadline; a forward jump shrinks the budget toward zero and aborts healthy inspections.

- Problem: `remainingInspectionTime` computes `deadline - Date.now()` and feeds the result to `setTimeout(remainingMs)` and `AbortSignal.timeout(remainingMs)`, which are monotonic. The seed sites (`terminateCodexAppServerOrphan`, `terminateCodexAppServerDescendants`, `prepareCodexAppServerProcessRegistration`, and the snapshot default) all use `Date.now()`. A wall-clock rewind of Δ stretches the remaining budget by Δ; a forward jump compresses it.
- Solution: move the deadline to the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) at the canonical owners, so the budget stays bounded while the monotonic inspection timers are in flight. `Math.floor` keeps the remaining value integral for `AbortSignal.timeout`.
- What changed: `transport-process-snapshot.ts` (`remainingInspectionTime`, snapshot default, exec callback compare), `transport-process-containment.ts` (4 seed sites + 10 same-domain compares), `transport-process-registration.ts` (2 seed sites + 1 compare). Test/support files that seeded deadlines with `Date.now()` updated to `performance.now()` to stay in the same clock domain.
- What did NOT change: no new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface. The deadline is still process-local (never persisted, never crosses a process boundary), so switching from a wall-clock epoch to a monotonic timestamp has no effect on any consumer that subtracts to compute a remaining budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The single canonical owner of the remaining-budget computation is `remainingInspectionTime`; fixing it there plus the seed sites unifies the clock domain for every caller of `readCodexAppServerProcessSnapshot` / `readCodexAppServerProcessCommand` / the containment and registration sweeps. This mirrors the monotonic-clock fix already shipped for sibling codex deadlines (#155863, #155855, #168144). `performance.now()` is global on Node 16+ and returns sub-millisecond floats, so `Math.floor` is applied at the owner to satisfy `AbortSignal.timeout`'s integer requirement (a float throws `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`). Same-domain comparisons (`performance.now() >= deadline`) are updated alongside the seeds to avoid mixing clocks. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface.

## User Impact

Codex app-server orphan and descendant containment now reliably respects the configured 2s inspection budget during host clock adjustments (NTP corrections, sleep/resume). Session cleanup no longer hangs past the deadline when the wall clock rewinds, and no longer aborts healthy process inspections when the wall clock jumps forward.

## Evidence

**Shipped-flow cleanup proof** — drives the REAL shipped Codex app-server client lifecycle (the same path the OpenClaw Gateway uses): `createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient` spawns the real `codex app-server` binary (v0.162.1), `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` completes the JSON-RPC handshake, then `client.closeAndWait()` runs the shipped teardown — `closeCodexAppServerTransportAndWait` → `terminateCodexAppServerDescendants` → `readCodexAppServerProcessSnapshot(deadline)` (the canonical owner this PR fixes). A wall-clock rewind is opened right before close, straddling the containment inspection's deadline seed and remaining-budget read:

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=post node --import tsx/esm proof-shipped-cleanup.mts   # this PR
post-fix (shipped client close, -90s rewind): handshake complete, codex pid=4065095
{ "rewindMs": -90000, "budgetMs": 2000, "elapsedMs": 708, "abortMs": 1999,
  "aliveBefore": true, "aliveAfter": false, "settledInBudget": true,
  "cleanedUp": true, "closeResult": { "exited": true }, "error": null }

$ PROOF_MODE=pre  node --import tsx/esm proof-shipped-cleanup.mts   # origin/main, -5s
{ "rewindMs": -5000, "budgetMs": 2000, "elapsedMs": 489, "abortMs": 7000, ... }
```

The spawned codex process is alive before `closeAndWait` and gone after; the shipped teardown settles in 708ms (well inside the 2s budget) and the armed `AbortSignal.timeout` budget stays at 1999ms despite the 90s rewind. Pre-fix through the same shipped flow: `abortMs` inflates to **7000ms** (2s + 5s rewind); post-fix stays bounded at 1999ms even under the larger 90s rewind.

**Evidence at a glance** — real `codex app-server` binary spawned as the inspection target, driving the REAL production `readCodexAppServerProcessSnapshot` (Linux full-tree path → `AbortSignal.timeout(remainingMs)`), 90s wall-clock rewind between seed and remaining-budget read:

| clock state | pre-fix (main, `Date.now()`) | post-fix (this PR, `performance.now()`) |
|---|---|---|
| wall rewind −90s | remaining inflates to **92000ms** (2s + 90s) | remaining ≈ **1999ms** (bounded by 2s budget) |
| normal (no skew) | 2000ms | 1999ms |

```console
$ PROOF_MODE=pre  node --import tsx/esm proof-real-codex.mts   # origin/main
{ "abortMs": 92000, "rowCount": 220, "error": null, "elapsedMs": 175 }   # pre-fix RED
$ PROOF_MODE=post node --import tsx/esm proof-real-codex.mts   # this PR
{ "abortMs": 1999,  "rowCount": 224, "error": null, "elapsedMs": 110 }   # post-fix GREEN
```

The rewind is a `Date.now` counter-model spy (first post-open call returns the pre-rewind value so the caller seeds with the untainted clock; later calls return the rewound clock so `remainingInspectionTime` reads the skewed clock); `performance.now` is left untouched — the precise cross-domain failure mode. `abortMs` is the budget captured at the real `AbortSignal.timeout(remainingMs)` call inside the shipped Linux procfs reader. The shipped `terminateCodexAppServerOrphan` reap entry point shows the same bounded settlement + observed cleanup (881ms, alive→gone) under a 90s rewind.

Focused test suite (post-fix worktree, 7 files on the codex app-server process-inspection path): `53 passed | 7 skipped` + `39 passed (39)`. Static checks: `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on all 10 changed files. Collision check: no open PR touches `transport-process-{snapshot,containment,registration}.ts`; sibling monotonic-clock PRs (#155863, #155855, #168144) cover different codex deadlines and do not overlap.

What was not tested: no real NTP step was injected into a live host clock; the rewind is simulated via `Date.now` spy (counter model) while `performance.now` is held fixed (the precise cross-domain failure mode). Windows `ps` path not exercised locally (Linux procfs tested, including against a real spawned `codex app-server` binary driven through the shipped client lifecycle).

prs.title: fix(cli): guard local plugin state writes at command boundaries
prs.body:
## Problem

A separate CLI process must not change plugin installation records, registry state, or plugin configuration while a Gateway owns local state. Some plugin commands already delegate mutations to the Gateway, but local fallbacks and standalone updates can still write beside it.

Supersedes #168420.

## Design

Reuse the command-boundary `runWithLocalStateOwner` guard from #168417. Existing install, uninstall, enable/disable, and reload Gateway routes remain unchanged. Local mutation paths acquire the existing offline owner and carry its assertion to existing effect callbacks. There is no new routing protocol, compensation, cancellation settlement, lease mechanism, or fencing.

Guarded paths:
- Local plugin install and hook-pack install fallback, including the deprecated `hooks install` alias.
- Local plugin uninstall and enable/disable fallbacks.
- `plugins registry --refresh`.
- `plugins update` and the deprecated `hooks update` alias.
- `plugins marketplace entries` when fetching and `plugins marketplace refresh`, because both can persist feed snapshots. `entries --offline` stays read-only.
- `hooks enable` and `hooks disable` configuration writes.

A running owner produces actionable stop-Gateway-and-rerun guidance; routed lifecycle commands continue to use their existing Gateway methods. Offline behavior is preserved. Update and marketplace refresh now save for the next Gateway start instead of writing locally then requesting a runtime refresh.

Accepted edge case: a Gateway starting mid-command is covered by the existing ownership guard at the effect. We do not add compensation or a second admission protocol around that race. Existing in-process Gateway callers retain their current owner.

## Proof

The requested Codex P1 autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

- AWS focused proof on `eac4c5d985671dcd3e29592af79718d794c7f1ef`: 12 test files, 227 tests passed with `--maxWorkers=1` (154.38 s wall time; Vitest runner 153.69 s).
- The 23 ownership cases cover refusal with an active owner, offline execution, effect-time revalidation, hook fallback, and unchanged install/uninstall/enable/disable Gateway routes. Hook enable/disable and all 37 existing migration scenarios also pass.
- Negative control: the registry-owner refusal test fails against the pre-fix runtime because the command resolves instead of refusing.
- Required CI is green on `0ac0b6fd583e62d6103c48bb77e40f98e2d78ea7`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38102314276.
- Type-aware oxlint and export-collision checks passed. Remote `check:changed` on `0ac0b6fd583e62d6103c48bb77e40f98e2d78ea7` passed formatting, every ratchet, production typechecking, and all core test typechecking groups. It stops only on Knip's existing `src/gateway/server-instance-runtime.types.ts: GatewayApprovalEventPublisherV2` unused export. The identical finding was independently reproduced on main `bbd2daf8b6def57eb0ac47c5e270c9b39cc168e6`; this PR does not touch that file.
- The only change after the 227-test run removed the obsolete mock-export baseline entry; test and production inputs are unchanged. Earlier CI caught stale update/migration assertions, a missing mock export, and the retired baseline entry; those are fixed.

Production delta: +193 / -156 lines (37 net), excluding tests, test support, and docs. The oversized runtime file does not grow.

Plugin loading is untouched, so the published-driver update cell is not required for this change.

prs.title: fix(cloud-workers): Stop cannot release a dedicated worker whose computer driver is wedged
prs.body:
Closes #166196

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Stop, idle reclaim, and `environments.destroy { force: true }` all fail and the paid machine keeps running when a dedicated cloud worker's attached computer-use driver can no longer release its session. Seen on native Windows after a UAC prompt stalled the agent; reproduced live on Linux below by keeping one turn's computer execution idle past the driver's 300 s idle TTL, after which every driver call, including the release, fails with `authorization context expired` / `DriverError.Tool`.

## User Impact

User impact: a dedicated cloud worker whose computer driver is wedged is destroyed on Stop, reclaim, or force, instead of retrying for an hour and parking with "Run crabbox stop <lease>". While its teardown is pending, `environments.list` reports `stopping` and no longer advertises a desktop that `desktop.observe` already refuses. Shared and unknown hosts keep today's behavior: their stop still waits for the computer session to be released.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider teardown already passes a reason (`provider-destroying`, then `provider-destroyed`) to the node tunnel for dedicated machines only, so a machine the provider is about to destroy does not need the worker's own stop acknowledgement. The attached-computer close joined that same teardown later without the reason, so one failed `__close_execution` rejected `stopOwner` before `destroyLease` on every attempt.

The computer owner now receives the same reason:

- `provider-destroying`: closing still fences local input; a failed native release is logged instead of blocking the destroy, and the owner keeps custody so a failed provider destroy stays retryable.
- `provider-destroyed`: the confirmed destruction releases those owners.
- no reason (shared or unknown host): a failed release still fails the stop, as before.

The environment projection applies the existing desktop admission rule (`destroyRequestedAtMs`) to `desktopAvailable`, and the summary maps a pending teardown to the existing `stopping` status; recorded errors still report `error`. The desktop docs describe both.

## Evidence

Live before/after with the shipped Stop flow: Crabbox on AWS (Linux desktop worker, profile `class: small`, dedicated), Gateway on a separate Linux host, model `xai/grok-4.7`. Same config and steps on both builds; only the checkout differs (`main` 4644b027 vs this patch at 9792aa67, which is patch-identical to the current head after the rebase below). Times are UTC; environment ids are replaced with `<env>`.

Trigger, no fault injection: one agent turn takes a `computer` screenshot of the attached desktop, runs `exec sleep 115` three times, then takes another screenshot. The CUA driver session idles past its idle TTL (`maxIdleTtlSeconds: 300n` in `extensions/cua-computer/src/driver-client.ts`), so the second screenshot fails as in the issue, and the end-of-turn native release fails the same way:

```text
[tools] computer failed: Error: COMPUTER_REFUSED_permission_denied: Permission denied: authorization context expired
```

(The same on `@trycua/cua-driver` 0.32.0 directly: after the idle TTL an action returns `permission_denied: authorization context expired` and `endSession` throws `DriverError.Tool`.)

Then Stop (`environments.session.destroy`) while an in-process client samples `environments.list` for 75 s, about 150 samples/s, printing only changes.

`main` 4644b027:

```text
01:23:38.883 {"status":"available","desktop":true,"state":"ready"}      <- unchanged for all 11,661 samples
01:23:43.551 res ✗ environments.session.destroy 34ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Attached computer cleanup failed
01:24:14.035 [worker-environments] Conversation environment cleanup will retry (worker:<env>): Attached computer cleanup failed | Session computer cleanup failed | Error: DriverError.Tool
01:25:14.070 [worker-environments] Conversation environment cleanup will retry (worker:<env>): Attached computer cleanup failed | Session computer cleanup failed | Error: DriverError.Tool
01:25:16.300 res ✗ environments.destroy {force: true} 27ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=worker environment destruction failed
environments.list afterwards: {"status":"error","desktop":true,"state":"ready","error":"Worker result abandoned by forced operator teardown"}
```

The lease kept running until a manual `crabbox stop`.

This PR:

```text
01:38:06.430 {"status":"available","desktop":true,"state":"ready"}
01:38:08.671 [worker-environments] Attached computer cleanup failed | Session computer cleanup failed | Error: DriverError.Tool; continuing provider teardown of the dedicated machine.
01:38:08.679 {"status":"stopping","desktop":false,"state":"ready"}
01:38:09.743 {"status":"stopping","desktop":false,"state":"destroying"}
01:38:09.749 res ✓ environments.session.destroy 1106ms
01:38:09.756 {"status":"unavailable","desktop":false,"state":"destroyed"}
environments.session.destroy -> {"stopped": true, "environment": {"status": "unavailable", "trust": "disposable", "worker": {"providerId": "crabbox", "state": "destroyed", "tunnelStatus": "stopped"}}}
```

EC2 reports the lease instance terminated at 01:38:09 (`User initiated`), from this Stop.

Regression tests through the real owners (computer service + transport owner with a deterministic native close failure; worker environment service + node tunnel manager):

- `computer-service.test.ts`: strict without a reason, non-blocking and retained on `provider-destroying`, released on `provider-destroyed`.
- `provider-node-teardown.test.ts`: a dedicated machine with a wedged attached computer reaches `provider.destroy` and `destroyed`; a shared host still rejects with `Attached computer cleanup failed` and never calls destroy; a pending dedicated teardown summarizes as `stopping` without `desktop`.
- On `main` (4644b027) the three new behavior tests fail with the reported chain (`Attached computer cleanup failed` <- `Session computer cleanup failed` <- `DriverError.Tool`) and `expected 'available' to be 'stopping'`; the shared-host case passes on both.

Cost (local, Node 24.21, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): the new `computer-service.test.ts` case runs in about 0.07 s; the three new `provider-node-teardown.test.ts` cases take about 2.7-3.0 s each, in line with the file's existing cases that share its service fixture.

Checks: the `pnpm check:changed` plan for this diff (lanes core, coreTests, docs), run step by step: format, oxlint, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, import cycles, the SQLite worker, assertion-safety, mock-export and timeout ratchets, boundary and docs-config checks all pass.

Regression run (`src/gateway/worker-environments`, the computer tool, environments RPC, desktop, and the other `summarizeWorkerEnvironment` / `desktopAvailable` consumers): passing apart from the items below. One existing expectation changes on purpose: the `environments.list` fixture in `environments.pool.test.ts` has `destroyRequestedAtMs` set and now reports `stopping` instead of `available`. The Control UI already maps `status: "stopping"` (or `destroyRequestedAtMs` in details) to its releasing pool state.

Inherited on `main` 4644b027, reproduced without this diff and not changed here:

- `check:max-lines-ratchet` step: `OPENCLAW_* count 456 exceeds budget 455`.
- `lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary`: advisory `ui-e2e: 722 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit`.
- Knip unused exports in files this diff does not touch (`tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`, `update-command-post-activation-inspections.ts`, `sessions-channel-fixture.test-support.ts`).
- `bootstrap.test.ts` (npm archive bootstrap), `workspace-sync-inventory.test.ts`, `placement-force-abandon.test.ts`, `local-workspace-template.test.ts`, and the `server.app-sdk-composed-resources.test.ts` timeout.

`worker-turn-execution.test.ts` and `live-chat.test.ts` each failed once in a heavily loaded parallel run and pass when run alone (live-chat 3/3). `destination-authority.e2e.test.ts` and `inference-authority.e2e.test.ts` were not run locally: their E2E runtime build did not complete on this host.

Rebased onto `main` 3666e847 because the previous CI merge ref included #168635's lint and SDK-surface breakage (`check-lint-core-2`/`-4` in `src/plugin-state/plugin-state-observation-cache.ts` and `src/infra/sqlite-worker-plugin-comparison.test.ts`, `plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`), which `main` fixed in f9940dc8. The patch is unchanged (same `git patch-id`); on the rebased tree `computer-service.test.ts`, `provider-node-teardown.test.ts`, and `environments.pool.test.ts` pass (22 tests).

Not changed here: the driver session expiring after 300 s idle inside one turn, after which later `computer` calls in that turn fail.

prs.title: feat(channels): status line on in-flight progress drafts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On chat surfaces, a long agent turn is a gap of silence. Progress drafts already show
*what* the agent is doing (`🛠️ Bash: run tests`), but never how long it has been going
or that a reply steers the run. In a group, nobody can tell whether the agent is stuck
or working.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR originally decorated delivered replies from the outbound delivery pipeline. That
design could never work, and reviewing it before landing is what caught it. Three
independent gates blocked it:

1. It required the `message-edit` capability, which exactly one channel declares —
   Telegram, and only because this PR added it.
2. Telegram never routes in-flight replies through core durable delivery:
   `sendPayload(payload, { durable: info.kind === "final" })`
   (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch-reply.ts:322`), so block replies fall to
   Telegram's own sender and never reach `src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`.
3. That call hardcodes `info: { kind: "final" }`, while the footer required `kind !== "final"`.

Worse, the activity label was fed from standalone tool-progress messages, which
progress-draft channels suppress — so even had it rendered, it would only ever have shown
the static `Working` fallback.

The root cause was architectural: the feature assumed intermediate replies flow through
core delivery, but Telegram owns its in-turn streaming precisely so they don't. So the
line now lives on the progress-draft compositor, which already owns in-flight status,
already receives tool/plan/approval events, and already tears the draft down on success,
cancel, and error.

That let the whole relocation layer go: no per-conversation records, no pending-strip
queue with retry, no terminal-run set, no mutex, no message-id tracking. The engine went
from ~340 lines of bookkeeping to a ~44-line pure renderer.

## User Impact

Channels running `streaming.mode: "progress"` get one trailing line on the live draft:

```text
▸ Exec: run tests · 2m · reply to steer
```

Configured per channel via `channels.<channel>.streaming.progress.status`
(`activity` default, `minimal`, `off`). It sits with the feature it belongs to instead of
a global `messages.*` key that would silently do nothing unless that channel ran progress
mode. Deterministic — no model call, no added latency, and it cannot drift from what the
agent is doing. Transport-only: never enters the transcript or model context.

It is deliberately kept out of both the draft text and the structured `lines` array, so
the rolling `maxLines` window can never evict it and id-keyed merging can never claim it.

## Evidence

Validated on a Blacksmith Testbox pinned to the exact head (`git rev-parse HEAD` asserted
against the local SHA before trusting any result — an earlier run in this session was a
false green from a lease bound to a different checkout):

- `pnpm tsgo` — clean
- `pnpm check:test-types` — clean
- `pnpm test src/channels src/config extensions/telegram extensions/discord extensions/slack`
- Focused: `status-footer` (10), `progress-draft-compositor` (41), `streaming` (30),
  `progress-draft-preview` (4)

New tests cover the template (including code-point-safe truncation that keeps surrogate
pairs intact, and word-boundary cuts), the compositor wiring, survival of a `maxLines`
overflow, teardown on final/cancel, the elapsed clock resetting per turn, config
resolution, and the Telegram renderer placing the line last on all paths.

Docs moved from `docs/concepts/messages.md` to `docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md`, where
the feature now lives; `docs_map.md` regenerated.

### Known gap

Matrix and MS Teams build drafts from the Layer-A primitives instead of the compositor,
so they show no status line. They degrade cleanly rather than breaking, and can adopt it
by moving to the compositor.
