prs.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
prs.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-08 JST / 2026-07-07 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@623534400684eca7c451cf587189fae714f2abe2` into the PR branch. The merge conflicted in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`; resolved by keeping main's pre-connect send-evidence cleanup and this PR's no-budget reconciliation-deferral path/tests.
- Follow-up main refresh in the same run: `origin/main` advanced again to `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; merged it with no conflicts and pushed final head `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready with head `1779a704bc1b3a9e7b57e994fea534fac68c2eec`, base `a7c4a0471d944e3c3bf2b3071a5b1b485548dc8d`, `mergeable=CONFLICTING` via GraphQL, and the local branch was 378 commits behind `origin/main`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`, base is `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; GitHub CI is pending on the refreshed head and `reviewDecision` remains empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- Current-head refresh validation:
  - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` was attempted locally after the conflicted merge, but the infra Vitest runner produced no test output for 150s and was interrupted; the narrower recovery-file run also produced no test output for 120s and was interrupted. This hang was root-caused and fixed in the follow-up below.
  - Functional PR diff remains scoped to 7 files: 2 source, 4 tests, 1 docs; 293 insertions / 36 deletions.

## Follow-up (2026-07-09): infra shard hang, replay-pacing skip, and summary counters

Fixed in `1ab8620ebfc43fef70dbf258e3888338bcd704ec` (`fix(outbound): skip replay pacing for unreconcilable deferrals`).

- Root cause of the CI/local hang: `recoverPendingDeliveries` awaited `recoveryReplayPacer.wait(deadline)` (a real `sleep`) *before* `drainQueuedEntry` for every eligible entry, including ambiguous rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter that only defer. Under the recovery test's fake timers (`delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts:574`, "rechecks deferred ambiguous entries after the backoff elapses"), the pacer's `lastReplayStartedAt` equalled the frozen clock, so `wait()` scheduled a `RECOVERY_REPLAY_SPACING_MS` `sleep` that was never advanced. That deadlocked the module-singleton pacer mutex (`waitQueue`), which then hung every later test that paced. The merge that surfaced it advanced `origin/main` to `7ff3f2dbf922`; the pacing feature landed on the branch across the same range.
- Fix: resolve reconciliation availability (cheap adapter/`reconcileUnknownSend` capability check) before the pacer in both `recoverPendingDeliveries` and `drainPendingDeliveries`. No-reconciler ambiguous rows now defer as a no-op — they no longer pay the 250ms send-replay spacing or eat the 60s `maxRecoveryMs` deadline (addresses the 2026-07-07 Codex review). Entries that actually reconcile or replay pace exactly as before.
- Reporting: the no-reconciler deferral now increments a distinct `deferredNoReconciler` summary counter and log clause instead of being reported as a delivery failure, so operator logs match the persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0` state.
- Validation (local, current head `1ab8620`):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts` — previously hanging shard now completes: **260 files, 4303 passed, 3 skipped, 156s**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts` — 4 files, 78 passed (adds a focused case proving a no-reconciler deferral consumes no pacer budget).
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` — clean.
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` — clean.
- Current-head GitHub CI after push: pending on the new head, including Real behavior proof and normal CI/security guard buckets.
- Previous scoped validation for the functional changes, before this main refresh:
  - `node scripts/docs-list.js`
  - `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`
    - 4 files passed, 69 tests passed.
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
    - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence (captured before the 2026-07-09 counter fix, so the summary still reports the no-reconciler deferral as `1 failed`; see note below):

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 1 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":1,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0}
deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

Note — this evidence predates commit `1ab8620`. The queue/state observations (no `deliver` call, one pending entry, `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`) are unchanged, but the summary and log now classify the no-reconciler deferral correctly. After the fix the same scenario reports:

```text
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff), 1 deferred (no reconciler)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":0,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0,"deferredNoReconciler":1}
```

This corrected behavior is asserted deterministically by `delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` (e.g. "keeps entries abandoned after platform send may have started pending without reconciliation" and the new "does not spend replay pacing on unavailable-reconciler deferrals" case). The terminal proof was not re-run on this machine because it hosts a production gateway; the recovery path's real `resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter(allowBootstrap: true)` bootstrap does not terminate in a bare non-gateway `tsx` process, so the deterministic Vitest coverage is the authoritative post-fix evidence.

What was not tested: no live Discord gateway/channel send was performed in this pass. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and Control UI/API delivery-state surface remain open under #87544.





## Current-main refresh (2026-07-14)

Head: `df16b89e76a23d26ddd1941e435386819b077cfd`

- Merged upstream `main` through `4da0eb19c570a561ed4a4f80756abc58b89dd1a4` and resolved the recovery, storage, and integration-test conflicts while preserving the current queue-policy and audit contracts.
- Moved channel reconciliation into `delivery-queue-reconciliation.ts` so the oversized recovery module remains below its current-main physical-LOC baseline.
- Recovery propagates deferral-persistence failures and leaves ambiguous sends pending when no reconciler exists, including rows whose historical retry count reached the normal replay limit.
- A later-available reconciler now runs before max-retry terminal handling: confirmed sends are acknowledged, while `not_sent` and unresolved results dead-letter without another replay. Proven `not_sent` outcomes audit as known queue failures for both ambiguous recovery states; unresolved outcomes remain unknown. Both accepted review findings were fixed and their threads resolved.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts` — 4 files, 91 tests passed.
- Targeted oxfmt, oxlint, scoped production-LOC ratchet, and fresh pre-commit autoreview passed; the final autoreview rated the follow-up correct at 0.93 with no actionable findings.
- Exact-head fork CI: [run 29305672121](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29305672121) — 70 success, 31 skipped, 0 failures.
- Crabbox was unavailable on this machine, so the narrow local test fallback above plus secretless fork CI were used.

prs.title: fix(update): FreeBSD package recovery refuses repair and retire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on FreeBSD, the printed package-recovery command refuses `repair` and `retire` with "managed handoff process start identity is unavailable" after an interrupted npm update.

## User Impact

User impact: FreeBSD operators can now `repair` and `retire` an interrupted npm package update with its printed recovery command, as on Linux and macOS. `status` already worked.

The recovery helper is written by the updater that runs the update, so this applies to operations prepared by an updater that includes this fix. Helpers written by already-published updaters stay digest-bound and keep `status` only on FreeBSD; docs/install/updating.md says so.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery helper is a sealed single-file runtime. In sealed builds the shared FreeBSD identity loader deliberately refuses to load native code from the host, and only the managed-handoff runtime substituted its own staged loader. FreeBSD leases persist the kernel process start time since boot in exact microseconds, and installed CLIs compare against that value, so a `ps`-based fallback would make a live helper look dead.

The package-recovery build now gets its own loader. It loads `koffi` only from the package trees the operation records: the live installation, then `anchor/previous` (where publication moves it), then `anchor/candidate`. One of them exists in every unfinished state, including the missing-installation window that `repair` exists for. It never searches the helper's own directory neighbors. The single-file helper and the v1 journal and control-directory layout are unchanged; staging an addon beside the helper would have changed that strictly validated layout for published drivers.

Update behavior: no journal, schema, or control-layout change, so published drivers and later candidates read these operations unchanged. Only the helper's loader changes, and it is fixed at preparation time by the running updater.

## Evidence

- FreeBSD 14.4-RELEASE amd64, QEMU TCG, Node 24.21.0, `test/scripts/managed-handoff-build-config.test.ts`:
  - main `8d1c7bcbce48`: managed case passes; package case fails with `Package publication recovery refused: managed handoff process start identity is unavailable` (same as the previously reported baseline `89a1e7e52451`).
  - this fix: 2/2 pass, package case 428s, covering status, repair, retire, a second operation, and stale-command refusal. Run with `--testTimeout=1200000` because TCG emulation exceeds the 120s default once the full recovery sequence executes; the first run with the default limit had no assertion failure before the timeout. The committed limit is unchanged.
- macOS (arm64): same file 2/2, package case 28s. The new build-graph assertion (package bundle uses its own loader, not the shared one) runs on every platform.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, scripts test tsconfig, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean.
- Build guards (from ClawSweeper's review): the new loader is registered in the exact sealed-recovery set of the export-collision guard (any other implementation still collides) and in declaration-input capture, with both loader URLs kept literal. `pnpm lint:tmp:export-name-collisions` exits 0; `check-export-name-collisions`, `write-unified-entry-dts`, `managed-handoff-build-config`, `ui`, `dist-artifact-ownership`, `tsdown-declaration-resolution`, and `write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts` tests pass (113 passed, 3 skipped).
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the first-party mock export ratchet on `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection-placement.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; it already fails at the merge base `8d1c7bcbce48` and is fixed on main by `00e095399b20`.
- Codex autoreview (P0–P2): scoped-clean for both commits.

Test cost: `pnpm test test/scripts/managed-handoff-build-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 110s wall on macOS (about 100s Vitest, mostly sealed-bundle compilation); the package case itself is 28s. No new test files; Linux and macOS CI already run the full package case, so CI cost is unchanged.

Related: the in-flight Koffi removal moves FreeBSD identity to `@openclaw/proc-safe`; this loader ports directly to that package's identity entry from the same recorded roots.

prs.body:
## Summary
- clarify the replay-unsafe Codex app-server timeout message so users know OpenClaw intentionally did not auto-replay after tool activity
- include completed item id/type/status/tool metadata in app-server idle-timeout diagnostics, matching the raw response diagnostics already emitted
- add focused coverage for completed item diagnostic details and update timeout outcome expectations

## Why
When Codex app-server emits completed tool/item notifications but never sends the terminal `turn/completed` event, OpenClaw currently reports that work may already have happened but does not explain that replay was intentionally suppressed to avoid duplicate side effects. This makes the incident look like a generic bot failure instead of a replay-safety guard. The extra diagnostic fields also make future reports easier to triage from trajectory/log data.

## Tests
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_INCLUDE_FILE=/tmp/openclaw-codex-tests.json node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex.config.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-notifications.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-notifications.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-results.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-results.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts`

Related: #87781 handles replay-safe app-server stalls. This PR covers the replay-unsafe/user-facing side-effect path.

prs.title: feat(approvals): configurable exec approval outcome echo
prs.body:
Related: #113262

Replaces #113357, which was closed as stalled without real-behavior proof. This
rebases the change onto current `main` (upstream refactored `handleResolved`,
so the previous diff no longer applied) and ships the missing proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Every resolved forwarded exec approval posts a second message to the chat target
(`Exec approval: Allowed` / `Exec approval: Denied`). In busy rooms that
follow-up can dominate the bot's traffic, and the strings were hardcoded with no
config key to suppress them.

## User Impact

User impact: operators forwarding exec or plugin approvals can now set
`approvals.exec.outcome` (or `approvals.plugin.outcome`) to `"none"` and resolve
approvals without the extra decision message landing in chat.

- `"message"` is the default and keeps today's behavior exactly.
- `"none"` suppresses only the resolved-decision follow-up. The approval prompt
  and its expiry notification are unaffected, and the decision stays queryable
  through `/approve` and the CLI.
- No migration and no breaking change: the field is optional and defaults to the
  current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The forwarder always published the resolved payload from `handleResolved`. This
adds a single configuration decision between resolution and outbound delivery.
The knob lives on the existing forwarding config next to `mode` and `targets`,
and is shared by exec and plugin forwarding because both use the same pipeline.

Scope is **forwarded approvals only**. Native approval clients — reaction
shortcuts, DM cards, and same-chat `/approve` — publish their own resolved
outcome through their channel adapter, and are intentionally unaffected. The
approval decision is still applied in every case; only the extra chat message is
suppressed. A `"update"` mode that edits the original prompt instead of posting a
new message is not included: it needs per-delivery message-id tracking plus edit
support on every forwarded channel.

## Evidence

Reproducible validation transcript against production code. Neither the forwarder
nor the config schema is mocked; only the outbound `deliver` boundary is.

```
$ pnpm test src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "forwarding outcome"

 ✓ keeps publishing the decision when outcome is unset (default)   23ms
 ✓ keeps publishing the decision when outcome is message            3ms
 ✓ suppresses the decision echo when outcome is none                2ms
 ✓ still releases the pending expiry when outcome is none           2ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 40 skipped (44)
```

`suppresses the decision echo` observes the delivery count at the channel
boundary: 1 delivery (the prompt) with `outcome: "none"` versus 2 (prompt plus
decision) by default and with `"message"`.

**Regression guard.** Reverting only the gate in `exec-approval-forwarder.ts` makes
exactly the two behavior tests fail and no other:

```
 Tests  2 failed | 42 passed (44)
 × suppresses the decision echo when outcome is none
 × still releases the pending expiry when outcome is none
```

The expiry test guards a real leak: `pending.settle()` is what removes the pending
entry **and** clears its expiry timer, so a suppressed outcome still settles with
a no-op terminal. Returning before `settle` would leave the entry in the registry
with its timer armed and fire an "expired" notice for an already-resolved
approval.

**Gates**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm test src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 44 passed, 0 failed (22.7s wall) |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | all lanes passed |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` (changed files) | 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` (changed files) | clean |
| `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` | 1282 config fences validated against the schema |

**Test cost.** The four new tests are 30ms total; the file's measured wall time is
22.7s with 1 worker, dominated by transform, not by the added cases.

**Target boundary.** What the knob does and does not touch:

| Path | Affected |
|------|----------|
| Forwarded approval decision echo (`approvals.exec` / `approvals.plugin`) | Yes — suppressed by `"none"` |
| Forwarded approval prompt delivery | No |
| Forwarded approval expiry notification | No |
| Native reaction shortcut outcome | No — channel adapter owns it |
| Native DM card outcome | No — channel adapter owns it |
| Same-chat `/approve` confirmation | No — channel adapter owns it |
| The approval decision itself | No — still applied |

**Gap.** No live-channel proof: the `deliver` boundary is mocked, which is
isolated channel-boundary evidence rather than a live Matrix/Slack run. The issue
asks for a Matrix deployment, and confirming it there is the natural follow-up
before treating this as resolving the reported room noise.

prs.title: fix(feishu): quick-action and confirmation cards fail to send
prs.body:
Fixes #79824.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening Feishu quick actions or a command-confirmation card receive no card because those two producers still emit a V1 action row inside a schema 2.0 card.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the supported V2 column/button row in the current quick-action and approval producers. Button labels, styles, command envelopes, actor/chat/session binding, expiry, and callback policy stay unchanged.

This updates the original fix to current main. Native-card normalization and presentation buttons already avoid legacy action rows, so their current owners and the old outbound implementation are not changed. Approval persistence, inbound forms, and streaming are outside this repair.

## User Impact

Quick-action menus and their confirmation cards no longer contain the legacy row rejected by the V2 schema. Confirm/cancel behavior and existing actor, conversation, expiry, and duplicate-callback safeguards are preserved.

## Evidence

- Current baseline `83c1767446cb101f239cbed430524e2934556ebe`: the candidate regression suite reports **8 failures** against unchanged production code.
- Candidate: **215 focused/adjacent tests pass**, including actual produced-button confirm/cancel, wrong actor/chat, expiry, and duplicate handling.
- Real producers, production JSON serialization, and callback dispatch were exercised through a **local HTTP schema fixture**: launcher, direct approval, and metadata-produced approval reject legacy rows before the fix and accept the V2 rows after it.
- Independent P0–P2 source review is clean. Scoped repository checks and exact-head/native landing receipts are linked in the current proof comment.
- **Limitations:** the HTTP schema validator and transport are controlled fixtures, not the authenticated Feishu service. No current-head visual render or production message was attempted; no Feishu credentials or operator runtime were used.

### Original contributor evidence and credit

Original fix and live reproduction by **@xiabee (Yunjie Xiao)**; original commit ancestry is preserved, including `09ecc9eba006808b5a679454183083daecbfd12e`. The maintainer port changes only the remaining current producers and focused tests.

The contributor reported a May 9, 2026 production hot-patch experiment on OpenClaw 2026.5.7 / Kylin Linux with the Feishu Windows client. Before that rewrite, the service returned `230099 / 200861 / unsupported tag action`; afterward, delivery recovered and a button callback reached the agent:

```text
Before: ErrPath: ROOT -> body -> elements -> [1](tag: action);
        cards of schema V2 no longer support this capability
After:  Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed
        handling structured card action feishu.payload.button
```

That historical report supports the schema diagnosis; it is **not** a current-head live validation or a claim that every old outbound path remains defective.

[Current exact-head proof, raw artifacts and landing status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79832#issuecomment-5681181015).

prs.title: fix: use Claude Code native models for CLI selections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI selections come from a static model list instead of the model menu allowed by the current Claude Code account and organization.

## User Impact

Claude Code's initialize-only model menu supplies canonical `anthropic/<id>` selections on the `claude-cli` runtime, including newly introduced IDs and native effort levels. Configured and selected older IDs remain listed. Pickers use the published snapshot without waiting for discovery. API-only and hybrid users retain their API catalog behavior.

No configuration or schema migration is required. Existing settings remain valid; new sign-ins no longer seed a static CLI model menu. A logged-out CLI retains configured rows as unavailable with `missing-auth`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport previously discarded the initialize model menu. Discovery now captures it once per account/config/environment generation, with cancellation and a bounded timeout, then publishes through the existing catalog owner. Hosted metadata enriches exact IDs only. Wildcard admission uses the native inventory rather than static manifest membership.

The Gateway path also needed its native discovery hook retained alongside the sibling API provider and the canonical refresh scope expanded to the native realm. Native menu discovery now consumes the plugin's generation-scoped Claude login probe directly. Credential-provider aliases remain unchanged, so saved account pins retain their existing credential identity; an API credential alias cannot hide or stand in for the independent native login.

For CLI-only users, the published menu also replaces hosted-only public rows rather than merely marking them unavailable. This keeps `models list --provider anthropic` consistent with the picker while preserving internal transport variants and the hybrid/API path.

Removed: static Claude CLI manifest membership, static CLI sign-in allowlist seeding/constants, and static-catalog wildcard admission. Existing Doctor canonicalization remains unchanged.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Earlier focused provider, transport, migration and catalog validation passed 222 tests, including the final projection/owner/auth-choice subset of 66. The earlier alias-exclusion approach was replaced after CI exposed a saved-account regression; the final repair retains credential aliases and moves native menu authentication to the plugin's own prepared login fact.
- The final saved-account repair passed all 42 focused tests: 14 Gateway CLI-runtime availability cases, 22 legacy auth-choice cases, and 6 native discovery cases. The four saved-account cases failed on the first merged candidate but passed on `origin/main`; keeping credential aliases and using the plugin's native auth probe fixed them without weakening assertions. The repaired build and the full release-to-candidate upgrade proof both passed.
- The final native catalog projection also passed all 44 catalog-decision/owner tests and targeted Oxlint with zero warnings/errors. Redundant per-row array copies were removed, and copy-on-write model enrichment uses an explicit loop; no snapshot rows are mutated. The release-to-candidate upgrade proof passed again on this final projection.
- Final lint-only corrections merged duplicate type imports and used non-mutating sorting in the sign-in test. All 92 Anthropic files passed targeted extension lint with zero warnings/errors, and all 19 migration tests passed. These changes do not alter emitted production behavior; the frozen runtime upgrade proof remains applicable.
  The Gateway trace reached `selection claude-cli ['claude-cli']` but then logged `hook ['claude-cli'] false`; the fixed Gateway publishes `providerOutcomes: [{provider: 'claude-cli', status: 'ready'}]`.
- Isolated Gateway protocol proof with a synthetic `claude`: all four captured native IDs plus configured `claude-opus-4-7`, all on `claude-cli`; both CLI list forms matched. Restricting `availableModels` to haiku left only haiku plus the two explicitly configured/selected IDs, in both RPC and CLI. Passive reads returned before discovery completed (143 ms unrestricted; 8 ms restricted). Dry resolution selected `claude-cli` for all five IDs.
- **Earlier real-account check:** RPC and both CLI list forms passed against the machine's Claude Code login, with native low/medium/high/xhigh/max effort levels. The passive picker returned in 94 ms while refresh took 10.2 s. Only the initialize-only child received the real HOME; OpenClaw used its own isolated profile and port. No prompts, login/logout, or edits to real Claude settings. The final revision's upgrade proof below uses only a secretless fake Claude child.
- The earlier revision's tracked `check-changed` passed formatting, core/plugin/extension typechecks and boundaries; its dead-export scan failed on exports in untouched model-auth/runtime modules and `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`. The current focused build completed with the advisory UI startup-size overage (366.4 KiB versus 366.1 KiB).

### SDK surface comparison after merging main

Merged `origin/main` at `97e81ce0d5d96449449b545b80fb0c989c591c78`. This PR adds no exports under `src/plugin-sdk`, no extension `api.ts`/`runtime-api.ts` barrel changes, and no package export changes. The focused surface-report test reproduces the same budget failures on that main commit and candidate `a521bb1472837e0aae2359e5ac6f85c9a709c976`: 3672 public exports versus 3656; 2133 callable exports versus 2122; 158 deprecated exports versus 154, including the conversation binding/runtime entrypoints. No budgets were raised and no unrelated exports were removed. The source-only Docker copies also fail the separate compiler-lifetime test because they omit Git tag metadata; that isolation limitation is not claimed as a hosted failure.

### Upgrade compatibility proof

- Repeated the upgrade using the current published stable `openclaw@2026.10.1`, confirmed by `npm view openclaw version`, in a secretless Node 24 Docker container. Earlier `2026.9.9` compatibility evidence is also retained.
- Used that release's real `models auth login --provider anthropic --method cli` command against an initialize-only fake `claude`. The release itself wrote its eleven static model rows. The isolated profile selected `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`, explicitly routed it through `agentRuntime.id = claude-cli`, and allowed `anthropic/*`. The released session-store SDK persisted a synthetic user-selected account pin and the session's model selection.
- Upgraded the same profile to the candidate, ran `doctor --yes --non-interactive`, then started the candidate Gateway on container loopback. All eleven configured rows and their explicit runtime settings survived, as did the selected model, session ID/model, saved `authProfileOverride`, and its `user` provenance. Doctor added the wildcard CLI runtime policy without removing the existing settings.
- Gateway `models.list` and the CLI returned twelve available canonical Anthropic rows on `claude-cli`: the eleven preserved configured IDs plus a synthetic native-only `claude-opus-5-6` from the fake initialize menu. That synthetic ID is not a claim about a released model. The selected old model, absent from the fake native menu, remained selectable. Dry runtime resolution of `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` returned `claude-cli`.
- After a successful native discovery, forced the fake Claude initialize subprocess to exit while its auth-status probe continued to report a valid login. The Gateway reported native discovery as unavailable, but kept all twelve rows available, including the unconfigured native-only model. The CLI also retained the published rows and reported the refresh warning. No Claude turns were sent.
- Fixed this at the existing catalog owner: retain raw provider-owned rows and accepted membership under the owner's same-auth check, then project canonical Anthropic identities for readers. A failed refresh does not masquerade as a successful refresh. Authentication changes invalidate retention; successful menus, including restrictive or empty menus, replace it.
- All 48 catalog-owner/decision tests passed, including success→failure retention, changed-auth invalidation, and restrictive-success replacement; focused lint passed with zero warnings/errors. The built candidate passed the latest-stable upgrade and transient-failure proof. No real HOME, credentials, or user Gateway was used.

Merge danger: two-way door; reverting restores the former catalog behavior and does not require rolling back stored state. Blast radius: Claude CLI model discovery/admission; saved-account credential aliases retain their existing behavior.

prs.title: feat: support picking a specific on-device TTS voice for Talk Mode
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves On-device Talk Mode text-to-speech on iOS and macOS always fell back to Apple's low-quality default voice, even when a user had downloaded and selected an Enhanced or Premium voice in Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content. macOS had no on-device voice or speech settings UI at all. ## Why This Change Was Made On-device synthesis only ever resolved a voice via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language:)`, which returns Apple's undocumented per-language default and ignores any specific voice the user picked. This adds a specific-voice picker (enumerated via `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()`) to both platforms' Talk Mode settings, filtered by the current recognition language, with graceful fallback to the previous language-only behavior if a selected voice is later uninstalled. macOS gains a new "Speech" settings section for this. Investigated and intentionally did not attempt to support selecting Siri voices specifically: Apple does not expose Siri voice identity to any third-party app via `AVSpeechSynthesizer`/`AVSpeechUtterance` on any current iOS version (confirmed via WWDC20 session 10022 and Apple engineer forum responses) — even `prefersAssistiveTechnologySettings` silently substitutes a same-language non-Siri voice. This is a permanent Apple platform restriction, not a gap in this change. A macOS global keyboard shortcut to toggle Talk Mode was developed alongside this but is being split into its own follow-up PR to keep this PR to one topic, per repo policy. ## User Impact Users can now pick a specific downloaded Enhanced/Premium on-device voice for Talk Mode in Settings, on both iOS and macOS, instead of always hearing the default system voice. ## Evidence - Full `OpenClawKit` shared package suite: 1311 tests / 101 suites, all passing. - Focused iOS Swift Testing suites (`TalkSystemVoiceSelectionTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, `TalkSpeechLocaleTests`) green via `xcodebuild test` on iOS Simulator; one pre-existing, unrelated locale-dependent test failure confirmed present on `main` before this change (`git log -p -S` verified) and unaffected by this diff. - macOS `SettingsViewSmokeTests` and `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests` green via `swift test`. - Manual on-device verification on a physical iPhone (iOS 26.6, Russian system locale) and the macOS app: downloaded Enhanced voices via system Accessibility settings, selected one in the new OpenClaw picker, triggered Talk Mode with no external TTS provider configured, and confirmed the selected voice (not the default) was used for playback on both platforms. ### Screenshots macOS — picker showing installed voices, "Yuri (Enhanced)" selected: iOS — same picker in a Russian-locale device, "Ruslan" selected: ### Fixes from review Two issues found during this review round, both fixed and covered by new regression tests: 1. **Directive-language override bug**: an explicitly-picked voice was applying even when a Talk directive requested a different language mid-conversation (e.g. a French reply could be spoken in a picked English voice). Fixed in `TalkSystemSpeechSynthesizer.resolveVoice` — an explicit voice now only applies when its primary language subtag matches the resolved synthesis language. 2. **Doubled quality suffix**: the macOS screenshot above was captured before this fix and shows the bug it caught — Apple's own `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.name` already includes a localized quality suffix for many modern Enhanced/Premium voices (e.g. "Yuri (Enhanced)", Russian "Милена (улучшенный)"), so appending our own suffix doubled it. Fixed in `TalkSystemVoiceCatalog.label(for:)` to detect an already-decorated name and skip the extra suffix.

prs.title: fix(telegram): isolate private DM topic inbound buffers by thread id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages in distinct private Telegram topics share one inbound debounce identity. Work waiting in one topic blocks another topic, and a text `/stop` in one topic discards buffered input from another.

## Root Cause

`serializeTelegramTopicConversation` in `topic-conversation.ts` had no case for `scope: "dm"` — private bot topics with a `message_thread_id`. It returned `null`, so the conversation ID fell back to the bare `chatId`. Every DM topic in the same chat shared one debounce identity.

## Fix

Added `dm-topic` marker for `scope: "dm"` in the conversation serializer, so distinct topics get distinct inbound buffers.

## Evidence

- 3 deterministic regression tests added (blocked-topic case, cancellation case, forwarded-message case)
- All 81 existing Telegram tests pass

Closes #142107

prs.title: fix(oauth): report authorization received instead of completion at code capture
prs.body:
Closes #127268

## What Problem This Solves

Six bundled local-browser OAuth flows tell the callback browser that OAuth/authentication is complete as soon as a valid code is captured, before token exchange and credential construction can still fail — so a later exchange failure leaves the operator holding a browser page that already claimed success while the CLI reports no provider-auth result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture-time pages now report only the established fact (`Authorization received` heading in the shared `oauthSuccessHtml`, `authorization received` titles in the Chutes/MSTeams/Meet/OpenRouter capture pages, factual OpenAI message text). Terminal `progress.stop("… OAuth complete")` calls are untouched — those run post-exchange. No signature changes, so no SDK baseline/entrypoint churn; the `oauthSuccessHtml` doc comment now states its capture-time semantics.

## User Impact

Operators watching the callback browser see `Authorization received … while sign-in finishes` instead of a premature completion claim; a subsequent exchange failure no longer contradicts already-rendered success.

## Evidence

- Updated `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.test.ts` callback-body assertion to the new message; `provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` escaping tests use pass-through titles and are unaffected.
- All touched files pass an esbuild transform check; local vitest lane cannot run in this Windows checkout (rolldown native binding failure at config load), so CI runs the affected suites on the exact head SHA.

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose outbound session key to channel adapters
prs.body:
Related: #117210

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin outbound adapters cannot correlate a send with the canonical agent session even though the delivery pipeline already carries that session context. Plugins currently have to reconstruct or omit that relationship.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an optional `sessionKey` to `ChannelOutboundContext` and forwards `OutboundSessionContext.key` through the existing channel-handler boundary. The field is additive and omitted when no session is present, so existing adapters and callers keep their current behavior.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can make session-aware outbound decisions and correlate sends with the originating session without deriving identity from unrelated fields. Existing channel adapters remain source-compatible.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `forwards the canonical session key to plugin outbound adapters`
- Focused regression test passes under Node 25.9.0.
- `pnpm build` passes under Node 25.9.0.
- Full `deliver.test.ts` result improved from 3 failures before the implementation to 2 pre-existing media-staging failures after it; the new regression changed from red to green.
- Static diff scan found no environment-specific literals or credential values.

prs.title: fix(ui): retain image drafts after temporary files disappear
prs.body:
Fixes #163956.
Related: azuretek/chela#143.

## What Problem This Solves
Image drafts can fail to persist when a selected temporary screenshot disappears after the image read completes.

## User Impact
Completed image reads no longer depend on the original file remaining on disk for subsequent browser draft storage. Drafts over the existing attachment-storage limit receive a policy-specific warning rather than a misleading database-failure warning. No limit is raised.

## Why This Change Was Made
Snapshot image bytes from the already-read data URL at payload registration, using the existing decoder, instead of retaining the selected File. Non-image ownership, including video posters, is unchanged. Policy-warning deduplication remains separate from storage errors so reaching the limit cannot suppress a later real failure.

Thanks to @azuretek for the report and patch. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the five touched production files.

## Evidence

Verified candidate: `3cb04ea6d88926c7a43d4db6406c4b415bde0da4`.

The candidate and main `81987cd91a5af220833778db5e440993e22db936` were built in isolated Linux containers and exercised through their real Gateway-served Control UI in Chromium 154.0.8037.57 (Debian 12, ARM64).

- **Candidate persistence:** Chat retained three 3 MiB images; New Session retained one 5.5 MiB image. CDP selected native filesystem paths, FileReader completed, the temporary source directory was deleted before the production load handler continued, and native IndexedDB committed all attachment bytes. No storage banner appeared; drafts were present after reload.
- **Paste control:** memory-backed pasted images committed in both Chat and New Session on both revisions.
- **Regression:** `pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/chat/attachment-payload-snapshot.test.ts src/pages/chat/durable-composer-storage-warning.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: candidate 3/3 passed, 1.18 s Vitest / 2.57 s wall. The snapshot regression on main failed because the returned Blob was still the selected File; its non-image control passed (1.18 s Vitest / 2.48 s wall).
- **Live Gateway smoke:** one real `gpt-5-mini` request through a passive proxy, low reasoning and 4096-token output budget; HTTP 200 and a visible assistant onboarding response. The model followed the fresh-workspace onboarding instructions rather than the requested marker. The proxy allowed at most one upstream call. Temporary credentials were deleted.
- **Hosted CI:** `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded on this exact head. No failing jobs; one cancelled `auto-response` automation job, not a selected test lane. No CI reruns or source changes were needed.

### Persistent-profile reproduction closes the rendered baseline gap

Candidate `3cb04ea6d88926c7a43d4db6406c4b415bde0da4`; baseline `daa9ee37ade523ed085b28429ee6bd4dbd46a6bc`. Run window: October 2, 2026, 9:21-9:35 PM Pacific (2026-10-03T04:21:00Z to 2026-10-03T04:35:00Z). Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64, Node 24.19.0, Playwright 1.63.0, Chromium 153.0.8010.12, headless **persistent disk profile**.

[Full raw logs, fixture, harness and inspected screenshots](https://github.com/azuretek/proof/tree/b8481a511c364c6f8ac888ba4fe9d1370bb2c6f5/pr-163964).

Setup: real Chat and New Session pages via Vite and normal token login to an isolated 2026.9.6 Gateway. This supplemental run is source-served, **not a production-bundle build**. Each changed production module is loaded from the named Git revision; expected/served Git blob hashes are in every log. Gateway display-name discovery alone is a privacy fixture; no storage outcome or warning is mocked. Profile display name is set through Settings.

Request in every case: native picker selects three image/png files of 3,145,728 bytes each (valid red one-pixel PNG padded with zeros); wait for three completed thumbnails; unlink their source files; type Image draft proof. Measurement: native IndexedDB put/transaction complete/abort events, with performance.now() milliseconds from document navigation. Fresh persistent profile per case. HTTP response counts are not applicable to this browser-local storage boundary; no message/model request was made.

| Route | Baseline native result | Candidate native result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Session | source deleted 2836.1 ms; put:3 at 3090 ms; DataError abort and actual warning | source deleted 4034.3 ms; put:3 at 4273.7 ms; commit; no storage warning |
| Chat | put:1 at 3505.9 ms; source deleted 3532.2 ms; DataError abort and actual warning; next put:3 at 3598.5 ms | source deleted 4441.5 ms; put:3 at 4537.4 ms; commit:3; no storage warning |

**Important reproduction detail:** use chromium.launchPersistentContext(aFreshDirectory, options). Our earlier New Session baseline used chromium.launch() plus browser.newPage(), hence off-the-record storage, and committed instead of aborting. Changing the context mode reproduced the native disk-backed blob error. This explains our own contradictory results; it does not establish how the separate ARM64 run was configured.

Chat schedules intermediate saves while reads complete. The final after proof waits for the transaction holding all three attachments, not an earlier one-image commit. New Session has one put:3 followed by commit. The observer never changes native return values or supplies an error.

**Limits / not covered:** this harness does not claim reload recovery, model sending, or production-build validation; the separate contributor evidence above covers built pages and reloads. The older isolated Gateway rejects sessions.messages.subscribe's subscriptionId parameter, visibly in both Chat captures; browser-local composer writes remain operational. No history/subscription success is claimed. The exact original user incident and other browser versions remain unproven.

prs.title: refactor(ui): simplify display refresh bookkeeping
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI carries request generations, chronology maps, and handoff protocols for display races that do not warrant their permanent complexity.

## User Impact

Normal UI features and rendering stay intact. Authorization, private account/profile boundaries, command FIFO, ordinary write settlement, bounded caches, and config/draft durability remain. Rare overlapping display refreshes are explicitly best effort and may show an older result until refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reevaluates the UI lane under the maintainer's sharpened provenance rule: synthetic/harness reproductions and agent/maintainer PR narratives do not establish a real incident. Eleven of the original fifteen KEEP groups are flipped or narrowed to existing effect checks. The remaining four groups are terminal execution/settlement, sandbox grants, transcript authorization, and config-write durability—not display chronology.

Removes 992 net production lines across model catalogs, progress cards, sidebar catalog loading, page controllers, and Current Work. Tests solely specifying removed race machinery are deleted alongside it. This is not a generated-file or test-count reduction disguised as production simplification. Final write-settlement repairs bring the result just below 1,000; this uses the campaign's 500–999 single-PR exception after the full-scope implementation pass.

Production delta against the branch merge base: **992 net lines removed** across 39 production files (+340/-1,332). Tests, fixtures and test-support are excluded.

### Coverage log

This is the public summary of `.local/p11-ledger.md`. Every original KEEP group was re-evaluated under the sharpened human-incident bar; 11 of 15 were flipped or narrowed.

| Original KEEP group | Final decision and retained boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Browser snapshots | Remove ordinal arbitration; retain command authority, navigation FIFO and geometry. |
| Theme catalog | Remove refresh generations; retain the cache and connection boundary. |
| Connection bootstrap | Remove duplicate generation ownership; retain measured startup prioritization and active-work accounting. |
| MCP context | Remove display generation; retain actual removal and broadcaster registration. |
| Progress cards | Remove read/dismissal generations; retain paid-work idempotency, conditional writes, bounded cache and one coalesced refresh. |
| Effective tools | Remove duplicate symbol/generation state; retain one actual client/target check. |
| Skills library | Remove read sequencing; retain private profile isolation, uploads, dirty drafts and one connection-scoped mutation-settlement check. |
| Provider discovery | Remove extra generation/cancellation; retain selected-agent checks and the embedded wizard's auth/reconnect owner. |
| Model catalog | Remove request scheduler/custody; retain bounded shared cache, account isolation, timeout and Peter's production startup retry (#164532). |
| Chat snapshot cooldown | Remove seed-time fences; retain transcript bytes, deletion, account/Incognito privacy and write settlement. |
| Profile/usage/plugin pages | Remove duplicate display generations; retain draft preservation and actual request/target ownership. |
| Terminal actions | KEEP: external command authority, FIFO and ordinary in-flight settlement. |
| Board MCP lifecycle | KEEP: sandbox grants and current authorization at dispatch. |
| Meetings | KEEP: revoked transcript access must retire parallel reads/exports; privacy boundary. |
| Config writes | KEEP: draft bytes, hashes, uncertain-write receipts and FIFO prevent normal disconnect/edit-during-save data loss. |

Further scope discoveries removed Current Work retirement clocks, sidebar chronology, live New Session group revalidation, Workshop automatic conflict replay, and Search health generations. Workshop mutations still check their existing scope before refresh, error publication and pending-action release; this is write settlement, not restored display chronology. Provenance and accepted outcomes for every removed mechanism follow below.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Shared set synchronization: same-turn detach/reattach can sync twice; consumers deduplicate the current set. #140811 introduced the generation during consolidation, without a human incident.
- Dropdown focus: unusual same-instance reparenting can focus the first item twice. Normal reopen replaces the element; disconnected menus cannot focus. #113647 was consolidation, not an incident.
- Model catalog request queue: overlapping discovery/read completion may display older inventory until refresh. #147926/#158132 synthetic lifecycle cases do not justify the queue/custody protocol. Shared requests, caller timeout, account isolation and bounded cache remain.
- Catalog generation arbitration: config/catalog changes during a read no longer revoke all read receipts. A subsequent event or refresh corrects display; #154839/#166250 do not supply a human incident for that mechanism.
- Progress-card read/dismiss chronology: same-client reconnect or an overlapping invalidation can temporarily show earlier card state. #153213's linked human issue concerns a WebKit regex stall, not these races. Conditional writes, response validation, refresh idempotency and timeout remain.
- Effective-tools reads: same-key reset/reconnect may accept a late display result. #126826's synthetic regressions do not justify a separate symbol/generation owner; client and target publication checks remain.
- Agent roster: the pending request identity replaces a second revision/connection fence. #128652 supports measured roster caching, not duplicate request generations; file writes and account ownership stay separate.
- Theme and plugin capabilities: a concurrent refresh can finish out of order until the next update. #153001/#145484 supply synthetic reproduction or hot-reload feature work, not a human actual-use report. Cache and connection boundaries remain.
- MCP context display: consumption during an outstanding read can redisplay prior context until the next event. #164277's demo-server testing does not establish a human incident for the display generation; the real broadcaster registration and removal operation remain.
- MCP settings feedback: an unusually retained/remounted card can show older completion feedback. #128490's isolated-Gateway reproduction does not justify the feedback generation; config writes and OAuth stay owned by their existing security boundaries.
- Sidebar catalogs: old host/page responses may briefly reappear after another scan or completed archive, but cannot restore archived provider data. #117158/#110211/#146535 do not justify per-host chronology/refetch custody. Archive authorization, pending deletion, bounded progress tracking and pagination stay.
- Current Work: a late full snapshot can briefly restore a retired row. #164573's synthetic equal-clock cases do not justify a persistent retirement/authority registry; next list refresh corrects it. Active-run interpretation, identity, filters and bounded event buffering remain.
- Browser display snapshots: same-tab refreshes use completion order. Earlier browser fix PRs do not justify snapshot ordinal arbitration. Live document/input checks, navigation FIFO and screenshot geometry stay.
- Chat prefetch cooldown: cache invalidation during initial timestamp seeding may leave a stale cooldown entry. The index only avoids redundant prefetch; transcript bytes, deletion and Incognito/account privacy are unchanged.
- New Session groups: changing group configuration while a draft is open does not revalidate its loaded defaults; reload obtains new defaults. #123276's automatic revalidation was feature hardening without a human incident.
- Provider/catalog discovery: an overlapping same-target discovery may finish out of order, while a different selected agent/client remains isolated. #147794 and the existing catalog-target implementation do not establish an incident for the extra generation/cancellation layers.
- Skills library display: overlapping library reads can complete out of order. #134068 supplies no human report for the read sequence; private profile boundaries, upload authorization, write conflicts and dirty drafts remain.
- Page display reads: Logbook, Portals, plugin details, personal instructions and usage no longer carry duplicate generations. Existing client/target/operation checks preserve actual writes and newer drafts. Their cited PRs provided feature/synthetic evidence, not human incidents for the removed layers.
- Skill Workshop: config conflicts surface through the existing owner and explicit retry instead of an automatic retry loop; read feedback uses the current scope. #161057 does not establish a human incident for the removed machinery.
- Search health: config changes during a test can leave its health result visible until refresh. #154135 does not justify a config-revision/generation protocol. Actual search authorization, one pending test, selected-agent checks and config persistence remain.

The small startup-only retry remains because Peter recorded an actual production Gateway startup incident in #164532. Measured caches, memory bounds, security effects, user-data durability and shutdown settlement are not traded away.

## Evidence

Current head: `a92e866a968454277a8e9118cfc98684e2818dec`. Exact-head [CI run 38100193413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38100193413) passed; the head's check-run inventory showed 54 successful checks, 40 intentionally skipped, and no failed or cancelled checks. One conflict-free rebase onto `76a282c7a1c6` was needed for the named `check-prod-types` failure: main had already removed its unused binding in `243b6dbf63d`. The production patch is unchanged (identical stable patch ID). The new exact-head ClawSweeper review is ready with zero findings (2026-10-11T01:08:35.215Z). Local corrective reviews remain scoped-clean through P2.

Rebased proof passes 781 unit tests and 24 browser tests across all 34 modified test files, all six UI test-type graphs, UI production types, focused lint, both cycle checks (zero cycles), and all three suppression checks. A local run of the exact CI-selected 190-file E2E set retained four source-mode initial-route-readiness failures before their actions ran: the first offline sidebar-delete case, first coarse-pointer sidebar-menu case, child-load-error case and agent-switch-roster case. Diagnostics show a connected Gateway, loaded agents, no page errors and a pending chat route. These remain recorded local failures, not a claimed fix or passing replay. The completed exact-head hosted E2E checks cover the same selected suite successfully under its normal CI environment; the redundant local run was stopped after hosted completion. No timeout was raised and no test was skipped. Earlier broad results below are not relabeled as a green full local run on this head.

Fresh current-main rendering proof is [in this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168656#issuecomment-6103769952) and embedded below. The frozen install was reconciled after the rebase brought Calendar's already-declared Solid compiler dependency; it changed no tracked files.

Focused owner/caller suites passed after repairing actual findings: model catalog, progress cards, agents, sidebar/catalogs, Current Work, browser ownership, chat snapshots/metadata, New Session, plugins, Logbook, Portals, personal instructions, skills, systems, usage and Search. The final Search browser run passed 24 tests; the final portal action run passed 23. UI typecheck passed. Runtime and static/madge cycle checks both reported zero. No new lint suppressions, timeout increases, retries-to-green, skips, protocol/schema/config-key changes or changelog changes.

Independent review identified actual late-result draft/action-state bugs; these were repaired with existing scope/operation checks and focused regressions. Rejected demands to restore live group-default revalidation and Workshop automatic conflict replay are the explicit best-effort tradeoffs above, not omitted findings.

First exact-head CI (`3d713fc`, run 38087909454) failed UI E2E shard 5/8 and cancelled sibling jobs. All six failures are attributed to this branch: four reconnect cases exposed the parent discarding the mounted setup wizard during a transient null selection, and two request-count expectations still described removed catalog retry/progress-generation behavior. The parent now leaves reconnect/auth recovery with the mounted wizard; the two count assertions reflect the accepted simplification while preserving visibility, recovered content and request-payload assertions. Focused bundled browser proof passed all 25 tests in 239.56 seconds. Cancelled jobs are not claimed as passing.

ClawSweeper also identified a newer Personal Instructions draft being overwritten after switching away from and back to the saving agent. A regression first failed with `First edit` replacing `Second edit`; a draft-value publication check preserves newer text without a selection generation. Follow-up review caught that the successful save must still update the saved baseline/hash. The extended regression verifies that reverting to the original text remains saveable with the new hash; it failed before that correction. All 18 Personal Instructions tests passed in 13.30 seconds (21.78 seconds including wrapper startup). These are measured local times, not hosted CI times. Focused lint, formatting and UI production typecheck passed for the repair.

Fresh review of `3e08204` identified old Workshop mutation settlement clearing a newer agent's pending restore. The new regression failed on that source; existing scope checks now protect follow-up loading, errors and lock release. All eight Workshop tests passed in 10.51 seconds (19.14 seconds including wrapper startup).

A sibling write-helper audit found the equivalent Skill Library reconnect case. Its regression failed because an old save cleared the new save's busy flag. Retained the existing connection capture around error publication and lock release, while keeping the read-sequence removal. All 17 library/Skills tests passed in 14.53 seconds (21.21 seconds including wrapper startup).

CI run 38090624794 on `3e08204` has one root failure: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` rejects the closed mock at `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection-placement.test.ts:56`. The file, checker and mock baseline were unchanged between CI's main base `8d1c7bcbce4`, its tested merge `fb3409eabaf4`, and the main checkpoint `0e6b2c23c8d`. Running the same mock-export check in an isolated checkout of `0e6b2c23c8d` reproduced the exact error. Main now contains the independent fix `00e095399b20`; this branch did not modify that file. The aggregate CI gate failed because of it; all 33 cancelled CI jobs had no separate failed step. Cancelled coverage is not claimed as passing. No CI rerun, empty push or rebase-for-green was requested.

The prior `fa309a9` run 38093342524 had two independent inherited roots: `check-prod-types` rejected the unused `env` in `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts`, fixed on main by `243b6dbf63d`; `checks-node-compact-small-1` failed three `plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` cases because the SDK export counts exceeded budgets. The SDK checker and its two platform-applicable tests reproduced on isolated main, outside this PR's UI graph. The downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failure and 25 cancellations were not additional product failures. The successful current-head run supersedes that incomplete CI coverage; no failed attempt was rerun.

Testbox verified source `77ec7a863de3cdf903200dc5397a4626b729b792` and ran the full UI suite: **22,390 passed, 44 failed, 6 existing skips** across 1,640 files. Every affected failure was then classified and repaired or removed only where it asserted the retired scheduling contract; the focused rerun passed **298 tests across all 15 affected files**. The final follow-up preserves the default two-argument transport dispatch. This is focused repair proof, not a claim that the full suite was rerun green.

The Testbox changed check passed conflict/line-cap/max-lines/assertion/mock-export/timeout ratchets, dependency guards and formatting, then stopped at an inherited graph-budget failure: 722 UI E2E roots versus the 720 limit. This branch adds no E2E roots; the budget/configuration and E2E inputs are unchanged from its base. UI production types, focused lint and translation verification passed separately. The local dead-export scans timed out at 600 seconds with no verdict; hosted CI must cover that gap.

The suppression allowlist test also fails on this branch's unchanged baseline entries from #168002; main already repairs those exact entries in `dab6a8de087`. No baseline was changed here. No local replay is represented as hosted exact-head CI.

New Session draft and Live Activity before/after captures are inspected synthetic fixtures, byte-identical across the change and on repeat capture.

prs.title: Keep Slack messages on readable chunk boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long Slack replies can break words or expose link markup when chunks are split without using the available formatting boundaries.

## User Impact

Ordinary Slack text sends use a 4,000-character rendered chunk budget. Already-rendered Slack text prefers paragraph, newline, then whitespace boundaries without dropping separators. Long replies may produce more messages. Slash-command response-window capacity is unchanged.

## Evidence

The new mocked `chat.postMessage` regressions fail against the original implementation and pass with this patch: two long labeled links remain intact in separate API payloads, and native-mrkdwn prose splits at whitespace without losing text. Additional regressions cover entities, link labels containing spaces, balanced code wrappers, paragraph boundaries, and long slash responses.

Across the focused Slack checks, 431 tests pass. Two upload-network guard tests fail identically against the untouched upstream snapshot in this environment. The alternate-origin upload test passes after adjusting its caption fixture to retain the same two-part delivery scenario. Targeted lint and formatting pass, and the patch applies cleanly to the pinned upstream source.

A fresh Node 26.3.0 run of `format.test.ts`, `send.blocks.test.ts`, and `monitor/replies.test.ts` passes all 161 tests. Running the package test entrypoint directly with `--maxWorkers=1` took 26.65 seconds wall time, including compilation and startup. Independent full-source review found no actionable introduced bugs, and the repository's Auto Review check is scoped-clean at its default P0 threshold.

The full Slack suite was blocked by a network request. The full repository build/check and live Slack delivery were not run. CI results and CI timing are pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary Markdown replies already use a parsed, render-aware chunker. Applying Slack's recommended budget before `chat.postMessage` lets that renderer choose boundaries before delivery. The native-mrkdwn chunker separately gains lossless whitespace-aware splitting while retaining protected-token and code-wrapper handling.

The 4,000-character recommendation is not a documented hard Slack limit. This change leaves slash-command transport budgets alone and does not resolve the existing fallback for a single URL or token larger than the entire budget. It does not add a general Markdown parser to raw native-mrkdwn input.

prs.title: fix(models): remove saved provider models on config removal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved provider models remaining in the model picker after an operator removes that provider's configuration while the Gateway is running.

## User Impact

Removing a provider now removes its saved plugin models without restarting the Gateway, but only when the cached endpoint matches the removed entry's explicitly configured `baseUrl`. Default-endpoint discovery, unrelated providers, and entries without an authored URL are preserved. Earlier removals are not cleaned retroactively.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config reload now prunes matching provider entries before refreshing the model inventory. It captures authored values before publication, so provider defaults are not mistaken for user-supplied endpoints, and compares canonical provider IDs. The existing per-agent write queue orders the prune after older discovery publications, and the existing SQLite writer applies the endpoint comparison atomically. No schema or persisted format changes are needed.

## Evidence

- Both focused suites pass: 14 model-publication tests and 118 Gateway reload tests. Targeted formatting, lint, and whitespace checks pass.
- The Gateway regression fails on unmodified production code at `e40606fdea9`: the removed endpoint remains in both agents' persisted catalogs. The default-endpoint and no-authored-URL controls pass on that same base.
- Runtime-only build passes. In an isolated live Gateway with local Ollama discovery refusing connections, removing `https://ollama.com` removes the synthetic model from `models.list` and the persisted plugin catalog. Re-adding the entry restores the model. All phases use the same Gateway process.
- Coverage also preserves unrelated providers in the same and separate catalogs, and orders removal after an older discovery plan publishes.
- Loaded-config regressions for an omitted endpoint, uppercase provider ID, and case-only key changes fail on the initial candidate and pass after the repair.

### Latest stable v2026.10.1 upgrade

[`v2026.10.1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.1) was published during this investigation (October 10 at 23:54 UTC). A fresh isolated git-source install of its exact tag, `e178c39e9aae3fa440735217f9aef9574f286677`, ran its installed updater against candidate `7888f5e952c4ce74f44c853d73af5bd91501fbf0`. This seed explicitly included `params.num_ctx: 8192`.

The update result reports **status `ok`**, the durable run reports **`succeeded`**, and the built commit and source HEAD both equal the candidate. `/readyz` recovered to **200** after an observed **640.599-second** update readiness gap. All four tested hashes were identical before/after this update:

| State | SHA-256 before and after |
| --- | --- |
| Settings | `84db0e995c348200a464a98d1aedf2134d0004af55b86140fffcdbad0df366d9` |
| Synthetic credential | `564b3fe5179e13831f2a5145a5d0d31aca48cb0c0dc6657b7477c0a2a642e491` |
| Ollama catalog | `7a42001222cb901bef9a5491a8fbcb1aa5e598d973ce4ce244562559f638d08c` |
| Unrelated catalog | `bb78ae837b0166228ea0e89537186654a894c2b028d3d3361442f7b6e7dfbeb8` |

Both catalogs' model rows were present after update and before removal. Removing the Ollama configuration pruned only its saved rows and model-list entry; the unrelated rows and credential hash were unchanged. Re-adding restored model visibility and the original settings hash. Gateway PID **26925** was unchanged throughout removal/re-add.

Same-profile `openclaw update status --json` exited **0**; run `3905229b-e9b8-4bd7-8666-e802ca5b5574` is **succeeded**, with no active/stale/abandoned run or pending package activation. Its retained recovery set is **stale because the update already succeeded**, not unresolved recovery. The sealed pre-update baseline manifest exists (SHA-256 `8018661fc6a560fd4f5621e52a2f5972bf3d1be750b6d4f9d5c793e1fcc8a849`); all **three** referenced payload files match their recorded hashes. The separate pre-update config backup and two recorded migration-original database backups also passed hash verification.

**Accepted caveat:** the outer **installed v2026.10.1 updater process exited 1 after successful activation**, during its post-update cleanup. The final log lines 245–247 (temporary path and profile redacted) were:

```text
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Cannot find module '…/source/dist/runtime-cleanup-DlrF_x2c.mjs' imported from '…/source/dist/runtime-cleanup-scope-C__wD_xL.mjs'
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> doctor`.
```

This is not claimed as a clean CLI exit. The installed driver's cleanup failure is outside this catalog-removal diff and is accepted as non-blocking for this PR; it is being investigated separately. The activation, durable success, unchanged state, recovery status, and subsequent live removal/re-add assertions above were observed independently.

### Published v2026.9.9 upgrade

[`v2026.9.9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.9) **is a published stable release** (October 8), not merely a main build. This proof installs its git-source tag, `bcfc88812a35243893585dbeca87ca41b48272ca`, and lets that installed updater upgrade existing state to `7888f5e952c4ce74f44c853d73af5bd91501fbf0`. The v2026.9.8 result below is an additional older-release control, not a claim that v2026.9.8 is the newest release. Both cells used runtime-only builds and the shared build cache.

The v2026.9.9 update exited **0**, returned **ok**, built the exact target commit, and recovered `/readyz` to **200**. The seed ran before the decision to explicitly configure `num_ctx`, so the initial strict settings hash caught the same existing Doctor normalization described below. A separate assertion verified the pre-update backup's seeded hash and then verified **exactly** the addition of `params: {num_ctx: 8192}`; no other tested setting changed. Settings hashes were `ee33f01df2efbdf39aae685e982fcc44695aa62c6678c0dddd47b3940e216844` before and `80bed54f26da4e6d24036550b73f146fac1e232d6a2dfad95263189d34fa3188` after that normalization.

Credentials and both catalogs retained the identical SHA-256 values in the table below across this upgrade, with the Ollama and unrelated model rows present before removal. Removing the authored Ollama entry pruned only its rows and model-list entry; the unrelated rows and credential hash remained unchanged. Re-adding restored the configured model and normalized settings. All removal/re-add assertions used the same Gateway PID, **52954**; they do not claim offline discovery-cache regeneration.

In the same profile, `openclaw update status --json` exited **0** with last run `06d0c5fb-0c0a-401f-a59c-d7943b501f3c` **succeeded**, no active/stale/abandoned run, no pending package activation, and `recoverySets: []`. The pre-update config backup exists with SHA-256 `08578fbf96de869379c19ce06c7db5dba7f40262e37a0d6a6de7f339f34c57b8`. The same-update rollback manifest has SHA-256 `d5984b83ec3c1d13008deff5e388d6789a0e172899d9e0891b363dfbee2755e8`; both referenced database backups exist and match their recorded SHA-256 hashes.

Observed update readiness gaps were **711.332 seconds** for v2026.9.9 and **398.555 seconds** for v2026.9.8. Both recovered successfully; this is not a zero-downtime update claim. The provider-removal/re-add flow itself did not restart either Gateway.

### Published v2026.9.8 upgrade control

An isolated git-source install of published [`v2026.9.8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.8) (`fc23bc864e4553c2d215e479eeec47b67a0bf943`) successfully updated to exact head `7888f5e952c4ce74f44c853d73af5bd91501fbf0`: updater exit **0**, result **ok**, built commit equals HEAD, and `/readyz` returned **200**.

The initial strict settings-hash assertion detected an existing Doctor normalization: it added only `params: {num_ctx: 8192}` to the synthetic Ollama model with `contextWindow: 8192`. The pre-update backup matches the seeded settings, and applying exactly that one change accounts for the complete settings-hash difference. This is existing [Doctor behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7888f5e952c4ce74f44c853d73af5bd91501fbf0/src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-core-normalizers.ts#L453-L525), untouched by this PR. No other tested settings changed.

| Preserved state | Before update | After update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Synthetic credential SHA-256 | `564b3fe5179e13831f2a5145a5d0d31aca48cb0c0dc6657b7477c0a2a642e491` | identical |
| Ollama catalog SHA-256 | `b44d6bceffcad2cf3e0f26b437bd4c618b6500a16ff7a1526a1d21a09aaf672f` | identical; model present |
| Unrelated catalog SHA-256 | `bb78ae837b0166228ea0e89537186654a894c2b028d3d3361442f7b6e7dfbeb8` | identical; model present |

After update, removing the authored `https://ollama.com` entry removed its saved catalog rows and model-list entry while preserving the credential and unrelated catalog hashes. Re-adding the entry restored the configured model and normalized settings. Gateway PID **60407** remained unchanged through removal and re-addition.

The same profile's `openclaw update status --json` exited **0**: last run `567f2d09-f938-4cb2-a4c2-69c88dba6575` **succeeded**, no active/stale/abandoned run, no pending package activation, and `recoverySets: []`. The pre-update config backup remains available (SHA-256 `558924b829241d95330f95467591390599c2417d0e6f34e891399e3fafae1a5b`), and the same-update rollback manifest (`1b91d9271577fc6e816641e08a17e19b9cf19931ac40e6a06ea93b6f091c4687`) references **two retained database backups**, both verified against their recorded SHA-256 hashes.

### Unrelated CI controls

The exact-head CI run [38096055847](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096055847) reported failures outside this PR. A clean current-main control at [`9b87a1a1f7d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9b87a1a1f7d62df6480321fdde3595f15449e25d) reproduced them:

| Check | Candidate failure | Clean main control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check-lint-core-1` | `plugin-state-observation-cache.ts`: shadowed `cacheKey`; unnecessary type conversion | Same two rules fail (`eslint/no-shadow`, `typescript/no-unnecessary-type-conversion`) |
| `check-lint-core-2` | `sqlite-worker-plugin-comparison.test.ts:95`: unbound method | Same `typescript/unbound-method` failure |
| `checks-node-compact-small-1` | SDK surface budget | Same public exports **3672 > 3656**, callable exports **2133 > 2122**, deprecated exports **158 > 154**, and deprecated conversation entrypoints **1 > 0 / 3 > 0** |

The control used `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/plugin-state/plugin-state-observation-cache.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-plugin-comparison.test.ts` and `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts --check`. Both reported the failures above. No unrelated source or SDK budget was changed.

`check-source-contracts` also reports the existing `resolveChannelDmPolicy` collision between `src/channels/account-resolution.ts` and `src/channels/plugins/dm-access.ts`. [Scheduled main job 114340367051](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38091757776/job/114340367051), at main `00e095399b203a2c71ef773fcf8ea1177bc2a5ef`, reports the identical name, file pair, and `sdk:true` collision.
