For `checks-node-changed-compact-small-12-1`, the exact failing `server.sessions.inbound-worktree-writer.test.ts` case (`checkout already restored=false`) was run three times on clean main `9b87a1a1f7d` and three times on this head. Main results: **timeout / pass / same “expected false to be true” failure**. Candidate results: **pass / pass / same assertion failure**. This independently reproduces the hosted assertion failure on unmodified main; the other parameterized case was excluded in all six runs.

Merge risk: two-way door for code, with rebuildable catalog entries removed only for explicitly matching endpoints. Reverting does not restore already-pruned cache entries; discovery can rebuild them, and re-adding configured models restores their visibility. prs.title: fix(anthropic): avoid usage polling with setup tokens
prs.body:
Closes #143419

## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic setup-token profiles can authenticate inference successfully but can surface misleading usage-polling HTTP errors because setup tokens are not reliable evidence of OAuth usage capability.

## User Impact

Setup-token users no longer send unsupported requests to Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint when the usage resolver positively identifies the selected stored credential as a setup token. If a supported claude.ai web-session credential is configured, usage loads through that fallback; otherwise OpenClaw skips setup-token usage cleanly.

Ordinary OAuth credentials keep using Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint even when their access token has the same `sk-ant-oat01-` format as a setup token. A preferred OAuth profile also stays preferred when a lower-priority setup-token profile coexists.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver now preserves configured credential order by asking the production OAuth/token selector for the selected profile first. Static API-key/token candidates are used only to retain enough provenance to tell whether that selected token is an onboarding setup token. This avoids the earlier mixed-profile regression where the mere presence of any setup-token candidate could preempt a higher-priority OAuth profile.

A selected setup token is wrapped in an internal usage token only when a claude.ai web-session fallback is available. The fetch path recognizes that internal marker and uses web usage directly. Genuine OAuth credentials remain on the normal OAuth usage path, including OAuth tokens that happen to use the same `sk-ant-oat01-` format.

Configured web-session failures are also no longer converted into an error-free empty snapshot. If the dedicated setup-token fallback cannot load web usage, the result reports `Claude web usage unavailable`.

Admin API behavior and the existing response-based fallback for OAuth `user:profile` scope failures remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added focused regression coverage proving an onboarding-shaped selected setup-token profile is classified as setup-token usage.
- Added mixed-profile regression coverage proving a preferred OAuth profile is preserved when a lower-priority setup token coexists, even when both tokens use the `sk-ant-oat01-` shape.
- Added a resolver control proving a genuine OAuth credential still takes the OAuth path when no static setup token exists.
- Added coverage proving a selected stored setup-token profile without a supported web session returns `{ handled: true }`.
- Added focused regression coverage proving a resolved setup token uses claude.ai web usage without contacting `api.anthropic.com`.
- Added regression coverage proving a full-length `sk-ant-oat01-` token on the ordinary OAuth fetch path still calls `/api/oauth/usage`.
- Added regression coverage proving a configured web-session HTTP failure returns an explicit usage error instead of a silent empty success.
- Remote diff review confirms credential selection occurs before setup-token classification and the new mixed-profile test covers the P1 reported by ClawSweeper.
- `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.claude.ts` and `extensions/anthropic/usage.ts` are not matched by the repository's restricted/security CODEOWNERS paths.
- Local tests were not run. This automation runtime does not provide a runnable repository checkout/dependency environment, so no local test result or real provider request is claimed. Maintainer-visible after-fix runtime proof remains outstanding.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used to trace the credential paths, incorporate ClawSweeper's findings, implement the focused repair, and review the resulting remote diff.

prs.title: fix: preserve Claude CLI chat context across account switches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes loss of conversation continuity when an existing Claude CLI chat starts a fresh native session after an account change.

Related: #140294 and #168726.

## User Impact

Account switches now keep continuity through on-demand history reading, including opaque native logins. The new session gets a metadata-only note; raw transcript replay and durable context remain blocked across accounts. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the switch-back note renderer, inline prompt delivery, tool-policy-aware history hint, and importer stripping for fresh Claude sessions after auth-profile, auth-epoch, or auth-unknown invalidation. The note describes earlier recorded messages without including their contents. Subsequent native turns do not repeat it. Brand-new chats receive no note, and unavailable `sessions_history` tools are never advertised.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Pinned `origin/main` (`f28e5ba25b1`) fails both memory/durable fresh-account regression cases: expected earlier-message note, received `undefined` (44 other tests passed).
- Focused coverage includes account/profile/epoch and opaque-auth starts, no raw replay or durable context, count/time/model/session-key metadata, unavailable history tool, empty chat, next-turn omission, importer deduplication and routed-prompt provenance.
- Final focused run: **104 tests passed across four files**, 156.24s with `pnpm exec vitest run … --maxWorkers=1` and `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1`; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. [Full CI on the implementation head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38100954474) passed in 7m51s. The subsequent docs-only review repair passed link checks (14,991 links, zero broken), docs formatting and `git diff --check`.
- Real Claude CLI with keychain login, isolated Gateway and workspace: **2/2 account-switch loops called `mcp__openclaw__sessions_history` with the exact chat key and returned the original token**. Account changes were simulated by changing only the saved native binding's prior auth-profile identity while the isolated Gateway was stopped, forcing the ordinary auth-invalidation path on restart.
- No-switch control returned the original token with no note or history read. All three following turns had no note. Native stdin/stream-json and stored chat history confirm exactly two metadata-only notes, original stored user text and no duplicate recall rows.
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `settings*.json` SHA-256 and mtimes unchanged. The one created native project directory was removed; no unexpected project directories were created.
- `pnpm build` completed successfully. Its existing Control UI startup-size advisory was printed; this change does not touch UI assets.

Two-way door: reverting removes the metadata note behavior without a migration. Blast radius is Claude CLI conversation preparation and decoration matching; other runtimes and raw-history account boundaries are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Inspected native proof excerpts (synthetic tokens only)</summary>

Native stdin for loop 1 (exact user-prompt text):

```text
[OpenClaw: 2 earlier messages in this chat from 2026-10-11T01:02:58.479Z to 2026-10-11T01:03:05.904Z, using "claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5". Their contents are not included here. Before answering a question that may depend on these messages, call mcp__openclaw__sessions_history({"sessionKey":"agent:main:account-switch-1","limit":100}) to read them; page older messages with offset if needed.]

What token did I give you? Reply with only that token. Do not guess.
```

Native stream-json tool call:

```json
{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01F5b3ZCq9mnqUYpXbTjQbzq","name":"mcp__openclaw__sessions_history","input":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:account-switch-1","limit":100},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}
```

The matching `tool_result` contains the earlier user message `Remember token ALPHA1739. Reply ACK only.` and assistant `ACK` under `agent:main:account-switch-1`. The final answer was `ALPHA1739`. Projecting the final `chat.history` response to user text gives exactly:

```json
[
  "Remember token ALPHA1739. Reply ACK only.",
  "What token did I give you? Reply with only that token. Do not guess."
]
```

Loop 2 independently called the same tool with `{"sessionKey":"agent:main:account-switch-2","limit":100}`, received the earlier `ALPHA2739` message and answered `ALPHA2739`. The no-switch control answered `ALPHA3739` without calling history. All three next-turn prompts were `Reply AFTER only.` without an earlier-message note, and all three answered `AFTER`.

</details>

prs.title: fix: model-authored tool-call markup is posted to the channel verbatim
prs.body:
Closes #153594

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a block of literal `<invoke name="Bash">` / `<parameter name="command">…</parameter>` markup is posted to the chat verbatim when a CLI-backed agent degrades into writing its tool calls as text instead of invoking them.

## User Impact

That markup is dropped in the shared reply normalizer, on the same silent-skip path as the existing artifact families, instead of being delivered as a user-visible message (in the reported case, a single ~40 KB Telegram message of several hundred `<invoke …>` blocks).

Ordinary replies are unaffected, including replies that surround markup with prose (those are still delivered, markup included, exactly as before), and replies that merely mention a tag inside parameter content — see the counterexamples below.

Replies whose markup sits inside a code region the sanitizer owns are also unaffected: an indented or fenced `<invoke …>` example is Markdown code and is delivered, not silenced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isInternalFormattingArtifact` gated only Harmony channel markers and box-drawing separators, so the Anthropic-style tool-call family passed straight through `normalizeReplyPayload` to every channel.

The detector is a **linear scan**, not a regex. An earlier revision of this PR used a single regex and review correctly showed it was unsafe: a lazy parameter body could expand past its own closing tag (dropping prose between two invocation blocks), and repeated blocks with a rejecting suffix backtrack exponentially. The scan walks tags once, so a parameter body ends at its first closing tag, and there is no backtracking at all. It recognizes a whole invocation only when an `<invoke>`/`<function_calls>` appears **outside** parameter content, and every non-whitespace character sits inside a `<parameter>` payload.

**No regex runs over model-controlled text anywhere in the detector.** The tag prefix is parsed by a direct character walk (`parseToolCallTag`), because even a per-tag regex is enough to reintroduce a blow-up — see the whitespace finding below.

## Review Follow-Up

### ClawSweeper's code findings, measured before/after

| finding | retired regex | revision 6 | this revision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[P1]` parameter body must stop at its structural closing boundary — prose between two invocation blocks | `true` → silently drops a reply containing `The answer is 42.` | `false` | **`false`** — prose preserved |
| `[P1]`/security: bound rejection time for repeated invocation blocks | 18 blocks `19 ms`, 22 blocks `311 ms` (still doubling) | `0 ms` | **`0 ms`** at every size |
| `[P2]` require invocation context outside parameter content — `<parameter name="data">Use <invoke name="Bash"> for execution.</parameter>` | `true` → sanitizer never gets to unwrap it | `false` | **`false`** — content preserved |
| `[P2]` avoid rescanning the suffix for every payload delimiter | — | quadratic — see below | **linear** — see below |
| `[P2]` preserve indented Markdown code before suppressing markup | — | indented code was **silenced** | **delivered** — see below |
| `[P2]`/security: overlapping whitespace repetitions in the tag regex | — | quadratic — see below | **no regex** — see below |

Both earlier counterexamples are regression tests, along with a 300-block input with a rejecting suffix.

### `[P2]` whitespace partition search in the tag regex — fixed

Revision 7 still matched each candidate tag with

```
/^<\s*(\/?)\s*(?:antml:|mm:)?(function_calls|invoke|parameter)(?=[\s/>])[^<>]*>$/i
```

`<\s*(\/?)\s*` repeats `\s*` either side of an optional `/`. When the rest fails, the engine tries every way to split a run of whitespace between the two repetitions — quadratic in the run length, synchronous, and reachable from a single malformed tag in model output.

The tag prefix is now parsed by a direct character walk, so no regex touches model-controlled text at all. All of the old grammar is preserved: optional leading slash, optional `antml:`/`mm:` namespace, the three names, the delimiter check that keeps `<parameter-value>` out, and self-closing detection. The whitespace test is a single-character `/\s/`, which has no repetition and so cannot backtrack.

A run of spaces inside a parameter, measured through the real normalizer on the shipped 2026.9.5 bundle:

| whitespace run | revision 7 (regex) | this revision (no regex) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5,000 | 17.1 ms | 3.8 ms |
| 10,000 | 60.7 ms | 5.0 ms |
| 20,000 | 219.4 ms | 6.2 ms |
| 40,000 | **838.8 ms** | **8.1 ms** |

Revision 7 quadruples per doubling; this revision is flat. A regression test covers a 200k-space malformed tag inside a parameter.

### `[P2]` quadratic rescan — fixed

The scan called `indexOf(">", index + 1)` for every `<`. A `<` that opened no tag did not advance past the range it had just searched, so a run of `<` characters inside a parameter re-searched the remaining suffix each time. The tag scan now stops at the first `<` or `>`, whichever comes first, because a tag can contain neither; a run of `<` therefore advances one character at a time.

Measured in-process against the real `normalizeReplyPayloadOutcome` in the shipped **2026.9.5** bundle, `n` invalid `<` characters inside a parameter:

| `n` | revision 6 | this revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 40,000 | 17.0 ms | 1.5 ms |
| 80,000 | 56.1 ms | 1.8 ms |
| 160,000 | 212.6 ms | 2.5 ms |
| 320,000 | **826.9 ms** | **3.5 ms** |

Revision 6 quadruples per doubling (quadratic); this revision is flat. Treat the absolute numbers as indicative — the shape is the point. The regression test asserts 200k delimiters stay correct and complete well inside a second.

### `[P2]` indented Markdown code — fixed

`normalizeReplyPayloadOutcome` consults this gate **before** `sanitizeUserFacingText`, which protects code regions via `findCodeRegions`. A whole reply consisting of `    <invoke …>` is a valid CommonMark indented code block, so revision 6 silenced a code sample the user asked for.

The detector now takes an optional `isProtected(offset)` hook and ignores tags inside protected regions. `normalize-reply.ts` supplies the regions lazily through the real `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode` from `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts`, so `tokens.ts` stays free of Markdown and pays for the parse only once a reply already looks like markup.

Verified against the real `findCodeRegions` bundled in 2026.9.5 (`block: true`, spanning the whole input) and end to end through `normalizeReplyPayloadOutcome`:

| reply text | revision 6 | this revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `    <invoke …></invoke>` (4 spaces) | suppress | **deliver** |
| `\t<invoke …></invoke>` (tab) | suppress | **deliver** |
| `<invoke …></invoke>` (bare) | suppress | suppress |
| fenced code block containing markup | deliver | deliver |

Note on the end-to-end case: in the live agent path the assistant text is already left-trimmed before it reaches `normalizeReplyPayload`, so a bare indented block cannot arrive with its indentation intact. This fix is therefore a correctness fix at the predicate level, proven by the unit tests and the direct probe above, not an end-to-end behaviour change.

## Evidence

### Unit — the repo's own `src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts`

| revision | result |
| --- | --- |
| unmodified `tokens.ts` | 99 tests, **1 failed** (the invocation case) |
| revision 6 | 99 tests, **99 passed** |
| this revision | 103 tests, **103 passed** |

The four added tests cover both quadratic paths, the `isProtected` hook, and indented/tab-indented markup using the real `findCodeRegions`.

### Real behaviour proof through channel delivery

The gap called out in the first revision is now closed. Reproduced on the shipped **2026.9.5** release bundle (`ec9c1a1`), Node 24.21.0, in an isolated `--dev` profile, with a live Telegram channel and a local OpenAI-compatible mock provider that emits exactly the markup family from the report.

Turns were driven through the real gateway and reply resolver:

```
openclaw --dev agent --message <trigger> --deliver --json
```

Two signals were recorded per turn: `result.payloads` (the normalized payloads handed to the channel) and the count of `telegram outbound send ok` lines in the gateway log.

| trigger | model reply text | unpatched release | this revision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zzartifact` | invocation markup only | **1 send** — markup posted to chat | **0 sends** — suppressed |
| `zzplain` | `The answer is 42.` | 1 send | 1 send |
| `zzmixed` | markup + prose + markup | 1 send | 1 send |

Only `dist/tokens-BTKQYTUd.mjs` was swapped between the unpatched and patched runs — same bundle, same config, same mock, same bot — so the fix is the only variable.

Delivered payload, unpatched, for `zzartifact`:

```json
[{"text": "<invoke name=\"Bash\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo end1</parameter></invoke>", "mediaUrl": null}]
```

Patched, `zzartifact` yields `result.payloads == []`.

**Precise scope:** the fix drops a payload only when it is *entirely* invocation markup. A reply that surrounds markup with prose is still delivered **with that markup intact** — pre-existing behaviour this PR deliberately does not change, so that adding prose never causes a reply to be dropped. The `zzmixed` row above is therefore not "markup is stripped everywhere".

**Limitation:** the model is an OpenAI-compatible mock, not a CLI-backed agent. It reproduces the reply text that reaches the normalizer (the reported input), not the upstream mechanism by which a CLI-backed agent degrades into printing its tool calls.

### Unrelated check failures

Three checks fail on this revision; none is touched by this diff. The entire diff is `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts`, `src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts`, and one import plus one call site in `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts`.

**They are not introduced by this revision.** The same shards already failed on the preceding revisions of this branch, before the latest change existed:

| revision | failing checks |
| --- | --- |
| `df92c485` | `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-52` (plus lint/type checks fixed since) |
| `ccd5edc` | `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-52`, `-54` |
| `d7f23d0` (this one) | `checks-node-changed-extensions-config-52`, `-54`, `checks-node-compact-large-29` |

- `config-52` — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.output-fidelity.native.test.ts`, both parametrized cases (`max_output_tokens=24000` and `64`): `Error: Expected native command execution`. The test launches a **real Codex app-server** against a synthetic `responses` provider on a local port and requires the app-server to emit an `item/completed` with `type: "commandExecution"`. Its imports are node builtins, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, and local app-server helpers (`createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient`, `createCodexNativeTestState`) — nothing under `src/auto-reply/`. 333 of 335 tests in the shard pass.
- `config-54` — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.checkpoint.test.ts`: `AssertionError: expected [ 'user', 'assistant', 'toolResult' ] to deeply equal [ 'user', 'assistant' ]`. It imports only local app-server helpers and `vitest`. 118 of 119 tests pass.
- `compact-large-29` — infrastructure, not a test failure: `Subagent announce failed: GatewayCredentialsRequiredError: gateway chat.history requires credentials before opening a websocket`. That shard nevertheless reports `178` test files passed and `3103` tests passed.

I could not get a `main` baseline — the recent `main` runs I could inspect are all `skipped` — and I have no admin rights to re-run the failed jobs, so the comparison above is within this branch. Other open PRs show the same pattern of unrelated shard failures, e.g. `checks-node-compact-large-20` on #153869 and `checks-node-compact-small-38`/`-43`/`-46` plus `control-ui-performance` on #153868.

`oxfmt --check` passes on all three changed files.

prs.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
prs.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude and Codex), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` did not consistently operate on the named agent. Reads and writes could instead target `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, while `models status --agent <id>` resolved the agent's effective chain. The `image-fallbacks` group also silently ignored `--agent`.

## Behaviour After This Change

- Agent-scoped reads follow the effective configuration: an agent without a local fallback override inherits `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`; an agent with an override reads its local chain.
- Every explicit `fallbacks add/remove/clear --agent <id>` write creates or updates that named agent's local fallback override. It never mutates the global defaults chain.
- Unknown agent ids fail before any config write.
- `image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` fails clearly because image fallback configuration is global-only in the schema.
- Calls without `--agent` keep their existing global behaviour.
- The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) remains global; only the text-model fallback list is agent-scoped.

## Implementation

The fallbacks subcommands now resolve and validate `--agent` using the same agent helpers as `models status`. The write path uses an agent-local fallback setter that materialises the named agent's override when necessary and preserves global defaults. CLI wiring accepts `--agent` on the parent or fallbacks subcommand, while image-fallback commands explicitly reject it. `docs/cli/models.md` documents the inherited-read/local-write distinction.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`: agent-local writes, inherited reads, clearing, and preservation of defaults.
- `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts`: parent/subcommand flag forwarding, unchanged no-agent behaviour, and image-fallback rejection.
- `src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts`: end-to-end agent-local mutation, global catalogue preservation, and unknown-agent rejection.
- Targeted command passed all 3 shards and 80 tests:
  `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/cli/models-cli.test.ts src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts`
- Scoped oxlint passed the seven changed TypeScript files with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- The repository-wide oxlint wrapper was also attempted; its type-aware `tsgolint` subprocess was SIGKILLed by the verification host's memory limit. The underlying oxlint phase reported 0 warnings and 0 errors before that infrastructure failure.
- Integrated current upstream `main` (`8d5ad804a65dddfd60a5e0d6e06e8a1108d8c035`) without conflicts; final head is `5475d31efc8c10229c70591c3b43f38717189245`.

prs.title: fix(arcee): make OpenRouter onboarding runnable
prs.body:
Closes #112747

AI-assisted: implemented and verified with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Arcee setup through OpenRouter should keep provider configuration, model references, and the stored OpenRouter credential under the same provider owner. The original July onboarding preset wrote an `arcee/...` route while storing the credential as `openrouter:default`, causing the first agent request to fail. Current main also has legacy auth-alias support; this PR makes new OpenRouter setup canonical and repairs previously persisted configuration.

The previous PR head had two compatibility defects: Doctor removed the old provider without migrating every agent model scope, and re-onboarding overwrote an existing shared OpenRouter endpoint/API mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New OpenRouter-backed Arcee setup selects `openrouter/arcee-ai/trinity-large-thinking` and owns its provider configuration under `models.providers.openrouter`.
- Doctor migrates defaults, keyed agent entries, legacy agent lists, primary/fallback references, model aliases, nested subagent/heartbeat/compaction/media selections, and explicit model-policy references before removing the old OpenRouter-backed Arcee catalog.
- Existing canonical model settings win on collisions. Migration is immutable and idempotent; direct Arcee configuration is unchanged.
- Both registered onboarding and the public catalog helper preserve an existing OpenRouter `baseUrl` and `api`, seeding defaults only when absent.
- Integration with current main preserves connection-only setup in merge mode and catalog seeding in replace mode, plus the eager public catalog helper. The Doctor repair is declared in the plugin manifest and uses the current lightweight migration SDK.

## User Impact

Fresh OpenRouter setup has matching credential and model ownership. Existing installations retain their proxy transport and authored model settings. Older OpenRouter-backed Arcee configuration can be repaired with `openclaw doctor --fix`; direct Arcee setup is unaffected.

## Evidence

### Current repair and upstream integration — 2026-09-17

Head: `54ab6358560c4f59a59b06bc820d335a5b08623d`. Rebased onto `9ace0a571f4151cd1f47eb8aaa7b8cc987c45cee` to resolve the actual merge conflicts; no unrelated main changes were reverted.

- Before the fix: five new regression cases failed and twelve tests passed on the old PR base. Failures covered defaults/entries/legacy-list migration and custom OpenRouter transport with and without an explicit API mode.
- Final current-main proof with Node 24.20.0 and pinned pnpm 12.4.0:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/arcee/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/arcee/index.test.ts` — **39 passed**.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/doctor-contract-declarations.test.ts -t 'matches every resolvable artifact'` — **1 passed**, 1 unrelated state-migration case deselected.
  - Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Registered interactive/non-interactive setup, credential isolation, merge/replace behavior, public helper behavior, migration scope completeness, input preservation, and idempotence are covered.
- [GitHub checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113097/checks) report the hosted CI status for the current head; the earlier head's green CI is not reused as current-head proof.
- No fresh paid model request or operator-Gateway deployment was performed for this repair. The historical live inference proof below belongs only to its explicitly identified earlier head.

### Historical live inference proof — original PR head

Performed on 2026-07-31 from PR head `f8ac6b1ce06ded770ee5325191fbfca274600bab` with a newly issued real OpenRouter credential. Private credential material was removed and never printed.

prs.title: improve: make session lists faster on large stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where session lists, filters, facets, and session-id lookups parsed every persisted session blob and repeated filtering and ordering in JavaScript, even though the v14 agent schema already promotes and indexes those fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway now treats `entry_json` as the canonical record and promoted SQLite columns as the indexed read surface. List selection, counts, creator facets, lineage predicates, ordering, and current-session-id lookup run through Kysely before surviving rows are parsed. Derived titles are projected into `session_nodes.display_name` at write time and backfilled once at startup. Runtime continues to assume the doctor-enforced canonical-key contract; no alias, compatibility, or fallback reader was added.

Pending `entry_valid` rows are intentionally excluded from indexed pages until a canonical writer rewrites them or `openclaw doctor --fix` repairs them. This accepts transient count/facet skew during a mixed-version writer window, as explicitly accepted by the maintainer, instead of retrying or reconciling on the read path. The maintainer also approved the additive title/index surface without a schema-version bump.

## User Impact

Large session sidebars and filtered session views load substantially faster while preserving pagination, visibility, creator facets, projected titles, and moved-child lineage behavior. Operators with pre-canonical stores must run `openclaw doctor --fix`, matching the runtime contract established by #116703.

## Evidence

### Performance

Seeded Testbox SQLite database: 12,000 canonical `session_nodes`, 2 KiB JSON payload per row, 25% archived, promoted interaction timestamps, and `entry_valid = 1`. Both paths were warmed, then measured as the median of five runs: the prior full-cache parse/filter/sort/slice path versus the promoted-column query with `limit = 100`.

| Path | Median |
| --- | ---: |
| Full blob scan + JavaScript selection | 70.27 ms |
| Indexed SQLite selection | 12.00 ms |
| Speedup | **5.9x** |

Final post-rebase perf proof: Testbox run 30674426726.

### Validation

- Final post-rebase focused proof: Testbox run 30669963436 passed 564 tests across Gateway session listing and lineage, accessor/conformance, SQLite query plans, TUI, and embedded-agent surfaces. This includes 94 accessor tests, 55 conformance tests, and the 12,000-row performance test.
- Exact post-rebase changed gate: run 30669963436, green, including the wizard lint shard, extension typecheck/lint, and 0 runtime import cycles.
- Post-rebase build: run 30669963436, green; no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warning.
- The first hosted head exposed an unrelated Madge cycle already fixed on moving `main`; current-main Testbox run 30669830915 proved 0 Madge cycles, and the branch was rebased onto that fix before the final proof above.
- Final title-projection leaf proof: run 30672101033 passed the full architecture gate with 0 Madge/runtime cycles plus 255 focused title/accessor tests.
- Final compile proof: run 30672730954 passed prod/test typechecks, all 125 extension package boundaries, and targeted lint; run 30673587220 passed the 100-test agent database fixture.
- Final conflict-surface proof: run 30673771719 passed architecture, production types, catalog-prewarm reconciliation, additive-schema repair, and the seeded performance test.
- ClawSweeper rank-up move applied: `pinned_at <= 0` is included in the unpinned indexed page, and the regression asserts both the zero-valued and NULL-valued rows remain visible. Run 30674426726 passed 95 accessor/query-plan tests.
- Final branch autoreview against current `origin/main`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- SQLite schema baseline and query-plan assertions are green; no schema-version bump.

### Protocol verdict

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts` changes documentation only. No field was added, removed, or retyped, so the protocol surface is compatible and no Swift/Kotlin regeneration is required.

### LOC accounting

Final GitHub diff: 59 files, **+3,587 / -1,703**. GitHub file stats classify this as production **+1,938 / -902** (net **+1,036**), tests **+1,636 / -800**, and generated **+13 / -1**.

| Deleted or trimmed | Why the cut is safe |
| --- | --- |
| `session-list-order.ts` and the synchronous list projection | SQLite owns canonical ordering; async bounded enrichment is the only list path. |
| JavaScript include-lineage chunk merge and byte-sort reimplementation | Producers switch to residual selection above 400 keys; bounded SQL sets fail loudly. |
| Pagination retry-exclusion threading | Canonical-invalid rows fail earlier; visibility retains the simpler retry-once contract. |
| Admin profile-specific work keys | Admin list visibility is profile-independent. |
| `"__row-context__"` sentinel and alias loop | `lineageKeys` is a first-class predicate and canonical opaque keys are authoritative. |
| Repeated retained-window tombstone probes | One shared helper owns the exception. |
| Read-side `entry_valid` settle/retry machinery | Writers set validity and doctor repairs; indexed reads exclude pending rows. |

Named tradeoff: the net +1,036 production LOC buys indexed selection/count/facets, exact `current_session_id` lookup, bounded child hydration, title projection plus streamed backfill and cache coherence, invalid-row-safe pagination, partial indexes, embedded/prewarm parity, and one leaf title-projection owner that keeps schema bootstrap acyclic. The residual combined-store deletion lands only with the goal-3 federation decision; this PR does not add a second path.

## Follow-ups

Goal 3 remains deferred exactly as ruled: either persist the current runtime controller into canonical lineage, changing today’s runtime-only ownership design, or redesign multi-store federation so indexed per-store queries compose without a materialized combined store.

prs.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
prs.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Migration note: This PR replaces #100371 with the same published head commit, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

## Exact-head authority-chain proof

At `fc3e2b425251d8fc7504488eff3842a1817a1cbe`, both lifecycle reset entry points are owner-gated and the exact-head behavior chain is inspectable in the [updated proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104690#issuecomment-5398588721).

- Personal Teams remove and reinstall-add signals rotate the session. The removal proof changes the active transcript path and clears the seeded pre-removal stale prompt, goal, delivery, CLI-session, token/runtime, and route fields.
- The real lifecycle owner changes the persisted session id and transcript path without retaining the old transcript.
- Harness/channel owners succeed; an unauthorized agent caller cannot reset an unlocked Teams row; revoked/replaced channel runtimes are rejected before mutation; and revocation during physical-owner reset cannot persist the caller patch.
- Failed reset work intentionally leaves a durable `initializationPending` boundary that blocks old-context reuse until retry succeeds; SDK documentation states this contract.
- Exact API diff from `2d7aec92fbb3` to `fc3e2b425251` reports no Plugin SDK API change.

Redacted verbose exact-head proof: Teams signals 2/2, real lifecycle store 1/1, authority final effects 4/4. Full focused suites: registry 7/7, session lifecycle 8/8, Teams lifecycle 17/17 and monitor lifecycle 19/19. Exact assertion-safety ratchet against CI base `bf83a4dde8f0`, scoped formatting, oxlint, SDK surface/API diff, whitespace, mandatory autoreview, and TruffleHog passed.

The preceding behavior head also passed the full Teams suite (93 files / 1,480 tests) and core/extension production and test type lanes. The final `fc3e2b425251` delta contains only four required SAFETY-comment lines. No unrelated file or `CHANGELOG.md` changed.

prs.title: fix(configure): accept --agent as the explicit setup owner
prs.body:
Supersedes #129431. Related: #126360, #128637.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: operators cannot explicitly choose the setup owner with `openclaw configure --agent <id>`, and selected-agent setup can miss workspace-local providers or write model/workspace defaults to the wrong owner.

## User Impact

`openclaw configure --agent <id>` and `openclaw config --agent <id>` consistently configure the selected agent across sections. Invalid or unknown selectors fail before setup effects. Without the flag, existing legacy defaults, System Agent selection, and interactive selection remain unchanged. No configuration schema or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry one validated owner through setup, discovery, credentials, and defaults. Explicit selection scopes workspace and primary/utility/custom-provider defaults to that agent; fully scoped provider callers only resolve an owner when a directory fallback actually needs one. Keep cancellation, authority checks, and persistence ordering intact.

Original implementation and report by @ctbritt (Christopher Allbritton); this continuation preserves the contributor commit and adds the demonstrated ownership/workspace repairs.

## Evidence

- 165 distinct focused tests passed across eight CLI, wizard, onboarding, and provider-auth files on the prior integrated head, including real workspace-only provider discovery and credential persistence with an empty sibling store.
- Behavioral red/green: removing workspace forwarding fails provider discovery; removing explicit-owner scope fails six ownership regressions. Exact restoration passes the selected regressions.
- Cancellation, retired authority, provider failure, invalid selectors, and workspace provisioning failure retain no-write/no-downstream-effect coverage. All six touched test files were audited in full; no behavior tests, valid failures, retries, or timeouts were removed or weakened.
- Independent production and whole-test-file review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The authored 18-file patch, all six complete touched tests, and 20 caller/helper review inputs remain byte-identical after the latest main integration.
- Local required changed-file checks passed before that main-only refresh, including core and all 25 core-test type shards, export scans, lint, and architecture guards. Fresh-head hosted CI is blocked by four gateway/task CI shard failures outside the authored configure/auth diff; native landing remains pending.

The focused runner was corrected to the existing command/plugin shards' process-fork contract after main's host-owned SQLite broker rejected thread workers. Real persistence remains enabled with physically verified private state paths; no live profile was used.

The initial hosted run exposed the pre-existing concurrent group-defaults fixture failure. Main already repaired it in `46dfea6a42010`; that prerequisite is now integrated without changing this PR’s authored patch. The exact conflict assertion is strengthened; this refreshed head receives its own hosted CI.

Current-head CI (`f2f9305`): the repaired concurrent group-defaults case and its 378-test group passed ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35800768069/job/106990911433)). Remaining failures are [task-history teardown with an active SQLite borrower](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35800768069/job/106990913185) and [task pagination returning an empty owned page](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35800768069/job/106990911354). prs.title: fix(gateway): restore show_widget canvas previews through Tool Search history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`show_widget` invoked through Tool Search (a `tool_call` run) renders its inline canvas live, but after a chat history reload the preview is gone: `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` restores nothing for these runs, while direct `show_widget` calls restore fine (#168625).

## Root cause

Two result shapes reach history that `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` never unwraps:

1. **Tool Search envelope row** — the outer `toolResult` row (toolName `tool_search`) carries a `{tool, result}` envelope (src/agents/tool-search.ts). The sanitizer deletes the row's `details` (no envelope key survives `projectToolResultDetails` whitelisting), so after reload the envelope survives only as the row's JSON text. The extractor read only `details.mcpAppPreview` and row-level text — the envelope JSON itself has no `kind: "canvas"`, so nothing matched.
2. **Nested tool record** — the `openclaw.nested-tool.v1` row projects a `toolResult` block whose canvas JSON sits in the block's own `content` text; the extractor never scanned nested blocks.

## Fix

In `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts`, add a fallback tail to `extractChatToolResultCanvasPreview` (direct-call behavior and `rawText` semantics unchanged):

- `extractCanvasPreviewFromResultRecord` — reads a target result record `{content, details}` via the existing `extractCanvasFromDetails` / `extractCanvasFromText`
- `extractToolSearchEnvelopePreview` — unwraps the envelope from `entry.details.result` while present (live path), else parses the sanitized envelope JSON text
- `extractNestedToolResultBlockPreview` — scans `entry.content` for `toolResult` blocks and applies the record reader

Everything reuses the existing extraction/dedupe machinery (`appendChatCanvasBlocks` still dedupes by viewId/url), so a preview already forwarded as content is not doubled.

## Evidence

- New focused tests in `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` drive `sanitizeChatHistoryMessages` → `augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks` end-to-end for both shapes (envelope row post-sanitize with `details` deleted, nested toolResult block, live `details.result` unwrap). They fail on current `main` and pass with this change; no mocking of the code under fix.
- The existing placement suite ("preserves first-accepted previews") is untouched and still covers the direct `mcpAppPreview` path.
- Module-level verification of the three scenarios (red on the base commit, green on this branch, direct-call regression green) is reproduced by the committed tests.

- [x] Concise Evidence section included
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] `autoreview` skill — not available here; in its place: every new branch was reachability-checked against the real sanitizer/envelope/block bodies, the full placement regression suite still passes, and the new tests were verified red on the base commit and green on this branch
- [x] Will follow the pull request review flow after Barnacle/ClawSweeper/maintainer feedback

Fixes #168625

prs.title: fix: serialized tool-call XML leaks into chat replies
prs.body:
Closes #138198
Related: #153594, #153635

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes raw GLM and invocation XML appearing in streamed and final chat replies when a model writes a tool request or a shadow copy as ordinary text.

## User Impact

Replies retain visible prose while hiding internal tool XML, including partial streaming prefixes. Completed literal explanations and inline, fenced, or indented code examples remain visible. Native calls continue to execute exactly once. No configuration or migration is required.

**Known limitation:** artifact-only replies without a native call or visible answer reach the existing empty-reply format failure (`chat` state `aborted`, no message). The baseline's already-supported JSON envelope reproduces that terminal behavior. Original transcript bytes remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `assistant-visible-text.ts` sanitizer owns GLM `arg_key` payloads and bare, `antml`, and `mm` invocation forms. Stream fallback, block snapshots, and completed payloads consume that owner. It holds ambiguous opening fragments during streaming, restores terminal literals, and carries XML context only across consecutive same-phase text parts, ending it at native tool/thinking blocks.

This preserves @ericcaiwx-star's contributor commits and incorporates @ruiling-smartbear's distinct invocation cases with Ruilin Gao's co-author credit. The competing reply-token scanner was not carried forward.

Main `6b8e69e470765791cd8ac91d721b497f9b58948b` was merged without rebasing. The sole conflict uses main's current subagent QA expectation, removing this branch's superseded assertion correction. One additional unused local binding inherited from main was removed to fix core typecheck error TS6133; environment-consuming callers are unchanged. The separately filed Memory QA issue is outside this repair.

## Evidence

Validation head: `84b0dfe52fbad2bd5c53aa513adf59ec59819d32`.

- **210 focused tests pass in 72.91s wall**, including the registered Telegram adapter. The tests ran after merging main; sanitizer/test bytes are unchanged by the subsequent unused-binding deletion. The original 30 handler regressions failed on main; six additional native-boundary cases failed before their repair. Final handler suite: 36 cases.
- Targeted lint and formatting pass. Core types pass after the unused-binding cleanup (6.79s). Required line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, timeout-race, mock-export, config-doc, and plugin-inventory ratchets pass.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview on the validation head: **scoped-clean through P2**.
- Final full build: **passed, 247.22s wall**. Final isolated Gateway replay: **all 11 cases passed, 26.538s total turn wall time**.
- Production **+295/-109 (net +186)**; tests **+323/-4 (net +319)**; docs **+1**. Production growth handles streaming ambiguity, terminal restoration, and native block boundaries. The contributor's per-test Gateway boot was replaced by focused handler tests and the actual Gateway replay.

The replay uses the built Gateway's real WebSocket `chat.send` entry point and a local OpenAI-compatible SSE fixture provider. It covers GLM shadow text; bare, antml, mm, and plain function_calls wrappers; native exec plus a shadow copy; artifact-only GLM/invoke/legacy JSON; and literal/code controls. Baseline main leaked XML. Candidate reply deltas, snapshots, finals, assistant events, and preambles contain no leaked markup; the native control executes once and returns `XML_PROOF_OK`; literal/code examples preserve exact bytes.

The campaign lead explicitly accepts this isolated Gateway replay as the required boundary proof and overrides proof-only live-Telegram holds. Live Telegram receipt and live GLM generation are not claimed. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head on October 11 at 00:07 UTC after the single re-review request: **no actionable findings**. Its proof-only Telegram hold is lead-overridden. Its remaining request for CI attribution is addressed below.

### Inherited Memory QA failure

The lead accepted **READY-WITH-INHERITED-QA** if the remaining CI failure is `memory-dreaming-sweep`, and filed that issue separately. Actual same-environment attribution used the unmodified scenario/planner/model-selection/profile configuration, fresh isolated state, macOS arm64, Node v26.11.1, pnpm12.9.0, and the `smoke-ci` mock-openai/Crabline Telegram defaults:

| Source | Exact SHA | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Previous PR head | `5eff359970282911ca2d4bf60093423fddd86b5f` | PASS; all three steps, one candidate/promotion, canary/marker and Light Sleep/REM artifacts, restored configuration | 210.31s |
| Main | `0e6b2c23c8d55292b67c6835c22c85dec6d0a575` | FAIL; both built-in attempts complete with zero candidates/promotions, then 180000ms promotion-artifact timeout | 512.99s |

Each checkout was built with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build qaRuntime`, then ran `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> qa run --repo-root . --qa-profile smoke-ci --concurrency 10 --output-dir <isolated-output> --scenario memory-dreaming-sweep`. prs.title: chore(deps): update fs-safe to 0.26.0
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates OpenClaw's direct `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency from 0.25.0 to the published 0.26.0 release, including its Android/Termux no-replace copy fix.

Refs #167791.

## User Impact

SQLite read-only snapshots gain the fallback for filesystems that refuse hard links. This is a dependency compatibility update: existing copy policies remain unchanged, and no new optional capability is adopted. Termux device validation is still needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

[Release](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.26.0) · [0.26.0 changelog](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/blob/v0.26.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openclaw/fs-safe/v/0.26.0)

Mirrors the 0.25.0 bump: all 13 direct pins/importers, the lockfile, and the reviewed-release allowlist move together. All eleven published fs-safe packages were verified against npm version, integrity, and platform metadata before editing. The three new native packages are FreeBSD x64, FreeBSD ARM64, and Windows ARM64 MSVC. The precise release-age exemption expires after 2026-10-17T20:00:18.006Z. The separate transitive 0.21.3 family stays under its dependency owner's existing pin.

| Audited release change | OpenClaw compatibility finding |
| --- | --- |
| `Root.copyIn` metadata and literal links ([#921](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/921)) | Audited all 16 production Root calls and the separate iMessage TempWorkspace call. `preserveMetadata` remains opt-in and `sourceSymlinks` defaults to `reject`. Existing explicit modes, `preserveSourceMode`, hardlink admission, publication callbacks, and bounds remain appropriate. No call-site adaptation needed. |
| ReFS cloning ([#920](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/920)) | Existing `clone: "auto"` calls gain supported acceleration and retain byte fallback; no new capability adopted. |
| Native mkdir collision code ([#895](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/895)) | No Root mkdir consumer relies on the former raw ENOTDIR collision result. Other raw errno classifiers belong to Node filesystem operations. |
| Recursive removal budget ([#904](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/904)) | No production removal uses a zero entry budget. The custom removal owner uses its own admitted traversal and nonrecursive Root removal. |
| Android/Termux no-replace publication ([#888](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/888)) | `sqlite-readonly-location` reaches `copySqliteFile`, which uses `copyIn` with `overwrite: false`, mode 0600, and publication receipts. It benefits directly from the hardlink-refusal fallback. No device proof is claimed. |
| Durable JSON queue hardlink refusal ([#889](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/889)) | Typed `helper-unavailable` remains a limitation for fs-safe durable JSON queue consumers on Android. Current OpenClaw subagent announce delivery is already SQLite-backed (`session-delivery-queue-storage` → state worker → SQLite kernel); it has no fs-safe durable JSON queue call site. Older OpenClaw builds using that queue retain the limitation. |
| Native Win32 diagnostics ([#919](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/919)) | Semantic codes are unchanged; creation-refusal recording and worker transport preserve the underlying diagnostics. No raw Win32 number assumptions need adaptation. |
| Pipes, leases, ACL inspection, FreeBSD and Windows ARM64 | No existing call-site impact; added native package availability only. |
| Performance ([#899](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/899), [#901](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/901), [#902](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/902), [#906](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/906), [#912](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/912)) and ZIP admission fixes | No calling contract changes. Plugin capture retains its synchronous copy APIs. Public ZIP admission still rejects malformed names. |

## Evidence

- Frozen dependency installation passed; verified all 13 direct pins/importers and all eleven 0.26.0 package records, including integrity and platform metadata.
- All selected typecheck lanes passed on Linux. All 104 generated npm lock mirrors passed, including `os`/`cpu`/`libc` constraints.
- 167 focused test files passed across the fs-safe, SQLite snapshot, plugin capture, sandbox, lock, temp, queue, copy, and direct-importer batches. The Darwin-only native filesystem test file was skipped on Linux. The final 13-shard remainder passed in 416.67 seconds. Initial `/tmp` capacity and permissive temporary-directory ancestry failures were corrected in the test environment without changing code or assertions.
- The synthetic hardlink-refusal probe passed through the actual `copySqliteFile` entry point on macOS and Linux: independent mode-0600 copy, no-clobber behavior, publication receipt, and no staging residue. This is not Termux device proof.
- Independent Codex autoreview was clean at P0–P2.
- The broad changed-check run passed its typecheck and lock-mirror lanes, then encountered six unchanged baseline max-lines lint errors. The exact-head CI lint/type jobs passed; the broad local run is not claimed green.
- No tests or runtime source changed; no test-cost increase. No CHANGELOG edit, per the repository's release-owned changelog policy.

### Exact-head CI and inherited failures

[CI run 38083104098, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38083104098) finished with 158 successful jobs, 19 skipped jobs, three failed root jobs, and the downstream CI gate; no jobs were cancelled. QA was rerun once. The other failed job results were carried forward from their original executions; the attempt-2 exports and job census retain that provenance.

The A/B baseline is `6b5284f579371f0e372b6c1882f863df19ffdb57` (fs-safe 0.25.0); the actual CI merge checkout is `c75cafb9f1a3830f70eb6c79ef3d5102ed2581ee`, whose second parent is this PR's head `0e8814c4b9d3802e718a92f132bc8ef20aea2597` (fs-safe 0.26.0). Relevant fixture and owner sources are unchanged between those trees.

| Failed root | Independent attribution |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-small-13` | Both versions reproduce the transcript cursor's zero-versus-one recorder assertion and cron's four-versus-two catalog-load assertion. The first fixture passes `promptError: true`, which returns before recording; the second combines initial catalog loading and fallback thinking hydration into one mock with a stale call-count expectation. |
| `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-22` | The memory cache-prune fixture holds a publication writer while waiting for an observer on `worker.run`, but pruning uses `worker.execute`. Baseline reproduces the first-case deadlock and cleanup cascades; the candidate's isolated first-case replay reproduces CI's 300-second no-output watchdog. |
| `QA Smoke CI (profile 4/4)` | Both revisions reproduce the private-completion assertion and the final 180-second dreaming promotion wait timeout after automatic scenario retry. The mock endpoint retains labeled runtime carriers as user messages; the fixture instead searches developer/system roles. The dreaming cron completes, but the promotion conjunction never becomes true. The latest hosted retry exhausts the ten-minute primary invocation while retrying the same scenario. Individual failed promotion conjuncts remain undiagnosed; the same result on 0.25.0 establishes that this bump does not cause it. |

These failures are outside this dependency-only change. The native inherited-failure exception retains failed CI status and the scoped passing evidence; it does not classify the run as green.

prs.title: feat(sandbox): add lightweight local SRT backend
prs.body:
Related: #163540

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw needs a local sandbox backend that confines commands and file tools without Docker. This adds the bundled `srt-sandbox` plugin through `registerSandboxBackend()` and corrects permission and process-lifetime defects in the original draft.

## User Impact

macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap and seccomp. Private writable paths remain usable while restricted host workspaces, managed skills and readonly resources stay protected. Command descendants are swept on completion, failure, cancellation, timeout and owner death.

Windows execution is disabled before native provisioning with SRT 0.0.76. Configuration compatibility and read-only dependency discovery remain available, but every Windows command, preparation and filesystem entry rejects before account, credential, WFP or ACL mutation. The pinned installer cannot establish exclusive ownership of its shared account or safely cancel and reverse partial grants. Native Windows execution must remain disabled until an owner-aware provisioning API and the documented VM qualification are available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commands, buffered execution and file tools share one authoritative filesystem policy, including canonical aliases and nonexistent descendants of protected roots. Linux mounts writable ancestors of readonly roots as anchors so an ancestor rename cannot move a protected child. Supplied mutation pins must match the complete destination and remain live; expired, consumed and mismatched pins reject instead of resolving replacement authority. Host custody stays outside guest signaling permissions. All command routes use this custody. Before launching macOS guests, the existing Seatbelt profile is tightened to reject `setsid`, `setpgid` and `posix_spawn`, preventing descendants from leaving the owned process group. Ordinary fork/exec remains supported; spawn-based launchers, daemonization and job-control group changes are unsupported and fail closed. The pinned wrapper is decoded as literal argv without executing command bytes on a host shell; an unexpected wrapper rejects before launch. Buffered commands now start a fresh SRT process with the current policy; this adds per-command startup overhead. Startup-hook and loader environment variables are rejected before host interpreters launch. Container-style readonly resource path projection is unsupported.

The six previous review findings are addressed as follows:

1. Workspace permissions: preserve `none`, `ro` and `rw`; protect canonical managed skills and readonly resources in command and file paths, including broad extra writable roots and symlink aliases.
2. Windows scope reuse: coalesce concurrent resolutions and reuse the same authoritative scope/policy across turns; reject different scopes and retired generations.
3. Windows provisioning retirement: remove the unsafe native provisioning path entirely. Execution rejects before installation or grants, including after retirement; no partial cleanup or shared-account adoption is claimed.
4. Streaming custody: host-owned liveness channels and guardians sweep descendants when the launcher or Gateway dies, while preserving output and exit status. Native macOS kernel restrictions prevent session/group-changing descendants from escaping that sweep; delayed-write proof covers ordinary buffered, broker and streaming routes.
5. Broker completion: execute buffered commands under independent host custody and sweep background descendants on success, failure and timeout. The session control process accepts health/policy RPCs only.
6. Windows network settings: reject all execution modes before persistent effects; runtime behavior, configuration hints and platform documentation agree.

Session settings JSON and control messages are ephemeral runtime state, not a stored-data schema migration. Temporary command settings are removed by their custody finalizer, session settings are removed on disposal, and the existing configuration-contract tests cover the accepted settings. No database or user-state migration is introduced.

## Evidence

- Upstream `main` fetched and incorporated at `2f1f73ccb2224bbe7d961b4c0d3b29cfdd51e7f8`.
- Exact tested/pushed head: `0cd129216b9a9bdc907ff956812059872fc41c83`.
- Full exact-head SRT suite (`--isolate`): macOS 125 passed / 11 Linux-only skipped across 18 passed and 2 skipped files; native Linux 120 passed / 16 macOS-only skipped across 17 passed and 3 skipped files. Both ran 20 files with zero failures.
- Real macOS and native Linux backend tests prove deny-all rejection, strict allowlist success and off-list rejection, open-mode success, and the platform-specific Seatbelt or Bubblewrap/proxy wiring. Six permission cases cover `none`/`ro`/`rw` with buffered broker routing enabled and disabled, command/file mutations, hidden reads, managed skills and readonly resources.
- Real process tests kill the launcher and Gateway and verify descendant termination; buffered tests cover background descendants after exit codes 0 and 7, timeout 124, and guest attempts to disable cleanup. Exit/signal reporting includes 143.
- Red-before/green-after regressions reproduce the permission, reuse, retirement-entry, custody, broker and network contract defects. Windows evidence is deterministic admission/rejection coverage; no native account, ACL or WFP proof is claimed.
- Extension production/test typechecks, type-aware SRT lint, format, inventory/config-doc and SDK boundary checks, frozen install and whitespace checks passed. Runtime import cycles: zero. The changed-surface gate and full production Knip scan fail on one inherited core export: `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts: observePlacementAuthority`. A clean detached worktree at the exact upstream base reproduces the same production and full-tree export findings; the core file and export scanners are byte-identical to upstream. No SRT dead-code finding was reported. The script export scan passes. Earlier broad typechecks passed; no claim of an all-green repository-wide gate is made.
- Independent review of the remediation scope completed with no actionable P0/P1 findings after correcting the verified findings.
- Native Linux proof ran with Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.5.1, Bubblewrap and vendored seccomp on Linux 6.19.13 ARM64 in an isolated runner with an init reaper and the mount/user namespace privileges required for nested sandbox execution. It covered all six workspace-access/broker-routing cases, readonly ancestor rename protection, hidden paths, network modes and process custody. Host process identities were matched through `/proc` rather than interpreting guest namespace PIDs as host PIDs. Native Windows VM access was not supplied; the platform support matrix and required fresh/existing/shared-SID qualification are documented in `docs/plugins/reference/srt-sandbox.md`.

No UI screenshots apply. This PR remains Draft. The inherited core export failure, hosted checks, native Windows qualification and the decision to retain this backend as a bundled plugin remain explicit landing considerations. A fresh ClawSweeper review is requested for this exact head; no readiness or merge action is requested.


### Redacted real behavior output

The pin regressions were first run against the preceding production bridge: 11 failed / 15 passed. On the final bridge, all 26 bridge tests pass. Consumed-pin cases first execute and verify a successful live mutation, then replace the parent and verify replay rejection; expired and mismatched cases also verify replacement paths remain unchanged.

```text
✓ |extensions| extensions/srt-sandbox/src/fs-bridge.test.ts > srt fs bridge — held-pin lifecycle (no fd leak on any path) > rejects an expired write pin before touching a replacement parent 292ms

```

Native Linux output from the exact-head full suite:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --isolate extensions/srt-sandbox
```

The detached-session regressions reproduced delayed writes in all nine cases before correction. A second native counterexample proved that blocking only setsid/setpgid still permits posix_spawn group changes. The final profile blocks all three routes. ## What Problem This Solves

Ports the terminal, browser, and desktop panels to Solid while the remaining Lit shell callers continue to use their registered tags.

## User Impact

No intentional behavior change. Existing routes, host tags, CSS classes, dock controls, and E2E selectors remain. Terminal sessions retain their per-tab DOM islands, and noVNC keeps ownership of its viewer DOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing synchronous controllers remain the state owners. Solid renders their admitted state through the canonical bridge and shared committed-DOM lifecycle. Each registered panel has one implementation; stateless Lit header helpers remain for unported callers. Solid document views use the bridge's returned components.

Tests now mount the Solid views and set public inputs before connection. The real-terminal E2Es observe the existing runtime factory instead of reading private Lit fields. Tab and picker IDs are scoped to each mounted view to preserve ARIA relationships when multiple panels share light DOM.

The additional production code primarily covers explicit bridge registrations, scoped light-DOM styles, and the Solid tab strip alongside the stateless Lit helper still used by unported callers. No new domain store, dependency, or configuration is introduced.

Release-note context: internal Control UI renderer migration with terminal/server-session and desktop/viewer lifetimes preserved.

## Evidence

| --- | --- |
| Solid bridge | 2 passed; 31.92 s |
| Solid panel lifecycle | 3 passed; 10.37 s |

Closes #157368

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: LINE pairing challenges and question-answer notices are sent twice (reply + duplicate push) when the reply request fails with an ambiguous network error such as an abort or `fetch failed`, where LINE may already have accepted the reply.

Also fixes the recovery gap this could create: a first-contact pairing sender whose challenge was not delivered could not obtain the pending code again for the pending request's one-hour lifetime.

## User Impact

User impact: LINE users no longer receive the same pairing challenge or question-answer notice twice during transient network failures. A first-contact sender who misses a pairing challenge under an ambiguous failure can get the same pending code re-sent once by messaging again; a sender whose challenge was delivered, whose pending request lives under a different LINE account, or who already consumed the one-shot recovery is never re-sent a duplicate. No config, schema, or breaking changes; the push fallback is preserved for definitive rejections (LINE 4xx other than 408) and for failures that never reached LINE.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sendLineHandlerText` (used for pairing challenges and question-answer notices) fell back to `pushMessageLine` on any reply error that was not a `CHANNEL_PARTIAL_DELIVERY` error. A push cannot deduplicate a possibly accepted reply, so ambiguous outcomes (AbortError, undici `TypeError: fetch failed`, ambiguous transient codes) produced duplicate messages. The main auto-reply path already refuses this via `canFallbackAfterLineReplyFailure`.

This change moves `canFallbackAfterLineReplyFailure` into `send-retry.ts` (shared with `auto-reply-delivery.ts`, which keeps its existing behavior) and applies it in `sendLineHandlerText`, so the fallback only runs when the reply was definitively rejected or never dispatched.

Recovery: when the reply fails ambiguously and no duplicate push was sent, `sendLinePairingReply` marks the sender as needing recovery (`pairing-reply.ts`). The marker is keyed by the LINE account, the sender, and the exact pending code, with a one-hour TTL matching the pending request lifetime. On a later message from that sender and account, if the pairing-store upsert reports an existing pending request with the same code (`created: false`), the code is re-sent once through `sendLineHandlerText` (reply preferred, duplicate-safe). The recovery re-send never re-arms the marker, so recovery fires at most once; a successful first delivery never marks the sender at all; and an ambiguous failure under one account can never authorize a resend under another account or for a different pending code.

## Maintainer decision: recovery tradeoffs

Two inherent tradeoffs of the bounded recovery need an explicit maintainer decision before merge (ClawSweeper Revision 6 recommendation: accept the bounded resend, document both behaviors, and prove the real transport path).

1. **One possible delayed duplicate.** An ambiguous reply error can occur after LINE already accepted the reply. The transport cannot tell whether an ambiguous failure delivered the message, so this recovery cannot distinguish "delivered" from "lost"; by design it allows at most one delayed duplicate (the same pending code re-sent once after an ambiguous failure, then the marker is consumed). This is the deliberate cost of recovering a possibly lost challenge. Alternative: drop recovery entirely, which avoids any delayed duplicate but leaves a first-contact sender unable to recover a lost code for the pending request's lifetime.
2. **Recovery is in-memory.** The marker is intentionally in-memory, so a Gateway restart within the one-hour pairing window drops it and the sender who missed their code waits out the window before messaging again to mint a fresh code. Making recovery survive restart would require recording "delivery unconfirmed" durably in the account-scoped pairing-store entry (a core `src/pairing` contract change with a migration), which is out of scope for this bounded LINE fix.

Recommendation: accept the transient, one-shot recovery for now (one possible delayed duplicate, no restart persistence) and track durable, acceptance-distinguishing recovery as a separate core `src/pairing` change if either tradeoff matters in practice.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts`:
  - "does not push a duplicate pairing reply after a fetch that may have reached LINE" and "...after an aborted reply request" — fail on the pre-fix code (push was called once) and pass after the fix.
  - "re-sends the pending pairing code once after an ambiguous first delivery" — a later message with an existing pending request re-sends the same code exactly once.
  - "does not re-send the pairing code when the first delivery succeeded" — the bounded recovery never repeats a confirmed delivery.
  - "re-sends the pending pairing code only once" — the recovery marker is consumed, so a third message does not re-send again.
  - "does not re-arm recovery when the recovery resend itself fails ambiguously" — an ambiguous recovery resend does not restore the marker, so a later message does not re-send again (covers the repeated-resend concern).
  - "does not re-send a pending code into another LINE account" — the same sender and same pending code under a different LINE account are not re-sent that code, isolating the account boundary (covers the cross-account recovery authority concern).
- Full affected suites pass: `bot-handlers.test.ts`, `auto-reply-delivery.test.ts`, `auto-reply-delivery-recovery.test.ts`, `send-retry.test.ts` — **162 tests passed**, no regressions (existing fallback and recovery tests still pass).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass (exit 0); `pnpm lint:extensions` and `pnpm format:check` pass.

Limitation: this environment has no real LINE account, so the delivery outcome is proven at the unit level through the channel's send functions rather than against a live LINE setup. A maintainer with a LINE account can observe the same behavior: trigger a pairing request while the reply HTTP request fails with a timeout/abort, then confirm no duplicate push is sent, that a later message from the same sender re-sends the pending code exactly once, and that the same sender under a different LINE account (or after the one-shot recovery is spent) is not re-sent that code.

Note: this change was authored with AI assistance; the root cause, fix design, and tests were reviewed against the existing `auto-reply-delivery` guard and its recovery tests.
