prs.title: fix(openai): drop transient reasoning replay state
prs.body:
Closes #113868

## What Problem This Solves

Native Codex Responses can emit temporary reasoning items whose IDs start with `rs_tmp_`. OpenClaw persisted those items in assistant `thinkingSignature` fields and replayed them on later turns even though the IDs are not durable replay state. A follow-up request could then fail with `invalid_encrypted_content`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This current-main rewrite places the rule at the two canonical owners:

- the stream writer keeps the human-readable reasoning summary but omits replay signature and provenance metadata for temporary native Codex reasoning;
- the consolidated replay converter drops matching signatures already present in older transcripts and clears adjacency state, so a later signed text item cannot inherit pairing from an earlier stable reasoning item.

The check is intentionally limited to the native Codex Responses backend. Stable `rs_*` items and temporary-shaped IDs from compatible proxy endpoints retain the existing behavior.

The old branch changed a duplicate provider conversion path that was later consolidated by #123762. This rewrite removes that obsolete surface instead of rebasing it.

## User Impact

Multi-turn native Codex Responses sessions no longer carry temporary encrypted reasoning state into later requests. Visible reasoning summaries and valid stable reasoning replay remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Exact head: `d54dd8160fa40ac3d090502891ebf5ef6ac170de`, based on current `upstream/main` `ed6e3aabf0`.

- Pre-fix owner regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts` failed in exactly two places: native `rs_tmp_*` state was persisted, and the same item was replayed after a stable reasoning item. Stable native reasoning and proxy behavior passed.
- Exact-head focused and sibling tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-transient-reasoning.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-stream-parity.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-prompt-role.test.ts src/agents/openai-responses.reasoning-replay.test.ts` -> 43/43 passed.
- Both consolidated replay facades are covered by the stable -> temporary -> signed-text ordering regression. The temporary item is absent and the text ID is not replayed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware ...` -> passed for all three changed files.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` -> passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-import-cycles.ts` -> 0 runtime value cycles.
- Scope: two production files, +25/-5 (net +20), plus one focused 161-line test file. The previous implementation was four files with production net +39 and edited an owner removed by #123762.

Direct dependency-contract check:

- OpenAI Codex source at `90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d` models reasoning as a first-class Responses item carrying an optional provider item ID and encrypted content: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L950-L999
- Server item IDs are deliberately read as opaque/permissive values: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/protocol/src/response_item_id.rs#L17-L34
- Codex forwards reasoning items as model request input rather than normalizing their provider lifetime: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/90854393966b21e9ebfd21b122334eb09a20c93d/codex-rs/core/src/client_common.rs#L53-L90
- The OpenAI Responses contract documents encrypted reasoning as state to replay for stateless multi-turn use, which is why excluding only observed temporary native items must happen before persistence/replay: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create

Known proof gap: this machine does not yet have a redacted exact-head two-turn native provider trace showing a real `rs_tmp_*` response followed by a request that omits it. No live-provider claim is made. No additional AutoReview was run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep normalized chat text stable across replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prompt-prefix reuse broke whenever a chat message ended in whitespace. Chat intake in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-request.ts` kept two versions of the user text. The first provider request sent the raw text, while the persisted transcript and every later replay used the cleaned, trimmed form. The first user item's bytes therefore differed between the first inference and all later turns, which invalidates the provider's prompt cache from that point on.

The split came in with `a9e51732dbd2192bd68882836f410b0143d33dc8`, which switched persisted text to the cleaned form without updating the first-inference path. Reproduced on a remote Gateway with a stub provider: the request bytes diverged at byte 32,045 between turn 1 and turn 2.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inference now uses the same normalized text intake already persists. There is one canonical user text instead of two diverging copies. Production +1/−1.

## User Impact

Conversations whose first message ends in whitespace or a newline keep a byte-stable prompt prefix, so prompt caching works from turn 2 onward. That means lower latency and cost on cached providers. The text the model sees is the same text the transcript records.

## Evidence

- The regression fails on main and passes with the fix. All 43 intake tests pass.
- On a remote Gateway, the original user item stayed byte-identical across eight turns.
- Native `pnpm test:changed` passed, along with all 28 test-type graphs, targeted lint, and 90 related tests. Changed-test wall time with `--maxWorkers=1` was 34.3 s.
- Compaction and transcript flows passed with no persisted-history loss: large tool results; compaction refused while a tool runs; HTTP-error and empty-summary compaction failures, which keep history visibly with a usable continuation; bounded manual summaries; Gateway stop/start; forks; subagent inheritance; and threshold-triggered summarization.
- `check-changed` is red only on dead exports in untouched files, which reproduce on unchanged main `1041e556285`.

Report only, not changed here: custom Responses routes still drop prior transient runtime-context messages without compaction. Every turn then differs at that carrier, where byte 26,493 changes from `"role":"user"` runtime context to the assistant answer, so those routes still miss the cache. The mechanism traces to `6dae3c273de` and `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts:157`. Changing it is a provider replay-policy decision; see open PR #167798.

prs.title: fix(models): make refreshed models work in local agent turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a model listed by `models list --refresh` failing its first `agent --local` turn with `Unknown model` when the provider is authenticated but has no configured model.

## User Impact

After signing in and refreshing the local catalog, users can run newly listed models without adding hand-written provider/model configuration. Gateway-backed listing remains Gateway-backed. Without a prior refresh, an unknown model still tells the user to run `models list --refresh --provider <id>`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two disconnected paths caused the failure: the catalog worker deliberately plans discovery without persisting it, and static runtime preparation omitted persisted catalogs for credential-only providers. Keep the worker read-only, as introduced by 1cb9f70 (catalog discovery isolation). For an offline CLI refresh, hold exclusive local-state custody and use the existing live standalone catalog preparation, which writes the existing per-agent SQLite catalog cache. Project those same admitted facts rather than starting a second refresh. Keep managed-proxy setup and cleanup around discovery.

Static runtime preparation now includes catalog owners for current credentials, using the existing registry reader and resolver. Removed credentials do not admit credential-only cached models. No schema, configuration, or additional storage format changes.

Explicit offline refresh carries the existing 180-second discovery budget through standalone preparation; ordinary preparation retains its 5-second default. The enclosing generation allows that discovery budget in addition to normal preparation time.

Maintainer-intent check: no matching changes in the touched files.

## Evidence

- Fresh main `aec6e7a56eb`: isolated profile, `paste-api-key` exit 0; refresh listed `opencode-go/deepseek-flash` and exited 0; local turn exited 1 with `Unknown model`.
- Regression failed on the original code: a persisted-only model resolved to `undefined`. The candidate passes both current-credential and removed-credential cases.
- 53 focused tests pass across catalog sources, catalog ownership, and CLI listing, including Gateway routing and proxy cleanup. The acquisition-boundary regression holds a provider for 125.1 seconds of virtual time, verifies exactly one discovery, and checks the resulting SQLite row. Before the budget fix, the provider timed out and the list was empty.
- Core and test typechecks, changed-file lint, and whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh candidate profile: before refresh, the error points to `models list --refresh`; after refresh, the existing SQLite cache contains `opencode-go/deepseek-flash`, and a separate `agent --local --model opencode-go/deepseek-flash` process received HTTP 200 and a visible reply with exit 0, without fallback.

Both then logged `auth usage committed but runtime snapshot publication failed error="Auth profile read owner was revoked"`. This warning also occurs on main independently of the new offline-refresh path.
- Other live-listed providers share this catalog/registry path; only OpenCode Go received a live-provider turn in this proof.

prs.title: refactor: migrate Reef trust and state to workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reef trust, registration, audit and replay flows depend on synchronous keyed-state callbacks.

## User Impact

Reef persists ordinary state through worker-owned operations while preserving conditional trust decisions and recovery behavior.

The final native peer-authority lookup remains immediately before delivery effects. Missing keys retain their existing ENOENT contract. This does not change persistent schema, durability or retention policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Migrates Reef state and trust to observe/compare-and-apply operations and propagates async completion through friendship, flow, notices and channel adapters. Cross-row observations prevent delivery or rejection-notice writes after peer revocation, and action authority is rechecked at worker admission.

This is part 9 of the nine-part S7 state/binding migration stack, now targeting main after [parent PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168485) merged. The original measurements below compare this part with stack parent `bbcd292f840e` on pinned main `413d5f9bb3f7`; final landing evidence is recorded separately below.

## Evidence

Changed lines against the parent: production **+668 / -548**; tests and fixtures **+829 / -626**.

Focused integrated receipts cover Reef trust revocation/concurrency, state, replay, friendships, and channel flows: **196 passed, 0 skipped**, mapped to 12/12 changed test files. These are recorded integrated file versions, not independent runs of every prefix; per-part counts are not additive. Stack totals are **3,296 passing receipts, 3,295 after removing one known relocation duplicate, and three skipped cases across 177 files; no required focused file remains missing**.

Recorded file spans total 49.539s. The relevant repaired integration batch took 496.047s wall time for 22 files; that is not a standalone timing for this part. File spans and invocation wall times are distinct; **CI runner seconds were not measured**.

Owner-reviewed native SDK digest: `ff7b090f43d2d90e4cd883d95840d6b752475a7a1769e295fb4cbb558a6ffb64`. **Zero released export removals**; the digest reconciles to this parent/head through the generated-only baseline change. The canonical SDK diff is empty.

The S7 family audit at c3667d2 resolved 18,862 inputs, 1,766 calls, 521 imports and 78 member references: 153 explicitly classified retained edges, zero unknown edges or async-contract errors. The publisher repair changed five scanned modules containing none of those captured family edges; retained-edge sources stayed unchanged. Final source differs from the passing repair head only by its generated assertion baseline. This preserves the original scan provenance rather than claiming a new full scan.

Core and extension production typechecks passed for all nine source prefixes; the final generated-only assertion-baseline adjustment does not change their code. The selected check-changed commands were executed, with the inherited failures below preserved.

Inherited failures remain explicit: Knip flags `.github/actions/setup-release-harness/narrow-lockfile.mjs` and `src/infra/sqlite-source-fence-admission.ts`; the production export scan flags `PUBLIC_SESSION_ENTRY_SCRIPT`; core lint has 10 unchanged max-lines findings; the environment-name count is **456/455**, including unchanged `OPENCLAW_PITCH`. Relevant source/config blobs equal the pinned base. No blanket check-changed-green claim is made.

Three scoped review rounds completed. Accepted correctness findings were repaired; remaining scoped follow-ups are recorded in the relevant PR descriptions.

Final repair checks passed at `4b7d96b620ea`: scoped lint (30.02 s), affected test types (342.12 s), import-cycle guard (23.46 s), and Madge (14.91 s).

Exact-final remote pnpm build passed in 369.642s. The qualified Matrix cold-import snapshot measured 104.992 MiB peak RSS, +58.199 MiB versus the empty baseline, and 383.791ms process CPU. Child/process-group cleanup and temporary-home removal were verified. This is a cold-import snapshot; the dependency closure is not attested. Statement-gate evidence follows separately; final landing update proof is recorded below.

<details>
<summary>Statement gate: original pairs, required whole-workload check and bounded startup diagnostic</summary>

The primary series contains three alternating parent/head pairs on the same host; all phase durations are valid. The warmed median rises **1006.8→1021.5 (+1.46%)**, so unchanged-owner attribution alone was not accepted. The table reports those primary medians and preserves the later ordinary fourth pair and cumulative results.

prs.title: fix(agents): restore context when switching back to Claude CLI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude recalling stale conversation details when an existing chat switches to another model and then returns to the same native Claude CLI session.

## User Impact

Returning Claude receives a metadata-only notice identifying the missed messages and how to read the current chat through `mcp__openclaw__sessions_history`. No missed turn contents are injected. Fresh sessions, reseeds, and authentication-profile or epoch changes do not receive this resume notice. Tool-policy restrictions omit the tool hint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prefix the native user prompt for the first return turn with the missed-message count, time range, models, and exact session key. Keep this notice out of the private UserPromptSubmit context path. Use existing transcript entries and admitted native reuse rather than introducing stored state.

Preserve the original user text in OpenClaw history: the native-history merge correlates the prefixed input with its canonical local turn, rather than displaying an extra prefixed user message. Unmatched imports remain intact.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. The authentication boundary from #140294 remains intact; metadata does not authorize transcript replay.

## Evidence

- Real Claude CLI, exact head `6cc99a4d0e89c957132567590fe90537c6689e1f`: **warm 1/1 and cold 1/1** called `mcp__openclaw__sessions_history`, received the other-model turn containing the new token, and answered that token (`BRAVO1852` / `BRAVO2852`). Cold proof restarted the isolated Gateway before returning to Claude. The intervening model was a local mock; Claude itself was real.
- One no-switch control had no notice. Both subsequent turns had no repeated notice. Native stream-json input/output captured the prompt bytes, tool calls, tool results, and answers.
- Both final chat histories contained exactly one original return-user row and no prefixed or duplicate user row.
- [Captured native inputs, tool calls/results, answers, and final user rows](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168726#issuecomment-6103291554) for the final-head warm and cold scenarios.
- Earlier head `3fc3bad1a66689912b4cab334bd4a303c029f4bc`: warm **2/2**, cold **2/2** read history and answered the new token. That campaign exposed the duplicate native-import row fixed in the final head; it is not evidence for final-head history correctness.
- Regression failed on `3fc3bad` for both plain and drift-prefixed native inputs, then the complete `cli-session-history.test.ts` passed **37 tests** (149.15 seconds wall time). Existing focused session-history, preparation, and prompt-context coverage passed **61 tests**, including fresh-session, auth boundary, hidden-tool hint, and once-per-gap cases.
- Current head `b55b8ac18302e8383016e2dba35fa525e1bbb524` merges main, preserving #163521 routed-prompt normalization. Switch-back note stripping now lives alongside drift-note stripping in the shared compare-only prompt normalization owner; unmatched imports and literal user text remain unchanged. No further native prompt cycles were run.
- Post-merge focused proof in secretless Node 24 Docker: all seven requested suites passed, **113 tests**, **398.48 seconds**. Removing only switch-back stripping made both import regression variants fail with duplicate prefixed user rows (**2 failures**, 7.48 seconds).
- CI remains blocked by an inherited SDK surface-budget failure: [this PR's exact-head failing shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38097126039/job/114345400720) and [an independent PR's identical three test failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38095788806/job/114341487193). Both report exports 3672 > 3656, callable exports 2133 > 2122, and deprecated exports 158 > 154. The CI gate then failed because of that shard and 27 fail-fast cancellations. This change does not modify the SDK surface or budget.
- Build passed. Claude user settings and CLAUDE.md hashes/mtimes were unchanged; isolated Gateways stopped and created Claude project directories were removed.

- Review repair `54dbf3c03ce1d4dc3df280366221e2d2516d8621`: native-history provenance extraction now uses the shared decoration-stripped view before reading the inter-session envelope, without changing stored content. Unmatched routed string/text-block imports retain their source provenance even with a switch-back note. Both new regression variants failed on `b55b8ac18302e8383016e2dba35fa525e1bbb524` (missing provenance) and passed after the fix. All seven requested focused suites passed **115 tests in 345.93 seconds** in secretless Node 24 Docker; formatting check passed. No new real Claude runs.

Small samples demonstrate the exercised paths, not a guaranteed model compliance rate.

Merge danger: **two-way door**; reverting removes the notice and import correlation without a schema migration or configuration change. Blast radius is resumed Claude CLI chats with intervening other-model turns, plus native-history matching of that notice.


Final test-only correction `6f9a0eb722c88dc77eff4ffb71c1d31d018c27fa` replaces direct property access on unknown imported rows with a structural assertion. The routed suite passed 14/14 (17.44 seconds), and the owning Gateway test TypeScript project passed. This fixes the prior head's CI type error; production code is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a paired node that never ends a directory listing keeps the gateway paging until the process stops.

## User Impact

User impact: a workspace directory read from a node stops with an error after 32 pages instead of growing the gateway heap for as long as the process runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

readDirectory already rejects a page that does not advance, and each dir.list call has a 60 second timeout. Nothing bounded how many pages one directory could request. The cap is per directory, so a tree walk still lists each child directory separately. 32 pages is 131072 names. The service lifetime signal already aborts each call. This change does not add a new signal to the bootstrap walk.

## Evidence

Same production function, before the patch and after it. Each dir.list answer stays truncated, with a strictly larger page token.

Before, current main, still inside the loop after 400ms:

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-f087.mjs /Users/sebastientardif/openclaw
{"outcome":"still-running","pages":424200,"ms":401}
```

After, patched worktree:

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-f087.mjs /tmp/oc-f087
{"outcome":"threw:Directory listing exceeded 32 pages","pages":32,"ms":1}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Node workspace directory reads can page forever when the node keeps returning a truncated dir.list page.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2, Node v26.10.0, worktree /tmp/oc-f087 at 7444227ae12.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From the patched worktree, run node --import tsx /tmp/proof-f087.mjs /tmp/oc-f087. The script imports createNodeWorkspaceBridge from extensions/file-transfer/src/workspace-bridge.ts and calls readDirectory. Each dir.list answer is truncated, with nextPageToken set to the page count times 4096. The same command against the unpatched checkout shows the loop still running.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the production bridge:

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-f087.mjs /tmp/oc-f087
{"outcome":"threw:Directory listing exceeded 32 pages","pages":32,"ms":1}
```

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-f087.mjs /Users/sebastientardif/openclaw
{"outcome":"still-running","pages":424200,"ms":401}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The patched bridge throws Directory listing exceeded 32 pages after exactly 32 dir.list calls, in 1ms. The unpatched bridge was still inside the loop after 424200 calls.
- **What was not tested:** A live enrolled node and gateway process. The page loop lives in the bridge, and the node payload is the input that drives it. A single directory with more than 131072 entries was not listed.

## Summary

A two-page workspace listing still returns every name. A continuation that does not advance still fails as Invalid dir.list continuation.

prs.title: fix: restore channel startup after stopped Tailscale failures
prs.body:
## Problem

Repeated managed-ingress startup failures while Tailscale is stopped can trip the channel restart-loop breaker before channels start. Restoring Tailscale then leaves channel startup suppressed.

## Solution and scope

- Classify the exact JSON `BackendState: Stopped` as a typed prerequisite error. Successful startup cleanup preserves that classification in the completion record; message-only errors and cleanup-wrapped failures do not qualify.
- The shared worker-backed lifecycle kernel excludes only completed, explicitly classified stopped-daemon failures from the unclean count and latest-unclean timestamp. Unfinished boots, unknown failures, and failed cleanup retain protection; admission and recovery-writer rechecks use the same owner.
- No schema, retention, or stored-history changes. Ingress still fails closed; OpenClaw does not start Tailscale or disable ingress. Historical untyped failures count until the existing window expires. Status interpretation follows the [pinned Tailscale contract](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/blob/9128778b6515f32e13d92e7380044fe025f9b08e/cmd/tailscale/cli/status.go#L81).

The installed-upgrade harness and redundant stopped-daemon helper test remain removed. The claim-boundary regression retains typed rejection, no-route-created, and reconnect-success assertions. The lifecycle, run-loop, and Tailscale implementation is unchanged from runtime-proof parent `8dcb0f2304be10bb1b663a53c4888677240c4e90`. Superseded UI, model-mock, and ledger corrections are absent from the final diff.

Against integrated main `4754d394130ae9106c863e97c31392fba6bd614f`: **10 files, +303/-17**. No replacement harness or new runtime feature is added.

## CI repairs

- **Source-scan preflight:** [CI at 8dcb0f2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38083481260) aborted on Node 24.21.0 with SIGTRAP and `Check failed: jit_page.has_value()`. The source-facts owner retries once without workers only for that exact pair and without a launch error. Normal parallel scanning is unchanged. Parser errors, unrelated faults, cancellation, and incomplete recovery remain fatal. The native cause was not reproduced locally; see [Node issue 66366](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/66366).
- **Inherited failures at 2eade213:** [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38095749515) settled with 48 successful, 5 failed, and 24 skipped jobs. Four failed leaves were the SDK tests, source-contract collision check, and two lint stripes; the fifth was the aggregate gate. Pristine main reproduces all three lint diagnostics and the SDK budget drift. Main's DM-resolver rename (`13296b17cd0f`) is incorporated unchanged, preserving the public SDK helper. The previously repaired unused environment declaration is also now in main.
- **Canonical lint/SDK repairs:** Main landed the same corrections in `f9940dc8` and clarified their migration attribution in `7562fd2b` during local validation. The overlapping three-file conflict is resolved using main’s exact blobs. These cache, worker-test, and SDK-accounting files are now absent from the PR diff; no duplicate local policy remains.
- **SDK accounting:** Canonical source reports at the last budget commit `e40606fd`, approved async-approval commit `4128f113` (#168482), and approved V2-binding commit `eacb8374` (#168483) establish exact totals:

  | Graph | Public exports | Callable exports | Deprecated exports |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Last recorded budget | 3,656 | 2,122 | 154 |
  | Approved async command/approval APIs | 3,668 | 2,130 | 154 |
  | Approved V2 conversation APIs and current main | 3,672 | 2,133 | 158 |

  Main now records those exact authored limits and the four documented legacy deprecations (inspection: 1, conversation runtime: 3). No extra headroom, public API addition/removal, environment override, wildcard allowance, or shipped-name-removal waiver is introduced. The guard's negative assertions are unchanged.

No hosted rerun, manual workflow dispatch, unchanged repush, or timeout increase was requested.

## Validation

Current signed head: **86f59f9d2df5d5a18cc98279bdbc00cc671f1d9f**.

| Resolved-candidate check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical main core/script lint repairs | Pass; 14.79s / 14.03s |

Local results apply to the resolved tree, not GitHub’s future merge-commit run. No test or assertion was changed during integration.

Retained, revision-bound proof:

Four cache/worker/SDK regression files pass **36 cases**, with **1 Linux-only skipped** (109.22s including 30.04s worker preparation). prs.title: fix(gateway): recheck MCP App approval before the tool runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An MCP App tool call can still run after the operator tightens approval. `approveTool` in the same runtime snapshots whether approval is required and returns a guard that throws if approval becomes required before the tool RPC. `prepareToolCall` asked for approval when it was required, then returned nothing. `executeMcpAppOperation` therefore had no guard to run before `callMcpAppToolWithElicitation`. A Codex approval-mode or annotation change during that in-flight call was not rejected. The App cannot change the policy itself. This stops the one call that already passed the old check.

## Evidence

Production modules, not the Vitest mock of `requiresMcpCodexToolApproval`. The script imports `prepareMcpAppExtensionRuntime`, `loadSessionMcpConfig`, `resolveProjectedMcpCodexToolApprovalMode`, and `requiresMcpCodexToolApproval` from the worktree. Config is `mcp.servers.demo.codex.defaultToolsApprovalMode: "auto"`. The catalog tool starts as `readOnlyHint: true`, then the same object becomes `destructiveHint: true` after preparation. An in-process harness returns that catalog and does not spawn `demo-proof`. State dir is `/tmp/oc-f088-proof-state`.

Before, parent file `918153ea335` for `src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts` only. The file was restored afterward and `git diff` was empty.

```console
$ PROOF_LABEL=before-fix pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-f088-proof-run.ts
label: before-fix
root: /tmp/oc-f088
loadedServers: demo
serverCodex: {"defaultToolsApprovalMode":"auto"}
resolvedMode: auto
predicateReadOnly: false
predicateDestructive: true
prepareReturnType: undefined
annotationsNow: {"destructiveHint":true}
predicateAfterFlip: true
guardThrew: none
executionGuardReturned: false
leaseReleased: true
```

After, commit `cf2241e1450`:

```console
$ PROOF_LABEL=after-fix pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-f088-proof-run.ts
label: after-fix
root: /tmp/oc-f088
loadedServers: demo
serverCodex: {"defaultToolsApprovalMode":"auto"}
resolvedMode: auto
predicateReadOnly: false
predicateDestructive: true
prepareReturnType: function
annotationsNow: {"destructiveHint":true}
predicateAfterFlip: true
guardThrew: MCP App approval policy changed before execution
leaseReleased: true
```

Supplemental Vitest, which mocks the predicate, still passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.test.ts` reported 21 passed. That run is not the proof above.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** An in-flight MCP App `prepareToolCall` now returns a guard. The guard throws if the real Codex approval predicate becomes required before execution.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Node v26.10.0, OpenClaw commit cf2241e1450, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-f088-proof-state`. Invoked with `pnpm exec tsx` against production modules. No gateway process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From `/tmp/oc-f088`, `PROOF_LABEL=after-fix PROOF_ROOT=/tmp/oc-f088 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-f088-proof-state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-f088-proof-state/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 pnpm exec tsx /tmp/oc-f088-proof-run.ts`. The before run swapped in parent `918153ea335` of `src/gateway/mcp-app-extension-runtime.ts`, ran the same command with `PROOF_LABEL=before-fix`, then restored the file.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.

```console
label: after-fix
loadedServers: demo
serverCodex: {"defaultToolsApprovalMode":"auto"}
resolvedMode: auto
predicateReadOnly: false
predicateDestructive: true
prepareReturnType: function
annotationsNow: {"destructiveHint":true}
predicateAfterFlip: true
guardThrew: MCP App approval policy changed before execution
leaseReleased: true
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `loadSessionMcpConfig` kept `defaultToolsApprovalMode: "auto"`. The real predicate is false for `readOnlyHint` and true for `destructiveHint`. Preparation does not open the approval dialog. On the parent file, `prepareToolCall` returns undefined while the predicate is already true, so the call would continue. On cf2241e1450 the returned function throws `MCP App approval policy changed before execution`.
- **What was not tested:** A Control UI session, a running gateway, and a live MCP server process. The harness was registered in-process and returned the catalog. If preparation had requested approval, the production `requestMcpAppToolApproval` would have thrown `MCP App approval service is unavailable`, because no approval manager was installed.

## Summary

`approveTool` already had this recheck. `prepareToolCall` now captures the same `required` flag, still requests approval only when that flag is set, and returns the guard that `executeMcpAppOperation` already invokes before the tool RPC.

prs.title: fix: generate task-focused titles for channel sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel-mirrored sessions can currently derive titles from transport addressing instead of the user's task. Slack records resolved mentions in forms such as `<@U123> (ohmybot)`, causing titles like `(ohmybot) This is my cookies...`. These titles are noisy, expose irrelevant wrapper text, and make the session sidebar difficult to scan.

The existing sidebar already provides persistent one-level custom groups, but collapsed custom groups hide whether contained sessions are running or unread. This weakens their usefulness as folder-like organization.

## Summary

- sanitize channel-originated title input before both model-generated and deterministic fallback titles
- strip leading Slack/Discord bot mentions, display-name wrappers such as `(ohmybot)`, and broadcast addressing while preserving the original transcript
- strengthen the title prompt so it names the task/topic and never copies credentials, cookies, or tokens
- keep current one-level custom session groups intact and improve collapsed group headers with true counts, running state, attention, and unread indicators
- document channel-title sanitization and the current one-level group model

## Evidence

Regression input:

```text
<@U0BNFBKJB7B> (ohmybot) This is my cookies for Nature so you can open the paper and review the figures for me
```

The title source passed to the model is now:

```text
This is my cookies for Nature so you can open the paper and review the figures for me
```

The generated-title regression expects a task-focused result such as `Nature paper access for review`; the deterministic fallback excludes both `(ohmybot)` and the raw mention token. A mention-only message produces no title.

Local validation on Node 24:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/session-title-source.test.ts src/gateway/dashboard-session-title.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **77 passed**
- `pnpm exec vitest run ui/src/components/app-sidebar.interactions.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **108 passed**

The sidebar test verifies that a collapsed custom group keeps the correct count and surfaces hidden running/unread state.

## Scope note

True nested folders are intentionally not included. Session `category` and the group RPC/storage contract are flat today; introducing hierarchy requires a separate schema/API/migration/authorization/drag-and-drop design. This PR preserves backward compatibility and makes the existing one-level folder-like groups clearer and more informative.

prs.title: fix: release worker capacity after forced descendant cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #160643

## What Problem This Solves

Force-stopping a node worker could leave an in-group descendant holding the lineage pipe open indefinitely. The worker anchor then waited for EOF before reaching its group kill, so cleanup failed and its capacity slot stayed reserved.

## User Impact

Forced worker cleanup now terminates surviving processes in its owned process group while preserving the anchor that records lineage completion. This repairs the macOS and retained process-group path; Linux native subreaper ownership remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing process-group owner enumerates and kills remaining in-group members before the anchor waits for lineage. Normal completion with observed EOF does not run a census. Separately grouped command relays retain their own cleanup authority; escaped or late-fork survivors still retain capacity until extinction is verified.

Production LOC: **+22** across two files; three changed files total. The bug-fix exception is needed for a selective kill that preserves the lineage observer, using the existing process census rather than new lifecycle state. No public config/protocol/schema change. Thanks @aniruddhaadak80 for the report.

## Evidence

- Real owned-worker regression failed on the original code in 5.94 seconds: cleanup exceeded its 5.002-second hard deadline with lineage EOF, closing receipt, anchor exit, and extinction still pending.
- Fixed code: all 6 owned-worker cases and 30 process-group tests passed; the new force-descendant case completed in 0.77 seconds. `pnpm test src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.owned-worker.test.ts src/process/supervisor/service-child-group-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 29.76 seconds wall time (owning file: 8.25 seconds Vitest duration, about 4.7 seconds test execution).
- Supervisor boundary: `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-supervisor.lifetime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "reclaims a killed worker"`: passed, 11.96 seconds wall time. It verifies descendant reclamation, slot release, and peer isolation.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 52adcc9ca6ad1202413fb7c6e8247bebc46170e3`: formatting, ratchets, dependency checks, and graph-boundary checks passed; core typecheck stopped at inherited TS6133 in unchanged `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts:519` (`env` is unused). The same unused declaration is present in the audited base; no changes in this PR affect that module. Main has since removed it in 243b6dbf63d2; this is a named inherited baseline failure, not a worker regression.
- Initial PR CI failed in unchanged `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` because the SDK surface budgets predated new async conversation APIs. Main repairs this in f9940dc8a794; that repair is integrated by a conflict-free merge of current main; the three worker-change files are byte-identical to the reviewed and tested candidate. No worker test failed in CI.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean at P0/P1; no actionable findings.
- Remote proof: Blacksmith Testbox run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096364933 (CLI proof exit records above; the lease workflow itself may show cancellation on cleanup).
- Testbox on Linux explicitly exercises the retained process-group contract; this is not native macOS runtime proof.

Landing: native review initialization waited over ten minutes on shared managed-worktree allocation. After stopping that operation and recovering its exact lock, the maintainer-authorized head-pinned REST squash fallback was selected with required CI green; no check waiver.

prs.title: fix: match machine join commands to the Gateway release
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes machine enrollment silently running an old cached npm release when the Gateway is newer.

## User Impact

`devices join-code` and the Control UI now suggest the Gateway's published npm version, not the invoking CLI's version. Both also show the short alternative for an existing OpenClaw installation. The default remains a background service with explicit session-host consent; command-only services remain available.

Source checkouts and unpublished builds prefer a resolvable matching channel tag. If npm cannot confirm a target, the command stays unpinned and a one-line note asks for a matching Gateway build. JSON keeps `joinUrl` and `command`, adding `serviceCommand`, `installedCommand`, and optional `versionNote`.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#168623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168623) / `8f91e4bb65f` established the one-paste service/session-host default but deliberately left npm unpinned. npm can reuse an old cached package. The Gateway now owns version selection and command formatting in the same RPC that mints the URL; CLI and UI consume its commands instead of independently rebuilding them.

The existing update owners supply install identity and channel policy. Joining does not run a full update/dependency inspection. This composes with the durable service installation work in [#168644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168644); it does not change node execution, service lifecycle, or upgrade commands.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- Regressions on `8f91e4bb65f`: eight Gateway/CLI-boundary cases and three CLI text/JSON cases fail for missing authoritative commands; the real browser regression reaches the setup RPC and fails waiting for the pinned command.
- Focused Gateway and CLI suites: 84 tests passed after the final lightweight-install-discovery refinement. The Gateway suite took 173.85s and CLI suite 43.42s on the loaded local host (including transform/setup); assertions took about 1.7s and 15.5s respectively.
- All five browser flows passed. After the final template simplification, the real bundled UI mint/refresh flow passed again (46.41s, including setup), covering the pinned command, installed alternative, and development fallback note. The Control UI Lit ratchet also passed.
- Real isolated Gateway text/JSON: baseline printed unpinned npm commands; candidate printed `openclaw@2026.9.9`, matching the Gateway release, plus the existing-installation alternative. Both exited successfully. This proof exercises command generation, not installation on a second machine; durable service installation is covered separately by #168644.
- The built CLI bootstrap guard passed. The local changed gate stopped at an unrelated existing mock-export violation in `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection-placement.test.ts`; the rebase picked up its existing `mock-isolation` explanation. Hosted exact-head CI is the final check.
- Inherited CI failure: [the final-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096158809/job/114342554800) failed `plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` on SDK export-budget drift: 3672 > 3656 exports, 2133 > 2122 callables, 158 > 154 deprecated exports, and two deprecated-entrypoint budgets. Clean `origin/main` at `dd4b258a3cfa6fdef41535e5518fe260f5665a9c` reproduces the same budget failures (2 failed, 3 passed, 1 Linux-only test skipped on macOS; 18.84s). The aggregate CI gate reports this failure; fail-fast cancelled the other unfinished lanes. This PR changes no plugin SDK surface or budget.

Production: +105/-17 lines; tests: +188/-27; documentation: +23/-2. The added production logic replaces independent CLI/UI formatting with one Gateway decision owner.

<details>
<summary>Real isolated Gateway terminal output (redacted)</summary>

Gateway: `OpenClaw 2026.9.9`. Both text and JSON commands exited 0. Only the ephemeral loopback port and single-use code are redacted.

Before (`devices join-code`):

```text
npx -y openclaw connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service --session-host
```

After (`devices join-code`):

```text
npx -y openclaw@2026.9.9 connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service --session-host
Already have OpenClaw installed? Run: openclaw connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service --session-host
```

After (`devices join-code --json`):

```json
{
  "joinUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code>",
  "command": "npx -y openclaw@2026.9.9 connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service --session-host",
  "serviceCommand": "npx -y openclaw@2026.9.9 connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service",
  "installedCommand": "openclaw connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/j/<code> --service --session-host"
}
```

</details>

### Connect a machine

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: unpinned npm join command](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9af80a8-039d-4b95-8102-1dd943a89672) | ![After: Gateway-selected npm version and installed alternative](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b627f4b-5bf8-49a9-ae0b-3e222aa9652f) |

The screenshots use synthetic Gateway data and the actual bundled Control UI.

## Bounded cost

Only explicit join-code creation performs registry work: at most two npm metadata GETs, each with a one-second deadline including the response body. No background polling, model calls, package-manager subprocesses, retries, or new caches. Existing prepared install identity is reused; if absent, the update owner's lightweight local classifier runs without dependency inspection, with its Git probe bounded to one second. No registry lookup is performed by CLI or UI.

## Compatibility and Risk

The RPC fields are additive. A new CLI needs a Gateway that returns the authoritative commands and explains how to update if it connects to an older Gateway. Published npm releases use exact versions; development/unpublished/offline results are explicitly marked as requiring a matching build. Shell quoting remains owned by the existing CLI argument helper.

Two-way door: reverting changes future suggestions and added response fields only. It does not change existing pairings, service state, or session-host consent. The blast radius is enrollment instructions and their presentation.

prs.title: fix(agents): store hook prompt context in the append-only runtime carrier
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #166271. On models that use append-only runtime context (`bindsClaudeThinkingPrefix`: Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1), `prependContext`/`appendContext` returned by a `before_prompt_build` hook was folded into the active user prompt for one run only and never stored. The next run replayed the earlier user message without the injected block, so the request was no longer an append-only extension of the previous one:

- every cache entry written during the run sat after that rewritten message, so none of them could be read again — a plugin injecting on every message (memory recall is the common case) restarted the prompt cache on every turn;
- every replayed thinking block after that message was dropped (`replayed thinking dropped ... prefix_binding_mismatch`, `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`).

OpenClaw's own per-turn context does not have this problem: it rides the runtime-context carrier, is stored hidden with the turn, and replays byte-identically. Hook context went down the older one-run rewrite path instead.

## The Fix

`prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptAssembly` gains `appendOnlyRuntimeContext`. When it is true and the prompt is non-empty, the joined hook `prependContext`/`appendContext` is no longer folded into `effectivePrompt`; `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` instead adds it as a `conversation-data` runtime-context fragment, so it is stored hidden with the turn and replayed unchanged — the same treatment OpenClaw's own facts get, so plugin text is not raised to instruction level.

One routing decision, published once: review round 2 caught that the routing predicate was re-derived independently at each consumer and keyed on different fields — carrier construction keyed on the transcript prompt, submission on the assembled prompt. A runtime-only turn (non-empty prompt, empty `transcriptPrompt`) therefore failed both: assembly skipped the fold, carrier construction excluded the hook text, and submission suppressed `prependContext`/`appendContext`, so the model never received it. Assembly now publishes `routePromptBuildContextThroughRuntimeCarrier` in its result, and carrier construction, submission, and the compaction budget all consume that single decision; the runtime-only submission path delivers the stored carrier to the model.

Redaction (review round 7, P1): the carrier bypasses the canonical prompt-projection redaction on both consumption paths — the provider dispatch and the durable custom-message append — so hook text that `logging.redactPatterns` would have removed from the recorded prompt previously reached both the model and the retained transcript unsanitized. Carrier construction now applies `redactTranscriptText` (same policy, same config object the canonical capture uses) to the joined hook context before it becomes a fragment, so dispatch and replay see identical sanitized bytes. The legacy fold path is untouched: it still passes through `capturePersistedModelPromptProjection`, which already sanitizes.

Kept on the legacy path:

- runs without the append-only contract (all other models): the one-run prompt rewrite, unchanged;
- context-only turns (blank prompt) on append-only models: the fold, so hook context alone still reaches the model;
- the transient per-run rewrite is also withheld from `submitEmbeddedAttemptPrompt` (`prependContext`/`appendContext`) and from `pendingAdditivePrompt` in the compaction request budget, since the carrier now carries those bytes and is counted through `pendingContextMessages` — no double injection, no double counting.

Trade-off inherited from the issue discussion: stored hook blocks accumulate in history until compaction or reset; the reporter's local patch of this shape estimated 500-850 tokens per injected block, and an explicit one-run opt-out on the hook result remains possible upstream work.

## Evidence

Reproduction and regression tests (all offline, no network):

- `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts` "prompt assembly hook prompt context": on `appendOnlyRuntimeContext: true` with a `before_prompt_build` hook returning `prependContext`, the assembly keeps `effectivePrompt` transcript-identical (`"Hello"`, no hook text) while still reporting `promptBuildPrependContext` for the carrier route; the legacy fold is pinned for append-only-off and for blank-prompt turns.
- `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`: the carrier carries `{ kind: "conversation-data", text: <hook context> }` (prepend and append joined in order), while `promptForSession`, `promptForModel`, and `llmBoundaryPromptForPrecheck` stay bare user bytes; with the append-only contract off, the carrier contains no hook text and the folded model prompt is preserved.
- Empty-transcript regression (review round 2 finding): `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` "routes hook prompt context through the carrier when the transcript prompt is empty" pins the runtime-only turn (`effectivePrompt: "Runtime ask"`, `effectiveTranscriptPrompt: ""`) delivering the hook text through the carrier — `promptSubmission.runtimeOnly` is true, `promptForModel` stays bare, and `runtimeContextMessageForCurrentTurn` carries the hook fragment; `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts` "publishes one carrier-routing decision for empty-transcript runtime turns" pins the published decision itself.
- Redaction regression (review round 7 P1): `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` "applies the transcript redaction policy to hook context stored in the carrier" — with `logging.redactPatterns: ["sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-[a-z0-9]+"]` and a hook returning a `prependContext` containing `sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-9f2`, the carrier fragment must not contain the raw secret and must equal `redactTranscriptText(hookPrepend, config)` byte-for-byte; `promptForModel` stays clean too.

Pre-fix red runs (tests only, fix reverted):

- Routing: empty-transcript regression fails — `promptSubmission.runtimeOnly` is `undefined` (no runtime context at all reaches the turn) and the hook fragment is absent from the carrier.
- Redaction: `expect(fragment?.text).not.toContain("sk-TEST-HOOK-SECRET-9f2")` fails — the raw secret is present in the carrier fragment, exactly the round-7 P1 path.

Post-fix:

- `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts`: 29/29 (28 pre-existing + 1 new redaction test)
- `attempt-prompt-build.decision.test.ts`, `attempt-prompt-submit.projections.test.ts`, `attempt-context-advancement.test.ts`, `interrupted-input-context.integration.test.ts`, `tool-result-truncation.test.ts`: all green on the same tree.

Branch state: based on `main` (`86b83b74b4c`), latest head `2c292a66e6c`: `9127c6220e5` (carrier fix) → `b83ee29f2c3` (oxfmt reformat) → `9fd3dc64b48` (routing-decision fix) → `8de9b32eea7`/`9ddeb41e672` (rounds 4-5) → merge of `main` → `7bdf4e4ae4d` (fixture) → `2c292a66e6c` (carrier redaction).

prs.title: fix(node): keep npx-installed services outside the npm cache
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes node services installed through `npx openclaw connect <join-url> --service` or `npx openclaw node install` pointing at npm's disposable `_npx` cache.

## User Impact

The one-paste command installs the selected OpenClaw release into a durable npm prefix under the node's state directory before writing the service. Removing npm's exec cache no longer removes the service's executable. Installation prints the package version, chosen runtime, service command, and a fresh-npx node update command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service argument resolver previously used the running package's resolved path. #167905 fixes pnpm's replaceable store-generation paths by selecting its existing stable link; npm exec has no stable link to select. This preserves that pnpm behavior and adds node-install promotion through the existing npm update owners (`resolveGlobalInstallTarget`, `runGlobalPackageUpdateSteps`, and their staged publication/rollback/cleanup).

There is one `<state-dir>/npm` prefix, not a prefix per release. The normal state-directory/profile resolver chooses its location. Run `npx -y openclaw@latest node install --force` on the node to update it, retaining the same profile/state-directory settings. An exact version or `@beta` can replace `@latest`. Reinstalling an already-selected version repairs damaged package files. No new settings or package manager.

This does not change `openclaw update` or its existing co-located Gateway selection behavior. Node auto-update still follows the node's npm channel, not the connected Gateway's version/build. The rebase preserves #168653's paired-credential filtering and explicit `--auth-from-env` service argument.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

Final code: `27b447dc07b737126124ff8847f2059cb8a4f921`. Packaged live proof ran on `292bd19fe934ecf4ee4e3b20b00a03a1b08f7933`; production feature code and docs are unchanged since that proof. The final revision only corrects regression-test platform handling and rebases onto green main.

- **Before:** the regression on baseline `e40606fdea96135758ec5bc0b1a355d08ead0c7e` selected `.npm/_npx/.../node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`. In the live isolated replay, published `openclaw@2026.9.9` completed real join-URL enrollment; deleting its npm exec cache made the saved command exit 1 with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- **After:** the canonical self-contained package passed `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build --allow-unreleased-changelog` and its tarball inventory/import-graph integrity check. Real `npm exec --package=<candidate.tgz> -- openclaw connect <join-url> --service` promoted that selected package into the node's state-owned npm prefix. Both actual launchd and systemd generators selected the durable entrypoint. After removing `_npx`, executing the persisted command as a separate process connected to the isolated Gateway. The published driver's device identity and node settings were unchanged.
- **Upgrade and repair:** seeded the durable prefix with published `openclaw@2026.9.8`, retained the enrolled node state, and invoked the candidate through fresh npx with `--profile upgrade node install --force`. The prefix became the candidate version. Overwriting its `dist/index.js` and repeating the same command restored the exact original file bytes. The runtime, device identity, and node settings remained unchanged; the repaired persisted command connected after deleting `_npx` again. The prefix contained only `bin` and `lib`, with one `openclaw` package rather than per-release directories.
- **Package identity:** the unpublished candidate shares the version string `2026.9.9` with the public release. An isolated loopback npm registry served the canonical candidate tarball for that version, while forwarding dependency requests to npm. This prevents accidentally testing promotion of the older public package with the same version string; no product behavior was mocked.
- **Focused checks:** 50 tests passed across `src/commands/node-daemon-install-npx.test.ts`, `src/commands/node-daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`, and `src/cli/node-cli/daemon.test.ts`. The new regression uses actual generators and executes their commands after cache deletion. The final portability correction keeps systemd coverage on non-Windows platforms and reads launchd artifacts only on macOS. That corrected regression passed (1.285 s test execution), and the `core-test-commands` type graph passed. Its unchanged durable-path assertion failed on the baseline as expected (pueue 2903).
- **Changed checks:** formatting, conflict/line-count/assertion/SQLite/mock-export ratchets, config docs, plugin boundaries, dependency guards, and the core type graph boundary passed. The prior head's local core typecheck stopped on unrelated `channel-presence-policy.ts:519` TS6133; the branch is now rebased onto the main fix rather than carrying a separate repair.
- **Independent review:** LAND on exact final head `27b447dc07b737126124ff8847f2059cb8a4f921`, including the corrected test, updater-step adapter, and paired-auth preservation.

Sanitized live results:

```text
before-cache-deleted: exit 1 (MODULE_NOT_FOUND)
after:  /state/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js
node host gateway connected: ws://127.0.0.1:<isolated-port>
upgrade: 2026.9.8 -> candidate 2026.9.9
sameVersionRepair: true
runtimePreserved: true
pairingAndSettingsPreserved: true
connectedAfterCacheDeletion: true
```

**Native-supervisor limitation:** supervisor activation was not verified. Native service installation reaches the existing systemd user-session/profile guards in the unprivileged container; macOS refuses native installation from an isolated HOME. The proof runs actual generated service arguments as a separate live node, not under an activated OS supervisor. Launchd XML was decoded in Linux and passed through the production generated-environment resolver; the macOS regression exercises the actual plist reader. No HOME-guard bypass, privileged container, existing Gateway, or real laptop installation was used.

**CI:** [final-head run 38097819645](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38097819645) passed, including production types, test types, lint, source contracts, and the corrected Linux regression. All applicable PR checks finished with no failure, cancellation, or pending check. The final head is rebased onto green main; no inherited failure waiver or SDK budget change is needed. ClawSweeper is **ready, 5/6**, and the independent reviewer returned **LAND**, both on `27b447dc07b737126124ff8847f2059cb8a4f921`.

## Bounded cost

Only npx-backed node installation needs an additional npm installation. It uses one state-owned prefix and the existing updater's staging, verification, rollback, and cleanup; it does not accumulate per-version prefixes. Reuse verifies the installed package and advertised content inventory, so a same-version damaged package is repaired. Ordinary node execution and model/session paths are unchanged. Non-npx installation adds only entrypoint inspection and installation diagnostics.

Source +104/-2, tests +88/-0, docs +34/-0; net +224 across seven files. The growth reuses the existing package updater rather than adding another installation or state owner.

## Merge Danger

Two-way code change, with a durable npm installation left in the selected node state directory if reverted. A revert restores the old npx service-install behavior; it does not remove an already installed package. Blast radius is headless node service installation and its printed diagnostics; Gateway installation and pnpm launcher resolution are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep updater-retired plugin aliases removed during record reconciliation
prs.body:
Closes #136025

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor restores a retired official plugin alias immediately after the updater successfully replaces it with the canonical plugin: `repairMissingConfiguredPluginInstalls` counts only `updated`/`unchanged` updater outcome IDs and restores every original missing record absent from that set, so the retired alias (e.g. `qqbot`) comes back alongside the canonical record (e.g. `openclaw-qqbot`), losing the updater's committed install-owner migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair now consumes the committed owner migrations attached to the updater result (`resolvePluginInstallOwnerMigrations`): an alias whose canonical target was repaired in the same run stays retired — its original record is not restored, it is excluded from install candidacy, and a change note records the retirement. Migrations are honored only when the canonical target was repaired in the same result, so a failed canonical update without migration metadata keeps the previous preserve-everything behavior (including no persistence write). Plain `skipped` outcomes are still neither success nor failure, per the issue.

Note: this issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`; opening anyway because the fix shape is marked clear (`fix-shape-clear`), the regression is reproduced with exact steps, no open PR or assignee exists, and the change is confined to the owning repair boundary.

## User Impact

After a successful canonical plugin update, Doctor no longer resurrects the retired alias record or attempts to reinstall it; operators see one canonical record plus an explicit retirement note.

## Evidence

- New `keeps a retired duplicate alias removed when the updater commits an owner migration` regression test following the issue's exact repro shape (mocked updater returning only the canonical 2.0.3 record, `updated` + diagnostic `skipped` outcomes, committed `{qqbot: "openclaw-qqbot"}` migration metadata, real temp package files).
- New `preserves original records when a canonical update fails without an owner migration` negative control asserting unchanged records and no persistence write.
- Both edited files pass an esbuild transform check; existing doctor tests that mock the updater without migration metadata are behaviorally unaffected (the resolver returns `undefined` → no-op). Local vitest lane cannot run in this Windows checkout (rolldown native binding failure at config load), so CI runs the full suite on the exact head SHA.

prs.title: fix(imessage): stop reflected replies from starting new turns
prs.body:
Closes #135704

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an outbound iMessage reflection could be treated as fresh user input when Messages assigned it a new row GUID but retained the original outbound GUID in `reply_to_guid`. In affected self-chats this could start a second agent turn and create a reply loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Echo detection now accepts the reply-parent GUID only when it is bound to the same normalized text in the same conversation scope. The in-memory cache stores that ID/text association directly, matching the persisted-cache behavior while preserving the existing conflicting-ID guard. A different reply body or the same text in another conversation still dispatches normally.

## User Impact

Affected iMessage users no longer have reflected assistant text reprocessed as a user message. Legitimate inline replies remain deliverable.

## Evidence

- Regression-first: before production changes, the focused test returned `dispatch` for the reported tuple (1 failed, 36 passed).
- `pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/monitor/self-chat-dedupe.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor/cache-lifecycle.test.ts` — 80/80 passed after the fix, including memory and persisted caches, a different-text reply, and cross-scope isolation.
- `pnpm check:changed` — all repository guards through formatting and plugin boundaries passed. The final repository-wide extension typecheck was blocked on this checkout by unrelated missing `yargs-parser` declarations in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp-options.ts`.
- `pnpm test:extension imessage` — all touched monitor tests passed; the Windows host then hit existing macOS-path and fake-`imsg` assumptions, and the runner was stopped after it stopped producing output.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Live macOS Messages verification was not run because this Windows environment has no Messages `chat.db` or `imsg` bridge. The issue report includes a live no-recursion observation for the same strict guard shape.
- Production delta: 89 additions / 74 deletions (net +15). The added state is the ID/text association needed for exact matching; two parallel “backed by ID” maps and duplicated inline cache types were removed.

prs.title: fix(ai): clamp OpenAI Responses max_output_tokens to model capacity
prs.body:
Closes #127560

**AI-assisted:** yes — built with Claude; prompts/session logs available on request.

## What Problem This Solves

An authored `maxTokens` above the selected Responses model's declared output capacity was sent unchanged as `max_output_tokens`. A valid `agents.defaults.params.maxTokens`, per-model, per-agent, or run override could make strict endpoints reject every affected normal turn and direct/local compaction with a deterministic 400, and a global override could poison fallback candidates independently (#127560).

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOpenAIResponsesParams` resolved `options?.maxTokens || model.maxTokens` and published it raw — the builder held both the request cap and the model capacity but performed no upper clamp. Sibling transports already enforce this boundary: Anthropic uses `clampMaxTokensToModel`, and OpenAI Completions clamps with regression coverage.

This clamps at that canonical last boundary using the existing helper, preserving current fallback semantics exactly (`undefined` and `0` still fall back to the model cap via the existing `||` shape). The model catalog's `maxTokens` remains the capacity owner for operators needing more real headroom. No caller sites were patched.

- Covers both OpenAI Responses and Azure OpenAI Responses, which share this builder.
- Codex Responses is unaffected: `sanitizeOpenAICodexResponsesParams` continues stripping the field downstream (composed-flow regression included).

## User Impact

Oversized token overrides no longer deterministically break turns on strict endpoints; they clamp to the model's declared capacity like every other transport.

## Evidence

Local, base = current `upstream/main`:

- New focused suite `openai-responses-params-max-tokens.test.ts` covers the issue's full matrix: below-cap preserved, oversized clamped (OpenAI + Azure), undefined/zero fallback preserved, Codex strip composed after clamping.
- Pre-fix failure proof: with the fix stashed, exactly the two oversized-clamp cases fail (`expected 200_000-capped value to be 4_096`) while preserve/fallback/Codex cases pass both ways; restored fix → 5/5 green.
- Adjacent transport suites unaffected: client.compact + continuation 20/20 green.
- oxlint (262 rules) and oxfmt clean; net production delta +3 LOC (clamp + invariant comment).

Known proof gap: repo-wide typecheck/test lanes not completable locally (host CPU saturation); CI covers them.


## After-fix strict-endpoint wire evidence

Rebased onto current `main` (head `938ed621`); focused suite re-run green on the new base.

The shipped transport stream function (`createOpenAIResponsesTransportStreamFn` → `buildOpenAIResponsesParams`) was driven at a real TCP socket against a local strict-contract Responses endpoint that mirrors real strict behavior: requests with `max_output_tokens` above its 4,096 model cap receive OpenAI-shaped `400 invalid_request_error` (`max_output_tokens_exceeded`); conforming requests receive a normal SSE completion.

Authored override in both runs: `maxTokens: 200000` against a model whose catalog capacity is `4_096`.

| Tree | Request captured on the wire | Endpoint response | Stream result |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfixed `main` | `"max_output_tokens":200000` | `400 invalid_request_error` (`max_output_tokens_exceeded`) | `stopReason: "error"` |
| this PR head | `"max_output_tokens":4096` | `200`, SSE `response.completed` | `stopReason: "stop"` |

That is the exact failure mode from the issue (deterministic strict-endpoint rejection of every affected turn) eliminated by the clamp, observed at the request boundary rather than in unit assertions.

**Scope note:** this trace uses a local strict-contract endpoint because no OpenAI API key is available in this environment. The clamp itself is provider-agnostic request shaping verified at the wire level here and by the focused builder suite; if a maintainer wants an api.openai.com trace attached before merge, say so and one will be added.


## Simple-path clamp (addresses the ClawSweeper P2 finding)

`applyCommonResponsesParams` — the shared simple Responses parameter owner reachable from plugin LLM completion without a managed transport requirement — now bounds authored `maxTokens` by the model catalog capacity while **retaining the established 16-token minimum**:

```ts
params.max_output_tokens = Math.min(Math.max(options.maxTokens, 16), model.maxTokens);
```

Both routes are now covered at their respective owners:

- Managed transport builder (`buildOpenAIResponsesParams`): clamped via `clampMaxTokensToModel` with wire-level evidence above.
- Simple owner (`applyCommonResponsesParams`): floor-preserving capacity clamp; OpenAI and Azure simple completions share this single owner.

New coverage:

- `openai-responses-shared.test.ts`: oversized request clamps to catalog capacity (`200000 → 8192`); below-cap request unchanged; the pre-existing floor table (`1→16, 15→16, 16→16, 32→32`) passes unchanged, proving minimum behavior retained.
- `azure-openai-responses.test.ts`: end-to-end fetch-capture asserts an oversized simple Azure completion sends `max_output_tokens: 8192` on the wire.

All four affected suites green post-change (106/106), including exact-head validation of the managed-path suite. Head is now `524a728c`.

prs.title: refactor(worker): simplify private protocol validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private worker protocol checks allocate an allowed-key Set for every parsed object and carry redundant schema construction.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Required, optional, inherited, and unknown keys retain the same validation rules; retention snapshots retain their duplicate rejection and canonical ordering.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check membership in the existing small key arrays, construct strict Zod objects directly, and use a single refinement for each duplicate check.

Production delta: **+35 / −52 = −17 lines**, across three files. This is a bounded cleanup; it does not meet the campaign's larger 200-line target. Existing types consumed by Gateway code remain exported.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/worker/node-workspace-retain-protocol.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed, 76.56 s wall including cold test preparation (Vitest 14.58 s; tests about 0.8 s). No tests added or changed.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0/P1 findings; source and caller references were checked locally.
- Key-check microbenchmark on Node 26, 200,000 valid objects per round, five measured rounds after warmup: 3 required keys 52.15 → 28.35 ms; 7 keys 90.13 → 45.70 ms; 15 keys 145.85 → 85.03 ms; 26 keys 199.04 → 159.46 ms. Three optional keys in each case. Both implementations accepted the same inputs, including inherited optional and unknown-key cases. These are local CPU measurements, not end-to-end latency claims.
- AWS Linux, Node 24.19.0, exact head `f2a62b222c6cdb351725bc883af08ddfbcc7533a`: **63 tests passed** across six whole files in **65.30 s wall**. This includes nine actual child-process worker scenarios using an isolated Gateway harness and a deterministic HTTP provider: local tool execution, durable transcript commit, cancellation, transport loss, placement fencing, and Gateway-proxied sibling inference. This is real process/wire proof with a synthetic provider, not a paid live-model latency sample.
- Full `pnpm tsgo:core` and changed-file Oxlint passed on that same head. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Initial full core typecheck found an inherited unused `env` in `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts`. Main already fixed it in `243b6dbf63d2`; merging main retained the identical three-file cleanup and the complete proof was rerun successfully. The first Testbox source-capsule preparation never dispatched tests; direct AWS provided the completed proof.

The required CI gate is red solely on inherited SDK surface-budget failures in [run 38097386401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38097386401), `checks-node-compact-small-1`. On the untouched main parent `76a282c7a1c6`, the same `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` file reproduces the two portable failing assertions: public exports 3672 > 3656, callable exports 2133 > 2122, deprecated exports 158 > 154. Its Linux-only compiler-join case is skipped on this macOS baseline; CI reports that same surface-budget excess there. The worker change does not touch SDK exports or budgets. No ratchet was raised.

Landing uses the campaign-authorized inherited-failure exception and head-pinned REST fallback after native review worktree provisioning stalled for more than ten minutes. The stalled process was stopped and its exact operation lock recovered.

prs.title: fix(codex): account and trace every provider response
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex app-server can emit more than one `rawResponse/completed` notification during a single turn, especially around tool handoffs.

OpenClaw previously had two related observability gaps:

- `attemptUsage` retained only the final provider response, under-counting multi-response turns.
- Codex diagnostics emitted only one turn-level model-call span. Consumers that reconstructed individual LLM calls from transcript timestamps could place the LLM span after its tool call and make several calls overlap until the final answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Accumulate exact `rawResponse/completed` usage once per `responseId` for attempt-level accounting.
- Keep the final response's usage and `contextUsage` as the assistant/current-context snapshot, so summed billing buckets do not inflate the active context window.
- Emit one request-level `model.call.completed` diagnostic per unique response.
  - Response samples and tool lifecycle boundaries are buffered and paired by order at turn completion.
  - A tool start closes the current LLM interval; completion of the final active tool opens the next LLM interval.
  - This remains correct when Codex delivers `rawResponse/completed` after the tool triggered by that response has already run.
  - Parallel tools form one tool phase. When one provider response emits several sequential tools, the shortest surplus tool-to-tool gap is discarded instead of being reported as an LLM call.
- Add `sourceTimestampMs` to completed model-call diagnostics so the OTel recorder can backdate completed-only request spans to their real completion time.
- Attach exact per-response usage to request spans when present, while still emitting a timing span when Codex omits optional usage.
- Attach accumulated `attemptUsage` to the turn-level model span.
- Hash the upstream response ID before exposing it in diagnostics and deduplicate repeated completion notifications.
- Map `reasoningOutputTokens` into `reasoningTokens`.
- Reuse the same response accumulator in bounded/settled-turn paths.
- Fail closed to thread-last usage when an exact response aggregate becomes incomplete.

Transcript timestamps are intentionally unchanged: an assistant tool-call message records when the model produced the tool call, not when that provider request began. Per-response diagnostics now own the LLM timing boundary.

The assistant-completion idle timeout configuration is not part of this PR: `#97233` already exposed `appServer.turnAssistantCompletionIdleTimeoutMs` on current `main`.

This change was AI-assisted. I reviewed the diff and validated the event contract directly against `openai/codex` app-server source and a real app-server turn.

## User Impact

- Token and cost accounting is accurate for Codex turns containing multiple upstream responses.
- Current-context reporting continues to reflect only the latest provider response.
- OTel consumers can render:

  `LLM request -> tool execution -> LLM request -> tool execution -> final LLM request`

  without deriving LLM starts from assistant-message timestamps.

## Upstream Codex Contract

Checked against immutable `openai/codex@95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74`:

- [`rawResponse/completed` is emitted once per upstream Responses API completion with exact, non-accumulated usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#L1450)
- [`response_id` is required and `token_usage` is optional](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs#L1820-L1827)
- [The sampling loop alternates provider responses with tool work](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L137-L149)
- [`RawResponseCompleted` is emitted when the provider response completes](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/95637f7056835fea66bdd0044414af480fc0fd74/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L2348-L2360)

## Evidence

### Real App-Server Proof

Ran the local authenticated Codex CLI (`0.146.0-alpha.3.1`) as `codex app-server --listen stdio://` with raw events enabled. The prompt required two separate sequential shell calls followed by `DONE`. The proof script used an ephemeral thread and redacted response/tool IDs.

Observed lifecycle, relative to model-turn start:

```text
LLM response-1   0ms .. 8878ms      total=23030
tool-1                 8913ms
LLM response-2         8913ms .. 11874ms   total=23125
tool-2                           11896ms
LLM response-3                   11896ms .. 13492ms   total=23178
turn terminal                                      13496ms
```

No LLM request span overlaps either tool phase. In this run each shell command completed within the millisecond resolution of the captured events.

Redacted projected output:

```json
{
  "rawResponses": [
    {
      "responseId": "response-1",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 22967,
        "cachedInputTokens": 0,
        "outputTokens": 63,
        "totalTokens": 23030
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-2",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23078,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 47,
        "totalTokens": 23125
      }
    },
    {
      "responseId": "response-3",
      "usage": {
        "inputTokens": 23173,
        "cachedInputTokens": 22272,
        "outputTokens": 5,
        "totalTokens": 23178
      }
    }
  ],
  "projected": {
    "attemptUsage": {
      "input": 24674,
      "cacheRead": 44544,
      "output": 115,
      "total": 69333
    },
    "latestResponseUsage": {
      "input": 901,
      "cacheRead": 22272,
      "output": 5,
      "total": 23178
    }
  },
  "requestSpanDurationsMs": [8878, 2961, 1596]
}
```

The accounting invariant holds:

```text
23030 + 23125 + 23178 = 69333
```

The latest context remains response 3 (`23178`), while turn accounting reports all three responses (`69333`).

### Additional Verification
