prs.title: feat: use selected GitHub identities on workers and approved nodes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud workers and approved Codex nodes need stock `gh` and HTTPS `git` to use the same selected GitHub execution identity as Gateway agents, including during long turns.

## User Impact

Workers and supported paired nodes use the effective System GitHub account or explicit agent override through a private execution profile, including sessions without a repository. Personal setup stays in Settings, and personal-publication credentials are not used as an execution fallback.

**Trust and upgrade implications:** this is trusted-host bearer-token delegation, not credential isolation. Node administrators or same-user processes can copy the selected token and use its existing GitHub permissions, potentially beyond the current repository or initiating user's permissions. Closing a turn stops delivery and removes the execution profile; it does not revoke a copied token at GitHub. Refresh-capable nodes are required; older nodes must update and reconnect. Unavailable configured managed credentials refuse the whole turn instead of falling back to native credentials.

**Owner decision remains pending:** SDK/security acceptance of that trust-boundary expansion and the upgrade/refusal behavior has not been recorded. Installed-old-node transition and unavailable-account Settings recovery also remain disclosed proof gaps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing identity selector and OAuth refresh owner, deliver same-account rotations through authenticated worker heartbeats or private node messages, and preserve live authority checks, process shutdown, write settlement, workspace reconciliation, and cleanup. Credential-only sessions receive no checkout metadata or publication authority.

## Evidence

### Second requested rebase — 2026-10-10

Preserved main's placement-read caches and writer postimages, retained the canonical retryable inventory-conflict classification, and removed its obsolete read-lifecycle import. A redundant one-caller observation wrapper was removed without changing authority or release behavior, keeping the module within its line cap.

**Verification:** 94 tests across placement authority, startup maintenance, and GitHub binding passed (105.17s wall, maxWorkers=1). After the wrapper removal, all 27 placement-authority tests passed again (62.59s). Production types passed (15.44s; final incremental 2.15s), scoped lint and SDK registration checks passed. Independent integration review reported no P0–P2 findings with disclosed context limits; focused followup review was scoped-clean. The full changed-check aggregate still stops at the earlier node-registry and delivery-recovery line-cap findings; no waiver is claimed.

Latest observed main **0fc11d74d3ed2d0089065a3a9c32b45ca745f4d2** gives a clean merge preview. Exact-lease push and remote ref verified. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38095763308), attempt 1, **failed at 2026-10-11 00:09:36 UTC**: complete two-page inventory **178 jobs — 142 successful, 19 failed, 17 skipped, zero cancelled**. The 19 failures comprise 18 underlying jobs plus the downstream CI gate: two UI shards, QA Smoke profile 4/4, source contracts, eight extension bundles, four compact Node shards, and two core lint shards. Logs include UI/smoke/Codex timeouts, SDK surface assertions, Feishu ACP routing, and AgentsAPI settlement errors. These observations do not establish PR-versus-main causality. prs.title: fix(ui): retire the live terminal copy once its run clears
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WebChat can render a final assistant reply twice — the stored transcript holds one clean copy (`thinking` + `text`, no `textSignature`), while the screen shows two identical stacked copies that survive until a reload. The live terminal projection and the persisted row are supposed to converge through the authoritative-terminal dedup, but the record that owns that dedup is only armed when the persisted final arrives with `hasActiveRun !== true`. When the final row lands while its run still reads active — long turns with tool calls interleaved make that ordering more likely — no record is armed, and nothing arms it later, so `reconcileAuthoritativeTerminalHistory` never retires the live copy and both renders stay.

## Why This Fix

`rememberAuthoritativeTerminal` now keeps such a terminal **pending** instead of dropping it, and the run-clear reconcile (`finishSessionMessageRunReconcile`, right before the history reload it already triggers) promotes the pending record via `armPendingAuthoritativeTerminal`. The existing history reconciliation then removes the live copy for that run, so the turn converges to the single persisted reply. A pending terminal for a different run is left untouched, and a terminal that already armed stays armed.

## User Impact

A completed turn no longer shows the same reply twice, and it recovers automatically at run completion instead of waiting for a page reload — the duplicate disappears as soon as the run clears and history applies.

## Evidence

- New `ui/src/pages/chat/terminal-message-identity.test.ts` pins the sequence: a final persisted with `hasActiveRun: true` keeps the live copy (the pre-fix state), the run-clear arming retires it, a pending terminal for another run is preserved for its owning run, and the already-clear path still arms immediately. These fail against the old guard because the record was never kept.
- `ui` typecheck (`tsconfig.ui.json`) clean, boundary-guard lint and formatting clean; the neighboring `chat-gateway` and `stream-reconciliation` suites show no new failures (the six locale-dependent "Retrying…" expectations fail identically before and after this change on a zh-CN host).


## Update (c34c8b750b9) — promotion moved onto the history owner

The previous revision armed the deferred terminal inside the run-clear reconcile, which the review correctly flagged: `chat.final` clears the run first and the reloads it triggers never promoted the record, and an already-cleared run skipped the hook. Promotion now lives in the single history-apply owner (`chat-history-hydration`), so every reload path — `chat.final`, session reconciliation, manual reload — arms the pending terminal and retires the live copy.

## Browser reproduction status (open work)

A deterministic Control UI E2E reproduction (mocked Gateway, not committed) puts the reporter's ordering through the real app: a run goes active, the persisted final lands while `hasActiveRun: true`, then `chat.final` completes. Against this branch it still renders two copies, and the instrumented trace pinpoints the second one: an **identity-less live projection** (materialized stream message with no `__openclaw` identity) survives beside the persisted final. The promotion fix works on that trace — the armed terminal retires the live-terminal copy — but retiring the identity-less projection needs a change in the stream-materialization/publish path rather than the dedup helper, so this revision does not yet close the reported duplication. Keeping the PR as work in progress rather than claiming the fix.


## Update (fdfd6791b83) — review findings on eligibility and per-run pendings

- **P1 eligibility:** the deferred record now requires the saved row to own the run's final reply (`ownsFinalReply`): stream-segment-keyed rows and text blocks tagged `phase: "commentary"` no longer arm it, so a commentary-only refresh can't set the run-wide suppression flag and hide the actual final.
- **Per-run pendings:** pending records are keyed by run id (`Map` per host) instead of a single slot, so a second run persisting while active no longer drops the first run's terminal; each run keeps its own retirement path (raises from the reviewer's notes).
- Tests: five cases now cover the happy paths plus the commentary-refusal and two-active-runs sequences.

**Still open:** the reported identity-less duplicate (the app-level reproduction still shows two copies after the fix — the surviving copy is a live projection with no run identity, so retiring it needs a stream-materialization/publish change, not the dedup helper), and the cursor-delta history path (promotion currently runs on page responses only).


## Update (61ffd8e733d) — commentary phase via its canonical owner

The eligibility check now asks `resolveAssistantMessagePhase` (the shared phase owner) instead of parsing `textSignature` itself. The direct read also drifted from the contract — signatures are serialized JSON, so an object-shaped fixture never matched — and the canonical owner is the only place that decides commentary vs answer. The commentary-refusal test now pins the serialized form.

**Still open from Revision 3:** retaining every promoted run until its own live copy reconciles (my armed record is still a single slot), the cursor-delta history path, and the identity-less duplicate from the browser reproduction.

prs.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): preserve GPT token limits for deployment aliases
prs.body:
Closes #114165

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and passed the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring Microsoft Foundry GPT deployments received the generic 128,000-token context window and 16,384-token output limit even when Foundry identified a GPT-5 model with larger documented limits. This could make OpenClaw compact or truncate prompts earlier than the selected deployment requires and advertise an output ceiling below the provider contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Foundry provider now owns an explicit capability table for GPT-5 models whose limits are documented by Microsoft. Capability resolution continues to use the discovered canonical model name, so custom deployment aliases receive the limits of the model they point to, while unknown models keep the existing conservative fallback.

This deliberately does not guess GPT-4.1 context limits because Microsoft documents different limits by deployment type and the current discovery metadata does not expose enough information to choose safely. The existing fallback already matches the documented `gpt-4o-mini` limits. The Claude Opus 5 half of the linked report was fixed independently on current `main`, so this PR does not duplicate that work.

## User Impact

Microsoft Foundry users selecting documented GPT-5 deployments now get accurate context-window and maximum-output metadata, including when the Azure deployment has a custom name. Unrecognized and deployment-dependent models remain on the conservative fallback instead of being overclaimed.

Thanks to @jaserNo1 for reporting the issue and documenting affected deployments in #114165.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new deployment-alias regression table failed all 19 documented GPT-5 cases: each resolved to `128000 / 16384`.
- A follow-up catalog audit added six official IDs omitted from the first pass. `gpt-5-pro` reproduced the same incorrect `128000 / 16384` fallback (expected `400000 / 128000`); the five chat variants already matched their documented `128000 / 16384` limits through the fallback and are now explicit table entries instead of accidental matches.
- After the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts` passes: 121/121 tests.
- The regression cases now explicitly pass the deployment list produced by Azure discovery, with a custom deployment name and separate canonical `modelName` for all 25 currently documented Foundry GPT IDs.
- The emitted configuration path is connected as follows:
  1. `buildFoundryAuthResult(...)` passes discovered deployments to `buildFoundryProviderConfig(...)`.
  2. Its deployment mapper calls `resolveFoundryModelCapabilities(deployment.name, deployment.modelName, ...)`.
  3. Capability resolution calls `resolveFoundryModelTokenLimits(modelName)` using the discovered canonical name.
  4. The builder emits `capabilities.contextWindow` and `capabilities.maxTokens` into each provider model entry.
- Production and test type checks pass:
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo`
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- Targeted extension oxlint, formatting, import-cycle, plugin-boundary, SDK API, dependency-policy, database-first, runtime-sidecar, and test-temp guards pass.
- `git diff --check` passes on the rebased branch.
- Fresh full-branch Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) reports no findings and rates the patch correct with 0.97 confidence.
- Limits are sourced from [Microsoft's Foundry Models sold by Azure documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure).

Credentialed provider proof is not claimed: the execution environment has neither Azure CLI nor Azure/Foundry credentials, so it cannot safely discover a real subscription deployment. The source-level before/after and emitted-config regression evidence above is reproducible without secrets; a maintainer or reporter with a Foundry deployment can add the remaining redacted live-discovery proof.

prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve bot-self reply context under group allowlist
prs.body:
Closes #82002

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users replying to a bot-sent Telegram group message (for example a cron or system notification) would lose the quoted bot text when the group uses `contextVisibility: "allowlist"`. The agent only saw the user's short follow-up (such as "what happened?") and answered from stale session context instead of the notification being replied to.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under allowlist visibility, supplemental quote/reply context and reply-media hydration treated every sender against `effectiveGroupAllow`. The authenticated bot's own account is usually not on that list, so bot-authored reply targets were filtered out even though replying to the bot already counts as an implicit mention in groups.

This change treats the bot's own immediate quote/reply target as visible under allowlist policy in both the session context builder and reply-media hydration. Unlisted human senders and forwarded origins remain gated. Deeper thread ancestors still follow the normal allowlist rules (including `allowlist_quote`, which only overrides `kind: "quote"`).

## User Impact

Operators using Telegram groups with group allowlists and allowlist context visibility can reply to bot notifications and have the quoted bot message included in the agent turn again. Unlisted third-party reply context stays hidden.

## Evidence

Pre-fix regression proof (production owners reverted, new tests kept): bot-self text and media cases failed; unlisted human reply target still correctly dropped.

Post-fix:

```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin:$PATH"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -t "preserves bot-self reply target|still drops unlisted human|hydrates bot-self reply media|redacts forwarded origin inside reply targets"
```

prs.title: fix(sessions): align CLI lifecycle and runtime state
prs.body:
Closes #124524

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the stock CLI and Gateway session projections against a real signed deployment, wrote failing parity regressions, and validated the shared owner change.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions list` could disagree with the authoritative Gateway in two operator-visible ways:

- archived sessions had no archive marker in JSON or the default table;
- an unlocked historical `agentHarnessId` was shown as the current runtime, even though the next turn follows current policy unless a compatible explicit override or locked transcript owns it.

This made successful lifecycle cleanup look ineffective and made historical execution provenance look like active routing drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change extracts the Gateway existing effective-session runtime rule into one shared resolver and uses it from both the Gateway and CLI. The CLI also projects `archived`/`archivedAt` from the existing timestamp and adds an `archived` table flag.

No new persistence, schema, migration, background reconciliation, configuration, or compatibility path is introduced. The Gateway loses its duplicate inline runtime-resolution block.

## Evidence

Regression-first proof:

```text
Before fix: 2 failures
- archived fields absent; unlocked historical OpenClaw harness reported as session runtime
- compatible explicit override reported with source session instead of session-key

After fix:
Test Files: 2 passed
Tests: 9 passed
```

Broader relevant Gateway validation:

```text
Test Files: 3 passed
Tests: 483 passed
```

Repository validation:

```text
preflight guards: passed
package patch guard: passed (no new patches)
database-first legacy-store guard: passed
typecheck prod: passed
typecheck scripts: passed
typecheck test root: passed
targeted oxlint on all six changed files: passed
format check on all changed files: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

The repository-wide oxlint core and extensions shards did not complete on the local host: both were terminated by the stock lint runner after abnormal multi-thousand-second elapsed-time jumps. No lint diagnostic was emitted before timeout. This is reported as an infrastructure timeout, not a pass; upstream CI remains the full-matrix authority.

## User Impact

Operators can verify archive cleanup and see the runtime that will actually handle the next turn. Historical harness provenance no longer masquerades as an unlocked runtime pin, while compatible explicit overrides and locked ownership keep their existing semantics.

prs.title: fix(skills): background skill reviews run after every turn that uses a learned skill
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: background Skill Workshop reviews (and their "💾 Learned" notices) run right after almost every turn in a conversation that keeps using a learned skill.

## User Impact

User impact: reviews now run only after 10 accumulated model iterations in a session, so skill-heavy conversations get a review every ~10 iterations instead of after each turn. A turn that changed a learned skill itself still resets the count. The skills a turn used still inform the review when it runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler had a bypass: any turn that read or viewed a learned skill queued a review immediately, whatever the iteration count. In a topic where nearly every turn uses the same learned skill, that made reviews per-turn. This removes the bypass and keeps the existing 10-iteration cadence, matching Hermes Agent, which reviews skills only after `skills.creation_nudge_interval` (default 10) tool iterations (`agent/turn_finalizer.py:763-769`, `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py:165-167` in NousResearch/hermes-agent).

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (maintainer's Telegram bot): in a topic where nearly every turn used `ssggplex-downloads`, a background review and notice followed the turn right after the agent's own edit (change feed 2026-10-10: agent patch 21:37 UTC, review patches 21:46 UTC). Across that day, reviews ran in 4 conversations, each right after a skill-using turn.
- `src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.test.ts`: the test that expected an immediate review after a learned-skill turn now proves such turns wait and count toward the threshold; 7/7 pass.
- `pnpm run tsgo:core` and `pnpm run tsgo:test:src` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Docs updated: `docs/tools/self-learning.md` and `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md`.
- No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes: `git log origin/main --author=pash@openai.com --author=sjf@openai.com` on the touched files is empty.

prs.title: fix(agent): use ctx.params.session for reasoning stream control (#134662)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reasoning-capable models (e.g., `ollama/glm-5.3:cloud`) with no explicit `thinkingLevel` configuration fall back to `medium` thinking via the documented fallback path. In this implicit-fallback state, the model's native reasoning **leaks into visible message content** — rendered inline as part of the assistant message body rather than as the separate assistant-reasoning section the UI toggle controls.

The root cause: the reasoning stream control code in `handleMessageUpdate` accessed `ctx.session` for model metadata, but `session` does not exist on `EmbeddedAgentSubscribeContext` — it lives under `ctx.params.session`. This caused `modelHasReasoningCapability` and `thinkingEnabled` to always evaluate falsy, so `openReasoningStream` was never called on `text_start` for implicitly-falling-back models.

## Summary

- **Root cause fix**: Access session via `ctx.params.session` (typed cast) instead of non-existent `ctx.session`
- **Catalog access**: Extract `catalog` via typed cast from `ctx.params` (was accessing non-existent `ctx.params.catalog` directly)
- **Code dedup**: Define `openReasoning` helper once at top of scope — was copy-pasted 5× with identical `typeof` checks
- **Test injection**: Add `openReasoningStream` to test context fixture for mock injection, enabling verification that `openReasoningStream` is actually called

## Linked context

Closes #134662

## Evidence

**Before fix** (from issue report):
- `ollama/glm-5.3:cloud` session with no `thinkingLevel` configured
- `/status` shows "think medium" via fallback
- Assistant reasoning appears inline, glued to visible reply
- Heartbeat poll delivers reasoning text + token as visible message

**After fix** (local validation):
- `openReasoningStream` is now called on `text_start` when model has reasoning capability and thinking is enabled
- Test "opens reasoning stream on text_start for reasoning-capable model with implicit thinkingLevel fallback" passes — verifies `openReasoningStreamMock` is called

**Local test results:**
```
$ pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.update-stream-items.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
```

**Type check:**
```
$ pnpm tsgo:core
# Exit 0 — no type errors
```

**Lockfile:**
```
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
# Exit 0 — lockfile is up to date
```

## User Impact

- Reasoning-capable models with implicit thinking fallback now properly isolate reasoning content into the reasoning stream
- Visible message content no longer contains leaked reasoning text
- Heartbeat suppression works correctly (bare token delivered, not reasoning + token)

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — reasoning content is now properly isolated (the intended fix)
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No
- What is the highest-risk area? Streaming reasoning stream control
- How is that risk mitigated? The fix only activates for reasoning-capable models with thinking enabled — normal models are unaffected

prs.title: fix(memory): prevent duplicate Gemini batch jobs after timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini native embedding-batch creation is non-idempotent. If a create response is lost or times out after the provider accepted it, an immediate retry can create a second paid remote job. The provider assigns the batch name only in the response and does not expose a caller-supplied idempotency key.

- https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/batch-api#best-practices
- https://ai.google.dev/api/batch-api#method:-models.asyncbatchembedcontent

## What Changed

This version treats batch submission as a crash-recoverable ownership protocol:

- Memory Core persists an exclusive reservation in the published memory database before Gemini's non-idempotent create call.
- Acknowledged provider batch names are attached to that reservation as soon as they are returned.
- Each request set has a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint; manifests retain content-independent custom IDs and chunk hashes, not source text, credentials, or vectors.
- Restarted managers adopt an acknowledged job only when its exact request fingerprint matches.
- Completed output is reconciled by stable chunk hash and published idempotently to the shared embedding cache, including when source enumeration has drifted since submission.
- Ambiguous create outcomes remain quarantined. Definitive non-ambiguous 4xx rejections (except 408) release the reservation.
- The reservation is cleared only after local cache/index publication commits.
- Closing a manager aborts local polling without cancelling or duplicating an accepted remote job.
- Gemini's native-batch failure mode remains fail-closed instead of fanning a large migration into synchronous paid requests.
- Status output exposes the submission, provider job, timestamps, and recovery state.
- Deliberate quarantine clearing requires both `--force` and `--clear-batch-quarantine`.

The ownership record lives in the published database while a shadow rebuild remains isolated. Independent managers serialize reservation changes through SQLite immediate transactions.

## User Impact

Interrupted Gemini memory migrations can resume acknowledged work without resubmitting already accepted requests. Operators get an explicit quarantine for genuinely ambiguous remote ownership instead of hidden duplicate spend or an uncontrolled synchronous fallback.

## Evidence

Exact candidate head: `ca2a3d6a9bcb7215a9dfba22f8407b06ab116206`

Candidate base at construction: `044cf2e6e027591e6361dbd2784a8b9c68959e18` (`upstream/main` at the time)

- Focused Google provider/lifecycle tests: **67/67 passed**.
- Memory integration tests: **235/235 passed**.
- Plugin contract suite: **1,117/1,117 passed**.
- Total: **1,419 tests passed**.
- Core and extension production/test TypeScript checks passed.
- Changed-file structural, dependency, formatting, documentation, SDK, and extension-boundary gates passed.
- Documentation validation passed: 1,294 MDX files, 13,239 internal links with 0 broken, and 1,224 config examples.
- Full production build passed, including 91 external plugins, 152 public SDK subpaths, CLI bootstrap, and Control UI performance gates.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- A secrets/logging audit found no credentials, request text, vectors, or authorization values added to logs.

The implementation has also been exercised against a real authenticated Gemini migration outside CI: completed jobs were reconciled, cache entries advanced, and a subsequent quota rejection occurred before a new provider job ID was assigned. Completed fingerprints were not replayed. No provider identifiers or credentials are included here.

## Scope

This PR intentionally adds no quota-size, parallelism, or retry-policy configuration. It does not alter production deployment files. Provider transport remains in the Google extension; Memory Core owns durable publication and recovery state.

## Required Before Ready/Merge

- Upstream CI must pass on this exact head.
- An independent exact-head review must complete; the author-side GCP environment does not currently have an independent Codex reviewer identity, so this is not being bypassed.
- Maintainers must approve the fail-closed ambiguity/quarantine contract and its operator-recovery tradeoff.

This PR is kept as a draft until those gates are satisfied.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report active unmanaged restart startup accurately
prs.body:
Closes #119958

## Summary

Fixes the unmanaged SIGUSR1 restart path that reports a 60-second health timeout even when the same gateway process has accepted the restart and is still progressing through startup.

## Root cause

The CLI sends SIGUSR1 and then polls only listener health. An in-process restart can retain its PID while the listener is intentionally absent, so PID and port state cannot distinguish active startup from a dead restart.

## Fix

The gateway loop owns a short-lived renewable startup-progress lease while awaiting each startup. The unmanaged listener waiter accepts a typed `still-starting` result only when that lease is fresh, belongs to the signaled gateway process, and began after this restart request. The normal 60-second listener window is not extended. Missing, stale, expired, or non-progressing lease evidence still fails the restart.

## User impact

A bounded still-starting result tells operators to run `openclaw gateway status --deep` instead of treating a healthy slow boot as failed and applying destructive recovery.

## Validation

Run the focused lifecycle, listener-health, run-loop, and lease regressions; then `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:changed`.

## Credit

Thanks @islandpreneur007 for the source reproduction in #119958.

prs.title: fix: Bun test runs can delete the checkout through handoff fixture cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: running the managed update handoff tests under the Bun runtime (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`) recursively deletes the test's working directory, which on 2026-10-10 wiped an entire git worktree.

## User Impact

No product change. Developers and agents can run the handoff test suites under Bun without risking their checkout; a bad cleanup path now fails the test loudly instead of deleting anything.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under Bun, the handoff helper is spawned as `--no-install <handoff.cjs> <handoff.json>`. Several fixtures assumed the script was `args[0]` and registered `path.dirname(args[0])` for `rm -rf` cleanup, so `path.dirname("--no-install")` became `"."`. The runtime-selection case in the lifecycle test and the single-flight `afterEach` were both destructive this way; the boundary, ownership, cross-process, and foreground fixtures also read params from leading positions.

All handoff fixtures now share one guarded tracker (`update-managed-service-handoff-artifacts.test-support.ts`) that rejects any path that is relative, outside `os.tmpdir()`, the tmp root itself, or the cwd or one of its ancestors, both at registration and again right before removal. Cleanup directories come from the start result's `logPath`, and argv reads go through one parser that validates the trailing `handoff.cjs`/`handoff.json` production contract. Production code is unchanged.

<details><summary>Sweep for similar patterns</summary>

Swept `src/`, `extensions/`, `test/`, `scripts/`, `ui/`, `packages/` for `path.dirname(<spawn/argv arg>)` feeding cleanup. Fixed in this PR: handoff lifecycle, single-flight, boundary, ownership, cross-process, foreground, command, and shared handoff test-support. Inspected and safe (cleanup uses returned `logPath`, a fixture-created root, a named flag value, or the captured args belong to `fs.mkdir`/`fs.open`, not spawn): handoff settlement, `gateway/server-methods/update.test-harness.ts`, `extensions/mxc` backend test, `test/helpers/auth-wizard.test.ts`, `media/store.test.ts`, worker-environment transfer tests, subagent-spawn authority support, `test/scripts/ios-release-e2e.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression `tracks the real handoff artifacts with Bun runtime arguments` (Unix, runs on Linux CI): drives `startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff` with a `bun` exec path through the real `resolveRuntimeArgs`, asserts spawn args are `["--no-install", script, params]`, and asserts every registered cleanup dir is inside the tmp root. A second test asserts the tracker throws for `.`, a relative path, `process.cwd()`, and the tmp root.
- Node runtime, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: lifecycle 64 passed; cross-process 15 passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only). Earlier iteration of the same diff also passed ownership, command, single-flight, foreground, recovery-systemd, recovery-launchd, native-lifecycle, triage, terminal-result, and system suites (292 passed total).
- Bun runtime: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 65/65 in a disposable `git worktree` copy (never in a real checkout), and the copy was intact afterwards. That run used the pre-simplification guard; the final guard only drops a realpath/symlink branch.
- `tsgo` (core cli-update test tsconfig), oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean.
- Test cost: no new timers, sleeps, or process boots; the new regression runs in about 1.5 s.


### Main repair and CI refresh

The original CI run 38094041782 failed on inherited main checks. Main now contains the unused binding fix (243b6dbf63d2), the internal DM-policy export-name fix (13296b17cd0f), and the plugin-state lint/SDK budget repair (f9940dc8a794; provenance comments in 7562fd2b9012). The SDK limits account exactly for the intended async approval/command APIs from #168482 and conversation binding APIs from #168483. The tool-result-error aliases were informational, not the source-contract failure.

Exact core lint, core typechecking, export-name and SDK surface checks pass locally. Focused Node tests for these main repairs passed 74 tests with one platform skip in 82.64 seconds. Codex review found no actionable issues. The plugin-state comparison file passed 14 tests in 21.52 seconds including preparation.

The refreshed PR head ceaff8a6d63b contains the repaired main. Its handoff diff is byte-identical to b2750ff704f0, and main changed no handoff files, so the prior focused proof remains applicable. New CI is run 38097285969; the original failed run was not rerun.

prs.title: feat(exec): add allowSymlinkPath config option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a workspace path contains symlink components (for example
`/mnt/ollama/.openclaw/workspace` where an intermediate directory is a
symlink), the exec tool hard-blocks host execution with
`SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval requires canonical cwd (no symlink path components)`.
Operators whose filesystem layout legitimately uses symlinks have no opt-out,
so `system.run` on those hosts is unusable without relayouting the disk.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts`:
  symlinked cwd accepted when `allowSymlinkPath: true`, and the approval plan
  exposing `requestedCwd` next to the canonical `cwd`; full suite passes
  (25/25) after re-integration onto current `main`.
- Rebased onto `origin/main` (`188fd77d91a`): the symlink check now lives in
  `src/infra/system-run-cwd-binding.ts`; the opt-in flag gates only the
  symlink rejection, while realpath resolution and file-identity (TOCTOU)
  revalidation are preserved on both the approval and launch paths.
- Default behavior unchanged: without the flag the denial message and
  identity checks are byte-identical to `main`.

---

## Summary

This PR adds a new `tools.exec.allowSymlinkPath` boolean config option that allows the exec tool to run commands in directories containing symlinks, or when the cwd itself is a symlink.

### Problem

When a user's workspace path contains symlink components (e.g., `/mnt/ollama/.openclaw/workspace` where an intermediate directory is a symlink), the exec tool hard-blocks execution with:

```
SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval requires canonical cwd (no symlink path components)
```

This is overly restrictive for environments where symlinks are a normal part of the filesystem layout and the user trusts the symlink targets.

### Solution

Add an opt-in config flag `allowSymlinkPath` that relaxes the symlink checks in `resolveCanonicalApprovalCwdSync` while still verifying that the resolved realpath is stable (file identity check against `cwdRealStat`).

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.tools.ts` | Add `allowSymlinkPath?: boolean` to `ExecToolConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add zod validation field |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.ts` | Thread `allowSymlinkPath` through `resolveCanonicalApprovalCwdSync`, `hardenApprovedExecutionPaths`, and `buildSystemRunApprovalPlan`; skip symlink checks when enabled |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` | Read agent-level or global exec config and pass to hardening |
| `src/node-host/invoke.ts` | Load runtime config in `system.run.prepare` path and pass `allowSymlinkPath` |
| `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts` | Add test: symlinked cwd accepted when `allowSymlinkPath: true` |

### Usage

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "exec": {
      "allowSymlinkPath": true
    }
  }
}
```

Or per-agent:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      {
        "id": "main",
        "tools": {
          "exec": {
            "allowSymlinkPath": true
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Verification

- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `src/node-host/invoke-system-run-plan.test.ts` passes (17/17)
- [x] `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` passes (24/24)
- [x] Config validated successfully on live gateway restart

### Notes for Reviewers

- This change is **opt-in**; default behavior remains unchanged (symlinks are still blocked by default).
- The identity mismatch check is relaxed but not removed: when `allowSymlinkPath` is enabled, we still verify `sameFileIdentity(cwdStat, cwdRealStat)` to ensure the symlink resolves to a stable target.
- The `fix(deps): update fs-safe hash and allow exotic subdeps` commit is included in this branch because `origin/main` currently fails to build without it.

prs.title: fix(tlon): preserve provider-native group message ids
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon group sends returned a fabricated `~ship/<unix-ms>` message ID instead of the provider-native dotted `@ud`. Reusing that delivery receipt for a reply targeted the wrong group post. Direct messages use a separate `~ship/<@ud>` contract and are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Tlon send owner now formats timestamps once with `scot("ud", da.fromUnix(sentAt))`. Group sends return that bare provider-native ID, while direct messages continue to prepend the sending ship. This repairs the producer boundary instead of rewriting IDs later in receipt or reply routing.

## User Impact

Agents and operators can reuse a sent Tlon group message receipt as the reply target, preserving native thread routing for both text and media sends. Direct-message IDs and existing numeric reply-ID formatting remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before the repair: 3 of 8 focused send-owner tests failed, covering group text/media receipts and root-to-reply target reuse.
- After the repair: focused Tlon send-owner tests pass 8/8; the full Tlon suite previously passed 285/285.
- Fresh publication check: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts` passes 8/8, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Extension type, lint, format, package-boundary, and architecture checks passed during validation.
- Direct dependency proof: `@urbit/aura` 3.0.0 declarations and implementation show `da.fromUnix(number): bigint`; `scot("ud", bigint)` renders decimal digits grouped with dots.
- Scope: exactly `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts` and `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts`. Production `+6/-3` (net +3); tests `+74/-2`.
- Exact-head CI is terminal green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- AI-assisted; the patch was inspected and validated. No agent transcript is included.

**Review required: live Tlon group root-to-reply roundtrip unavailable; do not merge until supplied.** No authorized live Tlon ship and disposable group channel were available. The deterministic poke-boundary test verifies the exact outgoing reply target, but it is not a live external-provider roundtrip.

prs.title: fix: resolve issue #157781 — @openclaw/kimi-provider: kimi-for-coding thinking profile stuck at off/on — K2.8 Preview supports low/high/max
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #157781: @openclaw/kimi-provider: kimi-for-coding thinking profile stuck at off/on — K2.8 Preview supports low/high/max

## Summary
`@openclaw/kimi-provider` (2026.9.6, latest) hard-codes a binary **off/on** thinking profile for every model that isn't K3. Since **Kimi K2.8 Preview** fully rolled out to Kimi Code on 2026-09-11 (same model ID `kimi-for-coding`, no client/config change needed), the backend now officially supports **low / high / max** thinking effort (default **max**), matching the K3 series. The plugin's policy surface hasn't caught up, so the Control UI shows only two thinking options and `sessions.patch` rejects `"max"`:
```
thinkingLevel "max" is not supported for kimi-coding/kimi-for-coding (use off|on)
```
## Details
In `dist/provider-policy-api.js`, `resolveThinkingProfile` returns the binary profile for all non-K3 model ids:
```js
function resolveThinkingProfile({ modelId }) {
	if (isKimiK3ModelId(modelId)) return { levels: KIMI_K3_THINKING_LEVELS, ... }; // 8 levels
	return {
		levels: [{ id: "off", label: "off" }, { id: "low", label: "on" }],
```

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause
`extensions/kimi-coding/provider-policy-api.ts` owns the Kimi provider thinking profile.
`resolveThinkingProfile()` returns the full 8-level K3 ladder only for K3 model ids
(`k3`, `k3-256k`, and legacy `k3[1m]`). Every other Kimi Coding model id falls into a
hard-coded catch-all branch:
```ts
return {
  levels: [
    { id: "off", label: "off" },
    { id: "low", label: "on" },
  ],
  defaultLevel: "off",
};
```
That catch-all is the only policy in effect for `kimi-for-coding` and
`kimi-for-coding-highspeed` (the provider catalog in
`extensions/kimi-coding/openclaw.plugin.json` defines only those two non-K3 rows, and
the legacy aliases `kimi-code` / `k2p5` normalize to `kimi-for-coding`).

## User Impact

See the linked issue for the reported before/after behavior; this change is limited to the paths shown in the PR diff.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof through the product entry point, before and after this change.
Every command below was executed in the reproduction container (see Environment).

prs.title: fix(qa): own screenshot and recording artifact freshness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Mantis desktop-browser QA could report screenshots or recordings left by an earlier run as current evidence when an output directory was reused. Empty or symlinked captures could also be accepted, and a screenshot-only success could subsequently fail the Discord status-reactions evidence workflow.

**Draft: the improved implementation is preserved for review, but mandatory real desktop proof is still outstanding. Do not merge or enable automerge yet.** This body replaces the previous head's proof claims; those older claims are not being carried forward as evidence for this rewrite.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture owner now retires exactly its screenshot, recording, summary, report, and error file before preflight. It settles every cleanup without following symlink targets or recursively removing directories. Failed transfers clean only the two possibly partial visual files. Both captures are inspected as regular nonempty files; the screenshot is required, while the recording remains optional. Inspection and cleanup failures retain both causes, and one result drives summary/report publication.

The status-reactions workflow preserves optional-video behavior through copy, independent preview generation, report links, and the evidence manifest. Required screenshots remain required. Existing SSH selection, non-deleting rsync behavior, lease retention, unrelated output files, and remote diagnostic logs are unchanged. A valid video accompanying an invalid required screenshot remains on disk for diagnosis but is not claimed by the failed result.

This is a source-trusted rewrite on main baseline `8c7de197cd6d535943d10a04312547b134cf00e2`, preserving the original author's credit. The contributor branch was not executed locally.

## User Impact

Internal Mantis QA operators get accurate capture evidence and usable screenshot-only status-reactions runs. This does not change the general browser automation runtime. No configuration, dependency, persistent-store, provider, or security-policy surface is added. The root changelog is intentionally omitted under the internal-only exception.

Runtime: **+97/-72 (net +25)**. Workflow: **+22/-19 (net +3)**. Tests: **+411/-1 (net +410)**. Consolidating the duplicate summaries absorbs most of the owner repair; remaining production growth enforces artifact lifecycle, regular-file validation, error preservation, and independent optional-video handling.

## Evidence

- The trusted baseline reproduced six failures through the actual producer with real local filesystem operations and rsync: stale video reuse, false screenshot success, empty captures, symlinks, partial-copy remnants, and preflight remnants. The fresh-capture control passed.
- Regression tests failed before their respective repairs. Final focused suites pass: **28 owner tests + 8 workflow tests = 36**. These cover sequential directory reuse, invalid capture combinations, copy/inspection/cleanup failures, stale reports and errors, directory/symlink safety, absent optional videos, either lane's preview failure, and required screenshot enforcement.
- The same actual-producer/local-rsync harness passes on the final tree with no findings. It uses synthetic PNG/video fixtures and substitutes cloud transport; it is **not live Chrome, X11, remote Crabbox, or Discord proof**. Its preflight check covers visual names; metadata retirement is exercised by the separate owner filesystem tests.
- Workflow tests execute the actual workflow shell step with controlled external commands and validate artifacts through the actual evidence-manifest loader. They do not publish to GitHub or Discord.
- Targeted formatting, `git diff --check`, and actionlint pass. Two independent code/proof reviewers approved the final tree. Native Codex autoreview and a distinct full-source Codex review are clean after addressing both the double-fault error-loss and stale preflight-report findings.
- Native extension typechecking hit its 90-second watchdog without diagnostics under host load; this was not a pass. Full types, type-aware lint, complete workflow gates, and exact-head hosted CI remain pending. No build/SDK preparation or weaker lint configuration was substituted.

Reproducible focused commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/mantis/desktop-browser-smoke.runtime.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/mantis-status-reactions-artifacts.test.ts
actionlint .github/workflows/mantis-discord-status-reactions.yml
git diff --check
```

### Remaining desktop proof

The real Mantis CLI must still run against an approved Linux desktop lease with a visible Chrome/X11 capture and actual SSH/rsync transfer, repeating the same output directory from PNG+MP4 to screenshot-only to failure. Standard Testbox cannot exercise this flow: its provider lacks desktop/browser capabilities and inspect does not supply the SSH endpoint/key/user required by the existing Mantis copy owner. Installing Chrome alone would not resolve that transport mismatch. No paid desktop lease has been acquired, and this PR does not add a provider adapter or alternate transport to work around the gap.

### Latest ClawSweeper findings and rank-up moves

The latest substantive review is August 19 on the original head; the August 26 comment is a review-start placeholder, not a new verdict.

- Optional status-reactions MP4 copy, preview/report paths, and full-video manifest entries: addressed, with both independent lanes covered.
- Refresh the old branch against main and rerun producer/consumer proof: addressed by the trusted-main rewrite and final 36-test plus filesystem/rsync run. Main advancing alone is not claimed as a reason for another rebase.
- Real desktop/workflow publication proof and exact-head CI: still pending; the PR remains draft. Earlier proof-sufficient labels and CLI-help output do not establish this rewritten head's real desktop behavior.
- The previous serialized-state warning concerned QA artifact fixtures, not an OpenClaw runtime store or schema migration; no persistent-store design change is included.

Named follow-up: **Mantis Slack/Telegram desktop artifact freshness**. Their separate producer lifecycles still warrant a dedicated sequential-reuse and cleanup audit with their own real-flow proof; this draft does not claim those owners are repaired or execute their authenticated flows.

prs.title: fix(signal): re-probe managed daemon liveness so hangs surface as disconnected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed signal-cli daemon is only proven alive once, at startup (`waitForSignalDaemonReady`). After that, the daemon's SSE endpoint stays idle between inbound Signal events, so a daemon that hangs (deadlocked, wedged on a syscall, etc.) without exiting its process keeps reporting `connected: true` forever — there is no other liveness signal, so the gateway health monitor has nothing to act on and never restarts it (#116295).

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a periodic (60s) liveness probe that re-checks the daemon's own `/api/v1/check` endpoint via the existing `signalCheck` adapter, started once `autoStart` brings the managed daemon up and stopped in the same `finally` block that already tears down the ingress monitor. A successful probe publishes a connected + transport-activity status patch (`createConnectedChannelStatusPatch`/`createTransportActivityStatusPatch`, the same factories the SSE path already uses); a failed probe marks the account `connected: false` with the probe error in `lastError`, which is what the gateway health monitor reads. Wiring reuses the account's existing `setStatus` sink (`createAccountStatusSink`), the same one `startAccount` already writes an initial snapshot through.

## User Impact

A wedged managed signal-cli daemon now flips to disconnected within ~60s of going unresponsive instead of appearing healthy indefinitely, letting the gateway's existing restart/alerting machinery react to it.

## Evidence

- `autoStart` (and therefore the heartbeat) only ever applies to `managed-native` transport, the exact case this issue is about — container-transport accounts don't spawn a daemon here and are unaffected.
- The probe reuses `signalCheck`, the same function `waitForSignalDaemonReady` uses for startup readiness, applied periodically instead of once.

Fixes #116295

## What Problem This Solves

Main dashboard/WebChat/channel sessions that are working when the Gateway restarts must resume automatically. A production restart on 2026-10-10 left two dashboard main turns interrupted indefinitely until a human sent another message.

Abbreviated timeline, UTC (c18792f4 → 3050cdc4): SIGTERM at 19:36:27; drain exhausted at 19:37:12.385; both reply admissions released for `restart-abort` at 19:37:12.408, before the shutdown marker; startup at 19:37:45 reported `started=0`. The affected rows retained `status: interrupted` and `abortedLastRun: true`, but no recovery claim. Separately, 51 archived recovery rows were repeatedly reported as `work_start_blocked` requiring operator action.

## User Impact

A main chat session (dashboard, WebChat, or channel) that is mid-turn when the Gateway restarts for a deploy, crash, or kill now resumes on the next boot without anyone typing a follow-up. Before, a restart whose connection cleanup ran a few milliseconds ahead of the shutdown marker left the session showing `interrupted` forever. Operators also stop seeing archived sessions reported as blocked recovery work on every boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The close prelude calls `runtime.connectionWork.beginClose(createAgentRunRestartAbortError())` in `src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts:402` before calling shutdown preparation. `AsyncWorkScope.beginClose` synchronously cancels inherited work, and the reply-admission listener in `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts:551` releases its database lease on that signal. This ordering exists in the old production revision too.

Shutdown collection and its subsequent owner recheck excluded already-aborted controllers, even when the reason was restart. Startup then required an existing recovery claim, so it could not repair the missed marker. Archived rows reached the generic work-start refusal before being classified separately.

### Fix

- Keep exact, still-registered restart-aborted runs eligible for shutdown marking and its owner recheck; retain session/generation and terminal-persistence checks. Warn when supplied runs produce zero marks, including counts and the dominant skip reason.
- Let the existing startup owner mark unclaimed interrupted main sessions through its existing recovery transition. Preserve live-owner checks at commit, startup cutoff, archive/tombstone exclusions, yielded continuations, pending delivery, and retry budgets.
- Preserve explicit terminal cancellations: `abortedLastRun` also describes killed turns, so an unclaimed completed outcome remains unchanged.
- Classify archived recovery rows as `archived`, deferred with no next owner, before work-start checks. Document the automatic resume guarantee and startup safety net. No schema, config, or changelog changes.

## Evidence

### Merge validation — `fa4f746dacfd`

Merged `origin/main` at `6cc0e8460192` without rebasing or amending. Resolved the overlap with #168650 by retaining dispatch-target resolution before `resolveSessionWorkStartBlock`. Its distinct `archived` reason is non-retryable; only that reason selects `skip("archived")` inside the existing block branch. The branch still records `decision.reason` and preserves pending/blocked behavior and `onPreparationPending`. The separate early archived check is removed.

Diagnostics retain both `work_start_pending` and archived/deferred/no-owner handling. The docs retain main's Session preparation paragraph and the recovery guarantee/startup safety net, with the combined skip-reason list and archived-deferred sentence. Main's new admission cases are unchanged, and the existing continue case still expects archived/deferred/none.

| --- | --- | ---: |
| `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 19 passed, 0 failed | 71.51 s |
| `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-startup-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 14 passed, 0 failed | 26.04 s |
| `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-marking.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 12 passed, 0 failed | 33.87 s |
| `pnpm test src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-abort.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 5 passed, 0 failed | 27.56 s |
| `pnpm test src/gateway/server-run-shutdown.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 1 passed, 0 failed | 17.33 s |

All 51 tests passed. Times use `/usr/bin/time -p` and include existing compilation/import and SQLite fixture costs. Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-agents-sessions` and `core-test-gateway-server` type graphs, and `git diff --check` passed. `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts` passed. Codex autoreview against the new merge base `6cc0e8460192d6dae2f1f3622665755d09b908b7` was scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. No PR merge or manual CI action was performed.

### Follow-up validation — `0503ea4969e6`

Fixed the two findings from head `f26dc47e2329`, with no other changes. Claimless startup now preserves a terminal receipt for the interrupted continuation, checking its lifecycle, writer, or delivery-source run ID. The regression pairs that delivered row with a claimless interruption whose receipts belong only to other runs; only the latter is marked. The admission test now expects `archived` / `deferred` / `none`, while retaining its startup-concurrency and shutdown-custody assertions.

All five files passed (46 tests). Times use `/usr/bin/time -p` and include existing compilation/import and worker-backed SQLite fixture costs; no new timers, sleeps, polling, or Gateway boots. The new focused regression failed before the fix (`marked=2`, expected `1`; 46.73 s).

The isolated Codex autoreview helper reviewed only the delta from `f26dc47e2329` and found no actionable P0–P2 findings. No merge or manual CI action was performed.

### Initial validation

| Command | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |

All wall times use `/usr/bin/time -p`. The final marking run used a separate filesystem module cache while static checks ran. These files exercise real worker-backed SQLite ownership, persistence, and dispatch admission using existing fixtures; no new sleeps, polling, or per-test Gateway boots. Wall time includes compilation/imports and host contention; the marking file previously passed in 45.70 s. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available.

The shutdown and claimless-startup regressions failed against the original behavior. After startup marking was fixed, archive classification failed independently. An added cancellation control also failed before preserving the terminal-outcome check. All now pass. Independent isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Changed-file formatting and lint, production types, all 28 selected test-type graphs, and the remaining policy/schema/import/authorization checks passed. `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` (run before committing) initially caught a test-fixture literal widened to `string`; an explicit session-entry type fixed it. The five unfinished type graphs then passed through `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-sessions","core-test-services-cron","core-test-ui-app","core-test-ui-components","core-test-ui-e2e-chat"]'` (41.40 s), and the remaining checks ran through the same exported changed-check planner.

One inherited check remains red: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` reports 16 unused exports in model-auth/prepared-model files and `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs` (98.79 s). The same command reproduced the exact same 16 findings on unchanged baseline `b66d8da2938d` in an isolated checkout (131.84 s). No changed file is in that list. The full-tree export scan passes. These unrelated findings were not suppressed or edited.

### Risk

Startup deliberately discovers more interrupted rows, so the important boundary is unfinished work versus a completed/cancelled turn or a current live owner. Those controls are covered and retained. Recovery uses the existing store, dispatch, retry, and delivery owners; it does not automatically replay an uncertain external side effect.

The historical lease log does not identify whether `operation.abortSignal` or inherited `workSignal` fired first for each turn. The prelude's inherited restart cancellation is identified from source and precedes marking; the fix tolerates either signal order and a missing shutdown marker. No live Gateway was modified or restarted for this work. This PR remains a draft.

prs.title: fix: reject the local Ollama placeholder during Cloud setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ollama Cloud onboarding accepts the local-only `ollama-local` placeholder as a hosted API key.

Related: #167433

## User Impact

Cloud setup now rejects the local placeholder with a link to obtain a real Ollama Cloud key. Local Ollama setup is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional API-key validator on the existing provider auth helper lets the Ollama plugin enforce its own credential rule after key/SecretRef resolution, before returning or persisting credentials. Interactive input and non-interactive flag, environment, and saved-profile credentials use the same check. Existing helper consumers retain their current behavior.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

- On the original implementation, all seven placeholder regression cases failed because setup accepted the local marker; the hosted-key control passed.
- Before the final lint-only fixture rename: **75 tests across 3 files passed**, covering full Ollama registration, all six Cloud-auth cases, and the shared provider API-key auth helper. Both file-size ratchets passed before the final test-context correction; extension-test typechecking passed with that correction.
- Runtime CLI proof: flag and environment placeholders are rejected with exit 1 before `--reset` changes the existing config or sentinel state. A synthetic non-placeholder key completes unattended setup with exit 0 and selects `ollama-cloud/minimax-m2.7`; this proves setup acceptance, not remote authentication.
- Targeted formatting passed. Local lint preparation timed out generating plugin SDK declarations before lint ran. The separate SDK API diff also failed during declaration rendering because its temporary checkout lost a Node type declaration; it produced no compatibility verdict. Hosted declaration, lint, and type checks remain required.
- The prompt-option fixture now uses a non-shadowing binding. Targeted type-aware oxlint passed, and all six Cloud-auth tests passed in 71.70 seconds (82.43 seconds including the test wrapper and worker cleanup). The branch also includes main's unused ownership-binding repair, `243b6dbf63d2d4c1bc7622ce67cd26c023c1bd64`.
- SDK surface attribution: this change adds one optional `validateApiKey` field to the existing helper options, not a new exported symbol. Its hosted report has 3,672 public exports, 2,133 callable exports, and 158 deprecated exports. A clean main control at `9b87a1a1f7d62df6480321fdde3595f15449e25d` reports exactly the same counts: branch minus main is **0 exports, 0 callable exports, and 0 deprecated exports**. Both also report one deprecated export in `conversation-binding-inspection-runtime` and three in `conversation-runtime`. The same budget failure is independently visible on unrelated #168724 in [this hosted job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38096055847/job/114342258289); its seven changed files do not include SDK exports or the Ollama auth helper. The existing budget drift is inherited, not growth caused by this optional field.

- The duplicate `createControlUiMockSameOriginGatewayScript` declaration in the mobile-sidebar e2e file was fixed on main by `48588a65222205adaa0187e62f683e046e1a9d3c`. This branch includes that main repair; no UI-specific change is part of this PR.

<details>
<summary>Isolated CLI capture (synthetic credentials)</summary>

`onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice ollama-cloud --ollama-cloud-api-key ollama-local --reset` exited 1:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Ollama Cloud requires a hosted API key from https://ollama.com/settings/keys; ollama-local is only for local Ollama hosts."
  }
}
```

The same command using `OLLAMA_API_KEY=ollama-local` also exited 1. In both cases the isolated fixture's existing config bytes and reset sentinel were preserved. With a synthetic non-placeholder key, unattended onboarding exited 0, returned `"ok": true` and `"authChoice": "ollama-cloud"`, and persisted primary model `ollama-cloud/minimax-m2.7`. Health checks were skipped: this is setup and reset-ordering proof, not a remote-authentication claim.

</details>

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous setup behavior. No config migration, credential rewrite, database change, or persisted format change. Blast radius is API-key setup; only Ollama Cloud opts into the new validation callback.

prs.title: fix(node-host): allow trailing whitespace in safe-bin commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Allowlisted POSIX node commands ending in a newline, space, or tab fail with `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: execution plan mismatch`. Authorization parses a trimmed payload, but the node runner compares that payload against the untrimmed argv token.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim trailing whitespace before matching the shell payload, then replace it with the command rebuilt from the authorization plan. Opaque transports and mismatched plans still fail closed. This restores accepted command behavior without adding configuration or changing the protocol.

## User Impact

Safe-bin commands sent through `node.invoke` / `system.run` run consistently with or without trailing whitespace. The separate Gateway-side safe-bin precheck for the agent `exec` tool is unchanged.

## Evidence

Validated head: `7b6ccfca61d7bf8c6cd0419c5b08c92ec71c7eff`.

- Secretless AWS, Node 24.21.0: `pnpm test src/node-host/invoke-system-run-allowlist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 7 passed, 1 Windows-only skip; 32.85 s wall time (Vitest 29.24 s).
- Same regression with the original production source fails because the newline payload returns `null`; the source was restored after the probe.
- Targeted formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 findings.
- Exact-head CI run [38018637174](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38018637174) passed.
- The contributor also supplied real Gateway → paired macOS node proof: newline and space/tab variants return the same `head` output as the clean command. Maintainer revalidation above is Linux boundary proof, not a repeat of that macOS run.

Production LOC: **0 net** (+1/−1); two changed files. The regression adds 55 test lines. No runtime-performance claim.

Thanks @yetval for the fix and original reproduction.

CI workflow wall time: 304 s in [run 38018637174](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38018637174); this includes shared checks and is not an isolated per-test cost.

prs.body:
Closes #136155

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where weekly skill collection reviews could never run for agents whose locked primary Anthropic model uses a Claude CLI subscription login and has no direct API credential. The review kept its intended primary model and disabled fallbacks, but it stayed on the direct provider path and failed before the configured CLI subscription seat could be used.

## Why This Change Was Made

The collection-review caller now opts into the existing subscription-auth CLI dispatch seam. This preserves the locked provider/model identity, empty fallback list, bounded `skill_workshop` tool allowlist, and proposal-only behavior while allowing eligible Claude CLI subscription credentials to execute through their owning backend. API-key-backed routes remain on the existing direct path because the dispatch gate already excludes them.

## User Impact

Agents configured with a Claude CLI subscription seat can complete automatic skill collection reviews without adding an Anthropic API key or widening the model fallback policy. Existing API-key users and non-eligible providers keep their current routing.

## Evidence

Failing baseline on current main before the production edit:

```text

  cliBackendDispatch: "subscription-auth"
received: field absent
```

prs.title: refactor(matrix): move thread bindings to workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix thread binding lookups and updates can access SQLite on the Gateway thread, and queued persistence must preserve newer binding changes and accepted activity.

## User Impact

Matrix binding reads use the worker-hydrated owner projection. Activity writes update the affected key, keep the existing coalescing policy, and publish committed facts before async completion. Shutdown drains accepted work before its final flush.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves Matrix thread binding persistence and all bundled adapters to the versioned async contract. Queued snapshots are captured at execution time; known partial commits reconcile acknowledged state, while unknown outcomes retire the manager. Released synchronous methods remain deprecated during the compatibility window. The session adapter is separated from persistence without introducing another state owner.

This is part 8 of the nine-part S7 state/binding migration stack. Targets `dbasync/sw7b-7-discovery` ([parent PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168484)); validation compares this part with its actual stack parent `37c6f593deb0`. The stack integrates pinned main `413d5f9bb3f7`.

## Evidence

Changed lines against the parent: production **+852 / -304**; tests and fixtures **+342 / -35**.

Focused integrated receipts cover Matrix thread persistence, subagent hooks, startup verification, and encryption: **48 passed, 0 skipped**, mapped to 4/4 changed test files. These are recorded integrated file versions, not independent runs of every prefix; per-part counts are not additive. prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes progress-card notes appearing in monospace in Telegram progress previews when a note has no checklist steps. ## User Impact Notes read as prose: bold when they are the headline, or unstyled beneath a progress label. Markdown and HTML-like characters in prepared plain notes remain literal. Rich-message and HTML output use the same styling. Render escaped literal text instead, and apply the same headline styling as other statuses. Rich messages still disable entity detection, and link previews remain disabled. Telegram may make bare URLs clickable in HTML mode; this is an accepted tradeoff rather than a reason to render prose as code. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. ## Evidence - Regression tests cover literal Markdown/HTML-like note text, label/no-label styling, and both Telegram output formats. - The existing native progress edit test now expects prose rather than a code entity. - On the unmodified baseline, the updated focused suite fails four cases specifically because notes are rendered as code (13 other cases pass). - All 29 focused tests pass on final head `cf5c681d15e931db31229306d656c775e0494b26`, including the registered progress-card integration suite (227.49 seconds wall time including runner setup). - A live Test Server run through the mock-model Gateway captured the progress `sendMessage` payload before and on that final head: - Before: `{"text":"Checking queues and jobs & results.","parse_mode":"HTML","link_preview_options":{"is_disabled":true}}` - After: `{"text":"Checking queues and jobs & results.","parse_mode":"HTML","link_preview_options":{"is_disabled":true}}` - The HTTP regression exercises `editMessageText` in both rich and HTML modes, including literal `&` and `` text. The live scenario emitted a progress send and a final send; native edit transport is covered by the HTTP regression. - Hosted review on the final head found no code findings and is ready for maintainer review. prs.title: fix: preserve keyboard focus when navigating scheduled tasks
prs.body:
Closes #127324

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost keyboard focus when opening a scheduled task, returning to the task list, or deleting the selected task.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can continue navigating without starting again from the page boundary. Returning to a task outside the visible list also brings its control into view. Focus moved elsewhere during a pending deletion is left alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel now remembers the originating task and hands focus to the next rendered control. Successful removal chooses a neighboring task in visual order, or the search field when the list is empty. Stale editor and reconnect completions cannot steal focus.

## Evidence

- Original main reproduced the missing Back-button focus after native keyboard selection. Before/after screenshots below use synthetic tasks and a mocked Gateway.
- 59 focused unit tests and 3 Chromium browser scenarios passed, including Back, next/previous/empty removal, promoted row ordering, 30 offscreen rows, cancellation, reconnects, and externally moved focus.
- All 10 selected core-test typegraphs passed. Formatting, structural guards, changed-file lint and coercion checks passed. Canonical `autoreview` found no P0/P1 defects.
- Repository-wide gates are not fully green: UI typecheck reports an unused `env` at `src/plugins/channel-presence-policy.ts:519`; the deadcode guard reports three existing `ChannelApprovalNative*Async` exports. Those files match base bytes and are not changed here.

Browser proof is Chromium with a mocked Gateway, not an operator deployment or a screen-reader audit. The after screenshot precedes a nonvisual controller-registration reorder; the exact final source separately passed the browser scenarios.
