prs.title: fix(gateway): keep routed CLI prompts off the owner's side in chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In sessions that run on the Claude CLI runtime, chat history merges the CLI's own transcript with the local OpenClaw transcript and drops imported rows that match a local row. Some imported user rows never matched, so the Control UI showed them as extra user bubbles, attributed to the human owner:

- Messages routed from another session (`sessions_send`, subagent completions). When a CLI session resumes after prompt drift, the drift note sits under the inter-session envelope, but `stripCliSessionDriftNote` only strips it at the start of the text. The imported copy had no provenance, so it showed the raw `[Inter-session message] ... isUser=false` envelope and the drift note as if the owner wrote it, next to the proper "From" row.
- Subagent settle messages. The local row stores the text without the envelope, the CLI row has it, so they never matched.
- Owner messages that went to the CLI with queued `System:` event lines above them. They showed twice, once with the system lines.

## User Impact

Routed messages show once, as the existing collapsed inter-session activity row, never as a bubble from the owner. Owner messages with queued system events show once. Stored transcripts, model prompts and routing are unchanged. Only the history merge and the imported row provenance change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `readInterSessionPromptEnvelope` reads the generated envelope (exact header plus the generated explanation line) and returns its provenance. Look-alike text is ignored.
- The Claude CLI importer records that provenance on imported user rows that start with the envelope, the same way it already records `cli_harness_context` and task notifications. It preserves the native text byte-for-byte so literal matching happens before any compare-only decoration removal.
- `stripCliSessionDriftNote` also matches the note right under an envelope.
- The merge (now in `src/gateway/cli-session-history-index.worker.ts` after #164419) matches imported user rows in this order. These are compare-only views; stored and displayed content is unchanged.
  1. Literal text.
  2. Text without OpenClaw-added context: the drift note and queued `System: [time]` event lines. A block of `System:` lines is only dropped when at least one line starts with a timestamp in the exact format the system event formatter writes (`[2026-09-30T17:16:38Z]`, `[2026-09-30 17:16:38 UTC]` or `[unknown-time]`), so typed `System:` text, including bracketed text like `System: [manual note]`, stays part of the prompt.
  3. Only for routed prompts: the body without the inter-session envelope, matched through a separate `routed_key` that includes the sender (source session and tool). A routed row only matches a row from the same sender, so equal bodies from different senders, or an owner message and a routed message with the same text, stay separate rows and keep their own CLI identity.

Rows that still fail to match now carry inter-session provenance, so the existing projection shows them as forwarded activity (or hides completion reports) instead of owner bubbles.

## Evidence

The evidence below was supplied on earlier revisions. Current-head maintainer proof is recorded separately below.

- Rebased onto current `main`. The history merge moved into the SQLite index worker (#164419), so the matching change now lives there. The new tests live in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.routed-prompts.test.ts` to stay under the test file line cap.
- Review follow-up (sender collisions): new regressions show that equal routed bodies from different source sessions stay separate rows and the wrong row does not get the other row's CLI identity, and that an owner message and a routed message with the same body stay separate. Removing the sender from the fallback key makes both tests fail.
- Also covered: a routed row stored without its envelope still matches its own import, with or without a drift note or queued event lines; typed `System:` lines without the generated timestamp stay part of the prompt.
- Second review follow-up: `System: [manual note]` above `done` no longer drops into the fallback and absorbs an unrelated local `done` turn. The new regression fails with the old `System: [` prefix check and passes now; UTC and `unknown-time` event lines are still stripped. `cli-session-history.routed-prompts.test.ts`: 10 passed, 46 s wall (mostly transform). `tsgo` on `tsconfig.core.json` passes.
- After the rebase: `pnpm test` on the CLI history, chat-history import, cli-session, input-provenance and operator-authority suites, 206 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core`, the gateway-root test typecheck, and the assertion, line-cap, max-lines, database-worker and test-timeout ratchets pass. The earlier `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure came from a new `as Record<string, unknown>` cast in `cli-session-history.claude.ts`; it is now an `isRecord` check.

- CI: the earlier `checks-node-changed-2` failure was a 120 s timeout in `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch-start.test.ts` ("uses the registered startup owner during cached queue"). This PR does not touch that area. `main` fixed that test in 6c42f8e696 ("test(agents): synchronize cached recovery execution observation"). Rebased onto `36c5dd3272` to pick it up. Locally, after the rebase: that file 5 passed in 27 s, `cli-session-history.routed-prompts.test.ts` 10 passed, `input-provenance.test.ts` 26 passed.

Earlier evidence (before the rebase):

- New tests in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts` (import provenance, look-alike rejection, dedupe under the envelope, subagent settle without envelope, system event lines) and `src/sessions/input-provenance.test.ts` (envelope parser). `cli-session-history`, `cli-session-history.claude-input`, `cli-session` and `input-provenance` suites: 125 passed.
- Replayed a real long-running Claude CLI session's local transcript and native CLI transcript through the merge and display projection, on main and on this branch. On main: 7 imported user rows with the inter-session envelope shown as owner bubbles. On this branch: 0. All other displayed rows are identical. A second, larger session went from 61 extra owner bubbles to 4. The 4 left are prompts with expanded media attachments or cron reminder text, a separate case.
- Control UI with the mocked Gateway, fed the projected history of the same synthetic transcript (main vs this branch):

Before: the relay shows twice, once as a raw owner bubble with the envelope and drift note, and the owner's own message shows twice, once with the `System:` line.

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rogeriochaves/openclaw/d85b0200162b8f9b5624595d1510b995d96509ac/ui-inter-session-cli-history/before.png)

After: one collapsed "1 update from Ops" row and the owner's message once.

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rogeriochaves/openclaw/d85b0200162b8f9b5624595d1510b995d96509ac/ui-inter-session-cli-history/after.png)

## Maintainer shepherding (2026-10-10)

Current head: `170602f2baf7ee3b3d5963a22df5fbd3cbac617d`. Rebased onto main `48588a65222205adaa0187e62f683e046e1a9d3c`; non-draft, independently mergeable.

- Removed eager importer drift-note stripping: native text remains byte-identical until literal matching completes.
- Added real JSONL importer-to-index regressions for string and text-block messages with colliding plain and decorated canonical turns.
- Retained main's normalized role/timestamp handling and removal of redundant history-comparison wrappers during conflict resolution.

Scope/LOC: production +172 net; tests +324 net (10 lines are formatter wrapping). Growth implements bounded native-input classification/provenance and sender-scoped matching at the existing importer/index owner boundaries; no configuration, durable database schema, or stored transcript rewrite.

Integration note: #163521 and #166080 both touch the importer and matching worker. Each is conflict-free against main; whichever lands second will need an integration rebase preserving raw-before-match ordering and forwarded-input provenance. No merge is authorized by this shepherding request.

Rebased onto `48588a652222` to pick up main’s shared UI-import, wrapper-inventory, and typecheck repairs. No unrelated CI workaround was added to either PR.
The new literal-match regression now asserts canonical `cliMeta` identity fields rather than expecting the native-only record `id` to survive canonical merge. It still distinguishes which canonical row consumed the imported message.

### Current maintainer proof

AWS Crabbox [candidate run_feae49a5acade8474a9c09c55a51f55e](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_feae49a5acade8474a9c09c55a51f55e), code head `0e32bb69fa242ae164e865b8562ca73d5f2215d5`, Node 24.21.0 / pnpm 12.9.0, 16 GB memory: **107 tests passed** across `src/gateway/cli-session-history.routed-prompts.test.ts`, `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`, `src/sessions/input-provenance.test.ts`, and `src/agents/cli-session.test.ts`, with one worker. The run then identified formatting in the routed-prompts test file; no behavioral failure occurred.

[Formatter + negative-control run_4de7087719b8e594d4c7c7371a76a37c](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4de7087719b8e594d4c7c7371a76a37c) applied the formatter and retained current tests while substituting only the earlier importer (`6a6a8f4d80c044a211e8b701f6d376727d20ac94`). **Both** literal string/text-block matching regressions fail as expected. Candidate importer restored afterward. The exact formatter diff was copied into final head `170602f2baf7ee3b3d5963a22df5fbd3cbac617d`; this final commit changes whitespace only. Fresh final-head CI verifies that formatting.

Both runs used a fresh public-network AWS machine with no instance role, no Tailscale, isolated HOME, and trusted bootstrap verification of the exact SHA and absence of IAM credentials before contributor execution. This proves native JSONL import and canonical-index matching; the earlier contributor screenshots remain the visual projection evidence.

Earlier 2 GB AWS fallback attempts were killed during subprocess compilation and are not counted as behavioral proof. No production/test workaround was added.

### Running compiled-Gateway attribution proof

[Exact-head Gateway trace: run_12eecc04ab5c929395644a7f4f8efea2](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_12eecc04ab5c929395644a7f4f8efea2), head `170602f2baf7ee3b3d5963a22df5fbd3cbac617d`. Built with `pnpm build`, started **`node dist/index.js gateway`**, and queried **`gateway call chat.history --json`** twice from separate CLI processes against the running Gateway. Agent model selection explicitly uses Claude CLI. Isolated canonical SQLite rows plus synthetic native Claude JSONL contain a routed prompt with the producer-built envelope and drift note, a queued-event owner prompt, an unmatched forwarded row, and equal-text owner/second-sender controls.

Both reloads return five displayed rows. The routed native row is absorbed by its canonical row and contributes `externalId: routed-native`; the other sender and owner keep their distinct native identities. Relevant response fields (synthetic data; opaque transcript IDs omitted):

```json
[
  {"role":"user","content":"OWNER_CHECK","externalId":"owner-native"},
  {"role":"assistant","content":"ROUTED_CHECK","senderLabel":"Forwarded from ops","sourceSessionKey":"agent:ops:main","sourceTool":"sessions_send","externalId":"routed-native"},

The linked passing run exercises the shipped history RPC and rebuilt worker output; earlier contributor screenshots cover presentation. prs.title: fix(agents): resume interrupted turns after session preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted turns could remain stranded after a Gateway update when startup recovery encountered a session still initializing or preparing its workspace. Recovery treated that transient block as a terminal operator decision and never revisited it.

## User Impact

Startup candidates resume when preparation completes, including after a transient recovery read failure. Archived, expired, restart-tombstoned, and provider-review-blocked sessions retain their existing restrictions. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The work-start owner supplies the blocking reason and whether preparation can resolve it. The existing startup scheduler retains pending candidates, rechecks their exact identity after committed session changes, and uses its bounded retry/backoff when preparation-triggered reads fail. Existing admission and durable recovery claims still own dispatch and exhaustion. Shutdown cancels the wait; replacement invalidates the captured candidate.

Candidate diagnostics name bounded conditions such as `initialization_pending` and `workspace_pending`. Historical logs recorded only `work_start_blocked`, so the original blocking field cannot be reconstructed from them.

Production LOC is +149 (176 added, 27 removed). The growth preserves one authoritative work-start policy and lifecycle-bound waiting/retry ownership; it adds no polling, persistent state, or separate recovery service.

## Evidence

- Baseline Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4kp1n54bk1xyrk4vk7nmms9`: both readiness regressions fail after their blocking fields clear (0/2 resumed). The added transient-read regression also fails on the preceding PR code.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4ktsc7hg848k27a59bwacws`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=10000` passes 19/19. Both readiness cases resume once; archive/replacement remain protected; a transient read retries without charging an attempt. Vitest duration 22.63s, wrapper 41.08s; the five added cases total approximately 4.2 test-seconds on that runner and use fake time for retry.
- Final AWS Crabbox `cbx_139228b4c282`, pinned head `97ca647e748e25fd23baac8721473af594aacb93` with source hashes checked: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions src/agents/main-session-recovery` passes 3,722 tests across 332 files; one existing opt-in snapshot benchmark is skipped. prs.title: fix(cron): avoid duplicate thinking metadata discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate live thinking-capability discovery when an isolated cron turn prepares and then executes the same model.

Related: #168566
Related: #168605

## User Impact

Cron turns reuse their per-candidate live metadata while preserving fallback model hydration, live thinking-level validation, and late discovery results. No configuration or persisted-state changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit 1a6d781104c (#168566) correctly removed the `needsThinkHydration` shortcuts so stale catalog rows cannot override live capabilities. It exposed a second lookup for the primary candidate: preparation and execution both queried the same provider/model/runtime. Commit e52cbaafcca (#168605) preserves fallback after provider timeouts by correcting context-engine finalization; it does not cause the duplicate lookup, and this change leaves its fallback behavior untouched.

The failing regression's four `loadModelCatalogMock` calls on main are:

1. The admitted full owner snapshot, with config/agent/workspace context but **no provider, model, or runtime selector**.
2. Preparation: `openai` / `gpt-5.6-sol` / `openclaw`.
3. Primary execution: `openai` / `gpt-5.6-sol` / `openclaw` again.
4. Fallback execution: `ollama` / `minimax-m3:cloud` / `openclaw`.

The old expectation of two counted the owner snapshot and fallback hydration, before the live-capability shortcuts were removed. Four is not minimal: the correct path is one owner snapshot plus two distinct candidate hydrations. The regression now supplies the owner snapshot independently and still requires exactly two live lookups, with exact candidate selectors and unchanged `off` / `medium` execution assertions.

Cache discovery promises within one thinking selection, keyed by provider/model/runtime, and reuse them between preparation, execution and retries. Cache the underlying discovery, not the timeout fallback, so discovery that finishes after the foreground timeout remains observable.

Move the two runtime-thinking cases into the existing thinking-capability test file to keep the forwarding file below its line cap without dropping coverage.

No overlap with designated maintainer changes in the affected files.

## Evidence

- Clean-main failure retained in pueue task 2358: 19 passed, the fallback hydration case failed with four calls instead of two.
- Whole forwarding file: 20/20 passed before moving its two thinking cases to the existing capability suite.
- Final isolated-agent suite: 45 files / 493 tests passed, including the full forwarding file and relocated thinking cases. Two earlier launches were terminated by the runner's 120-second no-output watchdog during startup; the completed run used a 300-second silence window, with test timeouts and assertions unchanged.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: formatting, line-cap ratchets, core typecheck and all 28 core-test type graphs passed. The command stops on inherited Knip exports in untouched model-auth modules, `prepared-model-runtime.ts`, and `tools/solid-lint/index.mjs`; no new unused exports. The known UI 722/720 root budget was not reached by this command.
- The existing late-discovery test additionally requires a single lookup while still observing the refreshed metadata after timeout.

## Gateway proof

Observed on built head `3b8c0b6054f58058a0f05cef072eea04d099ab60`, after merging current main (including `00e095399b2`). Started the real Gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`, using isolated config/state/workspace and loopback ports, then created and ran an isolated cron job through the supported CLI with `--thinking low --no-deliver`.

The primary was a configured local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint returning 503; the fallback was a configured direct `https://api.openai.com/v1` Responses route using real `gpt-5-nano`. The provider key was injected only into the process environment. Neither catalog nor runner boundaries were mocked or replaced. Existing debug logs show the real harness, transport, fallback decision, and durable cron result. Non-mutating Node Inspector conditional logpoints observe the actual built catalog/cache functions because those functions have no per-call debug event.

Redacted trace (local timestamps, unrelated startup output omitted):

```text
05:05:24.401 cron-selection-read provider=cron-proof-primary model=primary runtime=openclaw cached=false
05:05:24.404 provider-scoped-read provider=cron-proof-primary model=primary runtime=openclaw

05:05:27.371 embedded run start provider=cron-proof-primary model=primary thinking=low
05:05:31.303 model-fetch response provider=cron-proof-primary model=primary status=503
... ordinary same-model retries: eight primary HTTP requests total, no additional catalog reads ...
05:06:54.770 cron-selection-read provider=cron-proof-live model=gpt-5-nano runtime=openclaw cached=false
05:06:54.771 provider-scoped-read provider=cron-proof-live model=gpt-5-nano runtime=openclaw

Exactly one primary provider-scoped thinking read was reused at execution and across transport retries; the fallback received its own single read and completed a real provider turn. The Gateway shut down cleanly afterward. Build and live run completed through pueue; the checkout's built artifacts were reused without another build.

prs.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets
prs.body:
Related: #70903

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who resolve a provider billing or usage condition before its recorded reset time stay locked out of the saved auth profile until the stored window expires. There is no supported way to clear it, and the `models auth list` / doctor billing hint is a dead end.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New `openclaw models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>`: one owner-routed, locked write that resets the persisted cooldown, block, disable, and failure counters. It does not touch credentials or auth order. After the write it runs the same shared Gateway auth refresh (`models.authRefresh`) as the sibling `models auth` write commands, so no manual Gateway restart is needed.
- The `models auth list` / `models status` / doctor billing hint now names this command, including `--agent <id>` for the store it came from, because the mutation path rejects an ambiguous agent roster.
- Inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` failures have a health record (`inline-api-key:<provider>`) but no profile row. The command accepts that id when the record exists, so the hint shown for inline keys also works.
- `usage.ts` is a grandfathered oversized file, so the line-cap ratchet rejects any growth there. `updateOwnedAuthProfileUsage` moved unchanged into `usage-owner-write.ts`, next to the new reset. The dropped-bookkeeping log comes from `main`'s `state-observation.ts`. `usage.ts` shrinks by 29 lines (751 → 722). The move adds no test seam: the dropped-write test mocks the `store-runtime.js` module boundary, as `main` does since #164320.

It does not add polling, shorten provider backoffs, change fallback policy, or remove credentials.

## User Impact

Operators can re-evaluate a recovered provider with one command, without editing SQLite or repeating OAuth. If the failure still applies, the next request restores the cooldown normally.

## Evidence

Head `ba7b9103fb4`, on `main` at `4db022470af`. The last three commits address the Codex reviews on `804b5aa5bf7` and `0f6409cb35a`:

- **Inline keys (P1):** `clear-cooldown` accepted only saved profile rows, so `inline-api-key:<provider>` ids failed as "not found". It now accepts them. A real-store test records an inline billing failure, clears it through `clearAuthProfileCooldown`, and rereads the persisted store.
- **Agent in hints (P2):** the hints from `auth list`, `status`, and doctor now include `--agent`. The status row mapping moved unchanged into `auth-unavailability.ts`, so the grandfathered `list.status-command.ts` shrinks instead of growing.
- **Override store (P2):** `models status` under `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` / `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` reads a store that no `--agent` target reaches, so its billing hint omits the command instead of pointing at another store.
- **Shared state-db (P2):** doctor's Shared target now takes the agent that owns the shared-main dir, so state-db layouts also get `--agent`.
- **Broad mock (P1):** `usage-owner-write.test.ts` mocks only the locked writer, with a `mock-isolation` reason, instead of an `importOriginal` partial mock of the store runtime.

Results on this head:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --maxWorkers=1` passed on all 12 affected test files:
  - `auth-clear-cooldown`, `auth-unavailability` (new), `auth-list`, `list.status`
  - `doctor-auth.profile-health`, `models-cli`, `root-command-descriptions`
  - `usage-owner-write`, `usage.inherited-owner`, `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure`
  - `oauth-refresh-failure`, `failure-copy`
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `tsgo` test configs `core.test.agents-other`, `agents-root`, `commands`, and `commands-doctor` passed.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base upstream/main`, `check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main`, and `check:max-lines-ratchet` reported OK.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, plus `git diff --check`, were clean.
- The intermediate commit `a5c7d4e3ffa` alone fails the line-cap ratchet on `list.status.test.ts`; `0f6409cb35a` fixes it.

## Remaining merge evidence

- No inspectable real-flow proof yet of: blocked profile -> `models auth clear-cooldown <profileId>` -> Gateway auth refresh -> recovered provider request.
- Maintainer approval of the user-facing CLI contract is still required before merge.

prs.title: fix(plugins): reject embedded runs whose sessionId disagrees with the key's persisted identity
prs.body:
Closes #120787

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveRunSessionExecutionOwner()` derives the ownership scan scope (`agentId`, `storePath`) from the plugin-supplied session key. `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned()` then scans only that one scoped store, so a plugin-supplied `sessionId` that actually lives in a *different* agent/store is never observed - the ownership check silently passes. The caller's key then binds to a bogus fresh window in its own store instead of executing the foreign session (downstream binding anchors to the key-derived store), but the identity guarantee is broken and integrity-polluting windows get created.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scoped scan cannot see cross-store ids by design, so absence there must not imply safety when the caller also supplied a concrete id. This adds a fail-closed check after the existing scan in `src/plugins/registry-runtime-session-ownership.ts` (reached from `src/plugins/registry-runtime.ts` via `loadSessionOwnership()`):

```ts
if (directSessionId && sessionKey && entry && entry.sessionId !== directSessionId) {
  throw new Error(
    `Plugin "${pluginId}" may execute session "${sessionKey}" only with its exact persisted identity.`,
  );
}
```

Deliberate ordering and scope:
- Placed **after** `assertSessionIdentitiesOwned` so same-store mismatches keep their richer pre-existing ownership error (the scan finds locked foreign rows in the same store).
- Only fires when the plugin supplies both a session key with a resolvable entry *and* a differing explicit id; fresh-session create flows (id absent from stores, no key/entry) are unaffected.
- Locked-session flows return earlier with their own stricter identity rules.

## User Impact

- Embedded runs that pair an owned key with a foreign/differing session id are now rejected up front instead of silently creating a bogus execution window.
- Legitimate flows (matching id/key pairs, create-on-run, incognito scans) behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Focused proof (Windows, Node v24.15.0): `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run ``src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.sqlite.test.ts`` src/plugins/registry.runtime-config.test.ts` -> 2 passed + 16 passed.

Update: the production guard landed after review feedback (it was correctly flagged as missing from the initial head) — the check above is now in the diff. New regression test uses real per-agent SQLite stores: victim harness-locked session lives in agent `main`'s store while the caller owns a key in agent `researcher`'s store; `{sessionId: victimId, sessionKey: ownKey}` previously resolved (mock executed), now rejects with the exact-identity error and never reaches `runEmbeddedAgent`. The pre-existing same-store case still asserts its original `'owned by plugin "harness-owner"'` error.

prs.title: fix(googlechat): delete typing placeholder when a turn delivers no reply
prs.body: Closes #127567 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Google Chat users would see a permanent "OpenClaw is typing..." message when a turn produced no reply. In the default `typingIndicator: "message"` mode the placeholder is a real, durable message in the space, not a transient indicator. Its only owner is the reply-delivery path, so a turn that resolves silently (NO_REPLY), is cancelled, or throws before the first delivery leaves the placeholder sitting in the space with nothing left to remove it. ## Why This Change Was Made The monitor now keeps explicit custody of the placeholder for the whole inbound run. The first delivery claims it (clearing the outer reference before awaiting), and a run-level `finally` deletes it only when no delivery ever claimed it. Claiming before the await matters: `deliverGoogleChatReply` already owns thread-mismatch deletes, media-only deletes, and ambiguous PATCH outcomes, so the outer cleanup must never second-guess a placeholder delivery has taken over — including when delivery itself fails. Cleanup failures are logged through the existing error sink and never replace the turn's own outcome. Production +17/-6 LOC in `monitor.ts` (the rest of that file's diff is indentation from the added `try`); one new focused test file. ## User Impact A Google Chat turn that produces no reply no longer leaves a misleading "is typing..." message behind. Normal replies are unchanged — the placeholder is still edited in place into the first chunk. ## Evidence All results below are on the current head `5d0a48973da`, rebased onto `main` at `d5e94ecc093`. That rebase merged by hand with `main`'s `normalizeGoogleChatReplyTarget` reply-target change in the same block. Production delta in `monitor.ts` is unchanged at net +17, and most of that file's diff is re-indentation from the added `try`. ### Focused tests (`extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.typing-cleanup.test.ts`) ``` ✓ deletes the unclaimed placeholder when the turn resolves without delivering a reply ✓ deletes the unclaimed placeholder when the turn throws before delivering a reply ✓ keeps the original turn failure when placeholder cleanup also fails ✓ ends placeholder custody with a deferred turn and sends a late retained delivery as a new message ✓ leaves placeholder deletion to delivery once a reply claims it Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` Red-then-green: with `monitor.ts` swapped for current `main`'s version (`d5e94ecc093`) and the tests kept: ``` Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 4 failed | 1 passed (5) ``` The four failures are the silent-resolution, throw-before-delivery, cleanup-failure, and deferred-turn cases. The claimed-delivery case passes either way, by design. **Deferred turns.** This was raised in review and checked against core source. When a message queues behind an active run, `inbound.run` returns after `onDeferred` without delivering (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/lifecycle.ts`). The queued follow-up later delivers through the origin outbound route (`routeReply`, `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.ts`). That route posts a new message and has no reference to the placeholder, so holding the placeholder until settlement would never let anything edit it. The only way back into the retained per-turn `deliver` is a failed origin send. Even then, the drain keeps only the most recent follow-up callback per queue key (`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts`), so that callback may belong to a different turn. Deleting at `inbound.run` return is therefore the correct boundary. The deferred-turn test above pins this: one delete when the run returns, and a late retained delivery posts a new message with no edit and no second delete. ### Suites and gates - `pnpm test extensions/googlechat`: 34 files, 312 tests passed. - `pnpm check:changed`: exit 0. This covers format, extension prod and test typecheck, lint, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries, coercion and deprecated-API guards, and import cycles (0 runtime value cycles). - CI on `5d0a48973da` (run 36869732147) is green, including `check-lint`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. CI's change classifier skipped `build-artifacts` for this diff. I did not rerun a full local `pnpm build` on this head because the local build heap guard needs about 4.4 GB. ### Real Google Chat behavior: not available from the contributor side - **Live workspace.** I don't have a Google Workspace with a Chat app, service account, and webhook audience configured. Setting one up needs org-admin Workspace access, which I can't get as an outside contributor. - **Mock-gateway harness.** QA Lab's Crabline transport can run a real channel plugin against a local mock of the platform API, but its server channels are currently `discord, mattermost, matrix, signal, slack, telegram, whatsapp, zalo` (`CRABLINE_SERVER_CHANNELS` in `@openclaw/crabline`). Google Chat isn't supported, so there is no harness path for this plugin today. The evidence is therefore source-level, plus tests that drive the real `monitor.ts` event processor and mock only `core.channel.inbound.run` and the Google Chat HTTP API. If a maintainer has a Chat-enabled Workspace, these steps would verify it in a few minutes with the default `typingIndicator: "message"`: 1. Send a message that resolves with `NO_REPLY`. The "is typing..." message should appear and then be deleted. 2. Send a normal prompt. The placeholder should be edited in place into the reply. 3. Send two messages back to back so the second queues behind the first. The second placeholder should be deleted once its run returns, and its reply should arrive as a new message. ---

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve continuity across races and paginated history
prs.body:
Closes #114302
Closes #114304
Closes #114305
Closes #114306
Closes #114308

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes five Codex continuity failures where users could lose a message during a request-input race, fail to continue or fork paginated threads, leave request handlers running after disconnect, or miss client-close cleanup when observers throw or subscribe late.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change honors the compare-and-resolve result before steering, adds one validated full-history reader for paginated and inline Codex threads, and makes the client close transition abort active inbound handlers while delivering terminal state to every observer exactly once. The implementation follows the currently checked-out official Codex app-server contracts and remains internal to the Codex extension.

## User Impact

Messages survive request-input resolution races, paginated threads can be continued/materialized/message-forked, and disconnect cleanup is deterministic across active, throwing, and late observers.

## Evidence

- Steering, fork boundary, catalog, and lifecycle group: 227/227 passed.
- Client, shared-client, and turn-router group: 112/112 passed.
- User-input bridge: 6/6 passed.
- Upstream session fork: 6/6 passed.
- Production extensions typecheck, targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, public Plugin SDK surface, protected-path, and secret scans passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no actionable findings, correctness 0.98.
- Official Codex source was inspected at `18f50c9e628af083a52d9240de09fc2db24d79ce` for paginated-history and request-resolution semantics.
- AI-assisted implementation and review; no public Plugin SDK or generated protocol boundary changed.

prs.title: feat: preserve native question custody and recovery across Gateway restarts
prs.body:
Related: #167266

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary human-input workflows lose their pending question and continuation when the Gateway process restarts.

## User Impact

Recoverable native callers can hand off the asking turn, return after a Gateway restart, and answer the same question with its original deadline. The first committed answer owns one explicit continuation in the original conversation. Blocked or interrupted continuations retain the answer and show the next action.

**Maintainer design acceptance is required before merge.** This is a preparatory implementation of the proposed storage and recovery contract; it does not claim that the issue discussion accepted that contract.

**Storage upgrade:** per-agent schema 25 becomes 26 through the existing stopped-writer Doctor migration. Back up before upgrading. Older binaries refuse the upgraded database; rollback requires restoring the complete pre-upgrade backup with its matching binary. Pending and owed work remains retained; terminal continuation receipts expire after 24 hours. Capacity is bounded with visible refusal, without evicting obligations or native recovery exclusions. Legacy synchronous session deletion or generation replacement refuses durable-owned sessions before mutation; those operations must use the existing asynchronous worker owner. Alias canonicalization refuses relocation while durable native recovery exclusions remain, preserving the original session and recovery fences instead of discarding them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing native question owner gains canonical SQLite worker custody rather than a second database or scheduler. Registration precedes publication, settlement precedes acknowledgement, and the native session queue admits an exact conversation generation under the original caller's current authority. A previously admitted continuation is interrupted after process loss; ambiguous model or tool effects are not automatically replayed.

Secret, MCP, incognito, and callers without recoverable native authority retain their existing transient contract. Durable capability is acknowledged explicitly, and existing clients receive their original record shape unless they request continuation receipts.

Channel recovery revalidates the stored linked principal and current native command authority for accepted work. It does not repeat adapter ingress admission or claim that every changed channel allowlist was rechecked. Native mixed recovery cohorts without independent replay provenance retain unrelated work and require an explicit new user turn. Existing delivery ownership is preserved; unsafe orphan prepared output is retained rather than replayed through the model.

Existing ordinary channel conversations without a native lifecycle revision require an explicit native `/new` or reset before durable `ask_user` can be accepted. This PR establishes the revision for newly created ordinary inbound conversations; it preserves existing generations and does not backfill them during Doctor migration. A durable registration rejected for missing generation is not acknowledged or silently converted to durable work.

Longer deadlines remain a separate compatibility and product decision: the current 900-second default and 3,600-second ceiling are unchanged. The issue's six-day/seven-day acceptance target is not resolved by this PR.

## Evidence

The published `dc961f75` checkpoint passed 52 question RPC cases, 30 terminal dispatcher/work-owner cases, 19 startup/refusal/readiness cases, and three actual Gateway restart/crash scenarios. Those are prior-head results, not a claim that every successor check has run.

Successor repairs address the first CI run's feature-owned wrapper closure, Gateway inventory order, import cycles, worker-export classification, UI refresh races/template growth, and historical schema migration failures. Native wrapper eager-load coverage passes all 17 cases. The actual historical migration/maintenance/snapshot/provision cohort passes 125 cases (412.06-second native wrapper; two existing skips), including schema-14 upgrade and schema-23/24 question-table migration. The authorized missing-generation diagnostic and genuinely foreign-created session refusal pass all 29 Gateway cases.

Fresh storage review regressions first demonstrated that 25→26 preservation accepted deletion of existing pending canonical-validation work and mutation of `canonical_ready`. Both are repaired without weakening the schema-24 canonical-writer migration. All 34 selected witness/canonical-migration/Doctor cases pass (57.59-second native wrapper). Doctor coverage includes original sealed backups, partial migration, stale registry registration, and retry.

The shared Control UI owner passes all 72 selected cases. Four mounted question-document cases pass against the built UI (12.83-second Vitest wall time), including blocked/interrupted receipts surviving a late initial read after live resolution. The two new browser regressions failed with the receipt absent before the revision/identity repair. The existing two chat recovery cases produced the inspected captures below.

Core/UI types, affected test graphs, changed-path lint, import-cycle analysis, and the native line-cap, suppression, assertion, timeout, and mock-export guards are checked locally. Fresh independent successor review completed all three passes with no actionable P0–P2 findings after the two verified review defects were repaired. This is scoped code review, not maintainer design acceptance.

Queued-authority proof uses a real same-session foreground turn, the exact canonical claimed continuation, and live Gateway RPC unlink/reassignment while it remains queued. The allowed comparison passes after correcting the fixture's exec working directory and checking its native tool-result success marker (81.10-second test body). The unlink and reassignment cases passed in the preceding local run (80.97/81.14-second bodies); the admission/execution authority owners were unchanged by the subsequent witness/page repairs. No authenticated live Telegram claim is made.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Original principal allowed | 0 | settled | 2 | verified | 1, original recipient |
| Original principal unlinked | 0 | interrupted | 0 | absent | 0 |
| Sender reassigned to another principal | 0 | interrupted | 0 | absent | 0 |

The opt-in installed-stable proof passes using the actual npm `openclaw@2026.9.9` binary and isolated native state. It persists history and usage cache at schemas 24/19, creates and verifies a complete native backup, runs stopped candidate Doctor to 26/20 with the same cache digest, and confirms stable startup refuses the newer installation without changing canonical database digests. Native backup restoration then returns 24/19, the original cache digest, and working stable Doctor/Gateway/history/cache (121.44-second test body). The two corrected selected process cases pass in a 561.75-second wrapper including fresh private-QA runtime/declaration preparation; four other channel cases were intentionally unselected in that corrective run.

[The first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38045882515) also contains inherited failures independently reproduced at its exact main parent `6a9bccad9eca07ce9a461cae026785a2dd743dab`: missing managed-cleanup modules in copied docs/package harnesses, macOS launch nonce cleanup assertions, Gateway test typing, guest GitHub publication buttons, Bun cohort commentary mock pollution, `sessions.send` communication-target assertions, prepared-model hot reload, and the CLI models refresh assertion. The Bun reproduction used the exact CI-pinned canary and full selected cohort; isolated commentary tests pass. These are historical inherited failures, not repaired feature cases. Subsequent main changes repair some of these fixtures, so this list is not a claim that each still blocks the current head. No full current aggregate green or authenticated live Telegram/Slack proof is claimed. The channel tests use an actual bundled Telegram adapter and isolated local Bot API boundary.

The completed `c85477ed17dd` [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38049876762) used main parent `34128f148ebe`. Its introduced architecture failure was the extracted stopped-migration finalizer missing from the native raw-SQL schema/migration classification. `29c9e2cb00a` adds exactly that owner path; the full native `pnpm lint:kysely` check passes, and fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defect in that two-line change. No ordinary SQLite access or constructor guard is exempted.

On clean main `34128f148ebe`, native runs independently reproduce the same docs copied-module failure, native-launch nonce assertions, five UI geometry/history assertions, worker-placement assertion, three Agents API steering failures, two memory reindex-backoff failures, two Docker manifest failures, prepared-model hot-reload assertion, and damaged-archive cold-recall failure. The latter two run together: two failures and 22 passes in a 46.62-second native wrapper. These are attributed main failures, not feature regressions. Clean-main `sessions.send` reproduces all four communication-target failures with six passes (366.46-second wrapper including a fresh 270.5-second runtime build). Using that verified matching runtime, CLI and package cases reproduce both assertions with 73 passes and three existing skips (45.33-second wrapper). The exact CI-pinned Bun canary reproduces the same four commentary host-admission failures in the main-matched CI cohort: 41 files, 419 passes, four failures, 93.63-second Vitest wall time. An earlier concurrent-build attempt was invalidated by changed generated dependency topology and is not used as evidence.

The historical `29c9e2cb00a` checkpoint [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38050949395) is complete. All twelve failing test jobs are independently attributed to main: UI geometry/history, docs copied-runtime closure, worker placement, Docker workspace manifests, prepared-model hot reload, CLI refresh output, Gateway `sessions.send`, Agents API steering, memory backoff, damaged-archive cold recall, and pinned-Bun commentary mock pollution. No feature-owned failure remains observed at this head. The required aggregate gate is red because the selected UI and Node test groups are red; `security-fast` passes. That checkpoint was `MERGEABLE/BLOCKED`, not aggregate green. Its computed merge parent `e3415ea8c554` includes the independent main fix for package/native-launch fixtures. The architecture guard is green at this exact head. This run is prior-head evidence after the subsequent conflict repair; it is not successor-head CI. All eight failing UI geometry/history cases in that run independently reproduce against clean main at that exact newer parent, with the same bounds and offsets (27.04-second Vitest wall time; 17 intentionally unselected cases). This includes the three additional mobile failures introduced into the selected cohort after the main UI change. Other inherited reproductions above remain bound to `34128f148ebe`; the intervening main delta does not change their selected tests or owning implementation. Package/native-launch fixtures are the named exception already fixed on main. The Telegram Test Server doctor also reports no supported authenticated Convex launcher or configured broker access; local adapter evidence remains scoped and live userbot proof is outstanding.

## Conflict repair and review follow-up

The successor integrates main `48588a652222` to resolve actual merge conflicts. It preserves main’s revision-bound SQLite writer receipts, worker mutation guards, shared read snapshots, and relocated transcript-test imports. Cache publication and its write receipt now share the existing cache owner; ordinary inbound generation creation stays in the existing normalization owner. The native worker inventory is regenerated without guard exceptions.

Two accepted independent review findings are repaired: caller-selected question IDs wait for durable recovery before global registration, and the busy-session crash proof distinguishes an already-claimed interrupted continuation from an owed continuation eligible for replay. Three readiness regressions demonstrated the registration race before the repair. The deterministic storage proof reopens a committed answer and invokes real recovery twice, offering the canonical owed continuation exactly once.

A receipt-only UI race candidate was declined after inspecting the production lifecycle: standalone routes are fixed at startup, reconnect invalidates earlier receipt work, and every resolution advances the prompt revision before fetching its receipt. No reachable caller establishing the reported ordering was found. This is a reviewed disposition, not a claim that the independent report contained zero candidates.

The repaired readiness suite passes all nine cases. The native session and custody suites pass 100 and 14 cases respectively (719.69-second combined wrapper including the readiness shard). After the cache-owner move, custody, replacement-receipt, and identity-publication tests pass all 46 cases (208.16-second Vitest wall time). Core and UI types, affected test graphs, generated inventory, Kysely ownership, runtime import cycles, full Madge, and source line caps pass locally. The final native process proof passes both selected scenarios: busy-session answer ACK followed by immediate Gateway crash (81.52-second test body), and queued authorized Telegram-adapter continuation reaching a settled receipt, verified tool effect, and one original-recipient delivery (62.48-second test body). Four other channel cases are intentionally unselected. The 1,902.17-second Vitest wrapper includes fresh runtime preparation; the full native build itself takes 23 minutes 20.8 seconds on this host. No authenticated live Telegram proof is claimed. Older runtime proof above remains checkpoint-bound.

The first conflict-repaired checkpoint is `6f3143fad89173e4d246f6e88de76d24ae4d2718`. All affected test type graphs and changed-path lint pass; the normal merge commit also restores the correct main ancestry for the inherited environment-variable budget. Main advanced during that process proof, creating two additional conflicts, so this checkpoint is prior-head evidence rather than the final integration.

The final integration candidate is `f331ae61c58cb6967cfc31e2c95bd47153cc0256`, with main parent `00e095399b203a2c71ef773fcf8ea1177bc2a5ef`. Main’s newly added full-entry snapshot facts are forwarded through the moved cache publication function, while its revision-bound list postimage, physical write-token certification, and receipt capacity limit remain intact. Both test import sets are retained. The peer fixture moves unchanged into existing question test support to stay within the own-run suite’s line cap; no coverage is removed.

On this integration, all 112 focused cases pass (61 question authority cases plus 51 custody, replacement-receipt, and identity-publication cases; 350.42-second native wrapper). This includes upstream full-snapshot receipt and invalidation coverage. After the unchanged peer fixture move, all 29 own-run cases pass again (82.95-second wrapper). A fresh complete independent review returns no actionable P0–P2 findings in either pass. Affected test type graphs, changed-path lint, Kysely ownership, generated worker inventory, and runtime import cycles pass. The earlier native crash/channel process proof remains bound to `6f3143fad891`; it is not represented as rerun after this snapshot-receipt integration.

prs.title: fix(agent-core): preserve accepted handoff in tool settlement catches
prs.body:
Closes #126446

## What Problem This Solves

An accepted `sessions_yield` handoff intentionally aborts its active turn with `turnHandoff: true`. The abort-signal wrapper's pre-abort pre-check (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) threw `Error("Aborted")` with **no yield-handoff exemption** when the run signal was already aborted at wrapper-entry time, bypassing the non-rejecting race (`raceWithAbortSignal`). The execution catch (`readyExecution.execute` catch) then converted this to an error tool result, erasing the accepted continuation. The embedded run settled as `success` while the channel dispatcher had no queued reply payload — the user received no answer even though the delegated continuation was accepted.

## Root Cause

The non-rejecting exemption for `sessions_yield` handoffs lived **only** inside `raceWithAbortSignal` (`agent-tools.abort.ts:40-47`). The wrapper's pre-abort pre-check (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) runs **before** the race is set up and threw `createAbortError("Aborted")` unconditionally whenever `combinedSignal.aborted` was true — with no check for the yield-handoff reason. When the run signal was already aborted with `SESSIONS_YIELD_ABORT_REASON` (`{ code: "sessions_yield", turnHandoff: true }`), the pre-check threw `Error("Aborted")`, which the execution catch (`agent-loop.ts:1497-1509`) converted to `createErrorToolResult("Aborted")` — producing exactly the issue's symptom: `sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`.

The test at `agent-tools.runtime.test.ts:216-230` codified this behavior ("does not start sessions_yield when the run was already handed off" → rejects with `AbortError: "Aborted"`).

The delivery path then lost the reply: `buildEmbeddedRunPayloads` (`payloads.ts`) suppressed assistant text when `runAborted` was true, `terminal-resolution.ts:125-144` collapsed error-only payloads to `payloadCount = 0`, and `execution.ts:119` logged `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads`.

## Canonical Repair

**Producer fix (root cause)**: Add `isYieldHandoffAbort()` exemption to all three wrapper pre-checks (`execute`, `preparer`, `ready-closure`), matching `raceWithAbortSignal`'s four-part contract: `toolName === "sessions_yield"` AND `abortSignal.aborted` AND `combinedSignal.reason === abortSignal.reason` AND `reason.code === "sessions_yield"` AND `reason.turnHandoff === true`. When the run signal is already aborted with the canonical handoff reason, the pre-check no longer throws — the tool runs, calls `onYield`, and returns `{ yielded: true }` normally.

**Consumer fix (defense-in-depth)**:

- **Execution catch** (`readyExecution.execute` catch, `agent-loop.ts:1497`): preserves the handoff when the signal carries the marker (`isAcceptedYieldToolAbort`) AND the error is an `AbortError`. Returns a non-error result (`isError: false`). A genuine tool failure (non-`AbortError`, e.g. "yield bookkeeping failed") stays an error even when the signal has the marker.
- **`afterToolCall` catch** (`finalizeExecutedToolCall`, `agent-loop.ts:1612`): preserves the tool's already-produced result when both `isAcceptedYieldToolAbort(signal, toolName)` AND `isHandoffAbortError(error, signal)` match — i.e., the hook threw the signal's own reason object (e.g., via `signal.throwIfAborted()`) or an `Error` wrapping it as `cause`.
- **`afterToolOutcome` catch** (`finalizeToolCallOutcome`, `agent-loop.ts:1680`): same dual guard as `afterToolCall`.

A sibling tool's hook error, a different handoff owner setting `turnHandoff: true` on a tool merely named `sessions_yield`, or an unrelated `AbortError` is **not** masked (covered by regression tests).

## Scope of ClawSweeper P1 vs. This Fix

ClawSweeper's P1 finding ("Trace a production post-tool abort producer before preserving results") was raised against the **prior** version of this PR, which modified only the `afterToolCall` and `afterToolOutcome` settlement catches. The reviewer's core objection was that the inspected production `afterToolCall` callback delegates to an error-isolating extension runner (`dispatchHandlers` in `src/agents/sessions/extensions/runner.ts:700-707`), which catches handler errors internally without re-throwing, so **no production path was shown to throw the signal's handoff reason into either of those two catches**. The integration test replaced `session.agent.afterToolCall` wholesale to inject the fault — synthetic injection at a production boundary, not a traced production producer.

This revision changes the P1's premise by locating the **real** producer at a different boundary:

| Boundary | ClawSweeper P1 scope | This fix |
|---|---|---|
| **wrapper pre-check** (`agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87`) | Not inspected (prior PR did not touch the wrapper) | **Root-cause producer** — throws `Error("Aborted")` before `raceWithAbortSignal`, with no yield-handoff exemption. Traced and fixed. |
| **execution catch** (`readyExecution.execute` catch, `agent-loop.ts:1497`) | Not in P1 scope (prior PR explicitly left it unguarded, claiming "the yield tool returns normally") | **Direct consumer of the wrapper pre-check's throw** — guard added as defense-in-depth. The prior PR's premise ("yield tool returns normally, non-rejecting race") was incomplete: the non-rejecting exemption lives only inside `raceWithAbortSignal`, which the pre-check bypasses. |
| **`afterToolCall` catch** (`finalizeExecutedToolCall`, `agent-loop.ts:1612`) | P1 target — no production producer traced | **Still no production producer.** The production callback delegates to `dispatchHandlers`, which catches handler errors internally. Guard retained as defense-in-depth; the AgentSession integration test injects the fault by replacing the callback. |
| **`afterToolOutcome` catch** (`finalizeToolCallOutcome`, `agent-loop.ts:1680`) | P1 target — no production producer traced | **Still no production producer.** Same reasoning as `afterToolCall`. Guard retained as defense-in-depth. |

**What changed**: the issue's reported symptom (`sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`) is now traced to a concrete production code path — the wrapper pre-check throwing `Error("Aborted")` → the execution catch converting it to an error tool result → the delivery path collapsing the error-only payload to zero count. The prior P1 blocker ("no traced production producer") is resolved for the **execution catch** via the wrapper pre-check.

**What did not change**: the `afterToolCall` and `afterToolOutcome` catches still have no traced production producer. Their guards remain defense-in-depth: if a future callback or wrapper ever propagates the signal's reason (e.g., via `signal.throwIfAborted()`), the accepted handoff is preserved rather than erased. The issue itself names `finalizeExecutedToolCall` as a catch that "also rewrites the result to an error without consulting the handoff marker," so the guard is aligned with the issue's stated expectation even though the current production callback does not produce the throw.

## Evidence

### Root cause proof: wrapper pre-check produces `Error("Aborted")`

The wrapper pre-check at `agent-tools.abort.ts:85-87` (before fix):
```ts
if (combinedSignal.aborted) {
  throwAbortError();  // throws Error("Aborted") — NO yield-handoff exemption
}
```

This runs **before** `raceWithAbortSignal` (line 88), which is where the non-rejecting exemption lives (lines 40-47). When the run signal is already aborted with `SESSIONS_YIELD_ABORT_REASON`, the pre-check throws unconditionally.

The thrown error reaches the execution catch (`agent-loop.ts:1497-1509`), which converts it via `createErrorToolResult(coerceErrorMessage(error))` into `{ content: [{ text: "Aborted" }], isError: true }` — exactly the issue's `sessions_yield tool result: Aborted`.

### Focused committed proof (post-fix):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts
# 1 file, 31 tests passed (includes yield-handoff exemption tests)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts
# 1 file, 86 tests passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts -t "settlement fault-path"
# 1 file, 1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

### Updated wrapper test: yield-handoff exemption

The test at `agent-tools.runtime.test.ts` (formerly "does not start sessions_yield when the run was already handed off") now verifies the exemption:

```
it("lets sessions_yield run when the run was already handed off")
  → result.details: { status: "error" } (tool's own error, not "Aborted")
  → onYield not called (no claimYield)

it("preserves a sessions_yield result when the run was already handed off")
  → result.details: { status: "yielded", message: "Turn yielded." }
  → onYield called once
```

Format/lint/typecheck on touched files:

```
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts packages/agent-core/src/turn-interruption.ts   # All matched files use the correct format
node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts src/agents/agent-tools.runtime.test.ts packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts packages/agent-core/src/turn-interruption.ts           # 0 warnings, 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                  # no errors (exit 0)
```

### Boundary-level proof: embedded sessions_yield handoff through delivery

The existing qa-lab e2e suite covers the full accepted-yield lifecycle through external delivery: inbound trigger → `sessions_spawn` → child `sessions_yield` self-pause → requester stays parked (quiet window asserted) → follow-up run adoption (distinct gateway runId) → completion announce with exactly one outbound message. It runs against a real ephemeral gateway child process with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider and a mock channel transport (bus), not a unit mock.

```

✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts
  > plugin subagent sessions_yield follow-up
  > announces to the original requester only after the follow-up run ends

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

### Harness verdict JSON

```json

  "proof": "mock-gateway-yield-handoff-delivery",
  "command": "node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-self-yield-followup.e2e.test.ts",
  "harness": {
    "kind": "mock-gateway-ephemeral-child",
    "provider": "mock-openai (startQaMockOpenAiServer)",
    "channel": "qa-bus-mock (startQaBusServer + createQaChannelTransport)"
  },
  "flow": "inbound → sessions_spawn → child sessions_yield self-pause → requester parked (15s quiet window asserted) → follow-up run adoption (distinct gateway runId) → completion announce (exactly 1 outbound message)",
  "result": { "testsPassed": 1, "testsFailed": 0, "exitCode": 0 }
}
```

### Production-boundary fault-path proof: AgentSession integration test

A new integration test in `src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts` drives the fault through the real `AgentSession` → `Agent.prompt` → `runAgentLoop` → `config.afterToolCall` production call chain. It creates a real `AgentSession` via `createTestSession` (mock `streamSimple` provider), registers a `sessions_yield` tool that aborts with the canonical handoff marker, wraps `session.agent.afterToolCall` to throw `signal.reason` on the yield tool, and asserts the requester-visible delivery outcome.

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts -t "settlement fault-path"

✓ |agents-support| src/agents/sessions/agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts
  > AgentSession settlement fault-path
  > preserves the accepted sessions_yield handoff when afterToolCall throws  1666ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

### Fault-path coverage

| Path | Coverage | Pre-fix |
|---|---|---|
| wrapper pre-check — sessions_yield when run already aborted | agent-tools.runtime.test.ts (exemption test) | reject with "Aborted" (bug) |
| execution catch — AbortError after yield-handoff abort | agent-core unit (defense-in-depth guard) | rewrite to error (bug) |
| `afterToolCall` catch — hook throws signal.reason | AgentSession integration + agent-core unit | rewrite to error (bug) |
| `afterToolOutcome` catch — hook throws signal.reason | agent-core unit | rewrite to error (bug) |
| sibling tool hook error | agent-core unit (sibling regression) | pass (error preserved) |
| genuine yield-callback error (non-AbortError) | agent-core unit (genuine-error regression) | pass (error preserved) |
| different-owner handoff | agent-core unit | pass (error preserved) |
| non-handoff abort | agent-core unit (control) | pass (both) |
| happy-path yield→delivery | e2e (mock-gateway) | pass (both) |

### Known proof gaps

- **`afterToolCall` / `afterToolOutcome` catches have no traced production producer.** The production `afterToolCall` callback (`agent-session-base.ts:258`) delegates to `runner.emitToolResult` → `dispatchHandlers` (`runner.ts:700-707`), which catches handler errors internally without re-throwing. No production callback calls `signal.throwIfAborted()` or throws `signal.reason`. The AgentSession integration test replaces `session.agent.afterToolCall` to inject the fault — this is synthetic fault injection at a production boundary, not a traced production producer. These two guards are defense-in-depth, aligned with the issue's stated expectation that `finalizeExecutedToolCall` should consult the handoff marker.
- No live Telegram/Codex end-to-end run was executed; the boundary proof uses a mock-gateway harness with a mock OpenAI-compatible provider (per AGENTS.md the mock-gateway harness satisfies the real-behavior-proof gate for channel-visible changes covering the changed path).

## Diff Shape

- Production: `+132/-12` (net `+120`) — `isYieldHandoffAbort` helper + 3 pre-check exemptions in `agent-tools.abort.ts` (+30/-3), 3 helpers in `turn-interruption.ts` (+63/-6), execution catch guard + 2 settlement guards in `agent-loop.ts` (+39/-2), baseline cleanup (-1).
- Tests: `+785/-5` (net `+780`) — wrapper exemption tests, yield-preservation (execution/afterToolCall/afterToolOutcome), sibling-cancellation, genuine-error, different-owner, non-handoff control (agent-core unit); AgentSession integration fault-path.
- No config, protocol, schema-version, public API, or docs surface change.

Production growth is inherent to the fix: the wrapper pre-check exemption is the root-cause producer fix, and the three settlement-catch guards are defense-in-depth at distinct shared boundaries, all reusing the existing wrapper-layer tool-name and handoff-reason contracts.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): admit docker bind targets as exec workdirs like file tools
prs.body:
Closes #149941

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` rejects `workdir` under a `sandbox.docker.binds` target with `workdir "<path>" is unavailable or not a directory: command was not executed.` even though file tools read/write/list that same folder.

## User Impact

User impact: agents with an extra bind-mounted folder can run commands with `workdir` set inside it, consistent with the file tools' access to the same directory, instead of falling back to in-command `cd` on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec workdir resolver still validated against a pre-#148893 mount view (workspace + read-only skill mounts) while file tools moved to the authoritative `resolveSandboxMountSelection` (binds included), so the two tool families disagreed about the same configured mount. This adds a `bindMounts` field to the exec sandbox config, populates it in `createCoreCodingTools` from `buildSandboxFsMounts` (the same selection owner the file tools' fallback admission uses), and includes those mounts in the container→host workdir mapping table. Precedence stays deterministic (longest container root wins); binds shadowed by managed/protected targets are already excluded by the selection, and missing host directories still resolve to `unavailable`.

## Evidence

Red-green regression (pre-fix code via `git stash` of the production files):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` → new tests **fail pre-fix** (`{kind:"unavailable", requestedCwd:"/data"}`), **pass after** the fix (56/56 across both exec-workdir test files).
- Sibling suites green: `core-coding-tools.exec-workdir.test.ts`, `core-coding-tools.sandbox.test.ts` (70/70), `sandbox/workspace-mounts.test.ts` + `sandbox/fs-paths.test.ts` (41 passed, 3 skipped).

Runtime probe composing the exact production chain (`createSandboxTestContext` with `docker.binds: ["/tmp/bind-probe/data:/data"]` → `buildSandboxFsMounts` → exec sandbox config → `resolveExecWorkdir`), verbatim output:

```
selected bind mounts: [{"hostPath":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerPath":"/data"}]
=== exec workdir=/data, pre-fix config (no bindMounts) ===
{"kind":"unavailable","requestedCwd":"/data"}
=== exec workdir=/data, fixed config (bindMounts from mount selection) ===
{"kind":"sandbox","hostCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data","containerCwd":"/data","scriptPreflightCwd":"/tmp/bind-probe/data"}
```

Gates: `oxfmt` clean, `run-oxlint` 0 warnings/0 errors, `pnpm tsgo` (core) exit 0, `git diff --check` clean.

Not tested: a live Docker-sandbox exec (no Docker daemon on this host); the resolver and mount-selection layers above the engine are covered by the tests and probe, and the container-side `docker exec -w` behavior for an existing bind directory is unchanged. The autoreview helper's codex engine failed with an infra error (`codex engine failed (1)`, also seen on another PR today), so the pre-submit review was manual: additive optional config field, one call-site population, one mapping-table inclusion; no public SDK surface touched (`check-plugin-sdk-api-baseline` scope untouched).



Rebased onto current `main` (`26505c528b5`, head `9929483460b`): main renamed the boolean `includeShellTools` option to the tri-state `shellTools` in `CoreCodingToolsOptions`; the bind-mount admission now gates on `shellTools !== "disabled"` (same predicate main uses for sandbox admission). The `BashSandboxWorkdirMount` export flagged by the dependency scan is module-private again (no production consumer outside `bash-tools.shared.ts`). Gates on the new head: focused suite `bash-tools.exec-workdir.bind-mounts.test.ts` 3/3, `pnpm tsgo` exit 0, `run-oxlint` 0/0 on changed files, `oxfmt` clean, `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: feat(github): bind Gateway native commands to run-scoped App credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-local Codex native commands need run-owned App credentials without changing the configured System or agent account, blocking unrelated unbound turns, losing Git authorship, or retaining App access after the requesting binding closes.

Depends on #157500, which owns the issuer and private profile writer. This PR targets that worker branch, pinned to `352fba34455d20148b7c2c63fc789d8064066397` for this publication.

## User Impact

Eligible authenticated local native commands receive a private host-keyed `gh` profile, verified human `GITHUB_USER_LOGIN`, and Git author/committer metadata from the admitted operator's verified profile email. Configured System and agent `tools.github` selections keep their existing accounts. A missing trusted GitHub binding returns no App grant, preserving unrelated native work; an attempted App issuance or account verification failure remains an error.

The established pilot owner chose installation-wide access, including main sessions without a repository. The token inherits the App installation's configured repositories and permissions, which can exceed the requesting person's GitHub reach. Operators must install the App where this authority is intended. This documents the pilot owner's policy; upstream maintainer acceptance remains outstanding.

Local credentials renew before the one-hour expiry while the admitted run, operator, binding, and endpoint remain current. Cancellation, binding removal, authority loss, exhausted renewal, or finalization close the App grant and remove its profile. Transient revocation failure warns and retains retry ownership without changing a completed turn. This revokes the App token, **not independently configured native OS-keyring credentials**. Native host execution retains its existing same-OS-account trust boundary; use a dedicated OS user or sandbox for account isolation. Incognito, sandbox, remote, proxy, socket, and supervision placements do not receive this local App grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing environment owner binds both prepared and native environments to the host lifetime through a narrow generic `prepareLocalCommandEnvironment` capability. Its private GitHub implementation uses the canonical admitted authority, profile events, issuer, and profile writer. Codex projects the result into per-run native command policy and keeps it out of the shared app-server environment. No proxy, protocol-number change, permission widening, or competing credential manager is introduced.

The local renewal algorithm reuses the existing release work in `428cbb7307e`, adapted to current host/API and authority contracts. The retired incognito helper now uses the current SDK session-key owner. No release checkout or live session/installation was modified.

## Evidence

- Published candidate `82a090fe7d2` replays only this PR's nine own commits onto the worker replacement after its confirmed main conflict. There were no source conflicts; the five native production owners are byte-identical to `01d38492575`, whose fresh completed P2 AutoReview found no actionable issues including final environment-owner extraction. The affected local/host/Codex files pass 10/10, 8/8, and 2/2 after integration (58.10-second three-project wrapper wall). The prior incomplete review is retained accurately: it included the pre-repair index and a broad verification fallback; all staged defects were resolved, and attempted account verification remains strict.
- Focused local credential tests pass 10/10, admitted host environment 8/8, and Codex native policy/incognito 2/2. New System-selection, unavailable-binding, author, and cleanup assertions failed on the original source before repair. The new closure test observes revocation before manual finalization; renewal uses fake time and waits on retirement before reading the replaced stable profile. No real test sleeps or polling were added.
- Measured one-worker wrapper wall: local owner 23.24 seconds (20.59-second Vitest duration, test work under a second), final host owner 34.30 seconds (30.92-second duration, approximately five seconds of real admitted-host work), Codex policy 20.10 seconds (17.45-second duration). These existing boundary suites retain their real host/plugin assembly; no extra process boot per new case is added. CI per-file seconds are pending.
- Core and extension production types, core agent test and extension test types, changed core/extension lint, formatting, line and assertion ratchets, temp-authoring hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass. After extraction, the affected host suite and core types were repeated; unchanged proof was reused. The `OPENCLAW_*` budget is 475/475 on this main base. No broad gate/build was repeated during recovery.
- A September 30 current-source isolated probe exercised real admitted host preparation, Codex policy projection, **actual isolated Codex `command/exec`**, and stock clients: allowed private `gh api` 200, independently verified existing excluded private repository 404, successful `git ls-remote`, a disposable native commit with the verified synthetic profile email, canonical sign-in binding moved to another isolated profile, then the same native command profile returned 401. All five native owner/projection source hashes match the published source. The inherited issuer differs only by its reviewed caller/deadline composition repair, independently proven 10/10; the earlier live receipt is retained with that precise qualification. This used synthetic admitted authority and isolated canonical profiles and a disposable Codex process; it is standalone native execution, **not a full model-selected `exec_command` or Gateway turn**. No credential output, live user-session mutation, or App installation change occurred.
- Prior remote `cd13de29a1b` had successful CI run 36530997524. That is prior-head evidence. Exact-current-head required CI and ClawSweeper ratings are pending; the worker prerequisite has resolved its deadline and actual-main conflict and is mergeable, while long-turn/node renewal and admitted-dispatch proof remain in scope. Earlier unrelated test failures remain recorded in PR history; passing replays were not described as fixes.

No merge, automerge, release, or deployment is included.

Current CI qualification: worker `464913d519ae30b71fecaa184990d8807234f778` failed `checks-node-compact-small-15` in CI run 36765300511, job 110058337139. Three assertions in untouched `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` report public exports 4595 over 4594 and callable exports 2699 over 2698. The exact registered command completed exit 1 with identical diagnostics in clean detached source views of that published worker and pinned main `e6d8dae5c2009d0e754427de3d0ff7230d4da62e`; renewal work was absent in both views. This proves inherited baseline failure, not green CI. No budget increase, assertion change, rerun, or empty push was used; the upstream owner disposition remains pending. Native CI is observed separately and is not credited with the worker's result.

The dependency is now the issuer-only failed-final-cleanup repair `352fba34455`. The nine native commits rebased without conflicts; all native production owners remain byte-identical to the completed fresh P2 review, and local credential proof passes 10/10 after integration (21.57-second wrapper wall). The canonical issuer now retains cleanup independently after native finalization drops its handle, coalesces concurrent attempts, and retries HTTP/network failure to actual expiry. Fourteen issuer controls and real disposable204/lost-response/401/read401 proof pass. Cleanup cannot mint authority; process exit before successful revocation still relies on GitHub expiry. This closes the source-backed dropped-final-revoke finding without a native retry manager. Exact new-head CI/rating remain pending.
