prs.title: fix: Code Mode module access rejection gives no replacement guidance
prs.body:
<!-- Continuing the claim from #158675 (comment issued 2026-09-26T05:40:28Z). -->

Closes #158675

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Code Mode `exec` run that reaches for `require()` or `import` fails with the bare
sentence `code mode module access is disabled.`, which names no replacement — so the model
retries the same source shape, and in unattended runs (heartbeat/cron) that surfaces to the
operator as an `Exec failed` alert.

## User Impact

User impact: the first rejection is now self-correcting. The model receives the same
guidance it already gets when it submits shell-shaped source — call an enabled async tool
global, use `catalog.search(query)` when the bounded quick index omits the tool — plus an
explicit "do not retry with a module loader", instead of a sentence that only says what is
forbidden.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo already solved this exact feedback problem one file away:
`CODE_MODE_SHELL_SOURCE_ERROR` in `src/agents/code-mode-shell-source.ts` rejects
shell-shaped source and then names the replacement globals and forbids the retry. The
module-access refusal never got the same treatment, so the two `invalid_input` rejections
that fire at the same moment (`failurePhase: "input"`, `bridgeDispatchStarted: false`)
differ only in how actionable they are.

Scope lines, so reviewers can check them quickly:

- **Which modules or access shapes are rejected is unchanged.** `containsModuleAccess`,
  the unicode-escape pre-filter and every rejection condition are untouched; only the
  message they raise is extended. This is not a policy or permissions change.
- The leading sentence is kept verbatim, so existing assertions and log filters that match
  `code mode module access is disabled` keep working.
- The refusal now lives in one exported constant used by both core legs that raise it: the
  `prepareSource` pre-filter and the Node executor's translation of a guest
  `ReferenceError: require|module|process is not defined`. `prepareSource` is shared, so the
  rejection reported in #158675 gains the guidance for **both** executors.
- The bundled QuickJS executor's *own* runtime translation
  (`extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts`) is deliberately left alone:
  sharing the constant there means adding a symbol to the
  `openclaw/plugin-sdk/code-mode-executor-runtime` contract, and `extensions/AGENTS.md`
  requires docs, exported-subpath list, package exports and contract checks to move in the
  same change. That is a separate decision from a feedback-text fix.
- Issue suggestion 3 (a distinct `module_access_denied` code) is not taken: `invalid_input`
  is the machine-readable code operators and `failurePhase` tooling already filter on, and
  the retry loop is a message problem, not a code problem.

## Evidence

Red/green on the source-preparation path and the executor boundary, `.pnpm`-warm worktree on
branch `fix/code-mode-module-guidance-158675` at base `099220cc937` (`origin/main`), one
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/code-mode-runtime.test.ts src/agents/code-mode-headless.test.ts`
invocation per phase:

| phase | tree state | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GREEN | change applied | `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 161 passed (161)` / shard 1083.66 s |
| RED | same tests, both **production** files restored to `HEAD` | `Test Files 2 failed (2)` / `Tests 2 failed \| 159 passed (161)` / 717.32 s |

The two failures in the RED phase are exactly the two cases added here, and nothing else moved:

```
FAIL agents-core src/agents/code-mode-runtime.test.ts > Code Mode guest source validation > names the replacement tool path in the module access rejection
FAIL agents-core src/agents/code-mode-headless.test.ts > headless Code Mode > points the model at a tool global when rejecting module access
```

So the guidance text, not the existing sentence, is what the new assertions pin down; the
pre-existing module-access assertions (`src/agents/code-mode-runtime.test.ts`,
`src/agents/code-mode-headless.test.ts`, `src/agents/code-mode.guest-source.test.ts`) all still
pass unmodified, which is the point of keeping the leading sentence verbatim.

- The second case drives the rejection through the headless executor rather than calling
  `prepareSource` directly, and asserts the resulting `invalid_input` payload carries the
  guidance with `toolCallCount: 0` — i.e. the model sees it on the first rejection, before any
  tool dispatch.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on all four changed files; `oxlint` (230 rules) reports
  **0 warnings / 0 errors** on them.
- Local Node is **24.15.0**, below the declared `engines.node >=24.16.0 <25 || >=26.1.0`, so read
  the table above as a same-shape check rather than a supported-runtime run. The wider
  `agents-core` project, typecheck and the plugin/contract lanes are left to CI; no behavior
  outside these two rejection sites is touched, and the bundled QuickJS executor file is
  deliberately unchanged (see the scope line above), so its lanes should be untouched.
- **CI has now run all of them on the pushed head `eeb8de4d0371` and every lane is green**
  (read 2026-09-26T07:20–07:21Z): 109 check-runs = **52 `completed/success` + 56 `completed/skipped` +
  1 `CodeQL/neutral`**, **0 failures, 0 still queued**, with `mergeable = true` /
  `mergeable_state = clean`. So the src↔dist, boundary, contract, lint, typecheck and plugin lanes
  that the local run could not cover are green rather than merely unopposed. (`CodeQL`'s
  `neutral` is a standing repo condition on every head and is not evidence either way about this
  PR.)

### On the remaining `status: 📣 needs proof` ask

The automated review of this head recorded `Findings: None`, `Security: None`, "No stored-data
contract changes" and patch quality 4/6, and asks for one thing before merge: a redacted live
transcript of an agent in Code Mode receiving the guidance and then correcting itself through an
enabled tool. Stating exactly what this contributor can and cannot produce, so the gap is not
mistaken for a check that was skipped:

- **The model-visible path is verified in source, not assumed.** The refusal is not just a log
  line: for a failed run `src/agents/code-mode-execution.ts:545-548` copies the executor's `error`
  string verbatim into the tool-result `channels` that `output.takeResult(...)` returns to the
  agent loop (`:562`), and `:549-560` attaches the same `code` / `failurePhase` /
  `bridgeDispatchStarted` fields that appear in the issue's reported payload. The added headless
  case goes through that path rather than calling `prepareSource` directly, so what it pins down
  is the bytes the model gets back on rejection #1.
- **A live model run is not reachable from this contributor environment, and a substitute would
  be misleading.** There is no OpenClaw installation, no `~/.openclaw` configuration and no
  provider credential in this environment. The repo's own live Code Mode lane —
  `pnpm qa:code-mode-models` (`scripts/code-mode-model-matrix.ts`) — drives real providers through
  `matrixProviderEnv` / `matrixProviderAuthSelection` and has no mock mode at all, so it cannot be
  invoked here. The credential-free alternative (a `qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai`
  round-trip) is also not reachable inside a bounded run on this box — invoking `qa suite` from a
  cold `dist` first triggers a full TypeScript build, which did not complete in the five minutes
  this attempt was given (`tsdown failed after 2m 21.4s`, child status 143) — and in any case it
  would only re-prove *delivery*, which the headless case already covers: its
  follow-up turn is scripted, so it cannot demonstrate that a real model self-corrects, and
  labelling such a run as live behavior would misrepresent it. It is therefore deliberately not
  claimed.
- **What that leaves at risk is wording effectiveness, not correctness.** Which modules and
  access shapes get refused is decided by untouched code (`containsModuleAccess`, the
  unicode-escape pre-filter, every rejection condition), the leading sentence is byte-identical so
  existing log filters and assertions keep matching, and the review independently confirmed both
  that reading and that current `main` still returns the bare sentence at
  `src/agents/code-mode-source.ts:78` and `src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts:316`. If a
  maintainer wants the wording validated against a real model, that needs credentials this PR's
  author does not have; the mechanism itself is covered by the red/green pair above.

<details>
<summary>Diff shape</summary>

4 files, +33 / -3: one exported constant + two call sites in `src/agents`, and two added
test cases.

</details>
### Rebase onto `main` (2026-09-30)

`main` moved past this branch after the reviewed head above: upstream #160217 reworked the same
`formatGuestFailure` function in `src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts` so a guest failure carries
bridge identity. The branch was rebased onto `main` `728d16e21` and re-pushed as `9ae407850`, and
the module-access translation keeps that guard verbatim - only the rejection text changed:

```ts
if (
  !value.bridgeError &&
  value.name === "ReferenceError" &&
  /^(?:require|module|process) is not defined$/u.test(value.message)
) {
  return { code: "invalid_input", error: CODE_MODE_MODULE_ACCESS_ERROR };
}
```

So a genuine bridge/tool rejection whose encoded `ReferenceError` text happens to look like module
access still returns `internal_error` with `failurePhase: "bridge"`, rather than being
reclassified as `invalid_input`. The bundled QuickJS executor file remains untouched, so the
QuickJS-specific runtime translation stays outside this PR's scope.

Equivalence of the rebased patch to the head the table above was measured on: `git show eeb8de4d0`
and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` yield identical added-line and removed-line sets (33 added / 3 removed,
compared with `diff` after sorting); only context lines differ, and they come from #160217.
Local gates re-run on the rebased tree on this box with Node 24.18.0 and a repaired
`node_modules`: `oxfmt --check` clean on all four changed files,

prs.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

releases.body:
## 2026.10.1

### Highlights

- **Sessions and memory:** preserved usage across registry changes, delivered worker attachments from remote workspaces, prevented queued cancellations and transcript aliases from stalling active turns, kept continuation signatures aligned, and migrated embedding caches in bounded batches with oversized-row reporting. (#164217, #164219, #163708, #164230, #164251, #164289, #164287, #164303) Thanks @vincentkoc and @RomneyDa.
- **Replies and media:** restored inline playback for local videos, replaced rejected media links with useful errors, kept Telegram progress updates free of preview cards, and fixed speech-only replies when reasoning is enabled. (#164137, #163727, #164285, #164256) Thanks @ivan-magda, @obviyus, and @Twilight-Networks.
- **Updates and Doctor:** improved serving-verdict recovery guidance, kept repairs working with read-only managed config, removed repeated config, backup, metadata, and pnpm-root probes, reported successful cleanup as progress without corrupting JSON output, and treated a still-starting Gateway as a warning. (#164193, #161924, #164235, #162259, #164182, #164186, #164183, #164184, #163477, #164261, #162236, #164312) Thanks @DonnieFi, @JD8855122, @Patrick-Erichsen, @waynegault, and @RomneyDa.
- **Windows workspaces and browser startup:** fixed empty and nested Windows worktree creation, improved Linux Chromium discovery, and automatically started Playwright Chromium on ARM64. (#164202, #164249, #163510, #163281) Thanks @ly85206559, @jesse-merhi, and @obviyus.
- **Cloud workers and Crabbox:** surfaced the real cloud-worker failure, enforced Linux leases, overlapped worker-bundle downloads with bootstrap, removed unrelated warm-image cleanup waits, and prevented slow reads or unsupported backends from stranding workers. (#164129, #164187, #164128, #164231)
- **Plugins, Codex, and MCP:** preserved Bun package-import capture, reduced prerelease metadata requests, kept expired remote-exec approvals from poisoning auth profiles, restored node policy hooks, synchronized MCP forms/files/context, and routed background skill reviews through Workshop proposals. (#164223, #164185, #164237, #164270, #164277, #164292)

- **Safer recovery and responsive chats:** recovered interrupted database workers and Doctor migrations, kept background CLI replies from hanging, and preserved automatic chat following as new content arrives. (#163258, #165854, #167091) Thanks @goutamadwant, @hawkit, @RomneyDa, @Olli0103, @ericcurtin, @obviyus, @adele-with-a-b, @Patrick-Erichsen, and @vincentkoc.

### Changes

- Added Claude Haiku 5.5 support. (#166706) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Kept Code Mode `store`/`load` values available across cells, replies, and Gateway restarts. (#164086)
- Added Workboard sidebar navigation and personal board pinning. (#164604)
- Let MCP Apps call their tools while their views remain open, with inline message confirmations and synchronized forms, files, and context. (#164496, #164493, #164277)
- Added inline YouTube playback to Control UI chats. (#164576)
- Added native macOS sidebar identity details and plugin session catalogs, and used bundled Bun in the Linux companion. (#164591, #164436, #164401)
- Adopted sealed immutable installation generations with activation and recovery support. (#163799, #164306)
- Let the selected memory plugin own the pre-compaction memory flush. (#162177) Thanks @jalehman.
- Let every loaded plugin, including local paths and linked installs, use its own isolated state and ingress queues without changing trust requirements for privileged capabilities. (#165063)
- Added cloud-worker support for enterprise repositories. (#160108) Thanks @galiniliev.
- Added RPC response-size and main-thread heap diagnostics, with exclusive-handler sampling to avoid misleading measurements. (#164335, #164418)
- Migrated existing agents to local Claws. (#162329) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Reduced Sessions-board and state-path overhead by serving prepared facts, reusing card payloads per store revision, moving lifecycle mutations off the main thread, and retaining canonical state handles. (#164218, #164301, #163815, #164110) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- **Agents and subagents:** memory-saving turns no longer regain unrelated execution tools, finished subagent results are delivered even while a grandchild's delivery is still pending, follow-up messages no longer cut off returning subagent results, completed answers survive a reasoning-only tail, and sessions on small context windows recover after auto-compaction. (#166650; fixes #166644, #165987; fixes #138632, #168068; fixes #162761, #167567; fixes #167543, #167900) Thanks @jlapenna, @Oldrich333, @obviyus, @LifeViwer, @stackingrockss, @goutamadwant, @hannesrudolph, and @RomneyDa.
- **Updates and Doctor:** prepared activations settle when the live package already serves the candidate, rollback skips the maintenance drain when the Gateway is already stopped, dead legacy child-lineage leases no longer block every later update, triage stops prescribing repeated refused updates while activation recovery is pending, update repair leaves live current handoff owners alone, and Doctor maintenance no longer exhausts systemd service-inspection deadlines. (#167648, #167649; fixes #165266, #168043; fixes #168000, #167782, #168197, #168069; fixes #168031) Thanks @hannnnn-l, @farisoftfry, @Tosko4, and @RomneyDa.
- **Gateway startup with installed plugins:** valid startups no longer capture and discard plugin Doctor modules on every config read, Windows plugin captures use the fast pinned-descriptor copy again so Gateways with large plugins start without multi-minute stalls, catalog updates no longer recapture plugins after startup, model changes no longer freeze the Gateway with large plugins, and Windows launchers keep working after pnpm updates. (#168017, #167544, #161267, #167905; fixes #167835) Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @SMF12138, and @jjjhenriksen.
- **Codex, ChatGPT, and local models:** Codex replies no longer lose their last token when a provider stream drops the final delta, rejected cached ChatGPT tool continuations recover without rerunning completed tools, oversized proxy requests report context errors instead of one-token replies, resumed Claude sessions refresh their system context, Ollama tool calls work with Tool Search enabled, trailing Gemma 4 tool-call text is recovered, and managed llama.cpp memory indexing no longer runs out of memory on small hosts. (#168055, #167878; fixes #161254, #167817; fixes #167799, #167933, #167886; fixes #104868, #168020) Thanks @jacobtomlinson, @amittell, @yu-xin-c, @robburke, @jlapenna, @frankhli843, and @RomneyDa.
- **Channels, state, and memory:** Telegram keeps pending questions when `/verbose`, `/think`, or other settings commands arrive, Gateways on Bun no longer report false state-ownership loss, separate Docker CLI containers and recreated Docker owners keep Gateway state ownership, and memory-wiki status no longer recompiles an unchanged externally refreshed vault. (#168004, #167669, #164236; fixes #163961, #164546; fixes #155644, #167929; fixes #167914) Thanks @obviyus, @JakeMalis, @Alex-vonAllmen, and @etzelm.
- **Install and terminals:** global npm installs keep native packages to the current platform, and local browser terminals advertise RGB colors on headless hosts. (#165997; fixes #165602, #164325; fixes #164323) Thanks @TommyFive, @ooiuuii, and @obviyus.
- **Security and privacy:** rejected NUL execution arguments before startup, failed closed on unresolved peer credentials, prevented stale Codex sessions and foreign live owners from mutating successor workspaces, and kept private runtime context out of replies and saved conversations. (#164770, #165021, #164197, #164203, #163471, #164561) Thanks @shakkernerd, @eleqtrizit, @galiniliev, @KirDE, @RomneyDa, @consoleaf, and @JacquesLFR8.
- **Reply delivery:** retained completed answers instead of replacing them with blocker summaries or generic follow-up warnings, showed authoritative tool outcomes and native tool failures, and prevented silent-reply markers from leaking into previews. (#164896, #164774, #163545, #164116, #164259, #160582) Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, @joshavant, @ooiuuii, @jayzhou2309, and @imabotone-ui.
- **Telegram and Discord:** delivered later messages without deferred-ingress stalls, kept Telegram photo albums together and ordered under load, restored channel-routed handoff sends, and kept long Discord model IDs selectable. (#159265, #164549, #163926, #163863, #165137, #164311) Thanks @aatreya, @mbelinky, @ooiuuii, and @obviyus.
- **Other channels and hooks:** resolved workspace-qualified Slack users, migrated unscoped WhatsApp credentials through Doctor, stopped repeated Gmail error alerts on redelivery, and treated zero channel media limits as unlimited rather than blocking every attachment. (#160619, #163203, #164206, #163701) Thanks @LinzeShi, @obviyus, @jayzhou2309, @TrevorDGreen33, and @sxh313.
- **Models and providers:** fixed malformed Kimi K3 execution calls, preserved shared Codex clients after interruption, refreshed models from standalone Anthropic profiles, corrected Ollama Cloud thinking controls, restored Baseten setup defaults, and honored longer video-generation timeouts. (#165022, #165487, #156493, #162300, #155640, #162204, #164389, #164381) Thanks @serg0x, @Ram-G, and @RomneyDa.

- **Updates:** recovered archives without leaving Gateways stopped, settled replaced lease-database identities and moved package receipts, kept non-root launcher ownership and relinked launchers from stranding upgrades, preserved checkout plugin skills and historical webhook migrations during plugin convergence, and completed October beta updater compatibility. (#165854, #164849, #166394, #164636, #164438, #165882, #165855, #165303) Thanks @RomneyDa, @Olli0103, @szef-svg, @izrl613, @neilofneils404, @hrp6vv9mwr-glitch, and @shakkernerd.

(#167302, #167330, #167358, #164997, #165238, #165607; fixes #164254, #164214) Thanks @shanselman, @RomneyDa, @Hensarj, and @NovaeonStudio.

- **Doctor and service recovery:** imported retained session receipts and legacy entry state before SQLite migration, supported Linux filesystems without birthtime, quarantined unusable deletion journals, drained databases and command-owned workers before exit, kept maintenance entry points usable under lease-liveness checks, and recovered updates blocked by stale deferred session-import receipts bound to a replaced database while preserving original evidence and recoverable history. (#164867, #165866, #164363, #164509, #164503, #164853, #164915, #164697, #167538; fixes #167428) Thanks @hshs38033-cmd, @SunnyShu0925, @609NFT, @jayzhou2309, @StevenKrebs, @rosmiroslav-create, @RomneyDa, and @bipolar84.

(#165989, #166238, #164975, #163258, #165428, #166003) Thanks @DonnieFi, @dprev, @goutamadwant, @hawkit, @nano-richtera, and @RomneyDa.
- **Storage and memory:** removed large-store SQL-variable failures and rollback-journal lock failures, protected restore capacity, retained detached-maintenance database custody, released discarded transcript/output buffers and idle runtime state, reduced transcript-worker and background model-discovery memory, kept long leases from expiring early, and retained background memory synchronization and nightly dreaming across plugin reloads. (#164336, #164624, #164492, #164361, #164441, #164467, #164386, #166069, #167467, #167679, #167724) Thanks @jayzhou2309, @obviyus, @nkarkare, @triciah73, and @RomneyDa.

(#165669, #165301, #164537, #164521, #162033, #164331) Thanks @LiuwqGit, @JakeBotFleet, @goutamadwant, @exGeni, @cestercian, @RomneyDa, and @zhyx1996.

(#167588, #166687; fixes #167579; related #165686) Thanks @JIRBOY, @matthematics1137, @martinderm, @swampgorilla, @obviyus, @jjjhenriksen, and @RomneyDa.

(#161740; fixes #161738) Thanks @matthematics1137, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.

(#165880, #164602, #163487, #164560, #164534, #164486, #164735, #164574, #165275; fixes #164572) Thanks @RomneyDa, @Conan-Scott, @ericcurtin, @obviyus, @shakkernerd, and @ooiuuii.

(#167091) Thanks @RomneyDa, @ericcurtin, @obviyus, @adele-with-a-b, @Patrick-Erichsen, and @vincentkoc.

(#163201, #164364, #163842, #162036, #164151, #164161, #164368, #162844) Thanks @ooiuuii, @obviyus, @jalehman, @LinzeShi, @GoldArowana, @RvsL, and @zsh20000414.

issues.title: Telegram: classify remote media URLs with query strings by path extension
issues.body:
## Problem

The Telegram channel determines media type from the full remote URL string. For a valid image URL such as `https://cards.scryfall.io/.../card.jpg?width=672`, the inferred extension becomes `jpg?width=672`, so the channel treats it as a document.

As a result, consecutive remote images are sent as separate documents rather than a photo album.

## Expected behavior

Determine the extension from the URL path, ignoring its query string and fragment. The example above should be classified as a photo and be eligible for `sendMediaGroup`.

## Reproduction

Send an outbound Telegram message with several `.jpg` or `.png` URLs that contain query parameters. The debug log reports `type=document remote=True`; Telegram receives separate file attachments.

## Scope

This is distinct from #6121, which adds album delivery for media already classified as photos or videos.

issues.title: DeepSeek: reasoning_effort="minimal" sends contradictory thinking controls
issues.body:
## Problem

For the built-in DeepSeek provider, configuring `reasoning_effort="minimal"` produces contradictory thinking controls: nanobot sends both `reasoning_effort="minimal"` and `thinking.type="disabled"`.

DeepSeek's current [thinking-mode documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/thinking_mode) explicitly maps `minimal` to `low`, not to disabled thinking.

## Reproduction

Verified against HKUDS/nanobot main at `06fbd8c875fcaf3ee16258dc8e5cd597e68eeead` by invoking the actual request builder, without making an API request:

```python
from nanobot.providers.openai_compat_provider import OpenAICompatProvider
from nanobot.providers.registry import find_by_name

provider = OpenAICompatProvider(
    default_model="deepseek-flash",
    spec=find_by_name("deepseek"),
)
kwargs = provider._build_kwargs(
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
    tools=None,
    model="deepseek-flash",
    max_tokens=8192,
    temperature=0.7,
    reasoning_effort="minimal",
    tool_choice=None,
)
print(kwargs["reasoning_effort"])
print(kwargs["extra_body"])
```

Actual output:

```text
minimal
{'thinking': {'type': 'disabled'}}
```

The built-in provider routes `deepseek-flash` through Chat Completions, so this is the request-construction path used for that model.

## Expected behavior

For DeepSeek, `minimal` should express low-effort thinking consistently, either by preserving DeepSeek's documented alias with thinking enabled or by normalizing it to `low` with thinking enabled. Explicit `none` should continue to disable thinking.

## Code evidence

- [DeepSeek provider registration](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/06fbd8c875fcaf3ee16258dc8e5cd597e68eeead/nanobot/providers/registry.py#L520-L535) sets `thinking_style="thinking_type"`.
- [Request construction](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/06fbd8c875fcaf3ee16258dc8e5cd597e68eeead/nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py#L1030-L1044) preserves the wire-level `minimal` value but treats both `none` and `minimal` as disabling thinking.

## Impact and verification limits

A supported DeepSeek configuration does not consistently express the documented low-effort thinking behavior. This report establishes the request-level conflict only: no live/paid API call was made, and the server's precedence between the two conflicting fields has not been verified.

Using `reasoning_effort="low"` is a workaround; the same request builder emits `thinking.type="enabled"` for that value.

A focused fix should be provider-specific rather than changing the meaning of `minimal` for every provider. A regression test could cover DeepSeek `minimal`, `low`, `none`, and the unspecified/default case.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep mobile dropdowns open on trigger focus
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix a mobile dropdown that opens and immediately closes when the browser focuses its trigger after touch activation. The reported entry is Settings > Overview. The same shared component also serves non-modal chat, automation and host menus.

- Track the trigger inside each dropdown root without adding DOM wrappers or changing Radix open-state ownership.
- Do not dismiss on focus returning to that trigger. Keep real outside focus, outside taps, trigger toggling, item selection and Escape behavior.
- Preserve consumer focus handlers, forwarded refs, portal behavior and keyboard navigation. Do not use global focus suppression, timeouts or browser detection.
- Add regression coverage for controlled and uncontrolled menus, sibling menu isolation, touch selection and dismissal. Extend the actual mobile settings navigation test.

Related upstream report: https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/issues/2565

## Verification

- Reproduced the failure before the change: four failing assertions across the shared dropdown and mobile settings tests.
- Full WebUI suite: 155 test files, 2,668 tests pass.
- WebUI lint and production build pass.
- The homepage's pinned upstream snapshot also passes the 19 shared dropdown/settings tests after applying this commit.

The tests simulate the delayed focus event after a touch tap. They do not replace validation on the reporting phone. The local browser preview was blocked before loading, so this PR does not claim browser or real-device acceptance. Keep this PR in draft until that check is complete.

## Scope

No breaking changes. No gateway, execution, permission, persistence, protocol, dependency or translation changes. The homepage serves a prebuilt WebUI; a companion website PR will rebuild that bundle with this fix. No merge or deployment is included.

prs.title: fix(tools): keep the file's indentation when old_text is over-indented
prs.body:
## Problem

When `old_text` matches only after trimming whitespace, `edit_file` re-indents `new_text` like the matched block (`_reindent_like_match`, "Preserve the outer indentation from the actual matched block"). It handles only one direction: the block in the file indented deeper than `old_text`. When the model indents `old_text` deeper than the file, a common copy error from nested code, the function returns `new_text` unchanged and the extra indentation is written into the file:

- `"def foo():\n    pass\n"` edited with `old_text="        def foo():\n            pass"` and `new_text="        def bar():\n            return 1"` becomes `"        def bar():\n            return 1\n"`.
- The same edit nested one level (`"    def foo():\n        pass\n"`) becomes `"        def bar():\n            return 1\n"` instead of `"    def bar():\n        return 1\n"`.

In Python that moves code into another block or raises `IndentationError`, and the tool still reports success.

## Fix

When the file's indentation is a prefix of `old_text`'s, remove the extra part from every line of `new_text`, provided every non-blank line of `new_text` carries it. Otherwise `new_text` is written as given, as before. That includes `new_text` whose lines use a different whitespace character than the extra indentation, or where some non-blank line is indented less than it. The existing deeper-file branch is unchanged.

## Tests

prs.title: feat(telegram): support custom Bot API base URL and extra headers
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements #4702 — lets the Telegram channel target a self-hosted Bot API server or an enterprise gateway instead of the hardcoded `https://api.telegram.org`.

Adds two optional fields to `TelegramConfig`:

- **`api_base`** — custom Bot API endpoint. Forwarded to both the send and polling `HTTPXRequest` pools as `base_url`. Leave unset to keep using the official API (default).
- **`extra_headers`** — extra HTTP headers appended to every Bot API request (e.g. an auth token for a corporate gateway). Mirrors the existing `extra_headers` field on the provider config for consistency.

### Why

Some users sit behind regional or enterprise network setups where `api.telegram.org` is unreachable or must be routed through a private gateway. The channel already supports a SOCKS/HTTP `proxy`, but that doesn't cover self-hosted [Telegram Bot API local servers](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api) or gateways that require custom request headers. `python-telegram-bot`'s `HTTPXRequest` accepts both `base_url` and `extra_headers` natively, so this just wires the config through.

### Validation

- `api_base` is validated to be an HTTPS URL with a host (mirrors the existing `webhook_url` check); whitespace is stripped and an empty value normalizes to `None`.
- Both fields default to `None`, so existing configurations are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` passes
- [x] New unit tests:
  - `test_telegram_config_api_base_defaults_none_and_accepts_https`
  - `test_telegram_config_api_base_rejects_non_https` (parametrized: http/ftp/no-scheme/no-host)
  - `test_start_injects_api_base_and_extra_headers` (both pools receive `base_url` + `extra_headers`)
  - `test_start_without_api_base_passes_none` (default behavior unchanged)
- [x] Full `tests/channels/test_telegram_channel.py` suite: 97 passed

## Notes

- Minimal change, scoped to the Telegram channel only — no core/loop changes.
- Naming (`api_base` / `extra_headers`) matches the provider config to keep the mental model consistent.
- Manual end-to-end verification against a real self-hosted Bot API server is left to whoever has such an environment; the wiring is covered by unit tests.

Closes #4702

prs.title: feat(channels): add WhatsApp Agent Platform channel
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `whatsapp_agent`, an additive channel that connects nanobot to the **official** [WhatsApp Agent Platform](https://faq.whatsapp.com/1050934623978152) API (`https://api.whatsapp.com/agent/v1`, see the [Developer Manual](https://www.whatsapp.com/developer/WhatsApp-Agent-Platform-Developer-Manual.pdf)).

The existing `whatsapp` channel stays as-is. The two are different products, and both can run at once under different names.

| | `whatsapp_agent` (this PR) | `whatsapp` |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | Official agent API token | Linked device via Neonize (QR) |
| Inbound | Long-poll `GET /updates` | Device client |
| Reach | Only the agent's creator | Chats and groups the device can see |
| Groups | Not supported by the platform | Supported |
| End-to-end encryption | **No** — Meta processes agent chats | Yes, like a linked device |
| Availability | Limited countries / per account | Wherever WhatsApp can link a device |
| Account risk | Officially supported interface | Unofficial protocol |

**Benefits:** an officially sanctioned interface with no linked-device session, a much smaller blast radius (one conversation, no groups), no optional Python dependencies, and a token-based setup that needs no inbound URL or QR flow. **Tradeoffs:** no group support, no end-to-end encryption, and the rollout is limited by country and account.

## What it includes

- Authenticated long-polling with a durable cursor, dedup, and restart recovery.
- Read receipts and typing indicator, refreshed inside the 25-second window.
- Text replies split at 4096 characters, sent in order, with the first chunk quoting the inbound message.
- Inbound and outbound media (image, audio, video, document, sticker, generic binary) with MIME/size validation and digest verification.
- Voice-note transcription through the existing shared provider config.
- Per-method rolling-window pacing, protocol-aware retries, and secret handling.
- WebUI setup surface with locales for all 10 supported languages.

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **Durable cursor.** The cursor, dedup window, and creator identifier live in one atomically replaced state file. A wamid is recorded *before* its message is handled, so a crash re-reads the batch without answering twice, and `next_offset` is only accepted after the batch is processed.
- **No backlog replay.** The first poll omits `offset`, which resolves the head. Passing `offset=0` would replay up to 30 days of history into an auto-replying agent.
- **Token rotation resets the cursor,** because `next_offset` is only valid for the agent that issued it.
- **Retry policy.** Only confirmed non-delivery is retried (`429`, `503`/`131016`). HTTP `500` and read timeouts leave the outcome unknown, so they are **not** retried unless `retryAmbiguousSends` is set — a duplicate is more disruptive than a missed reply, and a repeated chunk would be especially bad. This is routed through the existing `should_retry_send_error()` hook rather than the manager's default retry.
- **Progress traffic is off by default.** Every poll, send, receipt, and media call has its own 12–15/minute budget, and progress messages would spend the send budget the real reply needs.
- **Single poller.** The API permits one poll per agent. A duplicate gateway produces `409`, which is logged clearly.
- **Reactions are receive-only,** matching the API, and an empty emoji is read as a removal.

## Security

- The token is only ever placed in the `Authorization` header. It is never logged, and the state file stores a SHA-256 fingerprint rather than the value.
- Media URLs returned by the API pass through the shared `validate_url_target` SSRF guard before any request; all requests disable redirects and hit the fixed API base.
- Inbound media is size-capped and verified against the reported digest (Base64) before it reaches the agent.

## Tests

```
uv run pytest nanobot/channels/whatsapp_agent/tests tests/channels \
  tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py nanobot/channels/whatsapp -q
# 491 passed

uv run ruff check nanobot/ tests/channels          # clean
uv run basedpyright                                # 0 errors (strict, whole repo)

cd webui && npx vitest run                         # 2661 passed
cd webui && npm run lint && npm run build           # clean
```

80 new package tests cover message/status parsing, status-only batches, int64 offsets, `204` offset reuse, first-poll head resolution, cursor persistence, dedup across a replay, restart recovery, token-rotation reset, token redaction, chunked/ordered sends, retry classification, rate-limit pacing, media size/digest/SSRF handling, and duplicate pollers.

Two unrelated failures in `tests/webui/test_transcription_ws.py` reproduce on a clean checkout of `main` and are not touched by this PR.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Live verification.** The round trip was confirmed against the production API with a real agent token: authentication (`GET /updates` -> `204`), a real inbound message parsed into the agent pipeline, durable cursor persistence, dedup on batch replay (0 duplicates), a real outbound send, and a `delivered` receipt for the sent wamid. Media handling (upload, download, digest verification, transcription) follows the Developer Manual but was **not** exercised end-to-end, since that requires sending and receiving actual attachments.
- Two behaviours differed from the manual in practice, and the implementation already handles both conservatively. A `to` that is not the agent's creator returned `500` / `code 2` rather than the documented `403` / `131005`; because `500` is classified as ambiguous, that request is not retried. An over-length `text.body` returned `400` / `code 100` with `message` set to the bare field name `body`; because the length heuristic keys off the field-name form, it is not misreported as an invalid token.
- `docs/guides/whatsapp-agent-platform.md` is the new guide; `docs/chat-apps.md` and the existing WhatsApp guide cross-reference it.

prs.title: feat(apps): add managed computer use with Cua Driver
prs.body:
## Current status — parked (2026-10-10)

This work is paused at the maintainer's request. Keep this PR as a draft. Do not merge or publish it until work resumes and the checks below are complete.

- Saved head: `16b3a0454aa785710c388871f4905b2ee28c33b0`. All 9 configured CI checks passed on this head. This is not full desktop E2E or release approval.
- Preserve the current implementation and branch. New Mac installs still use nanobot's bundled native app; existing official CuaDriver installations retain their identity. No switch to an official-driver-only default has been made.
- Developer ID signing and Apple notarization for the custom Mac app remain pending. An unmodified official CuaDriver release remains a separate integration option that does not require nanobot to sign that upstream app. It does not transfer the upstream signing identity to nanobot's modified build.
- No local installation, desktop permissions, or running gateway is changed by this handoff.

### Resume checklist

- [ ] Confirm the Mac distribution path: complete signing/notarization for the custom app, or explicitly scope an official-driver integration change and document its identity/capability differences.
- [ ] Align the final distribution's license metadata with its bundled components. The checked wheel still uses legacy `License: MIT`; preserve nanobot's MIT license and all third-party notices/source obligations, and verify the final SPDX expression and license-file index.
- [ ] Rebuild the final wheel/sdist from the final source revision. The earlier arm64 wheel predates the last WebUI change and is not a release candidate for the saved head.
- [ ] Verify downloaded installs on clean Mac accounts, on arm64 and Intel, without disabling system protections. Cover sequential grants, model image delivery and input, cursor/sharing indicator, Stop Sharing, cancellation, upgrade, disable, uninstall and reinstall.
- [ ] Complete native Windows/Linux desktop acceptance, or retain explicit experimental/preview limits. Browser fixtures are not native platform evidence.
- [ ] Recheck the current base, reviews and exact-head CI before merge. Follow the platform-wheel, source-material, size and publication checks in `docs/releasing.md`.

# Summary

Add Computer Use to Apps with one install, access, permission, connection, disable and uninstall flow. Nanobot owns the selected model and agent runtime; Cua supplies desktop observations and input.

- New macOS 14.2+ installs use the wheel's verified **nanobot Computer Use** payload. No Rust installation, per-gateway developer staging, or alternate permission owner is required. Missing native payloads fail explicitly.
- Preserve existing official CuaDriver installations and explicitly staged native builds. Changing identities requires disable/uninstall/reinstall; no grants or enabled connection migrate automatically. Linux/Windows retain official Cua Driver 0.33.4.
- Show desktop prerequisites before installing on Windows/Linux. Mark the Windows integration as experimental and Linux as preview; use platform-appropriate uninstall instructions. The branded native app and system sharing indicator are Mac-only.
- Keep installation inert and view-only the initial choice. Native permission setup requests one grant at a time. Checks neither capture content nor request grants.
- Bind window access to gateway-owned runs. Completion, cancellation, disconnect and idle timeout close sharing. System Stop Sharing revokes access and requires explicit Apps reconnect.
- Use the native Cua cursor and a real ScreenCaptureKit sharing indicator. Keep the settings UI's existing CSS/components; access choices now expand **and collapse** from the same row without applying a draft.
- Uninstall only the verified managed package. Optional native grant reset requires separate consent, is off by default, and never resets CuaDriver or other apps.
- Preserve inline MCP images for vision models and disable ambiguous desktop-action replay, without changing unrelated MCP defaults.

## Compliance and distribution repair

Native source, SDK patches, license collection and payload verification live in
`packages/computer-use/`. Generated SDK sources and build outputs stay ignored
inside that package. There is no new top-level `native/` directory or separate
Computer Use release-verifier script. The shared wheel builder calls the package's
verifier; Python runtime integration stays in `nanobot/apps/`. Installed paths,
module entrypoints, permissions and application identity do not change.

The native host embeds Cua SDK commit `d27f6a89d8aeef0f56363ee9bb60bbc565912b1e` (SDK 0.22.1), not the official 0.33.4 binary.

- Retain Cua/nanobot MIT grants and upstream derived-code credits, including yabai. Keep unmodified Cua marks as engine attribution, not nanobot's app identity.
- Collect exact-version dependency license text, including supplements where crate packages omit it; unknown or missing material stops the build.
- Include Inter's SIL Open Font License, Rust runtime notices/toolchain information, and unchanged UniFFI MPL-2.0 sources with the full MPL license.
- Bundle the host's source, artwork, lockfile, scripts and MIT SDK patch in `NANOBOT-SOURCES.tar`. Do not describe the dependency graph as MIT-only.
- Gate macOS wheel packaging on the native payload's checksum, architecture, identity, release profile, corresponding source and notices. A distribution update cannot silently change the installed payload or consent.
- Apply a documented MIT patch to keep the SDK's AppKit loop alive when macOS reports no active display. Display reconnection or first cursor work retries surface creation. This fixes a real connection failure caught by the package probe.

## Verification

- 280 focused Python tests passed across Apps, native transport, settings/presets, wheel/material packaging, MCP image observations, input/no-replay contracts.
- 218 tests passed after merging the latest main, including provider compatibility and installer/wheel checks; the final cross-platform settings fixture repair passed all 28 cases.
- 73 WebUI tests passed across setup, management dialog, Apps/OAuth, branding and i18n. Full WebUI lint and production build passed.
- Full Python Ruff and BasedPyright passed; native policy tests passed in the locked Rust **release** build.
- A real arm64 native package passed isolated default installation, code-signature/license verification, native status/tool discovery, view-only input denial, stop/restart refusal, uninstall and reinstall, with **zero screenshots and no permission requests**. The previously failing no-active-display startup now stays connected.
- Built a real arm64 platform wheel with the TUI and Computer Use payloads. Installed it outside the checkout into an isolated environment; the default site-packages payload passed install, connection, disable, uninstall and reinstall without `register_package`. Wheel/sdist passed `twine check`. Mach-O reports minimum macOS 14.2 for Computer Use.
- After package consolidation: 61 focused tests, full Python lint/type checks,
  clean SDK preparation, real arm64 release build, two native policy tests, and
  the default native installation lifecycle passed. A new regression verifies
  that generated SDK/build caches never enter the first-party source archive.
- All 9 package-consolidation [CI checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38029201051)
  passed at `0f94e641ecab92a1603eab1fbde0545ddc2044cf`. The consolidated package
  also passed an outside-checkout installed-wheel lifecycle and `twine check`.
- Platform presentation follow-up: 78 setup/settings/dialog/branding/i18n tests, locale key/interpolation parity for all 10 languages, full WebUI lint and production build passed. Browser fixtures verified desktop Chinese, narrow French/dark layouts, scroll/footer access, and non-Mac uninstall/cancel behavior. These are UI checks, not Windows/Linux desktop E2E.
- All 9 [final CI checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/38030346652) passed at `16b3a0454aa785710c388871f4905b2ee28c33b0`.

## Compatibility and remaining release gates

WebUI protocol 1 is unchanged. Named optional capabilities gate setup, reconnect, uninstall, native identity and grant reset. Manual MCP configurations are not replaced. The target remains the gateway computer, not the phone/browser displaying WebUI.

**This draft does not publish a native binary or a Python release.** The builder uses ad-hoc signing, not Developer ID or Apple notarization; it does not bypass Gatekeeper. Before public distribution, complete the documented downloaded-install/signing decision, both Mac architectures' native acceptance, and the existing release checklist. Intel package selection is tested with fixtures, not claimed as native execution. No macOS Actions runner was added.

The current revision has not rerun a complete permission-to-Astra screenshot/input E2E. Native Linux/Windows desktop operation is not proved by Mac tests. Existing development cursor/sharing evidence is not a substitute for final downloaded-release acceptance.

Window selection is not an app sandbox. The agent may select another window, and background input/focus depend on the app. Agent screenshots follow nanobot's normal media storage/model path; the native sharing preview is local and unsaved. macOS grants remain after uninstall unless the user explicitly requests native reset, which affects all instances of that native identity on the Mac.

The retained objc2 notices include upstream's Apple SDK provenance caveat. These are engineering compliance checks and preserved notices, not a blanket legal certification.

See the [setup/acceptance guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/codex/cua-driver-integration/docs/guides/computer-use-cua-driver.md), [native build guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/codex/cua-driver-integration/packages/computer-use/README.md), and [release gates](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/codex/cua-driver-integration/docs/releasing.md).

Hi! I'm Hugo from aimlapi.com — an AI aggregator that gives access to 1000+ models in one API, trusted by 400k+ users.

We'd love to be available as a built-in provider option inside nanobot — so we went ahead and did all the technical work on our side.

To build our partnership, we offer a 50/50 revenue share on all traffic from this integration. (P.S.: tracking starts as soon as this release goes live, so no earnings will be lost during setup)

My contacts: hugo@aimlapi.com (email / Slack), Telegram: @hug0the

aimlapi.com already works through the `custom` provider, but users must know the base URL, and they lose preset detection, the `nanobot status` check and the Settings model catalog. And those requests carry no attribution, unlike OpenRouter's.

- - Attribution headers on the same spec (`HTTP-Referer`, `X-Title`, `X-AIMLAPI-Source`, `X-AIMLAPI-Partner-ID`), built per provider by `factory._provider_extra_headers()` — the same mechanism as the existing OpenRouter attribution. from nanobot.config.schema import ProviderConfig

No layout changes — the provider appears under Settings → Models like the other gateways.

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes

Follows the existing OpenRouter attribution pattern (`HTTP-Referer` / `X-OpenRouter-Title` in `openai_compat_provider.py`). Nothing in the agent loop or routing changes; previously saved settings load unchanged.

prs.title: feat(webui): simplify local login and network access
prs.body:
When automatic browser opening fails, especially in WSL, opening the plain localhost address leaves a new user at a login page without a password they chose. The launcher now prints the complete authenticated login link in ordinary, dev, and `--no-open` modes. Local use keeps the generated credential and signs in through that link without asking the user to choose a password.

**Settings → System → Allow access from other devices** defaults to off for new installations. The first enable with a newly generated credential asks for a password and confirmation. New passwords accept 8–1,024 visible ASCII characters without requiring character combinations. Spaces, control characters, non-ASCII characters, and `$` are rejected by the gateway as well as the form; existing credentials retain their previous login behavior. The gateway saves the password and requested listener scope atomically, updates authentication immediately, and the current browser remembers the new password. The UI distinguishes the saved scope from the active address; the existing **Restart** action applies the listener change and reconnects. Access explanations appear on hover, focus, or click; restart notices and errors remain directly visible. Disabling returns to localhost after restart and keeps the password for later use. Competing tabs cannot overwrite the chosen password, and failed saves remain retryable.

Existing tokens, secrets, trusted-proxy authentication, and custom bind addresses are preserved, including passwords generated by earlier versions. Only new generated credentials are marked for password selection. The gateway keeps authentication and scope enforcement; non-loopback listeners require valid authentication, and choosing the initial password requires an authenticated local connection. The switch does not change firewalls, router forwarding, tunnels, or the separate OpenAI-compatible API service. The optional control uses `webui.access.v1` without changing WebUI protocol 1. The password is serialized as a JSON string; quotes and other allowed symbols remain literal data. Malformed non-ASCII authentication headers now receive 401 from bootstrap/token endpoints instead of raising an exception. Includes all 10 UI locales and user documentation.

First-run setup asks for one confirmation. Startup output groups the ready state, login link, model setup guidance, config, full-log command, and exit controls with blank lines, with green readiness, a cyan login link, and dim supporting information. Unconfigured instances get a concise **Next step** prompt to **Settings → Models**; errors for configured providers remain visible. The ready summary waits for the listener, routine gateway messages and the Vite banner stay out of the way, and warnings and errors remain visible. Narrow panes preserve the complete copyable link and keep the settings path together. Routine Git initialization is debug-only, and lifecycle copy uses direct instructions. Unix browser launcher failures produce one actionable fallback without raw gio/xdg-open stderr; Windows/macOS handoffs are preserved. Requesting an OS browser launch no longer claims the page successfully opened. Before reusing a listener with no matching runtime record, the CLI verifies the configured credential; an unrelated running instance produces an address-in-use message and stays running.

Closes [NAN-238](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-238).

Validation:

- Current-head CI: [PR checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/6150/checks).
- Current password/access suite: **21 passed**. Real listeners accept lowercase-only, uppercase-only, digits-only and punctuation-only passwords, including length boundaries; reject disallowed characters/types; and cover literal SQL/JSON-like password round trips, authentication, concurrent writes, save failure, local-only setup, persistence and listener restarts. Earlier CLI, transport and client-contract evidence is retained at `bd2d5f9e`; those paths are unchanged by the password-rule adjustment.
- Unchanged authentication and bootstrap regressions at `bd2d5f9e`: **39 passed**. A raw non-ASCII authentication header reproduced a 500 before the fix; both bootstrap and token endpoints now return 401 and remain usable.
- Current focused WebUI tests: **141 passed**. TUI client tests at `bd2d5f9e`: **39 passed**; the unchanged TUI bootstrap function also connected to the real isolated gateway and opened its WebSocket using a password containing JSON-like punctuation.
- Ruff, basedpyright, WebUI lint, production typecheck/build and `git diff --check` passed. The final diff has no TUI, WebUI bootstrap, remote-instance or remote-proxy client changes relative to the PR base.
- Actual Windows headless Chrome accessed a fresh isolated WSL gateway via localhost: rejected short/overlong, Chinese/emoji, space and dollar-sign passwords; saved an 8-character lowercase-only password; refreshed and reauthenticated; and applied both enable/disable restarts with accurate status notices. The previous Windows run at `bd2d5f9e` additionally verified a password containing JSON-like punctuation and hover/focus/click hints; those behaviors are unchanged. Test runtimes, independent ports and browser sessions were cleaned up.
- Earlier real CLI runs at `548098dc` covered ordinary, no-open, dev and dev+no-open, 48-column startup output, actual WSL browser-launch failure, and existing-listener credential checks. That launch/display behavior remains unchanged; the removed header helper sent the same legacy header for these ASCII credentials. The prior full WebUI test typecheck baseline is **356 existing diagnostics**, matching base `8080ea84`; production types pass.

Validation limits: Windows browser checks were headless; no separate physical LAN device was used. Save failure is injected at the persistence boundary in real-listener tests, with retry covered by form tests. The input review covers the changed access-password and authentication paths, not a full security audit of every publicly reachable feature.

prs.title: fix(telegram): classify remote media URLs by path extension
prs.body:
## Problem

`_get_media_type()` derived a media's extension with `path.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]`. For a remote URL such as `https://cards.scryfall.io/x/card.jpg?width=672`, the extracted "extension" becomes `jpg?width=672`, so photos and videos served with query strings are misclassified as `document` and sent as files instead of images/videos.

Fixes #6123

## Fix

For `http(s)://` URLs, parse the URL and classify on its path component, so query strings and fragments cannot leak into the extension. Local paths are classified exactly as before.

## Tests

- Added `test_get_media_type_classifies_remote_urls_by_path_extension` covering: remote URLs with query strings/fragments (photo, video), extensionless URLs, misleading query params (`file.bin?x=.jpg` stays `document`), and unchanged local-path behavior.
- Verified the new test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Full telegram suite: 176 passed. `ruff check` clean.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Add `nanobot update` for stable PyPI releases in a regular Python virtual environment.
- Add explicit `--dev` / `--update-dev` source updates with fast-forward-only checkout handling.
- Bootstrap a pinned, SHA-256-verified private Bun runtime when needed. Node is not required.
- Build TUI/WebUI source dependencies and preserve satisfied Python dependencies.
- Add Settings → About update controls, reconnect-safe progress, and optional host capability gating.
- Preserve Windows launcher recovery and the original contributor's commits.

## Repair after integration with main

- Verify both normal restart imports and isolated installed-package imports. Version metadata alone must not hide an old checkout.
- Refuse in-place source-to-release conversion. Use a separate environment and launch outside the checkout.
- Keep uv tool, pipx, system Python, containers, and Desktop on their owning update paths.
- Refuse implicit downgrades. The CLI requires `--allow-downgrade` for an intentional return to an older stable release.
- Treat an already-current install as a no-op without a restart request.
- Preserve an incomplete-installation warning after mutation failure or process loss. No automatic rollback is claimed.
- Report version-check failures instead of showing “up to date.”
- Ask WebUI users to back up the gateway and stop tasks before installation. This is an operator check, not an automatic maintenance lock.

## Current verification

On macOS with Python 3.11.4:

- 140 focused Python tests passed, including real Python import-resolution probes in a disposable environment.
- 129 focused WebUI tests passed, including old-host gating, update feedback, and localization.
- Ruff, affected-file ESLint, TypeScript checking, and production WebUI build passed.

Installation calls in regression tests are mocked. This round did not perform a real PyPI update, restart a live gateway, or run native Windows/Linux acceptance.

## Earlier contributor verification

The original contributor reported Windows isolated source update, Bun bootstrap without Node/uv, TUI/WebUI builds, stable switch-back, dependency preservation, browser reconnect/restart feedback, 234 Python tests, 33 WebUI tests, lint/type/build, and wheel checks. That evidence belongs to the earlier PR head; it does not validate the integrated changes above. Source-to-release behavior has since changed as documented.

## Draft gates

- Updates remain in-place. Back up data and stop other processes that share the environment. A failed installation may require a retry from the CLI.
- Installation verification is not live-process verification after restart.
- Complete real upgrade/restart and failure-recovery acceptance across supported installation methods and platforms.
- Add exact target/release-note confirmation and validate maintenance/restart coordination.
- Versioned stable/preview publication is separate from source checkout updates.
- Recheck required CI on the current head before review. Do not treat historical green checks as current evidence.

prs.title: feat(feishu): allow bot-to-bot messages in groups (allowlist + hop limit)
prs.body:
Fixes the group side of #5929.

### What was wrong

Feishu pushes `im.message.receive_v1` for bot authors when the app holds
`im:message.group_at_msg.include_bot:readonly` (获取群组中其他机器人和用户@当前机器人的消息),
and the message still has to @ the receiving bot. The channel then dropped it:

```python
# Skip bot messages
if sender.sender_type == "bot":
    return
```

So a second bot could never trigger a nanobot, and no option changed that.

### What this adds

Three opt-in `channels.feishu` settings (mirroring the Discord bot-to-bot fix in #3280):

| setting | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `allowBotSenders` | `[]` | peer bot open_ids allowed to trigger this bot; `["*"]` for any bot; empty keeps today's behaviour |
| `botHopLimit` | `2` | max consecutive bot-triggered turns per chat; a human message resets it (loop guard) |
| `replyWithMention` | `false` | reply to an allowed peer as plain text with a real `<at user_id=…>` — otherwise Feishu never routes it |

Streaming cards are skipped for those replies (a card cannot carry a real mention), and the
mention target is remembered per chat from the incoming message.

### Tests

`tests/channels/test_feishu_bot_senders.py` covers the allowlist (empty / list / wildcard /
whitespace), the hop cap, the human reset, and `botHopLimit: 0` (no cap). Docs: `docs/chat-apps.md`
(permission + new settings).

## Summary

Fixes #3292

Add a durable, session-scoped `focus` value to the existing `my` tool. Agents

- Clear the value by setting it to an empty string.

- Bound and normalize the value, mark it as metadata rather than instructions,
  and escape runtime-context delimiters in the stored text.
- Update the `my` tool documentation and AgentLoop registration.

This reuses the existing `my` tool and runtime-context architecture. It does
not add a new tool or change the public parameter schema for existing settings.
The focus block changes the model's effective turn context, but it is not a
security boundary and should not be treated as trusted instructions.

- Focused `my` tool and AgentLoop integration tests on the current upstream base: 131 passed.
- Ruff passed.
- BasedPyright passed for the changed Python files.

  failure was `WinError 1314` while creating a directory symlink in
  `test_equivalent_workspace_paths_share_one_store`; it occurs before nanobot
  code runs and requires Windows symlink privileges.

The regression coverage verifies persistence across a fresh session manager,
clearing the value, session isolation, and registration of the runtime-context

prs.title: feat(webui): connect to existing remote nanobot instances
prs.body:
## Why

Use a nanobot already running on a server from the local WebUI, without maintaining port-forwarding commands or a separate launcher. Conversations, model configuration, channels and tools remain on that server. This is not automatic worker deployment or remote execution with a local model provider.

## What changed

- Switch hosts from the sidebar footer. **Manage connections** opens a full page without changing the selected host or discarding its view. Saved servers support search, status, rename, connection details, disconnect and forget.
- Connect through existing SSH settings, including discovered aliases and explicit key/config paths, or use quick pairing: copy a command into the server terminal, confirm device access, then follow its return link. A connection-code fallback remains available.
- Discover the existing nanobot configuration, distinguish SSH/network/authentication failures, and retain recoverable pairing state. Repeated pairing to a verified destination is grouped without silently deleting older authorizations.
- Serve HTML, JavaScript, CSS and bundled branding from the **local installation**. Isolated host views receive authenticated server data; host switching retains their separate drafts and state. Eligible connections reuse a private SSH transport.
- Negotiate an explicit WebUI contract and show which machine needs updating. Include setup, security, troubleshooting and upgrade guidance in [the remote connection guide](docs/guides/remote-instances.md), plus a client/host compatibility review checklist.

## Security and compatibility

- Management requires an authenticated, loopback-bound local WebUI. Host identities are verified; no public administration port, SSH-agent forwarding or relay is introduced.
- Quick pairing creates an expiring, restricted SSH device key. It grants full access to the selected nanobot and its enabled tools, not an unrestricted SSH shell. Its WebUI credential is encrypted at rest in the local backend; pairing does not export provider keys. **Forget** removes local connection credentials; server-side revocation is a separate, documented action.
- Local-client mode requires WebUI protocol **1** and **`webui.core.v1`**. Older hosts without this declaration need a compatible update; their standalone WebUI remains unaffected. Matching package versions alone are not sufficient.
- Upgrading the earlier remote-page prototype retires its browser origins. Saved profiles, pairing grants and server conversations remain intact, but browser-local preferences/drafts need the documented precautions. Old prototype browser credentials require the documented site-data cleanup and server-secret rotation.
- No automatic host installation, update, restart, configuration migration or credential rotation is performed.

## Validation

- [CI passed on `d048c422`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/36957880026): Linux Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python 3.14/process compatibility, WebUI and Docker checks.
- After synchronizing main: **465 Python tests** passed, including real isolated gateway/proxy smoke, remote lifecycle/pairing and WebSocket tests; **406 frontend tests across 10 suites** passed, including host management, switching, pairing, API and session integration.
- Full frontend lint and the production TypeScript/Vite build passed after synchronization; the existing large-chunk warning remains.
- Earlier focused repair verification covered failed-forget recovery, stable origins after rename, compatibility refresh after destination edits, clean-source startup, lint, strict types and production build.
- Earlier macOS Chrome + Linux server acceptance exercised pairing/reconnect, local-owned asset hashes, remote chat/model management, isolated drafts, management navigation, restart and narrow layouts. Those live checks were not rerun during this base synchronization.
- Native desktop acceptance beyond macOS Chrome remains a limitation; automated Windows coverage is provided by CI. No claim of exhaustive cross-platform E2E coverage.

Repository documentation is included. Stable release notes and the versioned product website update follow the repository's release workflow.

prs.title: fix(webui): provide iOS PWA top-edge color surface
prs.body:
## Summary

Restore clear top controls in installed iOS PWAs, as reported in #5772.

- Add an empty, noninteractive, viewport-fixed color surface outside React's root so it survives startup and navigation.
- Enable it only in standalone mode on engines supporting `-webkit-touch-callout` and text background clipping. This is capability gating, not an iOS-version check.
- Preserve viewport fitting, safe-area behavior, header geometry, theme preferences and browser zoom settings. No gateway, protocol, configuration or stored-data changes.
- Document the WebKit sampling mechanism and verification limits in `docs/guides/ios-pwa-status-bar.md`.

The 11px surface inherits the body color; clipping its background to empty text prevents it painting over controls. This is a compatibility workaround, not an Apple-supported status-bar API.

## Verification

Reviewed head: `803b5e45330f81121d5a6717b4059dc6373fe163`, rebased on `9136fe364ef09bf7c711787c3c6940ceefd7b84a`.

- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37122809662) passed: WebUI lint, tests, coverage and build; Docker build. Python/TUI jobs were skipped by the changed-path filter.
- Fresh focused HTML/safe-area/theme tests: 7 passed; synthetic full-App production build and diff checks passed.
- iPhone Air simulator, iOS 27.0 (24A434), Xcode 27.0 (27A266a): the unpatched installed PWA reproduced washed-out top controls; the patch restored their clarity in light and dark themes. Ordinary Safari showed clear controls.
- On the rebased head, completely quit/relaunched the existing PWA without clearing data and confirmed new assets loaded with the saved theme. Checked sidebar open/close, A/B conversation switching, new-chat navigation, settings-page entry/return, keyboard open/close, and portrait/landscape rotation. Top controls remained clear and clickable.
- Scrolled to the first and last messages with the product's jump controls; the blur did not return. Runtime diagnostics confirmed native standalone mode, an 11px text-clipped surface, theme inheritance, and no horizontal overflow in the checked portrait frame.

## Limits

This is native iOS **simulator** evidence, not a physical-iPhone pass. The isolated fixture uses synthetic conversations/transport and no personal data or live model. Settings navigation was checked, not settings loading/saving. Finger-swipe delivery in the simulator tool was unreliable; scroll-position checks used in-app controls. Physical devices, older iOS versions and multitouch pinch were not exercised. Earlier desktop layout/click-through checks support the DOM/CSS contract, not iOS compositing.

The separately reported portrait session-mention issue is not changed here.

prs.title: fix(webui): fit session search above the mobile keyboard
prs.body:
## Problem

On iOS, session search can use the layout viewport while the software keyboard covers part of it. Results then sit behind the keyboard or Safari controls. In a short landscape viewport, the search field can leave no room for results.

## Change

- Publish the existing app viewport dimensions on the document element so body portals inherit them. Keep one viewport owner, including the native-host and zoom guards.
- Fit session search to that frame. In short, wide touch layouts, place the field beside the scrollable results. Keep the normal portrait and desktop layout.
- Keep oversized dialogs scrollable from their start. Put the scroll owner inside the modal scroll-lock boundary. Keep the content in charge of its exit lifetime, including cleanup and edit handoff.
- Add focused regression coverage and update the WebUI guide.

No gateway, wire, config, session storage, or search/filter logic changes. No breaking change.

## Validation

- Current head `6f21413f4bcc24cf2f7d131006068ac88d1e4996`: [WebUI and Docker CI passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37198253128). Python and TUI jobs were skipped by path routing.
- Full local WebUI coverage suite: 2,461 tests passed in 145 files.
- Touched-file ESLint, diff checks, production TypeScript and Vite build passed.
- iOS 27 Simulator, Safari, software keyboard: a 396px visual viewport contains the dialog at y=16, height=364px. A touch drag reached the last of 20 sessions; one tap selected it and closed search.
- Standalone PWA: portrait and landscape rotation with the keyboard open; long-list touch scrolling and selection; light and dark surfaces. At 128px available landscape height, the field and results fit beside each other in a 96px dialog.
- Shared-dialog regression checks: scroll an oversized rename form to its buttons, cancel it, open the mobile message-actions sheet, enter its links view, and dismiss it through the backdrop. Desktop empty/single-result search, selection and Escape dismissal also passed.
- The native fixtures import production App/CSS and use synthetic sessions. They do not contact a user gateway or model.

## Limits

Physical phones, Android, older iOS releases and native pinch gestures were not tested. The viewport lifecycle and zoom guard have unit coverage. This does not change the existing iOS auto-zoom behavior of small-font inputs in unrelated forms.

This PR remains a draft for maintainer review; it is not merged.
