prs.title: feat(webui): choose the chat for scheduled tasks
prs.body: ## Purpose Let users change the chat used by a scheduled task in WebUI. **Run and reply in** changes the execution chat, recorded turn, and default reply route together for future runs. It does not run in one chat and forward the result to another. ## User flow - Show one chat selector with a channel logo. Use the same display name as the sidebar, including user renames. Show a stable handle when names match. Names never determine the delivery route. - Select a chat and review the instructions as read-only text. **Edit instructions** opens the text field only when needed. **Save and change** saves both changes together. Cancel leaves the task unchanged. Name and schedule edits remain in the existing **Edit** dialog. - After saving, **Change back to** opens a confirmation for the previous chat. Users can also select that chat from the list later. Neither action recalls messages already sent. - Future runs and default replies use the new chat. Previous messages and run results stay available. Saving does not run the task, enable it, or change its schedule. - Keep Edit and Run now visible. Retain the draft on conflicts. If the selected chat disappears, keep its name visible and block saving. Restore focus after cancel or save. The controls have translations in all 10 locales. - Separate the chat name from its platform label. Show task instructions on the app's existing inset surface. Keep known content readable while choices load, reserve button width during save, and wrap long action labels on narrow screens. Do not show success before the host confirms. ## Ownership and limits The gateway resolves existing chat IDs in the same effective workspace and access mode. Chat-app targets need a saved incoming route and a running channel. The browser cannot submit a raw session key or recipient. The gateway checks the target again at save time. The cron owner rejects stale revisions and active or queued scheduled turns. It saves a detached snapshot before making the new binding live. Binding versions prevent stale CLI updates from restoring an old route. Each run keeps its own session identity for result links. This version blocks changes while **any** scheduled turn is active. System jobs, local triggers, unified sessions, and cross-host moves are outside its scope. Shared workspace memory and files remain shared. The delivery runtime is unchanged. There are **no agent loop, runner, or bound-cron-runner changes**, new dependencies, or separate CSS system. ## Normal replies and existing tasks New reminders need only instructions such as "Remind me to drink water". nanobot sends the final reply to the saved chat. The cron skill, tool descriptions, and scheduled-turn prompt now give the same guidance. Existing `message` calls remain supported, including multiple recipients and attachments. Changing the chat does not rewrite recipients in the instructions. The confirmation asks users to check them, not remove intended broadcasts. Scheduling guidance now distinguishes a fixed schedule from a flexible background check. A daily 8am reminder uses `cron`; repetition alone does not make it a heartbeat task. The always-loaded tool contract, workspace templates, and cron skill give the same guidance. Existing workspace files and heartbeat entries are not overwritten or converted. The user guide explains how to correct an old rule or an existing reminder. ## Compatibility and review decision The project lead confirmed maintainer agreement on the whole-chat design on 2026-10-07. The concerns in [#5513](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/issues/5513#issuecomment-5488297111) and [#5620](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/5620#issuecomment-5534384796) explain why execution, history, and default replies must stay together. This PR changes that whole binding for future runs; it does not add a separate forwarding route. - The optional capability keeps WebUI protocol 1. An older host keeps the read-only view and receives no new request. Ordinary old-client edits still work with a new host. - Storage locations and job IDs do not change. Existing supported jobs load through the current migration path. Task text is not silently rewritten. - **Downgrade after a chat change needs a pre-change backup.** Older writers discard the new binding-version and per-run-session fields. Follow the stopped, coherent cron-directory restore in the user guide. Mixed old/new writers after a move are not supported. - Tool-description changes can cause a cache miss on upgrade. Tool names, order, parameter types, and required fields do not change per run. Task-specific instructions stay in the current user turn. A chat change intentionally changes history. Suggested review order: gateway target resolution and cron save; execution/history/reply compatibility tests; selector, confirmation, change-back, and shared display names. ## Verification Reviewed head: `05e6e16e`. It includes main `b0d28af3`. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37500456067) passed all seven executed jobs; one conditional job was skipped. The final commit only removes stale draft-status wording from the design note. Runtime, UI, tests, and dependencies are unchanged from `41748db2`, so its focused and browser evidence below remains applicable. Merged by admin rebase as `d6ddceed` after the final checks passed. The merged tree matches the reviewed tree. [Post-merge main CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37501741051) passed all seven executed jobs; one conditional job was skipped. This change is on main; no stable release was published as part of this PR. - Latest layout follow-up: **87 WebUI tests passed**, plus production build, full frontend lint, and diff checks. Only the chat selector/review presentation, two assertions in an existing test, and its design note changed. No backend, runtime, dependency, or translation changes. - Browser checks used the production build and an isolated real gateway: light/dark desktop, Chinese 375/320 px, English 320 px, optional instruction editing, discard on cancel, confirmed save, and change-back. The disabled fixture returned to its original chat and instructions. English 320 px had no horizontal dialog or button overflow. Physical iOS and its keyboard remain untested. - Review on 2026-10-07: **11 focused backend checks passed** for the authenticated gateway, atomic saves, stale updates, run history, background results, default replies, explicit sends, attachments, and stable request prefixes. No new code defect was confirmed. - Additional browser checks covered Chinese and French at 320 px. A disconnected gateway left the draft visible and did not change the cron file. After restart, the test gateway issued new credentials; a page reload restored access and showed the unchanged task. This does not prove seamless reconnection. - A separate downgrade check loaded the cron implementation from base `b0d28af3`. Its writer discarded the new fields, as documented. With all writers stopped, restoring the complete pre-change cron directory restored the original binding, instructions, schedule state, and run record through the old reader on two starts. - Earlier focused checks and browser runs covered the same-name and rename paths, cancellation after a saved change, concurrent edits in two tabs, saving instructions with a chat change, reminder execution, and a follow-up that saw the saved result. Current CI covers their committed regression tests. Prompt tests do not prove that every model will choose the correct scheduling tool. Browser data and model replies are synthetic. Scheduler, agent, gateway, sessions, persistence, and audit reads are real; external senders are disabled. These checks do not prove real-platform receipt, physical-iOS behavior, live model instruction-following, live cache hit rates, or full remote-host acceptance. Existing build warnings concern old Browserslist data and chunk size. ## Documentation and screenshots [User guide](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/05e6e16e51dff0c941df36fd66336b1157a65bd8/docs/automations.md#change-the-chat-for-a-scheduled-task) · [Design and ownership](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/05e6e16e51dff0c941df36fd66336b1157a65bd8/webui/proposals/automation-chat/README.md) The existing screenshots show the production UI on an isolated gateway. They predate the change-back shortcut.

prs.title: fix(commands): keep slash-prefixed paths in normal chat
prs.body:
## Problem

The gateway rejects absolute paths such as `/tmp` and `/home/user/project` as unknown commands. This also prevents a user from sending a path while an agent turn is running. Temporary chats reject these messages at a separate ingress check.

## Changes

- Identify commands by registered names, not by a leading `/`.
- Send other text to the agent unchanged, including paths that start with a command name, such as `/new/file.txt`.
- Use the same name lookup for Temporary Chat admission. Keep its command allowlist and tool restrictions.
- Keep priority commands, bot-suffix normalization, and argument errors for registered commands.
- Queue paths like other chat text when the WebUI is receiving a response. Send registered commands to the gateway without waiting.
- If command metadata is unavailable, send slash-prefixed input directly to the gateway. Do not make `/stop` wait behind the active response.

The production changes are limited to the command router, Temporary Chat policy, and WebUI queue eligibility. No agent loop or runner changes.

## Behavior and compatibility

Unknown names such as `/neaw` now go to the agent instead of producing a spelling suggestion. This is intentional: `/tmp` cannot be distinguished from an unknown command by its spelling alone. Use `/help` or the command menu to find a command.

An exact registered name still wins. To discuss a directory named `/new`, use `/new/` or put explanatory text before the path. Chat platforms can apply their own command rules before the gateway receives a message.

No configuration, storage format, protocol, tool permission, or model prompt changes. Existing malformed registered commands still receive validation replies without a model call.

## Design references

[OpenClaw resolves registered text aliases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/70c839ac6bc812bf930ee7cc06a6895117c09d9c/src/auto-reply/commands-registry-normalize.ts). [Hermes uses its command registry to bypass active-session queues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/1744a19e0df568c647e4f3ff9c37f2a284a282fb/hermes_cli/commands.py). Its [command-name parser also rejects multi-segment paths](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/1744a19e0df568c647e4f3ff9c37f2a284a282fb/gateway/platforms/event.py). These support registry-based routing. No filesystem checks or path-shape heuristics are needed here.

## Validation

- 464 focused Python tests passed: commands, ordinary turns, running-turn follow-ups, session policy, and WebSocket ingress.
- Path regressions reproduced against the previous router and Temporary Chat methods.
- Tests verify that path text reaches the provider, remains ordinary chat history, and can enter a running turn. Temporary Chat tests cover admitted paths and rejected persistent/internal commands.
- Ruff, changed-production BasedPyright, and `git diff --check` passed.
- 149 composer tests passed. The path queue and unavailable-command-list cases failed before their respective fixes. Full frontend lint and the production build passed.
- Browser E2E used the production WebUI and a real, isolated gateway with a local deterministic model endpoint. Paths received replies and survived a page reload. A path entered during a response waited in the queue, then reached the model once. `/status now` returned a command error without a model call. Temporary Chat accepted `/new/file.txt` and rejected `/new`.
- A second browser run made the command-list endpoint return HTTP 503. During a held model response, `/stop` reached the gateway immediately. The UI showed `Stopped 1 task(s).` with no waiting message.
- [CI passed on the final PR head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37883546321), including 2,608 WebUI tests, Python 3.11 and 3.14, Windows compatibility, and Docker.

Unit tests use test doubles. Browser E2E used real HTTP and WebSocket connections, but simulated model responses. No live Weixin client or real model acceptance test was run.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve TeX formula boundaries in streaming Markdown
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes [NAN-204](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-204).

Streamdown's streaming layout splits Markdown with Marked before running the configured remark math plugins. A standalone `=` inside `\[...\]` becomes a Setext heading boundary; blank lines can also split the formula. The resulting blocks lose their paired delimiters, leaving bold headings and literal LaTeX. Assistant replies preserve the streaming layout after completion, so the failure remains visible.

- Preserve Streamdown's default grouping, but merge boundaries inside formula-bearing remark nodes and their enclosing lists/quotes.
- Reuse the existing math tokenizer with a segmentation-only policy for unfinished display formulas. Keep rendering strict, code literals excluded, and incomplete containers bounded.
- Require flow formulas to finish at a line boundary, avoiding a tokenizer assertion when Remend adds a synthetic link suffix to a partial TeX command.
- Add regressions for standalone equals, blank lines, streaming prefixes, containers, code literals, CRLF, and completion without replacing the streaming layout.
- Avoid empty inline TeX data tokens when a command immediately follows `\(`; preserve command and line-ending content without triggering the Markdown error boundary. Add the captured mixed-math response and all repaired prefixes as regressions.

No render delay, delimiter rewriting, or streaming-layout removal.

## Earlier validation

- Focused tests: **116 passed** (math, Markdown layout, image gallery, link actions).
- Full WebUI suite: **131 files / 2,134 tests passed** with `bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1`.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check`: passed. Build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- Real isolated gateway + Chromium against the production build: four formulas rendered, zero KaTeX errors or accidental formula headings, literal fenced LaTeX preserved, and following prose retained. Refresh and the authenticated persisted thread endpoint passed; browser console had no errors/warnings.
- Verification gateway/browser cleaned up; runtime removed and ports released.

The initial default-worker suite hit two lazy-render lookup timeouts in image/link tests. Both passed in the focused rerun and the full bounded-worker suite; no production timing workaround was added. Browser verification covers persisted replay; incremental prefixes and completion are covered by renderer/integration tests.


## Inline-token repair validation

- Focused math splitter, renderer and lazy MarkdownText suite: **102 tests passed**.
- Full WebUI suite after the tokenizer repair: **131 files passed**, using bounded workers.
- `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `git diff --check`: passed; existing large-chunk build warning remains.
- All **2,026 Remend-repaired prefixes** of the mixed Markdown response parsed without assertions. Short inline-command/list prefixes were also exercised through the real MarkdownText error boundary.
- Chromium against the changed source rendered **34 math nodes and 20 headings** in both streaming and completed states, with zero KaTeX errors.
- Isolated production gateway replayed the same message and an additional standalone-line quoted display formula: **35 math nodes, 20 headings, one table**, zero KaTeX errors. Authenticated thread endpoint returned 200; browser reload retained the rendered content. Production console captured before teardown had no warnings or errors.
- A final test-only change normalizes fixture checkout line endings. Both affected suites passed with the fixture explicitly converted to Windows CRLF: **30 tests passed**. The full suite and production browser checks precede this test-only normalization.
- Owned gateway, Vite and browser were cleaned up; verification ports released. No user session or service was modified.

Display openers following prose on the same line (for example `> Formula: \[` ) remain outside the current grammar. A display opener on its own quoted line renders correctly; this repair does not expand that separate syntax boundary.

prs.title: fix(webui): keep edit diffs visible and distinguish file creation
prs.body:
Completed answers hide file edit diffs behind their activity details menu, even when the user selects diff or collapsed diff display. The controlled expansion path introduced in #5831 bypasses the timeline splitting added in #5714. File creation also appears as Edited.

Restore timeline splitting for controlled activity so edit diffs remain visible when reasoning and tool details are collapsed. Preserve edit order and give the answer menu one disclosure container while each reasoning segment owns its own ID.

The gateway now records operation=create when a file did not exist before a successful tool call and exists afterward. WebUI shows Created for these events, including empty files, with translations in all ten locales. Creating a file with content still produces a diff; creating an empty file has no text diff. Writing into an existing empty file remains an edit. File change headers consistently show the operation, file path and line counts, including when a diff is visible. Creation, editing, deletion, progress, failure, summary labels and accessible descriptions remain explicit. Historical events without a creation marker retain their existing edit classification.

Review file activity labels and diff controls across all ten locales in their rendered context. Simplified Chinese uses 创建 / 编辑 / 删除; Traditional Chinese uses 建立 / 編輯 / 刪除. Japanese short labels use consistent action names; Korean creation matches the existing completion-label style. Keep natural completion forms in languages where they fit, and clarify long-diff, truncated-preview and collapse controls.

Validation:
- 118 focused WebUI tests, WebUI build and lint passed after restoring edit labels. All ten JSON resources retain their keys and interpolation tokens. The 36 file-edit event tests and targeted Ruff checks passed at 72eab497; the subsequent locale and header-label changes do not affect that backend evidence.
- New page-level disclosure regressions fail on the base commit for both diff modes and cover completion, expansion/collapse, order, and edit-only activity.
- Real isolated gateway and Chromium at 72eab497 (subsequent changes adjust translations, restore visible edit labels, and update expectations): execute edit_file to create empty/nonempty files and edit an existing empty file, then verify persisted API operation/diff fields, visible headers, accessible descriptions and refresh replay. No runtime or console errors; no external model calls.
- Disclosure browser verification and 119 focused tests were also completed at 0efd6461 before the label changes: both diff modes, menu expansion/collapse, order, unique disclosure target, and refresh. Those rendering and disclosure paths are unchanged by the later operation/label changes.
- Isolated runtimes removed and both ports released after verification.

prs.title: refactor(session): decouple history tools from WebUI replay
prs.body:
`search_sessions` and `read_session` currently read history through the WebUI replay API, coupling agent tools to display event reconstruction and pagination. This change moves history reads into `SessionHistoryReader` under `nanobot/session/`, using persisted session records directly, including messages before summary checkpoints.

When canonical history and the display transcript differ, tools now return canonical text; transcript-only conversations are excluded from tool search. Returned message indexes refer to the original session records. Results remain bounded and exclude hidden history, private runtime context, tool messages, and the current session. WebUI reference validation and display replay remain separate, and untitled search results derive their titles from filtered conversation text.

Both diagrams use the same three levels: callers, gateway services, and persisted data. Arrows mean calls or reads; HTTP/WebSocket router plumbing is omitted in both.

**Before**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph callers["Callers"]
        tools["search_sessions / read_session"]
        client["WebUI client"]
    end
    subgraph gateway["Gateway services"]
        access["WebuiSessionAccess"]
        display["WebUI list index / thread replay"]
        sessions["SessionManager"]
    end
    subgraph storage["Persisted data"]
        canonical[("Canonical session JSONL")]
        transcript[("WebUI display transcript JSONL")]
    end
    tools -->|"search / read"| access
    client -->|"list / history"| display
    client -->|"session references"| access
    access -->|"list / history"| display
    access -->|"metadata / raw history"| sessions
    display -->|"session listing / backfill"| sessions
    sessions --> canonical
    display --> transcript
```

**After**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph callers["Callers"]
        tools["search_sessions / read_session"]
        client["WebUI client"]
    end
    subgraph gateway["Gateway services"]
        access["WebuiSessionAccess"]
        display["WebUI list index / thread replay"]
        sessions["SessionManager"]
        reader["SessionHistoryReader"]
    end
    subgraph storage["Persisted data"]
        canonical[("Canonical session JSONL")]
        transcript[("WebUI display transcript JSONL")]
    end
    tools -->|"search / read"| reader
    client -->|"list / history"| display
    client -->|"session references"| access
    reader -->|"list_sessions / read_session_file"| sessions
    access -->|"metadata / handles"| sessions
    display -->|"session listing / backfill"| sessions
    sessions --> canonical
    display --> transcript
```

The tool path moves from `WebuiSessionAccess` and WebUI replay to `SessionHistoryReader` and canonical session records. WebUI display and reference-validation paths retain their existing data sources.

The Windows CI follow-up makes the OAuth callback-expiration test use a controlled monotonic clock after successful startup. This removes its 50 ms thread-scheduling deadline while preserving the expiration assertion.

Validation:

- 121 targeted tests passed across session tools, summary/history persistence, handles, WebUI mentions, and transcript replay on `f557ee58`; the subsequent change only modifies the OAuth test.
- All 7 OAuth tests passed after the follow-up. An injected 80 ms startup-resumption delay reproduces the original failure and passes with the controlled clock.
- Ruff passed for the changed Python files. Strict BasedPyright checks passed for the changed history modules.
- Isolated tool-registry smoke verification passed: archived canonical messages remain readable, WebUI retains its display transcript, and history files are unchanged by reads.

prs.title: fix(webui): prevent Windows manifest read/replace races
prs.body:
Concurrent transcript requests can read `manifest.json` while another request rebuilds it. On Windows, the open reader prevents atomic replacement and raises `PermissionError: [WinError 5]`, as seen in the [latest main CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37039650248).

Read the manifest under the existing lock shared by repair, rotation, and compaction. This closes the reader before replacement and retains single-flight repair. Strengthen the existing concurrency regression with a controlled overlap and simulated Windows file-sharing behavior so it fails reliably on the previous implementation, including on Linux.

Validation:
- Regression reproduced `PermissionError` before the fix and passes after it.
- Transcript tests: 45 passed.
- Real gateway smoke and WebSocket HTTP route tests: 121 passed.
- Repository Ruff, strict BasedPyright, dependency consistency, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local checks ran on Linux/Python 3.12; the PR CI matrix validates Windows/Python 3.14.

Focused browser checks also cover processing/completed states and reduced motion.

This changes client presentation only; gateway execution, security policy and client/host protocols are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(webui): restore CJK line height and refine text wrapping
prs.body:
The default `:root` line-height declaration comes after the equally specific CJK `:lang()` rules, so it overrides them on the document element. Move the default before the locale rules so Chinese, Japanese, and Korean Markdown uses the intended 1.8 line height; English remains at 1.625.

Balance Markdown headings, settings section titles, and shared dialog titles when they wrap. Use `text-pretty` for shared dialog descriptions to reduce isolated trailing words. Keep automatic mixed-script spacing disabled in code, monospace identifiers, and editable fields. The explicit `text-autospace: normal` declaration preserves the browser default; it does not introduce extra spacing on browsers already using that default. Unsupported CSS properties retain normal browser rendering.

Validation:
- WebUI production build and lint passed.
- Existing Markdown renderer and i18n suites: 99 tests passed.
- Isolated gateway with Chromium: English and Chinese settings at 1280px and 390px, light and dark themes; no document horizontal overflow or page runtime errors.
- Computed document styles verified CJK line height 1.8 for zh-CN, zh-TW, ja, and ko, English 1.625, and disabled autospace in the composer.
- A DOM-injected Markdown specimen using the built styles verified balanced headings, 28.8px line height at 16px, literal code spacing, and unchanged text content. This was a CSS specimen check, not a chat replay or a before/after visual acceptance test. Shared dialog wrapping has not been visually compared before/after.

Manual review: compare the same multiline Chinese reply and a wrapping dialog title/description at identical viewport widths on main and this branch. The visual differences are intentionally small.

prs.title: test: isolate Star invitation state and stabilize late-result waits
prs.body:
The Windows Python 3.14 job in [run 37350278970](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/37350278970/job/111899167793) failed when `test_independent_late_subagent_result_gets_complete_webui_turn` exceeded its two-second worker-completion deadline. The logs show the model turn completed, but the test still timed out waiting for the session worker.

WebUI completion events call `update_star_prompt`, whose instance-level state and file lock were not isolated by the shared test fixtures. Parallel tests could therefore share the real instance's invitation state and contend on a lock with its own two-second timeout. This is a concrete isolation defect; the original log does not establish that lock contention was the exact cause of that run's timeout.

- Redirect Star invitation storage to a per-test temporary directory through an autouse fixture.
- Make the invitation state and HTTP mutation tests use the same isolated store. Assert that it lives under the pytest temporary root but outside each test workspace, so directory enumeration and cleanup tests stay independent.
- Allow five seconds for the late-result test's synchronization waits, matching the nearby Windows-aware turn test. Events still control follow-up injection, and all event, routing, context, and persistence assertions remain intact.

Validation: 8849 tests passed and 41 skipped with four pytest-xdist workers on Linux/Python 3.12, using the CI test selection; all 160 serial CLI tests also passed. Ruff, strict BasedPyright (zero errors/warnings), and `git diff --check` passed. Windows/Python 3.14 execution is left to PR CI.

prs.title: refactor(ui): replace middle-dot separators with clearer hierarchy
prs.body:
WebUI and TUI use middle dots to join identities, status messages, tool arguments, statistics, and shortcuts, giving unrelated information the same visual weight. Replace these decorative separators with spacing, separate fields, layered tooltips, and complete status messages.

Tool activity keeps the action prominent and renders arguments or source names as secondary text. Search activity separates the source from the query and preserves multiple queries on separate lines, including when extracting `site:` scopes. Script line counts and channel workspace identities use separate fields. Browser tabs show the current conversation or host name. Hosted search summaries retain query line breaks; Slack table cells appear on separate lines with space between rows, preserving cell Markdown and fenced tables. Skill installation errors retain output line breaks.

Update all ten locales, remove eleven unused translation keys, and adjust TUI hints and statistics. Keyboard focus exposes truncated activity details through the existing tooltip. Mathematical middle dots and Korean prose punctuation remain intact. Search requests, tool execution, results, source links, state transitions, and wire/persistence schemas stay unchanged; display-summary strings change.

## Validation

- WebUI full suite: 2,518 tests passed. After the final multiline `site:` correction, all 92 focused activity/localization tests, production build, and ESLint passed again.
- Python: 171 focused OpenAI Responses, runner progress, and Slack tests passed; touched Python files passed Ruff. Unchanged skill marketplace checks reuse the earlier verification.
- TUI: unchanged since the verified initial commit; reuse 254 passing tests and TypeScript checks.
- Real isolated gateway and seeded replay: English and Simplified Chinese, light/dark themes, 1280px/320px widths. Verified query grouping, source identity, keyboard focus, no horizontal page overflow, conversation title, and refresh replay; zero console errors in the final browser run. The final `site:` correction preserves the tested fixture outputs and has a new regression test. Original model/host tooltips, CLI argument focus, and model settings flows retain their prior verification.
- Gate snapshot confirms identical source content before and after committing. Temporary browsers and gateway were cleaned up; runtime removed and ports released. No external model/search call was needed for display verification.

prs.title: feat(webui): add catalog loading skeletons
prs.body:
Apps can report an empty category after only one of the CLI/MCP reads completes, and Skills treats an unfinished or failed first read as an empty list. Add skeletons matching the Apps, Channels and Skills rows, wait for the sources used by the active Apps category/search, and keep available rows visible during pending reads and refreshes. Skills now distinguishes loading, retryable failure, a genuinely empty catalog and an empty filter result.

Replace the MCP management dialog's initial tool-inspection spinner with a skeleton matching its search toolbar and checkbox rows. Keep cached tools and draft selections visible during reinspection, and retain recovery actions for empty results and errors.

Make the Discover skeleton visible against settings panels in both themes and match marketplace rows, including rank markers and round install actions. Use it for trending lists and a first search while debouncing or fetching; keep loaded search results visible.

A shared status container handles loading announcements, hides decorative blocks from assistive technology, and respects reduced motion across catalog, marketplace and MCP tools skeletons. Each caller keeps its row layout, theme tokens and responsive grids. Add the Skills loading/error/retry and MCP tools loading strings to all 10 locales.

Validated in an isolated worktree:

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run test src/tests/catalog-loading.test.tsx src/tests/skills-marketplace.test.tsx src/tests/mcp-management-dialog.test.tsx`: 3 files / 21 tests passed after extracting the shared container.
- `bun run test:coverage` at `61c128ca`: 152 files / 2,544 tests passed; 92.12% statements and 86.93% branches.
- `bun run build`, including TypeScript's unused-local and unused-parameter checks.
- Real gateway + Playwright: staggered Apps responses, cached rows during navigation/focus refresh, Skills failure/retry and empty results, desktop/mobile layouts, light/dark themes, reduced motion, English and Chinese. Also verified MCP tool inspection, retries after errors and empty results, search and draft selection, plus Skills Discover contrast in both themes, initial search loading and retained search results. The browser used controlled CLI/MCP/marketplace fixtures and deliberate Skills failure/empty responses; no application JavaScript exceptions occurred.

Checked every new production call path: all three skeleton layouts, both Skills status props and the retry event have live consumers. `CatalogSkeleton` and `useSkills` each have 100% statement, branch and function coverage. Both marketplace skeleton variants have live consumers for trending and first-search loading. The shared status container has three live callers: catalog rows, marketplace rows and MCP tools. Removed the Channels spinner import after replacing its only use, and removed obsolete busy branches from the MCP tools empty state after introducing the skeleton's early return.

The additional test-inclusive `tsc --noEmit` check reports the same 327 pre-existing diagnostics as the base, with no new diagnostics. The required production TypeScript build passes.

The browser evidence covers the layout changes through `61c128ca`. The shared-container cleanup at `f5434899` preserves the rendered structure and CSS classes; the emitted CSS hashes are identical. Focused tests, lint and the production build were rerun after the cleanup.

prs.title: feat(webui): add a column directory picker and streamline composer actions
prs.body:
## Summary

Replace the native workspace chooser with an in-app directory picker for the connected gateway host.

- Use shared continuous corners across WebUI surfaces, preserve circular controls, and align picker fields with the dialog without gray focus outlines.
- Show the gateway host name above saved locations. Breadcrumb nodes navigate; the blank area of the path bar opens path editing. Keep filtering in a separate control to its right. Back, Forward, and Last visited folder restore directory columns, selection, filtering, and scroll positions. Canceling path editing preserves directory columns, filtering, and scroll positions. Apply the workspace only after Confirm.
- Use directory columns on desktop and a single folder view on narrow screens. Keep favorites and recent projects accessible as single-line 44px rows aligned with directory entries. Use a 176px saved-location sidebar, giving the aligned path and browser pane 64px more room, and omit redundant saved-location checkmarks. Use 13px primary and 12px auxiliary text on desktop. Align the path and directory pane left edges, keep the filter aligned with the pane right edge, and settle scrolling on whole rows with native proximity snapping. Omit repetitive folder icons and reuse the existing light/dark surfaces.
- Support path completion, hidden folders, folders without subfolders, and keyboard activation. Remove hjkl, arrow directory navigation, Alt+arrow history/parent shortcuts, and arrow selection in the path input. Keep Home/End, Enter, native text editing, and Tab path completion. Fix exact-path Tab completion so it does not enter the first child. Respect Finder's hidden flag on macOS.
- Keep browsing responsive with a bounded directory cache, shared in-flight requests, visible-row rendering, and a loading skeleton. Navigation history stores view coordinates rather than retaining directory entries. Reuse the sidebar selection animation for directory rows and saved locations.
- Keep modal overlays transparent after their exit animation until unmount. Restore picker trigger focus for keyboard and assistive activation without turning a mouse-opened Escape dismissal into keyboard focus.
- Group workspace and permission controls in the composer. Use voice input when the composer is empty and transcription is configured; otherwise show Send. Recording release clicks cannot send the transcript.
- Update all 10 supported locales and the WebUI guide.

## Scope and compatibility

- Directory listing, project resolution, and favorites use authenticated gateway APIs. Browsing returns directory metadata, not file contents, and does not grant agent access.
- The gateway owns path validation, execution, and access policy. Existing restrictions on enabling Full Access from remote clients remain intact.
- Directory browsing, resolution, and favorites are optional controls. A compatible older host without these controls retains manual path entry; the client does not call unsupported endpoints. The core WebUI protocol floor is unchanged.
- Favorites and recents use the existing instance-scoped workspace state. No session storage migration or data relocation is introduced.
- The native workspace chooser is removed. The native file chooser used for SSH credentials remains available.

## Validation

Compact-sidebar and shortcut follow-up at `7042ddeb3`:

- **40 focused picker and shared-highlight tests passed** on the frozen candidate. Touched lint, TypeScript, and production build passed. The local simplify, verify, and candidate-review gates passed; committing retained the same candidate content identity.

Mouse navigation, Back, native path editing, and Tab completion passed. The sidebar is 176px wide, adding 64px to the browser pane while keeping both toolbar/pane alignment differences at zero. The host name is not clipped, saved-location checkmarks are absent, and a 390px layout has no overflow.
- At 4x CPU throttling with 500 actual folders, 200 key presses and 20 scrolls rendered at most 18 rows. DOM nodes stayed at 543 and event listeners at 444, with zero extra requests or browser errors. This is a single-machine synthetic workload. The isolated browser and gateway were cleaned up.
- The earlier arrow/hjkl behavior documented in the historical validation below is superseded by this follow-up.

Keyboard-highlight follow-up at `b6d71eff2`:

- **42 focused picker and shared-highlight tests passed**. Touched lint, TypeScript, and production build passed.
- Real Windows Edge confirmed that arrows and j/k move the existing shared selection highlight, with no row ring or column outline and DOM focus retained on the listbox. h/l enter and leave directories; moving in an ancestor column updates the selection highlight without changing the workspace. Light/dark layouts and filter typing passed.
- With 500 actual folders and 4x CPU throttling, 200 keyboard moves rendered at most 18 rows. Event listeners stayed at 445 and DOM nodes changed from 546 to 538, with no browser errors. This is a single-machine synthetic workload. The isolated browser and gateway were cleaned up.

Picker-layout and navigation follow-up at `ec5ed5fcc`:

- **42 focused picker and shared-highlight tests passed**. Touched lint, TypeScript, and production build passed.
- Real Windows Edge verified the 13px primary / 12px auxiliary desktop text hierarchy, 44px saved/directory rows, and zero alignment differences between the path/pane left edges and filter/pane right edges. Light, dark, Chinese, and 390px layouts passed; mobile text inputs retain 16px to avoid focus zoom.
- Five desktop/mobile viewport sizes settled on whole rows without partial entries. Native proximity snapping supports wheel scrolling, far jumps, End, and history restoration with virtualized rows. Arrow/hjkl navigation keeps DOM focus on the listbox and leaves path/filter text input unchanged; the whole-column focus outline is removed.
- With 500 actual folders and 4x CPU throttling, 20 navigations and 20 scrolls rendered at most 18 rows. Navigation P95 was 195ms; event listeners stayed at 446 and DOM nodes changed from 588 to 581. No browser errors were observed. This is a single-machine synthetic workload. The isolated browser and gateway were cleaned up.

Modal-dismissal follow-up at `6921fd59c`:

- **48 focused picker, search-dialog, and automation-dialog tests passed**. Touched lint, TypeScript, and production build passed.
- Real Windows Edge reproduced the overlay opacity returning from nearly zero to one in the final mounted exit frame. Shared modal overlay styling now retains the transparent final frame through unmount. Frame sampling and animation-end checks found no opacity rebound across 36 dismissals, including outside clicks, Escape, Cancel, the shared search dialog, 10% playback, dark mode, reduced motion, and a 390px viewport. This motion evidence is reused across the final focus-only activation adjustment; overlay styling and presence are unchanged.

DOM nodes and event listeners stayed stable within every run. This is a single-machine synthetic workload. Both isolated gateways and browsers were cleaned up.

Picker-row follow-up at `be637c4d7`:

prs.title: feat(models): declare request APIs for providers and presets
prs.body:
## Summary A model name does not tell nanobot which request APIs a custom endpoint accepts. A Responses-only model can consequently be sent to Chat Completions, and a custom connection cannot declare that it accepts Anthropic Messages. This PR lets provider connections and model presets declare their request APIs, so configuration, Settings, and runtime routing agree on how to call the model. ## Behavior - Custom providers declare accepted APIs and a preferred API: Chat Completions, Responses, and/or Anthropic Messages. Presets inherit the connection default or choose an API within the connection's accepted protocols. Built-in OpenAI connection declarations provide defaults that individual presets may override. - Responses-only declarations prevent Chat fallback. Declaring both OpenAI APIs permits classified compatibility fallback when Responses is not required. A preset cannot fall back between Anthropic and OpenAI API families. - Custom Messages connections use the native Anthropic adapter with the configured endpoint, credentials, request extensions, and proxy. Automatic routing continues to use provider defaults and Copilot's discovered endpoint capabilities. - Settings groups connection capabilities, preset protocol selection, fallback controls, and the resolved Auto choice under Advanced options, collapsed by default. Basic preset setup keeps the preset name, provider, and model. Auto previews resolve while Advanced options is open. Field labels offer localized help on hover, keyboard focus, and tap. Declarations persist across saves, preset switching, fallback models, and runtime reloads; saves reject unsupported combinations and connection edits that invalidate existing model configurations. Protocol-editing controls depend on the host's advertised metadata. - The `deepseek-flash` automatic Responses default is scoped to DeepSeek's official endpoint. Existing Chat proxies keep Chat Completions for this alias; explicit Responses settings and V4 Responses routing remain supported. DeepSeek hosted web search is removed because [its documented Responses endpoint ignores that built-in tool type](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/responses_api/). Default and previously saved search settings now preserve nanobot's ordinary `web_search` function. ## Request sequence WebUI sends declarations and Auto-preview requests to the gateway's Settings handlers. Settings validates declarations through `routing.py`; Auto previews use provider defaults and cached Copilot metadata without constructing provider clients or probing remote endpoints. The sequence below follows one preset at runtime. Each configured fallback preset is resolved independently through the same factory when needed. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Runtime as Agent runtime participant Factory as Provider factory participant Routing as Provider routing participant Registry as Provider registry participant Adapter as Selected adapter participant Endpoint as Remote endpoint Runtime->>Factory: Configuration and active preset Factory->>Routing: Resolve connection and preset declaration Routing->>Registry: Read adapter capabilities Routing->>Routing: Validate APIs and select backend Routing-->>Factory: Validated ProviderRoute Factory->>Adapter: Construct selected provider Note over Factory,Adapter: Custom Messages selects the Anthropic adapter Factory-->>Runtime: Provider instance Runtime->>Adapter: Chat or streaming request Adapter->>Adapter: Apply declaration or model API default Note over Adapter: Optional Responses honors circuit state Adapter->>Endpoint: Request using selected API alt Successful request Endpoint-->>Adapter: Response or stream else Request error Endpoint-->>Adapter: Error alt Responses error allows Chat fallback Adapter->>Endpoint: Retry with Chat Completions Endpoint-->>Adapter: Response or error else No compatible fallback Note over Adapter: Preserve the original error end end Adapter-->>Runtime: Normalized output, stream, or error ``` Chat fallback requires a classified Responses compatibility error, declared Chat support, and optional Responses. Auto previews show the configuration default; the runtime circuit breaker can temporarily select Chat for optional Responses requests. ## Module dependencies Arrows point from a consumer to a dependency. These views show the modules involved in API configuration, routing, and execution; unrelated imports are omitted. The dotted edge marks function-local registry imports used by configuration validation and provider lookup. ### Routing and execution ```mermaid flowchart TB Runtime["Agent runtime"] Settings["settings_models.py
Validation and Auto preview"] Factory["factory.py
Construct providers"] Routing["routing.py
Validate and resolve"] Adapters["Provider adapters"] Cache["Copilot cache helper
github_copilot_provider.py"] SDK["SDKs and HTTP transports"] Runtime --> Factory Settings --> Routing Factory --> Routing Factory --> Adapters Routing -->|Cached Auto preview| Cache Adapters --> SDK ``` The Copilot cache helper lives in the adapter module. Routing calls it only to read known model APIs; the preview neither refreshes the catalog nor constructs a provider client. The factory also builds the optional model-failover wrapper; each fallback retains its own preset declaration. ### Shared types and input migration ```mermaid flowchart TB Settings["settings_models.py"] Factory["factory.py"] Routing["routing.py"] Adapters["openai_compat_provider.py
github_copilot_provider.py"] Schema["config/schema.py
Configuration types"] Registry["providers/registry.py
Provider metadata and declarations"] APIs["providers/model_api.py
API types, capabilities and defaults"] Migration["config/provider_api_migration.py
Legacy input conversion"] Settings --> Schema Settings --> Registry Settings --> Migration Factory --> Schema Factory --> Registry Routing --> Schema Routing --> Registry Routing --> APIs Schema --> APIs Schema --> Migration Schema -.->|Provider validation and lookup| Registry Registry --> APIs Adapters --> Registry Adapters --> APIs ``` ## Compatibility - Connections without an API declaration retain automatic routing. Legacy `apiType` / `api_type` configuration and settings inputs, including both `NANOBOT_PROVIDERS__OPENAI__API_TYPE` and `NANOBOT_PROVIDERS__OPENAI__APITYPE` environment aliases, are converted for the first release shipping the migration and the immediately following release; conversion is scheduled for removal before the third release. - Saves write the new declaration format. Rolling back to a version that does not understand it requires restoring the old configuration. - Python integrations must supply `ProviderSpec.request_apis`, replace `responses_models` with `responses` capabilities, and replace `OpenAICompatProvider(api_type=...)` with `model_api`. The legacy input conversion does not preserve those Python interfaces. See [Python migration examples](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/de8f9305bd8859e63c350f12f4a35d9ffa6a4da5/docs/development.md#python-api-migration). ## Related contributions | Source | Included scope | | --- | --- | | #5906, #6105 | Responses routing for OpenCode Go Muse Spark 1.2/1.3 models. | | #5935 | GPT-6 Copilot routing and model discovery. | | #6020 | SDK output serialization with API aliases for tool-call replay. | | #6051 | Interleaved tool item/call ID regression coverage; the parser fix is already in #6096. | | #5834, #5863 | Raw reasoning-text SSE regression coverage; the shared parser behavior is already in #6096. | Source authorship, cherry-pick references, and equivalent contribution credits are retained. Related investigations: #6086 (@drakeo338) and #6104 (@Apageoflove) identified the hosted-tool leak behind #6085. Their Chat-only filters are superseded by removing DeepSeek's obsolete hosted-search capability and discarding saved hosted-search entries before either request API. ## Verification - Provider, configuration, fallback, Settings, runtime, CLI, and frontend regression checks passed, together with the applicable lint/type checks and production WebUI build. - Deterministic HTTP fixtures and an isolated gateway with Chromium exercised protocol routing, fallback restrictions, configuration migration, and Settings save/reload behavior. No live paid-provider or Copilot acceptance is claimed. - [PR checks](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/pull/5204/checks). - Backend verification passed 2,153 tests across providers, configuration, Settings, CLI, agent fallback, and websocket compatibility. Scoped strict type checks and lint passed. Real local HTTP fixtures verified Chat, Responses, Messages, permitted and forbidden fallback, and migrated OpenAI defaults. A base-versus-head comparison loaded all 341 legacy JSON configuration samples across all 46 providers. Actual local SDK HTTP requests verified both legacy environment selector loading modes and that default/saved DeepSeek hosted-search settings preserve ordinary search function calls. - Settings verification passed 109 focused frontend, localization, and tooltip tests, lint/type checks, and the production WebUI build. An isolated gateway and Chromium verified directly visible API controls, Auto previews, keyboard help, declaration save/refresh persistence, rejection of connection edits that invalidate presets, and desktop/narrow layouts including Simplified Chinese/dark mode. A fresh browser run also verified removal of DeepSeek's switch, unchanged connection save/refresh behavior, OpenAI hosted-search persistence, and a narrow Simplified Chinese/dark layout. Verification services and fixtures were cleaned up. Fixes #5898 Fixes #6085

prs.title: fix(mcp): let the SSE read timeout cover tool_timeout
prs.body:
## Problem

#6066 (for #6065) made the streamable HTTP transport's read timeout cover `tool_timeout`: `read=max(_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT, cfg.tool_timeout)`. The SSE transport did not get the same change. `connect_mcp_servers` calls `sse_client(cfg.url, **sse_kwargs)` without `sse_read_timeout`, so the MCP SDK's default of 300 seconds applies.

Tool results arrive on the SSE stream. With `toolTimeout: 600` and a server that sends nothing on the stream while the tool runs, the stream raises `ReadTimeout` after 300 seconds and the call fails before nanobot's own timeout. Servers that send keep-alive events reset the timer and are not affected, which is the same reason #6065 was easy to miss.

## Fix

Pass `sse_read_timeout=max(_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT, cfg.tool_timeout)` to `sse_client`, mirroring #6066. prs.title: fix(mcp): render resource and audio blocks in tool results
prs.body:
## Problem

`MCPToolWrapper._render_call_result` handles text and image blocks and passes every other content block through `str(block)`. MCP tools also return embedded resources, resource links and audio. For those the model sees pydantic reprs, for example:

```
type='resource' resource=TextResourceContents(uri=AnyUrl('repo://octo/demo/README.md'), mimeType='text/markdown', meta=None, text="# Demo\n\nIt's a readme.") annotations=None meta=None
```

github/github-mcp-server's `get_file_contents` returns file bodies this way (an `EmbeddedResource` next to a short text message, or a `ResourceLink` for files of 1 MB or more). For a binary file or an audio block the repr includes the whole base64 payload, which goes straight into the tool result and the context. The docstring of `_render_call_result` already says base64 must not be forwarded for images; the sibling `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` renders the same resource types as their text or `[Binary resource: N bytes]`.

## Fix

In `_render_call_result`:

- `EmbeddedResource` with text contents renders as its text; with blob contents as `[Binary resource: N bytes]`, the wording `MCPResourceWrapper.execute` uses.
- `AudioContent` renders as `[Audio content: N bytes]`.
- `ResourceLink` renders as `[MCP Resource] <description or name>` plus its URI, the format `MCPResourceWrapper` uses for its tool description.

Image handling is unchanged, including image blobs inside an `EmbeddedResource`, which still become artifacts. A `ResourceLink` is rendered without its `mimeType` and `size`. As in `MCPResourceWrapper`, `N` is the length of the base64 string.

## Tests

- New `test_execute_renders_resource_blocks_as_text` and `test_execute_keeps_binary_payloads_out_of_result`, built from real `mcp.types` objects. On main both fail with the reprs above (the second shows `blob='JVBERi0xLjcK'` in the result); with the fix they pass. The fake `mcp.types` fixture gains the three real types the renderer now checks.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py`: 117 passed. `tests/tools/`: 1171 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `mcp.py`.

Not changed: `MCPPromptWrapper.execute` has the same `str()` fallback for prompt messages; that can be a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(tools): number read_file lines by newline like edit_file
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` numbers lines with `str.splitlines()`, which also breaks on form feed, vertical tab, lone CR, NEL, U+2028, U+2029 and the ASCII separators `\x1c`-`\x1e`. `edit_file` reports and checks `line_hint` by counting `"\n"`. So the two tools disagree on any file that contains one of those characters. Form feeds are a common page break in C and Python sources (GNU style), and U+2028 appears raw in JS/JSON string literals.

For `"alpha\n\f\n    beta\n    gamma\n"`, `read_file` prints `4|     beta` and "5 lines total", while `edit_file` places `beta` on line 3. The `edit_file` schema tells the model to copy `line_hint` from `read_file`, so `edit_file(old_text="beta", line_hint=4)` fails with "line_hint 4 does not match the old_text location. old_text appears at line 3."

Two more places inside `edit_file` number lines the `splitlines()` way: trim-fallback matches (so an exact match and a trim match of the same block report different lines) and the "Best match ... at line N" hint shown when `old_text` is not found, which the model then uses as its next `line_hint`.

## Fix

- `read_file` splits on `"\n"` (after the existing CRLF normalization; a trailing newline does not add an empty line, so "N lines total" is unchanged for normal files). A file with lone-CR line endings now reads as one line, which is where `edit_file` already placed its text.
- Trim-fallback matches and the best-match hint compute their line number by counting `"\n"` before the match, the same expression the exact and quote-normalized matchers already use.

Not changed: the `grep` tool still numbers lines with `splitlines()`. It reads files without the CRLF normalization, so it needs a separate change.

## Tests

- New `test_edit_file_line_hint_matches_read_file_numbering` (exact and trim-fallback cases): `read_file` shows `3|     beta` and "4 lines total", and `line_hint=3` applies. On main both cases fail with `assert '3|     beta' in '1| alpha\n2| \n3| \n4|     beta ...'`.
- New `test_edit_file_best_match_line_matches_read_file_numbering`: the not-found hint says "at line 3". On main it says "line 4".
- `tests/tools/`: 1172 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `filesystem.py`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): split legacy HTML sends by rendered length
prs.body:
## Problem

Two places send rendered Markdown through `_send_text` after splitting it by raw Markdown length (`TELEGRAM_MAX_MESSAGE_LEN`, 4000): `TelegramChannel.send()`, used for every non-streamed reply, and the legacy fallback in `send_delta()` when a rich draft is rejected. Neither checks the rendered size. Telegram's limit for `sendMessage` is 4096 characters of text after entity parsing, and rendering can grow a chunk well past that. Tables are the clearest case: `_render_table_box` pads every cell to its column width. A 3037-character Markdown table (a header plus 300 short rows) renders to 5460 characters of HTML, 5436 of them counted text.

Telegram rejects that message, `_send_text` catches the `BadRequest` and resends the chunk as plain text, so the user sees the raw Markdown (`| a | b |` rows, `**`, backticks) for that chunk.

`send()` covers replies with streaming off, cron and notification deliveries and other non-streamed sends (`richMessages` is off by default). `_start_legacy_stream`, `_flush_stream_overflow_legacy` and the stream-end edit already split with `_split_telegram_markdown_html_chunks(..., TELEGRAM_HTML_MAX_LEN)`, and the module comment above the constants says the rendered message must fit the 4096 boundary.

## Fix

Split with `_split_telegram_markdown_html_chunks(text, TELEGRAM_HTML_MAX_LEN)` in both places and send the raw chunks, as `_start_legacy_stream` does; `_send_text` renders them the same way it did before. The tool-hint blockquote branch of `send()` is unchanged: its counted text is the chunk itself, at most 4000 characters.

Like the other paths, the check uses the length of the rendered HTML including tags, which is stricter than Telegram's count. A heavily formatted reply of 3-4K characters may now arrive as two messages instead of one. When a table has to be split, the rows after the cut have no header row, so they are sent as literal `| a | b |` lines rather than the aligned box; before this change the whole table arrived as plain text.

## Tests

- New `test_send_html_expansion_does_not_overflow` (through `send()`) and `test_send_delta_rich_fallback_does_not_overflow` (rich draft rejected at stream end), both with the table above. On main both fail with `assert 5460 <= 4096`; with the fix every payload is sent with `parse_mode="HTML"` and fits.
- `nanobot/channels/telegram/tests`: 177 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `runtime.py`.

Not tested against the live Bot API.

prs.title: fix(matrix): keep HTML formatting in m.new_content for edits
prs.body:
## Problem

A streamed Matrix reply is sent once and then updated through `m.replace` edits of that first event (the throttled intermediate edits and the final one). `_build_matrix_text_content` puts `format` and `formatted_body` on each edit's top-level fallback, but builds `m.new_content` from `body` and `msgtype` only.

Clients that apply edits read `m.new_content`. From the spec, [Applying `m.new_content`](https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/#applying-mnew_content): "When applying a replacement, the `content` of the original event is treated as being overwritten entirely by `m.new_content`, with the exception of `m.relates_to`, which is left *unchanged*." Its example ends with "Note that `formatted_body` is now absent, because it was absent in the replacement event." So in Element and other edit-aware clients the finished reply shows raw Markdown (`**bold**`, headings, backticks, tables), although the first draft was rendered as HTML.

## Fix

When the text renders to HTML, put `format` and `formatted_body` inside `m.new_content` as well. This applies to the intermediate edits and the final one. Plain-text edits are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test_build_matrix_text_content_with_event_id_preserves_html_formatting`. On main it fails because `m.new_content` lacks `format` and `formatted_body`; it passes with the fix.
- `nanobot/channels/matrix/tests`: 123 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `runtime.py`.

Not tested against a live homeserver.

## Problem

`SkillsLoader.build_skills_summary` prints each plugin skill path relative to `<workspace>/plugins`. The plugin loader hands over skill paths that are already resolved (`_contained` uses `Path.resolve(strict=True)`), but the summary compared them with the unresolved root. ```
ValueError: '/private/tmp/.../real/plugins/demo/skills/hello/SKILL.md' is not in the subpath of '/private/tmp/.../link/plugins'

Common triggers on macOS are a workspace under `/tmp` or `/var` (both symlinks into `/private`), a symlinked home or data disk, or a synced folder.

## Fix

Resolve the plugin group's root too. The function already resolves it for the display root; the workspace and built-in groups are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `test_plugin_skill_summary_supports_symlinked_workspace` (workspace at `tmp_path/link -> tmp_path/real`, one enabled plugin skill). On main it fails with the `ValueError` above; it passes with the fix.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): keep redacted_thinking blocks across tool turns
prs.body:
## Problem

With extended thinking, Claude can return `redacted_thinking` blocks (reasoning flagged by its safety systems, returned encrypted in a `data` field) alongside `thinking` blocks before a `tool_use`. `AnthropicProvider._parse_response` kept only `thinking` blocks, and `_assistant_blocks` replayed only those. So the request that carries the tool result replays a thinking sequence that differs from what the model produced, or none at all when the turn had only a redacted block.

The Anthropic [thinking docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking) name this case directly:

- "Preserving thinking blocks": "Within the latest assistant message, the sequence of consecutive `thinking` blocks must match what the model generated in the original request: you can't rearrange, edit, or partially drop them. This includes `redacted_thinking` blocks."
- "Redacted thinking blocks": "If your code filters content blocks by type (for example, `block.type == "thinking"`) when round-tripping responses with tool use, also include `redacted_thinking` blocks. Filtering on `block.type == "thinking"` alone silently drops `redacted_thinking` blocks and breaks the multi-turn protocol described in Preserving thinking blocks."

The server's response to the dropped block was not reproduced against the live API.

## Fix

- `_parse_response` records `{"type": "redacted_thinking", "data": ...}` in `thinking_blocks`, in response order. Streaming ends in `get_final_message()` and the same parser, so it is covered too.
- `_assistant_blocks` sends those blocks back unchanged, in order, next to the `thinking` blocks. Blocks without `data` are skipped: the Bedrock provider stores its redacted blocks as `redactedContent`/`redactedContentBase64`, so after a `/model` switch from Bedrock an empty `data` would otherwise be sent.
- `extract_reasoning` only shows `thinking` blocks, so redacted ones stay hidden from users. The Bedrock provider already round-trips its own redacted blocks.

## Tests

- New `test_parse_response_keeps_redacted_thinking_in_order` and `test_redacted_thinking_replayed_before_tool_use`. Both fail on main (the redacted block is missing from `thinking_blocks` and from the replayed assistant content) and pass with the fix.
- `tests/providers/`: 1369 passed.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `anthropic_provider.py`.

prs.title: fix(tools): read SVG files as text instead of image blocks
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` decides whether a file is an image with `detect_image_mime(raw) or mimetypes.guess_type(path)[0]`. `detect_image_mime` recognises PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP from their bytes; for anything else the file extension decides. So `logo.svg` comes back as an `image_url` block holding `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` instead of its source.

That block is not usable. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI accepts SVG as image input (both take JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP), and the Anthropic converter's `data:(image/\w+);base64` pattern does not match `svg+xml`, so the block is sent as a `url` source with a `data:` URL. The model never gets the SVG markup it asked to read or edit. Binary `.bmp`, `.ico` and `.tiff` files took the same path.

## Fix

Treat a file as an image only when `detect_image_mime` recognises its bytes. That is the same set `utils/artifacts.py` maps to extensions. SVG then goes through the UTF-8 text path like any other XML file, and returns line-numbered source.

Behaviour change: binary files that are none of those four formats (`.bmp`, `.ico`, `.tiff`, `.avif`, `.heic`/`.heif`, gzip `.svgz`) now get the existing `Cannot read binary file ... (MIME: image/bmp)` error instead of an image block. Anthropic, OpenAI and Bedrock reject those blocks anyway. Gemini accepts HEIC/HEIF, so a `.heic` read on Gemini loses its image block; this PR keeps nanobot's existing image set (`detect_image_mime`, also used by `utils/artifacts.py` and the CLI's inline artifacts) rather than adding HEIC detection here. An SVG that is neither UTF-8 nor BOM-marked gets the same error, because `.svg` is not in `_is_text_extension`.

The second image check in the undecodable branch used the same inputs as the first one, so it could never match; it now only looks up the MIME type for that error message.

## Tests

- New `TestReadFileTool::test_svg_file_returns_numbered_source`. On main it fails because the result is `[{'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,...'}}, ...]`; with the fix it returns `1| <svg xmlns=...`.
- `tests/tools/`: 1170 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `filesystem.py`.

Not changed here: inbound attachments (`utils/document.py` `is_image_file` and `agent/context.py`) use the same extension fallback, so an SVG a user uploads still becomes an image block. That can be a separate PR.

prs.title: fix(slack): handle DM messages that mention the bot
prs.body:
## Problem

`SlackChannel._on_socket_request` drops every `message` event whose text contains the bot mention, so that a channel mention (Slack delivers it as both `message` and `app_mention`) is handled once. The check runs before `channel_type` is read, so it also drops direct messages.

So a DM such as `@nanobot hello` gets no reply, no reaction and no log above debug.

## Fix

Read `channel_type` before the dedupe and skip the dedupe for `im` events. Channel and `mpim` messages keep it. The mention is still stripped before the text reaches the agent.

With `restrict_to_workspace` off (the default), `MessageTool._resolve_media` expands `~` only to check whether a path is absolute, then forwards the original string. So `media=["~/report.pdf"]` reaches the channel as `~/report.pdf`.

issues.body:
## What

A `fallback_providers` entry supports a much narrower parameter set than the primary route:

| setting | primary | fallback entry |
|---|---|---|
| provider | ✅ `model.provider` | ✅ |
| model | ✅ `model.default` | ✅ |
| base_url | ✅ | ✅ |
| api_mode / transport | ✅ | ✅ |
| api_key | ✅ (`model.api_key`, `providers.<name>`) | via `key_env` |
| service_tier | ✅ `agent.service_tier` | ❌ |
| **reasoning_effort** | ✅ `agent.reasoning_effort` + `agent.reasoning_overrides.<model>` | ❌ |

(Keys actually read from a `fallback_providers` entry: `provider`, `model`, `base_url`, `api_mode`/`transport`, `reasoning_echo`, `key_env`.)

## Why it matters

There is no way to express *"when we fall back to model B, think at level X"*. Because the entry carries no effort of its own, `_reresolve_fallback_reasoning_config` has nowhere to look but the global — it can only re-derive from `agent.reasoning_effort` (+ per-model overrides). Every route change therefore re-resolves effort from the primary's config surface, and the fallback route's own requirements cannot be stated at all.

This bites when the fallback is a *different* model rather than the same model reached through another provider. It also makes a fallback entry unable to describe itself completely, which is awkward for operators who treat the chain as a first-class route.

## Proposal

Allow `reasoning_effort` (and consider `service_tier`) on a `fallback_providers` entry:

```yaml
fallback_providers:
  - provider: deepseek
    model: deepseek-v4-flash
    reasoning_effort: low
```

## Precedence — maintainer call

If the field is added, the ordering needs a decision. Candidate rungs:

1. fallback-entry `reasoning_effort` — most specific to this route
2. `agent.reasoning_overrides.<fallback-model>`
3. explicit user pin — `--reasoning`, the gateway session pin, a cron job's or kanban task's per-task `reasoning_effort`
4. global `agent.reasoning_effort`

**Open question:** should an explicit user pin outrank a per-model *config* override? Today the resolver puts per-model overrides first, so a configured override silently beats a level the user pinned in-session. That may well be intended — flagging it rather than deciding, since it changes behaviour established by #21256.

Related consideration: today `agent.service_tier` is not re-resolved on a route change at all, so it survives — unlike `reasoning_config`, which is. Whatever the chosen ordering, it would be good for the two to behave consistently.

## Related

Adjacent to #117908 (reasoning_overrides editor + fallback chain reorder) and #125110 (joint model/effort routing), but this is specifically about the fallback entry's parameter surface rather than the UI or routing policy.

issues.body:
## What happens

Opening a pull request against this repository from our fork fails, for our account only. Exact errors, reproduced twice within two minutes (2026-10-03 00:14–00:16 UTC):

```
gh pr create --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --head kuehnberger:fix/aux-cost-provenance-v2 --base main
→ GraphQL: kuehnberger does not have the correct permissions to execute `CreatePullRequest`

gh api -X POST repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls -f title=… -f head=kuehnberger:fix/aux-cost-provenance-v2 -f base=main
→ HTTP 404 {"message":"Not Found"}
```

## What still works for the same token / same account

| action | endpoint | result |
|---|---|---|
| create an issue here | `POST /repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues` | 201, works (used as a probe, then closed) |
| create a PR on our own fork | `POST /repos/kuehnberger/hermes-agent/pulls` | 201, works (PR #2 in the fork) |
| push branches to our fork | `git push fork` | works |
| read this repo, compare heads, read our 4 open PRs | REST/GraphQL | works |
| cross-repo compare of the new branch | `GET /compare/main...kuehnberger:fix/aux-cost-provenance-v2` | works (`diverged`) |

Repository permissions returned for our account on this repo: `admin=false push=false triage=false`. Token scopes: `repo`, `workflow`, `notifications`, `read:org`, `gist`.

## Controls (to rule out the obvious causes)

- **Not a GitHub incident** — githubstatus.com reports all systems operational, Pull Requests `Normal`.
- **Not repo-wide**: other accounts, including first-timers with `author_association: NONE`, opened PRs here at 00:06, 00:07, 00:12 and 00:13 UTC — i.e. within the same minutes that our attempt failed (00:14–00:16 UTC).
- **Not a block**: `GET /repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blocks/kuehnberger` → 404 (not blocked), same for the org endpoint.
- **Not a broken fork link**: our fork reports `fork: true`, `parent: NousResearch/hermes-agent`, `archived: false`, `disabled: false`.
- **Not an existing PR** for this head: `GET /pulls?head=kuehnberger:fix/aux-cost-provenance-v2` → empty.
- **Not interaction limits**: issue creation succeeded with the same credentials, minutes ago.

Our last successful PR creation here was https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127847 on 2026-09-29.

## Impact

One branch is ready and waiting: `kuehnberger:fix/aux-cost-provenance-v2` (4 files, +89/−0, 2 commits, `fix(usage): persist cost provenance on auxiliary-usage rows`, tests green on `main` `4e3fcd5cd7`). Its description is written; only the "Create pull request" step fails.

Our four existing open PRs are unaffected — we only comment/rebase them, and those API calls still work.

## Ask

Is PR creation currently restricted for external accounts (or for this account/fork in particular)? If the restriction is intentional, a sentence saying so is plenty and we'll stop retrying. If it isn't intentional, any pointer to what changed would help — the error message reads like a permissions check rather than a rate limit, which is why we can't diagnose it from outside.

Happy to move the branch out of the way, or to open the PR through another path, if that's easier.



---

issues.body:
## Symptom
Desktop "Context Usage" panel's **Conversation** legend row reports far more tokens than the model
actually receives, on reasoning-heavy sessions over routes that do NOT echo reasoning back.

Reproduced live (2026-10-04/06), session `20261003_112557_8af802` on a local vLLM route (custom
provider, `api_mode` chat_completions — a non-echo route):

| Source | Conversation-ish figure |
|---|---|
| Real provider `prompt_tokens` (agent.log, 137 calls, peak) | **129,579** (never near 196,608 compact threshold) |
| Session DB: assistant `reasoning` bytes | **659,371** (~164.8k @ bytes/4) — **not sent on the wire** |
| Legend "Conversation" row (what the panel showed) | **~257.6k** |

So the legend charged ~165k tokens of stored reasoning that the provider never sees. The real prompt
was 129.6k; the model never overflowed and auto-compact correctly never fired.

## Root cause (line-level, on current main)
`agent/context_breakdown.py`, `compute_session_context_breakdown()`:

- **Header** (correct): uses `anchored_context_tokens(messages, anchor, charge_stale_thinking=False)`
  → excludes stale reasoning → matches what the model sees.
- **Conversation category** (wrong): still
  `"conversation": estimate_messages_tokens_rough(messages)` — default `charge_stale_thinking=True`,
  so it bills the full stored `reasoning`/`reasoning_content` of every assistant message.

The single wire-truth predicate that the *trigger* path already uses is
`agent/message_sanitization.py::stale_thinking_reaches_wire(api_mode, provider, model, base_url)`.
The compaction trigger (`agent/turn_context.py`, `agent/turn_request_assembly.py`) and the
`ContextCompressor` all route through it. The category builder simply never adopted it.

#122257 clamped `context_used` to `context_max` and added the anchor prefix-digest, so the **header**
can no longer exceed the window — but the **legend category** is an independent per-category
`tokens_by_id` value and is still inflated. Net effect: header is capped at 100%, but the
breakdown rows still visibly over-count, which is exactly the impression that triggered this report.

## Why the trigger didn't fire (sanity)
Because the trigger uses the wire-truth predicate, the real 129.6k prompt stayed under the 196,608
threshold — correct behavior. This is a *display* accounting mismatch, not an overflow.

## Proposed fix
In `compute_session_context_breakdown`, estimate the Conversation category with the same
wire-truth the trigger uses:

```python
from agent.message_sanitization import stale_thinking_reaches_wire
on_wire = stale_thinking_reaches_wire(
    agent.api_mode, agent.provider, agent.model, agent.base_url)
...
"conversation": estimate_messages_tokens_rough(messages, charge_stale_thinking=on_wire),
```

(Read the route facts the same way `ContextCompressor._stale_thinking_on_wire()` does; keep the
two in lockstep.)

Add a behaviour test: a reasoning-heavy history (multiple assistant messages with `reasoning`) on a
non-echo route → Conversation category ≈ wire truth (excludes stale reasoning), and on an echo
route → still charges it. Assert the category and the header use the same `charge_stale_thinking`,
not a fixed number.

## Sibling paths to check (whole bug class)
Any other per-category / per-surface estimator that calls `estimate_messages_tokens_rough(...)` /
`estimate_tokens_rough(...)` **without** the wire-truth flag and then *displays* (not *decides*) a
token count. The display paths (context breakdown, `/context`, status-bar snapshot) are the ones
that should match what the model sees; decision paths already do.

## Repro
Any reasoning-heavy session (e.g. a long tool loop on a local/custom non-echo route), then open the
Desktop Context Usage panel. Conversation row ≫ the `prompt_tokens` in `agent.log` for the same
session.

cc maintainers — small, well-scoped, display-only; no cache/alternation impact.

issues.body:
In `agent/prompt_builder.py` (line ~2115), the `## Skills` preamble instructs the model:

```text
If a skill matches or is even partially relevant to your task, you MUST load it with skill_view(name)... 
Err on the side of loading — it is always better to have context you don't need...
```

While intended to prevent models from ignoring skills, in practice this can cause aggressive eager-loading of skills and breaks the progressive disclosure model. This leads to bloated context windows and excessive token usage.

This also overrides negative routing in the skill description. Even if a skill description says when not to call a skill, the uppercase `MUST load` in the system prompt overrides this.

Is the aggressive loading a deliberate design choice for model reliability, or is this potentially due for a minor rework?
