prs.title: fix(desktop): never propagate the installed-runtime skip flag into update relaunches
prs.body:
## Summary

A Desktop launch started with `--ignore-existing` / `HERMES_DESKTOP_IGNORE_EXISTING=1` (e2e harness, recovery/repair shell) exported the flag into the **posix update hand-off**, and the post-update relaunch inherited it — so the relaunched app skipped its own healthy installed runtime, fell back to first-launch bootstrap, and concurrent bootstraps collided on `.git/index.lock` (#124971). The reporter's logs show three consecutive launches logging `HERMES_DESKTOP_IGNORE_EXISTING=1; skipping the installed runtime` after an in-app update on Linux.

### Leak path (traced end-to-end)

1. `applyPosixHandoff` (`apps/desktop/electron/updater/checkout.ts`) spawns `scripts/desktop-update/posix.sh` with `sourceUpdateEnvironment(updateRoot, home)` — which is `{...process.env, ...}` (`checkout-source.ts:30`). The flag rides along.
2. `posix.sh` re-execs itself daemonized, preserving `os.environ` (the `os.execve(..., env)` at the hand-off daemonization step).
3. `launch_app()` runs `setsid "$RELAUNCH_TARGET" ...` — the relaunched app inherits the shell's environment, flag included.
4. On every subsequent resolve, `createInstalledRuntimeGate.resolve` (`backend-resolution.ts:19`) sees the flag and skips the installed-runtime rung → bootstrap-needed → first-launch setup → overlapping repository stages → `fatal: Unable to create .git/index.lock: File exists`.

The flag is **per-launch intent** for e2e/recovery shells — never a property of the installation that an update should propagate.

## What changed (three propagation surfaces, all dropping the flag)

- **`apps/desktop/electron/updater/checkout.ts`** — `applyPosixHandoff` now deletes `HERMES_DESKTOP_IGNORE_EXISTING` from the hand-off env. The update child and the relaunch it performs never need it.
- **`scripts/desktop-update/posix.sh`** — `launch_app()` unsets `HERMES_DESKTOP_IGNORE_EXISTING` before the `setsid` relaunch. Belt-and-suspenders: covers hand-offs spawned by other/older Desktop builds whose env still carries the flag (the script is refreshed from the checkout by every update).
- **`apps/desktop/electron/updater-process.ts`** — `collectRelaunchArgs` filters `--ignore-existing` from replayed argv, the same treatment as Electron's internal switches: a replayed flag re-arms the leak through argv even with a clean env.

The mac `open "$RELAUNCH_TARGET"` path does not inherit the shell env (launchd-registered bundle launch), which is why the incident is Linux-shaped; the `checkout.ts` env fix covers mac's `hermes update` subprocess regardless.

Not addressed here (bigger surface, worth their own PRs): a cross-launch bootstrap mutex for one Hermes home, and logging the flag's source at startup — both suggested in the issue; this PR removes the propagation that made them necessary.

## Testing

- [ ] WIP first version — `bash -n` syntax check passed on the modified script; unit test additions for `collectRelaunchArgs` filtering and the hand-off env (asserting the flag is absent from the spawned env) to follow on this PR.
- [ ] The issue's requested integration test (update → relaunch with healthy runtime asserts no first-launch bootstrap) needs harness work beyond this PR's scope; noted for maintainers.

Fixes #124971

prs.body:
## What changed

`cron/jobs.json` now holds only what the operator declared. Per-fire scheduler bookkeeping (`next_run_at`, `last_*`, `state` and pause markers, fire/run claims, `pending_slot`, `failure_streak`, quota holds, `repeat.completed`, ...) lives beside it in a per-profile `cron/runtime.db` (new `cron/runtime_state.py`). `load_jobs()` merges the two and `save_jobs()` splits them, so every caller still sees one dict per job, and an ordinary fire no longer rewrites `jobs.json`.

- **One schema decides the split.** `JOB_DEFINITION_FIELDS` (moved into the import-free `cron/constants.py`; `cron/job_definition.py` re-exports it, so profile distributions keep using the same list) plus `id`, `enabled` and `created_at` stay in `jobs.json`; `repeat.times` stays declarative and `repeat.completed` is runtime. Everything else is runtime, so a new scheduler field needs no registration: `quota_hold_until` / `quota_hold_cron_expr`, added to `main` after this PR was first written, are covered without being listed. An authored field missing from the list, or a key an operator adds by hand, moves to `runtime.db` on the next save, where it is still stored and merged back on every load.
- **`enabled` stays declarative on purpose.** Only pause/resume/trigger and a terminal completion write it (`_complete_job_record`), never an ordinary fire, success, failure or quota park.
- **Lossless migration.** A scheduler field found in a `jobs.json` record (a pre-split store, an older Hermes after a downgrade, or a hand edit) wins for that field, and `runtime.db` supplies every field the record does not carry. It is never a whole-record override. The first load moves the carried fields into `runtime.db` and strips them from `jobs.json` in one save. A legacy record keyed by `job_id` gets its id before the split, by the same rule as the due scan.
- **`main`'s load repairs are kept.** Junk entries are skipped before the merge; `repeat.completed` is normalized on the merged view (it now lives in `runtime.db`); structural repairs (bare list, `strict=False` control characters) rewrite the file once; an unlocked pass re-runs under `_jobs_lock()`.
- **Crash-recoverable two-file saves.** When a save changes definitions too, runtime rows and the new definitions commit together in `runtime.db` (a one-row journal) before `jobs.json` is renamed, and the journal is acknowledged afterwards. Runtime-row deletions for removed jobs are deferred to that acknowledgement. The next load finishes an interrupted save, or drops the journal if `jobs.json` was changed after that save began, and then no row has been deleted.
- **Hand-edited schedules are safe.** Each runtime row records a digest of the schedule it was computed for; if `jobs.json`'s schedule no longer matches, `next_run_at` and `pending_slot` are dropped and the due scan recomputes them. A schedule edit through `update_job` still clears a quota hold.
- **Degraded-lock writers stay narrow.** Within one `_jobs_lock()` section a save rewrites only the runtime rows it changed and deletes only `removed_ids`, mirroring the #80624 shrink-merge. The #80703 same-section fast path still skips re-reading `jobs.json`.
- **Backups copy the pair together.** Quick snapshots and full zip backups copy each store's `jobs.json` + `runtime.db` back to back under that store's lock, deciding the pair from disk at copy time; every other file (including `executions.db`) is copied outside the lock, so it is held for two small files. The post-update safety net (`restore_cron_jobs_if_emptied`) restores lost definitions together with their snapshot run state, only for jobs with no live row, all under the lock.
- `runtime.db` is handed back to the store owner when a root command creates it (same helper as `jobs.json`, #68483), and the TUI `cron.changed` signal watches it.

## Why

Closes #75607. Scheduler state and operator intent shared one file, so every fire dirtied the artifact operators back up, review, deploy or keep in source control, and a hand edit could race the ticker's next write.

## Merged current main (2026-10-10)

`main` @ `dce1e9b375` is merged in (merge commit, no rebase; the previous head `03ed543b78` is preserved at `archive/cron-runtime-ownership-03ed543`). `main` gained the unwritable-store handling (`cron/store_health.py`) on the same load/save paths this PR splits, so the merge integrates with it rather than picking a side:

- `cron/jobs.py`: the load-time repair save degrades the store on `OSError` (`store_health.note_unwritable`) and a save that lands `jobs.json` ends the outage (`note_writable`). While a store is degraded every save takes the full two-file path: a runtime-only save may write nothing (unchanged rows are skipped), so it must not confirm recovery. Without that, six of `main`'s `test_due_scan_save_failure.py` tests fail.
- `cron/runtime_state.py` (follow-up commit `99b685e85b`): `store_health` recognizes an unwritable store only by an `OSError` with one of its errnos, but a full disk or read-only store fails a `runtime.db` commit with `sqlite3.OperationalError`, which skipped the degraded path and failed the tick. Write transactions now raise `OSError` (ENOSPC / EACCES / EPERM, chained to the SQLite error) for `SQLITE_FULL`, `READONLY`, `CANTOPEN` and `PERM`. Two new tests use a real `max_page_count`-full database and a read-only `runtime.db`; both fail without the change.
- `test_skipped_oneshot_survives_recovery_by_any_save` simulated the second outage by failing only the `jobs.json` stage; it now fails `runtime.db` writes too, as a full disk does.
- Other conflicts: `cron/constants.py` keeps both sides (`JOB_DEFINITION_FIELDS` + `main`'s `is_recurring`); `tui_gateway/change_watcher.py` keeps the `runtime.db`(+WAL) watch with `main`'s `dict` payloads; `hermes_cli/backup.py` keeps the `root` parameter with `main`'s builtin generics.

The 2026-08-01 review's two points are both addressed on this head: no lookup filters tombstones any more (`get_job`, `resolve_job_ref` and `list_jobs` see every declared job; a legacy `runtime_tombstone` row is only read so the job loads as completed), and `cron-internals.md` / `cron.md` document the split, migration and paired backups.

## Rebuilt on current main (2026-09-27)

Rebuilt again, on `main` @ `8f897d2d23` (includes #80624's shrink-merge and the newer corrupt-store refusal and directory fsync, which the branch's journal and restore writes now also use). The previous head is `fc008f213c` (preserved at `archive/cron-runtime-ownership-fc008f2` on the head repository; the Sep 17 predecessor at `archive/cron-runtime-ownership-514e14b`). Changes since that head:

- The explicit `_RUNTIME_JOB_FIELDS` allowlist is replaced by the complement of `JOB_DEFINITION_FIELDS` (above). This reverses the earlier "unclassified fields stay declarative" rule: with the allowlist, `main`'s new quota-hold fields would have put `jobs.json` churn back on every quota-parked fire.
- The only merge conflict, `_load_jobs()`, is resolved in favour of keeping every repair `main` added.
- Three rounds of independent review found and fixed: structural repairs repeating on every load, `job_id` legacy records losing state, a discarded journal leaving deletions applied, backup pairs torn by a concurrent removal or migration, update recovery dropping run state, and root-owned `runtime.db`. Each fix has a regression test that fails without it.
- Full-backup pair locking, dropped in the Sep 17 rebuild, is back: the Sep 17 reasoning ("recoverable by design") did not hold once runtime rows can be deleted.

## Compatibility

- Existing stores migrate automatically on first load, with no operator action.
- `hermes status`, `hermes dump` and the update drain report read only declarative fields (`enabled`, `name`) straight from `jobs.json`, and keep working unchanged.
- **Downgrade:** an older Hermes reading a split store sees definitions without scheduler state: next runs are recomputed from now and repeat counters restart (a job with 4 of 5 runs used gets 5 more). A one-shot interrupted mid-run, or still running, can fire once more if the older build scans within its 120 s grace window; finished one-shots stay disabled because `enabled` lives in `jobs.json`. `runtime.db` is left intact, and upgrading again folds whatever the older build wrote back in.
- Back up `runtime.db` with `jobs.json`; version only `jobs.json`.

## How to verify

1. Start from a combined `jobs.json` (schedules, `last_*`, `repeat.completed`, a quota hold, a claim). List jobs: the merged view is unchanged, `jobs.json` no longer carries those fields, and `runtime.db` holds them.
2. Let a recurring job fire (or `hermes cron run <job>`), then diff `jobs.json`: it is byte-identical. Only intent changes (create, edit, pause/resume, a one-shot retiring) rewrite it.
3. Kill a process between the SQLite commit and the `jobs.json` rename, for example by making `cron.jobs.atomic_replace` raise during `update_job`. The next load completes the edit.

## Test plan

- [x] On this head (`99b685e85b`), full `scripts/run_tests.sh`: **56912 passed**, 298 failed, 1439 skipped (5481 files). The 84 failing files, run on unmodified `main` @ `dce1e9b375` in the same environment, fail 290 tests (sandbox real-home guard, uv cache / `plugin-core-dep` downloads, update/PM suites); the few that failed on only one side pass when run alone or fail identically on `main`. None is a cron, backup or watcher test. `tests/cron/test_definition_runtime_split.py` + `test_due_scan_save_failure.py`: 45 passed.
- [x] `check-windows-footguns.py` and `ruff check` clean on every file this merge touches.

Previous head (2026-09-27):

- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 6 --file-retries 0` over every test file that imports `cron`, touches `jobs.json`, or covers snapshots/backups (356 files): **6617 passed**, 136 failed, 162 skipped. 135 of the failures also fail on unmodified `main` @ `8f897d2d23` in the same run set (update/state-db/profile-PTY suites that touch the real host environment on the test machine). The other one, `test_holder_scan_sees_through_a_symlinked_home`, is a macOS holder probe in `hermes_state/`, which this PR does not touch; run alone it fails 4/4 on both this branch and `main`.
- [x] `tests/cron/test_definition_runtime_split.py`: 30 tests, including one regression test per review finding, each shown failing before its fix.
- [x] E2E on this head against an isolated `HERMES_HOME` with the real CLI: a `--no-agent` script job fired twice (`hermes cron run` + `hermes cron tick`; `hermes cron runs` shows both completed) left `jobs.json` byte-identical (same SHA-256), with `last_*`, `next_run_at` and the schedule digest in `runtime.db` and none of them in `jobs.json`; `hermes cron list` shows the merged view (`Last run: … ok`).
- [x] Existing assertions adapted: `test_profile_call_cannot_retarget_ticker_store_mid_write` reads the owning profile's `runtime.db`; `test_root_writer_restores_previous_owner` now asserts on the `jobs.json` chown specifically, since `runtime.db` is also handed back.
- [x] `ruff check`, `git diff --check`: clean. `check-windows-footguns.py --diff` reports only three pre-existing lines in `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_cron_profiles.py` that this PR does not change.
- [ ] Windows: the SQLite and rename paths use the same helpers as `jobs.json` / `executions.db`; hosted CI is the arbiter.

## Risk

**Medium.** This changes where cron persists state. The merge/split is confined to `load_jobs()` / `_save_jobs_unlocked()` and the backup pair copy; no scheduler, delivery or ownership logic changed.

prs.title: chore(memory): holographic leaves core for its community catalog plugin
prs.body:
## What moves

The holographic memory provider (local SQLite fact store, `fact_store` / `fact_feedback`) no longer ships inside Hermes. This PR deletes `plugins/memory/holographic/` and the tests that only covered it. The provider now comes from the plugin catalog entry `holographic`, which points at **[itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic) @ `46b6f908` (v0.6.1)**. That repo is community-maintained by itpartypattaya and is a fork of Nous's handoff copy. The catalog entry was reviewed in sweep 1011. This is the removal we announced for Oct 15, 2026. **Please merge on or after that date.**

## How users migrate

It happens automatically. `holographic` was already in `_LEFT_CORE`, so once the bundled copy is gone:

- `hermes update` installs the catalog plugin into every profile whose config says `memory.provider: holographic`.
- Desktop users and anyone who doesn't run `hermes update` get it on the first agent start, and Hermes tells them it happened.
- With `security.allow_lazy_installs: false`, the agent-start path installs nothing and prints the exact `hermes plugins install holographic` command instead.

**Data and settings carry over.** The catalog plugin keeps the provider name, reads the same `$HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db`, and reads the same `plugins.hermes-memory-store` config. Nothing gets copied or converted.

**People who installed Nous's archived repo by URL** (`NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic`) had no catalog record, so `hermes plugins update` would keep pulling the archive. Hermes now treats an install from that repo as the `holographic` catalog entry, so `hermes plugins update holographic` moves it to itpartypattaya's repo at the reviewed sha (`_HANDOFF_REPOS` in `plugins_cmd_catalog.py`, 13 lines, plus a test).

That live run surfaced a second problem, which this PR fixes in one line. A catalog **re-pin** (`hermes plugins update` on a catalog install) scanned the reviewed tree as if it came from an unreviewed community source, so caution findings blocked it. A fresh catalog install of the same sha already gets reviewed-pin trust. The 46b6f908 tree has 14 caution findings, so this blocked re-pinning *any* existing holographic catalog install, not just the handoff case. `update_plugin` now passes `reviewed_pin=True` when it clones the catalog sha. Dangerous findings still block.

## Other changes

- `gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py`: when a profile is unserved, the memory-store handle release now goes through `import_provider_module("holographic", "store")`. `profiles.py` already did it this way, and it no longer imports `plugins.memory.holographic`.
- Docs: the memory-providers page has a Holographic section with a catalog notice, the maintainer and a "Migrating from bundled Holographic" subsection. The provider lists in `memory.md`, `overview.md`, `integrations/index.md`, `cli-commands.md`, the `hermes memory --help` text, `config_defaults.py`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`.es.md` and `plugins/AGENTS.md` now show holographic as a catalog provider.
- Tests: tests that used holographic as "a bundled provider" now use byterover. The journal-mode contract no longer has a holographic row because the plugin owns that store now.

## Live proof

Spend-free, using the real CLI in an isolated `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME` under scratch. The user's real `~/.hermes` was not touched. The seed was written by the **bundled provider from origin/main**: `memory.provider: holographic`, `plugins.hermes-memory-store: {default_trust: 0.6, hrr_dim: 512, auto_extract: false}`, 3 facts in `memory_store.db`. Then I ran the branch, where the bundled directory is gone.

| Path | Step | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before migration | `hermes memory status` | `Plugin: NOT installed ✗` / `Install it with: hermes plugins install holographic` |
| `hermes update` hook (`memory_provider_migration.migrate_all_homes`, as `source_build.py` calls it) | migrate | `[profile 'default'] ✓ Memory provider 'holographic' moved out of core — installed its plugin from the catalog …` |
| | installed tree | `plugins/holographic` HEAD `46b6f9084bd6ebd13262fb2360f3314c352f4be8`, origin `https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic`, `plugin.yaml` version 0.6.1, install record `catalog.name=holographic, pinned=true` |
| | `hermes memory status` | `Plugin: installed ✓` · `Status: available ✓` · `holographic (local) ← active` |
| | `hermes plugins list` | `holographic │ enabled │ 0.6.1 │ catalog:community…` |
| | provider resolves | `_hermes_user_memory.holographic__source_…` from `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/holographic`; bundled directory does not exist |
| | facts via the provider | `fact_store list` → all 3 seeded facts (ids 1-3, trust 0.6); `search "staging server"` → fact 2 "orchid-7" |
| | config preserved | `memory.provider: holographic` and `plugins.hermes-memory-store` unchanged; the provider sees `default_trust 0.6, hrr_dim 512, auto_extract False` |
| | DB | `memory_store.db` byte-identical to the seed after the migration and the queries |
| Agent init (`recover_at_startup("holographic", say=…)`, as `agent_init.py` calls it), fresh copy of the seed | migrate | startup warning `✓ Memory provider 'holographic' moved out of core …` → `installed: True`, HEAD `46b6f908…`, 3 facts and settings intact |
| URL install of the archived Nous repo | `hermes plugins install https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic` | HEAD `e0106f2e` (0.1.1), record `{pinned: false, source: NousResearch/…}` |
| | `hermes plugins update holographic` | `Checking catalog pin for holographic...` → asks about the new dependency (snowballstemmer) → `✓ Plugin holographic updated to 46b6f908.` origin is now itpartypattaya, record `catalog.name=holographic, pinned=true`, version 0.6.1, 3 facts and settings intact |
| | same update **without** the scan-trust fix | `Decision: BLOCKED — community source + caution verdict, 14 findings` |
| Off-pin catalog install (`install holographic --ref eb436781`, then update) | re-pin | origin/main code: blocked, same as above · branch: `✓ Plugin holographic updated to 46b6f908.` |

## Tests

Suites run: memory provider, plugins, migration and related (`tests/hermes_cli/test_*memory*`, `test_left_core_migration`, `test_plugin*`, `test_plugins_cmd*`, `test_profiles`, `tests/plugins/`, `tests/agent/test_memory_provider.py`, `test_pre_compress_checkpoint_contract`, `test_journal_mode_config`, `test_shutdown_memory_provider_messages`, `test_multiplex_unserved_shared_ingress`), via `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 6`, same file set on both trees:

| | files | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| origin/main | 162 | 1839 | 154 |
| this branch | 155 (7 holographic test files deleted) | 1861 | 151 |

No test fails on this branch that passes on origin/main. The failures common to both are environmental. The local worktrees live under `~/.hermes`, which trips the conftest real-home guard (`TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home …/.worktrees/manifest.json`), and some suites need real `uv`. Five `test_plugins_cmd.py` tests show up as ERROR on main and FAILED on the branch, but run on their own they fail identically on both trees. The 8 failures that only appear on main (`test_memory_dependency_admission`, `test_web_memory_provider_setup_install`) were `uv` contention under `-j 6`; run on their own they pass on main (13/13). New test: `test_url_install_of_an_archived_handoff_repo_is_repinned_to_its_catalog_entry`. It fails without the `plugins_transaction.py` change.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aade67e/MfMWDHZ8hFshUrfDPII1G_QqYC4I21.png)

Re-lands #136424 at Teknium's direction. Holographic now has a standalone third-party maintainer (@itpartypattaya) and a reviewed catalog entry (`itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic` @ `46b6f908`), so it leaves core now instead of on Oct 15.

This reverts the revert (#136432: `435b7bd3a7` plus its health-waiver commit `b9ecc727e9`). All 30 files #136424 touched are byte-identical to `9e827685f2`. Everything #136424 carried is back:

- by-URL installs of the archived Nous repo are moved to the catalog entry;

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add Ace Data Cloud Nano Banana
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one independently installable community catalog entry for **Ace Data Cloud Nano Banana**. Image generation and HTTPS reference-image editing through your Ace Data Cloud account.

Source: https://github.com/AceDataCloud/NanoBananaHermes/pull/1
Exact source pin: `bb33202aefbc7aa750a52f6ef042ed0d3ca9ddd8`
Public real-call evidence: https://github.com/AceDataCloud/NanoBananaHermes/blob/bb33202aefbc7aa750a52f6ef042ed0d3ca9ddd8/tests/live-evidence.json

The source PR remains open for internal review; the pinned commit is public and validated. No core-tree integration, default bundling or recommendation is claimed. This is one of 17 independent Ace Data Cloud tool integrations aligned with our submitted Dify services, alongside the already-listed model provider.


## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (catalog entry only)

## Changes Made

- Add `plugin-catalog/acedatacloud-nano-banana.yaml` only. Capabilities exactly match registered tools and the declared environment key.
- Pin the unmodified Ace logo/catalog image to the same source SHA.

## Disclosure

Paid HTTPS requests go only to `https://api.acedata.cloud` for the requested operation/task query. Prompts and explicitly supplied HTTPS reference URLs are sent for processing. The plugin reads only `ACEDATACLOUD_API_KEY` from the active profile's secret scope; no local credential files, sibling repositories, telemetry, subprocesses, background processes, self-update or runtime core overrides. It returns links without downloading media. Credentials are not forwarded across origin redirects. Submissions are never automatically retried; task-query failures keep the original ID. README documents billing and recovery behavior.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <checkout-at-pin> --install-deps` on official Hermes 0.21.6: passed, security scan **safe**, no dependency additions.
2. `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 21 tests, with the sync-only test skipped on async media plugins. Covers non-final previews/errors, no submit retry, task-ID preservation, URL/schema validation, media selection and redaction.
3. Fresh isolated stable Hermes installation and real primary-operation call: **succeeded**. Submitted exactly once, then queried the same task to completion; returned primary media fully decoded. No existing user Hermes instance was changed. Other option combinations are not claimed as live-tested.
4. Local catalog schema validation passed. Source CI at the exact pin:
- https://github.com/AceDataCloud/NanoBananaHermes/actions/runs/37821818793/job/113464487918
- https://github.com/AceDataCloud/NanoBananaHermes/actions/runs/37821803944/job/113464431827

## Checklist

- [x] Read contributing guide and catalog admission policy.
- [x] Searched existing PRs and entries; no duplicate Ace entry.
- [x] Conventional catalog commit; only this entry changed.
- [x] Documentation, capability declarations, brand and platform impact checked.
- [x] AI assistance disclosed: implemented using Codex; validation performed as described above.
- [ ] Full core `pytest tests/ -q` / `python scripts/check` were not run locally for this catalog-only change; upstream CI remains authoritative.

## Screenshots / Logs

![Ace Data Cloud](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AceDataCloud/NanoBananaHermes/bb33202aefbc7aa750a52f6ef042ed0d3ca9ddd8/assets/catalog.png)

See the source evidence link for terminal output, media digests/codecs and verification limits.

prs.title: security(approval): treat consent as an allow-list, not a deny-list
prs.body:
## The problem

`_human_decision.grant()` in `tools/approval.py` runs the flagged action unless the answer is `"deny"`, `None` or `"timeout"`. Every other value is treated as consent.

The local CLI prompt is unaffected either way — `prompt_dangerous_approval` normalizes keystrokes through a lookup table, so only canonical words leave it. Two paths hand their answer straight through without normalizing:

- the gateway round-trip, `_await_gateway_decision`, an inter-process message
- third-party approval transport plugins

So a client that starts sending a different token after an upgrade, a truncated payload, or a plugin bug reads as a yes. Concretely, `""`, `"null"`, `"1"`, `"yes"` and `None` all approved the command.

## The fix

`CONSENT_ANSWERS = {"once", "session", "always"}`. Anything else is refused with `outcome="unrecognized_answer"` and the rejected value logged.

## Why this needs boundary normalization, not just an allow-list

A bare allow-list breaks a consent path that currently works.

`gateway/platforms/whatsapp_cloud.py` builds its Approve button as the payload `appr:<approval_id>:approve` and passes the literal string `"approve"` to `resolve_gateway_approval`, which stores it verbatim as the waiting agent's choice. With a strict allow-list and no normalization:

1. the user taps **Approve**
2. the agent unblocks, sees `unrecognized_answer`, and does **not** run the command
3. `whatsapp_cloud.py` still replies **"✅ Approved."**

A refused command, reported to the user as approved.

So `_canonical_choice()` lowercases and strips, then maps an affirmative alias set onto a canonical word *before* the allow-list runs. The alias set is the one `gateway/platforms/api_server_runs.py` already applies (`_APPROVAL_CHOICE_ALIASES`), so the two stay in step rather than drifting apart.

Every alias maps to **`once`**, the narrowest scope — an Approve tap is one operation and must never persist a session or permanent grant. There's a test asserting exactly that, and its mirror asserting a real `session` answer still does persist.

Case and whitespace are normalized for the same reason: `"ONCE"` is the same decision as `"once"`, and the values worth refusing are unrecognized ones, not differently-spelled ones.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_approval_answer_allowlist.py`, covering both the gateway path and the CLI callback seam:

- eight non-consent values refused (`"yes"`, `"ok"`, `"true"`, `"accept"`, `""`, `"null"`, `"1"`, `"denied"`)
- the three consent words still approve
- every alias still approves, including the WhatsApp `"approve"` payload
- `"deny"` keeps its own `denied` outcome rather than being relabelled
- `"approve"` proven not to leave a session or permanent grant
- a normalized `"  Session  "` proven to still leave one
- `None` from the CLI callback refused

## Scope

Purely additive: **244 insertions, 0 deletions.** No existing behaviour removed, and no existing test needed changing — the full approval suite (`test_approval`, `test_approval_interrupt`, `test_cli_approval_exec_ask_leak`, `test_execute_code_approval_cluster`, `test_modal_sandbox_fixes`, `test_cron_approval_mode`, `test_request_tool_approval`, plus the gateway approval tests) passes unchanged.

Happy to adjust naming or split the normalization out if you'd prefer it live in `resolve_gateway_approval` instead of `grant`.

## What does this PR do?

Cover recovery after a custom endpoint's background model-cache refresh fails. The cache should keep its last known catalog and allow the next picker open to retry. Existing tests cover refresh admission and successful writes, but do not exercise a failed worker followed by a successful retry.

The new test drives `cached_fetch_api_models` through the real refresh worker and a temporary JSON cache. It verifies that an exception or an empty fetch result leaves the cache unchanged, the next open retries, and a successful retry makes the new models visible without changing a sibling cache row. Main already implements this behavior; production code is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No new issue. Tests the existing refresh contract introduced in #76430 and generalized for custom endpoints in #81113. The cache-only refresh admission added in #106462 is exercised through completion and recovery.

## Type of Change

- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- Add one lifecycle test parametrized for `OSError` and `None` fetch results in `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_refresh_recovery.py`.
- Use the real fingerprint, cache loader/writer, custom refresh callback and in-flight cleanup. A small queued thread double makes worker execution deterministic; the injected fetch callback supplies synthetic results.
- Keep `HOME`, `HERMES_HOME` and cache state isolated. No threads, sleeps, network requests or real credentials are needed.

## How to Test

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_swr.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cached_fetch_api_models.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_fallback_rows.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_refresh_recovery.py
```

The full suite, other operating systems, live endpoints and concurrent thread scheduling were not tested.

prs.title: fix(telegram): bound the fallback path walk's connect budget
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes silent Telegram delivery loss when the network path to `api.telegram.org` flaps. The adapter wraps every send in a wall-clock deadline (`_TEXT_SEND_DEADLINE = 30s`), but the httpx client's connect timeout applies **per fallback path** inside `TelegramFallbackTransport` (sticky → IPv4 literals → hostname). Several hung paths can sum past the send deadline; the deadline then fires mid-walk and surfaces as a bare `TimeoutError` with no cause chain. The send classifier must treat that as non-retryable (a read timeout may already have delivered), so the delivery gets **neither a retry nor a plain fallback** and the obligation walks to `abandoned` (#136412: `abandoned=9, delivered=490`, all with `send_path_degraded`).

The fix bounds the path walk instead of touching the classification:

- `TelegramFallbackTransport` gains a `connect_budget` — the total CONNECT budget shared by one request's whole path walk. The sticky path is front-loaded (it gets `remaining - remaining/paths_left` — everything but one average share held back for failover — so at stock defaults it keeps the client's full 10s connect), and later paths split the remainder (`remaining / paths_left`), enforced by narrowing the per-request httpx `timeout` extension dict (`extensions["timeout"]["connect"]` — the same mechanism `AsyncClient._set_timeout` uses, honoured per request by the transport). A tighter configured connect is never widened; requests without a timeout dict are untouched.
- When the budget is spent, the walk stops and raises the last underlying `ConnectTimeout` immediately — that is the one error the existing classifier (`_looks_like_connect_timeout`) already treats as safely retryable, so `_send_with_retry` and the plain-text fallback engage instead of abandoning.
- The adapter passes `connect_budget=_TEXT_SEND_DEADLINE / 2`, leaving the other half of the send deadline for the winning path's TLS + request/response.

Deliberately NOT changed: a bare deadline timeout stays non-retryable — once the walk is bounded, that only happens when a connected request is slow to respond, where the request may already have been delivered and re-sending would duplicate.

`_shutdown_abandoned_app` moves from `adapter.py` to `telegram_network.py` (same network-resource theme, only 3 call sites, no external references) to offset the adapter growth per FILE_LINES.

## Related Issue

Fixes #136412

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/telegram_network.py`: `TelegramFallbackTransport.__init__` accepts keyword-only `connect_budget`; `handle_async_request` front-loads the sticky path (everything but one average share held back) and splits the remainder across the paths left, stops the walk when the budget is spent and surfaces the last connect error; new `_request_with_connect_budget` helper narrows only the CONNECT phase of the httpx per-request timeout extension; `_shutdown_abandoned_app` moved here from the adapter (unchanged).
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: `_build_ptb_requests` passes `connect_budget=_TEXT_SEND_DEADLINE / 2` to both fallback transports; `_shutdown_abandoned_app` now imported from `telegram_network`.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_fallback_connect_budget.py` (new): budget share allocation, budget-exhaustion surfacing the underlying `ConnectTimeout`, no widening of tighter connects, legacy behavior with no budget, and no timeout-dict injection.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_fallback_connect_budget.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_network.py -q` — Observed result: 24 passed.
2. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_closewait_limits.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_fallback_pool_release.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_polling_progress.py tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/ -q` — Observed result: 43 passed (existing suites, no regression).
3. `python scripts/check --base <upstream/main SHA>` — Observed result: 11 checks ok (health 0 blocking; the 8 failures in `test_adapter_settings_scoped_precedence.py` reproduce identically on a clean `upstream/main` checkout — pre-existing, unrelated WhatsApp-scope cases).
4. Deterministic budget-walk proof: with a frozen clock and a 15s budget over 3 paths, the recorded per-path connect caps are `15/3, 15/2, then the client's own tighter 10.0`; with each attempt burning 6s against a 10s budget, only 2 paths are tried and path 2's `ConnectTimeout` is raised — no third attempt is armed for the send deadline to mask.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.7 (Apple Silicon), Python 3.11

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A

- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

prs.title: fix(agent): honor stream_only_base_urls on same-provider retry paths
prs.body:
## What

Same-provider recovery retries for auxiliary LLM calls dropped the stream-only wrapper. The initial attempt routes through `_create_with_progress` / `_acreate_with_stream` with `force_stream` computed from `auxiliary.stream_only_base_urls`, but both recovery-ladder retry helpers (`_retry_same_provider_sync`, `_retry_same_provider_async` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py`) rebuilt the request and called the relay directly — so any endpoint configured as stream-only silently fell back to **non-streaming** on every recovery retry.

Both retry wrappers now compute `force_stream` from the same config source (`_provider_requires_stream`, recomputing the effective provider/base URL from the rebuilt client exactly as `_prepare_same_provider_retry` does) and route through the same stream-only wrappers as the initial attempt. The shared `_prepare_same_provider_retry()` preparation is untouched. The async wrapper mirrors the initial async path's full native-client exclusion tuple (`AsyncCodexAuxiliaryClient`, `AsyncAnthropicAuxiliaryClient`, `AsyncBedrockAuxiliaryClient`), so OpenAI-style `stream`/`stream_options` kwargs are never pushed at adapters that don't speak them.

## Why this matters

`auxiliary.stream_only_base_urls` exists for endpoints where non-streaming requests hang or fail (e.g. gateways behind short proxy read timeouts that silently drop long non-streaming calls). On such an endpoint the failure chain was:

1. Initial attempt streams fine, but a transient timeout triggers recovery
2. Same-provider retry goes out **non-streaming** (wrapper dropped)
3. The gateway holds the connection with zero output; the caller's stale watchdog kills it at ~90s
4. Retry loop repeats → the aux task (often compression, on the preflight critical path) never completes

The retry path is exactly where stream-only endpoints need protection most, because it is reached only after a first failure.

## How to test

New tests in `tests/agent/test_retry_same_provider_stream_only.py` (5 tests, sync + async):

```bash
pytest tests/agent/test_retry_same_provider_stream_only.py -v  # 5 passed
```

- sync/async: stream-only base URL forces `stream=True` on the retry; unlisted URLs keep the plain non-streaming call (behavior preserved)
- async native-client exclusion: a real `AsyncCodexAuxiliaryClient` instance on a stream-only URL still gets the plain call and `_acreate_with_stream` is never invoked

Existing suites:

```bash
pytest tests/agent/test_aux_progress_streaming.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): redelivered replies keep their original order and say when they were due
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A held reply that comes back through the ledger's redelivery path now (a) flushes in
`created_at` order and (b) states when it was originally due.

## Why

The boot sweep and the runtime reconnect sweep claimed undelivered rows with **no `ORDER BY`**,
so a flush followed SQLite storage order — which `record_obligation()`'s `INSERT OR REPLACE`
rewrites (a replace is a delete + re-insert, so the rowid moves). The claimed row also carried no
`created_at`, and the recovered-reply markers carry no timestamp, so the recipient had no way to
tell when a recovered reply had been meant to go out.

Observed on a personal deployment (single peer, Weixin/iLink):

- 19 replies were held between **08:58 and 20:39** — each send refused with
  `ret=-2 ... prepare failed` once the peer's reply window had closed.
- A gateway restart at **22:03:52** ran the boot sweep: all 19 were delivered in ~3 s
  (**22:04:17–22:04:20**), i.e. *after* the live messages sent at 21:04 / 21:29 / 21:33.
- The recipient saw a burst of morning replies after the current ones, and nothing in the
  messages said when each was originally due.

This is the at-least-once design working as intended — nothing is lost — so the fix is to make the
batch ordered and self-describing rather than to change *what* gets redelivered.

## Related

- #135921 / #135922 — the adapter-level hold queue. That path already flushes in order, before the
  peer's own reply. This is the **other** mechanism for the same failure mode (the ledger owns
  refused *final responses*), and it is the one that has no ordering guarantee.
- Independently reproduced in #135921 by @LtetMoi, who found the ledger exhausting `MAX_ATTEMPTS`
  and abandoning the row while a later inbound restored sending.

## Changes

`gateway/delivery_ledger.py`
- `ORDER BY created_at` on the two claim queries (`sweep_recoverable`, `sweep_failed_for_runtime`).
  The third query that reads the table is a `min()` aggregation — an `ORDER BY` there is a no-op,
  so it is deliberately left alone.
- `_claimed_row()` carries `created_at` (2 call sites, both already select it).

`gateway/run_startup.py`
- Redeliveries are prefixed with the new `gateway.redelivered_due` string, then the existing
  recovered marker (which distinguishes restart / reconnect / flood) is kept as-is.

`locales/*.yaml`
- New key `gateway.redelivered_due: "[Redelivered · originally due {when}]"` in **all 17 catalogs**
  (16 translations + English). `tests/agent/test_i18n.py` enforces key-set and `{placeholder}`
  parity across catalogs, so every language is covered rather than falling back to English.

`tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger.py`
- New test: a backlog whose **insert order is the reverse of chronological order** flushes
  oldest-first, and every claimed row reports its original `created_at`.
- The three exact-content assertions on redelivery markers move to a shared `_assert_stamped()`
  helper pinning the new shape (**stamp, then marker, then body**) — the marker text is unchanged,
  but it is no longer the first thing in the message.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger.py -q                     # 44 passed
pytest tests/gateway/test_restart_redelivery_dedup.py \
       tests/gateway/test_queued_final_ledger.py \
       tests/gateway/test_active_turn_recovery.py \
       tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger_fd_leak.py \
       tests/gateway/test_delivery_ledger_single_connection.py -q    # 41 passed
pytest tests/ -k "i18n or locale" -q                                # 150 passed, 11 skipped
```

The one failure in the last selection,
`test_discord_exec_approval_button_labels_localized_and_capped`, reproduces on unmodified `main`
(it is unrelated to this change).

## Out of scope

Whether a held reply should expire instead of being redelivered however old it is. Today the
ledger redelivers regardless of age (7-day retention applies to `delivered`/`abandoned` cleanup),
while the adapter queue in #135922 bounds its hold at 1 h. Making those two consistent is a
behaviour change and deserves its own decision.

prs.title: fix(copilot): resolve Claude reasoning-effort from live catalog
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`AIAgent` has two reasoning gates that resolve which `reasoning_effort` levels a model supports:

- `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()`
- `_github_models_reasoning_extra_body()`

For the `models.github.ai` / `api.githubcopilot.com` routes, both call `github_model_reasoning_efforts(self.model)` with no catalog and no `api_key`. With no catalog, the function falls through to the static GPT/o-series table (`_github_reasoning_efforts_for_model_id`), which has no entry for Claude, so it returns `[]`.

Result for Copilot-hosted Claude (opus / sonnet):

- `_supports_reasoning_extra_body()` returns `False`
- `_github_models_reasoning_extra_body()` returns `None`

A configured `reasoning_effort` (e.g. `high`) is silently dropped for every Claude-on-Copilot request, even though the live Copilot `/models` catalog advertises `capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort` for those models.

**Fix:** `get_copilot_reasoning_efforts(model_id, api_key)` in `hermes_cli/models.py` supplies the live `/models` catalog to `github_model_reasoning_efforts`. The catalog is cached in-process for one hour (mirrors `get_copilot_model_context`). Both gates are rewired to it. Degrades gracefully to the static table when the catalog is unavailable.

## Related Issue

Fixes #52384

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/models.py`: new `get_copilot_reasoning_efforts(model_id, api_key)` with 1-hour in-process cache.
- `run_agent.py`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, `agent/transports/chat_completions.py`, `plugins/model-providers/copilot/__init__.py`: rewire both reasoning gates to call `get_copilot_reasoning_efforts`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_copilot_context.py`: new `TestGetCopilotReasoningEfforts` covering catalog resolution, the empty-list regression, caching, expiry, and graceful degradation.
- `tests/plugins/model_providers/test_copilot_profile.py`: updated for new gate behaviour.

## How to Test

1. Configure Hermes with a Copilot provider and a Claude model (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4`).
2. Set `reasoning_effort: high` in config.
3. Send a message. Confirm `reasoning_effort` appears in the outgoing request body (was silently dropped before).
4. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_copilot_context.py tests/plugins/model_providers/test_copilot_profile.py -v` — all 95 tests pass.

## What does this PR do?

Extends the session-continuity fix from #37144 to DM channels, which the original PR excluded via `channel_type_raw != "D"`.

Root DM posts had `thread_id=None`; replies carried `root_id=<root post id>`. This produced two different session keys, so the agent lost all context on the first threaded DM reply. #37144 fixed this for channels but left DMs broken.

Removing the `channel_type_raw != "D"` guard gives DMs the same treatment: `thread_id = post.get("root_id") or post_id` when `reply_mode == "thread"`.

```diff
-        if (
-            not thread_id
-            and self._reply_mode == "thread"
-            and channel_type_raw != "D"
-            and post_id
-        ):
-            thread_id = post_id
```

prs.title: feat(gateway): Mattermost live-thinking bubble
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a **live-thinking bubble** to the Mattermost gateway: while the agent works, its internal thoughts are posted (and live-updated) as a `> 💭  _"..."_` blockquote message. When the agent is done, **the bubble is edited in place with the final response** — no delete/new-post sequence, no `(message deleted)` artifact.

### Changes

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: `edit_message()` and `delete_message()` implementations; `register_post_delivery_callback()` for deferred cleanup.
- `gateway/run.py`:
  - `_interim_assistant_cb` path: when `live_thinking` is enabled, post/edit the thinking bubble instead of sending commentary inline.
  - Gate `_live_thinking_adapter` on `edit_message` capability (adapters lacking it fall back silently).
  - Suppress `stream_delta_callback` when `live_thinking` is active — per-token edits would flood the MM API; the bubble IS the streaming UX.
  - Bypass `stream_consumer.on_commentary()` when `live_thinking` is active so thoughts reach the bubble path.
  - **Bubble replace on completion**: edit the bubble with the final response (3× retry + exponential backoff); `already_sent=True` + `_live_thinking_post_ids.clear()` on success. Delete fires post-delivery only as last-resort fallback after exhausted retries.
  - **Footer edit-append**: when a bubble was just replaced with the final answer, the runtime footer (`display.runtime_footer.enabled`) is edit-appended onto that same post instead of firing as its own standalone trailing post. Falls back to a separate trailing post only if that edit fails, so the footer is never lost.
  - Format thoughts as `> 💭  _"..."_` blockquote.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: document `display.live_thinking` config key.

## Related Issue

Closes #54228

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: `edit_message`, `delete_message`, `register_post_delivery_callback`
- `gateway/run.py`: live-thinking bubble post/edit/replace pipeline; stream suppression; retry+backoff
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: `display.live_thinking` documented
- `gateway/run.py`: edit-append runtime footer onto the replaced live-thinking bubble; fallback to trailing send preserved
- `tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py`: `TestLiveThinkingFooterEditAppend` — edit-append success, edit failure fallback, edit exception fallback, no-bubble regression guard

## How to Test

1. Configure a Mattermost gateway with `display.live_thinking: true`
2. Send a message that requires several tool calls
3. Observe the `> 💭  _"..."_` bubble updating in place during the run
4. When the agent finishes, the bubble should be **edited** to show the final response — no new post, no `(message deleted)`
5. Send a message where the agent responds immediately (no tools) — bubble should still be replaced with the final response
6. With `display.runtime_footer.enabled: true`, repeat step 4 — the runtime footer should be appended onto the same edited bubble post, not delivered as a separate trailing message

prs.title: fix(cli): sweep a custom-path checkout's desktop build output on GUI uninstall
prs.body:
`hermes uninstall --gui` now removes the desktop build output of the checkout it is running from, not only the `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent` tree install.sh writes. On a git checkout cloned to any other directory (what `hermes --version` reports as the install directory), the command used to report success while leaving `apps/desktop/{dist,release,node_modules}` and the workspace `node_modules` in place — and the next `hermes update` rebuilt the desktop app from artifacts it had never removed.

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py::source_built_gui_artifacts` discovers **both** GUI artifact layouts: `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent` (the install.sh layout) and the running checkout, derived from the module's own location (`hermes_cli/` sits directly under the checkout root). Candidates are deduplicated by lexical path identity, so an install where the two coincide still yields one set.
- `gui_is_installed`, `gui_install_summary` and `uninstall_gui` take an optional `project_root` and thread it through; with no caller-supplied root, discovery keys off the running checkout. The parameter exists for direct testing — the DI seam the AGENTS.md guidance asks for — not as a new configuration surface.
- `hermes_cli/uninstall.py`: `run_gui_uninstall` resolves the checkout once (`get_project_root()`) and passes it to both the summary and the removal. The keep-data/full sweep in `_perform_uninstall` already had `project_root` in scope and now passes it too, so the GUI-only path and the full wipe cannot disagree about what "the GUI artifacts" are.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall.py`: three tests — a custom-path checkout is discovered in the summary and removed by `uninstall_gui`; the standard layout is not listed twice when both roots resolve to the same directory; with no caller-supplied root, the running checkout is a candidate.

## Root cause

`source_built_gui_artifacts` derived its one root as `hermes_home / "hermes-agent"`, a layout that only exists when the checkout lives under `$HERMES_HOME`. The desktop build, the update tail and the rebuild decision all key off the **running checkout** instead (`PROJECT_ROOT/apps/desktop` in `update_cmd.py`, `root/apps/desktop` in `venv_sync.py`), so the uninstaller and the updater looked at different directories whenever they differed. The behavior the docs promise was implemented against the standard layout only.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall.py` | 7 passed (4 existing + 3 new) |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the uninstall family (gui_uninstall, cmd_uninstall, uninstall_dry_run, uninstall_full_wipe_sweep, uninstall_gui_userdata, uninstall_leftovers, data_uninstall) | 31 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped |
| Module identity on a custom-path checkout: same interpreter imports `hermes_cli.gui_uninstall` from `/home/turgutk/Hermes-Agent/hermes_cli/...`, and `_running_checkout_root()` returns `/home/turgutk/Hermes-Agent` | confirmed |
| Live `hermes uninstall --gui-summary` on that checkout | inconclusive **on this box only**: the checkout's `apps/desktop/{dist,release,node_modules}` and workspace `node_modules` were already absent when the fix landed (removed by a separate `pm` dependency sync at 14:53:55, not by this change), so the summary has nothing to list. The unit tests carry the proof. |

`git log -S` history and PR #40355 (the commit that added `gui_uninstall.py`) confirm the intent: its description already promises removal of "source-built dist/release/node_modules + build stamp". This is a gap against that intent, not an intentional design.

## Scope and caveats

- Tested on **Linux only** (Ubuntu/Debian host, Python 3.14 runtime). The change is path arithmetic plus threading one argument; macOS and Windows use the same function (`packaged_gui_app_paths` is the platform-specific part and is untouched), but I could not exercise those hosts.
- No documentation change: `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` already states the source-checkout behavior this PR makes true.
- No new dependency, no config key, no env var.
- Untouched on purpose: `desktop_install_record()` (`~/.hermes/desktop-installed-apps.json`) and the `~/.hermes/desktop-build-stamp.json` stamp already resolve under `HERMES_HOME` correctly, and the stamp is what keeps a *lost* bundle recoverable (#90495). Only the checkout-relative artifacts were mis-scoped.

## Reproduction

1. Clone the repo to a directory that is not `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent` (the default for a dev checkout) and run `hermes desktop --build-only` once, so `apps/desktop/{dist,release,node_modules}` exist.
2. `hermes uninstall --gui-summary` on `main`: `source_built_artifacts` lists only the stamp; the checkout's build output is invisible to the uninstaller.
3. On this branch: the same command lists `apps/desktop/dist`, `apps/desktop/release`, `apps/desktop/node_modules` and the workspace `node_modules`, and `hermes uninstall --gui` removes them.

No tracking issue: `gh search issues` / `gh search prs` (all states) for the symptom returned no match; the one adjacent hit (#103055, closed) is about the *rebuild* decision reading a stale stamp, not about the uninstaller's path scoping.



## Rebase adaptations (2026-10-03)

Rebased onto current `main` (`bd0affe5e5`). Two adaptations were required while resolving the
rebase conflict in `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py`:

- Upstream `f9fec19d96` ("fix(gui): keep shared workspace node_modules on uninstall --gui")
  deliberately stopped treating the workspace-root `node_modules` as a GUI artifact (the root
  `package.json` is an npm workspace shared by the TUI and dashboard; Electron resolves from
  `apps/desktop/node_modules`). This PR now follows that rule for **both** roots: it sweeps
  `<root>/apps/desktop/{dist,release,node_modules}` for the `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent` layout
  **and** the running checkout, but no longer removes either workspace-root `node_modules`.
  The regression test was updated accordingly.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): seed prior thread posts into first-turn context
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

When Hermes is drawn into an existing Mattermost thread for the first time (a reply carrying `root_id`, in a thread it has no session for yet), it had no context of the conversation it just joined. The receive path in `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py` read `root_id` for session keying and reply routing only; it never called `GET /api/v4/posts/{root_id}/thread`, so the LLM saw just the triggering message.

Slack already solves this with `_fetch_thread_context()`; Mattermost was the remaining gap tracked by #37695. This adds first-turn thread-history seeding for the Mattermost adapter, mirroring the Slack approach and reusing existing infrastructure.

Design notes:

- Seeded history is attached through `MessageEvent.channel_context`, **not** prepended into the message text. The gateway (`gateway/run.py`) applies the triggering sender's prefix to `text` only, then prepends `channel_context` ahead of a `[New message]` marker. Routing history through `channel_context` keeps each prior post's own `[username]` attribution instead of letting the trigger sender's prefix swallow the whole block.
- Seeding is guarded to the **first turn only** by `_has_active_session_for_thread()`, which uses `build_session_key()` as the single source of truth so the `group_sessions_per_user` / `thread_sessions_per_user` isolation settings are honoured. Once a session exists the thread history is already carried in it, so no refetch and no duplication.
- Senders not on the allowlist are tagged `[unverified]` (via the base `_is_sender_authorized()` hook) so the model treats their content as background reference rather than authoritative input. This preserves context without dropping it, and the header switches to a security-aware variant that tells the model not to act on unverified content. Without this, injected `channel_context` would bypass the triggering-author authorization check.
- The bot's own prior replies (circular context) and slash-command posts are excluded. Command-text normalization already runs before the message-type gate on `main`, so a leading-space ` /new` is correctly classified as a command and never receives injected context.
- Policy is exposed via `config.yaml` `mattermost.thread_context` (`on` default / `off`), bridged to `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` through the existing `_apply_yaml_config` hook — no new bespoke `.env`-only setting.

## Related Issue

Fixes #37695

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: add `_fetch_thread_context()`, `_has_active_session_for_thread()`, and `_resolve_thread_user_name()`; wire first-turn seeding into `_handle_ws_event()` via `MessageEvent.channel_context`; add per-root TTL cache and user-name cache; bridge `thread_context` in `_apply_yaml_config()`.
- `hermes_cli/config.py`: register `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` as a user-facing optional messaging setting.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/mattermost.md`: document the thread-context behaviour and the `thread_context` / `MATTERMOST_THREAD_CONTEXT` knob.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: add a `mattermost:` block including `thread_context`.
- `tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py`: 10 tests covering formatting/attribution, bot-and-command exclusion, `[unverified]` tagging, empty-root and cache behaviour, first-turn seeding via `_handle_ws_event`, no-seed on root posts, `off` disabling, and the YAML->env bridge.

## How to Test

1. Set up a Mattermost bot (see `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/mattermost.md`). In a channel, have two users exchange a few posts in a thread without mentioning the bot.
2. `@mention` the bot in a reply to that thread. The bot's first response reflects awareness of the prior posts; posts from non-allowlisted users appear as background tagged `[unverified]`.
3. Reply again in the same thread — no refetch occurs (history is now in the session).
4. Automated: `pytest tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py -q` — 69 passed.
5. Revert-to-fail proof: `git stash push -- plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py` then rerun the thread-context tests — 7 behaviour-pinning tests fail (the remaining negative-guard tests trivially hold with the feature absent); `git stash pop` restores green.

prs.title: feat(prompt): agent.skills_catalog_mode to compact the skills catalog on chat surfaces
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The messaging/chat system prompt re-sends a large stable cache prefix on every turn, and the `<available_skills>` catalog block is its single largest compressible line item. The renderer already has a names-only demotion lever (`build_skills_system_prompt(compact_categories=...)`), but it is gated behind the coding posture and the interactive-coding surface set, so it never fires on chat/messaging surfaces, which is exactly where the tokens burn.

This adds `agent.skills_catalog_mode` (`full` | `compact` | `names-only`), resolved once from session-fixed inputs (platform, config) and unioned with the existing coding-posture demotion set before the single render call, so the catalog stays a single cache-safe LRU entry that is byte-identical for the life of a conversation.

- `full`: no demotion (default for interactive coding surfaces; today's behaviour).
- `compact`: demote the non-coding category deny-list to names-only (default for messaging surfaces).
- `names-only`: demote every present category to names-only (max compaction; opt-in).

Never hides a skill: names-only demotion drops the description but keeps every name visible and loadable via `skill_view` / `skills_list`.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `agent/coding_context.py`: new pure resolver `resolve_skills_catalog_compaction(*, platform, config)` + `_skills_catalog_mode()` (config precedence over per-surface default). Reads no turn-varying state.
- `agent/prompt_builder.py`: `ALL_SKILL_CATEGORIES` sentinel (a distinct empty `frozenset` subclass) for names-only; renderer short-circuits "all present categories demoted" and keys the LRU cache distinctly from `full`.
- `agent/system_prompt.py`: resolve the catalog set alongside the coding-posture set and union both into the single `build_skills_system_prompt(compact_categories=...)` call.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: documents the new `agent.skills_catalog_mode` key. No new `HERMES_*` env var, config-only.
- `tests/agent/test_coding_context.py`, `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py`: behavior-contract tests T1 to T7.

## How to Test

```
pytest tests/agent/test_coding_context.py tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py -q
# 237 passed
```

Contract tests:
- **T1** chat default is `compact`, coding surface is `full`.
- **T2** every name present under `full` is still present under `compact` and `names-only` (never-hide invariant).
- **T3** `compact` drops only non-coding descriptions; `names-only` drops all, each category rendered as a `[names only]` line.
- **T4** determinism: resolver + renderer are byte-identical for identical inputs (cache-safety).
- **T5** config precedence: profile/base override the per-surface default; empty string falls through.
- **T6** measured saving gate (see below).
- **T7** no `HERMES_*` env var / `os.environ` read for the mode.

## T6, measured catalog reduction

Measured against a representative 204-skill catalog, `<available_skills>` block only, tokens via `tiktoken` `cl100k_base`:

| mode | chars | tokens | token reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full` | 19,786 | 4,678 | n/a |
| `compact` | 16,176 | 3,859 | **17.5%** |
| `names-only` | 5,295 | 1,390 | **70.3%** |

The reduction from `compact` varies with the category mix. On a coding-heavy catalog (many `github` / `gitlab` / `devops` / `software-development` skills that `compact` deliberately keeps full), `compact` reclaims ~17.5%; the full cut comes from `names-only` at ~70.3%, which strips coding descriptions too and is therefore opt-in, not the chat default. The synthetic-catalog unit test (`test_t6_compact_shrinks_block_at_least_50pct`) asserts >=50% on a non-coding-heavy catalog to guard the mechanism; the table above is a real-profile figure.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added and passing (237 passed)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` updated for the new config key
- [x] No new env var introduced (config-only, per repo `.env`-is-secrets-only rule)
- [x] Cache-safety preserved: resolver reads only session-fixed inputs; result joins the existing LRU cache key

prs.title: test(local-runtime): cover load-progress stream disconnect recovery
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Cover the load-progress watcher's stream lifecycle. The existing tests feed decoded events directly into `_apply_event`, so they do not detect a broken partial-line buffer or stale loading progress left behind when the SSE connection ends.

The new test drives the real `_watch` parser synchronously through fragmented UTF-8 input, disconnect, and reconnect. It checks that progress appears after a complete line, disappears before reconnect backoff, and resumes with only the new connection's model. Both clean EOF and a read error are covered. Main already implements this behavior; production code is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No new issue. Extends the managed-runtime behavior introduced in #100667. Endpoint detection in #103986 and authentication headers in #132811 address separate concerns; this test does not assert their header or endpoint policies.

## Type of Change

- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- Add `tests/hermes_cli/test_load_progress_stream.py` with one lifecycle test parametrized for EOF and `OSError`.
- Supply deterministic response chunks at `urlopen`, including a split UTF-8 character, an incomplete line, a keepalive and malformed JSON before a valid event. Real parsing, event application, progress getters and snapshot clearing run.
- Observe both response contexts closing and stale progress clearing. Run synchronously with isolated snapshot state and bounded fake backoff; no sockets, daemon threads, real sleeps, model downloads or credentials.

## How to Test

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_load_progress.py tests/hermes_cli/test_load_progress_stream.py
python scripts/check --staged
```

On macOS with Python 3.14.8: **14 tests passed**, and all **11** staged repository checks passed.

Two temporary mutations validated the added coverage: removing post-disconnect snapshot clearing, and discarding the accumulated partial-line buffer on each read. Each left the original 12 tests green; each failed both new cases on missing cleanup or missing parsed progress. Neither mutation is included. Restored production code passes all 14 tests.

The full suite, other operating systems and a live llama-server were not tested. Transport I/O is simulated; this does not validate network timing or a running server's SSE implementation.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution/test rules and compared related PRs across all states.
- [x] One focused test change and Conventional Commit; no dependencies or production changes.
- [x] Relevant tests, `git diff --check`, and `python scripts/check --staged` pass.
- [x] Documentation, configuration, architecture and tool descriptions: N/A.

prs.title: fix(update): keep the default source channel updatable when the archive is unreadable
prs.body:
# fix(update): keep the default source channel updatable when the archive is unreadable

## What

A release-archive read that fails for any reason **other than 404** — a 403 from a corporate proxy,
firewall or geo-block, DNS failure, or a timeout — raises `ChannelError`, and
`resolve_source_target` only ever catches `ChannelNotFound`. An installation that cannot read R2
therefore cannot update at all, on the default channel, until the network changes.

Transport failures now raise `ChannelUnavailable` (`ChannelError` subclass, so every existing
`except ChannelError` keeps working), and `main` follows the git branch for an unreadable archive
exactly as it already does for an unpublished record.

## Reproduction (real, no mocks)

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/releases/channels/main.json
403
$ hermes update --check
✗ Could not resolve the main source channel: Channel read unavailable: HTTP 403
$ hermes update --check --branch main
⚕ Update available: 914 commits behind origin/main.
```

GitHub is reachable on the same host (`git ls-remote origin main` → 200), so this is the archive
host, not the network as a whole. `--branch` works because an explicit branch never reads the
channel; the default path is what fails.

## Before / after probe

Same resolver the updater uses, with an opener raising `HTTPError(403)`:

| | reader | resolve `main` | resolve `stable` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `ChannelError` | **FAILED** `Channel read unavailable: HTTP 403` | FAILED |
| this PR | `ChannelUnavailable` | **OK** `branch=main commit=None` | FAILED `ChannelUnavailable` (fail-closed kept) |

## Why `main` may follow the branch here

`main` IS the source branch: its R2 record can only add a retirement, which is exactly why the
existing code already resolves it to the branch when the object is missing (404). An archive we
cannot *read* is no evidence that the record was never published — a 403 hides records that exist —
so the same conclusion holds, and failing closed there only removes the last remaining update path
on a blocked network. Every other channel stays fail-closed: R2 owns which build it delivers, and
guessing a branch for `stable`/`canary` would be a silent channel downgrade.

Related: #124309 covers the fail-closed rule for an *absent* `stable` record (404); this is its
transport sibling. #127553 is the same 403 class on the PM download path.

## Tests

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_release_channels.py::test_geo_blocked_object_is_unavailable_not_missing` —
  403 → `ChannelUnavailable`, still a `ChannelError`, and never a `ChannelNotFound`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_channel_integration.py::test_unreadable_main_record_keeps_following_the_git_branch` —
  `main` follows the branch, a passive `check_for_updates` reports no error and returns the branch
  head, `stable` still raises.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_release_channels.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_channel_integration.py -q
79 passed, 1 failed
```

The single failure is `test_retirement_refuses_to_downgrade_newer_source[shallow]`, which fails
identically on the unmodified checkout on this host (`PermissionError: [WinError 5]` while pytest
deletes `…/checkout/.git/objects/…` in teardown — a Windows file-lock flake, unrelated to this diff).

prs.title: fix(update): the main channel follows the git branch without reading an R2 record
prs.body:
The `main` channel now follows the git branch without first reading an R2 record. A WAF that answers that request with 403 can no longer stop `hermes update`.

**Bug (#128295):** on every update, an install on `main` first fetched `hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/releases/channels/main.json`.
- **What the record is:** it has never been published. The only thing it could ever carry is a "main is retired" notice.
- **Where it works today:** a 404 falls through to the git branch.
- **Where it breaks:** some regional WAFs answer the same request with **403**, which raised an error and stopped the update outright. #128323 (treat 403 like 404) and #128305 (identify updater requests to WAFs) both patch around that lookup.

**Fix:** `main` is the git branch, so `resolve_source_target` now returns the main branch target directly, the same way `stable` reads GitHub releases directly (#135847). No R2 request is made for `main`. Preview channels such as `pm-preview` still read their records, since they actually publish builds through R2.

**Live A/B:** a real checkout of the official repo on the main channel, an isolated home, and every `hermes-assets` request forced to answer 403 (standing in for the WAF). `hermes update --check`:

| tree | output | R2 requests |
|---|---|---|
| origin/main `9e827685f2f` | `✗ Could not resolve the main source channel: Channel read unavailable: HTTP 403` | 1 (`releases/channels/main.json`) |
| this PR | `⚕ Update available: 1 commit behind origin/main.` | 0 |

**Tests:**
- `test_main_follows_the_git_branch_without_reading_a_channel_record` is parametrized over not-found, 403 and timeout. It asserts that `main` resolves to the branch, `check_for_updates` reports no error, and the record is never read, while `canary` still reads its record.
- `test_source_check.py` request-order assertions drop the `main.json` entry. The unpublished-record test now answers 403 and asserts the record is never requested.
- `test_missing_channel_cannot_fall_back_to_main` keeps its stable/canary/preview cases. `main` is no longer a record-backed channel, so its case is gone.
- `test_source_check.py`: 39 passed. Locally, 72 cases in `test_old_updater_shims.py`, `test_update_target_identity.py` and `test_source_release_channels.py` fail identically on bare `origin/main`, because the home-I/O guard flags the worktree path. CI runs from a different path.

Once this merges, #128323 and #128305 have nothing left to fix for `main`.

prs.title: fix(checkpoints): never snapshot temp roots or unreadable system residue
prs.body:
## Problem

`ensure_checkpoint()` refuses only `"/"` and `$HOME` as "too broad".  A checkpoint project can
still resolve to the **temp root**: `get_working_dir_for_path()` walks up from a written file to
the nearest project-marker ancestor, and a path like `/tmp/scratch.txt` has no marker above it
until `/`, so it returns `/tmp` itself.  Both call sites in `agent/tool_executor.py` pass that
result straight into `ensure_checkpoint()`.

Once `/tmp` is a project, the shadow store ingests whatever lives there — browser caches, plus
root-owned system scratch (`snap-private-tmp/`, `systemd-private-*/`, `.org.chromium.Chromium.*/`,
`gdm3-config-err-*`) that the agent user cannot read.  `git add -A` then fails:

```
error: open("snap-private-tmp/snapshot"): Permission denied
fatal: adding files failed        # rc=128
```

The snapshot never succeeds, so the failure repeats on **every** turn that writes under that
directory — on the reported host ~40 `tools.checkpoint_manager: Git command failed` lines per day,
which in turn drove a standing "recent real errors" health alert.  Two independent defects are
involved: selecting an unsnapshotable root at all, and aborting the whole stage when unreadable
residue is merely *present* in an otherwise fine workdir.

## Fix

`tools/checkpoint_manager.py`, two minimal changes:

1. **Temp roots are never snapshot targets** (`ensure_checkpoint`).  `_TEMP_ROOTS` is
   `{tempfile.gettempdir(), "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm"}` normalized at import; the existing too-broad
   guard now also matches it.  Only the root itself matches, so anything *below* a temp root — a
   pytest `tmp_path` project, a real project under `/tmp` — still checkpoints exactly as before.
2. **Unreadable system residue is excluded** (`DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`, written to `store/info/exclude`).
   The four root-owned families above no longer abort a snapshot of a workdir that contains them.

Considered and rejected: snapshoting `/tmp` anyway (its readable payload is ~210 MB of browser
cache against a 500 MB store cap — it would evict real project history); `git add --ignore-errors`
(still exits non-zero and logs an ERROR line); skipping the temp root's whole subtree (breaks the
31 upstream tests that checkpoint `tmp_path` projects).

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_checkpoint_temp_roots.py` — 2 invariants:

| Test | On `main` | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| temp root rejected before any snapshot work; a child of it stays eligible | `assert True is False` (temp root was snapshotted) | pass |
| workdir containing unreadable residue checkpoints | `assert False is True`, store logs `git add -A (rc=128) … fatal: adding files failed` | pass |

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_checkpoint_temp_roots.py
  main:    2 failed        (the rc=128 above reproduced inside the store)
  patched: 2 passed
```

Regression `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/ tests/cron/`: 841 files / 11947 passed / 7 failed,
with the failure set **identical** to a clean `origin/main` worktree (840 / 11945 / same 7
pre-existing environment failures: `test_file_tools` host `/tmp/out.txt` pollution,
`test_browser_real_profile`, `test_microsoft_graph_auth[trio]`, `test_web_providers_searxng`,
`test_web_tools_config`).  No new failures.
