prs.title: feat(catalog): add hermes-muse companion assembly
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a community catalog entry for [hermes-muse](https://github.com/xiaohei-info/hermes-muse), an independently written personal assistant assembly inspired by Meta Muse. It follows goals and temporary interests, prepares reminders, maintains memory and a quiet Feed, and uses native subagents for research. The default installation includes one Skill, one state tool, four hooks, eight prompts and six native recurring jobs, including weekly outcome/cost review and monthly workflow audit.

The entry pins `e71945c6dd76b19f54dfeb6fedde24a94876e1b5` (0.1.25). This PR changes only `plugin-catalog/hermes-muse.yaml`. It is not a Muse service integration or a distribution of proprietary prompts.

## Related Issue

N/A — owner-submitted catalog listing. The existing hermes-muse-code provider is a different project.

## Type of Change

- [x] Community plugin catalog entry

## Current behavior and review status

Version 0.1.9 adds independently written proactive guidance: recognize concrete conversational plans, prepare useful in-scope work before interrupting, prefer one strong ordinary item, avoid silence-driven nudging, and maintain bounded working lessons in the companion AGENTS.md. No new jobs, hooks or runtime permission changes. Existing user files are preserved on upgrade; model judgment is not claimed as programmatically guaranteed.

Version 0.1.8 delivers notices directly in the existing patrol/watch output instead of creating a delivery-only Cron. A declared native `transform_llm_output` hook rechecks and finalizes approved notice bodies for the host-supplied task/session/execution only. It leaves ordinary conversations and review reports unchanged. Native receipt reconciliation requires this finalization and reads the exact execution, not a later patrol. Live acceptance caught v0.1.7 delivering a status summary; its release notes were corrected, and the v0.1.8 retest verified the exact notice body in Bot Chat, a bot reply, delivered receipt and unchanged Cron IDs.

Version 0.1.6 fixes a source-classification bug found in live acceptance: deliveries from existing native Cron jobs outside Muse are excluded from user signals too. It also documents explicit profile selection and enabling the `muse` toolset when platform tool lists are configured. No new background action restrictions were added.

Version 0.1.5 intentionally restores v0.1.2 behavior, then reapplies current-profile Bot Chat delivery. The project owner chose to preserve background state updates based on recorded user input. The v0.1.3 blanket Cron decision-action guard and plugin-specific 30-minute/4000-character watch limits have been removed. The v0.1.4 receiving-turn read-only tool restriction is also removed. **The earlier blocking review requests for those guards/limits are therefore not satisfied by this pin.** We are disclosing this product decision for a fresh admission decision, not claiming the prior requested changes are complete.

Original evidence/lifecycle checks remain: operations requiring real-user evidence need a recent recorded signal, and interest renewal requires a newer signal. Generated background output does not count as a user signal. Watches use native scheduling validation. The plugin uses the original host configuration loader, rather than claiming the optional readonly-loader recommendation is retained.

Selected reminders explicitly target bare native `bot-chat`, resolved in the job-owning profile. The receiving bot reads the result and replies there. There is no destination enumeration fallback, cross-profile selection, or source-session injection. Native missing-chat creation and busy-chat queueing are reused. Receipts distinguish admission from completed processing; unknown outcomes are not automatically resent, and queueing the same dispatched notice is idempotent.

Weekly and monthly jobs produce recommendations, save a bounded summary, and deliver their report directly to Bot Chat. They do not run a separate Skill audit. Their recommendation-only behavior is a prompt procedure, not an enforced tool sandbox. Existing user-created review jobs remain user-owned.

## Connected-source behavior in 0.1.10

All six fixed jobs invoke the model on their scheduled ticks. Empty local goals/interests no longer suppress source checks. The patrol procedure discovers available connections/devices, checks mail/calendar/reminder changes and upcoming deadlines, and records source coverage with watermarks that do not advance on failure. Weather/travel changes and interest news use the same evidence and attention rules; no provider is mandatory. These source reads and their factual quality are model-led, not attested by the state tool.

Hourly/nightly cursors are separate. Unsent notices can retire on verified source evidence. Already accepted goals can complete from verified outcomes across days, and externally referenced goals can close on verified authoritative cancellation; this does not require inventing a fresh user signal. New commitments, reopening, scope extensions and interest renewal retain their user-evidence rules. New research batches dispatch a native coordinator and use host callbacks/durable results rather than requiring user-driven wave advancement.

## Runtime fixes in 0.1.11

Native async-completion envelopes are excluded from user-signal processing and evidence-backed actions; historical misclassified rows are retained separately as background audit evidence. Free-form source records are archived, while new checkpoints use stable connection/account/resource identities and explicit expected/checked coverage. Partial coverage cannot advance success. Reported coverage remains model-led, not a provider attestation.

Direct same-profile Bot Chat reconciliation reads the native execution-specific persistent receipt after later job pointers change; unknown finalized records can become sent without any resend. Native integration compares the computed key with the actual host producer under a stub transport. Cron context is scoped to each task's purpose, and patrols reuse tested read recipes while continuing live source checks every tick.

## Context and experience in 0.1.12

Patrols receive all recorded real-user messages from the past day, removing the extra count and text caps from 0.1.11. Older context remains available through native retrieval. Prompt procedures prioritize useful depth, judgment and initiative; call savings must not come from skipped sources, reduced research, delayed useful results or silent model downgrades. These are behavior instructions, not guarantees of model quality.

## Follow-through fixes in 0.1.13

Hourly and nightly reviews return the next signal batch and remaining count until the run's initial snapshot is complete; timestamp ties stay together and arrivals after the boundary wait. Pending reminders expose policy blockers and earliest eligibility without claiming a delivery guarantee. Reverification can change non-promised urgency with recorded reasons/evidence, preserving snoozes, expiry and opt-outs. Verified tool aliases can reuse an existing source ID; duplicate observations are archived without transferring successful checkpoints. No new fixed tasks or host permissions. Version 0.1.14 also resolves already-merged IDs retained by in-flight patrols, preventing stale context from recreating duplicates.

## Unified prompts and receiving behavior in 0.1.15

System, scheduled-task, Skill and delegated-research instructions now share a result-oriented recovery contract: correct recoverable calls, respect dependencies/cooldowns, investigate gaps, and disclose consequential loss of baseline monitoring without inventing a goal. They prioritize useful depth, judgment and initiative over fewer calls. Fixed six-point/one-screen report formats and automatic next-pass deferral are removed; the stored review summary remains bounded.

One new receiving prompt is shared by Bot Chat envelopes and the receiving hook. Notices and governance reports are internal findings for a direct response to the user, not messages to acknowledge. Source text remains evidence, not authorization; reports do not create a second notice or become user signals. Host-bound output transforms still finalize only patrol/watch notices; governance transforms preserve report content while adding the Bot-only guidance. Other turns and non-Bot destinations retain their prior content. No new tool, hook, permission or recurring task. Wording quality remains model behavior, not a code guarantee.

## Current-conversation checks in 0.1.16

Patrol context reads recent tracked private conversations through native read-only SessionDB, including assistant outcomes and async-result evidence. It does not persist a second transcript or turn assistant results into user authorization. notification_review records a relevance verdict and fingerprints; preparation/finalization detect intervening dialogue changes. issue_key/supersedes can retire old unsent versions while preserving delivered/unknown history. Literal source-item titles and upstream item IDs (distinct from source-check collection IDs) are validated against the supplied snapshot, without claiming provider attestation or perfect semantic judgment.

The installation default ordinary daily cap becomes null, retaining quiet hours and explicit numeric limits. Only byte-identical untouched old defaults without recorded explicit preference edits migrate. Existing tool recipes retain verified calling conventions. No additional tool, hook, fixed job, connector requirement or core patch.

## Disclosure

First load writes missing templates, an ownership record and SQLite state under the active profile's muse directory, plus owned scripts and native Cron jobs. Hooks retain short real-user excerpts for upkeep; unprocessed signals remain until successful processing. Scheduled work and Bot Chat receiving turns use the user's configured model/tools and incur normal costs. No telemetry, self-updater, mandatory external provider, core patch, SOUL replacement or global-system-prompt rewrite is introduced. Existing memory tools and permissions remain in use.

Native remove leaves owned tasks for the documented assistant cleanup using install.json; remaining launchers exit silently after removal. User data is retained. The plugin does not grant itself gateway-injection permission or claim phone/read receipts. Research retains host/parent tool permissions; optional toolset allowlists are not implemented, and no enforced read-only sandbox is claimed.

## Validation

- Catalog schema validation passes for this YAML.
- Official plugin validation passes, including isolated registration and capability/security checks; no external dependencies.
- 83 unit tests and native integration run in temporary profiles. Integration covers registration, six actual Cron jobs, script gates, profile isolation, preserved user files/settings, restored background actions/evidence checks, Bot Chat routing/receipts, report summaries and exclusion of background deliveries from user signals.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/xiaohei-info/hermes-muse/actions/runs/38101904663) runs unit tests on Linux/macOS/Windows and native integration/official validation on the pinned public Hermes baseline.
- Official GitHub install/remove and owned-only cleanup are tested separately in a temporary profile.

Real model judgment, report quality and live-channel delivery remain user acceptance checks. This data-only PR does not claim a full Hermes runtime test run. Catalog acceptance remains the maintainers' decision.




## 0.1.17 operation review

The existing tool reads current-profile native tool arguments/results and owned Cron execution records, including persisted related child sessions. Initial scope is the prior 24 hours; subsequent reads use incremental checkpoints. Native output may contain sensitive data and is provided to the configured assistant for assessment. Only checkpoints/session references and minimal findings/verification/disclosure notes are saved in plugin state, not copied transcripts. Groups and unrelated jobs are excluded; missing history is not a completed audit. Existing hourly/nightly jobs do the work; no new Cron, hook, database, dependency or core change. Receiving prompts explicitly continue the same assistant’s work and responsibility without inventing completed actions. No general automatic rollback is provided. Existing admission exceptions described above remain unchanged.

Validation: 72 unit tests, real native integration including tool-result/child-session reads, official isolated plugin validation and GitHub install/remove smoke. Live upgrade preserves six fixed task IDs/settings and SOUL/USER/MEMORY/config files.

0.1.18 follows live acceptance: native tool_call-wrapped self-review queries are excluded while mixed mutating batches remain visible. A real model confused a page endpoint with the full snapshot; the server now retains the original boundary, rejects shortening it, and returns explicit continuation instructions. The live first pass read native results and advanced a partial checkpoint; this is not represented as a complete audit of all operations.

## 0.1.19 self-contained replies

Receiving guidance now assumes the user has not read internal delivery or tool traces, names the subject/change and integrates follow-up findings into a complete user-facing message. The private receiving hook applies this to all native Cron envelopes, including pre-existing non-Muse jobs; it neither adopts nor changes those jobs and still excludes their generated text from user signals. Unit and native tests cover this branch. No new job, tool, hook or service is added.

## 0.1.20 task-taking and voice

The existing system section, real-user pointer and communication/goals/proactivity procedures now connect requested changes to their practical consequences, actual task updates and verified confirmation. Check cadence stays distinct from notification cadence; explicit reports remain explicit reports. Natural conversational tone follows user preferences rather than imposing a character or script. Scheduling changes use existing native Cron update on the same ID; watch_create is documented as creation only. No new job, Skill, prompt file, hook, state store or authority is added. The system summary remains within the host prompt limit, with native integration checking the complete rendered content.


## 0.1.21 concurrent review and completion

Operation pages now have independent reference-only receipts retained for seven days. Concurrent reads cannot replace each other’s evidence; overlapping/repeated completion advances the shared checkpoint monotonically. Successful Skill/tool-discovery reads are excluded while failed reads and mixed mutation calls remain visible. Hourly upkeep owns the incremental full audit; patrol and Feed check their own work and nightly review writes confirmed alignment without waiting for that backlog.

Host-bound run records distinguish checkpoint processing, operation review, artifacts and final output from the scheduler’s exit status. A complete hourly task requires its audit snapshot; a complete nightly task requires fresh nonempty dream/alignment files. Interrupted work stays partial and remains visible to the next attempt. This validates evidence/stage presence, not semantic correctness or phone delivery. No new registered tool, hook, fixed Cron, dependency, database or authority is added; run_complete is an action of the existing state tool. The earlier admission exceptions remain unchanged.

Validation: 83 unit tests; native integration on Linux and the deployed Mac Hermes version using isolated temporary profiles; official plugin validation; Linux/macOS/Windows CI.


## 0.1.22 scheduled wakes

Off-schedule wakes now carry the native manual_run_at marker together with next_run_at. This prevents newer cron-expression repair from silently re-anchoring quiet-time upkeep and Feed preference refreshes without firing. The recurring schedule and enabled/state fields remain unchanged; a user pause is not reversed. Native integration verifies both due-scan dispatchability and paused-job preservation.


## 0.1.23 parallel operation review

Hourly upkeep allocates up to three disjoint compact audit pages and uses native delegation for parallel read-only judgments. The existing state tool adds operations_batch, operations_evidence and operations_commit actions; child contexts may read only issued evidence references and remain unable to commit checkpoints or change Muse state. Original evidence stays in the native store and can be expanded in chunks with linked calls/user context. The parent records findings, commits numeric batch/slots, and advances only contiguous reviewed progress; pending slots survive interruption. Near the host iteration limit it saves partial work instead of launching another wave.

Model-led judgments and read-only worker instructions are not an enforced host-wide sandbox. Normal model costs still apply; see the current routing behavior below. One profile-local audit.lock serializes batch allocation; the existing state database stores assignments, not transcripts. No new registered tool, hook, fixed Cron or provider requirement. Previous admission exceptions remain unchanged.


## 0.1.24 Cron delegation routing

Muse Cron self-review and research now use a plugin-owned delegation entry. Host-bound owned Cron calls inherit the live parent model and connection through the native per-call routing argument and join results before returning; ordinary chat keeps native profile delegation settings. Model-supplied routing/transport overrides are rejected. Native reasoning effort, permission and execution limits remain intact. The Skill and prompts select this entry; arbitrary direct native calls are not intercepted. No additional job, hook, database or provider is introduced. Validation: 88 unit tests, native integration on Linux and Mac mini, official validation and all CI jobs passed.


## 0.1.25 source completion and briefings

Receiving guidance calls for authorized original-item retrieval when missing packet details block a useful judgment; prepared findings retain source identity and locators. A provider-neutral briefing reference supports user-subscribed native reports using the same source and communication procedures. No new fixed job, service requirement, automatic job adoption or external-write authority. User-managed reports remain outside install.json and are explicitly covered in removal guidance. These are model instructions, not programmatic guarantees of retrieval or judgment. All CI jobs, 88 unit tests, Linux/Mac native integration and official validation passed.

prs.title: Reasoning-replay consumption eval: which providers actually read replayed reasoning
prs.body:
Adds a rerunnable harness that measures whether each replayed reasoning carrier is actually **consumed** by a provider/model, not just accepted. One live run covered 263 (route, model, lane) rows: 105 consume reasoning on every turn, 78 consume it only in-loop, and 64 accept it but ignore it.

## What it is
- `evals/reasoning_replay/harness.py` uses stdlib HTTP only and has no Hermes runtime dependency, so it measures the wire, not Hermes. `README.md` documents the method.
- **Step 1, text carriers.** A synthetic tool-call fixture carries a ~400-token trace with a canary sentence. Variants: `none` / `reasoning_content` / `reasoning` / `reasoning_details` (`reasoning.text`) / `all`. For Responses routes: summary/content reasoning items. For Gemini native: `thought` parts. Each variant runs **in-loop** (on the tool-call turn right before the request) and **cross-turn** (on a finished turn, followed by a new user message). The signal is the `prompt_tokens` delta against a byte-identical baseline, plus canary recall.
- **Step 2, real opaque carriers.** Turn 1 runs live against the same model; turn 2 is then sent with the captured carriers replayed verbatim and again with them stripped. Captured carriers include encrypted `reasoning_details`, Responses `encrypted_content`, Gemini `thoughtSignature`, and `reasoning_content`. OpenAI also gets a `reasoning.context: all_turns` cell.
- **Portal lanes.** The response id is classified on every call (`gen-` = OpenRouter, anything else = direct). `--want-direct` resamples a cell until it lands on a direct lane. Rows are keyed by (route, model, lane).
- `--route custom --base-url --key-env` covers any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The budget is enforced across runs through a `cost.jsonl` ledger. Results stay out of tree.

## Headline findings (live, 2026-10-10, $7.10 total)
| finding | evidence |
|---|---|
| Portal direct lanes for Fireworks `:US` (`glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `dsv4.1-flash`) reject `reasoning` and `reasoning_details` with 400 `Extra inputs are not permitted`, but **consume `reasoning_content` in-loop and cross-turn** (+408 tokens, canary recalled) | `kimi-k3:US`, `glm-5.3:US`, `glm-5.3-flash:US` all consume `reasoning_content` on every turn |
| Other Portal direct lanes (Together `dsv4-flash-0731`, DigitalOcean `glm-5.2`, Impala `glm-5.3` / `dsv4.1-flash`, `kimi-k3:US`) consume `reasoning_content`. `reasoning_details` is ignored everywhere, and `reasoning` is read only by GLM and Impala-DeepSeek | `glm-5.2` direct is in-loop-only (cross-turn Δ0) |
| xAI over chat (Portal direct `grok-4.5/4.6/4.7` and api.x.ai) **ignores every chat carrier**, its own `reasoning_content` included (Δ0). Over xAI Responses, encrypted items are consumed on all turns (+21 to +165) | xAI chat returns a short summary: 171-330 chars for 300-1100 reasoning tokens |
| OpenAI Responses: `gpt-5.4+`, `5.5`, `5.6-*`, `6-*` and `6.1-sol` consume encrypted items cross-turn **when sent `reasoning.context: all_turns`**. `5.6`/`6.x` also do so by default; `gpt-5-mini/nano` and `o4-mini` 400 on `all_turns`. Plain-text reasoning items are ignored (summary) or rejected (content) | `gpt-6-luna` +97 tokens both positions |
| Through OpenRouter on the Portal, the chat template decides. Qwen3–3.7, MiniMax m1–m2.7, Kimi k2.x, gpt-oss, Nemotron, Gemini 2.5/3.1 and older GLM are **in-loop-only**. GLM ≥4.6/5.1/5.3, Qwen3.8, Kimi k2.7/k3, DeepSeek V4 and Mistral consume all turns | local llama.cpp Qwen3-1.7B reproduces the template drop: +454 in-loop, 0 cross-turn |
| Claude through the Portal ignores text carriers but **consumes signed `reasoning_details` (anthropic-claude-v1) cross-turn** on Opus 5/5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 | +131 to +224 tokens |

**Policy gap.** For most models that consume reasoning, Hermes origin/main replays nothing on the Portal: `reasoning_details` is stripped off non-openrouter hosts, and `reasoning_content` is sent only for deepseek/mimo ids. That covers 135 consuming rows, including the Fireworks `:US`, Kimi and GLM direct lanes.

## Validation
- Ran live against the Nous Portal (224 reasoning-capable ids, the priority direct-lane set resampled until direct), OpenAI Responses and chat, xAI Responses and chat, Gemini native and OpenAI-compat, and local llama.cpp (Qwen3-1.7B).
- `ruff`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, and `check-windows-footguns` are clean.

**Not run (credentials expired or missing):**
- OpenRouter direct and HF router: keys expired.
- DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, DashScope, MiniMax, Fireworks, Groq, Cerebras, Mistral, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Copilot: no keys. Run them with `--route <name>` or `--route custom`.
- The Gemini free tier hit 429 on `3.5-flash`, `3.8-flash` (openai-compat) and `3.1-pro`.

## Infographic
![reasoning-replay-eval](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaddd22/Y1jxmXlGYx_ES5Thpi0FV_Z6jZtVr9.png)

prs.title: Alibaba's content guardrail ends the turn with the safety-filter notice instead of a 4-minute retry loop
prs.body:
Alibaba's content guardrail now ends the turn with the safety-filter explanation, instead of Hermes retrying a refusal for four minutes.

Qwen models served through OpenRouter (and so through the Nous Portal) hit Alibaba Model Studio's guardrail. The output side reaches Hermes as an in-band error, `{"code":502,"message":"Upstream error from Alibaba: Output data may contain inappropriate content.","metadata":{"error_type":"provider_unavailable"}}`; that exact frame was seen live on the Portal for `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`. The input side is DashScope's documented 400 `data_inspection_failed`, "Input data may contain inappropriate content." Neither phrase was in `_CONTENT_POLICY_BLOCKED_PATTERNS`. The 502 rode the server-error retry ladder and the status-less copy landed in the retryable `unknown` bucket, so Hermes re-sent the same content and got the same refusal.

## Change

- Add `"data may contain inappropriate content"` (it covers the input, output and combined wording) and `"data_inspection_failed"` to `_CONTENT_POLICY_BLOCKED_PATTERNS`, the same list that holds the OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, MiniMax and CommandCode moderation phrases.
- They now classify as `content_policy_blocked`: not retryable, fall back to the next model, and show the safety-filter guidance.

## Validation

**Live:** two real `hermes chat -q` processes, `origin/main` vs this branch, both built by `git archive`, each with an isolated home, pointed at a local endpoint that replays Alibaba's exact in-band frame:

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Requests sent for one user message | **17** | **3** |
| Wall time | **243 s** (retries + backoff, then "API failed") | **16 s** |
| What the user sees | generic retry exhaustion | "custom's safety filter refused this request… Provider said: Upstream error from Alibaba: Output data may contain inappropriate content." |

The 3 requests on this branch are the existing invalid-response retry plus the non-stream fallback. Both happen before classification and are unchanged here.

**Tests:** one parametrized invariant covers the in-band 502, the status-less copy and the DashScope 400. Its 3 cases fail on `origin/main` and pass here. `tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py` + the new `test_error_classifier_content_policy.py`: 195 passed.

Portal side: NousResearch/api#344 now surfaces the upstream's real message instead of "Provider returned error", so the input-side 400 reaches this classifier with its text.

## Infographic

![Refusal, not outage](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aade66c/M_JHrhOw7sBiM0tM--sam_AsFUiKbD.png)

prs.title: fix(image-gen): stop namespaced model ids and stale top-level config breaking saves
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two independent defects that made image generation fail for any OpenAI-compatible gateway whose model ids are namespaced (`ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `black-forest-labs/flux-1.1-pro`, `gemini/gemini-3-pro-image-preview`, ...). Both reached the user as unrelated, misleading errors.

**1. Cache writes escaped the cache directory.** Providers pass the model id straight through as the cache `prefix`, so `provider_media.cache_path` interpolated `ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image` into a filename and the `/` became a directory separator. The write targeted `cache/images/openai_ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image_<ts>_<uuid>.png` — a directory nobody created — and died with `ENOENT` *after* the provider had already returned a valid image. Every namespaced model id broke caching on every backend, since all of them funnel through this one helper.

**2. A stale top-level `image_gen.model` shadowed the provider-scoped model.** `resolve_static_model` tested the provider-scoped and shared top-level candidates against the catalog in one pass, so a leftover `image_gen.model: gpt-image-2-medium` won over an explicit `image_gen.openai.model: ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image` purely because it resolved against the built-in catalog first. The gateway then received a model it does not serve and answered `No credentials for provider: openai` — an error pointing nowhere near the real cause. This also contradicted the function's own docstring, which already documents `scoped → top-level` precedence.

## Related Issue

Fixes # (no issue filed — reproducing this requires a non-OpenAI image gateway, so it went straight to a PR. Happy to file one if you'd prefer the tracking.)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] 🔒 Security fix

## Changes Made

- `agent/provider_media.py` — added `_safe_filename_component()`; `cache_path()` now sanitizes both the `prefix` and the `extension`. Anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` collapses to `_`, the result is length-capped for filesystem component limits, and a value that sanitizes away to nothing falls back to a generic stem. Sanitizing the extension also closes a path-traversal hole: a crafted `prefix`/`extension` can no longer escape `$HERMES_HOME/cache/<kind>/`.
- `plugins/image_gen/_common.py` — `resolve_static_model` now decides the env var and provider-scoped selections *before* consulting the shared top-level knob, matching its docstring. The top-level fallback and the "never passed through" rule for it are unchanged.
- `tests/agent/test_provider_media.py` — 7 new tests: namespaced ids stay inside the cache dir (parametrized over 4 real-world id shapes), traversal refusal, extension/blank-prefix sanitizing, long-prefix capping.
- `tests/plugins/image_gen/test_openai_provider.py` — 2 new tests: scoped custom id beats a stale top-level catalog id; top-level catalog id still honoured when no scoped model is set.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/image-generation.md` — documented the model precedence ladder.

## How to Test

1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible image gateway with a namespaced model id and a leftover top-level model:
   ```bash
   hermes config set image_gen.provider openai
   hermes config set image_gen.openai.provider <named-endpoint>
   hermes config set image_gen.openai.model ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image
   hermes config set image_gen.model gpt-image-2-medium   # stale, from a previous provider
   ```
2. Ask the agent to generate an image.

**Before:** fails twice over — `No credentials for provider: openai` (the gateway was sent `gpt-image-2-medium`), and once that is worked around, `Could not save image to cache: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../cache/images/openai_ag/gemini-3.1-flash-image_...png'` despite the provider returning a valid base64 image.

**After:** succeeds; the image lands in `~/.hermes/cache/images/` with a sanitized single-component filename.

Proof the tests fail before the fix: reverting only `agent/provider_media.py` fails all 7 new `test_provider_media.py` cases (4 namespaced ids + traversal + sanitizing + length cap); reverting only `plugins/image_gen/_common.py` fails `test_scoped_custom_model_beats_stale_top_level_catalog_id`. Both suites pass with the fix applied.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

prs.title: fix(gateway): fail fast when the update process dies without an exit code
prs.body:
## Problem

When `hermes update` runs, the gateway's update watcher polls for `.update_exit_code` for up to **30 minutes**. The exit code is written by the wrapping bash shell **after** the update driver exits. The driver holds `.hermes-update-in-progress` (`pid\nepoch`) for its entire run.

If the updater is killed mid-run — e.g. an external restart of the `hermes-gateway` systemd unit with `KillMode=mixed` SIGKILLs the whole cgroup, destroying the driver **and** its bash wrapper (observed in production: a code-skew heal timer restarted the gateway during the desktop rebuild, `npm ci` was SIGKILLed, and no exit code was ever written) — the watcher polls the full 30 minutes and then reports a misleading "timed out" message, leaving a stale update lock behind.

## Reproduction (production observation, Aug 2026)

```
06:30:28  hermes-code-skew-heal: "Hermes runtime fingerprint changed; restarting serve + gateway"
06:30:38  systemd: Stopping hermes-gateway.service
06:30:41  systemd: Killing process 1402127 (npm ci) with signal SIGKILL
```

- Update driver (PID 1401783) was SIGKILLed mid-desktop-build
- No `.update_exit_code` was written
- Watcher polled for 30 min → spurious "timed out" message + 20-min stale lock
- Same signature on three consecutive update runs (Aug 14/17/18)

## Fix

Detect the **dead updater** and fail fast:

- In `_watch_update_progress` (streaming watcher): if the lock marker exists but its PID is no longer alive and no exit code has arrived, write exit code `1` immediately, delete the stale lock, and let the existing completion path report the failure with the output tail already streamed.
- In `_send_update_notification` (the post-restart path — this is exactly when the updater may have been killed, since the streaming watcher died with the old gateway): same check, same fast failure.

The check is conservative: a **live** PID or an **absent** lock never triggers it (the lock is only absent briefly at spawn and after clean release), so there is no false-failure window for legitimate long-running updates.

## Why this approach

- Fixes the **whole bug class**: any killer (external gateway restart, service restart, OOM, manual kill) produces an honest immediate failure instead of a 30-minute silent wait + misleading timeout.
- No premature success: writing the exit code early (before the desktop rebuild) would report success while the build is still running — rejected.
- Uses the project's existing safe PID probe (`hermes_cli.update_lock._pid_alive`, which is `/proc`-based and cross-platform — not `os.kill(pid, 0)`).

## Validation

- New unit tests in `tests/gateway/test_update_streaming.py`:
  - dead PID + no exit code → watcher fails fast (<2s) with "failed", not "timed out"
  - live PID → watcher keeps polling (no false failure)
  - `_send_update_notification` with dead PID → fails fast, not timeout
- Existing update tests pass: `tests/gateway/test_update_streaming.py`, `tests/gateway/test_update_command.py`, `tests/gateway/test_update_cron_drain.py` (29 passed)

prs.title: feat(apiserve): serve PicoClaw agents over HTTP for internal services
prs.body:
Adds an independent service that lets other internal services drive an agent with one HTTP call, without touching the existing channel, gateway or config code.

Endpoints (everything under /v1 authenticates with a Bearer API key):
  POST /v1/messages           synchronous turn, returns the reply
  POST /v1/tasks              asynchronous turn, 202 + task id
  GET  /v1/tasks/{id}         poll status and result (never re-runs the task)
  POST /v1/tasks/{id}/cancel  best-effort cancel
  GET  /v1/agents             the agent ids this key may use
  GET  /v1/usage              usage aggregated per agent / key / user
  GET  /health, /ready        unauthenticated probes

Key management ships in the same binary: picoclaw-api keys create|list|enable|disable|rotate. Keys are stored as sha256 only, the plaintext is printed exactly once (on create and rotate), and list never emits it or the hash — the hash doubles as the callback signing key.

Design points worth knowing before reading the code:

  - One upstream change only. pkg/agent/agent_message.go gains ProcessDirectWithAgent plus an additive variadic agent override, because the existing synchronous entry points cannot select an agent and silently run the default one instead. Nothing else under pkg/agent, pkg/channels or pkg/config was touched.
  - The service owns session key issuance (channel "api", account = key/tenant, sender = user) and records ownership in its own session_index table, so one caller cannot address another caller's conversation.
  - ProcessDirect* has no session concurrency guard upstream, so the service serialises turns per conversation. A timed-out turn cannot overlap its successor because the gate is released only after the turn actually returns.
  - The capabilities the agent type-asserts on the live provider (streaming, extended thinking, native search, Close) are forwarded by the metering wrapper. Hiding them silently disables all four.
  - The command surface is tighter than the spec on purpose: a message whose text starts with "/" or "!" is rejected unless it is /use, so a caller cannot reach the agent's built-in slash commands.

Verification: go vet and the race detector are clean for pkg/apiserve and cmd/picoclaw-api — the race run found and fixed a real sync.WaitGroup misuse between Start and Stop in the task pool. docs/apiserve-coexistence.md records a live coexistence run against the gateway. The repository's full suite has 17 failing packages, identical on the base commit and unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(docker-driver): wait out in-flight --rm auto-removal on stop
prs.body:
## Summary

Stops `DockerHandle.stop()` from reporting a failed teardown when Docker's own `--rm` auto-removal is still finishing.

- **Problem**: agent containers are created with `--rm`. `stop()` runs `docker stop`, which starts Docker's auto-removal, then `docker rm --force`, which the daemon rejects while that removal is in flight. `#confirmRemoved` probes `docker ps` once, still sees the container, and throws `session realization failed: unknown`. The container is gone a few milliseconds later.
- **Evidence**: on one Docker Desktop install, 60 of 164 absolute-ceiling kills over several days logged `Failed to stop session`. In one incident the daemon log shows the `ps` probe at `21:31:59.861` and "A container has been removed" at `.876`. A second `stop()` from `finishAndResolve` succeeds, so nothing leaks; the cost is a false error and a teardown marked incomplete.
- **Fix**: `#confirmRemoved` polls the same probe up to 10 times, 200 ms apart, and returns once the container is gone. A failing probe (daemon down) still throws at once, unretried, so auto-removal stays distinguishable from an outage. The original `rm` error is thrown only if the container is still there after about 2 s.
- **Concurrency**: the poll makes `stop()` yield, so concurrent `stop()` calls on one handle now share one teardown promise. Without that, a second kill could finish first, let the session respawn under the same deterministic container name, and the first poll would then see the new container. A failed teardown is not cached, so the retry in `finishAndResolve` still works.
- **Out of scope**: a throw while removing the main container still skips auxiliary container and private network cleanup in `stop()`. That predates this change.

## Related work

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `confirmRemoved`, "removal in progress", "session realization failed"). The change is limited to the Docker driver's stop path and its fake CLI.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/drivers/` -> 5 files, 152 tests passed
- `pnpm test` -> 274 files passed, 2 skipped; 3357 tests passed, 15 skipped
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> clean
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed files -> 0 errors, same 18 warnings as before the change
- New tests in `src/drivers/docker-driver.test.ts` (`removal racing Docker auto-removal`): in-flight removal resolves after 2 probes; a container that never goes rejects as `unknown` after 10 probes; a failing probe rejects as `runtime-unavailable` after 1 probe; concurrent stops issue one `stop` and one `rm`; a stop after a failed stop retries. The existing force-remove test now also asserts no probe runs when `rm` succeeds.
- With the `docker-driver.ts` change reverted, 3 of the new tests fail (in-flight removal, never removed, concurrent stops).
- `FakeCli` gains an optional `once` flag on a scripted response, used by the new tests.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Stopping an agent container no longer logs a spurious "session realization failed: unknown" when Docker is still finishing its own auto-removal.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None.

prs.title: Auto-drop automated senders in the unknown-sender gate (#3235)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3235. Bot/webhook senders (Discord `author.bot`/`webhook_id`, Slack `bot_id`, Telegram `from.is_bot`) tripped the `request_approval` unknown-sender gate exactly like humans, producing an approval card the sender could never click through. Deny is non-persistent by design, so a recurring webhook generates an unbounded stream of fresh cards.

Implements the issue's preferred option 1: surface a bot/automated signal on `InboundEvent` and have the gate treat such senders as strict regardless of `unknown_sender_policy`.

## Changes

- `src/channels/adapter.ts` — add `isAutomated?: boolean` to `InboundMessage` and `InboundEvent.message`.
- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` — populate it from Chat SDK's `author.isBot === true` in `messageToInbound`. `isBot` can also be the literal `"unknown"` on platforms that can't tell; that is deliberately **not** treated as automated, since misclassifying a human as a bot would silently and permanently drop their messages.
- `src/index.ts` — forward `message.isAutomated` through the host's `onInbound` stamping seam.
- `src/modules/permissions/index.ts` — `handleUnknownSender` now checks `event.message.isAutomated` before the policy switch: automated senders are denied silently (recorded as a drop) with no approval card and no decline-notify DM, regardless of `unknown_sender_policy`.

## Scope note

This repo checkout has no Discord/Slack/Telegram native adapter implementations on `main` (those live on a separate `channels` branch per the issue) — every adapter that would carry a bot signal (Discord, Slack) routes through `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts`, which is where this is wired. Native/legacy adapters that don't set `isAutomated` are unaffected (`undefined` == not automated == today's behavior).

## Test plan

- Added two tests in `src/modules/permissions/sender-approval.test.ts`:
  - An automated sender is dropped silently: no card delivered, no `pending_sender_approvals` row, no `agent_group_members` row.

## Summary

Fixes #2355 — installs (or refreshes) `~/.local/bin/ncl` on the `/update-nanoclaw` upgrade path, not just on fresh install.

**Note on history:** this is a clean re-attempt after #2356 was closed by a maintainer ("Something got messed with this - look at the changes") — that PR's diff had SKILL.md corrupted into a single base64-encoded line and carried an unrelated `FORK.md` file, unrelated to the fix. Neither problem is present here; this diff touches only the four files below.

## Root cause

`installCliSymlink()` in `setup/service.ts` was a private function only reachable from the fresh-install `service` setup step (`setup/auto.ts` → `runQuietStep('service', ...)`). The `/update-nanoclaw` skill (`.claude/skills/update-nanoclaw/SKILL.md`) never runs that step — it rebuilds and restarts the existing service directly — so an install that reaches 2.0.45+ via upgrade instead of fresh install ends up with `bin/ncl` working but no symlink on PATH.

## Fix

- `setup/service.ts`: export `installCliSymlink` (visibility change only, no behavior change).
- `scripts/install-cli-symlink.ts`: small CLI wrapper (same pattern as the existing `scripts/upgrade-state.ts`) that calls `installCliSymlink(process.cwd(), os.homedir())`.
- `.claude/skills/update-nanoclaw/SKILL.md`: Step 8 now runs `pnpm exec tsx scripts/install-cli-symlink.ts` before showing the restart instructions, so the symlink is (re)installed on every upgrade.

## Test plan

- Added 3 new tests to `setup/service.test.ts` covering `installCliSymlink`: creates the symlink, is idempotent on re-run, and does not clobber a real (non-symlink) file at the target path.
- Ran `pnpm exec vitest run setup/service.test.ts` — 13/13 passing (including the 3 new ones).
- Ran `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — clean, no type errors introduced.
- Did not run the full suite / full install per repo disk constraints in my environment; ran a targeted install via the local pnpm store (all packages reused from store, no downloads) just for this file's test run, then removed `node_modules` again afterward.

prs.title: Sanitize path-separator message IDs for attachment staging (#3206)
prs.body:
## Problem

`extractAttachmentFiles` in `src/session-manager.ts` gates inbound attachment
staging on `isSafeAttachmentName(messageId)`, which rejects any value
containing `/` or `\`. Google Chat message IDs are resource paths
(`spaces/<space>/messages/<id>`), so every one of them fails this check and
the function returns before writing anything — inbound attachments on
Google Chat are silently dropped. The agent still receives the attachment
metadata/filename in the message text, so it reports a file that was never
actually staged.

Slack/Discord/WhatsApp message IDs are opaque single-component tokens, so
they pass the check today and are unaffected.

## Fix

Added `safeAttachmentDirName(id)` to `src/attachment-safety.ts`:
- returns the id unchanged when it already satisfies `isSafeAttachmentName`
  (Slack/Discord/WhatsApp staging paths are byte-identical to before)
- otherwise derives a single-component slug (unsafe chars, including `/`,
  `\`, `..`, collapsed to `-`) with a short SHA-256 suffix of the original id
  appended, so two ids that differ only in stripped characters can't collide
  onto the same inbox directory

`extractAttachmentFiles` in `src/session-manager.ts` now sanitizes
`messageId` into `inboxMessageId` via this helper *before* it's used as the
inbox directory name / `localPath`, instead of rejecting the whole message.

### What did NOT change (security guarantee preserved)

This is a path-traversal guard, so I was deliberately conservative:

- `isSafeAttachmentName` itself is untouched — it still rejects any `/`,
  `\`, `..`, `.`, NUL, or non-basename value. Nothing was "relaxed".
- Containment does not come from `isSafeAttachmentName` rejecting the raw
  messageId — it comes from `safeAttachmentDirName`'s output always being a
  single, safe path component *by construction*, plus the unchanged
  defense-in-depth already in place:
  - `ensureContainedInboxDir` (symlink lstat + realpath containment check
    against the inbox root)
  - the `wx` exclusive-create flag on the actual `writeFileSync`
- The outbound side (`readOutboxFiles`, `clearOutbox`) and the A2A forwarding
  path (`agent-route.ts`) are untouched — those message IDs are host/container
  generated (`msg-<ts>-<rand>`, `a2a-<ts>-<rand>`), never externally supplied,
  and were already always safe.

## Tests

- `src/attachment-safety.test.ts` (new): unit coverage for
  `safeAttachmentDirName` — passes safe ids through unchanged, derives a safe
  component for a Google Chat-style resource path and for a traversal-shaped
  id, is deterministic, and does not collide two different unsafe ids that
  sanitize to the same slug.
- `src/host-core.test.ts`: replaced `should reject inbound attachments when
  messageId is unsafe` (which asserted the old drop-the-message behaviour)
  with two tests — one confirming a traversal-shaped id (`../../escape`) now
  lands in exactly one sanitized subdir of the inbox with nothing written
  outside the session's inbox root, and one confirming a Google Chat-style
  `spaces/<space>/messages/<id>` messageId now successfully stages its
  attachment.
- Existing regression tests for malicious *filenames* (as opposed to message
  ids) — pre-placed symlinks, `../../../tmp/pwned`-style filenames — are
  unchanged and still pass, since `isSafeAttachmentName` on `filename` was
  not touched.

Ran narrowly: `npx vitest run src/attachment-safety.test.ts
src/host-core.test.ts src/session-manager.attachments.test.ts
src/modules/agent-to-agent/agent-route.test.ts` — 69/69 passing. Also ran
`npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) and `npx eslint` on the changed files (0 errors,
only pre-existing unrelated `no-catch-all` warnings in code I didn't touch).

## Note (from the issue)

Fixing this alone isn't sufficient for Google Chat attachments end-to-end —
per the issue, `@chat-adapter/gchat` also omits `alt=media` on the Chat media
endpoint, causing `fetchData()` to 400 before bytes ever reach this code.
That's a separate bug being fixed upstream in `vercel/chat`, not addressed
here.

Closes #3206

prs.title: Telegram: trust channel's own identity in sender_scope gate
prs.body:
Fixes #2991

## Problem

Telegram broadcast-channel posts are anonymous — the Bot API attributes them to the channel itself via `sender_chat` (no `from`). `@chat-adapter/telegram`'s `toReactionActorAuthor` maps that to an author `userId` of `chat:<chatId>`. That identity is never a member of `agent_group_members`, so a wiring with `sender_scope='known'` (the default the channel-registration flow produces) could never engage on any channel post — every message failed the sender-scope gate silently.

## Fix

`setSenderScopeGate` in `src/modules/permissions/index.ts` now recognizes the wired channel's own posting identity — `userId` of the form `chat:<chatId>` where `<chatId>` matches the messaging group's own `platform_id` — and treats it as trusted, alongside the existing owner/global-admin/admin-of-group/member checks. This is suggested fix #2 from the issue: the channel posting to itself is not an unknown third party, so it shouldn't be gated by `sender_scope='known'`.

Scoped to `channel_type === 'telegram'` and the `chat:` prefix convention, which is specific to `@chat-adapter/telegram`'s anonymous-sender_chat/reaction-actor mapping — no other adapter uses this identity shape.

## Test plan

- Added `src/modules/permissions/telegram-channel-sender-scope.test.ts`:
  - a `sender_scope='known'` wiring now engages on an anonymous channel post whose `sender_chat` id matches the wired channel
  - a post claiming a different chat id is still correctly refused
- Verified against the pre-fix code that the first test fails without the change (reproduces #2991) and passes with it
- `npx vitest run src/modules/permissions src/router.test.ts` — 51/51 passed
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors (pre-existing unrelated errors in other files)
- `npx eslint src/modules/permissions/index.ts ...test.ts` — no new warnings/errors

issues.title: Session history is reloaded unbounded; auto-compaction cannot bound per-request context
issues.body:
**Summary**

Per-request context for a long-lived session grows without bound. Auto-compaction and `trimHistory` reduce the in-memory `agent.history`, but that result is never written back to the session store, and session restore reloads the *entire* stored history. `max_history_messages` is therefore not enforced across turns or session re-creation.

**Where**

- `src/agent/turn_persistence.zig` (`persistTurn`) — append-only: calls `store.saveMessage()` for user + assistant every turn. It never rewrites or prunes the stored session. Compacted history is not persisted; `Session.last_consolidated` is only a timestamp (`src/session.zig`).
- `src/session.zig` (`restorePersistedSessionState`) — on session creation, appends **every** stored entry into `agent.history`.
- `src/memory/engines/sqlite.zig` (`loadMessages`) — `SELECT role, content FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC` with **no LIMIT**.
- `src/agent/root.zig` — `maybeAutoCompactHistoryForModel` + `trimHistory` run **after** the LLM call (around line 2753), so they cannot bound the request that was just sent, and their reduction is not persisted.

**Effect**

In a single long-running process the in-memory history looks bounded (compaction keeps ~`compaction_keep_recent`), masking the issue. But on any session re-creation — process restart or session-cache eviction — the full accumulated store is reloaded and the next request is built from all of it. The stored session grows ~2 rows/turn indefinitely. Observed: a single request carrying hundreds of messages (well above `max_history_messages`) after the process was restarted, despite compaction appearing enabled and `compact_context = true`.

**Repro (generic)**

1. Open one session and exchange messages for many turns on any channel.
2. Restart the process (or force session-cache eviction) so the session is recreated.
3. Send one more message and inspect the outgoing request: it contains the entire accumulated history, not `max_history_messages`.

**Expected**

Per-request history is bounded by `max_history_messages` / `token_limit`: on restore, load only the most recent window (or compact/trim at restore time). The compaction output should be reflected in the store, or the store pruned.

**Scope / notes**

- `#939` fixed the `compact_context` flag being ignored, but does not bound the restored history.
- Minimal fix: bound `restorePersistedSessionState`'s load (limit `loadMessages`, or slice to the recent window) — keeps the full store for `history show` while bounding the prompt. Persisting the compacted history is a larger, optional follow-up.
- `/compact` operates on the in-memory history and does not change the stored session, so it does not help across a restart.

issues.title: memory: bound the persisted session transcript (compaction write-back with a sequence guard)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
Follow-up to #1053 / #1054 (credit: @O96a).

#1054 bounds what a session **restore** loads (`max_history_messages`), which fixes the unbounded per-request context. It does **not** bound the **store**: `persistTurn` appends user+assistant every turn and the compacted result is discarded, so the persisted transcript (and thus disk usage and restart/restore latency) grows linearly with session age even while the request looks fine.

## Proposed direction

After compaction, write the trimmed history back, or persist a compaction checkpoint and replay from it, e.g.

```python
compacted = trim_history(agent.history, max_history_messages)
agent.history = compacted
session_store.replace_history(session_id, compacted, up_to_seq=last_persisted_seq)
```

## Race hazard (must handle)

The write-back can race an in-flight turn. If a turn lands between the compaction snapshot and the store write, a naive `replace_history` silently drops it. Tag each persisted turn with a sequence number and only truncate up to the sequence the compaction snapshot was taken from.

## Scope

- `src/agent/turn_persistence.zig` (`persistTurn`) + the memory `SessionStore` (add a bounded replace / checkpoint API).
- Concurrency-safe: truncate only up to the compacted sequence.
- Tests: store stays bounded after many turns; no message loss when a turn interleaves with compaction.

Refs #1053, #1054.

prs.title: fix(session): bound restored history to max_history_messages
prs.body:
## Summary
- Bound the restored session history to the most recent `max_history_messages` entries when a session is restored from the store.

## Validation
- `zig build test --summary all` — 7491/7500 pass (9 skipped), 0 failures, 0 leaks.

## Notes
- `persistTurn` appends user+assistant every turn and never prunes the stored session, and restore loaded the entire stored history (`loadMessages`, no LIMIT) into `agent.history`. In one long-running process the in-memory history stays bounded by auto-compaction/`trimHistory`, so the issue is masked — but on any session (re)creation (process restart or cache eviction) the whole store was reloaded and the next request was built from all of it, silently defeating `max_history_messages`. Compaction runs *after* the LLM call and its result is never written back, so it did not help across a restart.
- Fix: restore only the most recent `max_history_messages` entries, matching `trimHistory`. The full session log is retained in the store for `history show`.
- Adds a regression test (`restored session history is bounded to max_history_messages`).

## Review feedback
- Thanks to @O96a for the review on #1053 — it confirms the diagnosis and correctly frames this as the read-path safety net: it bounds what restore *loads*, but not the store, which still grows every turn.
- The store-side follow-up (write the trimmed history back, or persist a compaction checkpoint and replay) is tracked in #1055, including the sequence-number guard needed so a write-back cannot race an in-flight turn and silently drop messages. This PR performs no write-back, so that hazard does not apply here.
- The store-side shape (an opt-in retention policy applied to every engine) is being discussed with the community here: https://github.com/nullclaw/nullclaw/discussions/1056

Refs #1053, #1055

prs.title: fix(library): keep the My Files preview open while its file is saved
prs.body:
## Summary
In the My Files (我的文件) preview, saving an edited Word document shows "加载中…" and reloads the preview. The same edit in the task's artifact panel does not.

Each save changes the file's mtime. The library's directory watcher reports `file_changed`, and `LibraryView` replaces the open item with a refreshed copy, from the list refresh and again from the detail fetch that reruns after it (this is when the header's 最后修改时间 updates, as in the report). `LibraryPreviewModal` memoized its artifact on the item object, so every copy cleared the preview, showed the loading state, read the whole file again and remounted the renderer. For the Word editor that means a new scroll container (back to the top) and lost focus. Favoriting from the preview header, and the detail fetch right after opening, replaced the item the same way.

The library design already requires `recorded/file_changed/repair/session_deleted` events to leave the open preview unchanged (`specs/features/library/2026-08-17-library-design.md`, line 234).

## Related Issue
User feedback, no GitHub issue: "在我的文件 tab 中直接编辑，保存后会重新加载，页面会闪动一下，但是对话预览面板编辑保存后不会".

## Changes Made
- `src/renderer/components/library/libraryArtifactCandidate.ts`
  - `getLibraryPreviewKey`: the file a preview shows and the renderer it gets (item id, path, artifact type, file name). Undefined while the file is unavailable.
  - `getLibraryPreviewContentKey`: adds the file version the index recorded (mtime, size), except for files that open in an editor that follows its file itself: Markdown, and the Office formats this window edits (`officeFormatForPath`).
- `src/renderer/components/library/LibraryPreviewModal.tsx`: loads by the content key and keeps the loaded artifact together with its preview key. Only a new preview key shows the loading state. A new version of the same file is read behind the preview shown and swapped in when ready. A failed background re-read keeps the content shown; a file that is gone arrives as an unavailable item.
- `src/renderer/components/library/libraryArtifactCandidate.test.ts`: 6 new tests.

The Office editors already reload external changes through the office bridge's directory watch and on window focus, and the Markdown editor polls its file. The artifact panel relies on the same thing (`refreshOpenOfficeEditor`, no file watch for Markdown).

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [ ] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `libraryArtifactCandidate.test.ts`, 6 tests: a refreshed copy of the item (favorite, sort time, latest session, file version) keeps the preview key; another item id, path, name or type changes it; unavailable files have no key; a saved .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.md keeps its content key; PDF, image and HTML get a new content key for a new version but not for a favorite; without the editor bridges, Office and Markdown files are re-read.
- `npm test`: 607 files passed, 18 skipped (6532 tests passed, 154 skipped).
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and ESLint with CI rules (`--max-warnings 0`) on the touched files: clean.
- Real app in an isolated instance (own profile via `LOBSTERAI_DEV_USER_DATA_DIR`, driven over CDP), with a .docx and a .txt added to My Files through `library.recordCandidates`. Observed in the DOM with a MutationObserver:

| Scenario | Old code | New code |
|---|---|---|
| Word: type in the My Files preview, click 保存; the header time updates (22:44 → 22:45 old, 22:45 → 22:46 new) | about 1.6 s after the save the modal shows 加载中… and the editor DOM is unmounted and rebuilt | no loading state, same editor element, the edit is written to the file |
| Favorite from the preview header | not run | no loading state, same editor element |
| A .txt changed by another program while previewed | not run | the new line appears in place, no loading state, same renderer element |

Markdown in My Files was not exercised in the app; it is covered by the key tests and follows the same path as Office.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
No visual change. The flash is transient, so before/after screenshots look the same; the table above records what the DOM showed.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [ ] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [ ] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [ ] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [x] None

Renderer only: no IPC, storage or OpenClaw config changes.

## Additional Notes
- Other preview types (image, PDF, HTML, text, code) still follow their file: when the index records a new mtime or size, they are re-read in place instead of reopening the modal.
- Not changed: opening an Office file still reads it whole as a data URL in `loadDetectedFileArtifact`, although the live editor reads it again through its bridge. The task panel does the same.

prs.title: fix(cowork): remove the progress card above the composer
prs.body:
## Summary

Removes the OpenClaw progress card that sat above the composer (added in #2778, restyled since). It showed the agent's self-reported plan, and in practice that plan was too often wrong or missing to be worth the space or the cost of making it accurate:

- **Inaccurate**: models update the plan when they remember to. In one test, a DeepSeek V4 Flash run spent 7 minutes on a slide deck while the card stayed on "第 1/5 步", then jumped to done; the steps were also in English for a Chinese request. Of 12 local runs that ended with an unfinished plan, 6 had in fact finished the work.
- **Inconsistent**: whether a plan exists is up to the model. Locally, only 39% of runs with 15+ tool calls wrote one, and 8% of runs with 5–14.
- **Costly to fix**: 78% of `progress_card` calls already take a model round trip of their own (about 6% of tool-calling responses in sessions that use it). Prompting models to update after every step would add more, and still not guarantee it.
- The step lines, the live status line and the elapsed timer already show that a run is moving, without relying on the model's word. Claude Code no longer gives its newest models the todo tools at all, and Codex keeps only a small step counter while a run is active.

## Changes

- **Renderer**: remove `OpenClawProgressCard`, `ProgressCardMarkdown`, `progressCardDisplay`, `useOpenClawProgressCard`, the expansion preference and the card's 11 i18n keys, and the mount in `CoworkSessionDetail`.
- **IPC / main process**: remove the `cowork:progressCard:get`, `cowork:progressCard:dismiss` and `cowork:progressCard:changed` channels, their preload methods and type declarations, the main-process `OpenClawProgressCards` bridge, and the router/adapter forwarding of the Gateway's `progressCard.changed` broadcast (now ignored like any other unhandled event).
- **Shared**: remove `src/shared/cowork/progressCard.ts`.
- Remove `third-party-notices/openclaw-progress-card-LICENSE.txt`, which covered the adapted card code.
- `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/README.md`: the plan completion check entry no longer points at the removed `progressCardDisplay.ts`.

## Unchanged

- A turn's process still lists each `progress_card` update: expand "耗时 X", then the step group, then "更新了任务进度 x/y" to see the checklist and note.
- The `progress_card` tool stays enabled in OpenClaw, so agent behavior is unchanged.
- `zz-openclaw-plan-completion-check.patch` (backport of upstream #160297) stays; it governs whether a run finishes its plan, not the UI.

## Electron-specific notes

- Three IPC channels and the matching `window.electron.cowork` preload methods are removed. Nothing else used them.
- No storage, OpenClaw config or restart behavior changes.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 606 files passed.
- ESLint (CI rules) on touched files, `tsc` for renderer and `electron-tsconfig.json`: clean.
- End-to-end in an isolated instance built from this branch, against a real Gateway and a scripted OpenAI-compatible mock that saves a 3-step plan, reads a file, updates and completes the plan, then answers. prs.title: fix: install Computer Use without a gateway restart and admit tasks after restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

User report (macOS): after installing Computer Use the gateway restarted as expected, but selecting the kit and sending the first message made the gateway "restart again".

From the 2026-10-09 logs, the second restart was not real (same gateway pid; no SIGTERM or new `[gateway] ready`):

1. The kit install forced a hard restart.
2. On that first start after its in-gateway auto-update, nsp-clawguard 2.5.5 ran a skill scan and wrote 1806 events synchronously, blocking the gateway event loop for ~60s.
3. The post-restart `config.apply` confirmation timed out, so LobsterAI queued a `config-delivery-fallback` deferred restart.
4. The user's task (16:27:14) was refused while that was pending. The refusal was rendered as the global "AI engine starting" overlay (since fixed by 4868faef). On the current branch the task is still refused, because without a confirmed baseline after a restart, admission returns `unknown`.

## Changes

- **Computer Use kit** (`kits/handlers.ts`): install and uninstall use an ordinary sync instead of forcing a restart. The diff is only `skills` + `mcp.servers`. OpenClaw 2026.8.1 hot-applies `mcp` (dispose-mcp-runtimes), and `skills` needs no reload. Uninstall now applies the config before deleting the runtime, so the running helper is disposed first.
- **Post-restart admission** (`openclawEngineManager.ts`, `main.ts`): the engine manager records the config file content each gateway process spawned with. Until that generation confirms an application, admission uses this content as its baseline, so tasks whose model is unaffected are admitted while the confirmation lags.
- **No useless respawn** (`openclawConfigRecovery.ts`, `main.ts`): if the running gateway spawned from the pending target, a failed confirmation retries after 30s and counts toward the existing stall breaker. It no longer escalates to a recovery respawn, which would only reload the same file and rerun plugin startup work.
- **Tool policy** (`openclawConfigSync.ts`): deny `computer`, `nodes` and `mobile_ui`. They need a paired OpenClaw node, which LobsterAI never has, so they always fail. `computer` also competes with the Computer Use kit's MCP tools; the logs show the model calling it and failing with `no connected computer-capable node`.

## Electron / OpenClaw behavior changes

- Installing or uninstalling Computer Use no longer restarts the gateway (hot config apply).
- Config recovery: a gateway that spawned from the target now stalls after 2 failed confirmations instead of respawning. The stall is non-blocking ("settings not applied" pill + Quick Repair).
- `openclaw.json` `tools.deny` now contains `web_search, computer, nodes, mobile_ui` (hot reload, no restart).

## Verification

- Targeted Vitest: 212 passed. Full `npm test`: one failure in `skillManager.watcher.test.ts` (fs watch timing, unrelated), which passes 3/3 in isolation.
- ESLint on changed files is clean; `npm run compile:electron` passes.
- E2E in an isolated dev instance (temporary profile):
  - Kit install with the gateway running: `needsHardRestart=false`, applied in 649ms, gateway pid unchanged, and OpenClaw logs `config hot reload applied (mcp.servers.computer-use)`. The whole install took 1.5s (51s in the user log).
  - Kit uninstall: applied in 344ms, no restart, runtime removed.
  - Bug repro: after an env-change restart, the gateway was SIGSTOPped at the confirmation's `config.get` → `mode=fallback` plus a deferred restart (the user's state). A task started then logged `admitted a task while config is pending; its model is unaffected` and was dispatched in 8ms. After SIGCONT the deferred retry applied with no restart, and the task reached `chat.send`.
  - With a vision model (qwen3.6-plus): `tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via tools.deny: computer, mobile_ui, nodes`.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Make the post-start confirmation read-only (spec 2026-10-09 §4). Here `config.get` returned ~1s before the freeze, so a passing content check would have avoided the fallback. It needs an `applicationGap` log from a current build.
- Report the nsp-clawguard 2.5.5 main-thread blocking to its owners.

prs.title: fix(artifacts): refresh previews when agents edit files in place
prs.body:
## Summary
An HTML file shown in the artifact panel's built-in browser did not refresh when the agent edited it, and the panel previews (SVG, code, text, images, documents) missed many agent edits as well.

`artifact:watchFile` only acted on `fs.watch` events of type `change`. Many real edits arrive as `rename`:
- On macOS, libuv reports a kqueue event without `NOTE_EXTEND`/`NOTE_ATTRIB` as `rename`. OpenClaw's host `write`/`edit` rewrite an existing file in place (`r+`, tail first, then prefix, then truncate when shorter), so a same-length edit such as `版本 1` → `版本 2` produces only `rename` and the inode stays.
- On every platform, an atomic replacement (a temporary file renamed over the target: OpenClaw with `workspaceOnly`, `sed -i`, our own Office and Markdown autosaves) produces `rename`, and the watcher keeps following the replaced inode, so it misses every later write too.

The watcher was also shared per path: any subscriber's `unwatchFile` closed it for every other subscriber.

## Related Issue
No GitHub issue. Found while verifying netease-youdao/LobsterAI#2832 (keep the open preview when a later reply rewrites the file); this PR builds on it.

## Changes Made
- `src/main/libs/artifactFileWatcher.ts` (new, with `artifactFileWatcher.test.ts`):
  - Each burst of events settles for 300 ms (as before) and is then confirmed with a `stat`. A file that still exists is reported, whether the events were `change` or `rename`. A file that is gone is not reported; it is looked for again every second, and reported when it comes back.
  - The watcher re-arms on the current file when the inode changed or a `rename` arrived. The `rename` rule covers ext4, which reuses a deleted file's inode number at once.
  - Subscriptions are counted per owner (renderer), so one view letting go no longer silences another.
- `src/main/main.ts`: only the IPC wiring is left (about 20 lines fewer). Owners are released on `destroyed`, `render-process-gone` and `did-navigate`, since a reloaded renderer never runs its effect cleanups. Changes are sent only to the webContents that subscribed, instead of every window.
- `src/shared/artifactPreview/constants.ts`, `src/main/preload.ts`: the three channels are now `ArtifactPreviewIpc.WatchFile`, `UnwatchFile` and `FileChanged`. The channel strings are unchanged.
- `src/renderer/components/artifacts/ArtifactPanel.tsx`:
  - The panel's auto-refresh no longer watches Markdown. `EditableMarkdownFile` already polls and version-checks its file. Now that the watcher survives atomic replacement, keeping the watch would re-read the file and report a refresh after every Markdown autosave.
  - `refresh_preview` analytics now carry `trigger`: `manual` for the menu action, `file_change` for the auto-refresh. The values are defined in `ArtifactRefreshTrigger` (`artifactAnalytics.ts`).

Office files keep their auto-refresh. Our own autosave now reaches `refreshOpenOfficeEditor`, but `OfficeDocument.refresh` compares content hashes, so a file the app just saved is a no-op: no reload and no conflict prompt. At most it adds one read and hash per autosave, the same check the Office directory watcher already runs after each save.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [ ] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `artifactFileWatcher.test.ts`: 10 tests.
  - 9 use a fake disk whose watchers follow files, not paths, the way kqueue and inotify do. They cover a lone `rename` for an in-place edit, debouncing, atomic replacement, a reused inode number, a deleted file coming back, a file that appears later, shared subscriptions, owner release, a check that finishes after unsubscribe, and watcher failures.
  - 1 runs on the real file system. Each of these mutations fails at least one test: ignoring `rename`, no re-arm on rename, no re-arm on a new inode, no polling for a missing file, and an unwatch that closes the watcher for every subscriber. 12 repeated runs passed.
- `npm test`: 6460 passed. 3 files failed only because the worktree had no `node_modules` of its own (`sheetCommandPolicy`, `mcpLaunchResolverManager`, `windowsInstallerContract` build paths from the repo root).
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, `npm run compile:electron` and ESLint with CI rules (`--max-warnings 0`) on the touched files: clean.
- Real app in an isolated instance (own profile, Vite/HMR/CDP ports, scripted OpenAI-compatible mock model). The browser tab's text was read with `webview.executeJavaScript`, and `artifact:file:changed` was recorded in the renderer. Same flow on the old and the new main process:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| HTML in the built-in browser: `write`, then three same-length `edit`s | stays at 版本 1, 0 change events | 版本 2 → 3 → 4, one event per edit |
| `exec` replaces the page atomically (new inode), then `edit` | – | 版本 5, then 版本 6 |
| `exec rm` the page, then `write` it again, then `edit` | – | no reload while it is gone (no error page), then 版本 8, then 版本 9 |
| SVG in a panel tab, edited from the shell (no new artifact): same-length in-place, atomic replace, in-place again | – | each one refreshes the panel |
| Word: `lobster-word__word_edit` twice in the open editor (autosave = atomic replace) | – | one save and one event per edit, status `saved`, no conflict, no further saves over 20 s |
| Markdown: editor autosave, then an agent `edit` | – | no watch and no events; the edit appears via the editor's own polling, and the user's typed line is kept |
| Analytics: auto-refresh, then menu → 刷新 | – | `refresh_preview` with `trigger=file_change`, then `trigger=manual` |

Every analytics request of the test instance was cancelled with `webRequest.onBeforeRequest`, installed through `--inspect-brk` before app ready, so none of them left the machine.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
No UI change. The table above records the preview contents read over CDP.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication
- [ ] Changes to window management
- [ ] None

`artifact:watchFile` and `artifact:unwatchFile` are now counted per sender, and `artifact:file:changed` goes only to subscribed webContents. The handlers ignore non-string paths and relative paths, which could never be watched correctly.

## Additional Notes
- Before this change, only in-place writes that grew a file (reported as `change`) reached the auto-refresh, and those were already reported as `refresh_preview`. With `trigger`, dashboards can split automatic refreshes from user clicks; automatic ones will now be far more frequent.

prs.title: fix(test): stop npm test from modifying tracked logs/cowork.log
prs.body:
## Summary

`logs/cowork.log` was committed by accident in 983ec2a0. `logs/` was added to `.gitignore` later, but the rule doesn't apply to a file that is already tracked. On macOS, every local `npm test` run appended a line to it, which left an unrelated change in the working tree:

```
[WARN] [resolveNodeShim] Failed to resolve Electron helper runtime: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received undefined
```

### Root cause

`src/main/mcp/mcpLaunchResolverManager.test.ts` (`resolveNpmCommand prefers bundled npm-cli.js through Electron runtime`) is the only test that writes to the file. I confirmed this by tracing every `cowork.log` write across the full suite.

- The test calls `resolveNpmCommand()`, which calls `resolveNodePackageCliCommand()` and then `getElectronNodeRuntimePath()`.
- On macOS, `process.resourcesPath` is undefined under Vitest, so the helper lookup throws.
- The error is logged with `coworkLog('WARN', 'resolveNodeShim', ...)`.
- The test's electron mock returns `process.cwd()` for `app.getPath`, so the log goes to `<repo>/logs/cowork.log`.

Linux CI returns early on this path, so CI never hit it.

### Changes

- Mock `../libs/coworkLogger` in the launch resolver test, as `coworkUtil.nodeRuntime.test.ts` already does for the same function. No production code changes.
- `git rm --cached logs/cowork.log` so the existing `logs/` ignore rule applies.

### Notes

- Pulling this deletes `logs/cowork.log` from your working tree. If your copy has lines appended by tests, git refuses the merge until you run `git checkout -- logs/cowork.log`.
- No Electron, IPC, storage or OpenClaw behavior changes.

## Testing

- `npm test` on macOS: 608 files passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed.
- `git status --ignored` was identical before and after the run, and the hash and mtime of `logs/cowork.log` on disk did not change.
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 src/main/mcp/mcpLaunchResolverManager.test.ts` reports no problems.
