issues.title: send_file_to_user audio file permanently wedges the session — LM Studio's 400 At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. is not recognized by the audio-fallback / media-capability classifiers
issues.body:
This is a third rejection shape of the family documented in #7015 (fixed by #7024) and partially addressed by the still-open PR #7654.

When the agent delivers a local audio file via send_file_to_user, the file is delivered successfully, but the tool result's output keeps the audio DataBlock (media_type: audio/mpeg, source: file://…) in the persisted session history. On every subsequent model call in that session, OpenAIChatFormatter (whose input_types defaults include audio/*) serializes the block into an input_audio part and the local endpoint rejects it:

Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio)', 'type': 'BadRequestError', 'param': 'audio', 'code': 400}}
Because neither reactive classifier matches this wording, QwenPaw's strip → retry → learn recovery never triggers:

_is_audio_fallback_error() (qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py) currently requires DashScope-specific markers (internalerror.algo.invalidparameter, "incorrect modal", "was entered", "may not be supported by the model", "wrong position") — none appear in this response.
The error also fails every _EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS regex (it contains no "does not support" / "is not supported" / "unsupported modality" phrasing).
Result: the exception propagates to the user, no rejects_audio capability is learned, the block remains in history, and every subsequent message in the session fails identically — the conversation is permanently unrecoverable from the user side (6/6 consecutive user messages failed across ~50 minutes in my repro) without manual history surgery.

Related PR(s): #7015 / #7024 (same wedge mechanism, DashScope shape), #7654 (open; adds DashScope URL-shape and llama-server audio input is not supported 500 — does not cover this shape).

Security considerations: None. No credentials or file contents are included; all details below are sanitized.

Component(s) Affected
 Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
 Console (frontend web UI)
 Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
 Skills
 CLI
 Documentation (website)
 Tests
 CI/CD
 Scripts / Deploy
Environment
QwenPaw 2.2.1, Python 3.12, Linux (aarch64)
Provider: lmstudio (local OpenAI-compatible server), model qwen3.8-flash-next (text + vision; audio input limit = 0)
Channel: WeChat personal (the console channel reproduces the same failure; the channel is not the cause)
Steps to Reproduce
Use an OpenAI-compatible local model with no audio input support (LM Studio / vLLM-family engine).
Have the agent generate a small .mp3 (e.g. via edge-tts) and deliver it with send_file_to_user — the file is delivered successfully.
Send any plain-text message in the same session.
Keep sending messages — every subsequent request fails with the same 400.
Actual Result
Every subsequent model call in the session fails with BadRequestError 400: At most 0 audio(s) may be provided in one prompt. (parameter=audio). No strip-and-retry occurs, nothing is learned into ModelCapabilityCache, and the session is dead until a human removes the block from sessions/<channel>/…json.

Verified with the runtime's own formatter: formatting the poisoned assistant message produced an input_audio part (~92 KB wire); after removing the block from the session JSON, the same format call emits 0 input_audio parts and the image blocks in other messages remain intact.

Expected Result
The audio-fallback path should classify this response, strip audio, retry, and learn rejects_audio for the model — like the DashScope shapes from #7015 / #7654 — so at most one turn degrades instead of the whole session dying.

Root cause (verified in installed 2.2.1 source)
agentscope.formatter.OpenAIChatFormatter.input_types defaults to ["text/plain", "image/*", "audio/*", "application/pdf"]; QwenPaw does not narrow this for models without audio capability.
The tool-result audio DataBlock is persisted into session history by send_file_to_user, so it is replayed on every request.
react_agent._is_audio_fallback_error() is DashScope-wording-only, and _EXPLICIT_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_PATTERNS has no pattern for at most N <modal>(s) may be provided in one prompt / (parameter=<modal>), so both recovery gates evaluate False and the error is re-raised.
agents.audio_mode = "auto" only governs inbound audio (transcription/placeholder); outbound tool-result media blocks bypass it entirely.
Suggested fix
Add a request-scoped pattern like at most \d+ (audio|image|video)s? may be provided in one prompt (and/or \(parameter=(audio|image|video)\)) to the audio-fallback / unsupported-media classifiers — most naturally as an extension of #7654, ideally mapping the parameter field so an image/video variant also routes to the correct stripping path.
Longer term, consider sanitizing (or capability-gating) non-text blocks in send_file_to_user tool results before persistence, so a delivered file never becomes model input in the first place — the delivered artifact is for the user, not the model.
Additional notes
Workaround in the wild (what unblocked the session): back up sessions/<channel>/<user>.json, replace the audio DataBlock inside the tool-result output with a text note, save. Session state is re-read from disk per request, so no restart is needed. Happy to contribute a regression test fixture reproducing this response body.

issues.title: [Bug]: OpenAI Responses API 的流式事件-空响应问题

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version
win10，desktop，2.2.2.b4

之前都能好好运行，但不知为何，突然出现发起会话运行1-3步就毫无提示中断会话。问AI后修复。
bug：
QwenPaw 使用 OpenAI Responses API 的流式事件。旧版 agentscope.model._openai_response._model 中的 _parse_stream_response 只处理了增量事件：

response.output_text.delta
response.function_call_arguments.delta
response.reasoning_summary_text.delta
但是，某些正常响应只在最后的 response.completed 事件中提供完整 response.output。旧代码只从这个事件提取 reasoning，没有提取：

message.content[].output_text：最终文本；
function_call：最终工具调用及其 arguments。
于是后端可能已经收到模型结果，却只保存 reasoning；前端收到的最终 assistant output 为空，显示“助手返回了空响应”。这也解释了为什么有时只运行几个步骤后突然结束：如果该轮的有效内容只出现在 response.completed.output，执行链没有拿到文本或工具调用。

修复方案
修复 _parse_stream_response：

在 response.completed 中遍历 response.output。
对 type == "message"，提取 content 中的 type == "output_text"。
对 type == "function_call"，提取 call_id、name 和 arguments。
如果此前已收到参数 delta，则按 call_id 去重，避免重复工具调用。
保留原有 reasoning、文本 delta、工具参数 delta 和 usage 处理。

issues.title: [Bug]: Feishu 入站图文混发（post 内嵌图片）被静默丢弃——仅解析文字、不下载图片、无任何警告（inbound，与 #2792 出站方向相反）
issues.body:
## Summary (English)

Incoming Feishu **rich-text (`post`) messages that contain both text and images** are only partially parsed by the Feishu channel: the **text is delivered to the agent, but the embedded images are silently dropped** — no media file is downloaded and no warning is logged. Images sent as a **standalone `type=image` message always work**. This is the **inbound direction**; outbound mixed-content handling is tracked in #2792.

## 环境 / Environment

- QwenPaw version: **2.2.2b4** (QwenPaw Desktop, `qwenpaw-backend` packaged exe)
- OS: Windows 10 (AMD64)
- Channel: **Feishu**
- Model: unrelated (pure channel-layer issue)

## 复现步骤 / Steps to Reproduce

1. 在飞书里给机器人发**一条同时包含文字和图片的消息**（文字＋图片合并在同一条消息里，飞书会打包成富文本 `post`）。
2. 观察 QwenPaw 日志：只有一条 `type=post` 的 recv 记录，**没有**对应的 `type=image` recv，`media` 目录也没有新文件落盘。
3. Agent 只收到文字，图片内容永久丢失，**日志中没有任何 WARNING/ERROR**（静默失效）。

对照组（均正常）：
- a) 单独发纯文字 → 正常；
- b) **单独发一张图片（不带文字）→ `type=image` → 下载落盘 → 正常**（实测 3/3 成功）。

## 实际结果 / Actual Behavior

日志实录（chat id 已脱敏）：

```
2026-10-09 12:07:00 | INFO | qwenpaw\app\channels\feishu\channel.py:901 | feishu recv from=unknown#c130 chat=oc_**** msg_id=om_x100b63b2cb35 type=post text_len=43
（同一消息中的 2 张图片：无任何 recv/下载记录，media 目录无落盘）

2026-10-09 12:09:32 | INFO | ... type=image text_len=0   ← 单独发的图片，正常收到
2026-10-09 12:10:01 | INFO | ... type=image text_len=0   ← 单独发的图片，正常收到
```

即：**图文混发 → 图片被静默丢弃；图单独发 → 正常**。用户侧表现为“发了图但 AI 说没看到/图老是收不到”。

## 期望结果 / Expected Behavior

1. 解析 `post` 消息载荷中的 `{"tag":"img","image_key":...}` 元素（飞书富文本文档：一条 post 可含多段落，图片元素需独立段落），按 `image_key` 走图片下载接口，把图片作为媒体附加上下文交给 Agent；
2. 多张图片全部提取，顺序保留；
3. **至少**：当消息含图片但未被处理时打一条 `WARNING`（标注丢弃了几张），避免静默失效——排查这类问题目前只能靠人工比对 recv 日志与用户描述。

## 备注 / Additional Context

- 相关但方向相反：#2792 是**出站**（Agent→飞书）图文同发丢图，本 issue 是**入站**（飞书→Agent），建议分别修复。
- 与 #7817 的区别：#7817 问题 2 是 **file/media/audio 独立事件**因缺 `im:resource` 权限被服务端过滤；本 issue 中**独立 `type=image` 消息完全正常（3/3 实测）**，丢的是**打包在 `post` 载荷内嵌的 img 元素**——是 channel 对 post payload 的解析缺口，不是事件推送/权限问题。
- 当前用户侧规避：图片单独一条消息发、一张一张发（实测有效）。
- 猜测修复点：`qwenpaw/app/channels/feishu/channel.py` 中处理 `type=post` 的分支（recv 日志所在 ~L901 附近），目前只取了 text 部分。

issues.title: [Bug] Console boot splash (LOADING CONSOLE) has no retry and no error surface; stale WebView2 cache after update can permanently block boot
issues.body:
# Title: [Bug] Console boot splash (LOADING CONSOLE) has no retry and no error surface; stale WebView2 cache after update can permanently block boot

## Summary

The console frontend boots through a static splash (`index.html` ships a hard-coded
`.qwenpaw-boot` / "Loading Console" placeholder). If any boot-time step fails — a lazy
chunk 404s after an app update, the WebView2 process loses the race during Windows boot
storms, or a backend-dependent call fails early — the splash stays forever. There is:

- **no retry** of the failed module load / API call,
- **no error surface** (no message, no "reload" button; the console log shows nothing to the user),
- **no auto-reload** when the backend becomes healthy later.

Recovery today is manual `Ctrl+R`, which works — the same session that hung for 12+ s
rendered fully within 20 s after one reload — but a user who does not know the trick sees
a dead app. Windows auto-start makes this worse: at logon the user is often not at the
machine, so the app sits on the splash until someone notices.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop 2.2.2-beta.4, Windows 10 (AMD64)
- Console served by backend at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (`qwenpaw\console\index.html`)

## Evidence (all reproducible locally)

1. **Splash is static HTML** — `console/index.html` contains the boot placeholder inline;
   if `assets/index-*.js` fails, nothing ever replaces it.
2. **~30 MB of JS chunks on boot** (e.g. `ts.worker` 7.0 MB, `ui-vendor` 6.4 MB,
   `editor-vendor` 4.3 MB). Under logon resource contention any of these can fail or stall;
   there is no loader-level retry.
3. **Hang reproduced and un-hung by reload** (2026-10-03): page pinned on "LOADING
   CONSOLE" > 12 s; after `page.reload()` the full chat UI rendered within 20 s.
4. **Settings panes show raw errors until a manual refresh** after backend restart —
   same root cause: one-shot fetches with no retry/error UI.
5. **Update leaves stale cache**: `index.html` (cached by WebView2) references hashed
   chunks from the previous build; after an update those 404 and the boot promise dies
   silently — permanent splash until the user manually clears cache or reloads.

## Suggested fixes (any would have saved the reporter hours)

1. **Boot watchdog in the splash page**: if the root app has not mounted within N seconds,
   show a visible error state with a **Reload** button and the failed resource URL
   (capture `window.onerror` + `unhandledrejection` + `script.onerror` on the boot chunk).
2. **Retry once or twice automatically** (module re-import or `location.reload()` with a
   `?boot-retry=1` marker to avoid loops), before showing the error state.
3. **Reload when backend health flips to OK**: the splash can poll `/health`; if the page
   is still un-mounted and the backend starts answering 200, auto-`location.reload()`.
4. **Cache-busting on update**: serve `index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (or a
   versioned URL) so an updated build can never reference a stale hashed chunk from cache.
5. Optional: an `app://reload` deep-link / tray menu item "Reload console" so external
   watchdogs (auto-start scripts) can trigger the same recovery as Ctrl+R.

## Reproduction

A. Splash hang without devtools:
   1. Start the app during a busy logon (or throttle CPU).
   2. Observe "LOADING CONSOLE" indefinitely; `GET /console/` is 200 and backend APIs answer.
   3. `Ctrl+R` → app boots normally.

B. Stale-cache boot block (update path):
   1. Update the app while the WebView2 profile keeps the old `index.html`.
   2. Launch: old HTML requests removed `assets/index-<oldhash>.js` → 404 → splash forever.
   3. Ctrl+R (or clearing `EBWebView`) fixes it.

## Related

- Reporter opened #8093 for a separate multimodal-gating issue (same install).
- A community auto-start script already had to implement its own "backend healthy but UI
  never rendered → kill & restart" watchdog (`start-tray.ps1`), i.e. the workaround for a
  missing in-app recovery is being rebuilt outside the app today.

issues.title: Console does not recover from a failed lazy page chunk load; every navigation stays on the error screen until a full reload
issues.body:
## Summary

When a lazily imported Console page fails to load, the UI does not recover. Every subsequent attempt to switch pages keeps showing the load-failure screen, and the only way out is a full page reload. There is a retry mechanism in the code, but it cannot succeed, and the error boundary's reset path cannot break the deadlock.

This is a robustness problem that turns a brief, self-healing glitch into a hard stuck state. It is not caused by the frame-parsing issue in #7813, but that issue can trigger it, which is how I hit it.

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.2.1, Windows desktop build
- Console over `127.0.0.1`, default webview shell
- Verified against the code paths in `main`

## Observed behavior

The failure mode is consistent and has a distinctive shape:

1. At some point a page fails to load and the error screen appears ("页面加载失败" / "Page failed to load").
2. From then on, clicking any item in the left navigation does not recover. The load-failure screen stays.
3. Reloading the page fixes it immediately and completely.

Point 2 is the part that matters. Because the error screen is sticky across navigation, the user cannot work around it in the app at all. I have hit this repeatedly, not once.

## Mechanism

### The retry cannot succeed

`console/src` builds lazy pages through a retry wrapper:

```js
const QP = 3, $P = 1000;
function Sr(e, t) {
  return e().catch(a => {
    if (t <= 0) throw a;
    return new Promise(n => setTimeout(() => n(Sr(e, t - 1)), $P));
  });
}
```

Three attempts, one second apart. But `e` is always the same factory, e.g. `() => import("./SomePage-<hash>.js")`. Every retry requests the identical URL. When the underlying cause is a transient fetch failure, the retry re-issues a request the browser has already recorded as failed, so all three attempts fail together. The retry adds latency but no real recovery.

It is also worth noting the retry only covers total failure. Nothing re-attempts after the retries are exhausted.

### The error boundary cannot reset

The boundary wraps the routed pages:

```js
componentDidUpdate(prev) {
  if (this.state.hasError && prev.resetKey !== this.props.resetKey) {
    this.setState({ hasError: false, isChunkError: false, restarting: false, restartError: "" });
  }
}
```

and it is mounted with the route pathname as the key:

```jsx
<ErrorBoundary resetKey={pathname} canRestartRuntime={...}>
  <Suspense fallback={...}>
    <Routes>{routes.map(d => <Route path={d.path} element={<d.Component />} />)}</Routes>
  </Suspense>
</ErrorBoundary>
```

So navigating to another route does change `resetKey`, and the guard does fire. The problem is what happens next.

### Why the reset does nothing

The lazy components are created once, from a build-time map of constant specifiers:

```js
function ee(e) {
  ...
  return p.lazy(() => {
    const cached = Tr.get(key, "default");
    if (cached) return Promise.resolve({ default: cached });
    return Sr(() => entry().then(m => ({ default: m })), QP);
  });
}
```

`React.lazy` stores the outcome of the factory in its internal payload. Once that payload settles as rejected, it stays rejected for the lifetime of the module. Re-rendering the same lazy element does not call the factory again; React sees the rejected payload and re-throws the stored error synchronously.

So the sequence after a route change is:

1. `resetKey` changes, the guard fires, `hasError` goes back to false.
2. React re-renders the children, which are the same lazy elements as before.
3. `React.lazy` finds a rejected payload and throws the cached error.
4. The boundary catches it and sets `hasError` back to true.
5. The load-failure screen is displayed again.

Because the lazy element is built from a constant specifier, step 2 can never produce a fresh payload. The deadlock is stable: every navigation ends in step 5, which matches the observed "any tab stays stuck".

A full reload is the only thing that works, because it discards the module registry along with the settled payloads.

## Relationship to #7813

These are separate defects, and neither fix covers the other.

#7813 is a frame-parsing crash on the streaming path. It aborts a turn but has nothing to do with page loading. However, it is a plausible trigger here: a crash of that kind can leave the app in a state where the next lazy page load fails, and once that happens this deadlock keeps the user stuck until they reload.

So this issue is worth fixing on its own. Fixing #7813 reduces how often it is triggered, but does not make recovery work.

## Suggested fixes

Two changes, and I would suggest both because they address different halves.

First, make the retry able to actually retry. Re-issuing an identical module specifier does not help when that request has already failed, so each attempt should use a distinct specifier, for example appending a monotonically increasing query parameter:

```js
Sr(() => entry(attempt).then(m => ({ default: m })), QP)
```

With a genuinely new specifier the browser performs a real fetch, and the existing three attempts become meaningful. Most transient causes here (backend restart, machine sleep/wake, proxy hiccup) would then self-heal without user action.

Second, give the boundary a way out for this specific case. The `resetKey` mechanism cannot work while the lazy payload stays rejected, so a chunk-load error should escalate to a bounded automatic reload instead of waiting for the user to press the button. A marker in `sessionStorage` (or a query parameter) can ensure the page only auto-reloads once, so a genuinely missing chunk does not produce a reload loop.

Either change alone improves things. Together they cover both "the transient cause is gone by now" and "the payload is poisoned and only a reload clears it".

## What I verified, and what I did not

Verified by reading the shipped bundle and the corresponding source on `main`: the retry wrapper and its reuse of one specifier, the `resetKey` prop bound to the pathname, the guard that resets `hasError`, and the lazy factory built from a constant import specifier.

Also verified on the affected machine: all static assets referenced by the entry chunk are present and every asset request returns 200 or 304, so this is not a missing-file problem.

Not verified: I could not reproduce the deadlock in a controlled browser session. There is no test harness available in this environment and the error state is in-memory, so it disappears the moment the page reloads. My account of the deadlock comes from reading the code paths above rather than from a captured trace, and I would rather flag that than present it as directly observed. If it is useful I can try to instrument a reproduction.

issues.title: [Security] MCP Driver 配置接口导致 root RCE —— 完整入侵证据链（已脱敏）

labels.name: invalid
labels.description: This doesn't seem right

issues.body:
# [Security] MCP Driver 配置接口可导致 root 远程代码执行（RCE）→ 服务器被植入挖矿木马

## 概述

我们在生产服务器上排查 CPU 满载时，发现并完整溯源了一起针对 QwenPaw 的入侵事件。攻击者通过 **QwenPaw 的 MCP Driver 配置接口**，以名为 `rce-poc-<hash>` 的 Driver 在服务器上以 **root 权限**执行任意命令，随后植入 SSH 公钥持久化，并部署 systemd 挖矿木马（C2 外连）。

> 说明：本报告中的受害者服务器 IP、主机名、合法 SSH 密钥等信息已脱敏；攻击基础设施 IOC 保留以便追踪。

## 影响

- **以 root 权限执行任意命令**（qwenpaw 服务配置为 `User=root`）
- 攻击者植入 SSH 公钥后可长期直接登录 root
- 持久化木马占用 CPU 200%+（2 核机器满载），并连接 C2 端口 7777/4444
- 从首次利用到被发现，攻击者在服务器上存活约 **17 天**

## 攻击链与时间线

| 时间 | 事件 |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-22 03:21 | 攻击者通过 qwenpaw 创建 MCP Driver `rce-poc-d2031bc5`，在服务器写入探测文件 `/tmp/.qp_rce_d2031bc5` |
| 2026-09-22 03:31 | 第二次利用：`rce-poc-d7c4a01d` |
| 2026-09-25 05:39 | 利用 `rce-poc-9fca6523` 执行命令，输出 `uid=0(root)` + `PLANTED`，**向 `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` 追加 20 行攻击者公钥** |
| 2026-09-25 05:40 | 攻击者用该密钥从 `176.65.149.237` 公钥登录 root（SSH 日志实锤） |
| 2026-10-06 05:34 | 部署持久化：`/etc/systemd/system/worker.service`（`Nice=-20`、`Restart=always`）+ 木马二进制 `/usr/lib/.s90a96339/worker`，同批落盘第二目录 `/usr/lib/.s6880ae36/` |
| 2026-10-08 16:44 | 木马进程链启动，CPU 100% 满载，外连 C2 `176.65.149.237:7777` / `:4444` |
| 2026-10-09 | 定位、取证并完成清理 |

## 关键证据（已脱敏）

### 1. qwenpaw 日志：MCP Driver 被用于 RCE

```
2026-09-25 05:39:33 | ERROR | ...mcp_stateful_client.py | Error in MCP client lifecycle for rce-poc-9fca6523 ...
2026-09-25 05:40:03 | INFO  | ...driver_config_service.py | Driver 'rce-poc-9fca6523' saved but not active yet:
2026-09-25 05:40:06 | INFO  | ...driver_config_watcher.py | Driver 'rce-poc-9fca6523' removed after card deletion
```

残留文件 `/tmp/.qp_rce_9fca6523` 内容（同一时刻落盘）：

```
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
PLANTED
LISTEN 0      128          0.0.0.0:22         0.0.0.0:*
```

其他残留（侦察输出）：

```
/tmp/.qp_rce_0c03517e → NET: -1 Mbps | CPU: 2 cores, AMD EPYC 7K62 | RAM: 1.9 GiB
/tmp/.qp_rce_d2031bc5 → NotDocker
```

### 2. SSH 日志：攻击者密钥登录实锤

```
2026-09-25T05:40:08+08:00 sshd: Accepted publickey for root from 176.65.149.237
    port 56962 ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:iV0yATXmWTilb70mKxz+G9i1TlSd3pcqNLISwLcVgi0
```

`/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` 修改时间 = 2026-09-25 05:39，其中连续 20 行为同一把密钥（指纹与上述登录指纹一致，comment 为 `dpsk`）。同期 SSH 日志中**没有任何其他成功登录**，排除爆破途径。

### 3. systemd 持久化（恶意服务原文）

```ini
[Unit]
Description=worker
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/lib/.s90a96339/worker
Restart=always
RestartSec=3
Nice=-20

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

### 4. 木马行为特征

- 进程链：`systemd worker.service` → 4 层同二进制进程，进程名伪装（`WittyGrove` / `HumbleGrove` / `PolarLaurel` / `worke`）
- 二进制路径：`/usr/lib/.s90a96339/worker`（8.5MB，隐藏随机目录）
- C2：`176.65.149.237` 的 7777、4444 端口（TCP ESTAB）
- 拒绝 SIGTERM，需 SIGKILL；`S<l`（高优先级 + 锁内存）
- CPU 占用 ~191%（2 核机器），load average 峰值 9+

## IOC

| 类型 | 值 |
|---|---|
| C2 IP | `176.65.149.237`（端口 7777、4444；SSH 来源） |
| 攻击者 SSH 公钥指纹 | `SHA256:iV0yATXmWTilb70mKxz+G9i1TlSd3pcqNLISwLcVgi0` |
| 恶意服务 | `/etc/systemd/system/worker.service` |
| 恶意路径 | `/usr/lib/.s90a96339/`、`/usr/lib/.s6880ae36/` |
| RCE 残留 | `/tmp/.qp_rce_*`、Driver 名 `rce-poc-*` |
| 首次利用时间 | 2026-09-22 03:21 (+08:00) |

## 复现条件（推断）

- qwenpaw 以 root 运行，且服务参数 `--host 0.0.0.0` 对外暴露（本次配置中 config.json 写的是 `127.0.0.1:8088`，但 systemd unit 的 `ExecStart` 显式传了 `--host 0.0.0.0`）
- 攻击者能通过 Driver 配置接口注册 MCP Driver，并使其在服务端执行命令/写文件

## 修复建议

1. **审计 Driver 配置接口的鉴权**：创建/更新 MCP Driver 必须强认证，禁止未授权访问
2. **最小权限运行**：不要以 root 运行服务；建议专用低权限用户 + 能力限制
3. **默认仅监听 127.0.0.1**，对外暴露需显式配置
4. **Driver 名称与命令执行审计**：拦截 `rce-poc` 类异常命名，记录 Driver 创建的来源 IP 与操作者
5. **文件写入限制**：服务进程不应能写 `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`、`/etc/systemd/system/` 等敏感路径

## 时间线（披露）

- 2026-10-09：事件取证完成、恶意载荷清理完成，提交本报告
- 受害服务器已完成清理（进程、木马、恶意密钥），证据备份保留在服务器本地

如需原始证据（完整日志、样本哈希），请回复，可通过安全渠道提供。

issues.title: docs(heartbeat): document silence semantics, concurrency, and the AGENTS.md heartbeat section

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
The heartbeat page currently documents *configuration* well (enabled/every/target/timeout/activeHours) but leaves out the *runtime semantics* users actually hit when they enable it. Verified against the current source (anchors in footnotes), the following five behaviors are undocumented and cause predictable confusion:

### 1. There is no built-in "silence protocol" — what happens when there is nothing to do

The most-asked implicit question ("how do I keep it quiet when there's nothing to report?") has no documented answer. Reality:

- `target=main` (default): the run's output is **consumed, not delivered** — silence is a side effect of non-delivery. The output still persists into the `"main"` session history.[^1]
- `target=last`: **every** event of the run is streamed to the last real channel — there is no "nothing to report" filter; staying quiet is the model's job, guided only by what you write in HEARTBEAT.md.[^2]
- `target=inbox`: a summary event is written to the agent inbox (`heartbeat_result`, or `heartbeat_timeout` / `heartbeat_error` on timeout/failure) — no channel delivery.[^3]
- Missing or empty HEARTBEAT.md, or current time outside `activeHours` → the tick is **skipped silently** (debug log only).[^4]

### 2. Concurrency semantics

- Ticks overlapping ticks: the scheduler job uses the APScheduler 3.x default `max_instances=1`, so a firing due while the previous tick is still running is **skipped, not queued**; `misfire_grace_time` is 60s.[^5]
- Ticks vs. user turns: the heartbeat path bypasses the channel per-session queue and the cron concurrency semaphore. Ticks always use session `"main"` while channel turns use per-peer session ids, so they normally touch disjoint state. If a turn is in flight on the same `"main"` session (possible via the console API, which accepts an explicit session id), both runs proceed **concurrently and session save is last-write-wins** — there is no lock on session load/save.[^6]

### 3. Why the agent does not react to its own messages

Every channel's inbound entry point drops events whose sender is the agent's own account before any other processing (for Matrix: the early "skip own messages" check in the room text/media handlers, comparing `event.sender` against the agent's MXID). This is what prevents a heartbeat → reply → room-echo feedback loop, and it is a per-channel convention (same pattern in the other bundled channels).[^7]

### 4. HEARTBEAT.md vs. the `AGENTS.md` heartbeat section — two different prompt-level mechanisms

- `HEARTBEAT.md` (per tick): the **entire file** (trimmed) becomes one **user-role** message on the `"main"` session — no system message, no wrapping template, no parsing of internal structure. The turn is tagged `request_context.source = "heartbeat"`, which downstream hooks use to skip auto-memory search for heartbeat turns.[^8]
- `AGENTS.md` section `<!-- heartbeat:start -->...<!-- heartbeat:end -->` (system prompt, every turn): explains the *mechanism* to the model. It is **stripped from the prompt entirely when heartbeat is disabled** and kept (markers removed) when enabled — so a disabled agent never sees heartbeat instructions, and a HEARTBEAT.md written "for the model" without that section has no mechanism explanation at all.[^9]

### 5. Config change takes effect on reload, without restart

The current page hedges ("settings apply as implemented; some setups may need a restart"). Verified: changing any heartbeat field triggers an **in-place job reschedule** (remove + re-add) on config reload — no restart needed.[^10]

### Proposed page additions (ready to paste)

The sections above, tightened, can be appended to the existing page under a new `## Runtime semantics` heading (before `## Heartbeat vs cron jobs`); the field table row for `every` can additionally note "invalid or empty values fall back to a 30-minute interval".[^\*] A one-line disambiguation box is also worth adding, since "heartbeat" names five unrelated mechanisms in the codebase (agent self-wake; SSE idle keep-alive at 25s; tool-approval keep-alive at 15s; a per-channel WebSocket ping at 30s; and the cron event-loop watchdog at 60s) — the agent self-wake heartbeat is the one this page documents.

[^1]: `app/crons/heartbeat.py` delivery branch per `target` — `main` consumes without send.
[^2]: same, `last` branch streams all run events.
[^3]: same, `inbox` branch writes summary/timeout/error events.
[^4]: skip paths: missing/empty file and activeHours window check.
[^5]: `app/crons/manager.py` job registration (`id="_heartbeat"`, `misfire_grace_time=60`, default max_instances).
[^6]: session load/save has no lock; heartbeat path bypasses channel queue and cron semaphore.
[^7]: `app/channels/matrix/channel.py` early own-sender drop at the top of the room event handlers.
[^8]: heartbeat query construction + `request_context.source` tagging.
[^9]: AGENTS.md section processing: strip-when-disabled / keep-without-markers-when-enabled.
[^10]: `app/crons/manager.py` `reschedule_heartbeat()` (remove_job + add_job in place).
[^\*]: `app/crons/heartbeat.py` `parse_heartbeat_every` fallback to 30 minutes on empty/invalid/≤0.

---


现有 heartbeat 文档把**配置**写清楚了，但漏了启用后用户真正会撞到的**运行语义**（以下均对照代码逐点核验）：

1. **没有内置"静默协议"**：`target=main` 的"安静"是**不投递的副作用**（输出仍留在 "main" 会话历史）；`target=last` **不过滤**"无事汇报"——保持安静只能靠你在 HEARTBEAT.md 里写的 checklist 引导模型；HEARTBEAT.md 缺失/为空或不在 activeHours 内 → tick **静默跳过**。
2. **并发语义**：tick 重叠时按 APScheduler 3.x 默认 `max_instances=1` **跳过不排队**（misfire 宽限 60s）；tick 与用户 turn 同处 "main" 会话（console API 可显式传 session id）时**并发执行、会话保存 last-write-wins**（session load/save 无锁）。
3. **agent 不响应自己的消息**：每个 channel 入站入口先丢弃自己账号发的消息（Matrix 在房间事件处理器开头比对 sender 与 agent MXID）——这是防 heartbeat→reply→房间回声反馈环的机制，属各 channel 约定。
4. **HEARTBEAT.md 与 AGENTS.md 心跳段是两回事**：前者整文件 = 每次 tick 的一条 **user 消息**（无模板无解析，turn 带 `request_context.source="heartbeat"` 标记，下游 hook 据此跳过自动记忆检索）；后者是每轮 system prompt 里的机制说明——**heartbeat 关闭时该段整个从 prompt 剥掉**。
5. **改配置免重启**：改任一 heartbeat 字段在 config reload 时**原位重排 job**（先 remove 再 add），无需重启（现有文档的"some setups may need a restart"措辞可精确化）。

建议以 `## Runtime semantics` 新节追加到现有页（`## Heartbeat vs cron jobs` 之前），另加一行**消歧框**：代码里"heartbeat"指 5 种互不相关机制（agent 自唤醒 / SSE 空闲保活 25s / 工具审批保活 15s / 渠道 WS ping 30s / cron 事件循环看门狗 60s），本文档只讲第一种。

prs.title: docs: add --agent-id targeting guide to CLI docs (#7047)
prs.body:
## Description

The CLI documentation lacks a dedicated guide to `--agent-id`, and several sections incorrectly say that every command accepts it. This adds matching English and Chinese guides, with examples for targeting an existing agent's cron jobs and chats, and accurate per-section notes.

The guide now distinguishes the current CLI's exceptions:

- `daemon logs` reads the shared log and has no `--agent-id` option.
- `channels send` requires an explicit agent ID; `channels list` and `config` default to `default`.
- `skills install` / `uninstall` operate on the shared skill pool when neither scope option is supplied. `--pool` and `--agent-id` are mutually exclusive.
- `agents create --agent-id` names a new agent. For `agents chat`, the option aliases `--from-agent`; `--to-agent` selects the recipient.

Merged current `main` while preserving the newer Skills command table and examples. The final diff changes only `website/public/docs/cli.en.md` and `website/public/docs/cli.zh.md`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7047

**Security Considerations:** Documentation only; no runtime behavior changes.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] Command coverage and defaults verified against current CLI source
- [x] English and Chinese content kept in sync
- [x] Website TypeScript and formatting checks pass
- [x] Website production build passes
- [x] Ready for review

prs.title: fix(console): recover from transient DOM-mutation render errors
prs.body:
## Description

The console can get stuck on the generic error fallback **forever** on a route whose render throws a DOM-mutation error, because `ChunkErrorBoundary` only clears its error state when `resetKey` changes — that is, on navigation.

Reported in #7888. On the affected machine, opening any chat route replaces the content area with "Something went wrong" while the sidebar keeps working, and neither the reload button nor F5 recovers it:

```
NotFoundError: Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node':
The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.
    at commitPlacement (react-vendor-*.js:40:25719)
    ...
Render error: NotFoundError ... (componentStack: ... ChunkErrorBoundary ...)
```

React raises this when a third party mutated the real DOM behind its back. We captured the injector with a diagnostic wrap on `Node.prototype.insertBefore`:

```
parent:    BUTTON.qwenpaw-dropdown-trigger.ApprovalToggle-module__trigger__*
refNode:   #text
refParent: FONT.
```

`<font>` is not an element React renders — a browser UI layer (appearance / translation / read-aloud style) wrapped a React-managed text node in it, in the same frame, next to the chat page's tool-approval toggle. The chat page is the exposed route because that toggle is the node being wrapped; other pages have no such node.

Reproducibility notes: reproduces with a real Edge profile, does not reproduce with a fresh `--user-data-dir`. Cache, storage, extensions and viewport size were all ruled out; the trigger lives in a multi-key combination inside the browser's `Preferences`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7888 (relates to #7815, same `resetKey`-only recovery defect)

**Security Considerations:** None. The change touches only DOM APIs in the renderer; no auth, network, or env/config handling is involved.

### Changes

Two orthogonal changes.

**1. `utils/domInsertTolerance.ts` — tolerate mutations performed behind React's back**

Wraps `Node.prototype.insertBefore` / `Node.prototype.removeChild` so a call that would have thrown is degraded instead:

- reference node detached → append the node anyway (position lost once, the next commit re-orders correctly);
- reference node under a different parent → skip this insertion and let the commit proceed;
- `removeChild` on a node owned by another parent → report success.

The call site is React's commit phase, which reconciles on the next render, so swallowing one mis-positioned insertion is safe and strictly better than failing the whole commit and blowing away the route. Valid calls are forwarded untouched, and it is installed from `main.tsx` before `createRoot` runs.

**2. `ChunkErrorBoundary` — recover in place, and stop getting stuck**

- Classifies DOM-mutation errors (`NotFoundError`, `HierarchyRequestError`, and the matching messages) and offers a **Try again** button that re-renders the same subtree, instead of forcing a full page reload for a transient race.
- Caps retries (`MAX_RENDER_ERROR_RETRIES = 2`) so a page that keeps failing falls back to the reload button.
- `retryCount` is intentionally preserved across `getDerivedStateFromError` for the same reason.
- Chunk-load errors are unchanged: they still get the targeted message and no in-place retry, since a re-render cannot fix a missing chunk.

The classification lives in `getDerivedStateFromError` rather than a field set by `componentDidCatch`, because the latter runs *after* the fallback has already rendered — a field set there is invisible to the first fallback render.

New i18n key `chunkError.retry` added across all seven locale files (en, zh, ja, ru, vi, id, pt-BR).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

## Testing

```bash

# types
node_modules/.bin/tsc -b --noEmit

# lint

# formatting

# new tests
node --max-old-space-size=4096 ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx \
  src/utils/domInsertTolerance.test.ts
```

## Evidence

All checks below were run on the commit in this PR (`08e069c`), inside `console/`, after `npm ci`. Raw output is quoted verbatim.

### Vitest — new tests

```
 ✓ src/utils/domInsertTolerance.test.ts (5 tests) 12ms
 ✓ src/components/ChunkErrorBoundary.test.tsx (5 tests) 678ms
     ✓ offers Hub users a runtime restart when a page fails  438ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
   Duration  6.71s
```

Covers: guard forwards valid `insertBefore`; guard appends when the reference node is detached; guard skips when the reference node belongs to another parent; guard tolerates `removeChild` across parents; guard is idempotent. Boundary recovers in place from a DOM-mutation error; boundary drops the retry button once retries are exhausted; boundary offers no in-place retry for a chunk-load error.

### tsc / eslint / prettier

```
$ node_modules/.bin/tsc -b --noEmit
tsc exit=0

$ node_modules/.bin/eslint <changed files>
eslint exit=0

$ node_modules/.bin/prettier --check <changed files>
Checking formatting...
All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

### Real-world reproduction — before / after

Measured on the reporter's deployment (NAS Docker, Edge 153, real user profile), driving the page over CDP. An equivalent guard was injected into `index.html` to prove the approach before writing this source-level patch:

| Scenario | Fallback page | Input box | Body text | Guard hits | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| New task `/chat` | no | yes | 11017 | 1 | pass |
| History session `3378972a` | no | yes | 11017 | 1 | pass |
| History session `244120ce` | no | yes | 11017 | 1 | pass |
| History session `36928ce5` | no | yes | 11017 | 1 | pass |
| Stress: rapid switching, 8 rounds | — | — | — | — | 0/8 failures |

Before the fix the page rendered 130 characters of body text (the fallback); after, 11017 (the full conversation). The guard hit exactly once per page load, matching the single injected `<font>` wrapper.

## Additional Notes

- The `<font>` wrapper itself is the browser's doing, so this patch does not try to prevent it — it makes React's commit phase resilient to it, and gives the boundary a way out if something still slips through.
- If you would prefer to keep `Node.prototype` untouched regardless of packaging, I am happy to split this into two commits so the boundary change can land independently; the guard is the part that actually stops the crash.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add clean unload and rollback-safe hot reload
prs.body:
## Description

Add a clean plugin unload path and rollback-safe hot reload so plugin install / update / uninstall no longer rebuilds every live workspace, and a failed update does not leave users on a half-applied new version.

This PR introduces a two-layer teardown ledger (`PluginInstance`) and a `PluginLifecycle` facade (`load` / `unload` / `reload` / `update_config`):

- Official `register_*` entries record real teardowns (HTTP, provider, control command, middleware, prompt section, channel, tools, hooks). Workspace contributions are projected and revoked by name via `WorkspaceProjector` (`start_one` / `stop_one` for channels). Uninstall no longer calls `_schedule_all_agents_reload`.
- Unload modes (`shutdown` / `unload` / `uninstall`) share one ledger. Author shutdown / uninstall hooks run before table rows are dropped. `shutdown` only stops hosted resources (`custody` / `effect`) and does not clear tables or disk.
- Reload probes new code into `plugin_<id>__probe` first; import failure does not tear down the old instance. Hosted resources that do not go quiescent abort the swap. Rollback restores the previous directory / modules and does not run legacy uninstall hooks. Boot recovers interrupted “updating” / “migrating” markers.
- `update_config` rebuilds contributions without reimporting; a half-successful `register()` is torn down before the old config is restored. Disable is `config.plugins[<id>].enabled = false` (reserved framework key).
- Boot dependency policy is local-only: missing deps mark the plugin `FAILED` without installing. Explicit install / update / `POST /plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies` still go through `DependencyGate` (imported host-package blacklist → require restart). Console repair / status UI is intentionally not wired.
- CloudPaw no longer monkeypatches `PluginLoader.unload_plugin`; agent cleanup is an `api.provision` teardown (uninstall only).
- `LifecycleDelegate` is the single predicate at the reserved branch points (`owns_commit` / `owns_dependency_env` / `notify_unload`). Name collisions fail loudly and name the occupant.

Out of scope (documented as deferred): `SourceWatcher`, dry-run / interval-intersection gate enhancements, and Console repair / last-unload UI.

**Security Considerations:** Dependency installation stays gated: boot never networks when deps are already satisfied; colliding with an already-imported host package (e.g. `httpx`) refuses the install and does not write site-packages. Unload / reload only revoke registrations owned by the plugin id; user `agent.json` / provisioned files are not deleted on `mode=unload`. Provision / directory swap are skipped when `owns_commit` is false.

prs.title: fix(hub): respect administrator token capability overrides
prs.body:
## Description

Hub model configuration auto-fills the provider's context window but can reject that same value as exceeding the effective input limit. A live DashScope discovery for `qwen3.8-max` and `qwen3.8-max-0902` returns a 1,000,000-token context window (`max_input_length_auto_detected`) and a separate 991,808-token input limit, which reduces `effective_max_input_length` to 991,808. Entering the automatically suggested context therefore fails frontend validation, regardless of whether the optional output field is blank or 131,072.

Treat model cards as defaults and reference information rather than hard limits on administrator configuration. Keep integer/minimum validation and remove the fixed API token ceilings as well, allow blank fields to use existing native defaults, and remove capability-derived maxima from the form and output input. Remove the equivalent catalog rejection on save. Apply explicit administrator context/output settings through the existing native model-card override fields so publication and gateway preparation preserve those settings, including self-hosted endpoints with larger capacities. Member authorization, configured organization/member budgets, and output reservations remain enforced.

This follows #8168, which fixed unresolved preset defaults but did not cover successful provider discovery with distinct context/input limits. No Research-specific code, new compatibility format, or test changes are included.

prs.title: fix(tools): resolve PEP 563 annotations before agentscope schema extraction (#7082)
prs.body:
## Closure note (2026-10-10)

Closed at the author's request after rechecking against current `main` (`7ec4df9c6d3ac88ba7d7291ca413ba2b8d2db07d`). Main now pins `agentscope[model-ollama]==2.0.9` following #8008. That version resolves plain-function type hints in the defining namespace with `typing.get_type_hints(..., include_extras=True)` before extracting the schema.

Verified with the real pinned dependency: a plain async tool with postponed `Optional[Path]` annotations builds a valid `FunctionTool` schema without this PR. The original regression test consequently fails its old expectation that registration must raise `PydanticUserError` before applying the helper (4 other unit tests pass).

A separate check found that `functools.partial` wrappers can still reach the raw-annotation fallback in 2.0.9. That compatibility enhancement is outside the retained scope of this PR and is not claimed to be solved by the dependency upgrade.

---

The original proposal and its historical evidence follow.
## Description

Starting the console (or any agent run) can abort during tool registration with:

```
pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `_StructuredOutputDynamicClass` is not fully
defined; you should define `Optional`, then call
`_StructuredOutputDynamicClass.model_rebuild()`.
```

**Root cause.** agentscope's `FunctionTool` derives each tool's JSON schema in [`agentscope/tool/_utils.py::_extract_input_schema`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/v2.0.6/src/agentscope/tool/_utils.py#L137-L155): it iterates `inspect.signature(func).parameters` and feeds `param.annotation` **verbatim** into `create_model("_StructuredOutputDynamicClass", ...)`, then calls `.model_json_schema()`.

Tool functions defined in modules that use `from __future__ import annotations` (PEP 563 — 548 modules under `src/` do) expose their annotations as *strings* at runtime, e.g. `"Optional[Path]"`. Pydantic treats each string as a forward reference and resolves it against the module that created the model — agentscope's `tool/_utils.py`, whose namespace only contains:

```python
import inspect
from typing import Any, Dict, Callable
from docstring_parser import parse
from pydantic import Field, create_model, ConfigDict
```

There is no `Optional` and no `Path` there, so the model stays "not fully defined" and `model_json_schema()` raises. In short: **the annotation string is written in QwenPaw's module but evaluated in agentscope's module.** The suggested `model_rebuild()` is unreachable from the QwenPaw side, and `agentscope==2.0.6` is a pinned third-party dependency.

This also explains why the failure looks intermittent — it depends on whether a registered tool happens to use a name that is *not* resolvable in agentscope's namespace:

| Parameter annotation | String under PEP 563 | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `code: str`, `n: int` | `"str"`, `"int"` | OK — builtins resolve anywhere |
| `d: Dict[str, Any]` | `"Dict[str, Any]"` | OK — only because agentscope imports `Dict`/`Any` |
| `p: Optional[Path]` | `"Optional[Path]"` | **fails** |
| `x: MyCustomType` | `"MyCustomType"` | **fails** |

**Fix.** Resolve stringified annotations to real type objects in the function's *own* module namespace (via `typing.get_type_hints`, which evaluates against `func.__globals__` where `Optional`/`Path` are imported) **before** agentscope introspects the function. agentscope then receives concrete types and Pydantic never creates an unresolved forward reference.

New helper `qwenpaw/utils/tool_annotations.py::resolve_tool_annotations`:
- Unwraps `functools.partial` / decorators so it mutates the same object agentscope inspects (agentscope uses `inspect.signature(...)` with the default `follow_wrapped=True`).
- Idempotent — after the first pass the annotations are no longer strings, so repeat registration is a no-op.
- No-op for unannotated functions and for already-concrete annotations.
- On `get_type_hints` failure it returns **before** writing anything, so annotations are never left partially resolved (behaviour is no worse than before the fix).
- Assigns a freshly merged dict in a single rebind, so readers never observe a half-updated mapping.

Wired into the three places that hand a tool function to agentscope's `FunctionTool`:

| Location | Path |
|---|---|
| `governance/tool_adapter.py::_policy_tool_init` | `PolicyGuardedTool` — main path for every workspace tool |
| `runtime/tool_guard.py::_guarded_tool_init` | `GuardedFunctionTool` — degraded-governance fallback |
| `agents/memory/proactive/proactive_responder.py` | direct `FunctionTool(...)`, which bypasses both wrappers |

The third site is hardening: it wires `browser`, which *is* a PEP 563 module, and is safe today only because its sole parameter is `code: str` (a builtin). Adding any `Optional[...]` parameter there would reintroduce this bug, so it now goes through the same helper.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7082

**Security Considerations:** None. No change to permissions, sandboxing, or governance decisions — only type-annotation normalisation for schema generation. Guard/policy behaviour is untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran tests locally and they pass (see Evidence for scope and limitations)
- [x] Verified against the pinned dependency version (`agentscope==2.0.6`)
- [x] No new lint violations (`max-line-length = 79` respected in all touched files)
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

New unit test module `tests/unit/utils/test_tool_annotations.py`:

1. `test_resolves_pep563_optional_annotations` — asserts annotations start as strings and become `Optional[Path]` / `Optional[int]` / `str`.
2. `test_noop_when_function_has_no_annotations`
3. `test_noop_when_annotations_already_concrete`
4. `test_unresolvable_string_annotation_is_left_untouched`
5. `test_agentscope_functiontool_builds_after_resolve` — end-to-end regression: `FunctionTool(tool)` raises `PydanticUserError` matching `"not fully defined"` **before** the fix, and builds a valid `input_schema` **after** it.

Manual check of the produced schema after resolution:

```json
"file_path": {"anyOf": [{"format": "path", "type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}
```

## Evidence

Verified against the pinned dependency in an isolated Python 3.11 venv with real `agentscope==2.0.6` (not mocked).

**1. Reproduced the exact reported failure**, then confirmed the fix, on a tool module using `from __future__ import annotations` + `Optional[Path]`:

```
raw __annotations__ (PEP 563 -> strings):
  {'operation': 'str', 'file_path': 'Optional[Path]', 'count': 'Optional[int]'}

--- BEFORE FIX ---
error type   : PydanticUserError
error message: `_StructuredOutputDynamicClass` is not fully defined; you should
               define `Optional`, then call
               `_StructuredOutputDynamicClass.model_rebuild()`.

resolved __annotations__:
  {'operation': <class 'str'>, 'file_path': typing.Optional[pathlib.Path],
   'count': typing.Optional[int]}

--- AFTER FIX ---
FunctionTool built OK; name = demo_tool
input_schema = {"properties": {"operation": {"description": "op.", "type":
  "string"}, "file_path": {"anyOf": [{"format": "path", "type": "string"},
  {"type": "null"}], "default": null, ...}, "count": {"anyOf": [{"type":
  "integer"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null, ...}},
  "required": ["operation"], "type": "object"}
```

**2. Unit tests — 5/5 pass** against real agentscope 2.0.6:

```
PASS: test_agentscope_functiontool_builds_after_resolve
PASS: test_noop_when_annotations_already_concrete
PASS: test_noop_when_function_has_no_annotations
PASS: test_resolves_pep563_optional_annotations
PASS: test_unresolvable_string_annotation_is_left_untouched
5/5 passed
```

Because test 5 asserts the narrow `pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError` type (not a bare `Exception`), its passing also confirms the precise exception class reported in the issue.

**3. Lint / syntax**

```
$ python -m py_compile <all 5 touched files>        -> OK

$ character-accurate check for lines > 79 chars
  (.flake8 max-line-length = 79) across all 5 files -> violations: 0
```

prs.title: docs(heartbeat): document runtime semantics of silence, concurrency, and reloads
prs.body:
## Description

Docs-only change to `website/public/docs/heartbeat.en.md` and `heartbeat.zh.md`.
The heartbeat page documents how to *configure* heartbeat but not the runtime
behavior users hit after enabling it. This adds a `## Runtime semantics` section
(before `## Heartbeat vs cron jobs`) covering the five behaviors from the issue,
and corrects two stale sentences.

What the new section documents:

- **Nothing to report is not filtered** — `main` (default) runs but never
  delivers; `last` streams every event (staying quiet is the model's job);
  `inbox` writes one entry (`heartbeat_result` / `heartbeat_timeout` /
  `heartbeat_error`). A tick is skipped silently when outside `activeHours`, or
  when HEARTBEAT.md is missing/empty; `last` with no recorded dispatch degrades
  to a run without delivery.
- **Overlapping runs** — the job leaves the APScheduler default
  `max_instances=1`, so an overlapping tick is **skipped, not queued**
  (`misfire_grace_time` 60s); ticks bypass the channel queue and the cron
  per-job concurrency limit and always use session `main`; concurrent runs on
  `main` are not serialized *with each other* and the later session save wins.
- **Own-message drop** — many bundled channels drop inbound events from the
  agent's own account (Matrix compares `event.sender` to the agent's user id;
  DingTalk skips `is_bot` messages; Mattermost compares the sender to the bot
  id). Not every channel does this.
- **HEARTBEAT.md vs the AGENTS.md heartbeat section** — HEARTBEAT.md is read per
  tick and becomes one user message tagged `request_context.source="heartbeat"`
  (which also skips auto-memory search); the `<!-- heartbeat:start/end -->`
  AGENTS.md section is kept without markers when heartbeat is on and stripped
  entirely when off.
- **Config changes apply without a restart** — a Console save reschedules the
  job; a direct `agent.json` edit is picked up by the config watcher (~2s) and
  re-registers it.

Also: notes the 30-minute fallback when `every` is present but
empty/unparsable/non-positive, and replaces the hedged "some setups may need a
restart" sentence.

One factual correction to the issue's own analysis: session load/save is not
lock-free — `save_session_state` is guarded by a per-path lock
(`src/qwenpaw/app/chats/session.py`). The real caveat is that concurrent runs on
the same session are not serialized *with each other* (last-write-wins), which
is what the new text says.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8082

**Security Considerations:** None — documentation only.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under
my direction and review.

Hub model configuration can reject a valid context window while provider discovery is pending or fails. Preset `ModelInfo` entries carry an unresolved `effective_max_input_length` default of 131,072, which currently takes precedence over the native token-defaults response. For example, the DashScope `qwen3.8-max` card resolves to 1,000,000 tokens, but entering that value triggers the generic missing-token/capability error.

Use the effective context limit only when the model card has a resolved, non-default source. Otherwise retain API-detected limits or the existing native token-defaults response. Output limits remain optional, and known model capability bounds remain enforced. When the context field is cleared, validate against the existing native default and omit the empty field on submission so the backend resolves its provider default. prs.title: fix(creator): keep review decisions publishable on long Windows paths
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows with a long runtime data root, deciding any Review in the `qwenpaw-creator` plugin fails permanently, and the first failed attempt makes it unrecoverable (report: #8163).

Two defects combine:

1. **The journal publish needs a longer path than the journal itself.** `runtime_files/atomic_store.py` staged every write as `.<name>.<8 random>.tmp`, about 14 characters longer than the target record. With Windows long paths disabled, a `journal.json` whose final path fits under the legacy `MAX_PATH` limit still failed in `mkstemp` (259 -> 273 characters) and left the `decision-<hash>` directory created just before it behind, empty.
2. **That empty leftover then blocks every retry.** `project_files/review.py::_assert_no_other_active_decision` read each other `decision-*` directory with `read()` instead of `read_or_none()`, so a directory without a `journal.json` raised `ReviewDecisionConflict` ("Review decision journal set is inconsistent"). Each attempt uses a new `decisionId`, so the stale directory always counted as "another" decision and the API returned a retryable 409 that could never succeed.

The fix:

- Stage the temp file with a short, fixed 12-character name (`.tmp` plus the 8-character random suffix) so the decision journal's staged path no longer exceeds its target (273 -> 259 characters).
- Treat a `decision-*` directory with no `journal.json` as the leftover of an unpublished attempt: log and skip it instead of failing. A journal that exists but cannot be read still fails closed, and a non-finalized active journal still blocks a concurrent decision.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8163

**Security Considerations:** None. This is local storage path-length handling; no auth, config or network surface is touched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

Every pre-commit hook passes on the files this PR changes, and the CI `Pre-commit` job (`pre-commit run --all-files` on Linux) is green on this branch. A local Windows `--all-files` run splits the file list into batches and surfaces extra `mypy`/`pylint` messages in files this PR does not touch; those do not reproduce under the CI job.

## Testing

From `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend`:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py::test_staged_temp_path_is_never_longer_than_its_target \
  tests/project_files/test_file_review.py::test_decision_ignores_leftover_directory_without_journal \
  tests/project_files/test_file_review.py::test_decision_still_rejects_unreadable_existing_journal -v
```

To exercise the second defect directly: create `reviews/<review-id>/decision-transactions/decision-<hash>/` with no `journal.json` and call `_decide`. Before this change it raises `ReviewDecisionConflict`; after it the decision succeeds and the leftover directory is ignored.

## Evidence

**Before** - clean `upstream/main` (`fb308f57`) with only the new test files added, sources unmodified:

```
FAILED tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py::test_staged_temp_path_is_never_longer_than_its_target
FAILED tests/project_files/test_file_review.py::test_decision_ignores_leftover_directory_without_journal
========================= 2 failed, 1 passed in 4.42s =========================
```

The first failure is the staged-path length (the old `.<name>.<8 random>.tmp` name made it 101 chars against an 87-char target); the second is the leftover-directory guard:

```
E  services.project_files.review.ReviewDecisionConflict: Review decision journal set is inconsistent
services\project_files\review.py:1201: ReviewDecisionConflict
```

**After** - this branch:

```
tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py::test_staged_temp_path_is_never_longer_than_its_target PASSED
tests/project_files/test_file_review.py::test_decision_ignores_leftover_directory_without_journal PASSED
tests/project_files/test_file_review.py::test_decision_still_rejects_unreadable_existing_journal PASSED
============================== 3 passed in 5.45s ==============================
```

**Broader subsystems** (the two test files this PR touches):

```
1 failed, 50 passed in 30.34s
FAILED tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py::test_hammering_readers_never_starve_or_slow_a_writer
```

That single failure is a pre-existing Windows file-locking flake (`PermissionError` on file rotation during a threaded read/write stress test); it fails identically on a clean `upstream/main` checkout with none of this PR applied:

```
FAILED tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py::test_hammering_readers_never_starve_or_slow_a_writer
============================= 1 failed in 14.36s =============================
```

**pre-commit on the files changed by this PR** (all hooks pass):

```
check python ast.........................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed
```

**CI on this branch**: `Creator Backend Tests` pass, `Real behavior proof` pass, `Pre-commit` pass, `Creator UI Build & Tests` pass.

## Additional Notes

Files changed:

- `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/runtime_files/atomic_store.py`
- `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/services/project_files/review.py`
- `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/runtime_files/test_storage_primitives.py`
- `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/project_files/test_file_review.py`

Known limitations / possible follow-ups (not addressed here):

- Leftover journal-less `decision-*` directories are ignored by the decision guard but never removed, and `ProjectReviewService._discover_decision_journals` still reads them with `read()` and reports them as `INTEGRITY_ERROR` outcomes at startup. Decisions now work regardless, but recovery output stays inconsistent with the new "ignore" semantics until that path is aligned or the directories are collected.
- The staged name is now a fixed 12 characters, so record names shorter than 12 characters (e.g. `base.json`, `spec.json`) still pay a small 0-3 character overhead over their target. The reported record (`journal.json`, 12 characters) is the one that mattered; a fully general bound would need the extended-length `\\?\` prefix or a target-derived name.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.

Note: #8163 is currently assigned to @xuanrui-L. Opening this in case the fix is useful - please close it if you would rather handle the issue directly.

prs.title: fix(providers): recover Responses output sent only on the terminal event
prs.body:
## Description

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8162

Some Responses API providers do not emit content deltas
(`response.output_text.delta` / `response.function_call_arguments.delta`) and
send the whole `response.output` only in the terminal `response.completed`
event. AgentScope's stream parser reads assistant text and tool calls from
deltas only, so such a turn came back as an empty assistant message and any
tool call in it was dropped.

`OpenAIResponseModelCompat` now watches the event stream: when the stream
produced no content delta, it holds the terminal event back and rebuilds the
reply with the existing non-streaming parser, which already handles text, tool
calls, reasoning metadata and usage in `response.output` order. Providers that
stream deltas take the original path unchanged.

Limits of this change:

- Recovery only triggers when *no* content delta arrived at all. A provider that
  streams some deltas and keeps the rest in the terminal event is not covered;
  merging a partial stream with the terminal output is a larger change and is
  not attempted here.
- Only `response.completed` is treated as a terminal event, matching the
  AgentScope parser. A stream that ends with `response.incomplete` (for example
  `max_output_tokens` truncation) is unchanged.
- I could not reproduce the reporter's provider/base_url, so this addresses the
  parser-level gap rather than a specific gateway. The maintainer questions on
  the issue still stand.

**Security Considerations:** none - no auth, config or network change.

- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)

Notes: pre-commit and pytest were run on the changed files and the affected test
trees (see Evidence); no auto-fixes were needed and no hooks were skipped. The
`--all-files` result quoted below was captured on the same checkout before the
last two-line edit; the final head was re-checked with `--files`.

## Testing

1. `pytest tests/unit/providers/test_openai_response_stream_recovery.py -q` feeds
   synthetic Responses API event streams (both shapes) through
   `OpenAIResponseModelCompat` and asserts the parsed reply.
2. Manual check: use a Responses API provider whose gateway only fills

issues.title: [Bug]: Web chat input doesn't regain focus after a reply finishes
issues.body:
### Affected component

web dashboard

### Severity

S3 - minor issue

### Current behavior

In an agent chat in the web dashboard, the message box loses focus while the agent replies and does not get it back when the reply finishes, so continuing the conversation needs a click on the box. Pressing Tab reaches it only after cycling through the other controls on the page (more than ten presses).

In `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx`, `handleSend` focuses the textarea, but the textarea is then disabled for the whole turn (`disabled={!connected || typing || !hydrated}`), which drops its focus. Nothing re-focuses it when `typing` returns to false; the only other `focus()` calls are after an image upload and after choosing a slash command.

This started with #6220 (first released in v0.7.5), which added the input lock during a turn. Before that, the textarea stayed enabled and kept the focus `handleSend` gave it.

### Expected behavior

When a turn ends (a completed reply, an error, or the Stop button), focus returns to the message box of the visible chat, so the user can keep typing. It should not take focus from a control the user deliberately moved to during the turn (another chat tab, the model picker, a dialog), so it should only re-focus when nothing else has focus (the document body). Chat tabs that are open but hidden keep running turns, so a turn ending in a hidden tab should not move focus.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Open the gateway web dashboard and an agent chat (seen in Firefox).
# 2. Type a message and press Enter.
# 3. Wait for the reply to finish.
# 4. Start typing: nothing goes into the message box until it is clicked.
```

### Impact

Affected users: everyone using the web dashboard chat.
Frequency: every turn.
Consequence: an extra click before each follow-up message.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master d03325172

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux, Firefox (Chrome not tested)

### Regression?

Yes, it worked before

### Pre-flight checks

- [X] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Tracker kind
roadmap / epic tracker

### Purpose
Live snapshot: 2026-08-29. Current named open items: 7 total, 4 issues and 3 pull requests.

This tracker coordinates a multi-PR rollout that brings ZeroClaw's persistent (cross-session) memory
subsystem to full parity with mature peer agent runtimes. A code-grounded audit (`crates/zeroclaw-memory` plus the runtime wiring, at `master`) found that ZeroClaw's memory **substrate and default-on loop are already
strong** - five durable backends behind one `Memory` trait, turn-end consolidation, agent-authored writes,
per-turn recall, hygiene, and a git-visible Core snapshot all ship on by default - but a cluster of
**already-built-but-unwired** modules leaves the curation, relevance, and observability surfaces below
their potential. The work is overwhelmingly *wiring tested code to seams that already exist* (a supersede
valve, an importance-weighted blend, a multi-stage retrieval pipeline, an audit decorator, a policy
enforcer), not greenfield. This tracker sequences that wiring as six coordinated epics so the shared
trait/store/event surfaces are each touched once, not per-feature.

### Scope and non-goals
**In scope (six epics, build order):**
- **A - Durable store: supersede / dedup / merge / budget / policy / kind schema** *(keystone; behaviour-neutral trait extension that every other epic builds on)*. Adds a `Memory::supersede` trait method (default no-op, mirroring the existing `store_with_metadata` idiom so all nine backends inherit a safe default), write-time dedup, fact-merge, a Core size budget with value-aware eviction, a `MemoryKind` field, and wires the existing policy enforcer. Closes the supersede/dedup/budget gaps.
- **B - Embeddings + retrieval + rerank (relevance plane)** *(keystone)*. Makes semantic recall default-viable, normalizes scoring, over-fetches -> blends -> re-sorts -> thresholds, lands a diversity (MMR) rerank behind the existing config knob, and routes recall through the existing multi-stage pipeline.
- **C - Memory types + knowledge-graph fusion + typed ingestion + cross-turn consolidation**. Adds a first-class memory-kind axis, fuses the knowledge graph into recall, resolves the procedural seam, lands typed multi-fact extraction, and adds a deferred cross-turn consolidation pass.
- **D - Context-injection assembler** - DELIVERED separately by #8619 (engine-level `memory_inject.rs` keyed on turn origin); no standalone epic-D PR. Remaining injection work (gated rerank/KG stages, pinned-first ordering, provenance annotation) rides the B/C child PRs.
- **E - Harden memory write/recall trust boundaries** *(safety hardening; lands before new default-on memory sources or destructive defaults are enabled)*.
- **F - Memory observability + operator surface**. Brings the audit trail live at the factory, completes the telemetry sinks, adds an introspection tool + health report + an operator CLI (`zeroclaw memory status|off|reset|reindex`) and a load-time config-honesty validator.

**Out of scope:**
- The two dimensions already at parity (multi-backend storage; default-on agent-authored writes).
- Model-weight / RL "memory" (continual fine-tuning) - a separate training-loop effort, not a memory-subsystem change.
- The self-improvement effort's non-memory epics (tracked separately); see Linked work for the co-owned planes.

### Linked work
- **Co-owned with the self-improvement effort (build once, both consume):** the durable-store + supersede trait (epic A), the embedding-provider wiring (epic B), the approval / policy plane (epic E), and the shared `ObserverEvent` enum + telemetry sinks (epic F). Coordinate so these are not built twice.
- **Merged baseline and first memory cohort:**
  - Epic A durable-store seam: **#8570 (MERGED)**
  - Injection unification, superseding epic D: **#8619 (MERGED)**
  - Baseline store-seam coverage: **#8892 (MERGED)**
  - Epic B relevance work: **#8895 (MERGED)**, **#8897 (MERGED)**, **#8898 (MERGED)**
  - Epic C typed classification/extraction: **#8900 (MERGED)**; C'2 knowledge-graph recall fusion remains future work.
  - Epic E boundary hardening: **#8984 (MERGED)**; later write approval and encryption-at-rest slices remain future work.
  - Epic F observability/config work: **#8893 (MERGED)** and **#8899 (MERGED)**; F4-6 status/health/CLI remain future work.
  - Architecture boundary record: **#9163 (MERGED)**.
- **Closed Hindsight stack:** #9063, #9064, #9065, #9066, #9067, #9068, and #9069 closed unmerged on 2026-08-29 after the stale-candidate deadline elapsed without a substantive author reply or pushed update. This retires those branches, not the underlying Hindsight/backend direction; any Hindsight work should come back as refreshed, smaller replacement work against current `master`, preserving the accepted memory-authority boundaries and resolving the prior review findings.
- **Open storage/enrichment path:** #9072 remains an open draft for separating authoritative storage from optional enrichment connectors. #9103 is revised but not accepted, so #9072's RFC-dependent storage/enrichment contract remains paused until the Lucid/Qdrant decision and the next Core vote complete.
- **Open defaults path:** #8995 remains an open draft and should stay last. It needs a defaults-values-only diff plus project-wide evidence for each opinionated default before it is counted as a ready cohort item.
- **Open consolidation/persona fix:** #9758 remains open with `needs-author-action`.
- **Closed superseded attempts:** #8992, #8993, and the closed #9063-#9069 Hindsight stack should not be revived as-is. Current work should use the accepted merged cohort, the open #9072/#8995/#9758 paths, or a refreshed replacement path.
- **Memory authority path:** #9048 is accepted for the conversation-history versus agent-curated-memory boundary. #6850 is in Core vote for the storage/lifecycle-policy boundary. #9103 is revised and still needs the bounded Lucid/Qdrant evidence and remove-versus-feature-gate decision before another Core vote.
- **Recorded decisions:** durable global memories (core/daily, session-unbound) must reach semantic recall in any session within the requester's identity scope - the B'3 fix; knowledge-graph recall fusion ships default-OFF until epic E lands; the earlier Dream Mode paths #5849 / #6693 / #7797 are closed, so cross-turn consolidation remains in this memory lane; `procedural_routing` config enum is removed (zero consumers).
- Design + plan dossiers: maintained in the author's planning notes; each child PR carries its own design summary and validation evidence.

### Routing evidence and next decision
- **Reason to stay open:** the first memory cohort has landed, but the tracker is still the live coordination surface for the storage/enrichment path, defaults path, consolidation/persona fix, possible refreshed Hindsight replacement work, and follow-up operability slices.
- **Next decision / revisit:** Finish the #9103 Lucid/Qdrant evidence review and #6850 vote, then revisit #9072 and #8995 against the accepted ordering instead of treating them as independent ready-to-merge work. If Hindsight returns, start from smaller refreshed slices rather than the closed #9063-#9069 branches.
- **Visible owner / cadence:** @Nillth; checklist updated as child PRs open/merge.

### Close criteria
Close when the remaining storage/enrichment, defaults, consolidation/persona, refreshed Hindsight if revived, and operability slices have either merged, been closed as superseded, or moved to focused successor trackers, and the per-dimension acceptance bars (supersede enforced on write, reranked top-k recall default-viable, one injection assembler, live audit trail plus operator CLI, write-path safety in place) are met under `cargo test` plus the engine-validation harness.

### Stale-exemption requested?
Yes - tracker itself is the active coordination surface
