prs.title: docs(security): correct sandbox backend auto-selection and fallbacks
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** `docs/book/src/security/sandboxing.md` said the Linux `auto` order was `Landlock (kernel 5.13+) → Bubblewrap → Firejail → Docker → none`. The selector doesn't do that. `detect_best_backend_with` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/detect.rs` tries Landlock only when the `sandbox-landlock` feature is compiled in, then Firejail, and never tries Bubblewrap on Linux. After the platform list it tries Docker only when the runtime kind is neither `native` nor `docker` (`auto_backend_compatible_with_runtime`), so the native runtime never falls back to Docker, and `runtime_fallback_backend` returns `none` when nothing is available, which builds a `NoopSandbox` and leaves application-layer security only. The page now states the real per-platform order, the feature gates, the Docker runtime-kind gate, and what naming a backend explicitly does.
- **Separate correction in the same PR:** the network section said sandboxed tools keep full egress and that "Bubblewrap and Firejail can block network when configured". Bubblewrap passes `--unshare-all` and never `--share-net`, so it blocks network unconditionally; Firejail passes `--noprofile` and no network flags, so it doesn't block it at all; Seatbelt denies outbound except DNS and localhost; the Docker sandbox always passes `--network none`. The section is now per backend, so a reader can tell which backends give them egress. I aligned the per-backend Bubblewrap and Firejail notes with the same facts, and dropped the `firejail_args` instruction there: `FirejailSandbox::new()` takes no arguments and nothing in the runtime applies the field, so the docs shouldn't tell users to rely on it. I also fixed the "Code reference" entry, which pointed at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/sandbox/`, a directory that doesn't exist, and the troubleshooting bullet, which quoted a `"Sandbox backend unavailable"` error no code emits and claimed the auto-detect logs which backends it tried. Selection logs the backend it settled on (`log_auto_backend_selection`) and warns with the name of an explicitly requested backend that isn't available (`log_requested_backend_unavailable`).
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only. No code or behavior change; backend selection on `master` is untouched, and #11559 is untouched.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime; two documentation pages change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11559. A maintainer asked for the selection-order correction in a review comment there; this PR doesn't close it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** (`N/A`; docs-only change with no runtime behavior to exercise)

### How I tested

Docs-only changes use markdown lint (`scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`) and added-link integrity (`scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`), plus the internal-link checker the `Docs Style` job runs.

For the selection order I read `detect_best_backend_with`, `configured_backend_selection_with`, `runtime_fallback_backend`, `sandbox_backend_available`, `landlock_available`, and `seatbelt_available` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/detect.rs` on `master`, and checked each row against the `cfg(target_os = ...)` branches and the `sandbox-landlock` / `sandbox-bubblewrap` feature gates. Platforms verified by reading the code: Linux (Landlock and Firejail branches), macOS (Bubblewrap and `sandbox-exec` branches), and Windows (no platform branch, so nothing before Docker). I did not run a live `auto` selection on any of the three platforms.

For the network section I read `wrap_invocation` in `security/bubblewrap.rs` (`--unshare-all`, and the tests assert `--share-net` is absent), `wrap_invocation` in `security/firejail.rs` (`--noprofile`, no network flags), `generate_policy` in `security/seatbelt.rs` (deny outbound, allow the mDNSResponder socket and localhost), the Docker sandbox command in `security/docker.rs` (`--network none`), and the Docker runtime in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/platform/docker.rs` with `default_docker_network` in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs` (`[runtime.docker].network`, default `none`). I also confirmed `FirejailSandbox::new()` takes no arguments and no production path reads `SandboxConfig::firejail_args`.

prs.title: fix(channels): honor Telegram 429 retry_after via shared per-token flood gate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a shared per-token flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`): every Bot API POST routes through it. Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open; Deliver calls (sendMessage, draft finalize, approvals) wait out `parameters.retry_after` up to a cap and retry once.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Preserves delivered-chunk progress: the existing `SendChunksError.delivered` resume contract is untouched, so a partial delivery still resumes without duplicates.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded).
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and any listener-side changes are explicitly out of scope (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send). No change to inbound/listener logic, other channels, or the agent loop. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per bot token the moment any call sees a 429. Cosmetic traffic (typing indicator, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window (bounded) and try again once, so replies are late instead of lost, and the token stops digging itself deeper.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting, blocked-window skipping, cross-chat window sharing); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-config
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test --test integration telegram_
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` shows 9 pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host + 3 `anyhow::anyhow` in Windows-only service code); none originate from this change. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` → `test result: ok. 1966 passed; 0 failed` (12 new tests: 8 unit in `telegram_rate_limit.rs`, 4 integration in telegram tests); `cargo test --test integration telegram_` → `10 passed; 0 failed`; `zeroclaw-config` targeted `telegram_config` suites pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Ran the build as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h after deploying the identical change: 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events (every prior incident lost replies), every turn after a 429 delivered successfully after the gate window. Did NOT verify cancellation mid-wait beyond unit-level reasoning.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** a2925d7ea on branch `fix/telegram-429-retry-after`; terminal CI output; production trace evidence above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- Upgrade steps: none required. The two new telegram channel keys are optional with defaults matching prior behavior (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 60`, `typing_refresh_interval_secs = 4`). Existing configs load unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge-sha>` (single commit on this branch).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `rate_limit_max_wait_secs = 0` would need no restart path changes; effectively the fix is one commit — reverting restores prior send behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** grep runtime trace for `failed to reply` or `Telegram sendMessage failed` reappearing, or users reporting vanished drafts/answers again.

prs.title: fix(channels): wait out Telegram retry_after instead of retrying sendMessage into a 429
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_text_chunks` used to answer an HTTP 429 on the HTML `sendMessage` with an immediate plain-text `sendMessage`. That is a second request into the same flood limit, and it cannot help because the formatting was never the problem. A 429 now goes through a new `send_message_honoring_rate_limit` helper. The helper reads `parameters.retry_after`, waits that long, and resends the *same* body. It does this at most `TELEGRAM_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` (2) times, and only while the wait is ≤ `TELEGRAM_MAX_INLINE_RETRY_AFTER` (60 s).
  - A penalty longer than 60 s, or a 429 that keeps coming after the retries, fails the chunk right away with `Telegram sendMessage rate limited (429 …)`. There is no plain-text attempt and no further request inside the window. A WARN event with `retry_after_secs` is logged. `SendChunksError` now carries `rate_limited: true` for this case. `finalize_send_chunks` then skips its resume. It returns `FinalizePartialDelivery` when some chunks were accepted. When none were, it returns a new `zeroclaw_api::channel::FinalizeUndelivered` error, which the orchestrator handles by not resending and not firing `message_sent`. Neither the resume nor the orchestrator's "send as new message" fallback sends inside the penalty window. Other failures keep the existing resume and fallback behavior.
  - Non-429 failures (for example an HTML parse error) keep the existing markdown → plain fallback. If the plain request itself gets a 429, it waits and retries the same way.
- **Scope boundary:** this covers the `sendMessage` path only, which serves `send`, `finalize_send_chunks` and the orchestrator's "send as new message" fallback, since they all go through `send_text_chunks`. When finalize is rate limited, the visible result is the last streamed draft text rather than a resent full answer. It does **not** change the `editMessageText` steps in `finalize_draft` (HTML edit → plain edit → delete+send). It does not add a durable requeue for penalties over 60 s, and it does not add adaptive `draft_update_interval_ms` backpressure. The triage comment suggests keeping that last one as a separate follow-up.
- **Blast radius:** Telegram outbound text sends, plus one new orchestrator finalize arm that only matches the new `FinalizeUndelivered` error. A reply that hits a short 429 is now delayed by `retry_after` instead of failing at once.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. This is the immediate-retry part of the send path; the finalize-edit path and the long-penalty queueing remain.

### What this does, simply

When Telegram says "too many requests, retry after N seconds", ZeroClaw used to resend the message right away as plain text. When that also failed, it gave up. Every extra request inside the penalty window makes Telegram extend the penalty, which matches the escalating `retry_after` values in the issue (536 s → 1390 s). Now ZeroClaw waits the time Telegram asks for and sends the same message again. If the wait is too long to do inline (over a minute), it stops instead of hammering, and it logs why. I prepared this change with an AI coding assistant, then reviewed it and ran the tests below myself.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is covered by wiremock tests that return real Telegram 429 bodies; reproducing a real flood limit needs a throttled bot token.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/lint jobs run `zeroclaw-channels` unit tests, which include the new tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Telegram flood-limit check.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64, rustc 1.99.0 stable):
  - New tests fail on `master`. I ran them with the source change reverted:
    ```
    test telegram::tests::send_text_chunks_waits_retry_after_then_resends_same_format ... FAILED
    test telegram::tests::send_text_chunks_does_not_retry_inside_long_flood_penalty ... FAILED
    ... panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs: the resend must wait for retry_after
    ... panicked at crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs: sent 0 chunk(s) then failed: Telegram sendMessage failed (markdown 429 Too Many Requests: {...,"parameters":{"retry_after":536}}; plain 429 Too Many Requests: {...,"parameters":{"retry_after":536}})
    ```
  - With the change (follow-up commit 20c2c139, rebuilt on the current branch): `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib telegram`
    ```
    test result: ok. 405 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 1572 filtered out; finished in 8.87s
    ```
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: passed. The first CI run failed it on the `Issue #11615` references in two test comments, which are now removed.
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-channels -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args`: clean for `zeroclaw-channels`. The only error is a pre-existing `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` at `orchestrator/mod.rs:4845` (`.map(&fmt_sel)`), which this PR does not touch; it's reported by the rustc 1.99 clippy on this box. Without `--no-deps`, the same lint also fires in `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new tests cover: a 429 with `retry_after: 1` followed by a 200 sends exactly two requests, both `parse_mode: HTML`, and the second waits ≥ 1 s; a 429 with `retry_after: 536` sends exactly one request and returns `delivered == 0` with a "rate limited" error; a 429 that keeps coming sends exactly 1 + `TELEGRAM_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES` requests, all HTML; a 429 on the plain-text fallback waits and resends the identical plain body; a rate-limited `finalize_send_chunks` with nothing accepted returns `FinalizeUndelivered` (not `FinalizePartialDelivery`) after one request; and `telegram_retry_after` reads `parameters.retry_after`, defaults a bare 429 to 1 s, and ignores non-429 statuses. I did **not** check against a real throttled bot.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run the full workspace `cargo test` on this box. The first CI run's `Test` failure was `component::verifiable_intent_notice_visibility::enabling_the_section_through_config_patch_records_the_notice_once` (a `zeroclaw config patch` trace check), which doesn't touch Telegram code. I didn't reproduce it locally. I ran the crate's telegram tests. On 20c2c139 a local `cargo clippy --no-deps` stops on pre-existing lints from my newer local toolchain (e.g. `orchestrator/mod.rs:4845`, outside this diff), so I relied on CI clippy for that commit. The follow-up also touches `zeroclaw-api/src/channel.rs` (new `FinalizeUndelivered` type) and the orchestrator's finalize match (one new arm). There is no orchestrator-level test for that arm, and none existed for the `FinalizePartialDelivery` arm either.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (the same `sendMessage` request is resent at most twice, after Telegram's requested delay)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No

prs.title: fix(security): apply configured firejail_args to the Firejail wrapper
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `FirejailSandbox` used to be a unit struct, and `wrap_invocation` built a fixed argument list. Configured `firejail_args` never reached the firejail command line, even though the risk-profile schema accepts them and `security status` feeds them into the sandbox config. The struct now holds validated extra arguments. `create_selected_sandbox` builds it through `FirejailSandbox::with_args(&sandbox.firejail_args)` on both the explicit-backend path and the auto-detect path. The arguments go after the wrapper's own flags and hardening flags, and before the wrapped invocation, so firejail reads them as its own options and not as arguments to the target command.
  - Validation follows the maintainer decision on #11594. An entry is rejected if it is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, is `--`, isn't a single `--option` / `--option=value` (for example `none` or `-q`), or names an option that would undo the wrapper. The rejected options are `--profile` (the wrapper sets `--noprofile`), `--include`, `--ignore` (it can drop the wrapper's flags), `--private` / `--private=…` (the wrapper sets `--private=home`; `--private-tmp`, `--private-etc=…` and similar are still allowed), `--allow-debuggers`, and `--join`, `--join-or-start`, `--join-network`, `--join-filesystem`.
  - If Firejail is selected but its arguments are rejected, the sandbox becomes `RejectedFirejailArgsSandbox`. It refuses every command (`wrap_command` / `check_initialization` return `InvalidInput` with the reason), the same way `FailedSeatbeltSandbox` does. It does not fall back to running without the arguments or to `NoopSandbox`, since either would present the configured hardening as active when it isn't.
  - `sandbox_posture`, which feeds `security status`, now describes the active Firejail backend as "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked (…reason…)". Before, it described a configuration that wouldn't be applied.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR doesn't touch #11538 / #11539 (the hard-coded `--private=home` / `--nowheel` launch failures) or the docs change in #11591. It doesn't edit the schema doc comment or the generated `config.md`. `firejail_args` still has no effect when another backend is active (Landlock, Bubblewrap, and so on), which matches its documented meaning ("when sandbox_backend resolves to firejail").
- **Blast radius:** Linux, and only when Firejail is the selected sandbox backend. With empty `firejail_args` (the default and all presets) the firejail command line is byte-for-byte the same as before; a test covers this. A profile that has non-empty `firejail_args` gets them applied now. If they're invalid, its shell commands are refused with the reason and no longer run without them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11594

### What this does, simply

A risk profile can list extra Firejail options in `firejail_args` (for example `--net=none`), but ZeroClaw silently ignored them while still reporting them back. Now they're actually passed to firejail. Options that would break or weaken ZeroClaw's own Firejail setup, or that aren't Firejail options at all, are rejected with a clear message. In that case commands are blocked, not run as if the hardening applied, and the sandbox status says so. I prepared this change with an AI coding assistant, then reviewed it and ran the tests below myself.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new behavior is in command construction and backend selection, which the unit tests cover without needing firejail installed. A live Firejail smoke test would add signal, but I couldn't run one here (see below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The Rust test and lint jobs run the `zeroclaw-runtime` unit tests, which include the new `security::firejail` and `security::detect` tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Nothing exercises a real firejail binary. The non-Linux `cfg` branches (where firejail isn't compiled) were only checked by reading them: I don't have a macOS/Windows target installed, so CI's cross-platform jobs are the check for those.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux x86_64):
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::firejail security::detect`
    ```
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_passes_configured_args_before_the_wrapped_command ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_wrap_without_configured_args_is_unchanged ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_accepts_single_options_with_and_without_values ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_rejects_args_that_are_not_options_or_undo_the_wrapper ... ok
    test security::firejail::tests::firejail_with_args_reports_rejected_args_before_probing ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::selected_firejail_with_rejected_args_blocks_commands_instead_of_dropping_them ... ok
    test security::detect::tests::firejail_posture_reports_rejected_args ... ok
    test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5663 filtered out; finished in 0.03s
    ```
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check`: clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`: no findings in `security/firejail.rs` or `security/detect.rs`. The crate still fails clippy on lints that already exist on master with this box's newer toolchain: deprecated `fetch_update` in `rpc/upload.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`. This PR doesn't touch those files.
  - On `master` the new tests don't compile, because there's no way to give `FirejailSandbox` arguments. That is the bug: the configured value has nowhere to go.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read every `FirejailSandbox` construction site: `detect.rs` was the only production one. `runtime_shell_assembly` and `security status` both reach it through `create_sandbox` / `sandbox_posture` with `risk_profile.sandbox_config()` / `sandbox_config_from_policy`, and both carry `firejail_args`. I did **not** run a real firejail (it isn't installed here), so I haven't observed `--net=none` actually cutting the network.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The only user-visible text change is the posture description string, shown above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I didn't run the full workspace `cargo test` / `cargo clippy --all-targets`, because only two files in `zeroclaw-runtime/src/security` changed. The crate's `security::` tests and lib/test clippy cover them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Configured Firejail options are now applied, and options that would loosen the wrapper's baseline (`--profile`, `--include`, `--ignore`, `--private`, `--allow-debuggers`, `--join*`) are rejected. A rejected configuration blocks commands and doesn't fall back to an unsandboxed run.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the default (empty) `firejail_args` and every preset. A profile that already sets `firejail_args` changes behavior: valid options now take effect, and invalid ones now block that profile's shell commands with a reason.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys. The existing `firejail_args` key starts doing what its docs say.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: if `security status` or a refused command reports "firejail_args rejected", write each option as one `--option` / `--option=value` entry, or remove the option the message names.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Emptying `firejail_args` in the risk profile restores the previous firejail command line exactly.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** shell commands failing with `firejail_args rejected: …`, or `security status` showing "Firejail selected, but firejail_args were rejected; commands are blocked".

prs.title: fix(providers): stop charging JPEG coefficient planes zune-jpeg never allocates
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The pre-decode JPEG projection charged full-image coefficient planes for every JPEG. zune-jpeg 0.5.15 allocates them only for progressive frames and for baseline frames whose first scan omits a component ([`all_components_in_first_scan`](https://github.com/etemesi254/zune-image/blob/31d81fed7551c8ccea456d9d8e2b1fd8bebb6995/crates/zune-jpeg/src/mcu.rs#L170-L185)). An ordinary single-scan baseline photo decodes one MCU row at a time, so the projection was about twice its real peak and 12 MP phone photos (about 37–42 MiB measured) were refused by the 64 MiB per-image cap.
  - The frame-header walk now continues to the first SOS and validates it the way zune-jpeg's `parse_sos` does (1..=4 selectors, SOS length exactly 6 + 2·Ns, distinct IDs present in the frame). The coefficient charge is dropped only for a SOF0/SOF1 frame whose first scan names every component; progressive frames, partial first scans, and anything the walk cannot classify keep it.
  - Every JPEG projection now also charges the two copies of the encoded input that are live during the decode: the owned buffer `validate_image_content_with_projection` moves into the blocking task, and the `Vec` that `image`'s JPEG adapter [copies it into](https://github.com/image-rs/image/blob/76e57184f22772dad1138e96954e57945406b15e/src/codecs/jpeg/decoder.rs#L28-L36). Without them the reduced projection would not bound the peak. Master charges neither, and its projection is already below the real validation peak for every progressive and split-scan file in the corpus below.
  - Every JPEG projection now also charges the metadata zune-jpeg copies out of the stream and keeps for the whole decode (EXIF, XMP, extended XMP, IPTC, ICC, MPF, gain-map payloads), wherever the segments appear, including between and after scans. Each APPn/COM segment is charged at twice its payload plus a fixed per-segment allowance. The walk mirrors zune-jpeg 0.5.15's three marker contexts, which disagree on which markers carry a length: before the first scan every marker except SOS and EOI is read with a length (RST, SOI, and TEM included); inside entropy-coded data RST carries none; after a scan, baseline decoding reads RST with a length and progressive decoding without. Every segment is skipped by the bytes zune-jpeg actually consumes, which is the declared length except for a length-6 APP0, which zune-jpeg reads one byte past its end (`zune_jpeg_segment_overread`, applied in all three walks).
- **Scope boundary:** The 64 MiB per-image and 256 MiB aggregate limits are unchanged. No resizing, no `0`/disable semantics, no changes to PNG, GIF, or WebP accounting. Those remain the separate #9887 slices.
- **Blast radius:** `projected_allocation` for JPEG only, which gates admission in `validate_image_content` and the aggregate decode budget. Ordinary baseline JPEGs are charged less and are now admitted; progressive, split-scan, and malformed JPEGs are charged slightly more (the two input copies), and JPEGs carrying large metadata are charged for it on every path.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9887 (the accounting-correction slice requested [here](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9887#issuecomment-6083091285)).

Two behaviours worth a reviewer's attention:

- **SOF1 (extended sequential)** gets the same reduced charge as SOF0: zune-jpeg 0.5.15 maps both to `BaselineDct` and only SOF2 sets `is_progressive`.
- **A second frame header before the first scan** now takes the existing malformed-header fallback. zune-jpeg parses every frame header it reaches, so a later SOF2 could switch the decode to progressive after the projection classified the frame as baseline. Ordinary JPEGs never contain one; previously the walk stopped at the first SOF and never saw it.
- **SOF1 is not in the measured corpus.** Pillow and `jpegtran` write SOF0; the SOF1 decision rests on the zune-jpeg source, not a measurement.
- **The metadata charge applies on every JPEG path, not just the reduced one.** The coefficient charge on master does not account for metadata either, so master projects about 0.6 MiB for a 256×256 image carrying 300,000 ICC chunks or 100,000 extended-XMP chunks (measured 27.4 and 31.0 MiB). The per-payload factor is 2× because extended XMP is briefly held twice during reassembly; the per-segment allowance is 192 bytes, covering zune-jpeg's per-chunk records (`ExtendedXmpSegment` plus its GUID, `ICCChunk`) in a `Vec` whose capacity may have doubled.
- **A regression in `ca6a55a1` that this commit fixes.** `jpeg_first_scan` inherited from `jpeg_frame_header` the assumption that every segment consumes exactly its declared length. zune-jpeg reads a length-6 APP0 as 7 bytes, so a hidden SOF0/SOS placed after one could classify a progressive frame as baseline and drop the coefficient charge (crafted 3840×2160 progressive file: 33.4 MiB projected before this fix, 52.1 MiB measured; master over-charges it at 76.8). The frame-header walk on master has the same off-by-one, but there it could not drop the coefficient charge.
- **The model is pinned to zune-jpeg 0.5.15.** The walks reproduce that version's marker handling, including the APP0 over-read and the context-dependent RST lengths. A zune-jpeg upgrade should re-check them; a guard that fails when the locked zune-jpeg version changes may be worth adding, and I have not added one here.
- **Two pre-existing issues this PR does not change** (found while reviewing it): `projected_allocation` itself runs `into_decoder()`, which for JPEG copies the input and parses every header-phase metadata segment before any cap is checked, so admission is not strictly "before any decoder is built"; and zune-jpeg re-sorts its pending extended-XMP segments after every marker, which is quadratic in their count and can block the parse for a long time on a file packed with them.
- **The validator's owned copy is uncharged for PNG, GIF, and WebP too.** `bytes_owned` is made for every format; this PR charges it for JPEG only and leaves the other formats' accounting unchanged, to keep the scope to the requested correction.

### What this does, simply

Before decoding an image to check it is valid, ZeroClaw estimates how much memory the decode will need and refuses anything over 64 MiB, so a hostile file cannot exhaust the daemon. For JPEGs that estimate assumed the decoder always keeps a full copy of the image's compressed coefficients in memory. It only does that for progressive JPEGs; ordinary phone photos are decoded a strip at a time. The estimate was therefore about double the real figure, and normal 12 MP photos sent over a channel were refused as too large. This PR makes the estimate follow what the decoder actually allocates, adds the two copies of the file held in memory while decoding, and counts the embedded metadata (colour profiles, EXIF, XMP) the decoder keeps alongside the image, and leaves the limit itself and the protections against tricky headers unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional. The harness below reproduces every number in this description.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `signal` (inbound image attachment) for the original report; the change itself is in the shared multimodal validator used by every surface.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A vision-capable model and any channel that accepts image attachments.
- **Steps to run:** Send an ordinary 12 MP JPEG straight from a phone camera.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The image reaches the model.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The image is skipped with `decoded canvas of 76192000 bytes exceeds per-image limit of 67108864 bytes` (4000×3000) and the model is told it could not be loaded.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Lint (workspace clippy) and the workspace test run, which includes the `multimodal::` unit tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not measure allocator peaks; that evidence is the harness below, deliberately kept out of CI as you suggested.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (Rust 1.98.0 in a podman build container, on `62b65592`)
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output, exit 0)

  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  (exit 0, no warnings)

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --lib -- multimodal::
  test result: ok. 203 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1768 filtered out
  ```
  New tests:
  - `ordinary_baseline_photo_passes_the_production_validator`: a 3840×2160 photo from `image`'s encoder (single-scan baseline) is admitted through `validate_within_budget` with one decode; its projection with coefficient planes would have exceeded the cap. The same bytes relabelled SOF2 are refused before any decode.
  - `sequential_first_scan_with_every_component_charges_row_scratch_only` (SOF0, SOF1, reordered selectors).
  - `progressive_or_split_first_scan_keeps_coefficient_planes` (SOF2 complete and partial; SOF0/SOF1 with one or two of three components).
  - `unclassifiable_first_scan_keeps_coefficient_planes` (no SOS, unknown ID, duplicate ID, wrong SOS length, truncated SOS, standalone marker before the scan).
  - `second_frame_header_before_first_scan_uses_the_malformed_fallback`.
  - `jpeg_projection_charges_both_input_copies`.
  - `near_limit_baseline_jpeg_is_refused_once_both_input_copies_count`: a 4000×4000 single-scan baseline frame with 10 MiB of input fits under the cap with one input copy charged and is refused before decode with both.
  - `metadata_heavy_baseline_photo_is_refused_before_decode`: the 3840×2160 photo above with the largest ICC profile JPEG can carry (255 chunks, about 15.9 MiB). Output plus both input copies fit under the cap; with the retained profile charged it is refused through `validate_within_budget` before any decode.
  - `jpeg_metadata_charge_follows_zune_jpegs_marker_contexts`: segments before and after the scan, a marker-like pattern inside an APP payload and inside a DQT payload (not counted), a stuffed zero, fill bytes, an RST inside the scan (no length) and between baseline scans (with one), data after EOI (ignored), and a truncated declared length.
  - `header_markers_zune_jpeg_reads_with_a_length_cannot_hide_metadata`: `FF D8 00 04 FF D9`, `FF D0 00 04 FF D9`, `FF 01 00 04 FF D9`, and an RST whose payload looks like an APP1 header, each in front of a profile that must still be charged.
  - `restart_markers_between_scans_follow_the_frame_type`: the same stream charged as zune-jpeg's progressive and baseline after-scan loops would parse it.
  - `app0_with_length_six_is_read_one_byte_past_its_end` and `app0_overread_cannot_hide_a_profile_from_admission`: a length-6 APP0 in front of `FF D9` or a fake frame header, and the 3840×2160 photo behind 255 blocks that read as DQTs under a 6-byte APP0 and as ICC chunks to zune-jpeg, refused before decode.

  `unsupported_jpeg_sof_marker_cannot_undercharge_admission` now declares 5000×5000 instead of 3000×3000: its encoded first scan covers every component, so the real frame's output alone must exceed the cap for the refusal to stay meaningful. The existing unprefixed-SOF and TEM tests are unchanged and pass.

  Checked against the defects they guard (each change applied alone):
  ```text
  always drop the coefficient planes        -> 5 tests fail (incl. progressive, split, unclassifiable, end-to-end)
  charge one input copy instead of two      -> jpeg_projection_charges_both_input_copies and near_limit_... fail
  accept a second frame header              -> second_frame_header_..._malformed_fallback fails
  treat SOF2 as sequential                  -> progressive_or_split_... and the end-to-end test fail
  accept unknown or duplicate scan IDs      -> unclassifiable_first_scan_... fails
  treat a partial first scan as complete    -> progressive_or_split_first_scan_... fails
  drop the metadata charge                  -> metadata_heavy_..., ..._both_input_copies, near_limit_... fail
  charge each metadata payload once         -> 6 metadata tests fail
  RST/SOI/TEM without a length in headers   -> header_markers_..._cannot_hide_metadata fails
  RST without a length between baseline scans, or with one between progressive scans
                                            -> restart_markers_between_scans_... fails
  RST with a length inside a scan           -> jpeg_metadata_charge_follows_... fails
  count patterns inside APP payloads        -> jpeg_metadata_charge_follows_... fails
  keep parsing after EOI                    -> jpeg_metadata_charge_follows_... fails
  no APP0 over-read, or over-read in only some of the walks
                                            -> both app0_... tests fail
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Peak heap during the production validation decode (an owned copy of the input, as `validate_image_content_with_projection` makes, then the `ImageReader` decode), measured with a tracking global allocator, against `projected_allocation`'s JPEG arm on master and on this branch (projection code copied verbatim from each revision). Verified live on `ca6a55a1`, before the second input copy and the metadata charge were added: a daemon built from current `master` with #11556 and this branch merged admitted a 4000×3000 phone photo received over Signal, the resolution refused on `master` with `exceeds per-image limit`, and the model described it. With both copies and their metadata charged, the 4000×3000 photos below project to 41–52 MiB and are still admitted.

  **Real images** (4000×3000, baseline, one scan, 4:2:0). The decode peak was measured before the photos were deleted; the measured column adds the validator's owned copy (the file size), and the branch column is computed from the formula (output 36,000,000 + row scratch 4,096,000 + 2 × file size; their metadata segments are a few hundred bytes and do not change the figures at this precision):

  | Image | File | Master | Branch | Measured |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Signal copy, refused on master | 1,874,364 B | 72.7 MiB | 41.8 MiB | 38.6 MiB |
  | Signal copy, refused on master | 1,629,309 B | 72.7 MiB | 41.3 MiB | 38.0 MiB |

```rust
//! Peak heap of ZeroClaw's JPEG validation decode (`ImageReader`,
//! `set_format(Jpeg)`, `decode()`; image 0.25.10 / zune-jpeg 0.5.15) next to
//! the current projection (copied verbatim from master) and the proposed one.

#![allow(dead_code)]
mod branch;
mod master;

use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering::Relaxed};

struct Tracking;
static CURRENT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
static PEAK: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);

unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Tracking {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let p = unsafe { System.alloc(layout) };
        if !p.is_null() {
            let now = CURRENT.fetch_add(layout.size(), Relaxed) + layout.size();
            PEAK.fetch_max(now, Relaxed);
        }
        p
    }
    unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let p = unsafe { System.alloc_zeroed(layout) };
        if !p.is_null() {
            let now = CURRENT.fetch_add(layout.size(), Relaxed) + layout.size();
            PEAK.fetch_max(now, Relaxed);
        }
        p
    }
    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, p: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        unsafe { System.dealloc(p, layout) };
        CURRENT.fetch_sub(layout.size(), Relaxed);
    }
    unsafe fn realloc(&self, p: *mut u8, layout: Layout, new: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        let q = unsafe { System.realloc(p, layout, new) };
        if !q.is_null() {
            if new > layout.size() {
                let now = CURRENT.fetch_add(new - layout.size(), Relaxed) + new - layout.size();
                PEAK.fetch_max(now, Relaxed);
            } else {
                CURRENT.fetch_sub(layout.size() - new, Relaxed);
            }
        }
        q
    }
}

#[global_allocator]
static A: Tracking = Tracking;

struct Header {
    kind: &'static str,
    progressive: bool,
    sampling: Vec<(u64, u64)>,
    frame_ids: Vec<u8>,
    first_scan_ids: Vec<u8>,
    scans: usize,
}

/// Marker walk: SOF type, sampling, first-SOS component IDs, total scans.
fn header(bytes: &[u8]) -> Header {
    let mut h = Header {
        kind: "?",
        progressive: false,
        sampling: vec![],
        frame_ids: vec![],
        first_scan_ids: vec![],
        scans: 0,
    };
    let mut i = 2;
    while i + 4 <= bytes.len() {
        if bytes[i] != 0xFF {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        let m = bytes[i + 1];
        if m == 0xD9 {
            break;
        }
        if m == 0x01 || (0xD0..=0xD7).contains(&m) || m == 0xFF || m == 0x00 {
            i += if m == 0xFF { 1 } else { 2 };
            continue;
        }
        let len = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[i + 2], bytes[i + 3]]) as usize;
        if matches!(m, 0xC0..=0xC2) {
            h.kind = match m {
                0xC0 => "baseline",
                0xC1 => "extended",
                _ => "progressive",
            };
            h.progressive = m == 0xC2;
            let n = bytes[i + 9] as usize;
            for c in 0..n {
                h.frame_ids.push(bytes[i + 10 + c * 3]);
                let f = bytes[i + 11 + c * 3];
                h.sampling.push((u64::from(f >> 4), u64::from(f & 0x0F)));
            }
        }
        if m == 0xDA {
            if h.scans == 0 {
                let ns = bytes[i + 4] as usize;
                h.first_scan_ids = (0..ns).map(|k| bytes[i + 5 + k * 2]).collect();
            }
            h.scans += 1;
            i += 2 + len;
            while i + 1 < bytes.len() {
                if bytes[i] == 0xFF
                    && bytes[i + 1] != 0x00
                    && !(0xD0..=0xD7).contains(&bytes[i + 1])
                {
                    break;
                }
                i += 1;
            }
            continue;
        }
        i += 2 + len;
    }
    h
}

const CAP: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

fn mib(v: u64) -> String {
    format!("{:.1}M{}", v as f64 / MIB, if v > CAP { "*" } else { " " })

        let fallback = pixels * 8 + u64::from(w) * 64 * 8;
        let master_projection =
            output + master::jpeg_auxiliary_allocation(&bytes, w, ht).unwrap_or(fallback);
        let branch_projection = output
            + branch::jpeg_auxiliary_allocation(&bytes, w, ht).unwrap_or(fallback)
            + 2 * bytes.len() as u64
            + branch::jpeg_retained_metadata_allocation(&bytes);

        let mut limits = image::Limits::default();
        limits.max_image_width = Some(16384);
        limits.max_image_height = Some(16384);
        limits.max_alloc = None;
        let base = CURRENT.load(Relaxed);
        PEAK.store(base, Relaxed);
        // `validate_image_content_with_projection` moves an owned copy of the
        // input into the blocking task and decodes from it.
        let owned = bytes.to_vec();
        let mut reader = image::ImageReader::new(std::io::Cursor::new(&owned));
        reader.set_format(image::ImageFormat::Jpeg);
        reader.limits(limits);
        let decoded = reader.decode();
        let failed = decoded.as_ref().err().map(|e| e.to_string());
        let measured = (PEAK.load(Relaxed) - base) as u64;
        drop(decoded);
        drop(owned);

        if std::env::var("RESIDUAL").is_ok() {
            let scratch = branch::jpeg_auxiliary_allocation(&bytes, w, ht).unwrap_or(fallback)
                + branch::jpeg_retained_metadata_allocation(&bytes);
            let residual = measured as i64 - output as i64 - 2 * bytes.len() as i64;
            println!(
                "RESIDUAL {:<30} output {:>11} input {:>10} measured {:>11} residual {:>10} charged-aux {:>11} covered {}",
                std::path::Path::new(&path)
                    .file_name()
                    .unwrap()
                    .to_string_lossy(),
                output,
                bytes.len(),
                measured,
                residual,
                scratch,
                residual <= scratch as i64
            );
            continue;
        }
        if branch_projection < measured {
            violations += 1;
        }
        let name = std::path::Path::new(&path)
            .file_name()
            .unwrap()
            .to_string_lossy()
            .into_owned();
        println!(
            "{:<30} {:>10} {:>11} {:>6} {:>9} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>8.1}%{}",
            name,
            format!("{w}x{ht}"),
            h.kind,
            format!("{}/{}", h.first_scan_ids.len(), h.frame_ids.len()),
            h.sampling
                .iter()
                .map(|s| format!("{}{}", s.0, s.1))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(","),
            mib(master_projection),
            mib(branch_projection),
            mib(measured),
            (branch_projection as f64 - measured as f64) / measured as f64 * 100.0,
            if branch_projection < measured {
                "  UNDER"
            } else if failed.is_some() {
                "  (decode failed)"
            } else {
                ""
            }
        );
    }
    println!(
        "\nmaster/branch = projected_allocation for JPEG at each revision (projection code copied verbatim). measured = peak heap during decode().\n* = over 64 MiB. scan1 = components in first SOS / frame. Branch projection under measured: {violations}"
    );
}
```

</details>

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change does lower a resource bound for one input class, so the risk is under-counting a decode: the reduction applies only when the first SOS is validated against the frame the way zune-jpeg validates it, anything else keeps the full charge, a second frame header takes the malformed fallback, retained metadata is charged on every path, and the measured peaks above, including the adversarial `meta-*` files, stay below the new projection.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; the change is confined to `projected_allocation`'s JPEG path and its helpers.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Daemon memory growth or OOM while validating JPEG attachments; `skipping multimodal image that could not be loaded` with `exceeds per-image limit` returning for ordinary baseline photos would indicate the reverse.
