prs.title: feat(rpc): core parity for workspace, catalog, canvas, pairing, channels and system methods
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** As part of the v0.9.0 gateway split, the core serves over RPC the channels, system, tools, canvas, files and pairing-user operations that the dashboard reaches over HTTP today, so the gateway can later become an RPC client (#11001). Each method returns the body its HTTP route returns: the shaping moves into the runtime and both surfaces serialize the same function.
- **Draft.** Every method below is implemented and rebased onto current `master`. `/api/upload` parity still waits on #11171.
- **Scope boundary:** no gateway route is removed or ported here; migrating those routes is separate work. `canvas/subscribe` belongs to separate work on the subscription hub. The chunked `file/upload/{begin,chunk,commit}` methods belong to #11171; this PR wires `/api/upload` onto them after it lands.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11001, #11000
- **Labels:** (maintainer-applied)

### Method status

| Method(s) | Status |
|---|---|
| `workspace/list`, `fs/{mkdir,rmdir,read,delete,move}` | implemented |
| `integrations/list`, `tools/cli-discover`, `plugins/list`, `a2a/identity` | implemented |
| `tools/list{agent}`, `canvas/{list,get,history,render,clear}`, `pairing/{list,revoke,revoke-all,new-code}`, `metrics/scrape`, `channels/{list,relink,bind}`, `system/{upgrade,upgrade-status,restart}` | implemented |
| `/api/upload` ↔ `file/upload/*` parity | waits on #11171 |

### Authorization

- `fs/*`, `workspace/list`: `files:{read,create,update,delete}`. With `agent`, the principal must be entitled to that agent; without one the operation targets the shared area every agent reads, so it needs access to every agent. Checked before any filesystem access.
- `integrations/list`, `tools/cli-discover`: `tools:read`. `plugins/list`: `plugins:read`. `a2a/identity`: `system:read`, plus the agent selector for a named agent (the catalog card lists only A2A-published agents, as the unauthenticated well-known route does).
- `canvas/*`: a new additive `Resource::Canvas` (`list`/`get`/`history` read, `render` update, `clear` delete). Direct canvas access needs every-agent access. An RPC-built session's `canvas` tool draws into the shared store, but only through its agent's namespace: every id it uses is stored as `<agent>/<id>`. It cannot name a canvas outside that namespace, whatever its principal's grants are then or later. A namespace is non-empty and contains no `/`, enforced where the namespaced handle is made, so every stored key belongs to exactly one namespace: `alpha` drawing `beta/default` and a hand-written `[agents."alpha/beta"]` drawing `default` cannot share a canvas. A session on an alias that cannot be a namespace draws into a private store. The dashboard sees an agent's canvases under that prefix. One namespace holds at most 16 canvases, so it cannot fill the shared store's limit of 100.
- `pairing/*`: administrators only, because a pairing code mints a bearer credential. `pairing/new-code` and `pairing/revoke-all` also require the local transport. The revoking and code-issuing methods take the config write lock first, re-resolve the caller's authority under it, and require admin on those fresh grants.
- `system/{upgrade,restart}`: administrators only. `system/upgrade-status` and `metrics/scrape`: `system:read`.
- `channels/list`: `channels:read`. `channels/{relink,bind}`: `channels:update` on a channel the principal's agent owns. `channels/bind` also needs config-write authority on the exact `peer_groups.<group>.external_peers` path it writes.

### Security fixes included

An agent alias was spliced into `<install>/agents/<alias>/workspace` unchecked. `PathBuf::join` with `..` or an absolute alias selected a directory outside the agents tree, so over RPC any principal with the wildcard agent selector and `files` grants could list, read, move or delete there. The HTTP route had a milder form (a single `..` segment). Runtime browse now requires the alias to be one plain path component, on both surfaces.

- **Workspace file operations no longer follow links out of the workspace.** The lexical path checks could not stop a link inside an authorized agent's workspace from pointing into another agent's workspace, so `fs/read` or `fs/delete` could reach it. Browse now opens the configured root as a directory handle (`cap-std`) and performs every read, list, delete, move and mkdir relative to that handle, including intermediate components. A link that escapes the root is refused; an absolute link target is refused even when it points inside; relative links that stay inside still work. The byte cap applies to the bytes actually read. HTTP and CLI browse callers inherit the same containment.
- **Revoking a paired credential takes the config write lock before the token is dropped.** Before this, a revocation dropped the token first and only then waited for the lock to persist. That had two effects:
  - A `channels/bind` that had rechecked its caller under the lock could still commit after the caller's token was revoked.
  - A pairing rotation checked admin once, then waited for the lock and issued a code even if admin was withdrawn meanwhile.

  Now `PairingGuard::{revoke_token, revoke_token_hash, revoke_all_tokens}` require a held guard on the config write lock, so every credential invalidator on every surface must hold that lock: the compiler enforces it. That covers RPC `pairing/revoke`, `revoke-all` and `new-code` rotation, HTTP `DELETE /api/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/devices/{id}/token/rotate`, `/admin/paircode/new` rotation, and the enrollment rollbacks. Each authenticates its caller again under the lock. A policy change and a revocation both order against any operation that rechecks and commits under that lock. In production the gateway and RPC share one process-wide lock.
- **Workspace mutations refuse a path that passes through a link.** Protected-entry checks run on the lexical path, but the root handle followed links that stay inside the root, so `via/SOUL.md` with `via -> .` removed the real `SOUL.md`. The pattern exists on `master`. Delete, move (both ends) and shared rmdir now open each parent directory without following a link, and act on the final name through that handle. mkdir creates each component, the last one included, the same way, so `via/SOUL.md` cannot take a protected name. mkdir and move also check the path's first component, where every protected file lives, not only the whole path, so `SOUL.md/child` cannot create a `SOUL.md` directory where the bootstrap file belongs. The check is linear in the path's length, and a move looks up its source before judging either path. The protected-name comparison folds case and trailing dots and spaces, as case-insensitive and Windows volumes do.
- **`channels/bind` rechecks authority under the config write lock.** A bind admitted on the caller's grants used to wait for the lock and then persist the peer without looking again, so a policy change committed while it waited was ignored. It now re-resolves the principal under the lock, rechecks channel ownership against the current config, authorizes the concrete peer-group path, and commits under the same guard.

## Testing (required)

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on:** `CI Required Gate`. Golden parity tests live in the gateway crate (`p6_parity_tests`, the only crate that reaches both the HTTP handlers and the RPC handlers); dispatcher-level routing, `Method::authz()` and selector tests live in the runtime (`rpc::dispatch::tests::p6_parity`); the alias fix has a browse unit test.
- **Local, at the rebased head (macOS):**
  - `cargo check --locked --all-targets` is clean for `zeroclaw-runtime`, `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-gateway`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: 629 passed, including the golden parity tests for these RPC methods.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- control`: 5 passed.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: 5342 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `forwarded_environment_demotion_while_queued_refuses_prompt_and_resume`, which fails the same way on an unmodified `master` checkout on macOS: the temp directory sits under a symlinked `/var`. This PR does not touch that code.
  - rustfmt and the comment-hygiene gate are clean.
- **Regression tests for the two security fixes:**
  - `a_scoped_principal_cannot_follow_a_link_into_another_agents_workspace` and the browse unit test `a_link_out_of_the_workspace_is_not_followed` (both Unix-only) cover the link escape.
  - The canvas tool: `a_scoped_sessions_canvas_tool_cannot_reach_the_shared_store`, `a_warm_session_narrowed_to_one_agent_cannot_reach_other_canvases` (every-agent access narrowed after the session exists) `an_agent_alias_with_a_separator_shares_no_canvas_with_its_prefix` (a raw `alpha/beta` alias beside `alpha`, including `canvas/list`), and the store tests `a_namespaced_handle_cannot_reach_outside_its_namespace`, `a_namespace_that_could_share_keys_with_another_is_refused` and `a_namespace_is_capped_below_the_shared_limit`.
  - Revocation and rotation ordering:
    - `a_revocation_cannot_land_inside_a_binds_authority_window` parks the real bind inside its lock-held window, shows an administrator's revocation of the binder's token queued on the lock with the token still valid, and shows the bind committing with it still valid.
    - `rotate_token_waits_for_a_config_writer_in_progress` covers the HTTP rotation route.
    - `a_device_revocation_waits_for_a_config_writer_in_progress` covers RPC revocation.
    - `pairing_rotation_after_admin_is_withdrawn_while_queued_issues_nothing` covers the admin grant withdrawn while queued.
  - Internal aliases: `an_internal_link_cannot_alias_a_protected_entry`, `an_internal_link_cannot_alias_a_protected_shared_directory` and `mkdir_through_an_internal_link_cannot_take_a_protected_name` (Unix-only). Protected names along a path: `make_agent_workspace_directory_refuses_a_protected_file_along_the_path` and `move_agent_workspace_path_refuses_a_protected_file_along_either_path`; `a_very_long_path_is_judged_in_linear_time` bounds the work on a million-component path.
  - Each of these fails against the previous code. The ordering tests also fail when a single invalidator uses a mutex other than the shared config write lock.
  - The recheck: `channels_bind_narrowed_after_admission_has_no_effect` (config-write paths cleared while queued), `channels_bind_resource_reowned_after_admission_is_refused` (channel moved to another agent while queued) and `channels_bind_authorizes_the_peer_group_it_writes`. `channels_bind_widened_after_admission_is_honoured` is an over-rejection control only.
- **Known coverage gap:** no socket or pipe conformance harness exists yet; these are dispatcher-level tests. No OpenRPC document exists yet; the OpenRPC generator derives rows from `Method::ALL` and the typed requests in `zeroclaw_api::jsonrpc`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. New RPC methods expose existing dashboard operations; each is classified in `Method::authz()` and the file operations are held to the agent selector. The alias fix narrows existing access.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. `pairing/*` exposes device listing, revocation and one-time code minting over RPC. It is restricted to administrators, and code minting and revoke-all also require the local transport.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Additive methods; the HTTP bodies are unchanged. An agent alias that is not a single path component is now refused on the HTTP workspace routes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert` of the PR's commits. No data migration.

prs.title: feat(rpc): cron, memory, skills, personality and quickstart parity with the HTTP routes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** As part of the v0.9.0 effort to match HTTP behavior over RPC (#11001), this PR brings the RPC cron, skills, personality and quickstart methods to the behavior of their HTTP routes, and closes the cron pre-approval bypass. (The memory methods' `agent` parameter, first planned here, landed separately in #11151; after rebasing, this PR no longer changes memory methods.)
  - `cron/add` passed `approved = true` ("RPC calls are pre-approved"), so a shell command the owning agent's policy gates behind approval was scheduled over RPC while `POST /api/cron` refused it. It now passes `false`. It also honours agent jobs and accepts `uses_memory` / `shell_output_format` with the HTTP rules.
  - Agent cron jobs are headless: they run later, without the submitting connection, so no named or scoped principal's tool ceiling can be carried to the run. `cron/add`, `cron/patch` and `cron/trigger` on an agent job are therefore admitted only for the shared operator; any other principal gets `FORBIDDEN` with an audited denial (shell jobs are unchanged). An agent job's `allowed_tools` is checked against the agent's current policy at submission, and the agent's policy is re-applied at every run.
  - An agent run's `allowed_tools` now bounds skill tools too. Skills are registered after the built-in filter, so an empty, unknown-only or unrelated list still exposed every eligible skill wrapper (and, through it, the builtin the skill wraps). The ceiling now bounds the finished tool registry by exact name, the same match as the built-in filter, the MCP access policy and `AgentBuilder::build`'s allowlist.
  - `cron/patch` validated a replacement command with `approved = true` too; now `false`. Adds `enabled`, `uses_memory`, `shell_output_format`. As on `PATCH /api/cron/{id}`, `command` or `prompt` (command wins) patches the field the job actually runs: an agent job's prompt, a shell job's command, which is still validated under the owner's policy whichever field carried it. Timezones follow the HTTP rules too: a new expression keeps the job's timezone, `tz` or `clear_tz` alone re-times the existing expression, and a blank `tz`, `tz` with `clear_tz`, or a timezone on a non-cron schedule is refused.
  - `cron/add` and `cron/patch` re-resolve the caller's grants and agent entitlement under the config write lock, which every accepted-policy publication holds, and keep holding it through the SQLite write. A revocation published while the request waited, including on a busy `jobs.db`, is seen at that recheck; one published afterwards queues behind the write. Native-token revocation is ordered the same way: this branch merges #11149 (which lands first), whose gateway device revoke, rotate and admin revocation take that lock before deleting the device, re-check the requesting caller under it, and only then remove the live token. A cron write held up on a busy store therefore commits before a revocation, or a revocation that wins refuses the queued write.
  - `personality/put` takes `expected_mtime_ms`; a stale write is refused with new code `PRECONDITION_FAILED` (-32005) carrying the current content and mtime, but only for a caller that also holds `personality:read` (the method itself needs only `personality:update`, so without read the refusal carries no file state). It was -32004 in the first push; renumbered because the open transport-bounds change #11171 claims -32004 for `CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED`. -32005 is unused on master and in every open PR. Handler errors now keep their `data`.
  - New `skills/create`, `skills/effective`, `skills/slash-option-kinds`; the effective-skill wire mapping moves into the runtime so HTTP and RPC share it.
  - `quickstart/validate` / `quickstart/apply` take `surface` (default `tui`; `test` refused).
- **Scope boundary:** No change to HTTP behavior or to the memory methods. Cron execution changes only in that an agent job's `allowed_tools` now also bounds skill tools.
- **Blast radius:** RPC clients of cron/skills/personality/quickstart; RPC sessions of any principal but the shared operator, which no longer get the scheduling tools or nested delegation; the gateway's skills adapter (mapper moved, behavior unchanged); the scoped tool assembly's per-run caller ceiling. Cron is the only caller that passes that ceiling to `agent::run`; the principal-narrowed `Agent` path already filtered its finished registry by the same exact-name rule, so it is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11001. Related #11000. Depends on #11149 (merged into this branch; lands first).

## Testing (required)

Local runs on the current head (rebased onto `master` `ad0dd3dec8`), macOS aarch64, `zeroclaw-runtime` only:
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::scoped:: cron_` — 151 passed, 0 failed.
- Parallel runtime gate (`cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=16`; 3 runs on an earlier head, 1 on each later one): 5292–5296 passed per run; the only failures (`forwarded_environment_demotion_while_queued_refuses_prompt_and_resume` and `session_prompt_waits_for_queued_provider_update_transaction` in every run, one timing flake in one run) fail the same way on unmodified `master` `0a2dae1837` on the same machine, and `forwarded_environment_demotion_…` passes in CI.
- New in this PR: `cron_add_over_rpc_refuses_an_unapproved_command_exactly_as_http` (RPC refusal carries the exact HTTP refusal text; no job created; `echo hi` control still lands), `cron_patch_over_rpc_refuses_an_unapproved_replacement_command`, `cron_add_and_patch_over_rpc_cover_agent_jobs_and_the_http_fields`, `cron_add_refuses_headless_agent_jobs_from_a_scoped_principal`, `cron_add_refuses_headless_agent_jobs_from_a_named_administrator`, `cron_patch_and_trigger_refuse_a_scoped_principal_on_an_agent_job`, `cron_add_checks_requested_tools_against_the_agent_policy`, `caller_allowed_ceiling_bounds_skill_wrappers`, `patched_cron_schedule_follows_the_http_timezone_rules`, `cron_patch_over_rpc_changes_the_timezone_alone`, `personality_put_refuses_a_stale_expected_mtime`, `personality_put_conflict_withholds_disk_state_without_read`, `constrained_session_loses_the_model_facing_cron_scheduling_tools`, `named_unrestricted_principals_leave_no_work_to_outlive_their_grants`, `a_named_principal_cannot_schedule_work_through_a_peer_agent` (both sessions built by the production registry; a scripted recipient answers a peer message with `cron_add`: the operator's message schedules the job, the named principal's session has no peer tool and the recipient is never called), `cron_add_revoked_while_queued_is_refused`, `cron_patch_revoked_while_queued_is_refused`, `cron_add_survives_an_unrelated_republication_while_queued`, `cron_add_holds_the_publication_lock_while_the_store_is_busy` (the last four from #11149), and, with #11149 merged in, its `a_token_revocation_waits_for_a_cron_write_blocked_on_a_busy_store` and `a_cron_write_queued_behind_a_token_revocation_is_refused` plus its gateway device-revocation ordering tests, `skills_effective_and_slash_option_kinds_answer_over_rpc`, `quickstart_surface_defaults_to_tui_and_refuses_test`; `skills/create` added to the existing path-traversal test.
- `caller_allowed_ceiling_bounds_skill_wrappers` assembles a real skill whose builtin tool wraps `file_write`, under empty, unknown-only (`missing__tool`) and unrelated (`file_read`) ceilings, and requires the wrapper to be absent and its target never invoked; naming `ops__write` admits it and invoking it reaches the target; no ceiling keeps it. With the previous `tool_search`-only ceiling restored, it fails on the empty case (`left: ["ops__write"]`).
- `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-runtime -- --check` — clean. No local gateway build or workspace clippy (disk constraints); CI covers both.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (skills/create uses the same bundle-confined ref resolution as skills/write).
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII in diff? No
- Prompt injection surface changed? No
- Closes authorization gaps: RPC cron add/patch no longer bypass command approval; over the RPC `cron/*` methods, a named or scoped principal can no longer schedule, patch or trigger a headless agent job, over RPC or through its session's model; a cron job's `allowed_tools` no longer leaves skill tools callable that it does not name.
- The model-facing route to the same effect follows the same rule (pre-existing on `master`). `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run` and `schedule` store or run work that later executes headless without the RPC principal's grants, so they declare `requires_unrestricted_principal` like `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and the pipeline, which can rebuild them inside a nested run. An RPC session now omits all of these for every principal except the shared operator, the rule the `cron/*` gate applies: a named administrator, or a named principal with wildcard tools and agents, is unrestricted when it acts, but its grants can be withdrawn while the job it stored waits to run, and nothing at the run re-checks it. `send_message_to_peer` is withheld the same way: an agent recipient runs a detached turn as itself, with its own tools, `cron_add` included, and only `InternalPrincipal::PeerAgent` for provenance. Skill and ref wrappers forward the flag.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for well-behaved clients. Behavior changes, all intended:
  - A client relying on RPC `cron/add` scheduling approval-gated commands is now refused.
  - A named or scoped principal can no longer add, patch or trigger agent cron jobs over RPC (shell jobs unchanged).
  - A cron agent job with `allowed_tools` no longer gets skill tools its list does not name.
  - RPC `cron/patch` with a new schedule and no `tz` now keeps the job's timezone instead of clearing it.
  - A stale `personality/put` from a caller without `personality:read` gets `PRECONDITION_FAILED` without `current_content` / `current_mtime_ms`.
  - An RPC session of any principal but the shared operator no longer gets the `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run` or `schedule` tools, even when its selector names them. The local operator, the gateway's paired devices (both the shared operator), the CLI and channels are unchanged.
  - A named administrator's, or a named wildcard principal's, RPC session also loses `delegate`, `spawn_subagent`, the pipeline and `send_message_to_peer` (constrained principals now lose the peer tool too), because a nested run or a peer's turn can rebuild the scheduling tools. Until a job can carry and re-check its submitter's authority, only the shared operator starts work that outlives its connection.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. New RPC methods and optional params only; one new error code.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `cron/add` or `cron/patch` refusing a command with "requires explicit approval" where a client expected success (intended); `FORBIDDEN` on agent-job cron calls from a non-operator principal (intended); a cron agent job no longer calling a skill tool its `allowed_tools` omits (intended).

prs.title: feat(rpc): config parity for the remaining HTTP config routes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The config routes the dashboard still reaches only over HTTP now also have RPC twins: `config/reload-status`, `config/drift`, `config/agent-options`, `config/section-picker`, `config/section-select`, `config/delete-plan`, `config/init`, `config/migrate`, and `providers/refresh-context-window`. Their logic moves out of the gateway into a new `zeroclaw_runtime::config_ops` module. Both surfaces call the same functions, so the output cannot diverge. Each surface still commits through its own write path: the gateway's principal-gated `persist_and_swap`, and RPC's `save_and_swap_config`.
  - `pending_reload` now belongs to the daemon generation and is shared with the gateway through `GatewayReloadControls`. RPC config writes set it too. Before this, a config write over RPC left the dashboard's reload banner off.
  - RPC `config/map-key-delete` now uses the same alias cascade as HTTP for every aliased section. Before this, deleting an agent over RPC was a plain key removal. It left `heartbeat.agent`, delegates and similar references dangling, and orphaned the agent's memory, cron, ACP and session rows.
  - An agent delete removes the agent's memory, cron jobs, ACP sessions with their transcripts, and its workspace. An admin or unscoped caller may run it. A scoped caller must also hold the agent, delete on memory, cron and sessions, and own every ACP session of the agent. The owner is also enforced inside the SQL delete, so another principal's transcript is never removed. Over RPC the predicate runs at admission and again under the config write lock, on freshly resolved grants and a fresh read of session owners. The delete also refuses while RPC chat sessions are running on the agent.
  - No write method adds authority. Every RPC config write authorizes the dirty set it persists, each path by the verb its effect needs: Create when the path appears, Delete when it disappears, Update otherwise, plus the verbs a route pins (a scalar clear is a Delete; a rename deletes one key and creates another). A path selector must also cover each one. This is the same `(path, verb)` classification the gateway's principal gate uses, now shared by both transports. It covers paths a cascade rewrites outside the addressed key: a delete scrubbing `heartbeat.agent`, or a rename rewriting references (and permission-profile selectors once rename cascades into them). Section-select is checked, with its effect's verb, before it scaffolds an agent workspace. Migrate needs whole-config (`*` or admin) authority.
  - Authority is held through the write's point of effect. A config write first finishes every wait: live-session preparation, then reading, writing and syncing the temporary file and the backup. Only then does it commit through a gate. At the canonical replacement, the gate re-resolves the caller's grants and authorizes every effect. Holding the paired-token set, it then rechecks the credential's liveness and replaces the file with one synchronous rename; nothing is awaited from the first check to the rename. A revocation lands entirely before the commit (refused, nothing written) or entirely after it. Policy publication can't interleave, because it happens only under the config write lock the writer holds. Migration and Quickstart commit through the same gate.
  - RPC error responses now carry the handler's structured `data`. The dispatcher used to drop it, so config refusals now reach clients with the same `{code, message, path}` body HTTP returns.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No HTTP route's path, request or response shape changes. The HTTP behaviour changes are listed under Compatibility.
  - No change to `config/set-many`.
  - The RPC `config/map-key-delete` envelope keeps its `{path, key, deleted}` shape, plus an optional `warnings`.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The gateway config and section handlers become thin wrappers over `config_ops`, authorized through `principal_gate` under the config write lock as on master.
  - Adds the RPC methods above.
  - Changes RPC `config/map-key-delete` for aliased sections, and RPC error serialization (`data` is now kept).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10823, #10824. Complements #11226: the RPC rename recheck here authorizes the permission-profile selectors its cascade rewrites.

### What this does, simply

The web dashboard and the RPC clients (TUI and others) should be able to do the same things to config. Several dashboard operations had no RPC equivalent: previewing what a delete will touch, picking a section item, initializing or migrating the config, refreshing a model's context window, and checking whether a reload is pending. This PR adds them by moving the dashboard's logic somewhere both sides call, rather than writing a second copy.

Building it exposed a real gap. Deleting an agent over RPC skipped all the cleanup the dashboard does. That path now runs the same cleanup, with rules about who may run it. The cleanup can't reach another user's conversations: a scoped user may delete an agent only when every conversation on it is their own. Every setting the delete, or a rename, rewrites is checked against what the caller may write.

**Open question for the maintainer:** the config-parity plan says "whole-document config/get with comments". RPC `config/get` with no `prop` already returns the same masked whole document as `GET /api/config`, and this PR pins that with a golden. Comments exist only on the HTTP PATCH write path, whose RPC twin is `config/set-many` (#10823). A read that returns the raw commented TOML would expose unmasked secrets, so it is not built here.

**Known limit:** the HTTP persistence boundary authorizes under the config write lock before its file I/O. It doesn't yet commit through the gate, so a pairing revoked during that I/O is not ordered against the HTTP write the way it is for RPC.

**Known limit:** the separate `zeroclaw acp` process creates ACP sessions outside the daemon's config write lock. A session it creates after an agent delete has read the session owners keeps its row and transcript, because the owner is enforced in the SQL. But the agent and its workspace are still removed around it. Closing that needs a cross-process agent-retirement fence, which is out of scope here.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Every method has a golden test that compares HTTP output and RPC output against the same JSON file, and the authorization paths have direct tests. There is no user-visible UI change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the runtime and gateway tests, which contain the goldens, selector, ownership and rename tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - `providers/refresh-context-window` success needs a live provider, so only its not-found refusal is pinned by a golden.
  - The cross-process `zeroclaw acp` race above is not tested.
- **Golden design:** the fixture config and one JSON file per method live in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/tests/fixtures/config_parity/`. Runtime tests (`parity_golden_*`) dispatch the RPC method; gateway tests (`parity_golden_*` in `api_config.rs`) call the HTTP handler; both must equal the same file. Covered goldens:
  - reload-status
  - drift
  - agent-options
  - section-picker (plus its direct-form refusal)
  - section-select (agent and memory)
  - delete-plan
  - map-key-delete cascade (resulting state)
  - init
  - migrate
  - config/get (masked projection)
  - refresh-context-window (not-found)
- **Authorization tests** (roster principals with scoped grants):
  - **Section-select:** refused outside the selector with nothing scaffolded; succeeds inside it.
  - **Aliased deletes:** an alias delete, and a provider-model alias delete, are refused when the scrub touches a path outside the selector, including when the grant narrows while the request waits for the lock.
  - **Agent delete:** refused for a scoped caller while another principal owns a session on the agent (that session and its transcript survive); refused when such a session appears while the delete waits; succeeds for a scoped caller that owns every session. It's refused on a hard reference and while an RPC session runs, and succeeds for an admin (reference scrubbed, workspace archived).
  - **Agent rename:** refused when the cascade rewrites a reference outside the selector (nothing written, no policy published, no workspace moved); succeeds with that path granted. Provider rename is refused when it rewrites an agent's provider outside the selector.
  - **Other methods:** init refused outside the selector; migrate refused for a path-scoped grant; refresh-context-window refused outside its target path before any fetch.
  - **Effect verbs:** a Create-only principal cannot change an existing `memory.backend` through section-select, leaving memory and disk unchanged; granting Update lets it through.
  - **Point of effect:**
    - A provider rename, and a provider `config/set`, parked after live-session preparation are refused when the connection's paired bearer is revoked during the wait. Released without a revocation, the same parked rename lands.
    - A write parked at its commit after every file wait (the synced temporary file and backup are on disk) is refused when the bearer is revoked there. The canonical file, live config and policy revision are unchanged, and no temporary or backup file is left behind.
    - A revocation issued while a write is inside its commit (authority passed, rename pending) does not complete until the rename is done, and then binds the connection's next write.
    - Quickstart revoked before its rename writes nothing. Revoked after its rename, it reports and publishes the committed result, so disk and live config agree.
  - **HTTP:** a scoped OIDC principal cannot delete an agent while another principal owns a session on it.
  - **Error data:** a refusal sent through the real dispatcher carries `error.data.code` and `error.data.path`.
- **Mutation checks:**
  - Removing the ownership predicate fails the RPC foreign-session tests and the HTTP test.
  - Removing only the post-lock recheck fails the test where the foreign session appears while the delete waits.
  - Removing the rename's dirty-set recheck fails the refused-rename test.
  - Removing the per-effect verb check fails the Create-only section-select test.
  - Removing the boundary recheck fails both revoked-during-preparation tests.
  - Removing the gate's recheck at the replacement fails the after-file-waits and Quickstart-before-rename tests.
  - Releasing the paired-token set before the rename (a check without ordering) fails the racing-revocation test.
  - Rechecking Quickstart after its commit fails the after-rename test.
- **Commands run and tail output** (affected crates only, at the head this body describes):
  ```
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: FAILED. 5321 passed; 2 failed; 8 ignored
    (one failure is session_prompt_waits_for_queued_provider_update_transaction, a 5-second timeout
     in a 96-second loaded run; it passes on its own, and effect classification adds about 15 ms
     per debug-build write)
    (the one failure is forwarded_environment_demotion_while_queued_refuses_prompt_and_resume,
     a master test whose temp-dir workspace check trips on macOS /var -> /private/var; it passes on Linux CI)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway
  test result: ok. 633 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
  test result: ok. 1753 passed; 0 failed
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                  # clean
  scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh          # Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read every blessed golden:
  - the provider api key is `***MASKED***`
  - delete-plan lists `heartbeat.agent` as a soft scrub
  - the cascade leaves only `helper`

  I did not run a live daemon end to end.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide clippy and builds were not run, to keep build disk use bounded; CI `Lint` covers clippy. `cargo test --workspace` is not used in this repo.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. Nine RPC methods, each with a `Method::authz()` arm. Writes authorize their persisted dirty set on grants re-resolved under the config write lock. Migrate requires whole-config authority. Agent delete is limited to admins, unscoped callers, or a scoped caller that owns every session on the agent.
- New external network calls? Yes. `providers/refresh-context-window` exposes over RPC the provider fetch HTTP already makes. Both surfaces authorize the context-window path before the fetch, which sends the profile's stored credentials.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The api key is still read only to pass to the provider fetch, and `config/get` stays masked (pinned by a golden).
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The fixture api key is a placeholder.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** Mostly. HTTP paths and response shapes are unchanged. Behaviour changes:
  - **HTTP agent delete:** a scoped principal is refused while another principal owns an ACP session on the agent. The owned-state cleanup now runs under the config write lock. Only ended ACP sessions are deleted, and a live one found during cleanup is reported. Memory rows and cron jobs are not purged when their export was not archived.
  - **HTTP migrate:** rewrites the file and flags a reload, but no longer installs the raw parsed file as the live config. That parse skipped secret decryption and env overrides; the loader already migrates in memory.
  - **HTTP refresh-context-window and section-select:** both authorize before their first side effect (the provider fetch, or the workspace scaffold).
  - **RPC `config/map-key-delete` on aliased sections:** now runs the cascade, refuses on hard references and live sessions, applies the ownership rule above, and may return `warnings`.
  - **RPC error responses:** now include `data` when the handler sets it.
  - **RPC config write verbs:** each write now needs the Config verb of each effect, not only the method's. For example, a `config/set` that brings a new map key into being needs Create, and selecting a memory or tunnel backend needs Update (plus Create on the section, as over HTTP).
  - **RPC config saves:** every save rechecks the caller's credential and grants at the canonical replacement, after every wait. A save refused there leaves the file untouched.
  - **Quickstart over RPC:** a write that took effect is reported as applied and published, including when a later personality-file step fails, where live config used to stay stale.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `alias deleted with config-ref cascade` / `agent deleted with owned-state cascade` log lines with non-zero warnings
  - RPC or HTTP `FORBIDDEN` on config writes that previously succeeded because a cascade or rename touched an ungranted path
  - `owned by other principals` refusals on agent delete

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
Phase 3: The Gateway. Separate the web surface from the agent core so the gateway is optional and can restart independently.

Source of truth: [#7432 - v0.9.0 gateway](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432#v090-gateway), including existing issues/PRs, missing work, sequencing, and acceptance evidence.

Deliverables: agree the full core IPC contract first; finish the supported local IPC server; ship standalone zeroclaw-gw; migrate vendor webhook behavior into channel plugins; and have Tauri package and manage both processes.

Completion requires a core artifact without web assets or HTTP server code, a working IPC-connected gateway, core/channel operation when the gateway is absent, and demonstrated two-process desktop lifecycle. Existing OIDC, principal-isolation, and ZeroRelay work must integrate with this boundary. WATI is already retired. Feature acceptance and normal review/CI/release holds still apply.

prs.title: feat(rpc): SOP parity for cancel, dispatch-event, decision-models and graph-legend
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** As part of the v0.9.0 gateway split, this PR adds the RPC methods the gateway will call once it moves out of process. The daemon RPC surface gains the SOP operations it was missing next to the gateway's HTTP routes. `sops/decide` also stops treating a client-supplied label as the approver's identity.
  - **`sops/decide` by run id, with the real principal.** `name` is now optional; the run id selects the run, and a `name` that is given must be the run's SOP. The approver the group-approval policy sees now comes from the connection's authentication. It used to be `ApprovalPrincipal::cli(tui_id)`, and the TUI id is client-supplied (accepted unsigned when TUI signing is off) and "grants no authority" by the dispatcher's own rule. That meant a claimed TUI id could satisfy a bare or `cli:` group member. The new mapping:
    - **Native pairing bearer:** the paired-token subject, exactly what the gateway's HTTP and WebSocket routes derive from the same token. `http:<subject>` members match, and one token is one quorum voter on every surface. The ledger's channel records `rpc`.
    - **Any other authenticated principal** (a `[users]` entry, an OIDC subject): a new `principal` approval source keyed on the canonical principal id, so members name it `principal:<id>` or bare.
    - **The unauthenticated shared operator:** anonymous, like `zeroclaw sop approve`. It cannot satisfy a `required_group`.
    - The approver's entitlement to the run's agents, checked before the decision reaches the broker, is checked again on freshly resolved grants under the lock that resolves the decision.
  - **`sops/cancel`** `{run_id, name?, reason?}`: the gateway's safe cancel (the step in flight finishes, and the run stops at the next boundary). It's idempotent (`outcome`: `requested`, `already_requested`, `cancelled` or `already_terminal`) and attributes the cancellation to the same principal. A scoped principal must be entitled to the run's agents, and that is checked again on freshly resolved grants once the lock that cancels is held, so a grant or agent entitlement withdrawn while the request waited for the engine cannot cancel. A run whose procedure is no longer loaded is refused for a scoped principal rather than passed.
  - **`sops/dispatch-event`** `{path, payload?}`: the webhook fan-in behind `POST /sop/{*rest}`. The caller keeps authenticating the delivery and applying idempotency, as the HTTP route does today. A scoped principal must be entitled to every matched procedure's agents, and that is checked where the run starts, not only when the call arrives. A preflight refuses early, matching on the topic as dispatch normalizes it, so a path that differs from a trigger only in characters the normalization removes (a zero-width space, say) cannot match nothing at the preflight and a forbidden procedure at dispatch. The enforcing check runs at run admission: after any decision-model wait, on the normalized match set, under the engine lock that starts the run, against freshly re-resolved grants. A grant or agent entitlement withdrawn while a decision model deliberates starts nothing, and a call whose every match is refused there returns `FORBIDDEN`. Each run that starts on an agent step is handed to a headless driver that holds the daemon's live configuration and reads it at each step's execution boundary: after the decision wait, the driver lease, generation admission and every engine lock the step takes, with nothing that waits between that read and the owner check, the tool policy and the turn. An agent disabled or re-profiled at any point before a step runs is not run under its former settings. The fan-in core (driver admission and result shaping) moves into `zeroclaw-runtime` as `sop::dispatch_webhook_event`, and the gateway route now calls it, so the two surfaces cannot drift.
  - **`sops/decision-models`** and **`sops/graph-legend`**: the two read-only authoring lookups. Decision models come from a shared `sop::decision_model_options`, also used by the gateway route (it never lists an API key).
- **Scope boundary:** The `sops/subscribe-runs` stream belongs to separate work on the subscription hub, so there are no run-change notifications or `seq` here. There's no new service principal and no change to who may call these methods beyond the existing `sops` grant classification. The gateway's own `decide` and `cancel` routes keep their current identity derivation. Idempotency for webhook deliveries stays in the gateway; moving it is outside this PR.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: `Method` gains four variants (compile-forced `authz` arms). The SOP approval principal gains a `Principal` source and three RPC constructors. The ledger's vote replay learns the `principal` label. There's a new `sop::surface` module. `sop::dispatch_webhook_event` takes the live configuration handle rather than a `Config`. The headless driver entry points accept a `SopDriverConfig`: `Snapshot`, built from a `Config` as every other caller still passes, or `Live`, which the driver reads once per step at the step's execution boundary. The RPC agent selector and SOP agent checks gain grant-parametric forms, so admission and the rechecks run one predicate. `SopIngress` gains an optional run-admission check (`with_admission_check`), and `ContentSafety::normalize_topic` and `sop::dispatch::untrusted_topic_matches` expose the topic normalization dispatch already applied, so an authorization preflight matches the same form.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: `SopDecideRequest.name` becomes `Option<String>` (wire-compatible; no in-tree struct literals). There are new `SopCancelRequest` and `SopDispatchEventRequest` types.
  - `zeroclaw-gateway`: the `/sop/*` webhook handler and the decision-models route call the shared runtime helpers, with no response change. The webhook handler passes its live configuration handle, so its drivers read the configuration when each step runs.
  - Docs: the approval-identity section of `sop/syntax.md`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11001 (matching gateway behavior over RPC), Related #11000, Related #8289.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `size:XL` (labeler-applied; `risk:*` is left for a maintainer).

### What this does, simply

The gateway is going to become a separate process that talks to the daemon over its RPC socket, so every SOP action the dashboard can take has to exist as an RPC method first. Four were missing: cancelling a run, delivering a webhook event, listing decision models, and fetching the graph legend. This PR adds them.

It also closes a trust gap in approving an SOP checkpoint over RPC. The daemon recorded the approver as whatever TUI id the client presented, and approval groups could match on that label, so a client could claim to be someone on the approver list. Now the approver is whoever the connection actually authenticated as: the same paired device the web dashboard would see, or the signed-in user. A connection that never authenticated can't satisfy a policy that requires a group.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The identity change is observable with one paired token and a policy-gated checkpoint.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (daemon RPC).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an SOP whose first step is a checkpoint with `policy: prod`; `[sop.approval.policies.prod] required_group = "release"`; `[sop.approval.groups.release] members = ["http:<sha256 of your paired token>"]`; and `gateway.paired_tokens` containing that token.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Start a run of the SOP (it parks at the checkpoint).
  2. Over the RPC socket, `initialize` with `auth_token` = the paired token, then `sops/decide {"run_id": "<id>", "decision": "approve"}` with no `name`.
  3. Repeat step 2 from a connection that is not paired, presenting `tui_id` = `ZeroClawOperator`, with `"ZeroClawOperator"` added to the group.
  4. `sops/cancel {"run_id": "<id of a second parked run>"}`, twice.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** step 2 resumes the run. Step 3 is refused with `-32010` and the run stays parked. Step 4 reports `outcome: "cancelled"` and then `outcome: "already_terminal"`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** step 2 is refused (`name` is required, and the approver is `cli:<tui id>`, which is not in the group). Step 3 clears the gate on a claimed label. `sops/cancel` does not exist.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` on the head. Test covers the runtime `rpc::`/`sop::` suites and the gateway suite, including the existing `/sop/*` webhook route tests that now run through the shared helper.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for the changed surface. No zerocode change, because zerocode already sends `name`, which is still accepted.
- **Commands run and tail output (local, Rust 1.96.1, at e69451ead6 on master 4f93bf5399):**

```
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets
Finished `dev` profile (clean)
$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets
(no findings in the files this PR changes)
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop rpc:: security::external_content
test result: ok. 1485 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
(one earlier run of this suite timed out in session_prompt_waits_for_queued_provider_update_transaction,
a session test this PR does not touch; it passed alone five times and in the full rerun above)
$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-api
test result: ok. 277 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 621 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
```

  New tests: sops_decide_sees_the_paired_subject_the_gateway_sees, sops_decide_counts_one_paired_credential_as_one_voter, sops_decide_sees_the_authenticated_roster_principal, sops_decide_ignores_a_claimed_tui_id, sops_decide_checks_a_named_sop_against_the_run, sops_cancel_is_idempotent_by_run_id, sops_dispatch_event_starts_webhook_sops, sops_dispatch_event_authorizes_the_normalized_topic, the five sop_run_start_* admission tests, the seven sop_driver_* configuration tests, the three sops_cancel_*_while_waiting_for_the_engine_* tests, the two sops_decide_*_while_waiting_for_the_engine_* tests, sops_decision_models_and_graph_legend_serve_the_gateway_shapes, sops_parity_methods_are_classified, principal::rpc_paired_subject_is_the_same_voter_as_the_gateway, principal::rpc_principals_are_keyed_by_their_canonical_id, surface::decision_models_are_sorted_and_carry_no_key, and dispatch::untrusted_topic_matches_uses_the_normalized_topic.

  With the fixes reverted, the tests that guard them fail and their controls pass. Without the admission check and with a raw-topic preflight, the revoked, narrowed and reowned admission tests, the normalized-topic test and the helper test fail. Without the cancel and decide rechecks and with the driver configuration read before dispatch, the revoked and narrowed cancel tests, the revoked decide test, and the disabled-owner and changed-policy driver tests fail, while the unchanged cancel, decide and driver controls pass. The driver's configuration read is pinned to the step boundary: handing the driver a copy when the dispatch returns fails the step-boundary and admission-wait tests, and reading the configuration once when the driver starts fails the step-boundary tests; the decision-wait tests and every control pass under both.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Pinned by tests:
  - A paired device in the group clears a checkpoint by run id alone, and a paired device outside it is refused, with the run left parked.
  - One paired token voting twice does not meet a quorum of two, and a second member's token does.
  - A roster user named as `principal:<id>` clears the gate, and another roster user does not.
  - A claimed TUI id matching both a bare and a `cli:` member is refused.
  - A named SOP that is not the run's is refused.
  - Cancel is idempotent and refuses an unknown run or the wrong SOP.
  - A webhook path starts its SOP; an unmatched path reports `no_match`; an empty path is refused.
  - A dispatch parked at its decision model starts no run when, during the wait, the caller loses `sops:execute`, its agent entitlement is narrowed away from the procedure's agent, or the procedure is redefined to a forbidden agent. The same wait with the policy unchanged or widened starts the run, so re-resolution is proven, not a blanket refusal.
  - A webhook path carrying a zero-width character that normalizes to another agent's trigger is refused, and no run starts.
  - The procedure's agent disabled in the live configuration while the dispatch is parked at its decision model, while the dispatch waits to admit its driver into the generation, or while the driver is parked at the step's execution boundary (after every wait it makes): the run starts, but the driver refuses the disabled agent and no turn runs. A risk profile replaced at the decision or at the step boundary is the one the step policy is built from, and an unchanged configuration runs as the configured owner.
  - A `sops/cancel` waiting on the engine lock while the caller's `sops:execute` grant is withdrawn, or its agent selector narrowed away from the run's agent, is refused and leaves the run, its cancellation record and its claim untouched; with nothing changed it cancels.
  - A `sops/decide` approval waiting on the engine lock while the caller's `sops:execute` grant is withdrawn is refused and the run stays parked; with nothing changed it resumes the run.
  - Decision models never list an API key, and the graph legend serves the canonical legend through the full request path.

  NOT verified: an OIDC-authenticated principal end to end (it takes the same `rpc_principal` branch as the roster user, keyed on `Principal.id`), and a live daemon. The tests use the in-process dispatcher.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No rendered interface changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace check and clippy, and the full workspace test suite. CI runs them; the changed crates were checked with `--all-targets` and their suites run locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The four methods use the existing `sops` grant classification: `read` for the two lookups, `execute` for cancel and dispatch-event, matching `sops/run` and `sops/decide`. Scoped principals are held to the agent selector of every procedure they act on.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes, narrowing. The approval identity on RPC now comes from the authenticated connection. A native bearer contributes only its SHA-256 subject, which the connection already retained for revocation checks; the bearer itself is never stored. A client-claimed TUI id no longer reaches the approval broker.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. `sops/dispatch-event` payloads enter the same untrusted fan-in path the HTTP webhook route already uses.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: covered above.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Wire: yes. `name` stays accepted on `sops/decide`, and the new methods are additive. Behavior: a `sops/cancel` or `sops/decide` whose caller lost the needed authority while it waited for the SOP engine is refused. A `sops/dispatch-event` call accepted into decision evaluation can now be refused with `FORBIDDEN` if the caller's authority over the matched procedure is gone by the time the run would be admitted. An approval-group member that matched only a TUI id (a bare label or `cli:<tui id>`) no longer matches over RPC. That match was never an authenticated identity, and the docs already said the CLI path is anonymous. Operators name the paired-token subject (`http:<subject>`) or the principal (`principal:<id>`) instead. Rust source: `SopDecideRequest.name` is now `Option<String>`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: replace any approval-group member that named a TUI id with the approver's paired-token subject or `principal:<id>`, as described in the updated `sop/syntax.md`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of this PR's squash commit. Votes recorded with the new `principal` source are not recognised by an older binary's quorum replay, so after a rollback they stop counting toward a pending quorum (fail closed, the gate stays waiting). Re-approve from a surface the older binary recognises.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a policy-gated `sops/decide` over RPC refused with `-32010` for an approver who should qualify. Check that the group names `http:<subject>` for a paired device or `principal:<id>` for a signed-in user, and that the connection authenticated as that identity (`initialize` reports `principal_id`). A `/sop/*` webhook response differing from before would indicate the shared helper diverged.
