prs.title: fix(config): migrate retired keys at schema version 4 and warn on a missing schema_version
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Credit:** this builds on @singlerider's #8754, opened 2026-07-06, which first identified these inert keys and proposed the move to schema version 4. Its still-valid retirements, its version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and its version 4 fixture and tests are carried forward here, with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the retirement commits. This PR also folds #11217, which reads an unversioned config in the version 3 format as version 3, and takes from @NiuBlibing's #9809 the shape of retiring a channel together with every reference to it.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11082 retired `[security.nevis]` but left `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at 3, so no migration ran. The table was discarded at load with a warning hidden unless `-v` was passed, and it stayed on disk with any plaintext `client_secret`. This PR bumps the schema to version 4 and adds a version 3 → version 4 step driven by a new `RETIRED_KEYS` table.
  - Each table entry names a key path, the version that retires it, whether it is removed or renamed, and the reason shown to the operator. A path segment `ANY_KEY` (`"*"`) matches every key at its level, so one entry retires a key in every `[agents.<alias>]` block or every runtime profile. Each concrete match is reported under its real path. A rename never overwrites an existing replacement, and a blocked rename creates no tables.
  - Retired keys are applied during migration and again on every load of a current-version config. A retired key that reappears in a version 4 file is dropped with a notice, not silently ignored by serde.
  - The same table also drives incremental saves. #11191 made `save_dirty` remove `[security.nevis]` from the on-disk document, since an incremental save rewrites only dirty paths and would otherwise carry a retired table and its secret forward. This PR replaces that Nevis-only helper with `apply_retired_keys_to_doc`, so `save_dirty` and migration share one retirement policy. Wildcard entries work there too, so the eight agent-inline tunables are removed from disk as well. The edit touches only retired keys, keeps comments and unrelated ciphertext byte for byte, and logs each removal only after the atomic write succeeds. #11191's tests are kept against the table-driven cleanup. A save first reads the version of the file on disk. A version 1 or version 2 file is not edited as it stands, because keys retired at version 3 (`[identity]`, an agent's `max_tool_iterations`) are still live inputs to its version 2 → version 3 step. An incremental save first carries the file on disk through the typed migration chain, then applies the dirty paths to the result, so those inputs are converted and keys another handle saved after this config loaded survive. A file whose version cannot be determined (an unversioned file of ambiguous shape) or is newer than this binary is refused by both save paths, so a load that fell back to defaults cannot relabel it and write over it.
  - Containers a retirement leaves empty follow one rule on both paths. A literal container such as `[security]` or `context_compression` is dropped. A table matched by a wildcard is an operator-named alias such as `[agents.coder]` and is always kept, so a reference to it never dangles. `toml_edit` writes nothing for an empty implicit or dotted table, so an alias that existed only as a prefix of retired dotted keys (`runtime_profiles.slow.context_compression.summary_model = …`) is written back as its own `[runtime_profiles.slow]` header, or as `slow = {}` inside an inline table.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate` edits a file at version 3 or later in place: from version 3, reaching version 4 only retires keys and re-stamps `schema_version`, so quoting, number spelling and comments on untouched lines keep their exact bytes. Older files still take the structural rebuild.
  - A `ZEROCLAW_*` environment override naming a retired key is ignored with a notice instead of failing startup as an unknown property.
  - Every change is a `MigrationNotice` carrying key paths and reasons only, never values. Notices print on stderr after every config load, with a line saying `zeroclaw config migrate` writes them. `config migrate` prints them itself and returns them in `--json`.
  - A config with no `schema_version` whose sections are plainly in the version 3 shape is read as version 3 (folded from #11217). That shape means at least one alias-keyed `providers.models.<family>` or `channels.<type>` section, none holding fields directly (the version 2 shape), and no version 1-only top-level key. The version is fixed at 3, not the current version, so the file still runs the version 3 → version 4 step; it reports an `InferredV3` notice telling the operator to run `zeroclaw config migrate`. The version 2 → version 3 filesystem relocation no longer runs for such a file. A version 2 entry whose only content is map-valued fields has the same shape: `[providers.models.openai.extra_headers]` is either the version 2 profile's headers or a version 3 alias named `extra_headers`. Each child table is checked against the real schema by reading the section as one entry and serializing it back; when a child also reads as a field, the file is refused with an error naming the section and asking for `schema_version = 2` or `3`, rather than choosing a reading that loses data. A version 2-only setting in a file otherwise in the version 3 format (a value directly under `[providers]`, or a key the version 2 → version 3 step moves off an agent, such as `provider` or `allowed_tools`) and an empty map-valued field make the shape ambiguous the same way. Any other unversioned config is still read as version 1, and that assumption now prints a warning instead of failing quietly. The version 1 migration reshapes sections written for a newer version. It folds hand-written channel aliases into `default`, the most likely cause of the "half my config is ignored" reports. Testing a real modern config with only its version line removed showed it also nests `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>]` one level too deep, stranding the model and URI. The warning names both effects.
  - Retired at version 4:
    - `[security.nevis]`, which was added in #3651 and never implemented. Its schema field, load shim and validation warning are deleted.
    - Eight agent-inline runtime tunables in every `[agents.<alias>]` (`compact_context`, `max_tool_iterations`, `max_history_messages`, `max_context_tokens`, `memory_recall_limit`, `parallel_tools`, `tool_dispatcher`, `strict_tool_parsing`). No agent field exists for them, so they were silently ignored; the runtime-profile copies are the live ones and are kept.
    - `runtime_profiles.*.context_compression.summary_model`. Only config diagnostics read it; its field and the two diagnostics about it are deleted.
    - `[node_transport]` (with its `shared_secret`) and the WATI sections `channels.wati` and `channels_config.wati` (with their `api_token`). These were retired earlier by code outside the table: the migration chain stripped `node_transport` silently between steps, and load only warned about WATI, so an incremental save wrote them and their secrets back. They are now table entries, and the bespoke detection, its load-only `Config` fields, load warnings, CLI prints and Fluent strings are removed; the table's notices report the same facts.
    - Top-level `[twitter]` and `[reddit]`, and `[channels.notion]`. No schema field reads any of them: Twitter and Reddit stay channels (`[channels.twitter.<alias>]`, `[channels.reddit.<alias>]`) and Notion stays the top-level `[notion]` tool section. `[channels.notion]` uses a new `RemoveChannel` retirement, which handles the references to the channel the way the `alias_refs` cascade does: matched after trimming, entries dropped from `[agents.<alias>] channels` and `[escalation] alert_channels`, and a `[peer_groups.<name>]` bound to it kept and reported, because the cascade treats that binding as hard and never deletes the group. Agent bindings are kept and reported too when dropping them would leave no binding anywhere, which would route every channel to the fallback agent. A test pins the reference sites and their strength to the cascade's, and `config migrate` does not rewrite a file for kept references alone. It runs wherever the table runs, including version 3 files migrated in place, current files on load, incremental saves and full saves (`save()` now applies the table to its output before the atomic replace, since a reference held in the typed config would otherwise be written back), so a later channel retirement gets the pruning with one table entry. A test asserts that no retirement names a current top-level section or a live channel type.
    - Keys the version 2 → version 3 step already drops but no current field reads, which a version 3 or later file could still hold: `gateway.pairing_dashboard.code_length`, `[swarms]`, `reliability.fallback_providers`, `reliability.model_fallbacks`, `tts.default_provider`, `transcription.default_provider`, `transcription.default_model_provider`, `transcription.default_transcription_provider` and a top-level `[identity]`. They are retired at version 3, so they apply only after the version 2 → version 3 step, which still moves `[identity]` into the agents first.
  - The one-time version 2 → version 3 filesystem relocation is pinned to the version 3 layout version. Without the pin, bumping to version 4 would re-run it on every version 3 install and move that install's workspace under a synthesized `default` alias.
  - A version 4 acceptance fixture, `fixtures/v4.toml`, is regenerated from this chain, and the round-trip test compares the generated text byte for byte.
- **Known limits:** `save_dirty` returns early when nothing is dirty, so a config nobody edits keeps its retired keys on disk until a full save or `zeroclaw config migrate`. Every load still drops them from the running config and prints the warning. Separately, `save_dirty` still runs the pre-existing `ensure_blank_line_before_sections` pass over the whole file; it is not TOML-aware, so it can add a blank line inside a multiline string that contains a line starting with `[`. That predates this PR and is not changed here.
- **Scope boundary:** This establishes the mechanism. The inert-key audit found 259 runtime-inert leaf patterns; the rest are not retired here, and `RETIRED_KEYS` is the vehicle for them, one entry each. Not ported from #8754, because master still reads them: `skills.prompt_injection_mode`, which is the fallback for each agent's effective skills mode, `runtime_profiles.*.prompt_injection_mode`, the twelve top-level tool sections (`composio`, `microsoft365`, `project_intel`, `google_workspace`, `linkedin`, `jira`, `notion`, `claude_code`, `claude_code_runner`, `codex_cli`, `gemini_cli`, `opencode_cli`) and the twitter and reddit channels. Their features stay on master. They can be retired in version 4 as `RETIRED_KEYS` entries in the change that removes their code, before this release ships, and `RemoveChannel` covers the two channels. ADR-017 still mentions Nevis users in an acceptance gate and is unchanged. This supersedes the version 4 step in #8754 and the version 3 → version 4 and version 4 → version 5 steps in #9809, whose multi-model shape is additive and needs no step. The schema stays at version 4. This PR also generalizes #11191's incremental-save cleanup, on which it is rebased.
- **Blast radius:** Every existing install. Version 3 configs migrate to version 4 in memory on load, silently unless a retired key is present. `config set`, `config init`, `config patch` and `models set` refuse until `zeroclaw config migrate` has run once, as with every earlier schema bump. Fixtures, dev templates, `demo/config.toml`, the k8s sample and the `Containerfile` default config move to `schema_version = 4`, and so do the `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.debian` default configs, `demo/zeroclaw.toml.example` and the Nix module template (from #11217, which declared them at 3).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11082. Builds on #11191. Related #8754. Folds #11217. Related #9809. Related #3651. Related #6877.
- **Labels:** to be snapshotted after the path and size labelers run. Config is a `risk:high` surface.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's config file carries a version number, so that when a setting is removed an upgrade can rewrite old files and say what it changed. Several settings had been removed without that happening, so they were quietly ignored. Some had been ignored from the start, like tuning knobs written under an agent instead of under its runtime profile. This PR adds a list of retired settings. The upgrade removes each one it finds and prints a plain warning saying why and what to use instead. One entry can cover a setting under every agent or every profile. The first entries are the removed Nevis login block, eight agent knobs that never did anything, and an old summary-model setting. A config file with no version number is no longer read as the oldest version when it is plainly written in the current shape, which used to silently merge your named channels into one called `default`. It warns either way.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** An empty temp directory used as `HOME` and `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Write a `schema_version = 4` config with `[agents.coder]` holding `runtime_profile = "fast"` and `max_tool_iterations = 40`, `[runtime_profiles.fast]` holding `max_tool_iterations = 12`, and `[runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression]` holding `summary_model = "haiku"`.
  2. Run `zeroclaw config get runtime_profiles.fast.max_tool_iterations` without `-v`.
  3. Run `zeroclaw config migrate --json`, inspect `config.toml`, then repeat step 2.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 2 prints `12` and warns that `agents.coder.max_tool_iterations` and `runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression.summary_model` were dropped, with reasons. Step 3 lists both notices, removes both keys from the file, and the repeat is silent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 2 prints `12` and nothing else. Step 3 reports nothing to migrate, and both dead keys stay.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint` (clippy `-D warnings`) and `Test`, which runs the config crate's unit and migration suites, the i18n tests and the component tests whose fixtures moved to version 4.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on head `3f047c33d5`, on master `e3775540d1` (merges cleanly with `e16fd898ba`):

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(exit 0)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1810 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 106 passed; 0 failed      (migration integration, incl. the V4 fixture and real-config tests)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
(exit 0)

$ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p zeroclaw-config --no-deps
(exit 0)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- i18n
test result: ok. 44 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo check -p zeroclaw --bins
(exit 0)

$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
```

  Also at this head: `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean, the gateway migrate tests, the i18n tests (44 passed) and `cargo check -p zeroclaw --bins`. The earlier run on `b81f88df11` also covered `zeroclaw-macros` tests and clippy for the gateway, channels, plugins and `zeroclaw` crates with Rust 1.98; this revision changes none of those crates except `src/main.rs`, which was checked above.

- **Incremental-save tests:** `save_dirty_removes_retired_nevis_table_from_disk` (the plaintext secret does not survive), `save_dirty_removes_retired_agent_tunables_from_disk` (wildcard entries, alias and live keys kept), `save_dirty_nevis_success_is_logged_only_after_atomic_replace`, `save_removes_retired_nevis_table_from_disk` and `retired_key_doc_cleanup_handles_every_nevis_spelling`. With the `save_dirty` hook disabled, the first three fail.
- **Review regression tests:** `doc_cleanup_keeps_aliases_in_every_toml_spelling`, `config_migrate_keeps_aliases_in_every_toml_spelling`, `structural_migration_keeps_an_emptied_dotted_alias_rendered` and `save_dirty_keeps_an_alias_emptied_through_dotted_keys` (aliases survive dotted, dotted-inline, inline and header-dotted spellings, and reload); `node_transport_and_wati_are_retired_on_every_path` and `save_dirty_removes_sections_retired_outside_v4_with_their_secrets` (no path or secret sentinel survives load, migrate or an unrelated incremental save at version 3 and version 4); `v3_migration_changes_only_the_version_line` and `retirement_migration_keeps_untouched_bytes` (byte-exact output with single quotes, `42_617`, `1e1`, `0x50` and trailing comments). Each fails with its fix reverted.
- **Catalog-completeness tests:** `retired_dashboard_code_length_is_removed_on_every_path`, `keys_dropped_by_the_v3_step_are_retired_on_every_path`, `save_dirty_removes_retired_dashboard_code_length` and `save_dirty_removes_keys_the_v3_step_retired` (migrate, load, document cleanup and an unrelated incremental save at version 3 and version 4, keeping the live sibling settings), and `a_v2_config_still_lifts_its_identity_into_agents`.
- **Real-config tests:** the migration integration suite runs the checked-in dev template three ways. Unchanged, it is not rewritten. With one retired key of each shape added, only those keys are removed and reported, comments survive, and a second migration is a no-op. With its `schema_version` line removed, it is read as version 3 with the inferred-version notice rather than as version 1, and the resilient load resets no section.
- **Unversioned-file and channel-retirement tests:** `a_plainly_v3_file_without_the_key_is_read_as_v3`, `an_inferred_v3_file_is_migrated_to_v4_and_keeps_every_channel_alias` (aliases kept on load, `config migrate` and the resilient load), `an_inferred_v3_file_still_loses_its_retired_keys`, `an_explicit_version_is_never_reported_as_inferred`, the version 1-reading cases (version 2 shape, version 1-only key, no alias-keyed section, the bundled version 1 fixture) and `v1_keys_still_current_are_exactly_the_current_top_level_sections`. `v3_to_v4_retires_top_level_twitter_and_reddit_but_not_the_channels` and `v3_to_v4_retires_the_notion_channel_with_every_reference_to_it` run a version 3 fixture through both the value chain and the in-place migration, checking the pruned agent channel lists, the dropped peer group, the kept telegram references and the comment on an untouched section. `notion_references_are_pruned_from_a_current_file_in_every_spelling` covers a version 4 file with dotted and inline tables. `a_retirement_never_names_a_key_the_schema_still_reads` guards the table. `a_map_only_v2_provider_profile_requires_an_explicit_version` (with version 2 and version 3 stated, each keeping its data), `a_map_only_v2_channel_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_ordinary_v2_profile_with_a_map_field_keeps_the_v1_reading`, `a_v3_alias_named_like_a_field_is_ambiguous_only_if_it_fits_the_field` and `a_schema_version_beyond_u32_is_refused_not_wrapped` cover the inference edges. `save_removes_retired_channel_references_from_a_new_file`, `save_removes_retired_channel_references_from_an_existing_file` and `save_dirty_on_a_missing_file_removes_retired_channel_references` check the written file and its reload, with the live telegram references kept. With the probe, the full-save pass or the checked cast removed, these seven fail and the ordinary version 2 and clearly version 3 controls pass.
- **Cross-review regression tests:** `save_dirty_over_a_v2_file_migrates_it_before_editing` (identity and the agent's iteration limit survive, as does a key another handle saved after load; version 2 original kept), `saves_refuse_a_file_of_unknown_or_newer_version`, `the_first_save_over_a_v3_file_keeps_it`, `config_migrate_keeps_the_pre_upgrade_original`, `an_env_override_for_a_retired_key_is_ignored_not_fatal`, `retiring_a_channel_keeps_the_last_agent_binding`, `channel_reference_sites_match_the_alias_cascade`, `a_v2_only_setting_beside_v3_sections_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_empty_map_field_still_makes_the_shape_ambiguous`, `v2_only_agent_keys_are_not_v3_agent_fields` and the gateway's `migration_reports_its_notices`. With each fix removed, the eight tests guarding them fail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a debug build with an isolated temp `HOME`: the three steps above; a version 3 config with `[security.nevis]` and a `client_secret` (the secret is gone from `config.toml` and kept only in the backups); a version 4 config that still holds `[security.nevis]`; and a config with no `schema_version`. Every warning appeared without `-v`, and every second load was silent.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `zeroclaw` CLI stderr, locale `en`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
$ zeroclaw config get runtime_profiles.fast.max_tool_iterations
12
warning: dropped retired config key `agents.coder.max_tool_iterations` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: agent-inline runtime tunables were never read; runtime profiles are authoritative, so set this key on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]` instead
warning: dropped retired config key `runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression.summary_model` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: the deprecated bare model id had no provider identity and was never read; `summary_provider` replaced it (context compression itself is not currently implemented in the runtime)
warning: these changes apply to this run only. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` to write them to <tmp>/cfg/config.toml.
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** As above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Clippy for `zeroclaw-runtime` ran on `--lib` only; its `--all-targets` run stops on a pre-existing unused-import lint in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` (macOS test build, from #10931). This PR touches only that crate's Fluent files.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `zeroclaw config migrate` now removes `[security.nevis]` from disk, including any plaintext `client_secret`; before, it stayed indefinitely. The backups still hold it: `config.toml.backup`, and the pre-upgrade copy `config.toml.v3.backup` described under Rollback. The migration guide tells operators to delete the backup; it should now name both copies. Notices carry key paths and reasons only, never values; a unit test asserts this. The pinned filesystem relocation removes a risk this bump would otherwise have introduced: re-running the version 2 → version 3 workspace move on version 3 installs.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - After upgrading, run `zeroclaw config migrate` once. Until then configs load normally, migrated in memory, but `config set`, `config init`, `config patch` and `models set` refuse, as with every earlier schema bump.
  - `[security.nevis]`, the eight agent-inline tunables and `summary_model` are no longer config keys. Set tunables on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]`; configure `[oidc.<alias>]` with `[users]` and `[permission_profiles]` in place of Nevis.
  - A config with no `schema_version` prints a warning on every command until it has one. One plainly in the version 3 shape is read as version 3 rather than version 1, so its channel aliases and provider entries are no longer reshaped.
  - Top-level `[twitter]` and `[reddit]` and `[channels.notion]` are dropped, as are agent channel and escalation entries naming a `notion` channel. A peer group bound to one is kept with a notice, as is an agent's last channel binding; `Config::validate` reports both as dangling until the operator fixes them.
  - A save over a config whose version cannot be determined, or that is newer than this binary, now fails instead of writing over it. A `ZEROCLAW_*` variable naming a retired key is ignored with a notice.
  - An unversioned config whose shape reads both as version 2 and as version 3 is refused until `schema_version` is added. A `schema_version` past the `u32` range is refused as newer than the binary instead of being narrowed.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate --json` gains a `notices` array.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits. #11191's Nevis-only save cleanup then returns with it. A config already migrated to `schema_version = 4` is then newer than the binary supports. A version 4 body is a subset of version 3, so setting it back to `schema_version = 3` by hand works; to restore the file as it was, use `config.toml.v3.backup` (or `.v1`/`.v2`). This binary writes that copy the first time it rewrites a file of that version, through `config migrate`, the dashboard's migrate, or a save, and never replaces it. `config.toml.backup` is not a reliable rollback copy: each `config migrate` replaces it, including a later retirement-only one of a version 4 file. The dashboard migrate's `config.toml.bak` is replaced by the next save.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** An unexpected `dropped retired config key` or `moved retired config key` line on stderr for a key that is still in use. `config migrate --json` shows the same entries under `notices`.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #8754 by @singlerider (its version 4 step and its still-valid retirements); #9809 by @NiuBlibing (its version 3 → version 4 and version 4 → version 5 steps only; the multi-model provider change stays in #9809); #11217 by @JordanTheJet (folded here).
- Scope materially carried forward: the inert agent-tunable and `summary_model` retirements, the version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and the version 4 acceptance fixture and its tests.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? Yes

prs.title: fix(agents): share durable committed-rename recovery across CLI, gateway, and RPC
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - An agent rename commits its config change before the workspace, memory, cron, ACP, and session state follow. A failure in between stranded that state under the old alias: the CLI could not resume (it reported the old alias as not configured), gateway and RPC resumed only through surface-local probes that read an unreadable store as clean, and a new agent created under the old alias inherited whatever was left.
  - Adds a durable recovery journal, `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` (`zeroclaw_config::agent_recovery_journal`), with a sidecar lock, atomic writes, and fail-closed reads. A record is written before the config commit and removed only after every follower is verified converged.
  - Adds one runtime-owned contract, `zeroclaw_runtime::agent_rename_recovery`, that gateway, daemon RPC, and CLI all run: validate both aliases before any path is derived, resolve the request against live config and the journal, arm the record, commit, converge the followers, re-probe, clear. Followers probe before they act, never create a store, and treat an unreadable store as unfinished work.
  - Refuses to create or reuse an alias retired by an unfinished rename at the two config-layer places an agent alias comes into existence (`alias_refs::create_map_key_checked` and the property-path auto-create), so CLI `agents create`, `config set|patch|init`, gateway map-key/section/prop/PATCH, RPC create/set, quickstart, and the agent-facing model routing tool are all covered. Deleting or renaming the pending target is refused too, and the delete previews report the same refusal.
  - Runs inside the lifecycle coordinator that just landed: the per-alias leases, the non-cancellable lifecycle job, channel-generation retirement, and CLI daemon routing are unchanged; the recovery contract replaces the rename follower cascade inside that job.
  - Fixes rename bugs found on the way: the memory follower was not retry-safe (a second `rename_agent` dropped an empty destination identity row or refused to merge), the cron residue probe ignored run-history ownership, the resume branch derived paths from unvalidated aliases, and restored ACP sessions kept the old default workspace as their working directory.
  - Adds `zeroclaw agents rename <old> <new> --abandon` as the explicit way out of a rename that cannot finish; it lists the state that stays under the old alias before dropping the record.
- **Scope boundary:** Followers are the default per-alias workspace, memory attribution, cron ownership (jobs and run history), ACP sessions (owner and persisted working directory), and session attribution. Not moved by a rename today and out of scope: control-plane task rows (delegate and peer-inbox), SOP and permission-profile references, parked SOP runs, and the cost ledger; each needs separate follow-up. Knowledge-graph ownership is not on `master`. Delete recovery for a custom workspace is #10149. An agent added through an environment override or a hand edit of `config.toml` is not refused; config load logs a warning for it.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (journal, create guards, protected runtime file names), `zeroclaw-runtime` (contract, path classifier, cron probe, RPC rename and delete), `zeroclaw-infra` (ACP and session store probes), `zeroclaw-memory` (factory path accessor), `zeroclaw-gateway` (rename, delete, delete plan), `zeroclaw-tools` (model routing tool), the CLI (`agents rename|create|delete`, `config set|init|patch`), docs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #10373. Related #10149, #9745. Builds on the lifecycle coordinator from #10621.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `memory`, `cli`, `tool`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

### What this does, simply

Renaming an agent moves its files and records to the new name after the config change is saved. If a move failed, the rest stayed under the old name, the command line could not finish the job, and a new agent created with the old name quietly took the leftovers over. Now every rename writes down what it is doing before it starts, any interface can finish it by running the same rename again, and the old name is not handed out again until everything has moved or the operator explicitly abandons the rename.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw agents rename|create|delete`), gateway `POST /api/config/rename-map-key` and `POST /api/config/map-key`, daemon RPC `config/map-key-rename`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config with an agent `agent_a` that has a default workspace containing a file, a cron job, and some memory.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Make the destination unwritable, for example create a regular file at `<install>/agents/agent_b`.
  2. `zeroclaw agents rename agent_a agent_b`: the config commits, the command exits non-zero and names the workspace follower.
  3. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: refused, naming the rename to re-run.
  4. Remove the blocking file and re-run step 2: exits 0, the workspace, cron job, and memory are under `agent_b`, and `<data_dir>/agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` is gone.
  5. `zeroclaw agents create agent_a`: succeeds, and the new agent owns none of the old state.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** as above. Gateway and RPC answer the failed rename with `renamed: true` plus warnings, and the CLI can finish a rename the gateway started.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** step 4 fails with "agents.agent_a is not configured", and step 3 succeeds, adopting the stranded workspace.

### How I tested

- **Head under test:** `72e23317dd5aaabc575bdb832a6dae5909e13f32` (merges `origin/master` at `89a6deb717`, which includes the lifecycle coordinator). Master has since gained two commits; they merge cleanly and only one touches a file here (new English CLI strings).
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required `CI Required Gate` rollup on this head (Format, Lint with `ci-all`, Test, Parallel Runtime Test, MSRV, platform checks). Parallel Runtime Test matters here because the contract lives in `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live two-process interleaving (a daemon and a CLI converging the same rename concurrently); the journal lock and the verification re-probe are unit-tested, the cross-surface handoff (gateway arms, CLI finishes) is tested in-process. The case-only rename test ran on a case-insensitive host (macOS APFS); the case-sensitive branch of that test did not execute here. Windows was not run locally; the path classifier's Windows shape is driven through its test seam.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                      -> clean
  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh         -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
  cargo check --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
                                                  -> Finished (only warning: pre-existing unused import, runtime service/mod.rs, identical to master)
  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
                                                  -> Finished
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime --no-deps -- -D warnings
                                                  -> all Finished, no diagnostics
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config   -> 1898 tests run: 1898 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools
                                                  -> 2939 run: 2938 passed, 1 failed (see below)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
                                                  -> 690 tests run: 690 passed, 7 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
                                                  -> 516 run: 515 passed, 1 failed (see below); with -j 4: 516 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --test component --test architecture
                                                  -> 323 tests run: 323 passed
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast
                                                  -> 5499 run: 5498 passed, 1 failed (see below); rpc::dispatch module with -j 4: 490 passed
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   -> pass
  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     -> pass
  ```

  The three failures are not caused by this change:
  - `rpc::dispatch::tests::rtg_10197_reaped_prompt_publishes_before_close_kill_or_delete_can_remove_it` (1 s timeouts, session delete) and the root binary's `filesystem_adapter_drives_a_run_with_maintenance_disabled` (file-event timing) fail only under full default parallelism on this machine; both pass alone and in their full suites at `-j 4`.
  - `web_search_tool::tests::test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free` fails deterministically on macOS: it expects a refused connection from a port that is bound but not listening, and macOS drops that SYN instead (reproduced with a plain Python socket). Linux refuses it, so CI is unaffected. This file is not touched here.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** An independent adversarial review of the branch reproduced its findings against a built binary (a custom workspace path letting a record clear while the old workspace remained, resuming a rename whose old alias was configured again, a case-only rename that could never finish on macOS, discovery locking a live agent, the model routing tool bypassing the guards, prepared-record effectiveness). Each is fixed with a regression test that reproduces it. The seven gateway/RPC and five CLI tests from the maintainer's committed-rename acceptance pack are ported with their assertions unchanged and pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output is covered by the CLI component tests; no visual presentation changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `72e23317dd`, CLI binary and in-process gateway/RPC handlers, test output above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the reproduction steps above; the component tests `committed_rename_cli_*` and `agents_*` assert the exit status and messages of each step.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `cargo test --workspace` for crates this change does not touch (channels, providers, plugins, and others) was left to CI; every crate with a changed file ran its full suite.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** One new state file under the existing data directory. Agent file tools are refused access to it and its lock and temp files through the runtime-config protected names.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a. The change narrows access: a retired alias can no longer inherit another agent's state. Refusals rendered by gateway and RPC do not name the pending target, and journal errors name the file rather than its absolute path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** The journal is new; an older binary ignores it (and can still recreate a retired alias).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** `zeroclaw agents rename` exits non-zero until the rename converges and gains `--abandon`; creating, renaming onto, or deleting an alias involved in an unfinished rename is refused on every surface listed above. Gateway and RPC response shapes are unchanged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: no action is needed for existing installs. An operator who hits a refusal runs the rename it names, or abandons it with `--abandon`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the landing commit. A leftover `agent-lifecycle-recovery.json` is inert to the previous binary; remove it by hand only after confirming nothing is left under the old alias.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** agent creation refused with "retired by an unfinished agent rename"; a rename that keeps reporting the same follower; agent creation or rename failing with "agent-lifecycle-recovery.json is unreadable".

prs.title: fix(tools): per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Binds `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, and `discord_search` to trusted per-agent ownership. Backend-stable scoped reads/writes close the prior check/use race, and Discord namespace predicates run before ranking and limits.
  - Makes typed live config the single agent/channel ownership source. Disabled aliases grant nothing; ambiguous duplicate enabled owners now fail closed instead of assigning an arbitrary agent. The alias view that answers those questions is a typed walk of the channel maps, so resolving ownership never serializes config on a caller's stack.
  - Preserves trusted session attribution across SQLite and JSONL restart, migration, retention, purge, and empty-transcript cases. Startup hydration touches only channel-marked sessions, so gateway and RPC sessions keep their owners.
  - Enforces Discord alias/channel provenance on search and on every archive write. Message and reaction ids are global, so archive creation now inserts a missing key and refuses to move a row already claimed by another alias or channel, matching the guarded edit/delete paths. Memory update/delete ownership checks stay atomic with the mutation.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `sessions_current`, `send_via`, peer-group semantics, the knowledge graph, or dormant session-tool registration. It does not guess ownership for ambiguous legacy data.
- **Blast radius:** Per-agent tool registration, channel routing/collection, both session backends and hygiene, Discord archive/search/mutation paths, SQLite memory mutations, the `Configurable` derive's generated surface, and affected Fluent tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9646. Related #9647. Related #8290.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `channel`, `config`, `memory`, `runtime`, `tool`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `channel:discord`, `memory:backend`, `domain:security`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

The authorization inputs remain trusted runtime/config identity plus persisted provenance. Model-supplied session IDs and Discord channel IDs are selectors, never grants. A true legacy single-agent install remains deterministic; duplicate enabled owners are configuration ambiguity and are rejected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the deterministic regressions exercise the security and retention boundaries without credentials.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` tool registration and `channel` persistence/search.
- **Setup / preconditions:** None for automated tests. A manual Discord A/B needs two neutral agents with distinct enabled, archive-enabled Discord aliases that both watch one channel.
- **Steps to run:** Run the session ownership/retention tests. Then let the first alias archive a message and a reaction from the shared channel, let the second alias observe the same two events, and run scoped `discord_search` as each agent. Separately, archive an owned Discord row and more than 200 newer foreign matching rows before searching as the first agent with `limit = 1`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign sessions and Discord rows remain inaccessible; the row stays in the first alias's namespace and only the first agent's `discord_search` returns it; the owned Discord result survives foreign ranking pressure; archived JSONL sessions cannot reappear through metadata; ambiguous duplicate channel owners expose no scoped grant.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Session tools and the shared Discord archive lacked a complete per-agent boundary, JSONL ownership metadata could outlive retention, and the second observer's archive write took over the first alias's row.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI covers the repository matrix (strict lint, workspace tests, Landlock, security, supported targets, MSRV, and the parallel runtime/channel gate). The previous head `6cef56af45ff41f33d569b40f8215a7ddc20c515` has an exact-head run, [34189025680](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34189025680): `CI Required Gate`, `Format`, `Lint`, `Test`, `Test (Landlock)`, `Check (all features)`, `Check (no default features)`, `Security`, `MSRV (declared floor)`, and the platform checks all passed there. That run is historical for this revision: it does not cover the channel alias enumeration change below.
- Hosted CI on this head (`c1c14d91f97a77573070c5d3cbf68e52ce82e3af`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34549879212. The non-required Windows advisory failed as detailed below.
- **Advisory Windows job:** [Exact-head job 103112026802](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34549879212/job/103112026802) ran 13,996 tests: 13,994 passed and two failed. `published_crates_never_include_files_outside_their_own_directory` failed on packaging-path handling, and `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` aborted with a stack overflow. The new `channel_alias_view_enumerates_maps_on_a_bounded_stack` regression passed on Windows. The RPC abort was also observed at this PR's exact base `46479bdca7` (see #10734); the separate dispatcher repair #10735 has since merged but is not included in this head. No Windows RPC pass is claimed here, and the earlier blank-package failure did not recur.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live two-bot Discord deployment. Storage, routing, search, archive creation and mutation, retention, and both session backends are covered deterministically instead. `cargo fluent check` and `cargo deny` were not run locally. I also could not reproduce the reviewed `session/new` stack abort on this machine (detail below), so the local evidence for that fix is a measured stack budget rather than a reproduction.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 macOS, `rustc 1.97.1`, at `c1c14d91f97a77573070c5d3cbf68e52ce82e3af`):

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean

  ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    -> ==> rust quality: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
         --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
       Finished `dev` profile in 4m 08s
       ==> rust quality: provider dispatch gate clean

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. Summary: 0 error(s)

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> Collected 0 added link(s) from 4 docs file(s).
       No added links detected in changed docs lines.

  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    -> Finished `dev` profile in 2m 41s

  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> Finished `dev` profile in 4m 32s

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
    -> Finished `test` profile in 0.62s (test binaries already built by the check above)

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib \
      rpc::dispatch::tests::process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack -- --exact
    -> test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 4257 filtered out

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-macros
    -> Summary [5.095s] 1640 tests run: 1640 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
    -> Summary [77.676s] 15650 tests run: 15649 passed (4 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
       FAIL zeroclaw-providers grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant
       (known macOS-local timing flake in an unrelated crate; nothing in this diff touches
        the grok CLI process-group path)
  ```

  Focused regressions for the reviewed findings:

  ```text
  zeroclaw-config   schema::tests::channel_alias_view_enumerates_maps_on_a_bounded_stack
    -> new this revision; restoring the property-surface body locally makes it abort on a
       stack overflow, and it passes with the typed walk
  zeroclaw-memory   sqlite::tests::store_preserving_provenance_never_transfers_a_claimed_row
  zeroclaw-channels discord::tests::overlapping_alias_cannot_take_over_archive_rows_it_also_observes
  zeroclaw-infra    session_store::tests::blocked_sidecar_rename_leaves_no_live_metadata_behind
    -> unchanged since the previous revision, where each was shown to fail against its own
       pre-fix implementation; all three pass in the full run above
  ```

- **Channel alias enumeration on a bounded stack (correction to the previous revision):** the earlier body claimed this defect was found and fixed during that pass. That was wrong. Narrowing the walk from `Config::prop_fields()` to `ChannelsConfig::prop_fields()` shrank the serialized subtree but kept the serialization: every generated `prop_fields` body begins with `toml::Value::try_from(self)`. Per-agent tool registration reaches that walk through `channel_refs_owned_by_agent`, so the cost still landed on whatever stack the caller was holding, which is the mechanism the reviewed `session/new` abort points at. This head removes the serialization instead of shrinking it: the `Configurable` derive now emits `map_alias_entries()`, a typed in-place walk of map-keyed child blocks plus each block's own `enabled` switch, and `configured_channel_aliases` consumes that. Channel maps still surface without a parallel channel-type table, and the walk never touches credential fields at all.
- **What I could and could not reproduce:** on this machine `rpc::dispatch::tests::process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` passes at the submitted head `6cef56af`, at the post-merge head before this fix, and after it, with incremental compilation both on and off; I could not reproduce the reported SIGABRT locally, so I did not use it as the before/after signal. What I could measure is the enumeration's own stack cost, with a config holding three configured channel blocks: the property-surface walk overflows a 48 KiB thread stack (and passes at 64 KiB), while the typed walk completes inside 16 KiB, the smallest stack this platform accepts. The new regression pins a 48 KiB budget, which the pre-fix implementation fails and this one passes with room. The cost also stops scaling with config size, which is the property the bounded RPC path needs.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Audited every ownership predicate at its storage linearization point, the canonical config resolver and duplicate rejection, startup hydration markers, JSONL transcript/sidecar archive and purge, and Discord provenance admission. For this revision I re-read the generated derive output for the new walk, confirmed the enumerated names and live `enabled` values are identical to the property-surface projection for the same config, and confirmed the only other caller of the alias view, `channels_by_alias`, keeps its existing contract. I did not exercise a real Discord account.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no rendered interface changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all`, `cargo fluent check`, and live Discord were not run locally. The changed Fluent catalogues are unchanged since the previously green exact-head run, and the remaining external gap would require credentials.

**Historical evidence (previous heads).** Exact-head [run 34189025680](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34189025680) covered `6cef56af45ff41f33d569b40f8215a7ddc20c515` (required gate green, advisory Windows failed). Exact-head [Quality Gate run 33805478225](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33805478225) was fully green at `a6744b2b568f4dc915b8bdf600df3f78c54cddcd`, and [run 33347452112](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/33347452112) was fully green at `9ceb67f447a5601173e9da203ae1d3eae5c3a6a5`. None of those runs covers the channel alias enumeration change on the current head.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; access is narrowed.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**; the channel alias view no longer serializes any config section at all, so the transient copy it used to make of decrypted channel values is gone.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Static tool descriptions and denial text are model-visible. Fluent owns those strings; authorization comes only from trusted runtime identity, live config, and persisted provenance, never model arguments.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; vulnerable cross-agent access and ambiguous ownership are intentionally denied.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing attributed SQLite and JSONL sessions need no action. Unattributed or ambiguously owned data stays fail-closed; restore a unique enabled channel binding or re-create/re-archive data through its intended owner. Scoped `sessions_send` no longer creates an unknown session key; establish the session through its owning runtime first. `sessions_list` and `discord_search` now enforce the profile's `Read` operation, so restrictive profiles must permit that operation. Where two enabled Discord aliases watch the same channel, the alias that archives an event first keeps the row and the later observer no longer replaces it.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual PR landing commit from current `master`; no schema down-migration is required.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Disabling the affected channel/tool is the immediate containment option.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected ownership-denial errors, a missing scoped tool for a uniquely configured owner, empty owned Discord results, channel startup errors reporting ambiguous enabled owners, or repeated `discord archive row belongs to another alias or channel; not overwritten` debug events for rows an operator expects a given alias to own.

**Current head:** `c1c14d91f97a77573070c5d3cbf68e52ce82e3af`

prs.title: fix(memory): add per-agent attribution and scoping to the knowledge graph
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds mandatory agent ownership to the shared SQLite knowledge graph. `KnowledgeScope` is bound from trusted registration; writes keep caller ownership and directional `read_knowledge_from` grants widen reads only.
  - Makes legacy attribution explicit and fail-closed, with a sole-agent automatic path or configured `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent` for ambiguous multi-agent upgrades.
  - Makes agent delete/rename recovery lifecycle-specific: delete probes exported memory while rename detects even an empty agent identity row; filesystem inspection errors retain residue; workspace/knowledge archives surface failures; cron and ACP rows are purged only after durable export.
  - Makes the fail-toward-residue rule uniform across surfaces. The gateway workspace mover and committed-rename probe no longer collapse a metadata error into absence, and the CLI deletion path archives through the shared helper instead of a hand-rolled copy that swallowed its errors.
  - Makes that fail-toward-residue rule platform-independent. A workspace whose parent is a file surfaces as an error on Unix and as an ordinary "not found" on Windows, so every surface now classifies a path through one shared `inspect_lifecycle_path` helper that re-walks the ancestors of a negative probe. An uninspectable workspace is residue on every supported platform, and the regressions assert that classification instead of the platform's error shape.
  - Gives every deletion archive an exclusively created leaf, so a duplicate delete inside the same clock second cannot adopt another attempt's directory, and writes the archive artifacts with `create_new` so a shared leaf could not replace a durable export even if one were reached.
  - Prevents shared inbound edges from suppressing the caller's own relation and requires a scope-visible anchor for every direct graph-neighbor query after grant revocation.
  - Validates lifecycle aliases before any recovery probe or filesystem path derivation, keeps unreadable RPC rename workspaces retryable, and serializes the global node cap across per-agent SQLite connections.
  - Boxes the RPC map-key delete future, which the master merge showed is needed to keep `process_line` inside the two-megabyte stack budget `master` now pins.
  - Resolves grants from live policy for each graph operation after acquiring the database connection. Purge verifies the archived snapshot in an immediate transaction, using durable edge generation identities to distinguish recreated relations.
  - Explicit agent creation and rename refuse aliases with retained knowledge or an uninspectable store. Property-based automatic creation still bypasses this check at `be62e0b5160f65f3ddc937c427691395d968eb75` and remains a requested repair.
- **Scope boundary:** Knowledge ownership is per agent alias, not per authenticated principal; different principals using the same agent share its knowledge. The unwired Postgres graph is unchanged. Knowledge tool schema/shape is unchanged, but row visibility is intentionally narrowed by `KnowledgeScope`. Gateway and RPC can retry committed rename residue; CLI cannot yet, and #10373 owns that shared recovery follow-up. Lifecycle requests now enforce the canonical alias grammar before touching recovery state. #10149 owns durable recovery for a failed custom workspace archive.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-memory`, tools/runtime registration, config, gateway/RPC/CLI alias lifecycle, SQLite knowledge/session/memory stores, cron and ACP cleanup, workspaces, and documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #9647. Related #9646. Related #10149. Related #10373.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `config`, `gateway`, `memory`, `runtime`, `tool`, `distinguished contributor`, `release-gate`, `domain:security`, `priority:p1`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `cli`, `topic:identity-access`, `release:v0.9.0`

Agent aliases remain the canonical ownership key already used by configuration, workspaces, grants, and lifecycle operations. The storage API requires scope so foreign rows behave as absent even if a caller knows an ID. Disabled configured siblings remain valid explicit read sources; they do not become writers.

### What this does, simply

Agents previously shared the same knowledge graph. This change gives each row an owning agent and limits an agent to its own knowledge unless an operator grants read access to another agent's rows. Deletion archives owned knowledge before removing it, and rename moves its ownership. The latest repair makes revoked sharing take effect for retained tools and stops cleanup from purging rows that differ from its archive. One gap remains: property-based configuration can recreate an alias whose old knowledge survived failed cleanup.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` and `tui` through the registered `knowledge` tool and alias lifecycle RPC/CLI paths.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Enable knowledge and configure neutral agents `agent_a` and `agent_b`.
- **Steps to run:** Capture a unique node as `agent_b`; search, inspect statistics, traverse, and relate by ID as `agent_a`; then add `read_knowledge_from = ["agent_b"]`, restart, and repeat. Exercise rename/delete once with a temporarily unavailable configured memory/workspace path, restore it, and retry. For the archive path, issue the same `agents delete` twice inside one second and inspect `<data_dir>/agents/_deleted`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign rows are absent before the grant; reads become visible after the directional grant while writes remain caller-owned. Failed lifecycle cleanup retains retryable residue. Explicit creation refuses an alias with retained knowledge; property-based recreation still needs the current review repair. The duplicate delete lands in its own archive leaf and the first attempt's export is untouched.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Agents shared one unscoped graph, and several committed lifecycle failures could be mistaken for completed cleanup.

### How I tested

- **Current reviewed head:** `be62e0b5160f65f3ddc937c427691395d968eb75`. The required [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36767407780/job/110069381765) passed. The current re-review inspected source and regression assertions; it did not run local Cargo or a live property-recreation reproduction.
- **Historical validation below:** Commands, counts, and Windows results below were reported for `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`; they are not current-head execution claims.

- **Historical head under test:** `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, which merges `origin/master` (`46479bdca7`) into the branch and adds the two portability repairs described below.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `CI Required Gate` rollup plus the advisory Windows nextest job. This head exists to repair a Windows-only behavior, so the advisory Windows job is the one that actually exercises what changed; the required gate covers everything else.
- Hosted CI on this head (`4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`): `CI Required Gate` SUCCESS, run 34554821248.
- **Advisory Windows disclosure:** On historical head `4291450ec0cc1bdb87c6d48f19be3e61950c25b2`, [Windows job 103129316312](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34554821248/job/103129316312) ran the repaired unreadable-workspace, path-classifier, duplicate-archive, existing-export protection, and refused-move tests successfully. The job remains failed: its initial batch reported 13,163 tests run, 13,160 passed, 3 failed, and 20 skipped. The remaining failures are the architecture publish-contract test and two runtime PowerShell tests; none is one of the repaired lifecycle regressions. Subsequent scoped batches passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No Windows execution is available locally, so the Windows result for that historical head comes from the runner; what is proven here is that the shared classifier returns `Uninspectable` for the `Ok(false)` shape Windows reports and that every lifecycle surface routes through it. No live two-agent daemon A/B, and no live multi-process duplicate delete. The duplicate-archive regression drives two cascades of the same alias inside one clock second in-process, which is the interleaving the finding described, but it is not a two-daemon race. CLI committed-rename retry remains #10373.
- **Commands run and tail output (historical head `4291450ec`):**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all --check
    -> clean (exit 0)

  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
    -> Comment hygiene gate passed.

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
    -> No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    -> No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
       (one pre-existing MD038 on an unchanged line of agents/internals.md, reported non-blocking)

  BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base origin/master HEAD) bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
    -> 1 link collected, 0 errors

  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-default-features
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  ./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict
    -> fmt clean; workspace clippy --all-targets --features ci-all -D warnings clean;
       provider dispatch gate clean (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --features channel-linq -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --all-targets --features gateway,agent-runtime -- -D warnings
    -> no diagnostics (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-run
    -> Finished (exit 0)

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test-threads=1
    -> 4305 tests run: 4305 passed, 5 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --features channel-linq
    -> 521 tests run: 521 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --features gateway,agent-runtime
    -> 383 tests run: 383 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-memory
    -> 532 tests run: 532 passed, 0 skipped

  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast
    -> 15654 tests run: 15653 passed (2 leaky), 1 failed, 24 skipped
    -> the single failure is zeroclaw-providers
       grok_cli::tests::unix_fake_child::timeout_kills_leader_and_descendant,
       a known macOS-local timing flake unrelated to this change
  ```

  Both repairs were proven to fail before and pass after, on this machine.

  The Windows-shape defect was reproduced by reverting the new classifier to the
  pre-fix rule (`Ok(false)` means absent), which is exactly the path Windows
  takes:

  ```text
  # classifier temporarily reverted to `Ok(false) => Absent`
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --test-threads=1 --no-fail-fast \
    -E 'test(a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes) + ...'
    -> FAIL a_blocked_path_is_uninspectable_in_both_probe_shapes
       panicked: a negative probe over a non-directory ancestor is not absence

  # after the fix, same command
    -> 5 tests run: 5 passed, 4270 skipped
  ```

  The cross-device failure was reproduced literally, by putting `TMPDIR` on a
  separate mount from the install root the pre-fix fixture reached into:

  ```text
  # pre-fix, TMPDIR on a separate filesystem
    -> FAIL duplicate_delete_cascades_cannot_share_an_archive_or_truncate_the_first_export
       ["workspace archive failed (<install-root>/agents/agent_a/workspace ->
         <tmpdir>/data/agents/_deleted/agent_a-<ts>-2/workspace): Cross-device link (os error 18)"]

  # after pinning config_path under the test's TempDir, same split-mount run
    -> 5 tests run: 5 passed, 4270 skipped
       and the install root was left empty, which is the property that was missing
  ```

- **Historical evidence (previous head `64d8944a4275a31aa39ce4094c5d655dce205ecf`):** the exact-head hosted rollup [run 34188562577](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/34188562577) completed with 37 successful checks, 1 failure, and 3 skipped. The required `CI Required Gate` passed; the single failure was the advisory Windows nextest job described above. Local focused suites at that head passed, which is the asymmetry this head removes: the assertions they made were Unix-only. That head also needed one master-driven repair, kept here as history: `process_line_session_new_creates_session_on_two_megabyte_stack` landed on `master` after the branch's previous head and aborted on the merged tree because the agent-delete branch of `handle_config_map_key_delete` left the owned-state cascade's future inline in the caller; it passed on `origin/master` alone, aborted on the merged head, and passed again after the delete future was boxed.

- **Historical evidence (earlier head `ab20806838a56a5ed9027e34c2517d4ee8af950e`):** the exact-head hosted rollup completed 38/38 successful check runs, including the required aggregate gate, strict lint, tests, Landlock, security, platform checks, MSRV, and the parallel runtime gate. Focused suites at that head were `zeroclaw-memory` knowledge_graph 30 passed, `zeroclaw-tools` knowledge 18 passed, `zeroclaw-config` knowledge 5 passed, `zeroclaw-runtime` `config_map_key_` 10 passed, and the gateway `agent_delete_`/`agent_rename_` suites 7 and 4 passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I read the exact-head Windows job log rather than inferring the failures from the summary, and confirmed that five of its six failures are this PR's own `try_exists().is_err()` assertions and the sixth is the inherited packaging assertion. I re-audited every filesystem probe on the lifecycle surfaces so that all of them, including the deletion archive and the knowledge-database probe inside the residue predicate, now route through the one classifier. I mounted a separate filesystem locally to reproduce the reviewer's cross-device failure instead of taking it on faith, and confirmed after the fix that the test leaves the install root untouched. Earlier rounds established the master baseline for the stack regression in a separate worktree. I did not run a live daemon interaction, I did not exercise the duplicate delete across two operating-system processes, and I cannot execute Windows here.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A; no visual presentation changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo deny check` was not re-run locally; it is unchanged by this head and the hosted security job covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**; `read_knowledge_from` is an explicit directional read grant. It defaults empty, validates aliases, and never widens writes.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; output shape is unchanged and storage authorization reduces visible rows.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Trusted config is the only grant source; mandatory storage-layer predicates, foreign-as-absent results, and caller-owned writes constrain it.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for ambiguous multi-agent legacy knowledge; it remains hidden until assigned. Single-agent upgrades are automatic.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**; adds `agents.<alias>.workspace.read_knowledge_from` and `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent`; alias lifecycle commands now cascade owned state and reject noncanonical/reserved aliases before recovery I/O. Explicit creation and rename also refuse retained knowledge or an uninspectable knowledge store; automatic property creation still needs the remaining repair.
- Storage schema: Adds durable `edges.generation` identities and an insert trigger for archived-snapshot comparison.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Multi-agent operators with legacy knowledge set `knowledge.legacy_owner_agent = "<enabled-alias>"`, restart, verify ownership, then remove the migration setting. Add read grants only when deliberate.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable knowledge, back up its SQLite file, then revert the eventual PR landing commit. An old binary does not enforce ownership and may create unattributed rows, so rollback is containment only. The `edges.generation` column and insert trigger remain in the SQLite database across a binary downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[knowledge].enabled = false`; remove `read_knowledge_from` entries to revoke sharing.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Legacy-ownership ambiguity warnings, owned-state cascade warnings, retained cron/ACP rows after archive failure, `workspace inspection failed` warnings on a delete or rename result, or repeated delete/rename results reporting configured-but-unavailable residue.

prs.title: fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This PR is stacked on #11225 (delegated memory principal scope), which introduces the retained `Agent.delegate_tool` handle and the delegate `principal_scope` cell this change builds on. Until #11225 merges, the branch shows both commits; please review the top commit only (`fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals`).
- **What changed and why:**
  - `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` list, read, and append to other sessions with no principal-ownership check. A non-admin principal that held them (wildcard tool and agent selectors included) could read or append to another principal's transcript on the same agent. Applying a non-admin principal's grants (`apply_principal_grants_to_agent`, which runs at session creation, at rehydration, and before every prompt) now withholds them. `sessions_current` stays: it takes no target and reports only the caller's own session.
  - The tool names live in one place, `zeroclaw_tools::PRINCIPAL_UNAWARE_SESSION_TOOL_NAMES`, with a sync test against the constructed tools. Skill aliases of those tools (a `builtin` or `mcp` skill tool whose `target` is one of them) are withheld with them, because a name-only denylist is bypassed by a renamed wrapper.
  - Nested executors that cannot carry the withholding go too: `spawn_subagent` rebuilds a full registry from config, and `execute_pipeline` runs the tool set captured at construction, which includes the session tools. Both are already marked `requires_unrestricted_principal`; that existing marker is what selects them, so their skill aliases follow as well.
  - The delegate is kept for wildcard principals, but the Agent marks it through the retained handle. The mark is an `Arc<AtomicBool>` shared with background, parallel, and nested bounded delegates exactly like `principal_scope`, and every child registry the delegate builds filters on it: the bounded base (the parent's build list, which still holds what the parent's registry withheld) and the independent target's own registry. An Agent whose registry holds a delegate it has no handle for drops the delegate instead.
  - Source of truth: the principal's resolved grants, re-evaluated by `apply_principal_grants_to_agent` on every prompt. The registry removal and the delegate flag are narrowing-only effects of that evaluation, like the existing selector narrowing; nothing snapshots policy, and nothing is ever restored to a live session. The system prompt is rebuilt only when the withholding actually removed a tool, so later prompts do not rebuild it.
- **Scope boundary:** This is containment: it withholds principal-unaware tools from the sessions of non-admin principals. It does not make the session tools principal-aware (principal-scoped read views and predicates for list, history, and the chat append path); that repair belongs under the session-ownership contract in the #8290 tracker. The agent-ownership scoping in #9746 is related but does not provide principal isolation. This PR does not touch `sessions.rs` or the runtime's session-tool registration. `sessions_reset` and `sessions_delete` are not registered by the runtime; the name list's doc comment now says each must join it if it ever is. Administrators and the unauthenticated shared operator keep every tool.
- **Not covered, and now documented:** runs that execute later under the agent's own identity, with the agent's configured tools, can still call the session-data tools. These are agent jobs created with `cron_add`, or given a new prompt with `cron_update` and started with `cron_run` (the same through RPC cron grants), whose output comes back through `cron_runs`; SOP runs; and the turns `send_message_to_peer` starts in another agent. None of them carries a principal today. The authentication docs now say so and give the interim mitigation: list `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send`, plus any skill tool that targets them, in `excluded_tools` of the risk profile of each agent those runs use. That removes the tools from every run of the agent, administrators' sessions included. Carrying a principal into scheduled, SOP, and peer runs is follow-up work under #8290. `schedule` creates shell jobs only; shell execution as the daemon account is the existing, separately documented limitation.
- **Blast radius:** RPC sessions of authenticated principals without `admin`, including wildcard ones, lose `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, `spawn_subagent`, and `execute_pipeline`, plus skill aliases of any of them and of `delegate` (wildcard principals keep the `delegate` tool itself). Their delegation children lose the same tools. Principals with a constrained selector already lost the nested executors and their aliases. Channel and CLI sessions do not go through this RPC posture and are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11127. Depends on #11225.
- **Labels:** `agent`, `channel`, `channel:core`, `docs`, `domain:security`, `memory`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:high`, `runtime`, `size:XL`, `tool`, `tool:delegate`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets several people (principals) use the same agent over RPC, each with their own sessions. A few agent tools can look at other sessions: list them, read their history, or post a message into them. Those tools only check which agent a session belongs to, not which person, so one user's agent could read or write another user's conversation on the same agent. Until the tools learn to check the person, this change simply takes them away from every signed-in user who is not an administrator, even users whose permissions say "all tools". It also takes away two helpers that could hand the tools straight back (starting a sub-agent and running a tool pipeline), and it makes delegated helper agents drop the tools too. The tool that reports "which session am I in" stays, and administrators and single-operator installs see no change. When a user is demoted from administrator, their open session loses the tools at its next prompt. This is not complete isolation yet: work that runs later under the agent's own identity, such as a scheduled agent job, a standard operating procedure, or a message to another agent, can still use these tools. The documentation now says so and shows operators how to switch the tools off for those agents until the tools learn to check the person.
