prs.title: refactor(cron): extract cron into zeroclaw-cron and land the precondition gate there
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extracts cron out of the transitional holding crate into `crates/zeroclaw-cron`, per #10546. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/cron/` is deleted rather than re-exported or shimmed, and the files move by rename so history follows the code.
  - Carries the accepted cron precondition gate from #5607 with it, so the feature lands in a permitted owner instead of the crate the contract says to stop growing. This supersedes #10220.
  - The host seam lives in `zeroclaw-cron::host`, not `zeroclaw-api`. `zeroclaw-cron` can see `zeroclaw-config`, so a `CronAgentRequest` carries the effective `SecurityPolicy` and the `Config` cron admitted the run under, instead of loose inputs the host had to rebuild a policy from. Rebuilding is what lost the action budget and made the executor hold a stale config; passing the policy whole removes both. The executor is injected per scheduler generation; nothing registers one globally.
  - Integrates the cron work that landed on `master` while this was open. Claim ownership uses #10414's per-execution tokens and live-token recovery; this branch's own process-wide `locked_by` design is gone. #9139's durable plugin outbox moves into `zeroclaw-cron` unchanged, since it shares cron's database and schema setup, and stays behind `plugins-wasm`.
  - Two supporting moves outside cron: shell-output decoding moves from `zeroclaw-runtime` into `zeroclaw-infra` unchanged, because the cron scheduler now decodes shell output (#10955) and cron cannot depend on the runtime; and `finish_agent_claim` becomes public, with claim-release fault injection behind a `test-util` feature that only the runtime's dev-dependency enables.
- **Scope boundary:** Cron plus the two supporting moves above. No other subsystem that `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` names is extracted. There is no cron schema change beyond #5607's `pre_hook` declaration; claim columns are #10414's. Agent execution, delivery and config semantics are unchanged except where the review findings below required it.
- **Blast radius:** Every cron consumer is re-pointed at the new crate: the daemon, the gateway API, RPC dispatch, the `cron_*` tools, SOP dispatch and the CLI. The runtime gains `cron_host.rs`. `zeroclaw-infra` gains `chardetng`, `encoding_rs` and, on Windows only, two `windows` features. The `cron` PR label now matches the new crate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10546. Supersedes #10220. Related #5607, #10414, #9139.
  - **Merge order:** #10599 should land **after** this PR. It changes the same cron files, and porting its fix into `zeroclaw-cron` afterwards is safer than carrying it across the directory move mid-review.
  - **Note:** #10836 becomes redundant when this lands. Its declarative-owner fix is included here as `3cbd4a4f7d`. Whether to close it is the maintainer's call.
  - #10546's last acceptance criterion names `ADR-016-cron-extraction-and-transitional-exception.md`, which was drafted on the closed #10545 and never landed; the ADR-016 on `master` is the holding-crate exception policy. That criterion needs correcting on the issue; it does not block this PR.
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `core`, `config`, `cron`, `daemon`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `skills`, `tests`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:security`, `domain:architecture`, `tool:cron`, `tool:shell`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `type:refactor`, `cli`, `needs-maintainer-review`

### Review map: @Audacity88's findings

| Finding | Status | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resolve conflicts against current `master` | Merged in, including #11066 | `9ac7076dde` |
| Reconcile `locked_by` with #10414's claim recovery | One design: #10414's tokens. Gateway and RPC manual runs claim through the same live-token registry; the manual runner takes an explicit claim mode so it does not re-claim a job the agent tool already holds | `cc62ea794f` |
| Include #9139's plugin outbox | Moved unchanged, behind `plugins-wasm` | `37590c4e6c`, `e0bd5c21f1` |
| Validate the integrated claim lifecycle | Aborted-run and stale-release regressions | `1e3820eed1` |
| Action-budget resets | Admitted policy crosses the seam whole, sharing its tracker | `72678ed916`, `79f414469a` |
| Stale configuration after reload | Executor holds no config; each request carries its generation's | `72678ed916`, `ae042f7da4` |
| Unreconciled manual execution | Reconciliation outcome recorded per database; manual runs of declarative jobs refused until it succeeds | `b73cae80e5` |
| Abandoned claims | Scheduled claims are tokened and released by a drop guard, so a run aborted by a reload leaves nothing behind | `1e3820eed1` |
| Inconsistent ownership | Declarative sync updates the stored owner; an unowned declarative job fails closed | `3cbd4a4f7d`, `a7b673a177` |
| Documentation discrepancy | Label, persistence and delegation docs updated; #10546 criterion noted above | `d025618869` |
| Startup catch-up ran unreconciled declarations (second review) | Reconciliation filter moved into `claim_due_jobs`, which every scheduled route shares | `ea9d0cf03c` |
| Hook cancellation left descendants alive (second review) | `ProcessTreeGuard` kills the hook's process group when its run is dropped, before the claim is released | `2212598e46` |
| Hook working directory (warning) | Documented `config.data_dir` behavior and added a relative-path regression | `9808cf03c192` |

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (daemon scheduler), gateway and RPC manual triggers (`surface: web`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config with a declarative cron job under `[cron.<alias>]` owned by an agent via `[agents.<x>].cron_jobs`.
- **Steps to run:** Start `zeroclaw daemon`, let a shell job and an agent job each fire, trigger one by hand with `POST /api/cron/<id>/run`, then read `GET /api/cron/<id>/runs`. For the claim lifecycle, reload the daemon while a long agent job is running and confirm the job runs again on its next occurrence.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The same behavior as `master` plus the #5607 gate. Jobs without a `pre_hook` record the same history and statuses. After a reload, the job is not left locked.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same, minus the gate, with the code in `zeroclaw-runtime`.

### How I tested

- **Current CI:** Required CI passes at `9808cf03c192`, including workspace tests, lint, and Windows compile checks ([run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36238326271)). Windows descendant cleanup has no runtime regression test.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Earlier CI at `d025618869`: 39 pass, 0 fail, `CI Required Gate` passing. The feature matrix (`all features`, `no default features`, `32-bit`, the plugin backends) exercises the new crate boundary under different feature unification, which is where an extraction usually breaks. `Check x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` is the only compile of the Windows half of the moved shell-output module and its `windows` dependency, which I cannot build locally. `Repository Structure` failed once on a flaky Apple-preflight retry test outside this diff (it fails intermittently locally too and passes on `master`); a re-run of the failed job passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The runtime half of the stale-config fix has no dedicated test; it is guaranteed structurally, since `RuntimeCronAgentExecutor` has no field that could hold a config.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                              # clean
  $ cargo check --workspace --all-targets                                   # 0 errors, 0 warnings
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-cron -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-cron                      236 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-cron --features plugins-wasm   247 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib cron         88 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra shell_output          7 passed; 0 failed
  $ cargo test --locked --test architecture publish_contract   10 passed
  $ python3 scripts/release/publish_crates_test.py    OK
  $ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh, docs_quality_gate.sh, docs_links_gate.sh   pass
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I checked that each new regression discriminates, by reverting only its fix and confirming it fails:
  - Reintroducing the manual runner's double claim fails three of #10414's own `cron_run` tests.
  - Disabling the manual reconciliation guard fails on "the manual run must be refused".
  - Making the claim guard release by job id fails the stale-release test.
  - Reverting the fail-closed owner check resolves an orphaned job to its disabled stored owner.

  The aborted-run regression caught a bug in my first version of the guard. The run's async block used only the job, and an async block captures only the fields it uses, so the guard stayed behind in the closure and released the claim before the run started. The future now binds the whole claimed job explicitly.

  I also checked that `master`'s cron changes survived the move: #10414's token-claim symbols are present, #9139's `outbox.rs` is byte-identical, and the moved shell-output module differs only in visibility.

  **What I did NOT verify:** a live daemon against a real channel, and Windows or Docker process-tree behavior beyond what CI compiles.
- **Visual interface changed?** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The host seam is still the security-relevant surface: cron decides whether policy admits a run, and the host executes it. Three properties were lost crossing it during development, the scheduler workspace, the tool-exclusion narrowing and the action budget, and each is now covered by a test. Passing the admitted policy whole, rather than inputs to rebuild it from, removes the class of loss rather than patching each instance. This PR also narrows two boundaries: a manual trigger can no longer run an unreconciled declarative body, and an agent can no longer reach a declarative job it no longer owns.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** for operators: config, the cron database, run statuses and every API, RPC and tool response are unchanged, apart from two new refusals. A declarative job with no enabled owner, or a manual trigger before reconciliation succeeds, is now refused with a reason instead of running. **No** for anything depending on `zeroclaw_runtime::cron` or `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::shell_output`, which move to `zeroclaw_cron` and `zeroclaw_infra::shell_output`. Both crates are experimental.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** beyond the `[cron.<alias>.pre_hook]` table from #5607.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Upgrade steps: none for operators. In-tree callers are all updated here.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merge commit. There is no data migration to undo; this PR adds no cron columns beyond #5607's `pre_hook` declaration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The extraction is structural.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Declarative jobs logged as "held until reconciliation succeeds", or manual triggers refused with "has not been reconciled", mean declarative sync is failing; look at the preceding sync error. A job that stays out of the due set after a reload would mean a claim was not released; that is the case the aborted-run regression covers.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #10220 by @JordanTheJet
- Scope materially carried forward: the #5607 precondition gate and the review fixes made on #10220, now in `zeroclaw-cron` instead of the holding crate.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No
- If `No`, why: #10220 has the same author as this PR, so there is no other contributor to credit.

prs.title: feat(bootstrap): add MCP launcher and its per-platform distribution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `feat/bootstrap-install-manifest` (stacked) — **Depends on #10590**; retarget to `master` once that merges.
- **What changed and why:** Adds `zeroclaw-bootstrap`, the thin standalone launcher an MCP host (Claude Code, Codex) runs to reach — or first-install — a configurable ZeroClaw on a host where the binary may not exist yet. It exposes four operations (`status`/`plan`/`install`/`handoff`) as both a CLI and an **stdio MCP surface**, and after `handoff` it `exec`s `zeroclaw control --mcp` on the **same pipe** — so a harness registers **one** MCP server that becomes the control surface. Plus its **distribution**: each release build leg emits a per-platform `zeroclaw-bootstrap-<triple>` asset, and `install-bootstrap.sh` is a `curl` installer that fetches + SHA256-verifies it. This is the proven, unblocked foundation of the configuration-MCP.
- **Scope boundary (deliberately EXCLUDES):** the control-MCP mutation/approve path, the spawn-plumbing/seccomp isolation work, the terminal-presence assurance class, and `instance.update` — all separate later PRs, some pending an open design decision. **`install` over MCP never installs**: it returns `human_approval_required` even given the correct plan digest; a human runs the approval command at a terminal. The launcher never reads/writes `config.toml` and approves nothing.
- **Blast radius:** New crate + a `curl` installer + additive release-workflow steps (build/package/upload the launcher asset; ship the installer as a release asset). No change to daemon/gateway/channels. Launcher assets ship **best-effort** — deliberately not in `required_assets`, which is single-sourced from the `zeroclaw-dist` registry (parity-enforced); gating them is a follow-up that extends the registry.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #10590 (zeroclaw-dist registry).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` + an stdio MCP JSON-RPC server
- **Setup / preconditions:** `cargo build -p zeroclaw-bootstrap`
- **Steps to run:** pipe NDJSON JSON-RPC into `zeroclaw-bootstrap mcp`: `initialize`, then `tools/list`, then `tools/call` `bootstrap.status`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `initialize` → `serverInfo.name = zeroclaw-bootstrap`, surface `pre-install-bootstrap`; `tools/list` → `[bootstrap.status, bootstrap.plan, bootstrap.install, bootstrap.handoff]`; `bootstrap.status` → structured `next_action` (`configure`|`install`). `bootstrap.install` returns `human_approval_required` and writes nothing.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the crate does not exist.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why:** Rust CI (fmt/clippy/test) on the pushed branch compiles and tests the crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** The release-workflow launcher packaging only runs on a real tag; verified locally instead (see below).
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-bootstrap -- --check` → clean
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-bootstrap --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-bootstrap` → all pass (cli_surface/handoff/install/mcp/plan/status suites)
  - `sh -n install-bootstrap.sh` → clean; `shellcheck -s sh install-bootstrap.sh` → clean
  - `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/release-stable-manual.yml'))"` → parses; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-dist --test parity` → 6 passed (workflow edits keep registry parity)
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Drove the stdio MCP server end-to-end on `aarch64-apple-darwin`: `initialize` (proto `2025-06-18`), `ping` ok, `tools/list` = the four tools, `bootstrap.status` → `next_action: configure` (detected an installed, verified binary and routed to the control surface). Confirmed `bootstrap.install` returns `human_approval_required` and writes nothing even with the correct digest. Not verified: the control MCP surface (out of scope).
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes` — `install-bootstrap.sh` writes the launcher to `~/.local/bin` (override `ZEROCLAW_BIN_DIR`); the launcher's CLI `install` (human-approved) writes under the per-user install dir. Per-user, no root; MCP `install` writes nothing.
- New external network calls? `Yes` — the launcher/installer fetch pinned release artifacts + the checksum manifest from github.com. Origin is compile-time-pinned; no arbitrary URLs; SHA256-verified before install.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- **Risk and mitigation:** Install surfaces are digest-verified against the release manifest and confined to a per-user path; the MCP path performs no install (human-presence required at a terminal).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` (additive)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes` — new `zeroclaw-bootstrap` binary and the installer's `ZEROCLAW_BIN_DIR` env var. New surfaces, not changes to existing ones.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` — the launcher is standalone; nothing on `master` depends on it.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** release workflow failing on the launcher build/package steps; `install-bootstrap.sh` erroring on a missing `zeroclaw-bootstrap-<triple>` asset (falls back to a source-build message).

prs.title: feat(channel/email): carry Cc and Bcc recipients on a single message
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This is the outbound Cc/Bcc slice of #9506. The earlier threading prerequisite #9523 has merged.
- **Review state:** Ready for review. Required CI passes on `752640966367e2e8027bf175a20d12181034bed5`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - `SendMessage` could represent exactly one recipient, so an email reply to a thread with people in `Cc` silently dropped them. Added `cc` / `bcc` (`Vec<String>`) with builder methods, following the flat channel-scoped-field precedent that #9523 established with `references` rather than introducing a nested envelope type.
  - `build_email_message` had no `.cc()` / `.bcc()`. It now emits both, so **one MIME message carries every participant** instead of one message per participant.
  - Every address is parsed through `lettre`, so a malformed entry fails the send. Silently dropping it would report success while a participant never received the mail.
  - The one-off CLI could not reach even the pre-existing `subject` / `in_reply_to` fields. `channel send` now takes `--cc` / `--bcc` / `--subject`, threaded through a `ChannelSendEnvelope`.
  - `check_envelope_supported` **rejects** email-only recipient fields aimed at a single-peer channel rather than ignoring them, because a silently dropped `--cc` is indistinguishable from a delivered one. It is a pure function so the decision is testable without constructing a live channel — the same extraction pattern #9523 used for `build_email_message`.
- **Revised since first push:** dropped a multi-`To` field (`additional_to`) and its `--to` flag. `recipient` is a cross-channel `String`, so extra `To` addresses needed an awkward second field, and no use case required it — reply-all is `To: sender, Cc: everyone else`, which `cc` alone expresses. Removing it cut 32 lines and one confusing seam from the public API.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR does **not** implement inbound `To`/`Cc` retention on `ChannelMessage`, a `reply_all()` constructor, an own-identity/alias list, or any reply-all-by-default policy. Those need the policy decision #9523 flagged, and without an agent-path consumer a `reply_all()` would be unused production code. Recipients here come only from operator CLI input, so this adds **no new trust boundary** — unlike #9523's `Reply-To`, which is attacker-controlled and is why that PR needed allowlist authorization. When the inbound half lands, every recipient derived from inbound headers will need the same per-recipient authorization #9523 applied to `reply_target`; this PR deliberately does not pre-build that surface.
- **Blast radius:** Two non-serialized `Vec<String>` fields on the shared `SendMessage` in `zeroclaw-api`, read by the email channel. Constructors default them to empty; four in-tree struct literals were updated. `WitSendMessage` is mapped field-by-field and does not carry these fields, so the WIT/plugin ABI is unchanged and Cc/Bcc are unavailable to Wasm channels. `send_channel_message` gained a `ChannelSendEnvelope` argument; the root command handler and in-tree test callers are updated. No config or schema change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9506; builds on merged #9523. #9506 remains open for the unimplemented Reply All work.
- **Labels (live snapshot):** `bug`, `core`, `channel`, `distinguished contributor`, `channel:core`, `channel:cli`, `channel:discord`, `channel:email`, `risk:high`, `size:M`, `cli`, `needs-maintainer-review`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — the recipient shape is user-visible and worth confirming against a real mail client.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw channel send`) and `channel` (email outbound construction).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A configured `[channels.email.default]` with working SMTP. Use bare `--channel-id email`; dotted ids such as `email.work` and `email.default` reject the new envelope flags before delivery.
- **Steps to run:**
  ```sh
  zeroclaw channel send 'Looping Bob in.' \
    --channel-id email --recipient alice@example.com \
    --cc bob@example.com --subject 'Re: Partnership discussion'
  ```
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One message arrives with `To: alice@example.com` and `Cc: bob@example.com`. This command composes outbound mail; it does not derive Reply All recipients or add CLI reply-thread headers.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `--cc` does not exist (`error: unexpected argument '--cc'`). The only way to reach Bob is a second `channel send`, which produces two independent messages and a fragmented thread.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head `752640966367e2e8027bf175a20d12181034bed5` passes required CI, including format, lint, test, security and build checks. The command results below are historical author runs on `fe2953298f1dadd9fbd9e93307fae19d73a86e81`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current automated tests cover the email wire/envelope builder and unsupported dispatch guards. They do not exercise live SMTP delivery or mail-client rendering. The historical SMTP/IMAP smoke below covers To/Cc; live Bcc delivery was not tested.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean

cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features channel-matrix
# clean, no warnings

cargo test -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-channels
# zeroclaw-api:      134 passed; 0 failed
# zeroclaw-channels: 1341 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
# integration:       3 passed; 1 passed; 1 passed; 0 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels build_email_message
# running 6 tests
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_rejects_a_malformed_cc_recipient ... ok
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_never_discloses_bcc_on_the_wire ... ok
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_omits_recipient_headers_when_envelope_is_empty ... ok
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_includes_references_header_with_real_ids ... ok
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_carries_every_participant_in_one_message ... ok
# test email_channel::tests::build_email_message_omits_references_header_when_empty_or_synthetic ... ok
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed   (4 mine + 2 from #9523)
```

  Historical note for the `fe2953298` run (current-head CI now passes): on `--features channel-matrix`: a plain `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on a **pre-existing** `dead_code` error for `extension_for_audio_mime` at `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/transcription.rs:38`. Root cause: its only consumer is `matrix.rs`, which is behind `#[cfg(feature = "channel-matrix")]`, so the function is dead under the default feature set. I confirmed it is not mine by re-running clippy with my changes stashed (warning still present) and by checking that my diff does not touch `transcription.rs`. It is identical on `upstream/master`. Enabling the feature clears it and lets the lint actually check my code, which is why the run above is the one I trust. #9523 hit and documented the same warning.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On the historical `fe2953298` revision, ran a live end-to-end send through a real Gmail SMTP account (isolated throwaway config dir; addresses redacted below), then read the delivered message back over IMAP to inspect the headers a real MTA actually produced:

  ```text
  Message-ID: <6a6bd450.1e1ac41d.3c2355.9c8e@mx.google.com>
  From: <sender>
  To: <recipient-a>
  Cc: <recipient-b>
  In-Reply-To: <parent-live4@zeroclaw.test.invalid>
  References: <root-live4@zeroclaw.test.invalid>
   <parent-live4@zeroclaw.test.invalid>
  ```

  One delivered message carrying both participants, with `Cc` intact — the exact shape that previously required two separate sends. The `References` chain arrives complete; it renders across two lines because RFC 5322 folds long headers, not because it is truncated (I initially misread this as a dropped id and re-checked with continuation lines included). The threading headers come from #9523 and are shown here because this branch contains it.

  A/B against `master` on the same config: `zeroclaw channel send ... --cc <addr>` fails with `error: unexpected argument '--cc' found`, and `channel send --help` lists only `--channel-id` and `--recipient`.

  Carry-forward check at `752640966367`: recipient/header construction, the send and SMTP transport methods, and Lettre 0.11.22 are unchanged from `fe2953298`. The later attachment-helper change does not affect this no-attachment smoke. This preserves the reported To/Cc result; it is not a new live test.

  Also confirmed the Bcc contract holds in the unit test at both ends: absent from the serialized message but still an SMTP envelope recipient — if that inverted, every To/Cc recipient would learn the blind-copied address.

  **Not verified:** Bcc delivery against a live server (asserted only at the construction boundary), rendering in a specific mail client, and any inbound/reply-all path, which this PR does not implement.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The historical default-feature strict Clippy run was not reported as passing for the reason above. Current-head hosted Lint passes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No** — the same SMTP path, with a wider envelope.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No** — all test addresses use reserved `.invalid` domains.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — recipients come from operator CLI input, not from inbound mail. No inbound header feeds these fields in this PR.
- **Trust boundary:** unchanged. Outbound recipients were never allowlist-gated (the email peer allowlist governs who may write *to* the agent), and this PR does not alter that. It also does not widen it: the addresses come from the same operator who could already pass `--recipient`.
- **Disclosure:** The INFO send log retains the primary recipient and adds only a Cc count. It does not list Cc addresses or describe Bcc recipients.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **For existing CLI invocations, config and WIT/plugin ABI, yes. Rust source compatibility changes:** downstream `SendMessage` literals must add `cc: Vec::new()` and `bcc: Vec::new()`; direct `send_channel_message` callers must pass a fifth argument, `ChannelSendEnvelope::default()` to retain the prior behavior. Constructor-based message callers remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes** — three new optional flags on `zeroclaw channel send` (`--cc`, `--bcc`, `--subject`). All are additive; existing invocations are unaffected. No config or schema change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the merged PR commit. No migration, persisted state or config-key cleanup is required.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The behavior is reachable only by passing a new flag; sending without them is unchanged.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A missing Cc participant or an SMTP error reported as `Failed to send message via <channel>`. The send log uses `Email sent to <recipient> (<N> cc, <N> attachments)`. A Bcc address in the serialized message would violate the blind-copy contract.

prs.title: fix(runtime): refresh capped native prompt after a streamed model switch
prs.body:
> **Follow-up to merged #11532.** The current diff contains only the streamed model-switch prompt refresh and its regression test. Current head: `9e4d4d91b7c46f6712bcb5ba85d7d42758156918`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (#11532 has merged)
- **What changed and why:**
  - A streamed Agent turn builds its pair of tool-protocol prompts once. When `max_system_prompt_chars` applies, each native request is rebuilt from that pair (#11532).
  - After an explicit mid-turn `model_switch`, the turn rebuilt the history system prompt for the new model but not the pair. Later native requests in the same turn could therefore still send the initial model label and workspace instructions until the next user turn. @Audacity88 flagged this as a non-blocking follow-up in the approving review of #11532.
  - The pair is now rebuilt together with the history prompt after the switch. If either rebuild fails, the turn takes the existing error path (trim history, return `StreamedTurnError`).
- **Scope boundary:** Only the streamed explicit-switch path in `Agent::turn_streamed`. There is no change to `finalize_system_prompt`, cap policy, prompt sections, the non-streamed `turn`, provider routing, or config.
- **Blast radius:** Structured Agent streamed turns that perform an explicit `model_switch` while a prompt cap is configured. Without a cap, the pair is never used for native requests and behaviour is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Follow-up to #11532. Related #5287.

### What this does, simply

An agent can switch models in the middle of a turn. After the switch, the model is supposed to be told which model it now is, and it should see current workspace instructions. With a prompt size limit set, the requests after the switch could still carry the description built at the start of the turn. This refreshes that description when the switch happens. The next user turn already rebuilt it, so the stale state only lasted until then.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the regression test drives a real streamed turn against a captured provider request, which is more direct than a manual check.

### How I tested

- **Refresh note (2026-10-11):** current head `9e4d4d91` includes a master refresh after #11532 merged. Every added and deleted line of the owned fix is unchanged from `4d957d78`, whose required CI passed. The local evidence below was recorded on `ba2fa3c7`; required CI runs on the current head.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, workspace tests) covers `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for this change.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1, head `ba2fa3c71a49ab3e367a372445f0af7185dee5ca` on #11532 head `4d4d4bf64` (rebased onto master `9fdb6378d`)):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                         -> exit 0
git diff --check                                                   -> exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- model_switch tool_protocol streamed_provider_switch system_prompt surface3_tests
  test result: ok. 117 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5510 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings -> exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --skip tunnel::tailscale
  test result: FAILED. 5614 passed; 1 failed; 8 ignored (see below)
```

- **Full-suite note:** each full run had one failure in a test that depends on process-wide state shared with other tests: `daemon::tests::pricing_refresher_runs_with_the_gateway_disabled` (including on this head) and, in one earlier run, `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock`. Both pass when run alone. The pricing test also fails in a full run that skips this PR's new test, so neither failure comes from this change. The `tunnel::tailscale` tests were skipped locally because one of them runs the real `tailscale serve reset` on the host.
- **New test:** `turn_streamed_model_switch_refreshes_capped_native_request`. The switch target is an OpenAI-family Chat Completions provider on a local fake server. The test captures the request sent after the switch and checks that it uses native tools, contains `Model: switched-model` but not `Model: gpt-4o-mini`, and stays within the cap.
- **Mutation check:** with the refreshed pair dropped (the turn-start pair kept), the test fails at `the capped native request must be rebuilt for the switched model`. With the fix it passes.
- **Independent exact-SHA review:** Agy with `gemini-3.8-flash-high` returned `READY` for base `4d4d4bf6` / head `ba2fa3c7` (one non-actionable observation about the undrained test event channel, the same pattern as the existing switch test), and earlier for `f798b422`. The Claude Opus lane was unavailable because of quota.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing live: no deployment ran this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full-workspace `cargo test` was not run locally. The change is confined to `zeroclaw-runtime`, whose full lib suite ran above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (the test server binds `127.0.0.1:0`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The model-visible prompt is the same one already built for history.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert 4d957d78`.

prs.title: feat(tools): defer built-in schemas through tool_search
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Add default-off `RuntimeProfileConfig.deferred_builtin_tools`. Keep permitted workspace and basic memory tools visible, advertise other admitted built-ins through compact discovery, and retrieve full schemas with the existing `tool_search` protocol. Apply exposure separately from callable-name recognition, argument recovery, and native streaming suppression.
- **Scope boundary:** Schema exposure only. Keep executable instances, tool permissions, approval rules, caller and principal restrictions, MCP activation, tool listing, and context-history recovery under their existing owners.
- **Blast radius:** Config, scoped tool assembly, shared native requests, Agent and lower-level text prompts, independent delegates, and channel startup prompts. Executable built-ins remain in `ScopedToolRegistry`; `ActivatedToolSet` records built-in schema metadata and selection only.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #5808.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded schema-deferral exception landed in #11436, approved by @tidux. The implementation remains within that recorded scope.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw tells the model what tools it can use and how to call them. Today, it sends every enabled built-in tool's full description and argument format before the model knows which tools it needs. That catalog consumes part of each request's context budget. Trimming conversation history cannot remove it from the protected system prompt.

This adds an optional way to send less of that catalog upfront. Permitted shell, file read/write/edit, and basic memory recall/store tools stay fully described. Other permitted built-ins appear in a short list. The model asks `tool_search` for a full definition when it needs one. Native tool-calling providers receive selected definitions on subsequent requests; text providers receive them in the search result.

Tools remain callable under the same permissions and approval rules. Looking up a definition does not grant access, and knowing a permitted tool's name still lets the model call it directly. The option defaults off. When search is unavailable, native requests restore permitted built-in definitions. Text prompts restore them within the configured prompt budget, including same-agent SOP steps that reuse the parent prompt. Full definitions remain when they fit; the existing identity/safety and timestamp priorities apply when they do not. Custom instructions appended before a model call retain their existing treatment outside the base prompt's cap.

When a step permits search but excludes other tools, its compact catalogue lists only that step's permitted built-ins. A scoped catalogue refresh only filters complete surviving blocks that fit in their existing space. It removes truncated blocks and leaves omitted catalogues omitted, preserving prompt assembly's budget decision. Both projections change only the provider-request copy, leaving the parent prompt and shared selection unchanged. Independent delegates use their target's permitted catalogue for both native and text providers. Each cross-agent SOP step uses its admitted configuration, including its prompt cap.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This reuses MCP's discovery protocol and existing conversation selection handle, without placing built-in executables in MCP's activation map or adding a second discovery tool. The integration spans existing assembly, prompt, request, parsing, and streaming consumers because hiding a schema must not hide a callable name or let protocol text leak into streamed answers. Keeping only the native-request filter would leave text providers unchanged and break structured argument recovery.

The large diff includes inline proof of policy filtering, narrowing, memory rebinding, eager fallback, native/text requests, direct calls, mixed batches, and streaming. No dependency, new execution subsystem, ownership-tier inventory, or history-trimming redesign is added. Internal schemas still support parsing; the optimization concerns definitions sent to providers, not schema-allocation costs inside the process.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Captured requests at the production Agent boundary and focused discovery/registry tests establish the schema-exposure contract without a credentialed provider.

### How I tested

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0.
- Eager fallback cap repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs) | test(cross_agent_step_) | test(scoped_protocol_refresh_keeps_hook_appended_text)'`: exit 0, `10 tests run: 10 passed, 5719 skipped`. Production SOP request capture covers a finite cap that truncates definitions, a finite cap that retains full permitted definitions, explicit unlimited zero, and configless scoped cap transport. It checks the Unicode character ceiling, timestamp orientation, continued denied execution, unchanged parent history and shared selection. The existing projection fixture covers repeated no-hook refresh and fresh requests with appended custom instructions; it preserves those instructions outside the base cap. Cross-agent isolation, tool scope, model-switch isolation and strict text-policy checks pass. The existing macOS compact-unwind linker warning remains. Initial fixture compilation failed on borrowed temporaries; a later assertion rejected a harmless trailing newline after orientation. Both fixture issues were corrected before this final full selection passed; production code was unchanged by those corrections.
- Prompt-limit repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs)'`: exit 0, 3 passed. The existing projection test now uses rendered catalogues and real capped prompts in native/text modes. It checks that partial or omitted catalogues are not restored, complete replacements cannot grow by Unicode character count, repeated refresh preserves history, and context and timestamp orientation survive. Production SOP request capture and strict text-policy checks also pass.
- Catalogue-scope repair: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -E 'test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(builtin_prompt_is_compact_filtered_and_omits_selected_schemas) | test(builtin_catalog_refresh_updates_only_surviving_deferred_names) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests)'`: exit 0, 10 passed. Production SOP request capture covers search allowed and excluded in native and text modes, continued execution denials, and unchanged parent history and shared selection. Existing projection tests cover repeated scoped refresh, duplicate and truncated catalogues, preserved unrelated sections and timestamp orientation, and strict text suppression.
- Scoped fallback repair validation: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::turn::provider_call::) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests) | test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(independent_full_target_receives_full_prompt_and_executes_uncovered_tool) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route) | test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope) | test(builtin_search_fallback_preserves_strict_policy_and_scoped_replay) | test(strict_non_native_prompt_policy_hides_text_tool_protocol_inputs)'`: 38 checks passed; the SOP scope test initially expected the native denial message in text mode. After correcting only that assertion, `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(run_tool_call_loop_enforces_sop_step_tool_scope)'` passed, exit 0. Together these cover all 39 selected checks. The production SOP test captures native and text requests, verifies permitted definitions when search is excluded, preserves execution denials and parent history, and leaves shared selection unchanged. The focused scoped-refresh replay test prevents duplicate protocol/schema blocks and verifies strict text non-injection and unrelated prompt sections. Production code was unchanged between these two runs.
- Discovery repair validation before master integration: `cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests) | test(turn_prompt_defers_builtin_definition_until_search_selection) | test(independent_full_target_receives_full_prompt_and_executes_uncovered_tool) | test(independent_prompt_respects_text_tool_policy_for_deferred_section) | test(independent_delegate_denies_prompt_required_skill_tools_without_approval_route)'`: exit 0, 7 passed and 5,473 skipped. The production independent-delegate test covers native and text discovery while retaining approval behavior. The rebuilt loop prompt and iteration-spec tests cover eager permitted definitions when search is excluded, continued exclusions, and unchanged shared selection state. Strict text-tool suppression also passes.
- `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -E 'test(tool_search::tests) | test(mcp_deferred::tests)'`: exit 0, 51 passed.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib runtime_profile_deferred_builtin_tools_is_opt_in`: exit 0, 1 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(/native_agent_requests_expose_builtin|text_agent_requests_receive|admitted_hidden_builtin|text_agent_executes_hidden_builtin|turn_prompt_defers_builtin|builtin_deferral|builtin_schemas_stay_eager|listing_assembly_keeps|removing_builtin_search|deferred_memory_selection/) | test(agent::turn::tool_specs::tests) | test(agent::turn::parse_response::argument_preservation_tests) | test(agent::turn::stream_consume::tests) | (test(agent::loop_) & test(stream))'`: exit 0, 66 passed. It covers captured native/text requests, hidden permitted direct calls and a mixed search/call response, schema-assisted structured argument recovery, streamed protocol suppression, scoped pruning/rebinding, eager fallback, and existing streaming regressions. The macOS debug harness emits the existing large compact-unwind linker warning.
- `cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --lib`: exit 0, no Rust warnings after making the now test-only import conditional.
- `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: exit 0.
- File-scoped `docs_quality_gate.sh` and `docs_links_gate.sh` for `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md`: exit 0, zero Markdown errors and six link-collector tests passed.
- **CI checks relied on and why:** [Required CI for the eager fallback repair](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38103681104) is pending at `4c8071b81a9ae545de0c100ef6b643d6e457d452`. The ten focused local checks establish the changed capped projection, production SOP requests, replay and retained hook behavior. [Previous required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38017092103) passed at `66ccab0d382c036ccc938fba730c671d42ee1351`; it does not establish CI success for this new repair head.
- **Known gap:** No credentialed-provider latency or token benchmark was selected. Request tests verify which definitions the production boundary sends, not an end-to-end performance number.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Executable ownership and grant checks remain unchanged. Built-in selection stores no executable instance. Narrowing removes schema metadata and selection, and memory rebinding updates the metadata from the retained registry. Exact MCP selection stays uncapped while combined keyword results remain capped.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The change concerns model requests and tool results, not visual presentation.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Propose one bounded holding-crate exception for
  #11578, which makes a context-window refusal diagnosable. When a request
  cannot fit the model's window the runtime refuses it locally, and the
  operator's journal line for that refusal was empty. #11578 carries the
  request's raw estimate and its raw system-prompt and tool-schema shares on
  `ContextWindowExceeded`, renders them through `breakdown()` with any
  calibration correction as a separate term, and adds them to the existing
  rejection and failure records. The review on #11578 confirmed the diagnostic
  repair at `94dd35cb0` and asked for this record as the remaining step,
  supporting a bounded instrumentation exception that keeps the existing
  agent-loop and cron owners and is reviewed at their extraction
  ([comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11578#issuecomment-6089341340)).
- **Why an exception rather than extraction:** the error type, both places
  that raise it, and the cron failure record all live in subsystems this crate
  already holds. Their owners, the agent loop in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel`
  extraction and `zeroclaw-cron` (#10557), are where the code moves when those
  extractions happen; moving three token counts ahead of them would split one
  error type across crates for no boundary the roadmap asks for.
- **Scope boundary:** Contributor placement contract only. No runtime behaviour
  changes in this PR. The row covers `src/agent/turn/{outcome,mod,max_iter}.rs`,
  the `cron_agent_job_failed` record in `src/cron/scheduler.rs`, and focused
  regressions in `src/agent/loop_.rs`. It is limited to token counts, never
  request content, and excludes any change to the refusal threshold, trimming,
  dispatch decisions, the localized user-facing text, recovery, retained state
  or config. #11578's journal-line change in `zeroclaw-channels` is outside this
  crate's contract and is not covered by, or in need of, this row.
- **Blast radius:** Placement authority for the listed paths and behaviour.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11578. Follows the exception-record precedent in
  #11524, #11440 and #11603.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's runtime crate is a temporary home for code waiting to be split into
its own crates, so changes that add behaviour there need the Core Team's
permission, written into a table in that crate's `AGENTS.md`. #11578 makes one
log line useful: when a request is too big for the model, the line now says how
big, and how much of it went to the agent's instructions, its tool
descriptions, and the conversation. That code sits in the agent loop and the
cron scheduler, which still live in the runtime crate, so this adds the one row
of permission it needs. Nothing runs differently because of this pull request
on its own.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`. This is a one-row contributor-contract
  proposal with no executable behaviour.
- **Commands run:** `git diff --check`; `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`
  (`No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.`). Every row in the
  active-exception table keeps the same four columns, so the table renders
  unchanged apart from the new row. The row adds no links.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The row is a
  placement permission for diagnostics proposed in #11578, which record token
  counts only.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No

Revert this PR's squash-merge commit to remove the recorded placement exception.
This does not change runtime code; #11578, if merged separately, must be
assessed on its own.

prs.title: fix(plugins): record socket and WebSocket egress denials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A refused `wasi:http` request logs a WARN `plugin_egress_denied` record naming the instance, host, reason, and the `zeroclaw config set` command that grants reach. A refused socket or WebSocket connect logged nothing: the guest got its typed error (`access-denied`, `destination-denied`) and the operator saw no trace. A channel plugin whose gateway host is not granted therefore retried silently.
  - The remedy builders and the two recorders move out of `wasi_http.rs` into a crate-private module, `egress_report.rs`, and all three adapters call it at the same points: a malformed request, a store with no egress service, and a refusal from the egress service.
  - Records gain a `transport` attribute (`http`, `socket`, `websocket`). `error_key` values (`plugin_egress_denied`, `plugin_egress_connection_limit`) and messages are unchanged, so existing log searches keep working.
  - The requested host and the reason are guest-controlled: the sockets `connect-request.host` and both transports' TLS profile names are unbounded WIT strings, and the reason for a malformed one quotes it `Debug`-escaped (up to 6x its size). Both are escaped and bounded while they are formatted, through a sink that stops the formatter at the budget (host 253 characters, reason 2,048). A guest-sized value is never rendered in full on the host, and control, bidirectional, and zero-width characters in a raw host reach the log escaped.
- **Scope boundary:** Guest-visible errors, the policy decision and its order, WIT, config, and dependencies are unchanged. Only refusals at the egress boundary are recorded. Not recorded, matching `wasi:http` today: timeouts, URL-shape errors, TLS setup failures after authorization (for example a missing profile secret), and dial or handshake failures; recording TLS setup failures under their own key is a follow-up. No deduplication or rate limit: every refused attempt is logged, as `wasi:http` already does, and suppressing repeats per instance and host is a follow-up, tracked in #11626.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-plugins` only. Log consumers see new WARN records for socket and WebSocket refusals and a new `transport` key on all three. HTTP records' `_file`/`_line` move to the new module. Most of the diff is a move; `git diff --color-moved` shows it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10999. Depends on #11228 for CI coverage: that PR adds `socket_plugin_e2e` and `websocket_plugin_e2e` to the plugin component job. Until it merges, the HTTP assertion below is the one CI runs.
- **Labels:** `docs`, `size:XL` (applied by the path and size labelers; `risk:*` and `domain:*` are set by maintainers. Proposed: `risk:medium` and `domain:security`, since guest-chosen strings newly reach host logs from two adapters)

### What this does, simply

When a plugin tries to reach a host the operator has not allowed, the plugin only sees an error. For web requests, ZeroClaw also writes a log line that says which plugin was blocked, which host, and the exact command that allows it. Plugins that use raw sockets or WebSockets (IRC, Nostr, Discord) got no such line, so a misconfigured one just kept failing quietly. This PR makes all three kinds of connection write the same log line.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the new behavior is asserted end to end by the tests below.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the plugin component and lib steps of `Check (plugins cranelift backend)`. `egress_plugin_e2e` (already in CI) asserts the HTTP record through the shared recorder.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the socket and WebSocket e2e suites run in CI only after #11228; I ran them locally.
- **Commands run and tail output:** macOS 26 (aarch64), rustc 1.98.0, `TMPDIR=/private/tmp`, at the head of this branch.

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                                  # clean
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings   # clean
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings                     # clean (module absent)
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasmtime   # clean
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-pulley   # clean
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
test result: ok. 274 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift
channel_plugin_e2e 14, egress_plugin_e2e 10, reference_plugin 9, reference_plugin_e2e 1 (+3 filtered),
sequential_egress_e2e 4, socket_plugin_e2e 7, tool_plugin_e2e 2, tool_plugin_timeout_e2e 5,
websocket_plugin_e2e 5: all ok
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ DOCS_FILES=<the two changed docs> bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No prose em-dashes in changed docs files. ... Summary: 0 error(s)
$ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Mutation checks: each change below was made alone, its target test run, and the file restored. Every one failed its test.

| Injected change | Test that caught it |
|---|---|
| WebSocket: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_websocket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| WebSocket: store with no egress service not recorded | `a_refused_websocket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| Sockets: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_socket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| Sockets: store with no egress service not recorded | `a_refused_socket_is_recorded_for_the_operator` |
| `wasi:http`: refusal from the egress service not recorded | `a_refused_request_is_recorded_under_the_http_transport` |
| Guest host recorded unbounded | `guest_supplied_text_is_bounded_in_the_record` |
| WebSocket reported under the socket family | `every_transport_is_recorded_under_its_adapter_family` |
| The reason rendered in full before it is kept | `guest_supplied_text_is_bounded_in_the_record` |
| The raw host recorded unescaped | `a_recorded_host_is_escaped` |

  `bounded_formatting_stops_at_the_budget` pins the property the "reason rendered in full" row relies on: a `Display` that would write forever is stopped at the budget, so the cost of a refusal record does not grow with the guest's input.

  Not verified: Linux and Windows locally.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo doc -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasmtime` with `-D warnings` fails on master already (private intra-doc links in `component.rs` and `wasm_channel.rs`, files this PR does not touch); the new module is private and adds no public docs. Full `cargo test --workspace` was not run: the change is confined to `zeroclaw-plugins`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: All No. Note for review: guest-chosen strings (the requested host, and reasons quoting it) now reach persisted and broadcast host logs from two more adapters. They are bounded per record, JSON-encoded, and limited per call by the frame's host-call budget; the writer drops rather than blocks when its queue is full. `remedy` shows the instance's grant lists, which `wasi:http` records already print and which are plaintext in config by design.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. No flags, config, or persisted state.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** missing `plugin_egress_denied` records for socket or WebSocket refusals, or a change in the guest-visible error codes (both asserted by the e2e suites).

prs.title: fix(agent): let an approved shell call be rerun later in the same turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `prepare_tool_calls` keeps a turn-scoped set of prompt-required `shell` signatures so a model that keeps asking for the same command can't make the operator approve it again and again. The set never dropped an entry, so after the operator **approved** a call and it ran, an identical call later in the same turn aborted the turn with `repeated prompt-required tool call 'shell' with identical arguments before approval`. That blocks legitimate reruns ("run the same apply again to confirm no changes", re-running a check after an edit).
  - The signature is now released when the approval gate returns `Proceed { approved: true }`. An identical call in a later iteration then goes through the normal approval prompt again.
  - A denied call (operator `Deny`) or an unanswered one (runtime fail-closed deny) still keeps its signature. Repeating it still aborts before the operator is asked again, so the denial-loop protection from #7901 stays in place.
  - The same-round set is unchanged: an identical call in the same batch is still deduplicated without a second prompt.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to shell risk classification, the approval gate itself, `ApprovalManager`, same-round dedup, `tool_call_dedup_exempt`, non-shell prompt-required tools, reentrant agent tools, or the ACP error path. It does not address the separate question in the issue of whether the ACP process exits after `-32603`.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-runtime` agent turn preparation for prompt-required `shell` calls only. An approved repeat now prompts again instead of aborting. Repetition is still bounded by `max_tool_iterations` and by the operator, who can deny the rerun, after which a further identical call aborts.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11612. Related #7820, #7901, #11507.

### What this does, simply

In supervised mode, ZeroClaw remembers which shell commands it has asked you to approve during a turn, so a stuck model can't flood you with the same approval prompt. It also remembered commands you had already approved, so if the model wanted to run the same approved command again, the turn just failed. Now an approved command is forgotten once you approve it, and running it again asks you again. A command you denied is still remembered, so asking for it again still stops the turn.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is covered by deterministic loop tests with a scripted provider and approving/denying channels.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and lint jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# clean

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- repeated_shell reprompts
# test agent::loop_::tests::run_tool_call_loop_aborts_repeated_shell_call_after_denial ... ok
# test agent::loop_::tests::run_tool_call_loop_reprompts_identical_shell_rerun_after_approval ... ok
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

# after review (d49d421): same turn with dedup_enabled: true
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- prompt_required shell_rerun repeated_shell
# test agent::loop_::tests::run_tool_call_loop_runs_approved_shell_rerun_with_dedup_enabled ... ok
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

# Same filter with the call_prep.rs change stashed (master behavior):
# thread 'agent::loop_::tests::run_tool_call_loop_reprompts_identical_shell_rerun_after_approval' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/loop_.rs:10051:28
# test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
# test result: ok. 5678 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
```

- **Tests changed:**
  - `run_tool_call_loop_aborts_repeated_prompt_required_shell_before_reprompting` asserted the old contract (an approved first run, then an abort). It is now a shared helper with two tests: `run_tool_call_loop_reprompts_identical_shell_rerun_after_approval` (2 approvals, 2 executions, turn completes) and `run_tool_call_loop_aborts_repeated_shell_call_after_denial` (1 approval request, 0 executions, the turn aborts with the existing error).
  - `run_tool_call_loop_prompt_guard_ignores_same_round_dedup_exempt_tools` now uses a denying channel. It still checks that a dedup-exempt `shell` is covered by the cross-round guard, which now applies to denied calls.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing beyond the tests above. I did not run a live ACP session.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` doesn't complete with the local toolchain (rustc 1.99.0). It stops on new lints in untouched crates (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `zeroclaw-providers`, `fetch_update` deprecation in `zeroclaw-tools`). `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets` without `-D warnings` reports nothing in the two changed files.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: An approved command can now be re-requested in the same turn. Each rerun still needs a fresh operator approval, so nothing runs without one.

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

prs.title: feat(slack): optionally accept bot and workflow messages
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Slack delivers Workflow Builder steps and other app posts as `subtype = "bot_message"` with no `user` field. Two independent guards reject them: `is_supported_message_subtype` allows only `None | file_share | thread_broadcast`, and the sender checks that follow require a non-empty `user`. There was no setting to change this, so @mentioning the agent from a Slack workflow silently did nothing.
  - Adds `channels.slack.<alias>.allow_bot_messages`, **off by default**. When enabled, `bot_message` passes the subtype gate. The peer allowlist always matches the posting app's `bot_id` for a `bot_message`, even when the event also carries a `user` field.
  - Opting in widens *which senders are considered*; it does not skip authorization. Operators can allow specific bot IDs rather than `"*"`.
  - **Own-post filtering fails closed (added after review).** Posts carrying `user` are compared with this app's user ID. A userless post can only be told apart from our own echo by comparing `bot_id` with the bot ID cached from `auth.test`; until that identity is known, no userless bot post is admitted at all, and `listen` logs a warning that the opt-in is inert for those posts on this run. Wildcard peers therefore cannot let the agent re-enter on its own output.
  - **Authorization boundary (added after review):** admission carries provenance. `inbound_sender_identity` returns `InboundSender { id, is_bot }`, and every `parse_approval_reply` call site is gated on `!is_bot`. Admitting bot text otherwise handed it the operator approval path, where a bot that could read an approval prompt could reply with the visible token and authorize a pending tool call. Provenance is taken from `subtype`, not from which field supplied the id, so a `bot_message` that also carries `user` stays bot-authored.
  - **Hybrid-post attribution (added after review).** A `bot_message` carrying both `user` and `bot_id` is authorized by the posting app's `bot_id` alone: an allowlisted `user` entry can never admit a post from an unlisted app, and a `bot_message` without a usable `bot_id` is rejected outright rather than falling back to `user`.
  - Applied at all three trigger paths (Socket Mode, polling, and thread replies), so behavior does not depend on which transport a deployment uses.
- **Scope boundary:** Which inbound messages can start a turn, and that admitted bot messages cannot consume human approval tokens. It does NOT change thread-context hydration (`slack.rs` still filters bot posts out of historical context; which messages the model is shown is a separate decision from what triggers a turn), does NOT add Block Kit or interactive support for bot senders, does NOT change the allowlist mechanism, and does NOT touch other channels.
- **Blast radius:** Confined to the Slack channel. With the flag off, the default and the value every existing deployment gets, inbound handling is unchanged: `bot_message` is still rejected by the same gate as before, and `inbound_sender_identity` returns the same identity the previous inline `user` extraction did. Only operators who explicitly enable it see new senders.
- **Docs:** `docs/book/src/channels/slack.md` gains a "Messages from other apps" section (the setting, the matching peer-group entry, the prompt-injection surface, the approval and self-echo boundaries, the restart requirement) and two troubleshooting rows.
- **Linked issue(s):** None

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`slack`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Slack workspace with an app that posts into a channel the agent is in as a `bot_message` (a Workflow Builder step, or on plans without Workflow Builder an incoming webhook of a separate app), and a peer allowlist covering that app's bot ID.
- **Steps to run:** Have the app post a message addressed to the agent.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** with `allow_bot_messages = true` and the app's bot ID allowlisted the post starts a turn and the agent replies once; with the setting absent or `false` it is ignored exactly as before.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the post is dropped with no way to enable it, first by the subtype gate, and if that were relaxed, again by the `user.is_empty()` check.

### How I tested

**Current-head validation, September 28:** The [follow-up test report](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10622#issuecomment-5874568165) records execution on `c156d63025b31a4197b6fe3b8b598fdce77e6fc9` with `channel-slack` enabled. The focused sender-identity, polling-ingress, bot/human approval, and opt-in tests passed: **24 passed; 0 failed**. This includes the new hybrid-attribution regressions. The same-head full feature-enabled suite passed **2,118 tests with 2 ignored**; the no-default-features Slack suite passed **1,038 tests**. Formatting passed and feature-enabled Clippy exited 0. This supersedes the earlier crates.io limitation. Required CI is green; Slack test execution relies on these explicit feature-enabled runs.

The earlier validation record below is retained with its original revisions.

```sh

cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-slack --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-slack --lib

cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets
cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** fmt and the `ci-all` compile/lint jobs cover the changed Slack code. The default workspace test job does not execute Slack tests; the explicit feature-enabled local commands above exercise them. Rustdoc and comment hygiene were also checked locally.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The default workspace test job does not enable `channel-slack`, so it does not execute Slack tests. The explicit feature-enabled runs linked above cover this gap for the current head. The advisory Windows and dependency-audit failures mentioned in earlier review records are historical; the current-head checks pass.
- **Earlier commands run and tail output** (`53b077cf3a`, before the hybrid-attribution repair):

  ```text
  test result: ok. 1917 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```

  Twenty-four tests added or replaced by this PR. The twenty below were run on head `53b077cf3a`; the four hybrid-attribution tests at the end of the list were added with the fix on the new head:

  ```text
  test slack::tests::bot_message_subtype_requires_opt_in ... ok

  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_uses_bot_id_only_when_bots_are_allowed ... ok
  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_drops_our_own_bot_echo ... ok
  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_ignores_blank_and_missing_bot_ids ... ok

  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_admits_userless_bot_ids_only_for_bot_message ... ok
  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_drops_our_own_hybrid_bot_echo_regardless_of_user ... ok

  test slack::tests::polling_ingress_keeps_the_opt_in_scoped_to_bot_message ... ok

  test slack::tests::polling_ingress_admits_foreign_bot_and_drops_own_echo_when_bot_id_is_known ... ok
  test slack::tests::allow_bot_messages_defaults_off_and_builder_sets_it ... ok
  test slack::tests::inbound_identity_rejects_hybrid_bot_message_without_bot_id  (added on c156d630; passed in the September 28 focused run)
  ```
