  On the new head the hybrid expectations changed: `bot_message_with_user_field_is_still_bot_authored`,
  `inbound_identity_drops_our_own_hybrid_bot_echo_regardless_of_user`, and
  `polling_ingress_drops_our_own_hybrid_echo_when_auth_test_has_no_user_id` now assert attribution to the
  `bot_id` (`B_APP` / `B_WORKFLOW`) instead of the `user` field.

  The initial attempt to validate `c156d630` was blocked by unavailable crates.io access. The September 28 feature-enabled runs above resolved that gap.

  The `polling_ingress_*` tests drive the production polling ingress (`listen` against a mocked `auth.test` and `conversations.history`) with `allow_bot_messages = true` and wildcard peers. The first serves an `auth.test` response without `bot_id` and the agent's own userless `bot_message` echo, and asserts no `ChannelMessage` is emitted. The second is the positive control with `bot_id` present: the foreign app's post reaches dispatch and the own echo does not. A third covers a whitespace-only `auth.test` `bot_id`, kept separate from the missing-field control. All of them, and the helper tests, were run with the fail-closed guards reverted and fail there; they pass with them.

  The four approval-boundary tests cover sender provenance and a seeded pending token. The exact escalation string from review (`abc123 approve <@U_SELF>`, trailing mention included) leaves the token untouched for a bot sender and resolves it for a human sender. These tests repeat the approval guard rather than invoke the receivers.

  `cargo clippy ... -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the rustdoc gate and the comment hygiene gate all exited clean on the earlier tested head `53b077cf3a`. Current-head formatting and Clippy results are linked above.

  Remaining earlier command results on `53b077cf3a`, stated in full:

  ```text
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-slack --lib
      916 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib
      1605 passed; 0 failed        (this environment)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib slack_config_
      8 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p xtask generated_prose_gate
      5 passed; 0 failed
  ```

  One caveat on the full config suite, raised in review and worth stating plainly: a reviewer running `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib` on this same head saw `1590 passed; 15 failed`. The identical 15 failures appear on an unmodified `origin/master` baseline in that environment, and they are the existing runtime-config/load-or-init tests resolving through a shared scratch home instead of each test's temporary HOME and workspace. So that command's result is environment-dependent: clean here, pre-existing failures elsewhere, and unrelated to `allow_bot_messages`, which the focused `slack_config_` run covers. Treat the full-suite line as environment-dependent rather than as a clean pass everywhere.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I traced all four `is_supported_message_subtype` call sites and confirmed the three trigger paths are updated while hydration is intentionally left alone. For the approval fix I read each of the three `parse_approval_reply` call sites and confirmed the gate is applied at every one. For the fail-closed fix I confirmed the three receive paths all obtain `own_bot_id` from the same cache and pass it into the single admission helper, so the rule holds regardless of transport.

  **Live delivery check** (details and channel history in the PR comment of Sept 14): a release build of head `c11266aac9` running as a daemon under systemd on Linux, Socket Mode, `mention_only = true`. The workspace is on Slack's free plan, so the app-authored post came from an incoming webhook of a separate app rather than Workflow Builder; it has the same shape (`subtype = "bot_message"`, no `user`, foreign `bot_id`). With the flag absent the post was ignored (no reply, no log activity over 2.5 min). With the flag on and that specific bot ID allowlisted, the agent replied once within 4 s and did not react to its own reply. Each config was applied and then the service restarted. The fail-closed change in the current head is a strict narrowing of admission and does not affect that run, where `auth.test` returned `bot_id`. An actual Workflow Builder post has not been observed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No user-visible interface state changed: this alters which inbound Slack messages start a turn, and renders no new output.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `c156d63025b31a4197b6fe3b8b598fdce77e6fc9` for the September 28 feature-enabled automated runs linked above; `53b077cf3a` for the retained earlier automated record. The live workspace check was run on `c11266aac9` and is reported as such below, not as current-head evidence.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A` for presentation. The behavioural evidence is the test output above and the channel history quoted in the live-check comment.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** with the setting absent, an app post mentioning the agent produced no reply and no log activity; with it enabled and the posting app's bot ID allowlisted, the agent replied once and did not react to its own reply. Changed state is config only, applied by restart.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Current-head execution is limited to the September 28 commands linked above. The retained config, runtime-check, rustdoc, generated-prose, and comment-hygiene results belong to earlier revisions, not new runs on `c156d630`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes** (opt-in)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes** (opt-in)
- Authorization boundary changed? **Yes**, see the approval-path note below

The `Yes` answers describe the same opt-in surface. Enabling `allow_bot_messages` lets non-human senders drive the agent, and app-authored text becomes model-visible, so a compromised or hostile workspace app could attempt prompt injection through it. Mitigations: the setting defaults to off; enabling it does not bypass the peer allowlist, which checks the posting app's `bot_id` for every `bot_message`; the config documentation recommends allowlisting specific bot IDs rather than `"*"`; posts carrying our own user ID are rejected; and userless posts are rejected unless our own `bot_id` is known and differs, so an unavailable or incomplete `auth.test` cannot open a self-reply loop even with wildcard peers. A second boundary matters as much: admitted bot text is barred from the operator approval path, so permission to post never becomes permission to authorize a tool call. Both boundaries are covered by dedicated regressions, including two that run the production polling ingress.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes**, one new optional key, `channels.slack.<alias>.allow_bot_messages` (bool, default `false`). Absent config behaves exactly as today.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: **none required.** The key is optional and defaults to `false`, so existing configurations keep today's behaviour with no migration, no schema change and no action on upgrade. To opt in: set `channels.slack.<alias>.allow_bot_messages = true`, add the intended app's bot ID to that channel's peer group (prefer a specific `B...` ID over `"*"`), and restart the channel, because this setting has no live-reload path. To opt back out, remove the key or set it to `false` and restart.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash sha>` on `master`; no data or schema migration is involved. Operators on a build that includes this change can also neutralise it without a rollback via the toggle below.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.slack.<alias>.allow_bot_messages` (default `false`). Removing the key or setting it to `false`, then restarting the channel, restores the pre-change admission exactly; there is no live reload for this setting.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an agent replying to app posts it should ignore, or replying repeatedly in a channel with no human input (self-reply loop). Grep the channel log for the warning `allow_bot_messages is enabled but auth.test did not return this app's bot_id`, which means userless bot posts are being dropped on that run, and for the agent's own `bot_id` appearing as an admitted sender, which must never happen.

## Note for maintainers: Slack tests do not run under default features

While validating this I found that `channel-slack` is in `channels-full` but not in `default-channels`, so `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels` compiles neither `slack.rs` nor its tests. My first validation pass looked green while never having built the file I changed.

That is pre-existing and out of scope here. The `ci-all` compile/lint jobs include `channels-full`, but the default workspace test job does not execute Slack tests. Automated Slack test execution can be followed up separately.

prs.title: fix(tunnel): report the URL tailscale actually serves the gateway on
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - With `tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`, the gateway ran `tailscale serve|funnel <local_port>`. Current Tailscale CLIs publish that as HTTPS on port **443**. The tunnel, however, advertised `https://<host>:<local_port>` (for example `:42617`), a port Tailscale never listens on, so the printed `Public URL` did not work.
  - The tunnel now passes the HTTPS port explicitly (`--https=443`) and advertises `https://<host>`, which uses the standard HTTPS port 443. Both now denote HTTPS port 443 without relying on the CLI default.
  - 443 is valid for both `serve` and `funnel` (funnel accepts only 443/8443/10000), so funnel deployments get a correct URL too.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change which local port is proxied, the `tailscale status` hostname resolution, other tunnel providers, or anything about WSS or enrollment (that is a separate PR, see Linked issue(s)). Does not make the HTTPS port configurable.
- **Blast radius:** Only `TailscaleTunnel::start()`. That affects the `🌐 Tunnel active` / `Public URL` startup output and the `tunnel_url` value the gateway passes on from `start()`. Nothing in the codebase or docs depended on the old `host:port` form (checked by grep).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11530 (overlapping Tailscale adapter work)

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw shares its web gateway over Tailscale, it prints the address to open. That address was wrong: it included the gateway's internal port number, but Tailscale actually serves the gateway on the standard HTTPS port. Copying the printed link led nowhere. Now the printed link is the one Tailscale actually serves, and the command ZeroClaw runs states the port explicitly instead of relying on Tailscale's default.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. It is a one-line check on any tailnet node.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `cli` (daemon/gateway startup output).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A host on a tailnet with HTTPS certificates enabled, a user that is a Tailscale operator, and `[tunnel] tunnel_provider = "tailscale"`.
- **Steps to run:** Start the daemon, copy the `🌐 Tunnel active:` URL, open it from another tailnet device, and run `tailscale serve status --json` on the host (the tunnel runs a foreground serve session, which plain `tailscale serve status` does not list).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The URL is `https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net` and loads the dashboard. `serve status --json` shows a `Foreground` session with `TCP 443 → HTTPS` and `<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net:443` proxying `/` to `http://127.0.0.1:<gateway port>`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The URL is `https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net:42617`, which refuses the connection or times out, while `serve status --json` shows the proxy on 443.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI passed on `d7a5ad379fbe196e4e5eb74cd90b5cfa647c77a5`, including formatting, lint, and tests: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37996867772.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No tailnet in CI, so the live URL is not exercised; the unit tests pin the arguments and the URL.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on head `8938519e4`, rebased on `upstream/master` `a7ec85708`, with rustc 1.97.1, in a dedicated target directory:

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

$ cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 58s

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_public_url_omits_the_local_port ... ok
test tunnel::tailscale::tests::gateway_serve_args_pin_the_https_port ... ok
test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5373 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I confirmed from `tailscale serve --help` and `tailscale funnel --help` (Tailscale 1.102.4) that `--https` is accepted by both and that HTTPS is the default mode. I grepped the repo and docs for any consumer of the old `https://host:port` form and found none. **Live run:** Serve mode on PR head `d7a5ad379`, Tailscale 1.102.4, Linux x86_64: the printed URL matched the foreground serve config and returned 200; the old `:<local_port>` form was refused. Details: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11531#discussion_r4239701222
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`. Only the URL in the existing `🌐 Tunnel active:` line changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Unit checks on `8938519e4`; live Serve-mode startup and `/health` on `d7a5ad379`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11531#discussion_r4239701222.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** before `🌐 Tunnel active: https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net:42617`, after `🌐 Tunnel active: https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net` (derived from the tested format function, not captured live).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The printed URL returned HTTP 200 on port 443 through the serving node's tailnet address. The old URL with the backend port was refused. `tailscale serve status --json` showed the matching foreground proxy; stopping the tunnel removed it.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally. The change is confined to one function in `zeroclaw-runtime`, whose tunnel suite was run, and the remaining crates are covered by required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The exposed listener is unchanged: Tailscale already served on 443, and this makes that explicit.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the URL fix with `git revert 8938519e4`.

prs.title: test(config): isolate null spelling aliases on macOS
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The Unix foreign-null-spelling policy test now removes each symlink after that spelling's resolve/read/write assertions.
  - This keeps every spelling pointed at its original target while avoiding `nul`/`NUL` alias collisions on case-insensitive macOS filesystems.
- **Scope boundary:** Test fixture lifetime only; production path resolution and filesystem policy are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** One `zeroclaw-config` unit test.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11634, where the macOS platform job exposed the failure.

### What this does, simply

The test checks several Windows null-device spellings on Unix. It created all of the spellings as symlinks in one directory and kept each link alive until the test ended. On the default case-insensitive macOS filesystem, spellings such as `nul` and `NUL` name the same directory entry, so creating the later fixture failed before the policy assertions ran. The test now removes each fixture after its assertions, allowing every spelling to be checked independently. The policy behavior under test does not change.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this is a test-only fixture-lifetime change with a focused automated test.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Quality Gate CI passed, including the changed test on Linux. Fork Scheduled Platform Tests run `38041545454` executed the full workspace suite on native macOS and Windows; the changed null-spelling test passed on macOS's default case-insensitive filesystem.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The fork platform workflow is red from unrelated failures inherited from the source branch. Its macOS failures are Telegram, Hailo, RPC grant, Tailscale, and Serply tests; Windows reports the same nine unrelated failures on both fix branches.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception
running 1 test
test policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 1772 filtered out

$ fork Scheduled Platform Tests run 38041545454 (native macOS)
PASS [0.015s] zeroclaw-config policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output, exit 0)

$ git diff --check
(no output, exit 0)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed that each alias is removed only after its original resolution, read-denial, and write-denial assertions complete. The native macOS full-suite run passed the changed test.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ab28e1641ad64c1502717c4e52527b6cba613697`, `zeroclaw-config` unit test.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The focused test passes on Linux and in the native macOS full suite, including the case-insensitive filesystem path that originally failed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests and clippy were skipped because this changes one line in a unit-test fixture and the focused test exercises the complete changed behavior.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: feat(runtime): add effort-aware local and cloud routing
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add an opt-in `runtime_profiles.<name>.effort_routing` policy that maps existing local and cloud route hints onto ZeroClaw's deterministic complexity classifier.
  - Keep simple and ambiguous turns local. Send a complex turn to the configured cloud route only when `cloud_escalation = "auto"`; the default `"never"` keeps automatic routing local.
  - Preserve operator CLI, session, and channel choices as manual overrides. A model-issued `model_switch` changes the active provider and model without changing the current automatic or manual ownership mode. For agents opted into effort routing, channel `/model auto` and its scoped variants clear manual channel selections and restore configured automatic routing; other agents retain ordinary model and route selection for a hint named `auto`.
  - Enforce the selected provider set before every Reliable attempt, including fallback, streaming, stream recovery, capability discovery, and configured vision routing, so a local decision cannot silently reach cloud through availability recovery.
  - Log the selected target, complexity tier, policy, surface, and message length without recording prompt text.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR does not add a model-assisted classifier, ask-before-cloud flow, escalation-frequency limit, separate cost cap, provider family, or model-discovery system. Existing configurations stay unchanged unless a runtime profile adds `effort_routing`.
- **Blast radius:** Opted-in structured Agent, direct CLI, daemon, and channel turns; runtime-profile validation; provider routing and reliability fallback; channel model-selection state; provider-routing documentation. Existing fixed routing and reliability remain unchanged when the policy is absent.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #7951. Related #11436. Related #5287. Related #7539. Related #7431.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can already route a named hint to a configured model, but it did not have one operator-visible rule for deciding when ordinary work should stay local and when harder work may use cloud. Reliability fallback could also cross that boundary after a local route was selected.

This PR lets an operator name one existing local route and one existing cloud route on a runtime profile. ZeroClaw uses its existing local complexity estimator before each eligible turn. Simple and ambiguous work stays local. Complex work reaches the cloud route only when the operator explicitly enables automatic escalation.

The routing decision also limits every provider attempt for that turn. A local decision cannot reach a cloud fallback, streaming recovery, or dedicated vision provider that the policy excluded. An explicit model choice still wins, and existing configurations do not opt in automatically.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

This is a cross-crate policy because selection and enforcement have different owners. Runtime profiles own the durable opt-in setting, the shared evaluator resolves the exact route and allowed provider references, entrypoints preserve manual-selection precedence, and `ReliableModelProvider` enforces the result immediately before physical provider attempts.

The implementation reuses `model_routes`, provider profiles, the deterministic complexity estimator, and the existing task-local provider context. Duplicate exact `model_routes` hints retain the existing final-entry-wins behavior, and effort routing uses the same resolution rule. The PR does not add another router or store prompt content. Direct CLI and daemon turns prune excluded provider profiles from a turn-local configuration because their large loop future cannot use the task-local wrapper without compiler type recursion; structured and channel turns use the task-local boundary directly.

The current policy has two modes, `never` and `auto`. Adding an interactive approval mode would require a shared approval owner across CLI, daemon, and channel entrypoints, so that behavior remains outside this slice.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A two-endpoint mock makes the route and fallback boundary visible without using a paid provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`, `channel`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure two distinct provider aliases that log received requests, add exact `local` and `cloud` entries to `[[model_routes]]`, and add the following block to the test agent's runtime profile:

  ```toml
  [runtime_profiles.local_first.effort_routing]
  local_hint = "local"
  cloud_hint = "cloud"
  cloud_escalation = "auto"
  ```

- **Steps to run:** Send a short message such as `Say hello`, then send an ASCII prompt longer than 200 bytes, such as 201 `a` characters. Repeat the long prompt after changing `cloud_escalation` to `"never"`. Finally run the CLI with an explicit `--provider` or `--model` override.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The short message reaches only the local alias. The long message reaches the cloud alias only under `"auto"`. Under `"never"` it stays local. The explicit override uses the selected route. Logs contain `Selected effort-based model route` with metadata but no prompt text.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The `effort_routing` profile contract does not exist. Turns use the configured baseline, existing hint routing, or independent classifier settings, and a local selection does not define a turn-wide local-only fallback boundary.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI is running on exact head `b5ded017138d589b04aaf113be0d8b5c9b53c850` after merging current `master`. It covers the aggregate Test, Lint, cross-platform, security, documentation, channel, plugin, runtime, and build matrix. Focused current-head tests cover the Fluent model-switch rejection, picker-revocation repair, real Agent and channel entry-point routing, active session- and scoped-operator override precedence, malformed-bracket media-marker privacy boundary, missing-hint fail-closed behavior, and backward compatibility for existing route hints named `auto`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Hosted CI cannot prove a real provider account's billing or latency. The focused tests use production route, fallback, stream, vision, session, and channel paths with local providers or mocks, so no external prompt was sent.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text

  git diff --check
  Result: passed

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime set_rejects_route_selector_as_provider_local_model

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime agent_turn_entry_points_apply_effort_route_and_attempt_boundary
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels effort_routing

  zeroclaw --config-dir <auto-config> agent --agent default --message "hello"

  Result: exited 0 with `cloud mock response`; the cloud endpoint recorded `cloud-model`

  zeroclaw --config-dir <never-config> agent --agent default --message <complex-prompt>
  Result: exited 0 with `local mock response`; the local endpoint recorded `local-model`

  zeroclaw --config-dir <auto-config> agent --agent default --message "hello" --model-provider custom.cloud --model cloud-model

  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I built an earlier exact-head `zeroclaw` binary and ran four real single-shot CLI processes against two loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The request logs proved simple `auto` stayed local, complex `auto` selected cloud, complex `never` stayed local, and an explicit provider/model override selected cloud. On the current master-integrated head, focused tests exercise the Fluent route-selector rejection, real channel provider dispatch for complex automatic selection, localized fail-closed behavior for a missing route, media-marker removal before classification even after unmatched bracket prose, opt-in `/model auto` reset, legacy route-hint compatibility outside effort routing, and both late picker-revocation branches. No prompt or credential left the machine.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No visual interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The supported `zeroclaw agent --message` CLI was exercised against two loopback providers on `1243830f97dc71317b0101914982e6efa7b27dae`. Focused Rust coverage on current master-integrated head `b5ded017138d589b04aaf113be0d8b5c9b53c850` verifies the Fluent route-selector rejection, final-entry route compatibility, provider-attempt boundaries, picker revocation, active manual channel choices under contradictory prompt complexity, automatic routing after scoped channel resets, malformed-bracket media-marker handling, missing-hint fail-closed behavior, and legacy `auto` route compatibility.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The live CLI sent a simple automatic turn to `custom.local` with `local-model`, sent a complex automatic turn to `custom.cloud` with `cloud-model`, kept the same complex turn on `custom.local` under `cloud_escalation = "never"`, and honored explicit `custom.cloud` / `cloud-model` overrides. Focused tests also proved fallback enforcement, model-issued switch ownership, fail-closed missing route configuration, final-entry compatibility for duplicate exact route hints, inert late-revoked `/model fast` and `/model auto`, real Agent and channel entry-point routing after scoped resets, local classification after malformed bracket prose plus an inline image marker, and preserved legacy selection of a route hint named `auto` outside effort routing.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests are delegated to required CI because the changed-crate clippy pass and focused production-path tests cover the local behavior contract. Optional external HTTP link checking was skipped because `lychee` is not installed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. An opted-in runtime profile gains the ability to choose a configured cloud route automatically. The feature is absent by default, cloud escalation defaults to `never`, and every physical attempt is limited to the selected provider set.
- New external network calls? Yes. A complex turn may reach an already configured cloud provider when `cloud_escalation = "auto"`. Classification itself makes no network call, and `"never"` prevents automatic cloud egress.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Existing provider profiles remain the only owners of credentials and endpoints.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The local estimator reads the current message for classification but does not add text to a model request or log the prompt.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Automatic cloud selection can change privacy exposure, cost, and latency. The explicit opt-in, local-only default, manual-selection precedence, fail-closed route resolution, turn-scoped provider allowlist, and redacted decision metadata bound that risk.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new block is optional and requires no schema migration.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Runtime profiles gain `effort_routing.local_hint`, `cloud_hint`, and `cloud_escalation`; channel `/model auto` and scoped auto variants now restore automatic routing after a manual selection.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing users need no upgrade action. To opt in, define two exact, distinct `model_routes` hints and reference them from the runtime profile. Within an opted-in effort-routing agent, `auto` is reserved by the channel command for restoring automatic routing. Remove the block or set `cloud_escalation = "never"` to keep automatic turns local.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-merge-sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Remove `runtime_profiles.<name>.effort_routing` to restore prior fixed/classifier behavior, or set `cloud_escalation = "never"` to keep automatic turns local without removing the route definitions.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A simple or ambiguous message reaches the cloud endpoint; a local turn logs a policy skip but still transmits through an excluded provider; `/model auto` does not restore automatic routing; config validation reports missing or unresolved local/cloud hints; duplicate exact hints do not use the final route entry.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): keep failed-turn status across reconnect and lag reload
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - A reconnect rebuild (after a daemon restart) now carries `TurnFailed` in each `ResumeEntry` and re-applies it in `restore_reconnect_state`. The rebuilt `ChatState` starts with `last_error` clear and `load_history` never sets it, so before this only `ResyncFailed` survived and a failed session came back green. `SessionLost` is still not carried: the rebuild's own re-attach resolves it.
  - The notification-lag reload (`replace_history_after_notification_resync`) now keeps `TurnFailed` and clears only the connection-class errors. A lag overflow reloads every tracked session, idle ones included, so one lag event turned every failed session green. Every dispatch from the pane already clears `TurnFailed` in `push_user_message`, so the kept value always belongs to the last turn this pane sent.
- **Scope boundary:** `ResyncFailed` and `TurnFailed` still share the single `last_error` field, so a failed resync replaces a failed-turn status and a later successful reload shows the session as ready. Splitting the turn outcome from the connection error is left out; it touches most `last_error` sites for a rarer case.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode client only. A failed session now stays red through reconnects and lag reloads until the next turn completes or the user sends a prompt. Queue dispatch does not gate on `TurnFailed`, so nothing that was dispatching stops.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11586
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's session list shows a red dot next to any session whose last request failed, so you can find the ones that need attention. When the daemon restarted, or when ZeroCode briefly fell behind on updates and reloaded its sessions, every red dot turned green again, even though the conversation still ended in the failure.

Now a failed session stays red through both of those, until you send it something new or its next request succeeds. One rarer case is unchanged: if ZeroCode's own reload attempts fail and later recover, the session can still come back green.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. The automated tests below render the real sidebar for both transitions against an in-process fake daemon. A live daemon-restart check in a real terminal was not performed on this head; if a reviewer wants that, it is the one thing the tests do not replace.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on the changed file
cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zerocode
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and clippy jobs cover `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this change.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` clean; clippy `Finished dev profile`, no warnings. `cargo test -p zerocode` on `f4003745b4`: lib `52 passed`; bin `1444 passed; 1 failed` — the one failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which fails the same way on `master` on this builder (environment-dependent; unrelated to this change).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Revert check on `f4003745b4`: with the two production changes removed (the `turn_failed` branch in `restore_reconnect_state` and the `TurnFailed` guard in `replace_history_after_notification_resync`; the field itself kept so the tests compile), all four tests below fail. The two renderer tests then report both dots `Green` where `Red`/`Green` is expected, so the rendered red dot depends on this change and not on the test setup. I did not run a live daemon restart in a real terminal on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** renderer-level automated tests, on head `f4003745b4`, in `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs` (`chat::tests`). Both draw the production `AgentSidebar::draw` into a ratatui `TestBackend` from the same `session_summaries()` rows the app hands the sidebar each frame, then read the status-dot cell (`●`) and its foreground color back from the terminal buffer per session row. The daemon side is an in-process fake: the tests answer the pane's JSON-RPC requests over the test transport; no daemon process runs.
  - `reconnect_rebuild_renders_failed_turn_red_and_recovered_session_lost_green`: two sessions, one with a `Failed` turn (`TurnFailed`) and one with a `session_not_found` failure (`SessionLost`). Asserts both dots render red before the socket drop. Snapshots `resume_entries()`, builds a fresh `Chat`, calls `set_resume_sessions` and runs its real `init()` (agents/status, session/new re-attach, config/list, session/messages answered by the fake). Asserts the rebuilt sidebar renders the failed-turn row red and the re-attached session-lost row green (the connection-error control), then checks `last_error` matches.
  - `notification_lag_reload_renders_failed_turn_red_and_recovered_resync_failed_green`: two sessions, one with a `Failed` turn and one carrying `ResyncFailed`. Asserts both dots render red. Overflows the notification channel so the drain reports `Lagged` and starts the real `Reattach` reload for every tracked session; the fake answers session/state (`idle`) and session/messages; the results are applied through `tick_transport_events`. Asserts the sidebar renders the failed-turn row red and the recovered `ResyncFailed` row green (the connection-error control), then checks `last_error`.
  - The two earlier helper-level tests (`notification_resync_reload_keeps_failed_turn_and_clears_resync_failed`, `reconnect_rebuild_keeps_failed_turn_red_and_clears_session_lost`) remain and assert the same transitions through `sidebar_status()`.
  No screenshots: the sidebar renderer and its styles are unchanged by this PR; the change is which status the renderer is given.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f4003745b4` (rebased onto master `8862e275ef`). Interface: the ZeroCode agent sidebar as drawn by `AgentSidebar::draw` into a ratatui test terminal. Evidence path: the four tests named above, run on a remote macOS arm64 builder and in CI's `Test` job on this head.

prs.title: fix(runtime): cap the structured Agent system prompt
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The structured Agent path (`Agent::turn` / `Agent::turn_streamed`, used by gateway web chats) built its system prompt without applying `max_system_prompt_chars`. The direct channel and CLI paths already cap the fully assembled prompt with `finalize_system_prompt` (#10465), so an agent with a small prompt ceiling worked from the CLI but received an uncapped prompt from the dashboard. With a small-context local model, the uncapped prompt overflows the context window.
  - `build_system_prompt_with_dispatcher` now applies `finalize_system_prompt` after the prompt is fully assembled, including dispatcher tool instructions, the tool-receipts addendum, deferred tools and pinned MCP resources. The timestamp orientation moves to the end of the assembled prompt and is appended once, so truncation cannot keep an earlier copy and then add a second one.
  - A turn can switch tool protocol after the prompt is built (hook-selected model, route hint or fallback). Both protocol variants are now built uncapped, and only the provider-bound request is capped after the switch; the history copy is spliced but not re-capped within the turn. When a cap applies and the request is native, its base is the complete native prompt with the tool section removed, then capped. It is never cut down from a history prompt that was capped for the text protocol, which can have lost `## Safety` inside the long tool section. When a cap has already removed the `## Safety` heading, the tool section ends at the preserved orientation so a switch never deletes it.
  - Text that a `before_llm_call` hook appends to the system prompt is kept: the request's protocol base is capped and the hook's suffix re-appended, as on the CLI path, including when an already finalized request is refreshed again after a history trim.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to `finalize_system_prompt` or its head-retention policy, to the channel/CLI prompt paths, to prompt section order, or to config. Known limits, matching the CLI path: re-appended hook text can take a request past the cap, and a hook that rewrites the system prompt instead of appending to it falls back to capping the whole request (with a text-capped history and a mid-turn switch to native, that path can still drop trailing sections). Capped native requests use the native prompt built at turn start. An explicit streamed model switch rebuilds the history system prompt but does not refresh that cached native prompt, so a later native request can retain the initial model label or workspace instructions until the next user turn.
- **Blast radius:** Agents with a non-zero `max_system_prompt_chars` (including the `local_small` preset) now receive a capped system prompt on structured Agent turns, as they already do on channel and CLI turns. With the default of `0` the prompt is unchanged apart from the orientation moving after the receipts, deferred-tools and pinned-MCP sections. `ToolProtocolPrompts` stays crate-private; its uncapped `new` constructor becomes test-only.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10465, whose scope boundary left structured Agent prompt assembly out. Related #5287: this is a focused enforcement slice of that broader local_small prompt-budget contract.
- **Labels:** `agent`, `runtime`, `size:M`, `risk:medium`

### What this does, simply

Some agents run on small local models that can only take a short system prompt, so ZeroClaw lets you set a maximum prompt size. The chat and command-line paths already respected that limit, but chats through the web dashboard use a different code path that built the full prompt and sent it without trimming it. On a small model that meant dashboard chats failed while the same agent worked from the CLI.

This PR applies the same limit, in the same way, on the dashboard path. It also keeps the limit in place when a turn switches how tools are described to the model, without dropping the safety rules or instructions added by hooks.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is covered by regression tests that check the provider-visible system prompt; a manual repro needs a small-context model.

### How I tested

- **Rebase note (2026-10-10):** rebased onto master `9cd75ac34` with GitHub's update-branch (base only; `git range-diff` shows every commit identical). The local evidence below was recorded on `ea0f071c`; required CI runs on the current head `58c4ded3`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, tests) covers the changed runtime code and the new regression tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for the changed code.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1, at this PR's head `ea0f071c6b79eb0cb41b58967c3531c4b200ff13` on master `32f90e9baff488c3a9d9b0b45a3505da7397c985`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                      -> exit 0
git diff --check                                                -> exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- system_prompt tool_protocol \
  surface2_tests surface3_tests timestamp_orientation
  test result: ok. 87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5376 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
  test result: ok. 5455 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

  New regression tests:
  - `streamed_agent_caps_fully_assembled_system_prompt_on_every_turn`: with a 4,000-character cap and a 5,000-character pinned MCP block, the initial prompt, the prompt rebuilt after a dispatcher switch, and the system prompt the provider receives on two streamed turns are each exactly 4,000 characters, end with the orientation, and contain it exactly once.
  - `scoped_protocol_switch_caps_request_and_keeps_history_lossless`: for a native-seeded history, a native → text → native switch caps each request, keeps one trailing orientation, and restores the history prompt exactly, including a pinned MCP block.
  - `scoped_switch_to_native_keeps_safety_when_text_history_was_cut_in_tools`: when the history prompt was capped for the text protocol inside its tool section, a switch to native still sends `## Safety` and the pinned MCP block within the cap.
  - `scoped_protocol_refresh_keeps_hook_appended_text`: text a hook appended survives with no switch and across a native → text switch, and refreshing an already finalized request again leaves it unchanged.
  - `scoped_protocol_refresh_caps_text_request_on_later_iterations`: after a switch, later text-protocol iterations are still capped even though history holds the full tool section.
  - `scoped_protocol_switch_keeps_orientation_when_cap_removed_safety`: when `## Safety` was already truncated away, switching protocols keeps the orientation in both directions.
- **Independent exact-SHA reviews:** Agy with `gemini-3.8-flash-high` and with `claude-opus-5-5-high` both returned `READY` for base `32f90e9baff488c3a9d9b0b45a3505da7397c985` / head `ea0f071c6b79eb0cb41b58967c3531c4b200ff13`, with only P3 notes (recorded under the scope boundary above). Earlier rounds on previous revisions found, and this head fixes: lossy re-capping of the history copy, hook-appended text being cut (also raised by the automated review on this PR), later text-protocol iterations sent uncapped, and `## Safety` lost on a text → native switch.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A local release build of master plus this PR (revision `42a3a21d`, before the hook and native-switch refinements) and two other open PRs runs the deployment that motivated the fix. In a fresh web dashboard chat, an agent with a 4,000-character ceiling on a 2,048-token local model (`qwen3:1.7b`) answered normally; before the fix, dashboard chats with that agent failed while the CLI worked. Not verified live: this exact head, hooks, or a mid-turn protocol switch (covered by the unit tests above).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full-workspace `cargo test` was not run locally; the change is confined to `zeroclaw-runtime`, whose full lib suite ran above, and required CI covers the rest.

### Follow-up, not in this PR

`finalize_system_prompt` keeps the head of the prompt and cuts the tail, on every path. When a cap applies, the tail sections (tool receipts, deferred-tool guidance, pinned MCP resources) are the first to go, and a cut can land inside an `<mcp-resource>` block. That is the existing channel/CLI behavior, so this PR keeps it for consistency. Section-aware trimming (dropping whole blocks or reserving budget for tool guidance) would change every caller and is better decided separately.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** (the same prompt content, now within the configured ceiling)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>`. Setting `max_system_prompt_chars = 0` (the default) also leaves the structured Agent prompt uncapped.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** A tool-calling turn replays a thinking model's scratchpad back to the endpoint as the canonical `reasoning_content`. Some OpenAI-compatible backends (notably certain vLLM builds) only accept the shorter `reasoning` alias and reject or silently drop the canonical key, breaking multi-turn tool use. This adds an opt-in wire rename.
- **What changed and why (mechanics):** Add `reasoning_key: Option<String>` to `ModelProviderConfig` and `ModelProviderRuntimeOptions`, and a `reasoning_key()` builder method on `OpenAiCompatibleModelProvider`. A new `attach_chat_body` rewrites `messages[*].reasoning_content` to the configured key when set (short-circuiting to the plain `.json()` path otherwise), and the chat-completions request sites route through it.
- **Scope boundary:** Chat-completions wire only. Stored assistant history stays under `reasoning_content`; only the outgoing request body is renamed. Blank and canonical (`"reasoning_content"`) values normalize to `None`.
- **Blast radius:** Wire serialization of OpenAI-compatible chat-completions requests when `reasoning_key` is set; no behavior change when unset (default).
- **Linked issue(s):** None.
- **Labels:** `providers`, `config` (auto path/scope labels; `size:*`/`risk:*` pending labelers/maintainers).

### What this does, simply

Operators pointing a `custom` (or generic OpenAI-compatible) slot at a vLLM endpoint that only accepts the `reasoning` field can now set `reasoning_key = "reasoning"` so the thinking model's scratchpad is sent under that name instead of `reasoning_content`, without changing how the assistant history is stored or how responses are parsed.

prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** the head is now `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b`, one commit on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. It supersedes `76275ecf6`. What changed:
  - Inventory: `agy_cli` is registered in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` as a Host-tier tool, listed in the tier table and prose of `tool-inventory.md`, and enabled in the runtime maximal-config inventory test. This fixes the `matrix_safe_policy_names_only_inventoried_tools` failure that appeared after master's typed tool inventory landed, and Greptile's inventory finding.
  - i18n: the tool description, parameter descriptions and errors are Fluent `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in the canonical English catalogue, with the generated tools-crate mirror regenerated. This addresses Greptile's localization finding.
  - Hardening of `agy_cli`'s own contract: a bare `--` in `extra_args` is dropped from the agy argv and flagged by config validation, so it can no longer turn the tool-owned flags into positionals. An explicit JSON `null` for `response`, `denied_actions` or `error` no longer breaks parsing, so agy's real status and error are reported; success still requires `status == SUCCESS` and no denied actions. The `--print-timeout` margin scales with small timeouts instead of collapsing to `1s`. The attached form `--dangerously-skip-permissions=<value>` now triggers the risky-flag warning (agy only; Codex matching is unchanged). Stderr appended to errors is capped like stdout. `agy_cli` is added to the Integrations-group test.
  - Not changed: the shared coding-CLI workdir refactor, Codex helper naming, the model-visible remediation text, and tolerance for non-JSON banner lines.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required Rust CI (fmt, clippy, tests) covers the new tool, config section, and wiring.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no `agy` binary. The live behaviour against real agy was checked locally (below).
- **Validation at `34d7aea08` (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1):** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` 0; Fluent generator `--check` 0; `zeroclaw-tools` lib 43 passed; `zeroclaw-tools` inventory docs-drift/source-scan integration tests 1 + 3 passed; `zeroclaw-config` lib agy/section filters 26 passed; `zeroclaw-runtime` `coding_cli agy_cli` filters 17 passed; `zeroclaw-channels` inventory/matrix filters 2 passed; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on tools, runtime, channels and config 0; `git diff --check` 0.
- **Mutation checks:** reverting the explicit-`null` handling fails 3 of the new tests; reverting the bare-`--` filtering fails 1 test in `zeroclaw-tools` and 1 in `zeroclaw-config`. The tree was restored byte-identical afterwards.
- **Review:** exact-SHA Gemini review via Agy (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`, bundle of the complete `0f8fb9d37..34d7aea08` diff, no tools) returned READY with no findings, blockers or test gaps. This is the only review lane for this revision; a second review was not run.
- **CI:** pending for `34d7aea08` at the time of writing. Earlier-head CI results are not carried over. `Platform Test (macOS)` and `Platform Test (Windows)` failed on the scheduled master run with the same unrelated tests, so any failure there is expected to be master-wide.
- **Live use (earlier revision, before the 2026-10-11 hardening):** the same patch ran in a local `release-fast` integration build (master `1d64833a9` + this PR + #11080) on aarch64 Linux since 2026-09-29; a live agent-driven `agy_cli` call returned the expected reply.
- **Historical local checks** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1), from earlier heads with the same agy_cli patch: `411d9ec42` amends `0543611e8` only to name `agy_cli.extra_args` as the ZeroClaw-side remedy in the auto-denied-permission error, plus one assertion. `500590f3c` changes only `agy_cli.rs` relative to `5d4b5bc7e`.

```text
# at 411d9ec42 (differs from 0543611e8 only in agy_cli.rs error text + 1 assertion)
cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-tools -- --check                        -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli
  test result: ok. 25 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 500590f3c
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings  -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- agy_cli coding_cli coding_agent cli_discovery attribution
  test result: ok. 41 passed; 0 failed
git diff --check                                            -> exit 0

# at 5d4b5bc7e (differs only in agy_cli.rs)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime \
  -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets -- -D warnings          -> exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- agy_cli codex_cli sections validation_warnings
  test result: ok. 68 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::registered_coding_cli tools::tests::coding_cli
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::tests::docker_without_workspace_mount_does_not_register_coding_cli_tools
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- map_tool_kind matrix_safe
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I ran the real tool code (`AgyCliTool::execute`) against agy 1.2.9 with a throwaway, local-only `#[ignore]` test that is not part of this PR:
  - A plain prompt returned `success=true` with the expected text.
  - With `extra_args = ["--sandbox"]`, a prompt that needs a shell command returned `success=false` with the auto-denied `RunCommand` explanation. agy itself exited 0 with `status: SUCCESS`.
  - A prompt beginning with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` was treated as prompt text, returning `success=true` with the expected reply, not as a flag.
  - The scratch workspace was empty afterwards.

  Not verified: behaviour on macOS or Windows, and agy versions other than 1.2.9. The live run was at `5d4b5bc7e`; `500590f3c` only adds stderr to the non-`SUCCESS` status error and two unit tests.

  Operator misconfiguration: a bare `--` in `extra_args` made agy 1.2.9 reject the following tool-owned flags (`Error: unexpected argument "--output-format=json"`, exit 2) without running anything. As of `34d7aea08`, `agy_cli` drops bare `--` entries from the agy argv and config validation warns about them, so the flags stay flags; a trailing value-taking flag in `extra_args` (for example `--effort`) is still operator argv and is documented as such in the tools overview.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full-workspace `cargo test` was not run locally. The changed surfaces are covered by the focused tests above and required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes**
- New external network calls? **Yes**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - Permissions and network: when enabled, `agy_cli` launches `agy`, which acts on files and calls Google's services under its own permission model, like the existing coding-CLI tools. The tool is disabled by default and gated by the same security policy, autonomy level and rate limiting as its peers, and the working directory is canonicalized and must stay inside the workspace. Operator `extra_args` that widen agy's permissions (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--add-dir`) produce a non-blocking config-validation warning that does not echo the values.
  - Prompt injection: agy's response is returned to the model as tool output, the same as for the other coding CLIs. Output is bounded by `max_output_bytes`.
  - Containment limit, stated in the docs: ZeroClaw validates only the starting directory. What `agy` touches after launch is governed by agy's own settings.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[agy_cli]` config section, disabled by default. Existing configs are unaffected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Upgrade steps: none required. To use the tool, add `[agy_cli]` with `enabled = true` and have an authenticated `agy` on `PATH`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Medium risk and opt-in: `git revert <sha>`. The `[agy_cli] enabled = false` setting, which is the default, also disables it at runtime.

prs.title: fix(mcp-builder): support mcp>=2 streamable_http_client import and custom headers
prs.body:
Fixes #1668

### Problem
In `mcp>=2.0.0`, `streamablehttp_client` was renamed to `streamable_http_client`, and custom HTTP headers are configured via `create_mcp_http_client` / `http_client` rather than as a direct kwarg to `streamable_http_client`.

Because `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py` unconditionally imported `streamablehttp_client` at module scope, importing `connections` or running `evaluation.py` fails on startup when installing `requirements.txt` (which specifies `mcp>=1.1.0` without an upper bound):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../scripts/evaluation.py", line 19, in <module>
    from connections import create_connection
  File ".../scripts/connections.py", line 10, in <module>
    from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client
ImportError: cannot import name 'streamablehttp_client' from 'mcp.client.streamable_http'
```

### Solution
1. **Compatible import:** In `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/connections.py`, import `streamable_http_client` and `create_mcp_http_client` with fallback to `streamablehttp_client as streamable_http_client` for `mcp<2.0.0`.
2. **Context configuration:** In `MCPConnectionHTTP._create_context()`:
   - When `create_mcp_http_client` is available, create `http_client` with custom headers and pass to `streamable_http_client(url=self.url, http_client=http_client)`.
   - On `mcp<2.0.0`, pass `headers=self.headers` directly.
3. **Regression tests:** Added `skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py` testing import resolution, stdio/sse/http transport factories, context manager creation, and validation error cases.

### Verification
- Ran `pytest skills/mcp-builder/scripts/test_connections.py -v`: all 5 tests passed.
- Verified `python skills/mcp-builder/scripts/evaluation.py --help` under `mcp 2.1.1` and Python 3.14: cleanly displays full usage and exits 0.
- Verified compilation with `python -m py_compile`.

prs.title: fix(skill-creator): isolate trigger evals and handle Windows and runtime failures
prs.body:
## Problem

Trigger evaluation can report false misses or invalid scores: per-worker command probes compete, select() on subprocess pipes fails on Windows, and unrelated tools stop the scan. Runtime failures also become non-triggers, incorrectly passing negative examples and misleading optimization.

Fixes #556.

## What changes

- Install one real candidate skill at `<temporary project>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, preserving its production name and candidate description. Parallel workers share it; concurrent runs use distinct UUID-based roots.
- Leave caller files untouched. The legacy `project_root` argument remains accepted but is no longer used.
- Reject same-name personal skill collisions, including those under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Resolve the Claude executable, including Windows npm shims. Read stdout/stderr with portable threads instead of select(). Close stdin and cap probes at eight turns.
- Keep scanning after Bash/Glob and other orientation tools. Match exact Skill names or skill-entrypoint Read paths, including Windows separators.
- Stop the probe process tree during cleanup: `taskkill /T /F` on Windows; a separate session/process group on POSIX.
- Treat error results, timeouts, truncated output and worker failures as invalid evaluations. Abort the batch instead of assigning zero trigger rates. Cancel pending work where possible; active workers finish their bounded cleanup.
- Preserve successful evaluation JSON. Initial optimization failures propagate; later failures preserve completed iterations. Empty and partial reports render correctly.
- Write candidate artifacts as UTF-8.

## Validation

Latest revision: Windows, Python 3.14.

```sh
# From skills/skill-creator
python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v
uvx ruff check scripts/run_eval.py scripts/tests/test_eval_failures.py scripts/tests/test_stream_probe.py
git diff --check
```

- **21/21 tests pass.** Coverage includes artifact isolation, exact matching, late triggers, configuration collisions, invalid batch rejection, cleanup and partial-result recovery.
- A real Windows .cmd wrapper launches a Python child; the regression verifies that the child cannot continue after timeout. This test requires process-termination permissions and was run outside the restricted sandbox.
- Ruff passes for the files changed in the latest revision. Whitespace checks pass.
- Tests make no model calls and need no credentials. Instructions and limitations are in `scripts/tests/README.md`.

## Scope and limitations

The temporary project excludes caller-project files and configuration. Queries requiring local fixtures need those fixtures made available separately. Personal and managed Claude configuration is not fully isolated.

The original investigation included live routing experiments on Claude Code 2.1.149. Those historical observations are not a claim about every current version. This revision has not rerun live model evaluation or POSIX integration. The candidate uses the standard skill layout independently of legacy command behavior.

Related work: #794, #996, #1027, #1755 and #1757. This PR combines a real-skill artifact with portable stream handling, full-turn detection and explicit failure semantics.

## What changed
`skills/docx/scripts/accept_changes.py` now returns an Error when `soffice` times out instead of reporting success, and only claims success after checking that the output DOCX no longer carries revision marks (`w:ins` / `w:del` / `w:moveFrom` / `w:moveTo`) in `word/*.xml` parts.

## Why
Defect 1 in #1770: `soffice` operates in place on a copy and the macro stores/closes the document itself, so a timeout leaves the output in an unknown state (possibly untouched, possibly partly processed) while the caller was told "Successfully accepted all tracked changes". `__main__` keys on `"Error" in message`, so the process also exited 0.

LibreOffice is not installed in this environment, so the fix is verified with mocked `subprocess.run` plus real DOCX fixtures:
- Timeout (`subprocess.TimeoutExpired`): returns an Error mentioning the timeout, never "Successfully".
- `returncode == 0` but the output still contains `<w:ins>`: returns "tracked changes remain in output document".
- `returncode == 0` with a clean output DOCX: still reports success.
- `_docx_still_has_tracked_changes`: True for each revision marker (`w:ins`, `w:del`, `w:moveFrom`, `w:moveTo`) and for a non-zip file, False for a clean DOCX.

### Problem
Running \package_skill.py\ directly as a standalone script (e.g., \python skills/skill-creator/scripts/package_skill.py <skill-path>\) fails with \ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts.quick_validate'\. Additionally, the docstrings and CLI help messages contain outdated references to \utils/package_skill.py\ and \skills/public/...\.

When executed directly as a script, Python places the script's immediate directory (\skills/skill-creator/scripts\) at \sys.path[0]\, preventing the top-level \scripts\ package from being resolved.

prs.title: Add document-typography skill: typographic quality control for generated documents
prs.body:
Prevents common typographic problems in AI-generated documents: orphan word wrap (1-6 words spilling onto the next line), widow paragraphs (section headers stranded at page bottom), and numbering misalignment.

These issues affect every document Claude generates. Users rarely ask for good typography, but they notice when it's bad.

**How it works**

The skill introduces a render-check-fix cycle: generate the document, convert to PDF, render pages as images, visually inspect, fix and regenerate. It also includes the M-count method — count how many capital M's (the widest character) fit on one line. Any real text will always be narrower, eliminating orphan wrap entirely.

**Included scripts**
- `measure_m_count.py` — Safe character limit per line using font metrics
- `check_orphans.py` — Reports lines at risk of orphan wrap
- `check_layout.sh` — One-command docx → PDF → page images
- `measure_line_width.py` — Visual line-width calibration

**Origin**

This skill emerged from iterative human-AI collaboration between [@PGTBoos](https://github.com/PGTBoos) and Claude. The user kept pointing out what the AI couldn't see (orphan words, widow paragraphs, layout balance) until the patterns were systematic enough to codify into a reusable skill. The M-count formula was the user's insight. The user actively wants to make LLMs more human-like, and sees this contribution as a help for both AI and humans writing skills.

- [x] SKILL.md with valid YAML frontmatter
- [x] Scripts are self-contained

prs.title: skill-creator: harden eval viewer (script breakout, DNS rebinding, cross-site POST, escaping)
prs.body:
## What

Hardens the `skill-creator` eval viewer (`generate_review.py` + `viewer.html`). The viewer is a local page that renders eval outputs (model-written, so untrusted) and saves feedback via a small HTTP server on localhost. Three gaps:

1. **Script breakout.** The page data is embedded as JSON in an inline `<script>`. A value containing `</script>` ended the block and the rest ran as HTML. Now `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 are escaped as `\uXXXX` in the embedded JSON; it still parses to the identical object.
2. **No Host/Origin check on the local server.** Any web page open in the same browser could POST to `/api/feedback`, and a DNS-rebinding page could read the data back. Now `do_GET` and `do_POST` return 403 unless `Host` is `localhost:<port>` or `127.0.0.1:<port>` and `Origin`, if present, is one of those hosts. Requests without `Origin` (curl, same-origin GET) still work.
3. **Incomplete HTML escaping in `viewer.html`.** `escapeHtml` did not escape quotes and several fields (`metadata.timestamp`, `evals_run`, `runs_per_configuration`, the delta fields, `configLabel`, `run_number`, including a `title` attribute) went into `innerHTML` unescaped. `escapeHtml` now escapes `& < > " '` and returns `""` for null/undefined, and is applied to those fields.

## Testing

Ran the same script against the original and patched files (Python 3 + Node):

| Check | Original | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| `</script>` payload does not add a closing tag | fails | passes |
| Embedded JSON round-trips to identical object | passes | passes |
| `escapeHtml` escapes `"` and `'` | fails | passes |
| Same-origin POST `/api/feedback` | 200 | 200 |
| POST with no Origin | 200 | 200 |
| POST with foreign Origin | 200 | 403 |
| GET with foreign Host (rebinding) | 200 | 403 |
| GET `/` | 200 | 200 |

`py_compile` is clean. The browser page only calls relative `/api/feedback`, so the normal flow is unchanged. A separate read-only review of the diff found no blocking issues.

## Not covered (follow-up)

- A port-less `Host: localhost` is rejected; browsers always send the port here because it is non-default.
- Some other values still reach `innerHTML` unescaped: `r.passed`, `r.total`, `r.errors` in the benchmark table, and `summary.passed/failed/total` in `renderGrades`. They are normally numbers; I left them out to keep this change focused. Happy to extend the patch.
- The same files exist in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` (`plugins/skill-creator`); I have not opened a PR there.

prs.title: Improve frontend-design skill clarity and actionability
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR revises the frontend-design skill to improve clarity, actionability, and internal coherence. The goal was to ensure every instruction is something Claude can actually follow within a single conversation, and that the skill's guidance is specific enough to steer behavior without being prescriptive.

## Background

I've been exploring Anthropic's open-source ecosystem after building a [GUI for Bloom](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/anthropicbloom) and [proposing new behaviors](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/10behaviorsbloom) for it. Looking through the Skills repo, the frontend-design skill caught my attention. Reading through it, I noticed a few places where the instructions, while well-intentioned, weren't quite actionable from the model's perspective.

For example, the original skill said "NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations" and "No design should be the same." The intent is clear: avoid repetitive patterns. But Claude can't see its other generations. Each conversation is isolated. These instructions are impossible to follow because they reference information the model doesn't have access to.

This got me thinking about what I call "model theory of mind": reasoning about what the model can actually know and how it processes instructions. A prompt can sound good to humans but be confusing or non-actionable for the model. I wrote up my thinking in more detail [here](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/scaffold).

## Key Changes

**Coherence fixes:**
- Removed instructions assuming cross-session awareness ("never converge across generations," "no design should be the same")
- Resolved internal contradictions ("pick an extreme" conflicted with "the key is intentionality, not intensity")

**Clarity improvements:**
- Replaced vague adjectives ("beautiful, unique, interesting") with concrete guidance
- Rewrote the Typography section to focus on actionable instructions rather than aesthetic judgments
- Added specific palette directions to Color guidance (bold/saturated, moody/restrained, high-contrast/minimal)

**Structural additions:**
- Added INSTEAD block to pair positive instructions with existing NEVER guidance
- Expanded aesthetic direction list (added dark/moody, lo-fi/zine, handcrafted/artisanal)
- Expanded spatial composition guidance (z-depth, full-bleed, dramatic scale jumps)
- Unified imperative voice throughout

## Validation

I built an evaluation system to test whether the changes actually improved outputs. The setup:

- 50 representative prompts covering different design contexts (landing pages, dashboards, portfolios, menus, band pages, etc.)
- Each prompt executed twice via API: once with original skill, once with revised skill
- Puppeteer captures full-page screenshots of both outputs
- Claude Opus 4.5 judges blind (screenshots anonymized as A/B) on five criteria: Prompt Adherence, Aesthetic Fit, Visual Polish, UX & Usability, Creative Distinction

Results across the Claude 4.5 model family: Haiku showed the strongest improvement (8-2), followed by Sonnet (7-3), then Opus (6-4). Across all three tiers, the revised skill won 21 of 28 decisive comparisons (75% win rate, p = 0.006).

Interestingly, the revised skill helped smaller models more than larger ones. My hypothesis is that Opus can compensate for ambiguous instructions, while Haiku benefits more from explicit guidance.

## More Detail

For a full walkthrough of the approach, reasoning, and specific edits: [Teaching Claude to Design Better: Improving Anthropic's Frontend Design Skill](https://www.justinwetch.com/blog/improvingclaudefrontend)

Happy to discuss any of the changes or adjust based on feedback.
